Su Lun was unaware, but his limited perception also allowed him to touch upon some of the mysteries of this magical alchemy. It was as if he was traversing an endless starry sky, then casually plucking a brilliant star from it and merging it into his body.
The process went smoother than anticipated, with no incidents that could be deemed unexpected.
Su Lun didn't know what had happened; his vision was a blur of red.
Soon, he became quite aware of the pain in his eye fading away, and the light in his left eye slowly returning.
"It worked…"
Su Lun roughly guessed what had happened and let out a deep sigh of relief.
The tingling sensation was an indication of muscle tissue regenerating, happening unbelievably fast.
The whole process lasted about three minutes, and then the red light of the magic formation on the altar finally faded completely.
And in the moment the red light dispersed, the statue with the "ꧧ" symbol also "cracked" open with a fissure.
Su Lun's left eye slowly focused, clear and dazzling, radiant like a newborn baby. Upon closer inspection, within the golden pupil, there was also a silver "moon." With a flash, the moonlight vanished deep into the pupil.
This was a very fascinating experience; the scene in front of him was still the same old altar, yet it now seemed like a strange "new world." Every object was incredibly clear, as if he was looking at a high-definition photograph without any filters, the minutest details visible. Even the densely packed, spiderweb-like cracks on the statues were discernible.
....
"So... what extraordinary ability have I awakened? Could it be [Enhanced Vision]?"
Confirming the ritual was complete, Su Lun looked around, then lowered his head to examine his own body.
His appearance seemed unchanged, except that his vision had improved significantly, his sight crystal clear even in dim light.
If that were all, he felt it was far inferior to Baldy's [Reinforced Skeleton]…
But just as Su Lun was internally complaining, a strange feeling emerged.
He meticulously examined his body, and after a searching glance as if trying to see through fog, strange text actually emerged in his eyes.
Su Lun (Fike Regadi)
Dark Spiritual Power: 233/1130
Charm: 9
Strength: 6
Agility: 6
Constitution: 5
Perception: 4
Skill: 8
Spiritual Power: 26
Talent: "Talent S-018-All-knowing Eye"
Skills: "Haigem Breathing Method", "Basic Firearm Mastery", "Advanced Combat Basics"
Overall Combat Evaluation: Remarkably average
At this point, it was as if time had paused for a moment.
Su Lun exclaimed in surprise, "A statistic panel?"
When he saw this string of data appear on his retina, he vaguely felt as if he was playing a game again.
But when he saw the "Talent S-018-All-knowing Eye" on the panel, he suddenly realized.
"So, this supernatural talent awakened by the sacrificial ritual is this ability? It doesn't seem very impressive..."
Su Lun muttered to himself, understanding why the sacrifice required was his own eyeball.
So this "directed awakening" meant an eye for an eye.
Su Lun's thoughts were quick to jump, and he didn't dwell on things he couldn't change, instead starting to criticize the evaluations on the panel.
Could my combat skills, competent enough to tackle ten on Earth, really just be an "Advanced Basics"?
That's hardly important...
And that archery technique, honed after depleting most of his savings at the shooting range, amounted to just "Basic Mastery"?
What would "Advanced Mastery" in shooting look like? Could bullets actually bend around corners?
Moreover!
An overall evaluation of remarkably average?
"Heh... compared to Baldy, it really is just remarkably average."
Su Lun scoffed at himself internally, propping his chin.
Looking at this evaluation, he also roughly understood the hierarchy of combat power in this world.
And that oddly named "Haigem Breathing Method" must be a "passive skill" the original body had learned.
Su Lun had previously felt a strange energy flowing inside his body, his breathing also naturally following a specific rhythm, almost like a "muscle memory" kind of thing that was instinctive.
And the Dark Spiritual Power must be something similar to the "internal family Qigong" from his past life.
But he looked at his attribute panel again and showed a hint of confusion. Most of the attributes were explainable, but the "26 points" in spiritual power was particularly striking.
Su Lun pondered, chin in hand, but before he could reflect further...
At that moment, something unexpected happened!
Just then, the altar, whose light had already dissipated, suddenly lit up again.
This time, it wasn't a golden light but a cold, misty glow shrouding it. It was like opening a gateway to hell, and he felt a chilling aura emanating from his soul.
"What's going on, has the alchemy formation activated again?!"
Su Lun was greatly puzzled, as the information on his retina hadn't recorded such a bizarre occurrence during the ritual process.
But he did not react, because this scene was very similar to when he had first awakened.
After the magical formation's light flashed, the last cloak-clad statue with a "☽" symbol lit up with a glow, and a faint black light seeped out from the statue.
This transformation process was much faster than before.
"Didn't my talent already awaken? Why is it happening again? I didn't make any sacrifices..."
Su Lun watched the familiar process, baffled.
At the same time, he felt as if something invisible was being drawn out of his body, inexplicably feeling much lighter.
It wasn't long before the octagram's light faded, and that statue cracked as well.
Now, of the five statues, none remained intact.
Su Lun clearly felt that the mysterious and reverential feeling previously emitted by these statues had suddenly vanished, turning into five ordinary stone sculptures.
....
Su Lun looked at the panel again, wanting to know what had happened to his body.
Then, he directly noticed another item had appeared in the talent section—"Talent S-004-Reaper."

chapters.title: Chapter 10 - 10: Extraordinary Items Reaped
chapters.content:
"Dual talents? What's that supposed to mean?"
Su Lun lacked basic knowledge of this world, so even with the extra talent revealed, he had no clue what it was for.
Moreover, he noticed his spiritual power score had dropped from "26" to "18".
His spiritual power decreased by 8 points, and that whispering sensation by his ears had completely vanished.
Su Lun speculated, "The principle of this altar is to offer items in exchange for some extraordinary talent. Before it was an eye for an eye. Now that my spiritual power has decreased, could it be... the original host's remnant soul has been fully sacrificed, granting me a new talent?"
He didn't dwell on this question, as there was no way to confirm it anyway.
But then, a bizarre thought popped into Su Lun's mind: What if one were not a transmigrator, what would a normal person offer to obtain this talent—commit suicide on the altar and sacrifice their own soul?
....
"What's the use of this [Talent S-004-Death Reaper]?"
After all, this wasn't a game; there were no skill usage instructions in reality.
Su Lun looked for a moment but was still utterly clueless, and his body underwent no noticeable enhancement.
He thought for a bit, stopped fretting over it, and continued to test the ability his eyes had gained.
Suddenly, he turned his gaze towards some stone sculptures, and a string of text emerged.
[Broken Sculpture]
Detailed Explanation: A sculpture that has lost its extraordinary powers, not worth observing;
This time, Su Lun roughly understood the use of this talent: "Isn't this just like the 'Identify Skill' in games..."
If one spoke of how the talent augmented combat ability... Well, it didn't enhance it much, to say the least, one could say it's completely useless.
This could basically be classified as an auxiliary feature.
At least, in a real fight, it was not at all on the same level as Baldy's [Strengthened Skeleton].
"Probably I haven't figured out the use of this 'All-knowing Eye', or maybe there are capabilities I haven't yet unlocked. Such a complex awakening ritual can't be this simple..."
Looking on, Su Lun didn't feel too disappointed.
At least, his vision had improved, which seemed to have made his marksmanship even more precise.
At that moment, he suddenly remembered something, descended from the altar, and took out the magic doll that Pestoya had given him to assess.
Upon examining it, he realized it was indeed a treasure.
[Cursed Object: Rune Puppet]
Quality: Gold
Description: It dislikes being controlled, preferring to control humans;
Cursed Attributes: Within a ten-meter radius, it indiscriminately exerts mental control over creatures with a spiritual power lower than 15, inducing hypnosis, limb disarray, madness...
Detailed Explanation: A mystical series material for the 'Puppeteer' occupation in Alchemy; after employment, substantially enhances technique and agility attributes, comprehending exclusive inherited skills.
Evaluation: Body compatibility 93%, this is already a profession advancement material of quite impressive quality.
If not for the "All-Knowing Eye", Su Lun wouldn't have guessed that a toy doll he regarded as a "souvenir" could be so powerful.
"Limb disarray, huh... Isn't that one of Pestoya's extraordinary abilities?"
As he read the detailed explanation, Su Lun immediately recalled the scene where his hands and feet uncontrollably moved to eat during the banquet.
Directly stripping control of one's body, this ability was indeed sinister.
"To think it's indiscriminate mental control..."
Su Lun observed, his expression growing stern. If not for his spiritual power being stronger than that of a normal person, having this thing close by would likely drive him insane on spot.
Well... It's akin to carrying around a dangerous "nuclear radiation toy."
And at that moment, he also noticed a new term in the detailed explanation—employment material.
He thought of the time when Bald Ivan had used a magic array to transform his metal scale armor. Could this be some kind of special technique for an advanced career?
Su Lun, with his head full of strange knowledge, also guessed that this so-called "initiation" was probably similar to a job change in a game.
"Pestoya's career must be 'Puppeteer'... But how to initiate?"
Su Lun's mind was filled with countless question marks as he sighed softly.
His understanding of this world was far too limited, lacking many essential pieces of common knowledge.
Now, having the ability of the "All-knowing Eye" seemed quite useful, at least it allowed him to see these magical items without being completely baffled.
.....
Su Lun put the puppet back into the wooden box.
To his surprise, upon a closer look, the rune-engraved puppet box itself turned out to be a treasure.
[Level II Rune Sealed Wooden Box]
Detail: A special alchemy box that blocks the fluctuations of spiritual power; upon closer inspection, you will find some text carved on it.
Su Lun had previously felt there was something special about the patterns on the box, and now, seeing this prompt, he looked closer and discovered those patterns were actually tiny characters tightly packed together, astonishingly constituting a "Beginner's Guide to Crafty Puppetry".
"Could it be that Pestoya, feeling my spiritual power was strong, deemed me suitable to be a Puppet Master and not only provided 'initiation materials' but also sent along a book on vocational skills?"
Su Lun suddenly thought of the well-behaved girl with golden hair and blue eyes, feeling an unshakable sense of regret in his heart.
What a pity...
He hadn't forgotten the promise he made to the girl, to ask her parents why they had burned her.
But the manor had been abandoned for at least a few hundred years, her parents were probably long gone.
This "promise" may never be fulfilled.
Then, looking again, he noticed the butterfly brooch that the little girl had affixed to his chest, which was also an extraordinary item.
[Pestoya's Brooch]
Focus +10
Detail: A brooch with a strong sense of resentment. A delicate alchemy product, it allows the wearer to learn, cast spells, work... with greater concentration. However, wearing it long term, the resentment makes one's temperament become perverse and violent.
(Note: Your extraordinary ability prevents you from detecting or understanding things that are far beyond your cognitive level, so after careful sensing, you also see a string of 'unknown???'...)
Su Lun looked at the brooch, originally thinking it was just a random gift from the little girl.
But unexpectedly, when he saw the "???" note at the back of the brooch, a string of question marks also appeared in his mind.
A sense of mysterious bewilderment suddenly enveloped him.
Was there something in the brooch that he couldn't yet understand? Something that made the "All-knowing Eye" determine it was beyond his comprehension—like explaining the concept of three or four dimensions to a two-dimensional being, who can hear and see but just cannot comprehend?
Anything that confounded even a transmigrator like himself must be no simple matter...
"Could there be some secret hidden in this brooch?"
Su Lun instinctively felt something was amiss.
At that moment, the troubling question that plagued Su Lun surfaced again in his mind: why did Pestoya's parents burn her?
Perhaps there was a problem with her very being?
In this world of extraordinary abilities, who knows what kinds of bizarre entities may exist.
If it weren't for the "All-knowing Eye", Su Lun might never have noticed anything unusual about the brooch.
But now that he had discovered it, he grew more wary.
Yet Su Lun thought again, since Pestoya was the big boss of this manor, even with these doubts, it was better not to linger here.
With that thought, he decided to leave this place first.

chapters.title: Chapter 11 - 11 [Reaper of Death]
chapters.content:
"The original owner" came to this manor in search for the ancient altar, to obtain that "S-class" superhuman talent through a ritual.
Su Lun did fulfill the original owner's last wish.
The difference now, though, was that he had awakened two talents.
Without a reference, Su Lun didn't know if this was good or bad, or even normal.
He had figured out some abilities of the All-knowing Eye, but he had no clue about the function of the Reaper.
The information left on the retina had nothing more to offer, the only useful thing being that map.
At least, he knew where the original owner came from, and he could follow the same route back to the "starting point."
Su Lun also planned to leave this place and find a human settlement to learn more about this world.
...
He looked around the basement carefully, nothing extra was there.
All five stone statues already had cobweb-like cracks that had spread to the altar, which seemed to have completely lost its function.
Su Lun didn't linger long and exited the secret passage.
Back in the ruined manor, Su Lun was already gasping for breath.
Heavy blood loss made his head feel dizzy.
And the items he had before crossing over had been taken away by Bald Ivan and his cronies. Now he desperately needed to find some food to fill his stomach and replenish his energy.
Otherwise, he knew he wouldn't be able to walk far alive.
"I don't even know what kind of entity Pestoia is, nor where that special space is..."
Staring at the ruined manor, Su Lun always felt as if everything before him was a dream.
According to what Marcus said earlier, Baldy and his group of more than a dozen all died in the manor; there should be bodies to be seen.
But now, after a walk around, Su Lun saw no bodies at all, and from the cobwebs in the passageway, he could deduce that nobody except himself had come here.
Su Lun didn't find anything in the house and walked out the front door.
Stepping into the yard, he then noticed the sky was murky, like night skies hidden behind heavy clouds, the surrounding scenery dim and fuzzy.
The manor seemed to be located halfway up a mountain, and with the "enhanced vision", Su Lun could finally make out the vague silhouettes of some large buildings in the distance.
It looked like a ruined ghost town.
There were no light sources in the town, shrouded in fog, and the shadows of some huge moving creatures could vaguely be seen within the mist...
Seeing this scene, Su Lun's gaze grew deeper as he muttered to himself, "The mysteries of this world are indeed becoming more and more intriguing..."
It felt like discovering an unexplored mysterious map in a game, his strong desire to explore making his heart flutter.
This was also one of the reasons he wanted to stay alive.
But if a dilapidated manor was so eerie and dangerous, it was clear that the ruined buildings in the distance were fraught with peril.
Su Lun didn't plan to explore the city ruins for now. He carefully checked the map on his retina, intending to find the route the original owner had come from and return the same way.
That map was even stranger, the route ran from top to bottom.
Meaning, if the scale on the map was not marked wrongly, Su Lun was now at least deep underground, hundreds of kilometers down.
Who would build such a massive city in such deep caverns?
This was the strange part.
Moreover, if this was underground, then what were those intermittent light sources in the sky about?
The cavern space was also oddly large...
However, having witnessed superhuman powers, Su Lun didn't dwell on these issues.
As strange as this world was, it was within expectations.
...
Su Lun double-checked the directions and planned to leave the manor.
But he had barely taken a few steps when, in the manor's derelict garden, he saw a bloodied man lying there.
The shiny bald head immediately made Su Lun alert.
Clearly, this man was the kidnapper leader from before, Ivan!
At this moment, his body's metal-scale armor had shed off, his skin was everywhere lacerated, as if he had been dismembered.
"This guy is still alive?!"
Su Lun looked at Bald Ivan's faintly heaving chest, slightly surprised.
He thought, with Pestoia's powers, killing this guy should have been easy.
"Could this also be a gift she deliberately left for me? Or perhaps Baldy had some life-saving means to escape that special space?"
Su Lun pondered for a moment, and instead of choosing to flee, he opened the wooden box and took out that rune puppet.
Then, he slowly walked towards Baldy.
It just so happened that he was in desperate need of life-sustaining supplies, and Baldy's arrival was well-timed.
Twenty meters, ten meters...
After reaching within ten meters, Su Lun also sighed in relief.
Even if Baldy still had the strength to resist at this point, the rune puppet should be able to control him.
Clearly, Su Lun's caution was somewhat superfluous; Baldy had already completely passed out there.
Facing the man who had almost killed him before, Su Lun didn't show the slightest mercy. He pulled out the dagger from his waist and then thrust it into the heart.
The sharp dagger stabbed precisely under the rib, instantly ending Baldy's life.
Su Lun looked at Baldy, now breathless, and then he sighed in relief.
At that moment, a bizarre scene occurred.
Su Lun focused his eyes and saw a grayish, glowing mist forming over Baldy's corpse.
He thought it was a "corpse transformation" or some sort of "evil spirit conversion," but before he could think further, he felt an intense desire inside him, unconsciously wanting to devour that "gray mist"...
It was like being extremely hungry and seeing food that you desperately crave.
"Could this be... a soul?"
Su Lun suppressed that craving, suddenly realizing something, then hesitantly reached out to touch the "gray mist."
The next instant, a series of images and messages flooded his mind.
"Obtained memory fragments of 'Ivan Adams'"
"You've gained some 'basic mechanical knowledge'"
"You captured a piece of information: 'Oh! Sabina that old lady's peaches are really big...'"
"Combat experience +5"
"Spiritual power +0.1"
...
"This 'gray mist' is actually Baldy's memory fragments!"
Su Lun found that suddenly there was something extra in his mind.
First, like watching a movie, he saw Baldy maintaining and modifying a mechanical arm and also saw Baldy fighting with other people...
However, after he devoured and assimilated the memory fragment, there was no barrier whatsoever; that memory felt as though it was his own "personal experience."
As for that erotic image that popped into his mind, compared to other surprising gains, it was naturally selectively ignored, although... it was indeed quite large.
Coming to his senses, Su Lun then realized, he seemed to have gained some of the skills that Baldy had learned.
He took another look at his own panel.
Sure enough!
His spiritual power had increased by 0.1, and there was an added skill in his skill bar: [Basic Mechanical Introduction].
The "Combat experience +5" gain made Su Lun estimate that even if he trained hard for three to five months, he might not be able to achieve such tremendous improvement.
He suddenly had an epiphany, understanding the wonderful use of this "S-class" talent ability: "This [S-004-Reaper] ability can actually strip memory fragments from the soul and then use them for oneself..."
Realizing the potential of this ability, he found it hard to believe: "Is this ability so incredible?"
This talent ability might not directly increase combat power, but it's absolutely a "god-level" ability for growth!
It can strip the memories from a dead target, thereby gaining some of the target's skills... no wonder it's called the "Reaper"!
The more Su Lun thought about it, the more he marveled at how impressive it was.
This also meant that as long as he had enough memory fragments, he could easily master more skills and abilities.
Magic, Alchemy, mechanical knowledge, combat experience, marksmanship... and so on. The skills that others need to spend a lot of time and experience to learn, he could master instantly.
His potential for the future was limitless!
Truly worthy of being an "S-class" talent!
Without a second thought, Su Lun noticed another problem.
Before Baldy was still alive, there was no "gray mist" on his body; it only appeared after he had been killed.
That meant, this [Reaper] ability seems to only strip the soul from the deceased?
"However, whether dead or alive, where are so many souls to reap..."
Thinking this, Su Lun's eyebrows slightly raised.
The next instant, he murmured something, as if speaking to someone: "Hey, hey, hey... don't get so excited, okay?"
At this moment, he hadn't yet realized that he had come to a brutal world where human lives were as cheap as grass.
Here, death was as common as the wind, always accompanying everyone.

chapters.title: Chapter 12 - 12: Rich Spoils of War
chapters.content:
Baldy died, and Su Lun began to collect his spoils of war.
The mechanical arm on his right arm had been badly damaged in the previous fight, with the gun barrel, air valves, and high-pressure pipes all sliced open.
However, this did not hinder Su Lun's research into this steampunk technology.
He had just stripped Baldy's memory, adding some basic "steam mechanical knowledge" to his mind, and now he roughly understood the construction of the mechanical arm.
"The technology tree of this world seems a bit skewed, a combination of Alchemy and steam power..."
Su Lun looked at the runes engraved on the mechanical arm, falling into thought.
Simply metal materials could not support such a complex structure, especially the ultra-high pressure steam cannon. These mysterious alchemical runes played a very important role in stabilizing the structure.
However, his mechanical knowledge was still quite limited, and he couldn't yet understand the principles behind these engravings and enchantments.
....
Without lingering, Su Lun started to scour the rest of Baldy's equipment.
Unfortunately, apart from the dagger he had taken moments before, almost all items on the corpse had been damaged. The musket was cut into several pieces, leaving only half a handle in the holster.
Su Lun couldn't help feeling disappointed – he hadn't found the supplies he wanted, wondering to himself, "Is this it? Don't these guys carry food with them when they leave home?"
Just as he was pondering this, suddenly, he noticed three black gemstone rings in Baldy's hand.
If he remembered correctly, one of them was even stripped from the finger of the dead Cock's Comb man.
Upon closer inspection, the "All-knowing Eye" immediately responded with information.
[Inferior Space Ring]
Details: A storage ring with 1/2 cubic meter of substandard space.
"Space equipment?"
Seeing this, Su Lun revealed an I-knew-it expression.
In this desolate underground, water and food should be more important than weapons; these guys not even having water bottles on them was abnormal.
He stripped off a storage ring and then put it on his finger; a thought later, he suddenly saw the storage ring's "black gemstone" was a folding space.
About half a cubic meter of space, it was densely packed with various bottles and jars.
Red and green, row after row, it looked like potions.
Su Lun casually took out a red test tube potion and identified it with the "All-knowing Eye".
[Inferior Healing Potion (Internal)]
Details: Rapidly stops bleeding, accelerates wound healing; despite its impurities, it has no serious side effects.
Then, he looked at a blue one, which was for restoring dark spiritual power.
The rest were some high-grade potions in test tubes with engravings, but in small quantities.
"Exactly, emergency medicine is essential for adventurers. Now it looks like I might not die after all..."
Su Lun felt a surge of joy.
A moment ago, he was worried about the lack of essential medicines, and that his wounds might get infected and inflamed, posing an unpredictable fatal threat.
Now, seeing these potions, he directly opened a mid-grade healing potion and drank it down. He also used a topical disinfectant potion to clean his wounds.
If it weren't for the "All-knowing Eye", Su Lun felt that even if he saw these potions, he wouldn't know that these test tubes contained life-saving medicine.
Of course, there were also poisons.
Now it seemed this innate ability was indeed a perfect match for him as a transmigrator.
Strangely enough, after taking the potion, Su Lun suddenly felt the injuries on his palms itch – he knew it was cells dividing rapidly, a sign that the wounds were healing.
Normally, this healing sensation would only become noticeable several days after the injury occurred.
"What a miraculous potion, if I had this in my previous life, it would be a lifesaving miracle medicine for surgery..."
Su Lun's current vision allowed him to clearly see his wounds healing at a visibly fast rate.
It looked like it might fully recover in less than half an hour.
However, he then mumbled, "It seems kind of wasteful to use a 'mid-grade potion' for such an injury..."
The super effectiveness of the "Mid-grade Healing Potion" seemed more suitable for more fatal injuries. The minor injuries on the palms might have been enough with just an inferior potion.
But using it on himself, Su Lun didn't feel it was a waste.
....
In the second storage ring, Su Lun found the food and water he wanted, but they looked quite hard to swallow.
The food was some kind of hard bread, black as a brick, and the water was not clear at all.
If he hadn't identified it as [Inferior Drinking Water], Su Lun wouldn't have believed this faintly black liquid was potable.
Not in a hurry to eat, Su Lun checked the last storage ring, and inside were indeed weapons.
There were two punk-style pistols and a short-barreled shotgun.
Then there were numerous bullets and some mechanical arm replacement parts.
The guns were good, and the bullets weren't just simple gunpowder ones.
After identifying them, Su Lun found among the ordinary bullets, there were some special bullets with magic engravings – [Alchemical Bullet (High Explosive)], [Alchemical Bullet (Armor Piercing)], [Alchemical Bullet (Magic Breaking)]...
There weren't many, but they all looked quite formidable.
In the last storage ring too, no other food was found, and Su Lun had no choice as hypoglycemia had already made him somewhat dizzy. He picked up the black bread and nibbled on a few bites, then gulped down some water with a slightly strange taste.
As he ate, he also felt very strange.
Considering the equipment Baldy carried, like firearms and bullets that were very well-made, the industry in this world should be very advanced. But the food situation was quite dismal.
"Could it be that those guys can't even ensure basic clean drinking water and food?"
Having transmigrated, Su Lun found it hard to understand how these people could possess such refined equipment yet lacked a pot of clean drinking water.
He faintly guessed that the living conditions in this world might be extremely harsh.
....
Su Lun sat beside Baldy's corpse and ate, watching the physical characteristics of a living being gradually fade from the corpse, the skin whitening, the body heat slowly dissipating...
While he was still checking the items in the storage ring, he suddenly noticed two glowing objects on Baldy's corpse.
A palm-sized blue scale armor slowly condensed and appeared from the skin of the corpse; and another item was a dark red strip that looked like a bundle of muscle fibers.
Upon identification, they were two special items.
[Diamond Scale Armor (Damaged)]
Explanation: Already damaged Alchemy gear, you might be able to extract some extraordinary materials from it;
[Cursed Item: Tough Magic Muscle (Damaged)]
Explanation: Magician power series 'Iron Strongman' initiation material; missing part of its cursed properties, it needs the curse runes to be redrawn for use;
"So this is the scale armor that made Baldy impervious to knives and guns? Turns out it's a kind of gear..."
Su Lun suddenly found it amazing, wondering what exactly this thing was. It could turn into a tattoo covering the body, be activated by magic arrays to materialize, and now, after death, it had peeled off.
The more he saw "Alchemy" appearing frequently in the All-knowing Eye, the more curious he became.
And after the "Magic Muscle" had peeled off the corpse, the corpse visibly shrank a great deal.
Su Lun also realized something, thinking to himself, "So initiation materials are used like this... directly merging into the body to enhance physical attributes?"
He immediately thought of the "Puppeteer" initiation material he also had, which after initiation could greatly enhance agility and skill.
It turns out, Baldy's exaggerated strength had this "Magic Muscle" as its underlying reason!
However...
Even though the principle was understood, Su Lun found that he still didn't know how to "initiate."
...
Having barely filled his stomach, Su Lun had also almost finished inventorying the items in Baldy's storage ring.
It wasn't that he didn't want to figure everything out, but using the All-knowing Eye to identify items was not without cost.
Identification required the consumption of dark spiritual power.
The higher the item's level, the more it consumed.
Now, the dark spiritual power inside him had only a few dozen points left in reserve. Even if he drank a recovery potion, it would take several hours to fully recover.
Since he had found the urgently needed medicine and water, there was no rush to know what use the remaining items had.
Su Lun loaded the two pistols with bullets.
One was loaded with regular bullets, the other with special alchemic bullets, and then he tucked them at his waist.
He planned to leave this place first, find a human city, and learn about this world.
When leaving, looking at Baldy's corpse and the desolate manor, Su Lun suddenly had another doubt.
"Based on this, the original owner came looking for this relic. Why did Baldy kidnap the original owner? Was he specifically tracking the original owner or a teammate turned hostile during the journey?"
Su Lun felt the former was more likely.
The original owner, no matter how foolish, might not share something as crucial as "Baron Isaac's treasure." And even if picking teammates, he likely wouldn't choose a group like Baldy who could turn hostile and murder for wealth anytime.
And based on the information left on the retina, the original owner's identity was likely very sensitive, seemingly an exile from a major family.
These conditions combined were quite intriguing.
"First, the chances of a random encounter in such a remote place are very low. And from the questions Baldy asked before, they didn't know about the treasure or the original owner's real identity. So, their purpose in following was simple, to kill and silence!"
"And the reason they didn't act immediately might be because Baldy was greedy, coveting some secret from the original owner, which led him to follow all the way here..."
"With no previous acquaintance, there's no old grudge. Thus, it's likely a case of 'murder for hire'."
Su Lun connected the limited information in his brain and roughly restored the truth of the matter.
He speculated, "This also means, the place the original owner came from, someone wants him dead? If I go back, I might still be targeted for assassination?"
Thinking about this, he frowned slightly; this was not good news.
It also meant that even if he returned to the city the original owner came from, he could not reveal his identity.
Otherwise, he might invite lethal danger.
"This really puts me in a difficult position..."
Su Lun thought of something and muttered, "Such a handsome face, high level of recognition."

chapters.title: Chapter 13 - 13: The Subterranean World
chapters.content:
Several days later.
In a dark pit within the complex cave passageways.
Su Lun tried to keep his breathing as quiet as possible while his gaze was intensely fixed a few hundred meters away.
There, a humanoid monster roamed aimlessly through the cave, hunting for food.
It still wore some human clothes and gear, but its form had swollen monstrously, resembling a giant ogre.
Su Lun watched the creature, his finger already resting on the trigger of his gun, armed with alchemical bullets.
The moment it drew closer, he would blow its head off with a single shot.
[Mutated Human]
Explanation: Beings that had mutated into monsters after they couldn't bear the erosion of cursed powers, possessing strong auditory perception. They had little intelligence, guided only by instincts for hunting and killing.
Fortunately, before long, the monster wandered off in another direction and didn't approach the spot where Su Lun was hiding.
Su Lun let out a sigh of relief, "Phew... How many more bizarre creatures are there under the ground..."
This wasn't the first time he had encountered such a monster.
He had met one three days ago when he emerged from that secret passage.
Back then, unaware of the cave's perils and not knowing that even the slight sounds of walking on stones could attract these creatures with an acute sense of hearing.
Luckily after his vision was enhanced, he noticed it just in time.
The beast charged at him like a mountain of flesh, nearly killing him on the spot.
You mustn't let these mutated monsters get close; even a minor wound could splatter your face with a disgusting mix of rotten flesh and mud.
Their corrosiveness was incredibly strong and foul-smelling.
Regular bullets did little to stop them, sinking into their bodies like into a pile of mud.
"Plop~" It made a bubble, but was utterly ineffective.
It was also fortunate that Su Lun was prepared, using several of those "high-explosive" alchemical bullets.
His precise shooting, like an artillery explosion, managed to blow the monster into pieces.
However, he didn't have many alchemical bullets left, and these caves housed more than just this type of monster.
If it weren't for his awakened "All-knowing Eye" which significantly enhanced his night vision, relying solely on the crude alchemical night-vision device would have gotten him killed many times over on this journey.
Su Lun had previously thought this cave world was a large mine or perhaps a cavern system.
But the subterranean space was unbelievably vast, not only filled with human city ruins but also a complete ecosystem underground with various animals, plants, and monsters... hiding in every dark corner.
Ever seen a glowing mushroom forest fifty meters tall?
Or lizards the size of dinosaurs?
Or red-eyed rats swarming like locusts?
Or a centipede over ten meters long, truly possessing a thousand legs?
Or those huge tentacle monsters with walls of flesh tumors and dense eyeballs?
Su Lun certainly hadn't seen them in his past life, and in just these few days, his mind had been filled with much strange knowledge. Under the "All-knowing Eye's" identification, he also recognized many bizarre creatures.
Most of these cavern creatures were grotesque and disgusting, feeling like mutants after nuclear radiation...
Such a living environment was extremely harsh for humans!
...
Fearing that the monster hadn't gone too far, Su Lun decided to stay in the pit a little longer to replenish his food and water.
"According to the map found in the Bald Storage Ring, I should be reaching the Class-B area where human activities are more frequent. Perhaps I'll encounter another expedition team, it'd be best to find someone to ask about the situation first..."
Su Lun looked at the map marked with symbols and checked the stock of his food and water, estimating that his rations wouldn't last him to the endpoint city where humans gather.
Alone, he had always been cautious and hadn't dared to recklessly shoot and hunt the cavern creatures, fearing it would attract even bigger troubles.
These past few days had gradually given him a more accurate understanding of this mysterious world with supernatural powers.
That there was such a massive city ruin underground showed that thousands of years ago, a large population of humans lived here.
Moreover, Bald Ivan and his team were not miners; it seemed their group was specifically an "expedition team" adventuring in the caves to search for supplies.
The paleness of their skin was not solely due to their lineage but rather a consequence of prolonged absence from sunlight.
Su Lun began to suspect that his destination was not above ground, but rather underground.
However, all these were mere speculations.
He reckoned that if he lived to see the "destination" in a few more days, things would become clear.
....
Before long, the feeling of satiation from the meal had provided Su Lun with enough glycogen to continue his journey.
At that moment, he recalled something and took out the [Pestoya's Brooch]that he had previously placed in the storage ring.
For days, Su Lun had been trying to decipher the unknown information labeled "???" on the brooch.
The mystery of Pestoya's burning had been confusing him.
An abandoned manor that had been deserted for a thousand years, a spirit species, a story riddled with suspicions...
It was as if a piece of the puzzle was missing "the key link".
Su Lun always had an intuition that there was something wrong with this brooch.
And with so many bizarre supernatural forces in this world, who knows, it could spell big trouble.
If he didn't know, it would have been better to remain ignorant.
But since he had suspicions, Su Lun did not intend to keep this potentially explosive item near him.
Now far enough from the manor, he was no longer worried about triggering anything untoward.
Without hesitation, Su Lun dug a hole in the pit and buried the brooch, making a mark on the spot.
He thought that if there was no issue, he could come back and dig it up once his knowledge was able to identify the hidden information on it.
He didn't know that just moments after it was buried, some will within the brooch awakened, muttering whispers from the abyss, trembling slightly.
....
Su Lun was unaware that just a few days after he left the "Storm Manor" through that secret route, a team of black-clothed men quietly arrived.
In the dilapidated manor, a blonde young man in a pink suit leisurely sipped his coffee. The eerie and terrifying atmosphere seemed all too familiar to him and did not affect his mood in the slightest.
Soon, the young man's subordinates had violently broken into the "Cursed Space" filled with bizarre dolls.
A brawny man in a black suit came over with a box and reported, "Young Master Ewen, we've exterminated the 'ghost species' in the manor's cursed space."
The brawny man's tone was easygoing, as if he had ample experience in dealing with such matters.
After a pause, he opened the box to show the spoils of war and continued, "This is the 'cursed object' found after killing the apparition. It's the foundation of the cursed space. Master Nick has already appraised it—its quality is very high, and it's extremely useful..."
The blonde young man glanced at the black butterfly brooch in the box, a women's accessory, and showed little interest, waving his hand and saying, "Miss Teresa likes to collect these ornaments. Send it to her estate when we return."
The brawny man in the suit replied respectfully, "Yes, young master."
....
This group seemed to have the same "treasure map" as Su Lun; they quickly found the underground tunnel and through the maze found the already shattered altar.
The blonde young man was still looking forward to the relics related to the most mysterious and powerful alchemical organization of the last era, the Twilight Cross Society, which the elders of his clan were astounded by. He fantasized that if the altar really existed as stated in the manuscript, he might awaken a legendary super talent.
However, he soon received "bad news."
The captain of the security in a suit approached with a slightly grim face and reported, "Young master, we've thoroughly explored the basement, and it indeed matches the content decoded in Isaac's Alchemy Manuscript. However, the ancient altar in the secret chamber has been destroyed; it's absolutely impossible to carry out any sacrificial rituals now. And..."
The blonde young man had a premonition of the bad news, "And what?"
The security captain said, "And upon careful examination, we found traces of recent human activity in the basement. Therefore, we assume that someone might have already triggered that altar..."
Hearing this, the blonde young man angrily said, "How is that possible! We are the only ones who knew this intel!"
Faced with the huge disappointment of missing the great treasure, he suddenly thought of something and furiously said, "Damn! That old man must be behind this!"
"What about the ancient city ruins on the other side?"
"We've sent people to investigate, but no one came back alive... The initial assessment, the danger level is at least 'red'."
...
Meanwhile, several days later, Su Lun finally encountered some living people again.

chapters.title: Chapter 14 - 14 Mechanical Prostheses
chapters.content:
"Lauren, congratulations on landing the job. Your 'Windwalker' profession is compatible with a wide range of alchemy materials. Our main targets this time are the 'Lightning Lizards' and 'Cave Hounds.' There are plenty of these monsters in the shallow layers of the caves. With a bit of luck, we have a high chance of obtaining cursed materials..."
"Yeah. If we encounter a 'Bizarre-level' aberrant monster, we might even be lucky enough to extract 'silver-grade' cursed materials. Then, we can ask the guild's Mechanic for help with the refinement, and you, deputy leader Lauren, could become a professional."
"Boss, brothers, don't tease me. Spending nearly all my savings on the job materials and that alchemy blueprint, if we don't score this time, I'll truly be broke..."
"Haha, don't worry, deputy leader Lauren. Once you're a professional, your combat power will skyrocket. The initial investment will pay off soon, and then we'll be counting on you to look after us..."
"..."
This was a fully-armed wild hunting team, eight people in total.
They chose to set up camp amidst the ruins of a derelict watchtower. And this location just happened to be on the essential path marked on Su Lun's map.
As they chatted, a team member on guard duty suddenly noticed an unusual movement in the depths of the cave and shouted, "Be careful, everyone. Someone's coming from over there!"
...
The speed of progress through the dark caverns was slow, and it was estimated that it would still take four or five days to reach the "city" that the former owner had intended.
But Su Lun was in a bad situation.
His food was nearly exhausted, and if he didn't find supplies, he might be forced to hunt some cave monsters for food.
But water would be a big problem.
Su Lun initially thought that there was an ecosystem underground, and water should not be scarce.
Having wandered through the caves for days, he did find a few puddles and dripping rock crevices. However, the All-knowing Eye identified these as varying degrees of "polluted water sources," which would cause aberrations if consumed.
Su Lun also vaguely understood why the water in Baldy's storage ring was murky but still drinkable.
Compared to aberration, murkiness was acceptable.
Su Lun had hoped to encounter some people to buy drinking water and inquire about the situation. Clearly, however, it was not a good choice to ask anyone met in such remote caverns for directions or water.
But now, he had encountered such a wild hunting team.
Having seen Baldy's ruthlessness, Su Lun didn't think the people of this world were particularly kind.
However, he had to risk making contact with this team.
Because, they had spotted him too.
Clearly, someone among them was a specialist in long-range perception. Moreover, they had their guns aimed at him even before Su Lun had laid eyes on them.
Su Lun had exceptional vision and, upon noticing the sniper on the lookout tower had already set up the sniper rifle aiming at him, he had no intention of resisting. He raised his hands to show he was not reaching for any weapons.
Around his waist hung a wooden box, which would release the puppet inside with a slight touch.
Eight people, two snipers, and the other six in the camp...
Su Lun observed them briefly and had a rough count in his mind.
The effect range of the "Rune Puppet" was only ten meters, the walk there was nerve-racking.
But if he chose to run, the snipers would probably shoot him down as easily as playing a game of whack-a-mole.
As he walked, he shouted, "I mean no harm... I just want to trade for some food and water."
....
"Boss, it's a human, not a freak."
"Hmm, looks like a poor sod who's on his own."
"Hey... that red gun at that kid's waist, isn't that the famous gun 'Three-Headed Ghost'? Wasn't that 'Iron Head' Ivan of the Crow Gang's gun..."
"Hmm, I've noticed that too. 'Ironhead' Ivan is not someone to be trifled with..."
"..."
The squad that camped in the ruins of the watchtower was clearly curious about the encounter with a lone human in this place.
After watching "Baldy" and seeing that he made no dangerous moves, they let him come over.
Yes, that "Baldy" was none other than Su Lun.
Without the option of plastic surgery, how could one quickly change their facial features?
Su Lun's face, with its high recognition factor, worried him that the troubles of his predecessor might burn their way to him.
Returning to the city with that face would definitely not work.
A purposeful disfigurement like slashing one's face would draw even more attention due to its direct intent.
Therefore, he resolutely employed a physical disguise method—shaving off his eyebrows.
If anyone has tried, they would know that to make a face suddenly unrecognizable, the most direct method is to shave off the eyebrows. This was absolutely a disfigurement-level disguise technique, and it worked damn fast.
Plus, Su Lun didn't carry the burden of an idol's image. To be on the safe side, he even shaved off his hair.
Then he applied eyeshadow to himself and painted a smoky makeup look.
He went from a gentlemanly handsome guy to a ruffian-looking punk in an instant.
Considering the clothing and style of Baldy and his company, this dark punk style was not strange in this world and was even a mainstream trend.
Just like the several members of this hunting squad in front of Su Lun, they were dressed in the same fashion.
....
Su Lun walked up to the dilapidated earthen wall, and at least ten guns were already aimed at his head.
Either his knowledge of steam machinery was insufficient, or he felt that though these guys' equipment was not as refined as Baldy's team, it was much more complex, with a stronger sense of technology.
They were equipped with various types of firearms, peculiar mechanical combat knives, mechanical shields, and external full-body metal skeletons for carrying weight, along with backpack-sized steam power boilers...
What was even more surprising was that the guy who looked like the "captain" had both arms made of finely crafted steam-powered mechanical limbs!
These were not the kind of external skeletal mechanical arms like Baldy's but fully replaced flesh and blood "cybernetic limbs."
"Could I have been wrong? Is this not a magical world but a cyberpunk one?"
Seeing this, Su Lun started to doubt his earlier speculation.
Perhaps the technological tree of this world had been skewed to such an extent that even a highly complex field like "limb augmentation" had been developed?
His limited knowledge of machinery made him confused.
How could this world, which seemed to be a combination of steam technology and magic, be connected to the high-tech neuro-driven prosthetics?
It was a strong clash of tech-mixing, like the Steam Era developing Light Sword technology from Star Wars. Theoretically, that technology is from several eras apart.
However, confusion was fleeting.
There was no sign of peculiarity on Su Lun's face.
Just then, the men on the wall also seemed cautious, shouting, "Stop right there!"
Su Lun stood still, very cooperative.
The captain with mechanical arms asked, "Who are you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 15 - 15: Team Annihilation Squad
chapters.content:
"Who are you?"
Facing the inquiry, Su Lun offered the explanation he had prepared, saying, "I am a Scavenger. Earlier, my team encountered a group of 'lightning lizards,' and I got separated from them. Now I'm short on food and water, and if you're willing, I would like to buy some, or perhaps trade for some..."
Lacking knowledge of this world, he tried to speak ambiguously.
The statement was half true, half false, not entirely fabricated; he had indeed run into a group of giant lizards earlier.
But unexpectedly, it seemed that these people were specifically out to hunt those speedy lizards that were as fast as cheetahs.
As soon as he mentioned this, Su Lun clearly caught a flash of excitement on the faces of several people opposite him.
As expected, someone directly asked, "You encountered a group of 'lightning lizards'?"
"Yes."
Su Lun turned and pointed down the corridor, saying, "To the left of this passage, in the direction of Zone B11, there's quite a large group. I guess that's one of their nests."
Hearing an accurate answer, the delight on the faces of the people opposite him grew stronger.
The captain with the mechanical prosthetic limb glanced at the sidearm at Su Lun's waist and then asked, "Are you alone? Which Scavenger group are you with?"
Without thinking, Su Lun blurted out, "I'm from the 'Straw Hat Scavenger Group'."
"Oh?"
The captain narrowed his eyes slightly, pondering something. His gaze then fell on the black storage ring in Su Lun's hand and asked, "Are you with the Crow Gang?"
At this, the expressions and gazes of the eight people turned subtly hostile.
"..."
Su Lun keenly sensed the change in their expressions, and an alert rose in his heart.
He did not understand the exact meaning of the term "Crow Gang," but he vaguely felt that the other party was very certain, as if they had seen something on him.
Clearly, there was a problem.
He felt the problem might be with the sidearm at his waist.
Without a comparison, he had not known previously, but now he realized that the rune-marked firearm he had found inside Bald Storage Ring seemed much more advanced than the weapons of these people.
But obviously, admitting to being a member of something called the "Crow Gang" might result in him dying on the spot.
Su Lun knew that continuing the conversation might lead to trouble, so he had to be deliberately vague, responding, "As you can see, I am a freelance adventurer. Sorry, I just wanted to buy some food and water, but if you don't have any to spare, then let's forget it."
"A freelance adventurer?"
The captain, upon hearing that Su Lun had no affiliation, shifted his gaze and suddenly became more amused.
However, he clearly saw that Su Lun had reservations, and his face suddenly showed a friendly smile. He gestured for his subordinates to lower their guns and said, "No, what I mean is...if you don't have a gang, you could choose us. As you can see, we are from the 'Steam Brotherhood.' You can call me Dick."
No sooner had he spoken than someone at his side added in introduction, "This is our captain, the famous 'Silver Mechanic Hand' Dick from the east side of Langge Street."
Su Lun glanced at Dick's silver mechanical arm with his peripheral vision and politely said, "Of course, I've heard of Captain Dick's renown."
Flattery will get you everywhere. Whether he recognized him or not, a compliment never hurt.
From their tone, he guessed that this "Steam Brotherhood" must be a sizable organization, and listening to the people nearby, this Dick must be quite powerful...
'Silver Mechanic Hand' Dick suddenly changed his demeanor and called out, "Brother, want to come into the camp to rest a bit? We can sell you some food and water."
"That would be greatly appreciated."
Though he was no longer being pointed at with guns, Su Lun felt he lacked the right to refuse.
He entered the camp, where a bonfire was burning.
Su Lun did not intend to stay long or dare to speak much. But clearly, they were always probing for his background.
"Brother, what do they call you?"
"I'm Su Lun."
"Brother, aren't you an official professional yet?"
"Hmm, not yet."
"Oh, then you should really consider our 'Steam Union.' Once you join the gang, there will be plenty of 'employment materials' and 'alchemy prosthetic blueprints' for you to choose from in the club.
As you know, in the outer city, no one can offer more resources than us except for the 'Cross Society' and the 'Crow Gang.' And if you want to modify mechanical prosthetics, only our 'Steam Union' is top-notch..."
"I'll think about it..."
Su Lun captured a lot of useful information from these people's conversation.
It seemed that within that city, there was a distinction between 'inner city' and 'outer city.'
And the outer city had three major factions...
Seeing that Su Lun hadn't agreed, Captain Dick then talked about the purpose of their trip.
He tentatively said, "We're out here to prepare cursed materials needed for alchemy prosthetics for our vice captain, Rauen. Our targets are the 'Lightning Lizard's leg tendons' or the 'Cave Hound's skin.' If you brother happen to have these materials, you could sell them to us..."
"Sorry, I don't have them. Our team encountered danger not long after setting out and got scattered, without much gain."
"..."
The atmosphere of the conversation seemed fairly harmonious.
The other party prepared three days' worth of drinking water and food for Su Lun.
Su Lun hadn't planned on thinking so poorly of human nature, but with their next move, he knew it was time to act.
They handed over their own water bottle, and upon identification with the All-knowing Eye, a few words were displayed: "Water with nerve paralyzing poison."
Their intent was now clear as day.
The reason they hadn't acted earlier was probably because they saw he was alone and were unsure if he had any trump cards or secrets. Now that they had probed enough, it was time to move.
Poisoning the water was the best choice.
If he drank, it would all be over.
Even if he didn't drink, with so many of them, it wouldn't be too late to act.
Now aware of their malicious intent, Su Lun's gaze towards those men also turned subtly hostile.
They seemed to be sitting around the fire chatting, but it was more like they were surrounding him.
Moreover, their fleeting glances were always on the flintlock at his waist, probably ready to preempt any move he might make.
Pretending to be oblivious, Su Lun unscrewed the water bottle; he had no intention of reaching for his gun.
He was well aware that even if he drew his gun swiftly, at best he could fire one or two shots.
And there were eight of them.
Not to mention the highly threatening professional—'Silver Mechanical Hand' Dick.
But the good news was, aside from two lookouts, the other six were all within ten meters of Su Lun.
And this distance was precisely the influence range of the "Curse Artifact: Rune Poppet."
....
With a sincere smile on his face, Su Lun pretended to be about to drink the water.
But just as the water bottle reached his lips, he paused as if suddenly remembering something, and said with a smile, "Captain Dick, thank you for your warm hospitality. Although I encountered some dangers on this trip, I did manage some gains..."
As he spoke, Su Lun calmly reached down to the cloth bag hanging at his waist, revealing the wooden box inside.
"Brother Su Lun, you're too polite..."
Although Dick appeared all smiles, a hint of wariness flashed in his eyes.
He was confident that even if what his opponent pulled out at this moment was a hand grenade, he would be able to avoid it immediately.
"This is something I found in the ruins of an estate before, and I haven't figured out its use yet, so I'm giving it to Captain Dick..."
Su Lun also pretended to be foolishly unaware, with a relaxed smile on his lips, as he opened the box and took out the rune puppet.
If this world contains such spirit control curses, there must also be things that resist mind control.
In his heart, he was actually calculating that, in case the effect didn't meet his expectations, he would have an excuse.
Clearly, the others were deceived by Su Lun's "kind" smile. Seeing that he did not make any dangerous moves that could cause a misunderstanding, the group of people let down their guard.
Naturally, no one expected him to bring out such an "ominous thing"!
....
It was the moment that puppet was exposed to the air—an eerie scene unfolded!
An invisible wave of spiritual power instantly radiated out.
Obviously, the puppet was more powerful than expected.
Even Captain Dick, upon seeing the puppet, his eyes instantly stiffened. The other five people by the campfire seemed to have their souls sucked away at that moment, their gazes dull and fixed.
This was the moment he was waiting for!
Seeing this, Su Lun's expression flashed with a hint of harshness!
Without any hesitation, he drew the pistol from his waist and pulled the trigger at Captain Dick's eye socket.
Earlier, Su Lun had been vigilant. As the only "professional" in the squad, this guy, like Bald Ivan, possessed many miraculous superhuman abilities.
So, even though he was under control, Su Lun felt this guy had to be killed first!
A "bang" sounded.
The head burst open like a smashed watermelon.
'Gained memory fragments*2 from "Dick Nelson"'
'You have mastered some "Intermediate Mechanical Knowledge"'
'Gained a memory fragment: "The number of aberrant incidents in the city is increasing, it feels..."'
'Steam Mechanic Combat Experience +4'
'Spiritual Power +0.13'
A "grey mist" appeared over the body, and with a sweep of his hand, Su Lun absorbed the mist into his soul.
He didn't even have time to digest the information he had received and immediately raised his hand to fire another shot at the sniper on the distant watchtower.
A shot hit the abdomen, and a figure fell down.
The two snipers were not within the puppet's control range, but they did not expect Su Lun to suddenly attack.
They also did not expect that, faced with their team of six, Su Lun could instantly "control" and kill their captain.
Su Lun fired two shots in quick succession because he knew he wouldn't have the chance to fire a third; the other snipers were not fools.
Then he decisively leaped back, taking cover behind a mud wall.
As expected, the next second, a "snap" sounded, and a bullet exploded a large chunk in the mud wall.
The bullet pierced right through the wall, narrowly missing Su Lun.
Then, "tat-tat-tat" of continuous gunfire shattered the nearly one-meter-thick mud wall in the blink of an eye.
At that moment, the only real threat left was the sniper hiding in the watchtower.
Su Lun knew that in terms of marksmanship and terrain, he was not in a favorable position. In a shootout, his pistol stood no chance against a sniper rifle.
Without caring about conserving ammunition, he directly pulled out his pistol loaded with special alchemy bullets and fired several shots towards the position of the lookout.
[Alchemy Bullets (Incendiary)]*2, [Alchemy Bullets (High-Explosive)]*2, [Alchemy Bullets (Concussive)]*2.
Although the large revolver was only loaded with six bullets, it completely overpowered the opposing sniper with its firepower.
At the moment, Su Lun didn't realize that this round of shooting had consumed what many gunmen would use in a year's worth of ammunition expenses.
The three types of special bullets were astonishingly powerful, and after being fired, the entire watchtower was directly blasted away.
The explosion a hundred meters away was quite loud, especially the last two "concussion rounds", which made even Su Lun, who was some distance away, feel his head buzzing.
He didn't delay at all; right after shooting, he charged out.
Because of his enhanced vision, he saw the struggling sniper attempting to get up in the thick dust, and then he fired two more shots.
"Bang!" "Bang!"
The body fell to the ground.
'Acquired 2 *Soul Shard of Xinos Carter.'
'You have gained some basic Alchemy knowledge.'
'Firearms experience +6'
'Spiritual power +0.07'
.....
Su Lun didn't dare to be careless, finding another sniper who had been shot in the abdomen and firing another shot.
Then, he returned to the campfire, looking at the five bodies weirdly twisted like marionettes, he unceremoniously fired four shots, killing four of them.
He left the deputy squad leader, Laun.
From the start of the attack to the end of the battle, the whole process didn't exceed one minute. A fully organized Scavenger squad was entirely wiped out under Su Lun's decisive action.
However, there was a slight problem.
"Stripping too many memories at once, my head can't really take it..."
After consecutively stripping the memories from three bodies, Su Lun found his own head feeling dizzy.
It was like having stayed up all night, with his thoughts muddled.
But he also noticed that if he didn't strip the memories promptly, the "fog" on the bodies would fade. The longer the interval, the lower the quality of the stripped memories. After about five minutes or so, the fog on the bodies would completely dissipate.
This made Su Lun somewhat understand the limitations of the [Reaper of Death] ability.
He rested for a moment, waiting for the Soul Shards in his mind to be fully digested before he finally opened his eyes.
Su Lun took a deep breath, looking reinvigorated, "With this [Reaper] talent, I feel like I can grow unstoppable in this world..."
The Soul Shards from the seven bodies brought him many benefits, suddenly filling his mind with all sorts of strange knowledge and a better understanding of this world.
He felt he had visibly grown stronger.
Just a few minutes of digestion, and he felt he had grasped the knowledge and skills that would typically take a year or two to learn!
....
Su Lun put the [Rune Puppet] back into the wooden box.
He looked at Laun, whom he had tightly bound, and muttered, "I didn't plan to communicate with you all this way..."
Unfortunately, you insisted on harboring malicious intentions.
After putting away the puppet, Laun woke from his mental confusion.
Waking up as if from a dream, he didn't seem to understand what had happened. But once he saw the corpses littering the campsite, and then looked at Su Lun, his eyes instantly filled with terror: "You..."
Su Lun didn't let him ramble another word, stabbing his knife into Laun's right leg and said coldly, "Now, I'll ask a question, and you'll answer one..."
PS. Please vote~

chapters.title: Chapter 16 - 16 Old Lington
chapters.content:
"So, I wasn't gunned down by these guys straight away just because they recognized where this musket came from..."
Su Lun felt somewhat relieved, as death had brushed past him once again.
After interrogating for over an hour, he mercifully dealt with the last survivor of the 'Silver Hand Wild Hunt Group.'
Only then did he realize that the reason this gang hadn't attacked him was due to the runic musket slung at his waist—the famed gun "Triple Ghost."
It was Crow Gang's 'Ironhead' Ivan's paired gun capable of accommodating the energy fluctuations of powerful special alchemy bullets.
It turned out that Baldy was quite infamous in a city called 'Old Lington'—a veteran assassin of the Crow Gang, ruthless and vengeful, and seldom dared anyone provoke him...
Seeing Su Lun alone, those guys harbored thoughts of robbery and murder. But they were unclear about his relationship with Bald Ivan, so they decided to test the waters first.
....
Indeed, fortune does not come without risk.
Su Lun managed to get the supplies he desired, adding ten storage rings along with ample water and food.
He did not know the basic prices in this world, but seeing that the combined number of alchemy bullets on these eight corpses was not as many as Bald Ivan alone had, he guessed that the price he had paid was probably not a small one.
However, it was definitely a profitable venture.
He stripped two most valuable items from the corpse of 'Silver Mech Hand' Dick.
A peculiar blood vessel and a bone.
[Cursed Object: Trembling Witch's Blood Vessel]
Quality: Black Iron
Detail: A requisite material for Magicians of the 'Artillery Master' Mech Class, it offers a moderate skill boost and a slight reflex enhancement upon employment; while its cursed properties are relatively well-preserved, re-enchantment is required for optimal use.
Evaluation: Body compatibility 61%, an unremarkable employment material.
[Golden Humerus]
Detail: First-class alchemy augmentation, highly compatible with gunner classes; it can replace some of the host's bones; Toughness +6, Stability +153%, Bone Durability +175%.
Two items with intact cursed characteristics.
According to Lauen, either of these items could fetch at least 100,000 Riso each on the black market.
While an ordinary mechanical worker in this world would not make more than 3,000 Riso per month.
This was already a fortune that could make one rich overnight.
Su Lun was also glad about his judgment, eliminating the 'Silver Mech Hand' Dick immediately.
As Lauen put it, official "professionals" are very strong.
Dick had both his mechanical arms modified toward the Artillery Master direction. He had replaced his arms with firearms and cannon limbs; given the opportunity, he was absolutely a human Gatling.
The flexibility of this type of "limb" and the attached exoskeleton were completely different levels.
Even if his brain was controlled psychically, his mechanical arms would automatically activate a counterattack device, an ability that came with the augmentation.
And mechanics were not within the scope of psychic control.
If Su Lun had hesitated earlier, allowing the automatic counterattack device of the mechanical arms to activate, he would undoubtedly have been the one to die.
...
Days later, following the route on the map, Su Lun finally met with monsters several times and almost met his demise, but he arrived safely at the city known as "Old Lington."
This was also known from Lauen as the only human settlement place.
An underground city.
"It really is spectacular..."
Although Su Lun had heard about the high walls of 'Old Lington' through rumors, when he saw the dam-like, hundred-meter-tall cement wall with his own eyes, he was still deeply shocked.
A city with an area comparable to the main city area of a provincial capital in his previous life, completely enclosed by such a high wall. Just the scale of this engineering was an architectural marvel.
Moreover, there were many terrifying traces on the high wall—the claw marks of giant beasts, craters resembling meteor impacts, corrosive marks caused by spells...
It was hard to imagine what intense battles had happened in the past, what kind of "beings" had left so many terrifying marks on this wall.
Indeed, this city was also an ancient relic.
Long before these humans appeared here, it had already stood silently here for hundreds of years.
The All-knowing Eye confirmed this assertion.
Su Lun focused on the high wall as a string of words revealed itself.
[City Wall]
Details: An ancient city wall built over fourteen hundred years ago;
....
Old Lington had four huge city gates in the north, south, east, and west.
If Su Lun hadn't known about this "Old Lington" in advance, he might have naively entered through the main gate.
Because that seemed to be the only viable entry into this kind of city.
If so, he would have been checked at the city gate. Without a "legal identity," he would immediately be subjected to individual scrutiny. The worst-case scenario was that the original owner's identity would be exposed, and Su Lun would face assassination once again.
As for outside the high wall? Except for coming out to scavenge, no one would choose to live outside the city for long.
Because... they couldn't!
It was like being in a nuclear radiation area for a long time; even without encountering monsters, the intense, berserk dark spiritual power would highly likely cause "mutations."
And the most common monsters outside the city walls were the mutated humans roaming around.
However, there was actually another way to enter the city, which was "gang smuggling."
....
Su Lun had learned a lot of useful information from that Laon's mouth.
Old Lington was divided into the inner and outer cities.
The inner city was a gathering place for the rich and elite, while the outer city was a civilian area.
Although the entire Old Lington was managed by Duke Roberto of the "Black Tower" and the Rafael family behind him, in reality, the actual control of the vast majority of the outer city was in the hands of the three major gangs.
The outer city had three major gangs: the "Steam Brotherhood" in the eastern district, the "Steel Cross Society" in the southern district, and the "Crow Gang" in the western district.
They also represented the three mainstream branches of alchemy in this world: the Mechanical Sect, the Fusion Sect, and the Ancient Spell Sect.
The essence of alchemy is "equivalent exchange of matter," and the "Ancient Spell Sect" has capabilities like mages, able to cast various spells. They excel in potion crafting, enchanting, and occult studies.
Although they can cast spells, they do not worship any elemental gods, and they do not invoke magic laws to perform spells but use a pure fusion of energy and elements. They employ alchemy rules to exchange elements equivalently, either transforming the form of an element or altering its properties.
For example, standing on the ground, an alchemist would use alchemy to transform the earth element into the Earth Spike Technique; they could also, by consuming more energy, convert the earth element into the fire element and release the Fireball Technique;
Whereas the "Mechanical Sect" is also known as the new sect.
Their alchemical research direction is more about creating mechanical devices, firearms, mechas, steam devices... and mechanical curse implant equipment!
The suspicious "mechanical prosthetics" that had puzzled Su Lun before were, in essence, semi-technological products based on alchemy, not pure technology.
And the "Fusion Sect" is a combination of both sectors, featuring mechanics who specialize in mechanical modifications and ancient spell magicians who study spells, welcoming all comers.
....
Since Su Lun couldn't use the original owner's identity, he had no legal status to enter the city.
He could only choose to join one of the three gangs to smuggle himself in.
The Bald Ivan he had killed before was a big name in the "Crow Gang," and what's-his-name 'Silver Arm' Dick was from the "Steam Brotherhood." Although no one knew that it was Su Lun who had killed these people, he felt it was better to be cautious.
Especially since he still had some loot to dispose of, he didn't want to get into trouble over it, just like when someone recognized Bald Ivan's famous gun, the "Triple Demon," and nearly got killed for his money.
"It seems I only have the option to join the 'Steel Cross Society'..."
Su Lun avoided the city gates and walked to a section of the surrounding wall in the southern district.
Looking up, there was already a rudimentary iron cage elevator on the city wall, waiting to help people enter.
Having no other choice, Su Lun approached if he wanted to enter the city.
Joining a gang had good benefits and provided plenty of extraordinary resources...
But in reality, most people in Old Lington would rather be workers for their whole lives than join a gang.
Because... the casualty rate among gang members was extremely high, and their lives were short.
They replaced the city's security forces and would also handle mutant incidents, violent conflicts, and scavenging missions within their districts... These combat-related fields had very high mortality rates.
It was a bit like being a mercenary in a battlefield for money in Su Lun's previous life.
Allowing chaos in the slum area was also the most important reason the "Black Tower" inside the city tacitly allowed the existence of the three great gangs.

chapters.title: Chapter 17 - 17: The Steel Cross Society
chapters.content:
```
Atop the city walls, a group of armed militants stood, their styles ranging from punk to black suit trench coats.
They all bore the distinct "Iron Cross Star" on their clothing, the gang insignia of the "Steel Cross Society."
Every day in Old Lington, there were people for various reasons wanting to join a gang, from desperadoes and murderers with nowhere to turn to those seeking to get rich quick or acquire extraordinary resources...
It was often on these high walls that combatants willing to venture outside the city to scavenge were recruited.
The gang leaders liked to wait here, scouting for new recruits.
"Look here, Kai, can't you put away your 'Blade' prosthesis? Flaunting it like this just makes people laugh at 'The Cross' professionals for not being worldly. We're both captains, can you act a bit more dignified..."
"Heh, big boss Smoker, I just successfully fused with the prosthesis, so I'm a bit excited."
"The higher-ups in the gang entrusted you with managing the three blocks on Green Street. Be careful from now on. There are many gambling dens and brothels there which might be lucrative, but the old timers in the gang have all avoided it. Do you know why you were allowed to scoop up this opportunity?"
"Isn't it because those 'Steam Party' guys have been causing trouble lately? No big deal... If they dare cross the line, I'll make sure to cut their heads off, haha."
"As long as you're aware. It's not just the 'Steam Party' causing issues, aberrant incidents in the city have also been on the rise. You'd better stay vigilant. If you need help, just let me know. For today's recruitment, pick a few that catch your eye..."
"Thanks, big boss Smoker. Heh, I just hope to snag a few good fighters today..."
"..."
The man speaking was a middle-aged man with an ominous glint in his eyes, lazily lying in his chair and smoking a cigar.
Beside him stood a young man whose hands and feet resembled "blades," faintly shimmering with a metallic gleam.
Su Lun looked up at the two men without much hesitation, stepped into the rickety chain-link elevator, and ascended the city wall.
....
"New here? Want to join our 'Cross'?"
"Yeah."
"What's your name?"
"Su Lun."
"What talent did you awaken?"
"'D-016-Hawkeye.'
"Oh? So your shooting must be pretty good, huh?"
"Not bad."
"Alright, follow me. You can call me Captain Kai."
"Okay."
The process of joining the gang was so simple it was hard to believe.
After a few straightforward questions, Su Lun officially became a member of the "Steel Cross Society."
Just as the intelligence before the interrogation suggested, the gang didn't care about your past. After all, the majority of those who join the gang don't have a clean history.
As long as you work for the gang, no one cares about your past.
And in return for your service, the gang would provide you with protection.
No one searched him, no one asked too many questions, no one pried...
Su Lun let out a sigh of relief, his storage ring was safe. The preparations he had made beforehand to prevent any accidents were not needed after all, which was a good start.
....
Captain Kai seemed to be only a few years older than Su Lun, but he appeared to have already mixed in with the gang for many years.
To live for many years in a gang, one needs to have certain abilities.
This Kai was a formal "professional," an agile assassin who had merged with a highly offensive alchemical prosthesis — the "Blade."
Su Lun silently observed everything, his eyes sparkling with anticipation and curiosity for this strange new world.
After waiting for nearly half a day, the day's recruitment finally neared its end.
Apart from Su Lun, Captain Kai had selected three other people.
```
```
One awakened with the ability of "D-082-Super Strength," another with "D-071-Stone Skin," and another with "D-031-Enhanced Smell," all of which were talents that could enhance combat capabilities to some extent.
"Let's go, boss Smoke-addict. I'll take the new guys for a patrol to show their faces..."
"Mhm."
Kai led Su Lun and the others away from the middle-aged man who hadn't stopped smoking, and they descended from the city wall.
Su Lun was silent throughout the journey, quietly following behind, nearly invisible.
This young man named Kai was quite talkative and seemed very pleased with the new recruits.
As they walked, he handed them each a stack or two of banknotes and explained, "In the gang, welfare is twenty thousand riyals a month, with extra money for missions depending on the situation. Since we're a newly formed squad, there's no need to go out hunting in the wilderness for the next three months, so you guys can enjoy yourselves..."
The new recruits easily received their first substantial "salary."
Twenty thousand riyals, which was already equivalent to more than half a year's salary for an ordinary factory worker in the city.
Su Lun was slightly surprised; he was unaware of this detail. But seeing the faint excitement on the faces of the three beside him, they didn't seem to find it strange.
Paying the salary before the work, in his previous life, that would have also been considered excellent treatment.
Is this still a gang?
Su Lun thought it through and understood.
In a gang, no member could be sure they would live to see the next month.
Getting paid first meant enjoying life first.
If anything happened, at least they wouldn't die in vain.
Moreover, after joining the gang, there wasn't any confinement or control, and freedom wasn't restricted at all.
Su Lun could even take the money and run away right then...
But nobody would do that.
```
