He held his rune musket, staying vigilant at the tunnel entrance, his gaze fixed on the graceful silhouette in the smoke.
It was not that he intentionally watched her changing; he was observing the mutated creatures.
Having removed her combat suit meant Leina nearly had no defense. After all, he intended to rescue her; if she couldn't change in time, he still could shoot to help hinder them for her.
However, with just that one look, his gaze inadvertently captured a glimpse of spring.
"Black hair? That's quite rare..."
Su Lun had sharp eyesight, almost seeing everything clearly.
Previously, with the gas mask and night vision gear obstructing his view, he didn't know what Lena actually looked like, only that she must be quite attractive.
Now, upon seeing her directly, she was even more beautiful than expected, even stunning.
She had beautiful, long, straight black hair, and her black pupils shimmered with a pretty golden light. Her figure was flawless, even without the shaping effect of her liquid leather attire. Her entire being emitted a pure aura unique to young girls...
Her bosom was proudly full and her waist delicate, emphasizing the impressive proportions of her hips and legs...
The porcelain-like skin was delicate and smooth, shimmering faintly in the weak firelight of the Darkness, making her seem more like a gentle jade sculpture. The smoky haze from the burning powder wrapped around her curvaceous body, adding a hazy beauty, a vision of silky smoothness.
Su Lun raised his eyebrows slightly as he watched Lena deliberately twist her body to cover herself, chuckling softly, "Hah, so you noticed me..."
Even when discovered, he didn't avert his gaze, his expression remaining calm throughout.
Because his focus was always on the intricate tunnels around him, not on the girl changing clothes. The seriousness on his face didn't fade but grew as the smoke cleared and his brows furrowed more deeply.
After all, the "Monster Repellant Potion" appeared to have successfully interfered with the black dogs' sense of smell, but that didn't mean they wouldn't return once the burning smoke vanished.
Moreover, the source of the danger had never been just the black dogs...
...
Clearly, Lena had come to realize this too.
She quickly changed into Su Lun's clothes, then left all her belongings behind and fled the area where she had changed.
But she did not immediately approach Su Lun; instead, she stopped at a safe distance at a fork in the path. If the monsters came after her again, she would be ready to run.
However, she probably wouldn't have the chance to run anymore.
Without her combat suit or any equipment, if this attempt failed, she was almost certainly facing a dead end.
....
A minute later, the yellow smoke from the burning powder dissipated completely.
At the end of the tunnel, more than ten ferocious liquid black dogs had gathered. They seemed to have been confused earlier, pacing in circles, their corrosive liquid evaporating, pocking the tunnel.
But as soon as the smoke cleared, they seemed to have detected a scent, excitedly rushing towards the pile of Lena's discarded clothes. The more than ten black dogs wrestled together, eventually merging into a large, dark monstrosity, completely blocking the tunnel.
Fortunately, they had no intention of lunging towards the distant Lena.
Seeing this, Su Lun finally let out a sigh of relief, "Finally, the bet paid off, the scent was external. Didn't waste a high-priced potion from Wan Li Suo."
As for Lena, the girl who was saved, a look of post-disaster joy appeared on her face, visibly relieved.
Only then did she turn her gaze to the man who had saved her life in a critical moment, her expression somewhat complicated.
She felt she should say something appreciative, but something came to mind, and she blushed.
Su Lun looked at Lena and guessed that a young girl, being bare in front of a stranger, might feel uncomfortable.
But he was neither a nanny nor a suitor, with no need to cater to her youthful sensitivities.
He waved his hand, motioning to follow, and said sharply, "Follow me!"
Saying so, Su Lun took the lead towards the deeper, darker stretches of the tunnel, not looking back to wait for her.
His attitude made it clear: follow if she wants.
Seeing Su Lun walking away so coldly, a look of surprise appeared on Lena's pretty face.
But his indifferent demeanor somewhat eased the awkward atmosphere.
The surrounding Darkness engulfed everything like a monster, making the unequipped Lena feel very insecure. Thinking it over, she followed, running barefoot to catch up.
...
As the two of them walked one after the other, Su Lun made no concessions for her, moving quickly.
The wind blew through her thin shirt, making Lena feel chilled and shy for a moment. She wanted to say something but, looking at the cold silhouette ahead, she swallowed her words.
Finally, after walking a long stretch, Lena broke the awkward silence, "Mr. Su Lun, thank you for saving me."
"Hmm."
Su Lun remained cold.
He did not want to get too entangled with her, considering she might be an acquaintance of his original self.
But he was curious about a few things, so he asked, "How do you know my name?"
Lena timidly replied, "Aunt Qian Tiao told me. She said your shooting is excellent, and you handle things calmly. In case of danger, she said I could seek your protection."
She paused, then added, "I didn't think it was necessary before, so I didn't mention it..."
Su Lun listened expressionlessly, not much interested in the details, and asked further, "Is Aunt Qian Tiao your real aunt?"
Lena nodded, "Yes."
"..."
Having satisfied his curiosity, Su Lun didn't speak further.
The rest, he could probably guess.
After the brief conversation, the two again lapsed into silence.
In the dark tunnel, only fragmented footsteps and breathing could be heard, slightly eerie.

chapters.title: Chapter 68 - 68: Bait, Please Adjust Your Attitude
chapters.content:
Both of them walked in the darkness, going deeper into the ground.
Leina watched as the corridor plunged into the depths of the earth, not an exit, and her heart's trepidation grew stronger.
She felt as if she were stepping closer to an abyss with every move...
Finally, unable to bear the eerily indifferent atmosphere any longer, she asked cautiously, "Mr. Su Lun, where are we going now? Aren't we going back to the surface?"
Looking around timidly, she probably thought that if anything were to happen in this environment, no one would hear her even if she screamed her lungs out.
"..."
Hearing this, Su Lun turned his head to look at her. He pondered for a moment before he spoke, "You don't think you're safe now, do you?"
"Ah?"
Leina felt somewhat guilty under his gaze, as if she could see the word "foolish" etched on her forehead.
Su Lun thought for a moment, then explained, "The noise from the explosion can travel far, enough to attract assassins to check it out. The mutated monsters are just a means of murder, but the mastermind behind them... is a person. If they find out you're not dead, do you think they will come looking for you?
If we go out now, I can guarantee that there are assassins waiting outside for you to deliver yourself to their doorstep."
If rescuing someone was as simple as dealing with a few mutated monsters, he wouldn't have hesitated multiple times before deciding whether to take action.
That mastermind is what he truly feared.
....
"Ah? I... I..."
Upon hearing this, Leina's mind seemed to be instantly bombarded with conflicting information, leaving her speechless.
She had been too preoccupied with being chased by monsters to think carefully. Then for the first time, she changed clothes in a strange environment under the watch of a stranger, and her head was still buzzing with confusion.
As she listened to him, she quickly understood.
Now, she realized that the man in front of her was indeed as her aunt had said, possessing an almost inhuman calm under any circumstances. (The original words were about how he behaves at the gambling table or something along those lines, anyway, that's the gist of it. It's not important anymore.)
Thinking of this, Leina realized she had indeed asked a very stupid question.
Such a smart gentleman must have also guessed her foolish and naive thoughts from before.
Her face reddened, she timidly expressed her apologies for her wild guesses, "I'm sorry..."
"..."
Su Lun did not pay much attention to her, seemingly indifferent, and continued to move forward.
In an attempt to relieve the awkwardness, Leina thought for a moment and then took the initiative to ask, "Mr. Su Lun, aren't you curious about why the trial went wrong? And who the mastermind is?"
Su Lun frowned slightly, as if he found her somewhat bothersome.
Probably because the claustrophobic environment made this lady feel uneasy, making her want to talk for some comfort. But in their current situation, was it really the time for small talk?
Indeed, women only affect the speed of drawing a gun.
He replied indifferently, "Not curious."
"..."
Leina's expression turned awkward.
Su Lun observed that she still wanted to say something, so he thought it best to nip this meaningless chatter in the bud.
He considered for a moment, then said in one breath, "If I'm not mistaken, your father must be critically ill or retiring, and then as the first in line to inherit the consortium, you are supposed to take over. Unfortunately, you also have some uncles and male cousins with strong mercenary intentions and...
the mastermind behind this attempt on your life, is probably a direct relative who would most likely inherit the consortium if you died, right?"
At these words, the shock in Leina's crystal-clear eyes intensified, and she exclaimed in disbelief, "Ah... how... how do you know that?"
"..."
Su Lun's lips curled slightly, feeling unamused.
After all, due to the undeveloped entertainment industry and communication in this world, the lower classes couldn't get a taste of the high society.
But this kind of family power struggle has been played out in the novels of Su Lun's previous world, and in real life among the major conglomerates. All the stories about a gambling king stubbornly clinging to life, the power struggles among his wives; the son of a certain chaebol in Korea forcing his father to abdicate; the wealthy prince pursuing the bodyguard and lover who cuckolded him...
Reality is bloodier than fiction.
The wealthier they are, the crueler they are to their kin.
There are no new stories.
Su Lun felt he had talked enough and fell silent.
However, the upside of his lengthy explanation was that Leina indeed took the hint, twiddled her fingers and quietly followed behind him.
She felt that this man seemed to guess everything.
Cool and collected like a monster.
....
As they delved deeper, the stench in the sewer became increasingly intense.
While walking, Su Lun suddenly realized something and turned back to look at the pained expression on Rena's red-flushed face, a helpless wry smile appearing in his eyes.
He had been preoccupied with other thoughts and forgot that this girl was clad only in a thin shirt, not even owning a gas mask.
But it seemed that since Rena had been dealt several verbal blows earlier, she was too embarrassed to ask for anything.
Su Lun shook his head slightly and then took out clothing, a musket, a dagger, and some bullets from the storage ring.
"The technology for bulletproof vests in the outer city is primitive and heavy, wearing one would greatly impair your agility. It's your choice. Without a bulletproof vest, you have no room for mistakes and must remain highly vigilant throughout. The catacombs are very dangerous, and a moment's carelessness could be lethal. But if you do wear it, should danger arise, you won't be able to escape..."
Rena took the heavy bulletproof vest, which was dozens of times heavier than the academy's battle uniform. Just as she was about to put it on, she heard Su Lun's analysis, hesitated, and with a timid response said, "I... I better not wear it."
Su Lun put away the bulletproof vest, then pointed to the musket hanging at her waist and reminded her, "Try out the musket to get a feel for it, but don't fire. The firearms in the outer city are not as refined as those at your academy, so the recoil will be significant. Just be mentally prepared in case you need to use it.
The other one is a runic musket, given to me by Charlie before, and it should suit you. But the alchemical bullets are limited, so please don't fire at will unless it's necessary..."
"Oh."
Rena felt that even though she understood everything, in front of this man, it seemed as if she understood nothing at all.
It was like she was a puppet being manipulated; whatever Su Lun said to do, all she could respond with was "okay," with no space for refusal.
Before this man even opened his mouth, he had considered everything.
The clothes belonged to men's garments from Su Lun, and they were very large on Rena. In the end, she still wore only that thin shirt, not even trousers, leaving her thighs exposed. Fortunately, the darkness camouflaged the embarrassment on her delicate face, and since Su Lun did not spare an extra look, she didn't feel too awkward.
Her shoes also didn't fit, so she went barefoot. However, as a Catwoman, she had naturally enhanced toughness in the muscles of her feet, so walking barefoot wasn't a problem. It was just that stepping in the damp sewer felt disgusting.
After distributing the equipment, Su Lun spoke again, declaring, "All right, from now on, maintain a sufficiently safe distance from me. Don't talk to me, don't make any unnecessary noise... Stay absolutely quiet."
"Ah?"
Upon hearing this, Rena looked perplexed.
Su Lun did not conceal his intentions and explained directly, "From now on, you are the bait. Based on the strength of the enemies that might appear, I will decide if I can save you once again. Don't look at me with that kind of expression. If you're with me, the enemy will just opt to take us both out in one go. I'm just an ordinary thug from a gang; only if I survive, you can survive..."
Su Lun had another unspoken thought: if the enemy proved invincible, he would not hesitate to abandon the "bait."
He paused, then added, "Of course, the ideal scenario would be that those enemies think you got killed by a mutated monster and don't come after us."
"..."
Rena listened, flabbergasted, her pretty face filled with a mix of awe and incomprehension.
Right, she thought, there were Assassins.
When she thought about it, his words seemed... to make sense?
But as sensible as they might be, something felt off to her about what he was saying.
Didn't gentlemen of high society, even in the face of Death, prioritize the lives of their female companions first?
Why would Mr. Su Lun send me to be the bait?
Although she had never experienced such a sudden event, Rena still felt as though the plot shouldn't unfold this way.
She wanted to ask, but didn't know what to say, as he had seemingly covered all bases with his reasoning.
Su Lun sensed the gaze of aggrieved stealth from behind but showed no intention of looking back. He quickened his pace, increasing the distance between them and said as he walked, "I'm just an ordinary guide... saving you was also in consideration of Sister Qian Tiao being your aunt."
Not claiming too much credit for himself would attract less trouble.
And by doing a favor for the grand boss Qian Tiao, it would be easier to communicate later.
Moreover, Su Lun's actions weren't about feigning indifference; they were the most logical choice.
Because he understood human nature all too well.
In the face of such a proud noble lady, being kind to her would be taken for granted, as she is accustomed to such treatment in her everyday life; however, when she realizes that your kindness comes with a price, then she will truly start to value it.
Bait is more valuable than dead weight.
To be a good bait, one must have the resolve of being bait.
In short, a fawning fool gains nothing while equivalent exchange is the eternal truth.
If you want to be saved, you must pay the price.
Though his words were harsh, this was also the method that Su Lun believed had the greatest potential to preserve Rena's life.
He was acutely aware that the Assassins daring to target this young lady were no simple foes.
PS. Sorry for the late update. Please vote~

chapters.title: Chapter 69 - 69: Rosa's Body
chapters.content:
Su Lun chose a path that delved deep into the underground caverns, already entering the city's sewer system where sewage flowed chaotically. He had intended to search in this direction for the scythe, and now it also served as a perfect place to avoid the assassin, whose pursuit was uncertain.
Although the environment was foul-smelling, the sewage effectively concealed the traces of their movement.
Unexpectedly, before encountering the pursuing assassin or finding the scythe, they first stumbled upon a corpse at a drainage pipe.
It was the half-naked body of a woman, entirely wrapped in cobwebs, pallid and lifeless, being pierced through the skull by the venomous fangs of a giant spider with red eyes, which was sucking on the brain matter...
Miss Lena stared at the body, wanting to scream out but then remembering something and quickly covering her mouth, her crystal-like eyes trembling with unhidden sorrow.
The corpse was unmistakably that of the previous female assistant, Rosa.
As Su Lun looked at the corpse, now cloaked in a gray mist, his eyes brightened, "Just died, still very fresh?"
He had harvested so much knowledge from Jack's corpse before, so why not from an assistant who could have been a teacher to the students?
....
To Su Lun, such a corpse was nothing short of a godsend, its value a hundredfold that of an ordinary professional's corpse.
However, Su Lun did not make a move. Instead, he squinted at the red-eyed spider about to feast, and identified the monster's attributes. "Is it yet another elite beast?"
At that very moment, the spider also looked his way.
Something crossed Su Lun's mind, but he did not avert his gaze.
In an instant, the six crimson spider eyes regarded him, and it felt as though an invisible hand was caressing his soul, but the sensation vanished as quickly as it had appeared.
At the same time, the All-knowing Eye displayed a negative body status.
"You have been subjected to a mental attack. The psychic fluctuation is weaker than your spiritual power, and you have resisted this negative status..."
As Su Lun saw it, just as the All-knowing Eye indicated, the mental attacks of these aberrant elite spiders were not enough to threaten his exceedingly high spiritual power.
"High spiritual power can resist low-level psychic spells... It seems that in this spider's lair, as long as I'm not surrounded by a swarm of monsters, it's not too deadly for me..."
Having encountered a live monster, he deliberately tested some theories.
Now, Su Lun felt confident in continuing the search for the scythe.
But Miss Lena behind him wasn't as fortunate. The girl had inadvertently locked eyes with the spider, and it was as though her soul had been siphoned away, leaving her standing there, dumbstruck.
Moreover, it seemed she was envisioning some sensual hallucination, for her cheeks flushed rapidly, and she began emitting strange little moans.
Su Lun watched Miss Lena, now stupified and walking towards the spider, without rushing to her aid. Instead, he observed her carefully.
While watching, he analyzed in his mind, "So this is what happens when one is affected. The monster's mental attack purely influences lust. If I block out the emotion of 'lust,' would that render this kind of psychic attack ineffective?"
The All-knowing Eye made it clear to him the methods of attack employed by the ghoulish spider; a direct gaze would stir up base desires, causing instantaneous loss of consciousness and easy capture as prey.
Just like the lady now in heat before him.
Miss Lena's breathing techniques were among the best for a first-order professional, and yet she was so easily bewitched. This meant that even second-order professionals, if lacking in spiritual power, would probably fall under the influence of these elite spiders.
Su Lun's gaze grew deeper as he seemed to ponder something, "Tsk tsk... It seems this young lady's fate is not yet sealed..."
....
Feeling he had observed enough, Su Lun raised his hand with a silencer-fitted pistol and shot the giant spider's head to pieces.
Just as the reconnaissance had shown, although deadly, these mutant creatures had extremely weak body defenses. Even ordinary bullets could easily blast large holes through them.
With the monster dead, Miss Lena snapped out of her obsessive state.
She instantly felt an embarrassing and unusual sensation in her body, and with her face possibly blushing out of modesty, she asked timidly, "What... What happened to me just now?"
"Don't look directly into the red eyes of those ghoulish spiders, or you'll be subjected to mental manipulation," advised Su Lun, without going into detail.
He didn't dwell on her current bashful appearance, which could have stirred the hearts of many young men, but went straight to the body of Assistant Rosa.
"Oh... the spider even dropped curse-material loot."
Su Lun looked at the cow-sized spider's corpse which was emanating a glow, and from it, there were actually two cursed glowing spider legs.
However, their quality was not great, merely common dark iron materials.
Disregarding the spider legs, Su Lun approached Rosa's body.
The gray mist on the body would dissipate over time, and each second's delay meant the loss of high-quality fragments.
He had to harvest quickly.
Then, drawing closer to the mist, he triumphantly separated a great deal of valuable information.
```
"Acquired 'Rosa Williams' Memory Fragment*5'
'You have gained some information: 'Daniel has been acting a bit strange lately, I saw him secretly opening some kind of signal device in the tunnel...''
'You have mastered a vast amount of 'Advanced Alchemy Knowledge'...'
'You have mastered the Arcane Alchemy Art [Wu-Shi (incomplete)]...'
'You have grasped a large amount of 'Alchemy Theory'...'
'You have mastered the skilled [Quick Sorcerer's Seals Technique]...'
'You have gained some 'Advanced Alchemy Spells Casting Techniques', Alchemy Experience +111'
'Spiritual Power +0.35'
It was an anticipated bumper harvest.
Su Lun felt his mind overflowing with an excess of "knowledge".
It was as if a large chunk of a shattered puzzle had suddenly snapped into place, giving him an indescribable sense of accomplishment.
....
"Did I actually grasp Rosa's arcane technique [Wu-Shi]?"
Su Lun, looking at a new skill that had appeared on his panel, immediately thought of the image of Assistant Rosa dragging countless strange moths by herself in the cave before.
The wraithlike cold fire that burned the creatures kept them at bay, leaving him still feeling uneasy to this day.
He was no longer an alchemy novice, and naturally, he knew that a skill dignified with the title "arcane" represented top-tier, scarce, and precious knowledge. Not only is it difficult to obtain the skill, but the learning curve is also steep, and mastering it depends on one's comprehension!
This [Wu-Shi] would be considered a top-level arcane secret technique even within the Inner City. To learn it would be like finding one in ten thousand.
However, because of his gift as a Reaper, Su Lun easily mastered this arcane level of alchemy.
A flash of curiosity crossed Su Lun's mind. At that moment, the dark spiritual power inside his body circulated in a special yet familiar manner, causing a small wisp of pale blue cold flame to suddenly appear on his fingertips.
"It actually worked..."
Su Lun looked at the flame, similar to one from a lighter, and his face lit up with joy.
This cold flame was not only an elemental dark spell that scorched, but it also imparted a "break defense" effect on physical attacks.
It allowed the user's "normal attack" to cause both physical and magical damage, drastically increasing the damage!
Since it was an incomplete secret technique, Rosa had only managed to summon two flame arms, achieving only a minor mastery in the arcane arts. If the technique were complete, one could even condense a full "Servant of Void" to envelop their entire body, as if a deity possessed them...
"What a powerful arcane secret technique."
After carefully sensing the specialty of the cold flame, Su Lun couldn't help but comment inwardly.
He felt that he could probably punch a hole through a concrete wall with just one finger now.
Although he didn't have Rosa's exaggerated flames, it was enough to make his normal attacks critically hit.
At the same time, he also reflected that assistants really lived up to their names, possessing a wealth of knowledge far richer than that of elite students.
The surge in alchemy knowledge made Su Lun feel as if he had "skipped grades," jumping from third grade directly to sixth grade in an instant.
But before he could fully digest all the knowledge he had acquired, his expression turned solemn when he saw one particular piece of information in the memory fragment, and he wondered with alarm, "Is something wrong with Assistant Daniel?"
....
There had always been suspicions of an insider within the trial team.
Otherwise, the enemy wouldn't have been able to accurately grasp their movements and precisely send that shapeshifting bug after Miss Lena.
However, he was not certain whether the traitor was a student or an instructor.
After Daniel had disappeared without a trace and Instructor August had never shown his face, Su Lun had preemptively assumed they had died.
But now, from Rosa's memories, he found doubts.
Lena was still immersed in grief, after all, Assistant Rosa had died saving her.
Su Lun's eyes shifted as he directly asked, "Miss Lena, what are Assistant Daniel's profession and talent? Does he have any particularly powerful trump card?"
Lena had been confused before, but she wasn't dumb.
Hearing Su Lun's question, she instantly guessed something and said, "Assistant Daniel's advanced profession is a 'Ranger', skilled in tracking and counter-tracking as well as close combat. Many of our combat practice sessions were taught by him..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's expression turned icy at the mention of "skilled in tracking".
And just then, he felt as if a pair of crimson eyes were staring at him from the darkness, muttering to themselves, "Scythe, Assassin, mutant monster..."
```

chapters.title: Chapter 70 - 70 I am the Puppeteer (Long for Votes)
chapters.content:
```
"Mr. Su Lun... Do I... do I really have to stay blindfolded? But I can't see anything..."
"Yes, because they have already arrived."
Su Lun didn't explain how he knew someone had come, and Miss Lena didn't ask any further.
Although the two hadn't known each other for long, Miss Lena felt an almost blind trust in this stranger introduced by her aunt.
She knew the assassin was formidable, and she knew the cave was filled with danger, yet from the man's demeanor, she had never detected a hint of panic; he was always calm and composed. This very calmness affected her too, giving her a sense of peace, as if she could face even death head-on.
And at that moment, led by Su Lun, blindfolded by a thick eye mask, she had no idea where they were headed.
Being blindfolded naturally meant completely giving up the notion of fighting.
Not that Miss Lena lacked combat skills—on the contrary, her basics were quite solid. Whether it was hand-to-hand combat, marksmanship, or alchemy, she far surpassed the average first-tier professional.
However, in the dire situation at hand, Miss Lena's combat abilities would not be enough, neither against the deformed creatures nor the assassin.
Instead, focusing on being a "bait" would increase her chances of survival.
After being blindfolded, she didn't notice the pairs of scarlet eyes that lit up in the darkness around them, nor did she see the nearly pathological sneer that spread across Su Lun's face.
In the face of danger, Su Lun once again felt that adrenal surging sensation, "he" too enjoyed this tightrope-walking thrill.
Escape?
Tsk tsk...
No... the person I want to kill, the forbidden items I want to take, the monsters... must be killed!
Aren't I lacking high-quality spider leg materials?
There are suitable targets right here, and not just a few.
"The upcoming battle will be very dangerous, but as long as I don't get killed first, you won't die before me... Remember, if you get poisoned, inject the antidote potion, but never remove your blindfold or run around..."
"Got it."
Miss Lena could only feel that Su Lun's voice was becoming increasingly chilling, and just hearing it, she sensed a burgeoning aura of murder.
When Su Lun let go of her hand, Miss Lena felt as if she was falling into an endless abyss, a thick fear enveloping her heart instantly. The world before her eyes was pitch black, no one spoke in her ear, and the trickling sound of sewage was unnervingly clear...
She felt a "person" remaining by her side, but intuition told her that it might no longer be Mr. Su Lun—it was an unfamiliar terror.
....
Soon after, a figure, just as Su Lun had predicted, quietly entered from the tunnel they had come through.
He saw the silhouettes of the two people in the distance, but cautiously stopped.
The gun in his hand was raised slowly, aiming at one of the two.
He didn't fire, but instead shouted to reveal his position, "Miss Lena, where are you..."
Daniel was well aware that even if he hadn't spoken, the small contraption he had triggered at the mouth of the tunnel had also betrayed his presence.
At that time, Miss Lena was startled when she heard Daniel's voice.
Indeed, everything Mr. Su Lun had surmised was correct.
She took a breath, and though she couldn't see, in order not to reveal any flaws, she pretended to be surprised and turned around. From a distance, she shouted towards the direction of the voice, "Assistant Daniel, I'm over here!"
Dannelni probably thought his role as a mole hadn't been exposed yet and was still performing, his tone extremely anxious, "Oh, thank God, I finally found you. You don't know how worried I was when I learned you were being chased by creatures... Miss Lena, did Assistant Rosa save you?"
Su Lun, hidden in a dark corner and hearing the probing, smiled coldly, "Knowing that the opponent is no match and yet being so cautious... no wonder he can play the mole."
He should have already found Rosa's body by now, but he pretended not to know.
All for the sake of saying these few sentences, to close the distance for a fatal blow!
Hearing this, Miss Lena directly said, "No, Assistant Rosa has already died trying to save me. It was the guide, Mr. Su Lun, who saved me."
But before she could finish speaking, she suddenly heard a "bang"—a gunshot. Almost simultaneously, a gust of wind brushed her hair, the sensation of a bullet whizzing past her ear.
Miss Lena was taken aback; Assistant Daniel, indeed, had fired.
```
However, the bullet wasn't aimed at her, but at the "Mr. Su Lun" by her side!
....
Once her sight was gone, Miss Lena focused all her attention on her hearing.
Upon hearing the gunshot, she instinctively flinched, realizing that something was amiss.
Although she was shocked that her beloved teacher, Daniel, was indeed the mole in this assassination attempt, what worried her more was the wellbeing of Mr. Su Lun beside her!
But before her anxiety could spread from her heart, she heard a second gunshot in an extremely short time.
"Bang"!
However, this shot wasn't fired by Daniel nor by "Mr. Su Lun" beside her. Judging by the direction of the sound, it came from another direction in the darkness.
Could there be a third person here?
In her surprise, Lena also noticed something odd. That was, after "Mr. Su Lun" beside her got shot, he produced a sound like that of splintering wood.
No, the moment she heard the gunshot and reacted, wood shavings and fragments had already splattered onto her.
A puppet?
Although Lena couldn't see, she guessed what was happening and felt an inexplicable surge of exhilaration and delight!
Had Mr. Su Lun anticipated that the enemy would shoot at him and arranged a puppet decoy in advance?
....
Ever since he saved someone earlier, Su Lun had guessed that the assassin would follow and had never relied on luck.
Even though the highly corrosive shape-shifting worms had completely eroded Lena's belongings, as long as there was someone adept in trace tracking present, the subtle traces the two of them had left in the corridor couldn't be concealed.
And coincidentally, this Daniel was a silver-clad professional "Ranger" especially skilled in trace tracking!
So, after peeling information from the memories of Rosa's corpse, Su Lun knew this guy would definitely come.
He was certain of one thing: if Lena didn't die, his entire role as the mole would be meaningless.
And Su Lun, wishing to outsmart this guy, chose not to leave Lena alone as bait.
After all, if there were traces of two people but only one appeared, it would undoubtedly alert Daniel the "Ranger," making an ambush pointless.
The puppet that stayed beside Lena was naturally meant to attract gunfire.
As for why Su Lun was confident that Daniel would shoot at "himself" first rather than killing Lena, he was eighty percent sure.
Given two targets, would a cautious "gun-expert" choose to kill a student who posed little threat and could easily be killed, or an unknown stranger with unclear origins?
Of course, there was also an element of betting involved.
But what kind of bait is it without risk?
Besides, regardless of who Daniel chose to shoot first, the outcome would be the same.
Whoever fired first would reveal their location and lose the advantage.
....
In a face-off between experts, when skill and experience are nearly equal, victory is often decided by the details.
From Lena's account, Su Lun also knew that Daniel was an authentic "gun-expert," one of the shooting instructors at the Black Tower Academy.
He had never dared underestimate him.
This wasn't some second-rate expert like Jack, but a marksman who might be even stronger than himself.
Against a marksman of the same level, it all came down to who could seize the initiative—victory and defeat often hung in the balance of a moment.
That recent query from Daniel was actually his attempt to lull his opponent into complacency, seeking an opportunity and the right distance to ensure a kill shot.
This cautious approach left Su Lun with no openings to exploit.
But that guy had never expected to shoot a decoy puppet with his bullet.
A shot missed, then... it was Su Lun's opportunity!
As the flash of fire lit up, Su Lun also pulled his gun and pulled the trigger without hesitation.
"Bang~"
The flame roared out.
The armor-piercing alchemy bullet burst out from the barrel, not aiming for the head or heart, but for Daniel's right hand that held the gun.
Because Su Lun knew, with the battle armor and gas mask, this shot certainly wouldn't kill the guy.
The Black Tower's battle suits had special reinforcement at vital points, and as long as the energy was sufficient, even an alchemy bullet might not break through. However, these suits also had their weaknesses, and to ensure flexibility, the stability at the joints was relatively weaker. (The intelligence also came from Miss Lena)
And the palm is where the human body has the most joints.
An armor-piercing bullet might not be lethal, but it was enough to break the bones in the hand.
At that gunshot, Daniel's musket immediately flew from his hand, a mist of blood exploded, and the stark white of bone could be seen.
But even after being shot, the fellow didn't let out a whimper, instead, he dodged with a swift movement, hiding behind a pillar.
Because Daniel had already judged from the timing of the gunshot that Su Lun was also a "firearm expert"!
He knew very well that if he didn't move, the second shot would surely follow.
....
"Such a cautious guy!"
Su Lun had fired one shot and broken the enemy's right hand, but the enemy did not give him a chance to land a second shot.
Gunslingers of equal rank were very clear on what the other would do.
To be an assistant at the Black Tower Academy, even at the first rank, one must definitely be the best among their peers. Daniel and Assistant Rosa, almost half-step second rankers, each had very strong combat methods.
Su Lun knew that even with a broken hand, that guy's real combat strength hadn't diminished much.
Because... Daniel's real strength lay in his close combat abilities!
And at this instant, suddenly from the darkness came a sharp "hiss", like the sensation of a high-pressure gas canister bursting, causing a wave of air that rippled throughout the space.
"Here it comes!"
Su Lun's pupils dilated sharply, and suddenly he saw a figure, like a cannonball, hurtling toward him.
With such speed, there was hardly any time to react, the figure smashed directly through a cement column, then collided with Su Lun's body.
The muscles couldn't react in time, but Su Lun was already prepared. With a bend of his fingers, the steel wires in his mechanical gloves pulled his body aside, forcibly shifting him a whole body's length to the side.
With a "thud," an invisible phantom passed by.
The two colliding figures crashed into the distant wall, instantly creating a large spiderweb of cracks.
Such a brutally forceful impact was enough to smash a flesh-class warrior to pieces!
Daniel thought he had succeeded, but he suddenly felt something was off about the "person" in his arms, and upon a closer look, it was actually a life-size puppet.
"This is bad!"
Daniel's face changed dramatically, instantly understanding something: his opponent was intimately familiar with his augmentations and innate abilities!
"That guy is actually a Puppet Master?!"
But by this time, understanding was already too late.
This kind of misjudgment was fatal.
.....
Just a few meters away from the shattered pillar, the musket was once again aimed at Daniel.
Su Lun knew the "Stalker" profession had strong perception abilities, which is why he deliberately made a noise to lure the other party into taking the initiative and charging at him.
This was the advantage of information asymmetry.
Su Lun was almost intimately familiar with Daniel's capabilities, while the enemy knew nothing about him.
If it were a fair fight, Su Lun's chances of winning would not exceed twenty percent!
This guy was a "new school" Magician, his alchemy mechanical augmentation—a fusion of steam machinery and traditional augments—was the black technology product known as the "Grudge Bone Jet".
Once it accumulated steam, a sudden burst could produce very strong thrust like a jet plane. This thrust could propel a person fast as a cannonball, with very strong direct line offensive capabilities, nearly impossible for peers to avoid.
Just this ability alone wasn't too troublesome...
The key was that this augment perfectly matched his talent!
Although his talent wasn't the rare B-class, it was still the mysterious series ability—"Talent C-001-Silencer"—with strong practical combat utility.
A peculiar talent that, upon close proximity, could instantly disrupt the enemy's bodily energy flow with a double-handed touch.
Once touched by his hands, spirit power, physical strength, magic power, and even blood flow... would be instantly obstructed or slowed.
This augment combined with his talent was simply a nightmare in close combat.
With the high-speed collision and close-ranged silencing, even professionals a rank higher could suffer a great loss!
This was also one of the most important reasons why Su Lun's first shot aimed to cripple one of his hands!
.....
Daniel's face was ashen, and he laughed bitterly inside, "He actually used Miss Lena as bait, heh..."
In the last moment of his life, he realized that every move he made was within the enemy's calculations. From entering this space, to firing his gun, to charging... the opponent had predicted every single one of his actions.
The key was, he never imagined someone would dare to use the heiress of the "Reiss family" as live bait!
Even for a rescue, who would dare?
But now, it was too late for regrets.
In a battle between masters, one mistake might still leave room for turnaround, but a string of mistakes was almost certainly a road to death.
The inertia from his charge was yet to dissipate, leaving him no time to dodge, as Su Lun's rune firearm had already spat flames.
A shot hit his intact left palm, rendering his most threatening hands useless. Then several more shots struck his ankle joint, knee joint, shoulder joint, elbow joint...
Bang, bang, bang, bang...
The gunfire was incessant.
If one shot didn't work, then he'd shoot the same place twice.
At such close range, it was impossible for Su Lun to miss.
Even the combat suit couldn't dissipate such terrifyingly concentrated impact energy, and his body became riddled with bloody holes.
Because of two missteps during their confrontations, Daniel had already forfeited his life.
The enemy was already a blood sieved carcass, yet at this moment, Su Lun's face showed no relief, instead, his pupils sharply contracted.
A murderous intent approached stealthily, making one's hair stand on end.
It was as he shot Daniel that from behind him, a jelly-like transparent figure in the darkness somehow stumbled, abruptly making a noise.
Su Lun's eyes narrowed slightly, as if not the least bit surprised, and thought to himself, "As expected, the Stalker..."
In that instant, he relinquished his rune firearm, and his hands sharply curled into claws. The back of his coat ripped open, revealing two peculiar puppets covered in glittering blue runes.
He reached into the void with both hands, and the two puppets floated by his side like guardians. Their wooden lower jaws constantly opened and closed, as if they were laughing heartily.
"Cackle, cackle, cackle..."
In the gloomy sewer, this sound was particularly grating.
At that moment, pairs of strange red eyes began to glow in the darkness around them, the creatures too were lured out of the darkness by a special provocative scent.
At this moment, the clarity in Su Lun's eyes was replaced by fierceness and a sinister smile, "Thinking of assassinating me, keke... I'm a 'Puppeteer', after all!"
PS. The group number is now in the introduction, interested friends can join~

chapters.title: Chapter 71 - 71: If there are no conditions to win, create them.
chapters.content:
Su Lun had anticipated the assassin that suddenly appeared behind him, far from being surprised.
Decisively, he tore open his leather jacket, and two puppets—one emitting a chilling wail and the other grinning grotesquely—flew towards the enemy. Their hands cracked, revealing dagger blades poisoned in black.
The assassin staggered, seemingly unable to comprehend why he had suddenly become momentarily distracted, bit his tongue, and instantly regained clarity. By then, he saw the poisoned blades already thrust before his eyes, a cold light flashing in his eyes.
With a clang, sparks flew.
The assassin blocked a dagger from one puppet but felt a bout of dizziness again: Not good!
Instinctively reacting to the danger, he performed an extreme backbend. At that moment, the dagger of another puppet passed narrowly in front of the assassin's cheek, accompanied by a slight corroding sound, tearing a slit at the edge of his hood.
"There's something odd about these puppets!"
The assassin noticed some trickery, just as he was about to reach out, he saw both puppets swiftly fly back.
Having failed to strike, he promptly withdrew.
At that moment, Su Lun, as the manipulator, also revealed a trace of regret on his face, thinking to himself, "Second-tier professionals, indeed not so easy to injure..."
The assassin, facing Su Lun, was even more startled, his eyes flickering cautiously: This guy is no ordinary puppet master!
....
Actually, ever since rescuing Lina from the pursuit of the metamorphic bugs, Su Lun's mind had constantly been reconstructing the entire assassination process.
He had long guessed that there might be a traitor within the trial team.
But that instructor, August, should be fine.
Otherwise, the assassins wouldn't need to go through such trouble to kill Lina. With his instructor identity and second-tier professional strength, there were countless opportunities to directly kill Lina.
Instead, the assassins chose to act in the caverns, deliberately applying a special scent on Lina to use the metamorphic bugs for the assassination… All this, presumably because of August's protection along the way, forced them to resort to this strategy.
Moreover, Su Lun had spotted another doubt.
That was confirming August had been following the trial team closely, yet this powerful person died without any disturbance, which was somewhat baffling.
After all, instructors from the Black Tower Alchemy Academy are rigorously selected strong individuals, and even if August had been ambushed, it was impossible for him to die without even sending a warning signal.
He hadn't understood why previously, but now knowing the fact that Daniel was the traitor perfectly filled the gap in Su Lun's suspicions.
In his mind, Su Lun could even reconstruct the entire battle process.
At that time, Daniel had left the trial team precisely to ambush August. His assistant instructor identity made it easy for him to get close enough for a successful sneak attack, and then he used his special talent "Magic Ban" to seal August's abilities.
But with his strength, he still couldn't kill a second-tier professional alone; thus, Su Lun deduced that there had to be at least one other second-tier professional in the assassin team, very skilled in stealth attacks.
Therefore, when a Stalker appeared behind him just now, Su Lun was not surprised in the slightest.
....
Facing second-tier professionals, especially agility-enhanced stalkers, firearms were almost useless.
Having witnessed the 'Red Demon' Goron cleaving bullets in half in the past, Su Lun did not entertain the thought that he, as a "Gun Master," would stand any chance against second-tier professionals.
Thus, he decisively abandoned his firearm, revealing his professional capability for the first time: puppet manipulation.
The reason "Puppeteer" is eerie lies primarily in the creation of various bizarre rune puppets.
The two blue rune-covered dolls by his side, one with a red and white grinning face and the other with a blue and gold crying face, were exactly two types of basic eerie dolls, "Wailing Baby" and "Mocking Baby."
These little things weren't like the rigid dead objects in puppet shows. Under the nimble fingers of Su Lun, they came to life, their limbs joyfully moving, joints twisting flexibly, and even the expressions on their horrifying faces were vivid, blinking, grimacing, angry, wailing...
They were like two specters dancing in the darkness, emitting creepy, strange laughter...
Upon their appearance, a terrifying aura instantly enveloped the surroundings.
Of course, these darlings were not only quaint and adorable in appearance. Their cursing effects were also extraordinary.
Both dolls were of the psychic cursing type, one attacking with sonic waves, impacting one's sanity upon hearing the sound; the other performing visual attacks similar to those spider creatures, creating hallucinations when one stared directly at its grinning face.
Knowing that there would be a fight later, Su Lun had strapped the two dolls to his back in precaution.
Although his puppet crafting skills were just at the beginner's level and the two eerie dolls were of low grade with a small attack range, this was enough to cause brief spiritual control over a close-range target.
This was also why the assassin sneaking around had suddenly staggered into view, having been influenced by the two eerie puppets.
....
"Gone again, huh. That guy's talent must be related to stealth abilities, 'Talent C-025-Chameleon,' 'Talent B-077-Invisibility,' or perhaps even the rarer 'Light Absorber'..."
Su Lun squinted into the darkness, his view once again losing track of the second-level assassin.
He didn't dare be careless, with the two puppets constantly emitting mental fluctuations, one laughing and one crying, to ensure that no one could get close enough to kill him.
Clearly, although the eerie puppets' cursing characteristics were strong, their strength was ultimately a major rank lower.
Su Lun did not think that these two puppets could save his life in front of a second-level assassin.
After all, when facing stealthy assassins, killing methods were not limited to close-range stabbing; assassins also excelled in various long-range weapons.
No matter how cautious and careful he was, the current situation was almost certainly deadly for Su Lun.
However...
If it were one-on-one, Su Lun truly had no chance of winning, but there were more than just the two of them in this dungeon!
The dark dungeon beneath Old Lington was not the domain of humans, but rather that of mutated monsters.
Since there was no chance of winning, then he had to create one!
Su Lun had made such a commotion in the cave that the lurking "Mutant Phantom Spiders" had long been ravenous.
He caught a glimpse of the dense mass of spiders above his head, his heart sneering repeatedly: "Heh, let's see who can survive among the monsters now..."
It was difficult to find a potion to block the monsters' senses, but to attract mutant monsters with bait was much easier.
Fresh human blood, corpses... were the best things.
The body of Daniel on the ground was still emitting steaming blood, and the broken "Inducing Potion" that Su Lun had previously shattered was also evaporating with a pungent smell.
Since the monsters were enemies, and the assassins were enemies, then a three-way battle would be good, wouldn't it?
"He" quite liked this feeling of dancing on the blade's edge.
....
Su Lun knew almost all of the monsters' traits and had countermeasures for them, but that second-level assassin knew nothing.
This was a type of mutant monster, which meant that the outside world had never seen them before.
Mental attacks were tricky and unpredictable, offering no room for error; once controlled, death was the only path.
Just then, those spider monsters did not disappoint Su Lun.
These eight-legged creatures hung upside down from the ceiling, moving extremely fast.
The first thing they did was not to attack the three humans in the space but to creep to the entrance of the tunnel, then spew webs, quickly blocking off the escape route.
"Sealing the entrance? Ordinary mutants don't possess such intelligence. In this group of monsters, there indeed lurks something 'eerie'..."
Upon seeing this, Su Lun's eyebrows slightly rose.
He had always felt a chilling, cold gaze from the dark, intermittently watching him. Now, seeing the spiders' unusual behavior of "blocking the door," he immediately guessed that within this tribe of Phantom Spiders, there was an "eerie" presence!
But, this suited him just fine.
He hadn't planned on escaping anyway, so whether the door was blocked made no difference.
He couldn't run, and neither could the assassin.
Just right for a three-way melee.

chapters.title: Chapter 72 - 72: The Spider Queen (Massive - Ticket Request)
chapters.content:
This second-tier assassin possessed a highly skilled stealth ability, and Su Lun's current perception was not enough to easily capture him.
But he had no intention of looking for that guy in the first place.
Because those dusky red eyes were enough to weave a net of spiritual power that covered the entire cave, leaving no one in the cavern able to avoid it.
What they had to do now was to see who had the larger slice of luck, who could survive.
Indeed, just as Su Lun had expected.
The moment countless red eyes lit up, his body's panel displayed numerous "psychic attack" notifications, like a tide of area-wide coverage, wave after wave. Even without directly looking at the monsters, one would be more or less affected.
Su Lun was still unscathed, but that assassin wasn't so fortunate.
Almost simultaneously as the spiders sealed the nest's exit, over ten meters away from Su Lun in the void, that hooded man also felt the impact of the psychic shockwave and revealed his form once more.
The guy was extremely vigilant, seeming to immediately sense the abnormal spiritual power fluctuations around him and directly pulled out a potion, stabbing it fiercely into his waist.
Watching that guy inject the potion and instantly become spirited, Su Lun guessed, "A sobering potion? Quite alert..."
However, the duration of a sobering potion was very brief, and as long as he remained trapped in this space, it was inevitably a dead end.
....
Professionals who could advance to the second tier, more or less, all had some tricks up their sleeves.
Perhaps taking a hint from Lena's dummy bait, the assassin also sharply realized that those red eyes of the spider monsters should not be looked at directly.
Confronted with such peril, the assassin decisively lowered his head, narrowing his gaze to his feet.
Su Lun, watching this little maneuver, also silently praised him for being impressive.
A professional assassin, indeed, had astonishing instincts.
But by doing this, his field of vision was reduced by more than ninety percent, which was definitely not easy, even for a second tier professional.
And the moment the assassin lowered his head, his hands shook, suddenly revealing two short blades flickering with lightning.
The man ignored the large spider dropping down from above his head and charged toward Lena, who was not far away!
"Tch, tch... can't even save his own life, yet he still aims to kill the target. Seems like he's a dead shot. But I've only just managed to save her; I can't let you kill her that easily..."
Su Lun was slightly surprised by the assassin's choice, but also thought it was just as well.
If the enemy wasn't targeting him, then he could free up his hands to strike back.
Seeing this, Su Lun's hand suddenly grasped as if catching hold of something invisible and instantly pulled it taut.
And just then, above Lena's head, the large spider that fell from the ceiling was suddenly dismembered in midair, as if cut into large pieces by an invisible blade.
Upon closer examination, surrounding Lena were threads of steel wire, as thin as hair.
The bodies of the Ghostface Spiders were fragile, and falling from a height, inertia caused their bodies to touch the threads, no different from hitting a blade's edge. In an instant, they were easily sliced into pieces, and green droplets of blood remained on the threads.
Seeing this, the assassin's eyes flashed with doubt, and his ambush instinctively halted.
The darkness of the environment and the need to avoid looking too high made it impossible for him to determine the exact nature of the threads.
Having been outwitted by that strange puppet earlier and still feeling apprehensive, his instinct told him that if this "guide" dared to confront him head-on, he must have other means hidden.
In reality, he didn't realize that Su Lun was simply gambling.
The threads were no match for a second-tier professional; what he was betting on was the opponent's cautious mentality.
Just at that moment, the assassin hesitated, but Su Lun didn't show even a hint of ambiguity.
With one hand controlling the silk threads, his other hand had already drawn the fire gun and did not give the assassin a chance to make trouble, and he fired several shots at that guy.
As expected, the assassin's nerve response speed had reached the extreme.
He caught sight of the orientation of the gun barrel, leaned backward to avoid a shot, then performed several consecutive backflips, perfectly dodging this round of gunfire. Even the "Curved Trajectory" hidden in the last shot just grazed by without hitting him.
....
Su Lun hadn't expected to wound him, his only goal was to distance them, and that had been achieved.
Because at that moment, the monsters on the ceiling had already launched their attack.
The "bizarre" creature also appeared to know that the second-order assassin was the most formidable threat among the three, instructing the giant spiders to surge toward the assassin.
Facing the tide of monsters, the assassin's methods were sharp and ruthless. He raised his hand to shoot out throwing knives that could pierce through several spider creatures at a time, even more lethal than the fire gun. With just a casual slash, he could easily sever half of a giant spider's body.
Even without daring to directly look at the red eyes of the monsters, he relied solely on listening for position and the movements of spider legs close to the ground, managing to dodge effortlessly, cutting through the spiders as if chopping melons and vegetables, not falling behind at all.
But... the ghastly spiders' methods of attack were not limited to this.
Moreover, there was an intelligent creature behind the scenes, secretly directing them!
It was then that the giant spiders on the ceiling suddenly stuck out their behinds, and torrents of white spider webs sprayed out.
When spider silk is fine enough, it appears as individual threads; but when it's as thick as a thumb, it becomes pools of sticky glue!
The assassin, relying on his agile movements, dodged this first wave of silk, but upon landing, he realized the sticky webs were already everywhere. It was like he had stepped into a swamp, his agility instantly restricted by a great deal.
Realizing the predicament, the assassin became somewhat panicked, but his first reaction was to attack Lena, not to flee, as at this moment the cave had been sealed by the spider webs... escape was now difficult.
Bombs and incendiary grenades were thrown around haphazardly as if they cost nothing, but in the wave of monsters, they were like a drop in the bucket...
....
On the other hand, Su Lun was also facing the same situation.
For him, a first-order professional without any implants, the spiders would be even more deadly.
But faced with the overwhelming spider webs, he did not dodge or avoid them, as a pale blue cold flame suddenly burst forth from his body.
As the spider webs touched the cold flame, they burned up like cotton upon fire, not even reaching Su Lun's clothes before they were consumed.
This was clearly the "Alchemy Arcanum: No Servant"!
This was also why he made Lena cover her eyes.
One reason was the fear of her being controlled by the spiders, and the second was to keep her from seeing his own methods.
If it were not for having previously stripped this skill from Rosa's corpse, Su Lun would certainly not have chosen the "three-way fight to the death" strategy.
Because of the cold flame, Su Lun had no need to worry about spider webs.
He freed both hands, dual-wielding guns, shooting at the approaching spiders from all directions.
With both guns blazing, he single-handedly formed a barrier of gunfire, preventing those fragile giant spiders from coming anywhere close.
For a moment, severed limbs flew everywhere, and green spider blood was splattered all around...
....
At the same time, because of the defensive barrier woven from steel wires around, the giant spiders were temporarily unable to approach Lena.
But this did not prevent them from spitting out spider silk from a distance.
Leina's heart was filled with extreme fear at this moment.
She could hear the dense gunfire and the sound of grenades near her ear... She could also hear the high-frequency "click-clack" movement of the monster's joints. Even without opening her eyes, she could guess that a massive number of monsters were eyeing her hungrily.
She stood there all alone, utterly helpless.
Just now she had been drenched in the foul-smelling spider blood, and now she was sprayed with a sticky substance...
But she couldn't open her eyes, nor could she move about recklessly.
All she could do was stand there, shivering uncontrollably, allowing the spider webs that sprayed over her from time to time to trap her securely.
However, fortunately, the spiders seemed to have the habit of storing food. Seeing that Leina wasn't escaping or showing any signs of attack, and after being stuck tightly by the webs, they didn't attack her anymore!
Leina, the bait, did not know why she was mysteriously out of danger for now...
But she could also hear the battles between Su Lun and that assassin raging fiercely from two different directions.
Suddenly, she heard the noise from one side abruptly stop.
Leina instinctively felt a pang of fear in her heart and prayed, "The sound of gunfire is still there, Mr. Su Lun must not be in danger yet..."
.....
At this very moment, Su Lun was killing like a madman.
The spider creatures were much bigger and clumsier than those flying moths they encountered earlier, and being merely crawlers, they were easier to hit.
He was almost getting a headshot with every shot, and when using alchemy bullets, he could kill a group with a single shot.
The spiders' two main trump cards, psychic control and webs, were completely useless against him, so Su Lun was like a god of death, killing or crippling hundreds of monsters in a short time.
Around him, the bodies of the spider creatures had piled up into a mountain, and more kept clambering over this "mountain of corpses" to meet their end.
There was not a trace of panic on Su Lun's face because, although there were many spiders in this nest, he did not believe they out-numbered his bullets!
But while he was in the midst of killing, the monsters suddenly disappeared.
The big spiders seemed to have received some signal and receded like the tide.
With a puzzled look, Su Lun looked into the distance and realized... The battle on the other side had already ended.
The "bizarre" creature hiding in the shadows, seeing too many of its minions dead or injured, finally showed itself.
And at this very moment, Su Lun saw the second-class assassin standing there like an idiot, absolutely still.
A spider spear easily pierced through his skull, skewering down straight through, leaving him chillingly slaughtered.
A formidable second-class professional had just died so easily under the "bizarre" creature's spider spear.
....
And Su Lun, watching the creature, his face turned solemn the moment he identified it: "Now we've got a real problem on our hands..."
Fortunately, it was a first-tier 'bizarre';
Unfortunately, it was a "Lord monster."
If 'bizarre' is a term humans use for the bosses among the mutant monsters, then a Lord monster is the boss among the bizarres, approximately ranging from "Gold+" to "Legend-".
And the bizarre that Su Lun and his group encountered at that subway hub station was just a "Black Iron level," several classes lower than the creature before them now.
Such creatures are extremely rare, usually found in very large-scale mutant monster groups with a slim chance of occurrence.
Encountering one of this level in the wilds was about as likely as winning five hundred million in the lottery for the Hunter's Wilderness group.
But once encountered, it almost always meant total annihilation.
"Lord-level creatures" tend to awaken unique abilities that allow them to crush those of the same tier, or even those of higher tiers.
Just like how this rank one lord easily killed a rank two professional.
Su Lun had guessed that there was "something strange" here. Neither iron nor silver would have surprised him this much.
But he hadn't expected it to be a lord.
....
This big BOSS was half human, half spider.
Its upper body was that of a naked female. Her skin was luminous and tender, exuding an ultimate sensuality and charm that made it impossible to look away. Her features were stunningly beautiful in a way that, at a glance, would immediately arouse instinctive desires in someone, making them want to pin her down and rub against her.
However, the bottom half was somewhat horrifying, a massive, menacing spider body with eight legs glistening a metallic shine... Fierce in appearance.
[Mutated Ghost-Faced Spider Queen (Lord)]
Explanation: A lord-level ghost-faced spider with powerful mental control abilities; due to mutations, its body has undergone unusual changes, regressing to ancestral bloodlines and its tier limit has been increased by 270%. The spider's flesh is exceptionally resilient, possessing high intelligence, a composite type of potent venom, and extremely fast movement speed...
Looking at the introduction of those "top-tier attributes," Su Lun didn't need to delude himself; he definitely couldn't win.
However, he didn't wait passively for death. He immediately raised his hand and fired two shots.
"Bang," "Bang"!
Armor-piercing alchemy bullets left two charred indentations on the Spider Queen's skin, and then, there was no 'then'...
The bullets fell to the ground, making two crisp "clang, clang" sounds.
"Skin that can block 'armor-piercing bullets'?"
Seeing this, Su Lun's brow twitched violently, and he lamented inwardly, "As expected, I can't kill it..."
But since he was going to face it sooner or later, he remained as calm as ever. He had identified the monster's attributes already, and opening fire was just to extinguish that last bit of vain hope.
In that moment, he seemed to make a certain resolve, muttering, "Can only try that, then..."
At that time, those two shots had also successfully attracted the Spider Queen's attention. A strong surge of spiritual power washed over Su Lun like waves, leaving him in a daze.
Even at this distance, watching his continuously diminishing spiritual power on his panel, he knew he could only hold on for a few more seconds before he would be completely controlled.
The spiritual strength of this lord-level creature had entirely crushed his own.
At this moment, the scene before his eyes flickered between realities: one moment it was a filthy monster's cave with the ghost-faced spider sprawling across it; the next it was an Elysium world fulfilling all sorts of fantasies, replete with naked beauties...
...
Su Lun felt his consciousness becoming increasingly confused, the crazed curvature of his lips growing higher, "It's time to gamble with my life..."
It wasn't entirely unexpected, it was just that he hadn't thought he would truly need to resort to this last move.
While he still retained a sliver of reason, he did not hesitate at all, pulling a potion from his right hand and fiercely stabbing it into his neck.
At the same time, he raised his left hand, curled his fingers into the air, and rapidly retracted the steel wire inside his mechanical glove, "whoosh," as if telekinetically pulling an object through the air, he grabbed something soaked in the nearby sewage into his hand.
Upon closer inspection, it was a dark, massive scythe.
And at the same time, the last bit of sanity in his eyes dissipated, turning blood-red. It was the moment he lost his reason that the overwhelming lust was also suddenly suppressed.
In this moment, with the black scythe in hand, Su Lun was like the Grim Reaper incarnate.

chapters.title: Chapter 73 - 73: Just One Stroke
chapters.content:
Actually, Su Lun had already found the black scythe lying in sewage while waiting for the assassin to arrive.
To his surprise, he used the All-knowing Eye to examine this legendary "Sealed Object" and suddenly felt somewhat...
Well... how should I put it...
Quite frustrating.
Those who had heard of the reputation of this Sealed Object only knew of the scythe's extreme lethality, that it could break through anything.
But no outsiders knew that its cursed properties were even stronger.
[Xiupunos's Night Scythe]
Quality: Legendary
Description: It is indestructible and can break through anything, but be careful that it might cut off your head in your sleep;
Cursed Property: The scythe can generate a remote slash that cleaves through voids, landing a 'split in two' effect on any substance not higher than the scythe's own sharpness limit; however, within an hour, the user's body will suffer 80% of the damage rebounded from that slash, even if it is no longer by your side, as the blade will split the void and arrive stealthily.
The more frequently it is used in a short period, the greater the power of the slash and the shorter the rebound time;
Explanation: Created by ancient alchemy magicians using alchemical laws, these kind of items typically possess some of the effects of Divine Artifacts. However, following the principle of equivalent exchange, the more powerful the cursed item, the stronger the negative effects; can be used as material for high-tier job advancement.
(Note: Divine Artifact—Sealed Object—Cursed Item—Common Alchemy Item)
Actually, a "Sealed Object" is just a more powerful cursed item.
Typically, their cursed properties are uncontrollable, so most of the time, these super-cursed items are sealed to prevent their overflowing cursed properties from affecting others around them.
Upon seeing the properties of this scythe, the first thought that popped into Su Lun's mind was: kill a thousand enemies, harm oneself eight hundred.
A super powerful weapon indeed, but with such a cursed property, it immediately became a "suicide bomb" that destroys both the enemy and oneself.
Having lived in this world for a while now, he had gained some understanding of "cursed properties."
It seemed that because the alchemists had no faith in deities, relying only on their own power and that of natural materials, certain powers that exceeded the current understanding of the user could not be directly wielded.
Therefore, those ancient alchemy magicians thought to use the principle of equivalent exchange to cunningly harness these powerful forces.
Alchemists believe in "everything has a price," and such is true for the use of power; to employ strength beyond one's threshold requires enduring a corresponding backlash.
Upon reflection, Su Lun found this quite reasonable.
Otherwise, why would a tier-one professional be able to casually create spatial rifts?
Even a Divine Artifact is only available to those who have grasped high-tier laws.
Thus, this black scythe was also a backup plan he had left for himself.
He did not plan to "bet his life" with it unless absolutely necessary.
....
Now, suddenly facing such a "lord-level" Spider Empress, even alchemy bullets couldn't hurt it, which was a guaranteed death situation for Su Lun. He felt he had no other means to handle it besides the black scythe.
But he had no regrets.
As long as he still eyed this Sealed Object scythe, he would sooner or later come to this sewer.
As long as he came, sooner or later he would be ambushed by this Spider Empress.
Previously unaware of this dungeon's situation, Su Lun thought that maybe when he reached tier two, he might have the capability to retrieve the scythe.
But now looking at the situation, even if he reached tier two, he feared it would just mean handing his head to the Spider Empress.
Just like that tier-two assassin before.
Yet this time, having someone to trigger traps provided the perfect combination of timing, location, and human alignment.
It allowed him to obtain the scythe and also a chance to gamble.
...
At this moment, knowing he was outmatched, Su Lun decisively chose to bet his life again.
Well... why say again?
It seemed not the first time, and he himself didn't think it inappropriate.
Holding the black scythe, the moment dark Spiritual Power was infused into it, the blade instantaneously ignited with dancing ghost flames. Su Lun keenly felt a surge of tremendous power controlled in his hand, an arrogantly domineering aura spontaneously arising within him. It was as if he could simply wield the scythe lightly to tear through the void.
But even though he himself was the holder of this black scythe, the sharpness of its blade also sent a chill down his spine, as if it was a fierce tiger that could devour its master, ready to backlash at any moment.
With the large scythe in hand, Su Lun's entire demeanor abruptly turned chillingly terrifying, like a devil who had just stepped out of the gates of hell. He tilted his head to look at the scythe in his hand, licked his lips, seemingly enjoying the sensation of controlling a super-tier power.
With a sharp weapon in hand, evil arises from the gall.
At this moment, nothing else existed in the eyes of Su Lun with his crimson gaze, as he looked up and stared at the Spider Queen not far away, his mouth curling into a smile, "Hehe..."
The Spider Lord, originally the leader of its clan, felt an innate sense of deadly crisis under that chilling glare.
At that moment, Su Lun fiercely stomped on the ground, charging towards the Spider Queen!
The eyes of the Spider Queen burst with red light, but she did nothing to stop his sudden charge. A look of confusion flashed across her exquisite face, shocked as to why her mental control was ineffective against this man. After all, he seemed far weaker than the human she had just killed...
Looking at that black scythe, fear gradually appeared on its face as well.
Indeed, it's eerie, the Spider Queen could feel that the scythe was dangerous, and instinctively did not want to touch it. However, she did not know what danger the scythe possessed.
Red-eyed Su Lun was swift as a cheetah, covering the distance of a hundred meters in just a few breaths. Facing the ghost-faced spiders swarming towards him, he showed no fear, his face only filled with murderous frenzy!
He faced a sky full of spider webs, his body ablaze with even more cold flames than before, with a scythe in one hand and a fire gun in the other, he dashed into the swarm of spiders as if he was in a realm devoid of others.
When he was just twenty to thirty meters away from the Spider Queen, this Aberrant Lord also sensed danger. She spat out spider silk to shield herself, and her sharp spider spears thrust forward; should that human charge forward, he would definitely be punctured with several bloody holes.
But she never expected that suddenly, red-eyed Su Lun would stop.
A sinister smile appeared on his face, then without hesitation, he swung his scythe horizontally!
In that instant, time seemed to slow down a hundredfold.
The scythe slowly fell, with the black fires burning, even twisting the very void into ripples. The blade vibrated at a high frequency, as if tearing a rift in God's Canvas, revealing a gaping void that showed the endless nothingness behind the world.
And the next second, an even stranger scene occurred.
Tens of meters away, the Spider Queen felt the danger and attempted to block with her spider spear. But suddenly, a rift in the void appeared near her neck. Without giving her any time to react, the rift vanished, and a head with a face full of shock thudded to the ground.
Green blood spurted from the headless body of the Spider Queen, shooting several meters into the air.
The ghost-faced Spider Queen, whose defenses could not even be broken by an alchemy bullet, was so easily beheaded by the black scythe.
One strike, just one strike.
The elite and lesser monsters nearby completely panicked...
Seeing their leader killed, these not-so-intelligent ghost-faced spiders lost their organization and instantly fell into chaos. Their instinct for survival made them feel that this place was dangerous, that the human was dangerous, prompting them to flee. After a frenzied scrambling, they flooded into the corridors deep inside the cave...
But just a few breaths later, in that vast space, apart from some spiders struggling in a pile of corpses with broken legs, not a single intact ghost-faced spider was to be seen.
....
Using the power of the black scythe for the first time, red-eyed Su Lun's face showed an unsatisfied greed.
He looked at the corpse of the Spider Queen and tilted his head, seemingly not fully satisfied.
Suddenly, he seemed to think of something and sharply turned his gaze to the only other living person in the space besides himself, Lei.
Like a wolf eyeing its prey, the murderous intent in his eyes grew more intense.
"There's one more, huh..."
Red-eyed Su Lun let out a sinister chuckle, just about to charge over, but at that moment, something happened. He suddenly held his head and showed a look of extreme pain, emitting a suppressed roar like that of a wild beast.
It was a frustration as if he had finally gained freedom, only to be forcefully dragged back and locked up.
Frustration and sanity alternated in his expression.
As the potion continued to take effect, waves of chilling sensation washed over his frustration, slowly letting sanity take over.
The red glow in Su Lun's eyes quickly faded, and then clarity returned.
"Huff... huff... huff..."
Su Lun gasped for air, his chest heaving tumultuously.
The whole person looked as if he had just been fished out of water, his back soaked with sweat.
He rubbed his slightly aching temples, his complexion returning to normal, as if the hysterical struggle that had just occurred on his body had never happened.
"The 'high-grade sedative' seems to be a bit forced... Next time, it seems I need to ask that mysterious pharmacist if he has some better stuff."
Muttering to himself, Su Lun turned to look at the headless body of the Spider Queen not far away.
Then he glanced at the still-living bait lady.
He then let out a sigh of relief, muttering, "Not bad, the timing was just right. The bait wasn't killed by that thing either..."

chapters.title: Chapter 74 - 74: Dark Gold Materials
chapters.content:
Su Lun looked somewhat physically weak, but he couldn't hide the joy in his eyes.
Lords and monsters almost always dropped materials above the silver quality, and there was a high probability for gold.
He looked at the glowing corpse of the Spider Queen, as if he were looking at a mountain of gold, "Tsk tsk, truly, high-level cursed materials have appeared..."
This was the first time he personally killed a monster and obtained high-level materials.
The body of this lordly monster was emitting a special gleam from many places, the characteristic luster of cursed materials.
Silk, poison sacs, skin, heads, blood, bones... even those internal organs, though not usable as equipment materials, were very high-grade and rare alchemical materials.
What Su Lun cared about most, naturally, was the spider legs required for his "Eight-armed Spider God Lance."
Originally, he hoped to acquire eight silver-quality spider leg materials and assemble them together, and he would have been satisfied. Gold was elusive. Yet, unexpectedly, in front of him was a very complete set of spider legs!
"Eh... are those actually dark gold quality spider legs?"
The eight radiant, metallic dark-gleaming spider legs on the Spider Queen's corpse instantly captivated Su Lun's gaze.
"Dark gold level" materials were even more rare than gold materials by half a tier, so rare that not even the top auction houses in the inner city might see them once in several years.
These were truly priceless items.
Intact structure, sturdy, resilient, barbed, with hooks and scythes, innate magic patterns... almost every aspect met the requirements of the blueprint, and even more. At a glance, he felt that this was probably the most suitable material for the blueprint of the "Eight-armed Spider God Lance."
This journey into the cavern, though not without risks, was worth it just for the acquisition of these materials!
....
"What kind of mutation exactly happened to this lordly monster for it to actually have condensed such high-quality mutated limbs?"
While incredibly pleased with his find, Su Lun felt that something was amiss.
