And that dilapidated manor was, unsurprisingly, the residence of Sir Isaac who was hailed as the "Alchemical Demigod" in the former era.
No wonder there was an altar capable of awakening S-grade talents in the basement of that manor.
There wasn't much recorded about Pestoya in the diary, and Su Lun didn't have enough clues to guess what kind of "misfortune" she had suffered.
What came next were hardcore research diaries.
"March 21, 1221, specimen number #001. I chose a fresh corpse and started the experiment..."
"May 1, I found a method from ancient books that could slow down the decay of corpses... an active potion + [Grade VIII Dark Attribute Mana Rune] could gather the spirit of the undead... I converted the hospital morgue into a research venue..."
"August 13, 1221, specimen number #624. I extracted a kind of active substance from the body of a super-tier abyss creature, which I named 'X Serum'. After injection, the fresh corpse regained some physiological characteristics of a living person..."
"Increasing the dosage of 'X Serum', the fresh corpse began to lose control, with tissue abnormalities and strange shapes emerging, eventually turning into a vile monster form, resembling a revertant abyssal creature... I adjusted the formula and continued to increase the dosage in an attempt, but the subject's body couldn't withstand, causing vascular and heart rupture..."
"The hospital corpses were no longer sufficient, and conditions didn't meet the needs for active research; I needed fresher corpses; I tried to approach those patients who were about to die..."
"The families of the patients noticed something unusual, so I dared not use hospital patients anymore. I entrusted a black market trader and bought slaves in the slave market..."
"November 7, 1222, specimen number #1135 showed signs of deformation after the X Serum injection but miraculously survived and even experienced an incredible enhancement in physique. I successfully extracted a biological antibody from the subject's blood that could suppress mutations. Oh, today is a day to be happy, the experiment has made substantial progress..."
"March 11. Today a 'rat' entered the laboratory and stole some research materials. It seems someone is interested in the 'X Serum', after all, it can invigorate the human body. Probably some nobles want to use it to extend their lifespan. I have no interest in interfering, let them be..."
"Failed again. Oh, what a terrible day..."
"April 24, 1224, specimen number #3335. The experiment finally made progress, I successfully refined the first active corpse. I began to try merging souls..."
"Damn it, even though I already successfully made the corpse possess all the biological characteristics of a living person and there was no issue with the bloodline, why did the soul merging still fail?! There was a clear bodily rejection of the soul... There's not enough time, I can't accept this..."
"... "
Page by page, Su Lun went through the content of the diary he could understand, and he roughly had an impression of the story.
It was about a powerful magician trying to find a way to bring people back from the dead, madly experimenting in the morgue, from corpses to patients, to live human experiments...
The diary suddenly stopped abruptly as if something unexpected had occurred, with no further details.
Chekhov had created a "living corpse," but ultimately couldn't endow it with life.
At least, according to the notes, he had failed.
...
"So that's how the 'active corpse' in the cursed space came about..."
After finishing the notes, Su Lun showed a look of realization.
While reading about the "living corpse," his first reaction was not to explore how the Resurrection Technique could be used, but rather he suddenly realized whether the blue-skinned "living corpse" could serve as a puppet medium for handling a scythe?
It had almost all of the living characteristics of a human and even possessed dark spiritual power...
The conditions for controlling a scythe were almost met.
But it was merely a thought.
The content in the notes was too advanced; even the basics were beyond his current comprehension.
Su Lun put away the notes.

chapters.title: Chapter 88 - 88 Controlled Potions
chapters.content:
Su Lun didn't rest at 88 Ginkgo Street, but randomly picked a hotel to catch some sleep.
In the evening, he received a reply from that mysterious Pharmacist at the "Three Muskets Tavern," agreeing to meet at the same place the next morning at ten.
Then it was another day of the usual patrol, followed by a night soaking in the gambling and dueling at the arena.
It's worth mentioning that the arena was bustling these two days.
It seemed that many Big Shots from the inner city were in the VIP rooms on the second floor, the house's stakes were getting higher, and the duels were growing bloodier. The gamblers were excited, and even Kai and the others thought this boom on Green Street was a good sign, because the livelier it was, the more money they made.
However, Su Lun, quietly watching everything by the ring, always felt there were undercurrents behind this abnormal bustle.
But he didn't worry needlessly.
To him, it was a good sign too.
The more bustling the arena, the more Soul Shards he collected.
....
At dawn, when the deathmatches at the arena ended, it was time for Su Lun to get off work.
He hired a few porters to move the equipment out of the basement at 88 Ginkgo Street.
Since he couldn't find a suitable place to live, Su Lun simply didn't bother looking any further and permanently rented a basement near Green Street's shooting range. Although the new dwelling lacked the thick Spiritual Power of the darkness, it was quiet enough once the door was closed. It could barely suffice as a mechanical workshop and a training ground.
And for shooting practice, he could go right next door to the shooting range.
After moving, there was still time left, so Su Lun fine-tuned two pieces of high-tech training equipment and gave them a try.
When the "Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation Device" was connected to his body, an energy like an electric current traveled through his muscles, constantly stimulating the fibers to tear.
Half an hour of training showed an evident effect.
Since Su Lun could track detailed changes in his body's data, he confirmed that this high technology was indeed effective.
Just speaking of muscle stimulation, the training effect while linked to the equipment was roughly three times better than without it.
Then there was the "Steam-Powered Cryotherapy Machine." After intense exercise, the muscles are in a state of high excitement and fatigue and need rest to recover. Variables like muscle power, endurance, and lactic acid thresholds would only improve positively.
Spending two or three minutes in the sub-zero temperatures of the cryotherapy machine, he immediately felt a significant relief in the feeling of fatigue in his muscles. This also greatly increased the efficiency of recovery, shortening the recovery period.
Although the equipment substantially improved his physical training effects, Su Lun was not satisfied.
In this world, besides high technology, the most exaggerated and direct enhancement for the body came from "Alchemical Potions"!
....
At ten o'clock, Su Lun arrived on time at the dilapidated warehouse where they had made their last transaction.
As this wasn't their first deal, the few lads pretending to be gangsters didn't seem so tense anymore.
Su Lun once again saw that mysterious Pharmacist.
For some reason, when he saw the man wrapped up tightly, he suddenly felt the term "Semi-Mutated Human" appearing in his appraisal to be somewhat jarring.
Su Lun's previous understanding of this was insufficient; he didn't grasp what it meant.
But after harvesting memories from several assistant teachers from the Black Tower on his previous journey through the dungeons, he gained some basic understanding of biology.
Only then did he find it inconceivable.
Theoretically, mutation is irreversible.
Once a person mutates, they're destined to become an irrational monster.
Therefore, the situation of "Danny," the mysterious Pharmacist being "semi-mutated" was very unusual.
This reminded Su Lun of some advanced knowledge he read in "The Living Dead Research Journal" the day before.
A thousand years ago, that mad Magician indeed successfully extracted a "mutation suppression sample" from living experiments, making the mutation of the living dead controllable.
Although Su Lun wasn't certain about Danny's situation, he always felt it was very similar.
Su Lun was pondering the issue, slightly distracted.
In the meantime, Pharmacist Danny took the initiative to speak, "Sir, what kind of Potion do you plan to purchase this time?"
Su Lun replied, "The [Mutant Monster Repellent Potion] you gave me last time saved my life, so I plan to stock up a bit more."
Although it was Leena he had saved, in a sense, it indeed also saved the identity of "Su Lun."
Keeping some on hand, he might need it one day in the future.
Hearing this, Danny seemed a bit troubled and said, "The main ingredient for that Potion is hard to come by in the outer city, and I don't have much of it left."
Su Lun: "What material do you need? Next time I go to the black market, perhaps I can keep an eye out for you."
Danny replied, "I need spinal fluid from high-level mutated beasts. The higher the level of the beast the material comes from, the better the effectiveness of the Potion. The batch I sold to you last time was made from the spinal fluid of a second-tier silver grotesque."
Listening, Su Lun asked, "Any grotesque's spinal fluid will do?"
Danny replied, "Basically, yes."
"Alright, I'll keep an eye out for you."
Su Lun nodded and then said, "I also want to buy that [Mutation Tolerance Enhancing Potion] you were looking to sell last time."
The [Mutation Tolerance Enhancing Potion] was for his preparations to fuse with the dark gold spider exosuit.
The deputy head who defected had looked over the materials the day before and told Su Lun one thing, which was that using top-notch materials would result in a very powerful finished exosuit, but the "accommodation value" requirements would also be extremely high.
He estimated that at least before Su Lun's first-tier inauguration, his dark Spiritual Power needed to reach around 1400 to ensure that he wouldn't mutate. But Su Lun was only at about 1200 when he inaugurated.
Originally, the deputy head offered to downgrade, using inferior materials instead.
But Su Lun rejected this proposal.
He thought of how the Pharmacist's "Mutation Tolerance Enhancement Potion" could increase curse attribute tolerance by 10-18%. If he took this Potion, he should be able to merge perfectly with that dark gold prosthetic armament.
....
"Sure, but I only have one left."
Danny had no intention of selling the special Potion he had on hand, and he couldn't sell it to others anyway.
Moreover, they had brought it with them for the transaction.
Su Lun smoothly got his hands on the "Mutation Tolerance Enhancement Potion," and that completed his task.
Then he asked, "Additionally, I need a bodily enhancement Potion without side effects, the higher the grade, the better."
Danny suggested, "I have a 'PTX Berserker Enhancement Potion' and a 'Lester VI Blood Cell Enhancer,' right here... These Potions are laboratory-grade material, not available on the market, you might not recognize them, but I can assure you their effects are absolutely top-notch. Want to give them a try?"
Su Lun didn't even need to see the Potions to agree immediately, "Sure."
Danny thought of something else and added, "I can sell the Potion to you, but I still hope you will only use it yourself and not disclose it to anyone. Otherwise... both you and I will be in a lot of trouble."
"No problem!"
Upon hearing the names of the Potions, Su Lun already knew what kind of trouble it was.
Because these were truly controlled substances!
He remembered the names of these two Potions; they were specialized physical training Potions used internally by the noble students of the Black Tower Academy, greatly enhancing training efficiency and promoting muscle growth.
These were high-grade Potions "exclusively supplied in limited quantities" by the Black Tower laboratory to the academy and the outflow of such through any channel was forbidden. If discovered, it was a serious crime punishable by the gallows!
Moreover, if he wasn't mistaken, the students were currently only using the "fifth-generation Potions," and Danny was offering the "sixth generation"?
Upon hearing the names of these Potions, he could almost confirm that Danny must be a Pharmacist that came from a top-level laboratory in the inner city!
In a flash, both Potions were handed over to him.
"PTX Berserker Enhancement Potion"
Details: After ingestion, it will cause your training to become supercharged, significantly increasing muscle strength during training, accelerating fatigue recovery, providing a continuous source of explosive energy, endurance, and concentration; the effects last for 12-13 weeks;
"Lester VI Blood Cell Enhancer"
Details: Taking the Potion continuously enhances cell vitality, muscle growth +60%, recovery efficiency +144%; the effects last for 16-18 weeks; individual constitution varies, figures may fluctuate by about 5-20%;
Using the All-knowing Eye, Su Lun looked at the astounding effects of the Potions, and he immediately decided to purchase them, "How much?"
The efficacy of these Potions was at least twice or three times stronger than the best body-refining Potions he had seen on the black market before!
Hearing the inquiry about the price, Danny's eyes showed some difficulty as he said, "They're not for sale on the market, so I don't know how much they're worth. But just the material cost of these two Potions is over five hundred thousand. You can have both for one hundred... let's make it eighty thousand."
"No problem."
The price was even below the cost, definitely a fair deal.
Su Lun immediately paid cash and took the two Potions.
He then asked, "I will need more of this type of Potions later on, is that possible?"
Danny showed a troubled expression, "That's... difficult. Without a laboratory-grade Potion room, even with the materials, such Potions can't be produced."
"Oh."
Su Lun felt somewhat disappointed.
However, obtaining such high-grade Potions was already an unexpected surprise.
The effects would last for several months, which was enough time for him to figure something out.
At this moment, Su Lun said, "I know you won't be selling Potions on a large scale, but if you have Potions you need to sell, you can contact me directly. At the very least, I can guarantee that your information will absolutely not be leaked, and the price will be satisfactory for you."
Ever since he learned about the mysterious Pharmacist's situation, he knew this fellow must be in great need of money.
After all, being a Pharmacist is also a very costly profession, and despite the high value of the finished Potions, the materials wasted during the refining process were also staggering. Merely relying on the petty thefts of the small fry around him wouldn't support his daily research.
After two transactions, they had established a basic trust. Hearing this, Danny nodded, "Hmm."
Reaching this point in the conversation, Su Lun suddenly remembered something and casually asked, "By the way, last time I was hunting in the caverns, I encountered a lot of mutated mutation monsters that I'd never seen before, and they were much stronger than the normal ones. Do you know what's going on with that?"
"This..."
Upon hearing this, Danny was clearly troubled, seemingly aware of the reason but hesitant to speak openly about it.
But having sold so many special Potions, he guessed Su Lun must have deduced some of his background.
After a moment, he brought up, "I heard there was a serious accident in an inner-city laboratory a few years ago that caused a leak of special substances into the city's sewer network, leading to biological mutations... I'm not clear on the details, but you'd better stay out of the sewers when you go hunting."
So it was a laboratory leak?
Hearing this, Su Lun nodded, "Hmm."
....
Two days passed, and Su Lun made a trip to the black market.
He got his hands on the "Eight-Armed Spider God Spear" alchemical prosthetic armament, just as he had hoped.
The finished product was even more perfect than anticipated!

chapters.title: Chapter 89 - 89: Eight-Armed Spider Spear
chapters.content:
In the dimly lit basement, Su Lun retrieved the alchemy equipment he had brought back from the black market.
This was a set of spider arms that, while unimposing when retracted, stretched out nearly eight meters.
Under the flickering light of the gas lamps, a dark, non-golden metallic luster reflected off the eight spider limbs. Upon closer inspection, each limb was densely engraved with intricate and mysterious runes.
The reason why a "Forging Master" was needed to craft this equipment lay in those runes. Engraving so many runes on such narrow spider limbs was definitely beyond the capabilities of an ordinary craftsman.
Although Su Lun was still far from a master in alchemy, his eye for quality was not lacking.
He could see that on these spider limbs, there weren't just single-layer runes but also interwoven, multiple layers of rune techniques.
It was like overlapping several different patterns on the same piece of paper, where each pattern had to remain distinct and complete without affecting the others. This required extremely high rune-carving skills.
Su Lun was very satisfied with the appearance of this equipment, its low-key and stable color, especially since it also met various professional needs.
With the identification from the All-knowing Eye, he was not afraid of any hidden issues left by the treacherous deputy dean of the black tower in the equipment.
And indeed, just as the designs had described, even with some special materials, there were some minor attributes enhancements.
[Eight-Armed Spider Spear]
Detailed description: First-tier dark gold quality alchemy equipment, requires high-level control skills; containment value rating A+ or above, dark spiritual power value 1350 points, mutation rate less than 8%; once merged, overall body toughness +25, elemental resistance +20, agility +12, toxin resistance +50%;
....
The profession of an alchemist is very ancient.
They explore the mysteries of nature, seeking the ultimate truths of the material world, but they do not focus on personal cultivation.
The great ancient alchemists also found that frail bodies were a shackle that limited their study of alchemy, while also making them weak in combat.
Some combat-oriented magicians thought of using special biological parts grafted onto their bodies to enhance their attributes.
But because direct transplantation would cause the body to have a rejection reaction with alien organisms.
Until a certain ancient era, a mysterious and powerful high-tier alchemist, Nicolas Flamel, came up with a method. He used the Space Law + the Law of Equivalent Exchange to develop a special type of equipment fusion method that could "deceive" the body into not rejecting it.
This method allowed external equipment to exist on the host in a form of "spatial markings". It remained sealed on normal days, and when needed, the seal was undone, and powered by dark spiritual power for use.
Subsequently, through generations of alchemists' improvements, this gradually evolved into the current system of "Cursed Mark Equipment".
And the "new-style magicians" are even more extreme, they no longer settle with biological limbs but think of replacing some or even all body parts with machinery...
....
After consuming a [Mutation Tolerance Enhancement Potion], Su Lun determined that the success rate of the fusion had reached 97%.
He did not hesitate and began setting up a five-pointed star alchemy formation on the basement floor with materials he had prepared beforehand. Like before, he started by muttering the universal alchemist incantations, then guided the formation to function.
"Abide by the Law of Equivalent Exchange, praise the glory of the primal creator, witness the miracle of creation through alchemy..."
After the five-pointed star lit up, a mystical "chemical reaction" began. The Eight-Armed Spider Spear gradually dissolved into the light of the formation, then slowly merged into his body.
Soon, the light of the formation dissipated, and the equipment fused perfectly.
Su Lun clearly felt a comfortable sensation akin to being soaked in warm water, and upon checking his attribute panel, he saw a significant increase in toughness and resistance.
This also meant... he was tougher to beat up now.
For instance, where a gunshot might have once pierced a fist-sized hole in his skin, it would now likely make a much smaller hole, greatly increasing his chances of survival.
With the successful fusion of the equipment, Su Lun was now truly a first-tier professional.
He thought for a moment, then formed seals with both hands, changing into eight different sorcerer's seals.
The essence of a "sorcerer's seal" is to guide the dark spiritual power inside the body along a specific trajectory, thereby quickly consolidating an alchemy formation and unlocking the "spatial markings" of the equipment.
Each sorcerer's seal represents a specific flow trajectory of dark spiritual power.
Different equipment sealing combinations also vary, following the distinctions of the "Earth Wind Water Fire" four elemental sources. Su Lun's Eight-Armed Spider Spear, derived from the earth-based "metal property" equipment, required eight seals aligned to form the "Pentagram Flash Gold Formation".
Also, because he had previously harvested the soul of assistant professor Rosa from the Black Tower Academy, he had acquired the skill [Quick Seal Formation]. Although it was his first time forming seals, there was a strangely familiar feeling. The eight seals were orderly and the dark spiritual power within his body surged rapidly.
The sealing was quick and precise, and in less than two seconds, the five-pointed star formation at his feet lit up.
As the light faded, eight fierce dark golden spider limbs suddenly appeared from Su Lun's back.
"So this is what it feels like to possess equipment..."
Su Lun felt incredible as eight spider spears emerged from his spine, and even the skin on his entire back became tough.
It didn't feel like wearing external equipment; rather, it was as if he had spontaneously grown eight arms that his brain could manipulate at will.
The ability to multitask allowed Su Lun to quickly get into the groove, as he controlled the spider limbs and carefully began to scale the wall.
The spider legs were covered in sharp velvety hairs and barbs, so gripping and ascending the wall was effortless.
Having previously killed the Spider Queen in the cave and stripped the "Intermediate Spider Climbing" skill, Su Lun found wall climbing with spider limbs to be completely smooth. After his body got slightly accustomed to the operation, he became increasingly agile.
With eight legs alternating on the wall, his speed increased rapidly, and in the blink of an eye, he had vaulted up to the ceiling and was hanging upside down there.
"Such a fast speed!"
Joy appeared on Su Lun's face.
After a brief trial, he was shocked by his own speed of movement.
Eight legs running were at least several times faster than his previous two legs and many times more agile.
After a brief test, his straight-line running speed had roughly doubled, but the increase in agility was far more dramatic. With eight spider legs, he could move past obstacles with ease, abruptly stop, change directions, leap, and climb...far outperforming two legs, with his obstacle-crossing capability multiplied manifold!
And after mastering it, he could even accelerate further.
If he had this spider limb attachment when he previously explored the cave, would he have had to run from the monsters?
Even if he couldn't defeat them, just by running, those deformed monsters couldn't keep up with him.
Su Lun had even envisioned a tactic perfectly suited to this spider leg attachment—"Kiting Flow"!
Striking while running, striking while chasing...
Coupled with his sharpshooter's long-range shooting ability, this three-dimensional mobility dramatically boosted his combat power.
Whether outdoors or in the city, it was an unprecedented ability for preserving life and pursuing foes.
...
However, the spider spears served more than just mobility; their attack power was not weak either.
The eight spider spears featured retractable "Toxic Spikes."
These spikes, engraved with "Armor-Piercing Runes" and "Durability Runes," could easily penetrate iron plates.
Su Lun leapt down from the ceiling, and the eight spider limbs spread out to cushion and absorb the impact, allowing his body to land smoothly without any shock.
At that moment, he operated a spider spear stabbing toward an old steam pipe not far away, penetrating it as easily as if sticking into soft mud.
"Such strong piercing power..."
Su Lun looked at the gleaming sharp spike on the spider spear with fascination in his eyes.
Although his marksmanship had been decent, his close combat abilities weren't particularly outstanding. Now, with this spider limb attachment, his close combat capabilities had surged dramatically.
Could an enemy with two arms defeat him with ten? Especially since he now had super elongated arms with a span of four meters each, eight spears stabbing simultaneously, instantly turning someone into a bloody sieve...
At that moment, Su Lun also took out a puppet manipulated by steel wires.
Although the spider limbs lacked fingers, having an extra eight limbs with the hardened velvety hair and barbs on the spider spears, which were meant for manipulating spider silk, made them as smooth and flexible as fingers, if not more so.
Now, controlling the steel wires, one spider limb could even control multiple wires, and with several limbs working together, he could manage even more wires.
This allowed Su Lun to control two puppets while freeing up both hands to hold guns.
"Now, with my hands completely free, I can manipulate puppets and cast spells while fighting..."
The more Su Lun experimented, the more enthusiastic he became; he also seemed to want to test the limits of his control, pulling more and more wires.
But soon, he couldn't help but laugh and cry.
After controlling four puppets, the wires were everywhere, in a chaotic mess, almost binding him up.
It was his first attempt at multitasking with eight tasks, and his skills weren't proficient enough, clearly straining his capacity.
However, even so, Su Lun was quite satisfied.
After all, the "Multi-tasking" skill could be improved by practicing...
He was very pleased with this eight-limbed spider spear attachment.

chapters.title: Chapter 90 - 90 Negotiation
chapters.content:
```
In the days that followed, Su Lun's life became fulfilling.
After successfully integrating the eight-armed spider spear prosthetic, he needed a lot of time to practice multitasking control over puppets, as well as climbing, teleportation, and combat...
Moreover, in order not to waste the two expensive body-strengthening potions he had bought, he also had to spend several hours every day on physical training.
Fortunately, the gang's daily routine was very relaxed. He only had to participate in the street patrols at seven o'clock every evening, and unless there were emergencies, he could arrange the rest of his time freely.
Lately, Su Lun had found that harvesting ordinary corpses was yielding less and less experience. As a result, he no longer wasted his time in the casino during the early nights. He only went to watch the last few fights when there were professionals dueling in the later hours.
Time flew by quickly, and before he knew it, more than a month of stable and enriching days had passed.
.....
On this day, Su Lun was tinkering with mechanical modifications in the basement.
The shabby basement had changed drastically from a month ago when he had just moved in. During this time, like an ant moving house, Su Lun had gradually moved a large amount of mechanical equipment and parts inside, even a small steam-powered lathe.
The walls were hung with various mechanical tools, purchased from different shops, as well as high-quality goods salvaged from the black market inner city.
He had transformed this place into his own mechanical workshop.
At this moment, Su Lun, wearing work clothes stained with oil and protective goggles and with two "PT3 Type Single-Cylinder Steam-Powered Arms" attached to his hands, was engrossed in his work.
The steam boiler provided tremendous power to the mechanical arms, allowing him to bend the steel material in his hands into the desired shapes without the use of a lathe.
He was crafting a bullet belt and ammunition box for his companion firearm "Green Demon."
This famous gun had an extremely high rate of fire and could withstand high temperatures without jamming. If used merely as a pistol, its firepower advantage could not be fully realized.
Even if he fired in bursts, even with an extended magazine, it would empty within seconds.
Therefore, he thought of the kind of bullet belt and external high-capacity ammo box used with heavy machine guns. In times of needing firepower suppression, he could simply hang the ammo box on his body, connect it with the belt, and the handgun would instantly turn into a rattle of heavy machine gun fire.
While his hands were busy, the eight spider limbs behind him were not idle either.
Because of the mechanical arms for work, it wasn't convenient for him to hold other things, so when he felt thirsty, a spider limb would bring him a cup of tea from several meters away on the table for a sip of water.
The eight spider limbs saved him a lot of time, completing simple yet time-consuming tasks.
For example: loading bullets into a chain.
Without needing to control very precisely, a few spider limbs working together could easily pour the bullets from a box into a specially-made bullet pressing device. Then, with a press of the handle and accompanied by a rhythmic metallic "click" "click" "click," bullets would be neatly loaded onto the chain.
Before long, the last two ammo boxes salvaged from the black market were modified, and Su Lun sighed in relief.
Looking at his work, he seemed quite satisfied and muttered, "Finally done, ten ammo boxes should be enough."
The ammo boxes were not only suitable for Su Lun's "Green Demon" but also for another thing in the room: a mechanical suit of armor.
Su Lun picked up an ammo box and walked over to a mecha hanging on the wall, trying it in a slot – it fitted perfectly.
This mecha was just a rough prototype assembled by Su Lun, quite crude, but basically shaped.
Su Lun named this iron lump "Iron Man Mark I."
It didn't have anything superfluous on it, not even a shell.
The spotty old frame of its body was adapted from the "Scavenger VIII Generation Exoskeleton"; at its core was a "PT9 Type Four-Cylinder Steam Boiler" scavenged from the old goods market, providing the power for this iron lump; the arms were simply two crude six-chambered guns, connected to bullet belts and armored plates.
Various other parts like hydraulic transmission devices and high-pressure valves were scavenged from old equipment...
Although lacking in technological sophistication, this creation was Su Lun's attempt.
He tried to control this type of mecha with steel wires like a puppet.
But because the technology was far from sufficient and the machinery too cumbersome, he hadn't even solved the issue of it easily falling over when trying to run.
```
Now, its only use was to serve as a semi-fixed artillery piece. Su Lun remotely controlled it to fire, making some simple teleportations and aimings.
It was also a small step forward in his own vision of becoming a mechanical puppet master.
....
It was midnight, and Su Lun still had several hours to freely arrange his time in his workshop.
After completing his mechanical manufacturing tasks for the day and in order to maintain enough reserved spiritual power, he put away the enhancement gear.
He took out an uncarved puppet, thinking he could practice making a "runed puppet," but before he could carve a few strokes, his communicator suddenly transmitted Kai's urgent flag-waving signal: "Everyone, grab your gear, assemble at the Big Elephant Tavern, speed!"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's brows furrowed.
The communicator was a tool used by the Cross Society gang members to summon people in the event of a very important emergency. For minor fights and skirmishes, shouting a few times on Green Street would gather twenty or thirty people; there was no need for a communicator.
In all the time he'd joined, it had only been used once on the first day when the Cross Society headquarters was attacked, and now he was hearing it again?
By the sound of Kai's voice, it seemed the situation was far from minor.
"Could it be those Steam Party guys stirring up trouble?"
Su Lun speculated, as Green Street and the Steam Party's territory often clashed, and if there was a significant uproar, it was likely those guys were behind it.
He didn't dawdle and changed out of his work clothes.
Since his battle gear was always stored in the storage ring, there was nothing much to pack. Su Lun left the basement and started his motorcycle, speeding all the way, arriving at the front of the Big Elephant Tavern in less than two minutes.
....
When Su Lun arrived, two groups were already facing off outside the tavern on the street.
The regular tavern-goers were gone, and the two gangs, totaling two to three hundred people armed with long guns and short cannons, were clearly divided at the entrance of the tavern. Their numbers were still increasing.
Su Lun glanced over and saw that on the Cross Society's side, there were not only the few dozen people from Green Street, but captains and gang members from other districts had also arrived.
It seemed like they were gearing up for a big showdown tonight.
The attrition rate among the lower ranks of gang members was high, and Su Lun was now considered an old-timer on Green Street. Due to his close relationship with Kai, although not officially appointed, the gang members also treated him as the "vice captain." Especially the newcomers, who nodded in acknowledgment upon seeing his motorcycle arrive.
An acquaintance among the newcomers came over and greeted Su Lun: "Vice-captain, you're here..."
Su Lun didn't see Kai and, noticing that tonight's setup was a bit exaggerated, asked, "What happened?"
The man whispered, "The Steam Party guys suddenly rallied their people to Green Street for some reason. The executives are negotiating inside the tavern..."
"Negotiating?"
Su Lun frowned at the news.
Looking at the arrogant Steam Party bikers nearby, he realized something was off.
This kind of large-scale invasion would usually mean outright war on any other day.
And yet they were sitting down for negotiations?
But given the current situation, he knew that a fight couldn't break out for now.
As there were executives negotiating, no matter how much the people outside jeered and provoked, they couldn't start a fight until there was noise coming from inside the tavern.
...
After roughly understanding the reason for the assembly, Su Lun decided not to mingle in the crowd and walked to the corner of the street, crouching near an alley entrance.
If a real fight broke out, places where people clustered were definitely the prime targets for hand grenades.
He crouched for only a short while before he saw Kai emerge from the tavern.
Kai also spotted Su Lun, signaling him to a secluded corner, probably having something to talk about.
The two met at the corner wall of the tavern.
Su Lun had never seen such an ugly expression on Kai's face, so he asked, "What's happened?"
Kai gestured for him to look inside the tavern.
Through the window, Su Lun glanced and saw that the tavern was devoid of customers, filled instead with burly men in black leather jackets brandishing guns.
Two officers from the Cross Society had arrived, "Red Demon" Goron and "Smoke Ghost" Sambu.
And across the negotiation table, Su Lun recognized the man with a scarred face from the Steam Faction, the second-tier officer "Mad Dog" Hogue Weisnat, whose gift was the beastial "C-003-Werewolf", formidable in battle and an old-time powerhouse of the Steam Faction.
Only then did Kai speak, "There's been a major issue in the inner city, we might be in trouble..."
Listenting to his tone, Su Lun's face remained unchanged.
If there's an issue, so be it, after all, the problems of the inner city wouldn't affect their ability to eat and sleep as low-ranking gang members...
Kai was concise, adding, "Just got the news, the top financial conglomerate of the inner city, 'Reyes Family,' has split into seven. The properties on Green Street now fall into the hands of the third branch. Young Master Martin Reyes of the third branch is here today, he's upstairs."
"Reyes Family?"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun started to feel as though the good news suddenly had something to do with him.
Wasn't that Rich Lady Lena's family?
Their Cross Society's patron, Lady Phino, also had very close dealings with the Reyes family...
What on earth had happened in this one month?
Could it be that Lena hadn't managed to hold power when she returned home, and her uncles and aunts had split the family?
Kai continued, "I'm not clear on the specifics. But word has it that the Black Tower's higher-ups pressured them, and the other large families of the inner city didn't want to see the Reyes family dominating alone. That's why the Reyes Family Head was forced to agree to the division of the conglomerate."
"..."
Upon hearing this familiar pattern, Su Lun instantly had a moment of realization.
The "Reyes Conglomerate" had nearly monopolized Old Lington's domestic water and mining industries, they were the textbook plutocracy.
But the end of a "plutocracy" is usually predetermined.
Either they are so powerful that they control the government,
and if they can't reach such heights, the eventual outcome is always a beating.
This was nothing new in his former life as well, like the Russian oligarchs, once so glorious at their peak but ultimately hammered down...
Old Lington was a privately-owned fiefdom; theoretically, everything in the city belonged to the "Duke Raphael", the private property of the lord. As long as the Black Tower, the supreme authority over the inner city, exists, even the largest "plutocracies" have to lie low.
However...
What did the breakdown of the Reyes family have to do with them on Green Street?
Looking at the Steam Faction, who were on the other side of the negotiation, Su Lun seemed to guess something.
It was then when Kai finally disclosed his concerns, "Most of Green Street's entertainment properties belonged to the Reyes family. Now that the Reyes family has split, the taverns and gambling dens have mostly fallen into the hands of the third branch. And somehow, those guys from the Steam Faction hooked up with Young Master Martin.
Now, they imply that they want our Cross Society to pull out of Green Street, leaving it for the Steam Faction to take over..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun immediately understood.
....
```
This kind of negotiation, Su Lun felt, was eighty percent likely to break down.
Just as expected, after just a few exchanges, the pub erupted with the slamming of tables and raised voices.
The noise was loud enough to carry out onto the street.
Mad Dog Hogue was unbending and aggressive, "Within three days, your Cross Society must pull out of Green Street, or else..."
While indeed the gangs rely on financial backers, that isn't the whole story.
Lands won with lives are not so easily ceded; the Cross Society wasn't that cowardly.
"Impossible!"
Smoke Ghost Sangbu slammed the table and interrupted the conversation.
He had a dark expression, his words slow but piercing as nails, "Green Street has always belonged to our Cross Society, Hogue. Stop with the bullshit. If your Steam Party wants territory, have the guts to take it by force!"
Lady Fino is the Cross Society's benefactor, and unless she speaks up, no one else's words carry weight.
With that, it meant the negotiation had completely broken down.
No sooner had the words "come and take it" faded, the nerves of everyone from both sides were struck raw, and looking across the pub, all raised their guns and aimed at each other in unison.
Su Lun and Kai were quick to react, drawing and aiming their guns at the Steam Party members inside the building at once.
This gun-drawing set off a chain reaction, as the members from both sides outside instantly tensed up at the "click-click" sounds of bullets being chambered.
The atmosphere suddenly became tense as a powder keg with a lit fuse, ready to explode at the slightest disturbance.
For a moment, the vast Elephant Pub fell deathly silent.
No one dared to fire that first shot.
If they were to really start fighting now, it would surely spark a full-scale war between the two gangs!
....
Gang negotiations are often about showing strength, and flipping tables is a frequent occurrence, but an actual fight at the negotiation table is less likely.
Usually, in such a scenario, a third party would step in to mediate, to cool things down and get both sides back at the negotiation table...
But unexpectedly, something no one anticipated happened.
Just then, a bottle of booze came flying out of nowhere, smashing onto the negotiation table.
With a "crash" it shattered, splashing liquor all over everyone.
Everyone was stunned. Such an act showed complete disregard for the gang members, a blatant provocation worthy of death.
The crowd turned their furious glares towards the second floor of the pub, but upon seeing who it was, their anger was forcibly swallowed back down.
A young man in a silver suit leaned against the railing, looking down at everyone with a sneer, "Hmph! A bunch of fools who don't know what's good for them. I give you a little sweetness, and you really start thinking you're something, huh?"
As soon as the words were out, the faces of the Cross Society members turned extremely ugly.
The remark was clearly directed at them.
Su Lun did not recognize the young man, but from his luxurious suit fabric, he guessed that he must be a Big Shot from the inner city.
Clearly, he was the main character of today, the third son of the Reyes family, Martin Reyes.
PS. Tickets requested for Monday~
```

chapters.title: Chapter 91 - 91: I'm Not Here to Negotiate with You
chapters.content:
The entertainment industry on Green Street was one of the most developed districts in the outer city.
Thanks to the backing of the mysterious Lady Philo, many wealthy people from the inner city flocked to this area for entertainment. Gambling activities such as the bloody gladiatorial arenas, which were not available in the inner city, generated an absurdly high amount of revenue just from the cut taken from those gambling tycoons.
Usually, such entertainment venues were overseen by the mob to handle issues more conveniently dealt with by local toughs.
For instance, thieves, scam artists, clients who refused to pay for prostitutes, rowdy drunkards, illegal human trafficking, hallucinogenic potions... and some other under-the-table dealings.
It wasn't that the mysterious big bosses behind the scenes were incapable of handling these matters, but outsourcing some of these issues for a fee would save a lot of trouble and even lead to mutual benefits without losing any dignity.
Originally, the situation was that the Cross Society had a strong fist and had secured the rights to oversee Green Street.
And because the backers of the Cross Society could bring high-quality customers to the entertainment industry of this street, everyone was quite satisfied.
But now that the third branch of the Reyes family had acquired the ownership of some of the big venues in the Green Street district, the situation had changed.
Young Master Martin intended to throw out the Cross Society and replace them with his closer allies, the Steam Party.
Many venues on Green Street, like the gladiator arena "Crimson Fortress" which Su Lun frequented, now had the Reyes family as major shareholders.
It seemed there should be no issue with one's own businesses changing hands to a different overseer.
But while it might have been legitimate, it did not follow the underworld code.
After all, the outer city was the turf of the three major gangs, inhabited by desperados who lived on the knife's edge and fought deadly battles over their earned territories. Why should they concede just because they were told to?
Negotiations, ideally, involved back-and-forth discussions.
The ultimate goal of gang violence was always profit.
Indeed, the Steam Party wanted to take over supervision, and it was negotiable if a substantial sum of money was offered and some benefits conceded.
That way, everyone could save face.
However, Young Master Martin now seemed to be demanding that the Cross Society bare their bottoms and "scram."
.....
"Smoky" Sam looked at the broken bottle on the table, a gleam of cold fury flashed in his eyes, but he restrained himself from showing his anger.
He stared at the young man in the suit upstairs and asked in a grave voice, "Young Master Martin, what do you mean by this?"
"What do I mean? Heh heh..."
Young Master Martin sneered dismissively, without even taking a proper look at this Cross Society executive, and said, "From now on, I call the shots on Green Street. Also, mind your tone; don't assume everyone is qualified to speak to me. I didn't come here to negotiate with you.
I'm just having Hog notify you that within three days, I don't want to see any members of the Cross Society in my venues."
After saying this, he finally fixed his gaze on Sam and asked, "Now, do you understand?"
With these words, not just Sam, but the entire Cross Society looked extremely displeased.
If it had been anyone else speaking so arrogantly, hostilities might have already escalated.
But facing this influential figure from the inner city, not a single person from the Cross Society dared to direct their guns at him, all choked up and red in the face.
Sam, with a stern face, spoke again, "Young Master Martin, it's not a big deal for the Cross Society to withdraw from your venues. But with the way you're doing this, Lady Philo might find it difficult to accept..."
Tit for tat, a general for a general.
Sam knew very well that he had no grounds to negotiate terms with this Young Master; his only course was to invoke the name of their financier.
Gang members were desperados struggling at the bottom rungs of society and merely 'enforcers,' disposable in the eyes of high society. Their lives were worthless.
Status?
Respect?
They were thinking too much. Just tools in the end.
Harsh as it might sound, this was the reality.
Upon hearing this remark, Young Master Martin coldly retorted, "If it weren't for Lady Phino's sake, I wouldn't even bother to come here personally. Besides, the matter at hand is one for my Reyes family to handle, and it has nothing to do with Lady Philo..."
His words effectively shut down any argument the Cross Society members could have made.
Not even giving face to the financier left no room for further discussion.
....
Outside the window of the tavern, Su Lun's brows furrowed.
The more prominent the family, the more they prized networking and connections, and the less they should offend others so "brazenly."
Young Master Martin seemed aggressive, displaying the arrogant mannerisms of a spoiled rich young master. Seeing him face a group of vicious gang members without changing his expression, Su Lun felt that this guy surely wasn't as superficial as he appeared.
It was one thing not to give face to the gang members, but not even giving face to Lady Philo? That was intriguing.
This approach of not showing any consideration felt like... the other party simply didn't care about causing offense.
"Things seem to have gotten complicated..."
Su Lun's thoughts raced.
He quickly realized that the incident on Green Street was just the surface of a deeper high-level power struggle.
The right to control a few streets wasn't enough to personally bring the Young Master here.
If there wasn't subsequent value, there was no need to save face...
Such events usually occurred when a building was about to collapse.
A thought flashed through Su Lun's mind, and from Young Master Martin's words, he rapidly deduced two possibilities: 1. Someone was planning to move against the Cross Society; 2. Someone was planning to move against the financial backer behind the Cross Society!
"Could it be that someone is preparing to move against Lady Philo, or perhaps the power behind her?"
The more Su Lun thought about it, the closer he felt he was to the truth.
He had known beforehand that the power behind Philo was, if not Lena's father, then closely related to them. After all, Lady Philo was Lena's aunt.
If anyone had the capability to force the Reiss family to split, wouldn't they strike while the iron was hot and also clip its wings?
Actually, when Lena was assassinated, Su Lun had suspected that there was more to it.
If simply assassinating someone could lead to advancement, then the decision-makers of the Reiss family must be foolish indeed.
Choosing assassination was probably to create internal strife.
Now, Lena hadn't died, the consortium was still forcefully split, and the upper echelon of the Dark Tower who had helped escalate the situation had surfaced. But what's done was done, and they had to swallow the criticism of their unsightly behavior.
Turning the Reiss family into seven parts was clearly because the adversary lacked the power to strike down this giant, so they created conflicts within it, won over some, divided some, and struck at some...
It was a very clever political tactic.
So, this was also why the third house didn't continue to support the Cross Society in the outer city but turned to the Steam Party instead. This was actually the real reflection of the inner city conflict transferred to the outer city.
Thinking this through, Su Lun also suddenly understood why Young Master Martin was so aggressive—it was because he knew someone was going to move against Lady Philo.
His thoughts vanished in a flash, and Su Lun muttered to himself, "If that's the case, this turf war is going to get a lot of people killed..."
....
Young Master Martin's few words slapped the faces of all the members of the Cross Society, and Kai next to him listened with clenched teeth, muttering under his breath, "This damned young master, I really want to blow his head off with a gun!"
Talk was cheap, but no one dared to actually move.
Even though the Reiss family had split, it was from one "oligarch" into seven "tycoons."
This third house was not to be underestimated and was definitely not a faction the outer city gangs could afford to provoke.
At that moment, Young Master Martin lost his patience to stay in the tavern any longer, and he tossed out two Gold Coins like it was charity, saying arrogantly, "This is for the drinks earlier."
Saying so, he didn't deign to give the Cross Society members another glance and said, "Remember, in three days, I don't want to see you here anymore."
Then, without looking back, he was escorted out of the Elephant Tavern by his bodyguards.
The Steam Party members, like foxes trailing behind the tiger's tail, wore smug smiles on their faces and followed the young master, strutting off.
The cadres Smoky and Red Demon both had dark expressions and remained silent.
The Cross Society's members were filled with rage, but no one dared to stop them.
....
After the enemies left, Kai and the other captains also swarmed into the tavern.
With just a command from their leaders, they were ready to grab their weapons and pursue.
"What do we do now, Boss Smoky? This damned Steam Party is going too far!"
"I say... let's just grab our weapons and go at it! I just saw those guys from the Steam Party looking so smug; I almost didn't hold back from shooting those dogs."
"Exactly! That so-called young master, I really want to twist his head off!"
"..."
The gang members weren't the type to fear stirring up trouble, especially the captains, who had clawed their way out of piles of corpses.
They weren't afraid of brawling, rolling up their sleeves and ready to fight at a moment's notice.
But the cadres obviously knew there was more at stake and considered the situation from a higher perspective.
Not having the right to enter, Su Lun just quietly listened from outside.
He felt that what he could think of, the cadres would surely also think of.
If they were to start a war now, the Cross Society would lose both morally and financially.
Even though they were a gang, did they dare to openly attack the young master of a major inner city family?
They would feel good killing him, but what about the consequences?
Did they think the security task force and garrison of the inner city weren't swift enough to eradicate a gang? Even if the people of the inner city couldn't thoroughly exterminate the long-entrenched snakes of the South City District, the Steam Party and the Crow Gang, these two large factions, would definitely be eager to help with the extermination.
Smoky suppressed the anger of the crowd and said, "I'm going back to headquarters to see what the boss says... Don't be impulsive, wait for news."

chapters.title: Chapter 92 - 92 Start the War
chapters.content:
"I'll be leaving first, the matters here are now in your hands. I'll handle the matters in the inner city, you can go ahead without holding back. In three days, I don't want to see the Cross Society's people still on Green Street!"
"Young Master Martin, rest assured, leave the matters to us."
"..."
After leaving the Elephant Tavern, "Mad Dog" Hog escorted Young Master Martin respectfully onto his luxurious steam limousine.
Watching the convoy depart, Hog also sighed in relief.
This was his first time accompanying such a Big Shot, and he felt immense pressure. Just now in the tavern, he truly feared that the Cross Society members couldn't control their temper, or that a gun might accidentally discharge...
Though with personal bodyguards around, this Young Master was probably safe from dying, but even if he were to be startled, Hog felt he would bear a great responsibility.
And if a fight had ensued, being on Cross Society's territory, they, the Steam Party, were sure to be at a disadvantage.
However, now that he had seen off this Young Master, the mission had been perfectly accomplished.
Hog, in a great mood, called to his fellow members to leave, "Let's go, brothers."
The roaring of several hundred motorcycles exploded in their ears, as this uninvited group grandly left Green Street.
.....
Shortly after, Hog returned to the Steam Party's gathering spot in the East City Wellington District.
This place was filled with various mechanical modification shops and parts stores.
Illegal limb modifications were also a significant source of income for the Steam Party.
Hog entered a heavy metal-style tavern and met with the boss "Butcher" Banner in a private room on the second floor.
"Boss, the job is done."
"No trouble from the Cross Society?"
"Nothing for now. It looks like they definitely have to swallow this dumb loss."
"Well done."
Banner was in a very good mood and chuckled while pulling a sultry woman into his arms.
The woman, seeing he was in a good mood, seductively asked, "Old man, why would Young Master Martin personally come to handle such a trivial matter?"
"Trivial matter? This is no small matter."
Banner chuckled, shaking his head with a joyful expression, and explained meaningfully, "If this Green Street matter gets resolved, the outside city's structure will change... the Cross Society might just take a big tumble this time."
The woman then asked, "But... won't the sponsor behind the Cross Society do something about it?"
Banner said, "Lady Philo in the inner city also has significant influence. Originally, if the Reyes family hadn't split, we really wouldn't have had any chance. But now... Lady Fino herself is in a bind, and she probably won't tear face over just a bit of outside city territory."
The woman seemed to understand something, "You mean, someone is moving against the Cross Society's sponsor?"
Banner was noncommittal and did not go into details, just smiling and said, "Who knows? We can't worry about the inner city affairs, just take care of Green Street for now."
"Oh."
The seductive woman didn't ask more; she thought of something else and then spoke softly, "But during the meeting the other time, I always felt that Young Master Martin's gaze on me was somewhat strange..."
Banner laughed, "Heh, a man, who could move after seeing you?"
The woman coquettishly glanced at him, "What if the Young Master really took a liking to me, what then?"
Banner displayed an unconcerned expression, "Then we'd just send you over."
"Pah~"
This statement made the sultry woman playfully start punching his chest while Banner laughed loudly, with his hands unapologetically roaming over the woman's graceful figure.
However, accidents often arrive unexpectedly.
Just as Banner was in a great mood, about to stretch a bit, rapid footsteps were heard outside the door.
Being a high-ranking professional, his perception was extremely sharp, and hearing the footsteps, his expression slightly changed.
Thud, thud, thud!
Soon as knocking sounded, Banner commanded in a deep voice, "Come in!"
As soon as the door opened, a captain with an anxious expression stood there, he spoke very quickly, "Boss, it's bad, there's been a big incident!"
This statement instantly wiped out the joyful atmosphere in the room.
Banner vaguely guessed something, his gaze suddenly turned cold, "What happened?"
"Just now... just now, the Reyes family's convoy was attacked by a mysterious group on Phoenix Tree Street in South City. The convoy was completely annihilated, and Young Master Martin... was killed!"
"What?!"
Hearing this, Banner's expression sharply changed, and he stood up swiftly.
In an instant, a high-ranking professional's terrifying oppression burst forth, making it hard for the few people in the room to breathe.
He asked, "Are you sure about the information?"
"Confirmed! A severely injured driver survived the scene, he said... in the attackers, there was one who could transform into a red giant."
"'Red Demon' Goron?"
Upon hearing this, Banner's eyes flickered rapidly, cursively muttered, "Damn it!"
He knew very well how much trouble Young Master Martin's death would bring to their Steam Party. Not only would the previously hard-earned cooperation be wasted, but the subsequent accountability would be the real trouble!
He immediately ordered, "Gather the men, head straight to take down the Cross Society's stronghold on Green Street! Notify the executives to assemble, prepare for a gang war!"
"Yes, Boss!"
The captain also knew the urgency of the situation and hurriedly took the orders and left.
.....
The sudden terrible news turned the few remaining faces in the room extremely ugly, with an atmosphere chillingly cold.
They had just been celebrating their Steam Faction's lucky bargain, only to now receive the news that Young Master Martin from the inner city had been murdered.
It was as though the sky had been punctured, leaving everyone stunned by the news.
Banner sat on the couch with a gloomy face, lost in his thoughts.
Mad Dog, sitting next to him, turned deathly pale. He had personally escorted Young Master Martin away not long ago, and now hearing the news of his death, he knew he couldn't disassociate himself from it.
Yet he didn't lose his reason in anger, raising his own doubts, "Boss, could it be that it wasn't Goron, but someone else who has awoken the 'Red Demon' talent impersonating him?"
It was clear to any observant person that the convoy deliberately left a survivor who recognized an ambush perpetrator with the 'Red Demon' talent, something seemed off.
"Boss, I always feel there's something fishy about this. It looks like a trap set intentionally to provoke a feud between our two factions..."
Mad Dog felt he had spotted the issue and analytically added, "After all, even if the Cross Faction feels aggrieved, so long as they aren't out of their minds, they wouldn't dare truly kill Young Master Martin. If we now attack Green Street and it turns out to be a misunderstanding..."
"Heh...you think I don't understand?"
Banner interrupted him with a cold laugh, saying, "Now whether the attacker was Goron or not, the Cross Faction will have to carry this blame!"
He sneered coldly again and added, "Plus, we in the Steam Faction won't have it easy either!"
You could tell that Banner was truly enraged to the extreme, "Now whether it was the Cross Faction who attacked the convoy or not, with the Young Master dead, someone must atone! Do you really think the big shots in the inner city will wait for us to slowly investigate the truth and find the murderer? If some people don't die today, nobody can settle this!"
"Ah...this..."
Upon hearing this, Mad Dog immediately realized the situation was even more serious than he had anticipated.
After unleashing his anger, Banner gradually calmed down from his rage.
He thought of something, his expression turning very ugly, almost as if he was mocking himself: "I thought those big shots in the inner city were targeting the Cross Faction. Now it seems, we've been played too..."
The identity of the murderer didn't matter at all!
The crucial thing was that their Steam Faction and the Cross Faction, the two major gangs, must clash and provide an explanation!
This fight would definitely lead to both sides suffering.
The person behind the scenes wanted to see just this situation!
At that moment, Banner suddenly thought of something, his eyes turning cold as he asked, "Mad Dog, besides you, who else knew the convoy route of the Lei Rey's family?"
Mad Dog's face instantly drained of color upon hearing this.
He realized at once that the boss asking this question meant he suspected there were also issues within the Steam Faction.
.....
After those arrogant guys from the Steam Faction left, the gangsters of the Cross Faction didn't leave Green Street.
Everyone knew that a major event was bound to occur within the next three days, and the gang members had also prepared for the inevitable clash.
Gang members from other districts also cancelled their breaks, each carrying guns and ammo, crowding and mixing in various bars.
And within the dilapidated building on Green Street, Kai led about forty or fifty of his men hunkering down in the building.
Fires burned in metal barrels, and the armory's firearms and ammo were distributed, mechanical arms, cannons, grenades, machine guns...it was entirely a war setup.
The veterans set up their rifles on tripods next to the bonfires, then gathered around to chat, joke, and play poker. A brawl was routine, no different from usual.
The newcomers, never having experienced such an ordeal, clutched their weapons, trembling.
The decrepit building was five stories high, standing on the top floor one could overlook much of Green Street.
Kai and Su Lun stood on the edge of the building, looking out at the brightly lit street.
A chill breeze filled their collars, slightly cool.
When Kai had left the bar, he was especially dejected. Now looking at the bustling street, he sighed, "If we lose Green Street this time, I really won't have the face to meet Old Smoke Ghost and the others."
This was his first time as a team leader, and Green Street was his first jurisdiction.
To lose it felt like having his wife snatched away.
Su Lun, seeing his expression, didn't have the heart to say outright that this matter was no longer something he, a mere team leader, could meddle in, nor something that the boss, Chak, could reverse.
He could only advise, "Team leader, I always feel like something big is going to happen. Be careful."
Hearing this, Kai grew even more irritated, "Hmph, if those guys from the Steam Faction really dare to come, I'll definitely kill them!"
"..."
Su Lun had anticipated a possible armed conflict, but he hadn't expected it to come so quickly and directly.
Kai was really a jinx.
No sooner had he spoken than suddenly a "bang" explosion sounded, igniting the entirety of Green Street.
Immediately, someone shouted a warning, "It's bad! The Steam Faction's people are attacking!"
Su Lun looked intently and saw that on the distant street, the Steam Faction's convoy was approaching massively, with transport trucks, motorcycles, armored vehicles, modified heavy trucks...even tanks. Scattered about, the total number appeared to be in the hundreds if not thousands!
Seeing this array, Kai also screamed, "Damn, how many people has the Steam Faction brought?"
Su Lun looked at the Steam Faction's convoy, his expression not too surprised. A fight was inevitable eventually...
If this had been before he merged with the Eight-Limbed Spear Armor, such a large-scale armed conflict would indeed be dangerous. But now...even if he couldn't overcome them, he still had a chance to protect himself.
Even looking at those well-modified combat vehicles, he silently mused, "Looks like I can harvest lots of mechanical knowledge again..."

chapters.title: Chapter 93 - 93: Sniped from 300 Meters
chapters.content:
The Steam Faction suddenly started the war, which was very unreasonable.
Logically, a three-day period had been given to clear the field, and the Steam Faction shouldn't have come to provoke on Green Street during this time.
Moreover, with the support of the third branch of the Rayes family, the Steam Faction just needed to wait a few more days, and the Cross Society would eventually leave Green Street due to the pressure from higher-ups. Even if there were conflicts, they would be minor skirmishes.
They could have taken Green Street without much cost, but now it looked as if they were intent on a gang warfare, which was incomprehensible.
Kai cursed as he looked at the number of enemies, "Have the Steam Faction gone mad? Do they want this to be a fight to the death between the two gangs?"
Su Lun, observing the sudden turn of events, had a strange thought cross his mind, and he murmured, "To act so recklessly… Could it be that the president of the Steam Faction has been assassinated, or perhaps… Young Master Martin has been killed?"
Apart from this reason, he couldn't understand what could drive the Steam Faction to such a desperate charge.
But whatever the reason for the Steam Faction's war declaration was, it didn't matter anymore; now that the enemy was at their doorstep, the Cross Society had to face them.
.....
The first shell exploded, destroying an armored vehicle of the Cross Society parked at the head of Green Street. The caravan charged into Green Street and the surrounding blocks like a flood of steel.
Fierce gunfire ensued, with shots fired and cannons booming on the streets.
The Steam Faction excelled in mechanical augmentation, granting them a massive technological advantage with cannons and armored vehicles.
Virtually each of their motorcycles was fitted with portable cannons and heavy machine guns, turning these hundreds of bikers into hundreds of moving artillery units.
The Cross Society was caught off guard by the scale of gang warfare and could not sustain a direct artillery fight for long; their men were soon forced into the alleyways between buildings, where urban combat began.
Initial estimates suggested that the Steam Faction outnumbered the Green Street Cross Society ten to one!
Furthermore, the majority of the Steam Faction members were augmented with mechanical limbs, which gave them an edge in large-scale firefights. A bullet hit was less likely to be fatal compared to a flesh-and-blood body.
Besides, while mechanical limbs might not be as agile as flesh, they offered substantial advantages in sustained shooting accuracy and steadiness among non-professionals.
....
Kai and Su Lun, along with their men, took position in front of a dilapidated building, which was conveniently located by a narrow alley.
This alley was too cramped for large war vehicles to enter, allowing them to set up defensive combat positions.
"Brothers, fight the bastards. Just hold on a bit longer; reinforcements from headquarters are on the way!"
"Wolff, take the rocket launcher and blow up the troop carrier on the street corner!"
"Damn it, we need someone who can bandage—get Batty's wound taken care of!"
"..."
The sound of gunfire was incessant, like rain, as Captain Kai shouted commands in a strained voice.
"Whoosh" "Whoosh" "Whoosh"... The whistling of bullets filled the air, and the oppressive threat of death weighed heavily on everyone's chest, making breathing labored.
Large-scale warfare wasn't the time for personal bravery; even Kai, who was very capable in close combat, had to stay behind cover and shoot. If he rushed out now, he'd instantly be riddled with bullets.
Gang members, after all, weren't the same as a regular army; although fierce in battle, they had many shortcomings.
For instance, they lacked medics.
Once injured, it was pretty much fatal for them.
The seasoned fighters still had experience; they shifted from cover to cover while returning fire effectively. However, the new recruits could make fatal mistakes due to nervousness and frequent slips...
A mistake meant death.
Before long, from the group of forty or fifty people, more than ten were out of action due to death or serious injuries. And because the resistance in the dilapidated building had been noted, more and more Steam Faction members gathered at the alley's entrance.
...
Su Lun took cover and occasionally fired his gun with cold precision.
His expression remained calm throughout.
After all, ordinary gunmen didn't pose much of a threat to him.
Even without peeking out to survey the area, Su Lun's capability to locate enemies by sound allowed him to easily determine where their shots were coming from. He could even dodge rocket attacks by predicting the trajectory and impact point from the sound of the rocket's ignition, avoiding fatal blasts with ease.
Su Lun's combat abilities had already surpassed most of the captains. With his marksmanship, he could easily suppress the twenty or thirty enemies at the mouth of the alley with little effort.
But he didn't do so.
Because that wouldn't solve the problem and would only bring real disaster upon the Green Street squad.
If the enemy realized there was a "gun expert" in the dilapidated building, an experienced captain would be sent to tackle this tough nut; and if Su Lun killed a captain, higher-ranking fighters would come...
Trouble would come in an unending stream.
Now that the enemy outnumbered them ten to one, no matter how formidable Su Lun was, it was impossible for him to kill them all.
The best choice was to continue whittling them down and wait for the reinforcements from the Cross Association to arrive. Only when someone could restrain the enemy's tier two professionals, could he let loose and counterattack.
What he needed to do now was to preserve himself, occasionally taking potshots to eliminate a few of the more threatening enemies.
....
The team members from Green Street Squad were pressed from the mouth of the alley to its end.
Just then, Kai suddenly realized the sniper atop the dilapidated building had stopped moving. Looking back, he discovered that their sniper had been headshot by the enemy at some point, his body half-dangling over the edge of the rooftop.
"Damn it, our sniper's been taken out!"
"Captain, it seems like some enemies have climbed up to the back of the dilapidated building!"
"..."
The Steampunk Gang enemies, pinned down at the entrance of the alley and not daring to rush forward, were actually largely deterred by the fact that the Cross Association had occupied the high ground early on, with the threat of the sniper.
Now, without the sniper in the high position, the Steampunk Gang pushed forward with their mechanical shields a significant distance outside the alley.
The situation grew increasingly dire, and Su Lun was still trying to figure out how long they could hold before they would absolutely have to withdraw.
But just then, he suddenly felt a sensation on his forehead akin to the pressure of a needle prick.
"Am I being targeted by a sniper?"
This was a premonition warning from "Malicious Perception," sensing the hostile gaze fixed upon himself.
The feeling was faint, indicating that the enemy was at a great distance.
But it was enough to put Su Lun on high alert.
Without any hesitation, he rolled away on instinct, and almost at the same time, a bullet struck the spot he'd just occupied, leaving a crater on the hard ground.
Su Lun looked at the bullet's trajectory and instantly determined the precise location of the sniper. Nearly rolling at the same time, he unhesitatingly drew the famed gun "Lightning Serpent," flung it forward, and pulled the trigger towards a small building's window 300 meters away in the 10 o'clock direction from the left front.
"Bang!"
A burst of special brilliance flashed from the muzzle like a serpent, the bullet fired, and then it accurately entered the window 300 meters away. The blood splattering suddenly on the windowpane showed that someone behind it had been hit.
Captain Kai, watching Su Lun suddenly roll and fire towards the flank of their position, instinctively followed the direction of the barrel.
He had just been wondering why Su Lun's pistol was angled so high, and when he saw the blood spatter on the windowpane, he realized why.
"A sniper?"
Kai looked at the expressionless Su Lun with eyes full of shock as if he had seen something unbelievable.
Su Lun was a "gun expert," Kai knew that.
He wasn't surprised that Su Lun could snipe the enemy sniper with one shot.
But using a pistol to accurately kill a target 300 meters away, wasn't that absurd?
Ignoring the marksmanship, who uses a pistol for sniping?
Kai, after all, was a professional, with far more experience than the average gang member. Glancing at the old, marked pistol in Su Lun's hand, he knew it couldn't be ordinary.
He had seen Su Lun not using the famed gun "Three-Headed Ghost" before and thought it was because Su Lun was wary of exposing himself, daring not to use it. Did Su Lun switch to something even better?
Kai didn't say much; now was not the time for idle chatter.
Without the high ground, they were at a disadvantage. Kai instantly thought of something, came over, and asked, "Brother Su Lun, can you lead a couple of brothers to take over the high ground of the dilapidated building?"
It was a very dangerous mission.
Snipers were targets that received special attention; once they fired and exposed their positions, the enemy's first choice would be to eliminate the sniper spot.
Kai and Su Lun had been through life and death together. If not for the need to hold his position, he would have chosen to go himself.
But Su Lun agreed without any hesitation, nodding, "I can."
It suited him just fine.
There were too many people at the position, too many watching eyes; it wasn't convenient to expose many of his tactics. Besides, because the position was a large target, it would definitely be the main focus of the enemy's attention. Even with his heightened perception, it was hard to avoid being accidentally hit by stray bullets.
Most importantly, if they couldn't hold on later, it would affect his "tactical retreat."
Su Lun thought it over and then added, "I'll go alone."

chapters.title: Chapter 94 - 94: One Man Overwhelms the Battlefield
chapters.content:
Su Lun didn't linger at the position in the alley, instead, he turned and made his way to a nearby dilapidated building.
Inside the building there was no light, only darkness.
Although he knew the enemy had already ascended the building, he guessed that there must be traps, cunning mines, or alarm devices scattered along the way.
After all, this decrepit building was a regular gathering place for the people of Green Street, and its layout was etched into their minds.
Therefore, Su Lun didn't choose to take the stairs but instead used the mechanical grappling gloves on his arms to shoot steel wires, clinging to the external obstacles and climbing up the outer wall until he reached the rooftop.
Not seeing anyone on the rooftop, he listened closely for a moment, then descended to the fourth floor.
Rappelling down to the fourth floor with the steel wire, he landed in a corner and observed two figures stealthily setting up a sniper rifle.
They were completely unaware that someone had silently approached them from behind.
Su Lun raised his gun and fired, "Biu~" "Biu~" two shots ended the lives of these two men.
He walked over and casually harvested the Soul Shards from their bodies.
'Gained 'Slaji Litt's memory shard*2''
'You have gained some 'basic mechanical knowledge''
'Firearms experience +6'
'Spiritual power +0.05'
'Gained 'Porter Haddad's memory shard*1''
'...'
The two wisps of mist provided Su Lun with some firearms experience, and that basic mechanical knowledge was exactly what he needed.
Indeed, working solo didn't interfere with his performance.
With two men killed, Su Lun gained a decent sniper rifle, two mechanical arms, and several items stored in two storage rings, which could be sold for about two or three hundred thousand in total.
Although he seldom used sniper rifles on a daily basis, his marksmanship was not bad.
Lifting the bodies, lying on a dust cover, Su Lun perched the enemy's sniper rifle on his shoulder and looked down at the battlefield below through the scope.
From this angle, he had a perfect view of Kai's position below.
Luckily, he arrived just in time. Had he delayed further, the people of Green Street, caught between two fires, would most likely have been annihilated.
In that instant, Su Lun aimed the scope towards the Steam Faction on the opposite side of the alley, targeting a man holding a portable rocket launcher.
"Bang," he shot the man in the head.
Then he pulled the bolt back, turned his aim to the man next to his fallen target who was casting a shocked look in the direction of the ruined building, and fired another shot straight through the man's chest.
With two shots, Su Lun killed two targets, and the enemy, realizing there was a sniper in the broken building, instantly dared not show their heads anymore.
.....
After firing two shots, Su Lun didn't look for other targets, but quickly packed up the sniper rifle and left his original position.
Just seconds after he departed, a flurry of gunfire swept over the spot where he had just been shooting.
Listening to the "tat-tat-tat" of the heavy gunfire, Su Lun knew it was the sound of the vehicle-mounted heavy machine gun on the armored car.
Armor-piercing bullets penetrated the concrete walls, turning the two bodies lying on the floor into a bloody mess. If he hadn't moved, that burst of bullets would have been directed at him.
Su Lun changed direction, hid behind a load-bearing column, and glanced at the battle below.
His eyes were utterly calm, and he didn't fire frequently.
He would occasionally take a shot only when he spotted a target that posed a significant threat to Kai and his team.
After killing another two people, a rocket flew over and blasted a big hole in the floor.
However, Su Lun had anticipated this and had already moved out of the way in advance.
