Kai muttered to himself, took out a suction cup to attach himself under the truck, and then installed one of Su Lun's modified magnetic alchemical bombs onto the pipeline.
After activating the detonator, he rolled out from under the truck as it frantically tried to speed away, but suddenly there was a loud "boom".
Although the vehicle wasn't flipped over, the alchemical bomb blew through the bottom blast shield right into the power conduit, completely immobilizing the truck.

chapters.title: Chapter 107 - 107: How do you know how to do everything?
chapters.content:
Su Lun looked at the sniper rifle that hadn't broken the glass and, to prevent any unexpected changes, put away the rifle and immediately charged down.
Although the truck had broken down, the cab had a bulletproof modification, and the people inside weren't foolish enough to open the door and come out.
Su Lun stopped Kai from wasting another alchemy bomb to blow up the front of the truck and used burst fire to penetrate the glass, killing two people.
Oh... there was a slight surprise.
The "barbarian" Buck, who surprisingly hadn't died in the previous explosion, burst out of the flames and swept over with a volley from the honeycomb gun on his right arm, nearly causing Kai to be injured.
However, after all, he was only a first-order professional and a mechanical gunman with limited ammunition. Su Lun and Kai, working together as professionals, quickly killed him on the spot.
Thus, all twelve members of the escort team in the three vehicles were killed.
....
Kai, looking at the steam faction's people who had been wiped out in front of him, wore a smile and said, "Heh heh, the entire vehicle is fitted with bulletproof plating. This cargo might be more valuable than we thought... And luckily, Brother Su Lun, you had prepared the alchemy bombs, otherwise they might have gotten away."
Su Lun felt that Kai was right—the truck was clearly a specially aged transport vehicle, which also proved that the goods they were transporting were very valuable.
He said, "Let's get moving quickly, they must have already sent out a distress signal. If we delay any longer, we might run into trouble."
"Mmm."
Kai nodded as well.
The reason the two had chosen this ambush spot was not only because it was secluded but also because they had considered the time it would take for steam faction reinforcements to arrive.
Now that they had dealt with the enemy so smoothly, they also had enough time to unload the cargo.
Su Lun didn't dare to be careless and walked up to the side of the carriage, then pressed his ear against it and listened carefully.
The carriage walls were thick, and he didn't hear any movement.
Meanwhile, Kai was fiddling with the lock on the carriage door, and quickly discovered that he was at a loss with the mechanical lock. He turned and asked for help, "Su Lun, this lock looks like a 'Cortes alloy lock'; it can't be opened without a key. Should we blow it open with an alchemy bullet?"
Su Lun shook his head and said, "An alchemy bomb costs six hundred thousand for a single one. Using a bomb to open a lock is way too extravagant. Also, what if there are good things inside and they get damaged by the blast?"
"That expensive?"
Kai immediately retracted his hand, feeling shaky at that price, even though he was a captain of the Cross Society.
In an instant, he looked at Su Lun with an expression of awe, exaggeratedly saying, "Brother, are you that rich?"
Su Lun didn't bother to explain much and gave him a glance, "The anti-tank mines weren't cheap either."
Robbery also required investment of resources because with their ordinary equipment alone, they could not possibly deal with the escort team.
Kai knew it wasn't the time for gossip and showed a resigned face, "So what do we do now?"
"Of course, we use another, more cost-effective method..."
Su Lun walked over, took out some materials, and started to draw a Hexagram Alchemy Array around the lock.
Kai, watching Su Lun draw the alchemy array, asked curiously, "What's this?"
He was purely a close-combat professional who, aside from the alchemy array that disarmed equipment, knew almost nothing about alchemy.
This was also a common issue among most professionals from the outer cities: capable in battle but nearly illiterate when it came to theoretical knowledge.
Su Lun skillfully finished drawing the alchemy array and explained offhand, "First-order alchemy 'melting technique,' a very practical auxiliary alchemy. The main materials for drawing the array are magnesium powder and a mix of mithril powder, which upon activation generate an extremely high temperature, capable of melting most known metals. It should be enough to deal with this lock."
Kai felt like he had learned a lot, but then asked again, "Aren't you a gunman? How do you know alchemy spells? Moreover, alchemy knowledge is very expensive and not easy to learn..."
"Got it from the black market."
Su Lun didn't elaborate much, the spell formula really came from the black market, but it was from the textbooks provided by Mr. Hei containing basic spells.
To the outsiders of the inner city, the expensive spell formulas were merely examples in the textbooks of the noble students.
It just so happened that Su Lun had stripped memory from two assistant teachers before and had some knowledge foundation, which made it easy for him to pick up.
As he spoke, he said to Kai, "Step back a bit."
No sooner had the words left his mouth than Su Lun formed a few sorcerer's seals with his hands and pressed one hand onto the formation. Immediately, the Hexagram Array lit up with a blinding white light. Even from a distance, a skin-pricking heat could be felt.
Then, a miraculous scene ensued.
Once the alchemy array was activated, the high temperature instantly melted the entire metal lock, causing the alloy to turn into a puddle of red liquid like magma, dripping onto the ground.
Kai, who was standing at a distance, watched in surprise and muttered, "How do I feel like you know everything..."
An gunman who could make alchemy bombs was understandable, but knowing alchemy too, that was strange.
Alchemy wasn't something you could just learn by drawing a Hexagram Array; it also required learning the spell formula, Quick Seal Formation, material combinations, a whole set of casting procedures...
Normally, even for a magician with great talent to learn a first-level spell, it would take at least a month or two of hard practice to become proficient.
Why would any gunman be so bored as to spend so much time learning a support spell?
Su Lun didn't offer him further explanation, "Captain, get ready to work!"
....
With the locks destroyed, the door to the truck's carriage was easily opened.
Kai no longer pondered why Su Lun knew alchemy and instead looked forward with anticipation to see what valuable cargo was inside.
But just then, Su Lun's ears twitched; he heard something stirring inside the carriage and his face suddenly changed, "Quick, get out of the way!"
Kai hadn't figured out what was happening yet, but hearing Su Lun's urgent warning, he didn't hesitate and leaped back.
In that instant, a huge dark shadow darted out of the carriage. It leaped out and with a powerful punch hit the ground where Kai had been standing a moment earlier, blasting a half-meter deep crater into the ground.
Kai let out an exclamation, "Damn, what the hell is that!"
Su Lun also stiffened his gaze upon seeing the monster that had just appeared.
[Abomination Warrior]
Detailed description: A first-and-a-half-order mutant monster created by Serum X, which had lost its sanity but could still execute simple slaughter commands through special conditioned reflex training; the potion enhancement gave it superhuman strength, high-speed movement, high recovery, high strength, high physical resistance, and medium magic resistance...
This was a nearly three meters tall, blue-skinned humanoid monster with an ugly visage.
"Conditioned reflexes? It must have been the incorrect way of opening the carriage that activated this monster..."
Looking at the identification information above the monster's head, Su Lun immediately made a guess.
It turned out that there was not only a full transport squad of the Steam Faction but also a guarded monster.
Just what was inside this carriage that warranted such cautious measures?
Blue skin, it kind of reminds me of a zombie...
As thoughts flickered through his mind, Su Lun's movements did not slow down at all. He immediately raised his hand and fired two shots at the monster in rapid succession.
"Bang!"
"Pop!"
The alchemical bullet fired in a rapid succession passed through the monster's occiput, but it penetrated only shallowly.
And more eerily, the bullet head was slowly being squeezed out by the muscles, the wound visibly wriggling and healing itself!
"Such high resilience!"
Su Lun was surprised to see that his two combined shots failed to injure the monster, which was not the usual outcome when he shot ordinary professionals—each shot would leave a gaping wound, but this creature only had a bullet hole the size of a pinky finger.
What was more terrifying was the monster's self-healing ability, which was so exaggerated it was hard to believe.
Meanwhile, Kai's reaction wasn't slow either.
After dodging a punch from the monster, he rushed forward with his arm transformed into a blade, and sliced down at the monster's unprotected thigh.
With the blade's cold light flashing, a normal body of flesh and bone would have been severed by this strike.
Yet when Kai made his move, his expression drastically changed, as if his blade had struck a tree bark, almost getting stuck in the monster's flesh.
Upon closer inspection, the cut had barely left a mark, causing no significant damage whatsoever.
Moreover, in the blink of an eye, the scratch had already healed as if it was never there.
Because of the momentary snag of his blade, Kai was about to dodge when a fist as big as a casserole pot smashed into his abdomen, hitting his ribs with the force of a charging rhino despite his attempt to evade.
With a "pfft," he couldn't help but spit out a mouthful of blood, his body flying out like a bullet.
In this encounter, Kai had fallen into peril.
....
Seeing the monster about to pursue Kai, Su Lun fired several shots from a distance, aiming to draw the monster's attention.
Watching various alchemical bullets explode at key points on the monster's body, Su Lun confirmed one thing—the monster had extremely high physical defense, but not particularly strong magic defense!
But the armor-piercing bullets from the double-shot had difficulty penetrating, and although ammunition like the "magic-breaker bullet" could inflict some damage, they couldn't cause much harm if they didn't penetrate the skin.
His successive shots successfully attracted the monster's attention. The over three-meter-tall body might have seemed bulky and clumsy, but it moved with incredible speed!
The monster turned its head and surged forward, the ground cracking beneath it, and charged like a cannonball towards him.
"So fast! This monster's speed has reached that of a second-order professional!"
Su Lun felt the overwhelming pressure bearing down on him but was well-prepared.
His muscles tensed to the extreme, and with a pull on the steel wire, he used the monster's passing momentum to spin several times in the air before landing.
Although it looked somewhat clumsy, Su Lun's mind was coldly analyzing many useful pieces of information: "Very fast in a straight line, but its ability to change directions seems inferior... strictly physical attacks, no equipment, doesn't cast spells, low intelligence..."
This was a monster whose certain attributes surpassed those of a second-order professional, yet it also had clear weaknesses.
He instantly judged that they could fight it!
....
Kai, seeing Su Lun knocked away, suppressed the discomfort in his chest and charged back into the fray like lightning.
He felt that as a melee assassin, although he could not overpower it, he could take a few hits without dying temporarily.
But Su Lun, a gunman with a frail body, was another matter. If the monster got close, one punch could be lethal.
In a rush, Kai said, "This guy's strength has already reached that of a second-order professional, we're no match. Get ready to retreat!"
Su Lun seemed to ignore him completely, with no intention of fleeing, his guns still firing continuously.
He was well aware that without alternating cover, Kai wouldn't last long either, and he urgently said, "You can't outrun it, don't run, dodge with tactics!"
If they chose to flee outright, the monster's terrifying speed would catch up to either one of them in an instant.
Once it caught them, a single mistake would result in instant death on the spot.
This was the tricky part of dealing with this monster; you couldn't kill it in fight, outlast it in attrition, or escape it in flight.
....
The monster was ferocious, its punches and kicks strong enough to split metal and break stones.
Kai moved with agility, maneuvering around the explosion-proof truck, now diving under it, now circling to the back, barely managing to protect himself.
But no matter how he attacked, it was like scratching an itch for the monster.
If the stalemate continued, the situation would eventually go awry.
Not to mention being killed by the monster, the mere fact that they were being held up was enough for the Steam Faction's reinforcements to arrive.
"Damn it! How could there be such a monster inside the carriage!"
Kai cursed angrily, seeing the cargo right before his eyes, yet they were forced to abandon it.
He also understood Su Lun's battle strategy—it seemed they were trying to kite the monster, alternating in drawing its attention to look for an opportunity to retreat—and he shouted urgently, "Su Lun, I'll hold it off, you snipe from a distance, we might still have a chance..."
He wanted to persuade Su Lun to retreat and gain enough distance for sniping, which would give them both a chance to escape.
But Su Lun's plan was clearly not to run away.
He vaguely guessed what was in the shipment and decided to take the risk.
"Stall it for a moment for me. Get ready to fight back!"
"???"
Kai paused in thought.
Before the words had settled, he caught sight from the corner of his eye that Su Lun had already stowed away his guns and was rapidly forming hand seals, with a pentagram array already lighting up under his feet.
"Such quick hand seal speed!"
Kai was astonished but could not understand what Su Lun was planning to do.
Was he going to unleash his equipment and fight it out?
But... you couldn't kill this monster!
In that instant, while the doubt had yet to show on his face, Kai's gaze suddenly froze.
The familiar feeling he had known in battle returned...
....
With an emotionless face, Su Lun completed the hand seals and uttered softly, "Equip... Disengage!"
As the pentagram array fully lit up, his eight-armed spider spear, glowing with dark golden light, loomed ominously.
PS. This Friday, or perhaps September 1, the shelf is coming. I hope everyone will come to support the subscription on QiDian then; otherwise, the pre-order numbers make me feel like kneeling. Thanks in advance.

chapters.title: Chapter 108 - 108: You Call Yourself a Shooter?
chapters.content:
What is Su Lun doing, unlocking his alchemy equipment now?
To facilitate his escape?
Kai's mind hadn't caught up with the situation a second ago, but in the next, his expression became very odd.
At this moment, he no longer found Su Lun's actions strange, rather his gaze was drawn to the sinister dark gold octo-spear, and it was his eyes that held a peculiar gleam.
What the hell is this thing?
Seeing this bizarre piece of alchemy gear was even more shocking to him than witnessing a monster suddenly burst out from the carriage.
If not for the pentagram that lit up on the ground, would you believe me if I said this was alchemy gear?
An alchemy suit shaped like a spider might not be unique in the outer city, but it would be something rare even within the inner city.
In a flash, Kai seemed to realize that he had never seen Su Lun's alchemy equipment before.
He had asked about it in the past, even thinking about helping to get a set suited for a marksman. But Su Lun had said he had already prepared a "decent" set, so Kai didn't question further.
But... is this it?
You call this kind of equipment "decent"?
Also, is this really the kind of gear a respectable marksman would have?
What's up with those eight spear legs? Do more feet mean faster running? But you'd also need to be able to control them!
Although Kai didn't understand what Su Lun was planning to do, seeing that familiar deadpan face filled him with an inexplicable trust.
That familiar feeling on the battlefield returned; if this guy said he could counterattack, then he was definitely capable of it.
.....
After unlocking his alchemy equipment, Su Lun was not done yet!
He understood well that mere physical damage would hardly penetrate the "Abomination Warrior's" skin. Even if the spear was incredibly sharp, its penetration depth was not enough to cause significant injury to the creature.
Upon unlocking his gear, Su Lun didn't stop; his hands swiftly changed the sorcerer's seals once again.
The alchemy formation lit up once more, his gaze growing sharper by the second. Finally, with the last sorcerer's seal in place, a soft chant escaped his lips, "Alchemy Arcanum: No Servant!"
In that instant, his entire body was covered with a layer of faint blue chilling flame. The eight spears were now enveloped in cold fire, turning into something resembling eight flaming spears, bizarre and fierce.
With the emergence of this chilly enchantment, Kai, who was watching from a distance, was no longer just surprised; he was utterly astonished.
The rank of an alchemy spell often correlates with the grandiosity of its casting. The chill flame that radiated a cold presence did not look like any ordinary spell; this was surely no commonplace alchemy!
However, the more advanced the alchemy spell, the longer it took to learn. And crucially, the knowledge of such high-ranked alchemy was not something you could simply buy if you wanted to.
Kai was already incredulous when Su Lun performed the "Melting Technique" earlier, and now here was another incomprehensible flame shield spell.
So this is you, who normally calls yourself a marksman?
....
Now was not the time to hesitate. Once the reinforcements from the Steam Faction arrived, they would have to face not just one monster, but something more complicated.
With his equipment unlocked, Su Lun wasted no time, raising his guns and firing simultaneously, immediately drawing the attention of the creature towards himself.
The monster charged fiercely, and Su Lun's eight spidery limbs all moved in unison. His body supported by all eight legs, dodged in a bizarre angle.
And in the moment of passing by, Su Lun's fingers grasped at the air, as several strands of wire pulled out a lead-grey trick puppet. As the strings were pulled, the puppet latched magnetically onto the right calf of the monster.
Almost simultaneously, Su Lun exclaimed, "Release!"
The runes on the doll lit up instantly, and in a flash, the monster's movement became as though its feet were filled with lead. Its legs, unbalanced in strength, stumbled and tripped over itself and fell.
This was none other than the intermediate trick puppet "Lead Sink Doll," inscribed with the earth elemental "Mountain Rune." As soon as the doll's feet touched the ground, it attracted earth elements continuously, growing heavier and heavier, until reaching the doll's threshold. What was originally a light wooden doll could now exert a pull of over a thousand kilograms.
The monster fell heavily to the ground, and Su Lun knew this was not enough to cause any real harm to it.
Almost at the same time, the eight spider legs pulled, and two more trick puppets, one black and one red, jangled towards the front with the creak of wooden joints.
When they got close to the Abomination Warrior, the black-faced doll's jaw split open, and from its mouth, a black tube appeared, spraying a stream of oil-like black liquid onto the creature; simultaneously, the red-faced doll beside it burst into flames, expelling a ten-meter long blaze resembling phosphorous flames.
Oil meeting fire burst into an inferno, engulfing the creature in a burst of flames like a flamethrower.
These two dolls were also among the latest trick puppets Su Lun had mastered, the "Oil Swallower Doll" and the "Phosphorus Fire Doll!"
The red-faced doll had an alchemy formation inscribed within. The flame it spat was actually a first-tier alchemy spell—"Inextinguishable Phosphorus Fire";
The black-faced one was not spewing ordinary oil, but a specially formulated combustible—"Refined Phosphorus Oil."
The fuel is extremely viscous, and once it adheres, it is impossible to shake off;
Phosphorous fire reacts even more vigorously with water, hardly extinguishable unless it burns out.
What use is strong defense and recovery?
A magician skilled in alchemy might have other means to extinguish the flames.
But a pure physical attacker, especially a dim-witted "Abomination Warrior," would suffer greatly from such burning.
....
The monster seemed impervious to pain, its back ablaze with roaring flames, apparently oblivious.
It rose to its feet, smashed the "Lead Sink Doll" clinging to its leg with a slap, and turned its head toward Su Lun.
But this time, the monster made a shaking motion with its head, as if to fling off the phosphorous fire that blocked its vision.
It was the shake of its head, delaying for a second, that it charged wildly toward Su Lun.
Su Lun caught the subtle shaking motion of the monster and immediately concluded, "Just as I thought! The monster also relies on vision to perceive its target, and the burning flames are greatly limiting its senses!"
The Abomination Warrior charged ferociously, dribbling flowing phosphorous fire as it ran.
A gust of wind, carrying a scorching heatwave, whisked past him, and this time, Su Lun likewise avoided the creature's charge with a clever use of his spider spear for support.
Moreover, this time it was much easier than before.
The monster's perception was limited, and its reaction was considerably slower.
For Su Lun, this reduced the crisis in an instant by too much.
Just watching the monster burn could have been an option, and although it was highly unlikely to kill it, it could at least maim it.
The subsequent kill would be much easier then.
But Su Lun knew he could not wait any longer.
This monster had an extraordinary vitality; if he did not make it quick, reinforcements from the Steam Faction might arrive.
Therefore, he had to strike on his own initiative.
And in the moment he brushed past the flaming monster, the creature collided with the wire, pulling it and consequently sending Su Lun flying backward with a "whoosh."
However, that was exactly what he wanted!
Su Lun's body flew backward, like the inertia thrust of a thrown javelin, providing him with an extra acceleration.
At that moment, he had already stood the eight spider spears vertically in front of him, and with a "click," "click," "click," the sharp black spikes at the tips of the spears were launched with a sharp sound.
Having missed the target, the monster realized something was amiss and came to a sudden stop.
In an instant, Su Lun was catapulted out by a huge inertia, the eight spider spears encased in ghostly cold flames, unfazed by the phosphorous fire on the monster's body, stabbing straight toward its various vital spots.
Four spider spears each targeted the back of the monster's head, its upper back, and both sides of its waist.
Maybe it finally felt pain, as the creature's movements visibly faltered.
Su Lun didn't relent, pulling on the steel wire, securing himself in mid-air. The joints of the spider spears were flexible; they could not only stab directly but also attack laterally. With a "zss" "zss," two slicing sounds of flesh being pierced emerged, and two spears stabbed into the monster's ear holes.
The spider spears even had better piercing effectiveness than alchemy bullets, with six spikes penetrating half a foot deep into flesh.
The eight-armed spider spear, permanently imbued with the "Sharp Rune," was not just sharp—it also carried the toxicity inherent to the cursed material!
"Corrosive Poison" granted the spider spear a remarkable armor-breaking effect; after penetrating, it instantly released "Blood-Poison" that slowed down the healing of the wounds.
The No Servant cold flames already carried dual physical and magical damage. The combination of two toxins allowed the spider spear to penetrate deeper, inflicting tremendous damage on the creature in an instant.
Su Lun was like a giant mosquito, with eight spider legs like proboscises, firmly adhered to the monster's back.
With many legs for support, he could comfortably dodge the monster's flailing arms, repeatedly driving the spider spear in and out, continuously creating new wounds on the creature. In a matter of moments, the monster's body was like a punctured water bag, with streams of blue blood jetting out one after another.
"Auu~"
The desolate wilderness echoed with the monster's furious roar.
The creature instinctively sensed the danger and tried to throw Su Lun off its back.
After several unsuccessful attempts, it accelerated suddenly and charged violently at the bulletproof transport vehicle.
With a heavy "thud," the immense force of the impact shifted the hefty vehicle sideways by several meters.
Su Lun, quick as a flash, tugged on the steel cable, springing off from the monster's body to separate himself before being squashed.

chapters.title: Chapter 109 - 109: Unexpected Cargo
chapters.content:
About ten meters away, eight spider limbs steadily landed, dissipating the force.
Su Lun shook his head, which was a bit dizzy from the tossing, and as he looked at the fiery monster before him, his furrowed brows finally relaxed somewhat.
Because he discovered the monster's defense was broken!
Previously, the damage from the fire gun was repaired so quickly that before a second attack could land, the initial wound had already healed itself.
But now, the phosphorus burning combined with the dozens of punctures from the spider limbs had inflicted tons of damage. The healing of the wounds was visibly strained, indicating that the monster's self-healing ability had reached its limit.
Although it was still healing, as long as the damage exceeded the healing rate, the monster would grow increasingly weaker.
Moreover, self-healing wasn't without a cost.
In the field of alchemy, energy is conserved.
Even though this monster had a terrifying self-healing ability, it still required the consumption of biological energy.
The more wounds it had, the greater the energy consumption, which would make it progressively weaker.
Because of this weakness, the monster's strength, perception, and reaction ability would all decline.
Thus, the pressure on Su Lun in the battle would decrease.
Besides, this abomination had one major flaw, which was "low intelligence"!
Reality only afforded him a brief moment to catch his breath. As soon as Su Lun landed, he saw the monster charging at him again.
Yet he remained calm and repeated the old trick, pulling on the "Oil-Swallowing Doll" and the "Phosphorus Doll" once again, covering the nearly extinguished flames on the monster with a fresh layer of phosphorus, reigniting them vigorously...
With no wisdom but only the instinct for slaughter, this was just like fighting a boss in a game, where one could pull aggro and choose a fixed pattern of attack.
After setting it ablaze again, Su Lun seized another opportunity, leaped onto the monster's back, and unleashed a flurry of stabs with his spider spear...
The blue blood sprayed more fiercely. The monster grew weaker, its movements slower and less threatening.
....
Kai, watching the battle from not far away, was at a loss for words.
He had thought about rushing in to help; even if he couldn't damage the monster, he could at least distract it, sharing some of the pressure with Su Lun.
But before he could act, he realized the scenario was unfolding in a direction far beyond his expectations...
It was one thing to know alchemy...
It was another to have spider limb implants...
And the spectral flames could also be overlooked...
But now, what the hell were these incomprehensible runic puppets?
He had thought those spider legs were just for running away, but it turns out...
My eyes tell me you're also a Puppet Master?
However, in the end, Su Lun had the upper hand, causing Kai, also aglow, to feel exhilarated: "What quality is this spider limb implant, and how he controls it so fluidly..."
A creature with the close-combat capabilities of a second-tier professional, whose defense and recovery were monstrous, was actually being suppressed by Su Lun?
Alchemy bullets couldn't penetrate the monster's defense, but the spider spear could... by now, he had no doubt that the implant's alchemical quality was terrifyingly high.
It definitely wasn't iron!
In fact, Kai felt even a silver implant couldn't be this strong!
Being a professional himself, he knew all about the prerequisites for merging with an implant.
That Su Lun could merge with a high-quality alchemical implant meant his spiritual power value at appointment must have far exceeded his peers.
Plus, to manage such fluid control over those eight spider limbs wasn't something an ordinary person could achieve.
"So he wasn't joking on the battlefield before; he was serious."
With this thought, Kai muttered darkly, "Damn, if it hadn't been for encountering this monster today, I'd never have known just how formidable this guy really is!"
Always covering for Su Lun as the team leader, turns out the joke was on me.
But seeing the scales of victory now tipping towards Su Lun, the tense fists of the spectating Kai gradually relaxed.
....
The battle had been destined to end this way from the moment Su Lun found the abomination's weakness.
Before long,
The fiery monster, weakened by continuous damage and the piercing thrust of the spider spear, let out a reluctant scream before collapsing thunderously to the ground.
Su Lun looked at the body and finally exhaled a long breath of stale air.
The whole battle process seemed to be just a repetition of a few routines: tripping, spraying oil to burn, and then poking...
But in reality, he was dancing on the blade's edge every moment, teetering between life and death.
The monster's strength didn't allow him any mistakes.
You could hit the monster a hundred times, and it wouldn't feel a thing, but one mistake, and the monster could seize the opportunity to kill you instantly.
It was his constant state of calm that reduced the probability of mistakes to the lowest.
However, with high risk came great learning from combat.
This was the first time he had used all his methods to kill a formidable enemy.
Though he had trained many times in the basement before, it was not real combat.
Fighting this "Abomination Warrior" gave him a lot of insights.
He also realized that the Puppeteer profession was very strong, not only because of the various miraculous effects of the puppets but also due to the operability of the profession.
If different puppets with various utilities were well-utilized, the combat effectiveness could nearly double, producing the effect of an entire team single-handedly!
This battle gradually made Su Lun understand the future planning of his profession.
Tank, damage output, healing, control, support... all these capabilities could completely be substituted by puppets with various functions.
He didn't need to team up with others; he was a team by himself!
....
Su Lun put away the equipment and slowly regulated his breathing.
At that moment, Kai quickly walked over, examining Su Lun as if he were a monster, and excitedly asked, "Brother, when did you become so powerful? What's with that equipment, what spell is that cold flame, and those puppets..."
Su Lun felt there was nothing good to hide but it wasn't the time to explain, he shook his head smilingly and said, "Now is not the time to discuss this, let's move the stuff, we don't have much time."
Kai pursed his lips, then suppressed his curiosity, "Right."
The two did not delay further and quickly walked to the back of the truck.
They looked at the cargo compartment filled with densely packed alloy boxes, their eyes filled with anticipation.
"Haha... Let's see, the goods guarded by this monster, what kind of treasures they will be!"
As Kai spoke, he casually opened a mechanical box.
Instantly, a blast of cold air hit them.
The two men stared for a moment because inside the box was a set of high-tech, brand-new armor.
"This..."
Kai looked at the armor and then back at Su Lun.
Wasn't it supposed to be second-hand mechanical equipment? This didn't seem right...
Gently touching it, his palm felt a chilly sensation of frost.
Helmet, armor, mechanical gloves, Frost Cannon, power boiler... each component was adorned with high-grade runes and enchanted coatings.
Kai, born in the slums, where had he ever seen such things?
Looking at the armor, he was delighted yet puzzled.
The loot was too high-end, making him feel it was somewhat unreal. It felt like he was just here to snatch a few scrap metals, but what he got were shiny gold bars instead.
He turned to look at Su Lun, his voice trembling slightly, unsure, "Brother Su Lun, what kind of armor is this? Is it... refurbished?"
Su Lun narrowed his eyes slightly, indeed recognizing the origin of this armor.
His expression thoughtful, he slowly said, "The latest mechanical equipment of the Inner City Guard—Frost Giant Combat Armor."
"..."
Upon hearing this, Kai's mind went blank.
Looking again, the compartment still had dozens of large and small mechanical boxes, still unknown what treasures were inside.
The two immediately realized, this batch of goods...was nothing like the information they had received!
This seemed like a big score.
PS. Some have doubted, so let me explain a bit more. Don't think this kind of low-profile escort group is unreliable, and the plot forced. The more valuable the items, the more low-key and safer the delivery is. If interested, you can search for '1931 Gold Theft Case'. There are countless similar real-life cases.
Many very valuable things are often transported in the simplest and most unpretentious way, and the process of loss is also very coincidental. Moreover, this plot also involves a hidden plot, in the Outer City, Black Tower is not without rivals.

chapters.title: Chapter 110 - 110 X Serum
chapters.content:
When Su Lun saw that one of the casually opened mechanical boxes contained a brand-new set of "Frost Giant" mech armor, he immediately realized that this batch of goods was not some "used mechanical equipment" that the Steam Party had bought for the inner city.
This kind of top-tech mech armor, not even fully issued to the elite forces of the inner city's City Guard, was impossible to have been sold to an outer city gang.
Without looking at the other boxes, Su Lun knew that the cargo in this truck far exceeded expectations and was of immeasurable value.
Not long ago, he had heard through the high-level professional circles in the black market that someone was seeking this type of armor, with a price tag exceeding fifteen million risos.
What was most critical was that the configuration of this escort team gave Su Lun a very strange feeling.
Would an ordinary transport squad be escorting something so valuable?
But after giving it a slight thought, it seemed quite reasonable.
The Steam Party's escort team had always been very active.
Who would have thought that a bakery, which sold bread every day, would occasionally mix in a package of powder that wasn't flour?
In the outer city, second-tier professionals were big shots, usually too dignified to rob a batch of "used mechanical equipment."
But in reality, the escort team led by the 'Barbarian' Bak was nothing but bait to divert attention. They might not even know what they were actually transporting.
Special armored vehicles and abomination warriors were the real security for this cargo.
Normal robbers trying to hijack this transport wouldn't be able to stop the special bomb-proof truck, and even if they did, upon opening the cargo hold and facing the "abomination warriors," it would be nearly impossible for an ordinary first-tier professional squad to survive.
Even if there were second-tier professional criminals, without the means to subdue the monsters, they could easily get trapped and killed, or get delayed until the Steam Party's reinforcements arrived.
Even if they managed to escape, they certainly wouldn't be able to take the goods with them.
Thinking this way, such a low-profile escort method wasn't far-fetched at all; in fact, it was quite ingenious.
Moreover, once Su Lun fully understood what the cargo was, he understood even better why the owner had chosen such a low-key method of transport.
....
Kai looked at the "Frost Giant" armor and suddenly felt at a loss.
In his life, he had never seen anything so fine.
He looked at Su Lun and asked, "What do we do now?"
"What else can we do? We've already stolen it, so of course, we'll take it away," Su Lun said with an unconcerned smile, and then added, "We'll just clean up the scene a bit."
They had killed the people and the monsters; at this point, even if they backed out, the cargo's real owner would definitely investigate thoroughly.
Upon hearing this, Kai's eyes lit up with delight: "Haha, that's exactly what I was thinking!"
With the boldness born from gang life, he had been thinking the same thing, but he worried that his greed would bring fatal trouble to the gang, and to Su Lun.
After all, the greater the value, the more the owner would pay to find the culprits. Many a robber had fallen on such ventures.
Now that he heard Su Lun echo his thoughts, he felt relieved.
You can't get rich without windfalls!
Scared of what!
The two started happily unpacking various boxes and packing everything up.
.....
The storage ring is a rudimentary use of the laws of space in alchemy. Because it's a subpar space, it can't be made too large—the larger it is, the easier it collapses, and the costs increase geometrically. A normal storage ring has about an eighth of a cubic meter of storage space; a larger one could have half a cubic meter.
Even Su Lun only got his hands on a storage ring of about one cubic meter after killing Jack, a noble student in the dungeon. It was barely enough to hold a puppet, but completely inadequate for these sizable mechanical pieces of equipment.
They had no choice but to take all the mechanical equipment out of the boxes. Any parts that could be disassembled or folded were crammed into storage rings. The large items that couldn't be disassembled were grouped together.
Those from the inner city used an iron box over two meters long to transport this "Frost Giant" mech armor, but the actual space occupied by the items inside was less than a third of the box. They probably wanted to avoid any scratches or damages to the enchanted plating, for aesthetic reasons or something...
But Su Lun and his fellow robbers naturally didn't have such concerns.
The two treated the mechanical arms and legs like firewood, brutally bundling them together, and wrapping them with canvas they had brought, so they could be easily transported on motorcycles later.
Their actions were quick, and it didn't take long to unpack most of the boxes.
Five suits of armor, ten handheld cannons, a number of light/heavy external mechanical skeleton parts, fifty rune pistols, twenty mechanical rifles, fifteen boxes of alchemy bullets, and various ordinary ammunition grenades...
Inside the truck, besides the shockingly valuable armor and ammunition supplies, there were all sorts of functional items like chemical protection suits, gas masks, instruments, and accessories.
Su Lun began to suspect that no one in the outer city could make use of such sophisticated equipment.
When he saw the batch of laboratory equipment, a strange thought immediately popped into his head, "Could it be that these supplies were being sent from the inner city to a secret experimental base in the outer city?"
These high-quality biohazard suits would be useless to the outer city dwellers and would typically only be found in laboratories.
And as if to confirm his suspicion, an unexpected incident occurred just then.
"Crack," a sound like a glass bottle shattering crisply echoed through the carriage.
Su Lun turned around and saw Kai looking innocently back at him.
Kai hadn't figured out what had happened, pointing to the fragments of the storage ring and the box on the ground, he said truthfully, "I... I saw that the box contained potions, so I put them into the storage ring. I didn't expect the storage ring to shatter..."
Kai had never encountered such a situation and didn't understand what it meant.
But Su Lun thought of something, and his expression briefly froze.
The storage ring shattered?
He immediately opened that box and then appraised it.
Sure enough, inside were things that operated on a higher plane of the Space Law than the inferior space of a storage ring.
There were neatly arranged five potions!
[X Serum Essence]
Detailed explanation: An active substance extracted from the bodies of super-cognitive "abyssal creatures," injecting and gaining substantial enhancement of bodily attributes, increasing the threshold of rank, remodeling bloodlines;
Effects: The subject will gain significant boosts over the following months post-injection. Dark spiritual power endurance limit increased by 230%-570%, strength by 270-350%, toughness by 220-325%, cell vitality by 880-1100%, maximum cell division count by 50%...
Results fluctuate due to uncontrollable mutation factors; after blood remodeling, inheritance of that abyssal bloodline is obtained, along with related growth traits, with each advancement in rank, an extra 3-10% increase in all attributes;
Side effects: The effects of this serum are extremely violent, and human injection who do not possess a bloodline higher than that of the abyssal creatures results in a 100% mutation; after mutation, attributes undergo non-directional mutation and gain substantial attribute enhancements; it will cause your skin to turn blue for a very long period of time;
...
"X Serum?!"
Su Lun's gaze became fixed as he instantly became deep in thought.
He never imagined that he would find five vials of the legendary "X Serum" in this batch of goods.
When he had seen that "Abomination Warrior" earlier, he had guessed that the big shots from the inner city had not given up on the research of that project.
But upon seeing this batch of potions, he realized that the experiment was actually so close, even located in the West City district!
He also knew that his guess was indeed correct, this batch of goods was really a supply meant for a secret laboratory the inner city had set up in the outer city.
"Things are getting a bit complicated, huh..."
Su Lun murmured to himself.
However, since the goods were in hand, any troubles were a future concern.
What he was more interested in was the value of the potion.
After all, those statistics appraised were just too eye-catching.
"Even a tenfold increase in cell vitality wouldn't reach such an exaggerated recovery ability. That Abomination Warrior must have undergone some mutation in its body after mutation..."
"Cell vitality and division count are attributes directly linked to lifespan; no wonder the big shots from the inner city are obsessed..."
"It also grants partial inheritance of the bloodline traits... If it doesn't cause mutation, it's practically a divine potion!"
"..."
Just speaking of the body's enhancement, this "X Serum" was ridiculously beyond human.
Dark spiritual power, strength, toughness, cell vitality... it was like an all-dimensional doubling of attributes.
It was even a significant leap beyond the attribute enhancements from a first rank advancement!
The feeling was that a single injection would immediately grant one a superhuman physique.
But that 100% mutation rate was just too glaring.
Su Lun looked at the information appraised from the potion, and a myriad of thoughts flashed through his mind in an instant.
Suddenly, he had a flash of inspiration.
X Serum + Mutation Inhibitor Potion = Undead, ah!
That "Research Diary on the Undead" had detailed methods for creating undead, and now it seemed all the hardware conditions were met?
Previously, without any clue about the whereabouts of the "X Serum," Su Lun had not paid much attention to the contents of the diary.
But now that he had several real potions in his hand, his thoughts immediately became agile.
Now that he had "X Serum," although the mutation inhibition formula was still in the research phase for the Black Tower, it wasn't much of a problem for Su Lun.
Because the diary contained a detailed formula!
Su Lun had always speculated that the undead could wield that forbidden weapon, the Black Scythe... If he could truly create undead, it might well add a powerful trump card to his hand!
Moreover, if the "X Potion" could be used on the undead, could it also be used on humans?
If the mutations in the living could also be suppressed, wouldn't he soar to great heights instantly?
Thinking of this, Su Lun felt that he should go back and take a good look at that "Research Diary on the Undead"...

chapters.title: Chapter 111 - 111 [PX-911 Mechanical Limbs]
chapters.content:
Su Lun's thoughts drifted for a moment before returning to reality.
Kai was still muttering on the side, seeming quite puzzled, "Strange, could it be that my storage ring is too old and has collapsed?"
If Su Lun didn't have the All-knowing Eye, he probably would be just as baffled right now.
But now he could guess that the storage ring might have collapsed because the potion's origin was identified as an unrecognized "****" creature.
Inferior spaces cannot store items that are too high on a magical or law-based level.
That "****" might represent some sort of indescribable high-entity creature.
Su Lun even speculated that the real main cargo the shipper wanted to transport was these potions, with everything else just as additional items.
These potions couldn't be placed in the storage space and could only be transported by a transport team.
The cargo must not be exposed, and even less the destination, the Steam Faction, a local snake in the west city, was the best partner for this!
....
Su Lun rummaged through the other boxes and found more.
Besides these five doses of [X Serum Original Liquid], another large box nearby contained a hundred doses of [Second Generation X Serum], which are also 100% likely to cause mutations but with only one-tenth the effect.
There was also a note left in the box, which read: "From Doctor Victor personally."
Su Lun glanced at the content, which basically said that someone called "Number 19" had still not been caught, the items had not been retrieved, there was not much original serum left in stock, and asked the doctor to use it carefully.
For some reason, upon seeing this "Number 19," the image of that woman with a bounty of three million immediately came to Su Lun's mind.
She was involved with the "X Serum Project," had escaped from the inner city lab, and hadn't been caught yet, almost perfectly fitting the condition written on the note.
It seemed that the item she stole from the lab was the key to making the serum?
However, clearly now wasn't the time to ponder this issue.
Su Lun felt that this robbery was becoming more unpredictable than expected.
If not handled well, it would definitely lead to big trouble.
And these potions were too special.
They couldn't be put into the storage ring; they had to be carried on his back.
Su Lun was also worried that there might be some tracking markers left on the boxes. Thinking it over, he took all the potions out, and after spraying them with [Scent Neutralizing Potion] and [Interference Powder], he finally put the more than a hundred potions into the potion bags he had prepared in advance.
Kai, watching him be so cautious, asked, "Su Lun, do you recognize this potion? Do you really need to be this careful..."
Without going into detail, Su Lun replied, "I have a rough idea of what this potion is. It might attract a lot of trouble; it's better to be cautious."
But Kai didn't seem very interested in the potion and just casually asked, "Do you also understand potions?"
Su Lun: "Somewhat..."
"..."
Kai rolled his eyes, as if he had gotten used to this guy knowing everything.
He didn't ask any more and continued to search through other items.
...
While Su Lun was still tinkering with that batch of potions, Kai opened the last few boxes and found something, exclaiming softly, "Su Lun, come take a look, what is this!"
Glancing over, Su Lun saw that in the last box, there was unexpectedly a set of incomprehensible machinery.
Kai took out a section of a shining metal arm and examined it, uncertain, "Is this... a mechanical skeleton? No, it seems like a mechanical limb?"
Su Lun was also quite surprised.
In this world, there was only a Physical Control system, so the core of controlling all machinery was actually humans.
Whether it's a mechanical skeleton or any sort of armor, its essence is a mechanical shell for humans to wear.
But this set of machinery marked with [PX-911 Mechanical Limb] was very strange.
It wasn't an external addition but appeared to be an actual mechanical limb, with arms, legs, and an energy conversion boiler for the chest cavity. Yet it was missing some connecting parts. To fully assemble a robot, it still lacked some linkage devices, and a head...?
Su Lun's knowledge of machinery was already not bad; even if he didn't understand the principle, he knew the probable origins.
But looking at this set of mechanical limbs, he was completely baffled.
How does one operate these?
Not being external, could they be meant to directly replace human bones?
But how could nerves directly control machinery? Was this some kind of specialized alchemical augmentation machinery part?
In an instant, numerous questions popped into Su Lun's mind.
And at that moment, Kai, holding the mechanical arm, inadvertently triggered some mechanism. With a "click," a sharp blade suddenly sprung out from the palm of the hand.
Kai jumped in shock, his grip loosening, and the arm fell down.
Then, the sharp blade easily cut a smooth gash into the edge of the metal box that contained it.
Kai looked on in disbelief, "This... this dagger is so sharp?"
Su Lun squinted at the dagger for a moment, and the identification revealed the metal it was made from was "Armand Metal," a type of extremely rare natural metal described in the Black Tower Academy textbooks as used by people in ancient times to forge Divine Artifacts, known for its superlative hardness and magical conductivity...
Seeing this, his interest intensified, and he picked up another mechanical arm to observe.
The arm felt smooth to the touch, yet there were no visible seams where the dagger could have been inserted.
"Eh..."
At this sight, Su Lun let out a soft exclamation.
It wasn't just the sharpness, but the precision and seamless integration of this set of mechanical arms that truly astonished him.
This was authentic "laboratory-level" technology!
Let alone the outer city, even the military enterprises in the inner city probably couldn't produce this level of precise manufacturing right now.
Just this section of mechanical limb alone was several tiers above in technological content compared to the "Frost Giant Combat Armor" they had seen before!
Upon encountering a mechanical structure he didn't understand, a desire surged within Su Lun to disassemble it and comprehend its construction and principles.
But now was clearly not the time for detailed examination, and he said to Kai, "Let's pack everything up, we don't have much time. I'll cover our tracks."
"Okay."
Kai didn't dare delay either, and the two of them packed up all the items.
....
Kai rode over on the hidden motorcycles, then stuffed the "worn canvas bags" full on both bikes.
Now that Su Lun knew the goods were not the "second-hand mechanical equipment" he had originally envisioned, he had to be even more cautious.
He had thought they were robbing a Steam Gang, but now it seemed they had hit an inner city secret laboratory's supplies!
Su Lun meticulously erased any traces they had left at the scene, including those from their two-day ambush. He then set up incendiary bombs near the truck...
After everything was done, the two of them mounted their motorcycles and sought a small path to leave the heist site.
Not long after they left, the truck exploded into flames, and any evidence was submerged in fire.
As they were carrying heavy items, the two did not ride quickly.
Kai was still reveling in the immense surprise of their haul; as they rode, he asked, "Hey, brother Su Lun, how much do you reckon we can sell this loot for? A hundred million at least, right?"
"More than that."
Su Lun shook his head.
Five sets of "Frost Giant Combat Armor" alone were worth 75 million, not to mention the other high-grade firearms, ammunition, and research equipment.
Especially the "X Serum" and the "PX-911 Artificial Mechanical Limbs"—those two items were the real priceless treasures.
Hearing this, Kai's smile grew even brighter. He had come from the slums and had never seen so much money before: "Heh, this time we sell it, and we'll be rich overnight for sure! I know a few reliable black market dealers, with goods this good, we're sure to get a great price..."
It wasn't that Kai was careless, but he was unaware of the true value of this haul and what it entailed.
If these were ordinary "second-hand mechanical equipment," once sold, it wouldn't matter who the owner was—there would be plenty willing to buy in the black market.
But he didn't know among the items was the inner city's top-secret "X Potion."
Selling this batch carelessly would definitely cause problems.
Su Lun solemnly negated his idea, saying, "No. We can't let these items enter the market any time soon, or we will run into serious trouble."
He felt that if he were the owner of the stolen goods, the first thing he would do is go to places that deal in stolen merchandise.
The black markets of the outer city would certainly be under close watch.
Mr. Hei had told him that the black markets had spies from umbrella organizations, and if they really went to sell the goods, they might end up 'delivering themselves to the doorstep.'
Kai, not understanding, asked, "Why not?"
Su Lun did not go into detail but simply said, "There are some very sensitive items in this batch that absolutely can't be sold through ordinary channels."
After a pause, he added, "Nobody can know about us robbing the Steam Gang's transport team. If it leaks out, it will be huge trouble for anyone involved."
"Okay."
Kai frowned; although he did not understand the origins of the combat armor and mechanical limbs, he had realized the gravity of the situation.
While he didn't comprehend what those items were about, he chose to trust Su Lun's words.
With enough trust between the two of them, he didn't ask further, simply querying, "So, what do we do with this batch? Hide it for now?"
"Yeah."
That was exactly what Su Lun had in mind, and he supplemented, "I have a safe channel for selling the goods, but I need to observe the situation for a while. We can't necessarily move the goods right away."
Ordinary merchants definitely wouldn't do, but he could trust Mr. Hei.
That defector being pursued by the umbrella organization surely had no connection with the owner of these goods.
The only concern for Su Lun was how to sell the batch in portions without arousing suspicion that they were the ones who had intercepted it.
After hearing Su Lun's explanation, Kai nodded in agreement: "Okay."

chapters.title: Chapter 112 - 112: Laboratory Explosion (Subscribe Please)
chapters.content:
Su Lun and Kai, following the planned route, rode their motorcycle for a while and then switched to a different bike and continued on.
The fact that they had not been chased up to this point also meant that they had handled the cleanup work very cleanly.
The first phase of the robbery seemed to go off without any slip-ups.
However, as they rode, Kai felt that the motorcycle's steering was somewhat unstable and muttered, "Hmm... Su Lun, why do I feel like the motorcycle is a bit wobbly today? Could it be that the load is too heavy, and it's damaged..."
Su Lun had in fact noticed the abnormality earlier, and his expression changed instantly as Kai was still speaking, "Get off the bike quick!"
He didn't explain any further and immediately pulled out a foldable bulletproof panel, and the two of them used it for cover.
The next moment, a mushroom cloud thousands of meters tall rose from the direction of the desolate park, several kilometers behind them!
It was as if something underground was trying to break through, violently churning and making it hard to stand.
Seconds later, it was as if thunder exploded next to their ears, deafening them.
Boom~
The shockwave came crashing down like an avalanche, the air pressure making it momentarily hard to breathe. A tremendous force pounded against the bulletproof panel, almost blowing them away.
Luckily, because they were a sufficient distance away, although they were a bit dusty and dirtied, they were not injured after the shockwave passed.
Dusting himself off, Kai looked towards the direction of the explosion, his expression incredulous, and he complained, "It couldn't be the incendiary bombs we threw that detonated some underground methane deposit, could it?"
Apart from that, there seemed to be no better explanation.
"Probably not. The distance is too far off..."
Su Lun stared at the rising mushroom cloud and responded.
Suddenly, he realized something.
The convoy they had just hit was headed to a secret laboratory...
And the explosion was exactly in that direction...
Could it be...
that the secret lab had exploded?
....
The explosion was very sudden.
The outskirts of the city were vast, but it was usually only around buildings that people gathered.
This "desolate park" in the west of the city seemed to be a park from ancient times, desolate and rarely visited.
Now thinking about it, wasn't this the perfect site for a secret laboratory?
Although it was unclear whether the explosion was intentional or an accident, Su Lun's first reaction was, "Could it have been bombed?"
Moreover, due to the explosion, a series of clues in his mind instantly connected, and an aloof face emerged before him—the S-rank female fugitive with a three-million bounty!
"Could it really be that woman?"
The thought flashed through Su Lun's mind, but the more he thought about it, the more likely it seemed to be her.
Previously, when he went to Knight Street to rescue Danny's three friends, he had encountered that woman.
At the time, Su Lun had not understood why she would brazenly cause trouble by going after a human trafficker.
Now, having intercepted this shipment, he knew that the Steam Faction was sending supplies to a laboratory studying the "X Serum," located somewhere in the west of the city.
He immediately deduced the reason the Steam Faction's guys were capturing the homeless and orphans.
Because he had once heard from Danny that the higher-ups at Black Tower had conducted many live experiments due to the "X Serum Project."
The research was still ongoing, so it made sense that they needed a large number of people for experiments.
Such a live experiment lab could not possibly be set up within the inner city, so the outskirts, where human life was as cheap as dirt, were more than appropriate.
And that woman going after the human trafficker was most likely trying to use the lead on human traffic to pinpoint the lab's location!
So, was it really her who caused the explosion?
....
"That woman stole some important items for extracting the 'X Potion.' If it's really her who blew up the lab in the outskirts now, the top brass at Black Tower would probably be furious..."
Suddenly, Su Lun took more interest in that woman.
People with convictions, it really would be a pity if they died.
While Su Lun guessed the reason behind the explosion, he had no interest in staying around, since it wasn't his house that had blown up.
He signaled to Kai, "Let's go, there will probably be a lot of people coming to gawk soon."
A relaxed smile also appeared on Kai's face, "Heh, this explosion really did us a big favor, the traces of the robbery at the scene are probably mostly destroyed now."
"Indeed."
Su Lun also raised an eyebrow, feeling they were quite lucky.
The two of them righted the motorcycle that had been blown over and began heading out again.
Since the explosion was man-made and it coincided exactly with the day of their robbery, it likely wasn't a coincidence.
That kind of secret lab, in the interest of secrecy, couldn't possibly have people coming and going like a marketplace; it was very likely that today was some sort of centralized supply day.
It was possible that not only the shipment Su Lun and his team intercepted was involved, but other supply convoys might have been targeted too, including those for experimental subjects.
That woman probably infiltrated by some other means.
However, all of it had nothing to do with them.
They were just ordinary petty thieves.
....
Su Lun and his companion did not bring the goods back to their residence on Green Street; instead, they found some dilapidated buildings and secluded spots in the sewers to hide the items in batches.
After setting up some warning mechanisms, the two burned their crime-related clothes and disposed of all possible traces that could be traced back to them, before finally returning to Green Street.
The news of the explosion in the western district quickly spread throughout the outer city, and even the high-ranking members of the cross society sent people to find out what had happened.
But the common gang members heard it was a methane explosion, it seemed that the Steam Faction had also deliberately controlled the information, with no word about "laboratory" leaking out.
As for the "robbery" Su Lun and his companion were involved in, it was unknown whether the Steam Faction was planning to investigate secretly or just chalk it up to the explosion. At least for the time being, there were no reports of anyone looking for the goods or the robbers.
But the calmer it was, the bigger the matter seemed.
Because Su Lun discovered... in the black market, the bounty for that S-tier fugitive had increased again.
This time there was no price listed, the notice read: those who provide valid information may, depending on the value of the information, obtain lifelong residency in the inner city, hereditary nobility, and any hex materials currently recorded by the Alchemy Guild...
Clearly, the bounty issuer was "desperate."
The unprecedented reward was enough to tempt almost anyone.
Lifelong residency in the inner city is a benefit countless people in the outer city would vie for desperately;
Hereditary nobility, even the grand families of the inner city probably couldn't resist; and
The reward of any hex material would tempt even second and third-tier professionals indifferent to fame and fortune.
And this was merely the reward for providing information!
Moreover, this Bounty Order not only posted her original photo but also various disguised ones, along with detailed data on height, bone structure, dimensions...
The pink-haired bunny girl outfit Su Lun had once seen was also distinctly included.
In other words, even if she covered her head, any determined person could recognize her by her figure!
Su Lun felt that, with such a reward, the "walking vault" would find it hard not to be caught.
Thinking of the next high-tier professional meeting in the black market, he planned to inquire about the goods and see if Mr. Hei might be interested.
Meanwhile, Su Lun had another important task at hand.
That was to decode the "Necromancy Research Diary"!
....
Previously, Su Lun hadn't paid much attention to the "Necromancy Research Diary" because he thought the research was pointless.
At least for the time being, it was of no use.
Translating the ancient ciphers would waste a lot of his time and energy, and the content was too advanced to be of immediate use.
Most importantly, without the "X Serum," a key component, it was impossible to successfully research zombies.
But now, things were different; Su Lun had the finished X Serum in his possession.
If he could successfully translate the journal and discover the medication that suppressed mutations,
He could not only attempt to create "zombies," but it seemed that using the serum on himself might be a great idea as well.
Since the robbery, Su Lun hadn't been running around; instead, he stayed in the basement, starting his study of the ciphers in the "Necromancy Diary."
The majority of the texts left by ancient Alchemists were encrypted.
The higher the content's level, the higher the degree of encryption.
Solo deciphering an ancient cipher one had never seen before was almost impossible.
However, modern studies in cryptography also have a shortcut—that is, "Cryptology" is now an established discipline in the black tower academy.
A myriad of cryptology experts and archaeologists study daily, deciphering the patterns in a vast number of ancient ciphers, compiling various cryptological methodologies into textbooks.
This has consequently made it easier for modern people to decode ancient Alchemy scrolls.
To the majority of ordinary people, who are dazzled by the cryptic methods, there are available formulas that can be applied directly.
Knowing the type of encryption and the key, many ciphers can be almost idiot-proof to decipher.
And Su Lun had the most complete set of "Complete Collection of Ancient Cipher Decoding" textbooks in Old Lington at his disposal.
The textbooks recorded almost all the cipher encryption and decryption methods available on the market.
This greatly reduced the time and difficulty in deciphering.
Moreover, Su Lun had a shortcut within a shortcut, namely the "All-knowing Eye."
Before he had read the "Complete Collection of Ancient Cipher Decoding," upon encountering ciphers with specific patterns, the All-knowing Eye might suggest "This is a text with a 'three-grid horizontal-vertical shift encryption pattern'...";
After reading it, it now directly identifies it as "a cipher compiled by the R'lyeh encryption method..."
This was a pattern he gradually noticed after using the "All-knowing Eye" for so long: the information identified by the eye would appear in the most understandable form in accordance with his level of knowledge.
The more Su Lun knew, the easier the content identified would be to understand.
Now, using it for deciphering, when Su Lun read the content of the diary, it would directly indicate the specific name of the encryption method.
Then he only needed to look up the relevant content of the cipher in the textbook, directly apply the formula, and he could decipher it.
This saved him a lot of time.

chapters.title: Chapter 113 - 113: Deciphering the Diary (Please Subscribe)
chapters.content:
By employing this crafty method, Su Lun spent several days holed up in the basement, burying himself in decrypting the diary's contents.
The diary contained much encrypted information, so he selectively studied the part about researching the aberration-suppressing potion.
Oh, it wasn't just ciphers, but also language.
It was fortunate that he had mastered the ancient written language of Gunnthra, commonly used by magicians during his previous soul-stripping, otherwise mastering this ancient language alone would have probably taken years.
However, even so, the decryption was still quite challenging.
The diary included many obscure medical terms from ancient times.
The worst part was that some ancient terms fundamentally meant something different in modern times.
Relying on "The Complete Book of Codes" and the convenience of the All-knowing Eye, Su Lun stumbled through several days of translation and actually managed to decode most of it!
He had now confirmed that part contained the complete method for concocting the "aberration-suppressing potion."
But the remaining twenty to thirty percent either couldn't be translated or the translations were inaccurate.
He handed the part requiring profound professional medical knowledge to Danny, who lived half a block away.
For the parts that truly could not be translated, he planned to seek consultation from Mr. Hei, the knowledgeable scholar.
Just then, the newly delivered edition of the Lyndon Daily News mentioned a gathering of the underground market circle.
.....
That day.
After being cooped up for several days, Su Lun finally emerged from the basement.
There were no unfamiliar eyes on the streets paying him any attention, which was a good sign.
It meant their robbery two days ago had been clean; so far, no one had traced it back to Green Street.
He rode his motorcycle to the black market in Shadow Alley.
Dressed in a cloak, he arrived five minutes before the agreed time in a secret space at the lower level of the black market.
The attendees were quite punctual; in the few minutes after his arrival, over a dozen people showed up.
There were more people than last time, and by the time Mr. Hei arrived last, over twenty individuals were standing beside the stone table.
The familiar process then began, starting with the intelligence exchange segment.
As expected, someone immediately asked about the explosion in the western city's deserted park.
"Does anyone know what exactly happened with the explosion at the western city's wasteland park two days ago? I heard even the supervisors from the Steam Party aren't allowed near the explosion site, and many mysterious people from the inner city arrived, seeming to be from the Umbrella Organization," someone said.
"I received some intelligence that there was a secret laboratory there. For some unknown reason, it suddenly exploded," another added.
"Heh, a lab in the outer city, wouldn't that suggest they were involved in some highly hazardous research?" another chimed in.
"..."
Everyone capable of reaching the second tier wasn't a fool, especially in the outer city; these cloaked individuals were all big shots with wide-reaching intelligence networks.
Upon hearing it was a laboratory that had exploded, they instantly deduced a lot of information.
Listening silently, Su Lun heard these tycoons exchanging words, and their conjectures almost completely matched his own.
"I had received news quite some time ago about those guys from the Steam Party secretly capturing wandering populations. Yet there's been no talk of anyone in the inner or outer city getting their hands on these people. It looks like the disappeared population and that exploded lab are highly related..."
"Living experiments? Those damned people at Black Tower really don't regard our outer city lives at all," another said.
"I'm not very clear on other details, but I am sure the one who triggered the explosion is the individual currently on top of the wanted list. Incidentally, I'd like to ask if any of you have any clues about her—ah, that bounty is quite tempting," another stated.
"I do have some intelligence, but it got traded for the bounty already. Someone saw her recently at the Black Baron Club in the western city. She killed the people trafficker, Dam, in the Knight district, then set the club on fire. Now that I think about it, she was probably trying to track down the whereabouts of the people..."
"Yo? I wondered why the Black Baron Club suddenly caught fire, it was her doing! Hahaha, why do I feel a bit thrilled about hearing about that explosion now..."
"I happen to have the latest intelligence; there was a major battle last night in the northern city. The individuals from the Umbrella Organization somehow found her and after a fierce fight, they gravely injured her," another contributed.
"So, she was captured?"
"No."
"She managed to escape?"
"..."
As the topic progressed to this, the informant seemed to hesitate for a moment before adding, "I heard that a third-party force got involved and broke through the Umbrella Organization's encirclement, then she took advantage of the chaos to escape."
"..."
Listening to this, Su Lun realized he had inadvertently shared the blame for the rescue.
However, when the informer mentioned the "third-party force," everyone present was taken aback.
Su Lun also thought, who else in Old Lington would dare to oppose the "Umbrella Organization"?
Then it dawned on him, wasn't he one of them?
Su Lun noticed that when the topic reached this point, no one continued further, as if everyone were cautious.
Mr. Hei was his usual composed self and didn't speak.
The subsequent exchange of information wasn't particularly noteworthy. Su Lun contributed some of his guesses to the information as well, participating in the process.
Then came the item trading segment.
The most discussed topic in this segment was still the information on the "Dawn City" relics.
Recently, many ancient relics had been excavated one after another and sent back to Old Lington. In the black market, these big shots had acquired many high-grade cursed objects and materials for trading.
After a lively round of exchanges,
Su Lun also saw many rare and strange items.
During this time, he found opportunities to inquire again about the "Secret Technique of Spiritual Power" and "the Wailing Witch's Cursed Hair." No one responded.
It was as expected.
However, toward the end of the session, a cloaked figure raised a buying request that caught his attention.
"I need a set of 'Frost Giant Battle Armor,' and it must be a complete set available immediately. I'm leaving the city in three days, and I'm willing to pay twenty million for it, or an equivalent cursed material..."
Upon hearing these words, Su Lun kept silent.
He and Kai did indeed have five sets of completed armor from the batch they had intercepted earlier.
But such items were special; once sold, their origins could only be traced to a few places.
He felt that this person was likely fishing for information.
Moreover, the buyer had made a clever request,
asking urgently, offering above market rate, and setting a time limit.
Anyone with channels who wanted to sell would definitely try to make a deal, as opportunities do not wait. Moreover, such goods were sensitive, and it was not easy to find a buyer daring enough to make the purchase.
Su Lun remained silent, and the scene grew quiet for a moment.
At this point, someone else spoke up, "I can get it, but I'm not sure about the timing. And... it might not be a complete set."
From the tone of voice, it sounded like the person from last time who had the channels to obtain the armor.
Hearing this, the buyer wrote a note, replying, "This is my contact information. But I will only wait three days. If you can get it in time, the price can be negotiated."
....
The trading session ended, and the small gathering was nearing its conclusion.
Su Lun sought out Mr. Hei, who was about to leave, and stated his business, "Mr. Hei, I've encountered some difficulties with ancient knowledge and need to consult you."
He didn't know if Mr. Hei could see through the concealed cloak, but clearly, he recognized him.
Mr. Hei seemed quite interested in ancient knowledge, "Oh? Let's hear it."
Su Lun took out the notes he had copied from the diary with sentences he didn't understand
With that question, this Scholar indeed knew.
He translated a few sentences offhand.
"This sentence is an ancient metaphor often used by Magicians, 'wheat falls to the ground and dies' refers to mercury dying in nitrate and sulphuric acid. The flowing 'living mercury' turns solid and dies, a play on words. It's usually used in the context of some material refinement process..."
"'The belly of the fire dragon stores mithril, take four parts from the fire dragon and nine parts from the magnet' is a highly sophisticated Alchemy process, the corresponding materials are..."
"Hmm... this sentence is quite difficult. It's a piece of specialized terminology from ancient medicine, using a dual encryption method... I might need some time to refer to some materials to ensure it's correct."
"..."
Su Lun listened as he translated those enigmatic codes he had been unable to decipher, his expression unchanged, yet he felt a continuous sense of amazement.
Mr. Hei truly was profoundly knowledgeable, seemingly aware of everything.
Thinking of his talents, Su Lun felt that, scholarship plus mind-reading, what a perfect match.
It seemed as if, without making a move, those wise eyes could see through everything about an adversary.
As it involved many ancient medical terms, Mr. Hei couldn't translate some content accurately on the spot, but he didn't refuse the small favor, "Give me the note, and I should be able to decipher it by tomorrow at the latest. I'll leave the note in the usual place..."
Su Lun nodded as he listened, asking, "Mr. Hei, what would I need to give in return?"
Mr. Hei, unconcerned, said, "These precious pieces of ancient knowledge are the best payment you have already made."
Pausing, he smiled and said, "Translating ancient scrolls is one of my favorite tasks. If you have more similar knowledge in the future, feel free to come to me, I would be glad to help."
Always the gentleman.
Even though he had guessed that Su Lun certainly had more ancient scrolls, he hinted it in the least offensive way possible.
"Thank you for your generosity..."
Su Lun sincerely expressed his gratitude.
He was not in a hurry to unload the goods he had on hand, planning to wait until this brief period of attention passed before asking.

chapters.title: Chapter 114 - 114: Creating the Living Dead (Subscribe Requested)
chapters.content:
Half a month later.
The basement on Green Street.
Su Lun was tinkering with a new battle puppet. He tried using steel wires to make it move, but its slashing and dodging movements were clumsier than those of a wooden puppet.
This life-sized puppet was not made of wood but was assembled from disassembled parts of the "PX-911 Mechanical Limbs."
Su Lun also knew that it wasn't that the mechanical limbs weren't sensitive enough, but that he wasn't activating them correctly.
Over this period of study, he had figured out many functions of these mechanical limbs.
The outer casing of the limbs was made of a special alloy that no alchemy bullet double shot could dent. Hidden inside were various weapons: knives, guns, energy cannons, retractable metal ropes, ejectors...
Once disassembled, it was simply a concentration of weapons containing top-tier technology.
There was also a mechanical heart with a blood-pumping function and mechanical lungs for oxygen supply...
Moreover, these weren't even the most stunning aspects.
During his experiments, Su Lun discovered that the part of these mechanical limbs he couldn't comprehend was the high-sensitivity mechanical tactile components that could be triggered by bioelectricity.
This was a very cutting-edge, laboratory-grade technology, so advanced that it far surpassed steampunk, making Su Lun even think that the technological tree of this world had reached the Cyber "Neuromechanics" level.
With these high-sensitivity tactile components, it meant that, in theory, they could be directly controlled by connecting to human nerves!
