Su Lun also thought that this limb might be what Danny mentioned, another top-secret project—a collaboration between the Black Tower medical research and mechanical divisions—the Super Mechanical Warrior Program.
Otherwise, it wouldn't be such a coincidence to find it on a transport vehicle headed to the laboratory.
After realizing this, Su Lun also restored in his mind the complete structure of this mechanical limb. Those missing parts might still be a complete human nervous system or some other driving tissue of alchemical implants.
In this world, there wasn't any intelligent control system; hence, they could install a human brain directly, creating a semi-mechanical human.
Just cover it with a layer of synthetic skin, and they would look no different from humans!
This was more thorough than the "new school" alchemists of the outer city, who still limited themselves to modifying mechanical limbs, while the top laboratories of the inner city had already developed almost entirely mechanical warriors.
Su Lun guessed that the woman with a bounty on her might be such a mechanical warrior.
....
But the mechanical limbs involved too much cutting-edge, laboratory-level technology, impossible for one person to fully research.
Su Lun had no intention of selling this device, nor did he plan to sever his own head to connect it.
So, in his hands, it could only be disassembled into parts.
He disassembled the indestructible dagger from the mechanical limb's arm and mounted it on his puppet; the spring blade from the mechanical leg was also disassembled and given to another puppet. Then, those high-precision parts of the boiler were useless, so he disassembled the alloy outer plate to make a bulletproof puppet.
As for those mechanical viscera, they gave him many inspirations for his "Iron Man Mark III"...
Su Lun was bustling joyfully as he tinkered with the mechanical puppet.
But suddenly, his ears twitched slightly, and an unusual noise caught his attention.
Su Lun stopped his work and sharply turned his head to look.
He became more certain; on the dissection table in the corner of the basement, cordoned off by a clear curtain, a breathing sound suddenly emerged!
"Eh..."
Listening to the faint noises, he was not shocked but rather delighted, "It worked!"
Su Lun didn't pay attention to the puppet in his hand and hurried over.
At that moment, he saw the corpse on the dissection table with its chest slightly heaving, and his eyes brightened.
....
Half a month ago, Su Lun went to the black market and found Mr. Hei to translate those profound ciphers, and then successfully deciphered the formula for the "Mutation Suppression Potion" devised by a crazed magician from a thousand years ago who had concocted a living corpse.
It was also thanks to Danny, whose original job at "Laboratory 7" was to research mutation suppression. Although the ancient formula was very complex, with some incomprehensible steps, since many of the theoretical aspects were interconnected, he combined his own knowledge in concocting and had successfully produced the first batch of "Mutation Suppressant" the day before!
The outer city wasn't short of corpses, and Su Lun also found a fresh corpse to experiment with straight away. After injecting it with the prescribed dose of the "Second Generation X Serum," the corpse began to slowly display signs of life. However, the effect of the second generation serum was much less potent than the original, and it was already the third injection.
If there were still no effects, he might plan on administering a fourth.
Unexpectedly, the corpse suddenly began to breathe!
It looked just like a sleeping living being, but according to the diary, this was merely a soulless husk. Even the living traits were not the corpse's own, but entirely a result of the active agents in the "X Serum" altering the body, forcibly reviving the tissues. In some sense, this corpse was no longer a human body.
Just moments after it began breathing, Su Lun noticed dark red spots starting to appear on the corpse, and the overall skin color was also gradually turning blue; he thought to himself, "The skin is turning blue, spots are emerging, the mutation is indeed beginning..."
The journal had detailed records of this mutation process, and Su Lun was not at all surprised.
He didn't delay, and he took out a Mutation Suppressant injection and administered it to the corpse.
A moment later, the spread of the mutation marks slowed down.
Su Lun didn't idle and took out a rune pen, then began drawing basic runes on the now-breathing corpse.
"Corpse Vitality Rune," "Level I Dark Attribute Mana Gathering Rune," "Wind Element Circulation Condensation Rune," "Level I Life Rune"...
The materials had been prepared in advance, and he had practiced the runes very proficiently in the previous days.
There was no need for him to research them himself, he simply painted them sequentially as recorded in the diary.
These were all low-level runes, so the difficulty of drawing them was not great.
The diary described that Chekhov used this set of low-level runes to create what he considered a "useless" active corpse.
Su Lun knew he definitely couldn't create those terrifying blue-skinned monsters from the cursed space with these low-level runes, and didn't intend to try.
What he needed was not the ultimate research of "resurrecting a corpse," but merely a "living corpse" that could maintain normal life characteristics!
....
Three hours later.
Suri had finished painting various yellow, black, white, and red alternating runes on the corpse.
The runes on the entire body collected the four basic elements of "Earth Wind Water Fire," and then interconnected in a cycle, endlessly.
"The ancient magician who created this rune combination truly had great talent..."
Su Lun set down the rune pen and looked at his work, sighing.
He could proficiently master these low-level runes, yet he didn't understand the principles behind them. Only a small amount of materials was needed to keep these runes continuously operating, involving a very profound mastery of rune crafting.
Adding more runes later on would also be convenient.
Having completed the rune drawing, Su Lun also let out a breath of relief.
Everything that needed to be done was done, he began to inspect the mutated state of the corpse.
"The X serum has altered the tissue structure of the corpse, significantly enhancing muscle strength. However, while the mutation suppression potion is effective, it also inhibits some of the effects of the serum..."
Su Lun was already very satisfied with this result.
All signs indicated that his first creation of a living corpse was about to succeed!
He wasn't aiming to create some kind of "abominable warrior"; the strength of the corpse was irrelevant, as long as it could withstand the backlash from the dark scythe.
Soon, the corpse's skin turned completely blue.
"Success!"
Su Lun felt a surge of joy.
This also meant that the serum transformed corpse had stabilized. Although there were some enhancements still to be made to the living corpse, it already completely qualified as a successful "rune living corpse".
...
The creation of the living corpse was only the first step; importantly, Su Lun intended to use it to verify his conjecture.
He used steel wires to pull and get the corpse to stand upright.
The living corpse stood there like a sleepwalker, eyes closed, expression dull, standing where it was. Neither alive nor dead, it appeared slightly eerie in the dark basement.
"Muscle strength is sufficient to support the body and the joints are also normal; it completely meets the requirements..."
Su Lun checked the state of the living corpse.
He had already determined that using that dark scythe required at least two conditions to be met: life signs and dark spiritual power infusion!
Moreover, the curse's backlash was likely directly related to these two conditions.
The "living corpse" just so happened to meet both!
After transformation by the X serum, dark spiritual power surged within the corpse, even higher than that of ordinary professionals, slightly spilling out.
This was also perfect, as it saved Su Lun the trouble of finding another way to activate the corpse to release dark spiritual power.
Su Lun fixed the dark scythe in the hands of the living corpse.
In that moment, the black fire emanating from the scythe seemed to be stimulated by the dark spiritual power, and immediately began to blaze intensely.
Seeing this, Su Lun vaguely felt that his hypothesis could indeed be correct.
Taking a deep breath, he tried pulling the corpse's arm gently with the steel wire, and it seemed he heard a tearing sound. Not far from the blade's tip, a small spatial rift eerily appeared.
"As expected, a spatial rift appeared!"
Seeing this, anticipation overflowed on Su Lun's face.
This time, his body had not used any dark spiritual power infusion, yet it had succeeded.
He could roughly confirm that his conjecture was correct!
After this one cut, he did not continue the motion.
He lowered the puppet and began the long wait for the backlash process.
....
An hour later.
Su Lun did not feel anything unusual about his body, but at that moment, he saw a wound suddenly appear without warning on the right arm of the living corpse in front of him.
"Success!"
Su Lun knew this was a sign of the scythe's curse backlash.
"My conjecture was indeed correct. As long as the conditions of a living body and dark spiritual power are met, a spatial rift can be created!"
Now, Su Lun's face was radiant, as if he saw a glimmer of light piercing through the fog-enshrouded future.
The scythe cut through everything!
The [Xiupunos's Night Scythe], which had previously only been used to gamble with enemies' lives, now became a controllable lethal weapon.
The curse's backlash not affecting his own body meant he could control the living corpse to swing the scythe without any reservations.
There was also a surprising bonus: because of the "X serum's" modification, the living corpse possessed strong self-healing abilities. The wound that had appeared was slowly healing.
This also meant that as long as the living corpse was not killed in one go, it could be reused over and over!
People using the scythe would be careful to avoid crippling themselves, affecting their combat effectiveness, but the living corpse was different.
Su Lun wanted a puppet; as long as the living corpse could create spatial rifts, it didn't matter to him even if it was severely maimed.
He estimated that before the corpse succumbed to lethal backlash, it could probably make five or six swings!
A single swing could kill a leader-level Spider Queen; what did five or six swings mean?
This meant that Su Lun now had the capability to kill high-ranking professionals!
However, Su Lun wasn't too excited; this was a result he had anticipated from the start.
Next, he had more problems to face.
The experiment was successful, but there were still many issues to address before it reached combat readiness.
Looking at the living corpse on the autopsy table, he stroked his chin, contemplating, "The living corpse's control isn't flexible enough; real combat would require significant improvements. The corpse's muscle strength is sufficient for it to stand and support its body, but it can't walk. What if I installed a mechanical skeleton and added a steam power boiler? Hmm...
the technology isn't mature yet, and it's less convenient."
As he thought, his thoughts began to wander.
"The phenomenon of the living corpse's dark spiritual power spillover also needs to be controlled, so we can control the intensity of the spatial rifts created..."
"The swinging amplitude and the infused amount of dark spiritual power determine the size of the spatial rifts, but it still needs more experimentation to get precise control data..."
Now that he had the living corpse, these dangerous experiments no longer required Su Lun to risk himself.
With ninety-seven vials of [Second Generation X Serum], he had enough to create more living corpses, obtaining the precise data he desired.
But looking at that two-meter-long big black scythe, Su Lun mused, "Furthermore, the biggest problem is that neither the living corpse nor the scythe can be placed in the storage ring, which makes it inconvenient to carry them around."
"Eh... Mr. Hei mentioned before that the second-tier professional advancement for a Puppet Master could choose 'Spatial Ability'. Some high-quality spatial curse materials can grant the ability to create real foldable spaces. Getting a foldable space that could contain the living corpse and the scythe would be perfect. However, such cursed materials are not so easy to find..."

chapters.title: Chapter 115 - 115 Did you not notice any changes in me? (Please subscribe)
chapters.content:
Su Lun had successfully created a zombie.
But he had another idea, which was whether he could inject himself with one.
Su Lun carefully flipped through the "Zombie Research Diary" and found some experiment records of living people being injected with "X Serum," which made him hesitant.
Even with a "Mutational Suppressant," the success rate of integrating the serum was only eighty percent.
The remaining twenty percent meant either an unknown directional mutation, deformation, or even direct explosion and death.
Moreover, the side effect of skin turning blue for a long time was also a major problem.
He wasn't concerned about his image; after all, he could accept a smoked style with no eyebrows and Baldy, it seemed that blue skin couldn't be uglier.
But ordinary people didn't know what seeing the skin meant, while those with keen eyes could tell at a glance that this was a side effect of the "X Potion." Once discovered by the people of Inner City, it would definitely cause major trouble.
He also didn't know how long this blue skin would last and didn't dare to try recklessly.
Anyway, there seemed to be no reason that forced him to risk using the serum now, so Su Lun planned to wait and see if there might be other ways to increase the success rate.
.....
Su Lun spent every day in the basement, tinkering with zombies, Puppet Masters, machinery, exercising physically, and studying alchemy...
He felt very busy, as if multitasking with eight spider limbs was not enough.
That was nearly a month, during which he only went out once to attend a small gathering of high-level professionals at the black market and barely left the house otherwise.
He also casually gathered information from various sources; it seemed that the follow-up investigation into the robbery he and Kai had pulled off was not making much noise.
After all, the lab had exploded; who still cared about a bunch of lost supplies?
Just like that, Su Lun managed to sell off some of the loot he had intercepted and converted it into some hard currency in hand.
However, the richer he became, the more worries he had.
Su Lun now wanted to purchase the "Spiritual Power Secret Technique" and the [Curse Hair of the Wailing Witch], and now added a second-tier advancement material that could awaken Spatial Ability.
According to Mr. Hei, the first two might still be purchasable. After all, many people didn't recognize the value of the Spiritual Power Secret Technique and couldn't use it; it was possible to find a good deal. As for the hair, almost only Puppet Masters could use it, and it could be bought at a reasonable price.
As for the cursed material that could awaken Spatial Ability, it was almost impossible.
Such rare advancement material essential for awakening "Spatial Ability" was in such high demand that not even the storerooms of the major financial clans of Inner City had stocks.
Not to mention whether a scavenging team that found it would consume it internally.
Even if it were sold, the wealthy financial clans of Inner City were the best buyers.
Su Lun felt that if he really wanted it, he might just have to try his luck scavenging.
The black market indeed had increasingly more to offer.
As the excavation of the "Dawn City Ruins" deepened, more and more people were joining the excursions beyond the city.
Of course, the casualty rate remained high, and many small scavenging teams didn't even see the ruins before being completely wiped out on their way there.
But the rewards were astounding.
From the messages sent back, it was clear that the ruins were not an empty city but seemed to have been destroyed by some terrifying disaster.
The city retained a large amount of ancient artifacts, and too many S-grade and T-grade cursed spaces appeared.
Hearing all this, Su Lun was not in a hurry.
After all, Mr. Hei had assessed that without a massive sacrifice of lives, it would take eight to ten years to fully exploit the ruins.
But because the potential rewards were so enticing, the major financial families of the city were also organizing scavenging teams and squads of daredevils to go underground.
The city's three major gangs were also stirred by the news, with multiple scouting scavenging teams from the Cross Society having ventured out of the city to scout ahead.
Upon hearing the news, Su Lun also had some ideas.
He now had a zombie capable of wielding a scythe and had some capacity to defend himself. If the opportunity arose, he planned to go and see for himself.
.....
Being gang members, it was inevitable for Su Lun and Kai, two lone wolves from Green Street, to get to work.
Others might forget these two, who hadn't shown their faces for months, but Phino was well aware of their core abilities.
One day, Su Lun exceptionally went out, rode his motorcycle to "Big Beard's Mechanical Repair Shop," and was waiting there. He chatted with the owner Lait, exchanging some mechanical repair experiences. At six thirty, Kai arrived right on time on his bike.
Kai called out, "Let's go."
Su Lun followed him, "Captain, why did you call me out here?"
Kai said, "The new place on Norton Street is opening tonight, and Phino asked us to make a show. It sounds like we might be following her lead from now on..."
"Oh."-
Upon hearing this, Su Lun revealed a look of realization.
Previously Green Street had been destroyed, and the Cross Society had been planning to recreate an entertainment street.
It just so happened that the recent strife in the inner city seemed to have subsided.
Lady Phino had stood unwavering through the turmoil, and the internal expansion of the Cross Society was beginning again.
There had been talk of setting up a new entertainment district for a while now, and I couldn't believe it was already built.
And that new street, it's right in the Norton Street area under Qian's jurisdiction.
....
They had plenty of time, so the two rode their motorcycles at a leisurely pace.
Kai was thrilled, riding his motorcycle like a victorious rooster, chest puffed out and head held high. He teased with a wink, "Brother Su Lun, haven't you noticed any changes in me?"
Su Lun glanced at him and naturally noticed something.
It had been half a month since he'd last seen the guy.
Kai's physique had obviously bulked up, stretching his leather jacket taut. Squeezing the arm holding the handlebars, his muscles rippled powerfully under the skin, as though worms of flesh were rolling beneath it, creating a visually striking impact.
Seeing Kai's deliberately showy flexing, Su Lun pretended not to notice and played along by asking, "Ah... what's up?"
Releasing one hand from the motorcycle, Kai flaunted his huge biceps, "Look at this, what's this?"
Su Lun couldn't help but laugh.
He felt he should be astonished, but he just couldn't muster it and simply uttered, "Oh."
"Oh?"
Kai rolled his eyes, realizing he had chosen the wrong person to show off to and felt rather deflated.
But he knew Su Lun's nature; even getting an "Oh" from him was quite something.
Though his display fell flat, it didn't dampen Kai's spirits as he excitedly said, "Brother, the body-enhancing potion you found for me in the black market last time is simply divine! My training this past month feels like it covers a year's worth of progress. I feel fantastic now!"
"Oh, that's good if it helps," Su Lun replied with a slight smile.
He, of course, knew all about that potion.
The [PTX Fury Amplifier] and [Lester VI Generation Blood Cell Enhancer] — he himself was using them.
He had bought so many second-hand devices for Danny; making money was secondary as he first needed to assure his own supply of potions.
Now the initial investment had started to pay off, and these two body-enhancing potions were his top priority in production.
Last time, using the excuse of splitting looted money, he casually handed a few to Kai.
"Brother, all else aside, this potion really saved me big time!"
Kai exclaimed excitedly, "Had it not been for striking it rich together with you last time, I wouldn't have been able to afford such expensive potions."
He knew very well that without Su Lun, it would have been impossible to intercept that shipment.
Pausing, a hopeful gleam appeared in Kai's eyes as he added sentimentally, "With such great body-enhancing potions, for the first time, I see the hope of advancing to a Tier 2 professional in my lifetime..."
"..."
Listening, Su Lun smiled.
People like Kai, who were spirited and brave, always worked hard.
But in reality, his strength seemed average among professionals.
The most critical difference, in fact, lay in the disparity of resources.
Be it breathing techniques, alchemical enhancements, or various martial skills, they were lacking.
For close-combat professionals without enough high-quality supplements, training efficiency was low, and they would accumulate hidden injuries. It might seem fine for a short time, but over the long haul, it could result in chronic illnesses affecting their whole life.
This is why it's difficult for out-city individuals to advance to professional levels, and even more challenging for professionals to promote to Tier 2.
After all, the need for body-enhancing potions is ongoing.
Like the two types of potions Kai uses now, costing nearly 500,000 each, not only are they "regulated potions" inaccessible in inner cities, but even if available, he couldn't afford them.
Speaking of which, Kai continued, "Once I hit a bottleneck, I plan to apply to join the guild's scavenger team to go outside the city for a hunt. Train a bit, and who knows, I might even make a big score.""
He paused, then added in a secretive tone, "Hey, did you hear? They've discovered a large ancient ruin underground, seems quite formidable.""
Su Lun knew he was probably talking about the Dawn City Ruins, but the information for the lower tier members was indeed very delayed.
He casually mentioned, "Isn't that ruin said to be very dangerous?"
"Dangerous or not, I'm going!"
Kai wore a carefree expression, unabashed admiration evident as he recounted the legendary stories he'd heard within the guild, "Back in the day, Boss Angel got really strong by encountering danger while scavenging outside the city, turning misfortune into a blessing, enabling him to merge with the Silver Enhancement [Thousand Killing Wings]…"
But then he suddenly stopped talking.
Kai suddenly remembered something, looked over at Su Lun who was riding next to him, and made an uninterested pout.
The other guild members got pumped up hearing Boss Angel's stories, but he knew Su Lun definitely wouldn't.
Because he was sure Su Lun's enhancements were far beyond just silver!
But having thought about it, he still never asked.
Seeing that he wasn't continuing, Su Lun also smiled, "There'll be time for that later."

chapters.title: Chapter 116 - 116: The Best Destiny I Can Think Of (Please Subscribe)
chapters.content:
Soon, Su Lun and Kai arrived at Norton Street on their motorcycle.
Everything looked completely different from their last visit. Brothels, gambling stalls, taverns, and unique bathhouses... a variety of dazzling neon lights illuminated the entire street block.
Yet, to Su Lun and Kai, the scene felt incredibly familiar.
"Crimson Fortress," "Elephant Tavern," "Emperor's Bathhouse," "Musketeer Inn"... one after another, the familiar signs were almost indistinguishable from the once bustling Green Street.
Kai's mouth puckered as he became nostalgic upon seeing the scenery, deeply moved as the former boss of Green Street.
Su Lun, however, seemed indifferent. Even if he had to start patrolling every evening at seven, it wouldn't take much of his time. At worst, he'd just move back here. Plus, with the Gladiator arena opening, he could harvest a wave of souls every night, which was a good thing anyway.
.....
Today was the street opening ceremony, and Norton Street was bustling with activity.
The president of the Cross Society, "Arbiter" Chak, along with a host of other executives, were also present.
Dressed in suits and looking very formal, they would pass off as successful businessmen if not for the occasional murderous intent that flashed across their brows, barely concealing the fact that they were ruthless gang leaders.
Most of the major stakeholders in the entertainment industry were the wealthy of the inner city. Today's opening drew many big shots from the inner city to cut the ribbon, and a variety of luxury cars lined the street from end to end. Portly old gentlemen and gorgeously dressed ladies, along with graceful socialites...
strutted the red carpet, providing Su Lun and other folks from the outer city a glimpse of what the rich of the inner city looked like.
People like Su Lun and Kai, who were idle and listless, naturally didn't have the qualifications to show their faces upfront.
The good-looking ones went to preside over the inner venue, while those dressed in leather jackets, with tattoos, having odd and ferocious looks, stood on the periphery responsible for security, lest they scare the noble ladies and lords.
With his tanned skin and bald head, Su Lun naturally stayed outside.
He was happy to keep to the sidelines.
Kai and the team captains of the Cross Society squatted on the side, chatting and shooting the breeze, when suddenly, a white stretch limo decorated with angel wings arrived in front of the red carpet.
Someone shouted, "Look, there's... a beautiful woman!"
The old birds, energized by the word "beautiful woman," all craned their necks to look toward the red carpet.
Then, they saw a stunning woman in a pure black dress flowing like quicksand step out of the car.
Su Lun glanced over and immediately recognized her as Lady Philo, the financial backer of the Cross Society.
Most of the Cross Society captains weren't high-ranking enough to know who was behind the gang's finances. Even those who'd heard the name hadn't seen her.
Kai took one glance and his gaze instantly locked on. Suppressing the excitement in his heart, he feigned nonchalance as he warned, "Don't cause such a fuss. If you disturb Lady Philo, the president will surely kick your asses."
Someone expressed their surprise, "Is that the legendary Lady Philo? Kai, have you seen her before?"
Kai replied, "In the past, indeed, I had the honor of being personally received by that lady. But let's not dwell on it..."
His teasing tone, coupled with a boastful expression, made him look utterly punchable.
"Tsk~"
The team captains all hissed together, though it did not dampen their enthusiasm for gazing at the beautiful woman.
"Goodness me, she's unbelievably gorgeous..."
"Hey... another one's getting out of the car. Kai, who's that young beauty beside Lady Philo?"
"Don't know her, but she's probably the daughter of some big family," Kai guessed.
"Could it be Lady Philo's daughter?"
"Nonsense! How could that lady have such an adult daughter?"
"..."
The old birds began speculating wildly with various gossips.
Allegations of affairs among the inner-city bigwigs were prime gossip material after dinner in the outer city.
Su Lun listened silently on the side because he had already recognized the person following Lady Philo.
Even with a black veil covering her face, Su Lun instantly recognized her by the long, beautiful straight black hair. Wasn't that the young girl, Lena?
```
Why would a young lady from a top-tier family come to a place like this?
However, seeing Lady Philo and Lena were able to leave the city for the ribbon-cutting ceremony made him think that the Reyes family's internal strife must have almost settled down.
He did not dwell on it much.
....
All the protagonists had arrived, and then it was the boring process of the ribbon-cutting.
A bunch of inner city bosses joined together for the ribbon-cutting and made their speeches.
But Lady Philo was quite low-profile - apart from showing her face when she got out of the car, she wasn't seen again afterward.
Su Lun appeared somewhat bored, leaning against a lamppost and fiddling with his coin-flipping trick, from palm to back, and then from back to palm...
Suddenly, he felt someone's gaze sizing him up from behind, and the coin in his hand paused slightly.
But on recognizing the familiar footsteps, he didn't pay it any more mind.
The next second, Su Lun felt his arm wrapped in softness, a warm body boldly hugging his shoulder. Before he even saw the person, he heard the familiar Big Sister's tone, "Hey, Su Lun, kid, where've you been these days? I haven't seen you at the casinos, and here I was, thinking of asking you to be my gambling buddy, but you're nowhere to be seen."
When Su Lun heard the footsteps, he knew it was Qian Tiao and greeted her with a smile, "Sister Qian Tiao."
Turning to look, probably because of the ribbon-cutting ceremony today, Qian Tiao was dressed quite formally. She wore a fitted, light blue kimono with her hair tied up high, not even showing her tattoos, looking quite gentile.
Qian Tiao asked again, "Where's the kid, Kai?"
Su Lun shrugged, "Don't know, he seems to have gone to see the excitement with the captains."
Qian Tiao patted Su Lun on the shoulder and said, "I've already told the president; from now on, you and Kai will come to Norton Street. You're my man now!"
Su Lun didn't really care, "Oh..."
Not finding Kai in the crowd, Qian Tiao beckoned Su Lun and led him away, saying, "Come on, let's go for a bath and while I'm at it, I'll introduce you to some people."
"Ah? It's the ribbon-cutting today, aren't you supposed to be watching the scene, Sister Qian Tiao?"
Su Lun thought it sounded unreliable.
The boss of Norton Street is supposed to be doing the grand opening, and you're going for a bath?
Qian Tiao made a face as if it was too much of a hassle, "There were too many small tasks at the site today; I left them to the captains."
"..."
Su Lun thought this hands-off boss was quite something.
It was precisely because there were so many tasks for the grand opening that they needed you, the boss, to hold down the fort.
Meanwhile, Kai suddenly popped up from somewhere, calling out from a distance, "Sister Qian Tiao!"
"I was just looking for you."
Qian Tiao called out to Kai, "Come on, to Akun's Bathhouse! Big Sister's treating you to a bath!"
Kai's eyes lit up at the prospect, "Sure!"
With Qian Tiao treating them, it was an offer they couldn't refuse. Even though Su Lun wanted to go back and study the living dead, he had to follow them.
....
After the bath, they felt refreshed and invigorated.
Late at night, Su Lun accompanied Qian Tiao to the newly opened gladiator arena.
The new arena was celebrating its inauguration, and the gambling-addicted young matron was eager to try her luck.
Because it was the opening day, some very skilled professional gladiators were there, and the matches were thrilling - Su Lun also gained a wave of valuable experience.
He stayed on Norton Street for the night, planning to head back early the next morning.
But just as he came out of the gambling den in the early morning, Kai caught up with him, saying that the executives had assigned them to escort a batch of goods to the inner city.
```
Later, I heard that it was the opening of a new venue, and the captains of the Cross Society were very busy.
It seemed that only the two of them on Green Street had nothing to do, so the officers, seeing them idle, assigned them to escort duty.
It wasn't any special task, just following the convoy and delivering a batch of valuable goods to the inner city.
The Cross Society had its own ruin-hunting groups, so the gang's warehouse would accumulate a lot of high-grade cursed materials and relics from outside the city.
Keeping these items in the outer city was of little use, as they couldn't be sold at good prices. Thus, every so often a batch would be sent to the inner city, handed over to the principal's company to handle.
With the principal's pass, there was no need to check identities when entering the city, which was a rare opportunity for gang members to access the inner city.
The old hands of the Cross Society were very fond of this mission.
It was a rare opportunity to gain experience and knowledge.
Kai seemed very excited too.
.....
In the afternoon, Su Lun and Kai arrived at the warehouse of the Cross Society headquarters in the Hessen Building.
Kai checked the goods loaded onto the truck, signed off on the inventory list, and was ready to depart.
A standard escort team consisted of three vehicles.
One captain with nine men, plus two truck drivers.
It was exactly like the convoy of the Steam Party they had ambushed several days ago.
Because they had just recently studied in detail how to rob a transport team, Su Lun and Kai always felt a bit strange, so they didn't sit in either the lead or tail vehicle.
Kai sent the driver to the car, then drove the truck himself, with Su Lun, they took the middle of the transport team.
They were afraid that the Cross Society might have some secret dealings with the inner city, which could attract some inexplicable attacks. Before boarding, Su Lun also purposely observed that the truck for this time's loading was not a special explosion-proof vehicle, and the cargo was normal goods.
After getting on the truck, the two of them exchanged a smile.
But they thought they were probably worrying too much, after all, with the escort missions taking place several times a year, it was not so coincidental that they would encounter an ambush.
....
They set out from the south of the city and after half an hour, they were approaching the inner city wall, which was several times more magnificent than the outer city wall.
From some stripped memories, Su Lun had a vague impression of the structure of the inner city.
Seeing the towering city wall in the distance, some of the images from his memories started to overlap.
The general layout of the inner city was like a cake, divided into eight parts, numbered 1 to 8. And at the center of the inner city stood a black tower so tall, its top couldn't be seen, like a candle planted on the cake.
At the base of the wall, hundred-meter-tall super chimneys were constantly emitting white smoke, which came from the super-steam boilers that powered the entire city.
The inner city wall was about two hundred meters tall, but the buildings inside were even taller.
As the convoy drew closer to the inner city, the wall in their view became more and more tangible.
On the wall facing them were white spray-paint markings, with a giant number "5" on them.
Below the wall was the fifth gate, corresponding to the inner city's fifth district.
Kai looked excited; he pointed at the super-tall buildings that rose above the city walls and commented in awe, "Hey, brother, take a look, that's the famous 'Sky Gardens' of the inner city! See that colorful ribbon in the sky there? Hehe... that's the legendary rainbow, an amazing sight you can't see anywhere else."
"Hmm."
Su Lun had very good eyesight and had actually seen it a while ago.
The lights of the inner city were as bright as daylight, giving a very luminous feeling.
It was like adding a layer of bright filter to those buildings, clean and transparent.
Even from a great distance, you could see a sea of green on the upper levels of the inner city's architecture, and white waterfalls cascading down from the tops of those buildings, with rainbows hanging between them...
On the rooftop garden draped with yellow-orange fruit, you could see a lady in white leaning against the railing, admiring the view as the wind lifted her skirts...
The high-altitude swimming pool, lush rooftop greenery, and the blue expanse of the buildings' glass... On the glass skyway, one could discern the blurry silhouettes of people walking about, laughing and chatting in pairs and groups...
The architecture of the inner city was beautiful and infused with technological sophistication; the outer city was like a post-apocalyptic wasteland, filled with greyness and filth.
Separated by just a wall, it was as though they were two different worlds.
After his excitement, Kai's tone turned somewhat melancholic, "Hey, brother. I won't lie to you, I've never been to the inner city in my life..."
Su Lun smiled, "I haven't been there either."
"Haha, this time we can go and broaden our horizons."
As he spoke, Kai's clear eyes reflect the shadow of that massive city and revealed a longing for something better.
Just getting a chance to see the inner city was a dream forever out of reach for many people from the outer city.
Kai suddenly felt a touch of sadness, "I'm an orphan from the tenements, no father, no mother. Apart from fighting and killing, I know nothing. I've heard that kids in the inner city learn to play instruments from a young age, learn business, go to colleges to gain knowledge... They grow up to become lawyers, dentists, teachers..."
At this point, Kai laughed self-mockingly, "Heh..."
After a pause, he continued pensively, "Brother, you know... I used to fantasize that I could fight for the best life for myself, which would be to advance by luck to the second tier and then work as a bodyguard for some inner city big shot... Haha, sounds pretty unambitious, right?"
Su Lun looked at him.
The eyes of the gang leader, who could still be called a youth, suddenly sparkled with light.
"Everyone in the gang says I'm brave and that I'm bound to achieve great things..."
Kai wore a smile on his face, but as he continued, he couldn't smile anymore, "Actually, you might laugh, but sometimes I'm very scared. Countless nights, I wake up from nightmares of fighting and killing, covered in cold sweat. Feeling my still-beating heart, it takes me a long while to realize that I'm still alive..."
Su Lun quietly listened, acting as a silent audience for once.
His gaze turned gradually profound as he looked at that city.
....
The journey was uneventful.
Su Lun and his companion both breathed a sigh of relief.
The truck approached the base of the city wall, seeming like a mouse under the feet of an elephant.
Because they had a special pass, they didn't undergo inspection and smoothly drove through the massive steel city gate.
By then, there was no trace of melancholy on Kai's face, replaced once again by his carefree smile.
As they neared their destination, Kai suddenly thought of something and said to Su Lun, "Let me tell you a secret, but you mustn't tell anyone."
Su Lun raised an eyebrow, "Oh?"
Kai spoke mysteriously, "Before we set off, Boss Smoker told me he would introduce me to a big shot from the inner city, and I might have the chance to enter the inner city ahead of time."
"Boss Smoker?"
At the mention, Su Lun flashed on some thought and frowned suddenly.
"Yeah! Boss Smoker said that as soon as I enter the city, someone from that big shot will contact me."
Kai nodded, beaming, "I'm telling you, if I strike it rich, I'll take care of you! Hahaha...."
Su Lun's expression faltered slightly, feeling that something was off, and asked, "You mean... Boss Smoker asked you to keep it a secret?"
"Yes."
Kai said, "He originally told me not to tell anyone, but I feel like we're brothers, and you would definitely keep a secret for me."
Why did it need to be kept secret?
An introduction to a patron wasn't something to hide.
Feeling instinctively wary, Su Lun asked, "How will this person contact you?"
Kai, still oblivious to any issues, answered, "I don't know. But Boss Smoker said that the person will find a way to get in touch with me..."

chapters.title: Chapter 117 - 117 The Lost Manuscript
chapters.content:
"Boss, the Cross Society's convoy escorting the goods has entered the city. They should arrive at the 'White Sail Warehouse' in about ten minutes."
"Has the list of escort personnel been confirmed?"
"It has been confirmed, three vehicles totalling twelve people. They are all old members of the Cross Society recorded on the list, no suspicious persons. The team is led by 'Blade' Kai, and there's another one on the list named Su Lun, not bad with a gun."
"Hmm, a gunman is just a gunman, no matter how strong, he's just a low-level threat. Stick to the plan. Once you confirm the item is in the cargo, immediately eliminate everyone who has come into contact with it."
"Yes!"
"Oh, and that 'Kai,' go and make contact with him. Give him an outer-perimeter evaluation; if he's capable, bring him in."
"Yes."
....
The Cross Society's convoy slowly entered the inner city through "Gate Number Five."
Once inside the city walls, it was like stepping into a forest of steel, a highly dimensional city. There were many buildings over three to five hundred meters high, resembling towering trees that formed the backbone of the city.
Supported by these skyscrapers, densely packed steel frame sky bridges, suspended urban train tracks, high-altitude pedestrian streets, and hanging steel layers were built... like layers of a multi-tiered cake.
These elevated structures connected the buildings, effectively dividing the entire city into upper, middle, and lower layers.
The architectural styles were clearly layered.
The lower buildings appeared elongated, with exposed brick walls and large stones, characterized by very evident Gothic styles with soaring spires, pointed arches, and large windows with colored stained glass, reminiscent of architecture from a thousand years ago; the middle layers with their steel frame structures, thick pipes, and steam boilers exuded a rough industrial steampunk vibe; and higher up, it transitioned into a cyber-world of futuristic technology with aerial gardens...
The city's designers had increased the residential capacity within the limited space several times over.
Though Su Lun's harvested memories were somewhat vague, he knew that the residents of the inner city also varied in social status.
The higher one lived, the more prestigious their status.
The lowest level was the inner city's civilian area.
The Cross Society's convoy traveled on the ground, similar to a light rail, as urban trains roared overhead. Next to the streets, flower stands blooming with bright flowers were visible, and people of all ages wore fitted, vibrant clothing.
"Wow... so many cars! Do all these guys in the inner city have so much money? It feels like every person can afford a luxury saloon..."
Kai had never been to the inner city before, and he kept exclaiming as he observed the starkly different scene from the outer city.
Each of these cars had a shiny finish and sleek lines, nothing like the old vehicles in the outer city cobbled together from scrap parts.
Seeing the cars on the highway suddenly made Kai think that the "cool modified motorcycles" in the gang seemed like naughty children covered in mud in front of these saloons.
Su Lun rested his chin on his hand, leaning against the car window, watching the bustling busy streets, yet his gaze seemed somewhat distracted.
Even though they had successfully transported the cargo to the inner city, where there should be no chance of encountering bandits, he still felt something was off.
...
The destination for the cargo escort was "White Sail Warehouse," an inconspicuous building beside the river at the bottom of District 5, with a glass roof resembling a white sail.
The space was vast, allowing the trucks to drive directly into the warehouse.
Kai called Su Lun to disembark, "Hey, bro, we've arrived. Once we hand over the goods, our mission will be complete."
Su Lun nodded, but he wasn't in a hurry to get off.
He deliberately observed the people receiving the goods in the warehouse, seven in total. They were staff from Lady Fino's subsidiary commerce association and seemed unproblematic.
Then he surveyed the layout of the warehouse. It was spacious, as large as a football field. Aside from a few vehicles, there were no places to hide, just a few thick, spray-painted steel columns supporting the glass roof overhead.
In that moment, Su Lun had instinctively thought of possible escape routes should danger arise.
Kai had already gone down and greeted the recipients.
He then went to the back of the trailer to open the password-protected door, and his crew started unloading the goods one by one based on the inventory list.
Having observed this, Su Lun didn't notice anything unusual and also descended from the vehicle.
"Butler Jackson, here is the inventory list of the goods. We checked it already before we left, and there are definitely no issues," Kai said.
"Sorry, but we still need to go through the process."
"Oh, inventory checking is quite a time-consuming task, that must be tough for you."
"Not at all. This is exactly why Lady Philo hired us."
"... "
As Su Lun disembarked, he watched as the Cross Society's members started unloading the items from the truck, while the old butler named Jackson was in charge of inventory.
The folks from the inner city seemed very detached, apparently having little interest in interacting with the Cross Society members from the outer city, even with Kai, the transport leader.
Kai seemed quite bored.
Seeing Su Lun come down, he approached, "Su Lun, after we hand over the goods, how about we take a tour around the city?"
Seeing Kai upbeat, Su Lun nodded, "Hmm."
But just then, suddenly a large man with a goatee dressed in a suit came from outside the warehouse and called out to the group asking, "Who's Kai?"
Kai frowned at the arrogant tone. He initially didn't want to respond but seemed to recall something and eventually spoke up, "I am."
The man wasted no time and coldly said, "Follow me, someone wants to see you."
With that, he turned and left in the direction from which he had come.
Far from being skeptical, Kai was actually excited. He gave Su Lun a meaningful look, "Brother, I'll be gone for a moment; please keep an eye on things for me."
"Okay."
Su Lun nodded but said nothing.
He knew that this goatee was probably the contact that Kai mentioned Smoke Ghost had arranged for him to meet.
He had nothing much to say.
After all, Smoke Ghost was Kai's former captain and the one who had promoted him within the gang. Su Lun often heard Kai express admiration for Smoke Ghost that resembled a child's admiration for his father.
But...
What Su Lun found strange was that this goatee came directly to the warehouse to fetch someone?
This was Lady Philo's warehouse; if the financial backer introduced by Smoke Ghost was an acquaintance of Lady Philo, why so secretive?
And that almost imperceptible watchful gaze near the warehouse entrance—was it a sentry or something else?
...
The items on the truck had already been unloaded, large sculptures and metal utensils were piled everywhere.
Then there were the smaller items like ancient books, scrolls, and cursed materials.
Having doubts, Su Lun quietly observed. Gradually, he noticed something—this goatee butler seemed to be examining those books very carefully.
The invoice simply listed "one hundred ancient books" without any detailed names.
The pile comprised of hundreds, perhaps thousands of books; it would take a lot of time to inspect each one.
Yet the butler painstakingly reviewed each book, as if looking for something.
This unusual behavior immediately triggered Su Lun's alertness.
What was this old man looking for?
He showed no such detail towards other old artifacts; it seemed he was searching for a particular book?
In that instant, several keywords flashed through Su Lun's mind—goods, books... gang's warehouse?
No!
Something was wrong!
Suddenly, he connected memories with those keywords.
Those were from his first day joining the Cross Society during that warehouse attack at headquarters!
At that time, Qian Tiao had captured an intruder, but they were killed en route by a mole from the Cross Society.
Su Lun connected all the clues and suddenly frowned, guessing a possibility that sent chills down his spine, "This guy is looking for 'Isaac's Alchemy Manuscript'!"
...
The thought emerged suddenly, casting a tremendous sense of impending doom over Su Lun.
What he had thought was a simple escort mission secretly harbored a sinister threat!
Su Lun had already learned through various channels that what the Cross Society had lost was indeed a copy of "Isaac's Alchemy Manuscript."
He had thought its loss was none of his concern, being a lowly gang member with no relation to such a precious item.
Yet now, he found himself unexpectedly entangled in the matter.
He instantly thought, "The Captain Miller who had shot the captive back then definitely wasn't the mole, at least not the mastermind. This means there was another key figure involved in the heist within the Cross Society that hadn't been caught.
With President Chak and the executives suddenly returning to headquarters, the mole knew they couldn't safely take away the manuscript and instead chose to hide it..."
Moreover, this was not just conjecture; it was confirmed!
Su Lun immediately recalled the key information obtained from the soul of that second-level attacker: "They would never guess where the manuscript was hidden."
"So that's what happened..."
Su Lun connected all the dots in his mind, revealing a deeply laid, vast conspiracy.
Since the manuscript wasn't taken away at the time,
where could the manuscript be hidden that would be least expected?
The Cross Society's warehouse!
"The manuscript had never left the Hessen Building; it merely moved from the Cross Society's treasury to an ordinary warehouse outside!"
Piecing various clues together, Su Lun quickly concluded, "That mole knew very well that even as an executive, revisiting the warehouse would be suspicious for him. But by using this method, he wouldn't have to personally risk retrieving the manuscript because every so often, the Cross Society automatically packages and transports the goods to the inner city...
Just by ambushing the transport team, he could find the manuscript hidden among those books!"

chapters.title: Chapter 118 - 118: Suddenly Started Killing
chapters.content:
"Damn it! Smoker Sanbu is the mole from the Cross Society!"
Su Lun reconstructed the truth of the whole situation in his mind. The more he thought about it, the pieces fell into place.
If Miller was not the real mole, then the one who could order him to kill the captives had to be an executive.
Even though several executives from the Cross Society were not in town at the time, no one would suspect this old member of the Cross Society.
But the secret Kai had told him made Su Lun immediately certain that Smoker was the mole!
Su Lun was sure that Kai had no knowledge of this. So... now that he had been taken away, could it be that Smoker actually valued his talents and planned to spare Kai's life?
Although he didn't know what Kai would face after being led away, it wasn't what Su Lun needed to think about right now.
He knew very well that once "Isaac's Alchemy Manuscript" was indeed in this batch of goods, the moment it was found would be the moment of death for the people in this warehouse!
...
Maybe the other party just wanted the goods and wasn't planning to kill anyone?
No.
Su Lun had no illusions because he had already felt the intent to kill.
His gaze swept through the layout of the warehouse again and suddenly felt that the situation was very bad.
Their position was right in the middle of the warehouse. If enemies outside stormed in, they would be caught in a crossfire from all directions.
Even using the train carriages as a cover, they would only be awaiting death.
He thought the other employees of the trading company probably wouldn't be a big problem, but this old butler who was flipping through notebooks definitely was.
Su Lun had originally thought that the barely noticeable sense of disgust was due to the innate superiority complex of the inner city people towards those from the outer city. Now he realized it was a hint of murderous intent.
Thinking of this, Su Lun also slowly moved closer and then, pretending to help, crawled into the train carriage. Although these carriages were not special anti-explosion types, they could still largely withstand a spray of bullets.
At that moment, the old butler was still searching through a pile of books.
Suddenly, he picked up a thick tome with a black and gold embossed cover, seemingly finding a certain mark, and his expression subtly changed.
Right then, the old butler did something that seemed very normal: he took off his hat.
Su Lun, who had been carefully watching his every move, noticed this and his pupils suddenly contracted.
This guy was signaling someone!
Seeing this, he no longer waited but took the initiative to ask, "Butler Jackson, have you found what you were looking for?"
Upon hearing this, the old butler's expression drastically changed, and he looked at Su Lun inside the carriage in disbelief.
And just in that moment, the sense of disgust in Su Lun's perception suddenly turned into sharp "intents to kill"!
Almost the moment he sensed the murderous intent, Su Lun didn't give the old butler any chance to strike. He swiftly drew his pistol from his waist and with a "bang," shot the old butler's head off.
The man died instantly.
....
When Su Lun suddenly erupted in murder, whether it were the Cross Society's escort members or those employees who followed the old butler, all were stunned.
Looking at the body with its head blown open, everyone thought Su Lun had gone mad. They were just about to scold him when they saw Su Lun throw out a few smoke grenades, which burst open with a bang.
"Damn, what are you doing!"
"Are you crazy!"
"..."
A series of curses broke out and then abruptly stopped.
Because, before the smoke even fully obscured their vision, the warehouse door was suddenly kicked open with force.
A group of men in plaid vest suits, wearing gloves and newsboy caps, filed in, wielding "Black Wheel submachine guns," and without a word, they sprayed a barrage of gunfire at the trucks in the center of the warehouse!
Ratatat...
Over a dozen submachine guns firing in unison, more than a dozen people standing next to the trucks didn't even have a chance to react before being turned into a sieve.
After more than ten seconds, when the drum magazines ran out of bullets, the sound of cocks clicking as they reloaded echoed throughout the warehouse.
The gunmen, obviously well-trained, eyed the spreading smoke, suspecting that the reloading break might provide the enemy with a chance to strike. Some were reloading, while others drew handguns from their waists, cautiously closing in on the smoke-filled truck.
In the depths of the truck carriage, hidden behind a metal sculpture, Su Lun was quietly counting something to himself: "Three in the front, five on the flank, eight near the truck head..."
He pinpointed the enemy footsteps and suddenly made his move.
Gunshots suddenly exploded from within the smoke.
"Bang!" "Bang!" "Bang!"
Three rapid gunshots and without seeing a single shadow, the three men approaching the truck were precisely hit.
The group of men in black was caught off guard but immediately returned fire, covering the fog with a barrage of bullets.
But in the next instant a vague shadow that looked like an eight-armed monster suddenly burst out from the smoke, moving incredibly fast.
Before the two men in black who had just gathered to block the truck could even see what it was, they were suddenly impaled through the chest by two spider spears and died instantly!
The men in black quickly reacted, trying to focus their fire on Su Lun. But Su Lun, using eight-armed spider spears to move, while his hands remained free, fired back.
[Malicious Perception]allowed him to precisely locate the positions of the enemy gunmen, continuously pulling the trigger to kill.
Bang, bang, bang...
The fierce exchange continued, with gunfire reverberating through the empty warehouse, resounding heavily.
If it had been the outer city, these more than ten gunmen would have been easy for Su Lun to kill and break through. After all, ordinary human reflexes and shooting skills posed a very limited threat to him now.
But!
The bullets that could have killed ten gang gunmen in the outer city only killed one person. The other bullets either missed or were dodged by those men, only hitting non-lethal areas...
"They're all professionals!"
Su Lun saw this, and internally he dreaded the worst. He had no intention of fighting it out, but rather, he fought as he retreated. The Eight-Armed Spider Spear vibrated at a high frequency during movement, creating a blur of shadows.
He didn't dare to rush out through the main gate of the warehouse; instead, he sprinted towards the nearest support pillar, rapidly climbed up it with the crisscrossing Eight-Armed Spider Spear, and disappeared in a wisp of smoke.
At this moment, the Eight-Armed Spider Spear installation demonstrated its astonishing effectiveness for escape, climbing walls and poles as if walking on flat ground.
.....
Su Lun had preempted by catching the group of men in black off guard.
After he dashed out of the car, his exceptional Spider installation and precise marksmanship elicited a soft gasp from the men in black.
They had thought the ambush was foolproof, yet they had lost five men and injured three at first contact?
Wasn't there supposed to be just one professional in the convoy?
What was the deal with this Spider-Man?
Moreover, since when did such formidable first-tier professionals appear in the outer city?
Despite the emergence of many questions, the leader of the men in black did not slow his movements.
"Heh, how could I possibly let you escape?"
As a look of scorn flickered across his eyes, his hands had already formed the sorcerer's seals.
In the next instant, a deep blue Hexagram Alchemy Array suddenly lit up beneath his feet. The moment the array's glow appeared, the vast warehouse suddenly felt like a cold wave had arrived, and the temperature plummeted drastically.
Meanwhile, Su Lun continued his strenuous effort to dodge bullets while climbing around the iron pillar, occasionally managing to fire back a few shots, which made some of the men in black dodge and flee.
Just then, he caught a glimpse from the corner of his eye of the man standing on the Hexagram Array and inwardly cursed, "A second-tier professional!"
Such complex sorcerer's seals were clearly of a second-tier spell.
This meant that the man was definitely a second-tier professional!
Furthermore, the second-tier ice spell seemed extraordinarily powerful. Not only did Su Lun feel the temperature drastically drop, but a chilling sense of impending death also made his skin crawl.
Without hesitation, Su Lun raised his hand and fired two rapid shots at the man in an attempt to disrupt his spellcasting.
"Bang!" "Bang!"
After the two shots, regardless of whether they hit or not, he didn't continue shooting. Instead, he turned the gun upwards and fired several shots at the glass ceiling next to the support pillar, creating a large hole in the glass.
Seeing the opponent cast an ice spell, he instinctively thought of a countermeasure, put away his pistols, and his hands quickly formed the sorcerer's seals.
....
But anyone capable of advancing to a second-tier professional was no ordinary person, and even those specialized in magic had sufficient experience dealing with gunmen.
The leader of the men in black watched as Su Lun aimed the gun at him, a complacent smirk creeping onto his lips.
A thought flashed through his mind: "The Mystique of Overlapping Shots... The outer city gangs actually have such an expert in firearms. This guy really knows how to surprise people. Heh, he might even be a wanted criminal in the organization..."
Just as the thought crossed his mind, he saw sparks emit from the gun aimed at him, but he didn't flinch or dodge. Almost at the same time, the bullet struck his forehead.
"Clang!"
"Clang!"
Two crisp sounds rang out as the bullets were deflected, rune glimmers flashed, scattering a brief flurry of frost.
The man in black was unharmed, his skin not skin at all, but a layer of frost armor!
The very next moment after being shot, the sorcery seal of the man in black had completed, he softly chanted, "Alchemy: Extreme Frost!"
Once the sorcery seal was activated, from the alchemy array beneath his feet spread a path of frost that snaked like a white serpent, zapping towards a load-bearing steel column not far away.
.....
"Such a fast casting speed!"
Su Lun had not expected those two shots to deal with the ice magician, but he hadn't expected the man to literally headbutt the bullets either.
Since he couldn't stop the opponent from casting spells, he could only watch helplessly as the piercing frost instantly spread over the iron column he was climbing.
Just as he was about ten meters from reaching the rooftop, suddenly, the spider spears he was climbing felt like they were stuck in glue, becoming increasingly difficult to pull free.
Upon closer observation, he noticed that the entire iron column beneath his feet was encased in a layer of frost, getting thicker by the second.
Almost instantly, the eight spider spears were not merely difficult to lift; they became completely stuck to the iron wall upon contact.
Just as Su Lun was about to be completely frozen there, unable to move, the leader of the men in black, seemingly confident of victory, shouted loudly, "Capture him alive!"
....
The gunfire abruptly died down, giving Su Lun a chance to catch his breath!
Because at that moment, he had completed the last sorcerer's seal he was holding.
Just as the frost was about to spread over the spider spears and reach his body, Su Lun's body suddenly burst into blue-purple cold flames!
As the cold flames emerged, the frost on the eight-armed spider spears instantly melted. He leaped forcefully, shooting up to the rooftop, and then vanished from the sight of the men in black.
"Huh..."
Seeing this, the leader of the men in black was startled.
Observing the cold flames, his expression turned serious: "The Williams family's unique alchemy secret technique 'Mystique: Wu Shi'? How could a thug from the outer city know it? An expert in firearms, spider limbs, and even Wu Shi, who is this guy really… could he be from that organization?"
Thinking this, he immediately pulled out a communicator, barking, "Attention all units, issuing a Level B emergency order. Commence the search for a fleeing suspect with the following physical characteristics... The Public Security Teams to search for suspicious individuals in districts, City Guards to strictly verify the identities of everyone leaving the city.
The suspect possesses near-Second Rank professional strength, all units please proceed with caution and try to capture him alive!"
Seeing Su Lun fleeing, a few of the men in black also chased after him.
Meanwhile, the remaining few changed into isolation suits and, with some special instruments, began rummaging through the pile of goods they had earlier shattered, apparently searching for something.
Soon, someone reported back, "Boss, it's not here!"
Hearing this, the man in black's expression grew even darker.

chapters.title: Chapter 119 - 119: Moonlight Inn (Additional for 'Sakura Dance Charm' Milestone Reward)
chapters.content:
Su Lun scrambled onto the warehouse rooftop, his eight spider legs displaying their superior ability to traverse any terrain.
Crawling sideways, moving vertically, jumping...
The men in black were more skilled than expected; the moment he got onto the roof, the guards outside spotted him, and bullets rained down in chaos.
Su Lun manipulated the spider legs to sprint madly across the warehouse roof, never touching the ground, but instead climbed over via the pipeline connecting the warehouse to another building.
It was lucky that the eight legs could grab onto the pipeline, enabling him to leap into the floor of the building opposite via the mechanical gloves' steel cables, finally shaking off the men in black on the ground.
He kept running, daring not to stop.
Fortunately, the buildings in the inner city were very crowded; he used his spider legs' excellent wall-climbing abilities and had escaped to another street within moments.
Then, he finally stopped in a secluded alleyway.
....
Su Lun retracted his prosthetic gear, then quickly treated the gunshot wound on his calf with hemostatic powder.
Although he had tried to dodge, the men in black had still managed to shoot him in the leg while he was navigating the iron pillars in the warehouse.
He swiftly took off his blood-stained clothes, bandaged the wound, then changed into a high-end suit similar to those worn by the inner city residents, washed off the smoky makeup from his face, put on a wig and a hat, pressing the brim low. He then sprayed his entire body with odor-eliminating medicinal water.
Having done all this, Su Lun quickly stored the clothes he had taken off into the Storage Ring.
Then, he looked at the thick book in his hand named "Precious New Pearl" with a somewhat complex expression.
He had tucked it into his chest with his spider spear as he was escaping.
Naturally, the book cover was a disguise. Even without looking at the content, he knew it had to be the "Isaac's Alchemy Manuscript."
On the black market, a single page of the manuscript could fetch up to three hundred million Riso, and this book had at least five hundred pages.
However, it wasn't that he coveted the manuscript for its value.
Whether he took it or not, his situation couldn't get any worse.
The intentions of the other party were already clear—they came to kill and silence him.
Moreover, escaping from the hands of a second-grade professional and city gangster, if he had been the Ice Mage from before, he definitely wouldn't let himself go either.
What's more important... he had definitively set himself on an irreversible path when he killed those men in black!
After all, those men in black had no ordinary background.
They weren't just any enforcers employed by some financial tycoon, but members of the "Umbrella Organization"!
....
During the battle earlier, Su Lun was puzzled.
Although it's common to have many professionals in the inner city, it was unlikely for a second-grade professional and a full team to intercept a minor gang squad from the outer city just like that.
After harvesting the memories of the two men killed by the spider spear, Su Lun finally understood the true identity of the robbers.
At that moment, Su Lun no longer harbored any hope for luck.
The Umbrella Organization was a massive entity in Old Lington, not to be trifled with. He had heard about it during his gang days; anyone could be killed, except for people from this organization.
Killing one meant they would relentlessly pursue you until death.
Now that he had killed so many, they would definitely seek revenge to the bitter end.
Moreover, even though others might not know his real identity, the Umbrella Organization, Old Lington's largest intelligence agency, definitely would.
If caught, there was only one outcome – death.
Oh, and they would extract all secrets before letting him die.
....
Su Lun knew that his involvement in this convoy was no coincidence. In a way, he was "implicated" by Kai.
It was likely that the official responsible for arranging this transport, was of Taiwan origin.
That guy, planning to send Kai into the inner city on the sly...
So, was he trying to get Kai into the umbrella organization?
At this point, Su Lun was also very puzzled.
Since he was an insider, it was highly probable that he had also leaked the transport information.
But how could he be a secret line for the umbrella organization?
Su Lun felt there was something wrong with this relationship chain.
He had once speculated that the mole within the Cross Society should be someone from an opposing conglomerate about the same "level" as Lady Philo, and it definitely shouldn't be someone from official departments.
Now, thinking about it, there were more and more doubts.
Could it be that he was a double agent?
Or, were there some elements within the Cross Society that even the umbrella organization dreaded?
Also, why did the people from the umbrella organization necessarily have to kill to silence? Wouldn't just quietly taking away the manuscripts do? Was it merely because taking Kai away was hard to explain, or did he not want to blow his cover? Or did he feel that those involved with the manuscript incident had to be completely cleaned up for some special reason?
Too many illogical points.
....
The notes couldn't be stored in the Storage Ring either, but fortunately, they weren't large, and Su Lun could tuck them inside the inner pocket of his coat.
After changing his clothes, he didn't linger in the alleyway and went straight out.
"It's definitely impossible to get out through the city gate, I need to think of another way..."
While walking, Su Lun was considering contingency plans in his mind.
His footsteps were brisk, showing no signs of agitation. Just like the ordinary residents of the inner city, he walked leisurely on the street, not at all like someone on the run.
What he needed to do now was to escape from the inner city as quickly as possible.
Originally, the Cross Society also had some channels for smuggling out of the city, but since he knew the enemy was the umbrella organization and he was an insider, those channels were no longer trustworthy.
After ruling out several escape plans, a feasible plan sprang to his mind.
"Danny used to stay at 'Facility No. 7' located on Queen Street in the Fourth City District. The sewers there connect to the ancient sewer network. This is currently the only safe way out of the city..."
Su Lun had previously asked Danny about detailed escape routes and also learned the exact location of that route leading to the outer city's sewers.
But while the plan was set, problems emerged again.
From the Fifth City District to the Fourth City District, he had to cross a large district, which was very risky.
Su Lun thought of Danny's super sensitive sense of smell.
He was certain that a security agency like "Umbrella Organization," even if it did not have someone with exactly the same abilities, would definitely have similar tracking methods.
For now, he had momentarily shaken off his pursuers, but it was most likely they would track him by scent.
After all, he had been shot and bloodied, and he had left his smell in the truck, leaving no room for luck.
Thinking all this, Su Lun walked towards the nearby bus station.
Upon arriving at the bus station, he paused in front of a map of bus routes, memorizing the general layout of roads in the Fifth City District.
Then he hailed a taxi and got in.
He had to escape before the enemy's hunting net tightened.
.....
Just a few minutes after Su Lun boarded the taxi, several men in trench coats hurriedly arrived at the bus station.
In their hands, they held a leash attached to a dog that seemed to have slight deformities.
The ugly dog sniffed around the bus route map where Su Lun had stood before and then started barking towards the eastern street.
Seeing this, the man holding the leash picked up the communicator and reported, "All units, please note, the target has taken public transport, moving from the west entrance of Merlin Road Station towards the east, heading towards District Six."
Not long after the report, a sedan arrived, and several people with the dog got into the car.
On the other hand.
Taking a taxi, Su Lun took the opportunity when the driver was not paying attention to stuff the blood-stained clothes he had changed out of into the backseat compartment of the taxi.
Then he only rode for two stops before getting off and heading to the street on the opposite side.
He switched to another taxi and headed in the opposite direction towards District Four.
He didn't think such small tricks could deceive anyone completely, but he hoped they would buy him some extra time.
However, evidently, those anti-tracking skills could mislead the enemy but could not stop another unstoppable method of the Umbrella Organization—roadblocks!
....
As Su Lun was about to leave District Five in this taxi, he saw a checkpoint for checking cars at an intersection up ahead.
The Umbrella Organization's men had obviously considered this and wanted to trap him in "District Five."
It was a one-way street, now even if Su Lun held a gun to the driver's head and ordered him to turn around, it would be pointless.
He saw the checkpoint, and naturally, the people in the checkpoint saw him too.
Turning around would only expose him faster.
Seeing the check, the taxi driver complained, "Oh, why would they suddenly block the road during the daytime? It's too early for a DUI check...and it's not the security guys but seems like some special municipal department. Maybe they are capturing a fugitive ..."
The driver muttered, suddenly thought of something, and then stealthily glanced at the passenger in the backseat through the rearview mirror. Seeing him calm as usual, he didn't dwell on it.
Su Lun naturally noticed the driver sizing him up but didn't speak or jump out of the car, sitting in the backseat as usual.
The car drove past and indeed was stopped.
A few men in trench coats knocked on the driver's window, "Sir, please show your ID card."
The driver pulled out his ID card, held it in his hand, and the card emitted green light.
The inspectors looked at it, compared it, and then handed it back, "Thank you for your cooperation."
Inner city ID cards' anti-forgery technology is extremely difficult to counterfeit.
Using someone else's is useless because the gadget is bound to biological information, and only glows when the holder squeezes it.
Su Lun naturally couldn't produce such a thing, and he had no intention of doing so.
His action naturally drew the attention of the inspection personnel, a few of them subtly closed in around him.
The situation was about to be exposed.
Yet even so, Su Lun didn't draw his gun but calmly rolled down the window and asked the person by the door in a cold tone, "Who here is in charge?"
While speaking, his face showed no trace of fear typical of a fugitive; his expression was resolute and calm, even intentionally emitting some of the killing aura he had honed in real combat.
At this question, even the trench coat man who was ready to check his ID hesitated for a moment, shocked by his aura, his thoughts stumbled, and he instinctively responded, "It's... Captain Mokos."
Su Lun didn't give him a chance to counter-question and said in a calm yet undeniable tone, "Call him over."
The man hesitated, "Yes."
Turning his body, he spoke a few words to a square-faced man who was checking another car at the checkpoint.
Soon after, the square-faced man came over and asked, "Sir, you were looking for me?"
While speaking, he was also sizing up Su Lun, clearly intimidated by the aura as well. He instinctively felt this was a dignified, highly capable, and obviously high-ranking professional.
Su Lun didn't give him much time to think, and said something baffling, "Those eternally at rest are not the deceased; in the mysterious eternity, even death itself will dissipate."
These words baffled the driver in front, but the square-faced man by the door suddenly changed his expression, suddenly becoming respectful and actually saluted on the spot, "Comrade Colonel!"
"Hmm."
Su Lun waved his hand, didn't say an extra word, and commanded the driver, "Drive!"
The driver, seeing people saluting outside the door, was also taken aback for a moment, realizing that there was a Big Shot on board.
Hearing the command to "Drive," he unconsciously started the vehicle.
Although the man in the trench coat felt that something was off, before he could react, the vehicle had already left the checkpoint.
....
Su Lun sat expressionlessly in the backseat, glancing through the rear-view mirror to ensure that no one from the checkpoint was chasing them, and then relaxed his hand that was on the gun.
If the move he tried just a moment ago hadn't worked, they would have been shooting it out by now.
This code phrase had been learned in the cursed space of a basement at 88 Ginkgo Street when he met the "Blind Detective" Bill.
Back then he hadn't matched it correctly, but now he hadn't expected it to be useful.
"So this is a colonel-exclusive code phrase of the Umbrella Organization?"
With some clarity in his mind, Su Lun remembered that the square-faced man had immediately reported a position upon hearing it, which obviously was the correct way to use the "code phrase."
But it probably wouldn't be that simple; there must be a follow-up part to it.
Su Lun didn't know the rest, so he didn't give those guys a chance to react and hurriedly urged the driver to drive on.
The deliberately leaked murderous aura was also to make the other person preemptively assume that he was a high-ranking official inside the system.
However, this method had many flaws, which might have managed to deceive on a regular day, but was bound to cause trouble at such a critical moment.
Seeing that the taxi had left the sight of the checkpoint, Su Lun got out of the car by the roadside.
Public transportation was no longer an option.
....
Meanwhile, at the command headquarters of the Umbrella Organization's No. 5 City District.
"Headquarters, the suspect has intercepted a taxi, and a set of bloody clothes was found. The information was incorrect, the suspect swapped to the opposite direction heading towards No. 4 City District."
"All units note, thoroughly inspect every passing vehicle at the related route checkpoints, especially public transportation. The target of the suspect is No. 4 City District, urgently retrieve the secret archives of smuggling channels..."
"Just received urgent intelligence, the suspect has impersonated an internal officer and used a Class A code phrase. Everyone, switch to Class B code phrases, communication to transfer to emergency channels."
"..."
One message after another was brought together at the command center by agents from all over the city, and the vast machine of the Umbrella Organization started to move, an invisible net gradually tightening.
....
Su Lun knew riding in a vehicle was no longer safe, but he thought since he had already entered No. 4 City District, he might try going on foot.
However, walking on the street, he soon encountered the patrol security team and members of the "Frost Giant's Armor" city guard squad. Being alone, he was once again asked for his identity papers.
Su Lun thought of employing the same trick that had just worked.
But this time, as soon as he started mentioning the "code phrase," the other party raised their guns.
After a fierce struggle, he barely escaped.
But his whereabouts had also been exposed.
Su Lun knew the Umbrella Organization had fully grasped his movements; it was impossible for him, a stranger in a strange land, to just head near the "No. 7 Research Institute."
For anyone, this situation would have seemed like a dead end, an individual against the entire inner city's defense system, and it was impressive that he had lasted this long.
But in this dire situation, Su Lun became even calmer.
