While his right hand controlled the reanimated corpse to slay the man in black, his left hand had already pulled out a puppet to shield his side.
Almost at the same moment, the cannonball collided with the puppet.
With a loud "boom," the all-defense-rune-equipped puppet was blasted to bits, showing the power of the cannonball.
Su Lun was also blown away by the impact, spitting out a mouthful of dirty blood, "Pu~"
Since the puppet blocked the cannonball that was meant to be lethal, he ignored his own injuries and during his backward flight, he raised his hand and slashed towards the source of the gunfire.
The person hadn't seen the "invisible reanimated corpse" but had heard the whizzing sound of the blade cutting through the air.
The instinctive sense of crisis of a high-class professional made him shatter the glass with a crash and jump out just after firing.
But even with such quick reaction, the armored covering of his upper thigh felt a coldness as a sudden spatial rift appeared and neatly severed both legs. His legless torso, spewing blood, leapt from the window.
The scythe's spatial rift appeared in a blink, and combined with Su Lun's precise striking ability, wherever his gaze locked, the rift appeared right there, almost impossible for anyone to dodge easily.
Having both legs cleanly cut off, the bleeding was enough to cause instantaneous shock, yet the fellow clenched his teeth, relying on one last bit of willpower to pull the trigger on his mechanical arm.
Su Lun wanted to deliver another strike to completely remove this thorn, but just then a burst of blood mist exploded by his side.
He realized something was amiss and quickly dodged.
It was fortunate that the legless man was seriously injured so the cannon had no "locking skill." Su Lun awkwardly rolled on the ground several times, which just so happened to dodge the lethal cannon attack.
On a second look, after firing, the legless man had also completely passed out.
....
Su Lun didn't linger over the corpse, but gazed at the blood mist around him, his brow slightly furrowed, "I've reached the limit..."
Indeed, using the knife too frequently had triggered the backlash to burst forth prematurely.
Three long cuts had sliced the undead into several sections, instantly erasing all signs of life.
The black scythe fell out as well.
Su Lun looked at his "Old Pal" that had helped him greatly, feeling somewhat emotional.
It was unclear whether it was because there was no time to spare or the Umbrella Organization thought that they didn't need many high-rank professionals to deal with Su Lun.
Fortunately, it seemed that there were only these three second-order professionals near Green Street.
"Old Pal" had completed its glorious mission.
Su Lun didn't look further, flicking out the steel wire from his mechanical glove, pulling the scythe and bandages back to his back. He then threw an incendiary grenade onto the body to completely destroy it.
Then he drew his twin guns and started firing at the members of the Umbrella Organization across the street.
....
The three trickiest second-order professionals were killed in a few exchanges, and Su Lun's crisis was instantly alleviated by ninety percent.
Ordinary professionals posed a limited threat to him.
Moreover, in the outer city, there weren't as many people wearing "Frost Titan Armor" as in the inner city.
These folks in coats and hats were the favorite targets of gunmen!
Even if they wore bulletproof vests, too many critical weak spots were exposed on their bodies...
After unleashing his mechanical suit, Su Lun retreated while fighting, using the buildings on Green Street to his advantage. With a pistol in each hand, he pressured the enemy from daring to poke their heads out, while also gathering Soul Shards and loot from the three second-order professionals he had just killed.
Since he had patrolled these blocks countless times before, he knew every alley here.
Having torn a hole in the encirclement, Su Lun reached an alley; just over the fence, and he could immediately jump out of the encirclement.
But just then, he suddenly noticed thick smoke billowing from the street corners.
Instantly, Su Lun knew who had arrived.
However, the sense of hostility was somewhat erratic, and he didn't rush to act.
He knew well, that this was the ability of Smokie.
Seeing the smoke, Su Lun deliberately lowered his gun's muzzle and put on a face of combined shock and joy, excitedly saying towards the thickest part of the smoke, "Smokie boss, is that you? Have you come to rescue me?!"
Upon hearing this, the figure of Smokie slowly emerged from the smoke.
This grim-faced man looked at Su Lun, who had caused a huge commotion, a complex flicker in his eyes hardly noticeable, yet he said, "Yeah. I'll take it from here, you find a chance to escape first."
He could never have anticipated that an insignificant "little fish" by Kai's side would bring him so much trouble!
As he spoke, Smokie, enveloped in thick smoke, slowly walked towards Su Lun.
The dense "malice" also grew more and more tangible.
"Perfect!"
Su Lun, appearing completely unguarded, had a face of ecstatic relief after a narrow escape, and even sheathed his guns back into their holsters.
But his smile had not yet spread across his face when it suddenly stiffened. The next moment, he swiftly pulled the black scythe from his back and slashed down at the figure before him!
The Smokie across from him instantly froze in confusion.
PS. That's all for the extra updates this month, ah... Brothers, crazy call for subscriptions!!!!!

chapters.title: Chapter 126 - 126: Guess If I Dare to Strike a Second Blow
chapters.content:
Su Lun always thought he had hidden himself very well.
After all, the fact that "Isaac's Alchemical Notebook" had remained undetected in the gang's warehouse for so long proved that his initial plan to deceive everyone had been successful.
But what he couldn't figure out was why, even after the goods had been delivered to the inner city, they were still robbed.
The high-ranking members of the organization had previously questioned him via communication why he had omitted such important information and why they had arranged for a "Lei" to join the escort team, who not only took the manuscript but also caused such a commotion...
How the hell would I know!
The strength of the ordinary gang members in the outer city—isn't that clear to you?
The members of the Cross Society on Green Street are merely shrimps; who in the gang doesn't know that?
The only professional in the escort team was the kid Kai, and he wasn't even at the scene, so who knew he'd have a "little brother" who's an almost second-tier expert?
A firearms expert, suspected to have a gold-quality spider alchemical implant, who masters the spell "No-Shi"...
If an ordinary professional could possess even one of these qualities, they'd definitely be a core member of the Cross Society, yet Su Lun hadn't revealed a slightest hint of it before.
Su Lun felt wronged when questioned by his superiors.
Are you sure you don't want to investigate if there's any defected elite from a special institution in the inner city, instead of asking when the outer city raised such a monster?
Could such elite first-order professionals possibly be cultivated in a place like the outer city, where resources are scarce?
And another thing!
With the Security Bureau, Mechanical City Guard, and numerous experts in the inner city, they can't even handle a first-order professional?
Su Lun felt that those guys had become too complacent because of their safe living environments, losing their basic hunting abilities.
No matter how strong, Su Lun was still a first-tier professional!
Even just a quarter of an hour ago, when Su Lun was notified to join the joint ambush, he couldn't believe that the unknown little gang member named "Su Lun" had just killed twenty or thirty pursuers in the inner city and escaped?!
But now,
seeing everything in front of him,
he believed it.
Just a minute ago, he had heard the report through the communicator that three second-tier officers from the umbrella organization participating in the pursuit had all been killed.
....
Su Lun blocked Su Lun's way, his expression complex.
Was it because he possessed a "Cursed Weapon"?
How could Su Lun not recognize that large black scythe? It was with that very "Cursed Weapon" that they had broken into the vault of the Cross Society headquarters.
The scythe was then taken away by an accomplice.
Later, when he heard no news of the accomplice returning to the city, he thought he had died in some corner of the sewers, but who would have thought... it ended up in this kid's hands?
The power of that cursed weapon was indeed formidable, almost beyond solution, but its cursed nature was also fatal. It was impossible to use it as a regular weapon.
Yet, even with the cursed weapon, the black scythe, a professional who kills three people in succession with it should have exploded to death by now!
Su Lun hadn't caught up with the previous fight, and now, watching Su Lun who greeted him with a smile, he thought he hadn't been exposed.
Then, unexpectedly, he was struck down by a fierce blow without warning.
....
"Fuck! How did this kid suddenly turn violent—could it be that I've been exposed?"
If one could hear Su Lun's thoughts at the moment, that would certainly be the curse.
Confused, the immense terror of death approaching instantly made his hairs stand on end.
As the black scythe swung down, a spacetime rift immediately appeared in front of Su Lun.
If this strike were to land solidly, it would split his entire neck diagonally in half.
But Smoke Ghost was, after all, an established second-order professional of many years.
Although Su Lun's movements were fluid and he had the advantage of a surprise attack, his slashing motion was too predictable. As soon as he began, Smoke Ghost instinctively sensed the danger and started to evade with all his might.
However, the space rift caused by the black scythe was simply too fast.
With a swing of the blade, the rift was upon him.
A sharp "swish" as metal cut through silk sounded, and blood sprayed, as an arm dropped to the ground with a thud.
Smoke Ghost's body, meanwhile, dissipated into dense fog, instantly merging with the surrounding mist.
"Didn't kill him, huh..."
Su Lun looked at the broken wall, his pupils slightly contracting.
The Octopus Spear was yanked, and his robes tore, pulling out a few "Wailing Dolls" and "Sneering Dolls" to protect all around his body.
He tightly gripped the black scythe in his hand, staring intently at the surrounding dense fog.
Not being able to kill Smoke Ghost with one strike was also within expectations.
The reason he had successfully killed those three second-order professionals from the Umbrella Organization before was chiefly because they didn't know about the black scythe in his hand, nor did they notice the "invisible living corpse," completely off-guard.
But Smoke Ghost had already seen the scythe on him and instinctively was on guard.
Moreover, Smoke Ghost had a very special ability.
Su Lun had often heard Kai boast about how formidable his old team captain, Smoke Ghost, was and had even detailed Smoke Ghost's strangely unpredictable ability in combat that he had witnessed.
Just now, despite Smoke Ghost trusting Su Lun's words and walking out without any guard, this crafty old fox also had habitual defensive measures.
The mist that constantly floated behind him was a cover, possessing an ability similar to "refracting shadows."
You see a person before you, but their actual position isn't there.
It's like a fish in clear water, you aim for the shadow with a harpoon, but you'll surely miss.
This is extremely practical in combat. The enemy aims for his heart, fires, and then finds the shot goes through thin air or hits a non-lethal spot.
That mist could even confuse all kinds of perception used by professionals.
So, that strike just now was also just Su Lun's prediction of Smoke Ghost's approximate location.
Being able to chop off an arm was already a good result. (Don't ask why he didn't slash horizontally. A wide-ranging horizontal slash would inevitably lead to a fatal backlash.)
....
Having an arm severed in their first confrontation, Smoke Ghost was filled with anger, but also a profound wariness.
The moment Su Lun revealed his killing intent, Smoke Ghost genuinely felt an imminent threat of death.
Seeing the "click-clack" drifting runes and grotesque dolls around Su Lun, alongside the black scythe he clutched in his hand, Smoke Ghost didn't dare show his face from within the fog, fearing another blow.
"How did you get [Xiupunos's Night Scythe] in your hands?"
The voice arose from all directions, echoing like in a valley, making it impossible to pinpoint his location.
Su Lun watched with the corner of his mouth lifted, sneering, "What do you think?"
Within his perception, that "malice" also dispersed, as if it was everywhere around him.
The fog could hide all traces of his being.
A most troublesome ability.
From within the fog, a cold laugh came: "Hehe... what if it is? You've already swung once, dare to swing a second time and the curse's backlash will immediately claim your life!"
Smoke Ghost thought Su Lun was unaware of the curse properties of the black scythe and specifically reminded him.
"Oh?"
Su Lun laughed casually, showing his white teeth and replied with a taunting tone: "Whether I dare swing a second time, why don't you come out and test me?"
Smoke Ghost was right.
The curse rebound was directly related to the physical strength of the user. A normal person's body was far inferior to that of a rune zombie. Striking twice in a row would most likely result in immediate death on the spot.
But the Smoke Ghost did not know that Su Lun had precisely controlled the power of the spatial rift.
The cut just now had been close enough, and the wound was not big. The rebound would be much smaller than last time in the cave.
If his damage calculations were correct, he figured he could strike at least four or five times before triggering an immediate rebound.
As soon as he said this, there was indeed no sound from within the smoke.
The Smoke Ghost did not dare to gamble with his life.
Besides, he did not need to show himself to kill someone.
"How come... Mr. Sang Bu is afraid to show himself now?"
Su Lun continued to provoke with his words.
Both chose this moment for a verbal confrontation, each with their own intentions,
Su Lun wanted the enemy to speak up, reveal more flaws, and to lock onto his location.
And the old schemer, Smoke Ghost, wary of the black scythe in his hand, did not dare to show himself, yet still spoke. In fact, it was to disguise his "invisible killer move."
The smoke growing thicker around seemed innocuous apart from obscuring vision, but in reality, it hid deadly intentions.
Su Lun, looking at the anomalies on the data panel, sneered. He was not flustered and directly took out the "Plague Doctor's Beak Mask" he had acquired earlier and put it on his face.
Because... there was a special fire poison in this smoke that even a gas mask couldn't filter out!
Seeing Su Lun suddenly taking out a gas mask and putting it on, the Smoke Ghost realized that his tactic had been seen through.
He had harbored some disdain, as his fire poison was a mixed damage spell of smoke and spell, which ordinary gas masks could not filter.
But upon seeing the peculiar beak design, the Smoke Ghost immediately exclaimed in surprise, "Is that Sergei's beak mask?"
Then, he realized something, and shock spread through the smoke again, "Did you kill Sergei?"
"Yes... Mr. Smoke Ghost, it will be your turn soon."
Su Lun continued his verbal onslaught, having roughly pinpointed the Smoke Ghost's location from the emotional fluctuations a moment ago.
But at a squeeze of the black knife, the guy disappeared again.
A few trick dolls were also patrolling nearby. The moment an opportunity arose, he would not hesitate to swing his blade down.
Meanwhile, Su Lun continued to taunt, "I'm also curious, how did you become a member of the Umbrella Organization... Mr. Inside Agent?"
A scornful laugh came from within the smoke, as the Smoke Ghost guessed Su Lun's thoughts, "Heh... You're trying to enrage me?"
The mist had now spread throughout the entire alley, no one would enter, and the voices could not get out.
He knew that as long as he did not show himself, that "Su Lun" was as good as dead!
In a contest between clever minds, victory and defeat lay in the details, and now it was about who could keep their cool.
Su Lun glanced at the increasingly thick mist around his body, "Oh? You think that without showing yourself, the fire poison will definitely kill me?"
The Smoke Ghost responded disdainfully, "Haven't you already felt it?"
"Heh heh..."
The smile in Su Lun's eyes grew increasingly ferocious.
He indeed had already felt the damage from the fire poison.
Looking at his skin, the burning sensation was fiercely stabbing at his nerves, a severe pain unbearable for ordinary people.
This thick white smoke not only scorched the heart, lungs, and respiratory tract but also permeated through the pores. In just this short moment, Su Lun had already felt a fiery burning sensation on his skin. His skin was gradually drying out and heating up, slowly turning the yellow-brown of tree bark after a fire, then gradually becoming a layer of charred ashes.
Without the Smoke Ghost lifting a finger, if things dragged on, he would be burned alive.
Moreover, reinforcements from the Umbrella Organization were continuously arriving. He could not delay and had to force the Smoke Ghost to act!
He had some reservations, but now, seeming to have no choice, Su Lun pulled out a green syringe, glanced at it, and decisively jabbed it into his neck.
Amid the smoke, the "Smoke Ghost" witnessed the scene and let out a cold laugh, "Healing medicine? Heh... you think too little of my 'Ash Poison'."
With his head tilted, Su Lun pushed in the potion, and a cooling sensation immediately surged to his forehead.
The sneer on his face became even more unfathomable as he mocked with a dismissive tone, "Oh... really?"
Because he could see his own data panel, he had once thoroughly tested the healing data of various healing medicines.
He also knew very well that even the best potion he had at the moment couldn't negate this kind of ongoing, cumulative fire damage.
But the moment this potion went down, a miraculous scene occurred.
The skin on Su Lun's body that had just been scorched and dry began to slowly heal!
Moreover, as if the healing was overflowing, his entire being was pulsating with a mighty life force, completely nullifying the burn damage of the fire poison.
"Huh..."
Seeing this, a light exclamation came from within the smoke.
Clearly, the Smoke Ghost was also astonished and asked, "What potion is this?"
"Do you want to know?"
Su Lun felt that his current state was excellent and taunted with a grin, "Too bad, I won't tell you."
However, after the violent energy healed the injury, it didn't settle down. Like a dam bursting, at first, it moistened the soil with spring water, and soon after, it became a violent flash flood, rampaging through his meridians and muscles. It seemed to want to destroy everything, to rebuild chaos.
So this was the feeling of a "Pre-Mutation Precursor"?
Su Lun felt that sensation as if a balloon were about to burst, teetering on the edge of life and death.
But it was also within his expectations. Unperturbed, he injected another potion into his neck. The coolness poured into his brain, instantly suppressing that explosive feeling.
Good.
The potion Su Lun injected wasn't an ordinary one, but the [X Serum Original Liquid] and [Mutation Suppression Medicine]!
The serum would transform his body, causing the cell activity to surge several times within a very short period, greatly enhancing his own healing ability.
Although it wouldn't reach the level of that "Abomination Warrior" from before, it seemed to be enough to withstand the fire poison.
....
The serum had only a 75% success rate, but at this critical moment, there was no room for Su Lun to hesitate.
The Smoke Ghost was clearly buying time, and if the delay continued, even if Su Lun could kill him, he wouldn't be able to escape the city in the end.
Besides, he had another plan for choosing to inject the "X Serum."
He had already used the Black Scythe once, and the backlash would appear in an hour.
Although the wound wouldn't be significant, to be on the safe side, his best option was to find a skilled doctor to help save his life, like Danny on Green Street, for instance.
But!
Currently under siege and needing to leave the city, he had no chance to wait for treatment.
Moreover, to kill the Smoke Ghost, he would need at least another slash at best!
When the double backlash of the curse erupted, his situation would be dire.
So, he thought of this "fight poison with poison" approach.
The super recovery ability brought by the "X Serum" could help him preserve his life to the maximum extent upon the sudden appearance of a wound.
The serum could not only solve the immediate problem of the fire poison but also the hidden threat of the backlash.
A 75% success rate was already enough for him to make a decision.
And.
After injecting the potion, Su Lun also gained the confidence to take the offensive!

chapters.title: Chapter 127 - 127 "§" Symbol
chapters.content:
Now that fire poison couldn't harm Su Lun, the Smoke Ghost's plan had fallen through.
If he didn't attack proactively, he wouldn't be able to do anything to Su Lun.
And Su Lun wasn't about to sit around and wait for death; he took control of the eight-armed spider spear and started to sprint.
He had previously been wary of being located by the Smoke Ghost and killed instantly due to any vulnerability shown, but now, after injecting the "X Potion," his body's resilience, resistance, and recovery ability were becoming stronger.
He was now confident that the Smoke Ghost couldn't kill him in one hit.
Rather, once the opponent couldn't help but act, it would be the moment to decide the winner.
Although he couldn't see his surroundings with his eyes, Su Lun could still generally distinguish which direction was south and charged headlong in that direction.
The spider legs possessed the ability to bypass obstacles as if teleporting; climbing over walls and scaling buildings without regard to the presence of a path, his speed increased more and more.
However, even so, the cloud of smoke pursued relentlessly, shadowing him closely.
Even in a relentless sprint that left him wide open, Su Lun simply didn't care.
The two chased each other from Green Street all the way south.
Su Lun had assumed the Smoke Ghost would not be able to resist attacking upon seeing his vulnerabilities, especially since heading towards the complex terrain outside the city would be even less favorable for the pursuer.
But unexpectedly, while both were seeking an opportunity to kill the other, something unforeseen happened.
A figure in a cloak came running at high speed, blocking the path ahead.
The figure began with a question, "Sambu, are you from the Umbrella Organization?"
The voice was disguised, indistinguishable as male or female.
....
Su Lun, seeing someone obstructing him, initially thought a high-ranking professional from the Umbrella Organization had arrived.
But upon seeing the cloak for an instant, his expression immediately became complicated.
The person was dressed in a black cloak, the design old-fashioned, with an obscured face.
It appeared somewhat like the concealment cloaks used within the secretive higher echelons of the black market, but the material and craft were visibly several grades higher.
It wasn't just ordinary plain black; the cloak featured elegantly simple patterns in golden lines, depicting snakes, eagles, lizards, fire dragons, thorny roses... symbols often found as allegories in alchemical texts.
The golden patterns on the cloak seemed decorative, but combined, they also resembled some complex alchemical formation, giving off a strong sense of mystery upon closer inspection.
The cloak looked like it was from a genuinely venerable ancient noble family.
Moreover, what particularly caught Su Lun's attention was another factor.
The instant the person had caught up to him, Su Lun had seen a golden "§" symbol on the back of the cloak.
Su Lun had encountered this symbol only twice before—once was when he had arrived in this world, in the underground altar of the Storm Manor, where one of the five statues had this symbol engraved upon it.
The other time was the seal at the center of the eight-pointed star on the back of the [Isaac's Alchemical Manuscript III] he held.
This was the third time he had seen it on the cloak.
Su Lun speculated the symbol was related to a certain S-rank talent.
Because when he had awoken [S-018-All-knowing Eye], the statue with the "ꧧ" symbol had shattered along with it; then when he awoke [S-004-Reaper of Death], the statute with the "☽" symbol also broke apart.
Usually, an obvious symbol on attire represents an organization.
Like the "Iron Cross Star" of the Cross Society.
This cloaked person must be from a mysterious organization.
Su Lun's first reaction was that it was Mr. Hei, given that Mr. Hei would have known he'd been to 88 Ginkgo Street's basement.
But given the aggressive demeanor of the cloaked person, he quickly dismissed the thought.
Mr. Hei always radiated calm, like a still well, whereas this figure was emanating a fiery presence, an overt aggression.
Since he didn't sense any "malice," Su Lun also stopped, not making any sudden moves.
The other had caught up in just a few bounds, indicating formidable physical strength.
Now that he was confronting the Smoke Ghost, the situation appeared not to be that of enemies.
...
Hearing the cloaked figure's demand, the Smoke Ghost asked in a deep voice, "Who might you be?"
The cloaked figure didn't respond, instead pressing further with the question, "You only need to answer, yes or no."
The Smoke Ghost obviously couldn't lie with his eyes open especially with Su Lun, who was privy to the truth, at his side. He could only shift the topic, "What does that have to do with you?"
"Then that's it," replied the cloaked figure with a somewhat domineering tone.
You won't admit it, it doesn't matter,
If I say you are, then you are.
As he spoke, his aura grew increasingly intense, apparently ready to take action.
The Smoke Ghost found the cloaked figure's pressing nature baffling and let out a cold snort.
But aware of the figure's ill intent, he no longer concealed himself and spoke plainly, "Since you know I am 'Umbrella', what is your intent in stopping me?"
From the cloaked person's aura, the Smoke Ghost deduced that the figure was surely a high-ranking professional. If it came to blows now, he, with an arm already lost, would definitely be at a disadvantage.
Moreover, there was a guy with a scythe, watching eagerly from the sidelines.
If his presence were to be revealed, he knew he would be in grave danger.
"What do you mean? Of course to kill you!"
But unexpectedly, invoking the identity of the "Umbrella Organization" did not improve the situation for the smoker; the cloaked person's aura flared up even more, and with a stomp, they charged at the puff of smoke!
....
"So strong!"
Su Lun's pupils shrank.
Just by observing the blast generated by the cloaked person's stomp on the ground, it was clear their close combat prowess was incredibly strong.
This was an advanced charging technique. That stomp was not just to exert force on the ground with the foot, but also to compress the air into a shockwave to propel oneself forward.
However, this straight into combat approach suggested a very explosive personality.
Yet knowing full well that the smoker was a member of the Umbrella Organization, they still dared to make a move?
In all of Old Lington, there truly weren't many people or forces that would dare to actively oppose the Umbrella Organization.
At this point, a thought suddenly flashed in Su Lun's mind.
When he had gone to the black market to inquire about news, someone had mentioned that a month ago, the woman who had bombed the west city laboratory and had a bounty on her head, was cornered in the north city by the Umbrella Organization.
Just as they were about to finish her off, a "third party force" appeared, tore through the Umbrella Organization's encirclement, and allowed the woman to escape once again.
Could this cloaked person be that "third party force"?
Although he guessed this, Su Lun wasn't planning on watching the fight between the high-level professionals play out.
With someone else holding off the smoker, there was no need for him to risk taking a second slash with the black scythe.
He was just about to take the chance to slip away when, unexpectedly...
The battle began abruptly and ended even more suddenly!
Even Su Lun, who had mentally prepared for the cloaked person's interception of the smoker and knew they were probably not weak, was filled with disbelief at the scene before him.
....
The smoker was concealed within the fog, a challenge for anyone to kill.
But unexpectedly, upon encounter, the cloaked person released their full power instantly!
When they burst forth, the deadly aura that flared like flames suddenly exploded, growing higher and higher.
In that instant, the purple-black flames condensed into an eerie phantom figure with a seductive face but exuding a dignified aura, resembling the image of a Rakshasa Woman from ancient mythology. With flame-like vertical hair and six muscular arms each wielding a weapon, it was indeed the figure from ancient myths.
"A mythological talent [A-022-Rakshasa Woman]?"
Su Lun's gaze stuttered as he remembered the description of this rare talent from the books he'd read.
"No, even an A-rank talent couldn't possibly be this strong!"
He recalled the talent's description of greatly enhancing one's physical body from the books, but he had never heard of a talent manifesting such an external phenomenon.
And in all of Old Spiriton Outer City, those with A-rank talents were usually widely known figures, yet he hadn't heard of anyone awakening such a mythological talent.
Could it be... a secondary awakening of talent like Danny's?
Who could this person be?
Su Lun had no time to ponder.
Because the fight was already over.
The cloaked person moved so swiftly, like a shooting star; their strength was so overpowering that they sent the smoker, hidden in the thick fog, flying with a single blow, spitting blood!
Even though the smoker had lost an arm, he was still a bonafide veteran professional of the second order.
Defeated in just one encounter?
Lying on the ground, spitting blood continuously, the smoker's face was as pale as death; apparently, he recognized the cloaked person and, filled with fear and shock, exclaimed, "It's you! How can you be this strong?!"
But in the next instant, the cloaked person didn't give him a chance to speak anymore, flickered, and delivered a savage kick to his head.
A chilling crack of breaking bones resounded.
The veteran member of the Cross Society, the long-established professional of the second order, "the Reaper" Sambu Kachinsky, was dead on the spot!
....
The fight was over before he even had a chance to escape.
Su Lun looked at the explosive crime scene, clenched the big black scythe in his hand tightly and then relaxed his grip, his face showing a mix of confusion, shock, and contemplation.
Her voice, face, even her figure could change with that cloak.
But the style was unmistakably familiar.
Thinking back to the smoker's expression before he died, Su Lun had a good guess about who this person was.
It was just beyond his expectation how overwhelmingly strong she had become...
What on earth was going on with this Cross Society, that they had an insider from the Umbrella Organization, and how did she become that "third party force"?
At that moment, the cloaked person, noticing that Su Lun hadn't fled and was looking at her with wide-eyed surprise, seemed incredulous and asked, "Do you recognize me?"
Hearing her tone, Su Lun grew even more certain of his conjecture and replied with a complex expression, "Yes, Sister Qiantiao..."

chapters.title: Chapter 128 - 128: Leaving the City (Extra for '3000 monthly tickets not yet reached')
chapters.content:
Su Lun had once thought that Qian Tiao might come to rescue him.
But he never expected that this gambling-addicted lady was so absurdly strong!
She supposedly ranked the same as the 'smoke ghouls' as a second-tier executive, yet now she demonstrated strength that completely overwhelmed those of her rank, slaying someone with a single encounter!
On further thought, if she truly was the "third-party force" opposing the Umbrella Organization, the situation had grown even more delicate.
As Rena's aunt, could the recent turmoil within the Reyes family hold some other hidden meanings?
What about Lady Philo, the benefactor behind the Cross Society?
And Mr. Hei?
A series of questions.
Su Lun's mind instantly formed a web of underground forces that involved both the inner and outer cities.
Qian Tiao's emergence was like revealing the tip of an iceberg, but what was hidden under the sea was still an even more colossal unknown and mystery.
In order to contend with the Black Tower, a corresponding level of strength, financial power, and manpower was necessary.
This "third-party force" already possessed all of these.
Although unknown to outsiders, the strength of the organization was undeniable.
...
Su Lun knew that since Qian Tiao came wearing a cloak of special significance, she naturally wouldn't favor using her original identity.
Perhaps the Cross Society could not afford the cost of antagonizing the Umbrella Organization right now, hoping for that "third-party force" to take charge.
Qian Tiao came over without any intention of taking off her cloak.
But the moment she spoke, the air of mystery vanished, "Oh dear, you actually recognized me. I originally didn't plan to meet you like this. But you should understand that if I came in that identity, many things would become inconvenient."
Whether it was the tone of voice or the content of her words, Su Lun was certain this was definitely that gambling-addicted lady.
A Cross Society executive, naturally, would not conveniently assassinate someone from the Umbrella Organization.
Hearing Qian Tiao's words, he asked, "Sister Qian Tiao, did you come to rescue me?"
Qian Tiao replied bluntly, "Yes. That girl Rena sent me a frantic message, saying you ran into danger in the inner city and asked me to think of a way. My original plan was to mobilize relations within the inner city to assist you. I had run halfway there only to unexpectedly intercept combat intelligence from the Umbrella Organization, learning that you had actually escaped.
Then rushing back here, I was delayed a bit more time."
Su Lun sincerely said, "Thank you, Sister Qian Tiao."
"I've said before, you're under my protection. Is there a need to be so formal?"
Qian Tiao looked indifferent.
Knowing her character, Su Lun didn't bother with more pleasantries.
After a pause, Qian Tiao gave Su Lun another glance, her tone laced with a hint of teasing, "I also heard that you have taken Rena hostage. I have no idea why that girl is still so helpfully on your side."
Su Lun shrugged self-deprecatingly, obviously aware that she was joking, and laughed, "You knew about that, too?"
Qian Tiao's tone was somewhat peculiar, "Yes. Not just me, every major family in the inner city is now in an uproar. They thought another 'great purge' was about to happen a few months ago and were terrified, trembling with fear, everywhere inquiring about the origins of this robber who dared to hold the Reyes family heiress hostage in broad daylight in the inner city."
"..."
Su Lun raised an eyebrow as he listened.
The Umbrella Organization certainly wouldn't divulge that the cause of the incident was their attempt to ambush a transport team from an outer city gang, only to be counter-slaughtered.
But the ruckus he had caused beforehand on "Dunwich Commercial Street" could not be concealed, and most likely, the case would be closed with him labeled as a common robber.
Without the intention of elaborating, Qian Tiao said, "Let's go, we'll talk as we walk."
Su Lun: "Where to?"
"To take you out of the city," Qian Tiao explained. "The Umbrella Organization has some formidable trackers. Now that you've stirred up such a commotion, they will spare no cost to hunt you down. It's impossible for you to stay in Old Lington City, better to leave and lay low for a while.
I can't afford to expose myself right now, otherwise, if something happens, I might not be able to take care of you."
"Oh, then wait for me."
Su Lun said this and, without forgetting, headed towards the smoke ghoul's corpse.
Under the guise of stripping the Storage Ring and 'onboarding materials' from the body, he also harvested the Soul Shard.
Silver onboarding material [Haines's Rune Pipe], a profession material for the second-tier "Ash Magician"; second-level silver prosthesis [Time Eater Hourglass], granting the ability to warp light and remain invisible amidst smoke.
These were very practical profession materials for the assassin line.
If it were not unsuitable for Su Lun's Puppeteer career path, he would have quite liked the smoke ghoul's ability to emit smoke and conceal himself.
(Curse Fusion Principle: After a professional advances, the curse characteristics of the onboarding materials will merge, and typically, a body will produce only one high-tier onboarding material and prosthesis.)
As for the memories he stripped, they were all as Su Lun had guessed, some information about the smoke ghoul being an internal spy for the Umbrella Organization.
The rest was just a boost in experience.
....
Watching Su Lun gather the spoils of war from the smoke ghoul's corpse, Qian Tiao didn't say anything either.
Their relationship didn't warrant such formality.
But at that moment, she also noticed the beak mask still on Su Lun's face and couldn't help but ask curiously, "Did you kill 'Plague Doctor' Sergei?"
"Yeah."
Su Lun nodded.
Qian Tiao was visibly incredulous, then said, "That guy's abilities are quite troublesome, specializing in Curse Magic and capable of resurrection... Most second-tier professionals can't handle him; I didn't expect you could actually kill him?"
"Well..."
Su Lun didn't know how to explain, since that was Mr. Hei's trap after all.
Seeing the cloak on Qian Tiao, though he had already guessed, he still asked, "Sister Qian Tiao, do you know Mr. Hei?"
Upon hearing this, Qian Tiao's tone changed to one of surprise, and rather than answering, she asked back, "Huh... How do you know about Mr. Hei?"
Upon hearing her response, Su Lun inwardly sighed "As I thought."
The third-party force, and Mr. Hei, or rather the mysterious organizer of the Shadow Alley black market, have a direct relationship.
He bluntly said, "I killed Sergei using some special means. But this involves some of Mr. Hei's secrets, and I'm not at liberty to say. Since you know him, Qian Tiao, you might as well ask Mr. Hei directly."
"Oh."
Qian Tiao didn't press the matter further.
After Su Lun had sorted out the spoils of battle from the smoke fiend and tossed an incendiary bomb to erase any traces, the two of them headed towards the southern city wall.
With such an expert providing high-level protection, Su Lun finally let out a sigh of relief from the sense of urgency that had been chasing him all day.
...
Compared to his curiosity about Qian Tiao's hidden identity, Qian Tiao was more curious about the various unthinkable methods Su Lun had displayed.
She looked at the calm Su Lun with a rather complex tone, "Even if I hadn't come, the smoke fiend wouldn't necessarily have been able to kill you, right?"
"Hmm."
Su Lun didn't deny it, calmly responding, "But the likelihood of me dying was also quite high."
"Tsk tsk, you really are stunningly impressive. The smoke fiend guy has strong assassination capabilities, ordinary second-tier professionals would suffer a great loss, but you managed to hold your own and even broke off one of his arms..."
Qian Tiao mused as she said this, as if something occurred to her, "Eh... did you know in advance about the smoke fiend's identity?"
Su Lun felt there was no point in hiding it, as Qian Tiao's influence would eventually uncover the existence of that card during the escort mission, and he said, "Yes. Didn't we go to escort some goods for handover in the inner city before..."
He briefly explained how he discovered the card and then deduced the reasoning process that the smoke fiend was an insider.
Qian Tiao, listening on the side, was amazed, "You really are meticulous in your thinking..."
Just then, looking at the large scythe on Su Lun's back, she asked, "How did that scythe come into your possession?"
"Picked it up on the way during the last dungeon trial."
"You used that scythe to chop off the smoke fiend's arm earlier?"
"Hmm."
Upon hearing this, Qian Tiao's tone suddenly turned grave, "This is a bit troublesome... The curse backlash from that sealed item is quite lethal. Hang on, let me make some contacts, and get you to an outside medical team, but time is tight, and we might not make it in time. Hopefully, we can save your life, kid..."
"Uh... I think it shouldn't be that bad. I can handle some of it myself. If possible, just having a doctor help out would be fine."
"Ah? I think you may not be aware of the curse properties of that black scythe."
"No, I'm aware."
"..."
Su Lun now had the spider arms, a trivial matter like stitching was a piece of cake.
Moreover, during his research on the living corpses, he had also brushed up on some emergency surgical knowledge and had learned to use the set of emergency equipment from the Black Tower Academy.
As long as it wasn't an instantly fatal wound like having the brain bisected, it wasn't a big issue.
He could solve it by himself.
Furthermore, now that he had the super recovery power from the "X Serum" modification and the "Life Conversion Alchemy Formation" he had learned from Lena, with these multiple layers of protection, Su Lun felt that the probability of dying on the spot was not great.
But having one or two doctors to help would be even better.
...
The two of them quickly reached the southern city wall. They did not go through the city gate; Su Lun climbed over the wall with his spider arms, while Qian Tiao leaped over the wall in a few bounds.
"I've arranged a wilderness hunting team from the inner city for you and set up a new identity. You'll go with them. There are great opportunities at the Dawn City Ruins but also great dangers... You're more cautious than I thought, so I don't need to say much more," Qian Tiao said.
"Hmm."
As they walked and talked, Qian Tiao had already arranged everything for Su Lun.
What he thought was an escape seemed more like a casual outing with a wilderness hunting group.
"Hmm. Qian Tiao, there's something I need to trouble you with. I rent a basement on Green Street where I've left some things. If it's convenient for you, could you clear it out for me?"
"Sure."
"Oh, and in the basement at 16 Green Street is a friend of mine. His name is Danny, a very skilled Pharmacist. I'm worried the Umbrella Organization might trace him, could you look after him for me?"
"Hmm."
"Qian Tiao, that external phantom you manifested earlier, was that a talent second awakening?"
"Eh... you know about that too? That's high-end knowledge relevant to top-level professionals, even info that the inner city has sealed off..."
"..."
As the two were talking, Qian Tiao noticed that Su Lun's face had turned an eerie shade of blue.
She asked, "Eh... Are you poisoned? Why is your skin turning blue?"
"..."
Su Lun felt somewhat helpless.
If she had appeared earlier, he wouldn't have had to take the risk with the "X Serum."
But it seemed to be a blessing in disguise.
Since there were no mutations, it should have been a success.
...
Qian Tiao never explained the issue about her cloak's identity, and Su Lun didn't ask.
But as they parted, Qian Tiao left him with a meaningful piece of advice, "Strive to grow stronger... Only from a high vantage can you see a different landscape."
"Hmm."
Su Lun smiled faintly.
Even with just a few words, Su Lun heard the implied meaning; he was not yet qualified to touch those high-end secrets.
PS. Brothers, please subscribe!

chapters.title: Chapter 129 - 129: Voodoo Doll
chapters.content:
The energy in both the inner and outer cities was immense.
Even after the incident Su Lun caused in Old Lington, she managed to find a decent doctor within an hour to help Su Lun deal with the backlash of the Black Sickle Curse.
Because Su Lun precisely controlled the strength of his slash, the curse backlash wound from the Black Sickle was not severe. With the help of the "X Serum" and the expensive life-prolonging "Life Transmutation Alchemy Formation," he made it through without any real danger.
Then it was time for the escape plan.
Originally, Su Lun intended to go alone and find an opportunity to join a miscellaneous group to Dawn City, but Qian Tiao's arrangement was clearly more appropriate.
She arranged a legal identity for Su Lun.
To avoid exposing his identity, Qian Tiao didn't arrange for him to join a Scavenger group associated with the Cross Society. Instead, she had him join a merchant caravan from the inner city.
Su Lun became a freelance sniper hired for a Scavenger Guild mission, possessing a registered badge and a series of recognized certificates issued by the Scavenger Guild, and his background could withstand scrutiny. He replaced a Scavenger called "Johnny."
....
One day, a massive transportation team was making its way through the deep, dark catacombs at a steady pace.
This was the seventh day Su Lun had been accompanying the "Thornbird Merchant Caravan."
In the team, the roar of steam machinery was constant, coming from dozens of steam-powered mechanical dogs. These simple mechanical animals lacked combat capabilities but could carry heavy loads, and their smaller size allowed them to navigate through the rugged mine tunnels of the catacombs. They were the mainstream means of transport used by Scavengers for hauling heavy items.
A large Scavenger camp was currently being constructed near Dawn City, requiring a lot of building materials. It was a good opportunity for merchants to make money, so there were a large number of transportation teams heading underground during this period.
The Scavengers, who were just about to undertake relic hunting in the ruins, also took on the merchants' hiring as a side job to earn some money for escorting the cargo.
The owner of the goods had hired five fully equipped small-scale Scavenger groups and some reputable lone Scavengers from the Scavenger Guild. There were about one to two hundred people in total—Su Lun blended in without attracting any attention.
Even though they had already encountered several small-scale mutant monster attacks over the past few days, which resulted in a few deaths, fortunately, there weren't any significant losses.
And because "Johnny" was a hired lone Scavenger, he had few acquaintances and hung at the back of the team without anyone bothering him.
Of course, this was a loner persona Su Lun deliberately crafted to conceal the abnormalities of his body.
Due to the side effects of the "X Potion," his skin had turned blue.
To avoid attracting suspicion, he always wore a gas mask and had expensive prosthetic skin gloves on his hands, leaving no bit of skin exposed.
Fortunately, Scavengers hunting in the catacombs are usually fully armed, so this disguise was not particularly conspicuous.
...
The transportation team moved steadily towards the depths of the ground.
On his back Su Lun carried a backpack and a large black box, which was a sniper rifle case used to hide the presence of his scythe, as he had failed to find a new body to create a living corpse in the past few days.
While walking, a thirteen or fourteen-year-old boy happily ran towards the tail of the team.
He was waving a gas mask in his hand and shook it at Su Lun, excitedly saying, "Mister Johnny, can you help me see what's wrong with my mask..."
This half-grown lad was named Tommy and was the youngest son of the leader of the "Drunkard Scavenger Group." Because he longed for adventure, his big-hearted father had brought him along.
The day before yesterday, during an unexpected mutant monster attack from above, Su Lun casually killed a monster and saved this boy, who was almost bitten in the neck. As a result, he earned the friendship of the Drunkard's group.
After his father brought him to thank Su Lun, the boy didn't act shy and would occasionally ask Su Lun for advice on marksmanship and mechanical skills.
"Mister Johnny, your parrot mask is really pretty," he said.
Tommy looked at the mask on Su Lun's face with eyes full of envy and pouted, "Compared to yours, mine looks like a 'Ugly Duckling Mask'."
"Heh, let me see..."
Su Lun took the so-called Ugly Duckling Mask from him. He didn't find it bothersome and examined it carefully.
Of course, there was no comparison.
The mask that Su Lun wore was not an ordinary gas mask but a Plague Doctor's Beak Mask that he had modified.
He had killed Sergey and thought he wouldn't need the thing.
But unexpectedly, after injecting himself with Serum X, Su Lun found that his cell activity became extremely high, and his body could automatically metabolize even slight toxins without any effect on him.
He had also tested the mask's curse features a few days ago. By carefully observing the attribute panel, he concluded that his current cell activity could almost withstand the side effects of the mask. Coupled with the top-grade antidote potions refined by Danny, the chances of being poisoned to death were extremely low.
Thinking it was necessary to wear a gas mask to cover his face anyway, he decided to simply modify the appearance of the beak mask.
After all, whether it was the 99% protection rate against poisons or the long-term wear that could enhance his resistance to toxins, there were no better gas masks than it.
But because it was a trophy object, in order not to be recognized, Su Lun had also transformed the originally cool and mysterious beak mask into a gaudy "Parrot Mask."
Not only did he change the main color from black to the yellow-green of a parrot, but he also added a mechanical device like a windshield wiper to clear the vision of the goggles. He even added a piece of mysterious-looking black cloth to cover the beak. This was the mainstream punk style in the market.
It was a simple mechanical modification, but it completely changed the style of the mask, making it look now "common."
Yet it was precisely this useless modification that caught little Tommy's keen interest.
Watching Su Lun check his work, Tommy muttered to the side, "Mr. Johnny, I want to make automatic flip-up goggles so that it can rest on the hat when I need a wider field of vision. But it always creaks, and no matter how much oil I apply, it still feels stiff..."
"Oh?"
Su Lun noticed that the young Tommy had a talent for mechanics, at least the idea was interesting.
He took a simple look and pinpointed the problem, saying, "Actually, you have done rather well. You can slightly shift the position of the gears here, so that the force transmitted through the steel wire will be smoother. It's jamming because you made the device too complicated. The more complex the mechanism, the more likely it is to have problems..."
Little Tommy listened very carefully by Su Lun's side.
Soon after, Su Lun handed the mask back.
The boy had a good grasp of the concept. He seemed to understand completely and beamed with joy, "Oh, thank you, Mr. Johnny. I think I know how I need to modify my 'Ugly Duckling Mask' now!"
With that, he cheerfully ran off.
Su Lun watched him go and smiled to himself.
The boring escort task had its small pleasures.
....
A few hours later, the day's journey ended, and the convoy came to a halt.
"Alright, we can stop here, we'll camp here for tonight!"
The one shouting was called Abagon, a tall and skinny old man. His face, as stringent as his personality, always made people feel stern. He was the most prestigious person in this transport team and also a manager of the "Thornbird Commerce Association" from the inner city.
At his command, excited cheers erupted from the group.
They could finally rest.
Mechanical dogs circled around the perimeter, gathering the commerce association's people inside. Those from the inner city always disdained staying together with the people from the outer city.
And the Scavengers had to set up their own camps.
Su Lun also took out a marching tent from his backpack, set it up in an inconspicuous corner for himself to sleep, and then crawled inside.
Finally, it was time to rest, and Su Lun felt this was the most comfortable time of the day.
He led the "Invisible Walking Corpse" into the tent, and then unwrapped the corpse cloth to reveal the rune-inscribed corpse and the large black scythe.
Su Lun also took off his poison-resistant mask, exposing his strangely blue skin to the air.
If a stranger were here and saw the two blue-skinned beasts in the tent, they would surely be terrified.
But Su Lun was used to it.
He took out a rune brush and began to reapply alchemical materials to the dimmed runes.
This was a Scavenger who had perished in an attack the day before. His body was intact, so Su Lun collected it to use as material.
As he refurbished the runes on the walking corpse, he examined the changes in the corpse's muscles and mumbled to himself, "The X serum has quite a significant individual variance in amplification. It seems that melee professions are better suited for creating walking corpses.
It's a pity that the body of the second-tier professional from before couldn't be taken out, otherwise, using their bodies could withstand more slashes..."
Although the backlash was always a clean cut, the recovery ability varied greatly.
Even though the walking corpse had been injected with three doses of the "second-generation X serum," Su Lun found that this female corpse was far inferior to the previous male one. Under the same conditions, the number of times it could withstand backlash was significantly different.
However, the impact wasn't too great... after all, they were expendable.
...
Thinking of the "X serum," Su Lun looked down at his own arm, the muscles bulging and knotted under his blue skin, his eyes reflecting a complex emotion.
He had been on the move for several days, and even without any high-intensity training, his muscles were continuously swollen with a pumped feeling.
It was an indication of rapid muscle growth.
His data panel made it even clearer, as almost all body-related stats had more than doubled, except for spiritual power.
Moreover, this growth was continuing at a diminishing rate and was expected to be fully assimilated over the next few months.
Once the serum was completely absorbed, Su Lun could anticipate his physical fitness surpassing that of an average melee professional by a significant margin!
Besides the increase in body stats, there was another very noticeable enhancement in his abilities.
That was the efficiency with which he absorbed "Dark Spiritual Power" during meditation, which had improved drastically compared to before the serum injection.
Previously, a night's meditation allowed Su Lun to increase by one unit of Dark Spiritual Power.
But now, a night of meditation increased it by three units!
Although the Dark Spiritual Power in the catacombs was indeed richer than in Old Lington, it wasn't to the extent of tripling.
And it wasn't just a matter of concentration, but also absorption efficiency and sensation.
Su Lun felt that previous meditations were like forcibly infusing his body with Dark Spiritual Power. But now, even if he didn't use breathing techniques actively, Dark Spiritual Power would automatically seep into his pores. Not only was his body free of any signs of deformity, but he also felt a delightful sensation, like drawing silk.
It was like... the vastly improved "Elemental Affinity" that Magicians spoke of.
Su Lun also estimated that with his current state, he should soon be able to meet the minimum attribute requirements to advance to a second-tier professional.
Moreover, with his body strengthened and a surge in Dark Spiritual Power, his capacity for containment would be very high, and he reckoned that he could at least endure second-tier Gold-grade or higher advancement materials and alchemical bio-enhancements.
This also made Su Lun look forward to his upcoming trip to Dawn City even more.
If he could find a powerful space curse object, there would be no concern that his body couldn't handle it, and miss the chance to integrate that kind of high-order profession materials.
....
Su Lun almost finished applying runes to the animated corpse, then wrapped it up again with the burial shroud.
At that moment, something occurred to him, and he took out a pitch-black doll from the storage ring.
This was an experimental item, a cursed doll which solidified the incantation of "Curse Magic·Grass Man".
Su Lun named it "Voodoo Doll".
But since this was a new creation, there was still too much functionality and data that needed testing before it could be used in combat.
Considering the half a month left of this tedious escort mission, Su Lun collected some blood samples to test. It was convenient that Mr. Abagon, the manager, had fallen off the mechanical dog during the previous journey downhill, spilling a bit of blood.
An idea flashed through Su Lun's mind, and a faint, apologetic smile appeared on his face, "With a distance of over a hundred meters, the effect should be decent... My apologies, stingy Mr. Abagon, but you will have to serve as my test subject."
Murmuring to himself, he took out the collected blood sample and smeared it on the alchemic formation on the back of the doll. The luster flashed away, and the doll seemed to instantly come alive, a grey fog appearing on the face of the doll, which originally had no features. It vaguely resembled Mr. Abagon, looking somewhat eerie.
Having a familiar understanding of the "Grass Man" incantation in his memory, there was naturally no reason for failure.
He picked up a runic steel needle, and then stabbed it into the doll's leg.
The incantation wasn't the sort that could easily kill with one strike, especially from a distance, without enough blood samples, not targeting the heart or head, it could only inflict torment.
No sooner had he stabbed the needle in than Su Lun's acute hearing allowed him to instantly hear a scream.
"Ouch..."
He had no idea what Mr. Abagon was doing, but judging from a scream, it seemed quite painful.
"Subtracting the time it takes for sound to travel through the air, from the moment of stabbing to the target's scream, there's been a delay of about 1.3 seconds. I wonder if it's his slow reaction, or if it's due to a delay caused by the distance of the spellcasting..."
Su Lun muttered to himself, then recorded the experimental data in his notebook: 'September 1st, Test Subject #001, average middle-aged male... Blood sample quality E, one hundred thirty meters, needle stab in the calf, 1.3 seconds delay until scream...'
He recorded the data.
After some thought, Su Lun took the runic steel needle and stabbed the same leg of the doll again, then pricked up his ears to listen.
"Huh... The scream was noticeably slower this time, maybe he was braced for it on that leg? Should I try the other one?"
Su Lun thought for a moment and then stabbed the other leg.
Shortly afterward, he heard Mr. Abagon's cries of agony and his cursing, and Su Lun finally confirmed something, adding a note in his journal: 'It is essentially confirmed that the spellcasting distance and reaction speed are inversely proportional, subsequent tests should focus on precise measurements of distance and delay...'
Then, after a few more stabs, he barely heard any screams, and the blood samples also became very faint.
Su Lun recorded further: 'Spellcasting consumes the target's biological samples, significantly reducing the curse's effectiveness, spellcasting distance drastically reduced...'
....
Su Lun tested the first version of the "Voodoo Doll" and came up with some fresh inspiration.
He pulled out a new piece of wood, planning to carve a doll that incorporated some improvements for a Magician.
But as he was carving, footsteps approached from outside the tent.
Tommy came in to inform him that Mr. Abagon had summoned all the mercenaries for an emergency meeting.

chapters.title: Chapter 130 - 130 Search
chapters.content:
Su Lun put away the half-carved wooden doll and put his gas mask back on.
Just as he stepped out of the tent, he heard Mr. Abagon's cursing voice in the distance. Focusing his eyes, he saw the man rubbing his legs as he emerged from the luxurious marching tent, "Damn it, this damn cave is no place for humans, my old cold legs have flared up again..."
Listening to this, the corner of Su Lun's mouth curled up slightly under his mask.
....
This time, the "Thornbird Trading Company" had hired five small Scavenger squads and some individual Scavengers. These five or six dozen fully armed Scavengers were also the main security force for the transport convoy.
Su Lun found a corner and listened quietly.
An emergency meeting usually meant there was a problem.
Before long, everyone had arrived, and Mr. Abagon got straight to the point.
"I've just received the latest news," he began. "Area D24, which we're about to enter in about three days, has been attacked by mutated monsters. Several transport teams were almost completely wiped out. But we must deliver these supplies to the campsite in the Dawn City Ruins on time, so I hope you all will be on guard.
When making camp and standing watch at night, send out extra patrols to ensure the safety of the transport team..."
It was obvious that this steward, who had never been outside the city before, was nervous, and he was spreading his fear to everyone in the transport team.
The more Scavengers headed towards the Dawn City Ruins, the less safe the journey became. Instead, like baiting a fishing spot, the scent of humans attracted more and more mutated monsters.
The caves were never human territory; they were always a paradise for monsters.
At his words, the Scavengers began to discuss among themselves.
"I heard about it last time I was here too. Near D24, there seems to be a highly active group of 'Three-Eyed Poison Lizards'. Several Scavenger squads have already encountered small groups of these creatures and suffered significant losses..."
"Those mutated beasts are troublesome," another added. "They're quick, they move in packs, and a single bite can infect you with a toxin that rots your flesh... Do you have enough antidote potions prepared?"
"Not too many. Hopefully, we won't encounter a large swarm of them, or we'll be in trouble."
"Let's prepare in advance. When we make camp, we should set the sentries further out..."
"Hmm, that's all we can do."
"..."
The leaders of the five Scavenger squads gathered to discuss their strategy.
After all, this was their livelihood; nobody was backing out because of the danger.
....
In an inconspicuous corner, Su Lun silently listened to the battle plans the squad leaders discussed.
The passages in the caverns were complex and winding. There were a number of paths leading to Dawn City.
The route the transport team was taking now was the shortest one recently mapped out by the Scavengers.
But it wasn't the secret man-made tunnel that Su Lun knew from before.
This route took many detours and passed through several areas marked as dangerous on the map.
However, Su Lun, who was traveling with the group, didn't really care.
Even as he listened, he didn't feel much urgency.
He knew about the "Three-Eyed Poison Lizards"; they posed a considerable threat to non-professionals. But for him now, the monsters that could be killed with regular muskets were no threat at all.
Besides, with the "Invisible Living Corpse" as a powerful weapon in his hand, even if a high-level mutated beast attacked, he had the means to fight back.
Even if it really came down to running away, most mutated beasts probably couldn't outrun him with his eight-limbed spider spear.
The meeting ended before long.
Su Lun had thought about going back to rest.
But Captain Benson from the "Drunkard Scavengers" approached him.
"Brother Johnny!"
"What's the matter, Captain Benson?"
"Heh heh, that kid Tommy has been causing you trouble these past few days."
Benson is a big-bearded man with a ruddy, drinker's nose, and a hearty personality.
Though their interaction had been brief, Su Lun had a good impression of him. Due to Su Lun's previous help with Tommy, the bearded man was always very polite to him.
Su Lun chuckled, "It wasn't much trouble."
Benson, with the helpless look of an old father, sighed, "Ah... that little rascal is quite the handful. I saw that he liked to tinker with machinery, and I originally wanted to send him to a repair shop as an apprentice. He wouldn't have been rich, but at least he would have had a worry-free life. But the kid didn't want that, insisting on becoming an adventurer, a true mechanic.
So, unable to persuade him, I decided to take him out to scavenge and see the world. I hadn't anticipated that we would encounter problems on the way. If it weren't for you, brother, the boy would've suffered greatly."
"Tommy actually has quite a talent for mechanics..."
Su Lun smiled, feeling that the big-bearded man had something more to discuss with him.
As expected, after Benson was polite for quite a while, he finally stated his purpose: "By the way... Johnny. The road ahead might be dangerous. If we do run into a large-scale attack by mutated monsters, stay close to our group so we can have each other's backs."
He said it very politely, also taking Su Lun's dignity into account.
Though he said it was mutual backing, in reality, he wanted to look after Su Lun, the lone wolf.
After all, in the eyes of ordinary people, a gunner was a profession that needed the protection of teammates, especially a sniper. Once cornered by monsters, they became weak in close combat.
Su Lun understood; this was an attempt to return the favor for saving Tommy before,
He did not say much, just smiled and nodded, "Yeah, sure, thanks."
....
And so, the transport convoy continued deeper into the catacombs.
Along the way, they encountered a few minor attacks by mutated creatures but managed to repel them without issues, thanks to the convoy's ample manpower and firepower.
As a sniper, Su Lun didn't need to get into close combat, an occasional potshot was enough for him.
Nobody minded having someone in the team who was both shirking duties and unsociable.
Su Lun's daily life was also very regular.
He studied his "Voodoo Doll", tinkered with some small machines, practiced meditation to increase his dark spiritual power, and recorded the detailed changes in his body data after injecting "X Serum"...
Then there was the study of Isaac's Alchemy Manuscript.
During the ambush by the Umbrella Organization at the "White Sail Warehouse", Su Lun was puzzled as to why those men, who could have taken the items quietly, chose to kill instead.
After the battle on Green Street, when Su Lun killed three second-order professionals from the Umbrella Organization and extracted memory fragments from the ice magician who had ambushed their warehouse, he realized that the Umbrella Organization wanted to "clean" because they considered the manuscript a "contaminant" internally.
They believed that the manuscript's curse properties could taint those who touched it, causing great harm.
Their orders were to eliminate anyone who had come into contact with the notes and to retrieve the manuscript.
Furthermore, this order came directly from the Black Tower Duchy!
But this only deepened Su Lun's confusion.
He had evaluated the manuscript and found no such "contaminating properties".
The only curse property mentioned was that touching the manuscript would involve one with its "fate", not knowing whether it would bring fortune or disaster. How could that be considered contamination?
Su Lun suspected this might also be a move by the higher-ups of the Black Tower to monopolize advanced alchemy knowledge.
After all, he also learned from another second-order professional's memory that the Umbrella Organization had been aware of the manuscript. Moreover, they suspected it was one of the legendary Sir Isaac's five manuscripts that recorded "Divine Alchemy".
Unable to make sense of it, Su Lun decided to look for answers in the notes.
He had been deciphering the manuscript these past few days.
Unexpectedly, with his not-so-sophisticated decryption techniques, he still managed to clumsily translate the contents of the manuscript.
The result was...
He discovered that this notebook was just a normal alchemy record, at least from what he had seen so far.
The content recorded above is also a special type of Alchemy armor growth.
Back then, Sir Isaac wanted to use a "Heart Implant" to withstand additional dark spiritual power, and also to endow the human body with a continuous recovery "Blue BUFF." This would allow Alchemy Magicians to never run out of dark spiritual power in battle, enabling them to cast even more powerful spells without worrying about the consumption of their energy...
Moreover, this manuscript is also very user-friendly. It seems that the Alchemical Demigod was afraid that his descendants would not understand his brilliant innovations, so he explained the process step by step from the basics, detailing how to gradually and successfully craft that type of "Heart Implant."
Within the first few pages that Su Lun understood, it documented the crafting diagrams for the "Isaac's Alchemic Heart (Level I)." The main material used was the heart of a first-order mutant monster. Although the runes and crafting formulas were complex, they were introductory knowledge that low-level professionals could slowly learn to master.
What's magical is that he could only see the content that followed once he understood the preceding parts.
In the past two days, after understanding the first few pages, he then deciphered the following pages, which contained diagrams for the "Isaac's Alchemic Heart (Level II)."
From this, it can be inferred that the later pages of this notebook might contain Level III, Level IV, Level V...
It was simply a most ordinary notebook.
This one is a textbook that records only Alchemy knowledge, and then more advanced Alchemy knowledge.
There's absolutely nothing that could be considered "contaminated."
Su Lun felt the only thing special was a sentence that bordered on "blasphemy."
Sir Isaac, with a tone of condescension, wrote on the title page: "So-called divine creatures are nothing but high-level materials in the face of great Alchemy."
Su Lun guessed that perhaps the final pages of this notebook dealt with using the so-called heart of a god to craft an "Isaac's Alchemic Heart?"
....
After several more days moving toward the deeper parts of the cavern, the transport team finally entered a high-risk area, and the atmosphere within the group grew increasingly tense.
That night, as usual, they chose a relatively safe place to camp and increased the number of guards for the night.
Su Lun set up his tent and began his daily research.
Unexpectedly, in the middle of the night, a group of unwelcome guests broke into the camp.
"We're under attack!"
"Everyone, prepare for battle!"
"..."
The sentries sounded the alarm, and suddenly there was an uproar outside.
Su Lun didn't dare to be careless. He packed up his Invisible Zombie and stepped out of the tent.
To his surprise, although there was a lot of commotion, a fight had not ensued.
Because the intruders were not mutant monsters, but a famed group of Bounty Hunters from Old Lington City.
And although several members of the scavenger teams guarding the camp were fully armed and alert, they didn't dare to actually engage.
This was due to one of the brash intruders being a second-order professional, "Flower Sword" Holle, an old swordsman skilled in courtly fencing, from the "Iron Knight Bounty Hunter Group."
Having signed a protection contract, the scavengers of the transport team were also obligated to safeguard the convoy. They stood armed, facing off against the uninvited guests, preventing them from penetrating the core of the camp.
Even though the opponent had a second-order professional, there were still a hundred or so people in the transport team. If a real fight broke out, it would most certainly be a pyrrhic victory for both sides.
The other side didn't dare to act rashly either.
Then Holle negotiated with Abagon for a moment, apparently saying something that made the trade association manager agree all too easily to allow them to search the camp!
"We are in pursuit of a very dangerous wanted criminal. Please cooperate with us, this is also for your own safety."
"Everyone, please come out of your tents, open your tents and large bags, we need to inspect them!"
"Take off your masks, we need to see your faces..."
"..."
Ten people from the Iron Knight Group came, and in addition to the second-order Holle, there were at least several other formal professionals, judging by their demeanor.
This was already a very strong team configuration.
Su Lun watched as the aggressive group barged into the camp, apparently in search of some "wanted criminal."
Upon hearing this, his brows furrowed as well.
Because he himself was a wanted criminal.
Could it be that the Umbrella Organization's people had followed him here?
That was his first thought.
....
The group kicked everyone out of their tents, then proceeded to check each one.
Su Lun was now in a suit of blue leather, which absolutely couldn't be exposed to light. Once he took off his mask, he would certainly draw attention.
But he was also puzzled... Wasn't the "Iron Knight Squad's" approach a bit too presumptuous?
After all, the people in this transport team were Scavengers with lawful identities. Bounty Hunters weren't a law enforcement department and didn't possess any search authority. This was also the most important reason why Qian Tiao had arranged for him to have this lawful identity—to avoid unnecessary trouble.
And naturally, the brazen actions also displeased a few Scavenger group leaders.
Captain Benson was direct in his address: "Hey hey hey, 'Iron Knights,' don't overdo it. We are Scavenger groups, not some wanted criminals. We have no obligation to cooperate with your search!"
Upon hearing this, the leaders of the other four groups echoed his sentiment, "Exactly! By what right do you search us?"
The Scavengers weren't cowards either, and it seemed like an armed conflict was imminent.
Their search blocked, Holle's face turned iron blue.
After all, ordinary Bounty Hunters wouldn't dare to kill lawful Scavengers.
But it seemed he had some urgent orders to fulfill, not having the time to waste words. He took out a wanted poster and a gold badge, directly revealing his identity, he coldly said: "This is a highest-level wanted notice issued by the Black Tower, I am a special enforcement officer for 'Umbrella' in the outer city.
Just half an hour ago, this extremely vicious wanted criminal stabbed Old Lington Intelligence Agency Chief Officer, Lord Haus. Anyone obstructing the manhunt will be regarded as an accomplice to the wanted criminal, and will be subject to summary execution!"
Seeing the gold badge displayed by Holle, the faces of a few Scavenger group leaders changed dramatically, and immediately, they no longer dared to speak up.
It was okay to provoke anyone else, but no one dared to provoke the Umbrella Organization.
....
On the other hand, Su Lun's expression became somewhat strange.
Was it really the Umbrella Organization's covert operation?
So a high-ranking official was just assassinated?
He looked at the wanted poster and also understood that these people weren't here to catch him.
Even from a distance, he clearly saw the face on the wanted poster.
Wasn't that the woman who had bombed the experiment?
The fuss that woman had made before was even bigger than his, and it was inevitable that she couldn't stay in Old Lington City any longer, escaping outside the city was expected.
But having escaped, she still didn't keep a low profile and made a big commotion again?
The so-called "Super Mechanical Soldier," built only for combat—every time he heard news about her, she was either causing trouble or on her way to cause trouble...
The fact that Holle was in such a rush to reveal his identity and search the camp meant they were sure that woman must be nearby.
However, Su Lun was not concerned about the woman's situation, but his own.
Because at that moment, someone from the "Iron Knight Squad" had already reached his tent, and then, holding a gun, commanded: "Hey, you... take off your mask!"
Upon hearing this, the gaze hidden beneath Su Lun's gas mask also turned cold.
A thought flashed through his mind: should he kill them all...
PS. These two chapters are transition chapters, written a bit oddly... I don't know what went wrong.

chapters.title: Chapter 131 - 131: The Soothsayer
chapters.content:
The cave was nothing like Old Lington City. If it came to a fight, there would be no reservations.
Su Lun could kill them, and then retreat at his ease.
With the complex terrain, even if Old Lington sent ten times the number of troops, they might not catch him.
However, doing so would ruin his plan to travel to Dawn City incognito, and he would have to abandon his "Johnny" identity.
But at this moment, it seemed like he had no other choice but to fight.
...
"Hey... you there, yes, you, take off your mask!"
The guy from the "Iron Cavalry Group" opposite Su Lun was still urging him to take off his mask.
After all, it was time to rest and set up camp. Most people in the transport team did not have their gas masks on. A brief glance was all it took for the man to spot Su Lun's anomaly.
Seeing that Su Lun did not respond promptly, the man's gun barrel lifted a bit, as if he would open fire immediately upon sensing something amiss.
There was no way he could remove the mask; problems would inevitably arise if he did.
Hearing the urging, Su Lun did not care much for the man before him. He could tell from the way the man handled his gun that he was no professional, posing a limited threat.
Su Lun's attention remained on the distant "Flower Sword" Holle.
If a fight were to break out, he would have to eliminate this man first to ensure nothing unforeseen occurred during the battle.
However, just as Su Lun was about to exert a slight force on his finger, preparing to command the "invisible undead" behind him to slit the throat of that second-order professional first—
Suddenly!
Several other members of the "Knight Order" searching the campsite found something and shouted, "Captain, I found this!"
This urgent cry drew the attention of everyone in the camp.
Su Lun also looked over to see that the man was holding a broken mechanical arm.
It was not an ordinary mechanical arm; it looked just like a living person's severed limb. However, underneath the tattered synthetic skin, a metallic luster reflected, and there was no blood flowing from the severed end, only some complex, damaged, and high-precision mechanical components.
