Otherwise, the badge on their chest wouldn't have mentioned "particularly attracts the murderer," nor would it feel so "real."
The rules of a plot-driven cursed space were simple: everything was constructed from the murderer's memory.
Things do exist in reality, but they do not exceed the murderer's knowledge.
For instance, if the murderer had never read the books on those shelves, they would be blank.
Only the ones he had read contained text.
Only if the murderer had the notion of "a badge is an alchemical object" in his consciousness, then it would be identified as alchemy.
This was a space where, with careful sorting out, the plot was quite straightforward.
With a little investigation, all clues would point to two locations: Red Tower Bell Tower and the white monastery.
But the difficulty lay in the fact that this was the focus of the backstory but not the key to breaking the curse.
...
Su Lun stepped out of the room and once again trod upon the damp cobblestone streets.
Snowflakes were falling from the sky, resting on his shoulders and hat, occasionally forming a thin layer.
Su Lun patted the snowflakes off his shoulder, wandering along the street.
The cold wind made his thoughts exceptionally clear.
He then visited a few more places, gathering several ancient books with scattered information.
He asked a few questions, and the situation was much the same.
Whenever the nun named "Alice" was mentioned, these NPCs would talk a lot.
There was also an old lady in an attic window directly facing the bell tower, claiming she had once seen a strange person on the tower...
These were all key pieces of information.
The police officer who had investigated the case back then must have found these pieces of information as well.
The original process required "players" to gather this information, after which they would be directed to that red brick bell tower to seek out the monster.
But Su Lun was not in a hurry to go there.
Different choices led to different endings.
Just like playing those open-ended role-playing games, Su Lun could kill the monster inside the bell tower or fulfill its last wish without understanding the game's background and still complete the game.
But then the storyline would end.
He would lose the meaning of coming to this cursed space.
So Su Lun chose the second option.
He took to the streets, planning to visit the monastery to figure out how the Wailing Witch was formed.
Now that he was certain this place was not "the space of the Wailing Witch," the monastery shouldn't be too dangerous.
It was just a normal scene.
But there, an important backdrop to the storyline would be completed.
.....
As he walked, mulling over his thoughts, Su Lun unexpectedly discovered a few lost lambs.
Inside a tavern, he saw a group dressed as detectives debating something at a table.
Although their appearances had changed, Su Lun recognized their origins from their conversation.
"Damn it! What's the answer to that question? Soro said 'ugly,' Martin said 'not ugly,' both were killed, and Gek didn't answer but was killed too! I suspect that cloaked monster just wants to kill for fun..."
"Stop complaining and think of other ways. We're temporarily safe staying in this room, but are we going to be trapped in this cursed space forever and never leave? I just got some information from the bartender. There's a strange person near the bell tower..."
"..."
This group was also thinking of a way to solve the mystery. It sounded like the three individuals not present had already been killed by the "murderer."
Su Lun walked in, didn't say a word, drew his gun, and started shooting.
"Bang bang bang" gunfire resounded through the tavern.
Although the tavern was destroyed by an explosion in retaliation by the enemy, the five people, including the team leader "Bomb Maniac" Collins, were all killed.
Su Lun put away his blast-resistant puppet, as if he had just taken care of a trivial matter.
He walked out of the tavern and continued toward the monastery surrounded by white walls.
A monastery in a city of alchemists who didn't believe in deities?
That was what Su Lun was most curious about.
And what was the relationship between the nun named Alice and the monster on the bell tower?

chapters.title: Chapter 142 - 142 Grand Gesture
chapters.content:
It was a snowy night.
Snowflakes fell on the white monastery's roof, making the building appear bloated.
The identity of a patrol officer was quite useful; Su Lun easily knocked on the monastery's grand doors.
Thick snow also covered the courtyard, where pigeons cooed in their sleep up high.
A brown-haired nun received him.
"Officer Johnny, what brings you here?"
"There's been another murder on the streets, and I'm worried the murderer might have hidden in the monastery. May I come in and take a look?"
"Of course."
The brown-haired nun led Su Lun into the monastery.
Inside the main hall, there were no statues of gods, but rather the "Ouroboros" totem revered by alchemists.
Su Lun wanted to extract some useful alchemy knowledge from these nuns, but it was clear he didn't get what he wanted.
"May I know how many nuns are there in the monastery now?"
"Six."
"I need to ask a few questions to the others."
"..."
"Right, where is Sister Alice?"
"I'm sorry, she is completing her weekly duties, maintaining the seal in the basement."
"A seal?"
"..."
The conversation was cut off halfway with no further details.
But at least Su Lun learned that these nuns were here to maintain some sort of seal.
...
After a while, Su Lun left the monastery.
Though he didn't meet the Alice he was looking for, he heard a sorrowful love story.
The narrative also completed the last piece of the puzzle.
Upon leaving the street, he had only walked a few steps when he heard the sound of footsteps crushing the snowy pavement.
Someone appeared behind him.
But the gaze that watched him bore no malice for the time being.
Su Lun calmly turned around and then saw a person enveloped in a black cloak.
He guessed this person was the "Midnight Murderer."
The cloaked figure spoke, "Do you think I look hideous?"
The raspy voice sounded as though it came from a throat scorched by Luotie.
Then he lifted his head, revealing a deformed monster's face.
Su Lun had already guessed who "it" was, and his expression remained utterly unfluctuated as he indifferently said, "Appearance has never been the key to judging beauty. In my eyes, goodness has nothing to do with the skin."
The clues previously identified by the All-knowing Eye were quite clear.
Answering "ugly" or "not ugly" wasn't the answer,
neither was not answering.
Emotion was the correct answer.
Feelings of disgust could provoke "it."
It was always on the edge of time and space.
This was also why for Su Lun, the difficulty level of this cursed space was "D-grade."
Su Lun was quite good at controlling his emotions.
Pausing, he looked back at the cloaked figure and sighed, "Mr. Brook, I've heard your story, and I'm sorry..."
The cloaked person fell silent upon hearing this.
After a long time, he spoke with his husky voice, "Sir, can I trouble you to meet me at the bell tower? I am going to die tonight, and I have a request to ask of you..."
Without hesitation, Su Lun instantly agreed, "Okay."
The cloaked figure before him was identified as [Soon-to-be completely deformed Abbas Meat Mountain affiliate].
Su Lun knew he was not the Bell Tower Monster.
Relieved by Su Lun's agreement, the cloaked figure vanished into the snowy night.
Su Lun didn't dwell on the cloaked figure,
he went straight to the red brick bell tower, knowing from the start that it was key to solving the case.
There was a thick iron door at the base of the bell tower, now open.
Su Lun walked in without hesitation.
With no elevator, he climbed the stairs step by step.
Gradually, strange patterns appeared on the surrounding walls, resembling autumn ivy covering the entire wall, the higher he went, the denser.
Later, he discovered that they were densely packed living blood vessels.
As he ascended, the walls began to show squirming human organs, intestines, and layers of pale yellow fat...
Even the steps under his feet had turned into fleshy tissue covered with a slippery membrane, wet and slick beneath his tread.
The air was permeated with the distinct stench of fresh, living organ tissue.
Su Lun felt as if he had entered the body of a gigantic monster, and just as he was about to reach the top, he saw a massive, throbbing heart.
This was the real challenge of breaking the cursed space.
Normal people entering this bell tower would probably throw a grenade to destroy everything on instinct.
But stimulating "it" upstairs could have severe consequences.
Su Lun looked at the information he had deduced. His face showed no change in color as he climbed step by step up the fleshy stairs.
Finally, he reached the top of the bell tower and saw a human face grown into the wall.
This was a gigantic aberration, its flesh completely merged with the bell tower.
Bell Tower Monster?
No,
more accurately called the Bell Tower Creature.
The voice came from below the two eye sockets that looked like a mouth: "Sorry if I scared you."
Su Lun had learned this man's story from Sister Alice, and shook his head, saying, "No, Mr. Brook. You are a respected and brave warrior."
"Yes, I do not regret going to war,"
the voice spoke with a hint of pride, "If there were time, I would discuss that battle with you. But I don't have time now…"
He paused, then continued, "Although I did not die in battle, I was infected with an aberration during a fight with an abyssal creature... Seven days ago, I returned here with the last bit of my determination, wanting to see her one last time. Unfortunately, my will could no longer prevent my body's aberration. A demon is devouring my sanity.
I didn't want her to see me in this monstrous state… so I hid here in this bell tower."
Su Lun listened, and from the direction seen by those eyeballs, he could spot through the clock's aperture the white monastery across the way.
In the last moments of his life, he silently watched over the girl he loved.
The voice then said, "If possible, could you help me fulfill my last wish, take my belongings to my beloved Alice. Tell her that I cannot keep our appointment, that she should no longer wait for me…"
"Okay."
Su Lun agreed, taking a harmonica that emerged from a fleshy tendril and examined it.
[Brook's Harmonica]
Description: Can you take it to my dearest girl?
Curse Feature: Love for a lifetime, that's a curse, right?
Details: Engraved with the names Alice and Brook; playing it can soothe Alice's soul;
With his last vestige of will, he managed to finish his words, then the face on the wall slowly closed its eyes.
The thunderous beating of the giant heart also gradually ceased, and the bell tower returned to calm. Only the "click," "click" sounds of the clock hands moving filled the space.
The aberration's life was incredibly tenacious, yet Brook had willingly given up his own.
At this point, the storyline of the whole cursed space was completed.
Watching the creature identified as [Abyssal Abbas Meat Mountain (Second Order Silver-tier Bizarre)] die, Su Lun took a long breath of relief.
He also knew that this was the correct method to break the "D-level difficulty."
A forceful attack would qualify as "A-level."
With such a massive size, even with a black scythe, it might not inflict effective damage.
Even if one were to blow up the entire tower, it might not kill Brook, but would instead completely enrage him into a very terrifying beast.
According to the original plot, apparently, Brook hadn't entrusted the harmonica to anyone until his death. The cursed space was formed by his obsession, hoping someone would return this "token" to Miss Alice.
Su Lun felt that he probably knew who the "Wailing Witch" was now.
Two related cursed spaces, like the distant bell tower and the monastery.
....
And as the signs of life in the mound of flesh before him disappeared, it gradually coalesced into a glowing piece of flesh.
[Abbas's Flesh]
Details: Second Order Silver material, used in crafting advancement materials, significantly enhances physical strength;
This was already quite a rare thing.
Su Lun collected the material, aware that the cursed space was about to collapse.
But... the story was quite good.
No cursed items burst out, huh?
Su Lun didn't think too much about it, as the scenery suddenly changed all around him.
Then, he found himself back in the ruins of Dawn City.
And beside him, Tommy was looking bewildered at the black whistle in his hand.
He looked at Su Lun, exclaiming, "Mr. Johnny!"
Su Lun guessed something, and asked, "You met that cloaked figure?"
Tommy said, "Yeah... he suddenly walked into the room and asked me if I thought he was ugly. I could sense his pain, so I talked with him for a bit. He gave me a whistle. Then... somehow I got out."
"..."
Su Lun thought that sometimes breaking a cursed space depended on power,
but sometimes, it really depended on appearance.
It's no wonder he felt that no cursed items had appeared in the space earlier, as it turned out to be with Tommy.
[Whistle of the Dead]
Quality: Gold
Description: Do you want to converse with demons?
Curse characteristics: With the demon's power, you will be tempted by the demon.
Details: Mystical series 'Necromancer' occupational material; occupational requirement, requires specific spirit medium constitution.
Su Lun didn't know what talent Tommy had awakened, but this cursed object was indeed a fine item.
"Gold quality" ancient relic, truly a rare profession.
Although he had never heard of "Necromancer," it was definitely not simple.
Tommy, holding a whistle, asked, "Mr. Johnny, what is this whistle, and why did that cloaked person give it to me? I feel it suits me..."
"A rare gold occupational material. Put it away."
Su Lun didn't say much because, at that moment, the expected scene was unfolding on the ruins of the monastery opposite them.
...
Loud arguing voices came over.
"We signed an equal exploration contract, what right does your Oliver family have to make us probe the cursed space!"
"Damn it, Battle Blade Group! You are violating the Wilderness Hunting Pact!"
"They never intended to let us get out alive..."
"..."
Not far from the monastery, dozens of men from the Battle Blade Group, armed with guns, were driving three independent hunter groups, including the "Drunkard Group," into the monastery, seemingly forcing them to probe the cursed space.
At that moment, they also spotted Su Lun and his companion who had appeared out of nowhere.
In an instant, everyone turned their gaze toward them, with the muzzles and cannons also pointed their way.
Tommy, seeing his father among them, drew his gun and charged forward, "Let go of my dad!"
The situation was exactly as Su Lun had predicted.
The Battle Blade Group finally tore off its disguise, dozens of malicious gazes piercing, sending chills down one's spine.
As the situation grew desperate, Su Lun scoffed inwardly, single-handedly triggering the silk thread in his hand, instinctively wanting to take control and first behead the second-tier team leader of the Battle Blade Group, then ambush kill the others.
But the next second, as he glanced at his hand, he subconsciously stopped himself.
Then, a puzzled look appeared on his face.
He looked down at his hand again, attempting that awkward finger-twirling motion, and discovered a problem.
Then he looked around at the environment and his hand again.
It was then that he realized, "Huh... turns out it's a dream. When did I get hit?"
The Wailing Witch's primary method was murder through dreams.
Su Lun had been cautious from the start.
Through a special kind of conditioned reflex, he confirmed that the scene before him was a dream of his own creation.
...
People in dreams normally are not aware that they are dreaming.
But to become aware that one is dreaming is something that can be achieved through certain techniques and training.
Su Lun had once trained for this to prevent his dangerous personality from harming others in his sleep.
It was the action of looking at his hand and twirling his fingers that he had done earlier. He had repeatedly suggested to himself before sleep, "When I'm in a dream, I will look at my fingers, then realize I'm dreaming."
(Note: Lucid dreaming, similar to 'Tang Wang's technique', modified for magic, don't take it too seriously)
Then, through long-term training,
It had become a conditioned reflex.
Now, although everything seemed incredibly realistic, Su Lun was sure he was in a dream.
....
In front of him, the Battle Blade Group had already grabbed Tommy and were closing in on him.
Su Lun chuckled, "Heh heh..."
In the dream, he was sure to be alive.
So although they might shoot, he definitely wouldn't die.
But not dying didn't mean he could escape the dream quickly.
Facing countless muzzles around him, he made no move to resist, instead, a faint smile appeared at the corner of his eyes.
Once he confirmed he was dreaming, everything else lost its meaning.
Su Lun took out a gun, pressed it against his jaw, and without hesitation, pulled the trigger.
He was very proficient, obviously not his first time.
....
Suddenly, everything went black.
As if awakening from a nightmare.
Su Lun looked around at the environment.
It was a snowy crossroads.
"Mr. Johnny? Where are we?"
Alongside him, a little boy dressed in thin clothes tentatively called out, his hand still holding a basket of matches.
The Little Match Boy?
This familiar scene had unfolded before him once again.
But due to the missing memories of the dream, he only felt that the scene was familiar, as if it had happened before, yet he did not realize anything.
"Did it snow in Dawn City a thousand years ago..."
Su Lun muttered to himself, wanting to respond to Tommy with, "Cursed space."
However, suddenly, he subconsciously glanced at his own hands, then looked around, his gaze instantly becoming grave, as if something had triggered a conditioned reflex, realizing something, "A dream?"
Tommy's gaze became vacant.
He stared incredulously as Su Lun drew a firegun and pressed it against his temple, hastily exclaiming, trying to stop him, "Mr. Johnny, what are you doing!"
Before he could finish speaking, Su Lun, with a smile tugging at the corners of his mouth, pulled the trigger without hesitation.
The more he spoke, the deeper he fell into the dream, the harder it was to extricate himself.
Another "bang" of gunfire.
Darkness fell before his eyes.
It was as if he had awakened from a nightmare.
....
This time, the scene had changed again.
Before him was a ruined convent surrounded by a dense fog that obscured everything, with only the scene within the convent clearly visible.
Inside the main hall of the convent, a five-meter-tall silver-haired nun was attacking several humans with her hair that could extend.
Seven people, five of them second-rung professionals, and two were controlling Magicians.
Of the five second-rungs, four had familiar faces, the previously seen Trickster Lloyd, the Raven Gang's executive 'Blood Raven' Langfero, the leader of the Warblade Group Blum, the Steam Party's executive 'Mechanical Tyrannosaurus' Toynbee, and one unidentified Mage in a robe.
The other two first-rung professionals also possessed very rare abilities to control the scene; one wielded the "Thorn Bind" Spell, confining the tall nun's legs, apparently having a special talent in controlling plants; the other emitted the Slowing Light Beam that slowed the nun's movements, which was also a special power;
Together, the seven surrounded the "Wailing Witch," with that Trickster Lloyd constantly shouting commands.
"Send another batch of slaves into the witch's dreamscape, stimulate her to enter the second state. That way, by killing her, we'll obtain the 'Endless Hair'!"
"Quick, control her! Now that her hair's attack range is limited, seriously wound her first!!!"
"Don't hit the head, ensure the skull is intact when gathering materials!"
"..."
Under their coordinated efforts, the tall nun was already covered in scars.
And the next second, who knows what happened, the fog around gradually turned red.
The nun, who had snow-white skin, suddenly became blood-red all over.
"Did the witch enter the second-rung berserk mode?"
Su Lun was startled by the scene before him.
He had thoroughly understood the abilities of the "Wailing Witch" from Mr. Hei and immediately realized what these people were up to.
....
"With such a grand show, am I dreaming?"
Watching the surreal scene before him, Su Lun doubted his own eyes, and instinctively this thought emerged in his mind.
He looked down at his own hands but discovered... it was actually the real world?!
Realizing this, suddenly, his memories seemed to connect like a film.
He instantly recalled the experience in the "Bell Tower Monster" space and the memories of committing suicide twice to exit the dreamscape.
Upon reevaluating his surroundings, the All-knowing Eye identified the result.
"White Convent"
Explanation: Special triggered cursed space, if you cannot distinguish between dream and reality, the danger level will be "T-grade". Kill the witch, and you can leave.
"This is the real world!"
Su Lun was greatly surprised.
This time, he no longer pulled out the gun to commit suicide.
But at the same time, he speculated, "It must be that right after I exited that 'Bell Tower Monster' space, I was immediately drawn into this space."
He guessed that these fellows had used some special cursed item, causing the "Wailing Witch's Cursed Space" to cover a large range of nearby areas.
This had led him to fall straight into the witch's dreamscape upon leaving the other space.
"How long had I remained in the Bell Tower's cursed space? When had these guys arrived?"
Su Lun's heart was filled with doubts.
But at the moment, there was no room for him to ponder in detail.
Recognizing these people's background, Su Lun instantly understood that this was Oliver's family's wilderness hunting group.
To gather hair materials, had they really brought five second-rung professionals? What a big move...
The power of a top inner city financial group was indeed as formidable as its reputation.
They were not only intent on killing the monster for materials but now also wanted to purposely stimulate the "Wailing Witch" into a frenzy to obtain higher-grade materials?
Having previously identified the "Gold-level" oddity, after the second form, it was definitely at the "Lord-level"!
Want to get the "Endless Hair"?
Su Lun's mind swiftly connected the recently captured information with what he was seeing, understanding what was happening, his eyes suddenly filling with malintent, "Tsk tsk... What a grand scheme!"

chapters.title: Chapter 143 - 143 Puppet Theater
chapters.content:
"Not enough, send in twenty more slaves!"
"Good, the witch's frenzy is complete!"
"Prepare to execute..."
"..."
Su Lun heard clearly that the Oliver family intended to send in a group of slaves in order to trigger the Wailing Witch's berserk state.
The witch, while killing people in their dreams, also required a division of her attention. By sending in more people at once and overloading her, the witch would have no choice but to enter a second phase of berzerking inadvertently, killing even more people.
As it happened, Su Lun was supposed to be the "fertilizer" accelerating the witch's frenzy.
But now, he had awoken.
Su Lun also knew that if the Oliver family managed to kill the witch and break the curse space, what would these people do with him as the sole survivor?
Previously, with only the "Sharp Knife Troop" leader Blum, a second-tier professional, Su Lun was confident whether in combat or in flight.
However, right now, there were five second-tier professionals just in front of him, and two first-tier individuals who were extremely difficult controller magicians. Under normal circumstances, Su Lun wouldn't even have the right to flee if any of them discovered him.
Moreover, besides those seven, there were certainly more enemies outside the cursed space.
But it wasn't all bad news.
The good news was that Su Lun was now outside the monastery in the mist, and those who were besieging the witch had not yet realized he was awake.
And within the thick fog by his side, he faintly saw several silhouettes standing there idly—these were all "fertilizer." Just as he glanced over in that instant, a few more shadows disappeared, likely killed in the dreamscape and then expelled from the cursed space.
Seeing this, Su Lun instantly knew what he had to do.
...
The silver-haired nun, who was already over five meters tall, was oppressive enough, but now she had entered a frenzied state, emanating a thick aura of blood that made it hard for anyone to look directly at her.
Her silver hair floated in the wind like sharp blades, and just a light touch was enough to cut through the monastery's stone columns effortlessly.
The hair split into needles, capable of puncturing the hard floor with a myriad of hole like raindrops;
Clustered together, it could strike a target heavily like a weapon.
Since she had entered a frenzy, her silver hair, both in quantity and length, was no longer limited and for a time, the entire monastery seemed to be caged by a web of silver hair, firmly trapping those seven people inside.
Seeing this, Su Lun's eyes narrowed slightly.
He knew that this was also the aim of these people—to stimulate the witch into the second phase and harvest her infinitely growing silver hair.
But he knew now was not the time to intervene.
The monster was not injured, and the seven individuals in the arena were obviously not completely restrained yet.
After all, they had come prepared, and even when facing a lord-class fiend, they were not at a disadvantage.
The Steam Party's "Mechanical Tyrannosaurus" Toynbee, transformed into a humanoid T-Rex, used his armor-plated mechanical limbs to keep a multitude of strands tangled up by himself;
Captain Blum of the War Blade Group wielded a wind-elemental two-handed sword like a giant windmill, clashing with the converging silver strands to produce a metallic clanging and sparks flying everywhere.
Langfero of the Crow Gang, known as "Blood Crow," had even stranger curse magic. The hexagram beneath his feet shone a dark green light, and he held a feathered crow in his hand. With one bite, he severed the crow's head, producing a chilling sound of bone crunching and chewing. It was that noise that made the Wailing Witch tremble all over, as if her own bones were being gnawed on...
Even Su Lun, not far off, felt a tingling scalp upon hearing this horrific sound.
However, the most exaggerated of them all was the Trickster Lloyd, the main force of the assault.
This was the first time Su Lun had witnessed the battle of a genuine Puppet Master.
....
Watching as the witch completely lost her inhibition and entered the second phase, Lloyd shouted, "Get ready, I have it under control, you move according to plan and strike to kill!"
No sooner had his words fallen than his hands quickly formed a set of sorcerer's seals, his gaze intense: "Plating · Release!"
As soon as the plating was released, the Puppet Master's body underwent a bizarre transformation.
It felt like he had suddenly lost all vitality as if he was no longer a living person but had become a puppet himself.
What was even more eerie was that the skin exposed on his body all cracked open. It was like a black-threaded cloth doll had its outer skin slit, revealing the black threads inside to the air.
And as his hands completed the final sorcerer's seal, those "threads" within the puppet body began to wildly surge, shooting out like living creatures...
After Lloyd released the Plating with his seals, he hardly paused before forming another set, muttering incantations.
He was unleashing his signature secret technique—[Mystic Art: Puppet Theater].
A complex series of thirty-six sorcerer's seals left onlookers dazzled. No sooner had he finished the seals than a giant blue Hexagram Alchemy Array, covering the entire monastery, lit up in the sky. Following the illumination, a massive cruciform phantom slowly materialized from the alchemy array.
At the same time, as if responding to the black threads on his body from afar, numerous black lines trailed down from the enormous cross in the sky, growing as they were whipped by the wind...
As these black lines descended, the puppets that Lloyd had previously placed around the monastery also began to "click" and "clack" to their feet.
In an instant, it seemed as though the entire monastery had turned into a large Puppet Theater, with everything connected by the black lines.
Like a pair of backstage hands, they controlled everything.
And the black lines were not just meant to manipulate puppets—they were there for "control"!
More and more black lines from the cross in the sky kept invading, like a black tide gradually spreading into the silver world.
Their numbers might not have matched that of the witch's silver strands, but their momentum was just as formidable.
The puppets manipulated by the black lines surged toward the witch, swiftly being entwined and controlled by the silver strands, wrapped into a bundle.
But this was exactly what Lloyd had intended.
The two types of strands tangled and interwove, the black lines gradually entangling completely with the silver hair, turning into tight knots of chaos.
The dozen or so puppets, like so many nails, pinned the witch firmly in place, leaving her unable to move or fight back.
Even though the silver strands could elementally dodge the black lines, the witch could not retreat at all and was only getting more entangled. The moment she gave up her defenses, her body would be immediately wrapped by these black lines.
The silk threads of both sides became entangled, like a mass of intertwining snakes, giving anyone watching goosebumps.
Lloyd's control was gradually achieved.
....
"These black threads are actually 'Tismoxing Iron Wire Worms'?"
Su Lun examined the black threads and discovered they were not inanimate objects but living creatures!
Discovered and named by an ancient alchemist called Tismoxing, these iron-eating parasites have bodies that can stretch up to a hundred meters and are incredibly tough due to their metal diet, impervious to the slash of swords.
Just these two characteristics made them the dream material for a Puppet Master's threads.
Seeing this, Su Lun suddenly felt his perspective was too narrow...
He had assumed that all Puppet Masters' threads were inanimate, but this was another possibility.
This "Trickster" actually used his own body as a host to nurture so many living parasites...
But witnessing this, Su Lun's interest was piqued, and he muttered to himself, "So this is how a Puppet Master can control the field with threads. But then again, how can that guy produce so many threads at once? Is it because of a mystic art or because of the implant..."
This was far more advanced than Su Lun's mechanical gauntlets. No matter how intricately designed the gauntlets were, at most they could only handle a dozen steel wires at a time.
Yet this 'Trickster' Lloyd had black threads sprouting from all over his body, a number that wasn't even in the same league.
There were plenty of threads, but after all, Iron Wire Worms were still bound by being 'physical threads,' susceptible to being pulled and cut as drawbacks.
But what if they could be replaced with the Wailing Witch's hair, capable of shifting between solid and ethereal?
At this thought, Su Lun was suddenly filled with anticipation.
And he finally understood why that young lord of the Olli family was so focused on the witch...
....
Hair and black threads crisscrossed, and the tall, blood-magic-using sister was completely controlled on the spot.
The black and silver threads wrestled each other, and the buildings they passed were carved into segments.
As Lloyd, a 'Trickster,' struggled to compete head-on with a lord-level aberration, he coughed up blood in a short standoff.
But at the same time, he bellowed, "Attack!"
On hearing this, the other second-level professionals also started to form seals, seemingly preparing to unleash powerful strikes...
However, what they hadn't anticipated was that almost at the same time, Su Lun heard the command and made his move as well.
His gaze, previously diffused, suddenly sharpened, as keen as a blade.
In the critical moment, as they were about to strike down the witch, he raised his handgun without hesitation, aiming for the head of the Blue Robe Sorceress who was casting "Slowing Light Beam."
But how keen was the perception of a second-level professional?
Out of the five second-level professionals present, apart from the 'Mechanical Tyrannosaur' Toynbee who was slightly slower to react, the other four instantly picked up on the anomaly.
They saw someone outside the monastery lifting a gun in the fog and all had the same thought: "An ambush!"
Although shocked that someone had awoken from the dream, they reacted immediately.
As Su Lun raised his gun, Blum, the leader of the Blade Brigade, stamped his foot violently, shifting his figure several meters to position himself in front of the Blue Robe Sorceress.
They knew well that it was a critical moment in their effort to kill the witch, and they couldn't afford the slightest error. If the "Slowing Light Beam" spell ended and the witch regained her normal speed, their situation would become very dangerous!
Seeing that the attacker wielded a gun, Blum also breathed a sigh of relief.
It was just a gun; he was confident he could fend it off with a swing of his sword. With him as a shield, no matter how expert the shot, it would not harm anyone!
"Tsk tsk... Close-combat professionals indeed react quickly."
Upon seeing this, Su Lun appeared to have anticipated it, a curve forming on his lips as he fired without hesitation.
As his right hand pulled the trigger, his left hand made a sudden grabbing gesture in the air, controlling the invisible zombie nearby to slash down with its blade!
"Bang!"
The special boom of an alchemy bullet echoed through the entire monastery.
Flames burst from the muzzle, the noise of the bullet masking the sound of the scythe cutting through the air.
Blum was also sharply aware of Su Lun's "little movement" with his left hand.
Nonetheless, he chose to block rather than dodge.
Because he knew that if he dodged, the sorceress behind him would get shot.
Besides, it was just a gunman, even an "Arms Master" couldn't kill him with a single shot.
As long as he could withstand this shot, once the others realized what was happening, it would be the death of that gunman!
However, he didn't realize he was facing Su Lun, the "S-rank Wanted Criminal" from Old Lington City's bounty list, nor did he know about Su Lun's [Xiupunos's Night Scythe], the deadly weapon he possessed!
Blum could block an alchemy bullet, but he was utterly unprepared to block a spatial rift.
The instant the gun fired, the sound of the bullet drew everyone's attention, unaware that the next moment, a dark spatial rift would silently appear right in front of Blum's forehead.
Even though he shielded his head with his weapon, the blade unequivocally sliced through his Famed Double-edged Sword as well.
The spatial rift continued its momentum, chopping off half of Blum's head before vanishing.
And just at that moment, a bullet passed through the split in the severed head...
The Blue Robe Sorceress, who continued casting spells without a chance to react, watched in bewilderment as the person in front of her had their head halved. Then... a bullet grew larger in her vision, striking her eye socket, and the world plunged into darkness.
"Boom~"
A bursting sound erupted, the Blue Robe Sorcerer's head exploded into a cloud of blood, and she fell to the ground with a thud.

chapters.title: Chapter 144 - 144 [Alice's Tears]
chapters.content:
"Done!"
Having finished off the two men in front of him, Su Lun's brows relaxed slightly.
Killing these two had been within his expectations.
Before he made his move, he had guessed that the action of raising the gun to fire was too obvious to conceal from high-ranking professionals.
The opposition would not just stand by and watch him kill that Control Mage, so there would definitely be someone coming to the rescue.
The scythe that he swung while lifting the gun held the true hidden killing intent. It was intended to take out a second-class professional who might come to aid the Control Mage while he was being killed.
Now, it seemed the effect was good.
....
Su Lun was well aware of his limitations.
After all, he was just one person, and as strong as he was, he was only first-class.
Even with a scythe in his hand, once discovered and the enemy on guard, it would be much harder to kill again.
A second-class professional would not just stand there and wait for him to make the kill.
So, Su Lun needed an ally.
In a situation with fewer people, how could he snatch the enemy's boss and kill an enemy several times his number?
The best approach was naturally to ambush and get rid of the enemy's controller, letting the monsters run rampant.
This was also why he chose to take out that Blue Robe Sorcerer immediately.
Just like now, the Wailing Witch, no longer covered by the "Slowing Light Beam," let out a piercing scream as if relieved, and in an instant, the speed of her hair attacks visibly surged by fifty percent!
Before, the few second-class professionals in the field could comfortably handle the siege of her hair. Now, they were suddenly overwhelmed and put in disarray.
Busy dealing with her hair, they simply had no chance to deal with Su Lun, the ambusher.
Seeing the few strands of surprised and murderous gazes turning towards him, Su Lun was not at all afraid. He did not stop the movements in his hands, again flexing his fingers to pull on the invisible zombie beside him, slashing towards another target not far away.
Seeing this, the Trickster Lloyd's face changed drastically, realizing something and hastily shouted, "Stop him quickly!"
Silver and black threads crossed, like tug-of-war contestants, he controlled the Witch with his threads, but at the same time, he was immobilized.
Lloyd knew very well in his heart that he was the key to control. If anything happened to him, the Witch in her fury would break completely free, and what awaited them was certain failure, even a desperate situation!
However, how could the few second-class professionals not guess that the spatial crack that had killed Blum was the work of the notorious banned weapon, "Xiupunos's Night Scythe"?
Knowing that, who would dare to block it with their body?
Moreover, they couldn't block it even if they wanted to!
The next instant, another spatial crack appeared, precisely at the Trickster Lloyd's neck.
Without a sound, the head fell.
Su Lun had thought his strike would definitely kill the immobile Puppet Master, but to his surprise, when the head hit the ground, he did not see the "grey mist."
"Huh... Not dead?!"
Su Lun's pupils shrank suddenly, and his instinctive reaction to danger made him dart behind the invisible zombie.
In the next moment, he heard the whistling of the wind, and several poison needles shot out from the severed head, "thud thud thud" hitting the invisible zombie in front of him, and fell to the ground.
Upon looking again, the headless corpse of Lloyd's robe split open, and out sprang an ugly dwarf about one meter tall.
"Is this Lloyd's real body?"
Su Lun had not expected that the notorious Puppet Master would actually be an ugly-faced dwarf.
....
Although the witch was strange and not highly intelligent, she knew the biggest threat was the one controlling her!
Lloyd dodged Su Lun's lethal moves but couldn't escape the omnipresent silver hair within the monastery.
After the beheading, the spell was interrupted.
Now he was forced to abandon the puppet body and also lost control over most of the black threads.
With the black threads no longer binding her, the witch's silver hair was entirely liberated, and a piercing shriek echoed throughout the cursed space.
In an instant, the sky was densely filled with silver hair spreading like a tidal wave, fast enveloping the monastery in a silver cocoon, strand by strand, clump by clump.
Previously, what they all desired from the rampaging witch—"infinite hair strands," now became their death warrant.
And as soon as the dwarf landed, a spear-like strand of silver hair stabbed at him, "clang" it pierced a fist-sized hole in the stone pavement.
The agility of the Puppet Master's flesh was limited, certainly not comparable to other professionals. Although the dwarf tried his best to dodge, he still got grazed by the sharp spear, piercing through his thigh, and blood pooled on the ground...
Moreover, to add to the despair, more than ten spears of silver hair quickly formed in the air and shot down with a "whoosh whoosh whoosh".
Lloyd's face was ashen.
In this moment of crisis, Toynbee—the "Mechanical Tyrannosaurus" closest to the dwarf—reacted swiftly. The mechanical arm, originally charging up to attack the witch's body, instantly shifted direction and launched, shattering the silver spears and thus saving the dwarf's life.
The silver hair filled the sky like a downpour, impossible to avoid.
The other second-tier professionals were struggling to take care of themselves, with injuries of varying degrees...
And the first-tier Blue Robe Sorcerer who cast "Thorn Entanglement" managed to dodge several spears but still ended up hopelessly pierced full of bloody holes...
With this, the witch was thoroughly unbound.
The previously deadlocked battlefield was suddenly broken, and the rout was like a dam burst, beyond redemption.
Seeing that the situation was untenable, the dwarf barked darkly, "Retreat! Exit the cursed space first!"
The four second-tier professionals gathered together, destroyed the silver hair above their heads, and tore a scroll before they were completely trapped.
The scroll shattered, and a magic portal appeared out of thin air. The group did not hesitate to charge through it.
....
"Thought I could kill a few more of them..."
Su Lun watched as the figures escaped through the light portal, feeling a slight tinge of regret.
Prepared to ward off falling into dreams and equipped with escape tactics, the people from the Oliver family had clearly come well-prepared.
They could escape, but Su Lun could not.
Not to mention the magic portal vanished the moment it appeared, even if it hadn't, he would not have followed them out and "delivered himself to death."
As the shrieking began, the "nutrients" in the mist were also swept clean.
In the vast cursed space, only the solitary Su Lun remained alive.
Now with no one else to draw fire, the only target for the towering blood nun was him.
"Just hope my previous deduction wasn't wrong..."
He exhaled a breath of turbid air.
Su Lun took off his gas mask and brought Mr. Brook's harmonica to his lips.
Having never learned harmonica in a previous life, this rather simple instrument had already been mastered proficiently from the Soul Shards he had collected.
Without overthinking, he started a slow folk tune, a melody he had heard hummed by NPCs in "The Legend of the Bell Tower Monster" space.
The melodious tune resonated throughout the entire monastery.
It was the moment the melody of the harmonica sounded that the ferocious, silver hair around seemed to understand the desolation within the tune. Suddenly, it softened, like the water plants in a clear pond, drifting with the breeze...
Su Lun played on, becoming more and more detached, the rhythm steady and unhurried.
In the distance, the over five-meter-tall Blood Nun also lost her ferocity, standing there dazed and listening quietly.
As if recalling something, tears slowly welled up in the corners of her eyes.
Su Lun continued to play the piece, and the scenery around him rapidly changed.
It was as though time had reversed, the broken walls and ruins instantly restored to their original state, transforming into that solemn and majestic white monastery.
Snowflakes began to drift down from the sky, and doves could once again be seen flying above the domes...
The scenery shifted in a flash, as if returning to a thousand years ago.
That young nun would often stand alone on the loft, playing that melody filled with her longing, waiting for her beloved to return safely from the battlefield.
They had promised that he would come back to her in that snowy winter.
But unthinkably, she waited until Dawn City fell into eternal darkness and he never returned.
....
After a while, the tune came to an end.
"I was entrusted by Mr. Brook to bring this harmonica back to you,"
Su Lun stopped playing, not sure if the transformed Alice could understand him. Seeing that the Witch had calmed down, he extended the harmonica toward her.
He continued, "He asked me to tell you that he can no longer keep the appointment and that you shouldn't wait for him anymore."
The gentle silver hair took hold of the harmonica engraved with "Brook&Alice," handing it to the young nun.
A smile slowly spread across her face as she seemed to see some beautiful vision before her, whispering softly, "Have you finally come back to see me..."
With a flash of light and shadow, the figure of a handsome man in military uniform appeared in the yard of the monastery. Smiling, he took his beloved girl's hand and said tenderly, "Yes, I have come back."
They had vowed to love each other for this lifetime.
Brook's short life had already faded atop the bell tower a thousand years ago;
And Alice...
Waiting for this one message,
Waited for a thousand years.
Su Lun quietly observed the scene before him.
He knew he was probably the sole witness to that tragic love story from a thousand years ago.
A young girl had waited a lifetime for a promise.
At that moment, the young nun placed the harmonica to her lips and tenderly began to play that familiar melody again.
As the haunting tune sounded, a sparkling tear slowly fell from the corner of her eye.
....
With no "malice" left in the nun before him, Su Lun also relaxed the steel wire he was holding.
Now that he had fulfilled Brook's commission and used the harmonica to resolve a mortal crisis, he felt accomplished.
Yet, he had not forgotten that before him stood a Lord-level apparition capable of striking down a second-tier professional on the spot.
Su Lun didn't possess the ability of the others to create a magic portal and escape.
If he wanted out, he would have to kill the source of the curse.
He had planned to find an opportunity to deliver a fatal blow.
But now, it seemed unnecessary.
As the tear fell, he also saw the "Lord-level apparition's" aura suddenly deflate, transforming from the sharpened aggression of a moment ago to an increasingly tranquil state.
And upon appraisal, the glowing tear on the ground was unmistakably a cursed object.
[Alice's Tear]
Description: A crystallization of all the magic power within the Wailing Witch, an extremely precious cursed material; it contains immense magic power and spiritual power, including the most complete spiritual matrix of the witch's lineage;
"All magic power condensed?"
Reading these words, Su Lun suddenly realized something.
Looking again at the nun, her presence was also growing weaker.
It appeared she had received the answer she'd been waiting for over a thousand years, her obsession was finally relieved, and she was about to dissipate completely from this world.
Without feeling any more hostility, Su Lun thought better of delivering the final blow.
As for the Witch's hair he needed, the monastery was strewn with it.
For the body, it would be enough to wait a moment.
The sound of the harmonica became more mournful and fainter by the moment.
As he listened, Su Lun began silently to gather the battle spoils and blood scattered around the courtyard.
.....
A second-tier professional had died, the leader of the Battle Knife Squad, Blum, yielding some battle experience.
And those two rare Mage Sorcerers gave Su Lun a little surprise.
They were graduates from the inner city's Black Tower Academy from the last two sessions, having high-quality Soul Shards, which awarded Su Lun a significant influx of spellcasting experience and alchemical knowledge.
And the headless "Alchemical Puppet" was naturally left behind by the Trickster, Lloyd.
The dwarf had fled in a panic, not even managing to strip the Storage Ring from the puppet.
A glance revealed many rare puppeteering materials that could be useful.
It was a bountiful harvest indeed.
But as he listened, the harmonica fell silent.
Su Lun turned his head.
He saw the nun lying on the ground, clutching her beloved harmonica, her lips still curled in a blissful smile, her demeanor peaceful.
"It's quite beautiful,"
he said to the body, and then walked over, dispassionately severing the glowing head of the Witch.
'You have acquired 2 memory fragments of "Witch Alice"'
'You have gained a snippet of information: "It feels like a very long time has passed, but I have finally waited for him, I am so happy..."'
'You have comprehended the [Intermediate String Control Technique]...'
'Spiritual power +7.5'
The cursed space began to collapse.
Su Lun undid his disguise, his body erupting with cold flames.
He had not forgotten that there were still people outside the cursed space waiting for him to walk into their trap.

chapters.title: Chapter 145 - 145: A Group Waiting to Kill Su Lun
chapters.content:
Outside the cursed space.
Danz Oliver, guarded by a host of bodyguards, wore a relaxed smile on his face.
Having spent such a great cost to hire so many experts, he was naturally determined to obtain the "Wailing Witch's cursed hair."
To speak nothing of the experts from the main Oliver family, the Crow Gang, which was funded by their family, was one thing, but it was quite something else to have enlisted the help of "Mechanical Tyrannosaurus" Toynbee, a high-ranking member of the Steam Party.
Of course, all this was thanks to the help of the lady in fox fur by his side.
Danze looked at the enchanting, graceful beauty beside him and felt in high spirits, laughing, "Hahaha... I must thank Mrs. Sabina for her righteous assistance in making this happen."
After all, this was an underground relic, not inside Old Lington City.
After all, the Scavengers were outsiders, and his Oliver family would not have been able to quickly assemble so many scavenger slaves in the camp without the help of the three major gangs.
He had just casually asked, and this beautiful lady from the Steam Party agreed to help without hesitation.
Upon hearing this, Sabina, standing beside him, also smiled, a flirtatious look emerging, "Young Master Danze flatters me; it was just a simple effort on my part."
"It's something that must be thanked."
Danze squinted and smiled, his gaze inadvertently drawn to the imposing sight at her chest that was impossible to ignore.
As the legitimate heir of the Oliver family, what kind of beauty had he not seen?
But this Gang Lady had given him that stirring sensation he hadn't felt in a long time. Despite knowing she was the woman of a rival family's gang leader and was untouchable, it only heightened his desire to possess her.
She seemed within easy reach, yet just out of grasp, with a hint of danger about her...
Danze was well aware of their mutual needs, yet he thoroughly enjoyed this feeling.
To conquer such a woman would be an even greater sense of achievement.
A crafty gleam flickered in Sabina's crystalline eyes, seemingly unbothered by showing off her proud figure in front of others, she said with parted red lips, "Young Master Danze, with the witch's hair, you should be able to advance to the second order, right?"
"Yes. The advancement materials and the prosthesis blueprints have already been prepared."
Danze nodded confidently, "I was originally just here to accompany the family's caravan to the relic and spend some time in the environment of dense dark spiritual power to enhance my body's resistance. But I never expected to stumble upon one of the few rare threads most suitable for a Puppet Master, the 'witch's hair'. It's indeed an unexpected delight..."
He did not hide his happiness in his tone, and he had even imagined how he would dazzle everyone in the realm of puppetry artistry in Old Lington with the prosthesis made from "endless hair."
Continuing, Danze did not forget to say very gentlemanly, "And it's also thanks to the Madam's great help."
Sabina's lips curled into a seductive smile, "Then I shall congratulate you in advance."
"Once I successfully advance, my Oliver family will host a celebration banquet. Madam, you must honor us with your presence..."
Danze had already begun inviting guests for the victory feast.
But the unexpected happened very suddenly.
He had not finished speaking when suddenly a six-pointed star magic gate appeared on the seal in front of him.
"Could it be that they killed the witch?"
Danze looked at the magic gate and was about to rejoice, but in the next second, his expression froze.
Because he saw several figures fleeing in disarray.
....
The four second-order survivors all had injuries, more or less, because the Wailing Witch had suddenly broken free and run amok.
Seeing the ugly dwarf with an injured leg, Danze's face changed drastically. He quickly went over and asked, "Teacher! How... How did you get injured like this?"
He had never seen anyone push his teacher to such a sorry state. After all, the alchemical puppet was an ancient relic purchased by the family at a great cost, indestructible. Who could have forced him to abandon the puppet and flee for his life?
Could it be that there was an accident in the ambush on the formidable witch?
How could that be...
They knew the witch's modes of attack like the back of their hand; how could there be an accident!
The same questions were apparent on everyone's faces present there.
Hearing the question, "Trickster" Lloyd could not hold in his anger and questioned furiously, "Damn it! How did that wanted criminal end up in the witch's cursed space? Didn't you notice when you sent people in?!"
This was the first time he exposed his dwarfishness before others, feeling the strange looks around him intensified his anger.
"Ah...?"
Danze was confused by this abrupt and bewildering question, "Teacher, what... what wanted criminal are you talking about?"
Lloyd was beside himself with rage, "Hmph, just a moment ago, we were just one step away from killing that second-order witch, but we didn't expect a sneak attack!"
Hearing this, Danze was both shocked and angry, "Teacher, you were ambushed?!"
Lloyd, teeth itching with hatred, continued, "Someone sent that 'S-ranked wanted criminal Su Lun' into the cursed space. Then that guy used 'Xiupunos's Night Black Scythe' to kill Blum and Pecor, eventually causing the plan to slay the witch to fall apart. I nearly died in there too!"
An issue in the ambush?
But listening, Danze's gaze trembled, and his face filled with disbelief, "How could that be... these were just ordinary slaves."
"Ordinary slaves?"
Lloyd snorted coldly and briefly recounted what had just happened.
With that explanation, everyone finally understood the situation.
But all the streets near the monastery had already been sealed off by a spatial blockade, only those who were sent in as a slave group could enter.
Recognizing "Xiupunos's Night Scythe," these people immediately guessed that the attacker was the recently notorious Su Lun from Old Lington City.
But how could a fugitive, whose wanted posters were plastered everywhere, be sent into the space?
Just as everyone was utterly puzzled about how the assailant could have infiltrated the cursed space, a captain of the battle-sword group suddenly remembered something.
He said, "That one, if he was wearing a parrot mask... I have a bit of an impression, there was such a guy in the 'Drunkard Group'."
Upon hearing this, Danze frowned, "Drunkard Group?"
The captain continued, "A minor freelance group that has already been sent into the cursed space. However, there was one guy with a parrot mask and a little devil who disappeared before Young Master Danze arrived."
"Why didn't you say so sooner!"
"I thought they had been caught in the witch's cursed space and were long dead..."
"Drag him away and execute him!"
"Please, Young Master Danze..."
"..."
Although the words of the battle-sword group captain solved the mystery for everyone, instead of being rewarded, he was immediately executed by an infuriated Young Master Danze.
This was a major incident; if their own leader hadn't already perished in the space, even a second-tier professional would have been executed on the spot!
What the hell were you doing, bringing a slave group here to scout for traps and end up bringing a fugitive with ulterior motives?
And almost causing the hunting team to be annihilated!
....
The man was killed, temper cooled a bit.
But at this point, there was no use fretting over "why the fugitive appeared in the space."
Moreover, the losses weren't too severe.
Only three professionals and a batch of slaves died, the witch's space was still here, the main force was intact; for the Oliver family, it wasn't a big problem.
The pity was the loss of two rare controllers, the Magicians.
Danze asked, "Teacher, what do we do now?"
"We temporarily can't enter the witch's space; without controllers, going in recklessly would lead to great casualties. To get the hair, let's wait until the family dispatches more professionals," he said.
Lloyd also sighed slightly, contemplating for a moment before speaking again, "What we need to worry about now is... the subsequent moves of that fugitive."
Hearing his teacher say this, Danze was puzzled, "Teacher, the fugitive hasn't emerged yet, so he's probably dead in the cursed space. After all, it's very hard to kill a second-stage witch with just physical damage. Moreover, using that banned scythe comes with a great cost, swinging it twice, whether he can survive is another matter..."
"We can't be careless."
Lloyd shook his head, as if struck by a thought, his brow furrowed and he said, "There was an intelligence report claiming that guy had a method to possibly evade the scythe's curse backlash. Now it seems very likely to be true. Otherwise, after killing three high-ranking Umbrella Organization fighters in Old Spiriton Outer City, he would have succumbed to reverse damage from the scythe long ago."
He paused, then continued analyzing, "If Su Lun was able to remain conscious in the witch's dream-making ability, then he surely came prepared. And since he dared to make a move, he must have been confident about his chances of survival."
Hearing this, Danze's brows furrowed, "A method to evade curse backlash?"
"Mm."
As they spoke, Lloyd thought of something and narrowed his eyes, "When that guy attacked earlier, I clearly detected him manipulating puppet limbs. I guess he must have used 'Oz Frostman's Shroud' to create an invisible puppet. That's probably also his method to avoid backlash from the scythe."
Hearing this, Danze frowned, puzzled and immediately said, "An invisible puppet? But teacher, I've seen that banned scythe with my own eyes and even if a puppet uses it, the curse's backlash should still track back to the source..."
Lloyd looked equally perplexed and shook his head, "I don't know. Perhaps it's some kind of special living person puppet. His puppet control technique is excellent, must be employed in some rare puppetry profession, might even have some ancient puppet crafting techniques..."
Danze's face darkened.
If one could really avoid curse backlash, how terrifyingly formidable would that banned scythe be?
And the fact was, Su Lun had already used this scythe to kill at least four second-tier professionals!
At this thought, everyone felt a chill on their necks.
At that moment, Lloyd thought of something and said gravely, which made Young Master Danze's spine chill even more, "It's possible that Su Lun came specifically for Young Master Danze... this point, we must be careful."
Danze, startled, said in confusion, "I have no grievances with that fugitive, why would he come after me?"
Lloyd's eyes cast a shadow, "No... you've met before."
Danze racked his brains, puzzled, "Huh?"
Lloyd added, "Remember at the camp market, someone stole those witch hairs from you? Just now, that Su Lun controlled a living corpse without leaving any trace, obviously using a transparent thread. Other than that, I can't think of any other thread that would fit the situation!"
Listened and realized, Danze exclaimed, "That guy?! Damn it, had I known, I should have killed him at the camp!"
"Don't be complacent, get ready, that guy might have other methods to escape from the cursed space."
Before Lloyd could finish his sentence, someone suddenly shouted, "Not good, the witch's cursed space is collapsing!"
At the same time, an eight-legged figure darted out.
"It's him!"
Lloyd's pupils contracted sharply, and he bellowed, "Kill that guy!"

chapters.title: Chapter 146 - 146 "King of Guns" Geiger
chapters.content:
"It's him, kill that guy!"
Su Lun heard the loud shout from afar, and without any hesitation, his eight spider legs sprinted and leaped as he ran wildly.
The direct heir of the Oliver family, Danzel, had arrived in person, and naturally, he was not without experts at his side.
With just a glance from the corner of his eye, apart from the four that had previously escaped, Su Lun also saw at least four or five second-tier professionals.
Only when he saw that enchanting woman in a white fox fur did he understand why there were Steam Party cadres in the team that had previously surrounded and attempted to kill the witch.
"The Oliver family is actually cooperating with the Steam Party supported by their competitors?"
A fleeting doubt crossed Su Lun's mind, but the speed at which he was escaping did not slow down in the slightest.
It wasn't just this group of second-tier professionals, but also over a hundred members from more than ten elite Scavenger teams of the Oliver family.
The intense glares filled with murderous intent were oppressive, making him feel like a spit-roasted lamb, continuously being turned over the flames.
...
The moment Su Lun showed his face, several rockets trailing long flames were already aimed at him and fired.
"Boom~"
"Boom~"
"Boom~"
The shells landed nearby, exploding incessantly.
Fragments of stone splattered against him, cracking upon impact.
Fortunate for Su Lun's keen senses, he was able to anticipate the trajectories of the rockets in time.
And it was lucky the agility of his eight-arm spider spear allowed him to traverse walls and ditches across the ruins with ease. Thus, he narrowly avoided the first volley of rockets without harm.
The bad news was, wherever he looked, enemies were all he saw.
The good news was, the ruins were spacious enough, with complex buildings within, allowing the superior teleportation abilities of his eight-arm spider spear to be fully utilized.
Having dodged the rockets, intense gunfire, like torrential rain, followed behind him.
But by then, Su Lun had already seized the opportunity to slip behind a building.
Then...
With a thunderous "boom," a fireball descended from the sky, and the building was instantly flattened by the bombardment.
"Second-tier magic professionals have made their move..."
Su Lun stumbled from the hot blast of the explosion but managed not to fall thanks to the stability granted by his extra legs.
However, he didn't dare look back, instead using the momentum of the blast to increase his speed by a fraction.
He could distinctly feel six or seven particularly chilling "killing intents" locked onto him from behind.
There was no need to think about it; those were the enemy's second-tier professionals in pursuit.
With his eight-arm spider spear, Su Lun could easily outpace ordinary professionals.
As long as he avoided the initial barrage of firepower, the hundred or so Scavengers from the Oliver family in the ruins of Dawn City were no threat at all.
From beginning to end, his troubles came from the few second-tier professionals who could both fight and chase.
Like...
The group of persistent black crows hovering overhead!
....
Su Lun dared not run towards the outer perimeter of the ruins.
He was well aware that running towards the outskirts would be safer, but those second-tier professionals would undoubtedly chase him relentlessly. Moreover, he was very likely to be surrounded and caught by various Scavenger groups mobilized by the Oliver family, with no chance of escape.
```
Only by running deep into the ruins would the chances of encountering people be lower.
The ruins were dangerous for him, and they were equally dangerous for those second-order professionals.
Only by taking advantage of the ruins' environment and its uncanniness to delay his pursuers could he possibly escape.
Fortunately, he had gathered a lot of information at the tavern yesterday, and Su Lun had a rough understanding of some of the dangerous zones in the eastern city. He hadn't dared to barge into those "death zones" and chose a direction to plunge headlong into the ring of ruins.
Su Lun looked at the crows flapping their wings above him and knew it was the doing of "Blood Crow" Langfero.
If these crows didn't die, he wouldn't have a chance to escape.
Without a second thought, he raised his gun and sprayed a volley of bullets.
Gunfire crackled.
Seven or eight crows fell at the sound, bursting into clusters of black blood mist in the air.
"This move again..."
Su Lun glanced at the blood mist and murmured to himself.
These crows were a sinister trick of the magicians. He still vividly remembered the scene of coughing up crows after an encounter with that "Plague Doctor" Sergei.
He had learned his lesson now, not only wearing a gas mask but also quickly avoiding the area where the crow's blood was scattering.
This wasn't Old Lington; there was no endless supply of crows here.
After changing the magazine, he raised his arm and fired another burst, and few of the pursuing crows were left flying.
Su Lun intended to kill off all the crows in one go, but at that moment, he suddenly became alert.
"I've been targeted!"
Su Lun sensed something and his expression shifted slightly.
His body instinctively turned to the side to avoid the killing intent.
But it was this evasive action that, instead of allowing him to dodge the bullet, made him "catch" it.
"Pop~"
A burst of blood erupted from his forearm, piercing a hole straight through it.
If it weren't for his current resilience from the "X Serum" and the bracer reducing the bullet's force, that shot would have blown his entire forearm off!
"How did it hit?!"
With his right arm broken, Su Lun felt not only astonishment, but also confusion.
He had dodged it, so how could he be hit?
But there was no time to think further as that familiar sense of fatality struck again.
"I'm in the sights of that gunman again!"
Su Lun's heart chilled and he instinctively tried to move and dodge.
This time, an odd scene unfolded once more!
He had figured out the direction of the hostile gaze from behind him, as well as the rough trajectory of the bullet, and his body instinctively moved out of the original path.
But even with such caution, a bullet still hit his back.
The gunman hadn't aimed at his original position, but seemed to have anticipated Su Lun's next footfall after dodging.
The enemy had anticipated his anticipation!
"'Gun King' Geiger?!"
Su Lun, realizing this capability, immediately guessed who the individual shooting from behind was.
Glancing back briefly, he caught sight of an individual holding a rifle. That figure quickly matched with the face in his memory, and he muttered to himself, "No wonder I was struck by two consecutive shots. It's not surprising it's this guy..."
The gunman was none other than the highly renowned "Firearms Master" of Old Lington City, one of the top figures among the gunman-professionals, known as 'Gun King' Geiger Kiriman!
```
The talent Geiger awakened was extremely compatible with that of a gunslinger—[B-098-Sixth Sense]. The old-fashioned rifle in his hand, the infamous assassin's sniper rifle known as [Lucky 777], was rumored to have taken the lives of well over a hundred professionals, not to mention countless ordinary folks!
His talent wasn't considered strong; in fact, it didn't enhance his body at all.
But to almost any gunslinger, it was one of those dream "god skills."
[Sixth Sense] wasn't some profound divination ability, just a kind of instinctual feeling. It allowed him to predict the target's next move, to dodge harm that was about to befall him, all without any side effects!
It wasn't a case of guessing right every time, but at least eight or nine times out of ten.
It was this ability that had kept Geiger alive through countless brutal battles, elevating him to the status of "King of Gunslingers" in the hearts of all Old Lington's professionals.
The two shots were less than ten seconds apart.
The angle was tricky.
The first bullet hit the arm, the second landed in the back.
However, because Su Lun had the alloy plate from the disassembled [PZ911 Mechanical Limb] on his back, the second shot didn't cause him any harm.
From a distance, Geiger, noticing this scene, was slightly surprised, "Eh... the material of this bulletproof plate is a bit special. Even my specially formulated 'armor-piercing round' didn't penetrate it."
Thinking this, he removed another bullet he had been biting on and reloaded, aiming at the fleeing eight-legged silhouette up ahead, with a mocking smile on his face, "To date, no first-class professional has survived three shots from my rifle. Looks like you'll need a fourth, buddy..."
...
And at the very moment Geiger was aiming, that shadowy sense of lethal danger struck at Su Lun's heart once again.
"A marksman who can predict with such accuracy... what a pain..."
Su Lun squinted his eyes, frowning tightly.
He knew that he probably couldn't dodge the next bullet.
But facing the 'King of Gunslingers', he didn't feel completely helpless.
This time, Su Lun didn't simply choose to teleport to evade; instead, as he darted, he pulled out four pitch-black puppets, positioning them at his body's vital points.
"Pop!"
Once again, the sound of gunfire.
The guy hit Su Lun's lower back once more.
And this time, the bullet was an "Explosive Alchemy Bullet."
When the bullet burst, Su Lun felt as if his back had been struck by an elephant, and he was blown away.
Being an "Arms Expert" himself, he immediately guessed Geiger's intention with the explosive bullet.
Being cautious enough of a sniper, Su Lun always kept his head hidden in the blind spot of the gunman's vision, even while fleeing.
Now that the second shot had tested out the alloy plate, Geiger knew he couldn't deliver a fatal blow to other parts, so he had to aim for the head. He wanted this shot to unbalance Su Lun, exposing his head for a final, lethal gunshot.
But...
If he had guessed that he would be hit, how could Su Lun not be prepared?
Even though the shot made him stagger, it wasn't a big issue. His Octopus Spear stabilized his body, keeping his critical head from being exposed to Geiger's gunfire.
The enemy, however, might not have been as lucky as he was.
This time, the bullet didn't hit Su Lun's body directly; instead, it struck one of the pitch-black dolls first.
The very instant the doll exploded, painful screams erupted from seven pursuers not too far away.
"Ah!"
The one who had teamed up in the [White Monastery] Curse Space to gang up on the second-class Magician clasped his head and shrieked in agony, as if enduring some intense mental torment.
The moment the second-class Magician clutched his head, Su Lun's eyes flashed sharply.
"Now!"
With a cold snort in his heart, he controlled the walking corpses to raise their hands and strike down.
The Magician was still in excruciating agony, unable to come to his senses, when a space rift had already appeared above his head.
Another supremely smooth cut, his skullcap flipped off, his head split into two crimson halves.
He died instantly on the spot!
At a distance, the few second-tier pursuers were all dumbfounded.
It was clearly "S-through Su Lun" who was shot, so why was it their comrade who got killed?
Now they already knew that Su Lun had the sealed item "Xiupunos's Night Scythe" in his hands, they were extremely cautious, so why were they still killed?
That scream from a moment ago was still fresh in their minds—Su Lun got shot, but why did one of their own suddenly get hit?
Could it be some sort of sinister spell?
Langfero, the "Blood Raven," knew Curse Magic too well, and was so frightened he turned pale, immediately realizing something, he loudly warned, "It's Curse Magic! Careful, don't hit the puppet on his body!"
He feared being even a second late; if someone hit the pitch-black doll on Su Lun again, someone would surely die once more.
Moreover, he guessed that one of them was definitely a curse doll mediated with his own blood.
Langfero knew that the spell couldn't kill him, but damn, paired with that black scythe, one controlled from afar, another killing from afar, it was simply "unsolvable"!
It gave no chance for any reaction; others couldn't save them even if they wanted to.
If this "combo" were to hit him, Langfero felt that he too would certainly be doomed!
Looking at the corpse beside him with its skull chopped open, the rank-and-file of the Raven Gang couldn't help but slow down a half step.
Because he knew, the further away he got, the lesser the influence of the "Grass Man's" curse would be.
...
Indeed.
This pitch-black doll was the "Voodoo Doll" that Su Lun had just made!
Back in the Curse Space, although the four second-tier professionals all managed to escape alive, they all suffered injuries and left behind blood in the monastery, enough for Su Lun to create a medium for Curse Magic.
The effect seemed to be very good now.
On the way to the ruins with the transport team, he had already tested the precise impact distance of the "Voodoo Doll."
Even though the effect of the Curse Magic on second-tier professionals was greatly reduced, Su Lun hadn't intended to use the spell to hurt anyone.
As long as he had a slight chance, the black scythe would follow right after!
Seeing that his strike was effective, Su Lun pulled out another eight or nine pitch-black dolls, trailing them behind him like kites, securely shielding his body.
Although only three of them were functional, he guessed his pursuers wouldn't dare take the risk.
If they hit the mark, someone would definitely die.
The tactical strike worked, and Su Lun had thought about blowing up the "Voodoo Doll" himself, which would almost certainly mean death for the other three.
But he didn't do that.
Because he wasn't sure how many more strikes the hateful living corpse could make.
With the two cuts in the Curse Space before, this was already the third.
If there were one more cut and immediate backlash was triggered, the hateful living corpse would die instantly.
Without the deterrent of the black scythe, it would also spell death for Su Lun himself.
Now this string of dolls seemed to be effective enough.
Even Geiger Kiriman, the "Gun King" who never missed, had stopped firing, not daring to shoot again.
That was sufficient.
With a bit more distance, the threat of the gunman would become smaller and smaller...

chapters.title: Chapter 147 - 147: 147
chapters.content:
Su Lun fled alone, six pursuers hot on his heels.
But upon seeing that he was about to escape into the extremely dangerous central area of the Dawn Relic, the chasers began to panic.
Now, seven second-tier fighters were after a first-tier, and not only had they lost one of their own, but if they let the target get away, would they have any face to return?
The curse space shattered, everyone understood that the "Wailing Witch" must have been killed by Su Lun, and her hair materials surely taken.
They had painstakingly created the opportunity and even pushed the witch into a second-phase lord, only to dress someone else for the wedding?
Would that Oliver family's young master let this go?
And at that very moment, unfortunately, the communication devices indeed transmitted Young Master Danze's furious roar, "Damn it! That guy took the witch's head, you must kill him and bring back my materials!"
The tone of command admitted no doubt.
Hearing this, the faces of several pursuers turned sour.
Apart from the Steam Faction executive "Mechanical Tyrannosaurus" Toynbee, the other five were guards and vassals of the Oliver family. Normally they were high-ranking fighters nurtured by the consortium, which also meant they absolutely had no qualifications to refuse Young Master Danze's orders.
Upon hearing the command from the communication device, the other second-tiers looked at each other, their frowns deepening.
"Trickster" Lloyd's face was so dark it looked like it could drip water.
Only he knew how much Danze was "determined" to get the witch's hair.
Although he was Danze's Puppetry Technique teacher, how could he be unaware of his student's capricious nature?
The fact that the assailant had escaped was a minor issue; if the materials were lost, the young master would surely fly into a rage.
Even his face as a teacher wouldn't work.
The little old man hesitated only for a second before urgently shouting, "Chase! That guy has already used Black Scythe three times; at most he has one more strike before the curse backlash immediately erupts. His invisibility puppet will surely die as well, and then, he'll pose no threat... otherwise, we might as well not return!"
His implication was clear; whoever took the last strike would be the unlucky one.
"Alright!"
The rest exchanged glances and, with steely resolve, charged forward.
As long as they had not awakened to betray the Oliver family, they must execute this order!
...
"Huh... They're coming again?"
Su Lun frowned deeply.
He had just killed a second-tier professional with the help of the "Voodoo Doll," and those guys had quieted down for no more than a moment, only for that feeling of being targeted to return.
Glancing back at the suddenly accelerated pursuers, Su Lun guessed, "Did they receive a death order from that young master?"
Thinking this, he, too, sensed that things were not good.
Consortium enforcers naturally had to serve the consortium.
But if those guys had no way out, neither did Su Lun himself.
Looking ahead with no hesitation, he immediately plunged into the deeper, mist-shrouded part of the relic.
That "Gun King" Geiger might be formidable, but after all, a gunner is not adept at rapid pursuit and capture.
In the mist-enveloped and complex structure-riddled Dawn Relic, as long as the distance was sufficiently extended, the threat of the gunner would lessen.
Yet, the enemy had obviously guessed this too.
They seemed to know that if they continued the chase, even if they caught up with him, their situation would be very dangerous if they ventured too deep into the relic. That was when they decided to settle the outcome in one go!
Gunshots rang out again.
"Bang!"
The sound of the gunshot was half a beat slower than the bullet.
Before the sound was heard, Su Lun distinctly felt his body being hit, stumbling once again.
And by chance, he was hit on the same "shield," which was the "Voodoo Doll" connected with the blood of that "Trickster" Lloyd.
A second after the doll burst, Su Lun caught a glimpse of the dwarf controller's figure halting.
Despite the closing lethal threats, Su Lun decided to kill this man first!
