Without any hesitation, he manipulated the invisible zombie, knife flashing down towards the dwarf.
This time, however, the attack did not go as smoothly as before.
When he swung the knife, the second-tiers unleashed their skills in unison, speed suddenly increased by several folds, rushing forward recklessly, determined to take Su Lun down in one fell swoop.
...
The speed of the Octo-Spear Spider might be quick, but that doesn't mean that second-tier professionals lacked the means for short-distance bursts.
Previously, no one used such tactics because they all had their own schemes, each hoping the other would step on the metaphorical mine.
After all, Su Lun was holding a scythe that killed whoever it sliced.
But now, they had received a death command and guessed that Su Lun's scythe only had one more slash left in it.
Seeing Lloyd being the one hit solidified their relief.
One's own misfortune was preferential to the misfortune of a companion.
Since that slash had been made, melee fighters with Teleportation abilities no longer had any reservations and burst forth at full power.
The "Mechanical Tyrannosaur" Toynbee reacted the fastest.
The modified jet propulsion device had been accumulating great pressure, and now it was released all at once.
"Pff" went the sound.
The white steam, like plumes of white smoke from a rocket launch, gushed forth like a tide.
He shot forward like a speeding bullet, covering hundreds of meters in a blink.
Even as Su Lun made several abrupt stops to change direction, Toynbee also made use of pressure release to stop abruptly, followed by several long-distance jet-boosted lunges, catching up to him in an instant. Then, a mechanical arm's claw "clicked" and shot out in mid-air...
As Su Lun controlled the invisible zombie wielding the Black Scythe to attack the distant dwarf, he had to exert himself to avoid that mechanical claw.
And it was this dodge that made the Scythe's trajectory slightly off. It did not cut the dwarf's neck but only managed to sever his legs.
Su Lun had no time for a follow-up strike because at that moment, the killing intent was upon him again.
Aside from the mechanical arm, closely following it was a suited bodyguard from the Oliver family.
The guy charged up a massive leap, his trouser legs bursting open to reveal frog-like exaggerated muscles, and in a flash covered a hundred meters...
"Boom!"
In the split second as Su Lun sheathed his weapon, the frog-legged suited bodyguard had already charged in front of him, slamming headfirst into his chest.
How swift could a second-tier close-combat job holder be?
Su Lun had no time whatsoever to react.
He caught the opponent's movement with his eyes, but his body couldn't keep up. In this critical moment, his thoughts raced, and he could barely use the spider legs to cling onto a dark puppet and shield his chest.
With that collision, "crack," the puppet shattered into pieces.
Su Lun was hit so hard that his eyes bulged, and a mouthful of old blood spurted out.
Another "boom" echoed, the massive force from the impact spreading from the point of collision like a breached dam.
It felt like being struck in the chest by a rampaging rhino, instantly giving him the illusion that his soul remained in place while his body was sent flying.
The next instant, his soul finally caught up, returning to his body.
Only then did Su Lun feel the vertigo from his qi and blood flowing backward through his limbs.
Flying backward, he had just started to feel his bodily existence when he heavily crashed into a building, smashing through two solid walls before finally coming to a stop.
Then, another mouthful of turbid blood sprayed everywhere.
If not for the alloy breastplate on his chest, that blow might have been fatal on the spot.
However, in even more agony was another person!
The very moment the dark doll shattered, Toynbee, the mechanical warrior who was rushing to assist from over ten meters away, suddenly let out a painful scream, nearly fainting while clutching his head.
The pain from the Voodoo Doll, which was bonded with his blood as a medium and exploded at such close range, could only be imagined.
Moreover, it was this tactic that prevented Su Lun from being caught in a pincer attack and instantly killed.
....
Su Lun was hit so hard that his organs were displaced, and he felt like his whole body was falling apart, unable to muster any strength.
In this critical moment, he didn't even have time to catch his breath, his eyes suddenly flashing with intensity, his gaze fierce and detached.
In the next instant, the expression of pain on his face disappeared, and his severely injured body seemed to no longer feel any pain.
Forcing his will to rise, he displayed his sharp spider limbs like spears in front of his chest, while the other four limbs rapidly dragged several odd puppets to protect him.
After this defensive action, Su Lun's hands reached out into the void, trying to grab the distant black scythe for a desperate final struggle!
But unexpectedly, he felt a different tension on the thread.
It wasn't the anticipated scattered flesh, but a complete, animated corpse?
Su Lun instantly understood, a surprised delight in his heart: "Eh?"
...
Even though Su Lun had controlled the precision and power of each slash, four slashes in quick succession brought him to the limit of backlash.
Especially the last one, from too far a distance, one slash was equivalent to the previous two.
The curse of the black scythe triggered instantly!
Although wrapped in a shroud, Su Lun couldn't see where on the corpse the wounds appeared, but at the moment of wielding the scythe, he could distinctly feel through the trembling of the thread the animated corpse "blood exploding."
Su Lun had thought he'd have to rely on his own flesh to wield the scythe desperately, but just then...
He surprisingly discovered the abomination didn't die!
Su Lun immediately understood what happened and thought to himself, "The backlash didn't hit the abomination's vital parts?!"
The wounds didn't appear above the neck or in the heart region, which for the abomination meant they weren't fatal.
Even if a limb was severed, a human would lose combat strength, but not an animated corpse!
Its terrifying regenerative ability would quickly heal the wounds.
This also meant...
The abomination had survived a round of curse backlash and could now withstand another four or five slashes!
With this realization, Su Lun's eyes shone brightly.
Despite spitting out blood in his sorry state, a mad grin spread across his face.
....
Thoughts flashed through his mind; reality was but an instant.
On the other hand, the frog-legged bodyguard had no intention of giving Su Lun any chance to live. After slamming him into the ruins, he kicked off the ground again, charging fiercely.
The whooshing sound of the wind assaulted him, so fast that the human reaction was insufficient.
But Su Lun was prepared for this, and the bodyguard, seeing the poisonous spear tips in front of Su Lun's chest, also realized the danger.
He dared not crash into the spears; instead, he came to an abrupt stop right in front of the spider spears and, using his momentum, performed a spinning kick.
Overwhelming force allowed his foot to burst through two strange puppets, and like a whip, it continued unabated, kicking heavily into Su Lun's side.
"Bang~"
A muffled sound accompanied by the crack of bones.
Su Lun suffered another heavy blow, his body flung like a sandbag and collapsing another solid wall.
"Pu~"
More tainted blood sprayed from his mouth and nose, nearly vomiting out his heart and lungs.
However, the bodyguard clearly had no experience with rune puppets. While he was inflicting a close-range heavy blow on Su Lun, he was also affected by the Wailing Witch's screams, and for a moment he was dazed.
It was during this dazed interval that Su Lun found the chance to breathe.
He got up without hesitation and injected himself with a vial of Potion to prevent fainting from the unbearable pain.
While administering the Potion, his eight spider limbs were already controlling the abomination outside the ruins, once again swinging the black scythe!
Su Lun looked at the momentarily dazed bodyguard, cracking a smile, his bloody teeth showing: "Hehe..."
I didn't die, so now it's your turn.

chapters.title: Chapter 148 - 148 [Thousand Threads - Lion's Mane Ballad]
chapters.content:
If it were just steel wires, they would have snapped countless times during such battles.
Regrettably, Su Lun now had plenty of witch hair in his possession.
Infused with dark spiritual power, it became an elemental substance. This transparent thread was not only undetectable by others but even with obstacles in between, the threads could manipulate the puppets as if pulled by magnetism.
It was just a flick of his fingers, and a space fissure instantly appeared on the bodyguard's neck.
Just as the man seemed to be coming out of his daze, and a fatal crisis loomed, his expression changed drastically. But before he could react, the black space fissure had already silently severed his head.
With a "gurgle," the head fell to the ground.
Watching this scene, a sinister smile spread across Su Lun's lips.
Yet, he did not dare to be careless and with another pull of his fingers, he once again manipulated the detestable living corpses outside.
At this time, the "mechanical tyrannosaur" Toynbee, who was under the effect of the curse magic, had also regained consciousness.
....
Toynbee, enduring severe pain in his head, charged into the shattered building.
He arrived just in time to see the scene of the bodyguard's head falling.
Then, seeing Su Lun flick his fingers again, a deep sense of dread flooded his eyes.
He had seen this gesture a few times before. Every time he saw it, a peer expert was inexplicably killed.
Toynbee initially planned to capture the "helpless" Su Lun and claim some credit.
But seeing this, that thought instantly dissipated, and instead, terror overwhelmed him.
Watching the headless corpse spurting blood, his instinctive crisis response prompted him to unhesitatingly release the steam boiler's pressure valve. He didn't dare to advance but rather, a burst of steam sent him flying backward.
Luckily for Toynbee, his quick reaction allowed him to escape just as a foot-long space fissure appeared where he had been standing.
The fissure that should have split open his chest missed due to his body being flung backward, sparing his life.
A mechanical leg broke off cleanly and clattered to the ground.
Although a broken mechanical limb does not cause pain and still left him with fighting capacity,
Toynbee dared not charge back into the ruins.
During his retreat, seeing the "stoically cold" Su Lun flicking his fingers again, he turned even paler with fear.
Having no intention of confronting him head-on, he hurriedly took cover behind another building.
Even so, a frightening space fissure barely missed him as it passed by.
Luckily he had chosen to dodge and flee just in time; otherwise, the tricky consecutive strikes would have certainly been fatal!
In his relief, Toynbee also cursed furiously, "Who the fuck said this guy could only strike once more?!"
Now he was watching as Su Lun killed Young Master Danze's bodyguard with one strike and then swung two more at him, looking as though he could keep going.
"Doesn't the use of that forbidden item bring cursed backlash?"
Amidst cursing, Toynbee was even more terrified. Without a cursed backlash, who could stop the black scythe?
With all fighting spirit drained, he did not forget to hide his body more tightly and muted his presence, fearing that if Su Lun sensed him, another strike would come his way.
....
"Did I evade it? Phew... My body's at its limit."
Panting heavily, Su Lun did not pursue the steam faction's officer who had flown away.
Forcing himself to execute three strikes with his fractured sternum had almost reached his limit.
As the urge to kill ebbed away, after a second or two, he felt his stagnant blood circulation begin to normalize and his strength slowly returned.
"The inner city really has some absurdly strong bodyguards..."
Su Lun looked at the headless corpse on the ground and muttered to himself.
He didn't dare delay any longer, removed the bodyguard's storage ring, and harvested the soul. He also didn't forget to throw an incendiary grenade to burn the blood he had spat out.
Unfortunately, he couldn't deal with the blood outside in time.
Su Lun had already heard the sounds of pursuers coming, so he continued to sprint deeper into the ruins while controlling the eight-armed spider spear.
...
"Seven second-tier pursuers, two dead, two crippled, and three remain..."
As Su Lun ran, he also thought about finding a terrain to kill off the remaining few.
But he was not confident about it.
Firstly, his severely injured body could not withstand intense combat;
Secondly, although he had dealt with the most threatening melee professionals, he was not confident he could kill Geiger, the "Gun King" with the "Sixth Sense" talent, using the black scythe.
Moreover, having used the black scythe to slash thrice already, Su Lun was not sure that the next backlash, the detestable zombie, could withstand it.
By now he had essentially shaken off his pursuers and saw no need to risk an ambush anymore.
Because he had run haphazardly while being chased, Su Lun looked around and felt that he had already reached a very dangerous area within Dawn Relic.
Not long after, the noise from the pursuing enemies behind him gradually faded, and his speed also slowed down.
The fog in the air grew thicker, and then, he saw a low, broken city wall.
That's when Su Lun realized that he had arrived in the "Central District of Dawn City" on the Scavenger's map—a black area.
The surrounding fog had already reduced visibility to an extremely low level, so he dared not venture deeper nor turn back, but coincidentally, he saw a building resembling a bunker and dashed into it.
....
A moment later, the fog in the air grew even denser, almost reaching the point where he couldn't see his own hand.
Su Lun didn't dare to leave the bunker.
It was a well-known experience among Scavengers that regions with thick fog tended to be active with high-level aberrant monsters.
Fortunately, after focusing on listening for a while, he heard no noise of pursuers coming after him.
Su Lun breathed a sigh of relief.
Only then did he start to carefully observe the bunker where he was hiding.
The bunker was not big, roughly ten or so square meters in size.
It looked like a wartime fortress.
The walls were exceptionally sturdy and thick, almost a meter thick. He had also noticed many irregular damage marks on the outer walls when he entered, which looked like they were made by large aberrant monsters stomping and smashing. There were no fractures, proving the structure was very solid.
After looking around, he saw no waste excretions from aberrant monsters, so Su Lun breathed another sigh of relief, thinking that no aberrant monsters were active here regularly.
The entrance and air vents were also very small, and he could easily block them to prevent aberrant monsters from entering.
Feeling it was safe enough, he decided not to go out for the time being.
With that thought, Su Lun used odor-eliminating water to remove his own scent. He then took out a bulletproof plate and a mechanical skeleton, and made a simple yet robust one-way door at the entrance before finally settling down to rest.
Not thinking about sitting because it was uncomfortable, he flipped through the dust and surprisingly found a good item: an ancient long sword of quality comparable to the famed swords on the market.
In the relics, anything that had survived the years was generally very valuable.
If put on the market, this weapon would be worth over a million.
Unfortunately, after searching more, apart from some broken pottery, he found no other valuable items.
Su Lun then leaned against and collapsed on the walls of the bunker to rest.
He gently pressed on the wound on his chest, feeling bursts of stabbing pain, the sensation of rib bone shards piercing the flesh.
It was fortunate that Su Lun had the Spider Spear as his legs. Otherwise, a normal person sustaining such a severe injury wouldn't even be able to walk, and could do nothing but await death.
However, the situation was improving.
Even without taking any healing medicine, Su Lun could distinctly feel the stabbing pain easing.
His injuries were healing quickly, rather than worsening.
The "X Serum" had endowed him with an ultra-high regenerative ability which was now exerting a tremendous effect. The heightened cellular activity was rapidly repairing his severely damaged body as if filling holes.
...
"Whew..."
Su Lun exhaled a long breath of turbid air.
His wounds were healing on their own, without him needing to do anything.
In this moment of rest, he finally had the leisure to tally up his recent gains.
The greatest gain, naturally, was the materials obtained from the "White Monastery."
Su Lun hadn't expected that this one trip out would completely resolve the "Silk Thread" issue.
The Oliver family members had aggravated the witch into a second stage lord status, thereby directly producing a very rare "dark gold material."
[Wailing Witch's Skull]
Details: Dark gold curse material; this is not merely a skull, but also a complex source of curse magic, with a complete structure and inherent magical patterns; as long as there is sufficient energy, it can indefinitely produce witch's hair.
Seeing the information identified from the skull, Su Lun's gaze trembled slightly.
It was not just the hair strands but even the source producing the hair strands that had been secured in one fell swoop.
With these hair strands, he felt like he truly was a Puppeteer now.
Of course, there was also the[Tears of Alice]that had gathered all the magic power of the Wailing Witch's body.
But Su Lun hadn't yet figured out how to use this material deemed "very rare" even by the All-knowing Eye, so he didn't dwell on it much.
Additionally, there were several storage rings and assassination-derived implants and induction materials.
He had killed two first-tier control mages and a second-tier company chief, Blum, in the space.
The implants and induction materials of the two magicians were not bad. The one controlling the thorns yielded a silver-class professional material for[Thorn Sorcerer]; the Slowing Light Beam magician's abilities came from his talents, so his magical implants and induction materials were normal and slightly damaged...
And although Blum's second-tier implants and induction materials were made of black iron, they were very valuable, the black iron implant[Swift Lizard's Magic Muscle]and the necessary [Airsprite Dagger]for induction.
Although the bodyguard was also second-tier, there wasn't anything special in his storage ring.
All together, they would likely fetch a good price.
What interested Su Lun the most, however, was the decapitated alchemical automaton and storage ring left behind by the "Trickster" Lloyd.
Now that he had some free time, he took out the automaton, which looked exactly like a real person, and started to study it carefully.
Upon inspection, it indeed turned out to be an ancient alchemy product from a thousand years ago.
The automaton's skin was very similar to the biomimetic skin Su Lun had seen on Number Nineteen, with high resistance to both physical and magical attacks. However, the materials and craftsmanship were clearly entirely different.
The automaton was hollow inside, containing just enough space for the dwarf to manipulate, along with some complex control components.
Su Lun tried it out and thought that he might be able to make a biomimetic puppet in the future.
....
Then, a pleasant surprise came!
In the pile of books within the storage ring, Su Lun discovered a large number of exclusive Puppet Master texts.
Moreover, he found a very important-looking golden chest. Upon opening it, inside was a second-tier golden alchemical implant schematic—[Thousand Threads - Lion's Mane Ballad]!
Looking over the schematic's effect description, it was exactly the same ability that the "Trickster" Lloyd had demonstrated with threads bursting from his body. When deployed, it looked like the mane on a lion's neck, wildly scattering...
The gold blueprint was almost something that the top finance tycoons of the inner city regarded as prohibited.
Su Lun felt that if he were to rely on his luck alone, he might never find such suitable gold blueprints for a Puppet Master in his lifetime.
"Now this is really a windfall..."
As Su Lun looked at his spoils of war, he suddenly felt that being chased and almost killed was worth it.
He also guessed that both the "Wailing Witch's Head" and these blueprints were likely advancement items prepared for Young Master Danze Oliver.
Now they had fallen right into his hands.
Amazing...
Indeed, hunting down professionals from the same field was the best shortcut to finding materials related to one's profession.
If there were an even better shortcut, it would be to hunt down professionals from the same field within the inner city.
Moreover, there were some Puppet Master-specific tomes that couldn't even be bought in the market, such as "Puppet Manipulation Techniques I and II", "Triple String Technique", "Thread Control Tactics"...
Su Lun claimed to be a "Puppeteer", but in reality, he was just a novice, only knowing a bit about puppet crafting, and completely ignorant of other professional skills.
In terms of professional proficiency, it was even worse than his side job as a "Gunslinger".
All puppet manipulation techniques were self-taught; no one instructed him, nor did he have Soul Shards to extract.
But now it was different.
With these exclusive professional tomes, there was no need for him to blaze a trail. These books were like a smooth pathway...
If he truly digested the contents of these puppet tomes, Su Lun felt that his puppet control level would improve significantly, and he would really be starting properly.
"It's a shame the dwarf's renowned Puppet Master secret 'Marionette Theater' wasn't in the storage ring..."
Su Lun muttered to himself, feeling slightly dissatisfied.
He thought that next time he encountered it, he must ask the Puppet Master thoroughly.
...
As Su Lun went through his spoils, he kept an ear out for any noise outside.
He thought the Oliver family's guys would catch up, but after waiting for an hour or two, they still didn't show up.
There wasn't even the sound of a crow flying in the sky.
He guessed it might be related to the thick fog outside.
Far from feeling relieved, he became even more cautious.
If the Oliver family's people dared not come, it meant the fog definitely harbored great dangers.
Luckily, he had this sturdy little fortress.
Su Lun had no intention of going outside anymore.
Then, as he waited, a minor mishap occurred.
Su Lun looked at his body, suddenly sprouting crow feathers...
Looking at the panel, there was an added "Curse Magic - Crow Feather Parasitism".
Su Lun frowned, guessing that his blood left on the previous battlefield had been tampered with by the 'Blood Crow' Langfero to concoct a curse.
But he only frowned.
Then, he began to pluck out the feathers.
If he didn't have "X Serum", he would probably die.
But now... aside from being disgusting, this level of curse wasn't of much use.
So, Su Lun stayed in the fort, the fog outside growing thicker, and then he noticed that the dark spiritual power in the air started to become more violent...

chapters.title: Chapter 149 - 149: Suddenly Handsome and Compelling
chapters.content:
"The concentration of Dark Spiritual Power is at least ten times what it was before..."
Su Lun looked at the attribute panel with a complex expression, not quite feeling good about it, nor feeling bad.
No wonder those pursuers didn't dare to follow.
After the fog intensified, the Dark Spiritual Power surged out like a fountain, spreading everywhere. This wasn't something ordinary people could withstand, nor could it be filtered by a gas mask due to its high distortion concentration.
Normal concentrations of Dark Spiritual Power were like the cold winds of winter, with each breath feeling like a cool breeze entering the body, slightly chilly; but now, at this concentration, it was more like blades of ice, making breathing feel like slitting one's throat.
But...
Su Lun knew this level was "dangerous," yet his body truthfully felt a thread-like comfort.
He had been paying attention to the changes in the Dark Spiritual Power since the fog had enveloped the area and had been carefully monitoring his body's data to avoid any accidents.
However, he realized there were no signs of any distortions in him.
Even with the Dark Spiritual Power reaching this terrifying level, he still didn't feel uncomfortable.
Instead... With each breath, his own Dark Spiritual Power values were soaring.
His body was frantically absorbing the special energy in the air, and this energy was also transforming his body.
Since there were no examples to refer to, Su Lun could only judge based on his own feelings: the data kept rising without any distortions, which should be a good thing.
He knew that this abnormal situation with his body was definitely related to the enhanced Dark Spiritual Power tolerance from the "X Serum."
....
Not to mention that the fog outside was now so dense that normal vision and walking were impaired.
Since there were no signs of distortions, Su Lun wasn't in a hurry to leave the bunker,
And... it seemed he couldn't get out anyway.
Although he couldn't see, Su Lun could hear from all directions many sounds that made his skin crawl after the fog had engulfed the area.
Sounds like the heavy footsteps of a very large monster, thud, thud, thud...
Sounds like the chewing of flesh and bone, crack, crack, crack...
Sounds like the screams of some distorted creatures being bitten to death...
Hearing more and more of these terrifying noises, Su Lun simply sealed off all the ventilation ducts and didn't dare to let out a single breath.
He knew he had encountered a phenomenon similar to a "beast tide" of large-scale distorted creature activity...
However, Su Lun's mindset was fairly good.
Since he couldn't leave, he calmly set about healing himself here.
The Storage Ring was stocked with plenty of food and water, and the bunker was strong enough to temporarily not worry about safety.
The fog in the ruins was moving, suggesting that this unusual activity was temporary.
Even if small creatures discovered him and burst into the bunker, he thought the Wretched Zombies and Black Reapers could still ensure his safety.
At least, the current situation was much better than just a while ago when he had been surrounded and chased by the Oliver family.
Su Lun prepared some food for himself and then sat down cross-legged to meditate.
This meditation lasted all night.
Although there was no distinction between day and night in the ruins, the "nighttime" was noticeably when the creatures were most active.
Dawn arrived, and there was no sign of the fog dissipating.
But Su Lun felt quite good.
Overnight, his body's strong healing ability had largely recovered his injuries; pressing his chest still caused a slight sharp pain, but the recovery rate was already very satisfying.
And after meditating all night, Su Lun also felt mentally refreshed.
On the data panel, the upper limit of his Dark Spiritual Power had visibly soared.
After advancing in his career, a night of meditation in Old Lington would typically increase the upper limit of his Dark Spiritual Power by about 7~8 units. In these Dawn City Ruins, just over last night, Su Lun had soared by over 100 units!
And, there was not a single sign of distortion due to the rapid absorption of Dark Spiritual Power, or any other negative condition.
Although Su Lun had known that the "X Serum" would enhance his body's tolerance to dark spiritual power, seeing the results still took him by surprise.
Last night, he meditated cautiously, but if he had absorbed without restraint, the numbers might have multiplied several times over.
Following this pace of cultivation, in about a little over a month, his dark spiritual power level would reach the upper limits his body could withstand. That would be a number several times higher than what is required for a professional to advance to the second tier.
From this perspective, this "mist tide" was not only harmless to him but actually an excellent aid in his cultivation.
Su Lun also speculated that the "unrecognized creature" from which the serum was extracted might be some sort of superior being that lived in a highly concentrated dark spiritual power environment, whose bloodline was especially suited for survival in such conditions. Su Lun's injection of the serum altered his body, now giving him some peculiar characteristics of this extraordinary bloodline...
Moreover, because of the significant increase in his dark spiritual power, Su Lun noticed another positive phenomenon; the blue tone of his skin was fading faster.
With the All-knowing Eye, he could accurately distinguish the data changes in his skin color.
Although the change was nearly imperceptible to the naked eye in just one night.
But the data indicated that the fading speed was several times that of yesterday.
The violent influx of dark spiritual power catalyzed the absorption of the serum, greatly shortening the time needed for the absorption process.
Originally, it was estimated that it would still take four to six months to digest the serum, but now it seemed that was no longer necessary.
....
The second day, third day, fourth day...
The fog showed no sign of dissipating,
and the creatures outside became increasingly animated.
And so, Su Lun passively stayed inside the cramped bunker and did not go out.
During this period, he encountered several mutant creatures passing by, including groups of small mutants and several times, terrifyingly large mutants.
Luckily, the small mutants couldn't damage the solid bunker and left after several attempts;
while the giant creatures, although they detected him, ignored him completely. It was probably like how humans view mice in the roadside holes, uninteresting even for filling gaps between teeth.
Occasionally, one or two large creatures, curious and attracted by the smell, would scratch with their claws, but since the bunker was sturdy enough, he passed these instances without any real danger.
Just like that, a month passed unknowingly.
Drastic changes were occurring in Su Lun's body.
....
One day, inside the bunker.
Su Lun was sitting in meditation.
Since the gas mask was useless, he no longer wore it.
However, his face no longer resembled the blue-skinned bald freak from a month ago. His skin tone had returned to normal, a full head of thick hair had grown on top, and even eyebrows had emerged.
Without the dark punk style of smoky makeup, his now sharply featured face suddenly became strikingly handsome.
This was not an illusion of Su Lun's but a direct data representation on his attribute panel.
"My charm has increased to 12?"
Su Lun was surprised when he first noticed the permanent value of charm changing.
Then, over the month, as he completely digested the "X Serum," his charm increased from 9 to its current 12.
Based on his observations, this data point rarely changed with increased strength. Unless one encountered someone with a charm talent like the Steampunk Party's Sabina, the charm value of a normal person wouldn't exceed 10.
The only explanation was that the serum not only made the body stronger but also had a special ability to enhance human appearance.
He guessed that perhaps the creature from whom the "X Serum" was extracted was naturally good-looking?
Su Lun didn't mind much, as it wasn't a bad thing.
Furthermore, the change in appearance was exactly what he wanted.
At least now, he didn't have to continue shaving his head and maintaining the dark punk style.
The previous disguise was to conceal his appearance to avoid recognition by bounty hunters.
Now that the bald image on the wanted posters was everywhere, maintaining the bald punk appearance was inappropriate.
Now that his hair had grown, it was perfect.
Moreover, his current appearance hardly needed to worry about the original owner's wanted order. Because Su Lun felt that absolutely no one would associate his current appearance with the original owner, "Fike Regadi."
Not to mention the transformation in demeanor, the addition of 3 charm points has completely changed his face.
Moreover, even physical measurements such as shoulder width, waist, and hips... had drastically changed from a month ago.
Having fully metabolized the "X Serum," Su Lun's strength had soared, his bones had become tougher, and all these increases were exaggerated, two to three times what they had been. Yet, his muscle dimensions hadn't turned him into a burly strongman; instead, he had become even more slender and proportionate.
But he also felt it was just right.
Whether as a Puppet Master or a gunman, overly large muscles could actually hinder agility.
Moreover, the most exaggerated was Su Lun's current dark spiritual power value!
It had gone from a maximum of 2214 a month ago to 23332 now, a more than tenfold increase.
This was already an extremely exaggerated number.
A normal professional advancing to the second tier needs a minimum of about 7000 dark spiritual power points to successfully integrate black iron materials for advancement; even some higher-requirement silver materials only need about 10000 points. (Tier advancement conditions: Material compatibility + current tier dark spiritual power value must reach a certain level)
But now, Su Lun had reached an astonishing more than double that.
Even when he practiced meditation with the "Haigem Breathing Method," he felt there was still a slight room for increase.
Although Su Lun was still unclear about what was so special about such a large dark spiritual power value, he guessed it was directly related to subsequent high-tier advancements. The more solid the dark spiritual power at a lower tier, the easier it was to advance to higher tiers, and the higher the limit.
Another immediate benefit was that he was hardly lacking in mana anymore.
Merely controlling the first-tier Arachnoid Spear, he could now maintain its external solution state for a very long period.
Using the "Flames of Non-Serverance" from before, which used to spill out an inch, now blazed out a full foot...
And controlling puppets with witch hair, his control range had become even further...
....
A month had passed, the fog around was gradually dissipating.
He estimated that in a few more days, this wave of "fog tide" would probably also be over.
The food and freshwater prepared in the Storage Ring were almost depleted,
and the "X Serum" was fully absorbed,
Su Lun felt it was time to leave the ruins.
After all, this ruins was not a benevolent place.
Su Lun thought, even if the Oliver family's battalions that were pursuing him were tenacious, they probably wouldn't stay in the ruins for a month.
Moreover, even if he appeared in front of those Bounty Hunters, eighty percent wouldn't recognize his now handsome and imposing face as the smoky-headed, "S-rank wanted criminal Su Lun."
...
This day.
The fog had almost returned to normal levels, and no more sounds of large aberrations were heard around the bunker.
Su Lun opened the ventilation shaft and took a careful look. He could see in the distance through the fog, some leisurely feeding bipedal creatures with sheep's heads and horns— "Fallen Satyr."
Grazing?
No, they were gnawing on the bones of their prey.
"Crack"...
"Crack"...
It was spine-chilling to hear.
Su Lun had been observing them for nearly two days now.
This group of upright goat-headed creatures numbered about fifty-six, seemed docile but were actually ferociously vicious. Fast, with a jumping ability, their sharp teeth and biting force could easily crush stones.
Especially the goat-headed leader, which was as big as a bull and possessed strength not inferior to a second-tier melee professional. The group could easily kill large prey when hunting together, and should not be underestimated.
Su Lun, with the Black Scythe in hand and his strengthened abilities, wasn't afraid of these creatures.
But he didn't want to start a fight as soon as he left the bunker.
After all, this was the inner circle of Dawn City, and the aberrations nearby were not limited to just these creatures.
After observing for a moment, the group of monsters showed no intention of leaving.
Su Lun thought he might have to wait another day.
Once they consumed the prey they captured yesterday, they would probably leave.
....
After observing for a moment,
Su Lun closed the vent and then made himself something to eat.
He broke the black bread into pieces, added some of his homemade "instant noodle seasoning packet," and chewed it down.
However, this was just an occasional act to taste something mild and fill the stomach.
The most important source of nutrition still came directly from injecting nutrient solution.
This month, digesting the "X serum" to enhance his physique required lots of energy, surviving solely on these nutrient solutions.
Su Lun quickly had his meal.
Then he took out the Puppet Scripture and started reading.
During this time, he thoroughly went through the puppet scriptures among the spoils, catching up on some puppet controlling techniques.
Only then did he realize that puppet controlling had so many tricks and shortcuts...
Playing with puppets and being a professional Puppet Master were completely different things.
As he read, his gaze shifted to the set of golden armor blueprints, Thousand Threads - Lion's Mane Ballad, in the pile of scriptures.
He had been coveting this item for a month.
Not only did he have the blueprints, but he even had the main material, the Wailing Witch's skull, and even the crafting auxiliaries found among the previous spoils.
But Su Lun, looking at these blueprints he studied meticulously more than ten times, still felt helpless.
He faced the same dilemma he encountered when he obtained the Eight-Armed Spider Spear blueprints: The blueprints and materials were too advanced.
Although he had been continuously learning and improving, and his level of crafting enchanted armors was not low,
without a master's level, he dared not touch the second tier golden blueprints + dark golden materials.
He really didn't feel confident and didn't dare to start carelessly and waste the materials.
So, he thought of "Mr. Hei."
Unfortunately... that mysterious character was probably still in the black market of Old Lington.
Su Lun didn't ponder over the blueprints much, thinking he would deal with it when the time was right, and continued to focus on reading the scriptures.
But as he was reading, his ears suddenly perked up, and he quietly exclaimed, "The mist has cleared, how could the 'big fellow' appear again?"
Then, like an earthquake, the ground began to tremble.
He was already used to such situations; every time a large monster passed by, it caused this kind of disturbance. The bunker felt like a horn lying on the ground, making everything exceptionally clear.
However... this time it sounded a bit different.
"Is a large monster fighting?"
Su Lun immediately noticed the rapid 'thump,' 'thump,' sounds, which did not seem like a monster walking, but fighting instead?
And it was not just the noise of hunting, but the sounds of a fierce battle between equals!
Fights between large monsters were incredibly dangerous. These monsters could unleash wind, spit fire, and pour water... The ancient architecture in the city was so damaged directly because of these large beasts.
Considering this, Su Lun didn't take any chances and opened the vent to look outside.
A huge deformed monster came into view.
But what amazed Su Lun even more was the "opponent" fighting with the monster!
Initially, he thought it was two monsters fighting, but on a closer look...
The one making the monster constantly wail in pain was actually a few humans?!
On closer observation, Su Lun's eyes became fixated, filled with disbelief, "Can someone actually dare to target such an overclassed monster?"

chapters.title: Chapter 150 - 150: Prohibited Object [Volgan's Furnace Lamp]
chapters.content:
```
Su Lun peered cautiously through the ventilation opening and immediately saw the giant humanoid monster towering over thirty meters tall.
It resembled an ancient soldier, with a round-topped, wide-brimmed ancient bronze helmet on its head, and shattered metal armor of the same hue on its shoulders and legs. Its robe was long decayed, revealing dark brown, corpse-like skin...
What caught the eye most was the hexagonal copper lamp it held in its hand, with a black rod attached.
The lamp was of a quaint design, with profound engravings on its body. The dark yellow glazed lampshade was smoked black, faintly revealing a flickering dim yellow flame that shone out, forming a halo nearly ten meters around the lamp...
It was this faint halo that gave off an extremely terrifying feeling, as if anything touched by the light would turn to ashes and smoke.
"A tyrant-level oddity?"
Looking at the monster, Su Lun's pupils suddenly constricted.
The All-knowing Eye identified the information of this monster; it was actually a tyrant-level oddity, a tier above the lord-level!
[The Lamp Bearer of Dawn City's Cemetery]
Explanation: An aberrant monster formed from the aggregation of resentment of ancient soldiers, a tyrant-level zombie species with superior strength, adept at controlling fire, extremely dangerous;
(Note: Anything above the third tier is considered 'superior' in the protagonist's current knowledge.)
This was the strongest oddity Su Lun had ever encountered in the ruins!
The pressure, mountainous in its intensity, caused a shiver that seemed to originate from one's very soul.
So strong that he felt even the lord-level Wailing Witch, in front of this being, would be reduced to ashes and smoke in an instant.
Even with the black sickle in hand, Su Lun felt he had no chance of winning.
The first thing he thought of upon seeing it was definitely to escape.
Because not only did he possess a forbidden item, but the lamp in the hands of this monster was one too!
[Volgan's Furnace Lamp]
Quality: Legendary
Description: Those who play with fire will eventually get burned;
Cursed Attributes: It can forge alchemical items out of the ordinary, possessing flames that can burn everything; using this lamp can activate a wide range of 'Ulken Lava Fire' to incinerate any material not ranked higher in law than the lamp itself; however, the fire attacks indiscriminately, scorching the user as well;
Explanation: An ancient lamp forged by alchemists imitating a divine artifact, it possesses powerful sealing capabilities; the lamp contains a strand of 'Ulken Core Flame,' capable of crafting extremely high-quality alchemical items; it can also be used as advanced materials for fire-based alchemy magicians;
Su Lun looked at this ancient lamp, feeling even more alarmed than when he first saw the black sickle.
At least the damage from the black sickle was controllable, and the curse backlash somewhat predictable...
But this lamp was an indiscriminate attacker.
Looking at it, Su Lun only saw four words—mutual destruction.
However, judging by the function identified for the hexagonal copper lamp, it seemed primarily to be an auxiliary forbidden item for forging, or perhaps for some top-tier alchemists with supreme fire control abilities to use in battle?
...
It was only after the All-knowing Eye identified the combination of the tyrant-level monster and the forbidden item that Su Lun felt this thing was simply beyond human capability to fight against.
Therefore, he was so surprised that someone dared to target it.
Scavengers?
Clearly not.
Even the largest scavenger groups, even those few top-tier groups that had third-tier professionals, Su Lun thought this monster could effortlessly wipe them out.
Yet in the foggy shadows before him, those several figures in black cloaks continued to provoke the monster.
It seemed they had a clear division of labor, with some luring the monster out from the center city walls, others disturbing it, and others taking action...
In just the moment that Su Lun looked over, the monster had already chased those figures to the vicinity of the central ring of walls.
Then, at what seemed to be the predetermined ambush site, one of the figures in black cloaks made their move!
```
```
He suddenly clasped his hands together at a rapid pace, forming a series of complex sorcerer's seals so bewildering that even Su Lun found them dizzying to watch. Beneath his feet, a complicated triple-mark suddenly illuminated; the innermost layer was an ouroboros, the middle was a double pentagram, and the outermost layer was a seven-pointed star...
"A Seven-Pointed Star Alchemy Formation?"
Su Lun watched the brown alchemy formation beneath the man's feet, his eyes narrowing slightly.
Normally, formations for Arts below the third-tier are pentagrams or hexagrams; a seven-pointed star only appeared in some advanced alchemy knowledge.
The moment this guy made a move, he opted for such a tactic?
The man in the black robe caused his garment to billow as if caught in an unfelt wind, and as the Seven-Pointed Star Formation lit up under him, his aura grew more and more powerful.
Just moments ago, he seemed as insignificant as an ant, but now his presence could stand toe to toe with that of the domineering and eerie overlord.
As Su Lun observed the pattern of the alchemy formation, he guessed something: "Super-tier Earth System Arts?"
The energy in the alchemy formation under the robed man shifted rapidly, with the earth elements nearby visibly condensing into specks of ochre spiritual light that surged towards him. In the blink of an eye, the ground underfoot of the "Dawn City's Graveyard Lamp Bearer" also manifested an expanded tenfold Seven-Pointed Star Alchemy Formation. The light grew intensely bright, and the alchemy formation altered the cohesion of the earth elements, turning the hard ground into mud.
Another blink, and it had transformed into a vast, dark swamp.
The monster's body was too large to avoid the trap and its legs sank into the swamp up to the knees instantly.
And it didn't end there!
After casting what was recognized as the super-tier Earth-based Alchemy "Great Swamp Technique," the man in the black robe changed his sorcerer's seals again; the earthen brown light of the Seven-Pointed Star Formation at his feet grew more blinding and seamlessly transformed into a completely different and complex Gold System Art.
Once the Art changed, the swampy morass began to harden incredibly quickly...
...
From a distance, inside the bastion, Su Lun watched this masterful display in awe: "A compound Art from Earth to Gold System? A third-tier magician may not even be able to smoothly transition between two different third-tier spells, yet this guy effortlessly shifts between two 'super-tier spells'? Just how powerful is he?"
At this point, he didn't even know how to articulate his feelings.
Although Su Lun had never witnessed a third-tier professional in action firsthand, he had gleaned some information from various texts and memories he had collected, giving him a rough concept.
"Multi-elemental transformation" is one of the highest level casting techniques within the realm of spell-oriented alchemists.
The smoother the transformation, the more it requires an exceptional understanding and control over elemental spells.
A normal third-tier professional talented enough to smoothly master the transition between two different third-tier elemental Arts is already considered a top-tier expert.
Yet, this cloaked figure had just consecutively cast two "super-tier spells" with what seemed like ease?
As the Art changed, the dense earth elements in the swamp pit abruptly turned into gold elements, and the brown muck in the blink of an eye solidified into a lustrous, gold-like metal solid.
With that, the huge soldier-like monster could no longer move its feet and was immediately immobilized.
The ability to transmute materials in alchemy was displayed to perfection by this robed individual.
....
"This mastery of spells is simply astounding; to think that Old Lington City had such an expert hidden within..."
Su Lun felt he might have underestimated the top-tier professionals of Old Lington.
He had previously thought that the Cross Society's boss Chak, a third-tier professional, was already one of the strongest in Old Lington.
Now it looked like at least this cloaked person was even stronger than Chak.
Initially, when Su Lun assessed the information about the overlord-level aberrant creature, he thought these people were "overestimating their abilities" and had misjudged the creature's tier.
But now, watching the robed man cast two super-tier control spells in succession, he realized that these people were not mistaken but rather came prepared, seemingly confident in taking down the creature and securing the item it was sealing.
However, even with its feet fixed by the metallic substance and unable to move, the colossal soldier-like overlord was not bereft of fighting power.
While the hand holding the lamp remained still, its other hand clenching the rusted greatsword suddenly swung a mighty blow towards the black-robed caster.
In the face of absolute strength, all tactics seem feeble and ineffective.
With the sword coming down, Su Lun figured it could easily bisect a ten-story building.
Moreover, it was not just a mere physical attack; a layer of fierce wind elements, visible to the naked eye, enshrouded the blade of the greatsword.
The swing of the over twenty-meter long sword appeared slow, but in reality, it was fast as a tornado, making evasion impossible.
```
Large swathes of wind elemental Sword Qi covered the area, pressing so heavily on the robed figure casting the spell that his robes whistled with the strain, and his form was rooted to the spot.
Even before the sword fell upon his head, the ground around had been crushed into layers of cracks by the terrifying Sword Qi, an extreme horror to behold.
Even the fortress hundreds of meters away where Su Lun lay hidden seemed like it was about to collapse from an earthquake, as dense cracks began to form above and sand and stones fell like rain.
Su Lun's eyelids twitched as he looked on. The fortress, which had withstood numerous bizarre lights without faltering, was about to be crushed by a mere wisp of Sword Qi?
Just how terrifying was this sword strike?
Before he could decide whether to run out now, Su Lun suddenly saw another robed figure, holding a dagger and fearlessly meeting the giant sword swinging down toward him.
Almost at the same moment, the spell-casting robed figure changed the seals with his hands again, and the golden Seven-Pointed Star Formation at his feet turned into a blue one of wind elements!
Su Lun's gaze was intense, "Still going? A three-element switch?"
The moment the wind elemental alchemy array activated, it seemed not to be forcefully blocking the attack, but more like channeling irrigation, directly guiding the destroy-the-heavens-and-shatter-the-earth Sword Qi on the giant sword into a tornado's spiraling form.
Once the Sword Qi tornado took shape, the ground cracked as if plowed by an iron blade.
However, the two people at the core of the alchemy formation seemed to be completely unaffected!
"Clang!"
A sharp metallic clang resounded throughout the ruins.
The robed figure wielding the short dagger had an astonishing power, his slender body, dozens of times smaller, firmly caught the giant's sword strike.
The instant the dagger and sword touched, a shockwave exploded from the center of contact, forming a visible air wave that sent sand and stones flying.
Even hundreds of meters away inside the fortress, Su Lun was unsteady from the blast that whistled through the vents, and he exclaimed in shock, "Is this the might of a top-tier fighter..."
It was this strike that made him feel that if a third-tier fighter were here, they would not die but would be severely injured by the slash, yet it was casually resolved by the cooperation of the two cloaked figures.
....
"They used a super-tier wind elemental control again. That magician must be skilled in at least three elements of spells..."
Watching, Su Lun's pupils quivered, finding himself at a loss for words to describe this robed magician.
They operated like a textbook example, with sorcerer's seals to their spellcasting, condensing elements with unassailable skill.
Su Lun found it hard to imagine just what identity this robed person possessed, to be skilled in at least three elemental spells.
He even suspected that this person might, like him, have awakened some talent that allowed them to harvest abilities from others.
Otherwise, how could it be so exaggerated?
Under normal circumstances, alchemy magicians specialize in only one elemental spell.
After all, human energy is limited. Only through specialization can one grow stronger and reach higher realms.
Therefore, the well-known second-tier masters in Old Lington City are usually magicians specializing in a single system, such as the mainstream earth, wind, water, fire...
Very few specialize in two systems.
Because to delve into an additional system, a magician must invest many times more time and effort.
But if it's "multi-elemental" beyond two...
Under normal circumstances, if not absolutely brilliant, such greedy and overreaching individuals are called "useless multi-elemental magicians."
And to cast super-tier spells, it definitely means that the magician must "master" that elemental spell.
....
However, Su Lun thought it was already inconceivable for the cloaked figure to master three super-tier elemental spells.
But it turned out that it wasn't over yet.
Right then, the Seven-Pointed Star Formation under the feet of the cloaked magician lit up again.
The light shifted from the blue of the wind system to the green of the wood system.
Although the transition took a few seconds and seemed a bit strenuous this time...
However, four consecutive elemental conversions were already at a level that is "unimaginable."
Watching one high-tier spell after another, Su Lun was surprisingly calm, only muttering to himself, "Four elements have been converted, how many elemental spells does this guy actually master..."
Then, he saw the cloaked figure throw a green bean into the alchemy formation.
The green light of the Alchemy flashed, and suddenly a green vine burst forth from the earth, growing rapidly in the wind. The frenzied power of the wood element wildly bolstered the vine. From a small sprout, it rapidly swelled in size, from the thickness of an arm to that of a water barrel, and then to something several people could barely embrace...
Then the main vine began to fork, branches spreading, growing thicker, continuing to fork, growing thicker still...
In the blink of an eye, the vine expanded hundreds of times in size and became a lush, towering, sky-reaching giant vine.
As the vine grew, it wrapped around the giant like a python coiling around a giant's limbs, and by the time the vine had reached full growth, it had already wound tightly around the tall soldier.
The creature tried to struggle, but the vine only grew thicker and its bindings tighter.
In that moment, Su Lun identified four high-tier alchemy spells: the "Earth System: Great Swamp Technique," the "Gold System: Transmute to Gold," the "Wind System: Tornado Technique," and the "Wood System Mysteries: Sky-reaching Vine..."
However, the aim of subduing the monster was naturally to kill it.
The creature probably intended to release the "Volgan Lava Fire" from the hexagonal ancient lamp it held, but before the flame could burst from the furnace, a pale blue dodecahedron with a purple seal suddenly appeared on the lantern.
Then, the flash of a sword, and the arm holding the lamp suddenly had a smooth incision.
The bizarre forearm was severed, dropping to the ground.
Without the ancient lamp, the monster was no longer a threat.
What followed was a straightforward execution...
.....
Su Lun counted, there were a total of five people in black.
Only three of them took action.
After seeing how brutal the methods of the cloaked magician were, he knew this battle had lost its suspense.
They had come prepared, familiar with everything about the monster, its means of attack, and familiar items for sealing it...
The tactical plan was flawless.
Before it could use its powerful move, the giant soldier's body had already perished amidst the vine's entanglement.
However, it was certainly comfortable to watch the excitement.
Su Lun also realized that those people had noticed him.
High-level practitioners like these could not have been observed for so long without them being aware.
Still, Su Lun was not panicked.
Because he had guessed the identity of these cloaked individuals.
He could think of only two forces in Old Lington capable of assembling such an extraordinary hunting array.
Either the Black Tower,
Or that mysterious "third party force."
Clearly, these people were not from the Black Tower.
One reason was that people from the Black Tower didn't need to hide...
The second reason was that Su Lun recognized two of them among the five.
When he saw that black-robed magician casting high-tier spells at will, a strong sense of familiarity came over him, this "all-knowing, all-powerful" sensation immediately reminded him of someone he knew—Mr. Hei.
And the one who could physically withstand the greatsword, he just didn't seem to have an ordinary body, especially with the mechanical jet propulsion sounds of "hiss" "hiss" during movement. If he wasn't mistaken, she was the super-mechanical warrior—Number Nineteen.
Su Lun looked at them appearing before him, his expression quite complicated.
PS. Please subscribe, please and thank you.

chapters.title: Chapter 151 - 151 Entrust
chapters.content:
"At least a four-element magician, Mr. Hei is indeed terrifyingly strong..."
Su Lun looked at the man in the black robe, who, after finishing casting his spell, retracted his aura and became indistinguishable from an ordinary person, and sighed softly with a complex expression.
Although he had suspected that the former vice-principal of the Black Tower Academy would be formidable when they first met,
seeing Mr. Hei in front of him effortlessly perform a high-level spell, he still found it unbelievable.
However, coming back to the point, shock was secondary.
Su Lun knew he had been discovered, and he felt it was now time to carefully think about how to handle the situation so as not to be mistaken by these big shots, who came to the ruins for procurement, as a petty thief coveting from the sidelines, and inadvertently get killed.
And as this thought crossed his mind, the few black-robed ones who had finished dealing with the grave garden lamp bearer also turned their attention elsewhere. Of the five, the two who had not taken action seemed to have noticed something. One of them turned his head and looked towards the bunker.
Their gaze met precisely at the ventilation point.
Su Lun couldn't see the face hidden beneath the man's cloak, but in that moment of eye contact, he felt as if he saw a hidden smile in the cloak man's eyes.
It was the kind of amused smile a cat gives when it spots a mouse.
Fortunately, it was not "murderous intent."
And in that split second when their eyes met, the arm beneath the cloak man's cloak suddenly lifted, making a gesture as if to throw a card.
Before Su Lun could even react, the golden card left the man's hand, spinning through the air, shooting into the vent as precisely as a bullet.
"Clang~"
A sharp sound.
The card lodged into the wall and then exploded into white smoke.
Before the smoke had even cleared, an incredible scene unfolded.
The cloak man who had thrown the card hundreds of meters away, suddenly materialized inside the bunker.
Su Lun, taken aback by this instant teleportation, did not make any misleading moves but spoke decisively without waiting for the other to act, "I am a friend of Mr. Hei."
....
As it turned out, birds of a feather flock together.
Mr. Hei himself was a true gentleman, and so were the people from his organization; none of them were bloodthirsty.
After Su Lun mentioned Mr. Hei's name, the card-ability cloak man uttered a soft sound of surprise and gave him a glance. But without another word, his figure disappeared into a burst of white smoke, returning to hundreds of meters away.
His arrival was sudden, and so was his departure.
Then that guy must have said something, and the five cloak people all turned their gazes towards the bunker.
But it was just a glance before they lost interest.
They were busy dealing with the soldiers' strange corpses and the very dangerous hexagonal copper lamp. It seemed they had no time to pay attention to this "lost Scavenger," who for some reason was present in this place.
Su Lun thought it pointless to keep hiding, so he decided to open the mechanical door he had made himself and finally stepped out of the bunker for the first time in a month.
At that moment, the black-robed spell caster who had put aside his work walked towards him.
As he approached, he lifted the cloak covering his head, revealing the amiable face of a middle-aged man, naturally, the mysterious Mr. Hei.
Seeing the hairier Su Lun, Mr. Hei first looked slightly puzzled, probably not matching him with anyone familiar.
But he seemed to have noticed something thereafter, took another glance at the spot behind Su Lun, and showed a trace of realization.
That was precisely where the invisible undead had been standing.
The subtle noise had not escaped his perception.
Something invisible?
The[Oz Ice Man's Shroud]is no secret as to whose hands it is in now.
He instantly recognized who this person claiming to be his "friend" was.
Mr. Hei smiled and greeted proactively, "Young Su Lun, long time no see."
Su Lun also stepped forward to meet him, nodding in response, "Mr. Hei, it's been a long time."
```
...
Mr. Hei always gave people a sense of approachability.
Without waiting for Su Lun to speak, he said in a joking tone, "I've been hearing about you quite frequently lately, you've really stirred things up in Old Lington and Dawn Camp, haven't you?"
After a pause, he continued, "Now not only the officials but also the black market, the Oliver family, the Crow Gang, and the Steam Party have all put a hefty bounty on your head, just waiting to claim it..."
Su Lun chuckled dryly.
He wasn't surprised by the news at all.
He had seized that fortune from Young Master Danze and had killed a few second-tier professionals, so being wanted was within reason.
Mr. Hei spoke, and after giving the long-haired Su Lun another glance, he teased, "But looking at you now, it seems that friend Su Lun doesn't need to worry about the warrants anymore."
Su Lun shrugged his shoulders and modestly said, "You flatter me."
After the pleasantries, Mr. Hei got to the point and asked, "By the way, how come you're here? This is after all the central ring of Dawn City, and moreover, the 'Mist Tide' has just ended. There's a lot of extremely strong anomalies and weird creatures around..."
The implication was clear, large Scavenger groups led by top-tier professionals were only cautiously active in the central area now, so how could he, a first-tier professional, be here?
And, at this particular time too.
"It's quite a coincidence, I was being hunted down..."
Su Lun briefly mentioned the process of being hunted down by the Oliver family.
Then, with a somewhat helpless gesture toward the bunker behind him, he added, "Then, I hid in that bunker for a month."
"You've been here for a month?"
Upon hearing that, Mr. Hei, whose eyes had always been untroubled, now showed a hint of surprise and curiosity.
It wasn't something that could be survived by merely hiding.
The 'Mist Tide' was full of dangers, not just the various monsters from the abyss, but the violent dark spiritual power alone was not something ordinary people could withstand.
The flicker of doubt vanished as Mr. Hei seemed to think of something. He didn't speak it, but a meaningful smile appeared on his lips.
"Yeah... roughly something like that."
Su Lun felt that the "X Serum" wasn't exactly a secret he couldn't talk about, Mr. Hei probably knew about it too, and there was no harm in mentioning it.
But the other party didn't ask, so he didn't bring it up either.
....
While the two were conversing, the other four cloaked figures had already cleaned up the remains of the dominant anomaly and tidied up the battlefield.
They didn't even say a word to each other, commmunicating with a glance, and then dispersed on their own.
It was like those ad hoc groups that disbanded on the spot after completing their tasks.
Three cloaked figures left, and one stayed behind. That was number nineteen.
Number nineteen was a mechanical warrior, equipped with many advanced mechanical augmentations, such as iris recognition, voice recognition, skeletal contour recognition, and other special physical recognition methods. She had previously collected data on Su Lun and now, with just one glance, she recognized him.
She walked over, nodded in greeting – that was her way of saying hello.
Su Lun didn't mind, for a cold mechanical warrior to say hello was already quite a good treatment.
Since the battlefield was dealt with, it was naturally not appropriate to stay for long.
Mr. Hei called out to Su Lun, "The noise from hunting that anomaly just now wasn't small, it might bring some troublesome creatures. Let's go, we'll talk while walking."
"Hmm."
Mr. Hei didn't probe into Su Lun's secrets, and in a mutual understanding, Su Lun didn't inquire why they were here or why they had hunted that dominant anomaly.
Nor did he try to learn the secrets of this mysterious "third-party organization."
Of course, without asking, both parties had already guessed part of it.
....
The three walked towards the east, in the direction of the ruins' exit.
```
With Mr. Hei and Number Nineteen, two super bodyguards protecting him, Su Lun no longer needed to be as excessively cautious as when he was alone.
He had just been thinking that with second-tier blueprints and materials in hand, he would need a Forging Master. Unexpectedly, he had stumbled upon Mr. Hei.
Just as he was about to voice his request for help, Mr. Hei seemed to sense something and spoke first, "Remember when I first met young friend Su Lun, you were an aspiring professional running around for a first-tier prosthesis. To think, after a few months, you're about to advance to the second tier."
Surprised by these words, Su Lun asked, "Mr. Hei, you can tell that I'm about to advance?"
"Yes."
Mr. Hei naturally read between the lines of Su Lun's question.
It wasn't about whether he had figured it out, but how.
He clarified directly, "The amount of dark spiritual power you exude with your breath is extraordinary. That level is beyond the reach of any first-tier professional. In fact, it's more than what many second-tiers possess."
"I see..."
Su Lun found it somewhat unbelievable, thinking it must be some special perceptive ability.
Considering it was Mr. Hei, who could casually perform advanced spells, Su Lun found nothing strange about it and went on with his request, "Then... Mr. Hei, I have an audacious favor to ask of you."
"Is it about preparing to forge a second-tier prosthesis?"
Mr. Hei smiled.
"Yes."
Su Lun, now used to Mr. Hei's prescience, nodded.
He took out the blueprint while saying, "I've found the perfect prosthesis blueprint and materials for myself, but ordinary forging masters can't handle this prosthesis, so I must trouble you..."
Mr. Hei cast only a brief glance at the blueprint Su Lun had handed over and said with a peculiar expression, "Isn't this the renowned Trickster Lloyd's signature prosthesis? Did you kill him?"
Blueprints held tightly by wealthy families would not be sold; the only explanation was robbery by murder.
"No."
Su Lun shook his head, adding, "I destroyed his alchemical puppet and cut off his legs. So I was lucky to get the blueprint."
Mr. Hei, not privy to this information, showed an intrigued expression when he heard Su Lun's account.
He then asked Su Lun, "Did you find the right main material? Lloyd made his name with this prosthesis, largely because he found the 'Tismoxing ironworms.' Only special silk can maximize the potential of this prosthesis..."
"I have."
Su Lun nodded and then took out a head with silvery hair flowing from it.
Mr. Hei suspected that Su Lun had the materials prepared, but even he, a widely knowledgeable Scholar, was briefly taken aback when Su Lun suddenly produced a human head.
He recognized it after a moment and asked with a tone of disbelief, "The Wailing Witch's head? And... a second-tier 'Infinite Hair' at that?"
"Yes."
Su Lun nodded and inwardly marveled at Mr. Hei's extensive knowledge, as he had identified the origin of the material at first glance.
An ordinary appraiser might not recognize this item.
Mr. Hei asked, "This is an extremely rare material, how did you obtain it?"
Su Lun, seeing Mr. Hei's curiosity about the head's origins, elaborated further, "Previously, I joined a team to hunt relics in the wilderness, and it just so happened that the Oliver family's scavenging team ran into us. Then I got dragged into a cursed space... So, that's roughly what happened."
About a month ago, at the bell tower street, a fierce battle took place where seven second-tiers chased down a first-tier professional, and two were killed and another two were crippled. Probably the Oliver family was too embarrassed to publicize this defeat.
No need for detailed explanations, someone like Mr. Hei could naturally infer the ins and outs of the situation.
Hearing this almost "bizarre" tale, Mr. Hei couldn't help but show a very strange expression, "Heh... I wondered why the Oliver family was so frantic to issue a warrant for you, so that's the reason."
Even Number Nineteen, who had remained silent the entire time, looked at Su Lun with a strange gaze upon hearing about the battle: You, a first-tier professional, managed to overwhelm a large hunting group?
Mr. Hei didn't press further and took the materials, returning to the previous topic, "Now that I've gotten the 'Furnace Lamp of Volgan,' the forging of the prosthesis will be quick. In at most three to five days, you can have the finished product."
After a pause, he added, "By the way, did you find the right materials for advancement?"
"No."
Su Lun shook his head and then inquired, "I'm looking for advancement materials related to 'spatial ability,' but it seems they're not easy to find."
"Hmm, spatial ability is indeed a good fit for the Puppet Master profession,"
Mr. Hei nodded after hearing this but wore a regretful expression, "I don't have any clues about such materials either. However, Dawn City will soon welcome a great Scavenger surge, and many ancient relics will appear. Spatial materials are scarce, but that doesn't necessarily mean there will be none. The Scavengers' Guild is a good place for information dissemination, so you might try your luck there. I'll also keep an eye out for you..."
"Hmm."
Su Lun nodded, having the same thought himself.
The information commission had been posted in the Scavengers' Guild for a month, and it was unclear if anyone had heard anything.
"As for the matter of the prosthesis, I'll have to trouble you then."
As he spoke, he did not forget the rule of commissioning, and added, "Then, may I ask what kind of remuneration I need to offer?"
Last time it was a favor, this time he had none left.
The master craftsman's fee would not be cheap.
Mr. Hei smiled, seemingly not having originally planned to charge.
But suddenly, he seemed to remember something and changed his statement, "However, come to think of it, there is actually something you could help with."
Help?
Su Lun was initially puzzled upon hearing this.
Was there something that such a high-level expert needed help with?
But he also said, "Please tell me."
Mr. Hei: "You're going to the Scavenger camp now, right?"
Su Lun: "Hmm."
Mr. Hei did not rush to speak, instead turning to exchange a glance with number nineteen beside him, seemingly asking her opinion, and she gave her tacit agreement.
Only then did he say, "If possible, I would like you to help Miss Nineteen gain entry into the camp."
Su Lun: "???"
Mr. Hei explained, "You know, she was once a super mechanical warrior, with outstanding combat mechanisms, but she lacks some living skills. I think she would find herself in far fewer troubles if she were with you. Of course, it's just about getting into the camp."
Number nineteen, standing beside him, listened to Mr. Hei's assessment of her and seemed completely unbothered by it.
She, a war machine created specifically for killing, indeed lacked many of the emotions and social graces of a normal human.
...
Enter the camp?
Just that?
Su Lun felt that this "commission" was really something Mr. Hei had come up with on the spur of the moment.
Upon hearing about entering the camp, his first reaction was: This woman is going to stir up some major trouble again!
No, it should be said that this time it's their "third-party organization" looking to cause some sort of trouble.
However, Su Lun had no curiosity or intention of inquiring further.
If Mr. Hei had something to say, he would naturally say it; if he didn't, it meant that it was definitely the kind of affair where "knowing only brings trouble."
After thinking it over, it didn't seem too difficult to manage, so he readily agreed, "Alright!"
If it was just about smuggling someone into the camp, this commission was practically a grade D difficulty.
Before, Su Lun had been worried that his identity as "Johnny" was blown, and that the conspicuous abomination of a body, whether invisible or not, could no longer be brought into the camp.
But without the abomination and the scythe, he wasn't entirely sure he could come out unscathed if anything went wrong.
Now with Nineteen, a super combatant, accompanying him, it was perfect.
The two fugitives could also provide mutual support for each other.
Moreover... there was this mysterious "third-party organization."
Besides the two of them present, the three who left earlier were definitely top professionals—this power was absolutely capable of forcibly taking down the camp.

chapters.title: Chapter 152 - 152: Another Big Move
chapters.content:
Mr. Hei probably also felt that his "commission" was a bit abrupt and lacking an introduction.
Although Su Lun didn't ask, he still elaborated, "You should now know that I and some like-minded friends have formed a loose organization. You might have guessed the purpose of its existence. However, precisely for this reason, the identities of some of our members are very sensitive and it's not convenient to expose them too soon. Otherwise, it would raise the alertness of the higher-ups in the black tower... Thus, this mission, unless absolutely necessary, will be completed independently by Miss No. 19."
"Hmm."
Su Lun listened and nodded, understanding his meaning.
Mr. Hei and his backing power definitely had ways to arrange for No. 19 to enter the city.
But they were planning to "make a big move" this time.
So once exposed, they would definitely be traced back to the source.
The people from the Umbrella Organization were no mediocrities either; that so-called omnipresent intelligence organization would definitely, through various traces, investigate the channels through which No. 19 entered the camp.
Even with thoughtful arrangements, there would inevitably be clues left behind, leading to a chain of events.
The more people involved, the more exposure there would be.
On the contrary, going in with Su Lun was not a big issue.
After all, although Su Lun was currently an S-class fugitive, other than the intelligence on the two disturbances, there was almost nothing else!
Even within the Cross Society, no further information could be found.
....
With two top experts providing an escort, Su Lun had no need to worry about safety.
The trio moved quickly, and soon they had arrived at the edge of the Ruins City district.
Here, the presence of Scavengers was frequently noted; Mr. Hei, not wishing to show his face in public, bid his farewell and left.
Now only Su Lun and No. 19 were left.
The two avoided the crowd and didn't rush to the camp but instead chose a high ground in the distance to observe from above.
Having not returned for just a month, Su Lun saw that the Dawn Camp had completely changed.
The city wall had been built nearly thirty meters high, and the area of the camp had expanded twofold.
A month ago, the tallest building in the camp was only two stories high; now there were already five- or six-story steel-structured buildings. The buildings were crowded and messy, yet they already had the appearance of a wartime town.
Dense steam pipes crisscrossed like forests, whooshing and emitting white smoke. Various mechanical artillery emplacements had turned this wall into a porcupine. There were even patrols in "Frost Giant Armor" on the surrounding wall!
And not only the buildings had proliferated; the number of Scavengers and caravans coming and going had also increased several times over the previous month.
Looking over, the queue of Scavengers lining up to enter the city gate had already formed nearly a kilometer-long line.
No. 19 observed the heavily defended camp with a somewhat solemn gaze, apparently reminding Su Lun, "The city wall is equipped with the 'Fenix Dynamic Touch Warning System' commonly used in the inner city laboratory. If someone climbs it, an alarm will be triggered immediately."
After thinking for a moment, she added, "Those highly sensitive components are extensively installed and not easily detectable. Even if someone tried to leap over, it would likely trigger the system."
Su Lun listened to her seriously analyzing the possibility of scaling the wall, and said with a strange tone, "You're not seriously thinking about climbing over the wall, are you?"
"Otherwise, how are we going to get in?"
No. 19 thought Su Lun was really asking her and responded with a puzzled tone.
While speaking, she also pointed to the queue entering the city gate, saying, "Wanted posters of both of us are posted right at the city gate. Of course, they might not discover you in your current state. But if I were to go, even in disguise, there's a high chance I would be discovered."
"..."
Su Lun, hearing her serious tone and attitude, didn't know what to say.
Indeed, Mr. Hei was right; this super mechanical warrior miss lacked a bit of "worldly sophistication."
Without saying much more, he asked a question.
"Do you have a wig and disguising clothes on you?"
"Yes."
"Good."
Su Lun felt that it would probably be too difficult to explain his plan to Number Nineteen, so he said directly, "Let's go change our clothes and get into the city!"
...
Despite her confusion, Number Nineteen followed Su Lun to a secluded area to change their attire.
Su Lun took off his Scavenger outfit of a trench coat and leather pants, and put on an extravagantly luxurious white suit with a bowler hat on top of his head. Paired with his dashing noble features, he was the spitting image of a wealthy young master, excellent in appearance.
