However, he immediately noticed a pair of feet with livor mortis on the white bed.
"A corpse?"
Su Lun was not surprised.
If the rumors were true that after midnight this room would be haunted, then it was plausible for a tenant here to have died.
But looking at the livor mortis, it seemed the body had been dead for a while.
Because a folding screen was in the way, Su Lun couldn't see the whole picture. He took a couple of steps, intending to move closer.
At this moment, the man opposite Su Lun seemed to think that his mind was not on the gun, and charged forward with a sideways glance, attempting to snatch the weapon and retaliate.
Then...
He was easily dodged by Su Lun, who struck him on the head with the butt of the gun.
There was no further ado as the trigger was pulled without hesitation.
"Biu~"
"Biu~"
The special sound of a silenced gun rang out.
Two precise shots shattered the kneecaps, and the man in front of him collapsed to his knees.
"Ah..."
A scream of agony.
As his cry of pain had barely emerged, Su Lun's gun was already pointed at his head, he said coldly, "If you don't want your brain blown out, shut your mouth."
The man endured the severe pain, sweat pouring down his forehead, and spat out resentfully, "We're both Scavengers, what... what do you mean!"
Su Lun spoke indifferently, "Tell me, what are you doing in this room, and all the information you know."
The man initially wanted to argue and hide his intentions, but hearing that indifferent voice, he had no doubt that if he said something that did not satisfy his captor, he would be killed instantly.
Withstanding the intense pain, he grimly threatened, "If you kill me, you're as good as dead too!"
Su Lun ignored his threat, for at that moment, he had already seen the body on the bed.
It was a male corpse with a blood-stained burlap sack covering its face.
Upon a glance from the All-knowing Eye, information immediately appeared.
[Faceless Man]
Details: A special malicious corpse containing strong fire attribute energy; one of the materials needed for an evil ritual; if damaged or the body is moved out of the room, the Caster would immediately discover it;
Upon further examination, the sack on the corpse's face was actually an alchemical item.
[Cursed Burlap Sack]
Details: A sack on the face—who would recognize you? This burlap sack, tainted with a special corpse qi, worn over the head, protects against specific vengeful spirits' attacks; it is a weapon, as well as a countermeasure against vengeful spirits;
Evil ritual?
These words especially caught his eye.
Seeing this, Su Lun's brow furrowed slightly as he suddenly realized that things were not as simple as they seemed.
His thoughts raced, and he immediately guessed the purpose of those taboo rooms on the first floor.
Seeing Su Lun appeared to be lost in thought, the man with the broken legs thought his threat had worked. He sneered and said, "Now that the door to Room 1021 is open, you're definitely dead! If you know what's good for you, just..."
But before he could finish, Su Lun cut him off, his face expressionless, "Are you trying to say that at midnight, this corpse will become a 'ghost species' and kill whoever enters next? And you plan to put on the sack from the corpse's head, so it won't attack you?"
As these words were spoken, any semblance of confidence vanished from the man's face, his complexion turning from white to black, his eyes wide with disbelief as he pointed at Su Lun, as if he were staring at a monster far more terrifying than any deformed creature.
"You... you... you..."
He roared inside his head, wondering why others would know this secret!
The man dragged his crippled legs, retreating nonstop until he finally leaned against the wall, with nowhere left to retreat.
Su Lun tilted his head, looked at him, and then pulled the trigger.
"Biu~"
"Biu~"
Two more shots broke the man's arms.
Su Lun had lost the patience to waste time on such people: "Now that the door is open, is there a way to prevent the corpse from turning into a ghost seed?"
With his limbs broken, the man was terrified by Su Lun's cruel methods.
Having his biggest reliance exposed, he knew he had no ground for negotiation, tremblingly said, "No... I don't know."
For the last time, Su Lun asked, "Tell me something you believe could save your life."
"I... I am a Scavenger exclusive to the Clark family..."
The man had not finished speaking when a bullet blew his head off.
Starting to assert his identity meant he had nothing worthwhile to reveal.
Su Lun had no interest in wasting more time on such people.
He walked over, removed the sack from the head of the corpse on the bed, and took it.
Now he had just over four hours until midnight; there wasn't much time left.
The corpse couldn't be moved or damaged; Su Lun didn't bother with it anymore and walked out.
....
To confirm his suspicions, Su Lun directly went to the "Room 1055" mentioned in the intelligence as strictly off-limits.
This room, too, had a "Do Not Disturb" sign hanging outside.
Su Lun's lock-picking skills were much more sophisticated than the previous guy's; it took him less than twenty seconds to open the door.
He then walked in and saw the hanging corpse with its feet off the ground, hanging from the ceiling, and had a moment of realization.
[The Hanged Corpse]
Explanation: Material needed for a certain evil ritual, a wind attribute vengeful corpse; damaging it or moving it out of the room would immediately alert the Caster;
The rope that the corpse was hanging from was also an alchemical object with a curse attribute.
The effects were more or less the same, used to avoid the damage from specific evil spirits and for restraint.
Then Su Lun went to "Room 1071" and found a [Drowned Woman Corpse] in the bathtub, and picked up a strand of [Damp Hair].
He had gathered water, wind, and fire attribute corpses.
The Scavenger team before him had figured out that there was something wrong with these three rooms, saving Su Lun a lot of trouble.
Finally, rooms 1090—1099 were unexplored, ten rooms in total.
Thinking it wouldn't take much time, Su Lun decided to check them out before midnight.
Of the doors marked with "Do Not Disturb," three had noises coming from the inside, indicating there were living people; naturally, there was no need to enter.
For those with no noises, he opened the lock to take a look.
Then in "Room 1099," he found an earth attribute [Large-headed Vengeful Infant] corpse on the bed and picked up an alchemical item, [The Vengeful Infant's Swaddling Cloth].
Looking at the four corpses with almost identical descriptions of special body materials.
Su Lun had a rough understanding of the "hidden plot" on the first floor.
Someone had set up an evil ritual and left four corpses in four rooms... perhaps even more?
But with many rooms in the hotel, just on the first floor there were ninety-nine, searching room by room would definitely not be enough time.
He felt he should go check the front desk to see who had checked into these rooms; maybe he'd find more clues.
As for the "Magician" he was looking for, there was no hurry.
The intelligence said that the Magician would only appear in an hour and perform at the hotel banquet hall; it would not be too late to go then.
....
The previous Scavengers lost their lives testing and confirmed that the first three rooms were "forbidden rooms."
Now that Su Lun had opened four rooms, it meant that likely four ghost species would appear eventually.
But he didn't feel much of a sense of crisis.
Since one "forbidden room" had already been opened, it was doomed that this group of Scavengers would be wiped out.
Su Lun thought that there might be a chance if they could figure it out.
Besides...
"Ghost species" were indeed formidable, but not truly unsolvable.
It's just that their methods were usually mental attacks, and they generally were immune to physical damage, so for the overwhelming majority of Scavengers who used knives and guns for physical attacks, they were unsolvable.
But in reality... it wasn't so extreme.
The so-called "ghost species" couldn't escape the category of energy either.
With magic, or certain magical methods, they could be injured as well.
For example, the cold flame of "Ninja."
As for the mental attacks of the ghost species, they also varied in severity.
Ordinary first-order ghost species couldn't control a healthy human as long as they weren't scared to the point of dropping their san value very low.
Want to scare Su Lun?
That didn't seem very realistic.
Want to control him forcibly?
That would probably require a very high-ranking ghost species.
From the current information explored in this space, it seemed that the first floor of the hotel wouldn't encounter such beings.
Things weren't too bad.
Moreover, that top-tier Card expert had also entered, so there was someone to back them up in case something happened.
.....
Without a room card key, Su Lun didn't have the privilege to go to the second floor guarded by guards at the stairwell entrance.
Thinking it over, he approached the hotel's registration front desk.
Similar to the previous "Bell Tower Space," the hotel had many space restorations of ancient people.
Guests, waiters, doormen, guards... there were easily a thousand "living people."
These NPCs didn't possess high intelligence, resembling pre-programmed robots who would perform certain fixed actions and react to certain fixed conversations.
They also wouldn't perceive these suddenly emerging Scavengers as outsiders.
As long as you didn't disrupt their normality, they would choose to "ignore."
This time, more than sixty Scavengers had entered.
It was evident that some had thought of getting some useful information from these hotel workers, like... which room housed a wealthy businessman or jeweler.
Directly stealing from them would yield a substantial gain.
But obviously, not just anyone could check the registration records.
When Su Lun arrived, a few Scavengers had just been rebuffed at the front desk and left cursing and swearing.
"Don't waste your time, those stupid receptionist girls won't reveal a single word."
"Yeah, ask a few more times, and they freaking call the guards. If you get caught, that's when it really gets bad..."
"But, on the other hand, those chicks at the front desk are pretty good-looking. If it weren't for not being able to force them, I really would like to try the taste of these ancient people..."
"..."
After waiting for the few to leave, Su Lun then approached.
Without beating around the bush, he got straight to the point, "Beautiful miss, could you do me a favor?"
As expected, even the NPCs reacted when praised for their beauty.
The blonde girl changed her indifference shown to the previous Scavengers and smiled brightly, "Sir, please tell me."
Knowing conventional methods were useless, Su Lun took out a badge and whispered mysteriously, "I am Officer Johnny, this is my badge. I am here on a secret mission to investigate an important fugitive, and so... I'd like to see the accommodation records."

chapters.title: Chapter 158 - 158 Using Magic Tricks to Cast Magic
chapters.content:
The police badge naturally was the one they had acquired last time in the clock tower space.
Because it was stored inside the storage ring, he brought it out directly.
Su Lun initially wanted to give it a try and hadn't expected the badge to be quite so effective.
The blonde young lady covered her mouth with one hand and her tone suddenly became respectful, exclaiming softly, "Oh, Officer Johnny, please wait a moment."
Then, Su Lun naturally got to see the registration records.
After flipping through them, he also saw the check-in records for rooms 1021, 1055, 1071, 1099.
The registered name was the same person, Teague Carlson.
It looked like a fake name.
However, the marginally good news was that only four rooms were registered under this name on the first floor.
And the two female attendants clearly described the appearance of the man who checked in.
There were only about half as many rooms on the second floor as on the first, and Su Lun glanced over them briefly.
Then, Su Lun looked at the name registered by the magician for room 2113, Robert Bell.
After that, he looked at the third floor, which had only ten luxurious suites.
Because he speculated that the third floor might be the "source of the curse" for this cursed space, he paid close attention, especially to the check-in dates.
Only one room had been checked into on the same day as the four other rooms.
Su Lun looked at the name of the tenant registered for that room and asked, "Do you remember this Miss Gloria Garry in room 3001?"
This question triggered a special dialogue.
The blonde lady seemed to remember something and replied, "Oh, that was an old nun. It happened to be my shift that day, and I have a vivid memory of it. Because the guests on the third floor are all VIPs, the doormen would help them with their luggage. But that old nun brought a very large box... the doormen offered to help her with it, but she didn't allow it and carried it upstairs herself."
An old nun?
A large box?
Hearing these two keywords, Su Lun suddenly thought of something.
The profession of a nun is quite rare in Dawn City, and from what Su Lun had heard, there was only one discovered monastery ruins left.
Coincidentally, he had experienced one himself, which was the White Monastery where the Wailing Witch resided.
And before entering the space, Su Lun had already identified that the source of the curse at Hotel 1911 was a "superior being's limb."
So upon hearing this information, he immediately guessed something, "It seems that the box must contain the contaminant. In that case, the seal underneath the White Monastery from before must have been sealing this..."
Having seen this far, Su Lun had already figured out some of the story's context.
He felt that he roughly knew who the old nun might be.
....
Su Lun chatted with the two receptionist girls at the front desk for a while, and managed to extract all the information they could provide.
Considering the time, he decided to go watch the magician's performance in the banquet hall.
Nothing else mattered; the advanced material was the top priority.
Unfortunately, as he left the front desk, he was cornered in the corridor by two Scavengers.
One of the guys with a modified mechanical arm sized up Su Lun and said cockily, "Hey, brother, you've been chatting with those two receptionists for so long, you must have gotten a lot of information, right?"
Su Lun had already noticed that the two had been observing him from before and guessed their intentions, so he didn't show a friendly face, "And then?"
They were part of the "Sand Scorpion Group," and their leader was the interim commander for this foray, a somewhat famous old pro. Of the sixty-plus people who came in, this group represented half, clearly having the absolute say in matters.
The man, seeing Su Lun's uncooperative demeanor, reminded him with a sneering smile, "Bro, you really are something. I've never heard of anyone who could get information out of those two receptionist chicks. What exactly did you say to them?"
The other person also flaunted the firearm at his waist, smiling mockingly, "Share some of that information with us. Since we've come together to explore this space, it's fate, let's get rich together, huh?"
The intentions of these guys were already quite clear.
They wanted to seize the information by force.
This kind of behaviour was commonplace among Scavengers in the wilderness, as Scavengers risk their lives for money and few are good-natured.
Hogging resources, cutting out the middleman, seizing by force...
Ordinary lone Scavengers only suffer silently.
Su Lun knew he was being taken for an easy target, and as they revealed their firearms, he didn't so much as lift an eyebrow.
He didn't even care to pay them any attention.
Killing someone here would involve the inn's security, and that could greatly affect his subsequent plans.
He glanced at the two of them and walked away.
The two men were stunned by Su Lun's attitude for a moment then followed, angrily saying, "Hey, are you deaf? Didn't you hear me speak?"
Su Lun turned around calmly as he heard they had drawn their guns and asked, "Do you dare to shoot?"
While speaking, he noticed from the corner of his eye that the attention of the guards had been attracted, and the intent to kill in his eyes also vanished.
He snorted coldly and didn't bother with the two blustering individuals anymore, and walked straight ahead.
....
The Sand Scorpion Gang?
If they really have a death wish...
Su Lun wouldn't mind sending them on their way ahead of time.
As for the two insignificant characters, Su Lun didn't waste time entangling with them and directly headed to the inn's banquet hall.
It was dinner time now, and nearly all the guests of the inn were dining there.
To observe the conditions of the guests in each room, now was the best opportunity.
But the inn's banquet hall had security, and one needed to show their room card key and meal ticket to enter.
When Su Lun arrived, there were already seven or eight Scavengers squatting there. They occasionally approached to strike up conversations, seemingly trying to coax some information out of these passing guests.
But apparently, to little avail.
These NPCs directly ignored those "strange" behaviors that were beyond their understanding.
Su Lun walked straight over, showed the room card and meal ticket he had processed from the front desk lady, and walked right in.
This action naturally caused bewilderment among the few Scavengers at the door.
"Eh... wasn't that guy just now a Scavenger like us?"
"He doesn't have a dark aura, he's definitely a Scavenger."
"Strange, how does he have a room card key?"
"..."
It wasn't that the Scavengers lacked the means to blend into the banquet hall, but those were all shady methods. There were assassins who scaled walls to sneak in, those who stole maid uniforms to disguise as waitstaff, and those who drew the security's attention to sneak in...
But there wasn't one who walked in so openly.
Seeing Su Lun's maneuver, the Scavengers were naturally quite surprised.
At this moment, the two "Sand Scorpion Gang" guys Su Lun had encountered at the front desk managed to shake off security and happened to see this scene.
Watching Su Lun go in, the guy with the mechanical arm turned an ashen hue and cursed, "Damn it, that guy must have gotten some important information at the front desk. Wood, you stay here, I'll go notify the boss!"
....
The banquet hall was bustling, with about a hundred or two guests dining.
The glittering lights shone brightly, lighting up the dining area with an orange glow.
Gentlemen in refined suits, ladies in low-cut evening gowns...
The dining tables were laden with a variety of appetizing foods and fruits.
On a stage not far away, singers and dancers were performing a bold and passionate dance.
Su Lun found a seat with a frontal view of the stage and sat down, sweeping his gaze over the dining guests. He didn't see the nun or the man fitting the description of "Teague Carlson" who had booked four rooms.
No sooner had he sat down, a petite and cute waitress dressed in a black maid's uniform approached with a professional smile, "Sir, would you like to order?"
Su Lun glanced at the delicious food on the neighboring table and indicated, "I'll have the same as them."
With that, he handed over a coin as a tip, in accordance with the custom.
The maid smiled sweetly and bowed deeply, "Of course, sir. Just a moment, please."
When midnight strikes, these waitstaff will transform into beasts with sharp teeth and claws. The "Bloody Maids" in the reports, who chase and gnaw at humans, refer to them.
Su Lun didn't look any further and turned his attention elsewhere.
The singing was melodious, tugging at the heartstrings.
The performance on stage featured dancers from the "Swan Lake Ballet Company," with their registration recorded at the front desk.
Originally, Su Lun visited the banquet hall mainly to wait for the magician's performance.
Fearing he might miss some special NPCs, the gleam in his left eye was constant, a sign of the sustained release of the All-knowing Eye.
But unexpectedly, there was an unforeseen gain.
At that moment, looking at the enchantingly provocative lead singer on stage, his gaze suddenly changed.
Identifying other NPCs in the restaurant displayed a uniform "Contaminated Ancient Remnant Manifestation" above their heads.
However, the singer performing on stage actually had a name, displayed as "Contaminated Dancer Barbara's Remnant Manifestation"!
Su Lun looked at the woman on stage, exuding charm, and suddenly felt a sense of familiarity.
Her beauty eclipsed all others, appearing as if she alone had been enhanced with a filter, a clear indication of high allure.
This made Su Lun immediately think of the Gang Lady Sabina and an idea surfaced in his mind, "Could she also be a woman with the 'Succubus' talent? Is she an ancient alchemist?"
Clearly, having a name meant she was different from the others.
And there was no information about this Barbara in the outside world.
Because she was a guest on the second floor.
Su Lun recalled the check-in records he had seen before, she was staying in room 2115, right next to the magician's room 2113.
The performance on stage continued.
Watching the fair and beautiful singer, Su Lun didn't conjure any erotic images in his mind, but his first reaction was, "If this woman transforms into a monster, it's likely going to be quite troublesome..."
He thought of Sabina's mental attack methods and frowned.
If she turned into a monster, her combat power would surely be formidable.
But...
Why would an alchemist be in a dance troupe?
Then he thought of the magician Edward, who also seemed like he was here to perform?
Su Lun thought of something, a trace of deep contemplation appearing in his eyes.
....
Before Su Lun could ponder further, a waiter pushed a cart over and began to serve dishes.
Although it was a cursed space, the food was real.
Colorful fruits, roasty aromatic grilled chicken, fine wine, and various exquisite dishes...
Delicacies from a thousand years ago were a luxurious treat,
Su Lun tasted a fruit, it was sweet and juicy.
In Old Lington, fruits were a luxury, especially ones he had never seen before.
Before he had even taken a few bites, the ballet troupe had left the stage.
Then, someone brought up several boxes.
It was time for the magic show.
At that moment, a dashing man in a tailcoat and top hat walked onto the stage and bowed deeply to the audience with impeccable grace.
Su Lun watched him, his eyes narrowing slightly, because this man was also identified as having a name, "Contaminated Magician Edward's Remnant Manifestation."
After the applause, Edward began his performance.
He first conjured a wand out of thin air, twirled it a few times, then with a squeeze, it exploded into streamers and disappeared...
Then he took off his hat and pulled out live rabbits, pigeons...
Then, he performed a spatial teleportation.
There were two cabinets on the stage, covered with black cloth a foot off the ground, into which he crawled and pulled the black curtain shut.
The next second, the black curtain of the cabinet several meters away was pulled open, and the guy walked out with a smile...
It was these seemingly common magic tricks,
Yet Su Lun watched with sparkling eyes, his heart beginning to surge.
He thought of a saying.
Some people, under the guise of performing magic tricks, are actually casting spells.
He was certain that this guy named Edward wasn't just performing magic tricks, but was truly casting a spatial spell!
Su Lun possessed the All-Knowing Eye, which rendered most illusion-based magic tricks meaningless.
If it had been a prop, it would have been identified immediately.
Like the hat, if it had a compartment, it would be identified as [Top Hat with Hidden Compartment]. But now, what was displayed was just an ordinary [Top Hat]!
The two cabinets used for the spatial teleportation didn't show up as [Cabinets with Mechanisms] but simply [Ordinary Cabinets]!
This guy had moved from one cabinet to the other, not using any twin substitutes or secret doors...
The magician had genuinely teleported from one to the other!
Seeing this, Su Lun immediately confirmed that Edward was a professional with spatial ability.
Telekinesis...
Spatial Displacement...
The abilities the magician demonstrated perfectly matched all of Su Lun's expectations for his own Tier-2 career planning.
"This magician's body is exceptionally agile, definitely bolstered with a high 'skill' attribute, plus the ability for spatial teleportation makes him excellent in both defense and attack. If advanced materials were to be produced, the match with my role as 'Puppeteer' could be very high!"
Su Lun, watching the performance on the stage, had a slight tremor in his gaze.
But while he was feeling expectant, he suddenly showed a touch of trouble on his face, muttering in his heart, "He has the ability to teleport instantly, he might not be killed even with a black scythe..."
.....
Su Lun's original plan was to kill the magician before midnight, before the contamination occurred, if he confirmed that the magician had the spatial ability he needed, and then take the occupational materials.
Otherwise, after the aberration, unforeseen events could arise.
But now, having seen some of the professional techniques Edward showcased in his performance, Su Lun realized that even without the aberration he wasn't confident he could kill this magician!
No hand signs, no signs of Alchemy formations lighting up, meant that this guy was very adept with spatial abilities.
Even using an invisible zombie for a sneak attack, Su Lun felt it likely wouldn't succeed and he might end up on the receiving end instead.
If you get killed by an NPC, it's a real death!
But spatial materials are hard to come by.
Having finally encountered a cursed space capable of producing them, Su Lun still counted on this special NPC to drop spatial occupational materials; he couldn't let it go just like that.
But if he couldn't overpower it by force, he had to think of other methods.
"This is a bit troublesome..."
Su Lun couldn't wait until midnight.
He found it difficult to imagine how troublesome this ability wielder would become after mutation.
"A+" difficulty on the second floor?
No!
If the two before him were to mutate, the rating would be at least "S-level", possibly even higher!
With this thought, Su Lun "whooshed" to his feet and headed straight for the backstage area.
Because he had thought of a breakthrough.
Hiding two strong alchemists within a performance troupe clearly pointed to a "main storyline" concealed within the background story of this cursed space!
If he couldn't kill them straight on, what about "storyline killing"?

chapters.title: Chapter 159 - 159: Seeing the "§" Symbol Again
chapters.content:
According to the original plot, the "pollution" would only happen at midnight, when everyone in the 1911 Hotel would turn eerie.
The Scavengers came for the materials precisely because they planned to take action after midnight when ordinary people mutated into the eerie and produced curse materials.
But Su Lun couldn't wait until then.
If the Magician were really about to mutate, Su Lun felt even less confident about killing him.
Moreover, now that the four "forbidden rooms" on the first floor had been opened, he felt that tonight's pollution event might involve other changes.
To solve the problem, it was better to act sooner rather than later.
...
Su Lun walked towards the stage and then entered backstage through the side door via the staff passage.
He planned to stop the Magician when he left the stage.
Because from the intelligence he heard, after the Magician stepped off the stage, no one ever saw him again.
Su Lun suspected he might use his Spatial Ability to teleport away, so he had no choice but to wait for him backstage.
Behind the stage was the dressing room, which was somewhat cramped.
The dancers of the "Swan Song and Dance Troupe" were changing costumes here.
With a staff member at the door, Su Lun took off his hat, revealing his face, and then flashed his police badge; he encountered no further obstacles and walked in.
The dancers were probably used to quick costume changes during performances and didn't mind not having private changing rooms. When Su Lun walked in, he saw a group of slender, young ladies with little clothing, changing into their performance costumes in the narrow dressing room.
On seeing a strange man enter, the ladies were initially startled like frightened deer, hurriedly covering their revealing bodies. But once they clearly saw Su Lun's handsome face, they immediately calmed down. Not only did nobody scream, but they also laughed and whispered among themselves. Some of the bolder ones even boldly threw him a coquettish glance.
"Handsome, who are you looking for~"
"I'm looking for Mr. Edward."
"Oh~ That's too bad, I thought you were here to invite our leader, Miss Barbara, to dinner..."
"..."
Continuing on his way, Su Lun responded with a very gentlemanly smile to these beautiful girls.
He wanted to get to the stage exit so he could wait for the Magician to prevent him from disappearing from his sight.
And after passing by, he saw that next to the dressing room, there was a small makeup area separated by a curtain. The lead singer Miss Barbara was inside, changing clothes and removing makeup.
The light was bright, and a large makeup mirror reflected the charming and seductive face.
Su Lun saw the woman with red, enchanting lips in the mirror, and the woman saw him too.
"What's the matter, handsome, did you lose your way?"
The voice was soft and cooing, making one feel as if their bones had turned soft.
Su Lun watched the woman turn around, his gaze involuntarily drawn to her rose-colored red lips.
Those red lips seemed to possess endless magic power, captivating one's gaze.
This was a psychological suggestion laced with mental power, a technique that could make people lower their guard without realizing it.
Narrowing his eyes slightly, Su Lun guessed that this woman was most likely a professional with a [succubus] talent or something similar.
He feared this woman might pull some sort of hypnotism on him, so he directly revealed his police badge, "I would like to wait for Mr. Edward, I have some matters to consult with him."
Barbara looked at the police badge, her eyebrows arching coyly, her tone even stickier, "Oh? A police officer... May I ask what business you have with Mr. Edward?"
Su Lun didn't sense any malice, nor was he careless, and he said indifferently, "Some official business."
Although Su Lun thought this woman must know the magician, he still wanted to wait and talk to Edward.
Hearing this, Barbara smiled seductively, pointed to the chair beside her, and said, "Handsome Officer, why don't you take a seat? Mr. Edward might still be a while before his performance is over..."
Su Lun glanced at her and didn't want to be too close to this practitioner of the psychic profession, declining what seemed an extremely enticing invitation, "I'm on official duty. I won't sit."
Because she was changing costumes, Barbara was also very scantily clad. As he spoke, however, his gaze inadvertently swept across the deep cleavage in front of her chest.
Seriously, did women with succubus talents all have such assets?
Barbara covered her mouth and giggled, catching that look. But far from minding, she brimmed with an inviting smile, generously showcasing her impressive figure, and boldly teased, "Handsome Officer, what are you looking at?"
"..."
Su Lun listened without changing his expression.
He figured that this was probably an occupational hazard of a succubus.
And in the few moments it took for that exchange, sudden footsteps came from the staircase backstage.
A man dressed in a tailcoat came down, and it was indeed the magician Edward.
The intimate atmosphere that had been building was instantly diluted, as Barbara said to Edward, "Mr. Edward, this officer says he has some business with you."
Edward, upon hearing "officer," seemed to be triggered by some keyword, only then did he turn his attention to Su Lun, who he had originally planned to ignore.
Su Lun directly displayed his police badge and said, "I am Joy, a patrol officer from Bell Tower Block, here to investigate some matters. I would ask Mr. Edward to please cooperate."
Edward seemed to recall something, "Bell Tower Block?"
When the other party responded, Su Lun immediately knew his guess was right: these two alchemists hidden among the crowd came for the old nun.
Edward eyed Su Lun for a moment, then continued, "May I ask, Officer, what matters are you here to investigate? And how... might I assist you?"
Su Lun did not feel any malice, which meant that the bodies in those four rooms were likely unrelated to the two people before him.
This gave him even greater confidence in how to use the plot to his advantage.
He stated directly, "Have you heard of the 'White Convent'?"
Upon hearing this, Edward's expression stalled and he frowned, "Oh, of course, I remember it's a convent in the eastern part of Bell Tower Street. But... could Officer Johnny elaborate a bit more, what does your search for me have to do with this convent?"
These people appeared to be living humans, but in reality, they were still high-level NPCs that would only react to certain specific plots.
Su Lun needed to trigger the storyline, so he spoke outright, "An old nun from the convent took something very dangerous with her that might contaminate others. According to the clues I've gathered, she came to this hotel. But in the process, I have discovered some other matters, that's why I need Mr. Edward's cooperation..."
Having said this much, Edward didn't continue to feign ignorance; he smiled, "Officer Johnny, your investigative skills astound me."
As he spoke, he directly took out a badge from his pocket that bore a gold ouroboros and a "§" symbol.
This action, however, took Su Lun by surprise.
He intended to ask Edward to assist in the investigation and lead him to take a look at those bodies, hoping to spark a conflict between him and the malevolent caster, and then find an opportunity...
But to take out a badge was to declare identity, wasn't it?
Su Lun guessed something and silently waited for the other party to take the initiative and introduce themselves.
Sure enough, Edward politely explained, "This incident has exceeded the scope of the police station's handling. Hence, now it is being dealt with by our special operations team. Please leave the matters here to us."
After a pause, he smiled and added, "Praise your dedication, Officer Johnny."
So that was it?
Hearing this, Su Lun immediately understood.
Both Edward and Barbara were officials from Dawn City handling anomalous events!
....
Having finished speaking, Edward looked as if he was about to leave.
But...
The fact that the hotel had become a cursed space meant that a thousand years ago, they had failed to prevent this incident.
The midnight contamination event was a reenactment of that year's tragedy.
If Su Lun left now, the situation would definitely revert to its original trajectory.
Although Su Lun had alchemy items he had acquired from the four corpses, he was likely to survive the midnight ordeal.
But he still needed spatial materials!
So, he certainly wouldn't let Edward just walk away.
Moreover, from the moment room 1021 was opened, it was destined that this Scavenger group might face annihilation.
Now with the presence of professional operatives from Dawn City, perhaps they could resolve the problem on the first floor in advance?
At that instant, Su Lun's thoughts raced, quickly weighing the pros and cons of this turn of events.
Would changing the plot too drastically trigger some kind of butterfly effect?
He did not know what would ultimately happen by altering the plot, but...
But recalling the tone of Mr. Hei's words last night, they seemed to be well-informed about this cursed space.
It implied that a certain powerhouse, still hidden amongst their team, had the capacity to handle all kinds of emergencies.
With that in mind, Su Lun no longer hesitated and directly said, "Um... Mr. Edward, since you are handling this matter, I'm relieved. However, I've come across some intelligence which I'm not sure if you are aware of..."
Listening, Edward turned his head to glance at him, "Oh?"
Su Lun said, "I examined the guest check-in records earlier and discovered that alongside Sister Elizabeth, there was an individual named 'Teague Carlson' who checked in. He booked four rooms and left four unusual corpses in them. They are the 'Faceless One', the 'Hanged Corpse', the 'Drowned Maiden', and the 'Big-headed Wailing Infant'...It seems like some sort of nefarious ritual is underway."
At these words, the two NPCs' expressions shifted dramatically; clearly, they understood what the four corpses signified.
Edward couldn't hide his shock, "The 'Quadrant of Fallen Spirits Ritual'! Damn it, she intends to unseal 'that object' here in this hotel!"
With that, Su Lun knew for certain that they didn't know about the existence of the corpses.
Edward's expression suddenly turned solemn, and he murmured to himself, "I hope we are still in time to prevent it..."
Su Lun, noticing the word "contaminated" above their heads, felt it was necessary to warn them, so he added, "Have you considered that you might already be contaminated?"
Hearing this, the two exchanged a grave look.
Barbara's seductive facade vanished as she suddenly formed sorcerer's seals as if to cast some sort of spiritual spell.
A few breaths later, she looked at Edward with a troubled face and said in a heavy tone, "Someone with high-level rules has clouded our perception; it must be the leaking essence from 'that sealed object'. If things are as Officer Johnny says... we, and possibly everyone in the hotel, have already been contaminated."
"..."
Edward fell silent.
However, a certain resoluteness appeared on his face.
He looked at Su Lun and said, "Officer Johnny, this matter is of great importance, and we may need your help."
Su Lun cast a puzzled look, aware that he might have changed the main storyline.
Edward, with a calm tone and firm resolve, said, "If we truly are contaminated, please, if you see any signs of an anomaly in us, make sure to kill us first."
As he spoke, he glanced over Su Lun's shoulder towards the area where the invisible zombie stood.
Indeed, this Spatial Ability user had long since noticed the presence of the invisible zombie.
"This..."
Su Lun heard the request and showed a look of difficulty, hesitated for a moment, then said, "Alright!"
He could never have predicted that without racking his brains for a way to obtain materials, the other party would take the initiative to bring it up.
Given the circumstances tonight, all NPCs in the hotel were guaranteed to experience anomalies.
With their cooperation, there was simply no need for a sneak attack; the difficulty of carrying out the killings dropped a hundredfold.
But...
This also meant that he had to stick with them constantly. Otherwise, how would he know when they'd turn anomalous?
At that moment, Edward added, "Officer Johnny, the intelligence you've provided is vital. I need to gather my companions. Those four corpses must be destroyed first!"
....
Su Lun followed Edward out of the dressing room.
They were off to contact his teammates in the hotel rooms.
To avoid alarming anyone prematurely, they agreed to act in five minutes, starting with dealing with the corpses in the four rooms.
Su Lun knew that touching those corpses would immediately alert the Caster orchestrating the evil ritual.
A major confrontation might break out sooner than expected.
But now, things seemed hopeful; at least, no one in the hotel had changed yet.
Since Edward and his colleagues were investigating the case, they naturally possessed some strengths.
Su Lun didn't expect the outcome to be one-sided.
As he left the banquet hall, Su Lun intended to find a place to prepare for battle.
But unexpectedly, he was intercepted.
Gallup, the leader of the "Sand Scorpion" group, along with over ten of his team members, was already waiting in the corridor.

chapters.title: Chapter 160 - 160: Hand-Rubbing Black Hole
chapters.content:
The Sand Scorpions watched Edward and Barbara come out and, following Su Lun's example, attempted to strike up a conversation to glean some information.
"Hey, Mr. Edward..."
"Oh, the beautiful Miss Barbara..."
"..."
No matter the opening line, unless a keyword was triggered, the two key NPCs paid no attention to the Scavengers they deemed "outside of their recognition" and simply left.
The group of Scavengers, feeling snubbed, turned their attention to Su Lun, who had come out afterwards.
"Hey, you!"
Gallup's face darkened as he called out to Su Lun.
He didn't beat around the bush and asked bluntly, "What did you say to those two just now?"
...
Su Lun was already aware that the Sand Scorpions had been watching his every move, from the moment he entered the banquet hall, to the backstage... to now.
Facing these folks who obviously meant trouble, his brows furrowed.
He felt it was a waste of time to explain even a word more.
Su Lun had no intention of entertaining these people and ignored Gallup's words, but he found his way blocked by members of the Sand Scorpions who were brazenly armed.
Only then did he ask coldly, "What do you want?"
Gallup asked again, "What exactly did you say to those two ancients a moment ago?"
That aggressive posture made Su Lun frown and he retorted, "Am I obligated to explain anything to you?"
As the esteemed leader of a Scavenger group, Gallup had his pride and naturally couldn't admit that he was strong-arming information.
He spoke with a righteous tone, "Didn't I warn you earlier when I came in not to trigger any special scenarios? Did you just ignore my words?"
At this point, one of the underlings stood forward, putting on the air of a reasonable person, and said, "The Chief Gallup is right! Those two ancients are guests on the second floor; if we don't make it up there by midnight, we're all dead. So, you have to give us an explanation!"
Asking for an explanation was just a pretext; what they really wanted was information.
Ever since this cursed space was discovered, around one or two thousand people had entered. It was clear to any discerning person that the "Magician" and the "Singer" were no simple characters, yet no one had ever managed to extract any useful information from them.
The Scavengers were also well aware that the first floor was just an appetizer; the truly valuable treasures were with the guests on the second floor, or perhaps even on the third.
Discovering any kind of alchemical knowledge or alchemical items was an opportunity to get rich overnight.
Now that a lucky fellow had found a "trick," how could they not be envious?
Seeing Su Lun's attitude of wanting to "keep it all to himself," Gallup threatened, "You'd better speak up. Otherwise, if someone fucks up and triggers some dangerous scenario, I won't hesitate to take them out first."
...
Su Lun was originally not opposed to giving some explanations.
It wasn't he who wanted to kill them, but rather the five major family Scavenger groups outside.
From the moment Room 1021 was opened, it was destined that this group entering the cursed space would be wiped out.
Now, if they didn't trigger a scenario, they were certain to die; triggering one, on the other hand, gave them a small chance of survival...
But the malice around him was piercing like needles.
These guys were truly intent on killing.
With not a single expression on his face, Su Lun asked calmly, "Are you going to kill me?"
"Hmph."
Gallup snorted coldly, the meaning clear without words: as long as you understand, kid.
However, what no one expected was for Su Lun to behave like a clueless kid, completely misunderstanding the gravity of the situation.
He just let out a single word indifferently, "Oh."
Oh?
Gallup turned an iron shade seeing Su Lun's blatant lack of respect.
The rest of the "Sand Scorpions" were also not pleased, their fur bristling like cats whose tails had been stepped on.
"Kid, our chief is talking to you nicely and you fucking ignore him? Do you really think we won't touch you just because there are guards around?!"
"Chief Gallup, don't bother talking to this type of person. I say, if he doesn't give us a satisfactory explanation, tie him up and take him to the wine cellar, and just kill him."
"..."
The Scavengers no longer hid their intentions, and their questioning turned into a blatant threat to his life.
Without the hotel guards, someone indeed would have died long ago.
However, it wasn't Su Lun, but them.
Once again blocked, Su Lun was also getting a bit impatient from being entangled.
He was no longer polite, "Beat it."
The Scavenger gang's insoleness wasn't developed in a day or two; they were used to being overbearing, and who would heed such arrogant words?
As soon as he said it, someone jumped out, "Kid, who the fuck are you to talk to me like that?"
With the conversation having reached this point, Su Lun no longer hid his murderous intent, a sneer spreading across his lips.
He cocked his head and scrutinized the group, "My name...knowing it means death, are you sure you want to know?"
Upon hearing this, the heart of every Scavenger gang member inexplicably shivered.
They immediately realized that they might have encountered a tough nut to crack.
It sounded like he had some background to be so arrogant, right?
But this is the Cursed Space, after all!
Heh... if there truly is a background, and we offend him, then we certainly can't let the person leave alive!
Gallup's gaze grew even colder.
Although some Scavenger gang members were frightened by this bravado, with more than a dozen of them there, they couldn't just chicken out like this.
The deputy gang leader, raising his neck and laughing contemptuously, said, "Hahaha... Do you think I'm easily scared? Come on, spit it out, what's your damn name, 'cause I'd die to hear it!"
Su Lun didn't waste any more words this time, simply stating, "Oh... My name is Su Lun."
Having said that, he left straight through the crowd without looking back.
This time, no one dared to stop him.
....
He said... his name is Su Lun?
This name seemed to possess some sort of magic power.
A question arose in everyone's mind.
The name seemed very familiar, yet they couldn't recall it at that moment.
No, it was more accurate to say, no one dared to think in that direction.
The group exchanged glances, seeing the puzzle and that inexplicable unease in each other's eyes.
After a long while, someone spoke up with a trembling voice, voicing the possibility that nearly all of them had thought of, "It seems like... the S-ranked fugitive who's been causing a ruckus lately is named... Su Lun."
With that, it was as if the whole world fell silent.
They turned their gaze toward the proud figure who had walked away, finally understanding where his confidence came from.
They suddenly realized that what that guy had said before wasn't a bluff, but the truth.
In the underworld, it's a taboo for robbers to be recognized and for fugitives to give out their names - it's a matter of life and death.
If it really was that "S-ranked fugitive," would he let these people who knew his identity live?
At that moment, they all heard the sound of swallowing.
Even Gallup, the Scavenger gang's boss, turned pale.
At this moment, even though that man had his back to them, Gallup didn't dare muster up the courage to draw his gun.
An "S-ranked fugitive" who is tough enough to hunt down second-tier professionals is not someone their small Scavenger gang could provoke, right?
Although they regretted it in their hearts, what was done couldn't be undone.
A ruthless gleam flashed across Gallup's eyes.
"Boss, if it really is that 'Su Lun,' we..."
"So what if he's a fugitive, am I supposed to kneel and beg for mercy? Damn it! Wait until midnight; we'll take that guy out first. With so many strange occurrences, I don't believe he's invincible! We won't go scavenging today; let's make a bounty!"
"Right, he didn't dare to make a move, similarly wary of the guard. We could even find a chance to trigger a conflict and have the guards arrest him. By then, even if it really is that fugitive, we could use the spatial rules to kill him!"
"..."
With this, the others also began to echo in agreement.
....
The Scavenger gang didn't have the guts to shoot on the spot.
Su Lun wasn't inclined to deal with them right now either.
He walked over, meeting Edward and Barbara who had just come down the stairs.
They had just come down from the second floor and called over a new partner, an old lady in a black robe with a face full of tattoos.
Edward introduced their partner to Su Lun, "This is Madam Archimedes, she is an [Exorcist], adept at dealing with some evil magic. We have another partner who'll be down soon."
"Hmm."
Su Lun, not one for small talk, led the three of them to the door of room 1021.
He used his lock picking skills to open the door.
Edward and his two companions were the first to enter, and then they saw the corpse on the bed.
The tattooed old lady also had a solemn expression as she said, "This is indeed the corpse of 'The Faceless.' Destroying the corpse will immediately alert the caster."
Edward also sighed, "Now that the people in the inn should all be contaminated, there's no need for evacuation. Prepare for battle."
Barbara, who was standing to the side, didn't speak, but at this moment, she had already completed her demon transformation, her pupils had turned red, and a tail had grown. Her body was enveloped in an eerie pink mist.
Su Lun didn't approach but instead stood at a distance, hiding his body behind the invisible undead.
Just as they were preparing to destroy the body, a man with a crew cut arrived belatedly.
When Edward and the others saw him, they clearly recognized him and greeted him, "Rosco, you're here."
But as soon as this man entered and they saw his face clearly, Su Lun's pupils suddenly constricted.
He looked at the man's unusually large earlobes and immediately thought of the description given by the receptionist.
With a sense of dread, Su Lun inwardly exclaimed, "This guy is the one who booked those four rooms... Teague Carlson!"
Upon identification, the name above this guy's head was also "Demon-transformed Beast Tamer Rosco."
....
These four corpses were arranged by him!
So it wasn't just that old nun. Among Edward's teammates, there was another who had been corrupted by magic.
Su Lun even guessed that the reason these people failed to handle the incident a thousand years ago was probably directly related to this guy.
However, even after discovering this, Su Lun's face showed no hint of surprise.
The people were already here, and there was no need to speak, as a fight was inevitably going to break out.
With three against one, the advantage was still theirs.
He dared not expose the truth aloud, fearing that "Demon-transformed Rosco" would target him as the primary attack objective. Instead, he silently took out his marionette and also formed a sorcerer's seal, quietly unraveling the vestment...
Edward and the others watched Su Lun deploy his spider lance and vestment with a sidelong glance, but said nothing.
Meanwhile, the old lady had taken out some red crystals and alchemical powder, intending to destroy the corpse.
Suddenly, the crew-cut man made his move!
His hands, without any warning, stretched out in advance and, in the blink of an eye, turned into two spotted poison snakes. Opening their mouths to reveal their poison fangs, they lunged towards the magician's throat and the cloaked old lady.
Edward sensed the danger and his figure flashed, instantly teleporting several meters away.
The cloaked old lady, however, was not quick enough to evade and was bitten on the neck by the poison snake.
"Rosco, what are you doing!"
"Careful, he's been contaminated!"
"..."
Several urgent shouts.
Rosco's face showed numbness, and a surge of black energy wildly inflated around him. An alchemical formation lit up beneath his feet, and in the next second, thousands of spotted poisonous snakes swarmed into Room 1021!
Stripe after stripe of poison snakes, mouths agape and fangs bared, surged toward the people in the room.
And more sinisterly, a shadowy, ash-colored alchemical formation also suddenly lit up beneath the corpse of 'The Faceless' on the bed.
The corpse... abruptly stood upright!
Su Lun, feeling a chill on his scalp, silently took out the sack he had previously removed from a corpse and put it over his head.
Peering through the gaps in the sack, he watched everything happening in the room.
The current battle did not yet require his intervention.
....
The crew-cut man suddenly turned traitor, catching Edward and the other two off guard.
But that didn't mean the three of them were without the power to counterattack.
The cloaked old lady had been bitten on the neck by a poison snake. Her complexion instantly revealed a black miasma signifying death.
However, at that moment, she took out a black cloth doll and sprayed it with a mouthful of black blood.
On closer inspection, the color on her face returned to a much healthier shade of red.
Watching as a tide of poison snakes flooded in, Edward also swiftly reacted. His hands rapidly formed sorcerer's seals, and a black hexagram array shone from beneath his feet.
Then, something miraculous happened.
Su Lun watched as the space in the palms of his hands suddenly twisted.
In just the blink of an eye, it was as if the space, this "canvas," was forcibly torn open, turning into two increasingly larger swirling black vortexes. The tide-like surge of poison snakes, yet to wreak havoc, was suddenly swallowed by a powerful suction force into those two palm-held black vortexes, their destination unknown.
Watching this battle scene from the side, Su Lun was astounded, "Creating black holes with your hands? How... How outrageous is this Spatial Ability?!"
He was also grateful that he hadn't planned to directly ambush this magician earlier.
This move, it simply stunned someone who had never seen Spatial Ability before.
....
On the other hand, the fight that erupted in the room had instantly reached an intensity where life and death were decided in just moments.
Barbara had transformed into a succubus, her body exploding into a cloud of pink mist, and when she reappeared, she was already enveloping the flat-headed man in front of her.
But the next moment, a sharp cry was heard, "Rosco has been completely contaminated, we can't control him!"
Before the words even settled, the skin on the flat-headed man's body suddenly swelled up, and huge tumors started puffing out from his body, tearing through his clothes... it seemed as though he would mutate into a monstrous creature any second.
"Kill him!"
Edward made a snap decision, shouting vehemently.
He retracted the black hole in his palm, brought his hands together, and made a compressing motion in the air; the space around the flat-headed man seemed to solidify, and his body instantly stiffened.
A flash of cold light within the pink mist, and before the newly-mutated freak had a chance to wreak havoc, a massive head rolled to the ground with a thud.
The elder woman in black took a deep breath, her tone solemn as she looked at the corpse in the room, "The Four Vengeful Corpses have been raised, killing one will only lead to their infinite resurrection. They must all be killed at the same time, or the caster must be killed to break the spell!"
Edward also shouted, "Hurry to the third floor! That old nun must be heavily contaminated by now! Kill her before she's fully turned into a demon!"
The turn of events happened too fast, there was no time for anyone to hesitate.
Without another word, Edward and his two allies rushed out.
The battle came suddenly, and ended just as abruptly.
From the flat-headed man's arrival to now, just a few fleeting moments had passed, and in room 1021, the snake was gone, the people were gone...
All that was left was a decapitated corpse on the ground and a [No-Face Corpse] standing stiffly on the bed.
Oh, and Su Lun, covered with a sack over his head, in the corner.
....
Outside, gunfire had already erupted, and the NPCs in the hotel seemed to have begun their mutations.
Su Lun, looking at the two corpses in the room, muttered to himself, "The plot seems to have gone off track..."
The person who checked into the room was Edward's teammate, something he hadn't expected.
But... it seemed to make no big difference.
In the end, they would have to fight either way.
The only difference was that the "Ghost Fog" that was supposed to erupt at midnight had started two hours earlier.
It was unclear whether this was good or bad.
Su Lun wanted to leave the room, but just then, he saw the [No-Face Corpse]'s head suddenly blossom open. Then, from within the petals, grew stamens, and several meters-long flesh-colored tentacles, studded with tumorous suckers, writhed and emerged from it...
The seven or eight tentacles, like snake tongues, probed the air in all directions, as if searching for living creatures by scent.
Su Lun remained still, the information he identified matching exactly what the elder woman in black had said.
[Demonized No-Face Corpse]
Detailed description: A second-tier silver rank zombie oddity; a special ingredient for an evil ritual, the oddity will infinitely resurrect within the formation unless the caster is killed to interrupt the ritual, or all four Vengeful Corpses are killed simultaneously.
Even though it was a zombie kind, it couldn't be killed.
Su Lun, looking at the formation that lit up in the room, guessed that this room was the "respawn point" for the oddity.
And at that moment, the tentacles seemed to detect the presence of a living person in the room, and the slime-dripping appendages groped their way closer and closer to where Su Lun stood...
But fortunately, the "sack" did its job.
Just when they were about an arm's length away, the tentacles seemed to sense a repellant odor and withdrew.
The [No-Face Corpse] ignored Su Lun and left the room.
....
"Whew..."
Su Lun let out a breath of relief.
A glow had begun to appear on the decapitated corpse in the room.
He walked over and picked up the gold promotional material [Beast Tamer's Whip].
Too bad it wasn't material for a Magician...
Su Lun's brow furrowed slightly.
It was just as the previous information had indicated, the oddities here easily produced high-tier materials.
But this also meant that if he wanted to guard Edward's body, he would have to go upstairs.
After considering, Su Lun took out a [Hanging Noose] and slipped it onto his arm, hooked the bag containing [Damp Hair] to his waist, and used the [Wailing Infant's Swaddle] as a cloak...
Only after preparing all this did he finally control his reanimated corpse and exit the room.

chapters.title: Chapter 161 - 161: Messing Up the Art Style Again
chapters.content:
When Su Lun emerged from room 1021, the hotel had already descended into chaos.
A mass of dark gray fog spread down from the second-floor staircase, giving this brightly lit and luxurious hotel a filter akin to the underworld, with a gloomy gray coldness in every view.
Inspection revealed that the fog was a special kind of "corpse gas".
The NPCs in the hotel had been contaminated over the past three days, and upon contact with this gray fog, they began to mutate. Their bodies uncontrollably sprouted disgusting tumors and strange tentacles... In the blink of an eye, they transformed from humans into clawing, fanged monstrosities.
Suddenly, the hotel was overrun with zombies, with constant screams and roars of agony... It was akin to a hell on earth.
From previous intelligence, Su Lun knew that this "Ghost Fog" was a gas that also highly likely to cause Scavengers to mutate.
But upon seeing it, he discovered that this "Ghost Fog" was a type of dark energy purer than regular dark spiritual power, which could also increase the upper limit of one's dark spiritual power through inhalation.
He even tried taking a few breaths and found...
His previously full and slowly increasing dark spiritual power value was rising again.
Moreover, his body had an even higher affinity for the "Ghost Fog", making breathing it utterly refreshing.
During inhalation, it also increased the efficiency of recovering consumed dark spiritual power. The amount of recovery was almost the same as what he currently expended when unleashing his implant gear and "Servant" form, with not even a hint of mutation...
This meant that in this environment, Su Lun could almost maintain his implant gear in active state indefinitely.
That was somewhat good news.
.....
Loud sounds of fierce combat came from above. It seems like Magician Edward and his group of three had engaged in battle with the old nun.
But Su Lun wasn't in a hurry to go upstairs.
Both parties were at their peak condition, and the battlefield above was bound to be extremely dangerous.
If he intervened, he might inadvertently get caught in the crossfire.
According to the thousand-year storyline, Edward's group was supposed to be wiped out.
Now... it was hard to say.
Given the abilities they had just displayed, all three were extremely strong. As long as they didn't undergo demonization, they would certainly have the strength to fight.
From the noise upstairs, the battle was intense and evenly matched, hence the ferocity.
So, he would wait.
Waiting for both sides to be weakened was the best opportunity to enter the fray.
Su Lun walked into the corridor, and after a thought, decided to check out the situation on the first floor first.
The circumstances today differed somewhat from when the previous Scavenger teams had entered.
When the last team of Scavengers entered, by the time midnight arrived, the only "wild monsters" they had to face were the staff and security on duty within the hotel. If they wanted to hunt other monsters, they had to open the doors room by room. Without opening the doors, the monsters would generally not come out on their own.
But today, due to the "Ghost Fog" erupting early, most of the guests were now in the banquet hall on the first floor.
It caused the monsters to mutate en masse, creating a chaotic frenzy of demons.
But this wasn't all bad news.
The silver lining was that because the mutation had erupted prematurely, although there were many monsters, their strength was not great.
Su Lun casually killed a [Mutated Waitstaff] in the corridor and discovered it was not a "Bizarre" level monster, at most it was an elite.
This differed greatly from previous intelligence, which stated that the lowest on the first floor were Black Iron Bizarre monsters.
Furthermore, there was another piece of good news for Su Lun.
Normally, the higher the floor, the stronger the mutant monsters became.
But now, since most of the guests were gathered on the first floor, the number of high-tier monsters on the second and third floors would be relatively less.
If he were to go up later, this would reduce the danger for him considerably.
...
[The Demonized Faceless Corpse] left a trail of wet, sticky sludge in the corridor.
Su Lun followed the trail and saw it use its tentacles, which were dozens of meters long, to catch a panicking Scavenger. Then it used its tentacles to probe into the victim's mouth and nose, quickly dessicating the person into a husk.
The Scavengers also noticed this head-blossomed creature and retaliated fiercely.
But normal bullets were practically harmless to this second-tier silver Bizarre creature. Even cannon fire only left minor wounds with little effect.
Because they were wearing head coverings, the strange creature paid no attention to Su Lun.
Su Lun knew he couldn't kill it, so he didn't waste time trying.
Since rooms 1055 and 1022 were not far apart, as Su Lun walked down the corridor, he suddenly saw a translucent shadow with an unnaturally long tongue floating by.
Upon closer inspection, this turned out to be the hanged corpse from room 1055 that had become a ghost type.
Because Su Lun had on him a "Hanging Noose," this ghost type selectively ignored him, and they passed by each other, one human, one spectre.
Without the threat of this second-tier entity, Su Lun felt as if the first floor also seemed to have no deadly dangers.
Thinking this, he directly made his way to the banquet hall, where the monsters were most concentrated.
Here, chaos reigned among the monsters, bullets flying everywhere.
The previously charming maid waitresses had turned into "Bloody Maids," the tall leggy dancers into "Desire Demons," and the ladies and mademoiselles had become all manner of bizarrely shaped zombies...
The Scavengers were engaged in a fierce firefight with the monsters.
"What on earth is going on! It's not even midnight yet, how could these ancients have mutated..."
"It must be that wanted criminal Su Lun's doing, damn it, if we'd known earlier, we should have killed him on the spot!"
"These mutated monsters don't seem to be that strong though..."
"Haha, we're going to make a fortune this time..."
"…"
When Su Lun arrived, he saw that the Scavengers had divided into two groups, hunting the monsters.
One group consisted of independent hunters, and the other belonged to the "Sand Scorpion Group".
Since most of these monsters were zombie types and most hadn't reached the level of strangeness, despite their numbers, concentrated gunfire could reap them like wheat.
But the good times did not last, as four special second-tier silver entities made their entrance, and the situation immediately turned one-sided.
In addition to the "Faceless Corpse" and "Hanged Corpse" he'd seen before, two more had appeared.
The "Bigheaded Wailing Infant" had turned into a zombie type with a massive head, a terrifying eye as big as a basketball occupying most of its skull, possessing immense strength and the ability to burrow underground;
And the "Drowned Woman Corpse" had become a ghost type radiating blue light, floating along, leaving a trail of water stains behind her.
It was these four second-tier entities that made the Scavengers' counterattacks pale and powerless.
The two zombie types were manageable, their movements were slow and they were difficult to shoot, but the Scavengers could use the terrain to avoid them.
But the two ghost types were much more troublesome, completely ignoring physical damage, able to pass through walls and float, leaving no chance to escape...
"Ah... those are ghost types!"
"Don't be afraid, we have more people, the ghost types can't control so many of us!"
"Don't fucking run! The more scared you are, the more it will target you!"
"…"
The Scavengers had theoretical experience in dealing with ghost types, but ultimately, not everyone could control the fear within their hearts.
Scared and mentally disordered, their sanity (san) dropped to a very low value, and they were immediately controlled by the ghost types' mental attacks. The spreading atmosphere of fear and the agonized screams of dying companions intensely stimulated the nerves of others, spreading contagion...
When Su Lun arrived, he watched as the two ghost types floated through the crowd, leaving bodies to fall like cut wheat wherever they passed.
For ordinary people who weren't skilled in spiritual power, there was practically no solution to their methods.
Those targeted by the "Hanged Corpse" seemed to experience an illusion of being hanged and suffocating, then instinctively made the motion to remove the noose from their necks. In reality, they would strangle their own necks, and as the sensation of suffocation grew more intense, they would grasp tighter until they strangled themselves to death in the struggle...
The "Drowned Woman Corpse" used a similar tactic, causing people to believe they were drowning and suffocating. This made them instinctively hold their breath to the point of asphyxiation. The water stains left by the dead bodies suggested that apart from illusions, the entity also had the ability to manipulate water elements...
Both ghost types were completely immune to physical attacks, which is why normal Scavengers feared them.
They might have stood a chance with a Magician specializing in magic, but independent groups hardly employed such costly professionals, so facing high-tier ghost types generally meant "total annihilation".
Even the use of "Demon Bane Bullets," the alchemical bullets designed for ghost types, was futile.
Besides not having enough bullets to kill the ghost types, even if they did manage to kill them, the special entities could revive indefinitely.
This was a deadlock.
…...
Su Lun watched from a distance, also roughly figuring out the abilities of the four second-tier entities.
Because of the "Four-Piece Anti-Trickery Set" on him, the four special creatures paid him no attention.
He also ignored those creatures.
But the other mutated monsters were very sensitive to the breath of the living, and they surged toward him.
Su Lun didn't hesitate, his guns belching flames.
From his past life's gaming experience, to fight a boss, it was best to clear out the minions first.
He wanted to clear out the monsters on the first floor as quickly as possible, to avoid any complications when going upstairs. For instance, as time passed, the monsters could become stronger; or the old nun upstairs might have some special method to summon minions to her aid...
Therefore, it was best to initiate the attack.
As long as it wasn't a trickery-level mutated monster, Su Lun's marksmanship could take care of it in just a few shots.
If regular bullets didn't work, then use alchemical bullets.
After Su Lun grew stronger, the people he killed also became increasingly powerful, resulting in him capturing more and more rich spoils of war. He had an abundance of various alchemical bullets, numbering in the thousands.
For a "Firearms Expert," ammunition was his confidence.
The mutated monsters, like sharks sensing the smell of blood, crazily swarmed him. He found a corner with walls on three sides, stood there, strapped on an ammo box, and began harvesting without expression...
Knowing that tonight was going to be a fierce battle, Su Lun did not skimp on ammunition.
"Pop," "Pop," "Pop," "Pop,"...
The rapid-fire sound of the submachine gun was continuous, occasionally interspersed with a few "Boom," "Boom" sounds of special alchemical bullets exploding.
Although the sound of gunfire was incessant, the rhythm was not chaotic.
The firepower suppression of [Blue Demon] and the precise sniping of [Thunder Snake] made Su Lun's noise alone equivalent to the firepower of a whole organized team of Scavengers in the distance.
Aiming for the eyes to explode heads, targeting joints to break limbs, stacking shots to breach defenses...
Utter calmness made Su Lun's marksmanship precise and deadly.
In fact, due to the gap in marksmanship and alchemical bullets, in a short while, the monsters he killed alone surpassed the total number killed by those several dozen scattered Scavengers.
After all, how could ordinary Scavengers, who hunt with their lives on the line, possibly be equipped with alchemical bullets costing eleven thousand each?
A single spray could mean several hundreds of thousands gone, which normal Scavengers could not afford.
This was a disparity in equipment,
and also a crushing superiority in skill.
Gradually, the pile of mutated monster corpses in front of Su Lun grew higher...
This scene, witnessed by the ordinary Scavengers in the distance, made them swallow their saliva fervently.
Merely Su Lun's spot-on marksmanship had everyone utterly astonished.
Especially the guys from "Sand Scorpion," their faces turned pale, their eyes filled with horror.
Only then did they realize how ignorant they had been before, thinking of killing this "Class S wanted criminal" for the bounty?
If those bullets hadn't landed on the mutated monsters but on them instead, they would probably have met the same fate.
Besides, Su Lun's methods were not limited to his marksmanship.
....
Most of the NPCs in the hotel from a thousand years ago were also ordinary people, and since they hadn't been fully "contaminated," they weren't considered strong even after mutating.
What was troublesome were the original professionals among the guards and guests.
After their mutations, they were at least silver-tier trickeries.
In this first-floor hall, there were at least three to four hundred people including guests and hotel staff, bound to hide some professionals.
Once the ghost fog erupted, they all came out.
Wall-crawling spiders with extreme speed, skull-crushing doctors who enjoyed knocking people's heads, meat mountains that couldn't be killed by alchemical bullets, chameleon-like invisible monsters...
These trickeries mixed in with the horde of monsters were the greatest threat to Su Lun.
But there were many mutated monsters, and Su Lun had "people" on his side as well.
Various trick marionettes stood in several rows beside him, keeping him tightly protected.
[Laughing Doll], [Wailing Doll], [Bomb-Proof Doll], [Lead Heavy Doll], [Oil Swallowing Doll], [Phosphorus Fire Doll], [Voodoo Doll]...
He now had a large amount of witch's hair strands, which greatly increased the number and efficiency of puppet manipulation he could manage.
The fine hairs on the Octopus Spear allowed for precise control of the threads, and even as Su Lun continuously fired his guns with both hands, it didn't affect the operation of the puppets at all.
These puppets also ensured that the occasional one that slipped through the barrage of fire was kept at a safe distance.
Even if there were one or two particularly tricky second-tier monsters, the invisible zombies behind Su Lun would slice their heads in half before they even got close.
With long-range means and close-combat abilities, the aberrant monsters found it difficult to get close.
....
There was enough dark Spiritual Power, and bullets were plentiful...
Originally, following this rhythm, Su Lun felt that it wouldn't be long before he could clean up the monsters on the first floor, except for those four.
But as he was fighting, an accident happened.
Just as Su Lun was killing in a smooth rhythm,
that "Giant-Headed Ghoul Infant" suddenly exploded without warning, turning into chunks of flesh scattered all over the ground...
Before he understood what had happened, the light and shadow of that "Drowned Maiden Corpse" also dispersed.
The two aberrant creatures seemed to have suffered some unseen attack and perished suddenly.
"Huh...?"
Su Lun was still firing, but as he caught a glimpse of this scene, a sound of amazed doubt escaped his lips.
He was certain that the sudden demise of those two second-tier monsters was not his doing, and neither could the Scavengers have managed it.
They had died inexplicably.
"Could it be Edward and the others upstairs did it?"
Su Lun suddenly realized something, but couldn't fathom what this remote monster-killing method was all about.
He didn't think too much about it though.
Because at that moment, his gaze fell on where the "Drowned Maiden Corpse" had collapsed.
There... a "grey mist" unexpectedly appeared!
Zombies rarely produce grey mist shards, but ghost species, being spiritual entities, have a high likelihood of producing them.
Because it was too far away, Su Lun didn't have the chance to collect the grey mist.
And within those few moments, the light and shadow fragments and flesh remnants of the two aberrant corpses seemed to be absorbed by the space, vanishing without a trace.
Looking back, the door to room 1055 in the far corridor from where the strange cries emanated, a new "Drowned Maiden Corpse" floated out intact.
And before long, a Giant-Headed Monster also came hopping gleefully into the banquet hall to continue its hunt...
They really could resurrect indefinitely.
....
However...
Upon witnessing this, a bold idea suddenly sparked in Su Lun's mind.
These four corpses truly could resurrect infinitely, but what would happen if their Soul Shards were stripped away?
This thought struck him, and Su Lun suddenly realized he had found a method to restrain these four aberrant creatures, no, perhaps even a way to kill them!
With this in mind, he no longer chose to hunker down in the corner, but ran to a position near the two ghost species, ready to put his idea into action.
Without waiting long, the "Demonized Hanged Corpse" also perished inexplicably, dissolving away.
The "grey mist" appeared once more.
Seizing the opportunity, Su Lun didn't wait for the grey mist to disappear, he rushed forward and devoured the mist.
'Gained 2 Soul Shards of "Demonized Hanged Corpse"'
'You have grasped "Mental Illusion·Suffocation Technique (Incomplete)"...'
'Spiritual Power +0.6'
As Su Lun assimilated the grey mist, his eyes lit up with excitement.
It actually worked!

chapters.title: Chapter 162 - 162: Stripping Wool so Much That Four Sheep Went Bald
chapters.content:
In the realm of Alchemy, everything can be exchanged through the principle of equivalent trade.
This is probably the principle behind why those four peculiar entities could infinitely resurrect.
But can souls be exchanged using a formation of equivalent alchemy trade?
Legend has it that during the age of gods, high-level Magicians could accomplish this...
But, that was just a "legend."
Now, it was simply impossible!
Although Su Lun did not know the level of the Formation set up in this restaurant, the so-called "Four-Entity Fallen Spirit Sacrificial Formation," it was definitely not the legendary "god-level."
With a part of each soul already devoured, it was impossible for the formation to resurrect an identical type of ghost!
As Su Lun had guessed, after he had devoured the gray mist, the "Hanged Corpse" floated out again.
This time, however, its spiritual radiance was significantly dimmer.
The appraisal displayed the word "weakened"!
....
"Just as I thought!" Su Lun exclaimed with a gleam of delight on his face.
The formation resurrected the ghoul, but it couldn't restore its soul completely.
If he could kill it a few more times, he even felt that he might completely devour this type of ghost...
Meanwhile, the commotion from the fight upstairs suddenly intensified as if the combatants had discovered something unusual, triggering another round of fierce battle.
Subsequently, the "Magic-transformed Drowning Female Corpse" also disintegrated for the second time.
This time, Su Lun saw clearly.
Right before the ghoul disintegrated, it seemed to suffer a fatal attack out of thin air, which caused its sudden death.
He didn't delay and skillfully rushed over to devour the gray mist.
"Gained 'Magic-transformed Drowning Female Corpse's Soul Shard*2'"
"You have comprehended 'Mental Illusion Art: Drowning Technique (Incomplete)...'"
"Spiritual Power +0.7"
Then,
The second reaping...
The third reaping...
The fourth reaping...
The four second-tier silver entities downstairs periodically exploded and continually resurrected, only to be harvested repeatedly.
So it went on and on.
Though Su Lun wasn't aware of exactly what was happening upstairs, it didn't stop him from joyfully harvesting soul shards.
The two ghost types were sheared by Su Lun over and over, and although the spiritual power and shards obtained were diminishing, each shearing caused the ghosts to weaken after resurrecting.
Even the two undead types, despite a very small probability, also burst into "gray mist" a couple of times because of repeated sudden deaths.
