"Heh, hiding this long before exposing yourself, you must have known about my ability to sense hostility..."
Su Lun raised his eyebrows at a relaxed pace.
He also deduced that the one targeting him was a firearms master.
Such swift targeting and firing were beyond the ability of a regular sniper.
Even in that brief glimpse, he clearly saw the guy who had shot through his arm thousands of meters away on a small slope — "Gun King" Geiger.
However, this time, Su Lun wasn't panicking in the slightest.
[B-098-Sixth Sense]Guaranteed hit?
For ordinary professionals, and even most second-tier professionals, it indeed was "guaranteed".
But here, there was also a cause and effect relationship that wasn't clarified.
Gaige sniped his target by using his ability to anticipate the target's anticipation and then pulling the trigger.
Anticipation came first, followed by firing the gun.
However, if the target dodged after he fired, they could likewise evade this "sixth sense."
No one did this because the speed at which a sniper rifle bullet leaves the barrel is very fast; ordinary professionals simply couldn't wait for the bullet to exit the barrel before dodging, as that would be akin to "waiting for death."
Previously, Su Lun couldn't either.
But now he could.
Feeling the sensation of being locked in a killing intent, he didn't make any preemptive dodging movements.
His enhanced All-knowing Eye clearly captured the other person pulling the trigger.
Then, as flames burst from the muzzle, a bullet engraved with runes, an alchemy bullet, was also propelled out.
At that moment, Su Lun's eyes sharpened, and everything seemed to slow down a hundredfold.
The gunpowder smoke burning at the muzzle froze, forming a fluffy cotton-blossom; the light also formed a slowly dimming diamond-shaped beam...
He could even clearly see the bullet leaving the muzzle, creating ripples of air waves. The recoil also made Gaige's figure tremble.
The bullet, too fast for the naked eye to capture, gradually exited the barrel and pierced through the air towards him...
Su Lun accurately judged that the bullet was aimed at his forehead, then slightly tilted his head.
At such a distance, his super-high neural reaction speed was enough to let him easily dodge.
The bullet whizzed past his ear, bringing with it a gust of wind.
"Bang!"
It was only after the bullet passed that a thunderous gunshot sound belatedly reached him.
This slow-motion action felt like it took a long time, but in reality, it was instant.
No one saw what happened.
It seemed like Su Lun just casually tilted his head and dodged a fatal headshot.
Not far away, the shooter Gaige,
seeing this,
his face drastically changed.
....
This sniper shot was like the command gun that initiated a roundup.
"Whoosh~"
"Whoosh~"
"Whoosh~"
A series of flares exploded in the sky.
Upon closer inspection, the flares burned and released layers of silver powder.
Like snow, they quickly blanketed the ground.
"Revealing powder, huh..."
Su Lun narrowed his eyes at the silvery powder filling the sky, his mouth corners under the mask slightly lifted.
The Oliver family indeed prepared thoroughly to deal with him.
With all this revealing powder, it was impossible for Su Lun to hide any invisible objects nearby.
This way, even if there were zombies driven by hatred, once they materialized, their slashing movements could be captured, and they wouldn't mysteriously appear through spatial rifts like before.
For those second-tier professionals, seeing the movement was enough to anticipate it.
This "revealing powder" directly reduced the threat of the Dark Scythe by a significant margin.
Nonetheless,
Su Lun wasn't surprised by this tactic at all.
Because, thanks to Sabina's information channels, he knew all about these people's roundup plans.
"So next is everyone charging fiercely?"
Su Lun's eyes sharpened, and with lightning-speed, he fired three shots, outright killing three people in front of him.
His neural reaction speed was now extremely fast; and even if the opponents grabbed their guns first, they posed no threat.
Then, with a clap of his hands performing sorcerer's seals, eight fierce spider spears coalesced behind him.
Pulling out a sealing scroll, he unfurled it in the air, revealing ten six-pointed star space sealing patterns drawn on it.
Before the scroll hit the ground, Su Lun quickly brought his hands together and lightly shouted, "Sealing - Release!"
The scroll exploded on cue, and more than ten puppets had already appeared around him, creaking eerily with the sound of wooden joints rubbing.
The sealing skill of the space scroll was certainly faster than taking them out one by one from the space ring!
Having completed all this, Su Lun ran towards the direction of the relic.
It looked like he was fleeing, but in reality, he wanted to break the enemy's encirclement to kill them one by one!
"Ten second-tier professionals, tsk tsk, the Oliver family really went all out this time..."
As he retreated, Su Lun's gaze captured the entire battlefield.
However, to his surprise, that Geiger didn't continue to shoot.
Turning his head for a closer look, Su Lun saw that a fight had broken out at the sniper point.
A cloaked figure with ghostly movements was entangled in combat with Geiger.
Su Lun guessed who the cloaked person was and frowned.
However, there was no time to take any extra actions at that moment.
....
The opposition had already devised a detailed encirclement plan and guessed that Su Lun would definitely flee towards the relic.
The moment the signal flare exploded in the sky, a second-tier earth mage had already cast a widespread "Quicksand Technique," covering the essential route to the relic.
When Su Lun stepped forward, the solid ground beneath his feet had already turned into soft mud.
In another breath or two, this mud would turn into quicksand.
By then, even the Eight-Armed Spider Spear would be deeply submerged in the sand.
This was clearly another tactic aimed at his escape.
Unfortunately...
Those guys underestimated Su Lun's current speed.
His agility was enough to let him accurately step on the hard broken stones, and he dashed out of the hundred-meter-wide quicksand pit before the ground fully transformed into sand.
The enemies worked in pairs, coordinating and covering each other.
Directly in front of Su Lun, besides that earth mage, there was also a female sorceress enveloped in roaring flames.
Second-tier professionals, none of them unknown.
The earth mage was Horace, the leader of Olli's family's large Scavenger group, known as "Sand Demon".
The female sorceress was none other than Virginia Eddie, the former spell instructor at the Black Tower Academy, now specially employed by the Olli family at a high salary, known as "Flame Maiden".
A master of fire spells, hot as the sun.
They were not surprised to see Su Lun burst out, and their deadly moves followed one after another.
Virginia's eyes were like torches, she pinched a sorcerer's seal in her hand, the six-pointed star beneath her feet shone brightly, her body turned from red to golden flames, and she softly chanted, "Elemental Mystery - Golden Scaled Fire Python!"
With a formation of the sorcerer's seals, she pointed forward with both hands, and a golden fire python shot out from her fingertips like lightning.
It was only as thick as a forearm when it appeared, but it rapidly grew in the wind, turning into a menacing giant python about ten meters long and as thick as a barrel. The fire python, covered in golden scales that shone brightly as if made not of elemental body but of pure gold, seemed unstoppable.
The ground turned scorched wherever the fire python passed.
Even though Su Lun was a hundred meters away from the fire python, he could still feel the burning heat searing his organs.
The overwhelming power of the fire element surged like a tsunami, seeming to burn everything in its path.
As expected from a former spell instructor of the Black Tower Academy, her move was an impeccable second-tier mystery spell.
This spell, with its fast speed and wide range, would force any second-tier professional to dodge its edge.
Moreover, the flames she condensed were not ordinary flames.
Virginia had integrated a special alchemical device that allowed her elemental nature to mutate — the "Elemental Core of the Golden Flame Raven".
It was this mutated golden flame that possessed extraordinary elemental penetration, capable of rapidly melting steel with its high temperature!
...
Area-effect spells also had a very tricky aspect.
They were almost impossible to block with physical means.
Even if one could block some of it with a shield, the omnipresent fire element could still burn the target from all angles!
Su Lun looked at the approaching fire python, with the firelight reflected in his eyes.
Far from dodging, he raised his hand and pulled out an alchemical golem.
The alchemical golem stood in front of him, and at the click of a mechanism, its arms suddenly split open into a trumpet shape.
Just as the fire python was a few meters away, a blue-purple compound seven-pointed star formation on the golem's arms suddenly lit up.
The power of wind and thunder mixed, creating a massive vortex of wind in an instant, turning into a black hole that devoured everything.
The ten-meter-long golden python had just charged forward, not even having time to show its ferocity, when it plunged headfirst into the vortex. The collision was extremely fast, and the golden light flashed by, suddenly dimming the surrounding light.
This was the latest version of the "Black Hole Puppet" made with the help of Mr. Hei!
....
Watching her spell, which she thought was certain to hit, being swallowed by a puppet, Virginia's face changed dramatically.
Seeing Su Lun charging over, she immediately sensed the crisis. Her body's flames surged and spilled out several meters, enveloping her completely in a thick layer of fire shield light.
Almost at the same time as the absorption, the alchemical golem that had absorbed the fire python suddenly opened its mouth and spat out a jet of golden flame.
Upon closer inspection, it was a downsized flame giant python!
However, this giant python was not aimed at the female sorceress but at the earth mage "Sand Demon" Horace!
At such a close distance, there was no possibility of evasion.
Horace had already sensed the crisis; by the time he saw the fire python, the alchemy was already complete. The color of his skin instantly lost its blood color, turning into a rock-like earthy yellow.
As the fire python surged over, the figure was completely engulfed in the sea of fire...
However, once the flames extinguished in an instant, what appeared was someone clad in what seemed like diamond armor, slowly opening his eyes.
This move had absolutely no effect on that "Sand Demon" Horus.
Su Lun looked with a calm gaze and muttered in his heart, "Silver Cultivation Armor[Scorpio Armor], its defensive power is indeed very strong…"
He was not surprised at all.
Because before coming here, he had already acquired detailed information about these ten people.
Their cultivation armor, abilities they excel in, their talents…
He knew them all very clearly!
Su Lun's speed did not decrease, he covered the hundred meters distance in the blink of an eye.
He did not give the enemy a chance to cast another spell, with a raise of his hand, several puppets had already flown towards the two people in front of him.
The female sorceress had a fire-based protective shield, normally any puppet approaching would be burnt to ashes, but... Su Lun had a [PZ-911 mechanical limb]in his hand!
Previously hard to control, now it posed no problem at all.
The dagger made of [Armand Metal] on the mechanical limb was specialized in breaking all kinds of elemental shields!
The mechanical puppet, unafraid of the flames, pounced forward.
It did not use any special technique, just like a scoundrel fighting in the streets, holding a dagger and stabbing her abdomen dozens of times...
Among the flames, two figures entangled awkwardly.
For a physically weak fire mage to be approached so closely, one could imagine.
Virginia Eddie's professional advancement was towards elemental mutation; she almost gave up on defense to maximize damage output.
Originally, in combination with the "Sand Demon" Horus's strong defense, it was no problem at all to protect oneself, not to mention killing anyone.
But why would Su Lun give Horus a chance to rescue?
Su Lun had not just two hands, but eight spider spears that could move and jump, and control puppets too!
While Virginia and the mechanical puppet engaged in close combat, several other puppets had already firmly clasped Horus's legs.
This earth mage had already concentrated thick earth elements under his feet for battle.
Now that those puppets had attached themselves to him, they immediately started sucking the earth elements voraciously, instantly becoming as heavy as a thousand pounds.
This was clearly the [Lead-sink Doll]!
With these thousand-pound dolls clinging to him, Horus was dragged down, unable to move, unable to escape.
Su Lun naturally did not expect that the two control-type dolls could injure this fellow protected by rock armor.
He raised his hand and drew [Thunder Snake], the moment he lifted the muzzle, he had already fired four shots.
"Boom!"
"Boom!"
"Boom!"
"Boom!"
Four beams of lightning surged out of the barrel, forming a straight line.
Horus, unable to teleport and having already prepared his defense, was very confident that even peers of the same rank could not break his elemental armor in a short time.
What more a firegun?
But hearing these almost continuous four shots, the disdain in his eyes hadn't even surfaced when he already sensed something terrible.
Firearms mystery, multi-layered firing?
But how could there be four bursts of firelight?!
In an instant, Horus's face drastically changed, disbelief evident in his eyes.
He had heard of this firearms mystery, a famous gun skill of the firearms master "Blind Detective" Bill, easily breaking armor.
However, this mystery placed an extreme burden on the shooter's body, and even that firearms master could only perform it three times.
That was already considered the pinnacle level of gunmanship.
Yet he thought, even if it was a triple firing, maybe it could shatter his elemental armor but would not be fatal...
But what about this "four-layered firing"!
....
Reality did not give Horus time to ponder, as four armor-piercing bullets successively hit right between his eyebrows.
The first bullet shattered a thin layer of skin, but the condensed earth element rippled slightly like water.
The second impact caused minute cracks in the elemental armor, and the ripples grew more intense.
The third strike broke through the elemental armor, but after penetrating the armor, the force was exhausted.
The fourth, the bullet directly shot through the brain, bursting it in one strike.
Blood exploded before his eyes, "grey mist" immediately emerged from the body.
The "Sand Demon" Horus was killed instantly.
Nearby, Virginia Eddie, who had been fighting the mechanical puppet in close quarters and stabbed dozens of times, saw her fire elemental shield flicker and vanish as her life dissipated.
In one encounter, Su Lun had already killed two second-tier professionals.

chapters.title: Chapter 174 - 174: 173
chapters.content:
Su Lun knew exactly what had surprised the "Sand Demon" Horace.
"Sequential Firing" was far from being as simple as pulling the trigger four times in a row. This gun art required not only high skill and proficiency with firearms but also extraordinary muscular reflex speed, strength, and resilience.
Though Su Lun's firearm skills might not have measured up to the "Blind Detective" Bill from before, when it came to physical strength, not a single gunman in Old Lington could reach his current level.
He lacked neither skill nor proficiency with guns, and his body was strong enough.
That's why he could barely manage to fire four shots.
Even so, after executing the "Quadruple Sequential Firing," Su Lun felt a sharp, burning pain in his forearm, as if a few muscle fibers had snapped.
It was worth it to take down this tough-skinned brute in a flash.
And it wasn't a big problem, for his highly active cells were rapidly healing those minor injuries.
...
One engagement killed two second-order professionals, and "gray fog" immediately appeared on both corpses.
Su Lun casually absorbed it.
'Acquired 3 memory shards of "Horace Walker"'
'You have gained a small amount of "Potion Knowledge"'
'You have mastered a large amount of "Wilderness Hunting and Combat Experience"'
'You have mastered a large amount of "Earth-based Alchemy Technique Fragments," increasing your Alchemy casting experience by +25'
'Spiritual power +0.8'
The memory strength of a professional Hunter Group leader yielded a plentiful harvest of hunting knowledge, which was not bad.
And that female sorceress gave Su Lun a little surprise.
Back when he stripped the two assistants from the Black Tower Academy, it felt as if Su Lun could soar on the spot. Now, after stripping a formal teacher, a vast amount of solid theory and practical combat memory shards flooded his mind, filling many gaps in his "skill tree."
'Acquired 5 memory shards of "Virginia Eddie"'
'You have received a piece of information: "Young Master Danze is really unrestrained, touching and feeling up in front of so many people... He seems to have a special fondness for mature women..."'
'You have gained a large amount of "Comprehensive Alchemy Knowledge"'
'You have acquired some "Intermediate Enchantment Knowledge"'
'You have proficiently mastered "Second-order Rune Drawing Skills"'
'You have mastered a large amount of "Fire Element Technique Fragments"'
'You have mastered the Fire System Technique [Fire Vine Entanglement Technique], increasing your Alchemy casting experience by +41'
'Spiritual power +0.9'
That felt good.
Mages usually possess higher spiritual power and stronger souls, resulting in more complete fragments when stripped.
Having digested those memory shards, Su Lun suddenly felt his pores relaxing and his face beamed, "The magic instructors of Black Tower Academy... Indeed, their memory shards are of extremely high quality!"
Previously, he had been intensively studying Alchemy theory.
Runes, spells, every branch of Alchemy required a considerable amount of time to learn.
Now that he had advanced to the second order, he needed to grasp second-order knowledge, and the difficulty had increased a notch.
Su Lun always felt his time was insufficient.
Because he could always control his focus, his learning efficiency was already not low. But to master mid-to-high-level rune knowledge without spending ten to eight years was out of the question.
However, no matter how hard he studied, could anything be faster than stripping finished soul shards?
If he didn't count the repetitive knowledge, the knowledge stripped from the body of "Virginia Eddie" could save Su Lun years of study.
From this perspective, having many enemies didn't seem to be entirely a bad thing.
....
Su Lun instantly took down an enemy in one encounter, tearing a hole in the encirclement.
He didn't stick around, and after absorbing the gray fog, he took off with two bodies in tow.
As to why he took the bodies...
Of course, he planned to harvest the storage ring and wait for the occupational equipment and inauguration materials to converge.
The possessions of a second-order professional are all valuable goods.
Moreover...
He felt that if he didn't give those behind the illusion of "we can catch up," they wouldn't chase so desperately.
....
For anyone, the combination of the "Quicksand Technique" and "Golden Scale Fire Python" tactics would either be lethal or peel off a layer of skin.
But now, not only had Su Lun handled it perfectly, but he had also managed a successful counter-kill.
Seeing the situation unfold, the experts sent by the Oliver family all turned pale.
How could they not have arrived first? Two old, battle-hardened second-order professionals couldn't even hold back the enemy for a moment and were killed instantly?!
Wasn't it said that the kid, aside from that sealed item, the black scythe, had no means dangerous to a second-order professional?!
But what about that puppet capable of absorbing second-order arcane spells?
They knew that the SS-ranked criminal was an expert in firearms, but what was this "Quadruple Burst" all about?
A master of firearms couldn't achieve this arcane shooting technique, and yet this firearms expert used it to take down a defensively skilled 'Sand Demon' Horace. Who would believe that?
Only then did everyone realize that the intelligence they had received was quite different from the actual situation.
Of course, they knew from the start that there was a catch.
A criminal showing up in the city on his own, exposing his identity by selling so much stuff, and specifically asking for the "Puppet Theater" was clearly a provocation to the Oliver family.
But even knowing it was bait, they had to bite.
The Young Master Danze of the Oliver family was now fuming with rage and would not rest until he killed "Su Lun," who had stolen his opportunity.
Furthermore, even with the catch, they had brought ten second-order professionals; what could go wrong?
This team composition was already considered an "almost foolproof" pursuit force.
Otherwise, to hunt down a first-order criminal, would they need to call out top professionals?
The faces of the eight remaining experts turned dark after seeing two of their peers of the same order killed before their eyes.
But they dared not stay, and continued to chase in the direction where Su Lun had fled.
Because the command had already come through their communicator.
"Keep chasing!"
If they took money from the Oliver family, they had to follow orders.
...
As Su Lun ran, signal flares and reveal powder burst in the sky all along his path.
"Reveal powder" was spread everywhere like rainfall.
The consumption of these special signal flares alone was no small sum.
Su Lun, of course, knew that the eight pursuers were relentless because in the ruins, there were several dozen teams disguised as wilderness hunting groups active nearby, waiting to capture him.
Because on his ear, he also had a communicator tuned to the same frequency obtained from Sabina.
He was clear about the enemy's movements and their capture plan!
The encircling pursuit teams needed more time to close in.
Su Lun would not foolishly wait for the enemy to completely surround him before taking action. After stripping the two corpses of their spoils, he discarded the bodies. Though his speed increased by a fraction, this was already intentional restraint; otherwise, if he were to control the Octo-Spider Lance and run at full speed now, no one in the ruins could catch up with him.
As he ran, he glanced back at the eight second-order experts behind him.
After consideration, he decided to kill a few more.
To reduce the threat for the upcoming battle.
....
The enemy's capture plan this time had almost taken everything into account.
The pursuers' professional synergy was perfect with close combat, magic, crowd control, tracking... they had it all.
But perhaps because he had just killed two, the remaining eight did not act rashly, keeping their distance.
Oh, to be precise, there were seven running, with one more flying above.
Su Lun looked up and glanced at the large bat.
This guy had a pair of bat wings as an augmentation, the famed Bounty Hunter "Dark Wing Assassin" Derek Wellman, who excelled in long-range sound wave attack techniques. Agile and not weak in close combat either. However, his defense was his shortcoming.
He probably thought that Su Lun couldn't do anything to him, continuously flying in the sky while launching sound wave attacks. They were like area bombardments, exploding all around Su Lun and creating holes everywhere.
If it weren't for Su Lun's own high agility, just these "sound wave cannons" would have been enough to give him a hard time.
But the opponent came prepared, and Su Lun wasn't without his own preparations.
He had long analyzed the information of his pursuers, knowing who among them was the easiest to kill.
This Derek Wellman was one of the priority targets to eliminate.
It might have looked like Su Lun was fleeing in a pitiful state, but in reality, everything was still within his expectations.
Just then, seeing that the time was ripe, Su Lun suddenly took out a bunch of mechanical spiders from his storage ring and scattered them on the ground.
The mechanical spiders landed and scurried around noisily, spreading out in a fan shape.
In these complex ruins, they were not constrained at all; they climbed walls and vaulted over rocks rapidly.
The pursuers behind didn't know what Su Lun was up to, but seeing his "unusual" actions, no one dared to probe rashly. As they watched the mechanical spiders rush towards them, they each brought out their defensive measures, their movements uniformly pausing.
"Boom~"
"Boom~"
"Boom~"
"..."
A series of explosions rang out, as dozens of mechanical spiders blew up thunderously.
The thick smoke quickly obscured a large area of visibility.
Those people thought Su Lun was trying to disrupt visibility to escape. There were urgent shouts through the communicators, "He's trying to flee, Wellman, go and catch him!"
The other seven were in the midst of the smoke, only Derek in the sky had unobstructed vision, so the task of pursuit naturally fell to him.
"Roger!"
Before his words ended,
A large bat emerged from the dense fog.
At this moment, he was completely unaware that Su Lun, taking advantage of the explosion earlier, had already activated his secondary implant.
When infused with dark spiritual power, the [Wailing Witch's Hair] becomes completely transparent.
If anyone could sense the energy fluctuations, they would definitely "see" Su Lun at this moment like a jellyfish, with transparent tendrils floating all around him. These tendrils kept extending towards the sky, increasing in number...
Bat wings could fly,
but their unique structure endowed Wellman with enough agility to easily dodge bullets.
But he couldn't fly very high.
The guy was pursuing Su Lun and felt an odd sensation around his body, subtly unsettling.
Having an alarm was one thing, but it didn't mean he could just stop the chase, did he?
Neither sound waves nor vision revealed any anomalies, so he didn't take it to heart.
But as he flew, Wellman suddenly saw the "Su Lun" hanging below make a grasping motion with all his fingers in the air.
A sudden sense of crisis overwhelmingly gripped his heart.
Wellman was on guard for Su Lun to control the few puppets nearby to attack, when suddenly he felt something terribly wrong, his expression drastically changed.
That's when he realized countless silver hairs had instantly formed around his body.
He immediately recognized what it was, crying out in his mind, "The [Thousands of Threads] augmentation... Damn it! Weren't they saying this kid was just a Tier 1 professional? This is clearly a Tier 2!"
Su Lun on the ground sharply narrowed his eyes, not giving him any chance to fly away.
His fingers danced skillfully, and working with a few spider spears, he suddenly clenched fiercely, uttering softly, "Secret Technique: Caged Bird!"
And then, the silver threads in his hands abruptly tensed!
....
Puppet Masters could not only use puppets to fight, but their threads were a formidable weapon as well. Especially a Puppet Master who had merged with the "Thousand Threads" enhancement, capable of controlling countless threads!
This "Caged Bird" control secret technique was exactly the one previously found in the storage ring of the "Trickster," Lloyd.
Utilizing a tremendous amount of threads to control the target.
Originally, this was a trick that could only be performed in his "Puppet Theater," but now Su Lun had the witch's hair that could become elemental. When casting this spell, it was a form of invisible killing!
Wellman's body was completely surrounded by silver hair strands, leaving him with no place to escape.
Even if his bat wings were agile and he wanted to fly away, it was futile!
Because at this moment, the threads around him had already tightened like a cocoon, trapping him tightly.
His bat wings were restricted and could not take flight, and his throat was slit by countless strands, trying to use sound waves, but not a single sound could come out of his throat.
No matter how exquisite your martial skills, no matter how agile your movements, once trapped, you wouldn't be able to move.
What if you could snap a hundred strands?
There were still a thousand, ten thousand more!
Su Lun's "Thousand Threads" alchemy enhancement's main material was the "infinite hair strands"!
The witch's hair also possessed strong "regenerative properties," and even if broken, it could rejoin!
It was at the moment when the threads had the enemy under control that Su Lun on the ground erupted with cold flames, yanked the threads with tremendous force, and his body shot up. At the same time, several sharp spider spears revealed their poisonous tips, stabbing forward.
One descending, one launching upward, the two figures were like magnets attracting each other, and with a "whoosh," they collided.
After advancing to the second tier, the level of the laws raised by a tier, and Su Lun's current "No Servant" cold flame could penetrate an assassin of the second-tier profession, as easy as flipping one's hand!
At this collision, several sharp spider spears easily pierced through Wellman, who was trapped like a mummy.
"Hiss!"
"Hiss!"
"Hiss!"
"Hiss!"
Four sounds of piercing through brocade and silk rang out.
Throat, heart, both sides of the waist, four spider spears crossed through, and blood spurted out like arrows.
A moment later, a gray mist emerged.
"You have obtained 'Derek Wellman's Soul Shards*2'"
"You have learned 'Introductory Toxic Potion Making'"
"You have acquired some knowledge of 'Sound Wave Attack Techniques'"
"You have grasped a small amount of 'Elementary to Intermediate Rune Knowledge', alchemy casting experience +11"
"Spiritual power +0.4"
Su Lun did not bother to digest those memory fragments too much. After landing, he gathered the threads and continued to run forward, pulling a "mummy" behind him.
....
Not far away, those seven second-tier professionals had just rushed out of the smoke area and happened to witness the spectacle of the spider spears piercing through the body.
The seven of them were thoroughly astounded.
They had thought the explosion of the spider bombs and the rising smoke was some lethal tactic, but it turned out to be ordinary smoke.
However, it was precisely because of their cautiousness that they delayed for a few breaths' time.
When their vision was restored, they saw another comrade had been killed...
How did that guy do it?
Wasn't Wellman supposed to be able to fly? How was he caught and killed?
They didn't see the dense, invisible threads in the sky, only a "mummy" trophy hanging behind "Su Lun," as if it was a silent mockery...
"Keep chasing, be careful not to get separated, that guy has very tricky methods!"
"Damn it, the intel is wrong, Su Lun must have advanced to the second tier! The Black Scythe hasn't shown up yet, and it's very likely that he is going for it. Everyone, be cautious."
"Have the troops set up to encircle him arrived? Good... We can't let him escape, drive him that way. Janet, we'll cover you, get ready to cast your spell..."

chapters.title: Chapter 175 - 174: Puppetry Technique - Hundred Guile Nightwalk
chapters.content:
Su Lun listened to the tactics being set up through the communicator, his expression revealing a trace of amusement.
Janet?
That name naturally belonged to Janet Williams, the "Dream Thief" in the team.
A professional in the mystical arts who excelled in spiritual illusions, her abilities bore some similarity to those of the Wailing Witch, capable of hypnotizing and killing in dreams.
She was also one of the elders of the "Mystical Studies Association" in Old Lington.
...
When Su Lun heard that name through the communicator, he knew what those behind him were planning to do.
He turned his head and saw that two guards had positioned themselves beside a female sorceress in a purple robe.
Because the Dream-Making Technique required complete focus and she couldn't afford to be distracted by attacks, this move was probably out of fear that Su Lun might suddenly pull out his black scythe so her comrades could save her in time.
Su Lun distanced himself a bit.
But he knew he couldn't avoid the Formation; distancing himself was just to prevent anyone from catching up to him when he was killing in the dream.
Second-tier professionals always had some bizarre, ability-cursed items in their possession.
Especially the experts fostered by massive conglomerates like the Oliver family, who were never short of valuable resources.
From his intelligence, Su Lun knew that the "Dream Thief" Janet held a cursed item that was highly compatible with her abilities—the "Angus's Dream Refraction Mirror."
An item that could utilize reflections to cast spiritual techniques from a distance.
Just as that female sorceress took out the mirror, Su Lun threw a bunch of mechanical spiders onto the ground.
This time, unlike the previous smoke spiders, these carried some special markings.
Having only made this small move, he then saw a projection of an ancient mirror forming nearby.
....
Caught, without any signs.
The surrounding scenes remained unchanged; he was still in the ruins.
Anyone else might not even realize they had fallen under an illusion.
Su Lun looked down at his finger movements, a sneer forming in his eyes: "Entered the dream, huh..."
The methods of mystical sorcerers were unpredictable, especially that mirror capable of casting spiritual techniques from afar, making it nearly impossible to avoid. For anyone else, just Janet alone would be a severe disadvantage.
Su Lun didn't show any signs of abnormality and continued running in the dream.
At that moment,
the sorceress in the robe caught up with him.
Although not adept at chases, this spiritual sorceress suddenly seemed to teleport, catching up in a flash.
Because this was her dream, she could have everything.
Since Su Lun knew this was a dream crafted by the enemy,
he didn't attempt to fight this woman.
Janet was the creator of this dream, the master of this realm; here, she was invincible.
Normally, the script would have Su Lun unaware that he had entered the dream, then he would start to retaliate.
But he would quickly realize in horror that gunfire didn't kill, spears didn't pierce... none of his methods worked.
While the opponent could slowly torment him to death.
This was very buggy; in the opponent's dream, you simply couldn't kill her,
but she could easily kill you.
Even though there was a time difference in the dream, Su Lun didn't plan to waste time with this "Dream Thief" Janet.
If physical means couldn't harm her, then he would use mental tactics.
The "Dream-Making Space" Technique was almost a guaranteed hit.
But this did not mean the technique had no weaknesses.
Normally speaking, in any spell, "range" and "spell strength" could only focus on one aspect.
To maintain such a wide-ranging dream technique, it was impossible to use any powerful single-target mental attack techniques.
You're skilled in spiritual techniques?
Funny, so am I.
Although Su Lun wasn't even a beginner in basic mental theory, he had bizarrely mastered several high-level sorcerer techniques, like the "Drowning Technique" and "Suffocation Technique."
These were skills he had collected from "Hotel 1911," with proficiency even reaching the "master level" for second-tier techniques.
Combined with his inherently strong spiritual power, although not efficiently utilized, he had quantity on his side.
Using quantity to overpower was also effective.
Just as Janet caught up, their eyes met.
Both sides directly engaged in a "visual illusion" confrontation.
The outcome was immediately clear.
"Ah..."
Janet screamed in agony.
Clearly, she was the losing party.
Although Su Lun also felt a bit dizzy, he thankfully did not suffer.
...
Just as the two clashed momentarily, the special explosion of the spider bomb reached Su Lun's ears.
Looking again, the dream had already been shattered.
Not far away, Janet seemed to have been hit hard, her figure suddenly plunging.
Boom...
They were intent on pursuing Su Lun, and those behind him had to follow his route.
This time's spider bomb was not any alchemic fog, but a high-explosive bomb.
Although he had no hope of killing these second-tier professionals, it was enough to make them feel threatened.
Dozens of spiders exploded simultaneously, and a wall of fire, tens of meters high, formed in the distance, blocking the view of both sides.
Su Lun pulled from his hat and an invisible puppet immediately appeared beside him.
He didn't hesitate to grab and manipulate the puppet to slash through the blasting flames three times in a row.
Although the flames blocked the enemy's view for a moment, they also blocked his own...
This slash,
was a gamble,
but not entirely a gamble.
Normally, if there's a bomb on the left, where would a normal person instinctively dodge to?
Naturally, to the right!
Su Lun clearly knew the position of the spider bombs and had precisely calculated the blast range.
The blast came first, followed by the slash, not giving the enemy any time to react.
He predicted where the enemy would appear after dodging the explosion, and these three slashes sealed off a large area behind the flames.
Anyone appearing in that space was bound to be hit.
Su Lun felt that he would at least hit one person with this slash.
After all, near his aimed direction was Janet, who had lost her ability to move due to spiritual shock!
Someone noticed Su Lun's movements, and a voice shouted through the communicator, "Be careful of the black scythe!"
Unfortunately, it was already too late.
By the time the words fell, three spatial rifts had precisely appeared behind the fire.
Although one of the three spatial rift slashes missed, two hit their marks.
One slash struck the unconscious Janet, and the other hit a close-combat professional trying to rescue her. A thigh was severed from the body, spraying blood like a fountain.
Although he didn't see a "gray mist" appear and the person didn't die instantly,
these three slashes directly removed two second-tier professionals from the chase.
...
Su Lun looked back, refraining from making another slash.
The two were gravely injured and posed no threat, making it unnecessary to waste another chance from the living corpse.
The Abomination had appeared, and since several slashes had been made, there was no need to retract them because it had already been marked with reagent powder, and its large silhouette was outlined with the silver powder, making further hiding pointless.
Seeing the Abomination appear, the remaining five were not shocked but instead breathed a sigh of relief.
"How did Su Lun not get affected by the illusion?!"
"Damn it, he must have some kind of curse object that wards off spiritual attacks! Forget the wounded for now, keep chasing. That guy's black scythe has been seen, he's out of tricks..."
"Now that his puppet has become visible, everyone be careful. Avoid the slashes and his flame gun, and he poses no threat!"
"Prepare to implement Plan C! Hold them off on your side, support is on its way..."
"..."
Su Lun, listening to the messages in the communicator, smirked subtly.
Having been pursued for such a substantial part of the day, those reinforcements were finally encircling.
Well... he couldn't blame them, only the vastness of the relic was at fault.
Excluding the 'Gun King' Gage, out of ten second-tier pursuers, three were dead, two severely injured, leaving five.
But the 'Trickster' he expected, Lloyd, had yet to show himself.
Su Lun was well aware that the guy was busy directing the relic's forces to surround them.
Now with the black scythe by his side, the remaining few dared not come close.
But what they didn't anticipate was that even with the addition of this towering invisible puppet, Su Lun's speed was not reduced in the slightest.
And then, as they chased, they were surprised to find that Su Lun had led them in a big circle and returned to where they had started.
The Oliver family immediately realized something.
"Not good! That guy is still planning to go back and kill Janet and the others!"
"To hell with him! If he kept running, we might still not catch him, but now he's courting death. Notify those in the siege to converge on us! Prepare for spatial blockade!"
"..."
That's right.
Su Lun had circled back.
He was still eyeing those two severely injured second-tier professionals.
One with a severed leg and the other unconscious, they were practically giveaways.
It would be a pity to let them go.
After all, it's the same fight, wherever it happens.
...
As Su Lun ran past, he saw the guy with the severed leg treating his own wound.
The man was unfamiliar, a professional bodyguard from the Oliver family, apparently named Johnson.
Even as a second-tier professional, injuries like having a leg chopped off could make one bleed out so quickly that they would immediately weaken. Especially during intense activity, when the blood pressure is extremely high.
Now...
The man looked at Su Lun who had returned and his eyes were filled with horror.
Though he had heard the news ten seconds earlier, with his leg severed, he simply couldn't run away.
Su Lun ran over and with a shot, knocked out the fainting 'Dream Thief' Janet Williams, harvesting a wave of Soul Shards.
A second-tier close combat professional is useless without legs?
No,
there were still options.
Johnson had intended to feign weakness and launch a surprise attack, but it turned out that Su Lun's combat skills were not weak at all.
Although Su Lun rarely engaged in hand-to-hand combat in ordinary days, he had stripped so many people of their combat memories that his Combat Technique had reached the level of a "combat expert."
Moreover, with his body modified by "X Serum," if it really came down to hand-to-hand combat, Johnson wouldn't necessarily have the upper hand.
Furthermore, Su Lun's enhanced auditory and visual perception abilities made it impossible for a severely injured person with a broken leg to ambush him!
When the ambush failed, the skirmish didn't last long before Su Lun speared those few people to death.
However, due to the delay, those five pursuers had caught up.
....
Seeing the pursuers arriving, Su Lun was not in a rush to leave.
Because by then, it was too late to escape.
The enemy's encirclement was closing in.
He calmly stripped the Soul Shards and cleared two bodies of their Storage Rings, then finally looked off into the distance.
A squad of about a hundred well-equipped people appeared opposite.
But their numbers weren't important.
What was important was that when they appeared, dense purple light surged around the streets near the ruins like beams of light from a projector, suddenly turning into several huge purple screens.
While Su Lun was collecting the spoils of war, a gigantic Hexagram Array lit up in the sky.
A few purple screens joined together to quickly form a massive purple "box" hundreds of meters wide and a hundred meters tall.
This box enclosed a large area around it.
Su Lun saw that he was trapped and was not surprised at all. He looked at the purple screens and thought to himself, "A large-scale spatial blocking barrier... they really are loaded."
Now that he had mastered Spatial Ability, he could clearly feel the strength of this barrier.
It was powerful.
So powerful that even a third-tier powerhouse might not be able to break it.
Moreover, he had just heard the enemy's battle plan; this spatial barrier could only be opened from the outside. Olli's family's commander had given strict orders that the barrier would not be opened until Young Master Danze arrived with the main force.
That meant, ultimately, only one side within the space could survive.
Of course, this was exactly to Su Lun's liking.
Everyone was trapped, leaving no choice but to clash head-on.
Oh, no!
The enemy couldn't escape, but it didn't affect him at all.
This kind of spatial barrier was like a glass cover; it didn't reinforce the space itself.
If Su Lun wanted to leave, he could simply open a spatial door.
However, having chosen to stay, he had no intention of leaving.
It would be a shame not to exploit the situation when all the fish were in the barrel.
...
As Su Lun became a turtle in a jar, the members of the Olli family didn't rush to take action and slowly closed in.
Of course, the most important thing was the fear of Su Lun's desperate struggle.
After all, with the Black Scythe in hand, if he really started hacking wildly in desperation, no one would take it lightly.
A siege that initially seemed a sure shot was unexpectedly devastating.
Ten second-tier experts participated in the hunt, and now only five were alive.
The surviving members each had a grim expression on their faces.
At that moment, not far away, a gloomy-faced dwarf also appeared — naturally, it was the 'Trickster' Lloyd, a grandmaster in the Puppetry Technique field.
If anyone hated Su Lun more than Young Master Danze, who had his opportunity stolen, it was him.
A highly respected master who turned out to be an ugly dwarf, shattering the masterly aura he had built, was more distressing to him than death.
Sabrina had mentioned to Su Lun that ever since his alchemic puppet was cut down, this guy had not shown up in public, probably too ashamed to face people.
Even during the fleeting moment he appeared, the sorcerer's seals in his hands had already condensed.
Once the embedding released, black threads started emerging from his body...
In the sky, the Hexagram Array gradually brightened, and an enormous cross phantom starkly condensed.
Su Lun had seen this routine before and was familiar with it.
He also knew that limiting the space with the barrier, aside from preventing his escape, was to maximize Lloyd's abilities.
Just like the time they killed the 'Wailing Witch' within a certain spatial range, Lloyd's "Mystic Art: Puppet Theater" was nearly unsolvable.
Su Lun squinted at the cross in the sky and muttered to himself, "I'm really coveting this art..."
Today's elaborate setup was primarily aimed at this guy.
....
It seemed that he felt assured of his victory, so Lloyd wasn't in a hurry to act and began his persuasive taunt," Kid, give up your resistance, and perhaps I might spare your life!"
"Oh?"
Su Lun heard this and smirked.
The words did not sound false.
If possible, they indeed wanted to capture him alive.
After all, he had too many secrets, and that Young Master Danze was very curious.
Like how he could use the black scythe without any side effects...
If he were to die, that might remain an eternally unsolved mystery.
Being stared at venomously by over a hundred people, that "malice" converged into a sharp spear, piercing Su Lun's head with pain.
The enemy numbered over a hundred, and he dared not underestimate them one bit.
Just from a glance, he saw three to four decades of certified professionals among them, not including those wearing their uniforms.
Even the non-professionals were equipped with precision gear, standard issue firearms, personal cannons, mechanical arms, tactical bulletproof vests...
Clearly, these were the elite forces of the Oliver family.
Leaving aside the magical sorcerers, just a hundred people firing their guns and cannons in unison would bring Su Lun to his knees on the spot.
Why call so many people, you ask?
Obviously, to die as shields.
The black scythe only has one blade; it can only slash once at a time. Despite the curse backlash, it wasn't possible to use the black scythe to kill over a hundred people, right?
Besides, in the interval between his attacks, the combined assault of these hundred people was enough to turn him into a sieve.
Lloyd, seeing that Su Lun had no intention of surrendering his weapons, coldly said again, "Kid, I'm giving you one last chance, surrender in three breaths, or else it's no mercy!"
His words seemed to be persuading surrender, but his heart did not relax its vigilance at all.
Because the SS wanted criminal before him was too calm.
Any professional who could progress to the second level was not foolish.
From the very beginning, they had suspected a trap.
Just now, Su Lun clearly had a chance to escape, but he returned for the spoils from two corpses, and then got cornered?
While Lloyd thought this had something to do with their "foolproof" capture plan, he couldn't help feeling that something was off.
It was like they had set a net,
and there was a bigger net...
....
With more than a hundred eyes on him, even if Su Lun could fly, his wings would be shot off on the spot!
Trapped in the corner of the barrier, he seemed to have no way to escape.
But the next moment, Su Lun smiled, tilted his head, and nonchalantly replied, "Then let it be no mercy then..."
As he spoke, his hands started forming symbols.
The Spatial Teleportation technique was more than familiar to him; it was perfect with a snap.
Seeing this sudden movement, Lloyd's expression changed drastically and he yelled without hesitation, "Attack!"
As soon as he spoke, the sound of triggers being pulled together resounded.
But it was too late.
Su Lun's foot had already stepped into the dark gate of space, and his figure vanished in the blink of an eye.
The gunfire flared for a moment, then faded.
"Spatial Teleportation?"
Finally, everyone knew where Su Lun's composed confidence came from.
Everyone's expression was as uncomfortable as if they had swallowed flies.
All this commotion,
and the result... they were played?
Lloyd, especially, turned black with rage, "How can he do Spatial Teleportation..."
Two months ago, he had personally experienced that this "SS wanted criminal Su Lun" was just a stage one professional relying on the black scythe with a bit of cunning.
How could he now...
Just when the Oliver family thought Su Lun had definitely escaped.
Suddenly, someone noticed a person appearing on top of the dilapidated building behind them.
"Look, he's there!"
"Be careful!"
".."
Upon closer inspection, if it wasn't Su Lun, who else could it be?
....
"Tsk tsk, you really have a lot of people..."
Su Lun smirked at the crowd, "But fortunately, I have quite a few people on my side as well."
As he spoke, he was already pulling out three scrolls sealed with the Spatial Technique.
The scrolls unfurled in the wind, nearly a hundred eerie dolls appeared, facing the hundred-plus people of Oliver, their wooden joints crackling with a sound like mocking laughter.
Su Lun's eyes slightly narrowed, his fingers clawed at the void as he uttered lightly, "Try my original Puppetry Technique... 'Secret Technique·Hundred Guile Nightwalk'!"
PS. My sleep schedule has been erratic lately, updates will most likely be around 6 PM. In the future, I'll try to make it by 12 PM.

chapters.title: Chapter 176 - 175 Chaotic Killing
chapters.content:
The way to unfurl the spatial scroll allowed Su Lun to summon a large number of rune dolls in a short time. Before the enemies could turn their guns, he had already summoned a hundred dolls.
By the time the enemies noticed and turned around, he had already pulled the strings to activate the dolls' mechanisms.
The puppets stood in two rows, eighty "Oil-Swallowing Dolls" in front and twenty "Phosphorus Fire Dolls" behind.
It was the moment the strings were pulled that the jaws of the two types of dolls suddenly opened—one spewing black oil, the other emitting pale blue phosphorus fire.
Watching the astonished expressions of the Olli family, a fierce look flashed in Su Lun's eyes as he softly exclaimed, "Try my physical fire technique..."
Raw and brutal.
In an instant, twenty red-faced dolls spat out a jet of fire, the phosphorus fire met the oil, and instantly transformed into twenty rampaging fire dragons, shooting towards the crowd.
Twenty multiplied by eighty, and in a moment, there were eighty fire dragons.
The improved "Oil-Swallowing Dolls" had greatly enhanced ejection power; their black tubes were like high-pressure water guns, shooting black fire oil tens or even hundreds of meters away.
This range of shooting was, under normal circumstances, almost no threat to most professionals. All they had to do was to keep their distance to easily dodge it.
But in the space confined by the sealing enchantment, there was nowhere to hide!
And because the puppets were controllable, twisting their heads and spraying wildly.
Blue phosphorus fire does not extinguish with water, and grows with wind—the places where the fire dragons passed were all covered in flowing flames. Instantly, several blocks within the seal were engulfed in raging fires.
Apart from a few magicians who could control fire, almost no one could withstand this head-on.
This round of eighty fire dragons spraying simultaneously immediately scattered the enemy's formation.
More than a hundred people scattered, each beginning to shoot with their guns.
....
"Kill him!"
At that command, gunfire erupted loudly.
Su Lun was not at all afraid, as the hundred dolls in front of him almost blocked all possible angles of shooting. He controlled the rune dolls to fly chaotically everywhere, presenting a scene of demons dancing wildly.
These hunters, truly the elite of the Olli family, quickly found cover and began to counterattack after a moment of panic. These guys had sophisticated firearms and excellent shooting skills. Despite the agile and flying dolls, the numerous gunpoints aimed and fired popping sounds.
Although the dolls had strong runes and enchantments, their low-tier wooden material did not allow them to withstand too many bullet impacts, especially as some people in the crowd had man-portable cannons and mechanical claws attacking. Almost every hit caused a doll to burst.
"Bang!"
"Bang!"
"Bang!"
"..."
After a round of sweeping gunfire, the Black-faced "Oil-Swallowing Dolls" flying in the front kept bursting apart.
But the bursting was not just that simple.
It was as if compressed gas cylinders were exploding, the sky bursting open with balls of flames.
Phosphorus fire splattered everywhere.
Watching the exploding dolls, Su Lun didn't feel a bit of pity; instead, he revealed a smile that showed things were going just as he planned.
This was not the earlier type of small-capacity doll, but one that he had modified with Spatial Techniques—spatial dolls.
When these burst, the spaces sealed within the dolls also burst apart. Like exploding oil barrels, the black phosphorus oil burst, filling the sky everywhere.
Phosphorus fire splattered, sticking on surfaces, and unable to be extinguished. In a moment, painful wails of agony were heard everywhere.
"Ah...quick...help me take off my bulletproof vest!"
"Damn it, my mechanical arm is red-hot, someone help me out here, let's take off this mechanical skeleton!"
"..."
Whether it was textiles or mechanical parts, once tainted with phosphorus oil, all one could do was wait for the oil to burn out. Not everyone knew the art of fire control to handle these sticky burning oils; even a small touch meant burns.
And the threat was far from over.
The "Oil-Swallowing Dolls" might seem much less threatening after bursting and losing their directed spraying capability.
But the explosion was more direct than spraying from the jets, rapidly spreading the burning area and reaching a state where it was absolutely unstoppable.
Within this restricted space of several hundred meters, phosphor fires were everywhere.
Initially, the Oliver family hadn't noticed anything unusual, but seeing more and more broken puppets surrounded by inextinguishable phosphor fire, someone realized the problem and shouted, "Careful, these flames are toxic! Put on your gas masks!"
....
Poison gas?
No, it was not just that.
It was true that phosphor fire could produce deadly poison gas, but that was not the main reason Su Lun used so much oil.
In fact, Su Lun did not expect it to burn or poison anyone to death.
It was to create thick smoke to obstruct vision and rapidly consume the oxygen in this space!
The burning of oil also required a huge amount of oxygen.
Outdoors it might not be noticeable, but in a confined space, these dozens of barrels of oil could deplete the oxygen in the air in a very short time.
This was a tactic Su Lun had thought of when he heard from Sabina that the Oliver family planned to use "Spatial Lockdown" against him.
The confined space was not only suitable for "Puppet Theatre," but it was also an extremely advantageous home field for his "Phosphorus Dolls."
Although it was a world filled with alchemy, and ancient alchemists had already been able to separate oxygen from the air,
laboratory research and civilian use were two different things.
Most people had no concept of isolated oxygen.
Filtering gas masks could solve most toxin issues but not the lack of oxygen. (Ordinary gas masks, don't even mention sodium peroxide or anything of that sort).
Soon, people began to experience difficulty breathing.
"Ah, I think I've been poisoned!"
"Quick, help me..."
"..."
The cries of agony continued, but they grew fainter.
The sharply reduced oxygen content in the air made them greedily gasp for breath.
Then they found it harder and harder to breathe, which instinctively made them want to remove their gas masks to take a few breaths.
But then they realized they were inhaling more poison gas.
Their faces soon turned a blue-gray, and they fell to the ground, frothing at the mouth.
The Olli family's hundred or so elites collapsed in great numbers like cut wheat in an instant.
Even the professionals quickly showed signs of oxygen deprivation.
Some magic-wielding Magicians who realized the situation shouted, "Don't shoot, stop shooting those oil-spewing puppets! Cast to replace the air, or we all die here!"
....
The gunfire ceased abruptly.
Su Ting, listening to their exchanges, unhurriedly took out a compressed air tank and connected it to his mask.
Ordinary Scavengers might not understand the cause of their breathing difficulties and probably assumed it was poisoning. But this was, after all, the Olli family's elite group, mixed with inner city academy-trained alchemists.
It wasn't surprising that they could see through it.
Using the principle of equivalent exchange to swap the poison gas for fresh air was indeed the correct response...
But would Su Lun give them that chance?
If he saw anyone casting any wind-based Spatial Technique, he would raise his hand and gun them down.
Those he couldn't kill on the spot must be elite magic-wielding Magicians, who were busy replacing the air and naturally couldn't afford to deal with Su Lun.
This one move directly neutralized the enemy's numerical advantage, instantly rendering ninety percent useless.
Now that the opponents had stopped shooting, Su Lun wasn't planning on letting them off. He pulled a thread in his hand and shouted, "Explode!"
The remaining dozens of intact "Oil Swallowing Dolls" instantly burst apart, splattering oil everywhere.
Now, the fire became unstoppable.
Moreover, the burning phosphor produced a large amount of high-temperature black smoke!
Because the oxygen within the sealed space was becoming scarcer, the incomplete combustion of the phosphor oil produced increasingly dense clouds of floating particulate smoke. The high-temperature smoke disrupted all optical detection methods, rendering even the best night-vision devices useless.
This was a physical visual obstacle even more effective than a smoke bomb.
Unable to disperse, the high-temperature smoke stayed contained, with the purple light screen's sealing barrier acting like a glass cover enveloping these few streets.
Visibility was getting lower and lower,
One hundred meters...
Fifty meters...
Ten meters...
In the blink of an eye, the dark fog enveloped most of the spatial area, and in some local areas, one couldn't see their own hands.
Now that everyone was blind,
It was all about perception!
Su Lun had done this because among second-tier professionals, his perception abilities held an absolute advantage.
Not to mention the evolved powers of the All-knowing Eye, he could still see further than others in the smoke. Combined with his super-sensitive auditory perception and malicious intent detection abilities, he could easily pinpoint the enemy's location.
Now, the enemy's numerical advantage was completely gone.
With unclear targets, even good shooting skills and equipment were useless.
Having done all this, while the opponent's formation was in total chaos, Su Lun instantly snuffed out his own light source and stopped firing as well.
He ignored the flamethrowing dolls and used Spatial Teleportation again, appearing dozens of meters away in the midst of a crowd.
Due to the extremely low visibility, the professionals from the Oliver family hadn't noticed that an extra person had suddenly appeared in their group.
....
The commander of Oliver's team also had extensive combat experience. Upon realizing that their sight was obstructed by the black smoke, he immediately guessed Su Lun's intention.
"Be wary of an enemy sneak attack!"
"Group in threes, back to back!"
"Do not shoot recklessly!"
At his commands, the surviving professionals grouped in threes, backing each other for protection.
This formation indeed made it hard to sneak up on them.
However, Su Lun had no intention of attacking them himself.
With a flick of a scroll, another dozen creepy dolls appeared out of nowhere.
This time, they weren't flamethrowing dolls, but "Nightmare Dolls."
These were hybrids of the earlier "Wailing Dolls" and "Giggling Dolls." Su Lun, having mastered the technique of dual rune engraving, had crafted these new dolls. They were immensely troublesome as they could induce both auditory and visual hallucinations simultaneously.
"Clang~"
"Clang~"
"Clang~"
As soon as the dolls appeared, their limbs split open, revealing dark, poisoned, sharp daggers.
At the command of Su Lun's octopus spear, the dozen dolls simultaneously flew towards the crowd.
Although the mental wails of the "Nightmare Dolls" still had a limited range and needed to be within one or two meters of a professional to affect their psyche,
But... the terror was in their numbers!
Their combined laughing was overwhelming, like ten thousand nagging aunts next to one's ear, capable of causing immediate mental breakdown.
Moreover, the puppets had no fear of death, and not even swords or guns could make them back off.
After the witch's hair fully elementalized, her control was virtually untraceable.
The dozen puppets were like a dozen Su Luns.
Plunging into the crowd, their eerie laughter could instantly blur one's mind.
Then, in a moment of distraction, it was a frenzy of stabbing.
For a moment, the darkness was filled with ceaseless screams and the loud crack of gunfire.
Su Lun, like a ghost, mercilessly harvested the lives of those professionals who were still alive.
A chaotic slaughter!
In the brief time of these two encounters, Olli's force of over a hundred people hadn't even started to act violently before the poison gas killed most of them, and strange puppets stabbed the rest to death—almost all were wiped out in an instant.
What was originally a spatial barrier intended to trap Su Lun inside turned out to be a death knell for these pursuers.
.....
"Ah..."
The wails and screams were unending.
Olli's family members, being second-tier professionals, were not short of means to save themselves. Although they were temporarily safe, they had no ability to stop Su Lun from killing.
This smoke obscured everyone's vision.
Amid the confusion of over ten movements, they couldn't discern where the real "Su Lun" was.
To act rashly was to fear suddenly encountering a spatial rift from somewhere, which might decapitate them.
Moreover, by now everyone knew that Su Lun had become a second-tier professional, so no one dared to underestimate him.
Let's not talk about when he held the dark scythe in hand; even in direct confrontation, why should one assume weakness when each was a second-tier professional?
And at that moment, they realized a stark reality.
Had they come to hunt down this "SS wanted criminal Su Lun"?
No!
Looking at it now...
From the beginning to the end,
It was Su Lun who had been baiting them out.
Coming to terms with that realization, the few living second-tiers were all bathed in cold sweat.
The death of their five companions during the earlier pursuit was not coincidence, but all within Su Lun's calculated plans.
Although they did not understand why Su Lun harbored such a deep killing intent,
the fact was, if they didn't find a way, they might all be annihilated.
And now awkwardly, the spatial barrier they thought trapped Su Lun only confined them!
They had not anticipated that Su Lun had awakened a rare spatial ability.
And then, faint and cautious voices transmitted through the communicator.
"Damn it, we need to figure out Su Lun's location and eliminate him, otherwise we probably won't last until the barrier opens... Mr. Lloyd, what should we do now?"
Before they could get a response, someone suddenly spoke eerily through the communicator: "Hey... have you guys not noticed that our entire plan from start to finish has been in Su Lun's hands?"
"You mean..."
"..."
That statement was cut off halfway, and suddenly the communicator went silent.
Everyone understood then—their communication channel had been intercepted.
.....
Listening to the silence in the communicator, Su Lun also realized that they had discovered his interception, and he internally chuckled, "Only just realized it huh..."
But it didn't matter anymore.
The plan was going smoother than expected.
By now, those guys couldn't possibly turn the tables.
The only uncertainty for Su Lun now was whether he could eliminate the few second-tiers in the space before the enemy's main forces arrived.
Of course, since the enemies were all well-known seasoned second-tier professionals, they naturally wouldn't just surrender.
Su Lun glanced at the silk threads descending from above and narrowed his eyes slightly, "The puppet show begins, huh..."

chapters.title: Chapter 177 - 176: It Looks Like a Bumper Harvest Is Coming
chapters.content:
"Trickster" Lloyd could be known as "Puppet Master" for good reason.
In Puppetry Technique, possibly only one or two people in Old Lington could match him, but certainly, none were stronger than him.
Dark smoke enveloped the entire sealed space, and just when everyone was at their wits' end, black strings suddenly burst forth from the giant cross in the sky, spreading wildly.
Countless black strings touched anything they could coil around and immediately began to bind.
At that moment, someone shouted through the smoke, "Don't panic, this is Mr. Lloyd's puppetry trick, no one resist!"
The black strings, like tiny snakes, probed everywhere; they bound people upon contact and did the same to objects.
Even the corpses on the ground were manipulated like marionettes, as if they "came to life."
The black strings were innumerable, covering the entire space, making them unavoidable.
It was as if an invisible hand behind the curtain was controlling the giant cross in the sky, transforming the vast sealed space into an enormous puppet theater in an instant.
One by one, the marionettes were lifted and roamed about.
....
"The nearly unsolvable puppetry secret within this range is indeed well-deserved..."
Su Lun watched, his brows and eyes showing a slight concern.
His own puppets around him were also entwined with black strings.
He tried to control one of the tricky puppets, and it struggled momentarily, then immediately triggered a chain reaction; countless black strings rushed over and twisted the puppet into pieces. Moreover, because of the commotion, the nearby controlled "puppets" also surged over.
Seeing the black strings covering the whole space, Su Lun knew it was time to get serious.
The previous fights could be outsmarted, but now, it was time to compete based on true strength.
This was Lloyd's "theater," where the black strings restricted everyone's ability to teleport in the space, making hiding meaningless.
He had no choice but to face the challenge head-on.
As the black strings threatened to envelop him, if bound, even Spatial Teleportation wouldn't offer an escape.
Even hated undead were the same.
Su Lun had no intention of fleeing like that; he narrowed his eyes at the black strings and murmured, "Well then... let's see how impressive the true Puppet Master's skills are!"
With that thought, his gaze suddenly became sharp as a blade.
In the next instant, he no longer concealed his presence, and as he released the second-order Spell, silver threads erupted wildly from his body, surging towards the giant cross in the sky.
Black strings against silver threads!
"A Thousand Threads" against "A Thousand Threads"!
Su Lun possessed "Infinite Hair," and although his technique was somewhat lacking, he had no fear of the "Trickster" Lloyd.
It was at that moment.
The black strings identified the "resisting" target and instantly converged together.
Countless silver threads and black strings tangled in a brief moment, intertwining into a chaotic mess.
Just like the scene within the "White Monastery" back then!
Both sides were again caught in a tug-of-war.
Right then, Lloyd's voice came through the communicator once more, "Located his position, forty-five degrees to the southwest of the space!"
This notification was naturally intended to expose Su Lun's location to the other five second-orders, hoping to replay the tactic of encircling the witch as before.
Su Lun snorted softly in his heart, completely undeterred.
Now being controlled on the spot, he again pulled out a spatial scroll, and upon unsealing it, another two or three dozen tricky puppets materialized out of thin air.
He didn't only manipulate threads with his hands; he also had eight spider spears!
The spider spears pulled dozens of puppets, protecting him tightly.
....
As Su Lun was restrained by the threads, his position was just revealed, and the "puppet legion" controlled by the black strings also closed in towards his location.
Originally, after Lloyd deployed his "Puppet Theater," it was a spectacle with much to behold in combat scenes.
Whether close combat, mage, assassin, mechanic... whatever the profession, everyone was his marionette in this "theater."
Even those with methods to avoid the black strings' control still had to face countless black threads' siege and the "puppet" army.
Puppets genuinely couldn't be killed; even dismembered limbs could still kill...
In the end, those trapped in the theater could only be drained to death.
That was the tricky part of this arcane art.
But if both were Puppet Masters, especially both fused with the same alchemical implant of "Thousand Silk Threads,"
the fight would get quite dull.
Su Lun had never thought he could beat the Puppet Master in the art of puppetry.
In their first encounter, he outright abandoned puppet tactics. Instead, he released a multitude of silver strands to roughly entangle all of the opponent's "puppets."
Once entangled, they both should give up puppetry and focus on wrestling.
When it came to controlling puppets, Su Lun was nowhere near the skill of the Puppet Master.
But if it was a wrestling match, he was confident.
Moreover, Su Lun's witch hair was endless. Only after controlling all the black threads of the cross on his head could he divide his attention to manage his own puppets.
He also thought that since he was "controlled," the enemy should've also taken a gamble.
....
Sure enough, as soon as they got entangled, a roar from Lloyd came from the darkness, "Damn it, he really fused 'Infinite Hair,' you guys move fast! This kid is tricky, I won't last long!"
There was a sliver of hope before.
Thinking that even if Su Lun got the witch's head, it would be useless.
After all, the dark-gold quality "Infinite Hair" had extremely strong cursed properties, and creating an implant from it required a very high endurance value.
Even if Young Master Danze wanted to fuse it, he could only downgrade and choose inferior ingredients to lower the containment value of the finished implant, forcibly refining the dark-gold main material into a gold-quality implant product, to ensure that the body wouldn't mutate after fusion.
But now that they tried,
the hair's tenacity, strength, and tension... were all shockingly excessive.
Lloyd immediately realized that this was definitely not a downgraded implant!
Gold level?
No, it must be dark-gold level!
If someone knew what Lloyd was thinking at that moment, they would have deemed Su Lun a monster.
Danze Oliver was a young master from the inner city's elite, with the best breathing techniques and cultivation resources. If he had to downgrade just to be able to fuse an alchemic implant, what right did a wanted criminal from the outer city have to succeed in fusing?
Only a Puppet Master could truly appreciate the power of "Infinite Hair."
If they didn't kill him today, he would truly become a terror once he grew up!
...
In the midst of thick smoke, they could originally see nothing.
With this loud shout, it seemed like Lloyd had carelessly exposed his position due to anxiety.
While wrestling, Su Lun couldn't move, and neither could Lloyd.
Exposing his position, it seemed like the perfect opportunity for an assassination.
Just swinging the scythe seemed like it would easily kill the dwarf master.
But Su Lun didn't fall for it, instead his expression hardened, and he grew more focused, paying close attention to his surroundings.
How could he not know about that very special alchemical item in his opponent's possession that just happened to counter "Xiupunos's Night Scythe"?
The Oliver family had been secretly collecting items that counter the curse of the black scythe, managing to deceive others, but not the Umbrella Organization. Their seemingly certain treacherous move had actually been revealed by Sabrina and reached Su Lun's ears.
This loud shout was nothing more than "drawing fire"!
"Tch, old sneaky bastard..."
If Su Lun really took a swing, not only would he fail to kill the dwarf, but the moment he struck, he'd likely be ambushed by the quick actions of the other second-tier enemies.
With this in mind, a mocking smile flashed in his eyes. He pretended not to notice and controlled the abomination to raise the black scythe, as if he was about to strike in the direction of the sound.
Now, the zombie with tracer powder on it couldn't hide its movements.
The moment there was movement, the response of the enemy was also extremely fast.
Su Lun suddenly felt a sharp murderous intent from behind, thinking, "Here it comes!"
The malice approached rapidly, almost blink-of-an-eye fast, appearing behind Su Lun.
And by the time the figure arrived, his ears belatedly caught a series of explosive sounds of steps tapping the air, "Pop" "Pop" "Pop"...
With that speed, there was no doubt that the comer was "Poison Snake" Bright Jials, the one from the intelligence.
An exceptionally adept second-tier professional assassin at stealth and murder.
Had the blade truly been slashed forward, no matter how fast Su Lun reacted, he wouldn't have been able to defend in time and would have inevitably suffered an ambush from behind.
He wasn't afraid of being killed, but the enemies were more than one, and he absolutely couldn't afford to be entangled at this moment; he must kill swiftly!
What the ambusher didn't expect was that Su Lun's move was a feint to begin with, as he suddenly changed direction and slashed towards the assailant behind him.
The timing of this particular slash was just perfect, it landed squarely on Bright.
....
Watching the scythe suddenly turn its blade, Bright's gaze also darkened as he realized things had taken a turn for the worse.
He had not even had the chance to make his move before the black scythe was already chopping down on his forehead. But the momentum of his charge left him no room to turn back, making it more like he was ramming his head onto the blade of the scythe.
Without any countermeasure, he instinctively held up his dagger in defense.
Normally, close-combat professionals could defend and retreat even when their ambush was discovered.
Unfortunately, this black scythe was an exception.
A single slash passed through extremely smoothly.
The renowned dagger was cut into two pieces, and then, continuing its trajectory, a gash as wide as a palm was sliced across his neck, from which blood gushed profusely.
Bright didn't have the chance to react at all; his body was completely drained of life.
In his mind, Su Lun silently counted, "Four strikes made, one more to trigger the curse's backlash."
Having killed the assassin, he didn't take the situation lightly at all.
And reality didn't give him any chance to catch his breath.
At the same time as he made his move, "malicious intent" came from three other directions.
Straight ahead, he heard a sharp "hiss" sound.
This turned out to be the noise of a portable steam boiler erupting with intense steam jets.
Even without seeing it, he knew that a mechanical warrior was charging furiously at him!
The noise from the steam boiler powering up was loud, and the friction sound from the mechanical arm's joints couldn't deceive an expert like him; thus the enemy had been hiding until now, not daring to make any noise. Only after building up energy could he surge forward, which is why he was half a step slower than the assassin.
Moreover, not just from the front, intense elemental fluctuations came from both Su Lun's left and right sides. Within the dense black smoke, red and purple glows flickered respectively.
Then, in the blink of an eye, a scorching chain of fire and a streak of lightning appeared right before his eyes.
At this moment, Su Lun's eyes were devoid of any emotion other than a near-numb calmness.
His brain operated like a high-speed machine, steering his body to make the most correct tactical response.
With a flick of the Spider Lance, the "Black Hole Puppet" spread its arms out into a bell shape, a black vortex appeared, and as the flame chain and lightning approached, they were rapidly sucked in.
Once the Puppet opened its mouth again, the spell of thunder and fire was spat out straight into the face of the mechanical warrior rushing towards him.
At times like this, the advantages of having multiple hands were immediately apparent.
While controlling the puppet, Su Lun's right hand swiftly drew his gun, pulling the trigger repeatedly towards the left side.
"Bang!"
"Bang!"
"Bang!"
The three distinct reports of alchemical bullets burst, ringing in the ear.
On the left was Leifaer-Jiemha, and on the right was Fire Mage Nidum David.
In such a situation, attempting a "Four-Stack Shot" clearly exceeded his strength, but using a "Three-Stack Shot" to shoot at the fragile-bodied lightning Magician was still perfectly feasible.
Su Lun didn't see the locations of the two men, but he could ascertain their direction from the noises they made while casting their spells.
Three shots were fired, and a muffled grunt was heard, indicating someone was hit.
Su Lun didn't bother checking on them, with the "Black Hole Doll" at his side, the Magicians' abilities were almost seventy percent nullified.
Furthermore, there was no time to check.
Because by this time, the mechanical warrior was already upon him!
