Risking their own lives and their direct line forces would obviously not be worthwhile, so it made more sense to recruit some Scavengers.
It would cost some money, but if danger truly arose, the losses would be smaller, and the chance of survival higher.
....
Su Lun's pupils flickered rapidly as he scanned the information on the screen, ten lines at a glance.
He analyzed the recent Scavenging trends.
Clearly, the pace of exploration was accelerating.
In the central region of the Relic, third-tier warriors had already begun to lead teams inside...
But they seemed to encounter not insignificant resistance, not to mention some top-tier warriors who couldn't reach the central city even after half a month, and some of the large Scavenging teams that had been at the forefront had disappeared altogether from the rankings.
In such cases, it meant either they'd earned enough and gone back, or they'd been wiped out.
Then, while looking, Su Lun actually spotted a coded message in the advertisement column.
"Is Mr. Hei looking for me?"
Su Lun saw that the message had been posted a day ago.
Without using any other contact methods, it seemed not to be too urgent.
Su Lun deciphered the content, which only provided an address: White Elephant Gambling Den.
"Eh... to have the rendezvous at a gambling den? That doesn't seem like Mr. Hei's style..."
That kind of old gentleman, although not particular about trifles, definitely had places he wouldn't go.
Like a brothel or a casino.
Su Lun thought he might have deciphered it incorrectly and checked again, but it was still the same address.
Could it be that the code was mistakenly crossed?
No, that couldn't be right, this wasn't a common code, but a predetermined cipher.
Not figuring it out, Su Lun decided to go to the designated place to see for himself.
...
Dawn Camp produced "nouveaux riches" every day, so naturally, gambling dens, these dens of iniquity, were never in short supply.
Su Lun had no interest in gambling, and since there was no gladiator arena here, he had never visited one.
For some reason gambling dens liked to be underground, and the boss of "White Elephant Gambling Lounge" had literally dug ten meters into the ground to create a medium-sized underground casino.
When Su Lun arrived, the place was buzzing with people.
The not-so-spacious gambling den was crammed with nearly a thousand people.
In the semi-enclosed space, smoke curled through the air, and the atmosphere was saturated with the mixed scents of sweat, tobacco, and intoxicating potions.
It was just like the gambling dens on Green Street once had been, full of slot machines, pachinko machines, roulettes... every corner of the gambling den was packed with these machines.
Each machine was occupied by gamblers, the clinking of coins clashing, the "klunk" "klunk" of the handle being pulled, a cacophony of noises assailing the ears.
In the central area, there were also poker tables...
The crowd still could not do without the gambling den girls dressed in revealing clothes.
Su Lun entered the casino, exchanged for some chips at the front desk caged in by a wire mesh, and then disguised as a gambler, he blended into the crowd.
He didn't exhibit any signs of looking for someone, and didn't start scanning around the moment he walked in.
Because he knew all too well, someone who doesn't look like a gambler entering a gambling den is the least welcome and the most conspicuous.
At that moment, he saw a gambler just leaving his seat, so with seeming interest, Su Lun sat down at a slot machine, inserted a coin, and casually pulled the lever.
"Clang~"
The scroll spun and then stopped on several fruit symbols.
Su Lun had spent quite some time on Green Street and being a Mechanic himself, he was no stranger to the workings of these machines.
These programmed machines might seem random, but there were certain tricks to them.
He gambled a few hands and even made a small profit.
But he wasn't there to gamble.
He thought that under normal circumstances, Mr. Hei with his ability to appear and disappear like a ghost would've quickly noticed him and then come to meet him.
However, to his surprise, after gambling for a while and winning a good sum of chips, no one had come.
Su Lun felt puzzled; perhaps the message was no longer valid?
After thinking it over, he decided to stand up from the slot machine and take a stroll through the gambling area.
...
In the main hall, there were several blackjack and craps tables surrounded by a large crowd of gamblers.
"Nine points, nine points, nine points..."
"Haha, twenty points, assured victory!"
"..."
The gamblers shouted desperately for the cards they wished for.
Su Lun wandered around aimlessly and didn't recognize any familiar faces, but he did catch some individuals behaving strangely.
"People from the Umbrella Organization, and they seem to be of a not-so-low rank..."
He quietly placed bets while forming some speculations in his mind.
He had learned many of the Umbrella Organization's internal secret codes and recognition methods from Sabrina.
Watching those professional members of the Umbrella Organization, he recognized them at a glance. But since their gaze didn't fall on him, Su Lun didn't feel they were there to catch him. If there had been any action, Sabrina would've warned him.
"Could it be because these people are watching that Mr. Hei hasn't shown up?"
Su Lun thought.
However, it wasn't long before he was proven wrong.
He saw an acquaintance.
....
Next to the basement hall, there were several small rooms, the VIP rooms reserved for high-stakes gamblers. Although they weren't closed off, screens hid the gaming tables, and one needed a certain amount of chips to enter.
Su Lun didn't see anyone at first, but he was attracted by a familiar voice.
"All in!"
"Call!"
"Four aces! Haha, your full house is nothing compared to this!"
"..."
Su Lun knew that voice all too well.
He muttered to himself with a puzzled face, "Sister Qian?"
So it wasn't a secret code left by Mr. Hei, but rather that gambling-addicted lady?
At that moment, all of Su Lun's confusion suddenly made sense.
No wonder they had chosen to meet in the gambling den...
No wonder he had waited so long without seeing anyone...
It turned out that the gambling-addicted lady was having too much fun and was waiting for him to find her.
Su Lun couldn't help but laugh and cry. He walked over, tossing a chip casually like an old gambler to the attendant at the door.
Even without showing enough chips, he smoothly entered.
Behind the screen, the gambling table was playing Texas Hold'em, with seven gamblers in total.
When Su Lun arrived, he saw the gambling-addicted lady joyfully sweeping up the chips on the table.
Looking at the amount, it was at least several million.
This kind of high-stakes game didn't allow spectators; only the gamblers could come in.
Su Lun walked over, and the lady offered him a chair, inviting him to sit down.
Su Lun took his seat naturally and then gave the lady a chip as a tip, also saying, "Exchange this for three million in chips for me."
The blonde lady smiled sweetly, "Of course, sir."
The arrival of a new person caught the other gamblers' eyes at the table, none of them spoke, and they fiddled with the chips in their hands.
Only the carefree gambling-addicted lady seemed still immersed in the joy of her winnings and didn't seem to recognize the now "charm level 12" Su Lun.
Su Lun knew it was Sister Qian's weakness, so he didn't plan to spoil her fun.
He had intended to play a few hands, but as soon as he sat down and glanced at the face of a middle-aged man who had been sitting with his back to him, Su Lun immediately realized that the situation didn't look quite right.
There was something odd about this game.
....
"Could it really be that guy..."
Although Su Lun's face remained impassive, his mind was already considering strategies for dealing with the conflict if it arose.
If it had been anyone else, he probably wouldn't have been so grave, but it happened to be this man.
If things were as he suspected, then they would be exceptionally tricky.
At this moment, the private room attendant happened to be walking over with a tray.
She bent over to place the chips on the table, turned her face towards Su Lun with a smile, and said, "Sir, your chips have arrived..."
Su Lun turned his head towards the girl and gave her the characteristic sleazy smile, "Thank you."
As he spoke, he handed over another chip, sliding it into the low V of the girl's neckline. It looked like a playboy's greasy move, but his gaze inadvertently swept over the bespectacled middle-aged man to his left.
Top experts all have extraordinary powers of perception, and the slightest change in emotion in his glance could be easily caught.
Su Lun dared not look directly.
But it was this brief glimpse,
by the time he clearly saw the man's face,
Su Lun was glad he had been cautious, but his heart sank, "It really is him! If he's not here for me, could he be here for Qian Tiao?"
"Good luck, sir~"
As thoughts flashed through his mind, the young lady beside him yiyi chuckled, threw a coquettish glance at Su Lun, and then left the side of the gambling table.
....
The other few at the gambling table didn't seem to mind waiting for this half minute.
The croupier shuffled the cards, and a new game began.
Su Lun acted as if nothing was wrong, occasionally observing the others at the table with the normal scrutinizing gaze of a gambler.
Even though a "troublesome" character had appeared at the table, he showed no sign of panic.
After observing for a while, Su Lun realized that the man wasn't here for him.
He also didn't make any effort to warn the gambling-addicted lady opposite him.
Qian Tiao might look careless, but her combat instincts were remarkably sharp.
Even if there was indeed a problem, she likely wouldn't be at a disadvantage.
Moreover, Su Lun knew that she had recognized him.
It was highly possible that she also noticed the anomaly in the gambling game.
Things seemed to be getting complicated.
Su Lun felt that they were most likely caught up in an "accidental incident."
The game continued,
Su Lun had harvested various miscellaneous abilities, and his card skills were not bad.
After a few rounds, the three million plus had quickly turned into over four million.
This was the temptation of Texas Hold'em, "Going all-in" could make one quickly rich, but also could empty one's chips at any time.
Today, Qian Tiao's luck also seemed to be not bad, as she had already amassed nearly ten million in chips in front of her.
Those who can gamble so big aren't simple.
After several rounds at the table, Su Lun had roughly identified the identities of the other players.
Besides a few who were obviously wealthy people from the inner city, the most suspicious one was a blonde man wearing suspenders and a white shirt.
Although his clothes were expensive, the air of a street thug couldn't be concealed.
He might pass on the outside, but not at a gambling table of this caliber.
This guy seemed to be unlucky, not getting good cards in several rounds and having lost the chips he had before plus another five million he added.
Previously, Su Lun only thought this blonde man was a bit unlucky, not noticing anything amiss.
However, this round, he saw the problem.
The "troublesome" bespectacled middle-aged man seemed to be particularly targeting the blonde.
....
After the first round of blinds, the pot had already accumulated several hundred thousand in chips.
The croupier dealt the cards, the three community cards were the Jack of Spades, the 3 of Spades, and the Ace of Spades...
Three spades, it was obvious someone would go for a flush.
The chance of stealing was very small.
Following a round casually, Su Lun, Qian Tiao, and the others all folded their cards.
Only two were left, the bespectacled middle-aged man, and the blonde young man.
The blond pushed his chips forward, "One hundred thousand."
Su Lun glanced at the slight furrow of the blonde young man's eyebrows, knowing that his cards were probably not meant for a flush. The fellow wasn't very good at cards, and when he had decent but not large cards, he would unconsciously show this slight facial expression.
The bespectacled man across was very composed, calmly raising the stakes, "Five hundred thousand."
The blonde hesitated for a moment, "Call."
Su Lun, seeing this, guessed that the blonde man most likely had a two pair hand, which is why he knew the other was going for a flush but still couldn't bear to fold.
He probably wanted to bet on a "full house" hand with "AAABB."
Just then, the croupier dealt another Diamond 4.
The blonde young man's wrinkles at the corners of his eyes tightened, obviously of no use to him.
And at this moment, the bespectacled middle-aged man became aggressive, raising the bet, "One million."
The tone was so even that it seemed like a flush.
This put the blond young man in a difficult position.
He had already bet nearly a million in this round, and folding would mean a huge loss.
But to see the fifth card, he'd have to call at least a million more.
He looked across at the man with glasses and said discontentedly, "Hey, hey, hey, uncle, are you trying to bluff me?"
The bespectacled middle-aged man responded indifferently, "If you want to see the card, put up the chips."
"..."
At that, a look akin to frustrated rage flashed through the blond man's eyes.
However, Su Lun noticed that the wrinkles at the corner of his eyebrows seemed to relax.
The blond man pushed forward almost three million in chips, as if to intimidate, "All in!"
....
To provoke, then go all in...
A bit of a trick, but not a particularly clever one.
Watching this, Su Lun slightly turned his gaze, thinking, "It's getting interesting. But what's this guy counting on to win? Cheating?"
At that moment, he suddenly realized something and focused on the gold coin the man was toying with in his hand.
Although the blond man had been fiddling with the coin all along, the change in his momentum just now seemed to match the rhythm of the coin...
With this thought, Su Lun took a closer look.
And indeed, there was a problem.
[Tabard's Lucky Coin]
Description: You won? No, you've lost everything.
Cursed Trait: Using the cursed power within the coin can bring you good fortune; but after using this good luck, the person closest to you will suffer misfortune; once touched, you will become more dependent, and your luck will worsen without it;
Detailed Explanation: This is a cursed Ancient Coin; once during the mythological era, a deity wanting to punish Their gambling descendant, created this coin of misfortune;
Seeing this, Su Lun's pupils narrowed slightly and he chuckled to himself, "So he does plan to cheat... tsk tsk, if this guy knew who he was up against, he'd probably regret his actions."
Using sleight of hand to cheat was, of course, out of the question; there were experts in this gambling hall.
But using a cursed item to cheat—that caught people off guard.
The other party had gone all in,
and the bespectacled middle-aged man was still calm, saying indifferently, "I'll call."
Then the croupier dealt the card, the last one was the "Club Jack".
Having gone all in, there was no final round of betting, and both revealed their hole cards directly.
The bespectacled middle-aged man had the King of Spades and the Nine of Spades, indeed a flush.
The blond man excitedly threw out his hole cards, a Jack and a Three, which together with the community cards made a full house, JJJ33.
He seemed delighted, reaching for the chips in front of him, "Haha, I didn't expect my luck to be this good... to actually gamble a full house!"
The bespectacled middle-aged man lost money but didn't seem to mind at all; a hint of a smile surfaced on his sickly face, "Yes, you're quite lucky, Mr. Bianco..."
"You...!"
With his name called out, the blond man's complexion changed drastically.
He didn't even bother to make any excuses, and without any hesitation, he quickly reached into his chest pocket and pressed his pocket watch.
In that instant, everything in his view seemed to slow down several times, everything around him turning into slow motion.
He violently pulled away from his seat, ready to flee the gambling den.
....
"An A-rank... oh, no, a newly promoted S-rank wanted criminal, 'Lucky Star' Bianco?"
Su Lun finally knew who this person was.
This guy had been committing crimes frequently recently, making quite a name for himself. It was said he ambushed the youngest son of an inner city tycoon and a rich merchant, then made it onto the S-list.
And in that instant, in Su Lun's view, he suddenly felt the blond young man's speed explode, as though he was a ghost about to slip away.
This speed was beyond what a second-tier, fully agile assassin could achieve.
Su Lun wasn't marveling at the speed but was slightly surprised to see the silver pocket watch just taken out from his chest, [Watkins' Pocket Watch].
Description: The consequences of disturbing the order of time are severe, do you want to try?
Cursed Trait: By pressing the pocket watch, the user can gain a time acceleration of 2~5 times their own; however, if you don't master the Time Law, using it will randomly shorten your life, perhaps by a second, or perhaps by a hundred years;
Detailed Explanation: A prized creation of an ancient alchemist named 'White Watkins', it was originally a family heirloom intended for his offspring;
Looking at the information identified, Su Lun muttered to himself, "So it's a rare time-cursed item, this guy's got quite the collection of treasures..."
Those who made it onto the S-list naturally had some tricks up their sleeves.
However...
Too bad.
If his pursuers were anyone else, with this time acceleration ability, Bianco might have actually gotten away.
But... the man before him wouldn't give him any chance to live.
Because this bespectacled man was none other than the leader of the Umbrella Organization—'Forensic Doctor' Servis Gerard!

chapters.title: Chapter 183 - 183: 182
chapters.content:
"Lucky Star" Blanco Quick suddenly erupted.
Before anyone else could react, he had already bolted several meters away.
The man with glasses still maintained his leisurely middle-aged demeanor, as if he hadn't done a thing.
Yet beneath this calmness,
Suddenly!
A streak of silver flashed by,
and a jet of blood abruptly spurted from Blanco's chest, his expression freezing there.
Su Lun, with his keen eyesight, clearly saw that the "silver light" was a slender surgical knife, which made his pupils shrink dramatically.
And shockingly, there was more to come!
The silver streak, fast like a bullet, had just passed when the middle-aged man, who had looked sickly, suddenly intensified his gaze. His figure flickered, and in a blink, he had teleported several meters away.
The middle-aged man turned his hand into a blade and fiercely thrust forward, penetrating Blanco's chest with his bare hands in an extremely bloody manner.
"Hiss" blood sprayed everywhere, filling the entire gambling hall with a thick stench of blood.
Su Lun witnessed it all, immediately becoming alert, "As expected, it's outrageously strong..."
The middle-aged man's face was splattered with crimson hot blood.
On his face, on his suit, it was everywhere.
But this guy, far from feeling displeased about being dirtied by blood, had an expression of enjoyment, greedily breathing in the warm scent of blood.
This all happened so fast that, to the average person, it seemed like lightning had flashed, and two shadows had collided.
But Su Lun saw everything clearly.
He caught the glimpse of violent excitement on the man's face as he killed, which he somehow found very familiar.
This guy, he seemed not quite right mentally.
....
In a single encounter, the S-class wanted criminal Blanco Quick was killed.
Now, the scene froze, and everyone in the gambling hall was stunned.
It wasn't as though violent conflicts or deaths hadn't occurred in the gambling hall before.
There had been knife and gun fights, beheadings, and even eviscerations...
But they had never seen anyone use their hands to penetrate someone's chest.
The glasses-wearing man stood rigid like a javelin. His murderous aura visibly condensed into substance, with a faint red glow emerging around his body...
The visual impact of this violent act was extremely strong, turning the gambling girls' faces pale with fright.
After a moment's shock, screams echoed through the entire gambling hall.
Suddenly, a team of undercover agents from the Umbrella organization rushed in, showing their badges and reassuring everyone, "Umbrella apprehending a wanted criminal, no need to panic!"
The man who appeared to be the team leader, a square-faced middle-aged man, glanced at the frozen scene and couldn't help but twitch at the corner of his eyes.
He walked over, showing a troubled expression, and said, "Sir, you shouldn't have killed him."
Only then did the man with glasses release the body, speaking in an indifferent tone, "Hmm... sorry. Suddenly felt like killing someone."
With that, he put down the body and leisurely took off his glasses from the bridge of his nose, then pulled out a white handkerchief from his pocket, gently wiping the blood off the lenses.
This seemingly ordinary action made the square-faced man internally flinch, his eyelids twitching fiercely, "Sir, I will report this incident as it happened."
"Hmm."
The man with glasses seemed unbothered and walked out, "I'll leave this place to you."
"..."
The square-faced man wanted to say something else but didn't know how to start.
At that moment, another team member quickly performed a preliminary examination of the body and reported, "Boss, confirmed, it's the fugitive 'Blanco Quick'!"
As he spoke, the middle-aged man slowly walked out.
....
Su Lun listened to the conversation of several people and was also rapidly analyzing the intelligence.
Obviously, the leader of this umbrella organization didn't recognize that the man with glasses before him was their chief.
But that wasn't surprising.
Because the legendary chief of the umbrella organization, forensic doctor Servis Gerard, was very mysterious, and very few people in Old Lington had ever seen him.
Su Lun had also gotten some information about his appearance from Sabina.
But not much.
All he knew was that this guy seemed to be a forensic doctor who enjoyed dissecting bodies on regular days, very low-profile and mysterious.
Su Lun had heard about his murderous hobby as well.
But no one knew the details.
It was speculated that it was related to his extraordinary job, or perhaps a natural talent...
Even though Sabina was a general in the umbrella organization, her understanding of this mysterious leader's capabilities was very limited.
She only knew he was very strong.
Unreasonably strong!
Su Lun watched the middle-aged man's retreating figure and heaved a sigh of relief.
At the same time, he felt very solemn.
"Such swiftness..."
He recalled in his mind, that move just now, even if it had been him, although he wouldn't have been killed in one encounter, the possibility of escaping to save his life was also not great.
Su Lun didn't dare to scrutinize everything about this guy and withdrew his gaze.
As long as he wasn't coming for him, it was fine.
....
The people from the umbrella organization cleaned up the body, and the gambling den became noisy again.
But it was like a campfire that had been doused with cold water: even though it still burned, the atmosphere wasn't as intense as before.
At least, at the table in their small hall, several big bosses from the inner city were scared pale and lost the mood to gamble, all leaving the scene.
With no one organizing the game, the lady gambler who was disappointed began to count her chips. While she was packing up, she also muttered, "I thought I was finally having some good luck tonight, thought I could win back what I lost yesterday... ah well, no more gambling, seeing blood spoils the luck..."
Su Lun listened to her muttering, with a slight smile on his lips. He walked over, pulled up a chair, and sat next to her, teasing in the persona of a wealthy young master, "Hey, beauty, care for a drink together?"
Qian Tiao naturally recognized Su Lun right away, but she couldn't act too familiar.
She sized him up from head to toe, a hint of surprise flashing in her eyes, bantering, "Yo~ handsome, are you asking me out?"
Su Lun smiled, "May I have the honor?"
Qian Tiao took no offense, her expression similar to that of a woman smitten by a handsome guy, readily agreeing, "Sure!"
....
The two exchanged chips and left the gambling den.
Today, Qian Tiao was dressed conservatively, not showing off large tattoos or carrying a knife, just a gentle housewife's attire.
But as soon as she walked on the street, Qian Tiao revealed her true colors. She casually threw her arm around Su Lun's shoulder, taking on a boss lady's demeanor, "Hey, hey, hey... I say, kid, you actually look pretty good with hair..."
As she spoke, she casually pinched Su Lun's cheek and scratched his hair as if checking if it was real.
After confirming, Qian Tiao squinted her eyes with a teasing tone, "Really though... this skin of yours is definitely a favorite among the matrons and missies."
"..."
Hearing the first part, Su Lun thought Qian Tiao was complimenting him, but the latter half felt off.
He wasn't sure if it was familiarity breeding fondness or what, but he always felt the gentle sinking feeling on his arm was a bit different from before.
He didn't forget there was serious business, and directly asked, "By the way, Sister Qian Tiao, was it you who sent the information from the Wilderness Hunting Guild?"
"Oh, almost forgot, I actually did have a little matter to discuss with you,"
Qian Tiao's eyes flashed with realization, her expression as if she just remembered the important matter, "Got something to borrow from you."
"..."
Su Lun looked at the bloodshot eyes and tentatively asked, "You haven't been gambling at the gambling den all day and night, have you?"
The news had been posted yesterday, and here she was still at the gambling den today, perhaps his guess was spot on.
Indeed.
The gambling-addicted woman didn't shy away from admitting it, nodding her head, "Yep."
She seemed to recall some unpleasant experience and frowned, "Lost some money yesterday, so I gambled a bit more. Just when my luck started getting better today, and I began winning some back, that whole mess earlier happened..."
"..."
Upon hearing the full story, Su Lun's expression turned slightly bizarre.
He had wondered why it was such a coincidence that a random encounter led them directly into the Operation Umbrella's fugitive capture.
It wasn't a coincidence at all, but rather by design.
Using her esoteric gambling skills, she had chosen a "bad luck charm" to gamble against, improving her own luck, otherwise she would have lost everything by now.
The wanted criminal "Lucky Star" Blanco Quick was using the "Tabard's Lucky Gold Coin," and the curse backlash was getting worse. Without the coin, his luck would deteriorate further, so it was normal for her to win against him.
Little did she expect that while they were gambling, the leader of Operation Umbrella would show up.
And that led to the scene Su Lun had just witnessed.
After she rattled off her story, Suriname then asked, "Miss Qian Tiao, do you know who that guy was?"
Qian Tiao raised an eyebrow, "He must be one of the high-ranking members of Operation Umbrella, very powerful, at least a 'T0 level' senior commander. I noticed him three hours ago when he came in. But since he wasn't coming for me, I ignored him. But speaking of which... the guy's gambling skills are indeed impressive."
"Oh."
Listening to her casual tone, Su Lun knew she was not overly concerned, then said, "I got a bit of intel; that person might be 'forensic doctor' Servis Gerard, the leader of Operation Umbrella."
"So it was him, no wonder."
Upon hearing this, Qian Tiao furrowed her brow slightly.
Thinking about it, she didn't seem surprised and muttered, "Probably because the little princess from the Duke's residence is coming, and he was sent ahead."
Seeing Qian Tiao's indifferent attitude, Su Lun didn't say much else but then asked, "By the way, Miss Qian Tiao, what were you planning to borrow from me?"
Qian Tiao glanced at the crowd on the street. Not speaking directly, she said, "This isn't a place to talk. Let's go somewhere else to discuss."
Su Lun pointed towards a street lit by neon lights. "A pub?"
Qian Tiao waved her hand, "Forget it, no drinking. I've been gambling for two days and a night, not feeling well."
Su Lun: "Then where to?"
Qian Tiao, looking at the people on the street looking for accommodation, suddenly remembered something and asked, "By the way, have you found a place to stay in the campsite?"
Su Lun honestly replied, "Yes. I'm currently staying at the Rose Hotel."
Qian Tiao swung her hand grandly, "That's perfect, I haven't found a place yet. I'll squeeze in with you tonight."
Su Lun found it a bit odd but was used to this columbine's gambling addict, so he complied, "Oh."
....
And so, Su Lun led Qian Tiao to the Rose Hotel.
Finding a room was difficult now, especially one with a private bathroom.
As soon as Qian Tiao entered the room and saw the bathroom, her eyes lit up, "Wow~! You actually managed to book a room with a bathroom? Wow, those big tycoons in the inner city would find it hard to get such a room now..."
Su Lun: "I've been in the campsite all this time, and the booking was tight, so I didn't cancel it..."
The room had a soundproof barrier, so there was no fear of being overheard.
But before he could finish speaking, the gambling-addicted woman walked straight into the bathroom, tugging at the sash of her kimono, completely unaware of the presence of a man in the room, and began to undress.
While undressing, she kept mumbling, "Wow, I can finally take a bath... After walking for more than ten days without soaking in a tub, I was almost suffocated..."
Saying this, the kimono was thrown out. "Please hang this up for me~"
Su Lun watched her completely naked back and shook his head with a wry smile.
Back at the Cross Society times, Qian Tiao had often asked Su Lun to join her in communal bathing, and they weren't strangers to it.
Being roommates didn't feel awkward at all.
He casually joked,
"Hey, hey, hey, Qianjiao, can't you spare me a little embarrassment?"
"Pff~ It's not like I haven't seen it before."
"..."
This big shot really didn't treat him as an outsider, seemingly indifferent to the distinction between the sexes.
Listening,
Su Lun smiled and didn't look any further.
Turning around, he took his clothes towards the room's coat rack.
Soon, the sound of trickling water came from the bathroom.
Su Lun hung Qianjiao's kimono on the coat rack and then asked, "Qianjiao, how did you end up coming to the ruins?"
Amidst the sound of the shower, Qianjiao's voice came from the bathroom, "Didn't the Duke's mansion issue an order for a national relic hunt? All the big and small forces were notified. Even the big and small gangs in the outer city had been assigned tasks. Not just us from the Cross Society; the Crow Gang and the Steam Party also sent a lot of people over..."
"Oh~"
The room was small, with no sofa. Su Lun tidied up his own things on the bed and then sat down on it.
From this angle, looking up, he caught a rather enchanting scene.
The hotel was decorated simply, and the bathroom was not made of solid walls, but frosted glass partitions.
Though the glass kept it unclear, a misty silhouette was still visible.
When sprayed with water, the moistened silhouette could be seen even clearer.
Su Lun, with his current eyesight, could see everything very clearly.
A tall and exquisite figure.
When Qianjiao turned her body to shower, he could even see some fine details of her proudly perked figure.
Su Lun wasn't intentionally trying to take advantage of this gambling-obsessed lady; it was just this casual glance that brought Sabina to mind.
Actually, upon closer comparison, Qianjiao's figure was really not much different from Sabina's—they both had slightly voluptuous figures, but each had their own charm.
Sabina was coquettish, while Qianjiao exuded a bold spirit.
Even as a close-combat professional, Qianjiao's muscles were more rounded, parts like her hips, legs, and abdomen looked long but also evenly full-bodied.
It's just that she was notorious in the underworld and didn't have a reputation for allure, so rarely anyone talked about it.
And then, maybe because he looked a few seconds too long, Qianjiao grumbled from the bathroom, "Hey, hey, hey... Can't you rein in your gaze a bit? Looking for a beating?"
After all, she was a top-notch expert with a strong sense of perception.
Su Lun then realized his rudeness and restrained his gaze.
As they were quite familiar, he imitated the way she once joked with him, smiled and said, "Not bad at all~"
His tone harbored no sleazy thoughts, just pure admiration.
Seemingly unsure how to respond, the bathroom fell silent for a moment before Qianjiao's faint voice came through, "You really are asking for a beating..."
Su Lun laughed, "Hahaha..."
But jokes aside, there was serious business to discuss.
Su Lun asked again, "By the way, Qianjiao, you said earlier that you wanted to borrow something from me?"
"Hmm."
Qianjiao responded and after a pause, added, "We need to assassinate someone. Just in case, we might need your Black Scythe."
Upon hearing this, a thought suddenly flashed through Su Lun's mind, and he asked, "Are you going to assassinate the young lady from the Duke's mansion?"
"Eh... how did you guess?"
Then, Qianjiao's reply came from the bathroom, "Pretty much so, but it's a bit complicated, can't be explained in just a few words..."

chapters.title: Chapter 184 - 183: The Secrets of the Dungeon (Please Subscribe)
chapters.content:
Qian Tiao was taking a shower.
Su Lun, having nothing to do on the bed, simply took out some alchemy books to read.
Now, he spent nearly all his free time digesting knowledge.
This was a habit he had developed before his transmigration; reading helped stabilize his emotions.
Soon, the sound of water from the bathroom ceased suddenly.
Qian Tiao walked out in a loose bathrobe, naturally wearing nothing underneath, and upon looking up, one could see the deep V at her chest. It must be said, close-combat professionals indeed had impressive physiques.
"Whew~"
She approached the dressing mirror and let out a long, pleased sigh, "I finally feel relaxed..."
Her smooth, aqua hair was unbound, making her appear less fierce.
Qian Tiao grabbed a towel from the rack, cocking her head as she dried her wet hair. With every lift of her hand, either the large sleeve or the neckline gaped, revealing much.
However, the two in the room remained calm.
Su Lun was reading his book and merely glanced up before refocusing his gaze.
There had been the sound of running water during the shower, so they hadn't delved into details; now that there was time, Qian Tiao continued with the earlier topic, "Su Lun boy, I heard you have a puppet that is immune to 'Xiupunos's Night Scythe'? Mr. Hei's plan is, it would be best to take that puppet with us."
"Hmm, it's a type of living corpse."
This information was on the wanted notice, so there was nothing that couldn't be lent.
Moreover, Su Lun had used that 'abomination' many times, and a scholar like Mr. Hei had probably guessed its origin long ago.
Speaking of which, he thought of something and said, "But controlling that corpse is somewhat tricky, and if one is not a Puppet Master, it would be very difficult. Moreover, a lot of practice is needed to precisely control the scythe's slashes..."
Although Su Lun thought that Mr. Hei and his people were strong, they might not be able to immediately handle a type of lockdown material they weren't familiar with.
Even if they were borrowing the living corpse.
Hearing this, Qian Tiao glanced from the mirror.
She just met Su Lun's gaze and added, "Mr. Hei said, you'd probably be interested in checking it out. So... actually, I came to borrow you."
....
"Borrow me???"
Upon hearing this, a voice instinctively responded for him.
No, I'm not interested!
Although he didn't know why Mr. Hei and the others wanted to ambush that little princess from the Duke's household, that battle was bound to be extremely perilous. Even the leader of the Umbrella Organization secretly came to prepare the ground, implying that the little princess must have numerous top-level experts around her.
Moreover, Black Tower is a very special place.
The top financial families in the Inner City, no matter how strong, also have their limits.
But now that Su Lun knew Black Tower was a gateway to the upper world, he understood the Duke's household had a depth he couldn't fathom.
Otherwise, with just Mr. Hei and his group's strength, which large family in the Inner City couldn't they overpower?
Now they still hide and take precautions, certainly wary of Black Tower.
This battle would definitely be a fierce clash among top professionals.
Su Lun was very self-aware.
As a newcomer to the second rank, although he had a few tricks, he wasn't fit to flaunt them in such a setting.
The clashes among top professionals, even the aftershocks were enough for him.
Lending the scythe is possible...
Lending a person...
Wait, Mr. Hei mentioned it?
Su Lun instantly thought of something and didn't hurry to respond;
He looked at Qian Tiao, puzzled, "Mr. Hei mentioned it?"
"Hmm. Although I also think you wouldn't want to go. But Mr. Hei said, after telling you our plan, you might be interested..."
Qian Tiao gave him a look.
She paused, then dropped a bombshell that would astound anyone, "After all, this time we are going to intercept a real higher-tier combatant. According to ancient terms, that person should be... a fifth-tier professional!"
...
"Fifth-tier?!"
Su Lun was startled at first, then he realized what she implied.
This was indeed beyond his expectations.
In Old Lington, the known strongest masters were only third-tier, like the heads of the three major gangs in the outer city, the presidents and vice presidents of major guilds, and the top experts in the inner city... all were third-tier.
This sudden emergence of a "fifth-tier," what was going on?
According to the ancient books unearthed from the ruins, it was clear that Magicians of old did not stop at the third-tier.
After all, the owner of the Dawn Relic, Sir Isaac from a thousand years ago, was hailed as a "Demigod."
Having absorbed the astonishing information in her words, Su Lun was momentarily amazed, but his first instinctual thought was: how many Alchemy Shards could a fifth-tier professional reap?
At this thought, he immediately became interested!
The Soul Shards of a higher-tier expert consisted not just of a volume of knowledge but also of an understanding at the level of laws.
It also meant... perspective!
"Linear equations with one unknown" might already be difficult for elementary students, but aren't they just introductory problems for junior and senior high school students?
This rule applies in the realm of Alchemy as well.
Without crossing certain tier thresholds, many higher-tier knowledge cannot be comprehended.
Once crossed, it becomes effortless!
Su Lun was now acutely aware of this.
When he was at the first tier, learning second-tier rune knowledge was extremely difficult, hard to understand, and hard to grasp. But after advancing, many of the previous challenging pieces of knowledge almost became understandable at a glance, reducing the learning difficulty by at least several times!
One can imagine, if he peeled off a fifth-tier professional's Soul, and actually grasped the knowledge related to laws, what would Su Lun's learning progress be like?
Not to mention whether he could harvest completed knowledge Shards, Su Lun felt that just by gaining "perspective," the understanding of other second and third-tier Alchemy knowledge would be like seeing it once and knowing it, wouldn't it?
Higher-tier knowledge was already monopolized by the Black Tower, which was not something that could be obtained by harvesting many third-tier professionals!
If it were a group of third-tier enemies, he really wouldn't want to go.
After all, the little princess must have a dozen or so third-tier protectors surrounding her.
If Mr. Hei couldn't care for them and he had to face one, Su Lun was not confident that he could survive against a third-tier professional.
But now, hearing this,
apparently,
they were not going to assassinate the little princess but to kill a fifth-tier guardian?
...
"How strong must Mr. Hei and his people be..."
Su Lun, hearing her lay out their plan, instantly felt that he had underestimated the strength of the "Mirror Organization."
But regret aside, he was indeed very interested in this plan!
If Mr. Hei and his people dared to make a move, they certainly felt confident about it!
"It looks like you've decided to go."
Chientiao caught the change in Su Lun's expression and commented faintly.
Su Lun nodded, "Yes."
"Good that you've decided."
Upon hearing this, Chientiao didn't say much more.
At this moment, she had finished drying her hair and glanced at Su Lun sprawled across the bed, the words babbled in complaint, "Eh, eh, eh~ Su Lun kid, can you scoot over a bit? There's only one bed and you're spread out like this, can you leave some space for me?"
Originally, Su Lun's thoughts were already drifting, his mind filled with the gains from peeling off the shards of a fifth-tier strongman.
Upon hearing this, he then glanced at the disheveled Chientiao.
This big shot, it really seems like she's planning to squeeze in with him.
The gambling lady didn't mind, so naturally, he didn't have any objections either.
"Oh."
Su Lun responded and shifted a bit to make room on half of the bed. Just as he moved, he suddenly felt a chilling blade whizz close by.
A slight sound, quiet like a swift knife cutting through the air.
Looking again, a large bed was split into two from the middle.
Because the knife was so fast, even the sheets and blankets on the bed didn't deform, the cut smooth and cleanly divided into two, with a palm-wide gap in the middle.
"..."
Su Lun looked at it, a wry smile appearing at the corner of his mouth.
He had clearly seen the quick draw of the blade but hadn't dodged. Obviously, this big shot was just trying to scare him, probably as retaliation for the teasing during the bath earlier.
Fortunately, the mattress was supported by numerous individual springs, so it didn't collapse even when cut in half.
"Alright, let's sleep."
Senjo looked at Su Lun, not scared at all, and felt bored with a slight pout.
She also didn't consider herself an outsider and happily lay on the other half of the bed.
With her legs crossed, her fair thighs were revealed.
....
Since they were going to battle, Su Lun naturally had to ask for more information.
He turned his head to look at the other half of the bed and asked, "Senjo, when are we likely to leave?"
"Don't know, waiting for the notice."
Senjo didn't even open her eyes, lazily responding, "Mr. Hei and the others are handling the plan; I'm only responsible for the fighting."
She seemed totally unconcerned about the details of the plan, letting professionals like Mr. Hei handle the scheming and plotting.
Sharing the same room, there was no awkwardness in the air.
Thinking about their mission to ambush a fifth-tier professional, Su Lun was indeed very curious about their strength.
As Senjo didn't treat herself as an outsider, Su Lun didn't either. He directly asked, "Senjo, what exactly is your tier of strength now?"
After a moment's thought, Senjo slowly said three words, "Hard to say."
Su Lun: "Hard to say?"
Suddenly, Senjo opened her eyes, stared at the ceiling, and thought for a moment, not intending to conceal it from Su Lun, "I broke through the third tier half a year ago. But because of my talent's second awakening and some special inheritance, my combat power is much stronger than a regular third tier. If I have to say... barely qualifies as fourth tier."
"Oh."
Listening, Su Lun's expression slightly changed.
The conversation that night indeed refreshed his understanding of many aspects of this world.
Su Lun was still pondering what exactly the fourth tier entails when Senjo took the initiative to speak again, "Aren't you curious why we are ambushing that fifth-tier guard leader?"
Su Lun initially thought it might involve some secrets and hadn't intended to probe.
But since she brought it up, he asked, "Why?"
Senjo said, "Advancing to the fourth tier requires a special item—Sun God Stone. The underground world with no sunlight doesn't produce that special energy crystal. However, those super-tier professionals coming from outside the tower might carry it, and their corpses can also accumulate it. If we want to break through the blockades of the Black Tower, we must have enough power. Right now, we are far from it."
Her tone was very calm.
But Su Lun could sense a heaviness in it.
Maybe because he planned to participate in the battle, he felt that Senjo's attitude towards him was clearly different now.
Probably as allies?
In the past, they might have just laughed off things, but now she chose to reveal some top secrets known only to a few to Su Lun.
She then asked, "Want to hear some trouble-invoking secrets?"
Hearing her serious tone, Su Lun thought for a moment before responding, "Yes."
Senjo looked at the ceiling, her gaze drifting as she started to speak.
"When you left Old Lington, didn't I tell you to get stronger?"
"Yes, I remember."
"Actually, I just didn't want you to deal with that kind of pressure too early... just like when I first came across the truth, it was really desperate."
"..."
"When you discover that the world you live in is a giant prison, everything you pursued becomes meaningless. The Black Tower has such a despair-inducing power, so no matter how hard you try, you can only ever barely survive in the dark dungeon. What's the meaning of life then? Until I encountered 'the Mirror'..."
At this point, the gambling-addicted woman suddenly turned around.
She leaned her head on her hand and smiled at Su Lun, "You've been doing quite well, I've been hearing news about you, and know that you've been growing stronger."
"..."
Su Lun listened quietly.
He had never seen Qiān Tiáo so serious before.
Even though she was smiling.
Qiān Tiáo continued to speak.
"Do you know how Old Lington came to be?"
She asked and answered herself.
"About over a hundred years ago, someone found the Black Tower using an ancient map. That person was Raphael I. The current Duke Raphael's grandfather. Back then, Old Lington was just ruins, void of any humans. Then, they filled it with a huge number of war slaves and prisoners from the outside world... The slaves had their memories of the outside world erased, and then they started to pave and propagate in the underground world, establishing a new order..."
"Actually, whether it's the tycoons in the inner city or the commoners in the outer city, there isn't really any difference. Ultimately, everyone is just 'miners' under Duke Raphael, generation after generation mining treasures from this ancient relic from a thousand years ago."
"Those inner city tycoons think the wealth is in their hands? Haha... they are just meat stewing in the pot."
"..."
This message, indeed, felt very heavy.
But Su Lun was a transmigrator, so it wasn't too hard for him to accept.
Ever since he found out his previous identity was sent from outside the Black Tower, he had guessed about the existence of the surface world.
Hearing this, he asked, "Can't the truth be revealed?"
With so many people in Old Lington, a revolutionary uprising would also be a formidable force.
Hearing this, Qiān Tiáo shook her head.
"There was an uprising fifty years ago. That time, the rebels had broken into the Black Tower. Then, the despair began. Unexpectedly, a group of high-class fighters came down from the upper floors, effortlessly slaughtered the leading top professionals... The rebel forces had no power to resist and were rapidly eliminated. Ultimately, the turmoil killed hundreds of thousands of people. Everyone connected to the uprising were annihilated under the charge of 'treason'."
It seems it was already tried...
Hearing this, Su Lun could already imagine the scene at that time.
A group of level 20-30 players storming the tower, then a bunch of level 50-60 bosses appearing.
Swish swish, the knives fall, and the group is wiped out instantly.
This issue seemed to touch some unhappy memories for Qiān Tiáo, her brow slightly furrowed as she continued, "Maybe some old people in Old Lington City still remember, but no one dares to bring it up. Once people from the umbrella organization even catch a hint of this topic, it's an immediate risk of family extermination."
"If all the people of Old Lington truly knew the truth, the only consequence would be, the Black Tower would send top fighters to cleanse the entire 'prison.' Then they would send another batch of people over... To them, miners' lives are simply worthless."
"So, you understand why we had to do it this way, right?"
...
After hearing Qiān Tiáo's story, Su Lun also showed deep contemplation.
If this were for ordinary people, it really would be despairing.
Advancing to the fourth tier requires the [Sun God Stone] which can only be found on the surface, meaning people in the caverns can only ever reach up to the third tier.
If there are fifth tiers outside, there might even be sixth, seventh, or eighth tiers.
Su Lun had completely no concept of such level professionals.
Thinking about it, was it like the difference between ants and elephants?
Many ants might manage to kill an elephant.
But in the world above the Black Tower, there are countless elephants, and perhaps even dinosaurs?
No wonder Mr. Hei and his group this time plan to intercept the fifth tier leader.
The lessons from the uprising fifty years ago had taught them that numbers were useless, and top fighters were the key to deciding the outcome.
If Qiān Tiáo and her group could advance to the fourth tier, perhaps they would have a chance to break through the shackles.

chapters.title: Chapter 185 - 184: Fifth-Order Professionals (Please Subscribe)
chapters.content:
Having discussed the secrets of the dark tower, the conversation shifted back to the current mission.
Qian Tiao seemed a bit tired too and said with her eyes closed, "Su Lun, be careful when the time comes. Although Mr. Hei's plans have never gone awry, I can only ensure that I don't die in battles of that intensity. Chances are, I won't be able to look out for you. Be careful not to die."
"Mhm."
Su Lun listened and smiled.
Not to mention anything else, this gamble-loving woman had always taken good care of him.
His mind was still digesting the shocking information he had heard tonight when suddenly he thought of something else.
Since the topic had come up, Su Lun didn't hesitate and directly asked, "By the way, Sister Qian Tiao, does that '§' symbol on your cloaks have any special meaning?"
As he spoke, he traced the shape of the symbol with his finger in the air, forming two S-shapes.
If it were Mr. Hei, Su Lun, even if curious, wouldn't have asked.
But with Qian Tiao, it wasn't as formal.
If it was something she couldn't disclose, she would directly say "I can't say."
If she could disclose it, it also meant that the information was not too secretive.
At this question, Qian Tiao casually responded, "That symbol represents a talent—[S-003-Fate Controller]. It was the talent that Sir Isaac awoke to. A thousand years ago, it was also the emblem of a special organization in Dawn City. You might have guessed, our organization indeed has some connections with Dawn City, but..."
She suddenly stopped there and changed her tune, "As for the rest, you can ask the boss when the time comes."
"I see..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun inwardly exclaimed, just as he thought.
Back in the [1911 Hotel] in the cursed space, when he saw 'Magician' Edward giving a half-kneel knightly salute to that cloaked figure, he had guessed that there must be some connections between Mr. Hei's "Mirror Organization" and the special operation group from old Dawn City.
As for a symbol representing a talent, he wasn't surprised.
When he saw that one of the five statues at the Storm Manor had this symbol, Su Lun had guessed it was some sort of S-level talent.
But surprisingly, it turned out that Sir Isaac, hailed as "Demigod," was the one who awoke to this strange-sounding talent.
[Fate Controller]?
Ranked higher than his own [Death Reaper], what kind of special abilities might it possess...
Su Lun was somewhat curious.
The "Mirror Organization" used this symbol to signify identity, which clearly held some special meaning.
Since Qian Tiao didn't elaborate, he didn't press further.
As they spoke, Qian Tiao seemed to remember something and added, "Last time at the [1911 Hotel], I heard you performed well. The boss even mentioned you specifically~"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun chuckled.
....
The "Mirror Organization's" hidden identity was the biggest secret in Qian Tiao's heart. Revealing it tonight, she truly regarded Su Lun as one of her own.
As they talked, the conversation flowed more openly.
From the secrets of the dark tower to alchemy, and then onto some personal topics.
They talked until midnight, significantly bringing them closer.
...
The next morning, Su Lun's biological clock accurately woke him from his meditation.
Qian Tiao, on the other half of the bed, was still sound asleep.
This gambling woman really didn't guard against Su Lun at all, that sleeping posture... was truly unrestrained.
Su Lun smiled, pulled the covers up over her, didn't wake her up, and started on his daily tasks.
Reviewing alchemy texts, crafting intrigues, studying mechanical gadgets...
He still needed to prepare for that upcoming ambush.
Although he wasn't the main force, if something unexpected happened, he needed to consider how to escape.
Su Lun had spent the recent times like this, finding nothing amiss with staying in his room.
Busy yet fulfilling, time also quickly flew by.
It wasn't until the afternoon that Sister Qian Tiao finally showed signs of waking.
It seemed she had caught up on the sleep she had missed during the previous two days and nights.
She groggily got out of bed, rubbed her eyes, and complained, "Oh... I was wondering why my dreams kept sounding like a rat gnawing on something. Turns out it's you, kid, messing with these broken pieces of wood early in the morning..."
"It's the afternoon now, Sister Qian..."
Su Lun thought she was talking to him and turned around to look.
But he realized that this gambling-addicted woman wasn't even looking at him; she floated past him as if sleepwalking.
Probably out of habit, Qian took off her bathrobe as soon as she got up in the morning and threw it on the bed, then went naked to the bathroom.
Su Lun watched, touched his forehead, and then his gaze returned to his puppet.
Soon after, he could hear the sound of the shower splashing.
....
Before long, the water stopped.
Su Lun heard someone coming out of the bathroom, but he didn't turn around and continued intently working on his own strange puppet.
The gambling-addicted woman seemed to have woken up after her bath and started dressing loudly in the room.
Seeing Su Lun manipulate eight spider limbs to make puppets simultaneously, she got curious and said, "Wow, you have a nice method there. One person doing the work of seven or eight..."
"I am a Puppet Master, after all."
Su Lun responded.
He glanced up and saw Qian wrapping her chest in the dressing mirror.
He only looked for a moment before averting his eyes and joking softly, "Sister Qian, don't keep wrapping it up. Medically speaking, it's not good for development."
"Tsk~"
Qian hummed indifferently, came over, picked up a half-finished "Nightmare Doll" from the table, and observed, "Your rune craftsmanship is quite impressive. Being able to draw second-level runes so proficiently, you'd be considered a top-tier rune enchanter in Old Lington."
"Still a long way off..."
Su Lun responded offhandedly.
It wasn't false modesty; his skill really was far from Mr. Hei's level.
The two of them were very close, skin touching, and he could clearly feel Qian's body temperature.
Although the gambling-addicted woman didn't use perfume, Su Lun also smelled a faint fragrance on her.
Ah...the scent of soapnut shampoo.
Qian only looked briefly, seemingly uninterested in the puppet, and set it down.
She went to the dressing mirror and tied up her lush green hair with a red cord.
Immediately, she looked spirited and bold.
Qian didn't wear makeup or fancy clothes, making her extremely efficient when going out.
She slipped on her kimono sleeves, covering the tattoos across her back and arms, and waved grandly at Su Lun, "Let's go, kid Su Lun, time to head out."
"Oh."
Su Lun thought there was some action, so he packed up his things and followed her out.
What he didn't expect was,
Qian directly took him to the gambling den,
and gambled heavily again.
Indeed, if a gambler has money in their pocket, they think about gambling.
But fortunately, the nearly nine million Qian had left from last night was all gone after not too long.
Now she was quiet.
For the following days,
the two of them stayed quietly in the hotel room.
Su Lun didn't feel any different having another person there, life went on as usual.
Even many times, when it involved knowledge from top professional fields, he could still ask Qian.
But this gambling-addicted woman became quite dull; without gambling, she kept complaining, "I have no happiness," or just slept a lot.
Ah... and also, she increasingly did not consider herself an outsider in the shared room.
...
Six days later, news from Mr. Hei arrived.
Finally, the team of Princess Theresa from the Duke's residence had set off.
Su Lun and Qian Tiao left the camp and headed for the designated ambush site.
It is worth mentioning that the team from the Duke's residence did not take the three routes familiar to the caravan, but chose a secret passage instead.
It was the same secret passage Su Lun had used when he crossed over to this place.
There had been no news about this passage, and Su Lun thought he was the only one who knew about it.
Unexpectedly, not only did the people from the Duke's residence know about it, but Mr. Hei and his associates were also well aware of it.
The map was very detailed.
Su Lun had an eight-armed spider spear, and Qian Tiao was a top professional, so they moved quickly.
In just half a day, they had already reached the designated ambush site.
It was a spacious cavern.
The area was large, with several passageways that could be used for a quick retreat.
....
Su Lun looked around the environment and immediately found a suitable place for hiding and launching a stealth attack.
Qian Tiao pointed to the expansive cave and said, "Alright, you stay here. Just find a place to hide and be careful not to be discovered. We will lure them here later, and everything will proceed according to the plan."
This gambling-addicted woman was wearing a suit of battle armor today, and her face showed a seriousness Su Lun had never seen before.
Before they set off, Su Lun had felt that she was constantly accumulating blade energy.
Her aura had also become increasingly dangerous.
Even though she deliberately restrained herself, standing next to her, Su Lun felt as if he was next to a sharp blade edge, causing a faint sense of dread.
The plan was thoroughly memorized; there was nothing more to explain. Su Lun nodded and said, "Hmm."
"Be careful yourself."
Qian Tiao warned him, then disappeared into the depths of the cave without further words.
The first ambush site was not here; this cavern was only the location for the kill.
Su Lun looked around the cavern, then unfastened his gear and climbed the rock wall with his eight-armed spider spear.
He used silk threads to hang himself upside down on the rock wall, and the invisible zombie also hid nearby.
There were no traps here.
The plan was simple and brutal, someone was to attack the team of Princess Theresa, but the actual target was one of the guards.
To lure the man here, then kill him.
As Mr. Hei said, the simpler the plan, the less likely it is to be seen through.
The more complex the trap, the more likely there are to be flaws.
....
After hanging on the web, Su Lun was like a spider patiently waiting for its prey, not making any noise thereafter.
During that time, he even saw two groups of three assassins rushing past.
He knew they were the professional assassins from the princess's team responsible for scouting.
They were there to check the safety of the road, eliminate traps, and ensure the team's safety.
Su Lun didn't dare to be careless and opened his senses, focusing intently on listening to the noises within the cave.
Finally, after waiting almost a whole day, a sound like mountains collapsing came from deep within the cave.
"They're here!"
Hearing the noise, Su Lun instantly became alert.
The sound of battle came from the cave, at first imperceptible, but soon roaring like thunder, making his scalp tingle.
"Hiss~ that's a bit too exaggerated."
Su Lun took in a breath of cold air.
Although he was mentally prepared, feeling the violent fluctuations of elements in the air, he also felt a sudden thrill.
He hadn't even seen it face-to-face yet, but the noises alone were enough to make his hair stand on end, let alone the terror of the battle itself.
"With a thousand words to say, an ordinary third-tier professional wouldn't stand a chance of escaping under that 'target'!"
He slowly inhaled and then minimized the sound of his existence to the lowest.
He restrained his emotions, leaving only a numbing calm in his eyes.
....
Just a few moments after the noise of the battle reached them, several figures dashed out.
Before they arrived, Su Lun heard the sound of the mechanical propulsion devices and immediately guessed that they were super mechanical warriors—Number 19!
Su Lun dared not stare directly, his gaze scattered, and he saw a sturdy red giant accompanying Number 19.
"A Stage Two 'Red Demon' awakening?"
Su Lun looked at the man and immediately recognized his talent.
But this Red Demon was much stronger than the 'Red Demon' Goron he had seen at the Cross Association before!
The Red Demon before him was not only red-skinned and muscled but also covered in a layer of lava armor, with flames spilling out a foot all around. The entire figure resembled a lava giant stepping out of a volcano's mouth, possessing such formidable defenses that Su Lun even felt a "Quadruple Shot" might not harm him.
Alongside this Red Demon and Number 19, there was another cloaked figure.
At this moment, a fiery, six-armed Rakshasa Woman's phantom materialized behind the cloaked figure, and even though the cloak covered her face, Su Lun knew this was the formidable Qian Tiao.
Right now, Qian Tiao displayed her never before seen six-armed state, her momentum sharp to the utmost.
Yet even with these three top-tier powerhouses joining forces, they were being chased in a wretched flight!
Whether it was the Stage Two Red Demon, Number 19, or Qian Tiao, none seemed capable of standing a single round.
At a touch, they were sent flying, crashing into a pile of shattered rocks.
The cannon-like noises in the cave came from these three individuals being frequently thrown about.
The three struggled collectively, covering for one another just to avoid being killed!
Behind them, a surging golden light approached.
...
Su Lun dared not directly face that "target," but the sheer aura of the golden light was like a collapsing mountain, instilling an innate terror as if beholding a great horror.
"What a domineering aura, is this a fifth-tier powerhouse..."
Su Lun murmured to himself.
In the blink of an eye, the group had already reached inside the grotto.
As the target reached the ambush spot, suddenly a purple light screen appeared in the surrounding space.
"A spatial barrier?"
Su Lun looked familiarly, neither surprised nor unexpected.
What surprised him more was that at that moment, he watched in disbelief as two cloaked figures emerged from the darkness nearby.
Yes, they walked right out of the darkness!
He didn't know by what means they used, appearing from the shadow of a rock without warning. It was like a portal, yet no spatial fluctuations were felt.
Su Lun was astonished; he'd hidden for a day and, incredibly, had failed to notice two people hidden a few dozen meters away!
Once the barrier was established, the battle began immediately.
One of them deployed an advanced spell "Thorn Entanglement" as soon as they acted.
Seeing the proficiency of the move, Su Lun thought it was probably Mr. Hei!
The other cloaked figure, upon emerging from the shadow, turned completely into a purple ghostly light, then vanished without a trace—clearly a top-tier assassin!
...
Su Lun looked at the base of the shadow on the ground, guessing that the golden light seemed to be a two-meter-tall gilded giant.
Mr. Hei's "Thorn Entanglement" took root and rapidly wrapped around the legs of the golden target, binding him tight.
But it only held for a moment before the gilded giant tore apart the entangling thorns.
A scornful sneer echoed in the sealed space.
"So you were targeting me..."
Even though ambushed, this fifth-tier professional did not seem to hold any regard for his opponents, scoffing, "Didn't expect...after several years without cleaning, the rats in the sewer have grown this fat...
PS. Brothers, if you can support a subscription, please do so, thank you!

chapters.title: Chapter 186 - 185 Elemental Theft
chapters.content:
The gilded giant realized that Mr. Hei and his group were planning to ambush him, but far from being alarmed, he instead revealed a mocking smile.
After all, the gap in their ranks was not something a little scheming could bridge.
Since there was now a spatial lockdown in the cave, Mr. Hei and his four companions no longer needed to hide their presence.
The five of them wasted no time in idle talk, showing their hidden tools right away.
In an instant, the five's momentum drastically changed; encircling him, they almost seemed to match the gilded giant in strength.
"Take action!"
In front of such a powerful opponent, they couldn't afford to be careless at all, as even a slight mistake could cause a fatal crisis.
The first to strike was the assassin who had vanished earlier.
Although Su Lun couldn't see him, he could distinctly hear the intense crackling of thunder elements in the air.
Looking closely, he saw the gilded giant's body surge with thunder lights, as if a very fast shadow was darting around him. In just an instant, it turned into several chains of purple thunder as thick as arms.
The thunder chains, composed of elemental disruptions, had no physical form, but the moment they formed, the gilded giant was bound on the spot.
When the gilded giant forcefully pulled at them, the thunder exploded, yet he found that the chains were elastic, and he couldn't break them with sheer strength alone.
His eyes narrowing slightly, he seemed to have guessed something and exclaimed with surprise and disdain, "Elemental thunder chains? Tsk, tsk... You bunch of rats have indeed found some nice toys..."
But with a cold snort, he dismissed it completely, "Too bad, how much power can you wield with such high-level cursed items? It would have been wise to keep it hidden; since you so wish to seek death, let me fulfill your wish!"
...
The thunder chains hindered the gilded giant's movements but couldn't completely immobilize him.
While speaking, his veins bulged on his hands, and he abruptly pulled the chains to form a seal, the sorcerer's seal, igniting an eruption of gold elements around him. His skin then started to form scales like an armadillo across his entire body, elevating his aura several levels higher.
At this moment, even with the thunder chains wrapped around him, his speed was as fast as before!
The gilded giant stomped fiercely and charged toward Mr. Hei and his group at the forefront.
Although Su Lun dared not stare directly at the target, he didn't know exactly what happened.
But merely the oppressive feeling of that golden light made him feel as if a gold torrent had swept over him, with a crushing momentum.
Like the flash of lightning, the enclosed space resounded with a "thud" like a bell, echoing throughout.
A red molten giant clashed head-on with the gilded giant.
The shockwave, like a tsunami hitting the coast, made the entire space tremble violently.
The few top professionals were unaffected, but there was still a small fry among them.
In the moment of impact, Su Lun only felt as if his head was right next to a cannon's barrel, rattled so violently that his expression flickered as if his soul were about to leave his body. Unconsciously, a trickle of blood had already flowed from his ears, while the continuous shockwaves still pierced through his eardrums...
Su Lun's eyes narrowed gravely, "Such a degree of combat really isn't something a tier-two professional could partake in..."
If it weren't for him blocking some pain perceptions, that aftershock would have really cost him heavily.
Forcing his scattered senses to refocus, he still hung upside down on the wall, like a rock, without making any movement.
....
The astonishing repercussions of their collision alone begged the question: How intense was the battle between the combatants?
The Red Demon caught the gold-lacquered giant's punch but immediately spat out a mouthful of black blood.
A direct hit from a fifth-tier combatant is indeed not easy to withstand!
Yet the Red Demon did not let go—his arms bulging with muscles, he performed a grappling lock technique that resembled hugging a pillar and instantly immobilized the golden arm. His body burst into flames suddenly, transforming into a magma giant, and he slowly drew the gold-scaled arm into his own body.
For a moment, the blazing heat seemed to melt the golden scales.
The Red Demon's talent already significantly amplified his strength, and after awakening a second time, he possessed the strength to move mountains. Even so, it was exceedingly difficult to shake the golden giant.
Seeing this, the gold-lacquered giant merely smirked.
Perhaps feeling assured of victory, he mocked in a leisurely manner, "A Fire Art 'Art of Gold Melting'? Quite a clever idea. But you have no idea how vast the difference between our ranks really is. The difference in the grade of our spells is not something a bit of cleverness can compensate for."
As he spoke, a Seven-Pointed Star Alchemy Formation suddenly lit up under the gold-lacquered giant's feet, and he uttered softly, "Flesh Alchemy·Indestructible!"
With this technique initiated, the scales all over the giant suddenly bristled, creating an eye-piercing sharpness, reminiscent of a hedgehog.
Even more shocking was that, upon the release of his fifth-tier spell, the bright gold dazzled the eyes, and the rich blood-like Seven-Pointed Star Formation under the Red Demon's feet suddenly dimmed. In an instant, it seemed as though the fire elements around them had been drained by the fifth-tier formation.
"Is this the fifth-tier professional's control over elements?"
Upon witnessing this phenomenon, Su Lun immediately recalled from the alchemy texts, "Rank Suppression! Elemental Plundering!"
Alchemy spells rely on an equivalent exchange with the surrounding elemental forces.
But the elemental energy in a given area is limited; how much can be converted and controlled depends entirely on the magician's power.
If two magicians cast spells at the same time, the one with the higher-tier spell/magician can plunder more elemental energy, even forcibly assimilating the lower-tier magician's spell into their needed higher-tier spell.
This is the disparity in ranks!
With this move, the scorching heat of the Red Demon was instantly quelled as if cold water had been thrown over him, and he could no longer trouble the golden giant.
Just after he had merged the fist into his body, not only did it not melt the arm, but the reversed scales exploded within him like thousands of needles, causing severe damage in an instant.
"Pff—" Another mouthful of magma-like black blood spurted out, scorching the ground and creating a puff of blue smoke.
The Red Demon, whose tier-three, section-two talents had awakened, faced a severe injury from confronting head-on.
But it wasn't for nothing!
His delaying also created an opportunity for Mr. Hei and the others to make their move.
....
As the gold and the red collided, Su Lun suddenly noticed a Seven-Pointed Star seal lighting up under Mr. Hei's feet, and upon observing the sequence of his seals, he realized it was a technique for unlocking inhibited gear.
"Fourth-tier implantation? So Mr. Hei has advanced to the fourth tier..."
Su Lun watched, greatly surprised, having never seen Mr. Hei's alchemical implantation before.
The sorcerer's seals were formed in an instant, the space within the seal suddenly transformed, turning into a library filled with bookshelves. On the mahogany shelves, there were densely packed various gold-stamped books.
What was strange, however, was that although the titles on the books were visibly clear, upon closer inspection, they became a blur.
Moreover, what was even more shocking was that a vast starry sky had appeared above the library.
At a glance, the stars were brilliant and the depths seemed limitless, the more one looked, the more magical it felt. It was as if it wanted to suck in one's gaze, making it impossible to look away.
Being extremely sensitive to spiritual power now, Su Lun looked at Mr. Hei's attire and immediately guessed something, "Does the attire include a spiritual spell? Could this be the very dangerous spiritual power secret technique that Mr. Hei mentioned he was practicing?"
"What a strange attire, actually being a library..."
While Su Lun was reflecting, he suddenly felt very odd.
He also realized that this might be related to Mr. Hei's profession as a Scholar.
Moreover, Mr. Hei was clearly also considering that there was still a second-tier professional individual. Fearing that the remnants of the battle would affect him, he had set up a bookshelf in front of Su Lun.
And it wasn't over yet!
When Mr. Hei deactivated his attire, his hands forming the sorcerer's seals had not stopped at all.
His entire being seemed to merge with the library, as numerous Seven-Pointed Star Magic Formations lit up on countless volumes.
In the center of the library, the gold-painted giant, aiming to capitalize on its victory, intended to land a few more punches to kill the Red Demon.
But observing the changing scenery around him, he frowned for the first time in a serious tone, muttering to himself, "He has already advanced to the fourth tier, and even merged with an attire like 'All-Embracing Abode.' No wonder he was confident enough to take action."
While muttering, he suddenly pulled out his arm, no longer concerning himself with the gravely injured Red Demon.
Instead, he charged fiercely toward Mr. Hei.
He wanted to eliminate the existence he perceived as the greatest threat first!
....
A professional capable of advancing to the fifth tier obviously wasn't foolish.
Previously lured there, the gold-painted giant had also guessed that this might be a strategy.
But he didn't mind.
He also wanted to see where the "rats'" companions were, so he could capture them all in one net!
A rat, no matter how fat, is still just a rat!
The strongest in the underground world are merely third-tier professionals; even with an ambush, he felt no threat!
But now, seeing Mr. Hei, who had advanced to the fourth tier, the gold-painted giant felt a threat for the first time.
The opponent, knowing he was a fifth-tier professional, dared to lock down the space and initiate a fight, must be confident in his ability.
The moment the library emerged, he faintly realized there seemed to be an invisible net closing in, giving him the sensation of being completely seen through. It was as if... his own underestimating attitude had also been part of the calculation.
Although the gold-painted giant still believed the individuals before him were mere rats easily crushed, observing Mr. Hei calmly forming seals, his instinct told him...
This man must be killed first!
....
Su Lun had seen Mr. Hei take action before, back at the ruins when he watched Mr. Hei seamlessly transitioning between advanced magic of four different types, which had stunned everyone.
But the aura of Mr. Hei now was completely different!
The set of intricate and complex sorcerer's seals in his hand illuminated the gold volumes in the library with a golden light, clearly displaying a fourth-tier gold-type spell.
The intricate patterning of the seals that lit up on the Seven-Pointed Star left Su Lun feeling as oppressed as when he first saw the runes on the blue-skinned living corpse in the basement of Green Street 88.
This spell, clearly more complex than any he had seen before.
Before he could ponder further, the two were already clashing.
How fast was that gold-painted giant?
With a stomp, he shot out like a cannonball, charging a hundred meters. That astonishing speed contrasted starkly with his hulking giant physique.
Yet it seemed as if the timing was entirely calculated.
As the gold-painted giant charged, Mr. Hei's final sorcerer's seal was also ready. He clapped his hands as if activating some special law; suddenly, the gold element in the space stalled, merging completely with the enormous 'All-Embracing Abode.'
Just a second earlier, the gold-painted giant, seeing Mr. Hei using a gold-type spell, had a hint of disdain in his eyes.
Facing a fifth-tier gold-type magician with a gold-type spell, what a foolish choice?
But just as his scorn was emerging in a hum, he suddenly sensed an anomaly in the flow of elements around him, his expression changing instantly as he exclaimed in his heart, "This isn't a normal secret technique... he... he actually knows 'Elemental Theft'!"
Mr. Hei paid no heed to the fist now nearly reaching him, his hand gestures changing: "Merge!"
At that moment, a bizarre scene unfolded.
The gold lacquer on the gold-painted giant, solid like gold armor, began to flow like melting wax, pooling on the ground.
Just now, in order to swiftly kill several individuals, this entity had condensed a large amount of gold element in the sealed space.
This left others with no elements to utilize!
Yet now, the thick gold element filling the space, instead of aiding the gold-painted giant, had become a quagmire due to the altered state of the elements, as if turned into a marsh, slowing him down more and more, almost trapping him completely!
...
Under normal circumstances, a fifth-tier spell against a fourth-tier spell would undoubtedly be crushed in one strike due to the disparity in tier.
The gap between their levels was not something that could be compensated for by any ordinary spell or secret technique.
But Mr. Hei, the magician, chose not to clash directly; he chose "Theft"!
He stole the gold elements condensed by the gold-painted giant, directly altering the state of the elements, giving a strong impression of "using the enemy's strength against him."
Employing what was perhaps less than one-tenth of the strength, he manipulated the full force of his enemy.
"What a masterful tactic!"
While Su Lun could not comprehend the intricacies of the spell, based on his current understanding of Alchemy, he guessed the principle behind Mr. Hei's tactics.
