To cleverly solve a spell means you need a thorough understanding of that spell.
This meant that although Mr. Hei was not a fifth-tier, he must have a profound understanding of fifth-tier spells!
Realizing this, he couldn't help but be amazed: "Just how much knowledge is stashed in Mr. Hei's mind..."

chapters.title: Chapter 187 - 186 The Terror of Mind Reading Technique
chapters.content:
Thoughts flooded his mind, yet reality's battle passed in just an instant.
Mr. Hei's move directly created an opportunity for the others to strike.
Number Nineteen pulled out a mechanical fist bigger than her thigh and mounted it on her arm.
Having retreated earlier, she hadn't dared to wear these heavy, agility-impairing gauntlets, but now, trapped in battle, she had no reservations.
Considering its archaic design, it seemed not a product of modern technology, but rather an ancient alchemical creation.
With one charging motion, blue energy runes immediately lit up. On that pair of fists, ripples that seemed to distort space visibly gathered...
Meanwhile, Qian Tiao had switched to wielding a red and a black long sword.
With dark spiritual power infusion, one blade glimmered with an eerie red glow, while the other was jet black, with dark mist swirling around it.
More terrifying was the sword qi accumulating around her, which was so sharp that it gave onlookers a piercing sensation just from her gaze.
At this moment, Qian Tiao seemed to have used some secret technique, her aura soaring ever higher, and the formidable sword qi on her back faintly merged with the fiery shadow of Rakshasa Woman behind her...
Looking again at the vanished assassin, he had already quietly appeared behind the giant, his dark green poison dagger fiercely stabbing towards the giant's back.
....
The gold elements on the Armored Strongman's body shifted from solid to fluid, greatly reducing his defense.
He had sensed this attack coming—though his movements were restricted, his reaction was not a bit slow.
"Ha!"
He gasped sharply and immediately counterattacked with a punch rich in gold elements. The assassin, unable to dodge in time, was hit directly in the waist and spat a mouthful of blood while still in midair.
Su Lun glanced sharply, knowing such a punch landing on the heavily armored Red Demon might not be lethal, but on the fragile assassin...
Before he could fully form his thought of danger, the assassin's body in his vision suddenly disintegrated into a mass of lightning and vanished.
"Elemental Talent 'A-039-Lei'?!"
Su Lun, watching the lightning fill his vision, finally confirmed the man's talent.
Moreover, this was another professional with a second awakening.
A normal 'Lei' talent signifies an extraordinary affinity for thunder elements, a natural trait for a thunder magician. But here in the Mirror Organization, this man is a close-combat assassin.
Once his body disintegrated, he instantly shed most of the punch's force.
And just as the assassin disintegrated, Qian Tiao's blades arrived simultaneously.
The Armored Strongman had calculated his punch well, intending to strike fatally and withdraw to defend. But unexpectedly, his target disintegrated. Unable to dissipate the force, his entire balance shifted.
This slight error, in the eyes of top-level fighters, was a massive vulnerability.
Qian Tiao's dual blades, one red, one black, sliced across his neck, emitting a "zipping" sound of metal being cleaved.
At the same time, Number Nineteen's charged punch also hit the Armored Strongman's flank, unleashing a spiraling force that exploded like a muffled thunder, blasting him completely off his feet!
With a "thud" of metal clashing, sparks flew everywhere.
The Armored Strongman fell like a meteor, causing the whole library to shake.
"Is he dead?"
Hidden in the distance, Su Lun sucked in a breath of cold air as he watched the trio's coordinated assault.
Any single move from that trio could have instantly killed him.
With the three attacking together, there was no escape.
Moreover...
Upon closer inspection, the weapons in their hands were all bizarrely effective ancient arms!
The assassin's dagger seemed to have some deadly poison. Although the dagger didn't completely penetrate, breaking through the defense meant it was largely successful.
As for Number Nineteen, just that one charged punch from her mechanical fist could probably smash an armored tank, let alone the guy taking the hit.
And Qian Tiao's thunderous dual strikes left two gashes nearly two fingers deep on the neck of the Armored Strongman.
But...
It seemed there was also metal inside the wounds, no blood visible?
In the next instant, Su Lun's pupils shrank as he noticed the spot where the Armored Strongman had fallen.
"No, he's not dead!"
Without seeing a rise of ash, he knew that man hadn't been killed!
....
"Heh..."
A laugh rang out as the Armored Strongman slowly stood up, his wounds visibly healing.
Cut, stab, punch marks... his body's metal surface seemed to have a memory, rapidly restoring to its original state.
Although he'd sustained minor injuries, he wasn't alarmed but rather pleased.
Because he felt he had fully grasped the strength of the few people before him.
The slight apprehension he had earlier had also dissipated,
even with a full-force blow of that degree,
he couldn't be killed.
The gilt giant stood up, not only recovering from his injuries, but his golden scales on his skin congealed once again, enshrouded in a hazy mist that resembled fine, sharp metallic air.
He looked at Mr. Hei and others, no longer in a rush to take action, scoffing, "Secondary talent awakening, ancient curses, extraordinary legacies... I must admit, your performance has truly surprised me. Heh heh... Those fools at 'Umbrella Organization' are really useless, to think they never noticed that the rats in the gutter had already gained the ability to bite."
Su Lun, not far away, furrowed his brows slightly upon hearing this.
Even though he was a transmigrator, the repeated term "rats" felt rather harsh to him. People from Old Lington really weren't regarded as humans in the eyes of the Black Tower folks.
However, it seemed like these words were meant to deliberately provoke Mr. Hei and his group?
Moreover, mockery was secondary.
Three melee combatants had exhausted their methods just now and hadn't inflicted any effective damage on the gilt giant.
Su Lun also felt that the current battle situation seemed very unfavorable for them.
The gap in level made the refinement of dark spiritual power and elements fundamentally different.
"A wooden knife" can carve into "stone," which already marks a remarkable swordsmanship skill.
But the gaps in density and material are irremediable!
The black scythe could likely ignore the armored defense and deliver a killing blow, but Su Lun felt that he had no chance of hitting his target.
The reaction speed of a fifth-order strongman, any stealth attack was utterly uncertain.
Su Lun felt that any attempt to swing his scythe would surely be noticed and evaded.
By then, keeping the black scythe as a hidden trump card would become utterly meaningless.
Fortunately, upon looking, Mr. Hei was as calm as ever.
Su Lun thus patiently continued to wait for an opportunity to take action.
....
The gilt giant had not died, and Mr. Hei seemed not at all surprised, since he had been constantly preparing some spell since earlier.
He seemed to have also seen through the "sharp metal air" on the gilt giant's surface and even took the time while making his seals to remind his companions, "This guy is practicing the fifth-order Flesh Alchemy — 'Vajra.' Don't attack recklessly, physical damage will be reflected back in equal measure. This technique cannot cover the whole body during movement, the bigger the movement, the bigger the flaw. Wait for the opportunity, find the flaw!"
Upon hearing this, his companions instantly understood and quickly drew back.
Hearing his technique's "weak point" revealed, the Armored Strongman's brow furrowed.
The solemnity that had just dissipated from his face reappeared, the other four posed no threat. But observing this cloaked figure, he instinctively felt a deep apprehension, as if all his secrets were being spied upon.
His earlier use of "Elemental Steal" had already put him at a slight disadvantage, and now this man had discerned the foundation of his fifth-order technique at a glance.
How did he manage this?
He must kill him first!
The gilt giant's thoughts surged, and with a fierce stomp, his body transformed into a streak of golden light rushing forward.
"Bang!"
A loud boom occurred as the golden light collided directly with Mr. Hei.
However, it was not the real person he collided with, but a withered tree used as a dummy stake.
The true body of Mr. Hei had already quietly teleported a hundred meters away.
"Puppet tricks! Mr. Hei sure knows a lot of miscellaneous stuff..."
Su Lun watched the scene before him, a Puppet Master himself, naturally familiar with this technique.
The key was, he was proficient in so many diverse areas...
This was truly enviable.
.....
The gilt giant was unbothered by the unsuccessful strike.
The sealed space indeed restricted his movements, but it also restricted everyone within the space!
Having just smashed that stake, he abruptly stopped and changed direction, barrelling toward another figure that had appeared to the left.
Knowing the enemy's technique specifics, the several fighters also refrained from launching hasty attacks, simply observing the Armored Strongman charging back and forth across the space.
"Bang!"
The second stake was shattered.
"Bang!"
The third stake was shattered.
Each interval was shorter than the last, making it seem that Mr. Hei was increasingly struggling to dodge.
It appeared the next punch might be fatal.
But crucially, it did not result in death.
As if all calculations were just perfect.
It prompted the golden giant to charge relentlessly again and again...
....
"What kind of spell has Mr. Hei triggered that it's taking so long..."
Su Lun, looking at the battle before him and seeing that Qian Tiao San Ren had no intention of helping as they were gathering strength, guessed that Mr. Hei was probably conjuring some extremely powerful spell.
The golden giant had guessed as much too, and its attacks became increasingly fierce.
Unfortunately,
It failed to kill Mr. Hei in several encounters,
and it was already too late!
Mr. Hei's spell had already been fully cast.
Once the sorcerer's seals stopped, a strange phenomenon suddenly arose in this sealed space.
Looking up again, the previously sparkling new stars on the library's celestial floor suddenly shone brightly, eerily transforming into eyes. Countless indifferent gazes descended from above, watching everyone in the space like the scrutiny of a deity, making one's skin crawl.
On another look, the cloaked Mr. Hei's aura suddenly became elusive. This gave Su Lun a very strange feeling, as if all the countless hollow eyes in the sky were Mr. Hei's eyes.
At this moment, no secret could be hidden.
"Has Mr. Hei's 'Mind Reading Technique' been activated?"
Su Lun guessed what it was, but since the spell wasn't targeting him, he didn't feel much.
The golden giant, however, discovered something and its expression drastically changed.
It charged again, but its punch didn't hit a wooden post but was easily dodged by Mr. Hei.
Another punch, dodged again...
Yet another punch...
Yet another punch...
None of the punches hit!
Once the spell succeeded, the situation turned.
Mr. Hei seemingly foresaw every move of his, dancing around gracefully, always precisely evading.
He was like a matador, who, far less strong than the bull, easily avoided the deadly horns.
The golden giant frantically swung his punches like a mad demon, the wind from his fists stirring sand and stones, yet he could not touch Mr. Hei at all.
Su Lun watching this miraculous scene, was so shocked he couldn't speak: "Is this... still a C-level talent?"
He could see clearly that Mr. Hei had turned a normally considered impractical ability, the Mind Reading Technique, into something formidable.
This simple mind reading was making a rank five warrior run around in circles.
Even though that guy was highly skilled, every punch landed on nothing, unable to even brush Mr. Hei's clothes.
This was no longer prediction, but a complete awareness of what the opponent would do next.
Every move was prevented at its inception.
From the moment the opponent formed a thought, a countermeasure was already in place.
This terrifying level of mind reading was unstoppable.
Even if the enemy reacted quickly, realizing the need to change tactics, as soon as a thought arose, Mr. Hei read it through his "mind reading."
Change or not, both were unsuccessful.
Mr. Hei had predicted every move of the enemy,
and that overwhelming fear of being completely controlled gradually engulfed the golden giant's heart.
....
Su Lun also noticed that Mr. Hei seemed to excel in controlling abilities, his attacking means were clearly his weakness.
While he could evade the attacks of a rank five close-combatant, he struggled to harm him.
However, Mr. Hei was not alone!
At that moment, the pair of eyes in the sky seemed to see through something, and Mr. Hei sharply shouted, "His vulnerability is in the back of his left thigh!"
Before his words fell, the already charged Qian Tiao San Ren immediately seized the opportunity and charged forward.
With the three of them cooperating, the golden giant avoided two, but was stabbed in the back of the left thigh by the lightning assassin.
"Swoosh!"
This time, the poison-tipped dagger slipped in much easier, piercing through and leaving a bloody hole.
Whereas the rest of this guy's muscles were as if forged from pure gold, the skin on this back leg was merely a layer of hardened shell; the knife puncturing it caused blood to spurt out.
"Defense broken!"
From a distance, Su Lun saw this scene and couldn't help feeling delighted.
Seeing blood meant that this guy's defense wasn't as invincible as it appeared.
Breaking the defense meant... he could be killed!
It was as if a feather had been added to a balanced scale, tipping the situation.
For the first time truly injured, a look of panic finally appeared on the face of the golden-painted giant.
The feeling of being calculated at every step rendered him unable to utilize his abilities, like a mouse gnawing at the soft flesh inside his mouth, perfectly capable of killing this tiny creature easily yet completely helpless against it.
He hastily gathered elements to cover his wound. However, the deadly poison on the dagger penetrated his meridians, causing him to stagger and nearly fall.
And just then, Mr. Hei's eerie voice sounded again, "The weak spot is on the right side, ninth rib!"
Hearing this, the golden-painted giant instinctively pulled back his arm to shield his lower ribs.
Although he reacted in time and wasn't injured, being continuously exposed made him dare not attack as recklessly as before.
And with his hesitation, the three fighters found they could fight more freely.
"The weak spot is on the right arm!"
"He's about to cast the area spell 'Flowing Gold Barrage', dodge in mid-air..."
"The weak spot is in the lower abdomen!"
"This leg wind has elemental cutting, tilt up 35°..."
"This punch can hit from a distance, Nineteen, be careful!"
"That's 'Metal Storm', don't move and it won't hurt..."
"The weak spot is..."
Mr. Hei repeatedly announced the weak spots, and the golden-painted giant repeatedly felt alarm.
No matter what moves or spells he used, they were all preemptively seen through, limiting his actions at every turn.
Although the few "mice" in front of him were knocked back by punches time and again, their tactical coordination and foresight meant they couldn't be killed!
Plus, there was a cloaked figure who, despite being elusive, always seemed to have another move waiting for him.
After being wounded multiple times, the golden-painted giant began to feel ominous and even dared not take the initiative to attack, only able to defend passively.
.....
Through this "explanation" by Mr. Hei, Su Lun understood the principle of the fifth-tier spell "Vajra."
If this guy doesn't move, he's virtually an iron turtle, impregnable.
But the moment he teleports, the gold elements can't cover his entire body fast enough, exposing his weak spots.
The ensuing battle had no suspense.
Mr. Hei completely grasped the enemy's mental strategy; no matter what he intended to do, it was clearly "called out."
The trio handled it more and more easily, slashing the enemy with injuries, seeing a hopeful kill, but the golden-painted giant then began to play dirty. Knowing that he was at a disadvantage, he simply stood his ground and went all out.
This guy had incredibly strong physical and magical defenses, making it hard for spells below fifth-tier to kill him.
Since you can't kill me, I'll just stand here waiting for reinforcements, seeing who can outlast whom.
Moreover, to be safe, he even took out a cursed golden sphere, which, when squeezed, covered him in an additional layer of heavy armor.
Now, the trio really couldn't do anything to him.
No matter how much they chopped or hammered, they were only inflicting superficial injuries.
Seeing this, Su Lun finally understood the role Mr. Hei had called him for.
From the beginning, Mr. Hei had anticipated this outcome.
....
Since the golden-painted giant gave up on teleportation, Mr. Hei and the others didn't hold back; the Thunder Chain wrapped around him over and over again, various control spells layered around him.
To move meant being struck by the blade.
To stay still meant being bound tighter and tighter.
Finally, after he gave up struggling, he was firmly trapped in place.
A fixed target, foolproof operation.
Su Lun didn't hesitate, controlling a zombie to deliver a slashing strike.
"Shua~"
A gigantic head thunderously hit the ground.
Regardless of your invincible defense, if you can't surpass the laws of the Black Scythe, you'll be cut in two.
Su Lun watched the "mist" rising from the nearby corpse, his anticipation bubbling forth.

chapters.title: Chapter 188 - 187: The World
chapters.content:
Only when the head of the fifth-order gilded giant fell and the grey mist began to emerge did Su Lun confirm that he had died.
The battle seemed perilous, with the second-phase Red Demon critically wounded, and the others from Thousand Paths sustaining various degrees of serious injuries.
But, in fact, it was not the case.
Seeing Mr. Hei remain composed throughout, Su Lun knew that things were probably within this man's control.
Su Lun had observed the entire battle,
and now, upon reflection,
he also noticed some discrepancies.
He guessed that Mr. Hei must have encountered fifth-order professionals before, or at least was clear about the capabilities of a fifth-order.
That's why his calculations were so precise.
Otherwise, to set up an ambush for a completely unknown fifth-order powerhouse, they would not have come with only five people.
It was as if everything was just right, not revealing more of the "Mirror Organization's" forces than necessary, just enough to kill him.
Moreover, Su Lun felt that even without the Reaper, Mr. Hei probably had other methods to kill the guy.
If one were to mention sealed artifacts, those top experts likely had no shortage in their hands.
After all, Su Lun had witnessed them possessing a "Volgan's Furnace Lamp."
Dawn Relic was a treasure trove, hiding too many high-order alchemy products from the ancient times.
"Mirror Organization" definitely had plenty of good stuff at their disposal.
Just like the weapons used by Thousand Paths during the fight earlier, they were clearly out of the ordinary.
Thoughts whirred through his mind, connecting one "coincidence" after another.
Su Lun felt as if he understood something.
Ever since he found out that the "§" symbol of the Mirror Organization was the mark of Sir Isaac of Dawn City, he had guessed that this organization's understanding of that ancient history buried in the dust far surpassed the Black Tower's.
He vaguely felt that Mr. Hei knew about the issues with his own talent through certain channels.
After all, the origin of his talent was the altar at Storm Manor.
....
The grey mist was right before his eyes, but Su Lun wasn't in a rush, and he casually walked over.
It was like visiting an elder's home; however tempting the food was, you couldn't just help yourself without the host's permission.
Having successfully killed the enemy, the cloaked figures quickly cleaned up any traces at the scene and then dismantled the sealing barrier.
They nodded towards Mr. Hei without saying much, much like last time, and dispersed on their own.
From the end of the battle to their departure, it took only three to five seconds.
Only Mr. Hei and Su Lun were left on the scene.
Mr. Hei removed his cloak, revealing his characteristic amiable smile.
As expected, he looked at Su Lun and got straight to the point, "I heard from the teacher that you might need this corpse..."
The teacher?
This appellation...
Upon hearing it, Su Lun felt slightly puzzled.
But in communicating with a "mind reader" like Mr. Hei, there was no need for beating around the bush. The conversation had reached this point, and he knew Mr. Hei must be aware of his talent.
Without confirming or denying, Su Lun just smiled and walked forward.
Devouring the grey mist was his top priority; the rest could wait.
This stripping was like the opening of floodgates, a torrent of memory shards violently surged into his mind.
'You have acquired 8 memory shards of "Grote Lester."'
'You received a piece of intelligence: "The situation in the empire is getting worse, and those pirates in the North Sea have become increasingly rampant. Last month, the trade convoy's steam airship was attacked, probably by a squad leader under the 'King of the North Sea.' Oh, those damned rascals..."'
'You have received some information: "Miss Teresa is getting more and more beautiful, but it seems she's been ignoring Young Master Ewen lately. The Duke probably intends to form an alliance with the Rega Land family through marriage, which would increase our say in the empire..."'
'You have comprehended a wealth of knowledge on the Flesh Alchemy Technique and mastered the "Diamond Body".'
'You have acquired the "Muscle Overload Micro-Control Technique" and mastered the "Extreme Air-Stepping Technique."'
'You have mastered a vast range of "1-5th order Alchemy Knowledge."'
'You've comprehended the incomplete fifth-order metal laws.'
'You've grasped some fragmented memories: The Duke's coastal territories, the Black Tower Mine on the reef, the Luying Empire, the Mechanical Sect...'
'You've mastered a large number of combat fragmentary information, combat experience +424'
'Spiritual power +4.3'
This was the first time Su Lun had stripped such "intense" Soul Shards.
He didn't have time to digest the detailed contents of those memories.
Suddenly, it hit him like the after-effects of drinking alcohol, his head felt heavy, and he felt drowsy.
It wasn't just the quantity of the knowledge, but also the quality!
This directly elevated his comprehension of the laws significantly, an impact far from the "gentle" experience he had when absorbing the Soul Shards of first and second-order professionals.
One was like a river flowing into the sea, and the other was like a torrential flood entering a river;
It was as if skipping straight from the Stone Age into the Steam Era, the mere sight of the vast gap between rules and tiers of laws was enough to make one feel dizzy and disoriented.
....
Not knowing how long he had been in a daze, digesting the massive amount of memory shards made Su Lun feel as if a long time had passed.
When his gaze refocused, there seemed to be an additional gleam of wisdom in his eyes.
"Indeed, too strong a Soul Shard will impact the main consciousness..."
Su Lun felt fortunate that he was capable of perfectly controlling and separating various other emotions to ensure the clarity of his main consciousness. If an ordinary person possessed this "Reaper" talent, they might not absorb much before they merged their own consciousness with the harvesting consciousness, turning into a "mental fusion aberration."
This S-level talent, albeit powerful, was not so easy to control.
It was like watching a movie,
You could see yourself as an audience member, gathering information;
But you couldn't immerse yourself to the point of becoming the protagonist, believing yourself to be a character in the story.
In this regard,
He, the patient, seemed to be a very "fitting" candidate for awakening this talent.
As for the gains,
They were too many to count...
Su Lun couldn't organize them all for the moment.
He gained innumerable fighting techniques, two complete skills.
The most precious was the understanding at the level of laws.
With the perspective of a high school student, even if one was a "scientific underachiever," revisiting elementary knowledge became instantly straightforward.
The first, second, and third tiers of Alchemy knowledge felt thoroughly integrated; even if they were not "of the gold element," an understanding of one opened the way to the rest;
As for the fourth and fifth tiers of knowledge, there were also some fragmented shards.
Although not yet forming a complete system, it was like seeing stars in the vast ocean, at least pointing out a general direction for the future.
After digesting the contents of the memory shards, Su Lun's eyes quivered gently, his heart experiencing a profound shock that lingered for a long time.
He murmured, "Endless Sea, Twilight Ruins, Ancient God Sites, Plane Fragments... So the world outside is this vast, with other races besides humans..."
So vast, so very vast...
This world was a hundredfold more fascinating than he had ever imagined!
....
Mr. Hei had already collected the materials from the corpse.
Seeing Su Lun's gaze clear again, he smiled warmly and asked, "How do you feel, Su Lun my friend?"
Being honest, Su Lun replied, "A bit dizzy."
Mr. Hei was not surprised and said, "Your spiritual power was about to spiral out of control. If you don't find a suitable Secret Technique to train and control that spiritual power soon, the situation will not be optimistic."
"Hmm."
Su Lun nodded, feeling acutely aware of this hidden danger.
But he did not dwell on this topic. Instead, he asked, "Mr. Hei, did you just mention your teacher?"
By now, he had confirmed that Mr. Hei indeed knew that his talent was "Reaper."
But what he was even more curious about was, in Old Lington City, who could be a teacher for the "all-knowing and omnipotent" Mr. Hei?
"Yes."
Upon mentioning "teacher," Mr. Hei's face was filled with respect. After pondering for a moment, he said, "Hmm... you can call him 'Mr. Jing,' and he is also the leader of our organization."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun realized the origin of the name of the "Jing Organization."
He immediately thought of his previous speculation.
Could it be that Mr. Hei's teacher—the one he had suggested saw a fifth-tier professional—was this very "Mr. Jing"?
Mr. Hei did not elaborate further but beckoned Su Lun to follow, saying, "Let's go, we can talk as we walk. Someone will come soon."
"Okay."
Hearing this, Su Lun followed Mr. Hei into the deeper, darker reaches of the cavern.
Due to the space barriers, the previous battle had left few traces in this stone chamber.
They took the bodies with them, leaving nothing behind.
Mr. Hei looked at Su Lun and smiled, "I used to be quite curious about what your talent was, Su Lun my friend, but it eluded me. It was only after the teacher told me that I learned you had awakened such an extremely rare talent."
Su Lun chuckled lightly in response.
Curiously, he asked, "Can your teacher discern a person's talent?"
"You don't need to be surprised. After all, the teacher is a scholar of extensive learning, and his understanding of Dawn City's history is beyond what others can imagine."
As Mr. Hei spoke, he seemed to be reminded of something, hesitating slightly: "Teacher's abilities are very special... but explaining it in detail would be quite complicated."
He didn't seem inclined to expound further, instead changing the subject: "If you're truly curious, you can ask him yourself the next time you meet. I think the teacher would be quite willing to solve your puzzle..."
Very special abilities?
Su Lun pondered for a moment.
Perhaps Mr. Hei was reluctant to discuss the secrets of that "teacher" behind their back, so he didn't ask further, but his mind instinctively conjured up the cloaked figure he saw at the "1911 Hotel."
He didn't even know whether that person was male or female, and probably wouldn't recognize them if they met again.
But from Mr. Hei's tone, should he have seen them somewhere else?
....
The two walked and talked along the way.
Su Lun also discovered that Mr. Hei's invitation was indeed the wish of the leader.
As per the old rules, present a gift, exchange equivalently, and also entrust him with a task.
Su Lun watched as Mr. Hei handed over a golden card and a sealed wooden box, not particularly surprised, "So... you want me to go into a cursed space and deliver this thing?"
Mr. Hei corrected Su Lun's words, smiling and saying, "No, not me. It's the teacher's intention."
Su Lun listened with increasing curiosity.
Although he knew Mr. Hei had no reason to send him to his death, he always felt something was off.
Mr. Hei didn't wait for Su Lun to guess wildly and plainly revealed the significance of these items: "What is sealed inside the wooden box is something brought out from the Black Tower laboratory by number 19. Under no circumstances should you open it outside, or else it might draw attention. After entering the space, find an ancient remnant named 'Sereya' and hand over the items to her."
After taking a breath, he continued, "Didn't I mention last time about the founder of your Puppeteer profession? Miss Sereya was actually the greatest forging Grandmaster and Puppet Master in Dawn City a thousand years ago. With this card as a token, you'll be able to communicate more easily."
The task itself was clear,
but listening to Mr. Hei, Su Lun's expression became increasingly strange: "Mr. Hei, may I ask... why did your teacher choose me?"
If possible, he definitely wanted to get his hands on the spiritual power secret technique of the Puppeteer.
However, it seemed that Mr. Hei had arranged everything for him.
Between the token and everything else,
it all looked like a "mouse trap with bait," didn't it?
But he knew, Mr. Hei had no motive to harm him.
And it wasn't necessary to go through such trouble.
Mr. Hei didn't hide anything and directly stated, "Because that 'Isaac's Alchemy Manuscript' is in your possession."
Su Lun: "???"
What does the notebook being with me have to do with anything?
And at that moment, Mr. Hei said, "Fate is an endless chain of cause and effect, and the development of the world itself follows this principle and causal relationship. That is a notebook touched by fate. If it didn't belong to you, it wouldn't be in your hands."
"..."
Su Lun found this very familiar.
On reflection, wasn't that the exact wording written in the notebook?
Although he knew this world had some strange and mysterious powers,
this...
still seemed somewhat unreliable.
He'd inadvertently come into possession of the notebook, which now appeared utterly useless.
And considering the situation, it was certain Mr. Hei knew the contents of the notebook.
So if I were to hand the notebook over to you now, wouldn't it then belong to you?
At that moment, as if seeing through Su Lun's internal complaints, Mr. Hei chuckled and uttered a profound statement, "You should know that Sir Isaac, who was hailed as a 'Demigod,' possessed a talent known as the 'Fate Controller.'
After a pause, he looked at Su Lun, who was still confused, and made a rare joke: "So, you don't need to ask me why, because fate is inscrutable, and I don't know either. Hahaha..."
Hearing this tone, Su Lun didn't know whether to laugh or cry.
Mr. Hei continued, "I've heard from the teacher that the manuscript records an ultimate secret of alchemy. But the manuscript touches upon a strand of the law of fate, one of the supreme laws of the world, and nobody can clearly explain what it is. So, all we can do is wait and see how things unfold. But for now, it seems most appropriate in your hands..."
"..."
Su Lun felt like he listened for nothing.
At first glance, it seemed to make sense. But upon further reflection, it was as if nothing had been said.
But with Mr. Hei admitting his ignorance, the topic was closed.
Moving on from the manuscript, Mr. Hei discussed the details of this commission, saying, "You might have guessed something, but don't mention it. Certain supreme beings possess indescribable powers. Once Their existence is mentioned, They will sense it."
"Hmm."
Su Lun nodded.
The manuscript detailed the method for crafting an alchemical augmentation known as the 'Heart of Isaac.' Thinking about the items number 19 took and the need to find a forging Grandmaster, the objective was self-evident.
Legend has it that gods must not be named directly.
He didn't ask further on that matter.
....
As they walked, Su Lun inquired about the "task" details, and Mr. Hei answered them all in detail.
His relationship with the Jing Organization was becoming increasingly close, and now there was no need for formality in their conversation.
Su Lun directly asked the most critical question.
"Mr. Hei, is that curse space dangerous?"
"The teacher said it is, but it won't be fatal to you. And if it's you... it would even be safer than if we went."
"Is it still because I have the manuscript?"
"That's one of the reasons."
"..."
Hearing there was no fatal danger, Su Lun also dismissed his concerns.
The more he understood about this world, the more he felt that Mr. Hei was trustworthy.
Moreover, he could sense from Mr. Hei's words that the "teacher" had an extraordinary understanding of the Dawn Relic.
Otherwise, others simply wouldn't know what lies at the core of the relic; they just knew there was a curse space there, along with an ancient remnant named "Lady Seria."
Furthermore, Su Lun himself was not one to shy away from risk.
Receiving a fifth-order Soul Shard as reward was actually more than enough for him to take the risk, even to the point of risking his life.
Such supreme knowledge was of great significance for the future of Su Lun, who was currently a "prisoner"!
Moreover, that space contained the exclusive spiritual secret technique of the founder of the Puppeteers that he needed most, so naturally, he had to make a trip there.
The two walked leisurely through the caves, with no pursuers catching up to them.
Su Lun also seized this rare opportunity to ask some of his questions.
What he was most curious about was Mr. Hei's omniscience, so he asked, "Mr. Hei, how do I feel like you know everything? Could it be that your awakened [Mind Reader], can also be used in knowledge learning?"
Mr. Hei smiled, probably having anticipated that Su Lun would be curious about this question, and clarified, "The [Scholar] profession I hold is a very special one. It practices the 'Law of Wisdom.' And my awakened abilities were also selected around the needs of the profession. My first-order awakening ability is 'eidetic memory,' second-order is 'brain domain development,' third-order 'heart of understanding,' fourth-order 'glimpse of truth'... Of course, the most important are the 'teacher's' instructions, plus some special opportunities. My talents could not be considered supreme, but I am diligent."
"Mr. Hei, what is brain domain development?"
"According to ancient texts, the potential of the human brain is actually limitless. But due to some reasons, it has been restricted, and its utilization is very low, so ancient magicians have thought about developing the extent of brain domain usage... however, it is also very dangerous."
"..."
Su Lun suddenly realized something as he listened to Mr. Hei's explanation.
But it was obvious that Mr. Hei was being modest.
To be so powerful without cheating,
and to say his talents couldn't be considered supreme... as if!
Listening to Mr. Hei's career planning, Su Lun suddenly started thinking about his own advancement to the third-order.
Controlling puppets... brain domain development?
Seems like a great fit.
Listening to Mr. Hei's description, it felt a bit like upgrading a computer's processor, enabling the brain to process more information efficiently.
"Brain domain development" was actually a concept in his previous life as well, but it was still theoretical.
In this world, ancient alchemy could do it with some extraordinary materials.
Su Lun felt that this world held too many hidden secrets...
But, the materials for developing the brain domain are not easier to find than spatial materials.
They are serendipitous and cannot be sought.
This could only be a future plan.
The two chatted for a long time.
Mr. Hei now probably felt that Su Lun has the strength worthy of learning some truths, so he no longer spoke in riddles.
If asked, he would almost certainly answer.
And he could answer like an encyclopedia!
Su Lun greatly benefited from this conversation.
And at that moment, he thought of another question he was very curious about, "And... Mr. Hei, I see that the members of your organization can all awaken their talents a second time. Is there a shortcut to talent awakening?"
One could say that, aside from Kai, all the people Su Lun had seen who had awakened their talents a second time were from the "Mirror Organization."
This inevitably made him suspect whether Mr. Hei and the others had a special method of awakening talents.
Turns out that wasn't the case.
It was just that their recruiting threshold was "second talent awakening."
As Mr. Hei put it, without a "second array awakening," except for some with special abilities, most had almost no ability to fight above their rank.
They could only be "targets of observation."
Just like the fifth-order professional they encountered before, a regular third-order would likely die after just one encounter!
Not much use for charging into the fray.
Mr. Hei: "A second-stage talent awakening can only be realized through life-and-death experiences, there are no shortcuts. Some laws of everything in the world are equal, like talent. The lower the rank, the easier it is to awaken, and the higher it gets, the harder it is. The difficulty of a C-rank talent awakening the second time is far lower than that of a B-rank... An A-rank talent that can awaken a second time, they have all gone through great hardships and have supreme talents..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun thought,
Even A-rank is so difficult...
What about S-rank?
Two S-ranks?

chapters.title: Chapter 189 - 188 Princess Teresa
chapters.content:
When Su Lun returned to the campsite, the news of Miss Teresa's team being ambushed had already spread.
Although no one knew what had happened, it was clear that additional guards had been stationed at the city gates. One could even see second-order professionals personally manning the gates, scrutinizing those entering the city for any suspicious persons.
However, this had no effect on Su Lun.
Since too many from the inner city had recently come to the Scavenger campsite, the entry fee had skyrocketed, and hotel accommodations had long been fully booked. Ordinary Scavengers couldn't afford to stay in the city, and many had pitched tents near the campsite's city wall.
This actually made things easier for Su Lun.
In an area of the tent section near the city wall, away from prying eyes, he used teleportation to enter the city.
The patrols inside the city were unusually strict as well.
He returned to the Rose Hotel, and after a short while, experienced a door-to-door inspection.
Thanks to his nearly perfect forged identity, he easily passed the check.
Su Lun didn't wander about but stayed in the hotel, meditating to assimilate the fifth-order knowledge he had stripped away that day.
....
Only after harvesting the memories did Su Lun learn that the people of the surface world did not absorb dark spiritual power to advance, but normal spiritual power.
He also learned that there were many factions among the ancient alchemists. The mainstream was called "Light Sorcerers," but there were also "Dark Sorcerers," "Necromancers," "Shadow Sorcerers," and "Toxic Sorcerers"...
Apart from the Light Sorcerers, the others were minority factions.
This underground city belonged to the "Dark Sorcerers" lineage.
In the following days, Su Lun was almost entirely immersed in digesting knowledge and contemplating those higher-order laws that exceeded his current level.
It was a delightful and magical experience, as if each moment brought a wealth of insight.
Su Lun devoured the knowledge like a whale, satisfying his hunger in one go.
After digesting it, he finally understood what those so-called "transcendent order barriers" mentioned in the texts were all about.
Indeed, the view from above was truly different.
The peaks that once seemed insurmountable (second order, third order) were merely slightly shorter hills, all within full view at a glance.
....
On this day.
Su Lun was in his room at the hotel.
Threads manipulated books that hung all around the room, while his eight arm-spiders, along with his hands, quickly flipped through these airborne tomes.
These were the textbooks from the Black Tower Academy that Mr. Hei had given him.
Although he had read them countless times, they contained much that he had not been able to understand before.
Now, Su Lun could read ten lines in a glance, swiftly going through the texts, deciphering the previously incomprehensible content that had been marked.
Especially those parts which required prior personal contemplation and understanding of alchemy knowledge, now nearly made sense at first glance.
After a while,
He had finally scanned through the texts, removing nine out of ten markers.
Su Lun let out a long breath, "Phew... I used to think the people from the Black Tower Academy were impressive with their amount of knowledge. But the high-order professionals from the outside world, they truly open one's eyes..."
Even in the surface world, fifth-order professionals were considered experts.
That "Grote Lester," as the captain of Duke Raphael's guard and a graduate from the "Luying Empire War Academy," possessed a systematic and incredibly vast knowledge.
Closing those texts, Su Lun's face was radiant, and he murmured to himself, "I've basically mastered the alchemy knowledge of the first and second orders. Now, I just need a bit more proficiency, and I can start working on third-order runes and enchantments. My rune puppets are about to get even stronger..."
He now deeply realized that "knowledge truly is a priceless treasure."
Su Lun profoundly experienced why the "Reaper of Death" was defined as an S-tier talent having a heaven-defying aspect.
Before, when harvesting peers of the same rank, it didn't feel remarkable. But now, having harvested across three major ranks, he had a sudden surge in growth.
The significance of knowledge gained absolutely can't be compared with obtaining a few sealed items!
After the third rank, every advancement on the extraordinary path has its barriers, it's not just about reaching the standard dark spiritual power values or finding materials to advance. One also needs to comprehend the corresponding laws, which is the true shackling element that countless alchemists die trying to overcome.
....
After digesting the knowledge in his mind, Su Lun suddenly thought of something and his hands began to form sorcerer's seals.
The seven-pointed star seal was slowly lighting up, but Su Lun seemed to sense something, and his brow furrowed. The sorcerer's seal changed again, losing one point and becoming a six-pointed star.
With the spell successfully condensed, on a closer look, his skin had suddenly turned as if cast from pure gold, with a visible sense of indestructible metallic quality to the naked eye.
This was naturally the casting of the Flesh Alchemy spell—[Vajra].
The original [Vajra] was a fifth-rank spell that involved very high-level laws and difficulty. In theory, a fourth-rank might barely be able to use it, but those of the third and second ranks would not even come close to managing it.
Yet, against all odds, Su Lun did it.
But there was a slight difference between this and that fifth-rank figure's dazzling gold manifestation, as Su Lun's golden coating also had a tinge of faint black.
The spell powered by dark spiritual power had some differences.
However, a complete spell required a huge amount of energy to maintain, and the current state of Su Lun's body and dark spiritual power couldn't sustain it.
Because he had a thorough understanding of the spell, he simply downgraded it a level on a whim.
The essence of the spell was to condense the element of gold into multiple layers of a highly refined state on the surface of the body, like overlapping gold leaf. Skimping on a few layers would decrease the defensive power.
After all, Su Lun didn't need a defense capable of withstanding fifth-rank attacks; a downgraded version was sufficient for him.
"So strong..."
Su Lun felt his body for a moment.
He took out a dagger and stabbed at himself, clearly feeling the sensation of scraping against metal as the sharp dagger failed to leave even a scratch on his skin.
Thinking it over, he then drew a musket and shot toward his own palm.
"Bang!"
The sound of the gunshot echoed in the room.
With a soundproof barrier in place, there was no fear of disturbing the neighboring tenants.
His palm trembled slightly as Su Lun looked at the deformed bullet in his hand, his gaze indifferent.
Then, he switched to alchemy bullets.
Another shot.
This time, the alchemy bullet made a slight indent on the skin, but it quickly recovered.
After firing two shots for testing, Su Lun had already roughly estimated the defensive limits of the spell. He pondered, "Both physical and magical defenses are high, able to block attacks from third-rank professionals for a short time at least. But the consumption is also significant. Moreover, the solidification of muscles clearly affects agility..."
The reason that fifth-rank "Grote Lester" could have nearly invincible defense was not only due to his spell proficiency but also directly related to his profession and alchemical grafts.
For a Puppet Master like Su Lun to achieve this level with the Flesh Alchemy Technique was already very satisfying to him.
At least, it gave him the ability to protect himself in a head-on encounter with third-rank professionals.
And it wasn't just defense; there was also body movement technique.
In this harvest, Su Lun also gained another complete skill [Extreme Air-Stepping Technique].
This was an advanced version of Kai's ghostly movement technique.
Typically, melee professionals above the third rank could possibly master it through arduous skill training.
To put [Stepping on Air] in simpler terms, it means "stepping on air". However, Kai's version only allowed for horizontal advancement, while this advanced skill allowed one to step on air and ascend vertically. The difference in skill difficulty was substantial.
Su Lun had tried it on the way back to camp before; he could leap through the air for short distances, and it felt very good.
Within a short distance, it was several times faster than the teleportation of an eight-arm spider lance.
One defensive move, one escape, his life-saving measures increased greatly.
....
As evening approached, Su Lun was, as usual, tinkering with his new odd puppet in his room.
But as he was working, suddenly noises from outside the window reached him.
"Hurry and look, Princess Teresa's entourage has arrived outside the camp!"
"Wow~ I heard that even the big shots from the inner city rarely see the little princess, and she actually came to the Scavenger camp. This is a rare opportunity; let's go have a look..."
"Hiss, what a lavish display. The guards from the Duke's mansion seem so strong..."
"..."
It was unclear whether it was because the main force was moving slowly or because they had encountered an ambush and had slowed down, but the young lady from Duke Raphael's mansion arrived at the camp several days later than expected.
Hearing the noise outside the window, Su Lun leaned against the window and looked in the direction of the sounds.
He had chosen this room before because it offered a broad view, allowing him to see the camp's gate and main street directly from his room.
Su Lun gazed out.
The entourage of Duke Raphael's young lady was indeed grand, with presumably hundreds of people accompanying her.
The crowd surrounded a carriage-like special steam machinery locomotive.
In the team, some even carried flags embroidered with the exclusive noble emblem of the harp and lion pattern of the Raphael family. The guards, in uniform dark cyan uniforms with cross helmets and sword-bearing heavy armor at the forefront, and there were dozens of women and slaves in servant attire, as well as butlers, tutors, cooks...
"So many strong people..."
Su Lun squinted to take a closer look.
This standard entourage of a high-ranking noble was enough for him to distinguish the primary from the secondary at a glance.
Apart from Miss Teresa's personal maids, the closer to the locomotive, the stronger their powers.
Because of some fragmented memories he had separated before, Su Lun felt some faces were familiar, yet he could not recognize them.
A fifth-tier guard captain had died, and clearly, there were other fifth-tiers in the team. Near the locomotive, the pale-faced man dressed in military attire with his cap brim pulled down low was obviously one of them.
And around him, those dozen or so robed magicians constantly emanated a thick elemental fluctuation, a sight others might not understand, but Su Lun knew it represented the fourth-tier magicians' defensive measure "Elemental Barrier."
Clearly, these were just the visible guard forces; who knew what was hidden.
This team was frighteningly strong.
....
The Dawn camp had originally been a war town existing for Scavengers, and did not have very spacious streets.
The team entered through the city gate and then stopped in front of the narrow streets.
The knights knelt on one knee while the maids opened the doors of the locomotive.
An old nurse led out a girl who was wearing a veil.
She wore a wide-brimmed hat with a pink bow, a floral short skirt, and simple little leather boots, and was not very formally dressed. But when she appeared, she exuded an air of nobility as if a swatch of color had entered a black-and-white scene, capturing everyone's gaze.
Su Lun glanced over, then retracted his gaze, not planning to look any further.
These high-ranking Duke's daughters were trouble the more you looked at them.
And just at that moment, he suddenly heard a knock on his door.
Upon opening the door, to his surprise, it was Qian Tiao, whom he hadn't seen for several days.
Su Lun greeted her, "Sister Qian Tiao."
"Mm-hmm."
Qian Tiao replied languidly with the exhausted expression of someone who had gambled for days and nights, stepping inside and muttering, "Ah, finally back..."
As she spoke, she headed straight for the bathroom and stripped off her dirty clothes, tossing them out, "Could you hang these up for me?"
"..."
Su Lun raised his eyebrows helplessly at the sight of her bare back. This gambling-addicted lady was getting more and more familiar; she used to cover up a bit, but now she didn't even bother with the bra.
The sound of water trickling came from the bathroom,
Su Lun hung up the clothes and continued tinkering with his rune puppet.
Before long, Qian Tiao emerged from the shower.
She was drying her hair with a towel when she suddenly asked, "Are you free tonight?"
Su Lun, who was engraving a critical rune, didn't look up, "Nothing much."
Qian Tiao inquired, "Then how about you change into a different outfit and accompany me to a wine reception?"
"A wine reception?"
Su Lun looked up at her, feeling that her tone was slightly different.
Qian Tiao explained, "Yes. That young lady from the Duke's household has arrived, and the major families in the inner city are naturally throwing a welcome reception. Plus, they'll be drawing lots for Scavenger assignments at the reception, and Rena, that little girl, isn't in the best situation... Well, and then, if you could disguise yourself with a new identity, you could help me keep trouble at bay..."
"..."
With that explanation, Su Lun finally understood.
Although Qian Tiao was an executive of the Cross Society, she was also the second Miss of the Evelyn family of the inner city. Few people in the outer city were aware of her identity, but it was common knowledge among the great families of the inner layer.
This gambling-addicted lady disliked the social gatherings of high society, yet she still had to consider her family.
She could ignore other receptions, but not the one welcoming the young lady from the Duke's household. For such an event, every household and anyone with a reputable name had to attend. No one dared ignore the Duke's authority.
Listening to her, Su Lun realized that he was expected to act as her...escort?
He didn't mind doing this small favor, but it was the first time Qian Tiao had spoken about her family affairs, and he was somewhat curious.
And as they spoke, he watched the gambling-addicted lady actually pulling a dark cyan court dress from her storage ring?
"Eh..."
Su Lun looked surprised.
As far as he remembered, aside from kimonos and battle armor, he had never seen her in any other styles of clothing.
Oh, there was also nightwear and the state of undress.
But...
A high-society lady's dress???
Qian Tiao, noticing that peculiar look, retorted irritably, "Hey... Su Lun kid, what's with that look? You think I want to wear this..."
At a high-society wine reception, entering in a flamboyant kimono heavy with social flair would probably attract more attention than Princess Teresa herself.
Su Lun smiled, "Ah... I think it looks pretty good."
"..."
Qian Tiao gave him a blank look, but ignored the comment.
After drying her hair, she started getting into her dress in front of the dressing mirror, grumbling as she went, "Putting on a dress is such a hassle..."
Su Lun refrained from staring at her as she changed.
But after a brief wait, when the room fell silent and he glanced over, he was taken aback by the sight.
It must be said, a gambling-addicted lady with her hair up high in a court lady's dress truly was a fine sight!

chapters.title: Chapter 190 - 189: Lena's Predicament
chapters.content:
Su Lun was seeing the gambling-addicted lady dressed up for the first time.
Her long dress, tailored from dark turquoise brocade with golden threads, outlined her graceful figure with stunningly beautiful lines. Adorned with swathes of light gauze, it seemed as though a gentle breeze was swirling around her, and the heroic spirit flickering between her brows made Su Lun take another glance without realizing it.
Majestic, elegant, and exquisitely charming.
Before the dressing mirror, the gang leader transformed her outfit, instantly resembling a lady of high society.
But she seemed quite uncomfortable in a dress, looking disdainfully at her reflection in the mirror while muttering under her breath unintelligibly.
At that moment, she seemed to notice Su Lun's gaze, turned around, and gestured at her dress, asking, "Su Lun lad, do you notice anything odd?"
Su Lun smiled and said only one word, "Pretty."
At that, she pursed her lips, "Don't just stand there, hurry up and change. The reception starts at nine, but we should enter early and wait for that little princess."
"Oh."
Hearing this, Su Lun put away the puppet in his hand and stood up.
At a twitch of his body, without taking off his clothes, he transformed his outfit as if performing a quick-change act, miraculously changing into a white suit.
Seeing his instantaneous change of clothes, she realized his underlying ability and raised an eyebrow, "Oh... using spatial abilities to change clothes now?"
Su Lun chuckled, "Just a little trinket I figured out, magical outfit change."
With that, he shook his legs, and shiny leather boots wrapped around his feet.
Then bringing his hands together and pulling, he held a cane with a silver handle in his right hand.
Feeling like something was missing, he looped a boutonniere with his left hand and magically placed a round top hat on his head.
After he was done, he glanced at the gambling-addicted lady, "Come on, we can leave now."
From head to toe, she sized up Su Lun with a teasing light in her eyes, jesting, "Tsk, this shell of yours is really not bad~"
Su Lun just shrugged with a smile, walked over, and extended his arm, which she naturally took.
At that moment, she suddenly noticed something, "Wait."
Su Lun stopped and watched as she wrapped her arms up, then carefully straightened his collar, smoothing out the creases.
"There, much better~"
She seemed pleased, a smile appearing on her pretty face.
....
Before Princess Teresa arrived at the camp, the major families within the city had already received news of the reception.
The Unicorn Inn, this was the Reyis family's property.
As the only daughter of the Reyis family's head household, Lena naturally came underground too.
In the penthouse suite, a maid was applying her makeup.
The elderly butler's face was grave as he reported the recent situation, "Miss, the situation isn't good. The Lord has sent word that several sub-families are becoming restless. We need to be cautious; they might act against you. And this morning, the large hunting groups who had signed employment contracts with us, 'Red Dragon Hunting Group,' 'Iron Eagle Hunting Group,' 'Holy Knight Hunting Group'... several of their leaders jointly sought us out and rejected our employment."
Lena frowned, one piece of bad news after another, "But didn't we already sign the employment contract?"
"Yes, miss."
The butler continued solemnly, "But they've compensated us with a hefty penalty and unilaterally terminated the contracts. I've been negotiating with the Hunting Guild, but it's not going well... I've heard that the second and third houses have teamed up with five major families from the camp to pay the penalty. Moreover, they've threatened to suppress any hunting group that works with us. So far, despite high offers, no other hunting groups dare to contact us. Therefore, aside from the staff you brought from the family and the 'Cross Society' hunting group, we don't have many people to rely on. The information I received claimed that this time all major families in the inner city must participate in hunting, which puts us at a disadvantage, and the hunting will be extremely risky. I'm worried that they aim to harm you, thereby pressuring your father and perhaps have even larger schemes..."
Lena listened, her expression growing more intense.
After a pause, the butler added, "Also, the Clark family sent someone to convey a message; they said they could help us out of our predicament, but likely with ill intentions. Since you said not to meet, I refused them. But perhaps at this reception, Miss, you might try to connect with some allies, families who have previously been on good terms, who might help us out of respect for your father..."
Lena replied, "Hmm. Understood."
....
Su Lun and she were not hurrying.
Though her lady-like dress looked truly pretty, she didn't really like it.
Su Lun held her waist as they walked with intimate gestures.
It's not that she was putting on airs, but this gambling-addicted lady really felt uncomfortable in her skirt.
"This damn skirt, I can't even stride! Move closer to me, these high heels are so awkward to walk in..."
As they walked, Su Lun listened to her complain about the skirt more than once.
Fortunately, the walking distance wasn't too far.
Along the way, they also encountered many well-dressed young ladies and gentlemen, all seemingly headed to a social gathering.
Seeing Su Lun and his companion's attractive pairing, there were plenty of envious glances.
The two of them walked and chatted.
She briefed Su Lun, "Your identity is now 'Zoro'. This identity is registered with the Bounty Hunters' guild. Although somewhat famous, no one has seen your face... You might encounter some members of my family, and they'll likely pester you with questions... So you understand, right?"
"Mhm. Understood."
After listening for a while, a brilliant smile spread across Su Lun's face.
The identity arranged by her was naturally perfect, in her words, "The best disguise is substitution."
This was better than any fake identity Su Lun could have created himself.
As for the rest, although she was vague, Su Lun had gotten the hint.
Being an older unmarried woman, she couldn't escape certain conventions.
Meeting family, she needed a shield.
"So, you fled to the association to escape marriage?"
"What else? Of course, that's one of the reasons. You already know the rest."
"Sister, people on the streets say you don't like men, is that true?"
"Pfft—false! Not only do I not like men, I don't like women either, I only like swords!"
"..."
The two were very familiar with each other, and these topics were discussed without any taboos.
Walking along, they suddenly spotted an acquaintance.
A young girl in an evening gown, surrounded by a group of guards, emerged from a building painted white with a sign "Unicorn Hotel" hanging on it.
Looking at her striking straight black hair, who could it be if not Lena?
She seemed a bit distracted and didn't notice Su Lun and his friend passing by.
She greeted, "Lena~"
Lena looked at her, seemed stunned for a moment, then recognized her. Excitement lit up her eyes, and she hurried over, "Ah...Auntie Qiantiao~"
Qiantiao walked over and ruffled her hair, "Little girl, what's on your mind? You look so sorrowful."
Despite her attempt to smile at these words, Lena's face still showed signs of worry.
With nothing to hide from her family elders, she said directly, "The butler just informed me that the wilderness hunter groups we had contracts with have all backed out..."
"Oh, small matter."
Qiantiao listened, then dismissively waved her hand.
To her, it really was a trivial issue.
She then introduced Su Lun, "This is my friend 'Zoro', a very skilled Bounty Hunter. He will also help with the wilderness hunt."
Lena glanced at Su Lun, who was arm-in-arm with her aunt, her curiosity hard to conceal.
She remembered, it seemed her aunt had never been so intimate with any man.
But she didn't dwell on it, instead she took hold of her skirt, curtseyed, and said, "How do you do, Mr. Zoro. It's a pleasure to meet you. Please take good care of me."
Su Lun nodded, "Mhm."
The duo, now a group, continued up the hill.
...
The address of the banquet was at the Storm Estate.
To welcome the arrival of Princess Teresa, the original Hunters Guild had also relocated.
The major families in the camp had pooled all their resources and renovated the thousand-year-old estate, transforming it into a brand-new, luxurious mansion.
After handing out the invitations, the guards stayed at the entrance of the mansion.
Su Lun, Olli, and Camilla entered the estate.
In contrast to the previously dilapidated and noisy scene, the Storm Estate was now completely rejuvenated.
The garden was lush, with brilliantly blooming colorful flowers, and even the withered trees had sprouted leafy branches. The greenery was meticulously groomed by gardeners and stepping into it felt refreshing and clear.
This garden was likely the result of the Magicians, who had used a vast amount of resources to cultivate it.
Upon entering the building, it was even more splendid.
However, Su Lun felt slightly strange inside the mansion because he always had the sensation of looking at the cursed spatial scene from the past. The estate from a thousand years ago had been just as prosperous.
Especially... the layout of such a mansion, anyone who knew architecture could tell at a glance.
The place that should have been the banquet hall, remained the banquet hall.
The location for holding this time's party was exactly where the "Bloody Banquet" had taken place.
The banquet hall was brightly lit with dazzling lights, with soft music echoing through the hall, and elegantly dressed ladies and gentlemen gathered smoothly, holding wine glasses and chatting merrily.
When Su Lun and his companions entered, they naturally attracted the eyes of those people.
But what was slightly awkward was that the three of them were immediately ignored.
Not even the most basic nod of acknowledgment was exchanged.
These were all young ladies and gentlemen from the major families of the inner city, who all knew each other and even had deep relations.
Olli had not frequented the high society circles for a long time, she didn't care to interact with these people, and it was normal for them not to care about her.
But it was particularly strange for someone like Camilla, a top-tier tycoon's daughter.
Back when the Reis family had not split, she was the center of attention wherever she went.
But now, not only did no one come up to greet her, they seemed to be avoiding something, their gazes evading incessantly.
Camilla didn't mind, but she was somewhat worried and said in a soft voice, "The butler told me that the situation in Old Lington City is also not very good. This time my father even had me bring almost all the high-level guards from home, I don't know if there will be any problems..."
Olli listened and dismissively said, "Don't worry... those guys' schemes are not so easy to succeed."
Camilla, "Hmm."
Su Lun scanned the banquet hall and based on his memory, identified some people's identities.
Standing next to Camilla, even he, as a third party, was subject to some inexplicable "malice."
He raised his eyelids slightly, and his lips curved into a smirk, thinking to himself, "Camilla's enemies are quite numerous..."
Feeling the continuous malicious gazes, Su Lun figured that if he was to go hunting in the wilderness, it would likely be that any random encounter would be with an enemy.
However, he didn't take this malice to heart.
With the major figure Olli around, the Reis family's situation wouldn't collapse, at least Camilla wasn't going to die easily.
If worse came to worst, with his, Su's, current strength, without a third-tier professional, hardly anyone would pose a threat to him.
Having many enemies...
In certain aspects, that wasn't necessarily a bad thing.
....
"Tsk tsk, Camilla is probably in big trouble this time. I heard that they haven't even hired a decent hunting group, and with just the people they brought from the inner city, they probably won't last long..."
"Now the major families of the inner city have united to isolate them, no one dares to help them..."
"I heard that Miss Sofia of the Reis second family and Young Master Danze of the Olivier family have been in close contact recently, and seem to be planning an engagement. When they join forces, the dynamics of the inner city are bound to change..."
"Yes, the Reyes family needs to reshuffle as well..."
"..."
Su Lun perked up her ears and quickly grasped the situation.
The Reyes family had indeed been a top financial conglomerate, but after dividing into seven, their influence had diminished greatly.
The seven branches that split off naturally opposed the main family, even becoming enemies.
Even former allied families had turned into enemies.
The instigators of the split had offended many, and those families that had kicked them when they were down naturally wanted to eliminate any future threats.
They too wanted a share of the spoils.
This time, Lena brought many direct family experts, and she was the only heir. A total annihilation in the ruins would directly affect the internal city's situation.
With internal and external troubles, the situation for the main branch of the Reyes family was indeed worrisome.
....
The three paid no attention to the whispered conversations around them and found a corner to talk.
No one bothered them, which was also good as they did not have to deal with so-called high-society socializing.
With Senior Qiān supporting her, Lena's worried expression eased somewhat.
However, as they talked, Qiān's "trouble" arrived.
A few ladies with their clearly displeased sons approached.
The middle-aged woman wearing a large emerald necklace greeted Qiān, "Oh, Ottilia, long time no see~"
This time, it wasn't just the young masters and young ladies, many families brought their wives who worried about their precious sons and daughters being mistreated.
Qiān looked at the newcomers and frowned slightly, but she still had to greet them, "Aunt Camilla, long time no see."
Su Lun listened to their exchange and glanced at Qiān, feeling somewhat curious.
So this gambling-addict lady's full name was "Ottilia Evelyn".
And upon hearing the address, that other glamorous, golden-haired woman, she was Qiān's stepmother?
And the defiant little boy, he was her half-brother in name?
Then there were various relatives from the Evelyn family, aunts, and their children.
A large group.
Next came various greetings.
The complexities of high society included greeting, returning greetings, introducing younger generations, greeting again, returning greetings, and asking after all family elders, recalling past relations between elders...
Then, it was time for marriage urging.
"Ottilia, you're not getting any younger. Stop mixing with the commoners in the outer city. I heard you also have connections with the mob? Oh my, if that gets out, people will say our Evelyn family has fallen on hard times..."
"You don't know, just yesterday I was talking to Madam Albertini about you. They say our Evelyn family has an old maid who can't get married..."
"Ottilia, you're not getting any younger. Doctor Enzo from the Smith family is a fine young man, their family owns eight hospitals in District Number Five..."
"..."
It wasn't just Qiān, Su Lun felt overwhelmed just listening.
Since arriving in this world, all he had encountered was fighting and killing...
Apparently, there were ordinary people too...
Listening to this large-scale marriage urging scene, which was no different from his previous life, Su Lun also finally understood why Qiān had brought him here.
After listening for a while, Qiān finally lost her patience, cut off the increasingly unreliable introductions, and pulled Su Lun up, introducing him to everyone, "Oh, almost forgot to introduce, this is 'Zoro' sir. My friend."
Su Lun could only force a smile.
He took off his hat and performed a greeting, "Zoro Cerna, honored to meet all you lovely ladies."

chapters.title: Chapter 191 - 190: Communication
chapters.content:
"Zoro Cerna?"
As Su Lun introduced himself, several women glanced over at him with evaluative eyes.
In fact, they had already noticed the man of extraordinary temperament beside Qiantiao.
But because he seemed quite young, they had not considered that angle.
Now, hearing Qiantiao's special introduction as "my friend," they all switched to the kind of scrutiny reserved for a potential son-in-law and looked him over again.
One of the women asked, "The Cerna family? Oh, from the No. 1 urban district's Cerna Biotech?"
Su Lun naturally had to play his role well, shaking his head, "No, not that."
The Cernas were not a prominent surname in the inner city, at least not among the commonly known major families, and the women racked their brains but could not figure out Su Lun's origins.
Qiantiao's aunt then tentatively asked, "Mr. Zoro, what profession are you in?"
Su Lun replied, "I am a bounty hunter."
Another woman, still unconvinced, inquired, "From the inner city's Order of Bounty Knights?"
Su Lun had heard of it; it was an organization the inner city nobles indulged in for amusement. He corrected, "No, a bounty hunter from the outer city."
The moment he said this, the atmosphere immediately turned cold,
....
The look in the ladies' eyes changed instantly, though their composure did not show anything odd.
However, the children nearby could not restrain themselves.
Hearing Su Lun's profession, several youngsters cast glances of disgust and disdain.
To the high society of the inner city, an outer city bounty hunter was a job even more demeaning than a bodyguard, a sort of blood-licking existence that never appeared in their normal view.
It wasn't meant as a serious insult, but their upbringing had deeply ingrained in them a certain perception of people from the outer city.
Bounty hunter = lower class individual.
This made them think that Qiantiao had found herself a petty thug.
Mrs. Camilla then turned to Qiantiao, asking, "By the way, Olli, have you known Mr. Zoro for a long time?"
"Yes. We are even living together now."
The atmosphere chilled instantly, which seemed exactly the effect Qiantiao wanted.
While saying this, she affectionately linked her arm with Su Lun's, her smile brimming.
Hearing they were "living together," the expressions of several noble ladies grew even uglier.
They could not explode with anger openly, so Mrs. Camilla could only pull Qiantiao aside, "Olli, come here for a moment, I have something to tell you."
....
Qiantiao seemed reluctant to go.
But she was still sternly pulled away by several ladies for a private talking-to.
With everyone gone, Su Lun was happy to have some peace.
His keen hearing caught everything crystal clear.
The noble ladies didn't seem to mind hiding their discussion; in fact, they seemed to intentionally want him to overhear as they talked while walking away.
"Oh, Olli, you actually chose a bounty hunter from the outer city? My goodness, I can guarantee you, our family will never allow you to be with such a person."
"You're being too reckless! If this gets out now, our Evelyn clan will surely become a laughingstock in the upper circles..."
"Also, stay out of the Reis family's issues this time. I know she's your sister's blood, but I was warned even before I came here... besides, it's an internal matter of the Reis family; outsiders shouldn't interfere... even if our Evelyn clan got involved, it wouldn't change the situation..."
"..."
Su Lun too was overwhelmed listening to all of this.
Every other sentence was about "family face," "family honor," "family interests"...
No wonder Qiantiao was reluctant to go back.
With her personality, if it weren't for the fact that they were relatives, anyone else rambling like this would probably have been met with drawn swords by now.
With one strike, a nosy woman was dead, and with two, a couple.
In an instant, the world became quiet.
.....
Julia was probably stuck being scolded for quite some time.
Only Su Lun and one other remained in the corner.
After all, Su Lun was unfamiliar with "Zoro" and Lena; the two had little to say to each other.
The atmosphere was slightly awkward.
Moreover, both of them were of the less popular sort at the social event, with nowhere else to go; the self-serve desserts, dancing, and mingling... none of it suited them.
Lena, thinking she should find a topic of conversation, started by asking, "Mr. Zoro, are you a bounty hunter?"
Su Lun nodded, "Mhm."
Lena then asked, "Have you heard of Mr. Su Lun?"
Su Lun, not knowing why she suddenly brought him up, said, "You mean the SS wanted criminal, Su Lun?"
Lena nodded, "Mhm."
Then, the two fell silent again.
Su Lun curiously asked, "Miss Lena, why do you ask about him?"
After thinking, Lena spoke with some hesitation, "Well... although Mr. Su Lun has committed crimes, he's not entirely evil. He once saved my… aunt. She has high standards and said you're a very capable bounty hunter, so you must be very successful... If Mr. Zoro comes across that Su Lun, could you possibly show mercy... I mean, could you refrain from harming him? There might be some misunderstanding; he deserves a fair trial..."
Her tone was conflicted.
It even became somewhat incoherent.
Clearly, in her conception, "all wanted criminals are criminals," but this clashed with her own understanding.
She believed Su Lun was a good person, yet she couldn't deny that the wanted poster depicted him as a criminal.
"..."
Su Lun was both amused and bewildered.
She was pleading for mercy on his behalf?
The information Lena had was probably all from the wanted poster.
The official wanted poster described him, Su Lun, with words like "extremely vicious" and "utterly wicked."
And yet, the girl was unexpectedly speaking up for him?
Though... her intentions were good.
The now "SS ranked wanted Su Lun" was a figure most bounty hunters would choose to avoid entirely.
Show mercy?
If it were another bounty hunter, it would be uncertain who would spare whom.
A thought flashed through his mind, and he also replied, "Alright."
Upon hearing this, Lena politely smiled, "Thank you."
....
Two people who were barely acquainted had little to talk about.
After only a few words, the conversation ended again.
But after not too long, a beautiful, blonde girl quietly approached.
Su Lun had seen this blonde girl before.
During the commotion in the inner city, in front of the Moonlight Inn, she seemed to be called Julia, Lena's close friend.
As Julia passed by, without even a glance at Lena, she said urgently, "Lena, I've heard about your situation, I'm sorry I can't help you. My father sent someone to warn me not to get involved with problems of your seventh branch. I wanted to hire some mercenaries for you, but none of the mercenaries or hunter groups are willing to cooperate once they know it's you, no matter the price I offer. I only have a few personal guards who will obey me, tomorrow I will send them to find you, and you can command them..."
While speaking, she looked at Lena with a face full of apology, "I'm sorry, I can't talk more, otherwise it would create trouble."
Lena watched her hurriedly departing best friend, a hint of loneliness crossing her face, "Thank you."
Listening by the side, Su Lun gave another glance at the blonde girl's fading figure.
"Being able to lend a hand at this juncture really does show true sentiment and loyalty."
....
This was Su Lun's first time attending a high society soiree, it seemed tonight was meant for witnessing the myriad facets of high society, the warmth, and coldness of human relationships, and the manipulative games they played.
Not long after Julia had left, a handsome, brown-haired young man approached.
Su Lun remembered him; this guy was Young Master Eli Clark from one of the five major clans in the camp, the Clark family.
A crony of Young Master Danze from the Oliver family.
One of the masterminds behind the current predicament of the Reiss family.
Young Master Eli held a wine glass with a light smile on his face as he approached Miss Lena, his tone frivolous, "Miss Lena, long time no see."
Miss Lena seemed disinclined to entertain this ill-intentioned fellow but nodded slightly out of courtesy.
Young Master Eli continued, "Miss Lena, oh... I'm sorry to hear you've been having some trouble lately. If you think of us as friends, perhaps you could share it with me..."
Miss Lena had no intention of wasting words with someone with dishonest intentions and cut him off, "Sorry, not necessary."
"It seems you are in a bad mood..."
Eli listened but showed no anger.
A knowing smile flashed in his eyes as he went on, "Now that Princess Theresa has arrived, and I've got word that in no more than three days, you, me... and everyone else will have to go into the relics to hunt for game. I heard Miss Lena has yet to recruit a hunting team?"
