The rough description is, the greater a person's influence in this world, the stronger their fate.
A person with strong fate, using this bow, might consume one year of lifespan and might take away all the lifespan of someone with weaker fate.
A person with weak fate, using this bow, might consume a hundred years and might only injure someone else's lifespan for a year.
Since fate and lifespan are both "uncertain factors," no one can clearly state whose fate is stronger.
This cursed item truly involves gambling with life!
....
Su Lun watched as Lu Ying's side brought out this bow and identified its attributes. His gaze also turned very strange, "This bow indeed counters Mecha warriors, but it's not easy to kill someone..."
Those from Mafa are all officers, who might become Grand Generals in the future, which means their fate is not comparable to ordinary people.
Using this bow to kill, the cost is not small.
However, Su Lun still underestimated the deterrence of imperial power.
These people clearly received a deadly order to keep those individuals.
He watched as the cursed longbow was taken out and the person drawing the bow shot an arrow without hesitation.
One arrow per second.
Pull once, change to another person.
"Whoosh" "Whoosh" "Whoosh"...
The arrows of light were shot out ceaselessly.
Those drawing the bow had just put down the longbow when their bodies visibly aged, transforming from their prime to decrepit old age in an instant, some even dying on the spot.
Watching this made bystander Su Lun's scalp tingle and his eyelids twitch, "There really are many sinister methods in this world..."
Not everyone is the main character doomed to survive till the end.
The fate of most ordinary people is roughly the same.
Besides, no matter how strong your fate, how many people's lifespans can it withstand?
If one isn't enough, then bring ten!
Is the Time Bow powerful?
Are the suicide soldiers strong?
No, Su Lun deeply felt the power of authority.
However, the effect was immediate.
Mecha warriors move fast, but their ability to change direction is a weakness, lacking agility, very easy to predict.
The royals from Lu Ying didn't bring out this curse bow to let some low-level soldiers shoot the arrows.
That would only waste the precious opportunity to pursue.
Su Lun noted that those who were shooting the arrows were all not weak in spirit, and highly aware, clearly being of officer rank.
This was truly exchanging life for life.
Both sides were sacrificing high-level talents in the fray!
And so, life for life, sometimes just two or three arrows were enough to take down a Mecha warrior.
When those dozen high-level Mecha warriors reached Pier No. 7, only five or six were left.
Su Lun wasn't concerned about who won or lost.
If he was not mistaken, that time arrow was only hitting the people controlling the Mechas, and the Mechas were unscathed?
Furthermore, just by chance, one ended up falling into the sea at Pier No. 5?
Seeing this, Su Lun quietly sneaked over.

chapters.title: Chapter 233 - 233: [Major Rank Destroyer IX Type Mechanical Battlesuit]
chapters.content:
The people of the Mafa Empire clearly had a premeditated plan; the remaining few mechanical warriors boarded the submarine, and as soon as the hatch closed, the submarine quickly submerged and then, in full view of the onlookers, disappeared at the No.7 dock of the harbor.
"Put a magic mark on that ironclad! Board the ships! Chase them!"
"Call in the trackers, they must not be allowed to escape!"
"Notify the fleet to intercept!"
"..."
This kind of war machine, the submarine, had never before appeared on the battlefield between the two countries, catching everyone off guard.
The few mechanical soldiers who served as the rear guard on the dock self-destructed after being subdued, and the commotion in the city subsided.
At the dockside, several major arms dealers looked at one another with complex expressions as they watched the fleet scramble in pursuit out of the port.
What was thought to be foolproof had encountered such an unexpected event.
They were shocked that such a submarine, capable of underwater travel, even existed, and were also concerned about how such a stealthy method would add uncertainty to future wars.
No one knew how many soldiers the Mafa Empire had managed to transport into the heartland of Luying through this manner.
...
At the same time, in a luxurious small building on a mountaintop in Gadolangte City, a purple-haired woman was standing in front of a floor-to-ceiling window, quietly watching the distant battle.
Watching the submarine vanish at the docks, she swirled the red wine in her glass, took a sip, and remained calm, evidently not too surprised.
At that moment, an old butler walked in and reported, "Miss, those people from Mafa indeed escaped by sea."
Yekaterina was still looking at the bay in the distance and said with a deep gaze, "Of course they fled by sea. They couldn't do it by land or air, so this was the only way they could have escaped. I thought they would use some special means. It turns out the information we received earlier was true; those folks from Mafa really developed a submarine capable of naval action."
The butler added, "Our people have already taken action. Even with their stealth submarines, they won't be able to escape."
Hearing this, Yekaterina shook her head, "No... call them back."
"Call them back?"
Hearing this, the butler looked puzzled and asked, "Miss, didn't we arrange all this to get the blueprints... "
Before he could finish, Yekaterina interrupted, "The Regaldi family has just sent a message, telling us not to interfere with the blueprint matter. They have the means to lock down the location of the blueprints and have already sent someone to act."
"The Regaldi family?"
The butler's expression slightly stiffened, showing his bewilderment.
He was astute and immediately thought of something, "Are you saying that Regaldi is involved with Duke Raphael?"
"Yes."
Yekaterina narrowed her eyes, her tone tinged with complexity, "The 'Super Mechanical Warrior' made such a show of strength on the battlefield, which made me think that Raphael, after a hundred years of operating that 'mine,' must have discovered many unbelievable things, which is why he dared to show his power. Now, it seems that the entire Luying Empire has underestimated that nouveau riche."
Pausing for a while, she then mumbled to herself, "Hehe, a nouveau riche who knows how to bide his time and a bunch of conspirators dreaming of restoration... what a perfect match indeed."
Listening to her words, the butler's face also grew solemn as he asked, "Miss, then shouldn't we get our hands on those blueprints even more urgently?"
Yekaterina's eyes also flashed with thought as she shook her head, "Forget it, we won't get involved. Let's see how they play their cards. And let me see what kind of hidden hand they really have."
After a pause, she uttered a more meaningful statement, "Besides... it's not certain that those people from Mafa took the blueprints with them when they went to sea."
The butler seemed to have been startled by her words and gasped, "You mean..."
The butler stopped abruptly in mid-sentence.
Seeing that her mistress clearly had no further interest in discussing the topic, he did not press on.
At that moment, Yekaterina too had turned away from the window, returning to the interior of the room, and asked, "By the way, what about the beastfolk?"
Remembering something, the butler said with an ugly expression, "About that plan, a very strange message just came from the docks..."
After listening to the butler's report, Yekaterina's face showed real surprise for the first time, saying, "What?! You mean to say that the person who bought the beastfolk set them all free?"
The butler frowned as if his face had turned into a chrysanthemum and said, equally puzzled, "Yes. I did not expect this either. But the messages from the docks have already confirmed it."
The usual script is, whoever buys these slaves will surely use them, or sell them on.
Then, at the right moment, our people would conveniently rescue them as a way to gain goodwill.
But no, those people just left the auction and immediately chartered a ship to set them free!
Without giving us any chance to react at all.
Too much money?
Or someone with the same goal as them?
Yekaterina's delicate eyebrows wrinkled for the first time, feeling that she could not understand the situation at hand.
After pondering without success, she then asked, "Has the buyer's identity been investigated?"
"Not yet."
The butler shook his head and continued, "There was a report that one of Keller Fischel's subordinates had made contact with the Snake Gang, it appeared to be about seeking that buyer. The dock's informant confirmed this, but there was no feedback. We don't know if they were taken out, or died in the earlier battle..."
"..."
Yekaterina fell into deep thought upon hearing this.
....
The docks were chaotic.
On Luying's side, nearly all the high-ranking professionals had boarded ships and left the harbor in pursuit.
The aftermath clean-up and salvage operations on the battlefield were also slowly getting underway.
No one noticed that amidst the chaos, a figure quietly slipped beneath the fifth dock.
The skill "Master of Submersible Stealth" allowed Su Lun to quickly and covertly dive into the water, then following the direction from his memory, he began to descend slowly.
His superior dark vision enabled him to see clearly in the pitch-black sea water.
It wasn't long before he found that particular mechanical suit.
As Su Lun swam over, he could still clearly feel that the Soul Shards hadn't completely dissipated, and with a simple peel, he obtained some information.
「Obtained 4 memory fragments from "Dias Fase"」
「You have acquired some information: "Our mission is to act as a decoy, even if it means dying in battle, we must get the blueprints out..."」
「You have gained some "mechanical knowledge"」
「You have acquired information on the "Colonel-level Ship-Cutter IX Mecha"」
「Mecha piloting experience +133」
「Spiritual power +1.1」
Although some of the Soul Shards had dissipated, Su Lun had peeled off only a little information.
But he also knew that this guy was a Colonel in the Luying army, operating a tier four mecha. It was the same one that had wielded the Ship-Cutter, splitting a building in half earlier.
This guy was a graduate from the "Mafa War Mechanical Institute", with a very solid foundation in mechanical theory.
Even if the memories were fragmented, Su Lun still peeled away a lot of useful mechanical knowledge. At least his understanding of the technological level in Rumafa wasn't entirely in the dark now. Most valuable of all were the many open-minded mechanical approaches...
For example, the general structure and design modification direction of this external mecha suit.
However, that piece of information "we are decoys"...
Su Lun had received the information, which was content spoken to this corpse in life.
It sounded like these officers were also decoys?
What does that mean?
Could it be that the blueprints were not on them?
A feint within a feint?
But since the submarine had already set sail, Su Lun didn't bother to delve into it further.
He didn't linger in the water for long. He tied the mecha suit with silken threads and pulled it with great difficulty into his storage space.
Noticing the dense footsteps on the dock, he didn't dare to come ashore right there. Instead, he swam stealthily to the gap between ships at the other end of the dock and observed for a while before finally landing.
At this moment, there were many people on the dock. They were cleaning up the battlefield, looking for traces.
Su Lun didn't dare to stay long. He avoided people's sight and quietly teleported several times to enter the city.
He passed by the ruined Oak Street, which had already been cordoned off, giving him no chance to scavenge.
But having gained a suit of mecha, he was already very satisfied.
.....
A big battle made the peaceful night of Gadolangte City noisy once again.
However, for the ordinary residents, the impact wasn't significant. Most of them were completely confused, even thinking it was a Pirate attack.
Even the information merchants didn't have many people knowing why the fight started.
After all, ambushing a Mafa delegation is something that even if the Luying royal family did it, they wouldn't dare to admit it.
It might eventually be settled as a Pirate attack.
There were patrolling soldiers on the streets, so Su Lun didn't wander around the city anymore and went back to the inn where he had booked a room in the afternoon.
Entering his room and setting up a barrier, he then took out the two-meter-tall "Colonel-level Ship-Cutter IX Mecha".
Looking at the intact battle armor in front of him, Su Lun's eyes were full of a burning desire for knowledge.
He had been hoping to get a Mafa officer's mecha suit, and unexpectedly, he had really managed to get one!
For Su Lun, this suit of mecha was almost an entirely new world of mechanical technology.
The external mecha suit technology of Mafa and the mechanical augmentation of Old Lington are two vastly different development paths.
Compared to them, this sort of external mecha suit is more suitable for Puppets.
With the actual item in front of him, Su Lun put on his magnifying glasses and began studying the mecha meticulously.
Once he started his research, he immediately became immersed in it.
"The blue inscriptions are tier four physical defense runes, the red ones are magic defense runes, and the purple ones must be for energy conduction. Huh...I see, so rune script can also be altered like this, with the changes most likely made to adapt the runes for mechanical use. Triple engraving, quite a sophisticated skill. Some parts don't even seem to be hand-engraved. Has Mafa's technology advanced to the point where even such complex rune carvings can be mechanized…"
Once he saw the runes, Su Lun couldn't take his eyes off them.
Tier four runes were his current area of research, and he wasn't entirely clueless about them.
As he watched, his brain automatically partitioned its activity—recording structures, inferring functions, contemplating questions...
His highly developed brain made his thoughts sharp and his thinking efficiency extremely high.
As he looked, he began to gain knowledge and learn about these complex tier four runes.
It wasn't just the runes; Su Lun took a look at the mecha's coating layers and was equally astonished. "The coating technology is also quite brilliant. The super strong anti-corrosion effect can avoid wear and tear. A pity, though, I can't get the coating formula..."
Then, he turned his attention to the weapon systems, tinkered with the giant Ship-Cutter knife, and took out his equipment to test it.
"The alloy of this Steam Ship-Cutter is quite special, isn't it? Even without energy infusion, its strength has reached level eight, nearly akin to Mithril Blue Steel. The main material is 'Dragon Blood Black Iron', which seems to be a special metal produced inland in Mafa..."
"..."
Su Lun observed the mecha from top to bottom for a while, his amazement growing stronger.
Only someone knowledgeable could appreciate the complexity and the astonishment of the mechanical technology on this suit of battle armor.
Su Lun also better understood what Mr. Hei had told him back then; with Alchemy, the more you know, the more you realize your ignorance.
Until now, Su Lun wasn't sure about his level of mechanical technology, but looking at it now, at least in the Empire of Luying, he could be considered a master.
But looking at the technology on this suit of mecha, he also felt a sense of wistfulness.
He realized there was so much more to learn and explore.
....
It took Su Lun a little over an hour to briefly review all the runes on the exterior of the mecha. The more he looked, the more he was astonished, "To support such a complex mecha, the 'energy core' of this armor must be the real high-tech. But... how to open it?"
He initially thought to remove the corpse first, but gave up after a quick consideration.
The fully covered armor fit seamlessly, even at the joints, there was extremely precise mechanical protection which prevented even water from seeping through.
So, he wasn't in a hurry to dismantle this set of mecha armor.
This was a task that required patience, and could not be rushed.
The armor had a self-destruct device, and disassembling it incorrectly would immediately trigger the self-destruction sequence.
Being knowledgeable in mechanics and equipped with the All-knowing Eye, Su Lun could grasp the details of the armor faster than others.
After he fully understood the runes on the armor and added to that the knowledge fragments extracted into his mind, he was quite confident that he could dismantle the mecha completely.
"Phew..."
Having generally figured out the outer structure of the mecha, Su Lun let out a long sigh and his expression grew more and more excited.
In his study of mechanics, naturally his thoughts went to his own mechanical puppets.
"A pure manual control system, a pursuit of extreme defensive capabilities in materials, resulting in the armor's bulkiness..."
Su Lun smiled as he observed.
The officer's armor was strong, but the heavy armor also made it look towering and clumsy, the feet covered in plate armor as if wearing oversized boots...
Because he was very aware that the pursuit of armor defense and functionality required a certain volume.
The higher the level of runes, the greater the demand for material strength; if the strength isn't sufficient, thickness must be added. Steam power devices also need certain volume, as do weapon systems, cockpit chambers... all these things take up space.
But as a Puppet Master, Su Lun's mechanical puppets didn't need to stuff a person inside!
Without a pilot, they wouldn't need to fear any mysterious series attack methods either!
His "mechanical puppets" certainly needed these technologies.
While it's true that he couldn't decipher the technology just by obtaining the finished product, it was of great significance to him.
Runes, enchantments, construction, conduction, kinetic energy, weapon systems...
Each technology was cutting-edge military tech not available on the market.
You couldn't even buy it with money.
Moreover, the shortcomings of mechanical armor are quite apparent; it requires a group to prevent it from being easily countered by targeted measures.
Previously, Su Lun had personally witnessed a coordinated battle of elite mechanical soldiers, with roles like shield combat, damage output, ranged, logistics, engineering...
A single combat mecha, no matter how powerful, couldn't possibly be equipped with all functions, but several mechas working together could form a formidable defense and inflict tons of damage!
Su Lun, the Puppeteer, was precisely skilled at controlling groups of puppets.
Once he reached the third order, with even better divided attention control abilities, one person's reaction could completely match that of a team.
A mechanical puppet legion was absolutely feasible!
....
The night had passed in this research.
When Su Lun noticed the light outside the window, he realized it was already morning.
At this moment, the room was littered with blueprints, on which were drawn structural analysis diagrams of the battle armor.
Su Lun's eight spider arms and hands had been busy all night, breaking down the runes layer by layer from the armor and transcribing them onto the blueprints.
Just the external runes alone had filled nearly a hundred sheets of paper.
By drawing these personally, the concepts in his mind became clearer.
He might not have mastered these runes yet, but he felt that once he was proficient in the tri-layer rune inscription technique, "copying homework" was definitely doable.
The difficulty with mechanical puppets wasn't in a single technology, but in bringing together the right technologies to forge a combat-capable armor.
One could say that for a mechanic to research this alone, it might take a lifetime and still not produce such a suit of armor.
A hundred years of the Mafa Empire's mechanical revolution, the wisdom of countless genius mechanics, led to these achievements.
Thousands of failed experiments, numerous technical tests and improvements, refined templates.
This also saved Su Lun a great deal of effort.
Once he fully mastered these technologies, Su Lun could certainly create lighter mechanical puppets.
"Phew..."
He exhaled a deep breath of turbid air.
Su Lun, with pen in hand, looking at the mechanical battle armor before him, couldn't help but feel contemplative, "However, without a large forging factory, items like plate armor can't be mass-produced in small workshops. And materials are a big problem too... It would be great to get a few more armors..."
He thought of something and chuckled, shaking his head.
To come across such a complete set of armor was already sheer luck. Otherwise, even if he could capture such high-end mechanical soldiers, they would self-destruct before letting him take the full armor.
Su Lun was very content.
Perhaps visit the legendary Mechanical Holy Land of Mafa?
The idea briefly crossed his mind.
He neatly stacked up the blueprints with his eight-armed spear and stowed the mechanical soldier into his storage space.
After tidying up the room and ensuring nothing was left behind, Su Lun stepped out of the inn's room.
Because he had booked an early boat, planning to leave Gadolangte City and head to the northern lands.
....
The intense battle last night left many scars in the city, with several blocks from Oak Street to the docks full of wounds.
But Gadolangte is one of the most important commercial ports in the North of Luying, with an astonishing daily turnover of people and goods, and by early morning, the port had returned to normal operation.
Su Lun walked the streets, listening to the passersby discuss last night's battle.
But battles on the level of national conflict didn't concern most ordinary people; they still went to work and ate their breakfast, with just a bit more gossip for after meals. On the docks, the porters were bustling about, and the sailors were busy with the sails, setting anchor and sailing out.
Su Lun had no intention of staying here any longer.
Last night's battle had little to do with him, but he had been involved in the killing of Viscount Primor, and he had personally killed several members of the Sea Snake Gang, with a set of battle armor on him...
Staying in the city, he feared, would lead to complications.
If he were to leave, the sooner, the better.
He had already been planning to go to the North to see for himself, especially now with the "prophecy" from the Dalu Druids.
He half-believed, half-doubted prophecies, but still felt that an earlier departure to sea wouldn't hurt.
At the port, he registered casually and found a merchant ship heading for the ice fields of the Far North.
The ride was free, with food and fresh water supplied on board.
Every day, many merchant ships sailed from Gadolangte to the North, and the ship owners were happy to take adventurers along who were on their way to hunt magical beasts. In case of attacks by pirates or sea creatures, adventurers could stand together in resistance.
Soon, a fleet of ten large and small ships set sail together.
Su Lun was on a medium-sized sailboat called the "Mopo Sang." The owner was an exotic goods merchant, heading to the North to collect demon cores, meteorites, rare ores, and various gemstones.
In addition to the crew, there were nearly a hundred adventurers on board.
Su Lun was assigned to a cabin for eight people, with the other seven from a group called "Night Cats Adventuring Party."
The cabin had only a dim oil lamp, small ventilation windows, and was very dark.
Once on board, Su Lun started reading in a corner against the hull.
Unless something unexpected happened, he would spend a long half month on the ship.
His night vision was strong, and the reading was unhindered. The dim light also conveniently disguised the fact that he was flipping through a tome of fourth-level alchemy.
The other adventurers didn't pay any mind to the guy who hadn't spoken a word since boarding and had been burying his head in books the whole time.
After boarding, everyone had little to do.
Other than sleeping, it was all about boasting.
The adventurers quickly struck up conversations.
Su Lun listened for a bit and quickly understood the relationships within this group.
The team leader was Mark, a forty-year-old with a big beard, a second-tier "Jungle Hunter," and an experienced adventurer. He was leading the team to the North to hunt magical beasts for money.
There were a few newcomers in the team from "Visota County" in the East. It seemed like their first time heading to the North, and they were listening to the veterans and the leader talk about how incredibly rich the Far North Ice Field was in resources.
"Captain, I heard that the ice plains to the north are even larger than our empire, is that true?"
"Larger? Ten times, a hundred times larger, practically endless! Us humans have only explored a tiny bit along the coast. I tell you, the Far North Ice Field is not the barren wasteland people from the inland think it is. It's just that we haven't set foot there much and don't understand it..."
"Legend has it that beneath the millions of years of ice, there are ancient ruins frozen in time. If fortune smiles upon you, you might dig up some ancient relics and get rich overnight. Half a year ago, the 'Hydra Slave Group' accidentally entered deep into the Silent Forest when they were capturing demi-human slaves and stumbled upon an ancient temple, finding several cursed artifacts with mighty powers, making a fortune..."
"Captain, can we also go capture slaves? Like ice giants or demi-humans, I see slaves selling for hundreds of thousands at the slave markets!"
"Capturing slaves isn't so easy anymore. Those demi-human tribes are now far from the coast, deep into the ice field. There are powerful magical beast packs there; it's hard to say who would become the prey. Specialized slave groups handle the slave business, let's not think about it and just hunt some magical beasts around the periphery of the ice field."
"Captain, have you ever encountered sea monsters? I heard that there are Gana people in the sea who don't wear clothes, descendants of the elves, each one beautiful and graceful and would repay humans who are good to them. If they find a handsome man, they would come aboard at night, hehehe..."
"Haha, you've been listening to too many fairy tales, kid. Speaking of sea monsters, you better pray we never come across one! Ever heard of the 'Siren's Song'? If you hear that thing, it means the Grim Reaper's knocking on your door. Five years ago, I saw with my own eyes a ghost ship adrift at sea, all the people on board were physically unharmed, but their souls were taken away. They say it was the work of sea monsters..."
"Hiss... that's terrifying."
"Captain, I heard there are treasures everywhere at sea, are those 'Pirate King treasure legends' real?"
"Of course, they're real! Sunken ships, treasures, this sea has plenty of gems... There are also ancient underwater cities! Every year you hear about lucky Navigators and Explorers finding some. It's just that our route has been pretty well explored already, if you really want to find those treasures, you need to venture into the unknown waters to the west. However, you need to be strong to be an Explorer and you need a good ship; those terrifying sea beasts in the deep sea, they don't eat veggies..."
"When I was young working on a big ship, I once encountered a huge sea creature that bit off half the ship in one bite. I barely escaped with my life..."
"Ever heard of dragons? Sometimes when the weather is clear, you can hear dragon roars coming from far out west..."
"And the stories of Serpent Island..."
"Let me tell you, the most famous legend at sea is the 'Cursed Ship'. It's said that sometimes, on a foggy night, lucky folks at sea encounter a Ghost Ship drifting on the water. The ship is loaded with gold and silver treasures and has wine and beautiful women; you can go aboard and take anything you want, party to your heart's content. But, anyone who boards must get off before midnight, otherwise, they can never leave again. Once the Ghost Ship vanishes, you would have to become a ghost along with it..."
"..."
The ship had sailed for half a day, and many stories had been told.
Su Lun was also quite intrigued.
The tales told by these old adventurers might not be reliable, but they certainly were rich in twists and carried strong narrative appeal.
They also informed him about many legends of this sea area.
Yet he hadn't expected the story of the "Cursed Ship" to become so lively, just as the spooky and thrilling atmosphere had begun to spread through the cabin...
Suddenly, there was a commotion coming from the deck.
"Oh, damn it! How could such thick fog appear in this area? Everyone, be careful, we have entered the fog zone, beware of pirates and sea beasts..."
Upon hearing this, everyone in the cabin simultaneously showed a strange look on their faces.
Su Lun felt it couldn't be such a coincidence to encounter a Ghost Ship.
Because it was daytime.
However, this fog did seem abnormal.
Having peeled away a pirate's memories before, Su Lun had picked up some knowledge of "navigational weather identification". He looked out through the vent and gauged the air pressure, humidity, and temperature, realizing that this weather seemed unlikely to form such dense fog...
Before long, he heard the sailors on deck exclaiming as if they had seen some terrifying monster: "My God... what is that!"

chapters.title: Chapter 234 - 234: Super Battleship
chapters.content:
Hearing the sailors' exclamations on deck, everyone in the cabin rushed out.
Su Lun didn't know why, but he had a slight sense of foreboding.
The fog wasn't natural?
He thought of something called "war fog," which is a large-scale artificial fog developed to conceal military movements on the battlefield.
Su Lun instinctively had a thought: they had been ambushed!
The sea looked boundless, but in reality, the shipping route from Gadronte Harbor to the northern lands was fixed to only those one or two mature routes.
Estimating their journey, they should currently be in a place called the "Bartholomew Strait." This strait was named after the navigator who discovered this shipping route.
This sea area was like the narrow middle part of a funnel, getting narrower and narrower. Near the strait, there was a large area of reefs, and passing ships could only be safe by following the established shipping lanes.
If someone were to set up a blockade, this would be one of the best ambush spots.
Moreover, this was an area frequently infested with pirates.
At the moment, since there were no sounds of battle, it seemed that the situation was not too urgent—at least there would not be an emergency such as encountering giant sea monsters, pirates, or running aground on a reef.
As these thoughts flashed through his mind, Su Lun put away his books and cautiously made his way to the deck.
He was also very curious about what the sailors had seen to elicit such exclamations.
Just as he looked up, the massive object in the fog rudely burst into his field of vision.
A... very huge steam-powered steel-clad warship!
The "Monte Cristo" the medium-sized sailing ship that Su Lun was currently aboard, seemed like a kitten compared to a male lion when placed in front of that exaggerated behemoth, appearing so fragile and defenseless.
This was a massive warship as gigantic as an aircraft carrier from his previous world, with a height equivalent to twenty or thirty-story buildings. Three huge smokestacks were spewing thick black smoke. Large rivets fixed steel plates around the hull, as if they were armoring the behemoth with a layer of armor, creating a strong visual impact of invincibility. The bow was as sharp as an axe, with a lion's head-shaped gold ram at the top, adorned with inscriptions oozing with firmness, visible to the naked eye, as if any ship that collided with it would be instantly destroyed into dust.
The most exaggerated aspect was that the ship bristled with artillery of various calibers!
Like the spines on a hedgehog's back, ominously displayed.
There were six long main gun barrels, each twenty to thirty meters, at the front and rear of the ship. Aside from that, there were turrets scattered all over the hull, with thousands of densely-packed gun barrels. There were also giant harpoons, alchemical crossbows, heavy machine gun control stations... a myriad of war weapons that made one's scalp tingle at the sight!
More is better, big is beautiful, caliber is justice, and within the range is the truth!
This was the shipbuilding philosophy of this steam-mechanical era.
This ironclad warship perfectly encapsulated the meaning of that phrase.
Massive!
Armed to the teeth!
Sturdy!
....
Ten wooden sailing ships on their way to the northern lands all stopped in front of this steel behemoth, with everyone crowding onto the deck, utterly astonished by the iron beast that lay before them.
"This... how can there be such a huge steel ship! My God, could it be that the Mafa Empire's fleet has come to attack us?"
"Look, it's not a Mafa ship. That on the warship is Duke Raphael's noble flag!"
"How is that possible... How could our empire have such a gigantic warship?!"
"..."
Beyond shock, there was only more shock!
The appearance of this massive battleship completely exceeded everyone's knowledge on board.
Seeing this battleship, Su Lun, in addition to being shocked, immediately realized something ominous: "Duke Raphael actually secretly built such a powerful warship?"
Seeing how shocked the crew members were, it was obvious that there was no news of it in the outside world.
And now it was exposed?
Sulin even suspected that the Royal Family of Ruleen might not be aware that Duke Raphael had this "asset."
Being a mechanic himself, he glanced at the caliber of the cannons and the length of the gun barrels on the ship, roughly estimating the range of these guns.
The larger the turret, the sturdier the ship's body needed to be to withstand the impact of the gunfire. Only an ironclad battleship could be equipped with so many and such massive cannons.
It was not just about size; this also involved complex mechanical engineering!
This type of warship might appear in the Mafa Empire, but absolutely not in Luying.
Because the technological content within the warship was at least several decades ahead of Luying's current warships!
....
No wonder there was a war fog—it was used to conceal this super dreadnought.
However, Su Lun was worried about something else.
You've seen the secrets, can they let you live?
Traditional sailing ships stand no chance against such maritime steel fortresses, even with top enchantments and materials, they are easily destroyed.
Apart from the advantage of speed in fleeing, none of their other qualities could compare.
The cannons on these sailing ships are like rifles against tanks—simply inadequate!
Sailing warships might have a chance to escape from ordinary ironclad ships,
But not from this behemoth!
The range of cannons this size could be tens of nautical miles; if you see it, you're within range, with no chance to escape!
...
Others didn't know what Duke Rafael was doing here, but Su Lun immediately guessed it.
Not long ago, the pirates under the "King of the North Sea" attacked Black Reef and looted Duke Rafael's "mines", and just yesterday, the [Super Mechanic Soldier Blueprint] was auctioned off at Gadronte Harbor...
This was no small grievance.
He was now concealed by the war fog, lying in wait here, obviously out for revenge.
"Could it be that the blueprint wasn't carried off by Mafa's people last night?"
Su Lun immediately thought of the Soul Shard from the mechanical soldier he stripped last night, "Our task is to act as bait..."
It was indeed possible!
Even with submarines, this was Luying's hinterland; it would be difficult for those people to break out of the blockade with the blueprint and escape.
It's not impossible, but the likelihood of being intercepted was greater.
"So... last night was actually a feint, the Mafa legion commander himself led people to break through as a decoy to attract fire. In fact, the blueprint didn't leave Gadronte Harbor at all last night!"
Su Lun immediately connected all the clues in his mind and deduced the rough truth of the matter.
He originally thought that such matters had nothing to do with him, but now it seemed he had been implicated.
Moreover, if Duke Rafael's warship was keeping such a high profile here, then he must have some precise intelligence.
"It seems that those guys have some means to locate the blueprint..."
Su Lun murmured to himself.
And now he was almost certain, the one with the blueprint was hidden on one of the ships in this fleet!
"Seems like I'm not having the best of luck..."
Su Lun felt as though if he did not leave the harbor, he might not be implicated.
Could the Druid's prophecy have been wrong?
Coming to the sea, not only did he not receive protection, but encountered danger instead.
But obviously, that was not the case.
The crisis stemmed not only from this ironclad ship but from something else!
Suddenly, a strong palpitation struck him, that familiar sensation of being "thought of" washed over him like dark clouds overhead.
This feeling, just like the one he had in Old Lington when he was tracked down by the divination of William Regadi's people!
Su Lun immediately had a bad premonition, "Someone is divining me!"
And by the time he sensed it, a gaze from the dreadnought locked onto him as well.
....
Half an hour earlier.
On the "Duke Rafael" battleship, in the captain's quarters.
The exquisite magic crystal chandelier illuminated the spacious room with a warm, dim yellow glow that bathed the chamber in a lush spring hue.
The cabin's decor was elegant and luxurious, exuding the noble air of aristocracy in every detail.
Directly opposite the door was a row of neatly arranged bookshelves, and in front of a vast sea chart was a solid wood desk. Adorned with navigation instruments, on the desk was an open bottle of red wine, and in two tall glasses remained some undrunk scarlet liquid. On the rim of one glass, there still lingered the faint mark of lips. Walking towards the inner room, the soft cashmere carpet was scattered with some clothing items—luxurious black gowns, women's intimate garments.
After a while, a mature woman with undiminished charm walked naked from the bed.
She picked up the clothes scattered on the carpet and chairs, standing in front of the dressing mirror.
Though the woman's face bore the grace of years, the splendid naked body reflected in the mirror shone with a luster no less smooth than a young girl's skin. One could tell from the skin alone that this was a noblewoman of exceptional care.
The middle-aged man also got out of bed, embracing her from behind, his large hands kneading the delicate and smooth skin, seemingly insatiable.
The man had a beard, a robust body, yet there was a calm and intimidating composure about him.
This man was none other than the current hereditary Duke of the Rafael family, Vogt Rafael.
"Lady Portia, the time spent with you is truly delightful," he said.
Hearing these frivolous words, the mature woman didn't find anything amiss; instead, she smiled coquettishly. She freed herself from those greedy hands and said, "Oh, Duke, I am but an old woman whose charms are fading. Your compliments should be reserved for those young girls..."
Lady Portia indeed was a duchess, but not Duke Rafael's.
Duke Rafael looked at the naked beauty before him and generously lavished his praise: "No, madam, in my eyes, you are the most perfect lover."
Lady Portia, not minding in the least, laughed lightly at his words.
This was praise for her.
Such ambiguous relationships were not uncommon in the Lu Ying noble circles.
It was no novelty for high-ranking nobles to have several lovers; not only were the lords and young masters promiscuous, but the ladies and misses were too. Even among the upper-class circles, the elites would brag about their numerous affairs.
Duke Rafael asked, "Won't you stay a little longer?"
Lady Portia had just put on her intimate garments and was pulling her skirt over her hips to cover much of her revealed charms, casually replying, "Didn't you say, Duke, that the blueprints will arrive in half an hour? We should also be going out... Although I don't mind, it would be rather awkward if William saw us, given that he is my son."
Duke Rafael laughed at her words, "Young Master William is indeed talented."
By this time, Lady Portia had already dressed, and she was now standing in front of the mirror, putting on a dazzling diamond necklace.
Duke Rafael, ever the gentleman, took the necklace from her hand and helped her put it on.
The two engaged in sporadic conversation.
"Duke, are you not the least bit concerned about the blueprint?"
"The blueprint's material itself contains a special marker. Whether through sealing in space or other hidden methods, I can lock on to its location. It can't be lost. Moreover, the core part of the blueprint is inscribed with spiritual power. Even if given to those pirates, in such a short span of time, they would have no ability to copy it. The infuriating thing is that they destroyed a lot of important research equipment in the institute, and those mechanics..."
"Oh? Is that so..."
"Those pirates have some smarts too, having sold what they stole immediately. Heh... It's hilarious that the royal family thought they could take advantage of the situation."
"Lu Ying has decayed to its core, the royal family's internal struggles never pause. Arms dealers only see the profits brought by war, without a care for anything else."
"Hmph, a bunch of bloated parasites; they will soon be the death of the entire empire because of their actions."
"..."
...
Before long, Lady Portia, now fully dressed, made her way to the deck.
A handsome young man in a white military uniform was diligently sorting through a pile of documents on the deck.
If Su Lun were here, he would certainly have realized that these documents contained various kinds of intelligence about him.
His identity within the Order of the Cross, photos of his bald punk style, social connections, movement trajectories, events participated in, and the methods he was skilled in...
By the young man's side, an old mage dressed in a court mage's robe was divining something with a strand of hair when he suddenly said, "Your Highness, the target has appeared within thirty nautical miles to the southwest. He's heading in our direction."
The young man was none other than William Regadi, the primary heir of the Regadi family!
William respectfully nodded to the old man, "Thank you for your efforts, Master Maburite."
He paused, then smirked, "Heh, he's coming right to us. That saves us the trouble of looking for him."
At that moment, Lady Portia had also approached.
She looked at her son and smiled gently, "William, what are you looking at?"
"My lady!"
Seeing her approach, the robed elder and several guards nodded in turn before leaving the deck, giving the two space for their conversation.
William glanced at the woman, seemingly guessing something, and said lazily, "Mother, I mean... even if we need to form an alliance with the Rafael family, you don't have to get that close to them."
Lady Portia, not minding his tone, replied, "No, it's not entirely about the exchange of interests. Duke Rafael is quite a charming gentleman indeed. What a pity that his Princess Teresa met with an accident, otherwise you could have..."
This sort of matter wasn't something worth fussing over in noble circles. William shook his head after listening, obviously not interested in the topic, and cut her off, "Whatever, as you wish."
Lady Portia reached out and took the intelligence report from his hands, "Still looking at that guy's information?"
"Yeah."
Hearing this, William said coldly, "Heh, that 'Brother Fick' hasn't been quiet even during his exile. It's surprising how much trouble he can stir up even in a mining pit."
Lady Portia casually flipped through a couple of pages before saying, "Rest assured, the bastard left by your philandering father and his lover poses no threat to your inheritance rights."
She looked at the astonishing achievements listed on Su Lun's report and immediately felt threatened, her tone shifting abruptly, "However, he indeed should be eliminated to prevent future problems."
William said, "The fact that Fick has caused such a stir clearly means he's come upon some great fortune. The intelligence from the branch family suggests that the old man has deciphered the hidden treasure map in 'Isaac's Alchemy Manuscript.' My Brother Fick must have found Isaac's legacy and received that legendary talent, or perhaps some other inheritances..."
Lady Portia also raised an eyebrow, disdainfully saying, "'The All-knowing Eye' is just an S-rank talent that isn't very useful, far inferior to yours. That talent can't undergo a second awakening and has almost no combat power. This time, William, you've received the recognition of the family's heirloom relic, and you will inevitably advance to the seventh rank in the future. With the support of family resources, reaching the pinnacle of alchemy is within reach... No one can pose a threat to you."
After all, they were once part of the Mafian Empire's royal lineage, the Regadi family had too many ancient secrets and treasures, their foundation incomparable to outsiders' imaginations.
William listened and, although he said nothing, the pride on his face showed he agreed with his mother's words.
Among his peers, whether in terms of talent, knowledge, or strength, no one could match him.
He had the confidence to look down upon his rivals!
At that moment, William's gaze suddenly turned cold as he thought of something, "Although those fools from the branch family are stupid, they have cleared some troubles for me. Almost all of them have been killed, yet this 'Fick' is still alive. Even the dimwit Eiven died underground... The report also says he has joined some mysterious organization, the Gold-Patterned Cloak. The strength of that high-order blood race is formidable, he could become a big problem in the future. So, it's better to eliminate him sooner rather than later."
"However, I believe our William didn't come personally just for this, am I right?"
At her words, Lady Portia smiled and changed the subject, "I remember Duke Lance's fourth daughter is named 'Yekaterina,' right? Oh, she was such a beauty when I saw her five years ago. I still clearly remember her lovely purple hair."
As a mother, she naturally knew what her son was thinking and teased, "I recall, she was also your classmate at the royal academy, wasn't she, William?"
William didn't bother hiding his thoughts, saying forthrightly, "Katyusha is the most outstanding girl I have ever met. And only I am suited to marry her!"
A glint of mockery flashed through Lady Portia's bright eyes, and she laughed again, "So, are you resentful because the elders plan to bring back Fick, letting that guy arrange a marital alliance with the Lance family, and that's why you have a murderous intent?"
"..."
At those words, a flicker of hesitation crossed William's eyes.
He neither confirmed nor denied it.
He felt vaguely that he should not let jealousy cloud his vision.
Portia, keenly catching the subtle change in her son's demeanor, spoke seriously, "No, my son, you did nothing wrong! Only the powerful can have everything. Always remember, we are royalty. The one at the top isn't that merciful, not even to anyone!"
Upon hearing this, as if something struck a chord deep in his heart,
William looked at his mother, and the wavering light in his eyes suddenly became resolute.
Portia spoke earnestly, "If you can secure the support of both the Lance and the Rafael families, our hope of restoring the nation is promising. Now Ruying has become a tree decaying at its roots, your father and those old-fashioned elders are still pinning their hopes on the Ruying royal family, heh... How foolish!"
After a pause, she gazed into the distant fog, advising, "My dear William, strive to become stronger... only the strong deserve to have everything!"
William responded calmly, "Understood, Mother."
While they were talking, they watched a fleet of sailing ships disappear into the mist.
At that moment, the Mage in the robe suddenly appeared on deck, pointing at one vessel and saying, "Young Master, my lady, the adventurer in the bald leather attire on the deck of the ship flying the parrot flag—that's the target!"
....
Su Lun felt rather speechless; on a ship, trouble comes from the sky.
When he sensed the gaze that had locked onto him, he understood immediately.
His actions had always been clean, hardly leaving any trail.
Being the object of someone's attention was undoubtedly due to his original... Regadi family!

chapters.title: Chapter 235 - 235 The Death of Su Lun
chapters.content:
Duke Raphael personally arrived, and naturally, he was determined to retrieve the "Super Mechanical Warrior Blueprint."
Su Lun suspected that there was a spy from the Mafa Empire among the fleet, on board one of the ships.
As expected, when the steel behemoth emerged from the mist, a figure suddenly leaped from the deck of the "Santa Maria," a sailboat not far ahead, and dived into the water.
The response was extremely decisive!
It appeared to be a high-order professional with no small measure of strength.
But obviously, Duke Raphael's side was also well-prepared. Almost at the same instant, dozens of professionals dressed in white military uniforms also leaped from the steel behemoth.
There were those who flew with winged gear, those who dove into the water with aquatic gear, and even those who skimmed across the surface of the water...
Dozens of people chased after the Mafa spy, forming an encirclement.
In just a moment, the sound of intense fighting came from the mist not far away.
....
Seeing the cannons pointed towards their fleet, Su Lun knew that Duke Raphael was set on annihilating the entire convoy.
With the spy drawing fire, he had intended to use teleportation to sneak into the sea and quietly leave, perhaps going unnoticed.
But now, with those several piercing gazes fixed on him from the deck, Su Lun knew concealment was meaningless.
Compared to this gigantic warship, the folks from the Lei family were the real threat.
"Probably another divination based on bloodlines, the original owner's troubles are really not small..."
Su Lun was filled with solemnity.
The Lei family was a top force, only slightly inferior to the royal families of the two major empires, and if the problem wasn't completely resolved, troubles could continue indefinitely.
But he couldn't understand why they were so adamant on killing him. Wasn't the original owner's father back in power? Who would persist in wanting to kill the original owner?
Su Lun thought it might be some bloody conflict of interest, like inheritance rights?
But right now, there was no time to ponder such details; he needed to consider how to escape this death trap!
The killing intent in those gazes was as glaring as staring at the sun, and the sensation of walking barefoot on sharp blades overwhelmed him, leaving Su Lun without any false hopes.
Without Mr. Jing by his side, he had no helpers to call upon; everything had to be relied upon himself.
He had never experienced such a brush with death, feeling as if his entire body was immersed in ice water. Hormones secreted in large amounts due to the stress, and his thoughts whirred into action at high speed.
Unable to conceal himself, he decisively prepared to make an all-out run for it!
His hands formed magician's seals, and with a tug, a spatial channel opened before him. Without hesitating, he stepped through it and instantly appeared a hundred meters away on the sea's surface.
As he fell, the seals Su Lun formed in mid-air were ready, and he uttered softly, "Gear·Release!"
In the instant that the Hexagram Alchemy Array lit up, an eight-armed spear appeared behind him.
The eight-armed spear had the exceptional ability to move through barriers, which had resolved countless problems for him in the past.
What was even more remarkable was that after Su Lun landed on the sea's surface, he didn't sink!
The eight-armed spear stepped on the water as if it were land, the spear's legs moving rapidly, disregarding the rolling waves, and he surged forward at high speed.
Because of the extreme speed, he even kicked up a white mist in his wake.
This was the newly developed water-walking ability of his eight-armed spear gear!
Having considered the endless oceans of the surface world, Su Lun had felt the need for an ability to move across water.
He had carefully studied the structure of the "water spider" spears, realizing that such spiders could move on water because of the numerous fine hairs on the spears that provided sufficient surface tension when in contact with water.
This had given him great inspiration.
Su Lun had already researched the functionalities of the "Eight-Armed Spear" gear to its limits, and controlling the fine hairs was no issue for him. Although there were slight differences between the structure of spears used by land and water spiders, this was not an insurmountable problem for Su Lun, an Alchemist who was an expert in engineering.
Back in Old Lington, he had already precisely tested the water-walking abilities of the spears.
Now it was time for them to come into play.
Su Lun used the eight-armed spear to move swiftly across the sea's surface, occasionally interspersed with spatial teleportation, covering a hundred meters in an instant.
With this slick escape combination, a look again showed that he had moved several hundred meters away.
This speed made it difficult for even fourth or fifth-tier professionals to catch up.
After all, it was the sea, where the majority of moving capabilities were restricted. Even standard winged gear couldn't match Su Lun's spear speed in its flight through the sky.
Plus, with artillery aiming from behind and the "All-knowing Eye" combined with his ultra-high neural reaction speed, he could also dodge in advance.
It looked like he was gradually getting out of danger.
However, Su Lun harbored no illusions.
Such a large ship surely had several high-order professionals specialized in pursuit.
....
On the deck of the gigantic warship, Lady Portia and William looked at the fleeing figure without any urgency on their faces.
However, Lady Portia squinted at the speed of Su Lun's escape and muttered with a sense of crisis, "Spatial Ability? That fellow actually found such rare advancement material underground… quite the luck."
As a Duchess, her insight was not low; Spatial Ability was a highly advanced and rare skill.
If he could develop this skill to a high level, the threat would not be small.
William raised an eyebrow, nonchalantly saying, "Just low-level use of Spatial Ability, far from a true understanding of Space Law."
Seeing that Su Lun had already run quite a distance, a family guard from the side spoke up, "Your Highness, Madam, shall I go capture the target?"
Listening to this, William shook his head, his gaze flashing sharply, "No! I'll go myself."
Once professionals ascended to the higher ranks, they would awaken some perceptive abilities beyond the five senses.
He had a feeling that if he didn't personally kill that guy, he would become a huge problem in the future.
He certainly didn't want to leave any threats for himself.
Lady Portia, standing beside him, also showed approval of her son upon hearing this, "Mhm. Go ahead, but be careful."
William looked at Su Lun, who had already submerged into the sea, and a mocking smile like a cat that had caught a mouse appeared on his face. He quickly formed forty-eight sorcerer's seals with both hands, his gaze intensifying, "Armor Dispel!"
As soon as the hand seals were completed, the deck suddenly filled with a dense concentration of wind elemental power.
Giant pale blue wings suddenly appeared behind William.
Upon closer inspection, the wings were not made of any physical substance, but were purely "elemental wings" formed from the condensation of wind elements!
As soon as the wings spread, the onlookers' cloaks on the ship fluttered in the sudden gust of wind, and William had already vanished from sight.
....
Su Lun had already been running for a while and was puzzled as to why no one was pursuing him.
Despite the absence of pursuers, those few strands of watchful eyes were still locked on him and had not shifted away.
The cloud of death continued to hang over his head, not dissipating but instead growing denser and heavier.
"Could it be... the opponent has an unbelievably fast professional among them?"
Even though Su Lun was perplexed, he dared not slow his movements.
Running on the surface of the sea was ordinarily suicidal.
Those who enjoyed fishing would understand how dangerous a high-speed target on the water could be. It is like lure fishing; such "high-speed targets" can easily attract the attentions of the big guys hiding beneath the water and be swallowed in an instant.
Besides, the seas of this world were not inhabited by merely large fish but various gigantic sea monsters!
But Su Lun had no choice.
Seeing that no one was chasing him, he once again teleported into the water and continued to swim stealthily, hoping to use the fog and the resistance of the sea water to shake off those few persistent threads.
Suddenly, his fears became reality.
Su Lun kept teleporting rapidly, his peripheral vision constantly alert to his rear.
Out of nowhere, he blurted out a curse, "F*ck!"
It was like a scene from a horror movie where, although Mr. Ghost was still far away, in the blink of an eye, he appeared right up close.
When the image of that teleporting figure with wings flashed before Su Lun's eyes, his heart skipped a beat with intense shock.
That astonishing speed was not achieved through spatial displacement, nor was it like Mr. Jing's special optical displacement technique, but purely a mastery of wind elements for hovering and rapid teleportation.
No wonder there was no hurry to chase; with this method, let Su Lun run forty-nine meters ahead, and on the fiftieth meter, he could be caught!
"This seems to be a young master from the Regalido noble family?"
Su Lun recognized the person's face, recalling a vague impression in his mind.
But whoever it was didn't matter; what was important was seeing his control over the elements, confirming he was a sixth-ranked professional.
Upon identifying the pale blue wings behind the man, Su Lun had an ominous feeling, "Legendary-quality flying armor[Wings of Wind God Bird]! The wings of a 'Wind God Bird' phantom beast...where did these guys find such an extinct elemental divine bird from countless eras ago?!"
Even as composed as he was, witnessing the winged figure surging hundreds of meters in an instant, he couldn't help but feel agitated.
Apparently, he wasn't the only one who had encountered fortune.
It was Su Lun's first time seeing "legendary-quality" alchemy armor.
He was currently equipped with two sets of dark gold-quality armor, so he naturally knew the monumental difference in effectiveness between grades of armor.
The person behind him being able to integrate a legendary-quality armor indicated that his own strength must also be incredibly strong.
A deadly foe!
"The Regalido family truly has profound resources..."
With a sigh in his heart, Su Lun felt even more bitter.
He had understood before that the Regalido royal bloodline had a high probability of awakening various "wind-related" talents.
It seemed this winged man possessed some sort of wind talent.
The compatibility with this armor must be very high.
"Could it be[A-003-Wind Speaker]?"
Su Lun looked at the liquid-like pale blue wind elements congregating around the man, and numerous thoughts flashed through his mind in an instant.
The talents ranked in the top four of the A grade were earth, wind, water, and fire, the four basic elements.
The chance of awakening such a talent was one in a hundred million.
This was an extremely rare and powerful top-tier talent!
Although under equal-level techniques, the[Wind Speaker]talent might not have the destructive power of[A-039-Thunder], nor the eerie effectiveness of light or dark elements.
However, elemental talents of the same rank could exhibit an almost invincible strength in combat, as they are nearly everywhere and inexhaustible.
They could easily manipulate elements in quantities a thousand or a million times greater than others!
Moreover, the four elements talent is the source of all elemental gifts, including control over some elemental variations.
Take "A-036-Flame Lady," for example, which is actually a hybrid talent between "A-001-Fire Thief" and the ability of the earth element. In a contest between the two, the latter would have an obvious innate advantage due to elemental suppression, especially when they are of the same tier.
But the more he deduced, the more Su Lun's heart trembled.
In an instant, his mind raced through countless possibilities,
but all pointed to one conclusion,
it seemed like... he was doomed to die this time?
....
The gap in rank was too vast, and whether it was the breeding gear "Wind God Bird's Feathers" or the wind element talent, both were factors that grossly exaggerated the enhancement of teleportation.
Even though Su Lun was running with all his might, in the blink of an eye, he was still caught up by that person.
Even through the water, he could feel the chilling killing intent, which was like an ice dagger to the bone.
At this moment, the winged man flying in the sky was not in a hurry to kill, seeming to want to get a good look at the "prey's" techniques.
Through the refraction of the light in the water, Su Lun could even clearly see the scorn on that person's face.
"The only chance is that the enemy underestimates me..."
Seeing this, Su Lun didn't hesitate at all, and formed the sorcerer's seals immediately, "Flesh Alchemy Technique: Third Stage Hormone Frenzy!"
Hormones surged into his limbs in large amounts, giving him the sensation of overwhelming power.
This was an amount sufficient to cause death.
This time, without Teacher Sereya watching over him, there was no one to pull him back at the crucial moment.
But without going all out, he was bound to die all the same.
After the hormone surge, Su Lun's speed increased several-fold. He was no longer swimming underwater; he was running wildly on the sea surface, his figure as fast as a white rainbow.
Seeing this, William flying above not only wasn't surprised but instead let out a disdainful chuckle upon seeing the "scene" he was hoping for, "Huh... This secret technique is quite high-level, actually allowing for such a huge physical amplification. It's not even recorded in the intelligence. It seems this guy has quite a few secrets..."
He also knew from the intelligence that this "Brother Fick" had a banned weapon-level black scythe. Although the chance of the other party hitting him was minuscule, he wasn't careless.
He wanted to wait.
After all, spatial storage is different from a storage ring. Should the target die, the spatial storage could collapse, and the contents could scatter just about anywhere.
But just then, before Su Lun's black scythe struck, he watched him pull out a pocket watch and press it.
"Watkins' Pocket Watch" could provide a 2-5 times speed boost for a short time!
Though it consumed life randomly, Su Lun couldn't care less about that now.
If he couldn't escape now, he wouldn't have a chance later.
He knew the gap in ranks was too large to choose battle.
Even if he took out the black scythe, he had no chance whatsoever.
Now he saw a pitch-black sea cave on the ocean floor, bottomless and dark, and immediately thought of last night's prophecy by the Druid of the Dalu tribe: "The prophecy tells me that you will go through a death ordeal in the future. But... the ocean will protect you."
This was his "death ordeal"!
If the prophecy was coming true, was the second half of it also true?
The ocean?
This was the only chance he could think of now.
The moment he pressed the pocket watch, Su Lun's speed surged again.
He gambled on the maximum five times speed!
With this increased speed, he dove into the deep sea, disappearing from sight in the blink of an eye.
....
Seeing this, William's calm demeanor shattered, and his brows finally furrowed as he wondered, "Does he have some other means of escape?"
The unequivocal rush towards the sea left one doubting.
Luckily, he came in person.
If not for his slippery escape tactics, others really might not be able to catch that guy.
Moreover...
At just the second tier, to display such an astonishing performance, one can only imagine how phenomenal he would be if he advanced to a higher tier?
For the first time, William truly felt "threatened" by someone of his generation.
He absolutely wouldn't allow, within the Regaldi royal household, the emergence of a genius even more exceptional than himself!
Moreover, that astonishing speed was heading towards a deep, bottomless sea cave. Even if he wanted to chase, it was too late.
Although he knew that such a temporary augmentation secret technique wouldn't last long, his instinct told William that he must not let this "Brother Fick" escape again!
The Regaldi royal treasury had many treasures, and though he was curious about the black scythe, it was still something he could do without.
Seeing this, William stood in the air, his eyes glinting fiercely as he formed the sorcerer's seals with his hands and uttered a light cry: "Condense!"
At a glance, following this spell, a colossal turquoise figure materialized behind him, a majestic entity with angry eyes, wielding an elemental bow and arrow.
This was the secret technique passed down through the Regaldi royal family, one of the four guardian spirits' ultimate mysteries—the Wind's "Phantom Guardian."
```
....
Su Lun's peripheral vision caught the scene as well.
But his heart held no surprise anymore, only charging fearlessly towards the pitch-black sea cavern.
William watched him flee and formed another sorcerer's seal, shouting out, "Wind Language Song: Rhombic Arrow!"
As the heptagram behind him lit up, he made a motion as if drawing a bow, and at the same time, the azure phantom also mimicked the action. The bow, made of wind elements, bent like a full moon, and with a "whoosh," an elemental arrow shot out towards the fleeing figure.
The arrow, silently formed from multiple secret techniques, hit the water without resistance. It crossed a kilometer in a blink and struck Su Lun's back instantly.
The next moment, the high-pressure wind elements within the elemental arrow exploded violently. The fierce wind pressed against the sea, pushing it to either side and instantly creating a giant whirlpool.
Within the storm, it was as if countless tiny blades were flying chaotically, a sight painfully sharp to behold.
Not only Su Lun's body but even the fish in the area were instantly shredded into tiny pieces by the ferocious wind elements, bursting into a mist of blood.
Su Lun was dead.
His body torn to pieces, utterly destroyed.
"Still too weak after all..."
As his consciousness faded, Su Lun truly felt what the experience of "Death" was.
This is death...
He felt as though he had grasped something.
Like sand through the fingers, he held on to it at that moment.
He held onto that indescribable, ineffable thing that Mr. Jing had told him about.
Without truly experiencing death, how could one understand the laws of death?
Now, Su Lun felt he was almost able to touch it.
...
Did Su Lun want to escape?
No.
He was gambling.
Gambling that the other party wouldn't find his body.
And wouldn't want to look for it.
Because he had a sealed item on him.
[Thanatos's Death Proxy]
Quality: Legendary
Description: A life borrowed from the god of death, dare you use it?
Cursed Feature: After a blood sacrifice, the proxy will take a lethal attack in place of the host; but after resurrection, you will hear whispers from the unknown for the next month, the seductive voice of demons; you may glean some high-level demonic secret techniques from it, but there's a high chance it will cause mental instability.
Detailed Explanation: An imitation Divine Artifact, trading souls with the god of death for a chance at rebirth;
He had found it previously at the Dawn Relic [Hotel 1911].
And now he used it.
Su Lun didn't know if the Death Proxy could resurrect him or in what form he would be resurrected.
But he thought of the Druid's words from last night, "The ocean will shelter you."
This was the best option Su Lun could come up with.
If he were on land, he might be relentlessly hunted down to death even after being revived.
The ocean?
That's probably what it meant.
.....
William in the sky watched the target explode into a cloud of blood, his face showing no emotion.
If this had been on land, he certainly would have taken an interest in seeing the body.
But now, it was probably hard to even find pieces of it.
Large chunks of the body sank into the sea, and the smell of blood attracted a school of fish. The fish darted towards it, muddling the water.
William glanced at the scene and then turned to leave.
He was certain that his strike had definitely killed "Brother Fick".
....
"Do you desire power...?"
Su Lun didn't know in what condition his consciousness was, as if he were half-asleep and half-awake.
But he heard a whisper coming from beyond.
He seemed to understand the meaning of death.
Too weak after all...
As his consciousness slipped away, he responded, "I do."
```

chapters.title: Chapter 236 - 236: Grim Reaper
chapters.content:
"Hey, everyone, look—there's someone in the sea!"
"Pull him up and let's see."
"Well, look at that—a rich guy. His storage ring is so big... Hey, there are even a few 'rune treasure chests' inside!"
"Just the chests alone are worth over a hundred thousand rix-dollars, and the contents must be very valuable. Looks like we're about to make a fortune."
"But Captain, we can't open these treasure chests..."
"Let's keep the man for now. When he wakes up, we'll ask him for the chest passwords and his identity. We might just hit a bigger jackpot."
"Tests show he's a second-tier professional... Don't be careless, take him to the cell, and remember to apply the anti-magic locks."
"Yes, Captain Boone."
...
In a dazed state, Su Lun seemed to regain a sliver of consciousness.
He remembered some things, but they were fragmented.
It was like being in a nightmare; no matter what, he couldn't open his eyes.
He tried to gather his focus to wake up, but it felt like some force inexplicably scattered it...
The murmurs echoing in his brain became more severe, and he couldn't make out what the devilish whispers were trying to say. He only felt his consciousness growing heavier, like demon hands tearing at him, dragging him toward an endless abyss.
It was like that nightmare of drowning, unable to die, yet unable to break free.
Suddenly, he heard a woman's hysterical scream.
As if triggering some deep-seated reflex, Su Lun abruptly felt his consciousness return to his body.
He heard heavy panting and that lecherous laughter tinged with depravity.
"Hey, Pablo, don't you play too rough. It'd be bad if you killed the hostage. This one belongs to the 'Tulip Commerce Guild.' We have to keep her for the ransom when the captain gets back."
"Relax, I'm just having a bit of fun, not taking a chunk of flesh. We only promised to keep a live person, not that we couldn't touch. Besides, the vice-captain and the boys all had their turn; why shouldn't I taste the flavor of these rich ladies and misses. Hahaha..."
"..."
Su Lun couldn't open his eyes.
His mind still wasn't capable of thinking clearly, passively receiving all this information.
He heard the cries and anguished sobbing of women, as well as other voices.
"Pirate lords, please, let my wife go, I'll pay the ransom..."
"Please don't harm my daughter. I'll give you all my fortune, just please stop hurting her!!!"
"Please, I'm begging you, stop... please... stop..."
"..."
The pleas were futile, met only with scornful laughter.
And in that moment,
Su Lun felt waves of intense negative emotions so poignant that they pierced the softest parts of his heart, bleeding him dry.
Surrounded by the ugliness of humanity, the depraved laughter echoing with greed and desire unlocked the chains that suppressed the demon in the depths of his soul.
Suddenly!
Su Lun regained control over his body.
He opened his eyes.
But... his eyes were filled with brutality!
Those were terrifying eyes, burning with red fury.
It was as if the will residing within the body was no longer human, but a hidden demon.
....
Su Lun gasped for air, finding his world tinted through a thick red veil, warping reality itself.
It seemed he was in the cabin of a large ship where dim candlelight illuminated the layout of the chamber.
Wooden crates, iron bars, walls, lights, shadows... all appeared as if they had melted under extreme heat, twisted and contorted.
The main consciousness couldn't comprehend the information his eyes received, nor could it think rationally.
Memories, jumbled like a scattered puzzle, slowly began to piece together, rising to the surface of his mind.
I must have died, killed by that guy...
No, it seems I am still alive...
Weakness is the original sin, isn't it...
Is this hell...
What's happened to me...
I seem to have gained tremendous power...
I've also lost something...
My consciousness, it's as if I am going mad...
Damn it!
Why am I so irritable!!!
Listening to the wretched cries near him, Su Lun's gaze slowly focused.
His thoughts, mushy like paste, weighed him down like a giant mountain. The heavy breathing in his throat sounded like the roar of a wild beast.
Instinct took over his body as he tilted his head, trying to identify the source of his restlessness.
At that glance, his vision gradually converged to see several people still held in the adjacent cells separated by iron bars.
A middle-aged man with a fat face and big ears was clutching his head and sobbing bitterly as he begged for mercy...
In the corner cabin, the lewd grins on the faces of two pirates and the "heh heh" sounds coming from their mouths... were so grating on the ears.
A young girl, not very old, lay there on her back, tears of helplessness and humiliation streaming from the corners of her eyes.
That numb gaze happened to meet Su Lun's pair of blood-red eyes.
There was barely a ripple of emotion; the stare was as lifeless as a corpse's.
Seeing that gaze of despair, Su Lun not only felt no surge of emotion, but a cry of morbid delight rose on his lips, "Such delightful despair..."
The emotions of despair seemed to nourish some evil soil at the bottom of his heart, and he let out a sinister "kekeke" laugh from his throat.
In an instant, bizarre phenomena abruptly occurred!
It was as if some terrifying will had descended upon the cabin, suddenly overpowering everyone with a spine-chilling sensation.
The whole cabin suddenly fell silent.
The fat middle-aged man stopped his crying and pleading, turning his head to look over...
Even the two pirates suddenly felt a chill down their spines, and they froze and turned their heads to look over...
And then, they all watched in unison as behind the young man shackled in chains, an unbelievable scene appeared!
It was a phantom of Death holding a black scythe, ethereal and insubstantial!
Underneath the cloak was endless darkness.
The moment the phantom appeared, it was as if the gates of hell had opened; death hung heavy in the large cabin. That indescribable will of terror descended like thousands of poison snakes creeping up their spines, choking the life out of the people in the room...
Su Lun's blood-red eyes stared at the two pirates, his face sporting a demonic grin;
The two pirates also stared at him, frozen in shock.
This exchange of gazes, as if they had seen some "great terror," locked their eyes wide open in horror.
In an instant, their bodies seemed to have been drained of color, turning ashen.
A foul stench of urine and feces wafted through the air as the breath of life fled in an instant.
With just one look, the two pirates were literally scared to death on the spot!
.....
Having killed the two pirates, the restless emotion in Su Lun's heart was vented, and the red glow in his eyes faded somewhat.
His rationality also took a brief respite, and he suppressed the surging frenzy of thoughts, beginning to ponder the situation.
He was suddenly clear about his current condition.
This sensation was very familiar to him.
Like numerous times before, negative emotions had taken over his body.
But this time, it was worse.
Su Lun had the ability to control his emotions.
Before, he had used this method to suppress a multitude of negative emotions.
To put it in perspective, he had used ten parts of rationality to imprison ninety parts of negative emotion.
Later on, after learning mental secret techniques, those ninety parts of negative emotion had become nourishment for assaulting his brain.
But now...
He guessed that he still had ten parts rationality, while those "unknown emotions" in his brain totaled up to a thousand, ten thousand parts!
Each type of negative emotion was like an instinctual desire: murder, hatred, violence, lewdness, irritation, depression, fear...
Once, these emotions were like "negative personalities" confined deep within Su Lun.
And now, each one was as strong as a giant, each capable of easily tearing through the bars of their cage to break free!
Rationality was like a dam holding back an apocalyptic flood, feeble as paper, always on the verge of collapse.
....
"I have been resurrected?"
Su Lun finally understood what was happening to him.
He didn't know how long he had been unconscious, but his mind was currently filled with numerous violent emotions.
His thoughts shifted, and he remembered the aftermath of using the "Thanatos's Puppet."
Those extras in his mind were the whispers of demons, the powerful demonic secret techniques, and potentially the powers that induce humans to become slaves of strength...
That was information beyond his brain's current capacity for processing, in the realm of super cognition.
"So the cost of using that sealed item was this great..."
Su Lun didn't feel much relief at having survived the ordeal.
His current state was still crazily hovering on the edge of death.
It was also fortunate that he knew how to control emotions, as well as having these moments to think for himself. Otherwise, if were anyone else, they might have already become a "slave" to their desires upon resurrection.
I seemed to have stared two pirates to death just now...
What power was that?
...
Su Lun had no time to think in detail as he felt the violent emotions threatening to surge back. He quickly glanced at his attribute panel, wanting to see what had happened.
But before he saw anything else, he immediately noticed a glaring negative status: [Spiritual Power Aberration]!
"My spiritual power has become aberrant?"
Su Lun finally understood what that uncontrollable stream of thought was all about.
If he didn't find a solution, his rational mind would be dispersed by that flood of negative emotions.
