Upon hearing that, Su Lun was reminded once again that Katyusha was certainly a top-tier noble.
But he was also curious; among the hereditary dukes and marquesses of Rue England, only a few families were of such high standing. Which one did she belong to?
The feast continued, and amidst their conversation, a commotion stirred among the crowd.
Seven or eight burly members of the Dalu tribe suddenly approached, carrying a large square wooden box.
Yuta said excitedly, "Look, that's the 'Poets' Honey Wine'!"
Su Lun saw it instantly, a seal on the large wooden box?
Hearing it was wine, he was also curious, what kind of wine was it that it deserved such treatment.
Katyusha, who had clearly heard of it, was full of expectation, "The ancient books record that this is the legendary wine said to make poets' inspirations gush forth?"
Yuta nodded, "Yes! It's brewed from the spring water of Sacred Lake and the nectar of the Divine Tree and it needs to be cellared for many years before it's finished. It's only taken out from the sealed cellar and used during very important rituals. I've grown up listening to the elders talk about it, but have never tasted it myself."
Clearly, this was to entertain the "Pledged One."
Katyusha, clever as she was, guessed something and blinked her eyes, "Earlier, the Clan Leader grandpa said he would give me some when I left. I didn't expect to taste it ahead of time thanks to Mr. Su Lun."
"Hehe."
Su Lun felt, too, that he was benefitting from Mr. Jing's good fortune.
....
The sealed wooden box was opened, and inside was an enormous clay jar.
The Deer Tribe Chief personally broke the clay seal, and a rich fragrance of fruity wine rushed forth, instantly filling the entire river bend.
Even though Su Lun was not fond of alcohol, the scent triggered a craving in his stomach to have a taste.
With the honey wine seal broken, Dalu tribe members, led by the Deer Tribe Chief, performed a prayer, praising nature for all it had given them.
Once the prayers were over, it was time for carousing.
A large cup filled with wine in a bamboo vessel was handed to Su Lun.
Su Lun's all-seeing eye glanced at it, quite surprised.
"Kuvarsil's Poets' Honey Wine"
Detailed explanation: In myth and legend, the divine wine said to coalesce the 'Divinity of Poetry' when drunk; an incomplete recipe passed down from the Dalu tribe, a top-notch wine, which after consumption gives a temporary insight gain—the higher the degree of intoxication, the easier it is to fall into a state of epiphany; it is tremendously beneficial for the inspiration of poetic creation;
"It really does have special effects, actually enhancing insight temporarily."
Su Lun felt like he was gaining new knowledge.
This was the first time he had seen alcohol with an enhancing effect.
And it was on 'insight,' of all things, which is the most ethereal and elusive.
Katyusha, holding her wine cup, was full of expectation, "Yay~ The legendary divine wine."
From the expression of the young miss, one could tell that this was something incredibly, incredibly precious.
Su Lun responded to the toast by the Deer Tribe Chief and the Dalu tribal elders, and everyone drank together.
Then he took a big gulp himself.
The drink was slightly cool at first, and just as he tried to savor it, a complex burst of flavors exploded in his mouth, reaching his taste buds, and in an instant, it was as if he tasted sweet fruitiness and the heat of alcohol, like a thundering herd of horses, yet like a gentle stream trickling softly. That level of complexity was indescribable.
And the wonders continued!
The potency of the drink was immense, leaving one with an almost otherworldly feeling.
It was a very pleasant experience, as if one wasn't drinking wine, but downing a mouthful of rainbows from the heavens, giving one a sublime feeling of floating in the clouds.
It brought surging emotions that one wanted to express.
That was the inspiration for poetry!
However, Su Lun's knowledge of poetry was not profound, and as he didn't drink much, the sensation quickly flickered away.
But something magical immediately happened to Katyusha beside him.
The alcohol hit her hard, and with just a sip, her face instantly flushed with redness, her neck becoming rosy as well. She looked incredibly shy, adding three parts of allure to her demeanor.
Yet unlike the others, a marvelous halo of light condensed around her.
Seeing this, not just Su Lun but even the Dalu tribal elders couldn't help but look with shock and admiration.
Katyusha seemed unaware of the changes occurring within her, covering her mouth as she belched daintily, "Ah... Mr. Su Lun, this wine has quite the kick~"
Su Lun was caught between laughter and tears.
Last time in Blizzard City, he had drunk with Katyusha and knew that this girl didn't have a high tolerance for alcohol.
This wine was fiercer than anything he had ever had before.
Moreover, the "Poets' Honey Wine" was an irresistible temptation for poets.
The more intoxicated one was, the more inspiration for writing poetry would flow forth.
Clearly, Katyusha was experiencing this, and although she spoke in a dazed manner, she picked up her cup again, eager to try, "Mr. Su Lun, Sister Yuta, let's toast~"
Then, the little cup-greedy girl gulped down a big mouthful.
Su Lun and Yuta exchanged smiles and clinked their cups together.
It's not often one gets to drink such fine wine, and he was feeling a bit tipsy too.
This wine was truly top-notch.
Moreover, Su Lun was amazed to find that the state induced by the wine actually made him feel surprisingly good! Those negative emotions, unexpectedly, settled down, as if he too was enjoying the soothing sensation of roaming through the ocean of poetry.
Su Lun couldn't stop himself from having another cup after cup.
After a few drinks, he too could feel that inspiration for creation was bursting forth, growing stronger and stronger.
Countless rhythms, words, and themes, like fragments scattered across the sky, flashed through his mind.
It seemed that just randomly gathering some of them could form a marvelous poem.
Su Lun felt that, as a lousy chicken in poetry, one could only imagine how splendid Katusha must be, since even the Deer Clan Leader never tired of praising her poetic prowess.
At this moment, the girl who loved her drink had cheeks flush with a rosy tint, her eyes slightly glazed with tipsiness.
The milky halo of light that surrounded her grew increasingly intense.
As she continued to drink, Katusha turned her gaze from the starry sky and suddenly asked, "Mr. Jing, may I include you in my story?"
Su Lun replied offhandedly, "If I am the protagonist, I wouldn't mind."
Hearing this, a thought seemed to strike Katusha, and her brows twitched slightly.
Though tipsy, her consciousness was not dulled, a mischievous spark flashed in her eyes as she chuckled, "You're quite greedy. But what if I want to be the protagonist in my story?"
Su Lun, also feeling a bit woozy, replied casually, "Ah... then let the story be a romantic love tale."
Katusha, utterly carefree, burst into laughter, shaking her head like a tambourine, "No way! Astrology tells me that I will be the brightest star in the sky. Love is an unnecessary distraction that would only slow down my sword-drawing speed!"
Su Lun watched her slightly drunk and boastful demeanor and remembered a saying, "How can you write a story that moves one to tears without having experienced a love that pierces the heart?"
To his surprise, Katusha didn't argue and mused, "Hmm... that does make some sense."
She tilted her head and thought, her eyes growing a bit hazy, "Once I figure out how to write our story, I'll tell you about it later."
Su Lun was indifferent, "Oh."
As they drank, their spirits soared higher.
Katusha became more and more intoxicated,
Suddenly, as if she had caught a bout of inspiration, the glow around her coalesced. Excited, she exclaimed, "Wow, Mr. Jing, Yuta sister, I am going to recite a poem for you!"
Su Lun nodded with a smile.
Yuta, too, was a bit drunk, her pretty face colored with a joyful blush, and said with a smile, "Sure."
However,
expecting nothing more than a poetry recitation, they thought nothing more of it.
Yet, an unexpected scene unfolded.
As soon as Katusha started to speak, the heavens and earth seemed to change.
"Wind!"
She seemed intent on composing a song in praise of the wind and pondered for a while before uttering just that one word.
But as that single word left her lips, the air around them trembled violently and suddenly began to blow!
The night wind crept up their collars; Su Lun, though woozy, was suddenly captivated by the thought, "Word Becomes Law? Is poetry really that powerful..."
Not just him, but the revered elders of the Dalu tribe nearby were also staring, slack-jawed.
The Deer Clan Leader and Wolf Granny exchanged a glance, full of wonder, "What a towering talent..."
The breeze gently stirred Katusha's skirt, as if responding to her call.
Suddenly, amid the haze of intoxication, Katusha's tone grew fierce, "Great Wind!"
Nobody had seen the face of the wind,
be it you or me;
But among the stirring leaves,
the wind is passing through there.
...
Katusha sang what sounded like a beautiful ballad, her words spreading out around her. The wind spirits seemed to respond to her, playfully darting around the forest and the treetops, rustling.
The vast expanse of the riverside bonfire was filled with the pleasant sound of her poetry recitation.
The Dalu tribe's deity in their faith embodied the "Divine Tree," and their bloodlines carried the legacy of the free-spirited and romantic wandering poets. Everyone at the feast was intoxicated by the beautiful melody of Katusha's recitation.
For the first time, Su Lun realized that listening to poetry could be such an enjoyable experience.
It was as if his soul was being gently massaged, and he felt completely relaxed.
By then, the wind had picked up, but it remained gentle.
The wind spirits lifted Katusha into the air, where she began to float slowly.
Su Lun felt as if he too were drunk, light as a feather.
No, it wasn't just a feeling.
He was truly floating.
Wrapped in the wind, he was lifted into the air.
Yuta was, too.
Katusha, with blurry eyes, slurred, "Mr. Jing, Sister Yuta, the night is lovely tonight. Shall we go look at the stars together?"
Yuta, also lost in that exquisite drunken state, agreed, "Sure."
Su Lun echoed the response.
Katusha was delighted.
The three of them rode the wind upward.
Once aloft, Katusha didn't forget to wave to the Deer Clan Leader on the ground, sweetly saying, "Grandpa Clan Leader, we're going to look at the stars~"
The Deer Tribe Chief said kindly with a smile, "Good. Just be careful not to fall."
A response came from afar, "We will be careful~"
Hearing this, Wolf Granny, who watched the three fly away, smiled contentedly, "Youth is wonderful."
....
The three flew higher and higher, the bonfire below growing more distant, until they reached the treetop canopy of a dense forest.
"There's a treehouse on the western treetop. I used to climb up here to watch the stars when I was a child..."
Yuta pointed in one direction, and they arrived at the top of a redwood, towering dozens of meters above the nearby trees.
There was a treehouse on the treetop, resembling a gigantic bird's nest with no roof, just several wooden planks.
From here, the brilliant Milky Way was in full view.
The three descended, and Katusha, freed by the effects of the alcohol, laughed heartily, her voice echoing throughout the dense woodland.
The wind spirits hadn't forgotten to bring them candied fruit and fine wine.
The trio continued to toast and drink copiously in the little treehouse atop the tree.
The night was enchanting, with hints of romance permeating the air.
Fueled by the wine, the three lay back and stared at the sky, gradually spacing out.
Katusha slurred her words, "Mr. Su Lun, do you know? I've never been this happy in my life~"
"Mm. I'm feeling pretty good too."
Su Lun also felt amazing at the moment, as if lying on a cloud, with his mind seeming to overflow with brilliant inspiration.
This soaring sensation grew more intense as the alcohol took hold.
Su Lun deeply savored this marvelous experience of "wandering in poetry."
"Mr. Su Lun, could you recite a poem for me?"
"Sure. If life deceives you, don't be sad, don't be in a hurry. In gloomy days be calm, and believe, happy days will come!"
"Wow... Did you write that?"
"No..."
"..."
Katusha, probably really drunk now, lacked any noble lady's restraint and clung to Su Lun's side, unabashedly pressing up against his neck as she spoke, very intimate.
Su Lun's ear was warmed by her breath, but he didn't mind her. However, looking at the girl with braids in front of him, he felt a strange illusion, seeing a beautiful purple-haired woman. It seemed familiar somehow.
At that moment, the girl, a bit fuzzily, asked, "Yuta, do you like Mr. Su Lun?"
Su Lun's mind hadn't even caught up yet.
Yuta's response came dreamily from beside him, "Mm-hmm..."
She said this as if asleep, the two very close together, with a large expanse of skin touching.
Back at the Emerald Holy Land, Yuta had changed into Dalu Tribe attire. The simple leather clothes were thin, like hot pants and a tank top, leaving much skin exposed to the air. This contact made Su Lun feel as if his arm had plunged into a swath of warm, soft flesh.
Su Lun himself could hardly keep his eyes open, but upon hearing her words, he likely smiled.
The conversation of drunkards can suddenly lose all response.
The three fell silent.
Katusha, who had the weakest tolerance for alcohol, had already slipped into a drowsy haze.
After a while, she finally uttered some mumbled words, "Ah, I think... writing a... love story... might be nice too..."
With that, complete silence fell upon the treehouse.
All three seemed to be sleeping.
The potent aftereffect of the "Poet's Honey Wine" stirred desires.
In his hazy consciousness, Su Lun thought he grasped something warm.
It felt smooth to the touch, so he stroked it.
Huh... it seemed to be a back?
Instinctively, he turned over and felt it again.
It still wasn't the satisfying touch he was seeking...
Half-asleep, Su Lun couldn't open his eyes, but his unreasonable hand moved back, carefully distinguishing, until he felt a slightly raised, moist warmth.
He pinched it.
Oh, so it wasn't a back.
Being drunk was frustrating; his mind knew what he was doing, but his body wouldn't obey.
It was these actions that probably woke the deep sleeper, and a plaintive grumble reached his ears, "Mr. Su Lun, you're being very inappropriate... I don't mind you taking advantage, but you're actually dissatisfied with me..."
Only after a while did he hear murmurs and sleepy babbles close to his ear, "Ah, I'm going to turn into a big gray wolf, and bite you to death~"
Su Lun felt he might have been bitten.
As by a wolf in a grand red robe, or perhaps a white wolf.
Gentle to the bone.
That night, endless sweet dreams.

chapters.title: Chapter 262 - 261 I Buried Myself
chapters.content:
```
With the "Eclipse" totem, Su Lun no longer had to constantly worry about mental aberrations.
He relaxed that taut string at the bottom of his heart and got thoroughly drunk for once.
The potency of "Poet's Honey Wine" was strong, with that floating, ethereal sensation lingering for a very long time.
Su Lun felt as though he had had a very long dream.
This sleep was very solid, bringing an unprecedented sense of security and joy.
The honey wine seemed to have also intoxicated the ferocious beast at the bottom of his heart, and they lay quietly.
He vaguely felt.
That in his sleep, as if someone had been chanting beautiful poems, melodious and pleasant, their echoes resonating within his heart. It was like resting on clouds, experiencing an ineffable and utmost tenderness that transcended words.
He didn't know how much time had passed.
The dream should end.
It was like the golden light of dawn spilling into his eyes,
Su Lun's closed eyelids fluttered slightly as his consciousness gradually realigned with his body.
Only then did he realize that the disturbance of his sweet dreams was the crisp chirping of birds beside his ears.
....
A gentle breeze brushed against his body, one side feeling slightly cool, while the other retained a soft warmth.
Still drowsy, Su Lun moved his body, and the smooth touch felt increasingly real.
It was then that he gradually became more alert.
He wanted to move his arms, only to discover they were trapped in a gentle embrace.
Without any barrier, skin touched skin.
Su Lun slowly opened his eyes to find that at some point, he was entirely naked, mumbling in his heart, no wonder it felt a bit cool.
Upon closer inspection, lying beside him was an equally undraped, stunning body.
The dawn's glow played upon her wheat-colored skin, emanating an amber-like delicate and soft light. The thin blanket on her body failed to conceal her exquisite figure. Strands of morning light shone from behind her, illuminating the contours of her waist and the curves of her hips like undulating hills, alluring and graceful.
This was naturally Yuta.
Their current position was extremely intimate, with Yuta's mostly bare body leaning against Su Lun.
Their extensive skin contact allowed Su Lun to feel her body temperature and the hidden softness beneath her lithe and athletic stature.
Su Lun had seen Yuta naked before, but this was the first time they had such close skin-to-skin contact.
His gaze lingered on her pretty face for a moment, then slid downward. He saw through her at a glance. The smooth visual touch, especially in the morning light, was particularly alluring. It was hard to look away.
Perhaps it was Su Lun's fixed stare that triggered her alertness, as her obedient wolf ears trembled slightly and her eyelashes twitched.
Yuta woke up as well.
Opening her eyes, her gaze was filled with the reflection of Su Lun, and she smiled faintly, "Mr. Su Lun, you're awake?"
The Dalu people weren't shy about expressing their love, and even though she was naked, Yuta barely flinched, her face devoid of any trace of shyness.
Su Lun also felt quite good, chuckling softly, "Hmm."
With that, he gently caressed her face.
Yuta didn't get up, maintaining their intimate position, snuggling up beside Su Lun.
In this treehouse, hundreds of meters above the ground, the breeze served as their blanket, and the clouds as their fleece. Morning light poured down on them, seemingly softening just for them as they savored this rare peace and quiet.
Su Lun gazed at the not yet fully brightened sky, his eyes profound.
It seemed as if he was still savoring that unfettered, pleasant feeling.
This was a solid sleep he had never experienced before.
Yes, and an enjoyment of extreme tenderness.
Neither spoke, Yuta's eyebrows curved, her fluffy white wolf tail sweeping through the air from time to time.
```
Su Lun looked on with curiosity and gently touched it with his hand.
The previous two times had been for healing, and while attending to her body, his mind had been free of distractions.
Now, it was completely different.
No need to avert his eyes, he openly appreciated her.
Yuta did not skimp on showcasing her figure, even turning her body slightly to make it easier for Su Lun to touch.
Yuta's figure might not boast an exaggerated proportion of curves, but it was very symmetrical. Her proud and full grip, waist and hips were just right. Her waist and abdomen had smooth lines, and touching them, he felt a special kind of softness and resilience. Then there were the playful wolf ears and the fluffy tail, which added a wild and natural beauty.
Su Lun played with the wolf tail for a moment, and then his hand landed on the perky part above, enjoying the wonderful feel.
Yuta didn't mind at all.
At that moment, she seemed to sense something and a teasing smile flashed in her eyes, "Mr. Su Lun seems quite spirited this morning~"
Su Lun raised his eyebrows and gently caressed her as a response.
"You seem to be very interested in my tail?"
Yuta said with a smile, not waiting for Su Lun to reply, as she flipped over and sat up.
With the change of position, Su Lun found it more convenient as well.
He could not remember what had happened in his drunken state; it seemed to have happened, yet it also seemed like a dream... not quite real.
And now, he was thoroughly enjoying the delicate sensation without being polite.
At this moment, Yuta seemed to have noticed something and exclaimed in surprise, "Eh~ Mr. Su Lun, there's also a bite mark on your shoulder."
As she spoke, she reached out and touched it.
Su Lun tilted his head and barely managed to see the imprint on his own shoulder.
A teasing glint flashed in Yuta's eyes; she obviously wasn't completely clueless and teased, "Could it be that I bit you when we were drunk? But that's not right, the marks I leave are not like this..."
She was from the White Wolf clan and had a pair of small, sharp fangs.
The bite marks were neat, clearly made by a human.
"Did Katyusha bite me?"
Su Lun felt a mix of amusement and dismay in his heart, vaguely recalling a memory from his drunken state— he seemed to have been bitten.
The girl's bite was quite substantial indeed.
But why did she bite me?
Su Lun tried hard to remember; it was as if Little Red Riding Hood had turned into the Big Bad Wolf?
Drinking could cause memories and dreams to blend together, leaving you unsure whether it was a dream or something that really happened.
However, coming back to it, he hadn't seen her upon waking up; where did Katyusha run off to?
Su Lun looked at himself and Yuta, both undressed; maybe she left to avoid embarrassment?
Yuta looked at Su Lun, a sly smile flickering in her eyes.
She didn't seem to mind, and she didn't dwell on the bite mark.
She laid her entire body on Su Lun's, affectionately rubbing ear against cheek.
Her tail brushed over his body, tickling him, like a tiny current touching every part of him.
Su Lun felt the experience was fantastic.
Yuta giggled as if she sensed something again, "Ah, Mr. Su Lun's spirits are even higher now~"
Su Lun smiled in response, unapologetically reaching up to embrace her.
Yes, it was a vibrant morning indeed.
....
After a while, the morning light finally completely pierced through the clouds and shone into the Emerald Holy Land.
Mist and clouds entwined, the whole Holy Land was filled with steaming vitality.
Yuta's bewitching figure was covered by a beast skin skirt and a vest as she busied herself tidying her disheveled hair.
Su Lun also sat up, searching for his clothes to put on.
But as he was putting on his pants, he accidentally felt something scratching his leg.
He reached into his pocket and found a letter.
Realizing what it might be, he didn't avoid Yuta as he opened it, and sure enough, it was left by Katusha.
Yuta, however, showed no interest in looking, as if he guessed what the letter said, and after getting dressed, he said, "Mr. Su Lun, I'll go down first. Otherwise, being seen by the clanspeople later will bring you some trouble~"
With that, the corner of his mouth lifted in a meaningful smile.
"Mhm."
Su Lun nodded with a smile.
Watching Yuta agilely leap down from the treehouse, landing on the branches, and disappearing into the dense foliage above within moments.
Su Lun withdrew his gaze.
As he dressed, he also took the time to read the content of the letter.
The handwriting was neat and graceful.
'Mr. Su Lun, thank you for giving me such a pleasurable life experience. I finally know what my story was missing. Unfortunately, the beauty of this world is fleeting, like the clouds at dawn, a gentle breeze blows, and they dissipate...'
'I'm sorry for leaving without saying goodbye. Because this is the best ending to the story I could think of. When I left, the sky was filled with colorful clouds, escorted by blooming flowers and a gentle breeze, no need for longing.'
'We will eventually blend into all beings, but there is a moment when we are unique to each other. Mr. Su Lun, you must remember, we once watched the stars together. My face is hidden among the stars... If you happen to think of me occasionally, just look up at the night sky. The stars will bring you my blessings.'
'By the time I wrote this letter, my story finally had a soul. Thank you.'
'If the story went on, Katusha would become a carefree grand minstrel. The wildflowers on the hillside bloom, fall, and flourish year after year without an owner. But our story ends here. We probably won't see each other anymore, take good care of yourself. —Katusha'
The content of the letter ended here.
But it seemed she forgot something and added another line afterward: 'Ah... I'm sorry, I only realized I bit you after I woke up. But you are really annoying...^◡^'
Su Lun, looking at the doodled smiley face, his mind suddenly filled with the image of the girl with small freckles and big braids, always polite and well-mannered.
After reading the letter, he murmured unwittingly, "Heh, this girl..."
Though he spoke playfully, he also discerned the undertone of farewell between the lines.
Leaving aside her mysterious origins, he actually had a rather good impression of the girl, Katusha.
She bore no ill will, and he had no desire to speculate with malice.
Even though it was a parting,
Su Lun didn't feel particularly sad.
Luing's territory might be vast, but there were only a few top noble families. With a chance to inquire in the future, he could surely find out which family's young lady "Katusha" was.
Su Lun put away the letter, didn't overthink it, and leapt down from the treehouse as well.
But as he descended, he found that Yuta was waiting for her.
And next to her, there was a white wolf youth with a profound gaze, none other than her younger brother, Arcu.
Su Lun only then realized that the morning light above was not from the next day's dawn.
They had been drunk and asleep in the treehouse for three days and three nights.
....
When Su Lun and the others woke up, completely unaware on the other side, a team was swiftly moving through the Silent Forest.
A troop of Dalu clansmen escorted a young lady in a red cloak to the outskirts of the forest.
Once there, the leading black bear Druid did not escort her any further, saying, "Miss Katusha, we will take you only this far."
With a bright smile, the girl in the red cloak waved her hand, "Mhm, thank you, Elder Pasu. The guards from my house have come to pick me up. You can go back now."
"Take care."
"Mhm."
"..."
The Dalu clanspeople disappeared into the dense forest, and shortly after, an imposing guard troop appeared within the woods.
Everyone simultaneously knelt on one knee, performing a Knight's salute, "Miss."
Katyusha nodded her head, showing no hurry to depart.
She cast one final glance back in the direction of the Emerald Holy Land, her pure eyes revealing a complex expression as if recalling something, the corners of her brows lifting in a smile.
Katyusha remained silent for a long time, and none of the guards spoke either, their expressions solemn as they stood quietly waiting at her side.
After a moment, the head elderly butler, looking slightly worried, quietly asked, "Miss, are you alright?"
At these words, as though her emotions had been interrupted, the last trace of longing in Katyusha's eyes finally dissipated.
Her expression darkened, as if she had lost something precious.
She softly replied, "I'm fine."
With those words, it was as if some thought had become clear to her, the wisdom in her gaze growing brighter and brighter.
It was then that Katyusha took out a black notebook and retrieved a fountain pen, rustling softly as she wrote a passage: "Miss Ugly Duckling bid farewell to the amiable Mr. Su Lun whom she found very pleasant to interact with... Reflecting upon it, he was an interesting person unlike any she had met before in her past life. Like a shooting star, he showed her a moment's beauty. She left behind a note, in her heart hoping that Su Lun would remember her. Ah, it seems she doesn't dislike him after all... Indeed, only through experience can one write the best stories. Miss Ugly Duckling also got her desired ending, the most beautiful one she could imagine..."
At this point, Katyusha's pen halted for an instant, as if she had made some difficult decision.
The pen in her hand, like a knife dividing the past and present.
Ultimately, she made the cut.
The last struggle in her eyes suddenly dissipated, becoming like a pool of still water without a ripple.
She continued writing to the last sentence, pausing after each word: "Miss Ugly Duckling buried herself in the past. That instant, she was reborn."
Once this passage was written in the notebook, Katyusha let out a slight sigh of relief.
Then, slowly emerging on that notebook, were a few lines: "Reality alignment 99%, story established!"
In an instant, the story beneath her pen seemed to resonate with some supreme cosmic law.
Katyusha's face was impassive as the two adorable braids over her shoulders suddenly became fluffy and disheveled. Her lovely flaxen hair flashed with light, magically transforming into a cascade of bright purple. Her freckles vanished, her figure became more graceful, and she suddenly shone radiantly.
The innocent cuteness vanished in a moment, her expression proud like that of a queen, commanding awe.
Yet, at this time, the marvel had only just begun.
The aura around the woman with purple hair rose higher, her body haloed with a strange white glow.
This was a state even more intense than when she recited poetry in the Emerald Holy Land.
She took out a flask from her Storage Ring and took a swig. Walking on, she continued to write: "She died last night, her heart as calm as still water; I am reborn this morning, in a world where spring abounds..."
Each stroke penned a world within the book.
The next instant, the marvel abruptly manifested.
World of the book, fantasy incarnated.
The woman with purple hair slowly closed her eyes, and concentric ripples visible to the naked eye gathered around her.
The elderly butler and the guards, as if they recognized the significance of this phenomenon, dared not look directly and promptly bowed their heads, prostrating themselves on the ground.
The woman with purple hair paid no attention to them as she stepped toward the forest. With each step, fresh, tender grass sprouted from the frozen mud beneath her feet.
Breaking soil, germinating, growing, blooming... a vista of vibrant life unfolded.
The path she walked turned into a small trail of flowers and brocades through the forest.
With each step, the ripples around her grew denser, gradually forming a special domain.
At that moment, the woman with purple hair came to a halt.
When she opened her eyes again, they were filled with brilliant stars.
"I've entered the 'Saint Realm'."
The voice was nonchalant, yet it seemed to carry an endless resonance, harmonizing with the universe.
Transcendent, sanctified.
At that moment, a fresh marvel arose, as the primeval and icy forest blossomed into spring.
Yekaterina didn't linger any longer, and walked forward.

chapters.title: Chapter 263 - 262 Mr. Su Lun is Very Impressive
chapters.content:
Su Lun descended from the treehouse to the ground and had not walked far when he saw Yuta and a young member of the White Wolf Tribe waiting for him under a tree.
"Arcu, I've told you, a hundred of you wouldn't be a match for Mr. Su Lun, and you're still not convinced."
"Hmph! I refuse to lose to a human! Although he's the 'Pledged One', but... but I still want to fight him. Even if you stop me now, sister, soon Gary, Dar, Umon... they'll definitely come too!"
"Have it your way. Just don't blame me when you get thrashed later."
"..."
Seeing the young boy scolded by Yuta without a comeback, naturally, it could only be her own little brother, Arcu.
Arcu watched Su Lun approaching with a look of defiance.
Yuta, on the other hand, smirked slyly.
As Su Lun walked over, he discovered that they had slept in the treehouse for three days.
Now everyone in Emerald Holy Land must know about his unusual relationship with Yuta.
However, Yuta didn't mind at all, so naturally, Su Lun didn't feel uncomfortable either.
But looking at the young Wolf Tribe member who had come to challenge him, his expression was a bit peculiar.
Even though the women of the Dalu Tribe were mostly attractive, Yuta was one of the top few in the tribe. Besides, being a respected Druid, the White Wolves were naturally very popular in the Emerald Holy Land.
Having taken someone from the Dalu Tribe's "vegetable patch", and an outsider human at that, it was no surprise that Su Lun was treated this way.
As for Arcu, the more he looked at Su Lun, the more displeased he felt, shouting, "Human, I challenge you to a duel!"
Knowing Su Lun's strength, Yuta was not worried in the slightest, she simply blinked and said softly, "Although he's my brother, Mr. Su Lun, you don't have to be polite when hitting him."
Hearing this, Su Lun didn't know whether to laugh or cry.
This was indeed the kind of treatment only a real brother could expect.
"Oh."
This time, Su Lun agreed to the challenge.
As Yuta said, perhaps giving him a good thrashing would save a lot of trouble.
He also knew the customs of the Dalu tribe, that only true warriors would be recognized.
Upon hearing Su Lun accept the challenge, Arcu finally breathed a sigh of relief, "Good! I'll wait for you by the river in the village!"
With those words, he walked towards the forest.
....
Yuta, hearing Su Lun accept the challenge, was also visibly excited.
Although she knew he could win, he still needed the tribe's recognition.
With no one else around, she joyfully jumped into Su Lun's arms.
Now that they were in an intimate relationship, they didn't need to "observe formalities" like before.
She wrapped her arms around his neck like a koala and said, "That brat Arcu does need a good lesson, lest he always thinks too highly of himself, ignorant of the ways of the world."
Su Lun smiled and held her with one hand to keep her from slipping.
The Dalu Tribe's leather skirts were thin and revealed much; touching them felt soft. The hindquarters of the White Wolf Tribe were already well-developed, and even in human form, the tight, toned muscles felt excellent.
"Ah~ Mr. Su Lun seems particularly energetic today..."
Yuta teased him, not really minding.
After being affectionate for a moment, Yuta got down.
The two walked towards the forest exterior.
But as they walked, Su Lun suddenly sensed something and looked south.
Seeing his expression, Yuta asked, "What's wrong?"
Su Lun frowned and after a moment said, "It seems someone is thinking about me."
It wasn't the kind of thinking that meant malice, more like someone was reminiscing.
Was it that direction... could it be that girl Katyusha?
He didn't dwell on it and followed Yuta out of the forest.
.....
It seemed there weren't a few in the Holy Land from the Dalu Tribe who wanted to beat up Su Lun.
When Su Lun and Yuta emerged from the forest, there were already dozens of people on the large meadow by the river.
Su Lun remembered a few names, Gary from the Black Bear Tribe, Dar from the Golden Leopard Tribe, Umon from the Grey Wolf Tribe... all were present.
Looking carefully, even the treetop heads from the village huts across the river, curious about the duel, had popped out quietly to watch.
The elders of the tribe were also curious about the strength of this "Pledged One."
As soon as Su Lun arrived, everyone turned to look at him in unison.
Yuta wore a radiant smile, bright as the warmth of spring.
This smile made the group of young men on the other side, flush with vigorous blood, unable to contain their fury, casting ever more resentful glances at Su Lun beside her.
Su Lun's expression remained unchanged as he casually sauntered over.
A duel was a duel, nothing fancy about the process.
After Su Lun stepped onto the makeshift arena that had been cordoned off on the grassy field, sure enough, those kids' hostility diminished considerably.
No matter the outcome, by taking up the challenge, he had earned their respect.
...
Arcu was not weak by any means.
Among this group of apprentice Druids, he was also among the very best.
Probably at the peak of the second tier, on the verge of breaking through to the third tier.
But for Su Lun, without any special techniques, such a level posed no threat at all.
The duel began, and the onlooking apprentice Druids were all screaming at the top of their lungs, as if they wished they could take the stage themselves and thrash the human who had 'stolen their vegetables'.
Even though he couldn't understand Dalu's language, Su Lun knew they were cheering Arcu on.
On the other hand.
Su Lun had only one cheerleader, and that was Yuta.
The Miss White Wolf's face was adorned with a bright smile as she cupped her hands around her mouth like a megaphone and shouted in the common tongue, "Mr. Su Lun, fight on~"
Her voice alone seemed to drown out several dozen others.
It was as if she was somewhat excited to see her little brother about to get a beating.
Arcu frowned upon seeing Su Lun just standing there, showing no intent to prepare for battle, and instantly felt underestimated. He questioned, "Aren't you going to release your alchemical enhancements?"
Su Lun sighed faintly but gave no response.
After all, this was just a sparring session, not a real enemy, so he naturally wouldn't use his full strength.
If he were to really go all out, he estimated that the fight would probably be over in two or three rounds at most.
It wasn't that Arcu was weak, but because all of Su Lun's combat skills were designed to kill—"killing techniques" prepared to take down his targets.
Not to mention forbidden objects, puppets, or silk threads, his combat skills alone would be enough trouble for him.
Arcu, though young, was also very smart.
He had guessed that Su Lun was very strong.
His sister had told him so, and although he verbally disagreed, his heart had never once doubted her.
He just wanted to confirm it, so he said, "Then be careful, I'm going to make a move. I'm very fast."
Listening to these words, Su Lun nodded, "Hmm."
The next instant, Arcu didn't waste any more words, and with a fierce push off the ground—
"Whoosh" went the sound.
It was as if a bomb had been planted under the grass, which instantly exploded into a large pit, and his figure aggressively lunged forward.
"Indeed quite fast."
Su Lun muttered to himself, his gaze slightly intensifying.
Arcu's speed was indeed quite fast among second-rank melee combatants; even an alchemist of the same rank might not be able to react in time.
Yet, despite the speed being fast, Su Lun could see it all clearly under his All-knowing Eye.
He watched the figure charging toward him and didn't act cocky, assuming a combat stance.
Although Su Lun rarely utilized combat techniques in his usual battles, he was truly proficient in various styles of combat techniques, and his physical fitness wasn't much less than that of a third-rank melee combatant's.
Just as his arms were raised, a massive force struck them.
"Hmm... the strength isn't bad either."
Su Lun wasn't at all surprised and inwardly complimented Yuta's brother for his indeed impressive strength.
He deflected the blow with a simple motion, dissolving the force into nothingness.
As the impact from the collision had yet to dissipate, Su Lun used the momentum to deliver a side kick that landed heavily on the figure's waist.
The Dalu Clan possessed a beast gene, and their innate combat talents were strong. Arcu, having been kicked, retreated with agility, effortlessly neutralizing the blow and looking for an opportunity to disengage and attack again.
Unfortunately, Su Lun wouldn't give him that chance!
Su Lun's combat reaction and thinking were so fast that he'd calculated various countermeasures even before his opponent made a move.
He never took his opponents lightly, not even in a sparring match.
He had already anticipated the next few steps when his foot kicked out.
Watching Arcu dodge his kick, Su Lun was not surprised in the slightest.
His foot hit the ground hard, and with a "snap" of air blasting, he used Stepping on Air to swiftly disappear from the spot.
Before Arcu could react, Su Lun had already reappeared in his retracing arc, launching a punch.
....
Arcu was greatly astonished; he hadn't expected his opponent to follow up so quickly!
Looking at that expressionless face, he realized just how strong the other was.
But he wasn't weak either!
Arcu's eyes hardened, and suddenly some fine fur appeared on his handsome face as he entered a semi-beast transformation.
With this slight change, he was able to catch the punch mid-air.
"Not a bad reaction."
Su Lun slightly raised an eyebrow, inwardly praising the move.
However, if it had been to the death, the opponent would have been dead!
Su Lun didn't mind giving Yuta's brother a taste of the real deal.
He surged forward once more.
.....
Nobody expected the encounter to be so fierce from the get-go!
In an instant, the entire riverside grassland was filled with echoes of punches, with ongoing cracking sounds everywhere.
The apprentice Druids were stunned, their eyes brimming with excitement.
"This human... oh, no, Mr. Su Lun is quite formidable."
"Indeed, not bad. But he's still a whole rank higher, so it's only natural he's at this level."
"Just watch, Arcu hasn't transformed yet. That kid is considering his sister's face, not wanting the human to lose too badly."
"I don't think Arcu can definitely win. Haven't you seen that Mr. Su Lun hasn't released his alchemical enhancements either?"
"Many human alchemical enhancements are not externally visible. That Mr. Su Lun's strength is on par with Arcu's, obviously he's augmented by a strength-focused enhancement."
"No wonder Yuta sent him a lifelong wolf claw, he does have some skills."
"...."
They watched, chattering among themselves.
The resentment in their eyes also diminished a lot.
Su Lun's strength had finally become "acceptable" in their eyes—at least barely so.
Meanwhile, Yuta, who was watching the battle, was exceptionally excited. Her clear eyes were full of Su Lun's shadow, as she cheered intermittently, "Go, Mr. Su Lun!"
She knew that Su Lun was a formidable Puppet Master and had expected him to dispatch a few puppets to resolve the fight. She never anticipated his hand-to-hand combat skills would be so strong!
....
The battle was fierce, and it seemed Arcu hadn't gained the upper hand.
But Su Lun knew that perhaps out of consideration for his "brother-in-law" status, Arcu wasn't using his full strength either.
Though the Dalu tribespeople did not have Alchemy enhancements or various methods like Alchemists, their beast transformation talents gave them remarkable combat power.
After dozens of exchanges, Arcu, understanding that he couldn't do a thing to Su Lun without transforming, suddenly pulled back to create some distance, dropped to all fours, and took on a crawling stance.
At the same time, a cold glint flashed between his fingers and disappeared; sharp claws emerged, and his body sprouted thick fur. Upon closer inspection, his entire being had turned into a majestic white wolf, even bulkier than his sister when she transformed.
Although it lacked some of the shrewd and ferocious maturity, it already possessed an oppressive and fierce aura.
The White Wolf spoke with a human voice, "You need to be careful. I'm getting serious now!"
Su Lun looked on with a slight smile and nodded in acknowledgment.
He anticipated Arcu's next move by focusing on the muscles rippling beneath the White Wolf's fur.
What surprised Su Lun even more was that the White Wolf suddenly leaped powerfully, creating visible ripples in the air beneath its feet, like waves in water.
"Eh...you learned 'Stepping on Air' after seeing it once?"
Surprise brushed Su Lun's mind.
The mastery of "Stepping on Air," a mystic-level movement technique, required extreme skill and talent to find that momentary pause when stepping on air.
Many high-ranking professionals couldn't perform it at all without the right feel, even if their muscular strength was sufficient.
Who would have thought that Arcu would pick it up on the spot?
His talent was indeed astounding.
Su Lun knew he could no longer afford to be careless and became a bit more serious as well.
He rapidly formed the sorcerer's seals with his hands and chanted softly in his heart, "Flesh Alchemy: Hormone Rampage!"
Hormones surged into his body, instantly giving him a feeling of explosive energy.
However, Arcu's speed was faster!
After transforming, he became several times quicker than before, charging over like lightning, and before Su Lun could even react, his claws reached Su Lun's chest.
"So fast!"
Su Lun certainly saw him in a new light now.
Among the second-tier close-combat professionals he had encountered, Arcu was definitely the strongest, absolutely overpowering others of his level!
But no matter how strong, he was still second-tier.
Su Lun anticipated his trajectory and knew he was too late to block. At that moment, his hands, previously forming the sorcerer's seals, changed again, sparking with the speed of lightning as he chanted, "Mystic Art - Vajra!"
The next instant, a "thud" like the toll of a bell reverberated across the entire riverbend.
The powerful shockwave of the touch instantly whipped up a green tide on the lawn, even the onlookers' robes billowed from the blast.
....
Su Lun felt the power of that claw, which was nowhere near as fierce as it appeared to be.
He naturally understood that Arcu had probably held back to avoid hurting him.
But...with his level four gold-based "Vajra," if it was just an attack of that magnitude, even if he was standing still, the opponent couldn't touch him.
Level four magic against level two did seem like a bit of bullying.
He smiled and shook his head, saying to the incredulous White Wolf opposite him, "You don't need to hold back. Otherwise, you cannot defeat me."
The transformed White Wolf, Arcu, had a complex look in his eyes.
Although he had moderated his strike, which could smash even rocks, how could it be that Su Lun was unscathed?
He finally understood that this human, as his sister had said, was truly powerful.
Yet, this only fueled his competitive spirit!
He shouted earnestly, "Alright! Mr. Su Lun, I'm going to use magic now, be careful!"
Hearing himself addressed as "Mr. Su Lun" instead of simply a "human," the corners of Su Lun's mouth lifted slightly.
The Dalu people really were kind-hearted.
Direct with their feelings, once they accepted you, they harbored no other thoughts in their hearts.
....
Su Lun had initially thought this friendly bout would hold no more surprises.
In terms of combat techniques alone, Arcu, no matter how strong, stood no chance.
But unexpectedly, Arcu actually used magic.
A true Druid could listen to the voices of all things, harness the power of nature, and cast spells that transform into various animals.
The White Wolf chanted a spell, and suddenly the weather shifted dramatically.
Strong winds howled in the sky and dark clouds swiftly covered the grassy plain.
With a crack of thunder, a downpour began, and amid the clouds flickered restless, serpentine lightning.
Such a display was truly formidable and intimidating.
"The force of nature powering wind, rain, lightning...a triple-elemental spell?"
Su Lun watched, curious, no longer in a rush to act.
Druidic casting was an entirely different system from Alchemy. With the power of faith, they were able to release various elemental spells more readily.
Yet Arcu's use of a triple-element spell indeed caught Su Lun's eye.
Still, there was that old problem—if it couldn't break through "Vajra," all the flashy spells were just for show.
"No, there's wood element too!"
The next instant, Su Lun sensed something and realized that the grass beneath his feet was growing wildly, entwining around his legs like vines, binding him in the blink of an eye.
Su Lun looked on, his eyebrows slightly raised in approval: "To think he actually laid an ambush in advance, his mind isn't bad at all."
At this thought, he raised his eyebrows as well, realizing that if he didn't pull out some other tricks, he probably wouldn't be able to hold out.
Although it wouldn't result in a loss, being trapped by those plants could still land him in a very embarrassing situation.
After all, the lightning building up above, the wind sharp as blades, and the clearly perception-altering and teleportation-limiting rain were the real joint killing move.
....
"When did Arcu learn to secretly cast four-elemental hybrid spells? Wow, with this move, he's definitely going to win!"
"Ha-ha... This time Su Lun is going to take a big hit! It might not be very polite, but it's so satisfying. He's the one who took away Sister Yuta!"
"Right, that's it! Now he'll understand the strength of us from the Dalu tribe, and treat Sister Yuta better in the future."
"..."
The onlooking young druids clenched their fists in excitement, watching Su Lun about to get hit as if they were the ones in the arena.
Yuta, who was nearby, looked at Arcu casting his spell, her eyes full of satisfaction, muttering to herself: "To think this child has already reached this level... he's been very hardworking."
But in a blink, her gaze shifted, even more curious about how Su Lun would respond.
After all, she knew that from beginning to end, Su Lun hadn't been taking it seriously.
....
Su Lun saw the lightning about to strike him and a resigned look appeared in his eyes.
The power of this spell compelled him to use some of his signature moves.
Feeling he had fought enough, he thought about ending this spar.
The plants around him had already woven into a barrier, enclosing him.
Su Lun didn't attempt to destroy the plant barrier. As the spell quickly completed, a spatial rift suddenly appeared beside him.
Then, his entire figure vanished from the spot.
For the first time, Su Lun used his Spatial Ability.
He "Flashed" to appear beside the White Wolf, who was about to spew Wind Blades.
Arcu was dumbfounded, momentarily at a loss.
Like a smoker choking on a puff, the Wind Blade Technique in his mouth was forcibly swallowed, and tears were almost squeezed out of his eyes.
The next second, his brain registered what had happened, revealing a bitter smile with a slight sigh.
He had no intention of continuing the spar either.
The forces of nature dissipated, and the thunderclouds in the sky instantly extinguished, losing their aggressive momentum.
Sunlight broke through the clouds, shining again on the riverside meadow.
As the dark clouds scattered, the air still carried a heavy mist, creating a beautiful rainbow.
Arcu transformed back into his human form, looked at Su Lun, and said earnestly, "I lost."
Reflecting on the encounter, he realized that Mr. Su Lun had been sparing him all along.
If the Spatial Ability had been used earlier, he would have fallen sooner.
No, even before that.
If they had fought in earnest, he felt he wouldn't have even had the chance to cast a spell.
"Mr. Su Lun is really powerful, to think he can also use spatial spells..."
Arcu's expression was very composed.
He acknowledged the strength of his sister's husband, indeed far surpassing his own.
Su Lun gave neither agreement nor disagreement, but also smiled and said, "You have good talent; you will definitely be strong in the future."
Listening to this, Arcu seemed to realize something, his previously furrowed brow suddenly relaxed, as if he had found peace of mind.
The observing young druids immediately lost their fire, and no one doubted "Mr. Su Lun's" strength anymore.
At that moment, Yuta also hurried over and, looking at her brother, said, "I told you, Mr. Su Lun is very powerful."
This was an expected outcome, and she showed no surprise, but she did look at a disappointed Arcu, offering consolation: "But our Arcu did well too, he has made great progress."
To her surprise, her usually argumentative brother didn't argue back at all, simply saying, "Yes, Mr. Su Lun is very impressive, I lost fair and square."
Yuta felt that her brother's demeanor was somewhat strange.
....
On the other side of the river bend, inside a treehouse.
The Deer Tribe Chief and Wolf Granny were also watching the battle from a distance.
Seeing the outcome, both elders had amiable smiles on their faces.
The Deer Tribe Chief remarked with a sigh, "Very strong indeed."
Wolf Granny replied, "Yes, throughout the entire fight he didn't use any prosthesis, Alchemy was only used in a few close combat professions. According to Yuta, his main profession is that of an impressive Puppet Master."
The Deer Tribe Chief stroked his beard under his chin with a full smile, "Living as long as I have, I'm quite eager to see just how astonishing Su Lun's Puppetry Technique is."
.....
As Yuta said, beating up her brother would save a lot of trouble.
After the duel, there were no more Dalu youths in the village who sought to challenge Su Lun.
And because of the duel, everyone became clearer about his relationship with Yuta.
The elders in the tribe sent their blessings, and the children greeted him with joy and excitement.
An atmosphere of friendliness and harmony.
Su Lun originally planned to rest for a few days, to clarify the situation in the "Cursed Valley" to the north, before setting out for the "Heart Stealer."
But unexpectedly, the next day a situation arose.
Yuta's brother and several passionate young druids secretly left the Holy Land to support the "Grey Wolf Tribe" to the north that was being besieged and overwhelmed by humans.
News came that a very powerful enemy had appeared.
It was not a slaving team, but a crack troop from the Lu Ying royal family!

chapters.title: Chapter 264 - 263: Rune Human Skin Umbrella
chapters.content:
The Dalu tribe's current situation is very bleak.
The great war in the Cursed Valley centuries ago resulted in the death of all the great druids, and the tribe lost the ability to communicate with the gods. Without the protection of the gods and the continuation of their lineage, they have not produced any high-end combat power since.
What's worse is that humans have reneged on their former pacts, and greedy slave traders have begun to delve into the Silent Forest to capture slaves, which has caused the population of the Dalu tribe to plummet, pushing them to the brink of extinction.
Now in the Emerald Holy Land, there are only two fifth-tier individuals; in terms of high-end combat power, they can't even compete with some of the larger slave-trading groups. They simply have no right to face them in battle.
Therefore, even if a tribe in the forest is in danger, the elders in the Emerald Holy Land dare not go to their rescue.
They might save them once, but not the next time.
If these elders were to die in battle as well, the Dalu tribe would have completely lost all hope.
Thus, for the continuation of their tribe, they have no choice but to hide and take shelter in various places within the Silent Forest.
This is why, when the news of the "Grey Wolf Tribe" being attacked came, the Deer Tribe Chief did not spread the word throughout the Holy Land.
They had heard too much of such terrible news over the years.
The young apprentice druids still have passion in their hearts, but they are the future hope of the Dalu tribe.
The elders wouldn't let them take risks either.
But still, the news spread.
There were a few apprentice druids in the Holy Land who were from the Grey Wolf Tribe, and they certainly wouldn't just watch idly as their tribe was destroyed and their people taken away to be sold as slaves. Arcu's good friend Umon was one of them. A few hot-blooded youngsters got together and quietly slipped out of the Holy Land, planning a rescue mission.
They would save as many as they could.
Druids, being stronger in combat than the average tribesperson, were the only ones with a chance to save some of their people.
...
In the forest, Su Lun rode on Yuta, who had transformed into a white wolf, quickly moving through the woods.
He had originally planned to head north to take a look, and now this detour was on his way.
From his previous communication with the Deer Tribe Chief, he had obtained a lot of detailed intelligence and roughly assessed the rank of the "Heart-stealer." It shouldn't be too outrageously high. He estimated that it was likely a third-tier, or perhaps a fourth-tier "Lord." It was still within an operable range.
Yuta had originally planned to secretly take him there. But when the Deer Tribe Chief and the others became clear about Su Lun's reasons for going and guessed his strength, they expressed understanding and support. They even planned to send a strong team to accompany him.
But Su Lun refused.
His situation was very special.
He was a Puppeteer, and a team of people made no difference compared to him alone.
If they encountered an enemy that was too strong, having more people was useless.
If they encountered an enemy they could beat, those few extras weren't necessary.
Having Yuta, who was familiar with the forest, as his companion was enough.
Together, even if they encountered a fifth-tier enemy, they would be able to protect themselves in the forest.
"The Grey Wolf Tribe is by Lake Rudasil, and a day's journey further north is the Cursed Valley. The elders in the tribe say that the last time they encountered the 'Heart-stealer' was near a 'Skull Grotto' not far from the valley, and the beast was hiding in the cave there."
"Hmm. We'll head to the Grey Wolf Tribe first, those boys like Arcu should have gone there."
"..."
Yuta wasn't angry at his younger brother for sneaking out of the holy land; he was just a bit worried.
Being hot-blooded isn't necessarily a bad thing for Dalu Tribe warriors.
....
On the other hand, along the shore of Lake Rudasil in the northern part of Silent Forest, a deadly competition was underway.
A group of soldiers dressed in silver armor from the empire had breached the Grey Wolf Tribe yesterday. The tribespeople were fitted with slave collars and escorted further north.
There were also some young knights searching through the jungle for the "fish that slipped through the net," who had scattered.
"These natives turn into animals when they run, slipping and sliding through the forest, making them hard to catch..."
"Hahaha... Yuke, my spear throwing skills were top marks during the academy's graduation assessment, a spear for each; how's that?"
"Bore, I've killed eight natives, and you have only five, what's there to show off? I'm going to turn their shinbones into specimens and keep them in my family's treasure room as my merits!"
"Hey, hey, can you all stop showing off? The trial mission given by the instructor requires at least five native heads each, and I have only killed one."
"..."
This is an elite reserve squad of the Sacred Judgment Knight Legion from the Imperial Royal Academy of Emperor Luying.
The knights were young, fresh graduates from the Imperial Royal Academy who had joined the army as reserve officers.
Hunting non-humans was their bloody trial before officially entering the battlefield.
At the same time, in the tribe's encampment strewn with corpses, there were several wooden cages crammed with Dalu Tribespeople.
These were the slaves who hadn't been transported away in time, also serving as bait.
A few middle-aged men in exquisite armor stood guard nearby, listening intermittently to the sounds of combat from the jungle, chatting now and then.
"These youngsters are pretty lucky to have non-humans to hunt. Back in our days when we graduated, we were sent straight to the battlefield without such opportunities to wet our beaks."
"Indeed. But then again, these natives are really foolish. Leaving a few slaves here as bait, and they just don't run; they keep coming to die."
"Instructor Sandru, those non-humans that escaped earlier seemed quite strong, probably Druids. According to the intelligence extracted from previous soul-searching, there's a place in this forest called 'Emerald Holy Land,' the sacred land of Dalu Tribe. It is said there are two Tier 5 beings. If those youngsters chase too far, won't they run into trouble?"
"Casualties are always part of a trial. Relax, with Rokshi watching over them from the shadows, nothing major can go wrong. Although I'm not too fond of that guy, he's known as 'Gravedigger,' and his abilities are quite formidable. Even if there really are Tier 5 professionals among these non-humans, he wouldn't necessarily be at a disadvantage..."
"Hehe, that's true."
"..."
After listening for a while, the men stopped paying attention to the fighting noises from the forest.
As they continued chatting, they moved on to the topic of the legion's mission this time.
"We initially came to capture some Icefield Giants, to acquire some [Giant's Muscles] for warrior enhancement, but we never expected to discover such an ancient ruin. Judging by the relics unearthed so far, the labyrinth might even predate the Dawn Era. This secret excavation is likely to yield significant findings."
"Yeah. From the look of it, there might be potent mysteries and [Cursed Objects]; maybe, if we're lucky, we might even find some mythological treasure."
"Those slave traders are really something, setting a date for delivery and then falling short on the numbers. Now we have to do it ourselves. The forest is so vast; this is hard labor..."
"I heard that a few days ago, the 'Sunshine Slave Hunting Group' encountered a lone adventurer in the forest and lost quite a few men..."
"Distortions of the truth, surely. Do you believe a Tier 3 adventurer, all by himself, could slaughter a slave hunting group with four Tier 4 professionals and seven to eight hundred elite members? While the fighting strength of the slave hunters isn't impressive, even you or I would struggle to pull that off. To kill seven or eight hundred people, the blade would be blunted, and all on his own? Hehe..."
"..."
As the men chatted away obliviously, they were unaware that Arcu and his companions were already lying in ambush for the group of knights undergoing their trial in the forest.
....
Su Lun and Yuta quickly made their way to Lake Rudasil.
The tribe's settlement of the Grey Wolf clan was just beside the lake, where the woods were not too dense and the view was quite open.
From atop a distant large tree, two figures were observing several people chatting in the village through a monocular telescope.
They didn't rashly approach but watched carefully.
After a long while, Su Lun put down the telescope, narrowed his eyes slightly, and muttered, "They're strong... So these are the elite royal troops of Luying?"
Even though they were too far to sense the fires of their souls, Su Lun could tell from their armor that those people in the village were the elite of the elite!
From the military insignia on their armor, the middle-aged man leading them seemed to be of the rank of colonel.
In Luying's military hierarchy, such a high-ranking position was usually held by professionals of the fourth tier and above.
"So that's the legendary Golden Gryphon Armor, troublesome indeed."
Su Lun's pupils contracted slightly as he pondered something.
With his current level of understanding, he could naturally tell the quality of the armor from the runes and enchantment traces on it.
The armors on those people varied, but they were at least of the "gold" or "dark gold" level for military officers.
The Imperial Royal Knight Legion of the Luying Empire has been able to sustain such a war of attrition against the mechanical army of Mafa for so many years, thanks to their alchemy, mechanical augmentation, and most importantly, their "Imperial Secretly-Forged" runic alchemy armors.
These were top-tier armors with defense strong enough to go head-to-head with mechanical battle armors.
It wasn't just about the indestructibility of the outer armor; the linings were able to absorb and dissolve the force of impacts, and some ingenious design at the joints ensured that knights' movements were not hindered at all, making them much more flexible than mechanical battle armors.
The armor also had high demands on the wearer.
To achieve ultimate defensive capabilities, such an armor would weigh at least half a ton and could go up to several.
To fight for extended periods on the battlefield, knights needed considerable strength.
"They've come to hunt the wild giants, huh. It looks like the Luying Empire must have found a shortcut that leads directly to the northern tundra..."
A myriad of thoughts flashed through Su Lun's mind in an instant.
The enemy was the royal elite, which was bad news.
But the good news was that he hadn't seen anyone who seemed like a fifth-tier presence thus far.
Yuta, using a telescope for the first time, adapted after some familiarization.
She keenly caught the tracks of flocks of birds occasionally startled into flight above the forest and analyzed, "There's fighting to the northeast in the forest, heading toward the 'Wildwind Path.' It could be Arcu and the others..."
As she spoke, she put down the telescope, looked at Su Lun, and asked, "Mr. Su Lun, are there formidable enemies among them?"
Su Lun stated bluntly, "This group of enemies is much stronger than the slavers. Although I haven't seen any fifth-tiers for now, we definitely can't confront them head-on. We have a chance only if we spread out."
Although he had killed several fourth-tiers, they were either pirates or slaver gangs.
What he was facing now was the genuine royal elite legion of Luying. Whether in terms of cultivation techniques, equipment, talent, or augmentation... they were one in ten thousand.
There was no room for carelessness.
Su Lun was fairly confident about taking down one.
But if several people from the village joined together against him, he didn't stand a chance.
Especially that colonel, aside from the Reaper, Su Lun didn't feel he had any way to take him down right now.
Yuta, hearing this, nodded seriously, "Mhm."
If he felt they were a challenge, the enemies must be extremely strong.
Su Lun had pieced together some information from reading lips and knew that those Luying knights were on an officer's trial.
The few officers in the village seemed to have noticed someone spying from afar.
But they didn't pursue, clearly not taking it seriously.
This was something that could be exploited.
Su Lun thought it over and said, "Let's go over there and take a look."
...
Meanwhile, several kilometers northeast of Lake Rudasil in the dense forest, a fierce battle was taking place.
The seven or eight young Druids of Arcu were not foolish; knowing the strength of the enemy, they had no plans to force a confrontation.
When they arrived, they found that most of the tribespeople of the Grey Wolf clan had already been transported away, leaving behind some who were injured and inconvenient to transport.
They naturally knew it was a trap, but they planned to rescue them first.
The youngsters discussed it and decided to lure the enemy.
Using the jungle environment, they aimed to kill the detestable humans and rescue their people.
However, the actual battle did not go as they expected.
They had heard from their people about the strength of the "slaver squads," but this time they indeed encountered the royal elite legion of Luying!
The decoy worked; they successfully lured the enemies out.
But... the battle was extremely brutal.
Even with traps set in case of danger that caught the enemy off guard and severely injured one.
That was all.
They soon realized that the other side had an absolute advantage in equipment.
It was equipment even more terrifying and powerful than that of the slaver squads!
Even the attacks of the Druids in their beast-transformed state caused only limited damage to the enemy's armor.
Claws could easily tear through leather armor, even ordinary mechanical gear, but on that runic armor, they left at most some slight scratches, doing no real harm to the enemy itself.
Even with spells, the lower tiers were just as useless against enemies clad in full-body armor.
And it was clear that the enemy had anticipated an ambush and did not panic when attacked; instead, they began to retaliate and encircle them.
Large-caliber sniper rifles, bombs, alchemy crossbows, cursed items... a constant stream of tactics emerged.
Whether at range or in close combat, Arcu's novice Druids had no advantage whatsoever.
Unable to rescue the captives, they were now the ones being hunted.
They could only rely on the forest for cover as they fought and retreated.
Soon, three of the eight who had snuck out from the Holy Land were dead in the chase, and the situation for the rest wasn't good; they were injured to varying degrees.
"Umon, stop being stubborn, let's get out of here!"
"It's my fault that everyone's in this mess. Arcu, you guys go ahead, I'll hold them off!"
"Damn it, if we go, we go together!"
"..."
These hot-blooded Dalu tribe youths would never abandon a comrade. They had come with the determination to face death.
They fought fiercely to the end.
....
When Su Lun and Yuta arrived, guided by the sounds of battle, they saw several people being chased in a sorry state.
However, fortunately, there were still a few alive – a stroke of luck amidst the misfortune.
Suddenly blocked by a huge white wolf, the group was collectively startled.
Arcu recognized it immediately as his sister.
"Sister!?"
Guilty flashed across his face as he realized she had discovered his sneaking out.
But now was clearly not the time for that.
He shouted, "Sister, get out of here, the enemies are really tough!"
Yuta glanced at the young men, not moving, and coldly rebuked, "You go first. We'll deal with you when you get back!"
Arcu, thinking his sister didn't know how formidable the enemy was, anxiously said, "Sister, their armor is very strong, you can't fight them head-on."
Yuta didn't have a chance to reply. Her gaze hardened and she disappeared into a white blur.
In the blink of an eye, with a "thud," she had sent a heavy-armored knight flying with a palm strike, breaking a large tree.
But the knight had armor to protect him and seemed unaffected; he immediately stood back up.
With a "whoosh," a javelin was thrown their way. Yuta sensed it and narrowly avoided it.
At that moment, seven or eight more people caught up, all fully-armored knights.
"Sister!"
Arcu certainly hadn't gone first; he resolutely stood by Yuta's side, ready to protect her.
His refusal to leave meant that the other apprentice Druids didn't leave either, all ready to stay and fight to the death if necessary.
....
Meanwhile, high in the treetops, Su Lun cloaked in his mantle and suppressing his presence, closely observed the area.
[Sacred Judgment Legion's Standard Javelin]
Quality: Silver
Description: Standard javelin of the Luying Royal Legion, made of tungsten steel alloy, with wind attribute piercing and acceleration effects;
Looking at the javelin, Su Lun muttered to himself, "They really are rich... the cost of that javelin must be worth two to three hundred thousand apiece."
He then observed the equipment worn by those knights.
Elite is indeed elite; the knights' armor, sabers, and firearms were all top-grade military gear that couldn't be bought on the open market.
The value of their full set of equipment was staggering; it wouldn't be an overstatement to say they were carrying half a city's worth on their backs.
Within his mind, Su Lun roughly estimated that just the value of the equipment on this small squad of ten exceeded the worth of the few hundred slavers he had taken down before.
Moreover, all of it was military gear that couldn't be acquired on the market.
However, these knights weren't the ones Su Lun needed to be wary of.
The soul fires of the trainee officers below were all within his sensing range, none of them particularly strong, ranging from second to third tier.
Without a fourth tier amongst them, even with their superior equipment, it would not be difficult for Su Lun to kill them if he wanted to.
But he knew there was a high-ranking professional secretly protecting the group.
Without pinpointing that individual's location, he refrained from taking action rashly.
...
On the ground, Yuta and her companions had already engaged in fierce battle with the enemy group.
With her in the fight, the combatants were momentarily in a standoff.
The heavy-armored knights had a weakness too; the combat greatly drained their stamina.
Although the attacks from Yuta's side did limited damage to the armor, they required much less stamina and were more agile, making it difficult for the armors to win quickly.
Seeing Yuta was not in immediate danger, Su Lun was not in a hurry to intervene.
He watched the trainee officers and their displayed tactics, his thoughts racing, "[B-036-Earth Dragon], [Talent C-071-Ape], [C-004-Divine Power]... This Judgment Legion really is like the legends say, mostly recruiting talented fighters with strength-based abilities, and their augmentations are all focused on enhancing strength..."
Su Lun was pensive.
The Luying military had several mature professional advancement systems. Soldiers advanced in this way would be incredibly strong in group combat.
However, as he watched, his expression suddenly changed.
"Have I been discovered?"
Su Lun's brows immediately furrowed.
He had been planning to observe from the shadows but hadn't expected to be detected by the enemy first.
It was just a moment before, that he clearly felt a soul fluctuation sweep over him like a radar wave.
This fluctuation would go unnoticed by normal people, but his spiritual power was so sensitive now that he immediately identified it as some kind of spiritual power sensing technique.
Su Lun was somewhat puzzled. He was wearing a mirror organization's cloak which usually rendered him undetectable by ordinary means.
This meant that the person lurking somewhere possessed a curse object with a sensing ability?
Since the enemy had already discovered him, remaining hidden was pointless. He immediately changed tactics.
Without any hesitation, Su Lun spread out a sealed scroll, formed sorcerer's seals with his hands, and chanted "Seal·Release!"
The next instant, a massive Mecha appeared out of nowhere.
The Mecha plummeted down rapidly, and Su Lun leaped down with it.
While he was still in descent, he swiftly assembled the Mecha onto his body using maneuvering threads. Before anyone on the ground could react, the Mecha's steam boiler charged and expelled a burst of steam with a "hiss," propelling his form rapidly downward as he slashed with his blade.
Because it was a surprise attack, those underground didn't have time to dodge when they noticed.
Su Lun's Ship-Cutter struck the knight who attempted to block with his sword.
This was the "main tank" of that team.
With a "clang," the ear-piercing clank resounded through the woods.
It was only a momentary standoff before the vibration of the Ship-Cutter broke the long sword in two, and then heavily cut into the opponent's armor.
Blood splattered everywhere as the knight, overwhelmed by the tremendous force, sunk one leg deep into the soil.
The fact that the cut didn't bisect him showed how astonishing the armor's defense was.
But Su Lun didn't give him a chance.
The initial slash had opened a breach and compromised the integrity of the armor, significantly reducing its defensive capability.
He lifted his arm and came down with a diagonal slash, following the gap and cleaving the knight in two from the chest, blood spraying wildly, and the sight turning crimson.
....
Su Lun killed someone in an instant.
This sudden change shocked everyone underground for a moment.
The few members of the knight order, upon seeing their comrade slain, were horrified and confused.
They instantly recognized that this was a battle Mecha from Mafa!
What the hell!
How could someone from Mafa appear in the Silent Forest?
Even Yuta, watching him slay a knight in armor she herself couldn't kill, had a slight surprise in her eyes.
As for Arcu and the others, their shock was beyond measure.
Such sturdy armor, split with a single slash?
But in that moment, they guessed the identity of the person.
Only humans would use such mechanical devices.
And the humans they knew were only two, one was Katyusha, and the other was Mr. Su Lun!
The one who would come to rescue them alongside his sister was fairly obvious.
Su Lun shouted, "You go first!"
His Mecha armor held back those on the opposite side, and both sides disengaged and stood off at a distance.
Upon hearing this, Yuta nodded her head.
Knowing Su Lun's capabilities, she understood that staying would only be a burden, so she commanded Arcu and the others with a sharp cry, "Go!"
.....
Now the situation was reversed, with Su Lun's side having the overwhelming equipment advantage.
The armor of the Imperial Royal officers of Luying might be incredibly defensive, but the properties of the armor worn by these reserve officers fell far short of the [Ship-Cutter IX-Type Mecha Armor] Su Lun wore!
Without any accidents, these people stood no chance of killing Su Lun.
Instead, they'd likely be killed cleanly by him.
Therefore, the one hiding in the shadows would definitely not just watch this happen.
Moreover, now that a battle Mecha from Mafa had appeared, the matter had become more complicated.
They couldn't help but suspect that the forces of the Mafa Empire had infiltrated the Northern Ice Fields, and might have even formed some alliance with the demi-human tribes.
Therefore, this Mecha warrior and those Druids could not be allowed to escape!
....
Su Lun was forcing that person to come out!
Everyone was shocked for a moment.
But Su Lun didn't stop. Now that he had made his move, he wouldn't give the enemy a chance to react.
In that brief moment, steam power built up beneath his feet and he rocketed forward, his mechanized body lurching as he swung his second slash!
Just as another was about to be cut down by the blade, a ghostly figure appeared before Su Lun. Holding a black long staff-like weapon, he steadfastly blocked the Ship-Cutter.
Su Lun, seeing his attack blocked, was not at all surprised, "So you've come."
However, upon seeing the person clearly, he did feel a hint of surprise.
To be exact, it was not because of the fourth-tier professional, but because of the weapon in his hand.
It was an ink-black umbrella!
Just now, for a moment, golden runes lit up on the umbrella's surface, and astonishingly, they absorbed the blow from the Ship-Cutter. Briefly, one could even hear the sound of ghastly wails and howls.
A flicker passed through Su Lun's left eye as he appraised it.
[Rune-Engraved Human Skin Umbrella]
Quality: Dark Gold
Description: Messengers of the underworld also need an umbrella to shield them from the sun;
Cursed Feature: An umbrella made of human skin holding resentful spirits, a prison for souls; it can increase the bearer's spiritual perception and enhance Necromancy Spell Penetration; consumes a large amount of Spiritual Power to actively deploy the umbrella, creating a 'Nightfall Domain' that deprives everyone within its range of their five senses; releases resentful spirits to inflict continuous psychic damage on the target; those who have not attained a certain level of mastery over the laws of Death will suffer from the curse's backlash, permanent sensory distortion, with a moderate probability of hearing whispers from unknown beings of the underworld;
Explanation: This is a damaged forbidden artifact, missing its ribs; it only has the canopy left. The collection of souls can strengthen this cursed object's characteristics, currently hosting 85546 malevolent spirits;
