Once Su Lun understood the details of the umbrella, the realization dawned on him.
Of course it could block the Ship-Cutter; it was a damaged forbidden artifact.
Seeing the whispers and feeling a sense of deja vu,
"Not being affected by the curse with the mastery of laws of Death? I wonder if my second-level Reaper meets the usage requirements..."
As Su Lun pondered, the cursed object seemed quite suitable for him.
He also understood why he had been detected.
It was truly because of this umbrella.
At the same time, he was also amazed by the depth of resources the Luying royal family had.
Not to mention those costly standard issue gears, just any fourth-tier that showed up had in their possession a damaged forbidden artifact.

chapters.title: Chapter 265 - 264: Necromancy, Stones, Harvest
chapters.content:
The hunchbacked old man in black clothes used an umbrella to block Su Lun's slash.
The two immediately disengaged and created some distance between them.
As the old man retreated, he closed his umbrella and his fingers flurried through enchanting movements, almost instantly conjuring sorcerer's seals.
Seeing this reaction speed, Su Lun knew he was dealing with a formidable opponent.
The old man in black fixed his gaze on Su Lun in front of him, though his peripheral vision caught a glimpse of Yuta and the others in the forest behind.
Clearly, he had no intention of letting them go.
The sorcerer's seals formed instantly, and he slapped the ground with one hand, "Spirit Summoning Contract: Hellhound!"
As Su Lun observed the old man performing the sorcerer's seals, he knew they weren't the usual elemental spell configurations and had his guards up. However, he never imagined it would be necromancy!
Necromancers are extremely rare in the alchemy field, even rarer than Puppet Masters.
They usually employ ancient contracts, offering sacrifices for an equivalent exchange to summon creatures from other-dimensional planes to assist in battle.
As the spell was cast, a black Seven-Pointed Star Formation pattern suddenly appeared under the old man's palm.
The formation seemed to open a spatial gateway, and Su Lun immediately felt a strong aura of death overwhelming him.
This smell would make anyone else feel dizzy and nauseous, but he found it strangely comforting.
"Is this contract summoning a creature from a necromantic plane?"
A thought flashed through Su Lun's mind.
He didn't need to guess much further, as at that moment, the necromantic array flashed with a black light, and suddenly five ugly, giant hounds engulfed in black flames appeared.
[Hellhound]
Description: A third-tier hell creature with a trace of divine lineage; adept in dark flame spells, tracking, and has a remarkable biting force;
Su Lun looked at these headless demonic hounds and knew they posed no threat to him.
The old man, evidently, intended them to chase after Yuta and his group.
Sure enough, after a fierce barking session, the demonic hounds dashed into the dense forest like lightning.
Su Lun wasn't particularly worried; Yuta and his crew were strong, and there was no immediate danger.
"This is the depth of the royal family's heritage..."
Su Lun sighed internally.
The hunchbacked old man before him, who he had encountered at the fourth-tier, was completely out of his league.
However.
If the opponent had tactics, his were not inferior!
While the old man was forming seals for summoning, Su Lun also took out a black-and-white chessboard.
Who knew what strange abilities the enemy might deploy; he had no intention of letting him escape.
With a flash of light, the two appeared within the space of the chessboard.
....
"Huh..."
The hunchbacked old man sensed the space shifting around him and let out a light huh.
Instinctively, he immediately lifted the black umbrella in his hand.
Su Lun showed no courtesy, lunging forward with his Ship-Cutter in hand.
This guy could block the Ship-Cutter; his melee capabilities were indeed strong.
But at equal levels, how could a fleshly body compare with machinery?
If he could kill with the mecha or perhaps pry some secrets from his opponent, that would be perfect.
But the old man was extremely decisive; after only a few exchanges, he realized that even if he wouldn't be defeated, he definitely couldn't break through the mechanical armor.
While dodging, as Su Lun watched him unhesitatingly take out a piece of meat, chew it briefly, and swallow it,
Su Lun's eye twitched as he observed the dark piece of meat.
[Cursed Corpse Chunk]
Description: A piece of meat over three thousand years old, which, after special curing, has acquired miraculous powers; consuming it can greatly enhance necromantic affinity and improve resistance to certain necromantic curses; high probability of contracting corpse poison.
Being able to swallow a millennia-old piece of rotten meat without batting an eyelid, Su Lun understood why necromancers weren't very sociable.
Being harsh on oneself naturally results in great effects.
After swallowing that piece of rotten meat, the old man's body emitted steaming black vapors, his aura abruptly changed, wrapped in black mists, and he looked terrifying.
The scent of the living vanished from him in an instant, and he appeared as though he had crawled out of a grave.
Su Lun immediately guessed what that guy was planning to do, feeling a fresh sense of great enlightenment in his heart.
"So it's possible to evade part of a curse's backlash using such an unorthodox method?"
He thought in a flash that if he ever heard uncontrollable whispers again, could he also use this method to suppress them temporarily?
However, eating rotting flesh... seemed a bit hard to stomach.
The thought vanished in a flash.
This guy, obviously knowing he couldn't kill Su Lun, was planning to use the power of that umbrella.
However, since he had identified the properties of the human skin umbrella, Su Lun also felt confident about his chances.
He also wanted to test whether his hypothesis was correct.
If he was right, this guy was dead!
.....
The hunchbacked old man was decisive, even willing to endure a curse backlash to use this tactic, which was not to be underestimated.
After consuming that piece of meat, the old man's sorcerer's seals rapidly changed, quickly forming into a spell pattern Su Lun had never seen before, and he exclaimed softly, "Incorporation · Release!"
Just then, a pair of blue phosphorus-fire wings congealed behind him, lifting him into the air, and his figure became even more ghostlike.
Su Lun watching the incorporation, twitched at the corner of his eye, "Gold quality incorporation, the wings of the phantom species 'Phosphorus Sparrow'?"
This time, he truly realized how extravagantly wealthy the Luying royal family was.
Their heritage was absolutely staggering...
Su Lun himself had survived many near-death situations, which had earned him the few restricted items he now possessed.
This guy, with cursed items, incorporations, and cultivation techniques all of superior quality, was enough to incite envy.
The incorporation not only enhanced movement speed but also increased affinity with necromancy; the match between the incorporation's attributes and abilities was very high, and his aura became even stronger.
Furthermore, the blue phosphorus fire on the wings was very effective in burning through the threads condensed by Su Lun's fourth-tier Space Law.
This made Su Lun's plan to kill the opponent solely with his mechanized armor fail.
With these wings, at least for the short term, he wouldn't be able to kill that guy.
The hunchbacked old man used this wing incorporation not just for teleportation to save his life.
But to give himself peace of mind to execute that particular spell.
Su Lun didn't use his powerful moves to stop him.
The first reason was that he wasn't sure he could definitely kill him.
The second reason naturally was to let him go ahead and use that spell.
After all, using it would greatly burden the guy.
Then there would be a chance to kill him.
And that spell, unless there was an unexpected turn, wouldn't affect him too much.
....
Su Lun's set of "Ship-Cutter IX Form Mechanized Armor" included a helmet made of invigorating alloy, so general mental spells had no effect on him.
The hunchbacked old man clearly realized this, which is why he resolutely used that cursed black umbrella.
Su Lun gave him the opportunity, and the guy finally used it.
As a complex array of sorcerer's seals formed, the old man's aura suddenly soared, and he emitted a low ghost-like voice, "Dark Domain: Nightfall!"
The vast checkerboard space was instantly enveloped in pitch darkness, like asphalt.
Su Lun felt as if he had been blinded by the nightfall, seeing nothing but darkness before him.
Not only was his sense of sight stripped away, but his hearing and touch vanished too.
He couldn't even feel his own body, as if only his lonely soul remained there, lost in thought.
It proved that in an environment of absolute darkness, fear could intensify a hundredfold.
If one were to remain in such a state for a long time, their spirit would eventually spiral out of control and break down.
But Su Lun was unusually calm.
This feeling made controlling his negative emotions much easier.
He even took the time to carefully experience this stripping of the senses, thinking to himself, "Using cursed items to execute a domain that seems like something only a seventh-tier professional could use? Tsk tsk, such a miraculous spell. With this move, probably most professionals would have their eyes wide open in complete darkness. My checkerboard space should also pull off something like this, close the doors, turn off the lights, it would be perfect..."
Being deprived of the five senses, for most people, meant being like lambs to the slaughter.
But Su Lun had Soul Perception, and he clearly sensed the opponent's soul fire, so he was not at all flustered.
However, what puzzled him was that the old man's soul fire form had changed from the initial human form to a shape with horns on its head and fleshy wings on its back.
"A mythological series talent, [A-029-Hell Messenger]? No wonder he dared to use that cursed umbrella so potent it's considered a restricted item..."
Su Lun recognized the origin of the shadow, but he was not surprised anymore.
The population of the Emperor Luying's Empire was vast, and even with a talent awakening rate of one in a million for level A talents, there were still quite a few.
Moreover, those who woke up with rare talents generally gathered under the nobles.
It was not strange for people of the royal family to possess such level A and B talents.
However, if it were just that, Su Lun, protected by his mechanical combat suit, wouldn't have had a major problem.
He couldn't sense the opponent or attack, but the opponent couldn't kill him either.
Obviously, the power of this dark umbrella was far more than just that.
When darkness fell, Su Lun suddenly heard a wailing scream beside his ear.
He clearly blocked his hearing, so where did this sound come from?
Su Lun immediately realized that it was a spiritual attack from the vengeful spirits.
These were the over eighty thousand vengeful spirits imprisoned by the Human Skin Umbrella, now attacking his mind.
This made Su Lun feel as if he had fallen into an abyss paved with the souls of the wronged, with hands of evil spirits trying to drag his thoughts into an endless abyss.
This was somewhat similar to the sonic attack of his "Nightmare Doll."
It was a range release; even if one didn't succumb in a short time, the longer the duration, the more chaotic the spirit would become, leading eventually to a mental breakdown.
What made Su Lun more curious was, how did this technique penetrate the vibranium helmet and affect his true body?
Tsk tsk… interesting.
"It must be the 'Necromancy Spell Penetration' feature of the dark umbrella, so powerful. Doesn't this mean that in the future when facing mechanical warriors, even if I don't use the Reaper's scythe, I also have a way to kill the opponent?"
Thoughts flashed through Su Lun's mind,
and he already considered the dark umbrella as his spoils of war.
Now, he had roughly figured out the effects of this cursed dark umbrella.
The testing was almost done.
It was time to end this.
Moreover, after that old man employed this technique, his aura had significantly weakened a lot.
The exhaustion of this "Dark Domain," as identified, was enormous!
If he let this domain continue, it could directly drain that hunchbacked old man dry.
But Su Lun himself wouldn't be able to hold out that long.
The spiritual attacks of those vengeful spirits were getting stronger, and even though he suppressed them, he felt increasingly irritated.
At that moment, his expression suddenly became stern, planning to make one last attempt.
If his guess was correct, it also meant that he might be able to control this cursed dark umbrella!
....
The hunchbacked old man seemed to think Su Lun had succumbed to the control of "Nightfall" and confidently stepped closer.
The old man got very close, probably wanting to find any flaws in the mechanical combat suit.
But just then, a sudden change escalated!
His eyes suddenly hardened, and he saw a silhouette of a cloak and scythe appear behind the Mecha.
It was the second stage Reaper's ghostly shadow!
"This!!!"
Seeing this, the hunchbacked old man instantly panicked, a fear from the depths of his soul.
Others might not recognize what this apparition was, but being a Necromancer, he clearly knew much more about the taboos of death!
He recognized the origin of this shadow, and his eyes went blank: "This is the S-level talent 'Death Reaper,' and a second stage awakening? How... how is this possible!"
Vengeful spirits are just minor ghosts; wouldn't they shiver at the arrival of the Grim Reaper?
As soon as the ghostly shadow of the Reaper appeared, the tens of thousands of vengeful spirits within the domain of Nightfall, like cats whose tails had been stepped on, panicked and changed shape. They had been greedily inhaling human breath moments before, but now they were terrified and bolted back into the floating dark umbrella in mid-air, daring not to show themselves again.
Su Lun's senses also instantly recovered, and his vision cleared.
"Pff~"
Seeing his technique broken, the hunchbacked old man's face turned red, and he couldn't help but spurt out a mouthful of blood.
The curse rebounded against him several times over, due to the forced breaking of the technique.
And just when his mind was still dazed, Su Lun would not give him a chance to catch his breath!
The threads that hadn't appeared before now densely materialized into solid form.
"Controlling Threads Secret Technique·Caged Bird!"
Su Lun had long locked onto his opponent, and once he made a move, it was a thunderous strike, leaving no chance for a turnaround.
Masses of silk threads controlled the field, not yet burnt through, as a mechanical arm quickly gripped the neck of the hunchbacked old man, firmly locking it in place like a vise.
A crisp snapping sound of bones breaking echoed.
The shock on the face of this hunchbacked old man hadn't faded before he completely lost his vitality.
His body went limp, turning into a corpse.
Su Lun watched as wisps of gray mist floated from the corpse in his hand, casually selecting a few interesting ones and devouring them.
'You have stripped "Roksh Luweio" of his soul, obtaining some "Fragments of Dark Laws," "Fragments of Space Law"'
'You are now aware of some usage details of the "Runic Human Skin Umbrella"'
'You have gained the understanding of a specific "Contractual Spirit Summoning Technique"'
'You have acquired extensive knowledge related to "Necromancy Techniques" and "Necromancy Runes"'
'You have mastered some information: "Information on the strong of the Sacred Judgment Legion..."'
'You have learned some "Royal Secrets of the Luying Dynasty"'
'Spiritual power +6.3'
Having digested the stripped information, Su Lun's eyes sparkled, "Heh... The people of the Luying royal family really have extraordinary knowledge!"
This guy definitely was the highest-quality tier-four professional he had stripped, his understanding of laws so solid, far stronger than those half-baked pirates he'd stripped before.
Su Lun's thoughts drifted.
Many of his ideas had greatly changed.
Although the Luying empire was a declining one, from some of the "Royal Secrets" he had stripped, like those of Roksh, there were many more high-level practitioners in the Luying royal family.
And the information this guy knew was just the tip of the iceberg; the entire empire was a massive, frightening "old monster."
"The strength of the Luying royal family really should not be underestimated..."
Su Lun mused to himself.
Having digested the memories, he also understood that Roksh's techniques were not so simple.
It just so happened that Roksh encountered Su Lun's "Reaper Phantom," which he countered.
Otherwise, even facing a tier-five professional, this guy could have shown considerable combat power.
Too bad.
This further convinced Su Lun of the thought that an alchemist must be well-learned.
Learning more always helps, reducing the chances of being countered.
...
As Su Lun digested the memories, two glowing objects slowly condensed from the corpse.
One was a crystal skull, a silver initiation material of the dark series, which could greatly enhance the capability to comprehend dark laws after advancement.
The tier-four gold outfit "Phosphor Peacock Wings" also condensed.
If Su Lun had no better options, these two materials were also somewhat compatible with his profession.
Even if not used, they could still fetch a good price.
The items were all high-grade, which was also the biggest reason this guy could use the black umbrella and withstand the curse backlash.
Thinking of the black umbrella, Su Lun turned his gaze over it once more.
He held the umbrella in his hand, a chill and bizarre sensation shooting straight to his forehead.
Yet strangely, there was a sense of familiarity.
The death aura on the black umbrella seemed to really like Su Lun's death laws.
Just by touching it, Su Lun noticed a difference, his heart thrilled, "With this item in hand, my soul perception range has expanded nearly fivefold!"
Not to mention its other effects, just this functionality alone made it an extremely practical cursed object for him!
He had already had a hunch, and now upon handling it, it might actually be feasible.
With his understanding of death laws, using this black umbrella, the negative consequences of curse backlash would be very low!
For Su Lun, this was certainly an item that could be used immediately!
His storage ring still contained many materials, potions, and scriptures of sorts.
However, now was not the time to thoroughly experience them.
If there were no surprises, someone should be chasing after him!
Su Lun packaged the items quickly, unraveling the chessboard space.

chapters.title: Chapter 266 - 265: The Omen Bird
chapters.content:
Having a human skin umbrella expanded Su Lun's sensory range by several times.
When he emerged from the chessboard space, he immediately sensed several powerful soul fires nearby. As expected, they were the same Ru-Ying military officers from the village earlier.
Fortunately, Su Lun had prepared in advance and used his old method of wrapping himself in shroud cloth for invisibility, while also controlling a walking corpse as a decoy.
As expected, as soon as it appeared, several figures flashed, and the walking corpse was immediately hacked into three pieces by two silver-armored warriors wielding huge swords, one in front and one behind.
The recent lesson from "Roksh Luweio" vividly taught Su Lun.
It made him realize that encountering professionals with strong backgrounds required extra caution since they might possess certain forbidden items. The abilities of professionals in this world were diverse and should never be underestimated.
This wasn't just Su Lun's speculation; he had deliberately extracted the memories of that hunchbacked old man earlier, learning the identities of the people behind him and some of their methods.
These individuals were instructors at the "Ru-Ying Royal War Academy."
Although their transcendental rank was not too high, they had rich practical experience and each possessed curses that enhanced their combat capabilities, which would make an actual fight extremely troublesome.
Moreover, military personnel were adept at coordinated attacks. They had prepared tactics for handling various professionals with seamless cooperation. Even if Su Lun went out in mechanical armor, he wouldn't gain any advantage whatsoever.
Not intending to confront them directly, Su Lun seized the opportunity to flash into the dense forest.
...
While the shroud cloth completely shielded his aura, the slightest noises of movement couldn't escape those fourth-level professionals.
After gaining some distance, Su Lun decisively deployed his eight-armed spider lance and began sprinting wildly through the dense forest.
The men behind him naturally pursued relentlessly.
Despite wearing heavy armor, these fellows were not slow, and all possessed highly advanced alchemical augmentations.
The one closest in pursuit, wearing gold griffin armor and known as Big Beard Sandru Heimer, nicknamed "Guile Sword," slashed the air, sending several sharp and cunning sword Qi that chopped down the giant trees in the forest like cutting wheat.
If it weren't for Su Lun's keen senses and spatial flash ability, he would have been cut into pieces long ago.
There was also that individual flying midair with shiny golden wings, "Metal Angel" Lei, whose main combat augmentation was the gold version of "Thousand Killing Wings." The metal feathers could be launched like a storm, wreaking havoc wherever they passed.
Fortunately, in the primeval forest, wing augmentations were not so effective. Flying low, they encountered numerous trees and obstacles, and flying high, the dense canopy obscured their vision.
And wind elemental accelerated golden spears shot through the air like bullets, exploding the giant trees...
There were also returning flying axes...
None of the individuals following him were weak in their methods.
However, the good news was that not all of them excelled in pursuit.
Such burst speeds were not sustainable.
And Su Lun himself, with spatial displacement and the eight-armed spider lance, could escape at a despairingly fast pace.
If they couldn't close the distance in a short burst, those behind him would likely have no chance to catch up.
If the opponents recklessly split up to pursue him, he wouldn't mind defeating them one by one.
The opponents clearly understood this as well, never revealing such a flaw. They knew very well that anyone capable of killing the fourth-rank hunchbacked old man Roksh could certainly kill any one of them as well.
Eventually, after a chase through the forest, Su Lun successfully eluded them.
.....
Meanwhile, in another part of the forest.
The place was in chaos, with evidence of battle everywhere.
The vegetation was scorched en masse into ashes, with some stumps still holding unextinguished, eerie black fires, and the air was thick with the smell of char.
Yuta, in his form of a white wolf, was also scorched all over, panting heavily while staring intensely into the depths of the dense forest.
They had just been through a fierce life-and-death battle, and if not for his protection, Arcu and the boys might have died here.
The running speed of the hellhounds wasn't a bit slower than their beast-transformed forms, and they were also adept in tracking, making them impossible to shake off.
Fortunately, all of a sudden, the five hellhounds were pulled back to another plane, allowing the group a moment to breathe.
Arcu refrained from looking his sister in the eye, as he tended to the severe injuries of the other two companions.
Yuta's deep blue pupils couldn't hide the worry, and after looking at Arcu and the others, she said, "This place isn't safe, you all go back to the sanctuary first."
"Oh."
Hearing her words, the boys all bowed their heads in response, each passing a trace of guilt across their expressions. They hadn't saved anyone and instead lost a few comrades, creating a big mess this time.
They hadn't expected Mr. Su Lun would come to their rescue.
But facing such strong enemies, their worries remained.
Arcu asked, "Sister, Mr. Su Lun won't be in trouble, right?"
Another young man, transformed into a black bear, also asked, "Yeah, Sister Yuta, that Mr. Su Lun..."
Yuta interrupted them, "The sudden disappearance of the hell creatures implies that the contractor has been killed."
Although she said that, her face also showed slight concern.
After all, she knew there were several other troublesome enemies not far away in the village.
Yuta didn't criticize much further, only saying, "In the future, you guys will be the hope of our Dalu tribe. Remember, always think thoroughly before making any decisions."
Although the price was somewhat severe this time, having a lesson was a good thing as well.
The group dared not meet her gaze, "Understood, Sister Yuta."
Ultimately, Yuta couldn't stop worrying and said no more, "You all go back first, I'll make a trip!"
With that, she courageously dashed into the dense forest.
....
Having shaken off his pursuers, Su Lun slowed down.
The greatest dangers in the forest were never humans; it was the magical beasts and all sorts of bizarre creatures that were far deadlier, and they were present everywhere.
He didn't dare to continue teleporting at high speeds in an unfamiliar environment; that would only attract the hunters in the jungle.
Using the black umbrella as a walking stick, Su Lun strolled leisurely.
With the perception amplification granted by the black umbrella, he could sense the soul flames within a one-kilometer radius, unafraid of being ambushed suddenly by anything.
He had not carefully felt it before, but now he genuinely appreciated the finesse of this black umbrella.
Having it in his possession, he sensed a realism far surpassing the information seen through the All-knowing Eye.
"This Guile Sword Umbrella is indeed a fine treasure..."
Su Lun felt moved and played with the black umbrella in his hands, becoming even more attached to it.
Although he had not tried using the "Nightfall Domain" function of the umbrella, he felt that its curse backlash would not be a big issue for him. This defective sealed item would greatly enhance his strength!
Thinking of testing it further later, he felt immediately capable of using it in real combat.
While walking and pondering over the effects of the black umbrella, Su Lun suddenly sensed a soul flame quickly approaching him.
"Yuta?"
Su Lun was not surprised.
He wore a necklace with Yuta's real name and a wolf claw, which allowed her to confirm his location from a great distance.
As expected, a familiar, massive white wolf burst into view from the dense forest.
Seeing that Su Lun was unharmed, a visibly relieved expression appeared in Yuta's eyes, and she asked, "Mr. Su Lun, are you alright?"
"I'm fine."
Su Lun, noticing her scorched fur, also asked, "Are you alright?"
"Just a minor injury."
Yuta's face showed complete indifference as she slowly transformed back into her human form.
She cared more about Su Lun than herself.
Injuries in her beast form also appeared on her human body. Su Lun saw the burn marks on her skin, took out a potion, and helped clean and treat her wounds.
Yuta, unembarrassed, sat bare-skinned, looking tenderly at the man before her.
The cooling essence of the potion soaked into the wound, visibly washing away the charred flesh as new flesh formed.
She noticed the black umbrella in Su Lun's hand, her brow furrowing at its unsettling aura.
It carried a deathly aura starkly different from the natural forces.
However, considering it was Su Lun's war trophy, her expression relaxed again.
Guessing something, Yuta said, "It's also lucky you killed those Hellhound contractors; otherwise, the situation would be very bad."
Su Lun nodded, his curiosity piqued as he asked, "How strong were those Hellhounds?"
Yuta replied, "Very strong. Unlike magical beasts, their bodies are largely composed of fire elements, making them hard to kill."
"Oh."
Su Lun listened to her description of the recent battle, his hands busy treating her wounds.
Although called "Hellhounds," they were not necessarily from the mythological Hell.
Most likely from some other realm like the "Abyssal Plane" that housed undead creatures.
The necromancy contracts in Alchemy originated from ancient alchemists who subdued creatures from different realms to facilitate enslavement, creating the spells for this purpose.
Current alchemists no longer have the capability to campaign against different realms; thus, such knowledge has grown increasingly rare.
The hunchbacked old man he had killed before had found a Necromancy Mysticism scroll from the Dawn Era in some ruins and succeeded in contracting a creature from an alternate realm like the Hellhounds.
Thinking this, Su Lun also recalled that the storage ring he had just acquired seemed to contain that tome.
He thought it might be worth trying to see if he could form a contract himself.
If he could obtain a few creatures like the "Hellhounds," skilled in tracking, they would be quite handy.
....
As his thoughts flashed through his mind, Su Lun finished treating the last torn and burned wound on Yuta's back.
"All done."
He put away the potion bottle and casually slapped Yuta's firm buttocks, which were very elastic.
Yuta smiled coyly in response, "Thank you."
She put on her clothes and looked at the darkening sky, saying, "It's getting dark; we need to find a place to rest."
"Yeah."
Su Lun nodded.
Yuta had been to the Grey Wolf tribe and was quite familiar with the forest in this area.
Soon, the two found a cave.
Because there were enemies in the forest, they did not start a fire but ate some dry food instead.
After resting for a while, Yuta went to sleep on the ground spread with animal skins, the day's travel and battles having drained much of her energy.
Meanwhile, Su Lun began to organize the day's spoils.
A set of incomplete silver armor, and some standard officer equipment from the Royal Luitton Army, these were the spoils from the apprentice officer killed by the Ship-Cutter Sword earlier.
There were also many spare items in the storage ring, alchemy bullets, potions, demon cores, energy crystal cores...
It has to be said, these guys were really wealthy. The equipment on this third-tier lieutenant was worth more than those on the fourth or even fifth-tier pirates.
After roughly checking everything, Su Lun searched carefully through that hunchbacked old man's storage ring.
The storage ring could not hold much, but everything in it was valuable.
There were three thick tomes: "Dark Magic," "Necromancy Mysticism," "Fourth-Level Seal Sorcery"... and several dark magic spell scrolls. Although copies, each one was of fine quality. Probably an official perk from Luitton.
The last thin, map-like ancient scroll, however, was the "Necromancy Spirit Communion Secrets."
Judging by the material and the degree of wear, it was an ancient item.
Su Lun gave it a look over.
Previously, he had pieced together memories from "Necromancy," so he could read quite swiftly.
In just a quarter of an hour, he had read through the secret text, and his brain quickly assimilated the content into his knowledge.
"I can only contract extraplanar necrotic creatures that do not exceed my own tier, otherwise, I risk being devoured by the necrotic creature?"
Su Lun pondered for a moment.
No wonder the hunchbacked old man summoned a third-tier Hellhound during the day.
"So, to be safe, I can only summon about second-tier necrotic creatures? And it's random?"
Su Lun pursed his lips.
Seemed hardly useful.
Although he felt it was somewhat trivial, he still decided to give it a try.
Performing necromancy not only required this contract scroll (coordinates) but also a mastery of either the laws of death or dark magic, and a bit of spatial law.
Now that he had everything he needed.
Su Lun thought it wouldn't be difficult and started setting up the Spirit Communion Array according to the scroll.
The first time was a bit troublesome, requiring sufficient offerings.
Su Lun spent over a hundred thousand materials to set up a pentagram formation, then placed a piece of rotten flesh that the guy had eaten during the day in the center of the formation.
With a clench of his sorcerer's seals, he activated the magic array, and a black light began to shine.
The first necromantic contract was like fishing—extraplanar necrotic creatures that fancied these "offerings" would be hooked naturally and appear within the formation.
Due to the constraints of the formation, they would obey some commands from the contractor.
It was somewhat like hiring them.
.....
Su Lun hadn't really expected to summon any powerful creatures.
He had seen plenty of extraplanar creatures before, especially during his time in Old Lington, where he had encountered many abyssal creatures.
He thought that even if a necrotic creature appeared, it wouldn't be surprising.
However, he never expected that after the black pentagram formation lit up and the void of the plane connected, he suddenly felt a strong surge of necrotic air assaulting him.
It wasn't that the presence was powerful, but it had a sort of bloodline oppression to it.
Su Lun felt uneasy and furrowed his brows, "Could something go wrong?"
The disturbance was even greater than the hunchbacked old man's summoning of a third-tier Hellhound during the day.
Yet, he had clearly set up a second-tier necromancy formation?
Su Lun was sure that he had followed the scroll's instructions perfectly when setting up the formation, without any mistakes.
And the ritual had stripped soul experience, so there was no possibility of encrypted misunderstanding.
The ritual was already underway, and if he forcibly terminated it, it would also adversely affect Su Lun, the caster. As he watched the shining phantom in the formation, he patiently waited.
Su Lun had been mentally prepared to see some kind of second-tier lord-level necrotic creature,
but unexpectedly,
as the light from the formation faded,
the silhouette slowly solidified into an unimpressive... raven?
"Just this?"
Su Lun watched as the formation's light disappeared, he and the bird eyeing each other.
However, unlike common ravens, this one had a black halo above its head.
When Su Lun encountered a creature he didn't recognize, he naturally cast an All-knowing Eye at it.
Then, his expression immediately turned very strange.
[Herald of Death]
Detailed Explanation: A second-level juvenile, mythical species; also known as 'Bennu Bird,' a mythical harbinger of the god of death, a guide of the underworld, capable of foretelling death; this bird feeds on decay and death energy, its existence sustained as long as death energy persists; contains some information beyond normal understanding;
Seeing the identification information of the bird, Su Lun realized he had summoned a very "special" being.
But unexpectedly, this bird seemed harmless, right?
With a shift of his gaze and noticing the details indicating "information beyond normal understanding," Su Lun immediately knew the bird had an extraordinary origin.
He instantly thought, "Could it be because my understanding of the Death Law is relatively profound?"
At that moment, probably because of the commotion caused by necromancy, Yuta also opened her eyes.
She looked at the bird Su Lun had summoned and then glanced at the traces of the Spirit Communion Array on the ground, asking in a peculiar tone, "Mr. Su Lun, did you summon this?"
"Hmm."
Su Lun nodded.
He was also curious about what use the bird might have.
The Dalu Tribe has traditions many human civilizations are unaware of, and he thought Yuta might know something, so he asked, "This is the 'Herald of Death.' Yuta, do you know what it's used for?"
On hearing this, Yuta indeed got startled, "The Herald of Death? The legendary guide of the underworld?"
She then looked at the crow, blinked, and perked up immediately.
Su Lun became more curious: "You know about it?"
Yuta nodded, but then said dubiously: "Legend has it that the 'Herald of Death' is the transformed soul of a deity. They often accompany the god of death, are proficient in the Law of Death, indestructible, and embody ominous and deathly omens. But... the birds of legend don't usually look like this."
"This is a juvenile. It should look different when it grows up."
Su Lun thought about it and said.
Without the All-knowing Eye, he would not have guessed this crow with a halo on its head to be a mythical species.
Since what Yuta said matched the information identified, he further inquired, "What specific use does this bird have?"
No sooner had he asked than the foolish bird "cawed" in a sound that seemed to express its discontent with his dismissive tone.
Yuta solemnly said, "It's the legendary bird of death, unseen by the living. It is said that those who have seen it... will be guided by it to the underworld."
"..."
Su Lun also twitched at the words, thinking if this meant the bird was a harbinger of sending people off?
This bird was truly a damned omen...
If it weren't for a sort of telepathy with the contracted creature, knowing it was harmless to him, on hearing Yuta's words, he'd definitely have turned hostile and sent it back through necromancy immediately.
Yuta also felt her words might sound ill-omened, so she changed her phrase, "It's just a legend, after all, nobody has really seen it."
Su Lun instantly felt uneasy, "So, does that mean this bird is actually useless?"
He had thought to try summoning a necrotic creature.
But it turned out it was the much-hyped "mythical species" that seemed less useful than even a hellhound?
No sooner had he made this comment, the crow "cawed" again, displaying even more dissatisfaction.
Su Lun's eye twitched, realizing this bird was not low in intelligence.
Just as he spoke, the body of the crow in front of him suddenly dissolved into a mass of black mist.
Just as Su Lun was puzzled, the creature abruptly perched on his shoulder.
"Oh..."
He softly exclaimed, immediately sensing something and was greatly surprised, "Does this bird also understand the Law of Death?"
What surprised Su Lun even more was that the bird's grasp of the Law of Death was even higher than his?
It was like being next to a fireplace, where you could clearly feel the flame was hotter than your own body temperature!
It seemed to have no offensive capabilities, but for Su Lun, it was extremely valuable.
It could help him enhance his understanding of the Law of Death!
Last time, it took one death to let Su Lun find a shortcut to understand a part of the Law of Death.
Such a method was not available a second time.
Su Lun did not want a second time either.
Now with the bird by his side, he distinctly felt a slight increase in understanding...
"Found a treasure!"
Su Lun was joyful inside, his expression immediately changing.
Seemingly sensing something, the crow on his shoulder "cawed" again, probably in a triumphant response.
At this moment, as Su Lun looked at the pitch-black bird, the more he looked the more appealing it became.
Hmm... truly delightful!

chapters.title: Chapter 267 - 266: Skeleton Burrows
chapters.content:
After discovering that the "Harbinger of Death" was a treasure, Su Lun spent the entire night studying its additional functions.
He thought that even in the necromantic realm of another dimension, such a "mythical species" creature would be very rare.
Fearing he might not be able to summon it again, Su Lun coaxed and deceived, planning to sign a Blood Covenant.
The crow seemed not to mind, happily agreeing after consuming two pieces of rotting flesh.
Although they couldn't communicate directly, as a contracted creature, they could simply share thoughts.
The intelligence of crows is already high, but this "Harbinger of Death" was clearly much smarter than the average crow.
Moreover, Su Lun had also gleaned some experience in raising crows, making their communication relatively smooth.
Soon, he figured out the other two abilities of the bird — "resurrection" and "shared vision."
After signing the Blood Covenant, Su Lun discovered his soul had mysteriously connected with the bird.
Channeling the power of the contract was like a video call, enabling him to see through the eyes of the Harbinger of Death.
After multiple trials, he had mastered this new ability.
Before, he wasn't very confident about hunting the "Heartstealer Demon," but with the crow, his confidence increased significantly.
It was a true "undying species" creature. Even if its body was shattered, as long as the death energy remained, it could resurrect next to the Contractor and reassemble itself.
In other words, it was an indestructible "unmanned scout."
The cost of using this ability was minimal, just a piece of tasty rotting flesh, and the crow would be willing to work for him.
Moreover, Su Lun also learned some legends about this bird from Yuta.
The ancient necromancy books recorded that the Harbinger of Death served as a messenger between the netherworld and other planes of existence. It was one of the most coveted contract pets for top-tier necromancers. They often accompanied real deities of death, devouring death energies. While consuming rotting flesh, they could occasionally gain certain abilities of the corpses, condensing death laws and becoming stronger over time.
This innate ability was somewhat similar to that of a "Death Reaper," one consuming corpses and the other souls. Weak earlier on but stronger later.
Su Lun also guessed this was why he managed to summon this mythical breed.
He was excited to see what the bird would be like when fully matured.
However, the only problem was that the bird was very picky about its food.
Su Lun tried feeding it various types of meat, but discovered it only ate the "Cursed Flesh" from their spoil of war.
Other meats, it wouldn't even glance at.
This also meant Su Lun couldn't keep it with him for long.
After all, there wasn't much of that type of meat, and once it was gone, it was gone.
After trying for a few hours and keeping some meat as a reserve, he released the necromancy spell and sent the crow back to the other dimension.
He thought about keeping the bird around for a long time once he found enough high-quality rotting flesh as "feed."
...
The next morning, sunlight entered the cave.
After resting and preparing, Su Lun and Yuta continued on their journey.
The Grey Wolf Tribe was about a day or two further north, located near the "Cursed Valley."
This area was a forbidden place for the Dalu tribe, and Yuta had never been there, only having heard the elders in the tribe mention it.
By the evening of the next day, the two had arrived at a place called the "Blood Fog Swamp."
They found their way obscured by swathes of blood-red mist.
Yuta looked at the rudimentary beast-skin map and pointed in a direction, saying, "Not far northwest of the swamp is the place where our ancestors encountered the 'Heartstealer Demon.' There should be a skull-shaped grotto there..."
"Hmm."
Su Lun nodded.
Looking at the blood fog ahead, he didn't plan to probe it with his body.
In the current situation, the crow came in handy.
Thinking this, he pinched his sorcerer's seals, and the five-pointed star formation lit up, summoning a black crow.
After feeding it a piece of rotting flesh, the Harbinger of Death took to the sky.
A flicker passed through Su Lun's right eye, and immediately, the view from the crow appeared.
The blood fog of the swamp was confusing, but because the mist was heavy, it covered just tens of meters above the ground.
The crow flew up a hundred meters, and the view instantly opened up.
Then, he indeed spotted the skull-shaped grotto Yuta had mentioned.
Su Lun softly exclaimed, "Found it!"
But he was simultaneously shocked, "Could it really be a fossilized skull? How enormous must that creature be?"
Perhaps it was not clear from the ground, but from the sky, it was unmistakable.
It looked like a human skull, with sockets and the shape of a mouth - a gray-white grotto that didn't seem naturally formed, but more like the rotting body of a humanoid lying on the ground.
It was truly massive, with just the two eye sockets measuring several meters in diameter.
Just as he intended to take a closer look, at that moment, a dark shadow swooped across the sky, a flying creature of unknown species, swallowing the crow in one gulp.
The vision cut off, and a swirl of dark mist on Su Lun's shoulder condensed into a crow again.
Su Lun fed it another piece of rotting flesh, replenishing its death energy.
He frowned slightly and said to Yuta beside him, "Let's go. Be careful."
Yuta nodded, "Hmm."
The Cursed Valley stretched from the north to the south, and members of the Lurian Judgment Legion had entered from the northern entrance.
The "Heartstealer Demon" Su Lun was looking for was in the south, unavoidable through this swampy terrain.
With the fog obscuring their sight and limiting visibility, the two moved slowly.
In the swamp, there were giant crocodiles dozens of meters long, black water snakes capable of swallowing buffalo whole, and tyrant leeches that could drain a person dry without them even noticing... and countless venomous insects.
Everywhere in the swamp was fraught with danger.
Had it been earlier, Su Lun would definitely have been extremely cautious with every step he took.
But now he held a black umbrella in his hand, his perception expanded several times, allowing him to easily sense and avoid the powerful beasts hidden in the mud and thus avoid unnecessary battles.
Yuta, being a Druid, was also proficient in various methods of pest control and draining miasma.
There was also the unmanned aerial vehicle, a black crow.
With the cooperation of the two and the bird, they managed to proceed quite smoothly.
Once they confirmed the direction of the cave, they quickly arrived in the nearby area.
....
Su Lun and his companion didn't rashly approach but chose a safe place to first observe the situation.
Near the cave, they discovered some human adventurers' scattered equipment and belongings.
It appeared that humans had passed through here recently.
Without any signs of battle, it was highly likely that they had become food for some creature.
The heart-stealing demon was a subterranean creature, usually not appearing on the surface, let alone in daylight.
However, its psychic tentacles could extend very far.
The elders of the Dalu clan had once passed by here, controlled without their knowledge, and then walked into the cave to become food for the monster.
This was also the terrifying aspect of the heart-stealing demon.
Had it been earlier, Su Lun would probably have slowly approached the Skull Grotto to test it out.
But if so, once discovered, they would have had to fight face-to-face with the puppets enslaved by the heart-stealing demon. Then continue fighting all the way down to find its main body.
This plan was not impossible, but it was a last resort
The situation inside the grotto was unclear,
Su Lun did not think that a creature as intelligent and evil as the heart-stealing demon would be without means of escape. Even if they could defeat those psychic puppets, the chances of catching it would be very low after signaling their presence.
Moreover, Su Lun did not know how many puppets it had, what species they were, or what rank they were...
Now with the black crow, it was much easier.
Su Lun didn't need to probe himself; remote control would suffice.
He released the black crow, which flew along the way and entered the skull-shaped cave.
Upon looking, the cave unveiled another world.
The black crow flew deeper into the tortuous underground, and then they saw a village.
"There are so many lizardmen?"
Light flickered in Su Lun's eyes as he discerned the shadows active in the glow of the magic crystals, clearly a bustling village.
The creatures were covered in scales with long tails, and he identified them as the subterranean species "lizardmen".
The black crow perched on a cliff rock, carefully observing everything inside the cave.
This lizardmen tribe had at least five to six hundred individuals.
Indeed, not rushing in was the right choice.
Lizardmen of the fourth rank grow horns on their heads, which are easy to distinguish.
Su Lun saw several horned individuals among the group of lizardmen. The horns were not long, meaning there was no particularly troublesome presence.
Moreover, upon closer examination, some of the lizardmen were wearing human leather armors and armors
They looked like the equipment of a "slave hunter team".
The meat they were sharing was that of human and Dalu tribesmen!
The scene was exceptionally bloody.
The devoured corpses had their skulls uniformly punctured with a hole, their brains sucked out.
Seeing this, Su Lun immediately realized that the heart-stealing demon must be here!
Such evil creatures, their favorite food was the brain matter of living beings.
"To think it controlled an entire tribe of lizardmen as its food supply..."
Su Lun's gaze turned slightly solemn.
If they went in head-on, he would first have to fight with these five to six hundred lizardmen.
Whether they could win was not certain,
Even if they truly won, the heart-stealing demon would probably take the opportunity to escape.
After watching for a while, the black crow did not spot any likely fifth-rank presences and continued deeper into the cave.
Not far in, it discovered a cave emitting a green luminescence.
The source of the green light was a pool in the cave, filled with fist-sized spheres.
The crow's gaze shifted and immediately saw several humans standing there, expressionless. Opposite them, a monster three meters tall with an ugly face and meaty tentacles piercing through human skulls and greedily sucking the brains out.
And those humans being used as "food" didn't resist or struggle until their death.
"It's here!"
Outside the cave, Su Lun saw this scene and immediately determined that this was the heart-stealing demon he was looking for!
Just then, perhaps due to the noise made by the black crow entering, the tentacled monster suddenly looked up, and an invisible shockwave hit them.
Su Lun only felt the scene before his eyes freeze like a paused tape, then it collapsed instantly.
When he looked again, the black crow had reformed on his shoulder.
....
The Reaper had died twice in a short time, suffering severe loss of its death essence.
Hard to recover with only food, Su Lun sent it back to the other realm.
Watching the Reaper revive again, Yuta asked, "How is it, is the Heart Stealer in the burrow?"
Su Lun nodded his head, "It is."
While speaking, the frown of contemplation never left his face.
Seeing him like this, Yuta was slightly worried, "Is it going to be very tricky?"
After all, passed down from the ancestors, it was a tremendously horrifying creature, and she also harbored an innate fear. The fifth-order elder who initially encountered it had barely escaped with his life. After so many years, that Heart Stealer might have grown even stronger.
"It is somewhat tricky. The burrow is large and complex, and there's also a tribe of about six hundred lizardmen..."
Su Lun explained the situation truthfully while strategizing inside his mind.
Having thought of something, his tone shifted, adding, "But I have some assurance."
The lifespan of a Heart Stealer is much longer than that of humans.
But accordingly, their advancement is very slow.
Therefore, Su Lun judged that this Heart Stealer was about the same as before, at most a fourth-order.
This was deduced from the fact that the strongest among those lizardmen was only fourth-order.
If the Heart Stealer were of a higher order, it would definitely have stronger "spiritual puppets."
Moreover, Su Lun had discovered a "significant advantage!"
The pool emitting a fluorescent light that the black crow saw in the burrow was the Heart Stealer's hatching pool!
Having thoroughly researched this evil species beforehand, Su Lun knew that Heart Stealers were hermaphrodites; they produce eggs in their brains and then place them in the hatching pool, a process that consumes a lot of vital essence.
Therefore, during the hatching process, when the creature is at its weakest in its life, its combat capability often drops a rank.
If it was a fourth-order lord Heart Stealer, then in its hatching state, it might have only the strength of a normal fourth-order, or even third-order.
This was the best opportunity to strike!
Having heard Su Lun's explanation, Yuta knew that he always deliberated deeply before acting and didn't say much, only asking, "What are you going to do then? There are six to seven hundred lizardmen; if we really fight, the creature might escape..."
"No! I'm not going in through the cave entrance!"
Su Lun shook his head, his eyes intense, and said, "That creature won't leave the hatching pool; I'll teleport directly there. Its physical combat strength isn't strong. As long as I withstand the mental attacks and kill it quickly, there should be no large issue."
Listening, Yuta also felt this was the best plan, "Can I help with anything?"
Su Lun had noticed the slick slime on the walls of the burrow previously and thought, "Not ruling out that the Heart Stealer might have other tricks. If I can't kill it or encounter other dangers, I might not have enough time to escape. Then you can tear the space scroll, and I can teleport directly to it!"
As he spoke, he handed Yuta a space scroll.
Having been inspired by necromancy the night before, he had thought of another method of escape.
That is "reverse necromancy."
By pre-sealing the energy needed for space displacement and the Blood Covenant in the scroll, Su Lun could teleport quickly and precisely without even forming sorcerer's seals.
This method allowed for even faster and further displacement.
Although he had meticulously calculated over and again, confirming the speed-kill plan had a success rate of over ninety percent, he was not careless.
This was the last line of insurance.
Yuta nodded her head.
....
Having prepared everything, Su Lun was ready to make his move.
The space inside the burrow was not large, and the mechanized armor was not agile enough. He didn't plan to wear it, but he took off the helmet made of invigorating alloy to wear. He also draped on a Gold-Patterned Cloak and held a human-skin black umbrella possessed by a vengeful spirit.
With these multiple levels of insurance, unless the Heart Stealer was sixth-order, it couldn't possibly control him.
Everything prepared, Su Lun suddenly disengaged his Eight-Arm Spider Spear implant and teleported to the entrance of the Skull Grotto.
Almost simultaneously, a wave of spiritual power swept over.
"Was I discovered after all!"
Su Lun was not surprised, dropped a few signal transmitters, then performed the Spatial Technique again.
Having previously explored the terrain inside the cavern, he teleported directly to a deep spot in the cave. At the same moment, he immediately heard dense footsteps converging towards him.
It was clearly the lizardmen controlled by the Heart Stealer advancing to kill.
Su Lun had no intention of getting entangled; he dropped two transmitters, then teleported again.
His vision in the dark was extremely good, and even in the dimly lit mines, he had no trouble seeing.
The scene before him changed again, and he appeared immediately in the cavern with the green fluorescent light that he had seen before.
In his Soul Perception, a very strong soul fire appeared right in front of Su Lun!
Then he and the creature with tendrils all over its face faced off in a stare-down.
The creature, apparently seeing "Spatial Magic" for the first time, was greatly surprised by this sudden appearance of an enemy.
Its reaction was not slow, with a glare, an invisible shockwave surged directly towards him.
"Soul Shock!"
Su Lun's pupils constricted slightly; even with the helmet and holding the black umbrella, the sensation like being hit with a blunt object at the back of his head made his expression flicker momentarily.
This kind of mental shockwave, if faced by a fifth-order professional, would likely succumb to it.
But Su Lun was overjoyed as he loosened his grip on the communicator in his hand.
Having endured that first wave of the attack meant, as anticipated, that the Heartstealer Demon had little effect on him!
The monster's attack was also very skilled, its tendrils lashed out like spikes towards his eye sockets while causing a soul shock.
This was its only close-range combat method.
A cold gleam flashed in Su Lun's eyes as he dodged the tendrils like lightning.
Without hesitation, he took out a chessboard, intending to directly draw the Heartstealer Demon into the space within the chessboard. However, unexpectedly, the chessboard space malfunctioned for the first time; ripples formed around the demon's body, which rendered it immune to the beam.
At this moment, a large number of lizardmen had already appeared in the cave tunnel behind him.
The Heartstealer Demon, clearly aware of its weakness in close combat, had summoned spirit puppets.
"A spiritual power barrier? Or is it immune because its spiritual power is stronger than mine..."
A flash of doubt passed through Su Lun's mind, but he wasn't flustered at all and changed his approach, ready to face off directly.
With both hands forming magician's seals, he softly exclaimed, "Mystic Art: Puppet Theater!"
Just then, densely packed threads appeared throughout the cave, a scroll unrolled, and dozens of puppets manifested, blocking the cave entrance and stopping the aggressively advancing lizardmen.
As for himself, he charged without hesitation towards the main body of the Heartstealer Demon.
In such a confined space, Su Lun, a Puppet Master, wasn't afraid of numerous monsters.
The Heartstealer Demon continued to release waves of spiritual shock, and Su Lun felt his consciousness becoming increasingly foggy.
What was worse, from deep within the cave suddenly came a sound like a giant serpent moving through the cave.
"Are there other spirit puppets?"
Su Lun faintly realized what the slime on the walls indicated.
Although he didn't know what kind of creature was coming, he knew he had to quickly kill the Heartstealer Demon in front of him. The sorcerer's seals transformed again: "Thread Control Secret Technique: Cocoon!"
Masses of threads, like a spider web, sealed off the various cave entrances.
The Heartstealer Demon had nowhere to retreat.
Su Lun charged violently, his whole body covered in cold flames, and his eight-armed spear jabbed around the creature.
He immediately confirmed that the physical combat strength of this monster was very weak, merely on the level of an ordinary tier-three magical beast!
Once Su Lun got close, the demon had no escape and was instantly punctured with several bloody holes.
Just as Su Lun was about to finish it off in a flurry of success, the sudden sound of friction was already next to his ear.
The wall made of threads was not thick enough; a pink tendril like a blind shot suddenly pierced through the wall and charged at Su Lun like lightning.
Before it hit, the tip of the pink tendril suddenly burst open like a flower, turning into a giant mouth full of sharp teeth, and the muscle that resembled the throat pulsed, spewing out a foul and pungent acid.
Su Lun's eyes hardened, and he immediately recognized the origin of this creature.
[Hell's Barb Beast]
Details: A tier-four lord level hellish creature with extremely strong vitality. Its skin has high tensile strength, can spit corrosive poison, and its tendrils move very quickly, extending up to a kilometer; low intelligence; highly sensitive to biological scents, it hunts all detectable living creatures;
"Another legendary creature from hell..."
Seeing this, Su Lun felt a great sense of misfortune.
What was in front of him was just one of its advancing tendrils, with its main body underground, followed by countless other tendrils!
Listening to the dense sounds of friction, it was clear that the tendril beast had surrounded the entire cave.
Su Lun was also grateful that he had chosen to teleport and attack swiftly. Otherwise, even if he had killed all the lizardmen in a direct, hard confrontation, this creature would still have lethally ambushed him.
This dense cave was not naturally formed but was the moving channel for the creature's tendrils. With this creature around, even if several tier-five beings came, they would likely die here!
The toughness of a tier-four lord beast's flesh was not to be underestimated; it would be very difficult to cut through!
Without wasting any opportunity to try, Su Lun performed a Flash to avoid the first tendril, without any hesitation, controlled the animated corpse to swing the Black Scythe, and directly severed one tendril.
A large amount of yellow-green corrosive fluid flowed out, filling the cave with a burning-like stench.
Meanwhile, his own body also controlled the spear to puncture seven or eight bloody holes in the Heartstealer Demon's body.
Instantly, the previously intense spiritual impact vanished.
It was a quick kill planned in advance; except for the Barb Beast, everything was within expectations.
"Success!"
Su Lun was delighted inside, and without taking another look, he immediately stored the dead body of the Heartstealer Demon into his storage space.
Once the Heartstealer Demon died, the lizardmen were momentarily dazed.
Although the Barb Beast had lost control, its predatory instinct was still active. Tendrils densely popped out in the tunnel, instantly devouring a large number of lizardmen.
The Black Scythe had already severed three tendrils, but had no effect whatever on its body hidden underground.
This creature, with its enormously terrifying body, was not something Su Lun hoped to kill.
He glanced at the brightly glowing incubation tanks.
Those fist-sized orbs were naturally the eggs of the Heartstealer Demon.
He took out a glass container and poured them into it.
At the same time, he pressed the communicator.
Upon taking another look, the surroundings had changed and Su Lun had already appeared on the surface.
"Quick, run!"
Without time to explain, Su Lun took Yuta and started running.
Behind them, near the entrance of the Skull Grotto, thousands of pink tendrils sprouted like bamboo shoots after rain, swaying in the wind like seaweed...

chapters.title: Chapter 268 - 267: Prosthetic Gear - Psychic Tentacles
chapters.content:
Su Lun dragged Yuta along in a frantic run, appearing somewhat disheveled, yet the expression of relief on his face was evident.
Thanks to his preparedness, the plan for a swift kill had ultimately encountered no mishaps.
Having successfully hunted a fourth-tier Heart-Stealing Demon Lord, his third-tier alchemy implant finally had a purpose, achieving his main goal for venturing to the northern ice fields.
Su Lun was naturally in high spirits.
The Hell Thorn Beast going berserk behind them was somewhat baffling, but since the monster's main body was virtually incapable of teleportation, as long as the tentacles emerging from the ground were avoided, there was no danger at all.
With an evacuation route prepared in advance, Su Lun and Yuta managed to flee the swamp with ease.
They reached a dense forest and stopped there.
The ground was firm, making it easy to detect any monster tentacles that might reach them.
....
Both panting heavily, Yuta caught Su Lun's relieved expression and asked with a smile, "Was it a success?"
"Mm!"
Su Lun nodded.
Without the information from the Dalu clan or Yuta accompanying him on this adventure, he wouldn't have stumbled upon such a grand opportunity.
The Heart-Stealing Demon's brain was the ideal material for the "Spiritual Tentacles." He was very much looking forward to seeing the astonishing effects of the successfully crafted implant. This type of implant crafting was quite special, as it had to be done while the brain cells of the Heart-Stealing Demon were not fully dead.
Not daring to delay, he said, "Let's go, we need to find a safe place. I must craft the implant as soon as possible."
Yuta flashed a grin revealing her sharp little fangs and replied, "Okay."
Soon, the two found a wolf den cave.
Yuta scouted nearby and found no signs of higher-tier magical beasts.
Only then did Su Lun relax.
As the main ingredient was difficult to find, the crafting process of the implant could not be disturbed; there was no room for error.
Yuta also realized how important this implant was to Su Lun, so she didn't interfere and instead helped keep watch outside the cave with great care.
With the corpse still fresh, Su Lun didn't dare waste more time. He took out the body of the Heart-Stealing Demon.
Since the other ingredients were prepared beforehand, he could start anytime.
Once the Eight-armed Spider Lance was unfolded, the melting array needed for crafting the implant appeared on the ground.
The fiery Hexagram Array lit up, and Su Lun, holding a scalpel, precisely removed the complete brain of the Heart-Stealing Demon. Following the crafting sequence he knew by heart, he commenced creating the implant.
Before long, the vast cave was flickering with intermittent orange-red glows.
This crafting session lasted three days and three nights.
....
Spiritual implants were quite niche and their creation was particularly troublesome, requiring a significant expenditure of experience.
Fortunately, Su Lun was proficient in all areas of forging, allowing him to craft on his own.
Now multitasking, he was doing the work of seven or eight people single-handedly.
He was a master craftsman, rune master, enchantment master, and material analysis master... a one-man team equal to an entire large forging group.
His strong cognitive control abilities also allowed him to methodically shape the implant into form.
Finally, on the evening of the third day,
Su Lun looked at the finished product floating within the alchemical glow and smiled contentedly.
It was a semi-transparent tentacle implant resembling a jellyfish.
"Spiritual Tentacles of the Heart-Stealing Demon"
Description: Dark gold quality alchemy implant; third-tier containment value rated S+ or above, fourth-tier A+, spiritual power not less than 750, mutation rate less than 5%; upon fusion, one gains the ability of spiritual tentacles, +88 spell resistance to mental spells, +70% mental strength, +10% mental spell penetration, +22% nerve reaction speed, +5% intelligence, +0.3% brain domain development;
"Tsk tsk... the fusion requirements are quite demanding," Su Lun said as he assessed the properties of the implant, visibly delighted.
Some attributes of the finished implant were even better than he had anticipated.
Mental resistance and spell penetration were exceedingly practical enhancements for his magical abilities. With a successful fusion of the implant, the mental control effect he aimed for would be even more perfect.
Initially, Su Lun had merely sought to obtain a third-tier mental leader monster, but unexpectedly encountered a fourth-tier Heart-Stealing Demon.
Under normal circumstances, he would have needed to downgrade the materials, crafting the implant into a "Gold Quality" or "Silver Quality," to ensure that he wouldn't mutate after fusion.
But since his own spiritual power had mutated, granting him an extraordinarily high spiritual power, he was able to meet the fusion criteria that would normally only be satisfying at the fourth tier.
It turned out to be a blessing in disguise.
Su Lun looked at the freshly forged "Psychic Tendrils" implant, meditated to recover some dark spiritual power for a while, and then immediately began the integration process.
He arranged the Hexagram Alchemy Array, placed pure crystals on the six points of the star, and drew mystic patterns with a secret mixture of mercury and lizard powder, which was then activated with the blood of a heart-stealing demon to energize the entire formation.
Standing at the center of the Hexagram Array, Su Lun held the implant in his hand and murmured, "By the law of equivalent exchange of all things, praise the glory of the original creator, and witness the miracle of creation through alchemy..."
A fiery radiance enveloped the whole cave as the wondrous fusion reaction proceeded violently.
This was not Su Lun's first time integrating an implant; his mind was as still as water. His body had enough endurance that even though the process of merging a psychic implant made him drowsy, he successfully completed it smoothly.
Two hours later, the light from the fusion formation completely dissipated, and Su Lun abruptly opened his eyes from his meditation, "It's done!"
As expected, he had perfectly integrated the tendril implant.
Eager to test his new ability, Su Lun formed the sorcerer's seals with both hands and shouted, "Implant·Release!"
In the next instant, a white hexagram array lit up beneath his feet, and Su Lun immediately felt the difference.
The "Psychic Tendrils" were intangible, invisible to the naked eye.
Yet, in the mirror image, Su Lun saw a faint white halo lingering all around his body.
He also clearly sensed them—the "invisible tendrils" he could control at will, much like his own war spear!
The tendrils could be thick or thin, and Su Lun focused a strand of spiritual power into the shape of a hand. Then, he tried to pick up a stone from the ground.
A miraculous scene unfolded before his eyes.
The stone, as if defying gravity, slowly rose from the ground and floated up before his face.
"Psychic manipulation of objects..."
Su Lun's gaze slightly narrowed.
Although it felt effortful, his eyes couldn't hide the delight within them.
"Psychic object manipulation" is vastly different from "Qi object manipulation."
Because Qi is a substance, any professional with a slight understanding of controlling Qi would more or less know some techniques, such as Sword Qi, Blade Qi, shockwaves...
But psychic power is imperceptible, escaping the normal methods of human detection.
To put it simply, it ignores obstacles and cannot be blocked!
While Qi leaves traces that can be blocked, psychic power leaves no trace to follow.
If harnessed well, this ability could become an invisible, deadly weapon.
But for now, it was obviously just the beginning.
After handling the stone for a while, trying to move it farther away, Su Lun immediately felt as if a child was lifting a weight of a thousand catties, unable to bear the burden.
With a clang, the stone fell uncontrollably to the ground.
Even so, Su Lun was very satisfied.
Once his psychic power grew stronger in the future, his ability to move objects through the air would also strengthen.
However, object manipulation was just an additional feature of the "Psychic Tendrils" implant.
What Su Lun was truly concerned about was the tendrils' ability to control living beings!
...
"Sigh... I've never been so eager before."
Su Lun's gaze was profound as he whispered to himself, "I hope it works..."
He formed the sorcerer's seals with his hands once more and released the "Thousand Threads" implant.
This time, strands of pale blue threads floated from his hands.
Su Lun tried to attach the psychic tendrils to the threads, and they spread out smoothly without difficulty.
"As I thought, this idea is feasible!"
Ecstatic with his successful attempt, Su Lun was overjoyed.
He had previously tried and found that a witch's hair was an excellent conductor for psychic power.
Thinking that the combination of hair and tendrils would manifest significant qualitative change, he was proven right—he succeeded!
It was like installing wires on a battery; he could now send the "electric current" to much farther places.
This would instantly increase the control distance of his psychic tendrils by several times, even dozens of times!
And they became controllable, penetrating, precise, and stable, not prone to dissipation!
This was also one of the most important reasons why he had to choose this type of armor advancement.
Armor not only needs to be a perfect match with the profession, but the combination of multiple performances can also stack up the practical efficiency, creating some ingenious uses.
This is why those ancient families all have their own inherited set of exclusive "advancement sequences." Centuries of trial and error have yielded combinations of armor and professional materials that can maximize combat power.
While his thoughts were still spinning in his mind, Su Lun immediately planned to put it to the test.
At that moment, he took out a zombie from his storage space.
Then, he carefully attached a silk thread with spiritual power tentacles to the neurons in the back of the zombie's brain.
He had already thoroughly read the various human anatomy diaries of the forensic doctor Gerald, and now he had a nearly perfect grasp of the human nervous system.
It was at the instant when the spiritual tentacles touched the neurons, Su Lun immediately felt as though he was holding a "Transformer" in his hand, which he could manipulate at will.
He sent a "control signal" to lift an arm from his mind, and the zombie indeed raised an arm!
Moreover, the attempt was not at all clumsy despite being his first try; he adeptly tried various manipulations.
Because three days ago, when Su Lun killed the Heart Snatcher, he also conveniently stripped the monster's soul of the [Experience with Spiritual Tentacle Control]!
The ability of the Heart Snatcher to control any intelligent creature was a mythological bloodline talent. Although Su Lun couldn't strip away the talent, he had stripped its usage experience.
He had ample proficiency in how to control it.
The zombie in front of him began to perform various complex movements under Su Lun's control.
The movements were as fluid as those of a living person, with no stiffness at all.
It didn't look at all like the previous "marionette" style!
If one isn't enough, then two, three, four...
Su Lun didn't even need to move his fingers to control the threads like before, those zombies perfectly executed the same actions as the "control signals" he sent.
Neural signals precisely activated muscles, commanding the flow of spiritual power...
"This is when my Puppeteer profession truly takes off," Su Lun thought, with a tremble in his gaze.
Seeing this, he truly realized the viability of the path he had planned for his future.
One thread to control one zombie, the controllability of the puppet army was finally arriving!
Although it seemed like he controlled zombies the same way as before, the essence was worlds apart.
Previously it was physical control; he needed to manipulate hundreds of threads to control the zombies, making them perform the actions he envisioned. But because it was external control, some actions were greatly limited, and the agility of the zombies was poor.
Now, with only one thread, he can truly bring the zombies to life.
As flexible as his own shadow.
This also meant that Su Lun freed up a large number of threads and could now control even more puppets!
This also meant that the zombies wielding scythes were no longer stiff, making it more likely to hit their targets; controlling the cumbersome combat Mecha no longer required countless threads—one thread could solve it, and it was more agile...
....
Before long, the entire cave was filled with various blue-skinned zombies.
They were like a party, some dancing, some keeping the beat, some...
Although there was only one living person, the scene was exceptionally lively.
Amidst such a terrifying scene, Su Lun took pleasure in it.
He gradually became proficient with the control techniques of the new armor [Spiritual Tentacles], and he also discovered some shortcomings.
For example, the control distance—signals would become less accurate the further they were sent.
Another point was that before, he felt the "multi-focus" ability was sufficient, but now he suddenly found it lacking!
One thread could control one zombie, but no matter how divided his attention, it couldn't outnumber the threads.
However, these were not major issues; his spiritual power would enhance over time, and these aspects would gradually improve.
"Tsk tsk..."
Su Lun was very pleased with his new ability.
However, strong as the spiritual tentacles were, they also had a problem—they could only control living bodies.
Right now, other than controlling the zombie with the black scythe, his other puppets were wooden, and some mechanical.
In the short term, these spiritual tentacles wouldn't be able to exert their full combat power.
"When can I get Duke Raphael's 'Nerve-Mechanical Technology' and create a mechanical puppet army; only then will I truly soar..."
Su Lun looked at the mechanical battle armor before him, which was easily controlled with an animated corpse stuffed inside, and felt a sense of wonder.
Now that the first step had been taken, the future held great promise.
....
Soon, Su Lun retracted the animated corpse horde, and for the first time in three days, he finally stepped out of the cave.
As he walked out of the soundproof barrier, he heard some noises, which came from Yuta, who was on alert up in the trees.
Yuta clearly noticed him too and excitedly jumped down from the tree.
She looked at Su Lun, whose face was adorned with joy, "Mr. Su Lun, have you successfully integrated the battle gear?"
"Yes."
Su Lun nodded and then turned to her, "You have worked hard these past few days."
Yuta gave a graceful smile, not minding that she had been in the tree for several days at all.
She didn't bring up that topic but instead expressed concern, "You seem to be in a good mood, Mr. Su Lun. Is the new battle gear really powerful?"
She was actually quite curious what battle gear refined from a monster like the "Heart Stealer" would be like since even the clan leaders thought it was a helplessly evil creature.
"Want to see it?"
Su Lun smiled and suddenly thought of something as he lifted his hand slightly.
Yuta blinked with curiosity, thinking she might see something.
But suddenly, to her surprise, she found that her hand had involuntarily lifted?
Su Lun certainly didn't dare to try it directly on Yuta's main nerve, but instead, he had cut off the nerve signal transmission in her arm, so as to control her to make the motion of raising her arm.
"Eh..."
Yuta let out a soft gasp and immediately understood, deeply shocked, "This is the monster's control ability!"
"Mhm."
Su Lun nodded with a smile and also asked, "How does it feel?"
Yuta thought for a moment and said, "I can sense the intrusion of spiritual power. Um... I should be able to break free of the control with willpower."
"Mhm."
Su Lun nodded thoughtfully.
The Heart Stealer had a mythic bloodline talent allowing it to control many spiritual puppets.
Even though Su Lun himself was human and could reach the same level of Spiritual Power, the effect would still vastly differ.
He estimated that at full power, he could control professionals of the third, or even the fourth, tier.
But the extent of this control was another question.
The target's spiritual power, willpower, equipment, and other factors would all impact the controlling effect.
The more dispersed the control was, the more difficult it would be to maintain.
A lot of practice was needed to determine specific data.
However, it was not a major issue.
Su Lun had intended to use this battle gear to control animated corpses anyway.
....
When Su Lun came out, it was already dusk, and neither of them planned to travel through the forest at night.
