Upon hearing this, Barrett's brows visibly knitted together, his voice cold as he said, "Oh? And these are the last words you wish to speak before death?"
Though he skirted the issue, deep down he was well aware that the young man behind the crow-beaked mask was likely telling the truth.
"..."
Su Lun noticed a hint of struggle in his microexpressions, there was evidently still a shred of conscience left.
But it was a choice between loyalty to the Lurian Royal Family and conscience, and only one could be chosen.
The struggle in Barrett's eyes lasted only a moment before it faded away.
At his level of power, his mind was very firm, and decisions were made in an instant.
Avoiding the topic, he coldly asked, "Cortes has been infiltrating the military intelligence department for so many years, now risking exposure just to save your life. I am more curious, whom do you work for?"
"..."
Realizing the implication of his words, Su Lun immediately sensed danger.
The adversary clearly acknowledged his point but did not pursue the topic of the seal, meaning he had chosen "loyalty."
Su Lun naturally would not betray Katya.
Even in death, he couldn't bring himself to commit such a betrayal.
Besides, speaking wouldn't change the situation.
Knowing there was no room for negotiation, he held no illusions in his heart, his hands moved with lightning speed, forming the sorcerer's seals.
"Hmph!"
Seeing this, Barrett snorted coldly.
His reaction was quick, as he launched a punch straight forward!
With the fist that twisted space, one punch struck Su Lun's chest, sending him flying backward into a spatial fissure.
....
The scenery shifted around him, and Su Lun had passed through the wall to appear behind it.
But this time, the wall was not shattered.
No pursuers, the immediate danger was resolved.
Su Lun also let out a sigh of relief and couldn't help but spit out a mouthful of bloody phlegm with a "pfft" from the bitterness at his chest.
Assessing his own injuries, they weren't too severe, he chuckled self-deprecatingly, "Heh, that guy still showed some mercy..."
That last punch from Barrett was clearly held back, probably out of a sense of "duty."
One punch forced him into this conspicuously problematic space, not pursuing him to the end, leaving him a sliver of a chance at life.
Su Lun looked at the labyrinth that was similar in style to the one before, his gaze filled with solemnity.
For the Black Crow to issue a death warning, the situation was certainly not as simple as it seemed.
"Could this timeline be before the Burial God Ritual again? What chaos..."
Su Lun, seeing no tree roots in the underground palace, thought of something.
He observed his surroundings, trying to locate any potentially "lethal dangers."
Suddenly, the wolf claw amulet hanging from his chest momentarily grew warm.
Su Lun was overcome with a surge of strong empathetic sorrow.
Listening closely, it seemed to be Yuta's sobbing?
The sound was initially intermittent, then gradually became clearer.
"Mr. Su Lun, I'm sorry, I'm late..."
"But... how could you be dead..."
"..."
Hearing this, Su Lun felt a chill run down his spine as if he had seen a ghost.
I'm alive and well, how could I be dead?
And where is Yuta?

chapters.title: Chapter 278 - 277 Notes I Wrote for Myself
chapters.content:
"Mr. Su Lun, I'm sorry I'm late..."
Yuta's sorrowful, self-blaming sobs echoed through the space.
Su Lun's first reaction was that he was hallucinating.
He immediately tried various methods, only to find that he wasn't in an illusion, nor was he influenced by some special spiritual power field.
The attribute panel was all normal.
Right now, everything was very real.
Meanwhile, the sobbing sounds continued next to his ear.
"I came as soon as I received the communication signal, but you..."
Su Lun confirmed it was Yuta's voice.
She was crying very sadly.
Am I dead?
Su Lun, listening to the content of the words, realized something: Yuta must have seen his body, which was why she was crying so sadly.
But there seemed to be a missing link, which made the scene very eerie.
I am clearly alive and well, so why would "Yuta" say I am dead?
Moreover, where is the voice coming from?
....
Su Lun's thoughts in his mind started to whirl.
Assumption 1: I am hearing hallucinations (mostly ruled out)
Assumption 2: It's really Yuta, or some other 'Yuta' speaking (✓)
He instantly had an analysis of the current situation in his mind.
Having ruled out the first assumption, his thoughts automatically went to complete the possible logical links of the second assumption.
The Wolf Fang Amulet hanging from Su Lun's neck was Yuta's actual Wolf Fang, which had some kind of spiritual connection with her.
Su Lun didn't know exactly why he could hear Yuta's cross-dimensional conversation, but it probably was because of this Wolf Fang.
So, Yuta was here and had seen his own body?
But why can I hear her speak yet not see her?
Su Lun ruled out that he was in a spirit state.
He considered that it might be something similar to a "phonograph"?
No!
A chaotic timeline?
Su Lun suddenly realized something.
If I'm not dead now, could there be a possibility: Yuta might have seen "the future me"?
....
Yuta was just in this corridor, maybe even right in front of his eyes!
But not on the same timeline.
Was it after I had died?
Some special force allowed him to hear her cries across time and space.
"So... will I be trapped here to die?"
Su Lun concluded, his gaze immediately becoming serious.
Black crows give warnings, so this space must definitely have some "lethal danger."
There's no doubt about that.
Wasn't Yuta supposed to be outside, so how could she appear in the cursed space?
A thought flashed through Su Lun's mind; he instantly understood that probably she had sneaked in for Dalu tribe's inheritance. This silly girl probably didn't tell him because she was afraid he would worry.
But now was not the time to think about that.
If another timeline's version of himself had really died, Su Lun had to quickly figure out the cause of his death, perhaps now he could avoid it and survive.
He tried calling out to Yuta, discovered she couldn't hear him speak.
"Yuta" saw his body, the best way was to ask her directly.
It would also confirm if his guess was correct.
But since the voice could only travel one way, how could he let her know?
Su Lun saw the Wolf Fang Amulet on his chest, an idea flashed through his mind, and he immediately thought of a method.
"That's it! Since my body is still here, it means the Wolf Fang Amulet is also still there..."
Su Lun's eyes whirled, he pulled off the amulet, then carved a line of small characters on it: "I am Su Lun, Yuta I can hear you speak. If you see this, tell me what you saw."
He quickly carved these characters, his eyes sparkling with anticipation.
If things were as he guessed, Yuta in a later timeline saw his body.
Then, she should be able to see the characters on this Wolf Fang!
.....
The moment he finished carving the characters, the sobbing sound by his ear suddenly stopped!
The Yuta on the other side seemed stunned for a moment, then cried with joy, "Mr. Su Lun, is it really you?"
Su Lun, hearing those words, felt elated: My guess wasn't wrong!
He hurriedly carved another sentence on the Wolf Fang: "It's me! Can you see the characters on the ground?"
The Wolf Fang being quite small, he wrote some more words on the ground: "I might have fallen into a space with a chaotic timeline. Describe in detail what exactly happened and what you saw."
Just after writing those two sentences, indeed, Yuta's response came through the air, "I can see them! I'm sorry, Mr. Su Lun, I didn't heed your advice and sneaked into the cursed space..."
Indeed, just as Su Lun thought, Miss Druid had sneaked in.
She continued, "I suddenly received a communication from you through the device specifying a route, asking me to come over... I came and then I saw you... no, a corpse. The corpse had the Wolf Fang Amulet I gave you, and then I thought it was you."
"..."
Su Lun, hearing this, his mind went blank again.
Was it my corpse that contacted Yuta through the communicator, leading her to this place?
What is this situation, resurrecting a body?
...
Su Lun hastily carved another line on the ground: "What else?"
The Yuta from another dimension saw the characters on the ground, obviously also hoping it wasn't Su Lun's body.
But after looking carefully, she probably suspected she was caught in an illusion or something else, her tone becoming uncertain, "It's a mummy, appears like a natural aged death, very old, very old. It seems... it truly is your body. Mr. Su Lun, are you a spirit now?"
A naturally dead mummy?
Su Lun heard this, his gaze shifting.
It meant, he didn't die from an accident but was trapped until he died of old age?
No!
If there was no misfortune, Su Lun felt he should at least have a hundred and eighty years of lifespan left.
Moreover, the food supply simply couldn't support dying of natural aging.
Doubts flashed through in succession.
Su Lun's mind raced at high speed.
He rapidly ruled out some incorrect logic.
Thus the only possibility left was, there was some strange "chaotic timeline" in this space, "letting" "himself" age and die in a moment?
....
Su Lun thought about this, and immediately realized the problem was serious.
Since he was not dead now, he thought about saving himself.
"If it is really my own body, since I have tried to contact Yuta using the communicator, I must have considered something. I definitely wouldn't let her take the risk... even, 'I' was very aware that I would die."
Su Lun knew himself too well.
He quickly thought of something and carved another line: "Yuta, check the storage ring on the body, and see if there is something like a notebook."
As he spoke, he also took out a notebook and began to record everything that was happening now.
Perception can be deceived, and even memories can be distorted, erased, or altered by some extraordinary powers.
But a "poor pen" won't!
This clumsy method sometimes works wonders in certain situations.
And Su Lun himself had the habit of taking notes, and he thought that if he were trapped in a maze, he would definitely leave notes to crack it!
Once the line was carved, Yuta's response indeed came through the air, "Eh... there really is one!"
Su Lun felt like he had grasped the key point and immediately carved: "Read what is on there."
....
"Yuta, you received the communication, which means you definitely sneaked in here, you... When you see this notebook, it means that the delayed communicator I made could withstand the erosion of more than two hundred years. Tsk tsk, the craftsmanship is pretty good... In the last moment before deciding to step out of this space, I recalled my life. Although it was brief, it was splendid. I have no regrets about coming here. I'm writing this because I've left some things for you, and some words... Oh, don't be sad. I quite liked you."
Su Lun was surprised to hear Yuta reading these words from the notebook; he wondered if he had heard wrong.
Such grandiose words, were they really written by "himself"?
Could it be that he thought about these things in a desperate situation?
In the air, Yuta's reading turned into uncontrollable sobbing.
She continued reading.
"You must want to know what happened, why I died here. If nothing unexpected occurred, am I a dried-up corpse by now? Hopefully, it wouldn't scare you. If I'm not wrong, I've fallen into a 'time distortion zone' where the time ratio to the outside world is 1:3700. That is, if I spend one day in this space, the equivalent of ten years passes in the normal space. And I've been here for over twenty days, so if I were to go out, my body would instantly age two hundred years. Thus, what you see should be a corpse that died of old age."
That was it!
Upon hearing this, Su Lun immediately realized how the events had unfolded.
He abruptly looked around the cursed space and blurted out a curse.
In this place, one day equals ten years outside?
No wonder people are trapped to death.
But at the same time, he grew hopeful.
Because according to his character, he would definitely not wait to die but would find ways to decipher this space.
And moreover, since he had left notes, it meant there must be a detailed process to break it!
...
Yuta continued reading: "I explored every part of the maze and found a way to break it, but it was too late. I spent more than twenty days in this space to break it, and after coming out, it was more than two hundred years. If I had stayed hidden in the space, I could have lived much longer. But when I came out, I would turn into nothing but dust... I never lived a life of compromise. So, I decided to come out. This is how I chose to leave this world, with peace of mind. Don't be sad. By the time you read this note, it simply proves that everything I predicted was right. If you encounter similar trouble, you can also use this method to get out."
Yuta likely had tears streaming down her cheeks, touched by the emotion across time and space, and she began to cry, "Wah... Mr. Su Lun, please don't die..."
But in Su Lun's heart, there was a different feeling, hearing this he immediately conceived hope.
He carved on the ground, urging Yuta to read everything out loud, afraid the signal might suddenly cut off: "We are not dead yet. But if you don't finish reading, I might really die."
"I" spent over twenty days figuring out how to get out last time, and another attempt would likely take no less time.
One day equals ten years; he couldn't afford that.
Fortunately, fate did not play tricks on Su Lun, nor did any accidents happen.
Yuta too realized the seriousness and kept reading the contents of the notebook.
"The notes towards the end are a bit chaotic, but I've organized them for your ease of reading. If you need, you might want to see what I did at the end of my life. Nevertheless, this 'time distortion zone' is quite interesting... this world is wonderful, it's just a pity life is too short. I understood some of the meaning of death, it seems I also grasped some of the meaning of life... give me some more time, I could possibly make my life even more splendid, letting the world know I was here... but, there's no more maybe."
"..."
The rest of the content was mostly the methods to break the "time distortion zone."
Su Lun carefully recorded on the notebook the method "he" had left behind to break the region.
He had also seen "himself" take too many detours.
Because he had to grope through the entire maze to find clues to get out, he had wasted too much time.
Now, all he needed to do was follow the strategy in "his" notebook, bypassing the exploration process.
Soon after, Su Lun finished understanding the method and determined in his heart, "So this is how to get out..."
With this strategy, he was confident that he could handle it in half a day at most!
....
The notebook read up to this point; logically, there shouldn't have been any important content left.
What needed to be explained had been explained, and everything that needed to be said had been said.
However, in the last few pages, Yuta read a few sentences that caused Su Lun's just-calmed heart to suddenly feel a chill down his spine.
"It feels like I have forgotten something very important, which is astonishing. How could I have done such a thing? Was there something guiding me to do it? Or did I see something that made me think this way?"
"Huh... Why did I write down these words? Was it due to some external influence? I am sure that there is something else in this space, something beyond my understanding!"
When Su Lun heard these sentences that sounded like "mad ravings," his hair instantly stood on end.
He looked around at the dim space and couldn't help but think, "Could it be there is some other terrifying presence here besides the chaos in time?"
Fear stems from the unknown.
Since he had written those words in the notebook, then that thing must certainly exist.
Some kind of monster?
The chaotic rules of the God Burial Ground?
Or something else...?
Su Lun's eyebrows were tightly furrowed.
At least that "thing" hadn't killed his other self in that timeline, it had only caused him to forget something, which seemed not too serious?
However, there was one more sentence at the end of the notebook.
"I wanted to understand the source of this feeling, so I carefully searched through all the items I was carrying, item by item... Then, I finally noticed something unusual. That is: I couldn't remember how I got the [Replica of the Original Rune]!"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun suddenly became very alarmed.
He instantaneously felt a chill down his spine as if a ghost had blown on the back of his neck.
A deep, terrifying thought.
Su Lun was surprised to find that he actually couldn't remember how he had acquired that [Replica of the Original Rune]!
"I remember, it seemed like I had fallen under a monster's illusion, and I then scraped it off from the stone wall?"
Su Lun saw the [Thousand Illusions Demon Crystal] in his storage space, recalling the origin of the rune.
Just like that?
Scraped off from a mural?
It seemed logically sound.
But it felt like it shouldn't have been that easy.
Su Lun immediately realized why he had written that sentence in the notebook.
It was then he discovered, his memory was missing something.
Not much, but crucial.
Within this cursed space, there might be a "special presence" that his subjective consciousness had forgotten or otherwise overlooked.
....
However, now was not the time to ponder this question in detail.
Time in this space passed so shockingly fast that every second wasted was a massive loss of life.
Su Lun engraved the last sentence on the ground: "I am going to break the space now, Yuta, be careful."
A gentle response also came through the air: "Okay. Mr. Su Lun, you... be careful too."

chapters.title: Chapter 279 - 278: Arm, Crown, Hourglass
chapters.content:
Su Lun recorded everything he was now preparing to do in his notebook.
Because he was not certain that even with his own "strategy," other variables wouldn't occur.
After all, what if this wasn't the first time he "died" in this space?
If there was a first time, there could be a second, a third...
And possibly countless times.
The "himself" who left the notes might not necessarily have succeeded on his first try.
It could be the only version of him that the current timeline's self could see.
Making detailed notes might, perhaps, provide a lifeline to another self in another timeline.
With this thought, his mind started to infinitely nest.
"No wonder it's one of the supreme laws of the 'Time Law,' it truly is the most elusive..."
Su Lun gathered his increasingly complex thoughts; failing to understand them, he stopped trying to figure them out. He merely sighed, acknowledging that the chaotic laws of the God Burial Ground were indeed beyond mortal comprehension.
.....
"According to the route in the notes, there's no need to waste time revisiting most places in this maze..."
The route was now etched into Su Lun's memory.
First thing to do to get out, he had to find the black iron coffin in the Giant's Hall of Valor.
"The notes mentioned that the item sealed within the coffin is likely one of the energy sources of this cursed space. It might also be one of the objectives of the Royal Legion..."
Su Lun carefully walked through the corridor.
Another timeline's self had already meticulously explored almost every corner of this underground palace and had clearly recorded the dangers and mechanisms.
Su Lun didn't have to explore blindly this time, which saved him a lot of effort.
He had some concerns that the actual situation might differ from the notes, but these were dispelled as soon as he stepped into the maze.
Since the notes were left by "himself," as soon as Su Lun saw those words and matched them with the surroundings, he could immediately grasp the meaning of the sentences and flawlessly understand what he needed to do next.
Following the route map, he easily avoided the monsters inside the underground maze.
Soon, he arrived once again at the previously visited "Giant's Hall of Valor."
The timeline should be before the Burial God Ritual, and the place now didn't have its usual entangled roots.
However, there were many spatial rifts.
And now, there were more drifting ghosts.
These ghosts were no longer normal spirits; they had become mutated spectral aberrations.
The iron, silver, and even gold monstrosities were everywhere.
"The notes said to wear a Mirror Organization cloak, open a black umbrella and a phantom of death, and be careful to avoid the spatial rift at ten o'clock, because there will be monsters there..."
Su Lun looked at the detailed reference on his notes, planning not to miss any step.
One could imagine that the "past self" had probably spent a lot of time here, trying many times cautiously to find this correct route closer to the coffin.
After observing that the environment matched the description completely, he then donned the cloak, opened the Human Skin Umbrella, and a phantom with a scythe appeared behind him before he proceeded.
After making these preparations, the drifting spectral creatures in the sky seemed not to notice an extra living person here, and continued drifting on their own.
Su Lun let out a long sigh of relief.
Shortly, he easily approached the coffin.
However, getting close wasn't easy.
The black iron coffin wasn't chained yet, but from several meters away, Su Lun felt an overwhelming pressure.
Mysterious, evil, ancient, terrifying, indescribable...
Previously seen from afar, and now up close, these unclear auras hit him like a tsunami.
It was as if an invisible force was repelling all foreign objects from nearing the coffin; with every step Su Lun took, he had to withstand tremendous pressure.
"This necromantic aura really is exaggerated... If one hadn't grasped the law of death, it would probably be difficult even to get close to this coffin."
Su Lun took thirty-five steps, stopping at the position noted in his notebook.
He also clearly saw the ghastly bas-relief on the coffin, the carvings depicted a story of the Hundred-Armed Giant King battling a horde of demons.
In the end, the dimensions collapsed, the Hundred-Armed Giant King perished, and his enormous body was torn apart, shattered into countless pieces scattered everywhere.
Su Lun gazed at the mural, his gaze sharpening, and then he noted down something more in his notebook.
The Massacre Demon-Subduing Coffin
Detailed explanation: A coffin of fallen corruption iron forged from the underworld. It contains seals and prohibitions beyond your understanding;
The notes did not mention the possibility of moving the coffin, and Su Lun did not dare make any unnecessary attempts.
Following the method described in the notes, he took out a space scroll and released a mechanical Mecha.
Then he controlled the Mecha to forcefully open the coffin.
Yes, sufficiently cautious, this was very much in his style.
This was one of the most dangerous places in the underground maze, where the "past him" had hesitated due to concerns about triggering something dangerous, saving it until the end to take the risk and explore.
In the end, it also caused a substantial waste of time.
The mechanical Mecha moved forward, the necromantic essence rapidly corroding the runes and plating on the Mecha, and the living corpses inside instantly decayed into ashes.
Luckily, the witch's hair could forcibly be reconnected, and Su Lun intermittently controlled it, finally managing to get the Mecha close to the coffin.
The steam boiler accumulated power and, just before a shutdown, pushed open the heavy lid of the coffin.
The "click" "click" of metal friction sounded like a hellish demon grinding its teeth, making one's hair stand on end.
As the coffin was gradually opened, revealing just a slit, Su Lun saw a coffinful of "black water."
He had been curious about what exactly was inside the coffin, but now he already knew from the notes that it contained the arm of a Hundred-Armed Giant King.
Only, its rank... was a bit preposterously high.
Just a segment of a corpse's arm exerted such a daunting presence, one could only imagine how fearsome it was when alive.
Moreover, it wasn't black water in the coffin, but rather a dense mist-like liquid of necromantic essence.
Originally, knowing the steps to opening the coffin, he could have reacted more quickly.
But Su Lun, in order not to cause unexpected changes, did not do so. He counted a seven-second interval in his heart, then took out a transparent bandage, which was indeed the "Oz's Iceman's Binding Cloth."
This thing was genuinely an "enchanted object," used for invisibility on ordinary days and seldom useful otherwise.
But now, using it to wrap a corpse could not have been more suitable, as it could contain that surge of violent corpse energy.
The water inside the coffin was very black, yet very clear.
From where Su Lun stood, he could clearly see the jet-black, crystal-clear, sinuous arm.
Just the arm alone was nearly three meters long, visibly brimming with power.
The identification showed, as well as a name, just a row of question marks.
[The Arm of the Hundred-Armed Giant King Briareus]
Detailed explanation: ???
The laws exuding from this corpse's arm were terrifying, and even from such a distance, Su Lun felt the special reaction of corpse dissolution forming a terrifying dark energy, like a black hole with the ability to tear through everything.
This object, Su Lun's current elemental barrier, definitely did not have the qualification to approach.
To touch it physically felt like trying to grab a red-hot iron barehanded, just thinking about it made his scalp tingle.
He lifted his hand, and a transparent cloth strip floated over, slithering like a snake into the coffin.
The exceptional material of the burial cloth remained completely unaffected by the necromantic essence, swiftly wrapping the arm tightly like a mummy.
The moment the energy was completely sealed, Su Lun immediately felt a relief in his scalp, the oppressive atmosphere around him instantly cleared.
The feeling of walking on a knife's edge finally dissipated.
He walked over and took the transparent object out of the coffin.
He did not know what use the Giant King's arm would have in the future, but now it had a big use.
Only by obtaining this arm could he pick up another crucial tool for breaking through the maze located elsewhere in the labyrinth.
Su Lun also collected the liquid of gathered necromantic essence in the coffin using a container.
Though he was not a necromancer, for the "Herald of Death," it was the best nourishment.
Such pure necromantic essence could not be found anywhere else.
....
After securing the arm, Su Lun then unfurled the black umbrella.
He looked at the "Solar Eclipse" totem on his chest that had turned slightly pale, it also seemed it wouldn't last much longer.
Without any accidents, the totem would completely collapse after this.
Su Lun formed a sorcerer's seal with both hands and softly chanted, "Nightfall Domain · Release!"
Although unaware of whether this move had any significance in breaking through the space, since the "past him" had done so, he did not hesitate much and followed suit.
The black curtain spread from under the Human Skin Umbrella, the runes on the umbrella lighting up with a brilliant golden radiance.
Instantly, as if attracted by something immense, the drifting spirits of the Giant tribe rushed towards the black umbrella like moths to a flame.
Then Su Lun watched as each spirit dove into the pool like stones splashing water, disappearing without a trace.
Before long, the vast space had become empty.
The Human Skin Umbrella, having absorbed the souls of the wronged, shone with a glossy black luster.
With the addition of a few thousand giant clan spirits, the efficacy of the Human Skin Umbrella likely increased by about twenty percent.
This is the power of a growth-capable cursed object.
Su Lun put away the black umbrella.
Gazing at the empty Hall of Valor, a thought suddenly flashed through his mind, "Could it be that there are no spirits in the Hall of Valor on the other timeline because I absorbed all the resentful spirits here?"
At the same time, he thought, "So, if I go out now, will there be an arm inside the coffin those people from the Royal Legion opened, or not?"
With this thought, his face immediately showed contemplation.
Like Schrödinger's arm, no one knows whether there is one in the coffin or not before opening it.
The "Time Law" in Su Lun's mind became increasingly complex, seemingly tangled with quantum mechanics.
....
Su Lun didn't figure it out, nor did he ponder further.
He left the Hall of Valor and, following the route outlined in his notebook, navigated through twists and turns until he arrived at a massive stone door within the labyrinth.
His past self had tried countless methods at this stone door to no avail.
It was only later discovered that specific Earth lineage was needed to open it.
And since the giant clan worshipped the Earth Mother Goddess, a special prohibition for opening this stone door was: the giant clan.
Now, Su Lun was the only living person in the entire underground palace, so that severed arm finally came into use.
Touching it with the arm, the stone door easily pushed open.
The space inside was unsurprisingly vast.
It was like a treasury of the giant clan.
But everything inside had been moved out, with just a few scattered weapons and shields that had all decayed.
In the most conspicuous place, there remained an item, a gold crown nearly a meter in diameter.
[Giant King's Crown]
Detail: A legend states that only kings of the giant clan are entitled to wear this crown, which contains inheritance messages that only their clan can comprehend;
Su Lun grabbed the crown and immediately left.
He circumvented a monster's lair and climbed the "Endless Dark Staircase", eventually returning to the great hall of the giant city.
This was the final step in breaking this bizarre timeline.
....
The last step written in the notebook was: "I discovered that the statue of the Hundred-Armed Giant King in this timeline does not have a crown, and once returned to its place, it is possible to move the positions of the giant guard statues. Then, I found my deduction completely correct, this is the key to breaking the 'Time Paradox'..."
Su Lun looked at the sculpture of the Hundred-Armed Giant on the throne, his gaze somewhat complex.
After a moment, he muttered with great emotion, "How much effort did another timeline's me have to put in to find out that placing the crown back would be the method to break the space?"
Without the notebook, he felt it would take tend days or even a fortnight to find the right method.
Without any delay, Su Lun went up and placed the crown on the head of the stone sculpture. He respectfully bowed, "My apologies, Your Majesty, the Giant King, for the disturbance."
Saying this, he went down and began moving thirty-six guard statues.
Having come this far, even without the notebook, Su Lun knew what to do next.
He had carefully observed when entering before; the positions of these thirty-six guard statues differed from those in the other timeline.
But they could not be moved.
Only the king has the right to command them, and the Giant King's statue had to wear the crown.
Su Lun moved ten of the statues, positioning them according to the timeline in his memory.
He speculated that there might be other ways to arrange these statues, corresponding to other timelines.
It was somewhat like the pointers on a clock, specific positions indicating specific times.
If it were a puzzle game, Su Lun would certainly be curious about other solutions.
But now, he just wanted to return to his original timeline, to make it out alive.
Suddenly after all the moving, Su Lun put the statues in their place.
Then, in this great hall, a gilded hourglass, over half a meter tall, suddenly appeared. The transparent glass container was filled with some pale blue crystalline sand.
[Sand of Time]
Detailed Explanation: A god-tier material containing the Law of Time, serving as the core of this time domain's restrictions;
Watching the hourglass, Su Lun exhaled deeply.
He had finally cracked this special space with a chaotic timeline.
He stored away the crown and the hourglass, then walked out of the suddenly appearing "Door of Time".
The surroundings changed, and Su Lun found himself back in the corridor from before.
....
"Huh... Yuta is not here? Could the timeline still be incorrect?"
Su Lun didn't see his own body, nor did he see Yuta, which he found somewhat odd.
But then it occurred to him, "In this timeline I am not dead, which means my body won't appear. If my body doesn't appear, Yuta wouldn't receive the communication signal to follow up, right?"
Su Lun checked and saw that the engraving on his wolf fang necklace was still intact.
However, the scenario of conversing with Yuta seemed as if it had never happened.
Had the chaotic timeline resulted in different parallel spaces?
Then, were there other timelines where "Su Lun" also existed?
His mind was suddenly flooded with many complex thoughts.
Time and space, intertwined together.
Such thoughts gave him a headache.
"Regardless, at least I'm alive," he said.
Su Lun felt that his current advancement couldn't comprehend such profound matters, and he didn't force himself to understand everything.
He set aside those complicated thoughts and focused on the present.
"So, that means Yuta is in this space, not far from here?"
Su Lun's brow slightly furrowed.
In this cursed space fraught with dangers, he naturally worried about Miss Druid.
He took out his communicator, hoping to make contact.
But at that moment, his hand touched the notebook in his bag.
He thought it over and decided to write down the experiences he had not yet had the chance to record.
However, when he opened it, he was stunned.
The notes detailing his journey so far were all fine.
But at the end,
there were a few sentences, Su Lun's own notes, but he had absolutely no recollection of having written them.
'I only realized when I opened the notebook that I seemed to have forgotten something very important. Even the thought of it only came to me after seeing the notes. I realized there might be some kind of existence beyond our understanding...'
'Huh... Why would I write these sentences?'
'It seems some mysterious force made me forget about its existence. Even as I write to remind myself, this action might also be forgotten.'
'...'
Reading these sentences gave Su Lun goosebumps.
This wasn't the first time he had discovered that he'd forgotten something.
And the last page contained one last bizarre sentence: 'Could the strength of the Daru tribe have been insufficient to stop the powerful deep-sea giant, with a "third party" involved too?'
Su Lun immediately realized that something had happened in the "Time Anomaly" that he had now forgotten.
"A third party? What exactly did I see in the space that led me to this conclusion?"
Su Lun's expression became very strange.
As he hadn't yet been caused to forget by that mysterious power, he quickly recorded his current thoughts in the notebook: 'That mysterious force of forgetfulness seems to pose no threat to me, but it's irresistible. It's as if "it" does not want to be remembered, does not want its existence to be noticed.'
Unable to make sense of it after thinking for a long time, Su Lun closed the notebook.
Deciding to consult Mr. Jing later.
....
But just after closing the notebook, the frown on Su Lun's face immediately relaxed, as though he had completely disregarded the contents of the notes.
He tapped his head as if he had spaced out for a moment, "Huh... What was I doing just now? Oh, right, contacting Yuta..."
With this thought, he took out his communicator and asked, "Yuta, where are you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 280 - 280: 279
chapters.content:
The communicator signal had not been sent out long before Yuta responded.
That Miss Druid was indeed here.
Before long, Su Lun found Yuta in the underground palace.
After asking, Su Lun realized his worries were unnecessary.
Compared to his own near-death experiences, Yuta's experience seemed almost like a cheat code.
As soon as she entered, she immediately felt the guidance and protection of the Dalu ancestors' spirits, and then she smoothly entered deep into the cursed space.
Even more miraculously, as she walked, she casually picked up a "Holy Artifact."
Then, without encountering any danger, she just waited until Su Lun contacted her.
....
"So, you just casually picked up the Dalu Tribe's Holy Artifact, 'Dagda's Magic Cauldron', outside?"
Su Lun looked at the golden object hovering next to Yuta, his expression somewhat incredulous.
This cursed space was indeed full of treasures.
But every artifact he obtained had involved great risk to his life.
And Yuta had just casually "picked up" such treasure?
The cauldron, resembling both an incense burner and a vessel, contained a brilliantly colorful liquid: red, yellow, blue, green... all sorts of elements mixed together, looking like a stewed rainbow, extremely beautiful.
'Dagda's Magic Cauldron'
Description: One of the four sacred artifacts of the Dalu Tribe, a divine weapon gifted by the god of nature; enhances the user's affinity for natural elements, magic recovery, and spell penetration gains a huge boost; the holder gains powerful elemental spell comprehension and is protected by a natural barrier; it is a vessel to communicate with the gods, devout believers can sense their presence; only those with natural divine power can wield it;
The attributes identified were impressive, allowing manipulation of almost all elements, truly a 'Divine Artifact' for elemental mages.
However, similarly, only the natural divine power of the Dalu could wield it, enviable to others.
What surprised Su Lun even more was that due to the magic pot at her side, the aura of this Miss Druid felt very special to him, ethereal and elusive.
"Hmm."
Yuta nodded timidly.
She looked like a little girl scared of getting scolded for a wrongdoing, and she glanced stealthily at Su Lun, cautiously said, "I'm sorry, Mr. Su Lun, I shouldn't have kept it from you. But this is our closest approach to our ancestors yet, I... I couldn't give up."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun shook his head with a smile.
The 'Four Sacred Artifacts' indeed held extraordinary significance for the Dalu Tribe, concerning their heritage and survival of the tribe.
The ancestors of the Dalu Tribe had been searching for the artifacts for centuries, a desperation that could make them forsake their lives.
Su Lun naturally understood Yuta's decision.
Besides, his survival owed much to Yuta's fortune.
Although no communication through space had occurred in this timeline, had Yuta not entered, the previous "Time Warp Domain" might have been a dead end.
"Next time, you can just tell me straight," he said.
Su Lun knew why Yuta had kept it from him and didn't say much, gently stroking her cheek.
After a pause, he asked again, "So, where are you planning to go now?"
Seeing that Su Lun didn't blame her for the trouble, Yuta blinked and seemed very happy.
She smiled, showing her little fangs, and replied, "I plan to see what those humans are up to. Our ancestor's heroic spirit left instructions that we must not let them break the seals here."
Hearing this, Su Lun also nodded, "Hmm."
He was naturally interested in seeing for himself too.
Though previously he had been frantically chased by the sixth-order 'Ferocious Beast' Barrett, he was now incredibly familiar with the underground palace, confident that even if pursued again, he could escape using the terrain.
Besides, with that Holy Artifact in Yuta's hands, her combat power was not simple.
....
Su Lun switched to a different route, quietly approaching the Hall of Valor.
From a distance, he released a black crow and carefully flew over.
In his view, the Hall of Valor was littered with toxic beast carcasses, and the perilous incense burner had disappeared.
It seemed that the previous tactic of diverting disaster had caused some trouble for the Sacred Legion, but not much.
The legion had dwindled to about a hundred people left.
Su Lun and Yuta didn't go out and hid deep in the corridor instead.
The breaking of the curse space was nearing its end, and it was no longer something they could stop.
What they had to do was wait for an opportunity.
"There shouldn't be an arm in that coffin. Those guys will probably get quite a shock when they see it..."
The reflection in Su Lun's left eye showed the scene the black crow had seen; he watched as those people used the decoder to unlock the rune iron chains binding the coffin and were carefully opening it.
He had once been up close to that black coffin and knew what state it should have originally been in. The absence of oozing necromantic aura had already confirmed that the arm was definitely not inside.
So, the cause of the past indeed led to the present effect.
Theoretically, it is possible for two identical items to appear in the same curse space.
But the condition is that there is enough energy.
However, when something like the "Hundred-Armed Giant King's arm" that supported the curse space as the "source of the curse" was taken away, it would no longer be possible to have enough curse source to form a second one.
As expected.
The 'click' 'click' of metallic friction echoed through the Hall of Valor, and a man in a trench coat cautiously approached.
Then, from the gap, they saw the empty inside of the coffin.
Immediately afterward, an incredible shout came from the corridor, "How can it be empty?! The seal hasn't been broken; how can the contents be gone?"
However, before those people could think more, the surrounding scenery began to collapse.
Those people had disrupted the seal, breaking the stability that maintained the entire curse space, and naturally, the space started to fall apart.
...
Su Lun watched as the environment around him transformed; they were also in an underground labyrinth.
But clearly, the roots around were more lush.
Previously, the scene in the curse space was probably from a timeline five hundred years ago; now, this place was the real world. The air was moist and humid, the corridor was filled with broken collapses, and thick moss covered the stone slabs.
The gray elm trees that had grown for five hundred years compressed and deformed this relic, wrapping it more tightly.
However, having escaped that perilous cursed space was also a good thing.
Su Lun's gaze swept around, reassessing the place where they were now.
The change in environment meant that the escape route planned earlier was different now.
But just then, Yuta's expression turned very strange, as if... she had been greatly shocked, looking somewhat out of her body.
Su Lun thought she had encountered some problem and asked, "What's wrong with you, Yuta?"
Hearing the query, Yuta seemed to snap back from her trance.
"Mr. Su Lun! I...I..."
In an instant, her face showed uncontrollable ecstasy, and she excitedly said, "I...I think I can sense the call of the great nature god!"
It had been five hundred years since the Dalu tribe had broken the inheritance after that battle, and they had not felt the call of a deity since then.
Now, she had felt it!
"You felt the call of the spirit of nature?"
Su Lun thought of the previously identified information and was not too surprised.
He saw Yuta's eyes suddenly glimmer with tears and genuinely felt happy for her.
At least, her risking her life to come here had finally paid off.
However, being happy was one thing; Su Lun's gaze involuntarily shifted towards the magic cauldron floating beside her.
He felt that Yuta's aura was becoming more and more ethereal, like being on the fourth, fifth, or even sixth level, and kept rising higher...
"It's really exaggerated..."
Su Lun smiled, squinting his eyes, and muttered to himself.
This is one difference between an alchemist and a follower of the gods.
The strength of an alchemist comes entirely from oneself, alchemical implants and cultivation, which can only be difficultly improved step by step;
The main source of a follower's strength, however, comes from the deities.
The magic spells of the followers are more like prayers, hoping for a response from the deities, just like the Dalu tribe's spells that all go "Great God of Nature above, please grant me the power of the XX element...".
Without the response of the divine, the power of the spell would be very minor.
But once responded to, or blessed by a deity, the power was hard to predict.
....
Yuta sensed the call of the nature god and knelt on the ground with devout faith, muttering arcane incantations in the Dalu language.
A miraculous scene then unfolded before their eyes.
From those twisted roots, small green dots, like fireflies, suddenly emerged, floating around Yuta before merging into her body.
Gradually, her body emitted a soft glow, and a surge of magic power spilled out.
The magic power gradually responded to the Holy Artifact "Dagda's Magic Cauldron" near her. The cauldron radiated a prismatic sheen, as splendid colored ribbons of light flourished around it, lighting up the entire corridor.
Su Lun had not expected such a grand disturbance and hastily shielded the surrounding energy fluctuations.
Yuta was enveloped in a green orb of light, her aura growing stronger. Her clothes dissolved into specks that vanished into the air, and her skin subtly shifted from a wheatish to a translucent amber hue, purified of all impurities. The force of nature seemed to cleanse her marrow and purify her veins.
Watching the power that obviously did not belong to Yuta, Su Lun grew more curious and guessed something, "Is this the way of the Dalu tribe's heritage? Divinely bestowed power, truly a miraculous method."
The phenomenon lasted for about a quarter of an hour, after which the glow around Yuta slowly began to fade. Her skin tone also gradually reverted to normal.
But the green light did not completely disappear, instead remaining on her skin, leaving behind arcane red totems. They appeared on her forehead, cheeks, chest, back, abdomen... all over her body.
Being close to her, Su Lun did not need to avoid any intimacy.
He curiously looked at the red totems on Yuta's bare body.
He had a "Sun Eclipse" totem himself, but compared to these red totems, the difference was stark.
"This is a very high-level totem... Seventh tier? Eighth tier? Ninth tier?"
Su Lun pondered for a moment.
Though the totem mysticism of the Dalu tribe and the runes of alchemy were different systems, some aspects were common.
He could naturally see that Yuta's totem wielded a kind of authority originating from the very principles of laws.
At that moment, Yuta suddenly opened her eyes, an authority similar to that of a wolf king reigning supreme radiated from her.
This aura was so intense that Su Lun furrowed his brows.
But an instant later, Yuta controlled the leaking aura, returning to her gentle demeanor.
Looking at Su Lun excitedly, her voice trembled, "Mr. Su Lun, I... I felt the presence of the great nature god!"
"Hmm."
Having witnessed the entire process, Su Lun naturally guessed that the power likely originated from a deity.
He smiled and nodded, sharing Yuta's happiness.
"Our Dalu tribe now has hope!"
Unable to contain her joy, Yuta spread her arms and leaped over.
Su Lun wrapped his arms around her warm and soft body, giving her a warm hug.
Yuta buried her head in Su Lun's shoulder, crying with happiness, repeatedly muttering, "The gods have not abandoned our Dalu tribe, we... our Dalu tribe is saved!"
The centuries-old despair of the entire tribe was finally fully released at this moment.
The darkest times had passed, and dawn's first light appeared.
Su Lun gently stroked her smooth back, softly saying, "Yes, things will get better."
Sensing the call of the nature god was a great boon for Yuta.
However, now was clearly not the time for that discussion.
Just as Yuta was still immersed in her joy and excitement, suddenly, a fierce argument erupted from deep within the corridor.
Having been monitoring the group through a raven, Su Lun knew exactly what had happened.
It seemed that there was some conflict within Rue's group.
....
In the real world, the Giant's Hall of Valor was buried deep within the roots, and the ground where the coffins had been placed, previously marked by a nine-pointed star, had become a seemingly bottomless pit.
Even through the raven's vision, the sight of that black hole gave Su Lun a chilling sensation.
It was as if the hole connected to the underworld itself, carrying with it evil, destruction, and unspeakable horrors.
At that moment, two groups of people were confronting each other beside the pit.
On one side were three men in trench coats, and on the other was the less than one hundred-strong Sacred Judgment Legion.
Barrett, the legion commander Su Lun had met earlier, seemed to have changed his mind about continuing to decipher the seal.
"General Barrett, do you understand what you are doing? You are defying a military order!"
"No, I am not trying to prevent the seal from being unlocked. But after all, the northern ice field is too far from the Imperial Capital, and there may be some discrepancies in the transmission of intelligence. What I mean is, Her Majesty might not be aware of the situation of this relic... I think the most prudent method is to first preserve this relic, and after I personally report back to the Imperial Capital, we can excavate the relic later."
"Hmph! Are you questioning our military intelligence!"
"No... no no. Yegel, we are old friends, you know I did not mean to question your military intelligence. But I think the situation may involve some factors we currently cannot control, so it is appropriate to be cautious."
"You...!"
"..."
Su Lun watched as the argument between the two parties became increasingly intense and sighed in relief, "It seems that my previous words were not entirely in vain; Barrett still has some conscience. Otherwise, if these guys really forced the seal open, I would be powerless against them..."
However, things were clearly not so simple.
The few men from the military intelligence in trench coats were not so easy to appease.
The leader named Yegel suddenly took out a Golden Lion Token: "Barrett, this is the Empress's hand-order, seeing the order is as if seeing Her Majesty herself."
As expected, once the golden order was shown, the soldiers of the Sacred Judgment Legion looked at each other. Even Barrett solemnly crossed his chest. The soldiers behind him knelt in unison, performed a knightly gesture towards the token, and shouted in unison: "Glory is my command!"
Yegel sneered and, holding the golden token, shouted coldly, "Sacred Judgment Legion, heed the order! Per Her Majesty's secret order, continue deciphering the seal!"
Hearing this, Barrett still maintained his kneeling posture from saluting and did not rise immediately.
He stared deeply at the ground, pondering something.
The legion commander did not move, and neither did the soldiers behind him.
"You... you guys..."
Seeing that the group remained unmoved, Yegel's face turned dark in an instant, and he shouted angrily, "You defy the Empress's secret order—are you trying to rebel!"
Listening to the jarring word "rebel," the faces of the Sacred Judgment Legion soldiers turned ugly.
As knights who had been loyal to the royal family for generations, this was the greatest insult to them.
After hesitating for a moment, Barrett finally spoke, his voice extremely low, "My Sacred Legion has always been the most loyal guard to Her Majesty!"
Hearing this, Yegel's expression slightly relaxed.
But at that moment, as if Barrett had made a decision, he then said with conviction, "However... I still insist on my opinion; this relic absolutely cannot be unsealed now! As the commander of the Judgment Legion, I have the right to make the most reasonable decision based on the situation on the battlefield, and this is also the right granted to battlefield commanders by Her Majesty and the Congress! I also believe my judgment is in the best interest of the Empire!"
Upon these words, the soldiers behind him immediately echoed their commander, shouting, "Glory is my command!"
Hearing this, Yegel's face became very unsightly, and his speech became less polite, "Barrett, do you know what you are saying? Defying the Empress's secret order, you and your subordinates will be sent to a military tribunal, and the punishment could be death! Moreover, you would also destroy the centuries of honor of your Judgment Legion, and even implicate your families and friends in the Imperial Capital!"
This threat was fully laden with implications.
Betraying a royal command was not a simple matter of death for a knight.
Ultimately, it would lead to total disgrace and extermination of their families.
Yet even so, Barrett's gaze was firm and his tone unyielding: "I am well aware of what I am doing."
....
In the eyes of others, Barrett was seen merely as a crude man who only knew how to fight.
A professional ascending to the sixth tier—how could he be unaware of some secrets?
Having fought battles, sailed, and explored all year round, unearthing relics and encountering various indigenous intelligent races, the legends he had heard, and the secrets he knew were not few.
His experiences far exceeded those of the nobles in the Imperial Capital who had never left their doors.
Previously, in the cursed space, Bazil may have been just suspicious.
Now, seeing the piece of high-order chaos law leaking out of the black hole, he felt an inexplicable heart palpitation; how could he not guess that this situation totally matched the words of that crow-beaked masked man?
He knew, even if it was not some "God Burial Ground," this relic had significant issues!
He even suspected that something was wrong with the high ranks of the military intelligence.
Even that... something was wrong within the royal family!
Before sorting it out, this relic must not be opened!
.....
Seeing Barrett's attitude, a fierce light suddenly flashed in Yegel's eyes. Holding the golden token, he declared, "By Her Majesty's secret order, I now announce that Bazil is defying military orders, and his position as commander of the Sacred Judgment Legion is revoked!"

chapters.title: Chapter 281 - 280 Heresy
chapters.content:
"What, they want to remove the regiment commander from his position?"
"What right does the Military Intelligence Department have to announce the removal of an imperial royal army regiment commander from his position?"
"Those guys from the Military Intelligence Department, they've truly lost their minds!"
"Hmph! Yeager, your position in the Military Intelligence Department, at best, equals that of the regiment commander. What qualification do you have to say this?"
"..."
The moment the trench-coated man spoke these words, it was as if cold water had been dropped into a boiling pot of oil, instantly igniting the fury of the crowd.
Barrett's face showed no change, as if he had anticipated this. But behind him, the soldiers of the Sacred Judgment Army, one by one, became increasingly agitated, rebuking loudly.
They had reached the depths of this relic only after the Sacred Judgment Army had lost ninety percent of its members in battle, all to carry out their orders. And now they wanted to remove their own regiment commander from his position?
By what right did these damn Military Intelligence Department dogs have?
The soldiers' emotions became more and more heated, like a group of tigers released from their cages that couldn't be reined in, their presence pressuring the other two trench-coated men to the extent that their faces underwent a drastic change.
However, the leader named Yeager was not the least bit daunted.
He looked at the men before him with a cold eye, then at the silent Barrett, and asked sternly, "Barrett, are you planning to condone a mutiny within the Judgment Army? Think carefully, I am carrying out a secret edict from Her Majesty the Queen. If this really caused an uproar, it's not just you—all members of the Judgment Army, including those who died earlier, will be implicated... Even they will be held accountable posthumously..."
Upon hearing these words, Barrett's eyes became as dangerous as a ferocious beast's.
After pondering for a moment, he seemed to have reached a compromise, quietly tearing off the star rank from his armor and said indifferently, "I accept the order to be relieved of my command."
Upon hearing this, his deputy and some soldiers behind him, faces full of confusion and anger, boiled over again.
"Commander! You're right, we all support you!"
"That's right! Even if it goes to a military tribunal, we will go together. I refuse to believe that the empire's laws would dishearten royal knights who have been fighting abroad and shedding their blood for the empire!"
"Commander, your Barrett family has been royal knights for generations. Without Her Majesty the Queen personally speaking out, no one has the right to dismiss you from your position... Don't listen to those bastards from the Military Intelligence Department!"
"..."
Barrett glanced back at his men, feeling increasingly uneasy in his heart.
The current situation also confirmed to him that, while it might not necessarily be Her Majesty the Queen, there was definitely a big shot at the royal high levels who was very eager for this relic.
Such eagerness, so much so that it smelled of "conspiracy."
Barrett didn't say it out loud, but he also couldn't let these brothers, who had followed him through life and death, take risks with him.
He said with a resolute face, "Now, I issue the final order. All of you, withdraw from the relic immediately!"
"Commander!"
The crowd was deeply moved and angered upon hearing this, resolute to stick together through thick and thin.
But Barrett had no intention of changing his mind, and he spoke to a deputy beside him, "Kamur, according to military law, you are now the highest rank in the Judgment Army and will automatically assume the role of the regiment commander. Take the brothers out. And then report the situation here back to the imperial capital, truthfully."
The sturdy warrior named Kamur looked troubled, "But..."
Before he could finish speaking, Barrett added, "On a personal note, I will also prevent anyone from breaking these seals."
Kamur, hearing this, immediately understood what his regiment commander intended to do. Although he wanted to persuade him otherwise, he also knew the commander's character and realized that it would be futile.
He banged his chest and saluted, "Yes, Commander!"
The deputy knew full well that if they didn't leave, the Judgment Army would be confronting the Military Intelligence Department head-on.
No matter how it ended, it would be akin to the consequences of a "rebellion."
Moreover, they didn't think that those few people from the Military Intelligence Department could do anything to Barrett, who was left behind.
After all, Barrett was very strong!
....
The three trench-coated men from the Military Intelligence Department stood to one side, watching as the deputy led the men away, remaining silent.
In any case, they were now at the site of the seal, and the soldiers were no longer of much use.
However, the leader named Yeager looked at Barrett, who remained in place and challenged, "Barrett, are you certain you wish to obstruct us? You no longer have a rank. If you obstruct the execution of Military Intelligence Department's duties, I have the authority to execute you on the spot."
Barrett, hearing this threat, did not care in the least, and simply said, "These seals cannot be broken for now. No one is allowed."
Hearing this, Yeager's gaze turned cold, and he shouted sharply, "Then you can't blame us!"
As soon as he finished speaking, a layer of pale blue flames erupted from his body, which was unmistakably the royal secret top-tier fire-based Secret Technique "Wu Shi".
.....
Suddenly, intense sounds of combat echoed through the corridor.
The stability of the underground labyrinth had been compromised due to several high-level professionals fighting, making the battle aftermath exaggerated. Rocks rumbled and fell down, indicating signs that the entire underground palace might collapse.
Su Lun hadn't expected that Luying and his people would actually start fighting, and his expression turned peculiar.
He had witnessed Barrett's strength. With him blocking the way, theoretically, those three men in trench coats stood no chance.
Yet he was curious, those from the military intelligence were no fools, where did they get the confidence to attack?
"Could it be... that person behind the scenes had some other moves up their sleeve?"
Su Lun had an idea.
They were so eager to break the seal here, obviously aiming for the super-grade items within the God Burial Ground.
They possessed such detailed intelligence, it undoubtedly must be directly related to the great battle five hundred years ago.
But the two sides back then, the Dalu clan was completely annihilated, and the great Druids turned into giant trees, sealing this place.
Theoretically, there shouldn't be any treasure maps or the like that could leak information about this place.
That being said, the Luying royal family... there seems to be a significant problem.
Su Lun realized something, his expression turning slightly strange.
Yuta, who was unaware of what had transpired, thought that the seal had been broken and spoke gravely, "We must not allow them to break the seal!"
The Dalu clan had the duty to guard this place.
Su Lun nodded, "Mhm."
The two of them quietly moved closer.
....
The Sacred Judgment Legion had already left the underground, leaving only four people in the vast Hall of Valor.
Three men in trench coats and "Ferocious Beast" Barrett.
A fierce battle broke out between the two sides.
Su Lun and Yuta hid at the entrance of a corner cave, looking down at the fight below from a vantage point.
The battling sides seemed evenly matched, going back and forth without the one-sided situation Su Lun had anticipated.
"The guy from the Luying military intelligence is actually at the sixth order? No, that's not right... Even if he was just on the sixth order, he shouldn't have a chance of winning."
Su Lun pondered in his mind.
Although he didn't know why Barrett, who had become self-aware, was trying to prevent the seal from being broken, Su Lun hoped at this moment that he would win.
In a blink, Su Lun turned his gaze to the trench-coat man named Yegel, his eyes narrowing slightly.
This man was surrounded by a fierce cold fire. The flames condensed into a distinct blue fire armor around his body, making him look like he was wearing a ghostly armor. Every move he made radiated a domineering aura capable of destroying heaven and earth.
"The complete form of the Wu Shi Secret Technique?"
This was the first time Su Lun had seen "Wu Shi" at this level.
He knew this Secret Technique himself, but the extent of his mastery was only an outflow of a cold fire veil, enhancing some close combat abilities and fire resistance.
However, compared to the level of condensed armor before him, it was night and day.
Yegel, clad in the cold and dazzling armor, raised his hand and caused sand to fly and stones to roll, with the flames causing ripples to surge through the air. The armor not only amplified close combat abilities but also provided an absurdly strong defense. Not even Barrett's space-distorting power punch could truly touch that man's body.
"Hiss~ This armor condensed by Wu Shi, its level of refinement in terms of principles, is even stronger than the 'Giant's Strength' defense..."
Su Lun finally understood the practical use of this Secret Technique.
Penetration, dual damage of physical and magic, elemental affinity, Elemental Armor... its uses were numerous, covering both offense and defense.
He himself had only grasped the basics.
However, he could also see that Barrett, transformed into a black ape, had the upper hand. Presumably out of concern for the opponent's military intelligence status, he hadn't delivered a killing blow.
After all, he hadn't even used his "Giant's Strength" armor.
But as he watched, Yuta beside him noticed something peculiar and said with a strange tone, "That man in the trench coat has a very strange power. I can feel an evil aura."
"Oh?"
Su Lun, hearing this, also focused his attention on the fight.
At his current level of skill, he couldn't quite understand a battle of this magnitude. But upon Yuta's comment, he too felt that the trench coat man's rank six seemed a bit too "watered-down." Shouldn't a senior official from the Luying Intelligence Department be much stronger than this?
....
Bazil fought against three opponents and didn't fall behind in the slightest.
Before long, the other two from the Intelligence Department were beaten down, lying on the ground unable to get up.
However, as the fight progressed, Bazil suddenly stopped.
Looking at the man in the trench coat, he began to feel unfamiliar with him, and with a somewhat astonished tone, he said, "Yeager, I didn't expect you to advance to rank six?"
Upon hearing this, Yeager let out a strange "heh heh heh" laugh, "Yes indeed."
Barrett obviously noticed something and changed his tone, narrowing his eyes and saying, "However, that power doesn't seem to be your own. No need to hide it anymore, show your true capabilities. Otherwise, with this level of strength, you guys should just leave."
"Oh?"
Yeager tilted his head to look at Barrett with nothing but arrogance in his eyes.
Seeing that Barrett was determined to stop them, he no longer held back: "Tsk tsk, are you that eager to die?"
As he spoke, he seemed to stop hiding his strength, and the aura around his body gradually intensified. The previous fierce battle seemed to have been just a warm-up, and only now was he preparing to get serious.
Barrett, hearing this, didn't show any change in expression.
But upon seeing the man's aura, he frowned heavily, revealing a look of grave concern.
However, in the next instant, something unexpected happened.
Red lines dense as a network of veins emerged from Yeager's pores.
"Red lines" swelled in the wind, and in the blink of an eye, his whole body seemed to explode into chaos, enveloped by an evil aura.
....
From a distance, Su Lun almost thought this man was a Puppet Master, about to use a secret technique like "Puppet Theater."
But the All-Seeing Eye immediately identified something odd about the technique.
Those red lines weren't threads, but rather parasitic organisms with fluid moving through them, like veins.
This move was eerie in every aspect.
What was more bizarre,
he didn't first attack Barrett, his opponent; the red lines instead stretched toward the two heavily injured comrades from the Intelligence Department as if leeches had detected the scent of blood.
Barrett didn't kill those two, but they were already out of fighting capacity. Seeing the red lines coming, they tried to dodge in horror. However, the red lines easily penetrated their bodies and began greedily devouring them.
"Ah... Captain, what are you doing!"
Their screams had just begun when they were abruptly silenced.
In an instant, the two were sucked dry into mummified corpses.
Watching from afar, Su Lun's brow furrowed: "This isn't Alchemy!"
Barrett, clearly seeing the trick, roared, "The power of heresy!"
Within alchemical civilization, any power system that wasn't Alchemy was considered heretical.
Alchemist Magicians are a group of humans who revered the study of the ultimate secrets of the world—they don't oppose the existence of other powers, but faith is an exception.
Apart from believing in the "original creator," Alchemist Magicians would absolutely not become devotees of any deity; it was a matter of principle!
Especially in Luying, a traditional Alchemical Empire, there would definitely not be any considerable "heretic Magicians."
Anyone spreading the faith of a foreign god would be sent to the gallows.
It was absolutely impossible for the royal family to harbor any!
Yet this Yeager was a high-ranking official of the empire's Intelligence Department!
The realization was chilling.
Barrett finally realized that his speculation might have come true—a major crisis had arisen within the royal family!
Now, Yegor's killing of the two companions revealed a clear motive, to cover up the fact that he was a "heretic magician."
Next, it was certain that real battle would ensue.
Without any hope for luck, Barrett quickly formed the sorcerer's seals with his hands and let out a fierce shout, "Armor Release!"
The air was filled with the snapping sounds of bones, and his body visibly swelled, growing from two meters tall to a nearly five-meter imposing black gorilla. Of course, this was the releasing of Giant's Armor.
....
"I'm telling you, Barrett, wouldn't it be good to just carry out your orders? Why seek death?"
Those red threads swiftly condensed behind Yegor, and in the blink of an eye, they formed a mass of blood-colored flesh wings. His face contorted, demon-like, gruesome and terrifying. In this state, he hardly resembled a human being anymore.
The unmasked Yegor's aura soared ever higher, and the blue flame created by his body's [No Servant] secret technique instantly turned into a sinister red-and-black hue. Exuding terrifying energy from where he stood, the complicated network of roots that filled the surroundings turned black and decayed upon contact, then crumbled to dust and scattered in the air.
With a severe expression, Barrett's tone grew less courteous as he demanded, "So, your aim in breaking the seal here is under the command of that 'heretic'?"
Yegor did not respond directly, "A dead man needn't know."
Barrett snorted coldly, "Since you've turned to heresy, there is no need for sentiments. In the service of the empire, I have fought in many battles and executed numerous heretic magicians. Today, I shall capture you and present you before His Majesty myself!"
Listening to this, Yegor seemed as if he had heard a joke, laughing coldly as he spoke in a hollow voice, "You have no idea what you're up against."
Without further ado, Barrett formed the sorcerer's seals with his hands again, and the ground beneath his feet suddenly burst open with ripples.
With a "smack," at a glance, he had already charged forward.
....
Watching from a distance, Su Lun immediately realized that things had taken a serious turn.
The domain of decaying power surrounding Yegor seemed to be the "Realm" attainable only by a seventh-tier professional.
Yuta, as if recognizing something, suddenly changed her expression, "This... I've felt this in the Cursed Space before, it's the aura of that ancient deep-sea giant!"
"..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun was not overly surprised.
The clues pointed to a connection with that battle in the past, as Cursed Valley in the depths of Silent Forest had been discovered by the likes of Ruying.
If not the Dalu's side, then it must relate to the mysterious and powerful deep-sea giant's side.
Suddenly, the tide of the battle made a drastic shift.
Barrett, who initially had the upper hand, suddenly became the disadvantaged party.
Despite still appearing fierce, the shortcoming of a power-type professional was evident; failing to finish the opponent immediately led to a gradual weakening over time.
Under normal circumstances, Su Lun would definitely flee this scene.
There was no point in contributing another loss for his side.
However, seeing Yuta's resolved expression beside him, he knew she probably wouldn't leave. The Dalu had a responsibility to protect the seal, and their ancestors had died here; naturally, she wouldn't back down.
Thinking this, Su Lun's brow furrowed slightly. He took out a communicator and updated Mr. Jing, who was on his way, about the situation.
He originally wanted to ask his senior for advice, but instead, he received astonishing news.
"What! Senior, you're arriving soon?"
Su Lun was surprised to hear this.
The agreement was to return in three days, and by all counts, it had only been two.
However, Mr. Jing on the communicator was even more astonished, "Wasn't that the agreed time? Did something unforeseen happen?"
Su Lun realized something, pulled out a pocket watch, and looked at the date, his expression immediately turning strange.
He thought the date was "today," not expecting it to be "tomorrow."
Then he realized, there was a whole day missing in his memory.
As he took out his notes intending to record this bizarre lapse of time, he saw notes he had previously overlooked.
It then dawned on him that the issue stemmed from the earlier "time anomaly zone."

chapters.title: Chapter 282 - 281 [S-005-Time Messenger]
chapters.content:
Su Lun knew that Mr. Jing would soon arrive at Cursed Valley, so naturally, he wasn't in a hurry to leave.
But while he still remembered that bizarre situation that puzzled him, he directly asked Mr. Jing about it.
"Senior sister, I've encountered a problem that has me very confused..."
Su Lun shared everything he encountered and what was recorded in his notes.
After listening, a response came from the communicator, "You mean to say, you saw some 'special existence', but you forget about It?"
Su Lun: "Mhm."
Mr. Jing: "From your description, it sounds a bit like the ability to control time. There is a god-level talent related to time, [S-005-Time Messenger], which is the statue you saw in the basement of Storm Manor with the '✹' symbol. I've thought of some secrets that my father mentioned before. Mmm... It's not very good to go into detail. That 'existence' is either beyond your comprehension, or It doesn't want you to remember It. Usually, this situation involves some very high-level causality..."
Su Lun felt somewhat lost in the fog and uneasy for not understanding clearly.
He pressed on, "Ah? So what exactly is it?"
Mr. Jing seemed to know something but didn't elaborate, responding, "You don't need to ask in detail. If you ask, you'll ignore it just the same. If It doesn't want you to be aware of the existence, then there is no need to dig deeper. When the time comes, you might remember on your own. But likely, it isn't a bad thing."
"I see..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun finally felt at ease.
His senior sister was counted among one of the most learned people in their group.
If she said so, then the problem shouldn't be significant.
Even if there was a problem, pondering further would be futile.
After all, by all accounts, if Su Lun had spent more than a day in that "time anomaly," his life span should have declined by over a decade, or so he guessed.
But it didn't seem like it had.
Although there was no lifespan value on the data panel, he analyzed some data on metabolism and judged that his body probably hadn't undergone such significant changes.
Su Lun guessed it probably had something to do with that "existence" Mr. Jing had mentioned.
But without a threat, the actual truth didn't seem so urgent to know anymore.
....
The battle in the Hall of Valor became fiercer and fiercer. In this enclosed underground, it wouldn't be an exaggeration to say mountains were collapsing and the earth was splitting.
Both Su Lun and his companion dared not get close.
Even the watchful ravens, there to observe the battle, were killed several times by the aftershocks of the fight.
Barrett, as the commander of the royal legion, indeed had astounding strength.
Although Su Lun had met him before, it had always been on the run, and that guy had never displayed even a tenth of his true power.
Now was the true time to see the "Empire's Ferocious Beast" unleash his full strength.
Su Lun observed various top-notch techniques of a fighter on Barrett.
As expected of the commander of the royal legion, his punches and kicks were so fundamentally solid that Su Lun had never seen anyone who could compare.
At this moment, Barrett was clearly fighting with all his might.
His double-stage talent [Ape], along with a series of alchemy enhancements, were all focused on increasing strength. His power had grown to such an exaggerated level that it was astounding to any lower-ranking professional.
There was no need for armor; his muscles, tough as steel, were the best defense!
A milky-white aura swirled around his body and fists. When he struck, the space itself twisted, exuding an absolutely domineering and unrivaled aura.
But while the techniques were one aspect, what Su Lun couldn't comprehend was that mountain-splitting, earth-shattering momentum – it was a vague and indistinct sensation.
"Is that the 'energy' Senior Sister mentioned we need to cultivate?"
Su Lun pondered thoughtfully.
In this world, there weren't too few professionals of the fifth rank, but those who could advance to the sixth rank were rare as phoenix feathers and unicorn horns.
This was because there was a very high "threshold" for this rank.
Su Lun, blessed with the talent of the Reaper, could kill several fifth rank professionals and after stripping their comprehension of the laws, he almost had no threshold to advance all the way to the fifth rank.
But to advance to the sixth rank, no matter how powerful the dark spiritual power was, or how perfect the laws were, it was impossible without one condition.
And that was "energy".
To this day, Su Lun remembered Mr. Jing's words: Without cultivating one's spirit, it's like a person without bones; despite all the skills, one's achievements would ultimately be limited.
The reason why sixth rank professionals were outrageously strong was directly related to this threshold.
Seeing the "resolute energy" emanating from Barrett, Su Lun's eyes narrowed slightly, and he faintly felt as if he had grasped something.
....
The pace of the battle was fast.
Wave after wave of violent surges exploded in the air.
Barrett's moves were broad and powerful, capable of smashing boulders weighing several tons with a single punch.
Although Su Lun could not quite understand those moves infused with sixth rank laws, comparatively, the others were even more incomprehensible to him.
The one covered in red lines, Yegel, had methods too bizarre, able to restore his limbs instantly with the help of those red lines even after they had been blown to pieces.
The magic used by that guy wasn't from the alchemy system but the divine system.
Su Lun was completely baffled by what he saw.
Yuta, who was sensing with his eyes closed next to him, suddenly opened his eyes and exclaimed, "That guy has borrowed the power of an evil deity, drawing the vital energy from the surroundings to replenish himself, thus achieving an immortal body."
"An immortal body?"
Su Lun frowned upon hearing this.
Looking at it this way, if the battle dragged on, Barrett would eventually be defeated.
Clearly, Barrett, who was engaged in the intense battle, had realized this too.
He knew he had to fight quickly and decisively.
Even an immortal body had its breaking point; if that point were shattered, it couldn't recover.
Barrett, an old soldier seasoned on the battlefield, would certainly understand this.
It was at this moment that the stalemate suddenly changed.
Reflected in Su Lun's eyes was the battle scene in the Hall of Valor, from which he discerned something and murmured, "Are they going for broke..."
Finally, Barrett completed his energy accumulation!
"Flesh Alchemy: Open!"
He let out a fierce shout, ringing like a bell and echoing through the corridor.
Following that roar, his momentum surged wildly, and a steaming white vapor rose from the surface of his body.
