Barrett did not pause, his hands quickly forming magician's seals, and his aura suddenly turned cold and stern. With his hands well-formed in the sorcerer's seals, he lifted them up and let out another fierce shout, "Power Mystique: Ten Direction Fierce Beast Ban!"
With the emergence of this secret technique, a formidable ferocity instantly enveloped the entire area.
In the space of the Hall of Valor, ten white vapor beasts suddenly coalesced.
The ten apes placed their hands together, forming a hammer to unite their strike, encircling Yegel on the spot.
Though the action didn't look fast, the oppressive force of the power law seemed to solidify the space around them, rendering all things in all directions unable to move.
Even the black crow, watching the battle from a great distance outside the force field, felt so pressured it almost collapsed.
Su Lun witnessed this scene and saw the underlying technique, thinking to himself, "A secret technique for a short burst of fury? Among professions based on pure strength, a body's durability might be more suited for spells like 'Hormonal Rampage'."
His own physical strength could only withstand three stages of hormonal release before it became life-threatening. He estimated that this giant's body could at least sustain six stages. Such an increase in combat power could be even more exaggerated than what was currently displayed.
....
Barrett's momentum reached its peak, and finally, Yegel's complexion changed.
How could one underestimate this desperate strike?
This kind of pressure at the level of laws, where one power suppresses ten, offered virtually no alternative means of coping.
One could only withstand it head-on!
But the exaggeration of this fellow's power law was such that, after gathering strength for so long, even true Seventh Order professionals would struggle to break free, let alone someone like him who only had Seventh Order fighting strength with the help of external forces?
Yegel saw that he could not move, his facial features even became distorted under the immense force. But he didn't panic much, and a fierce light glowed in his eyes.
He seemed to give up resisting, speaking fervently, chanting the honored name of some evil deity: "Oh great lord of disaster, your devout follower requires your bestowed power..."
While the incantation was still being chanted, the fists of the ferocious ape already thunderously fell.
"Boom!"
The ten-headed ferocious ape fiercely struck the ground, creating a vibration that shook the entire space, similar to an earthquake.
The exaggerated power squeezed space, making a thunderous explosion.
Barrett's eyes were bloodshot, the skin of his muscular body turned from black to pink due to the high heat, emitting wisps of smoke.
The giant ape he transformed into hammered down with alternating fists, the space under the fists visibly twisted.
At the same time, the ten fierce apes condensed by fighting spirit also hammered down fiercely into space.
I strike mountains with divine power!
The rhythm of the ferocious ape's hammering was the same, one after another, one after another...
The commotion was akin to mountains collapsing and the ground splitting.
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
The vast underground space trembled intensely with each strike.
A large number of falling rocks quickly turned to dust upon entering the air field surrounded by the ten apes but, surprisingly, disintegrated into powder instantly.
Only then did the watching Su Lun realize that the seemingly invisible pressure wielded such terrifying tearing force!
Although Barrett had yet to condense his own domain, this power field fascinated the watching Su Lun.
Meanwhile, in the center of that power field, Yegel's elemental barrier had collapsed under the hammering, and his windbreaker had turned to dust. His skin was also torn to shreds, revealing, like a human anatomical chart, his black and red muscle fibers. However, what was eerie was that these muscle fibers seemed to come to life, turning into squirming red worms.
With each strike from the giant ape, Yegel's body would explode into large clouds of blood mist, limbs burst into bloody meat, splattering everywhere.
But in an instant, they would be restored as before by the red threadlike worms.
The air was filled with a malodorous scent of blood that made one feel wicked.
But for the moment, he didn't die explosively!
But casting such a powerful spell naturally came at a price.
Since the opponent hadn't dropped dead yet, Barrett on the other side was obviously under tremendous pressure. With every hammer strike, crimson blood spilled from his eyes, ears, mouth, and nose, and his momentum weakened a bit.
During this stalemate, it seemed Yeager couldn't withstand the continuous hammering; the red insects covering his body started seeking a new host, invading underground and spreading to the tree roots in the crevices of the rock walls.
If the consumption persisted, it was difficult to predict who would last to the end.
The most likely outcome was a pyrrhic victory for both sides.
Su Lun hoped for such an outcome; it would be for the best.
But, watching Yeager, who was still reciting spells despite being under attack, Su Lun knew that things might take an unexpected turn.
Sure enough!
What was initially an evenly matched situation suddenly took a drastic turn.
...
Alchemists relied on their own true strength; whatever skill they possessed was that much, and they could at most rely on alchemical cursed items.
But those heretics had the backing of certain special entities, making their combat power difficult to measure accurately.
Especially those followers who could receive responses from deities.
Sure enough!
As Yeager spat out his final incantation, a hideous smile emerged on his face awash with gushing blood, "Hahahaha..."
His mad laughter echoed around, and Su Lun, hiding in the tunnel, heard it loud and clear.
And as that laughter subsided,
An indescribable and terrifying will suddenly descended upon the place.
Before, Yeager was like a boat tossing in a tsunami with a risk of capsizing at any moment, but in an instant, with the mysterious will's empowerment, his aura abruptly changed, and he began to mock, "Tsk tsk... Barrett, is that all you've got?"
The voice sounded as if it came from the mouth of a demon from hell, sending shivers down one's spine.
At the same time, the black crow cawed sharply.
Su Lun knew it was a warning of imminent death.
He closed his right eye, leaving only the left open.
Su Lun was well aware that some beings should not be faced directly!
Others might not know what this mysterious will was, perhaps only feeling an instinctual fear.
But Su Lun had previously experienced such a scene.
"Damn it, that colossal deep-sea creature is a deity-level entity..."
Su Lun's complexion turned very unsightly.
He had encountered it once before in the Dawn City Ruins.
But back then, the fallen angel was caught in Sir Isaac's millennium-old scheme, and with Mr. Jing's various preparations, it didn't cause much of a stir.
Now, facing this wild deity, Su Lun felt a massive headache.
Although it was just the descent of will, without its full strength being present,
Su Lun knew that it was beyond his ability to interfere.
Seeing the situation, Su Lun's first instinct was to grab Yuta beside him and retreat as the smart move.
But before he could act, Yuta sensed the presence of the mysterious will and spoke first, very solemnly, "Not good! That being seems to be absorbing power from the seal; I must stop Him!"
Before Su Lun could react, Yuta turned to him, her eyes filled with a gentle and complex emotion of farewell, "Mr. Su Lun, you must leave this place. I have to stop Him!"
In the end, she had only two options.
As she spoke, not waiting for Su Lun to answer, the red totem on her face suddenly shone brightly, and the rainbow light from the magic cauldron beside her was dazzlingly intense.
With another glance, her entire being had transformed into a streak of light and disappeared into the tunnel.
....
Watching Yuta's departing figure, Su Lun's gaze was filled with solemnity.
He knew he could not dissuade her, so he didn't speak.
It was the mission of a Dalu Druid, with a priority above their own life. Yuta's faith was resolute; she would go no matter what.
Su Lun deeply respected her choice.
But he was genuinely worried.
Although Su Lun was unclear about Yuta's combat ability now that she had a holy artifact by her side,
he was very aware of one thing: even with external power, if the inherent combat strength isn't strong enough, the cost of using too high-tier powers could be immense.
He had seen in the Dawn Relic how a Fallen Angel, possessing Duchess Raphael, used power far beyond her capabilities, paying with her life.
"If it's just a will descending, perhaps the problem isn't too serious..."
Su Lun, though cautious, was not afraid of death.
After all, he had already experienced death twice, and to him, death was not so frightening.
In an instant, he thought back to the battle in the Dawn City Ruins where a divine being had truly descended, possessing a second-rank individual, yet the combat power displayed wasn't too exaggerated.
Now only a will has arrived, augmenting a sixth-rank person.
Perhaps... the strength of a seventh rank?
If her abilities had the upper hand, there might be a chance to exploit.
In an instant, Su Lun had analyzed many useful pieces of information.
Thinking it over, he picked up the communicator and reported the situation to Mr. Jing: "Senior sister's situation isn't looking good, seems like a divine will has descended..."
After finishing, he received Mr. Jing's calm reply from the other end: "Hmm, I see."
Su Lun hung up the communicator, took a deep breath, and without hesitation, dove into the tunnel leading to the Temple of Valhalla.
....
By the time Su Lun arrived, Yuta was already locked in fierce combat with Yegele, who was covered in tentacles.
Barrett, unbeknownst to when, had already lost an arm.
Back in his human form, he was bloodied all over, having crashed heavily into the distance and embedded in the rock wall, his life and death unknown.
Just as Su Lun arrived, he happened to see in the far tunnel a few soldiers holding the "Death Banner of Nelgale," sneaking in and taking the opportunity to rescue Barrett.
Yegele, now engrossed in his intense battle with Yuta, seemed to have no interest in the life or death of a few insects.
As long as they didn't stop him from breaking the seals, everything else seemed insignificant.
Moreover, he was entangled by the sudden appearance of Yuta and couldn't disengage.
Around Yuta swirled a seven-colored elemental aura, while the Holy Artifact, the magic pot, floated beside her, providing her with an endless source of magic power. With a raise of her hand, the winds and clouds surged, and the dazzling spells shone brilliantly.
On the other side, Yegele was surrounded by a dark red aura of death, drawing in more and more of the red threads from the surrounding life force. These threadworms converged into various forms of tentacles, leaving behind red and black auras that corrupted all vitality as they passed through.
The grand Hall of Valor was a battleground where red and black energies of calamity clashed with the multicolored forces of nature.
Both individuals were employing spells that didn't belong to the alchemy system, and both were using powers not their own. Su Lun found it all very confusing, yet he could definitely sense the exaggerated fluctuations of the elements.
"If this goes on, Yuta is in grave danger..."
Su Lun watched with furrowed brows.
Observing the situation, even if Yuta seemed to be holding on for now, the longer the fight dragged on, the more her body would be overdrawn.
Su Lun felt he should do something.
Whether it worked or not, he still had to try.
However, after observing for just a moment, he also realized that there was not a complete lack of opportunity.
The good news was that the tentacle monster Yegel had become was aiming to break a seal. It used countless red tendrils to siphon off life force, but at the same time, it anchored itself there.
With the black scythe, there might just be a chance to strike.
Su Lun had been controlling his thoughts and had never truly entertained the idea of killing the creature. He knew even the mere thought of taking action would intuitively alert such a formidable enemy.
The shared vision of the black crow would also confuse the enemy's sense of hostility.
So, there was only a fleeting chance for an attack!
Now, at the very instant Su Lun's intent to kill arose, he didn't hesitate at all. Controlling the zombies beside him, he calculated the distance perfectly and slashed at the tentacle monster in the southern side of the Hall of Valor from afar.
Simultaneously, Yegel immediately sensed it. His gaze shot towards the corridor where Su Lun was hiding like a bolt of lightning.
Unfortunately, the numerous tentacles that had spread out to absorb life force made his body too large and his movements to teleport away extremely clumsy.
Furthermore, Su Lun's decisiveness also gave him the chance to land the blow.
With a "swoosh," the space rift accurately hit the torso of the tentacle monster.
Su Lun's heart tightened: "I hit it!"
The space rift had cleanly split the humanoid core of Yegel in two.
Such an injury would have undoubtedly been fatal for an ordinary person.
But after that very strike, countless tendrils suddenly connected the two severed halves of the body back together.
A mocking smile appeared on Yegel's face.
Raising his hand, he summoned a flaming spear that flew towards Su Lun from a great distance.
The spear moved incredibly fast; almost in the same instant it was thrown, it pierced through the body of "Su Lun" a kilometer away.
....
With a "bang," Su Lun's shadow was revealed to be nothing but a stump of wood.
This was clearly the effect of using a "Puppet Substitute."
On a closer look, "Su Lun" had reappeared inside the Hall of Valor, readying another attack.
Yegel did not hesitate and hurled another flaming spear.
"Su Lun" was impaled once again.
However, the figure disintegrated.
This time, it was an illusion projected by "Robert's Monocle."
Then, seven or eight "Su Luns" appeared in various corners of the hall.
Seeing Su Lun's emergence, Yuta's pretty face also showed a trace of urgency.
She naturally couldn't just watch as Yegel killed Su Lun, so when he was distracted, she also stabbed forward with several wooden spears.
The wooden spears and the tentacles engaged in fierce battle again...
....
Deep in the corridor, Su Lun, wearing a monocle, saw the scene through the vision of the crow and analyzed, "Immune to physical damage, huh..."
Luckily, with Yuta dragging the enemy, he was also able to make some attempts.
From these attempts, he confirmed that the black sickle couldn't kill the immortal Yegel.
That bizarre regenerative ability, unless one could simultaneously deliver dozens of strikes to cut the fellow into small enough pieces that couldn't reconnect, otherwise it was impossible to kill.
But clearly, Su Lun couldn't do it.
However, the probing just now wasn't entirely futile.
"The puppet wasn't discovered in advance, which means, that guy can't sense the existence of the threads. The puppet can control a large space..."
Su Lun's mind was like a rapidly operating calculator, analyzing swiftly.
Most of his combat power was in the puppet.
But the puppet wasn't completely flawless.
The source of the threads was on him, so as long as one could sense the threads, they could lock onto his real body.
Conversely, as long as they couldn't lock onto his real presence, the chances of surviving were very high.
"Moreover, that guy can't distinguish the illusions created by the monocle. Be careful, and it might be possible to find an opportunity..."
Su Lun's thoughts in his mind diverged in an instant, analyzing various countermeasures.
Of course, the biggest advantage was that after testing it himself, he confirmed that the "heretic's" real body must be very far away, with the projected will able to exert at most tier seven standards.
With Yuta restraining it, it at least can't devote too much attention to deal with him.
"Only the last resort is left to try."
Su Lun thought of something, and a sharp light flashed in his eyes.
The gap in rank was too great. Discovering the black sickle couldn't kill that guy, he thought of the last resort.
That was firepower coverage.
Time waits for no one, without any hesitation, Su Lun took out the mechanical battle armor from the spatial storage.
The mechanical battle armor was controlled by a living corpse, but it didn't have its own will. Then there were the threads that Yegel couldn't detect. Theoretically, being careful, it might catch the enemy by surprise.
....
Inside Valhalla, the confrontation continued on.
Even with the Holy Artifact continuously supplying magic power, Yuta was gradually falling behind.
Encountering power far exceeding her own for the first time, she wasn't using it skillfully, and the burden was becoming greater, she persevered solely with a will that feared not death.
Su Lun controlled the mecha and stealthily made his way over.
The black sickle wasn't completely useless, at least that slash when it cut through disrupted the integrity of that guy's protective field.
The recovery interval gave a slight gap, which was the opportunity Su Lun was looking for!
Right after the mecha quietly reached the designated position, he repeated his old trick, slashing out with the black sickle, while the mecha's six-cylinder Fire God Cannon instantly produced a long flame serpent. That was the special glow of alchemy bullets leaving the barrel.
Previously he had been reluctant to use such an extravagant method, with the expense of ammunition costing several tens of millions of Liso per minute, it just wasn't worth it against regular enemies. But now, it couldn't be more appropriate.
Right as the spatial rift cut to the accumulator monster in the instant, the integrity of the field was split open, and alchemy bullets surged in like a tide.
The bullets blasted apart many red threads, looking like countless smashed watermelons on the ground, the scene was incredibly bloody.
But it was a pity that the blood thread creature's regenerative ability was too strong.
That mysterious will also had methods Su Lun couldn't comprehend.
After a moment, Yegel's body restored to its original state, and the field expanded again.
That domain capable of corrupting everything shielded in front of the body, even bullets that hit it were completely corroded away just meters from the surface.
Seeing this, Su Lun sighed slightly, "Still no good..."
He had done all he could.
Before he had time to feel more regret, he suddenly felt an alert in his heart and bolted backward explosively.
"I've been discovered!"
Su Lun didn't hesitate at all and dashed toward the corridor behind him.
In the moment of escape, countless dense red thin lines suddenly sprouted from the rock walls around him.
Only then did he realize that Yegel had imperceptibly spread the blood thread creature into the depths of the corridor.
Unable to sense Su Lun's position in other ways, he had resorted to this most crude method.
In an instant, the blood thread creature in the corridor converged into tentacles and grabbed at Su Lun.
The tentacles were extremely tough, and severing them required a lot of energy.
Chop one down, and countless more will spring up.
Su Lun's expression was grave, not daring to tangle with those threads, he teleported repeatedly, narrowly missing being caught by those red tentacles multiple times.
But because he had observed the escape route beforehand, he narrowly evaded the tentacles' reach without danger.
After escaping for about one or two kilometers, the red tentacles were no longer so dense.
This zone was beyond Yegel's attack range.
Su Lun also stopped.
For the moment, he was temporarily unharmed.
But looking at the dense tentacle-covered walls in front of him, it meant that he had been completely cut off. He wanted to go in but couldn't.
Yuta inside could only face the enemy alone.
Although he had done all that he could, Su Lun's complexion wasn't too good.
"It will be at least a few hours before Senior Sister can get here, she might not last that long. Should I use explosives to cause a targeted collapse? No, that fellow is immortal, explosives have limited effect..."
His brows were deeply furrowed as he considered whether other methods might be of some help, but again, he had no solution.
Suddenly, a flash of light appeared before his eyes, and a person wearing a gold-patterned cloak appeared before him?
That method of appearing was quite special, and also very familiar.
It was like a flash of mirror light, and then the person was there.
"Senior Sister?"
Su Lun thought he might be hallucinating, so he blinked.
But no matter what, he was indeed in the real world.
Looking at the proud and aloof face revealed under the lifted cloak, who else could it be if not Mr. Jing?

chapters.title: Chapter 283 - 282: Outer Gods (Wishing everyone a happy 2022)
chapters.content:
"Senior sister, how did you get here?"
Su Lun thought he must be seeing things.
Because the last time they communicated, Mr. Jing was still far from Cursed Valley.
Even without any delays, it was estimated that it would take several hours to arrive.
But now, she suddenly appeared before his eyes?
"Mm."
Mr. Jing lifted her cloak, revealing that cold and beautiful face.
She looked at Su Lun, the corners of her mouth curving slightly as she said indifferently, "You seem to be in good shape. It looks like I haven't come too late."
It was only in front of this junior brother that she ever wore such a relaxed expression on her face.
"You really came..."
Su Lun felt a sense of unreality as he listened.
But he could not hide the joy in his eyes.
No matter how Mr. Jing got here, the fact was she had arrived!
With "Golden Leg" here, this seemingly desperate situation instantly gained the capability for a breakthrough reversal.
Mr. Jing glanced at the dense red threadworms in the corridor, her brow furrowing slightly as she seemed to detect something unusual about these worms.
She didn't delay, saying to Su Lun, "I'll explain later. I'm going out first to deal with that Outer God's follower."
"Mm."
Hearing this, Su Lun naturally didn't have to say much then and there.
He also thought that if his senior sister had come ahead of time, she must have anticipated something.
Just as this thought crossed his mind, Mr. Jing's hands were quickly forming the sorcerer's seals, her expression becoming fierce.
Su Lun watched the sequence in which she was constructing the seals and found it strange.
This wasn't the start of any elemental spell, nor was it any sorcerer's seal system Su Lun had ever seen. It felt more like... a unique spell she had created herself?
Before Su Lun could guess, Mr. Jing had already gathered the sorcerer's seals, softly chanting, "Domain: Mirror of All Aspects!"
It turned out to be a seventh-tier domain?
A look of realization crossed Su Lun's face.
This was also the first time he had witnessed an authentic domain of laws.
This was quite different from the Black Umbrella's "Nightfall Domain," and the corrosive domain of the tentacle monster before.
As soon as she cast the spell, a faint luminescence lingered around Mr. Jing's body, which seemed to be surrounded by shards of a shattered mirror. Even though the domain wasn't aimed at Su Lun, standing within the domain's scope, he instantaneously felt as if he couldn't sense anything around him. It was as if this space had come under Mr. Jing's control.
And just like that, Mr. Jing's voice had vanished into the corridor.
Su Lun, gazing at the spot where the mirror light had flashed past, muttered, "Senior sister has become so strong..."
....
"She really did come..."
Su Lun felt an incredulity that lingered for a long time.
But with the arrival of strong reinforcements, the heavy stone in his heart suddenly fell.
Such a high-level battle was surely like a scene from hell, and he had no desire to get physically involved.
Su Lun decided to wait in the corridor and then sent a black crow flying in to watch the battle.
However, the battle was too intense. The fallout from high-tier laws colliding was a catastrophic disaster for lower-tier creatures.
The black crow was shattered by the aftermath of the battle several times.
Each time it reformed, it cawed in grievance, voicing its discontent.
Fortunately, Su Lun had previously collected a rich amount of death energy in the coffin, and after pouring a few mouthfuls into the crow, it felt ready to go again.
Even with the black crow, Su Lun never saw how the battle in the hall of valor unfolded from start to finish.
Yegel, or rather the "heretic," fought desperately.
The destructive force generated by their clash surged wave after wave.
After about a quarter of an hour, the commotion of the collapsing corridors below steadily subsided.
"It's over."
Su Lun's furrowed brows finally relaxed.
Although he guessed that his senior sister's strength must be formidable, she had said herself that she hadn't fully recovered her power.
And, Su Lun also didn't know if this enemy, who appeared to have the will of a deity, had any other tricks up their sleeve.
Now seeing that the battle was over and those red threadworms on the rock walls had shriveled and blackened, seeming to have died, the outcome was quite clear.
"But speaking of which, what tier is senior sister at now?"
Su Lun's curiosity mounted.
Hearing from the communicator that Mr. Jing said the battle was over, he didn't ponder over it further and, with several spatial displacements, quickly traversed the collapsing corridors.
This haste was partly out of concern for the safety of Yuta and Mr. Jing.
Another reason was that he needed to clean up the battlefield.
After all, the corpses were still warm.
He might make it there in time if he hurried.
....
Su Lun quickly arrived at the hall of valor.
The previously intact space was now shattered into pieces.
Mr. Jing stood above a sealing artifact-level ancient light mirror at the mouth of a pitch-black hole, performing some sort of spell.
Seeing Su Lun arrive, she nodded in acknowledgement.
Mr. Jing appeared to be engaged in something very important, so Su Lun didn't disturb his senior sister.
In a moment, he also saw Yuta, who was sitting nearby, recuperating. He too breathed a sigh of relief.
A magical pot enveloped her, and streams of rainbow energy were repairing her wounds, which didn't appear too severe.
Though her aura was very weak, fortunately, she was unharmed.
Su Lun's brows completely unfurled as he walked over, tousled Yuta's hair, and asked, "Yuta, are you okay?"
Yuta also revealed a relieved expression, replying with a somewhat pale smile, "Yes. I'm fine."
She paused, glancing at the figure in the gold-patterned cloak at a distance, blinked her eyes asking implicitly.
Su Lun smiled and said, "That's my senior sister, the one I've told you about, also the daughter of Sir Isaac."
"Oh."
Upon hearing this, Yuta's eyes lit up, and she finally relaxed completely.
Even though Su Lun had forewarned her about everything, including Mr. Jing's existence,
the arrival time of the person in the Gold-Patterned Cloak was much earlier than scheduled.
And it was too coincidental, arriving just when the great battle broke the seal.
She couldn't help but be extra cautious.
Although this mysterious person had indeed helped her kill the enemy, her current actions were puzzling.
But now, listening to Su Lun's confirmation, Yuta finally let go of her concerns.
Since it was a descendant of Sir Isaac, then they were friends of the Dalu tribe.
....
Yuta was in worse shape than she appeared. Only after seeing Su Lun did she completely let down her guard.
But it was also because that taut spirit relaxed, she suddenly fainted.
Su Lun hurriedly checked her injuries, which weren't too bad.
The power of nature had a special healing effect, more effective than any potion.
There was no need for Su Lun to worry, as the magical pot was healing Yuta's injuries.
With Mr. Jing fussing over the seal and Yuta healing, Su Lun didn't need to intervene.
He walked to the center of the battlefield and saw the segmented carcass of the tentacled monster.
Upon noticing the "gray mist," a phantom of Death appeared behind Su Lun and devoured it.
'You have stripped the soul of "Yegel Sellet," gaining some Tier 5 "Fire Elemental Law" and a fragment of Tier 6 "Calamity Law";'
'You have gained extensive experience in using "Mystique: Wu Shi," comprehending the [Infinite Samurai: Emperor of Flames], with +555 casting experience.'
'You have stripped a substantial amount of "Espionage Expertise"'
'You have acquired some "Intelligence from the Luye Military Intelligence Service"'
'Spiritual Power +14.7'
Su Lun originally thought that Yegel's Soul Shard would provide many answers to his questions.
Unexpectedly, he didn't strip any information about the "heretic" behind the man.
Even the high-level secrets of the Luye Military Intelligence Service were not there.
Only some not very important intelligence was stripped.
It was after assimilating the information about the military intelligence that Su Lun understood that high officials there had mental restrictions and training.
If they encountered soul searching or dream invasion techniques, the restriction would instinctively erase the sensitive information, preventing probing and information leakage.
As for the "heretic" information...
Su Lun felt it might be some highly sophisticated method that directly erased that part of the memory.
And the Law fragments were stripped rather haphazardly.
The Tier 5 'Fire Elemental Law' seemed to be something Yegel had originally comprehended.
This matched the intelligence Su Lun knew before: the guy was supposed to be a Tier 5.
The fragment of Tier 6 'Calamity Law' resembled something foreign, with very little presence.
But for Su Lun, it was a "treasure."
After assimilating it, he felt a sudden spark of insight in his understanding, as if
in the pitch-dark night, upon looking up, he saw a few stars.
Though not enough to illuminate the path ahead, they marked the position and altitude of certain specific existences.
An incredibly rare discovery.
It was also Su Lun's first contact with such high-level laws.
Elsewhere, he had no ability to kill a Tier 6 professional and strip their fragments.
As for the experience in using "Wu Shi," Su Lun had previously watched the man use it with shock, so he prioritized it over other skills and stripped it effortlessly.
The people from the intelligence service had practiced this secret technique from a young age; in essence, Su Lun had stripped decades of experience in one go.
[Infinite Samurai: Emperor of Flames] was an advanced form of this secret technique.
With this stripping, his proficiency skyrocketed to the point of "integrated mastery."
Su Lun now just needed enough dark energy to immediately cast this secret technique, which would multiply his survival and combat abilities several times over.
....
After digesting those memories, Su Lun's gains were not insignificant.
Immediately after, his gaze fell on the bits of flesh on the ground.
More precisely, the countless rotting, blackened worms.
"Parasites?"
Su Lun frowned tightly.
He had stripped a "Control Insect Magician" before and knew of many bizarre insects.
But he had never seen this kind before.
There was no information about these worms in Yegel's memory, obviously directly related to that "heretic."
Through Soul Perception, he sensed faint traces of souls in the pool of blood and flesh,
but they were rapidly diminishing.
It was a sign of the worms dying off quickly.
However, there was one exception.
"Not completely dead?"
Su Lun muttered to himself.
He maneuvered a thread, and at the place where life force was the most concentrated, he found a heart.
As soon as he picked it up, those blood vessel-like nematodes burst out, like leeches craving blood, they stood erect, probing towards Su Lun, continually extending and inspecting.
Perhaps because the heart was the last bastion for these parasites, they had not died off.
Su Lun watched with a deep frown, initially thinking of burning them with a fire to resolve it completely.
But now the situation wasn't so simple, so he took out a container and placed the heart inside.
It was the same runic glass bottle once used for the heart of a Fallen Angel.
He figured that if it could hold the heart of a real deity, it could naturally contain that of a Tier 5 or 6 professional.
Having looked for a long time without finding anything of interest, Su Lun didn't waste any more time.
He thought he'd ask Mr. Jing about it later.
...
Since it was a battlefield clean-up, one naturally had to be thorough.
Su Lun set the jar aside and then found a storage ring amid the remains of the bodies.
The storage space was quite large, likely belonging to Yegel.
There were many items inside, a mixture of sorts, with not a few fine goods.
Worthy of a royal intelligence operative.
Suddenly, Su Lun saw two large silver bricks in the storage ring and felt a small surprise, "Huh... is this the 'Activated Silver'?"
The amount didn't look much at a glance, but after all, it was already refined.
If one were to really calculate, it was probably a hundred times the quantity that could be refined from the two giants Su Lun had previously hunted.
But before he could be happy for long, Su Lun suddenly remembered something, "My deadly poison incense burner!"
He hadn't forgotten that his deadly poison incense burner was taken away by Luying and the others.
Moreover, the Sacred Judgment Legion had left with nearly a hundred people, meaning they took all the spoils of war with them.
"This is going to be troublesome..."
Su Lun suddenly felt the storage ring in his hand wasn't as appealing anymore.
He didn't know if he could catch up if he went out now, and even if he did catch up, Su Lun was powerless.
Mr. Jing was his senior sister, not his enforcer.
Moreover, the legion commander Barrett had staked his life and fortune to prevent Yegel from breaking the seal...
Even if they were enemies, it was just a matter of stance and faction.
Thinking of this, Su Lun's thoughts began to scatter.
He suddenly felt that the people who left were likely to share Luying's grim fate.
"The Luying royal family is clearly in trouble now, and Barrett even stopped the 'heretic' from breaking the seal. On returning, he'll probably be unable to escape death..."
Su Lun immediately felt very vexed.
The items seemed to be slipping through his fingers.
The other things were still manageable, but the Activated Silver was an irreplaceable main material for alchemy golems.
Just as he was feeling aggrieved, a soft voice came from beside him, "What are you thinking about?"
He glanced over and, of course, it was the amiable Mr. Jing.
....
Since there was no one else, Mr. Jing took off his cloak.
Although she seemed approachable, Su Lun could tell her aura was becoming more elusive.
Looking at that strikingly beautiful and familiar face, Su Lun curiously asked, "Senior sister, have you recovered your cultivation?"
Mr. Jing shook her head and calmly responded, "Not yet."
Su Lun looked at her, and it was clear from her ease in the recent fight that she hadn't exerted much effort. Believing she wasn't a stranger, he curiously asked, "Senior sister, have you reached the seventh rank now?"
Mr. Jing smiled without answering, giving him a glance. She naturally guessed her junior brother was curious about her rank and said, "After hibernating for a thousand years, I should fully recover and smoothly advance to the eighth rank."
She paused, not meaning to hide anything from Su Lun, and added, "With some more great opportunities, it is possible for me to reach the ninth rank in this lifetime."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's expression immediately became animated, "That's amazing!"
A true Golden Leg!
Whether she can advance to the ninth rank or not, an eighth rank professional is already a top-tier powerhouse.
Mr. Jing simply smiled noncommittally.
Su Lun didn't dwell on the topic. He glanced sideways and noticed that the black hole behind him had disappeared?
Seeing his confusion, Mr. Jing replied, "I laid an Illusion Technique on the seal; it won't be easily noticed now. Even if someone touches it, I can be here in no time."
Upon hearing this, all was good.
Su Lun didn't ask any more questions. Instead, he was more curious about something else and blurted out his question, "Senior sister, didn't you say it would take several more hours for you to get here? Why..."
This had been a question he hadn't had the chance to ask earlier.
Because he knew his senior sister was a very rigorous person.
If she said a time, it would definitely be that time.
Yet, this time she had arrived early.
And, coincidentally, she arrived at the most critical moment of the battle, solving the urgent crisis.
This made him very curious.
Mr. Jing looked at him, her expression serene, and explained, "Divination and prophecy aren't uncheatable. Earlier, when I heard you say those people were eager to develop the Cursed Valley, I guessed that some of them might have foreseen my arrival would bring some changes. So, I used a little trick..."
Su Lun, upon hearing this, seemed to understand something.
But it definitely wasn't as simple as "deceiving" him.
It was about deceiving the enemies as well.
This allowed her to seize the opportunity and arrive in time.
Otherwise, there might have been serious trouble.
Mr. Jing didn't hold anything back and explained patiently, "The essence of most divinations is following natural laws to compute possible outcomes, not definite ones. It means that certain divination rules can sometimes be misled through clever tricks. Of course, the prerequisite is that you have a thorough understanding of those rules. My father happens to master the laws of fate, and I happen to know a bit more because of it..."
"Oh," Su Lun said, feeling like he sort of got it, and yet didn't.
So, did she use some methods to deceive certain divination rules of this world?
Not being quite ready to understand those methods, he didn't ponder deeply.
In the end, one thought remained in his heart: Senior sister, awesome!
Then, Mr. Jing added meaningfully, "It's like the situation you asked me about earlier. When existences are forgotten by all, they are non-existent in the cause and effect of the world. That is also a very clever way to deceive the rules of the world."
"Oh,"
Su Lun, upon hearing this, instinctively felt it was profound.
But after a moment of reflection, his thoughts briefly went blank: Huh... what did I ask?
Mr. Jing caught the fleeting look of bewilderment in his eyes and smiled showing her teeth.
Clearly, she wasn't interested in lingering on the topic, and after sizing up Su Lun and noting his not insignificant progress, she didn't skimp on her praise, saying, "Your third rank realm has stabilized, huh. And you've cultivated your 'qi' well."
"Hehe."
Hearing his senior sister's praise, Su Lun did not play coy and smiled without any false modesty.
But upon mentioning "energy", he instantly thought of the insight he had when he observed Barrett before.
Unable to grasp it firmly, he straightforwardly asked, "Senior sister, what exactly is 'energy'? I heard it's a prerequisite for advancing to the sixth order?"
"That's not absolute. Some professionals who have consumed a large amount of resources can also advance to the sixth order. However, 'energy' is the inevitable path to becoming a strong person, and it's essential for condensing a domain at the seventh order. Otherwise, you'll find that, apart from understanding the laws, the domains you condense will vary greatly in power..."
It seemed that this question was not easy to answer, so Mr. Jing paused for a moment, pondering.
She then said, "If one must provide a specific description of 'energy'... you could say, to become a powerful being, one must possess an imposing presence."
"Imposing presence?"
Su Lun contemplated for a moment and felt it was very similar to what he had seen in Barrett before.
Since he was praised for cultivating his energy well, he shamelessly asked, "Senior sister, do I have that 'imposing presence'?"
"You're still far from it," Mr. Jing replied after giving her junior brother a look, then teased him, adding, "Sometimes you're too cautious, overly careful in considering things, which makes your energy cultivation slower. Although there's nothing wrong with that, you lack the determination to follow through without hesitation and some level of dominance."
Su Lun was not bothered by this "lesson" and instead let out a chuckle.
Since he had already asked, he took the opportunity to ask further, "Senior sister, then how can one quickly condense their energy?"
Mr. Jing said, "Each person's condensed energy is different, and the path they eventually take is also unique, so no one can say for sure. However..."
She raised her eyebrows lightly, and her tone shifted abruptly, "For instance, last time at Black Reef, when you came back to save me, that was very good. Some decisions you make without caring for gains or losses, those that come from the depths of your heart, will allow you to rapidly condense your own 'energy'."
"Oh..."
Listening, Su Lun finally felt like he understood a bit.
In layman's terms, this explanation meant: Be indifferent to life and death, and don't hesitate to take action when challenged?
....
The senior sister and junior brother, who hadn't seen each other for a long time, caught up with old times.
Soon, Su Lun steered the conversation toward the current situation.
He hadn't had time to go into detail over the communicator before, but now that they were face to face, he laid out everything he knew.
In the end, he also asked, "So... senior sister, what exactly is that 'heretic' entity?"
Mentioning this, Mr. Jing's expression turned slightly solemn. After pondering for a moment, she said, "It should be a 'foreign god'."
"Foreign god?"
Su Lun showed confusion, as this was a very unfamiliar term.
Mr. Jing explained, "Any deity that is not from the alchemy system, we generally refer to them as 'foreign gods'."
She paused, glanced at the heart in the jar while musing for a moment, then added, "Currently, there are flaws in the laws of our plane, and under normal conditions, it's impossible for deities to be born. Therefore, it must be a remnant from the ancient era. If nothing unexpected has happened, this 'foreign god' is probably one of the 'demon gods of the heavens' that destroyed the Dawn civilization. And although we're unclear about what exactly transpired in the great war that caused the civilization's discontinuity, we can be certain that all invading 'foreign gods' perished."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun questioned, "Then why is this one still alive?"
Mr. Jing didn't seem surprised and explained, "This kind of existence has appeared in history before. It's very difficult for a god to completely perish. Moreover, even after a god falls, the remnant wills, laws, or shattered divine fragments of these ancient foreign gods can contaminate other beings. Therefore, they usually create some 'false gods' who think they are deities. During the Atlia Empire era, the authorities eliminated many similar heretics."
Now understanding, Su Lun felt less pressure, "So, this tentacled monster isn't necessarily a true deity?"
Mr. Jing dismissively said, "Even if it is, the threat isn't significant at the moment. Once a god is wounded and lacks faith, recovery is not easy, and it's not very powerful right now. At least the fact that the main body hasn't personally come indicates many problems."
After a brief pause, she continued, "During the war that destroyed the Dalu clan five hundred years ago, that 'foreign god' must have also suffered heavy damage. Otherwise, it wouldn't have lain low for hundreds of years. Moreover... there might be other reasons it dares not show itself. Just contaminating a few believers isn't a big problem."
"Other reasons?"
Su Lun faintly felt that this statement seemed to resonate with some of his own familiar thoughts.
But he tried to remember, and couldn't recall anything at all.
Mr. Jing didn't say much more, instead, something occurred to him, his gaze becoming slightly solemn, "From the intelligence we have so far, I think I have an idea of what It intends to do."
Su Lun looked at the fragments of flesh on the ground and had a guess as well, saying, "Does it want to use imperial power to restore its strength?"
Yegel's identity was quite particular; this wasn't hard to guess.
"Hmm."
Mr. Jing nodded and continued, "That 'Outer God' seeks to find a method to reconstitute its divinity in this God Burial Ground, but it has failed. It won't succeed in the future either. Therefore, It is left with only one choice, and that is to spread faith. An ancient saying goes: Reestablish the faith, and a god remains a god. Although I do not know how It managed to extend Its reach into the Luying royal family, it seems the issue won't be small."
Su Lun listened with only half an understanding; concepts like faith felt very abstract to him.
Mr. Jing continued to explain, "Actually, 'faith' is not necessarily frightening. Ancient texts record that our plane once had many followers of different deities. Just like the Dalu tribe worships the nature god, who embodies peace, poetry, and nature in its divine essence and does not do anything like annihilating lower beings. But we must fear the Evil Gods. Such beings can bring ruin to life, invade planes to transform them into divine kingdoms, and enslave living beings. If that's the case, for us alchemists without a god to believe in, this could be a civilization-destroying calamity..."
At this point, Mr. Jing's gaze fell once again on the heart stored in the glass jar, and suddenly a chill arose in his tone, "Now it seems, this 'Outer God' is very likely an Evil God. If that's true, then under no circumstances can we allow It to succeed..."
"Hmm."
Su Lun was influenced by these words and felt an inexplicable sense of excitement in his heart.
He knew that his senior sister had ambitious aspirations, always contemplating many problems from the perspective of the survival of human civilization.
On her, there was an undeniable radiance of character.
Mr. Jing thought of something and sighed lightly, "Now, with the two great empires in chaos for hundreds of years, human alchemical civilization has almost stagnated for centuries. This can't go on... Thus, I want to rebuild 'Dawn City' as a free exchange place for alchemists, to enhance and propagate alchemical civilization. But there are also many problems now. The noble autocracy means those in power hoard over ninety percent of society's resources. Social stratification is rigid, and many actions are restricted. To establish such a free and neutral place, we can't avoid dealing with those nobles' power plays. Even if 'New Dawn City' can be established, it is bound to face resistance from both great empires and the noble classes. This is inevitable. Those who cling to power will never allow a 'free territory' to thrive... Besides, from what we see now, Luying's situation is very complicated, and significant changes may occur. Therefore, I need stronger military power, not just me alone, I may have to establish an organization strong enough to help me achieve this goal..."
Su Lun listened and also felt that Mr. Jing would face significant resistance in the days to come.
The greater your ability, the higher the stakes you consider.
But hearing his senior sister's words, although it was just a budding idea, was she getting ready to start a "revolutionary army"? Going against the two great empires would essentially mean revolution.
But, talking is just talking.
Su Lun felt that Mr. Jing's plan currently had nothing to do with him.
He didn't feel any sense of urgency either.
But as if by telepathy, as soon as this thought crossed his mind, Mr. Jing turned to look at him and said seriously, "You too should work hard to become stronger."
Su Lun pointed at his own nose, "Me?"
He had an inkling, and his eyelids twitched violently.
"Yes."
Mr. Jing smiled gently, "You are the disciple of my mother, and you have obtained my father's notes. The goal of rebuilding Dawn City, naturally, requires your help as well."
"..."
Su Lun rolled his eyes and said despondently, "Senior sister, you think too highly of me..."
It wasn't that he was selling himself short; it was just the reality.
With the talent of the "Death Reaper," as long as he didn't die, he was confident he could advance to the fifth rank.
But beyond that, it was hard to say.
Rebuilding Dawn City, such a grand ideal, would likely end up in a head-to-head confrontation with the two great empires. Without being at the eighth or ninth rank, one wouldn't even be qualified to dream about it.
Mr. Jing, however, did not say much more and smiled meaningfully.
PS. Wishing everyone a happy new year~ And, by the way, a small request for monthly votes and subscriptions.

chapters.title: Chapter 284 - 283 [S-009 - True Solution of All Phenomena]
chapters.content:
Su Lun had also guessed that the previous great battle had not been as easy for his senior as it appeared. After all, she had been forced to leave her retreat prematurely, her strength had not fully recovered, and she had traveled a long distance only to engage in a fierce battle, during which she seemed to have sustained some minor injuries.
After chatting for a while, Mr. Jing began meditating in a seated position.
Yuta was still unconscious and recovering from her injuries, leaving no one else to talk to. Su Lun was not idle either; he started to get busy with his own affairs.
The mechanical armor was severely damaged and urgently needed repairs; the two pieces of "Living Silver" he had recently obtained were not enough to make an alchemical golem, but that did not prevent him from studying and familiarizing himself with the various properties of this legendary puppetry material; he also needed to digest and understand the skills and laws he had acquired previously; and he had discovered some issues with his mental tentacles in real combat...
Su Lun soon immersed himself in his busyness.
The crypt was very dim, illuminated only by a not-so-bright blue magic lamp, which lit up a small area and cast the shadows of three figures.
From the collapsing tunnels around them, one could occasionally hear small, scattered sounds, like the noises of deformed creatures following the scent.
But with his Golden Leg senior by his side, Su Lun was not worried at all.
This meditation lasted for two days and two nights.
Finally, Yuta woke up.
...
Su Lun had been keeping an eye on Yuta's condition; her breathing was steady, and her injuries were healing.
Suddenly, he sharply heard a change in Yuta's breathing and opened his eyes from his meditation.
Yuta looked like someone recovering from a severe illness, her expression blank for a moment as if she had just remembered what had happened.
She turned her head and saw Su Lun, her eyes filled with the joy of having survived a disaster.
A glance at the mysterious cloaked woman nearby also added a hint of caution to her pretty face.
Su Lun approached and asked, "Yuta, how are your injuries?"
As he spoke, he also did not shy away from checking her injuries himself.
Yuta responded, "They're mostly healed now."
At that moment, Mr. Jing also opened his eyes.
Realizing he had not formally introduced them, Su Lun said to Mr. Jing, "Sister, this is Yuta, a Druid from the White Wolf Tribe of the Dalu Clan."
Then turning to Yuta, he said, "This is my senior, Lady Ophelia Fei Isaac; you can also call her Mr. Jing."
Yuta nodded politely, her expression slightly reserved, and took the initiative to greet her, "Mr. Jing, hello."
After all, she was facing a presence whose seniority was immeasurably high.
Sir Isaac was a witness to the ancient pact signed with the ancestors of the Dalu Clan, his own daughter...
Truly a figure of ancestral stature.
Even without that connection, this mysterious Lady Ophelia was Su Lun's senior.
Yuta felt as if she were facing elders like the Clan Leader and Wolf Granny, which gave her a kind of invisible pressure.
Mr. Jing nodded.
Naturally reserved, her tone was just like that of a caring elder, as she said indifferently, "Being able to awaken the Sacred Totem of the Dalu Clan is also a recognition by the god of nature of a great Druid. You need not be so formal."
She naturally noticed the relationship between Su Lun and Yuta, and as she spoke, a smile appeared on her lips.
Hearing this, Yuta obediently nodded and said, "Yes."
Observing the tone of their conversation, Su Lun's expression became somewhat strange.
The two seemed normal enough, but suddenly... it felt like an adult speaking to a junior?
He commented internally that although his senior had lived for over a thousand years, she looked, in every aspect—appearance, temperament, and physique—nothing different from a young woman. Her character was also gentle and kind, and there shouldn't really be any generational gap.
It did not seem right for Yuta to be treating her like one would treat the Wolf Granny.
Su Lun recalled regular interactions with Mr. Jing. His senior, aside from being somewhat cold, did not seem to care about seniority much and was quite amiable.
He couldn't understand why.
And didn't know how to broach the topic.
Anyway, the atmosphere had become somewhat strange.
Their exchange was brief.
Noticing that a previous black hole had disappeared, Yuta couldn't hide her concern and directly asked, "Mr. Jing, how is the seal here? The God once decreed a divine edict for our Dalu Clan to guard this place..."
Mr. Jing responded, "The seal is secure. I have set up a barrier to make it less detectable. That deep-sea giant should not return anytime soon."
Relieved by this answer, Yuta sincerely said, "Thank you for resolving the crisis of our people and for saving me."
Though she expressed gratitude, the worry in her eyes did not completely dissipate.
The relic in the Cursed Valley had troubled their Dalu Clan for five hundred years, and now that it had been discovered by people like Luying, trouble would surely follow.
Mr. Jing, seeing the still troubled look on Yuta's face, guessed her thoughts and declared emphatically, "My father once represented human civilization in signing the pact with the Dalu Clan. Although times have changed and some humans have forsaken the agreement, my Isaac family has never forgotten. From now on, the pact between humans and the Dalu Clan will be upheld by us."
Hearing this, Su Lun included himself in the affirmation and nodded.
Far from viewing the pact as a burden, he felt honored to protect certain matters on behalf of civilization.
Upon hearing this, Yuta's eyes shimmered.
She crossed her arms in front of her chest and bowed deeply, "The Dalu Clan will forever remember this pact."
...
Yuta's injuries had mostly healed.
This visit to the Cursed Valley not only thwarted the heretics' attempt to break the seal, but by a fortunate coincidence, she also recovered one of the four sacred artifacts—the "Magic Cauldron of Dagda."
It was a complete success.
Moreover, she was the first Druid in five hundred years to reawaken to the call of the god of nature. This was tremendous news for the Dalu Clan. She needed to return quickly to the holy ground to share this exciting news with the Clan Leader and her people.
Moreover, a descendant of Sir Isaac had also personally arrived.
The Dalu Clan's friend deserved a grand welcome.
It seemed that everything was getting better.
The environment rich in the aura of death within the ruins was not suitable for Mr. Jing to recover his strength, so Su Lun and his two companions decided to set off immediately, heading to the Emerald Holy Land of the Dalu clan. Mr. Jing also needed to meet with the elders of the Dalu clan.
The Cursed Valley was fraught with dangers, but unlike the cautious approach Su Lun and his companion had taken earlier, their return was swift.
Now that the trio had a top-tier powerhouse among them, they didn't have to worry about any monsters.
What was originally a journey of half a month's duration, took just a few days as they were already approaching the Emerald Holy Land.
....
In these few days of constant companionship, although Yuta and Mr. Jing had become somewhat familiar with each other,
the atmosphere was still a bit strange.
Su Lun couldn't pinpoint what was odd.
But when he was alone with Mr. Jing, although they didn't speak much, they could occasionally joke around.
The same was even more so with Yuta, where laughter abounded, pleas were intense, and they could even engage in playful intimacy in the primeval forest.
However, when the three of them were together, the atmosphere would become eerily solemn, serious, and small talk was scarce.
Even when they did speak, it involved very serious matters, such as the troubles of the Dalu clan or current problems...
Su Lun guessed it might be because of Mr. Jing's seniority.
That day, the trio found a cave in the primeval jungle to stay for the night, planning to overnight.
The campfire was burning strong, roasted meat on the rack was fragrant, and some orange-red fruits were served on fresh leaves.
Yuta, like a host serving a guest, was passionately dividing the food.
Mr. Jing, being of a vampiric lineage, had little need for normal food and only ate a few bites out of courtesy.
Su Lun, on the other hand, had a great appetite; Yuta's grilling skills were impeccable, and the long journey required energy replenishment, so he feasted heartily.
Soon, night had fallen, and the sky was twinkling with brilliant stars.
The night in the Silent Forest was extraordinarily beautiful.
In the forest, the night breeze shook the leaves, creating a rustling sound like the continuous roar of ocean waves.
According to the past few days' routine, after dinner, the three of them would rest separately.
Because of the presence of others, Yuta couldn't make overly intimate gestures and usually lay down quietly next to Su Lun to sleep.
Mr. Jing would sit in meditation.
Until dawn.
Having spent several days together, Su Lun realized that Mr. Jing must have been injured during the previous battles, so he had not disturbed her throughout the trip.
But today, Mr. Jing seemed to have adjusted her condition.
After dinner, she didn't immediately enter meditation, but instead initiated some casual conversation.
She seemed quite excited about the Emerald Holy Land, saying, "My father once told me, the Sacred Lake Gaius Lake of the Dalu clan possesses a beauty of this world; under the sunlight, myriad glows descend from heaven, piercing through to the other world. I wonder if after a thousand years, the water of the Sacred Lake still holds the same scenery…"
Upon hearing this, Yuta's expression slightly dimmed, responding, "The steps to the Sacred Lake have been unvisited for hundreds of years. The elders in our clan say that only those called by the deities are worthy to ascend. I've only heard about the scenes of the Sacred Lake from the elders, I've never seen it…"
Mr. Jing's eyes slightly curved, "Oh, is that so."
They had been fine not talking, but once they started, Mr. Jing's "ancestral-tier" status immediately stood out.
What she knew and could talk about were all things known a thousand years ago.
And once Yuta responded, her words naturally revolved around "ancestral" legends. Mentioning those topics, Miss Druid always carried a strange reverence and slight nervousness.
Mr. Jing was a very serious person, especially with those she was not familiar with, hardly ever making jokes, so she always seemed rather aloof.
But Su Lun knew that his senior sister was actually quite easy to get along with.
So, the task of warming up the atmosphere was still up to him.
Hearing the two potentially leading the conversation to a standstill, he immediately took over, "Yuta, how much longer until we reach the Holy Land?"
In answering Su Lun's question, Yuta visibly relaxed more, "By tomorrow evening, we should arrive. When the clan leader and the elders learn of Mr. Jing's arrival, they will definitely be very happy…"
The closer they got to the Holy Land, the more intense her anticipation grew.
The prophecies passed down in her clan had now all been fulfilled, "The warrior honoring the ancient covenant will appear once again, rescue the clansmen, and bring back the sacred object."
It seemed now that the warriors were Mr. Su Lun and Mr. Jing.
In Yuta's eyes, it was as if she could already see the joyful cheers of her clansmen, her eyebrows curving like crescent moons with happiness.
Mr. Jing smiled but didn't speak.
It seemed as if she felt there wasn't much else to say.
Yuta wanted to say something, but due to restraint, she didn't.
They needed to find some topics.
Seizing the rare opportunity when Mr. Jing was free, Su Lun decided to bring up some of his doubts.
He said, "Senior sister, have you ever heard of the Cyclops race?"
"Cyclops?"
Mr. Jing seemed also unfamiliar with the term, but it also seemed vaguely familiar as she tried to recall, asking, "Where did you see this race?"
Su Lun said, "I saw it in the cursed space of the ruins in the Cursed Valley. In the city of giants, there was a mural, and I guess it could be the origin of the 'All-knowing Eye' talent…"
He detailed the content of the mural he had seen and shared some of his own speculations.
After listening, Mr. Jing appeared somewhat enlightened: "Now that you mention it, I do remember some things."
Pausing, it seemed she recalled something, her beautiful brows furrowing slightly, she continued, "My father traveled to many places when he was young. When I was a child, he used to tell me bedtime stories about his adventures in the western deserts and perilous seas. My father once mentioned that on some islands in those dangerous sea areas, he encountered a type of giant capable of battling dragons. I have a deep impression of it because in the story, that kind of giant had only one very large eye on its forehead…"
"Really?"
Su Lun also looked surprised and pleased.
He had never heard of the Cyclops race before, and by all accounts, they were considered an extinct species.
He asked this question to see if his world-wise senior fellow apprentice knew any legends, ancient books, or relics about the Cyclops.
Who would have thought that the Cyclops race still existed a thousand years ago?
Perhaps they still exist now!
"Hmm."
Mr. Jing nodded, naturally guessing why Su Lun had asked this question.
She continued, "Many human talents originally come from ancient deities. According to what you said, your 'All-knowing Eye' might indeed be directly related to the Cyclops race. If that's the case, your talent's second awakening might even take the shortcut of 'reverting to ancestral bloodline'."
Su Lun had merely asked out of curiosity, to see if he could learn more about the origin of the 'All-knowing Eye'.
Listening to Mr. Jing's explanation, it also pertained to a second awakening?
The second awakening of the 'Reaper of Death' could be pondered through the enlightenment from the brink of life and death. But for this All-knowing Eye, there was completely no clue.
Now, hearing this, it seemed possible to make some efforts in the bloodline aspect?
However, before Su Lun could ask in detail how this 'reverting to ancestral bloodline' worked, Mr. Jing poured a bucket of cold water over his thoughts, dispelling them.
She shifted the conversation and said, "However, these are, after all, mythological tales whose authenticity is uncertain. Besides, I'm not sure whether the Cyclops my father had seen is the same kind you spoke of. Most crucially, that island lies in the extremely dangerous sea region of the West Sea where dragons exist..."
"..."
Su Lun heard this and gave a bitter smile.
Indeed, a race involved with mythological stories wasn't that simple.
The topic uncovered, Mr. Jing's extensive knowledge was revealed.
She suddenly thought of something, and casually said, "Speaking of your 'All-knowing Eye', I remembered a very powerful talent that might be somewhat related to your ability."
Su Lun asked, "Oh?"
Mr. Jing said, "'S-009-Universal Deconstruction', also a Pupil Skill released through the eyes. This talent is very strong. As long as the gifted one can understand the composition of matters, they can break down everything into its primal structure. Speaking of which, it fits very well with your 'All-knowing Eye' talent. That talent requires self-understanding, and your talent understands everything. Moreover, the source of that talent, legend has it, also comes from an ancient deity."
At this point, she paused for a moment before continuing, "The myth you mentioned about 'gaining knowledge through eye extraction' makes me feel these two talents may have the same origin. However, level S talents are very rare. I have only heard of the 'Universal Deconstruction', and have never seen any gifted ones before."
At this, Su Lun's expression slightly changed.
But he didn't take it too much to heart.
Myths are indeed elusive, and adding legends and speculations makes it even less reliable.
He took it as his senior sister telling a rare story.
As the conversation went on, Su Lun suddenly remembered something. He took out a stone rune sealed in a box and asked, "By the way, Sister, Yuta, can you look at this and see if it has any use? I got this in the Cursed Space before."
As soon as Yuta saw it, sensing something, she said, "This appears to be a highly advanced solidified form of rune language. I can feel that the laws engraved within it are very complex..."
Su Lun spread his hands and said, "Hmm. This is a 'Replica of the Primal Rune'. But aside from the name, I also have no idea what it does."
Clearly, the alchemist understood runes better. Mr. Jing looked at the object and immediately realized what it was.
She sealed the box carefully, looked at it for a while, and exclaimed, "This is a great treasure. Even though it's a replica, the rune language structure it contains is among the most top-notch I've seen in over a thousand years."
If Mr. Jing said it was a great treasure, it naturally was so.
A glint of joy appeared in Su Lun's eyes, and he curiously asked, "Then...Sister, how do I use this?"
Mr. Jing evidently knew and casually responded, "Keep it close and slowly comprehend it. Once you thoroughly understand it, you might become the top master in the field of runes of this era. However, it demands very high requirements in terms of insight and proficiency in runes. You might need decades to completely grasp the high-level rune languages contained in it."
"Decades?"
Su Lun's eyelids twitched upon hearing this.
The use of this stone rune was indeed thrilling, but the method of using it was problematic.
He had looked at it many times for days and apart from the "???" information, he had comprehended nothing.
This situation indicated that he probably hadn't even reached the threshold of comprehension.
He might not understand it in his lifetime.
It felt like a very impractical thing...
Seeing Su Lun's expression, Mr. Jing smiled slightly, "If you want to quickly understand this thing, there actually is a clever shortcut."
Su Lun immediately responded, "There's a shortcut?"
His knowledge level was much lower than his senior sister's.
He knew a lot about low-tier stuff, but he was completely in the dark about the domain of these top-tier items.
Instead of directly answering, Mr. Jing said, "Alchemists are strong because they know how to utilize tools."
Having guessed something, Su Lun's eyes flickered, and he instantly said, "Sister, are you suggesting that I refine this object into a 'Promotion Material'?"
Mr. Jing smiled coyly, which was as good as a confirmation.
The conversation immediately opened a new train of thought, and Su Lun's mind raced.
....
The essence of Promotion Material is to help alchemists forcefully understand things they originally cannot comprehend.
Then to slowly digest it.
This is the strength of the human alchemic vocational system.
It is also the basis on which alchemists stand.
It's like Su Lun's second-level comprehension of the 'Space Law'.strictly speaking, he only used the Promotion Material to forcefully open a gate to peer into the Space Law. He understood just the superficial aspects, which definitely doesn't count as fully understanding it. How far he can go in the future still depends on the level of his later comprehension.
But this first step of opening the gate is the most crucial.
It is the first step from nothing to something.
Now that he had this 'Replica of the Primal Rune' in his hands, once he used the method of Promotion to forcefully understand it, his proficiency in runes would definitely improve qualitatively.
That's precisely what Su Lun needed at the moment.
'Rune Studies' in the early stages looked merely like drawing patterns, but in fact, this subject is one of the most profound branches in alchemy.
The early stage focuses on working on the patterns that require improvement in 'drawing skills'.
But after reaching the intermediate and advanced levels, it involved those mysterious realms, requiring an understanding of rules and a perception of natural laws.
Su Lun, currently in the field of runes, felt somewhat powerless.
It wasn't that his foundational skills were insufficient, but rather his understanding couldn't keep up anymore.
The Reaper's talent had solidified his foundation in a short time, which was very useful in the lower levels. But for complex runes post-fourth or fifth levels, or more complicated variant Lu'en runes, he felt extremely impotent.
Those advanced runes that needed to integrate laws and intentions, even if he tried to copy them exactly, he couldn't produce them.
It's like everyone can paint, and when copying a tiger, some people's work looks just like skin, but others make it seem "alive."
This is the divide between a rune master and a grandmaster.
Su Lun was now trapped in this bottleneck in the field of runes.
Advancing his skill further would be extremely slow.
If he really followed the usual process, relying on proficiency to improve, he estimated that it would take a lifetime to possibly reach the "Rune Grandmaster" level, depending also on insight.
Yet, rune skill was a capability that strongly amplified his combat power.
Su Lun himself was a Puppeteer, with a significant part of his strength lying in puppets.
And in making puppets, the greatest technical challenge lay in rune skills.
Especially with alchemical golems, the higher the level of the runes, the more powerful the final product.
Currently, it seemed his skills were not enough to support him in creating too powerful a puppet in a short time.
He felt that using an advancement to open the gates of runes was totally worth it!
....
Su Lun, listening to Mr. Jing mention this method, naturally knew how to operate it.
His senior sister didn't need to beat around the bush or be overly polite.
He directly asked, "Senior sister, if I want to refine this rune into a job material, what should I do?"
Ingredients aren't meant to be eaten directly; they need to be cooked first, easier to digest.
Professional advancement items are the same; forcefully digesting them would only waste such fine raw materials.
Mr. Jing, with a smile brimming with implications, guessed his thoughts and responded, "I might disappoint you, even though I know some basics, I don't have the specific blueprints for refinement."
"Ah..."
Hearing this response, a muscle in Su Lun's eye twitched.
Even senior sister didn't know?
Like a recipe for ingredients, the optimal combination is surely the result of countless failures and time.
Now with the materials in hand, it was impossible for Su Lun to slowly figure out how to refine them into job materials just by his own efforts.
The effort required might not be less than directly comprehending the rune.
Su Lun, seeing that trace of jest in his senior sister's expression and demeanor, knew there might be a turning point.
He directly asked, "Senior sister, do you know where we can find the blueprints for refinement?"
Mr. Jing did not keep him in suspense, saying directly, "Within the ranks of alchemists, there's a small classification called 'Rune Magician.' This branch specializes in runes. And they also have systematic methods of professional material refinement. The only problem is that traditional alchemy has been stagnant for nearly a thousand years, and I'm not sure how much of the tradition is left."
"Rune Magician?"
Su Lun pondered for a moment, his mind vaguely recalling some impressions.
Among the memories of the Reaper, at least one person had heard of this branch.
This was good news.
Mr. Jing thought of something else and added, "While I'm not quite sure where the practitioners of the Rune Magician lineage are today. Remember, there are other people in our organization, you can ask around more in the future. Everyone is very capable, and by now most should be accustomed to the world on the surface. More and more information will be available..."
"Oh."
Su Lun then realized he was not alone.
He was still a member of the "Mirror Organization."
Assassin "Lei," Red Demon "Kai," Number Nineteen, Mr. Hei, Card, Decay Flower...
And of course, the most familiar one, Qian Tiao.
Each one was a highly capable companion.
When he joined the Mirror Organization, he had been told that it was a loosely structured group, but everyone would help each other out.
Talking about this, Su Lun muttered, "I wonder how Qian Tiao is doing these days..."
"Her?"
Mr. Jing's face revealed a bit of helplessness, "I contacted her a few days ago, she's thoroughly enjoying being a pirate. I heard she's already made a bit of a name for herself in the North Sea."
Su Lun couldn't help but laugh and sighed, "She really became a pirate, huh."
Gang boss turned pirate captain does sound somewhat fitting.
....
As they chatted more, the three of them gathered around the fire, and laughter filled the air.
Su Lun picked some lighter topics.
Yuta occasionally chimed in.
She was very interested in Su Lun's past, listening intently. It was only now that she learned Mr. Su Lun had also once been a slave to others.
"Mr. Su Lun, how did you meet Mr. Jing?"
"I remember the first time I met Senior Sister was in a private room at a gambling house. Senior Sister was wearing a very stylish black dress..."
"Hmm, I remember it was about selecting a guide within the Cross Society. Qian Tiao recommended you. The first impression was quite good..."
"..."

chapters.title: Chapter 285 - 284: The Narwhal Slave Hunters
chapters.content:
The next morning, only a wisp of blue smoke remained in the campfire.
Su Lun and his two companions tidied up the traces of life in the cave and continued on their way.
Before long, three figures were quickly making their way through the dense primitive forest toward the Emerald Holy Land to the south.
The snow and fallen leaves bore a trail of very light footprints which the cold wind swept over, and as the snowflakes fell, they soon covered up the traces of their journey.
However, without any warning, Su Lun suddenly collapsed onto the ground.
Yuta quickly stopped and helped up Su Lun, whose eyes were shining with a red glow, and asked with concern, "Mr. Su Lun, what's wrong with you?"
Mr. Jing observed his condition, her elegant brows slightly furrowing, and said, "It must be the outburst of those negative spiritual powers."
As she spoke, she reached out her hand, pinched a single sorcerer's seal, and with a delicate finger touched Su Lun's forehead, uttering a light command, "Mirror Seal·Suppress!"
In an instant, a faint blue Hexagram Array sank into his forehead.
The clarity returned to Su Lun's eyes.
....
"Sorry for the trouble," he said.
Now that his sanity had regained control of his body, Su Lun looked at Mr. Jing and Yuta with a somewhat bitter smile at the corners of his eyes. "I don't know what happened, suddenly, I just heard the whispers of death..."
The [Eclipse] totem on his body had already completely collapsed when the time anomaly field was broken that day. Later, when he reaped the soul of the intelligence official and also used the Shadow of the Reaper and the black umbrella, it naturally backfired.
Just now, his attempt to forcefully suppress those irritable negative emotions had caused his body to fall uncontrollably.
However, this backfiring was within expectations.
The reason he wasn't too concerned was that Mr. Jing was by his side, so naturally there was no danger.
He had just thought he could hold on until returning to the Emerald Holy Land, but it erupted unexpectedly.
After Mr. Jing checked Su Lun's condition, her brows knit together slightly in concern. "I can't handle your current situation. I can only suppress it forcefully. If you can't find a permanent solution, you should try not to use the Reaper's second phase abilities in the future," she said.
"Understood."
Su Lun nodded.
He thought that upon his return, he could ask the Deer Tribe Chief and Wolf Granny to inscribe a new totem for him, which should sustain him for a while.
"Um..."
Yuta, who had been silent this whole time, finally spoke.
In front of her elder, she often appeared very reserved.
After waiting for Mr. Jing to finish speaking, she timidly interjected, "Mr. Su Lun, I have prayed to the Divine for this issue before, and He responded..."
"Huh?"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun was taken aback.
It was as if his brain had received a signal that needed processing.
Only after a moment did he come to realize what he had heard and asked in astonishment, "You... you prayed to the nature god about this?"
He knew that Yuta cared about him, but to pray to a deity—what was that about?
Communicating with a god, such an invaluable opportunity, and she used it to ask about this?
And more importantly, that deity actually responded?!
"Yes."
Yuta, still in the presence of an elder, blushed slightly as she explained, "It wasn't a deliberate prayer. The Divine can sense the true convictions and thoughts in a druid's heart. I... I have been concerned about Mr. Su Lun's mental affliction. So, when I was called upon, the Divine also knew of my thoughts. And then He responded..."
Su Lun listened, somewhat dumbfounded.
That works?
Mr. Jing, off to the side, seemed to think of something and a gentle smile appeared at the corner of her eyes.
Yuta naturally noticed that look and, stealing a glance at Mr. Jing, continued, "The laws of nature inherently contain all the beautiful emotions in the world, and the Divine does not mind the prayers of His devout followers. Besides, Mr. Su Lun, you saved our Dalu Tribe, which means you saved the Divine's followers; you're a friend of our Dalu Tribe. The oracle told me that if I go to Sacred Lake and pray, I will be able to use the Divine's power to inscribe a Sacred Totem that could probably completely solve Mr. Su Lun's problem."
"An oracle?"
Su Lun listened, his expression complex.
He finally realized that there might be a turning point in his mental affliction.
Originally the Dalu Tribe didn't have a seventh-tier Druid who could solve the problem.
But now Yuta had appeared, a Druid who had been summoned anew by the Divine, and she became a variable.
Su Lun also felt somewhat taken aback; he had actually received an oracle directly from the nature god?
Yet, Su Lun also had some concerns.
