```
Now that they couldn't find the cause, it was time to eliminate all the unsettling factors!
His eyes flashed with malice, and he barked an order, "Come on, gather all the villagers and chop them down! I want to see where that demon is hiding!"
A fifth-tier professional, he was considered a master anywhere he went.
Given the current situation, whether there was a conspiracy or it was indeed the work of a demon, if there truly was strength to wipe them out, they wouldn't be doing it surreptitiously.
Round up and kill everyone, and then the demon would surely show itself!
Upon hearing this command, the guide Yongshu immediately pleaded, "Lord, you can't kill! The demon is worshipped by the villagers of the Sword Forging Village with incense. It protects this place. Anyone who harms the villagers will surely be cursed."
Hearing this, Hanz was unmoved and shouted fiercely, "Do it!"
"Yes, Captain!"
The pirates obeyed the order, ready to go from house to house gathering people up.
It was then that someone finally noticed the object of worship was missing from the shrine.
"Captain Hanz, the sword is gone!"
"What sword?"
"The sword that was previously enshrined in the shrine!"
"Damn it, who the hell took that broken sword, hand it over!"
"..."
Despite the questioning, no one responded for a moment.
But it was at that moment a strange, cackling laugh suddenly rang out among them, a sound as terrifying as that of an evil spirit echoing in everyone's ears.
"Are you looking for this sword?"
...
The sudden response made the hundreds of people in the snowy field feel as if a poison snake had slithered up their spines, causing goosebumps to erupt all over their bodies.
Following the direction of the voice, they saw someone in the crowd draw a long sword.
It was one of the four squad captains who had come, the ninth squad captain "Rain Sword" Akos, with a bounty of 41 million Riso, a somewhat famous fourth-order swordsman.
Seeing this, Su Lun had already quietly retreated. The black crow on his shoulder cawed once, and he slightly curled the corners of his mouth upward, closed his right eye, and watched the increasingly interesting situation before him with great interest.
With a loud shout, Hanzi demanded, "Akos, what are you doing?!"
"Aren't you looking for me?"
Akos squeezed a few cold words through his teeth.
He cocked his head, his face stretching into an increasingly sinister smile, glanced at the crowd, and with a flick of his finger, "clang," the sword was drawn from its sheath.
In an instant, it was as if the gates of hell had been opened, and an evil aura suddenly enveloped the surroundings.
All eyes were mysteriously drawn to the blade of the sword.
Upon a closer look, they discovered that the blade bore patterns resembling eyes. It was at the moment of unsheathing that the eye pattern on the sword eerily opened up!
As if someone had abruptly woken from their sleep, the eyes snapped open!
It was... an actual human eye!
And the more fear-inducing sight was yet to come!
In that moment, as the long sword was fully drawn, the blade revealed countless eyes densely packed together. These eyes, both large and small, seemed to come alive, frequently moving, and staring at every person in the crowd from all directions.
It was then that Su Lun saw the full appearance of this "Demon Blade" for the first time.
'Ghost King Hundred Eyes Sojo'
Description: Ranked third among the twelve masterfully crafted famed swords; made from heavenly meteorite iron, it seals the demonic spirit of the Hundred Eyes Demon King, possessing the characteristics of inducing bleeding, breaking armor, resilience, and unstirred;
Demonic Power Characteristics: 1. [Blind] The user causes vision impairment to targets within a certain range and absolute blindness to targets with lower realms; 2. [Visible Hell] The powerful demonic power can invoke the darkest and most evil aspects from the depths of one's heart, showing the dreadful state of hell and confusing the mind; 3. [Transparent Vision] The user shares the vision of hundreds of eyes; 4. [Great Demonic Sword Qi] Possesses the sword qi of the Hundred Eyes Demon King, with the intensity of the sword qi affected by the user's Sword Dao prowess; [Cut the Spiritual Body] Can inflict slash damage to special spiritual bodies and target souls.
Detailed Explanation: The sword, worshipped with incense for a century, has become a hellish ghost blade, imbued with the swordsmanship, Sword Intent, and Sword Qi of its previous wielders; a spirited instrument chooses its master, and if not recognized by the Demonic Sword, whoever carries it will be eroded by demonic power, leading to permanent blindness, a nature for bloodshed, and a deranged mind.
Earlier in the room, Su Lun had seen the lavish attributes of this Demonic Sword.
Now that he had seen its full appearance, despite the somewhat horrifying design, he still found it breathtakingly impressive.
The attributes of this Demon Blade were definitely of the [Sealed Object] level.
Blindness, enhanced vision, damage to spiritual bodies...
Each characteristic was a surefire divine-level trait for a swordsman.
One could say that even a pig wielding this sword could instantly become a master of the Sword Dao.
However, the cost of usage was not small.
Su Lun had previously heard from Qiantiao that truly good swords had their own "temper," and not everyone could wield them.
Seeing the description of "path of hell" identified by the All-Seeing Eye, he felt it definitely wasn't suitable for him.
But since Qiantiao was the Rakshasa Woman, he wondered if she could use it?
...
The moment the long sword was drawn, an enormous centipede's phantom appeared abruptly behind the sword-wielding Akos!
The centipede was snow-white, tens of meters in length, its belly, and back covered with countless eyes, its thousand feet like sharp scythes, presenting a fearsome and intimidating appearance.
"Is this the demonic soul of the [Hundred Eyes Demon King] that's been sealed away?"
Su Lun raised an eyebrow, the reflection of the snow-white centipede shimmering in his left eye.
He was unprepared before, his vision stripped away, but now he was just enjoying the scene.
However, those pirates weren't so fortunate.
The moment the Demon Blade was unsheathed, those who were close by were immediately engulfed in darkness and screamed in fear.
"Ah... I can't see!"
"Damn it, what's wrong with my eyes..."
"..."
Ordinary people were not like Su Lun; even after being stripped of their vision, they still had other senses.
These ordinary pirates instantly became "blind while seeing."
Moreover, it was not just about being unable to see; they were probably witnessing the "scenery of hell."
Su Lun was well aware that the impact of such negative emotions could cause those of weak will to collapse instantly.
Those affected by the Demon Blade brandished their vicious expressions amidst great agony.
They pulled out their swords and began swinging at those around them as if everything in their eyes had become the most evil thing that needed to be killed...
Then, the slaughter began!
The "Rain Sword" Akos was originally a seasoned fourth-order swordsman proficient in intricate court swordsmanship, as dense as rain. Now with the Demon Blade in hand, his aura erupted in an instant, evolving from swordsman to sword expert, and then to great sword expert... and kept rising!
Around his body, snowflakes converged into a tornado, visibly forming a sword qi twister.
In that split second, the pirates whose visions had been stripped hadn't even had the chance to figure out what was happening before their bodies bore scale-like dense cuts, as if they had been sliced by countless blades...
With a single slash of his sword, Akos's sword qi extended hundreds of meters, leaving behind death and injury in its wake.
This sword qi was not something his rank should be able to unleash.
Even Su Lun, watching from a distance, was impressed.
But as much as he was amazed, he also noticed that Akos's mental state had completely descended into madness, thinking to himself, "He's completely controlled by the sword's demonic power indeed, truly living up to the name 'Demon Blade.'"
....
It seemed they were waiting for the pirates to converge in a group for an easy slaughter. That's when "Akos" suddenly made his move, blinding them first and then cutting them down with an area-wide sweep of Sword Qi. This tactic was near unbeatable.
When the Swordsmith Master Sojo Kenshin forged this sword, he must have intended to achieve this effect.
Pirates below the third rank didn't stand a chance to react; six to seven hundred pirates were instantly wiped out by several tornadoes of Sword Qi. The snowy ground was littered with limbs and severed arms; where it was once covered in a blanket of white, it was now stained crimson...
"Damn it, Akos, stop!"
"The boss has been possessed by a demon, brothers, stop him!"
"Don't harbor any illusions, kill him, or we'll all die here..."
"..."
The pirates were instantly stunned, but they quickly rallied together, preparing to kill him.
But "Akos" was already not weak, and with the Demonic Blade in his hand, it was as though he had grown hundreds of eyes on his body, letting him easily evade attacks from every direction. No sneak attack could touch him.
Even the fifth-rank "Tea Beard" Hanzi was pushed into an extremely awkward position, dodging desperately from place to place.
Being the strongest, "Akos" relentlessly pursued him, hacking wildly along the way.
After being deprived of sight, Hanzi could only rely on his hearing to dodge attacks.
Originally, having advanced to the fifth rank, he should have had an absolute suppressive advantage over those of the fourth rank.
But now, the situation was utterly one-sided.
"Akos" displayed superb swordsmanship, perfectly executing "technique overpowers strength." The Demonic Blade's armor-piercing effect allowed the blade to easily slice through elemental barriers, dealing fatal wounds to Hanzi.
If it weren't for his fifth-rank advancement, which had fused with void gear granting him Spatial Teleportation abilities, he would have been cut down by the blade already.
From a distance, Su Lun knew that the overall situation was settled.
There were originally hundreds of pirates, and there was a chance of success.
Although "Akos" had the Demonic Blade, after all, he was just one person.
Alas, the opponents were too weak.
The pirates were lazy and had never trained in any specialized combined attack tactics; mostly, they only knew two tactics: "swarm in" and "scatter."
Su Lun shook his head as he watched.
This was several classes below the team fighting cohesion he had seen practiced by the Judgement Legion.
This lot had already been left with shadows in their hearts by the demons at sea, their morale was naturally low. Now stunned by the impact, once they found they couldn't win, the vast majority thought about fleeing far away to save their own skins.
In the end, after several of Tea Beard Hanzi's close associates were chopped down, he was left struggling to hold his own and "Akos" landed several blows on him.
The pirates from the other squadrons, seeing the situation, also knew the tide had turned.
They had already been frightened out of their wits by the demon. When someone shouted "Run for it!", the remaining couple hundred pirates scattered outside the village.
....
"It's over..."
Su Lun watched the people flee, his eyes flickering with an unusual light.
The mastermind had never shown his face, relying on a handful of demons and a single Demonic Blade to block this group of pirates at the gates of the Mountain Hermit country.
However, it seemed the mastermind had no intention of completely annihilating them, letting these people escape could exaggerate the horror here when spread, most likely putting the blame on "demons causing chaos."
This way, faces were not completely torn, and any subsequent trouble would be much less.
In the future, anyone thinking about coming to Mountain Hermit would have to think twice. The King of the North Sea would also be informed of Mountain Hermit's stance and would weigh the pros and cons before considering the matter of taxation.
Su Lun's mind was racing as the battle before him was nearly concluded.
In the vast village, only corpses littered the ground.
"Akos" had killed everyone who was still breathing, and at that moment, he suddenly turned his head and saw Su Lun, who was standing in the snow with his umbrella.
The two locked eyes.
The man's eyes were white, and behind him, the ghostly white centipede shimmered with demonic power.
In the man's gaze, Su Lun saw the endless torments of hell.
Yet his face bore no fear.
Death was not an unfamiliar experience,
He was no stranger to it.
Suddenly, Su Lun flashed a devilish grin, his eyes full of ghostly amusement, "Seeing the sights of hell, tsk tsk, demonic power indeed triggers the most evil and fearful thoughts in people's hearts..."
He glanced at the sword in the man's hand and tilted his head, ready to face any attacks that might come at any moment.
But after several breaths of standoff, "Akos" suddenly avoided him, appearing to give up the intention to kill.
Then, under Su Lun's watchful eye, the man went mad!
After hacking wildly in the snow, he poked his own eyes out with his hands and then plunged the knife into his heart.
Su Lun observed the madness unfold with an expressionless face.
He murmured softly to himself as he looked at the body kneeling in the snow, "Demonic Blade."
He walked over.
Collecting the fragmented souls scattered among the corpses, Su Lun then stopped beside "Akos's" body.
He seemed to ponder something, hesitated for an instant, but eventually reached for the "Ghost King Hundred Eyes Sojo" embedded in the corpse.
...
Meanwhile, in a certain room.
Ever since the killing began, a pair of eyes had been coldly watching everything.
Seeing Su Lun ready to draw out the Demonic Blade, the onlooker chuckled, "Heh, overestimating oneself!"

chapters.title: Chapter 308 - 307: Gone for a Year
chapters.content:
"After Akos died, the overwhelming demonic energy of 'Onimaru Hyakume Munemasa' also began to fade. The eerie human eyes on the blade also closed, and this famed sword from legend returned to its original state."
The sinister energy gathered and disappeared completely, leaving the sword blade snow-white with densely packed cloud patterns. In the snowstorm, it looked particularly pleasing to the eye.
Su Lun admired it for a moment before slowly drawing the sword from the corpse.
As he pulled out the sword, the blood droplets on the blade, drawn by gravity, coalesced into larger drops, then ran down the blade and dropped onto the pristine snow, resembling splatters of red plum blossoms. Upon closer inspection, the blade did not have a single drop of blood on it, and its cold light gleamed visibly sharp to the naked eye.
Holding the sword handle, Su Lun immediately felt the sword's sinister aspects. Instantly, demonic energy scattered his reason, and his vision filled with endless scenes of terror. He saw the most evil thoughts at the bottom of his heart, saw the terrifying visions of infinite hell.
With the great weapon in hand, it seemed as if a voice at the bottom of his heart tempted him—kill, kill, kill...
A flash of red light in Su Lun's eyes was followed by a slight warmth in the 'Eclipse' totem on his chest, and then his clarity was restored.
For ordinary people, the assault of demonic energy could mean the difference between life and death. Even the most steadfast will, if exposed for a long time, would eventually erode.
Unfortunately for Su Lun, this was not a major issue. Be it frantic negative spiritual power or the visions of hell, he was no stranger to them.
The Sacred Totem of the Dalu tribe could perfectly devour those uncontrollable negative spiritual powers, so this Demon Blade posed no great threat in his hands.
Perhaps because he had not been transformed into a "sword slave," the 'Onimaru Hyakume Munemasa' held by Su Lun issued a soft ringing sound.
Su Lun's fingers tightened suddenly, firmly gripping the Demon Blade trying to break free.
To unload the oppressive demonic aura, he swung the blade forward, cutting a trench over ten meters long in the snow with a sharp burst of Sword Qi.
The sound of the Sword Qi tearing through the air faded into the wind, and Su Lun's eyes misted as he murmured to himself, "So powerful..."
The surging Sword Intent supported him, making him, a Puppeteer, momentarily think about changing professions.
Indeed too powerful.
The thought vanished in a flash.
Su Lun chuckled lightly.
Even though he held it in his hand, he still sensed the blade's resistance, and his eyebrows slightly furrowed with a hint of helplessness.
Su Lun was not afraid of the blade's malicious nature, but the blade also did not acknowledge him, a Puppeteer, as its master.
That feeling of "different professions, different paths" made him no longer want to try controlling the blade again.
Strangely enough,
with that thought, the blade in his hand quieted down as well.
Truly full of spirit.
Su Lun pursed his lips and mockingly said to himself, "Heh, I really can't use it."
He always believed that swords and blades were mere tools for killing—what is considered right or wrong depends entirely on the human heart.
The blade was called "demonic" because users attempted to employ powers beyond their control.
When no longer pursued, it ceased to act maliciously.
Su Lun raised one hand, crooked his finger, and used a thread of silk from afar to draw out a tattered cassock from the temple as well.
The cassock enveloped 'Onimaru Hyakume Munemasa,' which then completely calmed down.
Having done all this, his gaze caught something in a distant house behind him, revealing a meaningful smirk.
....
The person hiding inside the house watched as Su Lun drew 'Onimaru Hyakume Munemasa,' expecting another soul to fall to the sword.
But after watching for a while, she just stared as Su Lun calmly put away the blade, even wrapping it in a cassock.
This act truly surprised her.
Normally, anyone who got this blade would be instantly mad with demonic energy, wouldn't they?
The pair of eyes hidden in the darkness flashed coldly: "Does the North Sea Fleet actually have someone capable of taming 'Munemasa'? Could it be Oleg's hidden card?"
Although no one could control the blade for now, such a renowned sword could not possibly be just taken away by an outsider.
Thinking this, she went out.
...
Su Lun heard footsteps behind him, turned around, and saw the guide, Song Yong Jiushu, running over anxiously.
"Oh dear... are you alright, sir?"
This guy watched as Su Lun began to walk away and hurriedly followed, his steps slightly unsteady.
"What's going on?"
Su Lun, with an expressionless face, turned around and asked the obviously troubled guy. A teasing glint briefly appeared in his eyes as he jokingly said, "Oh, you're still alive?"
Yongshu's face stiffened, thinking he had gone unnoticed, and awkwardly said, "I was afraid of dying, so I hid. It saved my life, please forgive my cowardice, sir."
Seeing that Su Lun wasn't paying him any attention and was about to leave the village with the sword, he quickly tried to stop him: "Sir, this sword is a sacred offering of the Sword Forging Village. You cannot take it with you. It will bring you misfortune."
"Oh, will it?"
Hearing this, Su Lun chuckled lightly.
He naturally knew that taking the sword would bring misfortune to ordinary people, and the name Demon Blade was not unfounded.
Moreover, if he hadn't noticed anything unusual about the village, he probably wouldn't have thought of taking the village's treasured sword.
But now, the sword was merely a "tool" for this fellow to kill people.
Those villagers, no, there was a significant issue with this village too.
Su Lun narrowed his eyes and said, "What if I insist on taking it away?"
Upon hearing these forceful words, Yongshu's face darkened, and he said hesitantly, "This…"
Without revealing his identity, he couldn't keep this famed sword.
But once he did reveal it, the King of the North Sea would have an excuse to make trouble directly.
After all, the scheme of killing someone with a borrowed sword could still be blamed on the "Demon Blade".
But once someone revealed the truth, it would become a man-made event.
The problem would become unsolvable.
For a moment, the guide's face looked as troubled as a daisy, but he didn't show any flaw in his act as he pleaded, "Oh dear, please don't, my lord. On the boat before, and just now when entering the village, those nobles didn't listen to my advice, and that's why…"
Su Lun had no interest in continuing this charade with the fellow, and he interrupted his rambling with a teasing tone, "Mr. Guide, can you tell me what exactly is going on with this village?"
He knew that taking the sword away wouldn't be the end of it; rather than being ambushed on the road, it was better to clarify things right here.
Hearing this, panic flickered through Yongshu's eyes, unnoticeable to others. He attempted to feign ignorance again, "Ah? This is Sword Forging Village, haven't I told you before…"
"Heh."
Su Lun once again interrupted him with a cold laugh.
After walking around for a while and making his preparations, he stopped, and a fierce killing intent suddenly surged from him.
He stared intently at Yongshu's face, a glint of coldness flashed, and he said in a deep voice, "What I mean to say is, the people of Sword Forging Village died a year ago. Why are they still 'alive'?"
This was what he truly cared about.
Even more important than obtaining the Demon Blade!
Without figuring this out, he felt as if his understanding of the world was obscured by a barrier, so severe that it might make him doubt everything he saw!
"..."
Upon hearing this, Yongshu suddenly stopped, his face that had been currying favor by smiling ingratiatingly just moments earlier turned cold instantly.
He looked at Su Lun, dropping the pretense and said coldly, "How did you find out?"
"Planning to leave? Did you really think you could escape? You didn't think I was just making small talk all this way without a plan, did you…"
Su Lun had not failed to notice that this guy was preparing to flee.
But since Su Lun had chosen to unveil the truth, how could he give this person a chance to escape?
Even as he spoke, he unhesitatingly flexed his fingers, and countless sharp threads had already surrounded Yongshu, and in the next instant, would slice him into countless pieces.
....
Before entering the village, Su Lun only suspected that the guide had issues.
After entering the village, he knew there was a problem with the "Demon Blade".
But it was the conversation with Koike Koichiro that made him realize the entire village had issues!
Because he had seen Koike Teppei at the Geisha house and knew some of her family situations through their conversation.
Thus, his conversation with Koike Koichiro allowed him to quickly gain the other party's trust.
But it was this conversation that revealed a major problem!
Su Lun remembered clearly that Koike Teppei said she was sold nine years ago and is now sixteen years old; however, Koike Koichiro said he sold his daughter eight years ago, and she is now fifteen.
The difference of an entire year, yet all other information matched perfectly!
Such an important matter, neither person could have possibly gotten it wrong.
Moreover, since they did not know each other before, both had no motive or reason to lie to Su Lun.
Therefore, when Su Lun heard this "contradiction," he immediately sensed that something was amiss.
If the theory that one of them is lying is ruled out, then this discrepancy in time becomes significant.
Finally, after connecting all the clues, Su Lun came up with the most reasonable explanation: The people of "Sword Forging Village" had died a year ago!
But strangely, based on any method of discernment available to him at the moment, they should seem to be "living" people.
But in reality, in the most logical conclusion, they should be dead!
No, to be precise, it seemed as though the villagers of Sword Forging Village had been frozen in time a year ago,
Like... a frame of a movie film!
They appeared lifelike under specific conditions.
Su Lun had also suspected that he had inadvertently fallen into some special cursed space.
Even after carefully observing everything in the village, the All-knowing Eye could not detect any anomalies.
In such cases, either the cursed space was so vast that it was beyond his field of vision,
or this "Sword Forging Village" existed in a form that he temporarily could not understand.
Therefore, he urgently wanted to know the truth.
....
When Su Lun suddenly acted, the silk threads he had already set up instantly formed a solid trap, and "Song Yong Jiushu" had no chance to evade; the sharp threads instantly cut into his body.
Su Lun had not intended to kill him upon arrival and had thought of controlling him first to see how things would unfold, but as soon as the silk threads touched him, Yongshu's body deflated like a punctured balloon, and a skin husk fell down.
Indeed, the original guide had been replaced.
Su Lun silently commended how seamlessly this fellow had hidden, not showing the slightest sign of abnormality.
Meanwhile, with a "pop," a smoke bomb exploded, and a shadow escaped from the cage of silk threads.
"Ninpo: Vain Flash Shadow Kill Technique? Indeed, a ninja... But how could I let you escape so easily!"
Su Lun's eyes narrowed sharply, and as he opened his black umbrella, he immediately perceived abnormal fluctuations in the far-off dirt, still rapidly escaping towards the outskirts of the village.
"Subterranean Escape Technique?"
His eyes narrowed slightly.
This was his first encounter with a ninja, and he found this technique very astonishing.
Although there were similar Earth System Arts in alchemy, the principles were completely different.
Facing it for the first time, there was no trace to follow.
The ninjutsu of the Mountain Hermit country were unique; although there were many legends about the various mystical aspects of ninjutsu outside, almost no one had seen a truly highly skilled ninja. After all, they were believers in divinity, and some of the ninjutsu could not be explained by common sense.
Su Lun thought about the situation in this village,
Could it be some kind of ninjutsu?
His mind raced, but his actions did not slow down.
Su Lun had long heard that ninjas were adept at using the environment to hide themselves, but for someone with Soul Perception, it was almost ineffective.
The moment Yongshu attempted to flee underground, Su Lun raised his hand and fired a cannon shot.
With a loud "bang," the ground cracked open, and a person sprang out.
This individual was dressed in standard ninja attire, with only her cold eyes visible from behind her mask.
Previously unknown by what means, she had used human skin to disguise herself as Yongshu, even altering the perception of her soul's essence. Now back to her original form, she appeared to be about fourth tier. This was close to earlier estimations.
There were scorch marks on her clothes, clearly she hadn't completely avoided the earlier blast.
Su Lun didn't give his opponent a chance to catch her breath; as he forced her out of hiding, his fingers pulled, and dozens of silk threads stretched tightly once again.
The ninja drew a short dagger from her back, blocking several threads, but in the next instant, her body suddenly dissipated into a cloud of black mist, evidently using Ninjutsu again.
"The gap in '[Vain Flash]' is about 1.5 seconds; with that level, you cannot escape..."
Su Lun was still learning about ninjutsu, all these were merely probes.
After a few exchanges, he had also discerned some details about his opponent.
Ninjutsu was tricky, but once fully understood, he could find a way to counter it.
Su Lun used Flash to avoid two shurikens that came flying at him like lightning, then he teleported a hundred meters away and punched into the air.
He was well aware that the target was hiding in the air.
Before the ninja could escape, she felt a heavy kick land on her stomach.
She immediately realized that hiding was meaningless, as her opponent had another method to pinpoint her location. As her body bent like a shrimp, she exploded into a cloud of smoke again.
Su Lun, feeling a void under his foot, kicked onto a piece of clothing.
His gaze shifted to the graceful figure in the distance, and he was slightly surprised, "Ho... a female ninja, huh?"
The substitution technique in ninjutsu seemed to require shedding a layer each time?
...
Su Lun's eyes showed no emotional fluctuation as he chased after her again.
The female ninja actually had good skills and reactions; if she weren't so panicked, she wouldn't be in such a mess.
But as long as she decided to confront Su Lun, he could find a chance to kill her!
Unfortunately, her instincts were remarkable, and she was wholly focused on escaping; Su Lun couldn't do much to her in a short time.
But her instincts seemed to perceive something; when Su Lun was about to use his Human Skin Umbrella and his black scythe, she suddenly took out an ancient clay jar. Once she opened the lid, streams of black silk swarmed over.
"A yokai '[Enter Inner Sparrow]'? So that's how 'Yongshu's' skin husk came about."
Su Lun identified the item and did not dare to be careless.
This "Black Sand" was also one of the famous hundred ghosts of Mountain Hermit Country.
It was a type of parasitic ghost bird, smaller than human pores, that would swarm into human bodies and then consume all the tissue under the skin. The infested person wouldn't even realize they were dead and could still move normally... it was very bizarre.
Almost at the same time, Su Lun burst out with a bluish cold flame, and within the blink of an eye, it solidified into a giant spirit wearing armor made from shadows.
It was this layer of flame that overflowed, forming a barrier a few meters thick. The black sand ghost birds that came close were incinerated, unable to get near at all.
Seeing this scene, the serious-looking woman expressed a look of confusion and shock, and urgently shouted, "Secret Technique of 'No Servant,' are you from Ruei's group?"
At that moment, she was truly puzzled. She had thought he was one of Oleg's men, but seeing this method... Such proficiency in the Secret Technique of 'No Servant' definitely marked a complex identity!
But if he were one of Ruei's people, why would he be lurking in a pirate gang?
Moreover, the Dark Spiritual Power-driven cold flame of 'No Servant' and those used by the Ruei royal family were slightly different. The "Fire No Servant" divine shadow on Su Lun had a sinister and evil feel to it.
She seemed to have recognized something, and completely lost any intention of fighting, adding, "Wait, we can talk!"
"Hmph!"
Su Lun snorted coldly and ignored her.
Having witnessed the strangeness of ninjutsu, he did not dare to let his guard down.
He did not feel that giving the opponent a chance would enable him to maintain the upper hand.
If they were to talk, it would be after capturing her!
Just then, Su Lun, who had prepared earlier, shone a beam from his chessboard.
But this time, the chessboard missed for the first time.
Su Lun noticed the scenery around him change suddenly; the figure in front of him softened, as if melting like asphalt into a black shadow. Only a set of clothes were left behind, naturally, the ones the female ninja had been wearing.
The chessboard space hadn't trapped the person, but had trapped the shadow of the female ninja instead.
"Shadow Woman?"
Su Lun watched the escaping shadow and realized this was another type of monster.
There were soul fluctuations, clothes, and a covering of demonic aura; one couldn't distinguish the real from the fake.
Su Lun immediately released the space and returned to the snowy land, only to see no shadow of the female ninja.
His eyes showed deep thought as he picked up the clothes from the ground and kept them.
....
The person had run away, and Su Lun's face showed a trace of difficulty.
The female ninja was skilled in various ninjutsu escape techniques, making her very hard to kill.
However, his frustration was fleeting.
Although he hadn't obtained the "truth," fortunately, the Demon Blade had ended up in his hands, which was already a significant gain.
After chasing far out just now, Su Lun thought it over and quickly ran back towards the direction of the village.
But when he returned to the valley, he was once again shocked by the scene before him.
Not long ago, it was still "Sword Forging Village," but now it had turned into a pile of ruins. Like it had been through a great fire, in the snowy land, the former houses were only left with some charred wooden stakes. There were also corpses everywhere.
Su Lun stood in the snowy land, his expression growing increasingly solemn as he looked at the scene before him. His left eye gleamed brilliantly, turning frequently, yet he could not detect any anomalies.
He naturally judged that these charred marks were at least a year and a half old.
This was the real "Sword Forging Village."
But what about the Sword Forging Village he had seen before?
What about those "living people"?
If it were not for the "Ghost Circle Baimoku Sojo" in his hand and the real touchable corpses, he would really feel as if tonight's experience was a dream.
Su Lun wandered around the village, reaping some spoils of war, and after not finding any clues that could solve his puzzles, he quickly left the valley.
The Sword Forging Village was seeping strangeness from all quarters, and even in the chilly wind and heavy snow, he did not want to stay overnight.
The female ninja was very likely to return, and if one could not beat her alone, she could call for others.
...
Su Lun walked through the mountains, clearing his own trails as he went.
Now that the ninth fleet's vanguard was almost entirely wiped out, Su Lun's original infiltration plan naturally no longer worked.
Thinking it over, he contacted the gambler widow.
"Sister Qian Tiao, I've run into some situations..."
He briefly explained the previous situation.
Soon, a response came from the communicator, "That's good, the plan to assassinate 'Rune Old Man' had a bit of an accident, and I've run into a bit of trouble and need your help..."

chapters.title: Chapter 309 - 308 Shinfuku Mitsuko
chapters.content:
Su Lun braved the snowstorm and left Sword Forging Village, and didn't encounter any further accidents along the way.
Mountain Hermit Country did have monsters, but not to the extent that you'd run into a horde just by walking around, as had happened before.
Because it was premeditated, the vanguard of the Tenth Fleet had been scattered, and the crisis had naturally been resolved.
Su Lun traveled dozens of miles by night, stumbling upon a few wild beasts that lacked foresight and casually killing them, then found a cave to spend the night.
Early the next morning, he changed into the attire of a ronin from Mountain Hermit Country and left the Izumo region, heading for Chikada.
Senjo said she had run into a bit of trouble, and he needed to go there.
Although Mountain Hermit was poor, it was fortunate that there were horse carriage roads between the domains, and though the roads were in poor condition and muddy with snow, they were passable by carriage. Of course, that also meant they could be traversed by a mechanic motorcycle.
With a few hundred kilometers between the domains, it would not be timely to rely on his legs alone. Su Lun took out mechanical parts he had prepared in his storage space and assembled a steam off-road motorcycle, then raced along the road. Where there was a road, he rode; where there was a village, he tried to avoid it, using the eight-armed spider spear to cross mountains and ridges.
Finally, by the afternoon of the second day, he reached the agreed-upon location, the bamboo sea of Chikada Ryun Village.
...
At the same time, several people were hurrying along the road in a slightly disheveled state.
The person in the lead was Senjo, and beside her was a pale-faced man dressed as a samurai, who would have been recognized by Su Lun as the one he had seen outside the "Nagano-ya Geisha House" before. Behind them followed Lolota, holding a sword, and several black-clothed ninjas wearing masks.
The group had various injuries, with bloodstains on their clothing, new and old. It seemed they had been through several battles without time to tend their wounds and had been fleeing in haste. Especially Senjo, who had several congealed scabs on her body, but even weirder were the enigmatic sealing symbols densely covering her hands. The runes glowed subtly, as if rusted machinery, making her limbs extremely stiff.
As the sky darkened, their expressions became increasingly grave.
As if something terrible would descend upon the land once night fell.
The pale-faced man, anxiety written across his features and a gentle, apologetic demeanor, said, "Miss Senjo, I'm sorry, the failure of this operation is because I didn't provide detailed enough information, dragging you down with me. We simply can't kill the 'Ghost Samurai;' if we keep this up, I'm afraid we'll all be wiped out. They are after me; you don't need to risk your life following me any longer..."
Even though they had been chased for three days and nights, Senjo's valorous face showed not a hint of fear. Hearing this, she shook her head with a firm tone, "Having accepted employment, it is natural to keep the promise and protect you to the end."
The pale-faced man, unable to hide his gentle aura in distress, said, "No, what I mean is, the employment ends here. Since it's our information that was faulty, Miss Senjo, you aren't breaking the contract by not joining us in dangerous predicaments..."
Senjo, upon hearing this and looking towards the distant bamboo forest, spoke again, "The situation isn't that bad yet; my reinforcements should have already arrived."
"Reinforcements?"
Hearing this, the pale-faced man looked surprised, "But... this is Sagara of Uesugi, a person from the Shogunate. He must have received orders by now and is gathering samurai to hunt us down. Even if reinforcements do come, it'll likely be bad news at this point..."
This is Mountain Hermit Country, and all the domains have received orders to kill, making any number of reinforcements futile.
Senjo didn't argue and thought of something, "Let's try it. That guy is rather formidable. As long as we can take care of the Ghost Samurai, there shouldn't be a big problem."
Having said thus, the pale-faced man didn't continue to insist.
The group approached the bamboo forest and soon spotted a ronin with a wide-brimmed hat waiting on the road ahead.
Everyone tensed up in an instant, and the ninja guards had already drawn their swords.
However, Senjo recognized the person with one glance, relaxed slightly, and called out, "You're here, huh?"
Naturally, the ronin with the hat was Su Lun.
He looked at the ragged state of the few people before him, raised an eyebrow, and asked, "Senjo, I'm not too late, am I?"
Senjo smiled, "You're just in time."
Behind her, Lolota looked at Su Lun. Although she didn't recognize his disguised appearance, recognizing the voice, she guessed that this was Mr. Su Lun, the one who had helped them counterattack "Cyclops" Sock back in Blizzard City!
Recalling how he had single-handedly controlled a puppet army to withstand a thousand foes at sea, her little face immediately lit up with excitement.
Since they were quite familiar, she didn't hold back and greeted, "Mr. Su Lun!"
Su Lun smiled, walked over, and patted her head, "Lolota, long time no see."
Hearing their conversation, the pale-faced man, guarded by four ninjas, started in surprise; this was the assistance Senjo mentioned?
His gaze swept around the bamboo forest and saw no one else.
Only one person?
This was the assistance?
But, he didn't seem very strong.
Naturally, Su Lun also recognized the group from the soul fire within them as the people he saw before at "Nagano-ya Geisha House," the ones who had tried to assassinate the "Demon Sword" Ashi with Senjo.
Seeing the "Twelve Good Craftsman's Famed Sword 'Kiku-pattern Jingu Guard'" in Lolota's hands, he knew that their assassination was successful.
Thinking of the trouble Senjo mentioned, it seemed they had attempted to assassinate "Rune Old Man" and had failed...
The course of events was becoming clear.
To kill a son first, then his father, was to wipe out the Mountain Hermit Country Shogunate General's entire family.
Though he didn't know why they wished to do so.
Yet, having failed in their assassination, the situation didn't look good at all.
Senjo's soul fire was stronger than before, likely having advanced to the fifth rank. But her aura was very bizarre, and noting her hands covered in runes, Su Lun frowned and asked, "Senjo, what's wrong with your hands?"
"A small problem."
Qian Tiao still wore a carefree expression, "When I attempted to assassinate the Rune Old Man earlier, he got me with a sealing rune. The meridians in both my hands are restricted, preventing the flow of dark spiritual power, so I can't use it for now. But it's not a big issue, it's not life-threatening."
After a pause, she glanced at Su Lun again and asked without any pretense, "Young man Su Lun, can you solve it? Otherwise, it might get tricky when it gets dark."
A light flashed in Su Lun's left eye as he examined the mystical runes on Qian Tiao's arms, as if analyzing strands of data code, his mind swiftly deconstructing and interpreting to find the correct method of breaking the seal.
Moments later, he gave up and said solemnly, "The structure of this sealing rune is very complex, it appears to be a 'Hexa-Rune Chain Variant' of the Anti-Magic Rune language; the caster has set multiple traps, forcing a solution could injure you. I've detected some leads, but it may take a significant amount of time to break the seal."
Rune sealing is a bit like an encryption lock, which can only be opened with a specific way of encryption. If opened violently or incorrectly, it often either permanently locks or injures the victim of the spell.
Hearing this, Qian Tiao raised her eyebrows slightly, sounding a bit serious, "This could be troublesome. If the seal cannot be broken, my strength will be greatly limited. Once the ghost warriors come out, you might have to deal with them."
Su Lun looked at the sky; the winter sun always set early, and now the sky was darkening, with only a faint light lingering on the horizon, "Sister Qian Tiao, what exactly are these 'ghost warriors' you mentioned? How strong are they compared to other professionals?"
"Around the third or fourth rank, but the troublesome part is... they cannot be killed."
Qian Tiao said thoughtfully.
Recalling the dangers along the way, she added, "They're a kind of hellish yokai, somewhat like ghost types that only appear at night. The minor ones are manageable; though they can't be killed, they're not too threatening. The most troublesome is a major demon wearing a general's armor, with considerable demonic power. The armor is impervious to blades, and even if you kill its host, it will resurrect infinitely after death..."
"I see..."
Su Lun was listening to Qian Tiao's introduction, forming a rough concept of the 'ghost warriors' in his mind.
They sounded like entities that ignored physical damage, were immune to most spells, and resurrected after death... some sort of armored demon?
Indeed, traditional tactics would seem futile against them.
Meanwhile, the pale-faced man who had been observing Su Lun by Qian Tiao's side suddenly interjected, "Sir, I know some information about this monster..."
She had been listening to their conversation all along and knew that this man was a reinforcement trusted immensely by Miss Qian Tiao.
Although she was surprised that Su Lun was alone, his composure clearly indicated his strength.
She felt it necessary to share all the intelligence she had so they could face the situation together.
On hearing this, Su Lun slightly turned his attention toward her, he'd been preoccupied with Qian Tiao until now and hadn't noticed the others.
Seeing this, Qian Tiao managed to interject and introduce her, "This is Princess Shinfuku Mitsuko. Uh... her status is somewhat special."
Special?
Princess Shinfuku Mitsuko?
Was this a woman?
No wonder he had felt that the pale-faced man spoke with a certain softness.
But for some reason, Su Lun actually felt it was better that she was a woman.
After all, since assimilating the "X Serum," which boosted his charm over ten points, he hadn't encountered anyone who overwhelmed him in looks.
Previously, he thought this fair-faced individual was a match,
but now that he discovered she was a woman,
his mood suddenly improved.
Sensing the hesitation in Qian Tiao's words, Su Lun also perceived her unique status.
Qian Tiao didn't elaborate further and directly introduced Su Lun as well, "This is my friend, Su Lun."
Upon hearing Qian Tiao's introduction, the Princess bowed deeply at a ninety-degree angle, performing a greeting typical of Mountain Hermit Country.
Pausing briefly as if she felt it would be impolite to keep hiding her identity in this situation, she introduced herself, "My name is Shinfuku Mitsuko. It's a pleasure to meet you, Mr. Su Lun."
At this revelation, Su Lun was suddenly enlightened.
The Shinfuku family?
If he wasn't mistaken, Mountain Hermit Country only had one place with that surname.
It was the royal family of Edo in Mountain Hermit Country.
Was she royalty?
Not at all surprised that someone would show such a reaction upon hearing her name, Shinfuku Mitsuko said, "I apologize, Mr. Su Lun, but there's no time for details now. The ghost warriors will likely appear soon..."
Upon hearing the name and considering the situation in Mountain Hermit Country, Su Lun guessed why they had attempted to assassinate the "Mountain Hermit Old Man," who was the Shogunate General.
He didn't press for details, but nodded instead, "Alright, Princess, please explain the situation with the ghost warriors."
Shinfuku Mitsuko began to explain, "The armor is the famed 'Iron Red Scale Coating Five Plate Harness' from two hundred years ago, belonging to one of the strongest warriors of that era. It was the armor of Grand General Oda Nobuo from the Warring States period, who was killed by a traitorous vassal during the Honnoji Incident, leaving his lingering resentment embedded in the armor, which turned it into a powerful demon. Those ghost warriors were likewise transformed from the resentment of his subordinates... I'm not sure how those from the Black Dragon found them..."
Mountain Hermit Country is known for its famed swords, and its armors are similarly exquisite.
However, due to the complex craftsmanship and low production of such armor, which included weak spots for swordsmen to exploit, it was only suitable for sword-wielding warriors and didn't offer as comprehensive protection as the full-body knightly plate of Luying.
As a result, Mountain Hermit Country's armor wasn't as renowned internationally.
These 'ghost warriors' were spirits of the armor?
No, it should be the spirit of the armor.
After hearing the intelligence, Su Lun felt a certain confidence in dealing with them.
He suddenly thought of the Demon Blade "Onimaru Hyakume Masamune" he had just acquired.
Intending it as a gift for Chitose, he took it out.
"By the way, Chitose, I found a famed sword. Do you think you can use it?"
As he spoke, Su Lun took out the long sword wrapped in an old monk's robe.
Chitose, hearing this, didn't seem to care whether the sword was famous or not, but was more interested in the gesture itself, smiling with raised eyebrows: "Oh, is this a gift from you, Su Lun?"
"Yes."
Su Lun nodded, a calm smile on his face.
He unfolded the robe to reveal the snow-white scabbard and spoke gravely, "This blade is a bit sinister. Be careful with it and see if you can use it."
Chitose hadn't realized the sword's particularities yet, but affected by Su Lun's tone, she took him seriously and casually asked, "What kind of sword is it that's got you so tense, kid?"
The Demon Blade was very still, slowly revealing its true form.
Just then, Shinfuku Mitsuko, who was nearby, recognized the handle that was showing. She couldn't help exclaiming in shock, "Is this... the Demon Blade Masamune?"
Others might not recognize it, but how could she, a princess from the Mountain Hermit royal family, not know?
The moment she spoke, her face dramatically changed, and the four ninjas by her side also took on a stance as if they were facing a great enemy, retreating a good distance.
"Demon Blade?"
Upon hearing the name, Chitose was surprised, but more than that, she felt an expectation and excitement: "Is this the legendary famed sword 'Onimaru Hyakume Masamune'?"
"Yes."
Su Lun shrugged, seeing her reaction, and didn't forget to add a word of caution, "That's why I'm telling you it's tricky."
"Where did you find it, kid?"
When Chitose heard it was indeed the famous sword of great renown, her eyes immediately glimmered a faint green.
This was the pinnacle treasure that all swordsmen dream of!
When the robe was removed, just by looking at the scabbard, her excitement came out in a soft cry, "What a magnificent sword!"
Which swordsman could resist the temptation of a famed sword, especially when it was ranked third among unparalleled famed swords?
"It's a long story; I can explain later when we have time. This sword..."
Su Lun knew Chitose's character all too well; he had seen that gold-sparkling eagerness at the gambling table, clearly showing she was hooked.
He was about to warn her again about the evil nature of the blade when someone else spoke up first.
"Miss Chitose, be careful! Don't touch that sword!"
Shinfuku Mitsuko, who was nearby, suddenly interrupted, warning with a grave expression.
Although she didn't know why Su Lun had the Demon Blade, she knew that no one could control it.
Thinking that Su Lun and Chitose weren't aware of the sword's terrifying nature, she hastily said, "This sword has the great demon 'Hundred Eyes Demon King' sealed within. It's said to have become a hellish demonic weapon, and all its previous owners have met untimely deaths, resulting in endless slaughter... It's simply not something a living person can control!"
With someone else taking over the explanation, Su Lun saved his breath and supported her statement, "Princess Mitsuko is right."
He also raised his eyebrows, looking at Chitose and added, "So, Chitose, see if you can use it or not. If not, just keep it with me for the time being..."
"Hmm. I've already sensed the demonic power."
Chitose's excitement faded, replaced by an utterly solemn demeanor, as if she were facing a very sacred decision.
A good sword chooses its master.
Likewise, a swordsman also chooses a sword that fits them.
As she looked at the legendary famed sword, Chitose truly couldn't look away.
She listened to Su Lun's cautionary words but still took a deep breath and reached out her hand, unwavering, wanting to grasp the Demon Blade.
Su Lun was still worried and asked, "Are you sure?"
"Yes! But I may also die."
Chitose appeared indifferent, as if she had prepared herself for death in an instant, and firmly said, "I have no regrets. This is the resolve one has from the moment they start wielding a sword."
With that, she glanced at Su Lun, her eyes shimmering, and nodded slightly, "Thank you, regardless. I really like this gift."
"..."
Su Lun said no more.
He was well aware of Chitose's temperament; once she had made up her mind, she would go through with it.
Mr. Jing once said that Chitose's progress in the Sword Dao was directly related to her genuine dedication to it.
In her world, what she loved most was undoubtedly the sword.
However, as it was a gift from him, and she was still in his presence, how could Su Lun let Chitose fall into danger?
Silken threads had already silently covered Chitose's entire body, ready to control her immediately if anything went wrong.
As for spiritual distortion and the like, Su Lun had plenty of experience to deal with it.
If things truly got out of hand, he would first sever the control of the nerves over the body, tie the person up, and take them to the sacred land of the Dalu clan to seek Yuta's help in dealing with it.
Su Lun was almost completely confident.
...
The Shinfuku Mitsuko nearby, however, was unaware of this. She watched as Chiyo planned to draw the "Demon Blade" forbidden by the Mountain Hermit, anxious and wanting to say something to dissuade her.
But just at that moment, a ghostly apparition of a fire-haired Rakshasa Woman burst forth from Chiyo's body, seething with blood and vapor.
Upon a closer look, her whole demeanor had suddenly become unreachably high.
Her Rakshasa aura actually resonated from afar with the demonic power of the blade, as if one were seeing two fierce flames burning.
"From now on, I shall be your master, is that fine..."
Chiyo took the "Onimaru Hundred Eyes Soujirou" and muttered to herself as if speaking to an old friend, caressing the blade with a face full of fascinated devotion.
With a "clang," the sharp blade slid from its sheath, and demonic energy surged skyward.
Su Lun frowned upon seeing this and his fingers trembled slightly, already preparing himself.
He had felt the weirdness of this Demon Blade firsthand before, and knew very well that this was the most dangerous moment.
At this point, Chiyo's aura was clashing intensely with the Demon Blade, as though she were taming a wild horse. The red glint in her eyes had already lit up, and the ghostly Rakshasa behind her became more and more solid.
The Rakshasa Woman had obtained a blade from hell, and it was as if the gates of hell had opened and she could see the endless landscapes of the netherworld in her eyes.
Even Su Lun, as a bystander, broke out in a cold sweat in an instant.
Chiyo, now holding the Demon Blade, seemed increasingly unfamiliar to him. She appeared neither human nor ghost, closer to a divine being...
If it hadn't been for the steadfast determination in her eyes, Su Lun would have no hesitation in controlling her and sheathing the blade again.
...
The overwhelming demonic power and Chiyo's already grand sword master level of oppressive feeling made Su Lun's scalp tingle.
The moment the Demon Blade was unsheathed, the Shinto Shrine Maiden and several Ninja guards had already retreated dozens of meters, their faces extremely solemn. Lolota had also been pulled far away by some threads to avoid the range of the overflowing Sword Qi.
Only Su Lun did not retreat half a step, fully focused on observing Chiyo's condition.
The Shinfuku Mitsuko, seeing the situation potentially getting out of control, bit her silver teeth, pulled out a string of golden bells, and suddenly a majestic aura also rose from her. It was another indescribable sensation that seemed to come from a high-ranking deity, ready to intervene if anything went wrong and prevent Chiyo from succumbing to the blade's possession.
"Kagura bells? A Shinto Shrine Maiden?"
Su Lun caught a glimpse of this scene from the corner of his eye and faintly guessed the Mitsuko's profession, somewhat surprised.
But at this moment, he couldn't afford to think about anything else.
He knew this was a critical moment for Chiyo to conquer the Demon Blade. Now was not the time for disorder, nor was it time to retreat. However, under the dual pressure of hierarchy and spiritual power, Su Lun was also struggling to endure.
That "Demon Blade Soujirou" in the hands of an exceptional sword wielder truly unleashed that world-defying, overwhelming demonic power.
Su Lun also faintly felt that things seemed to be getting out of hand.
The most dangerous aspect was that he saw the resolve in Chiyo's eyes starting to waver.
Chiyo suppressed the Demon Blade with her Sword Intent and aura, but the Hundred Eyes Demon King sealed within the blade seemed unwilling to be controlled and struggled more and more fiercely.
Both sides released ever-rising spiritual power.
Because she was a friend, she had never released her killing intent towards Su Lun before.
Now, directly confronting this aura, the Sword Intent oppressed Su Lun to the point where every hair on his body seemed to burst.
Su Lun, caught in the middle like a small boat floating on stormy seas, felt as if the surrounding tempest could overturn him at any moment.
Yet at the same time, the towering demonic aura also stirred up the violence in his heart, and a red light flashed in his eyes.
In the next instant, a ghostly apparition holding a black scythe suddenly rose behind Su Lun.
As the apparition manifested, a mysterious air enveloped the entire scene, drastically reducing the pressure. In an instant, the energies in the area were at a three-way standstill.
Su Lun appeared as if the true embodiment of Death had descended, his eyes dominating and unmatched. He glared at the blade of the Demon Blade where one after another vicious blood eye opened, his thoughts inexplicably irritable. If this damned blade really hurt Chiyo, no matter how good the blade was, it would be of no use!
As if sensing Su Lun's thoughts, the hysterical demonic energy of the Demon Blade suddenly retracted a bit.
Chiyo's right hand, which was holding the blade, finally stopped trembling more intensely. She switched to gripping the hilt with both hands, while the ghostly apparition of the Rakshasa Woman behind her also slowly started to form an evil longsword in her hands.
The storm was abating.
...
"Lord of the Netherworld, Rakshasa Divine General..."
At the same time, not far away, the Shinto Shrine Maiden holding the Kagura bells was utterly astonished. She watched the scene of the two confronting with their sword auras with disbelief shimmering in her eyes: "They...they..."
No wonder she was regarded by Sister Chiyo as reinforcement. So this Mr. Su Lun is truly that powerful!
(PS. Lord of the Netherworld ≈ the title for Death within the Mountain Hermit nation's Shinto religious system)

chapters.title: Chapter 310 - 309: Amaterasu and Tsukuyomi
chapters.content:
In the boundless bamboo sea, the rustling never ceased to the ear, as the wind and snow blew, sounding like the continuous roar of the ocean waves.
No one spoke; everyone watched the astonishing phenomenon in front of them with tense attention.
The Reaper, Six-Armed Flame Asura Woman, and the phantom of the great centipede demon conjured by the Demon Blade...
Though Su Lun didn't know what had happened before, he could tell that Chitose trusted the Shinto Shrine Maiden called Shinfuku Mitsuko. To ensure Chitose safely subdued the Demon Blade, he disregarded everything else and decisively used the second-tier ability of the Reaper to suppress the evil energy.
Fortunately, after the sword intent and the malevolent Qi contended for a while, the red light in Chitose's eyes gradually receded.
Su Lun also breathed a sigh of relief.
Finally, the redness fully retracted from Chitose's eyes, and her gaze became clear again. The long sword in her hands reverted from its fierce open-eyed state to its original pure white appearance.
"Tsk, tsk, tsk..."
Chitose clicked her tongue in amazement, swung a beautiful flourish with her sword, then sheathed it, not forgetting to express her admiration, "What an exceptional sword. Compared to the 'Kiku-pattern Jingū Ichisuke' ranked twelfth, this one ranked third is on a completely different level."
Seeing that she had fully contained her aura, Su Lun finally asked, "Have you subdued it?"
"Not yet."
Chitose raised an eyebrow, glanced at Su Lun with a touch of helplessness, and said, "The hundred-eyed spirits sealed in this Demon Blade were just frightened by you, that's why they've temporarily capitulated. It won't be easy to truly subdue it; it requires daily nurturing with Sword Qi."
"..."
Hearing this, Su Lun's brow furrowed slightly, and he hesitated over whether to persuade her further.
This Demon Blade felt like a ticking time bomb, unpredictable in its potential to explode.
Yet, unexpectedly, Chitose seemed completely unconcerned, casually affixing the blade to her waist with an air of great satisfaction.
She looked at Su Lun beside her, then hugged his shoulder openly and laughed, "I really like your gift."
Seeing her demeanor, Su Lun knew he wouldn't be able to dissuade her and shrugged, saying, "As long as you like it."
He had already made up his mind to keep an eye on this gambling-addicted lady's condition, lest she be harmed by the Demon Blade.
....
The onlookers who were at a distance, seeing that Chitose was safe and sound, all approached.
Lolota ran over excitedly with a bright face, shouting, "Teacher!"
Although the girl was young, she was also a formidable swordsman. Her gaze likewise fixed on the 'Onimaru Hyakumezsou Masanori' at Chitose's waist, unable to look away, "Teacher, do you want me to hold your sword for you?"
She wanted to touch it but was stopped by Chitose, "You can't handle this sword at your current realm."
Lolota pouted, her face full of regret, "Oh."
Then, Shinfuku Mitsuko approached, patting her chest as if a weight had been lifted, let out a long breath, and said, "Miss Chitose, what you did just now was really too risky."
She was still somewhat frightened and could also see that the malicious energy lingered around the blade, saying, "This Demon Blade holds the souls of countless who perished by its cuts, souls that not even the high monks of Senso-ji Temple could purify after years of chanting. Now that you carry it with you, it might bring you..."
Before she could finish, Mitsuko noticed the resolve of Chitose, the swordsman, and she swallowed her remaining words.
Thinking it over, Mitsuko then untied a red string from the handle of her Kagura bell and tied it to the end of the Demon Blade's hilt, completing it with a beautiful knot.
Su Lun appraised it for a moment, realizing that the red string was actually the Shinto spiritual implement "Amaterasu Exorcism String," which had the effect of warding off evil and subduing demons. Moreover, the effect was not weak; measured against alchemic items, it could also be considered of high quality. This gift was far from light.
With this string, the malevolent spirits sealed within the blade would be greatly restricted if they sought to cause trouble.
The ethereal red string adorned the snowy-white blade, instantly diminishing its sinister aura and making it look even more attractive. Chitose liked this new aesthetic, and she thanked Mitsuko, "Thank you, Miss Mitsuko."
"It's nothing."
Mitsuko nodded her head gently, showing a soft and gentle side of a woman, indicating she had no intention of continuing with her male disguise from before.
She then turned her gaze back toward Su Lun, asking curiously, "Mr. Su Lun, if I may be so bold as to ask, how did you come by this Demon Blade?"
Her look towards Su Lun was entirely different now. After seeing the phantom of the Lord of the Netherworld, she knew that the man before her was far from ordinary.
"It's a long story..."
The experience at the Sword Forging Village had also left Su Lun puzzled, and considering Miss Mitsuko was a Shinto Shrine Maiden of the Mountain Hermit nation, he thought she might know more.
He then recounted the situation, "I went to 'Sword Forging Village' before, and something strange happened..."
Upon hearing this, the bystanders listening to the bizarre experience all wore faces of disbelief.
Chitose exclaimed in astonishment, "You saw a destroyed village before, and the people inside were all alive?"
After all, she knew that Su Lun possessed the talent of the All-knowing Eye and could not be fooled by illusions.
Therefore, the situation became all the more eerie.
If it weren't for the guide who was actually a Ninja in disguise, one could really say it was "monsters causing chaos" with no one able to find any flaws.
But with the appearance of that Ninja, it was clearly a man-made trap.
Someone had artificially controlled the abnormalities of Sword Forging Village.
Even after hearing the story, Shinfuku Mitsuko wore a puzzled look on her face.
After pondering for a moment, she said, "The Demon Blade had been enshrined in the Sword Forging Village's shrine for over a hundred years, a fact known by very few. But a year ago, Sword Forging Village was suddenly engulfed by a bizarre fire, all villagers died, and 'Onimaru Hyakume Munemasa' also vanished without a trace. It's said to be the work of monsters, but the intelligence I received points to the involvement of the Black Dragon syndicate in the background."
Being a royal princess, she naturally knew some hidden information.
On hearing this, Chitose's beautiful visage tensed, "Are you saying, the mastermind behind this is also the Black Dragon syndicate?"
"Mm."
The Princess nodded, "Mr. Su Lun said that the person was skilled in Ninjitsu and controlling demons, probably a member of the Koga Ninja clan. The Black Dragon syndicate has many skilled members from the Ninja clans. They are loyal to the Takeda Shogunate."
Su Lun, hearing this "also", seemingly guessed what Chitose and the others had experienced.
The Black Dragon syndicate is the largest organization in Mountain Hermit, somewhat like a mafia but also serving as a semi-official intelligence agency. The organization is mainly active in the Edo region, with a mixed membership of ronin, Ninjas, martial artists, merchants, and various performers from the underworld.
Their puppet master, it is said, is the Shogunate General Takeda Nobuyasu (the alias of the Rune Old Man).
However, linking these facts, the logic also worked out. The agents of the King of the North Sea were coming to collect taxes and declare sovereignty, which would most affect the power holders of Mountain Hermit: the Shinfuku royal family and, of course, the Shogunate General with significant authority.
Having a motive to dispatch someone to assassinate is also plausible.
But Su Lun had little interest in power struggles. He was more curious about the 'year of disappearance' and directly asked, "Princess, do you know why I saw the already destroyed Sword Forging Village? Moreover, I am certain that I saw living people."
Upon hearing this, the Princess also showed a look of confusion, and after thinking it over, she said, "I'm not quite sure what that situation was. However, in our Mountain Hermit, there's a legend that the heavenly god 'Lord Tsukiyomi' has the power to create realistic illusions. It's said that under that type of Illusion Technique, everything is completely identical to the real world..."
Illusion Technique?
Su Lun frowned upon hearing this and looked up at the sky.
This answer did not help to resolve his confusion.
He had the All-knowing Eye, and unless this Illusion Technique was so advanced that it was beyond the scope of cognition, it would not be possible for him to miss any sign.
And besides, this was only a "legend," which was not very reliable.
He had previously studied some customs of Mountain Hermit and knew that people here worshiped a great number of gods, said to number in the tens of thousands.
The most famous of these were the sun god "Amaterasu Omikami"; and the moon god "Lord Tsukiyomi," also known as "Tsukuyomi-no-Mikami," the deity governing the night.
However, these were mythological tales; the era was too remote to distinguish between truth and fiction.
At least the nature gods worshipped by the Dalu clan still exist. The many gods of Mountain Hermit are now just stories to be listened to.
The Princess perhaps sensed Su Lun's thought and said with a sincere face, "Honestly, I am a Shinto Shrine Maiden of the Sugaha Shrine lineage. Although Shinto's influence is now weak, the gods truly exist. Mr. Su Lun, your situation, can only be most logically explained this way."
"Mm."
Su Lun, having listened, did not say much more; although he was an Alchemist, he still respected other people's religious beliefs.
Chitose, on the other hand, seemed to think of something, speaking with a grave expression, "Now that you mention it, I do recall some details of the previous assassination attempt."
Pausing, she added, "When we went to assassinate Takeda Nobuyasu, and that unexpected change occurred, could that not have been the same method? Otherwise, how could it be that you, Princess, had no hint at all."
Upon hearing this, the Princess seemed to realize something, her expression becoming serious, "I had always thought Takeda was the biggest enemy, but now it seems there might be an even more deeply hidden presence behind him. Otherwise, our well-prepared assassination should not have failed..."
The assassination attempt had failed in a very strange way.
Until now, no one could understand where the problem lay.
....
Su Lun listened to the two people's brief analysis and replay of events and also roughly understood what they had been up to before.
In the Mountain Hermit Kingdom, the "Shinfuku Clan" of the divine royal family seemed to be in power nominally.
But in reality, the actual authority was controlled by Takeda Nobuyasu, the Shogunate General, and many of the lords were also obedient to the shogunate.
The imperial power was in name only.
Furthermore, Su Lun also gleaned that there were some issues related to faith, which seemed to shake the foundation of the divine right of the Mountain Hermit Kingdom's imperial power.
Therefore, the royal family wanted to reclaim their power.
But with the Shogunate General holding significant power, it would be impossible to overthrow him by normal means.
The only way was assassination.
Shinfuku Mitsuko, the royal princess, had been secretly preparing for years to resolve the Takeda Shogunate through assassination.
And this time, it was about secretly recruiting a group of experts to ambush in the Edo residence.
However, the assassination plan, which was supposed to be fail-proof, collapsed due to some "bizarre mishap."
The circumstances were so strange that Senjo didn't understand how they had failed.
From the Princess, Su Lun also learned about the "Rune Old Man's" experiences after defecting from the Emperor Luying's empire to Mountain Hermit. This guy indeed had capabilities, climbing from being a mere son-in-law to his current position, just one step below the top, all within a mere twenty years.
One would have thought he'd be the final boss, but the assassination revealed there were hidden forces behind the scenes.
The more they analyzed the situation, the clearer it became. The Princess, after all, understood the state of Mountain Hermit. She suddenly said, "I've thought of someone!"
Senjo apparently also knew some inside information and guessed, "Are you thinking of... Yoteihime?"
"Yes!"
The Princess nodded, "That woman appeared after Takeda made a name for himself. Many domestic authorities were infatuated with her beauty. Now that I think about it, it seems as if there are no connections between the two, and yet there are countless ties. Takeda's smooth rise to Grand General definitely had some external force behind it!"
"..."
Su Lun listened with some confusion.
The legendary "Number one beauty under heaven"?
What did a courtesan have to do with governance?
It sounded like yet another tale of a beauty causing the downfall of a nation.
Although Su Lun wasn't clear about what exactly happened, he was aware that the "Rune Old Man" had defected with a powerful cursed object.
Could there be some connection?
The Princess seemed to have grasped a crucial point and stated confidently, "That's right! If we can escape this time, we must thoroughly investigate that woman's background when we return to Edo."
...
Watching the few people talking without any sign of leaving the bamboo forest, one of the Princess's guards suddenly returned and said, "Um... Your Royal Highness Princess, shouldn't we leave now? After nightfall, the [Ghost Warriors] will likely appear."
Upon hearing this, the Princess glanced at Senjo and then turned her questioning gaze to Su Lun.
She already knew that the "reinforcements" before her were not to be underestimated.
Currently unable to shake off the pursuit, she could only rely on these two people.
Senjo, too, understood the current situation and asked Su Lun, "Are you confident?"
Su Lun replied with a relaxed face, "I've made some preparations, and I'm somewhat confident. However, I haven't seen the [Ghost Warriors] with my own eyes, so I don't know if the measures I've prepared will really be effective."
Whether he could win or not, he wasn't a hundred percent sure.
But he felt quite confident about escaping and saving their lives.
So there was no need to feel urgent.
"Let's give it a try then. If we keep on running like this, we'll be cornered sooner or later anyway."
Hearing this, Senjo didn't say much; she simply sat down casually on the ground, heaving a sigh of relief, "I've hardly had a moment of peace in these three days and nights; it's a good time to rest now."
As she spoke, she looked at Su Lun and said nonchalantly, "I'm counting on you later."
"I'll do my best,"
Su Lun responded with a wry smile.
But since he was there to help, naturally he would give it his all.
Upon seeing Chisen's demeanor, Shinfuku Mitsuko also let out a small sigh of relief. She was always very polite, bowing and saying, "Mr. Su Lun, thank you for your trouble."
Su Lun was still somewhat unaccustomed to this formality and quickly said, "Please don't mention it."
At that moment, it seemed Chisen had thought of something. She took out a pottery jar from the cloth bag behind her and then pulled out a scroll, saying to Su Lun, "Oh right, these are for you."
"For me?"
Su Lun felt surprised. He looked at the dark pottery jar, which was identified as the "Soul Sealing Jar."
"Yes!"
Chisen said lazily, "Didn't you say you wanted the Magician's heritage? That's what the scroll is. And inside the pottery jar is the sealed soul of 'Ghost Sword' Ashi; that guy's rune expertise is not bad, I think you might need it. You owe Princess a thanks for her help."
"Ah...?"
Su Lun, hearing this, looked at the two items in his hands in disbelief.
The main reason he had come to Mountain Hermit was to find the Magician's heritage and then create the "Replica of the Primal Rune" to advance to the fourth order.
Now, he had it in his hands so easily?
This gave him an almost dreamlike, unreal feeling.
Princess, being perceptive, seemed to guess something and interjected appropriately, "Takeda initially came to Kamakura and, to quickly gain the trust of Lord Hosokawa, he handed over the heritage of the Secret Techniques he brought. Later, Hosokawa offered it to the imperial family, and that is the very one we have here. This was the condition of Chisen's agreement to our employ. For this, she also took a big risk."
Was this the condition for Chisen's attempt to assassinate Rune Old Man?
Su Lun, upon hearing this, finally understood that Chisen had already done so much for him without his knowledge.
The most reliable way he had previously thought to acquire the Magician's channel was to come to Mountain Hermit and target that "Rune Old Man." But a sixth-order professional was not so easy to kill, especially one who held military authority like the Shogunate General.
Even the second before they spoke, Su Lun hadn't thought of any other way to acquire the heritage, except for calling his senior sister to help.
But now, the Secret Technique was in his hands, as if by some fantastic dream.
Chisen, who seemed carefree and blithe on the outside, was actually very meticulous.
Even with the Secret Technique, learning and mastering it required exceptional talent.
She had also thoughtfully left the soul of 'Ghost Sword' Ashi.
Su Lun was not one to stand on ceremony, and with a raised eyebrow, he smiled, "Thanks, sister Chisen."
Their relationship was already quite close; they didn't need the formality of exchanging gifts.
As if he would hesitate to give Chisen a priceless Demon Blade.
Chisen was dozing with closed eyes and, without looking straight at him, casually said, "It's not as complicated as you think. I came to Mountain Hermit in search of the 'Sword Saint' Akutagawa Ryuichi to ask for the true solution of the Sword Dao. Helping you out... was just a matter of convenience..."
Su Lun smiled.
He was very clear in his mind that the danger of this trip to Edo was not as easy as Chisen made it seem.
....
Before long, nightfall came and the sky completely darkened.
The group made their repairs in the bamboo forest. Tonight's moonlight was beautiful, the bright white moonlight spilling over the land.
Su Lun sat in meditation as usual, his expression unchanged, while Chisen beside him continued to sleep soundly, and Lolita, holding a sword, looked very tense.
Not far away, the Princess and her ninja guards never lost the seriousness in their eyes, always keeping watch over the bamboo forest.
After all, the pursuers were coming for them.
Suddenly, a crow cawed "caw caw" from the bamboo branches.
Hearing the noise, Su Lun abruptly opened his eyes, looking at the depths of the dark bamboo forest, and exclaimed, "They're here!"

chapters.title: Chapter 311 - 310 Divine Weapon Descends
chapters.content:
```
The repeated pursuits over the past few days had cast a deep shadow on Shinfuku Mitsuko and her companions, and upon hearing Su Lun's words, "They're here," everyone immediately entered a state of combat readiness. The group of ninja bodyguards instantly drew their weapons and closed in to protect the Princess.
The atmosphere in the bamboo forest became instantly tense, and everyone could hear each other's heavy breathing.
The Princess glanced at Senjo, but her gaze actually lingered on Su Lun, conveying an unmistakable meaning: What do we do now?
Although she knew that Su Lun was certainly strong, he was after all just one person.
The ghost warriors were fallen warriors who already died in battle. They were numerous and still employed their military formation and encirclement tactics from life, with formidable combat strength. The key issue was their undying nature—that was the most troublesome part. In such a situation, even fifth- or sixth-rank professionals would find no advantage in battle. Otherwise, their group would not have been decimated to this extent.
If they were to clash head-on as they had in the past couple of days, there would undoubtedly be heavy casualties, and they might not even last until dawn.
With a formidable enemy on their heels, Senjo maintained her usual nonchalant demeanor of "indifference to life and death, quick to draw the blade". She noticed the Princess's gaze, shrugged her shoulders, and indicated for her to look at Su Lun at her side.
Feeling the stares of several eyes on him, Su Lun appeared calm, but he was actually feeling a bit of pressure.
Just by hearing how the ghost warriors had chased Senjo and the others to this miserable state let him know they were not to be underestimated.
His original plan before coming here was that, if truly overpowered, he would take Senjo and Lolo Ta with him and flee.
However, the reality was that the Princess was quite righteous, having urged them several times to split up and escape.
This actually made Su Lun feel that running away without a fight would be kind of... dishonorable.
Besides, it seemed Senjo's intention was to repay a favor by ensuring the safety of the Princess as much as possible.
Well then, he would give it his all.
...
Senjo's hands were sealed, and her hand seals were very stiff.
