She could not betray her own faith, but on the other hand, they were friends she believed she could share life and death with. Ultimately, she chose to sacrifice her life to give Su Lun and his companion a chance at survival..."
...
Hearing the Princess's answer, Izanami did not hide her mockery: "Heh heh... Such ludicrous sentiment!"
She suddenly became irate, almost scolding: "Foolish believer, then have it as you wish! You shall give up your life, and I will let your friend leave!"
The moment Su Lun heard this, he muttered, "This is trouble."
Gods, just like humans, possess jealousy, resentment, greed... all sorts of inferior traits.
According to legend, Izanami, because of her death, arrived in the Netherworld. Her partner, Izanagi, attempted to retrieve her. But on seeing her decayed body, he was horrified and fled in panic. Since then, Izanami has harbored "malice" towards the world of the living.
It was said that from that point on, she envied all perfect love, friendships, and familial bonds.
In layman's terms, this deity had some psychological issues.
Su Lun immediately spoke up to interrupt: "No! Princess, if you have the chance, leave this place first!"
He did not doubt that Izanami could send them away, but definitely not in exchange for the Princess's life.
Meanwhile, Senjo also perceived the determination in the Princess's expression and shouted, "Princess, don't do it!"
But it was already too late.
The Princess looked back at them, her lips curving with a sorrowful smile, "Mr. Su Lun, Senjo, I am delighted to have met you in this life. Knowing you has made my days the most wonderful..."
With those words, her body radiated a dazzling light. In the eyes of Su Lun and his companion, she transformed into a sky full of pink cherry blossom petals, scattering into the air.
The Princess knew all too well she was facing a true deity!
This was the only chance she saw for a living escape.
If she were to go, who else could communicate with this noble deity?
The fate of Su Lun and his companion was almost certain death.
The Princess could not be so selfish.
She decisively ended her life, not giving Su Lun, her companion, or even the noble deity the time to react.
Since the deity had agreed,
there would be no chance for her to regret once she was dead.
It was worth it.
...
The Princess's body dissipated upon the altar, her smiling visage vanishing amidst the profusion of cherry blossoms.
Senjo shouted in distress: "Princess!"
Su Lun clenched his teeth tightly, unable to utter a word, his expression dark.
He had pondered over every possible scenario beforehand, but had never anticipated this one.
Before his sorrow could unfold, it was then that voice from the heavens sounded once more with a hint of taunt: "Alright, since she chose to end her life in exchange for yours, decide amongst you, who will stay and who will leave..."
Upon hearing these words, Su Lun's gaze turned icy.
This was playing with human nature again...
In the eyes of that lofty deity, humans, these lower beings, were probably just a source of amusement in her endless years.

chapters.title: Chapter 343 - 342 Desperate Situation
chapters.content:
Death came unexpectedly.
The Princess gave up her own life, with a determined attitude that was heart-wrenching.
Su Lun watched the pink cherry blossoms disperse on the altar, his eyes filled with countless emotions.
At that moment, scenes of his acquaintance with the Princess flashed through his mind. This serene and elegant shrine maiden always presented herself with impeccable manners—pure, kind, fresh, and with an "antiquated" charm that often became the subject of teasing. When teased, her cheeks would blush; although a princess always waited on by others, she would clumsily assist him with his daily affairs; even though she had the chance to survive, she gave that chance away...
Although they hadn't known each other long, Su Lun had come to regard her as a very, very important friend.
Now, her life was fixed before him, dispersing with the drifting petals, never to return.
Su Lun raised his hand to catch some, but the petals slipped through his fingers. In his mind, he saw the Princess's tragically beautiful smile as she looked back at him.
Somehow, Su Lun felt an overwhelming sense of loss.
This was the first time he had experienced the death of someone very important to him.
It came so suddenly.
So unexpectedly.
It made him suddenly realize that life was indeed so pale, so fragile.
Like a breeze that had passed by, and upon reflection, she was no longer there.
Qian Tiao by his side was equally sorrowful.
The Princess had used her own life to provide them with a chance to leave.
But they didn't want it.
...
Just then, a mocking laughter came from the sky.
"Have you decided who you want me, the 'Yomi Country Lord,' to send away from the Netherworld?" She urged.
Every word in that sentence was filled with arrogance and sarcasm.
In Her eyes, whether Su Lun and his companion lived was merely a matter of Her benevolence.
Their lives, as insignificant as ants, hardly mattered.
Hearing this, Su Lun sneered inwardly.
No wonder they say that in the eyes of the gods, lowly humans are like ants.
Reminded by this, his swirling thoughts instantly cleared, and with a hand on his chest, he bowed and said, "Your Excellency, Yomi Country Lord, may I offer a price for you to send both my friend and me out of the Netherworld?"
"Oh?"
Upon hearing this, the entity in the sky seemed not at all surprised.
She did not hide her scorn as she said, "Greedy humans, do you really think you are worthy of speaking with me? If it were not for that foolish shrine maiden's choice to use her life to open a path for you, you would not even be worthy to stand before me."
In the eyes of Izanami, the entire Netherworld was Hers, including Su Lun and Qian Tiao at present. The two humans naturally had no bargaining power.
"..."
Su Lun remained unfazed upon hearing this.
Indeed, it had been a good decision not to go directly to the shrine to find this King; the choice was correct.
This negotiation was in no way equal, and they had nothing of interest to offer Her.
Rather, they were still alive probably because this deity was momentarily amused by playing with human nature and had indulged in extra conversation.
But...
Was She really a deity?
No, something must be wrong.
Even though Fujiwara Hayato was powerful, he could not surpass the rank of a "demigod" in this world, and the characters he created were definitely not "gods"!
Qian Tiao glanced at Su Lun.
She wanted Su Lun to agree to leave first.
But the words reached her lips and then retreated back down her throat.
Who would leave?
Nobody would.
There was an unspoken understanding between them that they would absolutely not abandon each other's lives just to survive alone.
Since there was no room for negotiation, Su Lun had no intention of wasting any more time on this path.
"If that's the case, Your Majesty, the great King, we give up the choice," he replied, still politely.
"Heh heh... Do you know what that means?"
Upon hearing this, Izanami's tone turned even colder, as if the sight of human nature twisted did not amuse her as she had hoped.
"Give up this opportunity, and your foolish friends on the other side will have died in vain," She said.
When Su Lun heard Her mentioning the Princess again, his face showed a slight change, and he said in a deep voice, "Yes, we've made our decision."
Pausing for a moment, knowing it was not wise to linger, he once again folded his arms across his chest in a salute and gestured to Qiantiao to prepare to leave.
But it was this attitude of shared life and death that seemed to completely infuriate the psychologically twisted deity. She thundered angrily, "Foolish humans, what if I insist on making you choose?"
In dialogue with a deity, one can only comply, there is no choice!
No sooner had the words fallen than a mountainous oppressive force instantly descended upon them.
It felt as if a mountain had been pressed down upon them both, leaving them gasping for breath.
This was tangible murderous intent!
If they did not choose, they would die.
...
Feeling this domineering and oppressive murderous intent, Su Lun's expression was very calm as he murmured to himself, "So we've finally come to this point..."
A violent glint suddenly flashed in his eyes.
It was as if all the endless rage had been provoked.
This was the scenario he had anticipated!
His life was his to fight for, not for the Princess to exchange with her own life!
Also, could Qiantiao's prophecy of death truly not be averted?
At this moment, there was a sense of impotent fury in Su Lun's heart.
If he were stronger, could he change everything?
He was very aware that from start to finish in the eyes of Izanami, they were ants that could be crushed at any moment.
It seemed as though they had a choice, but in reality, there was none.
Izanami would certainly not settle for an "incomplete ending."
However, this was also the worst-case scenario they had been prepared for from the very beginning.
"Heh..."
Su Lun's lips suddenly curled into an indifferent smirk.
Ignoring the presence above, he glanced at Qiantiao and spoke in a seemingly trivial manner, "I once asked my senior sister how to gather supremacy, and she asked me back whether I had ever risked my life for someone in this lifetime. I said no."
After a pause, he looked at Qiantiao's valiant face and smiled, "Now, I do."
If he had to live while bearing the lives of two friends,
He, Su Lun,
was not that spineless.
Hearing this, Qiantiao also smiled in response and shook her head, "Su Lun, I know you would definitely join me in death, and I would do the same. But if there's a chance, I want you to live well."
Red glints flared in Su Lun's eyes, unable to heed her words.
He bared his white teeth in a spiteful grin, the fury in his heart igniting instantly, and sneered, "Then let's fight for our lives first!"
If you've never risked your life for someone else, how can you peacefully allow someone else to die for you!
Just as he spoke, the phantom of the Reaper holding a scythe suddenly rose up behind him.
In an instant, the pressure vanished, and control over their bodies was regained immediately.
"Good! Then let's fight!"
Next to him, Qiantiao shouted valiantly, the Raksasha phantom with flames on its back appeared abruptly behind her. Her hand rested on the Demon Blade, and the Magatama thunder drums gathered instantly, with lightning snakes of dominance dancing all around her.
....
The two of them suddenly sprang into action, without any hesitation, turning around and charging fiercely towards the foot of Cangshan.
Watching their fleeing figures, Izanami in the sky let out a chilling, strange laugh, "Hahaha..."
Her jealousy of all the beautiful emotions in the world was now being performed one after another right before her eyes.
The attitudes of Su Lun and his companion had offended a supreme deity!
The voice of Izanami was almost twisted, "Foolish humans, do you think you can come and go as you please before the true presence of this deity!"
Now that the face had been torn off, there was no need for Su Lun to be polite.
He looked back, his left eye, the All-knowing Eye, directly challenging the existence in the sky.
He gazed upon the deity who had, perhaps, never been truly seen by humans.
And then, his pupils suddenly constricted.
It was this look that seemed to expose him to unspeakably horrific things.
"Indeed, it is the 'Great Terror' of legend..."
Su Lun trembled violently in his heart.
He couldn't describe the terrifying scene he had witnessed, even filtered through the All-knowing Eye, it remained ineffable.
If he hadn't been able to strip away his fear, this single look would have probably paralyzed him on the spot.
Legend had it that even Izanagi had been frightened by the decayed body of this Yomi Country Lord, this so-called "Great Terror" of the world was as the tales foretold!
It was this very look that brought a furious roar from the skies.
"Mortal, you dare to look directly at me! Ah... cursed be..."
Her exceedingly hideous body, to be seen by others?
And to look directly at it without being dominated by fear?
...
Hmph!
Su Lun sneered in his heart.
Out of sight, out of mind, but with this look, he found that the level of the Death laws concentrated by this Yomi Country Lord wasn't much higher than his own.
It was like comparing heights; although he fell short, he could see that Their height wasn't that much greater!
A divine tier?
Therein lay the problem!
In all other aspects, there were no flaws, but on the level of laws, They definitely did not reach the divine tier.
Su Lun felt that this might be one of his chances to break through.
The more critical the moment, the clearer his mind became.
Various countermeasures flashed rapidly through Su Lun's mind as he ran, his hands forming sorcerer's seals without cessation. The "Eight-Armed Spider Spear" and "Rune Vajra" spells were ready, poised for battle at any moment.
....
Su Lun and Qiantiao ran down the mountain at breakneck speed, as swift as fleeting light. In just a few breaths, the two of them had already reached the foot of Cangshan.
But at that moment, the infuriated Izanami moved!
It's unclear if it was out of disdain or some other limitation, but She did not kill them outright.
But then, suddenly, the skies stormed, and an exceedingly exaggerated surge of ghostly energy emerged near Cangshan.
Seventh tier?
Eighth tier?
Or even higher?
Su Lun had never seen such an exaggerated fluctuation of energy. He was greatly puzzled: How could Her realm of laws support summoning such an immense amount of ghostly energy?
In comparison, their two energies were like a frail boat always on the verge of capsizing amidst a tsunami.
This technique was beyond their capacity to resist.
Qiantiao's face showed a sudden change, and with a light shout, "Be careful!"
Before Su Lun could grasp why Izanami had such an almost "unanswerable" move at her disposal, the two of them saw the billowing evil aura form into a massive stone gate thousands of meters tall right in front of them.
The stone gate was ancient and thick, as if summoned from an aeon ago. The door was carved with countless ferocious ghost head reliefs, with various demons and monsters from Mountain Hermit intricately included. Standing in the void, it exuded a strong and mystical aura.
Su Lun couldn't make sense of the purpose behind the appearance of this massive gate. Upon appraisal, he realized it was a summoning spell—Divine Technique: Gate of Yomi.
In that moment, the stone gate slowly opened, like a dam releasing its waters, a myriad of evil spirits revealed themselves from behind the door.
An instant later, Qiantiao also understood the situation.
Behind the door was a vast, thick crowd of ghosts and demons, with various ghostly eyes shining with oily gleam—green, red, white... swarming in countless numbers.
This door had summoned all the evil spirits of the Yomi Country.
At the front, six of the "Eight Great Ghost Kings" of Ghost Town remained: River Red Child, Mirage Monster, Ghost Weasel, Seeing Over Hermit, Red Tongue, all present.
There were also various legendary Ghost Kings from hiding, such as the Nine-Tailed Tamamo-no-Mae, the Godly Great Tengu, the Ugly Hour Demoness, the Flying Head Barbarian...
Moreover, there were many legendary figures from history, all of whom could be seen.
Yomi Country Lord's summoning, all sorts of ghosts and demons responded without fail.
And behind these Ghost Kings, there were a million ghostly followers!
In an instant, a million ghosts poured out like a broken dam, turning the entire sky black with their ghastly qi, so dark that one couldn't see their own hand in front of them.
Upon seeing this, both Su Lun and Qian Tiao's faces drastically changed at the same time.
They thought they were facing a single enemy, but what they were facing was... the entire Netherworld!
....
Ghosts were wailing and wolves were howling, while chilly winds howled.
The two looked at each other.
Su Lun said, "Qian Tiao sister, this looks pretty bad..."
Qian Tiao's eyes blazed with a surging will to battle, showing no fear, "Didn't we anticipate this already?"
Her Sword Intent became sharper and sharper, like a spearhead charging towards the distant tide of ghosts and crashing into them.
Su Lun followed her with a wry smile.
Differently from the first day they arrived in Yomi Country, where they had been desperately trapped without escape, they had arranged a retreat in advance. The bombs Su Lun had placed in various canyons and ravines had also been effective, allowing them to escape along the way, setting off explosions.
"Boom-boom-boom~"
"Boom-boom-boom~"
"Boom-boom-boom~"
"..."
The mountains were collapsing and the earth was splitting, mountains exploded and collapsed, roads destroyed, bridges shattered...
Su Lun, having anticipated similar scenarios, made arrangements that were sufficiently capable of stopping a million-strong army.
Despite this, at least several dozen "Ghost King" level ghosts and those skilled in Escape Technique, still pursued them.
Without Izanami's summoning, Su Lun wouldn't have known the Netherworld was hiding so many formidable beings.
And an endless stream of ghosts continued to pour forth from the "Gate of Yomi".
Even though Su Lun and Qian Tiao were incredibly fast, the few Ghost Kings that entangled them slowed them down.
The Ghost King River Red Child had the ability to change mountains, rivers, and lakes, releasing a spell that transformed the terrain before them into a swamp...
Mirage Monster could conjure a mirage that left one in a fog, clueless of direction...
Ghost Weasel controlled the omnipresent ghost flames, unafraid of slashes...
Their methods were endless.
To become a Ghost King, each had their own cunning, causing endless troubles for Su Lun and Qian Tiao.
No matter which power they used, they would always encounter monsters that could counter them.
Luckily, Qian Tiao's Sword Intent had matured, making her combat prowess unparalleled.
With the Thunderous Hell in her hands, her Sword Qi cut hundreds of meters, clearing a path with a single stroke. Even those claiming to be indestructible like Shuten-doji had to avoid her sharp edge.
Otherwise, if they were at their previous strength when they first arrived, upon the opening of Yomi's doors, they would have been instantly overwhelmed by the deluge of ghosts.
Su Lun followed Qian Tiao, reaping the ghostly qi and Soul Shards of the ghosts they passed. The once-elusive Ghost Kings were now aplenty, which greatly boosted his "experience". The shadow of the Reaper behind him solidified more and more.
As his comprehension of the laws of Death increased, the feeling that was once like gazing through fog became clearer in Su Lun's heart.
He always felt that this was the key to breaking the situation!
...
But unfortunately, human effort has its limits.
Though Qian Tiao's slashes were ferocious, the wave of monsters showed no sign of diminishing.
Despite their best efforts to flee, Su Lun and Qian Tiao were ultimately surrounded and cut off by ghosts coming from all directions.

chapters.title: Chapter 344 - 343 Section 3 Rakshasa Woman
chapters.content:
"Sister Qian, let's head to the south. There's a ten-thousand-foot cliff behind the ruined temple where we stayed before. I'll take you down!"
"Okay!"
Su Lun had anticipated that they might be pursued.
His plan was to use the terrain to shake off their pursuers.
With the eight-armed spider spear, he could nearly ignore any terrain obstacle. With Qian Tiao clearing the way in front, he could look for opportunities to break through. Occasionally, using the silk thread to pull Qian Tiao along, their combined speed was definitely not slow. Even those ghosts flying in the sky could hardly catch up with them.
Just like right now.
At the beginning of the battle, this plan seemed to have no issues. It appeared that Su Lun and his partner were in danger, but there was actually a good chance of escaping to safety.
But gradually, problems began to arise.
This was the land of the Yellow Springs, home not only to monsters but also to that unfathomable King, Izanami.
That "divine being" clearly would not let them escape so easily.
Su Lun had not expected that Their methods could alter the course of mountains and rivers, making the sky fall and the earth collapse...
The terrain had turned into an obstacle for Su Lun and his companion's escape.
...
Before long, Su Lun and his partner reached the abyssal cliff which they had scouted before.
They had once spent the night in this ruined temple.
Behind the temple was an ancient pine tree, beside which stood a rudimentary stone table carved with a chessboard. From there, one used to be able to see the bottomless ten-thousand-foot cliff.
Su Lun had long thought of descending from there, following the river downstream through the depths. Such complex terrain would be difficult for the ghosts to follow.
But now, hope turned into despair when they looked.
The cliff...
Had actually disappeared without a trace!
In its place was a barren and bumpy landscape.
Seeing the cliff that had vanished without a trace, the faces of Su Lun and his partner turned very grim.
Although they did not know how Izanami managed to do it, it was no longer important.
This escape route was completely hopeless.
And what was worse, in the shared sight of the crows in the sky, the "Gate of the Yellow Springs" in the heavens continued to spew out ghosts without end. It was as if a hole had opened in the sky, and a black tide was pouring out from all sides.
Su Lun's face was somber.
This moment, he found himself in an unprecedented mental dilemma.
He could think of no strategy that could allow them to escape under this "absolute control."
Qian Tiao glanced at him and guessed what was happening, her expression hardly changing.
The two stopped running and did not continue.
They leaned against the ancient pine tree, gasping for breath.
Their furious flight had depleted their spiritual power considerably. Qian Tiao, whose sword Qi could slash hundreds of meters and who had slain several "Ghost Kings," was actually using moves that drained almost all her spiritual power.
She had been persisting only because Su Lun had told her there was a way out here.
However,
It turned out that there was no escape.
Qian Tiao calmed her heavy breathing and did not dwell on matters of life and death. Instead, she noticed that Su Lun was not himself and asked, "Su Lun, are you alright?"
"I'm fine."
Although Su Lun said that, an eerie gleam appeared in his eyes.
He knew exactly why Qian Tiao was asking.
Because the identification panel clearly showed several negative status effects like "Mild Corruption by the Qi of the Yellow Springs," "Moderate Pollution by Demon Qi," "Severe Pollution by Ghost Qi," and so on.
As Qian Tiao had fought her way through and Su Lun had reaped along his path, in a short time, he had absorbed a massive amount of demonic qi.
This qi was mixed with the Power of Faith, impurities, negative energy... and many other strange existences. It was too much to handle in one go, and his body simply couldn't digest it healthily.
By forcibly absorbing it, the demonic qi directly corroded his body and soul.
Su Lun's current condition seemed to be teetering on the edge of "half-human, half-ghost."
It was an emergency that threatened his life, even worse than the previous "mental aberration" condition.
But Su Lun had no choice.
His intuition told him that improving his "death rule" would be the key to breaking out of this situation.
Now that Izanami had confirmed it was impossible to communicate and had shown hostility, if Su Lun desperately didn't absorb that demonic energy, even if he escaped, he couldn't think of any other sliver of possibility to get out of this cursed space!
But now, it's still just a little...
Su Lun felt that he still needed a large amount of demonic energy, perhaps to see some "opportunity".
But at present, whether it was him or Qian Tiao, both were at their limits; it simply wasn't possible.
Besides, what if he bet wrong?
....
Is this where it ends?
Yes.
It seems there's no other way.
When one choses to face death head-on, no desperate situation will induce fear in her anymore.
With this thought, Qian Tiao's previously extremely solemn expression suddenly relaxed.
She noticed the hint of frenzy in Su Lun's brows and spoke calmly, "Su Lun, you've always been very composed and rational at any time before. It's this distinct quality of yours that gave me... a kind of indescribable sense of security. Don't blame yourself, you've already done very well."
Su Lun remained silent upon hearing this.
He did indeed blame himself.
He blamed himself for being powerless.
It was the same with the Princess before, and now with Qian Tiao as well.
After a pause,
Qian Tiao thought it was the end of her life, and it seemed like she should say something.
It seemed she recalled something, her eyes shimmering, she continued to speak, "Before, the Princess asked me if I liked you, I felt that was not the case. Later on, when I thought about it carefully, it wasn't that I didn't like you, but it wasn't that ambiguous feeling between a man and a woman either. To me, you are very special. If I had to say, perhaps, you are the most important man in my life? Yes... important enough for me to entrust my life with you."
At this point, she smiled sweetly, "So... even though I find some of your actions a bit dull, I didn't reject you either."
For the first time, Qian Tiao "confessed".
As she spoke, her always spirited and handsome face showed a hint of tenderness.
Her tone was very calm, and she didn't speak quickly.
But the calmer she was,
the more uncontrollable the frenzy in Su Lun's heart became, and the demonic red glint in his eyes grew harder to suppress.
Looking at the faint smile on Qian Tiao's face, he seemed to see the Princess's last parting smile.
A strong sense of desolation surged up.
He knew, he was about to lose something very, very important in his life.
Qian Tiao looked towards the approaching "wave of evil spirits" and thought there probably wasn't time to say much more, so she just said, "Su Lun, we definitely won't be able to escape like this. I know that without me, you actually have a chance to survive. If there's even a sliver of a chance to live, you... must find a way to survive."
Fury raged silently in Su Lun's heart; he wanted to do something but realized he was powerless.
The Eclipse Totem on his chest was burning hot, and the beast inside him seemed about to break out of its cage. He struggled to control his emotions, "Sister Qian Tiao, what are you talking about..."
Even if there was a real chance, how could I possibly abandon you and live alone?!
Qian Tiao understood his thoughts very well.
But she knew all the better that her dark spiritual power was already depleted, absolutely without the ability to make another charge like before.
When the monsters would enclose them, it would be their time of death.
It was time to make a choice.
She said directly, "My Rakshasa Woman talent has a secret technique that can 'seize all beings' essence and energy', this will be my strongest stance in this life. To die in battle is the fate of a Rakshasa Woman. In this lifetime, with the Sword Dao and friends, I have no regrets."
"I will try my best to create... even if it's just a sliver of an opportunity for you."
After a pause, she looked at Su Lun's near-ferocious expression, afraid that he would do something foolish, and added another sentence, "You are someone worthy of my entrusting my life to. Don't let my death... be in vain."
...
Close-combat professionals more or less all have a desperate secret technique, Su Lun has the Hormonal Burst, and Qian Tiao naturally has one as well.
Qian Tiao said this and took out a fist-sized rune case from the pocket she carried with her.
Su Lun had seen this kind of case before; it was once used by Mr. Jing to seal the limbs of the Fallen Angel.
Every member of the Jing organization had one of these.
Qian Tiao took out the rune case, without any hesitation, she made a hand seal with one hand and uttered softly, "Release!"
The runic glow on the case lit up as if triggering some mechanism, and the case opened.
In an instant, a flood of dark spiritual power burst out from the case!
Upon closer inspection, two jet-black finger segments were inside.
Even with just a finger, an intimidating pressure that made one's scalp tingle instantly swept through the area.
Qian Tiao gathered Gang Qi in her hand and took the finger out.
After a glance, she slightly raised her eyebrows, flicked her finger, and popped the two segments of the finger into her mouth, swallowing them directly.
At this point, Su Lun finally understood what she was doing.
She had cut off her own retreat.
The "Fallen Angel" was a true god-tier being. How could a fifth-order professional withstand the energy and laws contained in just one of its fingers?
It was like a radiation source; you can slowly draw energy from it, but you can't just devour it all at once.
No matter what the secret technique was, in the end, Qian Tiao was bound to die without a doubt.
Su Lun wanted to stop her from this crazy suicidal act.
But... it was too late.
And he couldn't bring himself to say it.
In the current situation, if they didn't fight with all they had, they would die all the same.
Neither of them had a choice.
...
After swallowing the finger of the Fallen Angel, Qian Tiao's body curled violently like a shrimp, and the veins on her forehead bulged instantly.
It seemed she was enduring immense pain, clenching her teeth tightly and emitting a low growl from her throat.
But at the same time, an absurdly overwhelming dark Spiritual Power, far beyond her rank, was erupting out like an avalanche, and it was getting more and more exaggerated!
And behind her, the almost collapsing second form of Rakshasa's shadow suddenly solidified.
Not just solidifying, the six-armed Rakshasa shadow, with flaming spikes and armored hide, eyes flashing like lightning, full of life, with the three magatama behind it glowing in the Radiance of Thunder, lit up the dilapidated temple with a purple-red glow.
Once this shadow appeared, it brought an overwhelming sensation as if a demon from hell had arrived.
Qian Tiao's six arms detached from her armor, holding six blades, her eyes fierce. The wild dark Spiritual Power surging through her was like flames, blazing furiously.
That wild Spiritual Power was ten times, dozens of times higher than before!
The uncontrolled outflow of dark Spiritual Power created shockwaves one after another, sending dust and pebbles flying and tiles shattering within the ruined temple.
However, as a consequence, her skin began to show patches of black energy spots, a sign of physical mutation.
....
A few breaths later, Qian Tiao seemed to have adapted to that violent energy.
She turned her head to look at Su Lun for the last time, smiled faintly, and said, "I'm going!"
With that, she stomped fiercely on the ground and with a "snap," the boulder where she stood shattered like a spider web into countless fragments.
At another glance, the shadow dispersed.
She had transformed into a purplish-red thunder dragon, charging into the ghost tide without any hesitation.
That figure, striding away sword in hand, was so proud and aloof.
Watching her figure, Su Lun had no thoughts of trying to escape for his own life.
"Sister Qian Tiao, if you're willing to die for me, how could I, Su Lun, be a coward who fears death?!" he thought with a fierce sneer in his heart, pulling out a spatial scroll, and instantly made a hand seal, "Seal·Release!"
With a "boom," a mecha armed with the Ship-Cutter landed heavily on the ground, naturally, it was the "Colonel-level Ship-Cutter IX Mechanical Armor."
The Mecha's defense was very strong, and it wouldn't be defeated by a common Ghost King in a short time.
But once this suit of armor was donned, it also meant losing the possibility of escape.
Once surrounded, there was nothing left but to fight to the end.
Just in the brief moment they delayed, the first batch of evil ghosts had already caught up and were ferociously attacking.
Su Lun was half a step slow in covering himself with the Mecha. With a "click," the helmet and the main body armor merged, and his eyes also showed a determination as sharp as a blade's edge.
After the steam boiler charged up with a "whoo" emitting white smoke, the pressure relief valve opened, and the heavy steel body charged like a truck straight into the ghost tide.
The Mecha, known as the "battlefield meat grinder," wasn't just for show.
The several meters long Ship-Cutter swung like a giant windmill; with every swing, it was sure to take dozens of lower-level monsters with it.
No demon dared to withstand the special vibrations of the Ship-Cutter.
Like a flesh-and-blood millstone, wherever Su Lun passed, he left behind a trail of severed limbs and broken bodies.
Even the spectral monsters that could ignore the steel armor and penetrate the cockpit could do nothing to him.
With Su Lun's current spiritual power, those spectral ghosts would find it hard to control him!
Amidst the horde of ghosts, Qian Tiao's might was even more exaggerated.
A massacre in all directions, no one dared to stand in the way.
After swallowing the "finger," she no longer worried about the darkness Spiritual Power.
Around her, in the sky of the region several miles around, there was lightning and thunder, with Sword Qi carrying the Sword Intent of "Radiance of Thunder" slashing down, and tens of thousands of bolts of lightning exploded from the sky towards the ground.
The "boom" sound was deafening, and a thousands of six-armed swords hacked through the horde of ghosts, creating storms of lightning and thunder.
Under the Ghost King, almost no ghost could be her match in a single strike. Above the Ghost King, there were few who dared to touch its sharpness.
Wherever she passed, corpses were strewn everywhere, filled with the stench of ghostly blood and severed limbs...
After the Demon Blade "Guimaru Hyakume Zongzheng" tasted blood, its power was even greater, and only now did it display the true might of a hellish demon weapon.
The two cleaved their way through like cutting vegetables, charging relentlessly.
Yet even with such fierceness, the two were like two drops of cold water in a pot of boiling oil. Although they caused a violent, boiling reaction, how could that extinguish the rolling oil?
Far from decreasing, the number of monsters was growing.
Su Lun's eyes were already bloodshot with killing.
He was still recklessly absorbing the demonic Qi and ghostly Qi from those monster corpses...
Hoping to grasp the last chance of a turnaround.
The feeling in his heart became clearer and clearer, but he was still a bit short.
It seemed there was no chance to see the true face of this cursed space world.
"Clang," "clang," "clang"....
The defensive shields on the battle Mecha emitted piercing cracks, as runes and plating layers were rapidly consumed.
Su Lun knew he couldn't last much longer.
It was the same for Qian Tiao.
Despite her ferocious appearance, with such an intense level of darkness Spiritual Power, her body could collapse at any moment.
Even though almost no demon dared to directly confront her, every time she slashed out with the "Radiance of Thunder," she couldn't help but spit out blood.
Her body simply couldn't withstand such an exaggerated energy surge.
Moreover, it was probably because of Izanami that those monsters, even though they knew death awaited, still rushed into the Radiance of Thunder Hell like moths to a flame.
They gave Qian Tiao no opportunity to catch her breath.
Su Lun looked at the figure fighting among the monsters, his heart filled with all sorts of unpleasant emotions.
To watch someone important to him die before his eyes, powerless to help, how utterly desperate.
Black Crow watched from a corner, sharing vision, and he saw in the sky that Izanami, filled with mockery.
This "deity" seemed to be watching a play, one that added not light but excitement to the underworld.
As for those ghosts, no matter how many died, she wasn't moved in the slightest.
...
Qian Tiao was very clear about her current state as well.
Just then, through the communicator, her last transmission came: "Su Lun, I've just had an epiphany, it seems I can break through to the third stage of Rakshasa Woman. I can probably create a chance for you. But I don't want you to see me in the state of a wretched death. You must find a way to survive..."
It was a farewell.
Her tone was tender like never before.
There was no hysteria, as if she was narrating something very ordinary.
It was like... the last words of an old friend.
Upon hearing her words, Su Lun, who had been bloodshot with killing, suddenly sobered up.
Looking again at the figure standing with a sword not far away, his eyes moistened.
It was right after the transmission ended that the Bodhi bead hanging from Qian Tiao's waist made a crisp sound as it shattered,
A dark golden Buddhist light infused into the Rakshasa phantom looming behind her.
In an instant, the Rakshasa phantom went from illusory to solid, seeming like it was cast from pure gold.
With a majestic appearance, it was fierce on one side, Buddhalike on the other.
Rakshasa Golden Body!
Seeing this, Su Lun was deeply shaken.
Qian Tiao had an epiphany just before her death, breaking through the third stage of Rakshasa Woman!
At that moment, the wind and clouds surged between heaven and earth.
Qian Tiao pointed her sword to the sky, laughed freely and heartily, and shouted loudly, "Izanami, do you dare to take my strike!"

chapters.title: Chapter 345 - 344: Their Story Ends
chapters.content:
Su Lun achieved enlightenment in the midst of battle and successfully advanced to the third rank of Rakshasa Woman.
At that moment, the six-armed Rakshasa behind her was no longer an illusion but a fiercely frowning golden body of cast gold. Upon closer inspection, it was slightly ethereal yet was the condensation of Gang Qi at its utmost purity. This Gang Qi, like armor, radiated golden light one foot from her body, visibly exuding an indestructible and substantial aura.
Su Lun's eyes were filled with darkness as he watched.
Both Mr. Jing and the previously encountered "Sword Saint" Akutagawa Ryuichi had praised her for possessing an almost immaculate heart of Sword Dao, which promised immeasurable mastery in her future sword path. Now, she had utilized the opportunity provided by the "Bodhi Seed" to break through the legendary triple talent unlock.
Unfortunately, it was her swan song.
As Su Lun herself said, this was the strongest she would ever be in this lifetime.
At that moment, she pointed her sword towards the sky, fearlessly invoking the name "Izanami."
The sky above was terrifyingly low, with tumbling purple-red thunderclouds seeming to slowly descend, rumbling as if to shatter the heavens with thunder.
Once the majestic Rakshasa Golden Body appeared, even the myriad demons and ghosts were stunned.
A group of Ghost Kings looked at each other, none daring to touch its sharpness.
Just then, it suddenly sounded as though a chant of Buddhist scriptures began resonating beside her ear, echoing through the heavens and earth.
"I see the evil ghosts of hell, Mara's forms, all forms do not enter my eyes... I see the Lords of Hell, the Yomi Country Lord, Yama, all gods do not disturb my heart... Across nine mountains and eight seas, there is nothing I cannot sever, all specters and spirits, there is none I cannot slash. With my sword drawn, I can split mountains, sever rivers, cleave seas, and slay demons and gods..."
Before these words had even finished, a strange phenomenon suddenly occurred in the sky.
A crack abruptly appeared in the thick thunderclouds, and a blinding golden light shone down from the gap. In the gloomy Land of Yomi, it was as if a golden sword had pierced down from the heavens.
Wherever the Buddha's light shone, evil spirits scrambled to evade, wailing in pain, instantly burned to ash by the radiance.
That beam of light ultimately pierced through the murky mists and shone upon Su Lun's Rakshasa Golden Body.
For a moment, the golden light intensely flared, as if a deity had descended.
As if prophesized by divine command, the Sword Intent accumulating within her also reached its peak with the chanting.
Furthermore, the inexhaustible dark Spiritual Power continuously gathered in the sword, the Sword Qi overflowing for three hundred meters. It seemed as if her single strike could shatter the entire Yomi.
Just then, an even more astonishing scene unfolded.
Looking up, a grand Rakshasa Golden Body of boundless golden light suddenly appeared in the crack, majestically overlooking all beings of Yomi.
Suddenly, the giant Rakshasa Golden Body in the sky frowned fiercely and glared at the Yomi Country Lord who had been watching the battle from the beginning.
Immediately afterward, there came the venomous curse of Izanami, offended, "Wretched ants, you dare to offend a great deity!"
"Hmph!"
Su Lun let out a cold shout.
Regardless of whether the Country Lord responded or not,
Her swing was already imbued with the intent to "slay a god."
But how could those mountain spirits and ghosts tolerate a human offending their revered Country Lord?
How could they allow Su Lun to bypass them and confront their king directly?
Although they instinctively feared the glaring Buddha's light, at the shout of the Ghost Kings, the immense spectral energy that had just calmed suddenly surged again.
That ghostly energy gathering black torrents sweeping across the sky,
like tidal waves crashing against the shore, seemed intent on extinguishing the Buddha's light in the sky.
But it was already too late.
The entire world was pitch black,
but suddenly, a beam of light lit up.
It was feeble,
isolated and forlorn,
but it...
pierced through the endless darkness!
With six arms wielding the sword, Su Lun charged fearlessly into the black tidal wave of ghosts, her mouth full of exhilarating laughter: "Hahahaha...Izanami, your demons and ghosts can't stop me!"
Like a War God, wherever she passed, she demolished all in her path, unstoppable.
....
At that moment, Su Lun had already charged up to Izanami,
The high and mighty deity seemingly felt fear for the first time.
Is He a god?
No!
He is far from it!
The "Fallen Angel" was indeed a genuine god-tier being. Could any part of its body be matched by Izanami, who attempted to simulate the appearance of a deity through unknown methods?
Under the pinnacle strike of Chizuru's blade, it too felt the fear of being erased.
At that moment, as the myriad ghosts failed to stop the human charging fiercely towards them, Izanami finally made her move.
She raised her hand, and a bizarre sea of green flames appeared in front of her.
Those flames, as if capable of burning everything, left nothing unburned in their path—be it mountains, rocks, vegetation, fairies, or ghosts.
Yet Chizuru did not stop advancing.
In the last instant before plunging into the green inferno, she looked back one last time.
It just so happened that her gaze met Su Lun's from afar.
The last backward glance of her life,
She smiled.
In Edo, the blind Qin Master had once foretold this scene: Chizuru would advance into the sea of fire with her sword, but her face would show no regrets, no complaints.
...
Ah...!
Ah...!!
Ah...!!!
Su Lun watched in agony as Chizuru's body began to burn.
He knew that Chizuru was creating an opportunity for him.
Without drawing Izanami's attention, even the strongest lifesaving methods would have been futile.
At that moment, Su Lun seemed to hallucinate, as if hearing those words of farewell again, "Su Lun, goodbye. Live well. Don't let my death be in vain."
Su Lun suddenly calmed from his almost frenzied state.
Afraid of dying?
No.
Having once experienced death, he no longer harbored such fear.
To die alongside someone he could entrust his life to was worth it for this lifetime.
Yet at this moment, the more he watched Chizuru's figure, the more those words echoed in his mind: "Don't let my death... be in vain."
Just like the previous Princess, Chizuru sacrificed her life hoping Su Lun would survive.
It was like being haunted.
That sentence echoed incessantly in his mind.
Why should I!? Why should I carry on living carrying the weight of your lives!?
Su Lun raged within, manipulating his mechanical armor to furiously battle through the ghostly mist tide, seemingly attempting to drown his sorrow with slaughter. He wanted to charge forward and join Chizuru in striking down that supreme deity.
But why...
Why am I powerless!
Su Lun could only watch helplessly.
The more he killed, the calmer he became within.
Suddenly, he stopped.
Just then, Chizuru roared from a distance, finally unleashing that long-accumulated ultimate secret Technique.
In Asakusa Temple, Su Lun had once practiced swordplay with Chizuru for a long time.
They had once had a conversation like this.
"Inside me lies the strongest sword, still uncut. But one day, it can cut down all gods and demons. Su Lun, help me choose a domineering name..."
"Tyrant Dragon Slash?"
"Pfft, could your naming be any more clichéd? Can't you think of a name... um, something that sounds poetic?"
"How about... Dawn of the New World?"
"Yes! That's it. My sword will bring the 'light of dawn,' a blade that brings hope."
"..."
And so, Chizuru had chosen a beautiful name for this sword technique—"Secret Art·Dawn of the New World!"
...
With a single slash, the towering Rakshasa Golden Body illusion in the sky also swept down its blade.
In an instant, thunder rained down filling the sky, the noise and movement reaching an exaggerated peak.
The rolling thunder elements pervaded the entire field of vision.
This slash directly shattered the "Gate of Yomi" in the sky.
The lightning connected into a net, covering vision, perception, energy fluctuations... everything.
The sea of lightning obliterated almost all the demons in the center of the battlefield that couldn't escape in time. Yet, right where Su Lun was, the lightning was slightly less potent.
Su Lun knew this was his only chance to survive.
This was what Qiantiao had sacrificed his life for.
Grief appeared in his eyes, he gritted his teeth, still made a magician's seal, and detached from the armor's cockpit.
No demon paid any attention to this spot; all eyes were drawn to Qiantiao's slash.
After a loud "rumble",
Su Lun could no longer hear or see.
....
He didn't know how long it had been.
Su Lun woke from his deep sleep.
He struggled a bit and realized he must have been buried.
Moments later, Su Lun's memories seemed to pick up from a "fragmented state".
"Did I survive..."
Su Lun murmured to himself.
But he couldn't muster any joy at having survived the ordeal.
He remembered everything.
Qiantiao had delivered the final sword strike.
Su Lun hadn't seen it.
He had jumped into a crevice in the ground, hidden himself, and now he had woken up.
This was a technique Su Lun had learned from Mr. Jing, a vampire's "Feigned Death Dormancy Technique," using some alchemist potions that allowed him to suspend breathing and reduce his bodily functions to an extremely low level to enter a state of feigned death. Together with the "Wrapping Cloths of an Oz Ice Man" to conceal his presence and a "body double" he had cultivated from his own body's tissues, these multiple methods almost completely blocked any means of detection.
It seemed the plan was a success.
He was still alive, which meant he hadn't been discovered by Izanami.
Su Lun struggled a bit and disengaged the "Thousand Threads" implant gear, sending sharp strands of filament into the soil's crevices, extending outward like plant roots.
Then, he felt the ground.
About ten meters above.
Using the filaments, Su Lun loosened the soil, straining like a zombie crawling out of a grave, finally able to breathe again.
He sighed with relief, shed the wrapping cloth, and looked around.
Due to that battle, the scene was a complete wreck; mountains and rivers were shattered, and the ground was fissured everywhere. More terrifying, a bottomless abyss abruptly appeared in the distance.
The abyss was oddly shaped in the form of a "T."
The horizontal part looked as if it had been burnt by flames, with obvious signs of scorching.
The vertical part of the cut was very sharp, dozens of meters across, as if it had been slashed.
Su Lun remembered the last scene he saw was Qiantiao charging at Izanami with that slash.
Had he killed her?
No.
The vertical slash marks were completely blocked by the scorch marks.
In his last glance, Su Lun identified the origin of those green flames.
[True Flames of the Fire God Kagutsuchi]
Detailed explanation: The unquenchable divine fire, one of the primeval true fires of the heavens; condensed from high-level gods' death laws and fire laws, it can burn everything; as long as there are targets, the flames will not extinguish.
"Even that sword Qi was burnt away..."
Su Lun looked at the traces of the battlefield, analyzing the results.
[Fire God Kagutsuchi] in the Mountain Hermit mythology is a very special existence, He is a divine child born by Izanami.
But because she gave birth to this Fire God, Izanami also died from those special flames, and thus became the Yomi Country Lord.
The flames controlled by this deity were the primal true flames that could kill a True God.
"Fujiwara Hayato really did find some special treasures... Could it really be from the Land of Yomi?"
Su Lun thought to himself, the curse space must naturally hold the collection of that great adventurer and literary master.
Suddenly, as these thoughts ran through his mind, it was as if thunder exploded in his head!
He realized, "I understand now... I finally understand what this cursed space is all about!"
....
Meanwhile, in the Land of Yomi, inside a tavern in Ghost Town.
An elegant old woman leisurely held a book, engrossed in reading.
The passing ghosts and monsters around her seemed not to see her, completely ignoring her presence.
As she read, she occasionally murmured to herself.
"Gustav, you still love writing tragic endings. Those tragic novels you wrote made readers throw stones and shattered a lot of your house's windows. Don't you know readers dislike such stories? Or, are you holding a grudge because I obeyed my family and married to the south?"
"You actually used high-level rune symbols to depict the deity in the book... Oh my, your literary talent truly has no match in this era."
"Oh...? If the world is a prison, then love is the key to unlocking it. You still leave some hope for those gorgeous romances."
"..."
She read the final ending in the book, which said: "Su Lun ultimately survived. Having absorbed a massive amount of ghost energy, he surpassed the threshold of Death's laws contained in space and saw the true nature of the world."
This was an unfinished book.
But the story concluded here.
Seeing this, the old woman seemed to glimpse an ending that satisfied her, and her eyes suddenly smiled, "Eh... I thought I might need to lend him a hand, but it seems not. Katya's judgment is indeed good. I really look forward to seeing how far that girl can go..."
The story continued, but she didn't keep reading.
Because at this point, the old woman saw the words the author left for her: "Natasha, I can't wait for you anymore. I can only leave my story in this book. I hope one day, you will read it."
Upon reading this, she smiled tenderly, her eyes blooming like flowers, as if she was responding across the ages to the writer, "Yes, I am here."
Having finished someone else's story, she seemed to decide to take action herself.
Holding the novel, she gently spoke to herself, "Gustav, you are gone, and I am also at the end of my life. Our story has reached its conclusion. But I know, you are surely waiting for me there. When this story is opened anew, our tale should begin anew as well. I am curious what I look like under your pen..."
Reaching this point, the elderly woman seemed to have used up her last bit of energy, as she slowly closed the thick novel.
With the anticipation of a young girl, she opened the never-before-opened first page and began reading from the beginning.
The story started with the words: "It was a sunny and pleasant morning; I finally enrolled in the much-longed-for Royal Academy of Rueil. And there, I met the most beautiful girl of my life..."
The old woman read on, tears brimming in her eyes.
Just then, something magical happened.
The scenery around her began to transform, as if the space itself was twisting and time rapidly rewinding.
The wrinkles on her face visibly changed. Deep creases slowly faded, then smoothed out, turning her visage into that of a jade-like young girl.
Her silver hair also gradually took on color, turning into a cascade of purple, wavy locks.
The shriveled and stooped figure became voluptuous, with a rounded chest and pert buttocks, exuding the unique beauty of youthful radiance.
Such an exceptionally radiant young girl she was.
Once, she too had been this young.
The surroundings shifted from Ghost Town to a classroom in the Royal Academy of Rueil.
She closed the brand-new notebook and heard someone greeting her.
Turning her head, a young man with a sunny expression extended his hand, introducing himself warmly, "Hello, my beautiful classmate, my name is Gustav. I am happy to meet you. I dream of becoming a great literary master and adventurer! Now, we are classmates."
He was not particularly handsome, and his clothes were cheap, indicating his humble background.
But the bright sunlight outside just happened to shine on his face, illuminating a pair of pretty light blue pupils that were deep and pure, as if hiding the stars in a summer night sky.
The purple-haired girl extended her slender hand, returning a noblewoman's smile, "Hello, my name is Natasha."
Their hands gently clasped together, each feeling the warmth of the other.
From their very first meeting, Natasha had a premonition that she was about to embark on a passionate love affair.
Just then.
Some notes appeared in a notebook describing the author's personal thoughts: "Actually, I've known all along that we weren't suitable, but you still refused all suitors and accompanied me on a path that had no outcome. Although it wasn't long, it was unforgettable. Natasha, I hold no grievances, only some regrets. It's regrettable that at the most dream-driven and empty time of my life, I met the most beautiful you. And this life, I am forever grateful for having met you... I've written our story into this novel, so that our youth will never fade. Forever loving you—Carl Gustav Jung."
The story of Gustav and Natasha, a commoner boy and a noble girl, concluded here.

chapters.title: Chapter 346 - 345 The Truth of the World
chapters.content:
```
"I've finally understood!"
A look of sudden realization appeared in Su Lun's eyes.
In the previous battle, he had devoured a great amount of demon qi like a whale consuming its prey, and the laws of death within him had also increased significantly. After several days of dormant rest, his body had completely absorbed those foreign energies.
Now awakened, Su Lun had a very clear feeling, that his understanding of the death laws had surpassed even Izanami, whom he had encountered before!
Since Izanami represented the upper limit of the laws of this world as the Yomi Country Lord,
It was precisely because he had broken through that "upper limit" that the foggy perception in Su Lun's mind had been swept away, becoming utterly clear.
"Wrong, so wrong… It turns out that from the very beginning, my line of thought was incorrect. The 'god' in the novel world isn't Izanami, nor is it any other character, but the 'author' of this story. He created this story, this 'world'!"
Su Lun took out the notes he had made and saw the clues he had written down; he understood everything.
He flipped through the notes rapidly, and the points that had previously baffled him, when viewed from a higher perspective, became instantly clear, "I had completely ignored the most crucial premise before—that I am trapped within a cursed world constructed by a novel's framework. In other words…I might have been dimensionally reduced! In this world, I feel like I am a 'person,' but in reality, I might just be a special existence described by a segment of text."
A single leaf obstructs the view!
Just like in a maze, your vision is always obstructed by walls.
Only when your horizon and cognition extend beyond the walls, can you see the correct path through the maze—and not be blindly burrowing through, following its designated logic.
"Previously, my logical thinking, world cognition, and judgment were all confined within a closed-loop circle, much like a maze. Without the ability to go beyond this 'upper limit,' I couldn't see the true nature of this world. Therefore, that is the difficulty of the 'T-grade space.' Without touching the limits of these laws, anyone who comes here is bound to die!"
Su Lun also instantly understood why, when they first arrived in the Netherworld, despite the ghosts being filled with hostility, they couldn't perceive it at all.
Under normal circumstances, this would be impossible.
Not to mention the Ghost King, why didn't they perceive the hostility from those lesser ghosts with their senses?
But in the logic of the book, it all made sense.
If the story's logic doesn't require you to discover (this plot), then, you won't discover it!
The dimension limits your imagination, forcing you to think along its designated logic.
Just as ants are unable to comprehend the construction of a highway next to their anthill.
In the cognition of such creatures, perhaps, it's akin to the end of the world.
A two-dimensional being cannot understand the concept of three-dimensional space either!
But does that mean they aren't living beings?
No, of course not!
Now, looking back, many encounters did have significant flaws.
But they have always gone unnoticed.
Fantasy manifesting within a perfectly closed logical loop and trapping people inside.
This is the greatest challenge of this cursed space.
Having thought through everything, Su Lun's eyes sparkled with vitality.
"The All-knowing Eye had actually identified the way out before, and even made great efforts to articulate the answer. However, after I entered the space, my cognition was limited, and I couldn't think of the 'author.' Thus, I also failed to realize the truth behind breaking the situation."
Su Lun couldn't help feeling a bit wistful.
What seemed like simple logic turned out to encapsulate a loop.
Within a certain world, that world dictates your imagination.
And so, you would never doubt any "illogicality" in this world.
Because, within this world, as long as something exists, it's considered logical.
Good heavens, that's inconceivable.
Su Lun felt as if he had touched upon some high-level "world enlightenment."
...
Ultimately, he knew how to get out.
At this thought, Su Lun released a long sigh of relief.
```
```
However, the excitement after the decryption only lasted a moment before his face regained its calm.
It seemed like he found out too late.
Qian Tiao and the Princess were dead, and he himself was in a "half-human half-ghost" state.
Since the author of the "Death Novel" was a "True God" of an unfinished story, could it be possible for him to rewrite the ending?
At that thought, a glimmer of hope reappeared in Su Lun's eyes.
If possible, he was willing to pay any price to save them both.
But he was also uncertain.
Because his current state was very strange — in the book, yet somehow transcending the story.
So,
if the past story had been set in stone, would there still be the present if the past ending changed?
This seemed to be a contradiction.
Su Lun pondered for a long time but couldn't come to a clear conclusion.
He noted this thought in his notebook, planning to find that "author" first.
That would be the decisive factor.
....
The battlefield was a mess, with the air of death lingering everywhere.
Su Lun summoned the black crow again, took to the skies, and found a road back following the direction of Ghost Town.
But as he walked, he suddenly felt something abnormal in his body.
Looking at the data panel, he exclaimed in surprise, "My physical strength has actually increased? And it's still continuing to grow..."
The displayed bodily data had skyrocketed by a large margin — strength, agility, neural response speed, resilience... it was an all-around increase, roughly by two or three tenths.
This would only happen during the injection of "X serum" for bloodline modification.
Originally, this would be a positive phenomenon.
However, Su Lun now frowned.
Because this increase was beyond his control.
How long it would last and in what direction it would grow were unpredictable.
Any uncontrolled body mutation could be called "mutation."
That is to say, he was now experiencing a "physical mutation."
The reason was naturally due to absorbing too much "demonic qi" and "Netherworld qi," which contaminated his body.
But due to certain factors, he had not completely mutated into a monster.
Checking the panel, Su Lun guessed it was his own "X serum" resisting the uncontrollable changes. The [Fallen Angel] was a genuinely divine-tier bloodline. From birth, they were gods. This was something lower beings could not compare with.
Just as he had suppressed the danger of a "mental mutation," he now found a new problem and felt somewhat troubled.
Nevertheless, he wasn't too concerned about his own state at the moment.
Dragging on a life only possible by carrying the lives of two important friends didn't seem worth celebrating or cherishing.
...
Su Lun walked on the mountain path at an unhurried pace.
Seeing the exaggerated signs of battle, images of fighting side by side with Qian Tiao flooded his mind, a mix of emotions: "Sister Qian Tiao's strength was really exaggerated. I never expected she would even break through to the third stage of the [Rakshasa Woman]..."
The world he saw now was quite special — like watching a sci-fi movie that was both real and illusory. He could immerse himself in it as if it were the real world, or he could observe everything from the perspective of an outsider and see some additional things.
Thinking of talent, Su Lun suddenly remembered that his Laws of Death had also increased manifold in an instant.
Although he hadn't broken through to any third-release state, there was a significant difference now.
A sudden insight struck Su Lun's mind.
```
```
Oh...
In my hand, there is a sealed forbidden item that requires control under the laws of Death?
The "Xiupunos's Night Scythe," this formidable weapon had been by my side since the days in Old Spiriton Outer City, helping me through one fatal crisis after another.
Though it slices through space fissures, the actual force driving it is the laws of Death. (Power, elements, once strong enough, can all create space fissures.)
A replica of the reaper's weapon is naturally governed by the laws of Death.
Because using this sealed item carries a very dangerous curse backlash, previously I could only use undead to control it, using them to divert the backlash.
But now, as soon as I grasped it, I immediately felt a sensation of effortless ease, as if there was some inexplicable "handiness."
It's as if I could control it?
Upon closer identification, I finally confirmed that I had reached the usage threshold for this sealed item!
"That means... from now on, I can use this black scythe at will, without worrying about curse backlash?"
I suddenly felt a sense of unexpected joy.
This is completely serendipitous.
Although I am now adept at controlling undead to use the black scythe, their endurance has its limits.
An undead could, at most, swing the blade five times, and I had to control the arc of the strike.
Handy, but wasteful of corpses, and superfluous motions that easily alert opponents.
Yet now, holding it myself, I can hack away as I please!
Ten slashes, a hundred slashes, a thousand slashes...
Until the target is chopped into mush.
I held the black scythe and casually swung once, a nearby rock was abruptly bisected by the space fissure.
I carefully sensed the feeling of using it, clearly capturing the entire process of the laws of Death surging from the scythe, activating the alchemy matrix and runes emitting energy fluctuations, and thought, "Hmm... it's not completely evading the curse's backlash. There will still be some if the cutting surface is too large. Nevertheless, this meets the normal need for slashing."
The scythe finally feels right in my hand.
And... something else that's different, previously using the black scythe was just about leveraging its inherent properties.
Now, having infused it with the laws of Death, I can control even the ripping degree of the space fissure!
It's like a sharp sword which is completely different in the hands of a swordsman compared to a layperson.
I feel like I've gotten stronger.
But at the same time, I let out a long sigh.
If I had been stronger before, maybe I could have changed something.
...
I wrapped the black scythe in a burlap bag and slung it over my back.
I entered the Ghost Town once more.
The author of this "Cursed Novel" is Fujiwara Hayato, and I know he is key to breaking the curse on this space.
I have harvested many random skills before, and although I'm no great writer, I have learned some of the common knowledge of novelists.
Therefore, though I'm not sure if Fujiwara Hayato will be in this Netherworld after his death, I can definitely find a "Fujiwara Hayato within the book."
In any novel, there's always a character that reflects some aspect of the "author," be it emotions, cognition, or values...
Usually, that's the protagonist of the novel.
But in this "Netherworld," I haven't found any main character.
So, I must search within the Ghost Town.
Different from the times I came here before with trepidation, as I now enter the city, my heart is calm and still.
As long as I don't want to, these ghosts and monsters seem as if they cannot see me at all.
```
```
He was an existence that had "transcended" this world.
The number of ghosts and monsters in the city had clearly decreased a lot, especially the powerful presences that were few and far between.
The previous battle had also caused Ghost Town to suffer a great deal.
Su Lun kept walking, walking, watching the various ghosts, and spirits of the dead like watching a movie.
Suddenly, as he passed a teahouse, he heard a storyteller narrating a "love story between a noble lady and a poor boy."
Su Lun stopped.
Because he was too eye-catching.
As if the entire world in his eyes was black and white, with only that person being in color.
Su Lun knew, he had found the person.
It was a monster, called the Storyteller.
They say he was a destitute scholar with some talent but neglected by others. After his death, his resentment turned him into a monster who kept telling stories, hoping to gain people's recognition.
The man saw Su Lun and, as if awakening from a deep dream, his eyes immediately became clearer.
He gave Su Lun a slight smile and said, "Has someone finally come to look for me?"
....
Su Lun and the man sat by the window on the second floor of the teahouse, looking at the dejected storyteller with a complex gaze.
He had seen this fellow several times before but never once realized that this monster might be the key to getting out.
Clearly, the clues lay within his stories, yet without having gone through the events himself, he couldn't grasp their deeper meanings.
Su Lun sighed and asked, "Should I address you as Mr. Fujiwara, or Mr. Gustav?"
The middle-aged man said indifferently, "Either is fine. Because they are both my names, yet I am neither of them. I am just a story character with a bit of obsession, that's all."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun pondered for a moment, then directly asked, "Can you tell me, what exactly is going on with the Netherworld?"
Even now, it all seemed like a complete "world."
It was precisely because of these past days' experiences that Su Lun's understanding of this world had deepened, making it all the more inconceivable.
Fujiwara Hayato chuckled and said, "But I know what puzzles you."
Pausing for a moment, he continued, "Actually, no matter how knowledgeable a person is or how many principles one understands, it's impossible to construct a completely flawless world. So, I thought of a method to use external forces to help me complete this world. That's why I turned the novels I wrote into cursing artifacts, to collect some souls of the dead. Those souls live and practice in the 'Netherworld Country.' Everything they experience is to perfect and simulate this world. It will become more and more perfected..."
"..."
Su Lun found this explanation to utterly overturn some of his understandings.
This guy actually used such a method to extrapolate and create a world?
This means, what's the difference with that of a god?
Fujiwara Hayato said, "Don't be so surprised. And don't think that this act is heartless. The laws of the world are very peculiar. Especially in the eyes of us magicians, all energy is in one 'pot,' merely in different forms; the essence isn't much different, including you and me. This isn't entirely my own idea either—I remember it was during an adventure, in an ancient ruin, where I discovered the secret techniques of the gods..."
"..."
Su Lun listened somewhat confused, only half-understanding.
He was very interested in this method of world creation.
Fujiwara Hayato had said only half but did not continue, "However, I can't explain too much to you... To ensure I keep certain specific memories and not forget the person I am waiting for. So, there are some questions I can't answer for you. If you want to know those truths, you'll have to verify them yourself."
On hearing this, Su Lun suddenly thought of Katusya's great-grandmother whom he had met before.
She bought so many of Fujiwara Hayato's novels; naturally, the two knew each other.
While Su Lun was curious about their relationship,
he was more concerned about another issue.
He directly asked, "Previously, my companions died in battle, is there a way to resurrect them?"
Fujiwara Hayato looked at him with a half-smile, "It's possible. But there's a cost."
```

chapters.title: Chapter 347 - 347: 346
chapters.content:
Su Lun sighed in relief when Fujiwara Hayato said there was a way.
Although he knew the cost would not be small.
He calmly asked, "May I ask, to resurrect my friend, what must I pay?"
Fujiwara Hayato glanced at him and answered directly, "Although your friend died in a dimensionally reduced novel world, which requires a relatively smaller price, reversing life is still taboo. Thus, you must still offer your soul to the 'demon'."
"Oh."
In the eyes of an alchemist, everything requires an equivalent exchange. Upon hearing this, Su Lun showed no surprise.
He even felt fortunate to have the qualifications to trade with a demon.
In the end, he was not powerless.
He asked, "What must I do?"
Fujiwara Hayato responded, "Since you managed to escape from this novel space, your soul has gained value to be claimed by a demon. Have you heard of the 'Cursed Ship'?"
"I have heard of it."
Su Lun nodded, recalling a story well-known among seafarers, "Sometimes on foggy nights, fortunate souls might encounter a ghost ship drifting on the sea. The ship is loaded with gold, silver, fine wines, and beautiful women, all of which you can freely take and enjoy. However, one must disembark before midnight, or they'll never be able to leave, and once the ghost ship vanishes, they must join the crew of spectral beings."
Fujiwara Hayato said, "I know an ancient secret technique for offering one's soul in a trade with a demon. You could naturally use it to resurrect your friend. The price is, at a specific time, you must board that 'Cursed Ship' and journey to its final destination. Put simply, you are paying your 'future' to the demon to fulfill your current wish."
"Is that all?"
Su Lun was quite surprised.
He thought it would involve sacrificing his soul and dying on the spot...
Was it just a matter of boarding a ship?
In his view, given his current physical condition and not knowing how long he would live, this was an ideal "price."
Su Lun also guessed that the "Cursed Ship" was no ordinary ghost ship. It seemed to involve some great secret.
"Yes. Do not underestimate this 'price'. The things you receive through equivalent exchange, what you get and what you must pay, are surely equally precious..."
"Thank you, Mr. Fujiwara. Please tell me that method."
"..."
Fujiwara Hayato revealed the method, and Su Lun carefully wrote it down.
Now he finally saw hope for the resurrection of the two women, and it lightened his heart.
He curiously asked, "Mr. Fujiwara, have you been on that ship?"
"Of course. I too have traded with demons for certain matters. But..."
Fujiwara Hayato appeared to struggle with a failing memory, stopping mid-sentence, "Sorry, my limited memory cannot offer you more explanations. This world holds too many secrets. If you wish to explore them, take a look for yourself. Being an adventurer is quite an interesting experience."
"Yes."
Su Lun nodded, not pressing further, as he had learned all he needed to know.
He glanced at the man before him and stood up saying, "I must take my leave, Mr. Fujiwara."
Fujiwara Hayato smiled, a look of satisfaction in his eyes, "Yes. Farewell, young man."
...
This cursed space could no longer confine Su Lun. As his thoughts shifted, the surroundings rapidly changed.
The uniquely bleak realm of the underworld gradually receded and the view brightened.
Su Lun saw the long-missed sunlight, warm on his skin.
Having been in the dark for so long, he was slightly unaccustomed and squinted his eyes, taking a good while to adapt.
Su Lun looked around and found himself back in Edo Castle, on the same desolate hill where he was previously swept up.
To his surprise, there were no sounds of war from within the city.
The "Black Sun Grand Festival" seemed to have passed, and the eclipse had ended, leaving fairly good weather.
Looking around, the city bore some signs of bombardment and battle scars.
"Wonder how long it's been outside..."
Su Lun murmured to himself, heading towards the city.
On inquiring casually, he discovered that they had spent a month in the cursed space, while five days had passed outside.
Moreover, the situation in Mountain Hermit had changed dramatically.
"The Emperor of the Sun forced to abdicate?"
Su Lun felt a pang of sorrow hearing this.
Through further inquiries, he understood the whole course of events.
Because the "Great God Tsukuyomi" had appeared and the current Imperial Princess's whereabouts were unknown, the battle a few days ago met almost no resistance except from the imperial dynasty, and the Takeda government seized the throne, becoming the new "Moon Emperor."
The divine right of kings meant that even the followers of the Shinto religion and all the inhabitants had to obey the divine will.
There were naturally no voices of opposition within the country.
The Takeda shogunate quickly stabilized the situation with strength and the will of the gods.
Moreover, due to the method of polluting the sun, the Takeda shogunate's Black Sun Grand Festival almost completely eradicated all the "foreigners" lurking in Edo Castle, making the domestic faith purer and almost free from any hidden dangers.
Even if the King of the North Sea's fleet were to come, they had to weigh whether they could afford to lose another fleet.
...
After gathering information, Su Lun walked out of the teahouse and strolled along the streets of Edo.
What surprised him more was that after the Takeda shogunate seized the throne, Ote Himeya was still working as a geisha in a geisha house?
"Is she continuing to hide her identity and then manipulate everything from behind the scenes?"
Su Lun guessed something.
He now knew that Ote Himeya was an alchemic artificial person, so he was sure she played a decisive role in the chaos at Mountain Hermit.
However, what he did not understand was that "the Great God Tsukuyomi" had truly descended.
Su Lun thought of "Izanami" that he had encountered in the underworld, although these personified gods did not possess real divine tiers, they also had certain inexplicable powers.
"But this is also good. Since she's not in the imperial palace, it's easier for me to get close to her."
Su Lun thought and then walked toward the Ginza district in the west city area.
He didn't know how long his physical condition could hold out. While he hadn't yet "mutated" into a monster, he had to get things done.
In the world of the novel, Fujiwara Hayato, the author, was waiting to rewrite the ending, and time was limited. If delayed any longer, that lingering regret might not last much longer, and the princess and Senjo might never return.
...
The post-war Edo Castle seemed much lonelier.
The Takeda shogunate had become the new emperor, and it seemed that the student movements had also been suppressed. The "New Learning" students, who were frequently seen marching in black school uniforms, were no longer visible on the street.
The current situation in Mountain Hermit was leaning toward completely shutting the country off from the outside world.
The people remain ignorant, the information secluded—does this create purer faith and more consolidated royal power?
Su Lun was not surprised.
He stepped into the street that used to be a bustling geisha district. He hadn't walked far when he passed in front of a geisha house with a sign that read "One Foot Interval."
The names of geisha houses usually had some poetic flavor. This name stemmed from a rather famous haiku from Mountain Hermit: "The light breaks continuously, brightening and dimming at one foot interval, how can one bear the solitude?"
The geisha houses remained the same, but the scenery had changed.
Local people in Mountain Hermit were mostly very poor. Without foreigners and pirates to bring business, the entertainment industries in the west city's Ginza also declined, presenting a dead and depressing sight throughout the streets.
Black crows fluttered in the sky, perching on high eaves to survey their surroundings.
Su Lun, holding a rune-decorated black umbrella disguised as a walking cane, and with a black scythe wrapped in a canvas behind his back, passed by without attracting any notice.
Sensing around, there were some ninjas and ronin mingled on this street, but none were particularly strong.
After some consideration, he could understand why.
Now the entire Edo Castle was controlled by the Takeda shogunate and the Black Dragon Association, and there were no treacherous foreigners present; naturally, there was no need to be overly cautious.
Moreover, the fact that Ote Himeya was the leader of the Black Dragon Association had nearly been hidden from everyone. If strong bodyguards constantly followed her, she would have revealed flaws long ago.
Furthermore, her inherent battle strength was not weak. It was nearly impossible for someone in Edo to harm her.
According to information previously mentioned by Senjo, Ote Himeya's inherent battle strength was not strong, around the level of a fourth or fifth-tier professional. But because she was an alchemic body, immune to both physical and magical attacks, almost no conventional methods could harm her.
