From the deck came the exasperated and furious shout of the courier, but the voice suddenly cut off.
The very next second after Su Lun made his move, with the black sickle in hand, he swung down, and a rift in space fell, claiming a head.
Su Lun took action, and Banner on the deck decisively gave the command, "Yang Fan, take the helm and head south! Everyone, launch the war fog!"
Although the crew didn't understand what was happening, most of them were veterans of the "Steam faction" with absolute trust in Banner. Upon hearing the order, they began to busy themselves amidst the fog.
On the sea surface, more and more "Fog Bombs" were being launched, and the scope of the fog was increasing.
...
"Team nineteen, what's the situation on your side!"
"Stop right now, or we'll open fire!"
"..."
The exasperated voice of the Commander came from the communicator.
Banner didn't respond, knowing they must have guessed that they were trying to escape.
Moreover, this escape obviously had a trick to it. As long as the Mafa people weren't foolish, they would also immediately guess that they indeed held the "neural mechanical technology"!
Knowing that the technology was onboard, they naturally wouldn't bomb them indiscriminately.
If the technical personnel were blasted to death, this top-secret technology would truly be missed.
Soon, Su Lun heard the sound of a second round of cannon fire. The blasts sounded significant, but judging by the trajectory of the cannonballs, most were aimed too high and shot towards the distance.
This was merely a chaotic warning salvo.
Seeing this, Su Lun also breathed a sigh of relief, fearing that the other side hadn't guessed and would send a barrage of fire.
Since they dared not bombard them, they took no notice and continued at full speed.
The defensive and offensive capabilities of their mechanically-refitted battleship far surpassed the pirate ships of Team Nineteen by numerous times, but the only drawback was its speed. The storm and the waves disrupted the formation, which also increased the distance between the two sides.
The battle had begun, and both Su Lun and Dr. Banks had come up to the deck. They watched the raging sea intently, as if trying to capture something.
If the ship could not be caught up to, then submarines would surely be dispatched.
The storm had much less impact on submarines underwater.
Dr. Banks said solemnly, "Mechanical submarines should appear soon."
Everything was proceeding according to plan, but the most dangerous situation was approaching.
"Hmm."
Su Lun nodded, indifferent as he took out several scrolls and smashed them towards the water's surface. Clapping his hands together, the sorcerer's seals instantaneously congealed. Purple spatial runes appeared, and six glass jars materialized out of thin air.
With a "crack," the glass shattered, and several mechanical octopuses crashed into the water.
In the water, Su Lun's "Soul Tentacles" could only control within a limited range, so he had to wait quietly for the enemy to come.
...
The sea churned with the wind howling violently. Su Lun, holding a black umbrella and dressed in a raincoat, watched the sea surface with detachment in the pouring rain.
Dr. Banks stood by, fully on guard.
Although he disliked combat, that didn't mean he lacked fighting ability. A mysterious force kept the rain an inch away from his body, unable to touch him.
"They're here!"
Su Lun's eyes narrowed.
Because at that moment, dozens of human souls emerged from the seabed into his perception range.
It probably wasn't the "secret research base," but... they'd capture whatever it was first!
It wasn't long before structures resembling shark fins appeared on the surface, and the communicator relayed another warning: "Team nineteen, you are now ordered to stop immediately, or we will sink your ships at once!"
Hearing the warning, Su Lun and Dr. Banks didn't show the slightest intention of heeding it, continuing their frantic escape instead.
They were certain that the other party wouldn't open fire and sink them, so now it was about running as far away as possible.
The greater the distance they put between themselves and the "Princess," the smaller the danger would become.
As they had anticipated, despite repeated warnings, the submarine never launched a torpedo, only doggedly gave chase.
Su Lun wasn't sure if there was any high-tier combat power aboard the submarine chasing them, so he refrained from acting.
He wanted to wait until a thousand threads were close enough.
However, Su Lun had underestimated the technology of Mafa.
The guys didn't dare launch a torpedo to destroy them, but they did launch something even more exaggerated than a torpedo.
A "whoosh" sound echoed.
Something resembling a torpedo shot out of the water.
Su Lun saw the trajectory of the projectile.
But he thought it was just a warning shot.
Because the torpedo's trajectory wasn't aimed at their ship at all, it was off by tens of meters.
But in the very next moment, the torpedo left the water with a "boom," and suddenly exploded in mid-air.
There was a flash of light, no violent explosion, but a visible shockwave expanded rapidly from the center of the explosion like lightning.
The shockwave swept across the entire sea surface in an instant, and the ships of the 19th Fleet were also affected, shattering all the bulletproof glass into pieces.
Su Lun had anticipated the explosion and Rune Vajra had readied its defenses. But when the shockwave hit, what surprised him was that the shockwave seemed to have no effect on human bodies?
It was then that he realized this wasn't an ordinary gunpowder bomb, but a "Shockwave Bomb"!
"This projectile will directly destroy the ship..."
Su Lun's face showed a strange expression.
This was the first time he had learned of such a projectile in Mafa.
The ships of the 19th Fleet were just ordinary pirate ships, whether in terms of materials, enchantments, or coatings, they were all quite common. Hit by this "Shockwave Bomb," the hull swayed in the waves and "crack, crack" sounds of wood breaking could be heard everywhere about the ship.
"Boss, it's not looking good, the mast has broken!"
"Boss, water is leaking into the cabin too!"
"Oh, heavens, our ship is falling apart. Quick, launch the lifeboats!"
"..."
The ship descended into chaos.
Through the communicator, bad news came one after another.
Su Lun didn't need anyone to report; he could already feel the ship starting to capsize, soon to sink into the sea.
He wasn't panicky at all and leaped into the sea.
It was at this moment, he sensed that the submarine was very close to them!
Su Lun controlled his eight-armed spider lance, and six mechanical octopuses hidden in the sea were instantly activated.
The tentacles of the octopuses contracted and extended in the water, allowing them to teleport tens of meters. In the blink of an eye, the six mechanical octopuses were close to the submarine, and with the suction cups on their tentacles, they clung tightly to the hull.
Then, the various tools on the tentacles began to cut into the hull...
...
The Mafa soldiers aboard the submarine had just been celebrating that a single shot had sunk the ship and were preparing to capture those floating in the sea when they suddenly sensed that something foreign had attached to the hull!
Just like the last time Su Lun encountered in the Rock Caiman Strait, the mechanical octopus was designed with specialized cutting tools, and the people on the submarine didn't dare to entangle in the water, rapidly surfacing instead.
As soon as the submarine's hull emerged from the water, more than ten soldiers in mechanical armor came out from the submarine's cabin, intending to deal with the mechanical octopus clinging to the ship.
But how could Su Lun let them have their way?
He controlled six mechanical octopuses and in the blink of an eye wrapped around six mechanical warriors.
Mechanical octopuses naturally restrained mechanical armor. Once adhered to by the tentacles, low-tier mechanical armor had almost no means to break free. In the end, they could only be slowly dismantled by the octopus and killed.
However, the opponents were well-trained professional soldiers.
The moment six octopuses clung to six mechas, the other soldiers who were not ensnared, carrying ship-cutter swords, hammers, saws... showed no hesitation out of concern for their equipment, fiercely slashing away.
They struck with such determination that even if it meant killing their comrades, they were intent on eliminating these mechanical octopuses.
"How decisive!"
Su Lun felt a sense of admiration in his heart.
He also guessed that these fellows might be aware of the "mechanical octopus" and had corresponding tactics to deal with it.
Otherwise, they would definitely not be so decisive.
But Su Lun only had six finished octopuses in hand, naturally, he would not just watch as his hard-made mechanical octopuses were killed.
And since he had chosen to take action, he also had his own set of tactics in place.
In his hand was another cursed artifact highly compatible with mechanical speech—the "Xiupunos' Night Scythe"!
The octopus had many tentacles, with its most important battle capability being "control." Some tentacles controlled the target while others were attached to the ship's hull, rendering the mechanical warriors practically immobilized.
And the Night Scythe's favorite targets were those that were stationary!
Hidden behind the wreck of a distant ship, Su Lun watched as the octopus seized control of the targets and decisively raised the dark scythe, "swish" "swish" "swish"... six slashes in a second.
Previously, when he controlled the living dead, the best one could barely make three to five slashes before collapsing.
But now that he had reached the understanding required to utilize the Death rule, such slash attacks were completely free of any curse backlash, ready at hand.
With six sharp slashes, six spatial rifts appeared not far away.
Even a fifth or sixth-tier professional would find it difficult to break through the "Lieutenant Colonel" and "Colonel" level mechanical armor, which were instantly severed at the neck.
Then four of them triggered their self-destruct mechanism and exploded into a burst of flames.
Su Lun felt a twinge of pain as he watched, thinking to himself, "It's a pity they blew up..."
Each piece of Mafa officer-level armor had a unique self-destruct device. It wasn't located in the same position; any external damage triggered an immediate self-destruction.
The two that didn't explode were probably because their triggers were not on the neck.
Su Lun watched his "spoils of war" get destroyed, and although pained, he was not idle.
Since he was controlling all the mechanical octopuses alone, there was no issue of coordination whatsoever.
After he killed the six Mafa soldiers, without any gap, the mechanical octopuses detached and swiftly reattached to another six.
Then it was the same tactic again: adhering, controlling, the Night Scythe slashing swiftly.
Using this method, Su Lun had killed all the mecha warriors, over ten of them, who had emerged from the hangar in an extremely short amount of time.
The rhythm of this battle was almost exactly as he had previously rehearsed.
But Su Lun was not the least bit complacent; he watched the mechanical submarine that was about to be cut open with a grave expression.
Because... he knew the most troublesome opponent was about to come out!
...
In the past few days, Su Lun had also gathered some intelligence: the highest commander aboard a Mafa Empire standard submarine typically held the rank of "Commodore."
That also meant the equipment was of a "Commodore-class" Mecha, roughly equivalent to the combat power of a fifth-tier professional.
And "Commodore-class" was a watershed for Mafa military Mecha.
Below this specification, the attacks were almost all "physical attacks," which Su Lun could easily deal with;
But the Mecha above it possessed some truly magical abilities. For example, "Brigadier-class" Mecha, even in top-tier professional combat, performed very strongly.
Given the special identity of the "Princess of Frost Moon," Su Lun dared not be certain about the military rank of the submarine captain in her protector team but guessed it was highly likely to be "high-spec."
As expected.
It was after Su Lun had killed more than ten men emerging from storage in two or three encounters that the people in the cabin also came to their senses and immediately more than ten Mecha warriors charged out.
This time, a formidable enemy came!
The leader, clad in fiery red mechanical armor, was instantly recognized by Su Lun for his rank, as well as the model marked on his armor — "Brigadier-class Demon Blade X1 Mecha!"
"So it's 'Brigadier-class' after all!"
Su Lun's gaze turned icy.
Meaning, this guy had at least the combat power of a regular sixth-tier professional!
The moment this guy appeared, he drew a mechanical sword from his hand, flowing with magma.
The name displayed by the identification was "Magical Energy Magma Python Knife"!
Before Su Lun could think further, he watched the man raise his hand and slash down with the knife.
A miraculous scene unfolded, the crimson sword didn't slash down but softened like a whip, lashing toward a mechanical octopus not far away!
"A whip?"
Su Lun watched, his face suddenly pale.
With a "whoosh" of air breaking, before he could have the mechanical octopus dodge, the crimson whip struck the octopus.
It was like metal meeting strong acid, Su Lun watched as the whip rapidly corroded the enchanted plating on the octopus's mechanical tentacles, then swiftly ate away at the runes.
After a brief struggle, Su Lun could no longer feel the nerve signals from that part of the octopus's limb.
This one strike had directly "crippled" a mechanical octopus.
"So powerful."
Su Lun watched, his eyelids twitching.
He only had six octopuses; how could they withstand such treatment?
At this encounter, he controlled the remaining five octopuses to jump into the water, not daring to linger for battle.
Almost at the same time, Su Lun watched as that "Brigadier" turned his gaze toward him.
Clearly, this guy had just seen Su Lun use his black scythe to kill his subordinates on the ship!
Su Lun felt a tingle on his scalp as he was stared at.
However... it wouldn't be easy for this guy to kill him.
Su Lun wanted to find a chance to avoid him first.
But just then, from the distant sea surface, a series of "pop", "pop", "pop" came as air burst.
Glancing sideways, a teleporting swordsman running wildly from the sea surface with wind and thunder approached.
Behind her, a raging sea of thunder surged, as the six-armed Rakshasa shadow's three thunder drums activated a sky full of thunder, extravagantly exaggerated to the extreme.
If not Lei, then who could it be?

chapters.title: Chapter 359 - 358 Listening to the Voice of Sea Beasts
chapters.content:
Su Lun had guessed earlier that the submarine might not be able to handle elite generals.
But it wouldn't be someone too high-ranking, at most a "Commodore."
After all, top-ranking generals like "General Stars" were few in the Mafa Empire, and their mechanical power armors were strategic-level resources that almost never left the country as a "dowry."
Moreover, the noble pageantry had a set of fixed rules that had continued for thousands of years, especially for the royal family. The pageantry was also fixed.
Princes had the pageantry of princes, and princesses had the pageantry of princesses, one must not overstep their bounds.
Simply put, the Thirteenth Princess, Scatty Harris, didn't qualify to have a "Commodore" level high-ranking general as part of her dowry.
Su Lun was sure of this, and that's why he had come up with his current plan.
The original plan was, if it was a "Brigadier General," then he could kill.
If it was a "Commodore," they would probably have to retreat.
Although Qian Tiao had entered the realm of the Sword Saint and her sword skills were exquisite, she was only Fifth Order. If it really came to a fight, the difference in power from a higher order was not so easily erased.
And mechanical power armor was essentially the nemesis of sword fighters.
Just like right now.
...
Qian Tiao had made her entrance, countering the commodore-level officer with an incomparably domineering stance.
But even though her Sword Qi was sharp, able to split the sea surface with a hundred-meter long Sword Qi and even sever the waves, it left practically no mark when it fell on that set of "Commodore level Blade X1 Type Mechanical Power Armor."
The mechanical armor had a layer of dissolution barrier on its surface, able to visibly dissolve any energy attacks.
The Magic Energy Magma Whip in the Mecha's hands was also incredibly sharp, capable of crippling mechanical octopuses with a single lash, let alone the flesh and blood of humans.
And this set of "Commodore level" armor wasn't an ounce awkward like low-tier armors. Its magic energy power system had almost no charge-up delay, its action interval was extremely short, and it was very agile. Even the slight rigidity, inherent to all mechanical devices that cannot be eliminated, was offset by its strong defensive and offensive capabilities.
The mechanical armor's super defensive advantage was here.
It could take a beating for a long time, but you shouldn't let it hit you.
One lash, one blow to the soul.
Qian Tiao could head-on clash with the armor, but she also had to dodge the whip.
A few encounters and exchanges, and she didn't gain any advantage.
Facing such an opponent, Su Lun used all his means. If they ganged up on it, they could have a chance to kill, but it would take a significant amount of time.
Unfortunately, the "Princess" and its eight escort ships were all nearby, and there was simply no time for a protracted battle.
They had to retreat first!
Su Lun watched the fierce battle ahead, his eyes shifted, and he immediately came up with a plan.
He didn't go to help Qian Tiao, but instead, controlled the mechanical octopus and headed for the submarine!
Without that "Commodore level" armor, other mechanical soldiers were almost all easy to control and finish with one cut for Su Lun.
Moreover, Su Lun's black scythe posed a significant threat to the submarine.
No matter how sturdy the steel armor was, before a spatial rift, it was like cutting through butter.
The "Commodore" seemed to realize this as well.
Watching as Su Lun killed two more of his subordinates, he didn't dare to tangle any more and charged straight at Su Lun, trying to restrain him. As soon as Qian Tiao entered, this guy was also clearly aware that relying on just one warship, self-preservation was difficult, let alone keeping people. Not feasible, the already damaged submarine also got the order to dive quickly.
Su Lun squinted at the diving submarine. He was confident that he could sink the ship.
He had Spatial Displacement, so catching up was not difficult.
But as this thought flashed through his mind, it was replaced by another, better plan.
Even if he sunk it now, he had no time to salvage.
When "Princess" arrived, they still had to leave.
And besides, the submarine was a warship, not that "secret mechanical research facility."
Just securing this submarine wouldn't satisfy his appetite.
With his thoughts flashing, Su Lun watched the submarine dive into the sea and didn't pursue it, but pretended to be tied up and together with Qian Tiao, they continued to oppose the "Commodore."
Lower-tier professionals couldn't interfere with a battle of this level, so Su Lun informed Dr. Banks to have the lower-order crew members underwater leave first. In a blink, the battle on the sea surface was left with just "general versus general."
To deal with mechanical soldiers, Su Lun had no intention of depleting the few puppets he had.
He took out his rune black umbrella, pinched the sorcerer's seals with both hands, and a dense throng of red Spiritual Bodies enveloped by a furious will emerged in a surge. There were nearly a hundred thousand vengeful spirits in the rune black umbrella, and these resentments could continuously attack the target.
Su Lun had personally experienced the super-powerful "Necromancy Spell Penetration" of the black flash. He knew full well that even though the mechanical armor had inspiring alloy that could resist most mental attacks, the persistent attacks of the vengeful spirits would increasingly affect the person inside the armor.
And since vengeful spirits were immune to all physical attacks, not even the "Magical Energy Magma Python Knife" could hurt them.
If it really came down to attrition, once the "Commodore" was mentally controlled and reacted even a bit slower, Su Lun could immediately kill with his black scythe!
Su Lun also figured out that the "Commodore" was trying to delay them, waiting for the main force to come and surround them.
But they had no intention of fighting a prolonged battle.
He and Qian Tiao kept up the fight while leading the person into the depths of the storm.
```
The "Commodore" kept his distance all along. After probing, he also understood the limited attack range of Su Lun; the grudge spirits from the black umbrella could cover hundreds of meters around. As long as he didn't approach that range, he wouldn't be affected.
But how could they possibly keep Su Lun, whose teleportation ability on the sea surface was extremely strong, if they didn't dare to engage in close combat?
With a simple trick, he and Qian Tiao vanished amidst the raging wind and waves.
...
Soon after, aboard the "Dawn".
Su Lun and Qian Tiao leaped onto the deck.
As soon as they boarded the ship, they heard Tanni's voice overpowering the sound of the torrential rain, commanding the sailors to control the sailing ship.
"Hard to port, we're going to surge up the waves!"
"Right, secure the sails, we must harness the storm, not let the storm push us around!"
"Everyone hold tight, we're going surfing!"
"..."
On the deck, Lolo Tata, the Giant Three Brothers, the Sumo Wrestler, swordsmen... everyone was working in unison, pulling the ropes vigorously, intent on executing every command with precision.
Their ship was in the center of the storm with waves tens of meters high, washing over the ship and the crew like water spilled from a bucket.
Such a storm surge, for the vast majority of sailors, signified a catastrophic weather event that meant death.
In encountering such weather at sea, there's usually only one conclusion: "Shipwreck"!
Yet, under Tanni's command, the three-masted sailing ship "Dawn" not only didn't sink, but it surfed the waves smoothly, gliding over the increasingly high swells, performing one astonishing, inconceivable voyage after another.
Even Su Lun was astounded.
He used his Octopus Lance to secure himself on the deck, but his center of gravity kept shifting with the tilt of the ship, to the left, to the right, vertically inclined... almost capsizing upside down.
Lifted by the waves, then plunging from heights, there was also that intense feeling of extreme heaviness and weightlessness as when riding a roller coaster.
This was Su Lun's first time experiencing such thrilling navigation.
Each time the ship felt like it would be overturned by the storm, but at the critical moment, it miraculously rode the next giant wave.
It was as if... they were not combating a vicious storm.
But rather, they were beloved children of the ocean, surfing through the storm, revelling with abandon.
The waves washed over the hull, the "whooshing" sound incessant in their ears.
The heavy rain soaked them both.
The blue hair on Qian Tiao's forehead stuck to her face.
The recent fight had left her feeling somewhat unfulfilled, but looking at the young man passionately directing in the pilot house, her eyes could not hide her admiration as she remarked, "Su Lun, the navigator you found is quite remarkable."
"Indeed,"
Su Lun looked on with sparkling eyes and a satisfied expression.
He'd anticipated this, but witnessing it firsthand, the shock in his heart was no less intense than Qian Tiao's.
When making the battle plans earlier, Su Lun had shared some of his ideas.
He'd asked Tanni, could he pilot a ship in such extreme storm conditions?
Tanni had confidently assured him that he could.
Su Lun had put his full faith in him, handing over the helm of the ship to Tanni.
In this moment, seeing the confidence in the eyes of the young Naga hybrid, Su Lun knew his trust was well placed.
Tanni was undoubtedly one of the finest navigators in Pirate City Hastlin, or even across this vast azure ocean.
Qian Tiao, with the excited expression akin to discovering a treasure, laughed, "Haha... from now on, he's our 'Dawn Squad's' Chief Navigator!"
...
The ship continued to rock violently; Tanni had said that the storm might persist for several more hours.
In the shared vision of the black crows, the "Princess" at the edge of the horizon was no longer visible.
In such a strong storm, the slightest misstep could mean shipwreck. Even if they desired the "neuro-mechanical technology," it's unlikely that the precious 'Frost Moon Princess' would recklessly chase after them herself.
And while there might still be submarines pursuing them, Tanni had already directed the vessel to widen the distance considerably.
This one wasn't "cursed by the sea as a hapless fool"; the waves and the storm favored him.
Wherever Tanni went, the storm followed.
The ship, boosted by waves and fierce winds, moved as swiftly as an arrow released from a bow; even submarines wouldn't be able to catch up at this speed.
The situation looked perilous, but the most dangerous moments had already been passed.
...
With Tanni and the crew maneuvering the ship, and Qian Tiao staying on deck, there was no need for Su Lun to worry, so he walked into the captain's quarters.
There, Dr. Banks, 'The Butcher' Banner, and some of the core members of Squad 19 had already been waiting for a while. Although many members had been scattered at sea, this was already the best outcome. Those who were separated had been prepared with life-saving equipment. After the storm, they would just slowly gather them up in this sea region.
Dr. Banks, seeing Su Lun's safe return, also let out a sigh of relief.
```
Su Lun didn't ask anything else and directly asked with anticipation, "Doctor, is the marking done?"
Dr. Banks smiled and said, "No problem. I've marked that submarine with a bio-marker. No matter how far away they are, I can sense the position of their fleet."
Hearing this, a pleased expression appeared on Su Lun's face, and he let out a long sigh of relief, "All our effort wasn't in vain."
Previously, Su Lun actually had the opportunity to sink that submarine, but he chose not to do so.
The plan was to let the prey travel further away to catch a bigger fish.
The success of this tactic was related to one of Dr. Banks's abilities. He could mark objects with "Eternal Cells". As the "parent body", he could sense the exact location of those cells.
Conventional magical markings or other device markings can easily be detected and removed in the military field.
However, this kind of biological marking is very secretive, like microorganisms clinging to the hull, virtually undetectable.
Thus, Su Lun and his team could constantly monitor the position of the escaping submarine.
If the "secret mechanical research institute" was indeed located in a submarine as Su Lun suspected, then such an important base would certainly have protective forces.
Surface ships are too conspicuous targets; submarines are the best choice.
The number of these submarines coming from the Mafa Empire, the "Frost Moon Princess" Scatty, wouldn't be too many.
So... the chances were high they would be together.
As long as the position could be confirmed, once Su Lun's octopus legion was formed, the success rate for the next interception would be very high!
....
Su Lun watched the magic crystal lamp in the captain's cabin shake violently for a long time, and finally, after two hours, the waves subsided.
Sunlight pierced through the dark clouds, shining down on the deck.
The storm had washed the ship, giving it a fresh, shiny appearance.
Su Lun and Dr. Banks walked onto the deck, and when the crew saw them, they greeted them one after another.
At that moment, Tanni also jumped down from the mast and landed on the deck, saying, "Mr. Su Lun!"
Su Lun looked at the person who had contributed the most to the success of this operation and smiled, "Tanni, you've worked hard. Your navigation skills are really great."
Hearing the praise, Tanni bashfully turned his head, but his clear, pale blue eyes lit up with an inspired luster.
This wasn't his first time steering a ship, but it was the only time it had gone so smoothly.
On such a huge sea vessel, everyone trusted him, followed his commands... No one looked at him differently because he was the "sea-cursed misfortune," nor did anyone look down on him for his youthful appearance.
He felt a strong sense of... being trusted!
By his side, Qiantiao also patted Tanni's shoulder and said, "Tanni, you did well. From now on, you're our Dawn Group's navigator!"
As soon as Qiantiao spoke, he formally acknowledged the new crew member's status.
Hearing this, the sailors on board cheered, praising and welcoming the new member to their ranks.
"Welcome our new group member, an excellent navigator!"
"Oh, I can't believe we've just sailed out of such a disastrous storm 'without a scratch'! Hahaha..."
"Tanni is the most impressive navigator I've ever seen!"
"Yeah. It's really amazing!"
"..."
The crew members were generous with their praise,
Tanni, looking at those warm, family-like smiling faces, felt warmth in his heart. His eyes welled up with tears as he said excitedly, "Thank you, Mr. Su Lun, thank you, Sister Qiantiao, thank you, everyone..."
He had come to Pirate City when he was very young, and because he was a hybrid of a sea demon and a human, he was always discriminated against and excluded.
He was even called the "sea-cursed misfortune."
Before she could talk, his mother told him to live well, for destiny would be kind to everyone who faced life positively.
So, he had always tried to live on.
Even though his mother had completely turned to stone and hadn't spoken for many years,
he still remembered his mother's words.
He had always lived actively and optimistically, earning money and diligently learning navigation skills...
His dream was that one day, he would have his own companions, steering their own great sea ship, exploring every corner of the ocean.
As Tanni thought about these things, tears suddenly filled his eyes and began to flow uncontrollably.
He had never encountered such amicable people; everyone was full of goodwill, and for the first time, he experienced respect and equality. That feeling was wondrous, like the warm sunshine after a storm, warming his heart.
It was not like the deceitful, depressing, and dark atmosphere of Pirate City.
At that moment, he saw the beauty of the world.
Seeing Tanni burst into tears, Lolota handed him a handkerchief, teasingly smiling, "Here... this is for you. Our teary-eyed navigator."
"Thank you, Miss Lolota."
Tanni accepted it, smiled shyly, and looked quite comical with tears still hanging at the corner of his eyes.
Qian Tiao also couldn't help but chuckle. She smiled and then introduced, "This is Mr. Banner. Many people on the ship should recognize him, from the Old Lington Steam Party. Now, he and his team members are also part of our Dawn Group!"
With that, the ship immediately became lively.
"Wow...welcome, old friends from the Steam Party."
"..."
Most of those who came from the Steam Party and the Cross Society were high-level officials, and many knew each other. Meeting on the ship felt like "old friends in a foreign land," so no one felt like an outsider.
Qian Tiao didn't introduce Dr. Banks; that was the doctor's own preference.
Even now, as a member of the "Dawn Group," he didn't want his presence known and preferred to quietly engage in scientific research.
....
The escape plan was perfect.
Almost every detail unfolded as Su Lun had previously anticipated.
Now, their task was to follow the bio-markers and distress signals left by Dr. Banks and slowly salvage the crew members previously scattered at sea.
The sea was calm, and the ship sailed unhurriedly on the ocean surface.
The sky had cleared and was cloudless.
On the sea, the "Princess" fleet had completely vanished, and the previous tension had entirely dissipated.
Qian Tiao stood on the mast enjoying the sea breeze, Dr. Banks was holed up in the cabin tinkering with his laboratory, Lolota practiced her swordsmanship as diligently as ever, and Banner and his brothers were working hard to integrate into this new team...
The Dawn Group had welcomed some new members, and everyone was very happy.
Su Lun basked in the sun on the deck, enjoying the rare leisure time.
But suddenly, Tanni jumped down from the mast.
With a puzzled look on his face, he said, "Mr. Su Lun, I've noticed something and need to report to you."
Su Lun looked at him and asked, "What is it?"
Tanni frowned and said, "There seems to be something very strange in the water."
Hearing this, Su Lun was puzzled and instinctively asked back, "Strange creatures in the water?"
The others on the ship also looked over.
"Yes."
Tanni hesitated for a moment, as if recalling some unpleasant memory.
Seeing the crowd's kind and curious gazes, he mustered his courage and said, "The fish have noticed something very strange in the sea."
When Su Lun heard this, something crossed his mind, and he asked, "You... you can communicate with fish?"
Tanni nodded and said, "Yes. Since I was young, I've been able to understand what little animals say, but it wasn't something I could always hear. But now, it seems I can hear them all the time."
He had once told others that he seemed to understand the voices of little animals.
But the ability was inconsistent, and when he tried to prove it, he would fail to hear them and was ruthlessly mocked for it.
After that, he never mentioned it again in front of others.
"Oh."
Su Lun realized that this might be a natural ability.
Somewhat like "Innate Ability C-021 - Beast Speaker."
People are more likely to awaken innate abilities during major ups and downs, or when their state of mind undergoes significant changes.
However, Su Lun wasn't sure if this was Tanni's innate ability.
Because he could also passively attract storms.
That was a gift of the naga race, the favorites of the ocean and the storms.
Still, Su Lun was more curious about something else rather than pursuing that question.
He asked, "What is it?"
Tanni organized his thoughts and tried to describe it, "Well... it's actually been there for a while. It seems like 'eel,' 'multi-tailed sea snakes,' 'octopus,' or some other tentacled sea creature. But 'they' shouldn't be in these waters, and now, it seems like they are following us."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's gaze turned sharp instantly.
Some studies suggest marine life have an exceptionally strong perceptive ability, in certain aspects even stronger than human sensory professionals. When strange things come into a marine area, the fish are the first to know.
Tanni didn't know what they were, but Su Lun did.
From the description, he immediately realized there were other mechanical octopuses under the sea!
Su Lun asked, "How many of these creatures are there?"
Tanni replied, "At least several dozen."
"That many?"
Hearing that, Su Lun was not worried but instead delighted.
He hadn't snagged the 'Frost Moon Princess' dowry submarine – was Duke Raphael planning to compensate him with some mechanical octopuses?

chapters.title: Chapter 360 - 359: Great Harvest
chapters.content:
Su Lun really felt like he had struck gold.
Not only was Tanni one of the best sailing masters in Pirate City, but the ability he now displayed to "listen to the voices of sea creatures" was also a great help to the Dawn Group.
Otherwise, without realizing it, Su Lun would not have noticed that they were being watched.
The mechanical octopuses acted very covertly in the sea, as they possessed the soul fluctuations and some life characteristics of normal octopuses, making it difficult to distinguish them from regular octopuses unless seen with one's own eyes, even for practitioners with sensory abilities.
With these advantages, they were easily overlooked in the deep sea areas dense with marine life.
But as for the tracking,
with a little thought,
Su Lun knew that these octopuses were probably not originally after them but were more likely following that "Frost Moon Princess" Skadi.
The alliance between Mafa and the King of the North Sea allowed the pirates to grow swiftly. This greatly impacted several major nobles whose dominions lay within the raiding range of the North Sea Fleet, with Duke Rafael at the forefront.
Thus, if there was a chance, the person with the most motive to assassinate the princess would definitely be Duke Rafael.
But now the assassin, instead of following the "Princess," turned to follow the Dawn Group, and Su Lun guessed it was probably because of the mechanical octopuses that appeared during the recent battle. That individual hiding in the sea wanted to figure out exactly what was going on.
After all, the princess could be ambushed at another opportunity.
But Duke Rafael's exclusive techniques must not fall into the hands of outsiders!
...
Now that they knew they were being tracked, naturally, they had to flush out the tracker.
Moreover, considering the situation with the Dawn vessel, they couldn't shake the pursuit even if they wanted to.
"It won't be easy to lure that guy out..."
Su Lun listened to the position described by Tanni, where that individual was hiding in the deep sea, far away and very cautious.
That person probably didn't surface because they weren't confident they could take down everyone on their ship.
With Tanni's ability to communicate with schools of fish, they could indeed confirm some of the mechanical octopuses' positions.
But since they were constantly on the move, capturing them accurately was difficult.
It would be rash to dive into the sea, and there might not be any results.
If they struck at the snake without killing it, it would lead to big problems later on.
The key issue was that they weren't sure where the "controller" was.
Once Tanni brought this up, many people on the ship started paying attention.
Even Qian Tiao cast an inquiring look, clearly asking: Are we going to make a move?
Su Lun shook his head, not intending to startle the snake.
He raised his hand to signal that everyone should keep doing what they were doing.
Seeing this gesture from him, the crew also understood tacitly, and no one asked out of curiosity.
Meanwhile, Su Lun's mind was rapidly considering strategies.
In his head, he reviewed all the scenes after leaving Pirate City, reenacting the entire process from the beginning and pondering, "Since that person has been trailing us until now, they must have some special way to keep track of the 'Princess.' Either there is an insider, some special positioning ability, or it might be a mystic's power like divination or prophecy..."
Su Lun ruled out various possibilities one by one.
The Royal Guard of the "Frost Moon Princess" consisted of elites; tracking them without being noticed was difficult.
Furthermore, there were submarines in the water, and even with mechanical octopuses, constant close tracking seemed unlikely.
If they were too far, then how were they managing to follow without losing track?
Mystic divination abilities?
That would require a highly skilled practitioner, especially since Mafa's Royal Princess would surely have treasures to prevent divination.
Moreover, since they were using mechanical octopuses, it's not likely a traditional alchemist.
The likelihood of an insider existed, but that chance was small as well.
For the moment, Su Lun wasn't certain what means the "controller" used.
As he pondered, his thoughts drifted away.
It was at this moment that he faintly heard crew members communicating through communicators by his ear.
"First Mate Hays, there's a distress signal three miles north. It might be a brother who has fallen overboard, should we go take a look?"
"Alright! Turn the rudder!"
"..."
At that moment, the "sizzle" of the signal sounded unusually clear in Su Lun's ears.
Though the Dawn was not large, relying on shouting alone was inefficient for communication between the cabin and the deck. Especially in bad weather like they had encountered before, when the sound of wind and waves could drown out human voices, making communication ineffective.
To convey orders accurately, almost every ship was equipped with mechanical communicators.
When Su Lun heard this, a sudden brainstorm flashed through his mind.
"Right, the communicators!"
It was only then he realized he had been neglecting something due to preconceived notions.
In his hand was a "Dagus Goblin Communicator," which allowed for long-distance secure communication regardless of obstructions.
Such communicators were excellent, but they didn't have the capacity for mass production.
Therefore, to equip them widely in the military, they relied on conventional mechanical communicators.
But these mechanical communicators had a fatal flaw; all their channels were open. The communication waves would propagate indiscriminately within a certain range, which could potentially be intercepted and decoded by others.
Even the advanced communication devices of Ruying and Mafa military couldn't avoid this issue.
Su Lun's eyes shifted as he guessed in his mind, "That guy must have some ability to decipher and capture communication signals, which is how he located the 'Royal Princess'..."
Suddenly, he felt like he had a way to lure that guy out.
The plan formed in his mind in an instant.
Su Lun signaled to Qian Tiao, then took out the ship's communicator and pondered before saying, "Hey, Captain, no joke, those six mechanical octopuses you got this time are really useful. We almost took out those Mafa submarines..."
A glint flickered in Qian Tiao's eyes, and he immediately understood, following up with, "That's for sure."
Su Lun continued, "Ah, if 'Old Ghost' could get us a few more, we wouldn't have let that submarine get away."
As the conversation reached this point, Qian Tiao had guessed what Su Lun was up to and added, "Duke Rafael's laboratory isn't that easy to get in and out of. Getting these mechanical octopuses was already tough enough."
Su Lun said, "The folks from the Royal family of Luying are offering a reward on the black market for information, and they're willing to spend a lot of money to buy these 'mechanical octopuses.' Even if we sold them in bulk, we could make a fortune. I heard that our mechanical octopus blueprints could be traded for at least the title of a 'hereditary marquis,' not to mention we've got three of the latest 'experimental grade' products. I'm thinking, when we get back, we should have a chat with those military intelligence guys from Luying. Oh, right! The Mafa folks would definitely want them too. When the time comes, we can negotiate with both sides, get a good price..."
Qian Tiao knew that Su Lun was trying to lure out the enemy and agreed, "Yeah, let's decide on that. Once we pick up the man overboard, let's sell the blueprints when we get back. They're no use to us sitting on them anyway."
Despite being close by, the two used communicators to talk.
This type of unencrypted channel was almost effortless to eavesdrop on.
If it was as Su Lun had speculated, then their conversation should have already been intercepted.
If that was the case, it was highly likely that the guy would make his move.
...
There were actually some flaws in the conversation between Su Lun and Qian Tiao.
For instance, why they would fight with the Mafa people, why the blueprints, the mole... these couldn't withstand scrutiny.
But he was certain that the "puppeteer" would take the bait.
Dr. Banks had been the head of an experimental project under Duke Rafael back in Old Lington. So, they were very familiar with the strict confidentiality management system of the laboratory.
Duke Rafael had many secret laboratories working on various projects.
But the laboratories were independent of each other and kept secrets from each other.
Even casually inquiring was considered a serious crime.
Moreover, to preserve technological confidentiality, the biological department, combat department, and mechanical laboratory were completely separate entities. There was almost no communication between members of different departments.
And since the "puppeteer" had come to the North Sea to perform an assassination, he was almost certainly from the combat department. Hence, he likely had no idea about the laboratory's situation.
So, he wouldn't know the specifics about the "mole."
But the conversation between Su Lun and Qian Tiao would make someone's imagination run wild!
Even though three mechanical octopuses had been lost previously in the Rock Caiman Strait, there were six at present. There were also three "Mechanical Octopuses.plus," which were what Su Lun emphasized in the conversation as "the latest products from the laboratory."
The puppeteer definitely didn't know that there was someone else who had mastered "neuro-mechanical technology."
Under normal circumstances, even if a mechanical octopus was captured by any power, even if it fell into the hands of the Mafa military headquarters, it was virtually impossible to have them reverse-engineered so quickly.
In anyone else's mind, the only reasonable explanation would be that something went wrong within Duke Rafael's laboratory, and things leaked out.
But none of that mattered.
What mattered was that there was indeed a problem now, so they had to find a way to mitigate the damage!
The "puppeteer" couldn't chance letting Su Lun and his team leave, and couldn't wait for backup; he had to risk an attack.
Otherwise, once they returned to Pirate City Hastlein, he would lose any chance of acting.
Moreover, he was quite confident in his mechanical octopuses.
If dozens of mechanical octopuses attacked at once, even top professionals would have to keep their distance.
Even if they couldn't kill the enemy, damaging the ship in these deserted waters would be enough to wear these people down to death.
...
As expected.
Shortly after the conversation, Tanni immediately confirmed through the fish in the sea that the group of mechanical octopuses was approaching from underwater.
Su Lun calmly set up some energy barriers beneath his feet, and as he opened the rune-covered black umbrella in his hand, an invisible force of Soul Perception spread out.
With Soul Perception, everything was crystal clear.
Since the enemy was approaching, Su Lun was only then able to perceive clusters of special Soul Fires, which were none other than the mechanical octopuses.
Among these clusters of Soul Fires, there was one that was particularly distinct.
The Soul Fire of a human was completely different from that of an octopus.
With a quick scan, Su Lun instantly identified the guy, who was the "puppeteer"!
He quietly shared this information with Qian Tiao and a few others on the ship, including Dr. Banks, who had the strongest fighting capabilities.
Since the enemy had decided to attack, they were very decisive.
Just then, the sailors at the ship's rail also saw shadows rapidly approaching underwater and cried out in alarm.
"Captain, there are monsters in the water coming towards us! There's a lot of them!"
"Damn it, those tentacled beasts are attacking our ship!"
"..."
Most people didn't understand what was happening, but they could clearly feel the ship's body shaking violently. A "thud" and "crack" could be heard coming from the lower deck.
These were sounds of the ship being chipped away.
Mechanical octopuses were known as the ultimate "ship-breaking weapon." Under normal circumstances, two or three mechanical octopuses could dismantle a wooden sailboat in a short amount of time, let alone dozens.
Just one touch from them, and a three-masted ship started showing signs of capsizing.
Su Lun looked at the situation without the slightest panic, a hint of joy in his heart: "Thirty-eight? Geez, that's quite a number..."
The "Manipulator" didn't make a move earlier, which means that their strength was just so-so.
Otherwise, if they were truly confident about taking them down, they would have acted earlier.
No need to worry too much.
Just then, Su Lun also captured the location of the Manipulator's Soul Fire, and with a roar shouted, "Thirty meters underwater, at the nine o'clock direction! Move, grab that guy!"
"Got it!"
Upon hearing this, Qian Tiao, Dr. Banks, Banner, and a few of the strongest forces on the ship, leaped into the sea without paying any attention to those mechanical octopuses and swam towards the ocean floor.
At the same time, Su Lun pinched his Suren Sorcerer's Seal, and the energy baryte under his feet burst into dazzling light, instantly forming a huge cross in the sky.
"Puppet Mastery · Puppet Theater!"
The moment the cross in the sky lit up, the transparent strands that had been set up on the ship for a long time had also rapidly condensed into physical form.
Those mechanical octopuses were busily trying to break the ship.
Above the sea were churning mechanical tentacles everywhere, making the water look as if it was boiling, extremely terrifying.
The crew were still fighting valiantly.
But whether it was swords or sabers striking those mechanical tentacles, aside from a spark, there was hardly any damage.
Neither musket bullets nor individual bombardments could leave many marks on those mechanical tentacles.
Facing such cluster attacks from mechanical monsters, the Dawn seemed to be in danger of annihilation.
The Manipulator probably thought of a "one-hit kill," sinking the ship and killing as many people on board as possible in an instant. That's why all the mechanical octopuses were concentrated and charged over together.
Unfortunately for them, there was Su Lun on the ship!
To exert force, the mechanical octopuses definitely required a solid anchoring point. Each of those tentacles also adhered to the hull, spreading onto the deck, the cabin, the masts...
It was this kind of close contact that gave Su Lun the opportunity to wrap them with his tendrils.
The moment those dozens of mechanical octopuses appeared, numerous threads that had already covered the entire ship quickly condensed into solid forms. Like capturing prey that fell into a spider's web, the octopuses hardly struggled before being tightly entangled.
Under normal circumstances, it would be impossible for Su Lun to control dozens of powerful mechanical beasts with his threads simultaneously.
Not even the strongest strongman could handle such a feat of strength.
However, after extensive research and crafting, Su Lun now had a complete understanding of the construction of the mechanical octopuses.
As the threads wound around them, the [Spiritual Tendrils] skillfully penetrated the armor joints, finding the octopuses' nerve tissue. Without much effort, he easily stopped those dozens of mechanical octopuses at the source.
Though the Dawn was almost destroyed in an instant, the octopuses only acted ferociously for that moment.
The next second, they were like someone had hit the pause button, staying still on the spot.
The crew members, who were previously in a state of confusion, were instantly dumbfounded, turning their heads to look at the figure standing on a piece of ship wreckage, their eyes shining brightly.
The old team members of Dawn, like Lorota, who had seen Su Lun's abilities, looked at the sky full of threads.
Their expressions changed from shock to extreme joy.
"Mr. Su Lun is mighty!"
"Hahaha... Mr. Su Lun is indeed formidable!"
"..."
Who would have thought that a moment ago it was the brink of annihilation, and in the blink of an eye, it was reversed?
....
This scene even had the "Manipulator" dumbfounded.
The sinking of that pirate ship was as planned, caught by a single encounter.
But what was going on now?
He never would have thought that someone could use this method to crack the nearly invincible mechanical octopus legion.
How could this be...
They had even defeated the fully-equipped naval ships of Mafa without allowing them any chance to fight back, how could they be defeated so easily?
Before he had any more time to think, his surprise turned into horror as a sword qi charged with the force of thunder slashed directly at him.
He saw several figures rushing towards the location where he was hiding!
Every time, he had controlled the mechanical octopus legion from within the sea, never being exposed before. How did these people ascertain his hiding place?
...
If the enemy's trace wasn't discovered, it would be fine, but once found, how could they allow their target to escape?
The methods of Qian Tiao and the others were extremely sharp, there was no chance they would let him escape, even in the sea.
Moreover, after Su Lun took control of the mechanical octopuses, he quickly "turned" the group of octopuses and cornered the Manipulator in the water.
Before long, the fellow was cornered with no way out and was killed by a single strike from Qian Tiao.
This guy was a "Super Mechanical Warrior," and as expected, his own combat ability was around the level of someone with a fourth or fifth-order profession.
However, his mechanical limbs were a bit special with fins on his arms and legs, equipped with a delicately designed [Mechanical Aqua-lung] enabling long periods of underwater swimming and strong concealment abilities. And as expected, a [Communicator Decrypter] was also found on his person.
As for prisoners?
They weren't needed.
Su Lun had the ability to strip Soul Shards.
He devoured the gray mist on the corpse, selecting the information he was interested in.
'You have stripped the soul of 'Sid Haivent.'
'You have gained experience related to the maintenance, repair, and upkeep of mechanical octopuses.'
"You have acquired a large amount of knowledge about mechanical warriors, mechanical experience +554"
"You have harvested a portion of the organizational structure, secret codes, and strength distribution from the memories of Duke Raphael's special legion"
"You extracted some information: 'One of Duke Rafael's large secret bases is located near 'Prospector Sea Island', specializing in the manufacturing of mechanical creatures'..."
"Spiritual Power +4.1"
"..."
...
"The base where Duke Raphael manufactures mechanical octopuses is near a place called 'Prospector Pirate City', in the Nameless Wasteland Sea to the west of the black tower?"
After Su Lun harvested this guy's memories, he immediately became spirited.
It seems that this time, it's not just about harvesting a few dozen mechanical octopuses, but also about uncovering a bigger secret?
These mechanical warriors have been imprinted with an absolute loyalty "thought steel stamp" in their consciousness since they were produced. No matter how they are tortured or even hypnotized, they would not reveal any secrets.
But Su Lun's soul separation technique directly bypassed those will barriers and peeled away this big secret.
"Finally, I know where Duke Raphael's secret factory is..."
Su Lun's thoughts immediately became more active.
A large research base means a large amount of materials, advanced mechanical equipment, numerous research documents, finished products, semi-finished products...
"Damn, becoming a pirate makes my brain reflexively think of one thing, to rob?"
In an instant, Su Lun even came up with some battle plans in his mind.
A completely isolated military base... That means, as much as possible, it's something outsiders should know little about, so its defenses may not be particularly strong.
Was it like the former Old Spiriton Underground City?
Although the intelligence from inside the base isn't detailed, perhaps... some manipulations could be made?
While Su Lun's thoughts were rapidly turning, his teammates in the distance also started to clamor.
A surprise attack battle had ended without much danger, with hardly any casualties.
But the problem was, during the recent battle, their ship had been turned into pieces by the mechanical octopus.
Fragments floated everywhere on the sea surface, with some crew members on lifeboats, others clinging to barrels, masts floating around, looking both miserable and ludicrous.
"Captain Qiantiao, our warship is destroyed, what should we do now?"
"Yeah, this is the Nameless Wasteland Sea, hardly any ships pass by, and it's almost certain we can't get back on lifeboats. The communicator's signal is too far, we can't call for help..."
"Oh~ This is really bad, are we going to feed the sharks together with our mighty captain?"
"..."
The crew members weren't particularly pessimistic, actually somewhat delighted in their misfortune, taking after Qiantiao's heartiness.
Hearing her crew's self-deprecating jokes, Qiantiao rolled her eyes.
She looked at Su Lun again and asked, "Su Lun kid, you should have some preparations, right?"
She was very clear about Su Lun's personality. Since he took action, he must have anticipated this outcome.
Upon hearing this, Dr. Banks also cast an inquiring look at him.
On the sea without a ship is a terrible situation indeed.
Su Lun spread his hands and said, "I do have some preparations indeed. But it will take some time."
Hearing his words, the members of the Dawn Team all let out a sigh of relief.
This Mr. Su Lun, every time in desperate circumstances, could bring them a great surprise.
At the same time, they also wondered, with no ship left, what could be done?
Even if he had spatial storage, at most, he could take out a few small lifeboats, which wouldn't solve the problem at all.
Su Lun didn't explain further. He took a deep breath, pinched the sorcerer's seals, and a black hole slowly formed in the palm of his hand.
Indeed, this was the sorcerer's seals to unlock the fourth-tier armament [Endless Stomach of the Space Whale].
With such a huge storage space, Su Lun naturally wouldn't waste it.
He anticipated possible contingencies, so he crammed all sorts of odd items into the space – mostly large objects that didn't fit in his regular storage space.
The biggest of these was... an entire three-masted sailing ship with a displacement of nearly a thousand tons!
It was indeed possible to store it.
But whether it was storing the ship or releasing it now, both processes were extremely draining.
Su Lun's Spatial Ability was like an ant dragging an elephant. Just opening the "miniature void world" already felt like his dark Spiritual Power was being drained by half.
With no other choice, he took out a pile of Energy Baryte, absorbing it while continuing to pour Dark Spiritual Power into it, enlarging the black hole enough for the ship to come out.
...
The Dawn Team's crew members watched the eerie spatial black hole appear, not understanding at first what Su Lun was up to.
They gathered the floating items from the sea, watching with interest.
However, when a huge three-masted sailing ship slowly emerged from the black hole...
All their gazes froze.
Nobody expected Su Lun to be carrying a warship with him!
Qiantiao, with sparkling eyes full of surprise, murmured to herself, "This kid really did come prepared..."
Even the composed Dr. Banks looked astounded, saying in disbelief, "That... is indeed an extravagant preparation."

chapters.title: Chapter 361 - 361: 360
chapters.content:
Under the astonished gazes of everyone around, Su Lun conjured a three-masted sailing ship out of thin air.
No longer needing to soak in the sea, the crew laughed and chattered as they boarded the ship.
With information from the fish obtained by Tanni, they scoured the nearby waters again and found several more mechanical octopuses.
With the previous ones included, they had captured a total of forty-three.
It was truly a bountiful harvest.
Not counting the cost of labour and technology, the material cost alone made each mechanical octopus worth more than a hundred million liso.
This haul of spoils saved Su Lun billions in costs, as well as one or two months of non-stop production time.
And now, with a small army of mechanical octopuses, they finally possessed a formidable group fighting force.
With a total of forty-eight and enough materials left to produce a few more, Su Lun could, like the guy before him, take on a full fleet head-on.
With these ship-breaking tools, the mechanical octopuses, dozens of them attacking at once, were the nightmare of all warships.
Su Lun also felt that his once-conceived "Mechanical Puppet Army" was finally showing signs of coming to fruition.
As for other mechanical monsters, just these mechanical octopuses alone, with another thousand, wouldn't it be like locusts crossing the land, gods blocking killing gods, demons coming slaying demons?
Although mechanical products performed poorly in the realm of high-level professions, they could still undergo a qualitative change through quantity.
If a thousand were not enough, then ten thousand...
Su Lun felt that the future held great promise.
As for how to acquire ten thousand mechanical octopuses, he already had a "clue."
Beyond the spoils of war, perhaps the greatest gain this time was that piece of intelligence.
He had obtained information on Duke Rafael's secret research base!
When Qiantiao and the others heard this news, they all said they must seize the opportunity to strike a blow. The people of Old Lington, having been "miners" for generations, harboured some resentment against the mine owners.
Su Lun also found it feasible.
After all, they were pirates now!
What if they managed to raid it and realize the dream of a mechanical army?
...
The Dawn Group had a new ship, which was less conspicuous.
Even if they encountered the group from the "Frost Moon Princess" again, they wouldn't be recognized immediately.
The crew were in high spirits, busy salvaging items from the sunken ships before. They also helped paint and tidy up the cabins. The captains were organizing the crew to find their own cabins in preparation for the celebration after the big battle.
As the "New Dawn" sailed, they continued to search for crew members lost at sea during the previous storm.
Su Lun naturally didn't need to worry about these trivial matters.
On the deck, he and Qiantiao were enjoying the sea breeze.
By his side, stood Lolota holding a sword.
This young girl was now always by her teacher's side, sensing the profound and mysterious Sword Intent of the "Sword Saint Realm."
Tanni was silently by Su Lun's side as well, staring into the sea.
Enjoying the breeze was one thing, but Su Lun was more interested in seeing if there were a few "fish that slipped through the net" still to be caught in the sea.
Such windfalls from the sky were always welcome.
After all, who knows how much of Duke Raphael's influence had infiltrated the area.
...
The excitement on Tanni's face didn't fade for a long time.
This new member of the Dawn Group was incredibly earnest and full of energy. He gazed at the sea, acutely sensing everything around him, listening for the responses of the sea creatures.
This was Tanni's first time on a large seafaring vessel, and he felt he couldn't let everyone down; he had to excel as the Dawn Group's chief navigator.
Su Lun watched, a trace of thought flickering in his eyes.
Today they had encountered two fierce battles in a row, but thanks to their meticulous planning, the Dawn Group did not suffer heavy losses.
However, the actual process was rife with danger, and one wrong step could have led to their complete annihilation.
And in the future, such situations would become more common.
The veterans in the group were aware of this, but for a new member, Su Lun thought some things needed to be explained.
The Dawn Group operated with freedom, with almost no restrictions.
If someone felt tired, no longer wishing to wander, they would even receive a severance package.
But since Qiantiao started with those old timers from the "Cross Society," except for those who fell in battle, no one has left.
Looking at Tanni's somewhat youthful face, Su Lun decided to speak up, "Tanni, I was too preoccupied with the battle earlier and didn't ask for your opinion... By the way, what do you think of our Dawn Group?"
After all, they hadn't known each other for too long, and Su Lun's initial invitation for Tanni was merely a transaction.
He offered to provide a potion to delay his mother's petrification in exchange for his cooperation in this unplanned venture.
And because of this right decision, Su Lun saved himself a lot of trouble.
But throughout, no one had ever asked Tanni whether he truly desired to stay with this team for the long term.
After all, his identity and background were also somewhat special.
Upon hearing Su Lun's words, a look of panic flashed across Tanni's face. Thinking he had done something wrong, he anxiously asked, "Mr. Su Lun, what do you mean by that? Have I done something wrong?"
When he was with other pirate crews before, he was always ostracized and neglected by those mean-spirited pirates. Especially due to his special "cursed physique," after encountering storms at sea, he would often be disliked and cursed by others.
At this moment, he thought he had done something wrong.
After all, if there hadn't been the previous storm, those sailors wouldn't have fallen overboard.
Seeing the unease on his face, Su Lun explained with a smile, "What I mean is, our Dawn crew is not an ordinary pirate crew. In the future, we may do a lot of meaningful things, venture to dangerous places, and face many battles, just like today's. The journey ahead will be filled with danger."
He paused for a moment, then continued, "Although we of the Dawn crew really need an outstanding navigator like you, we must also follow your wishes. This is not a transaction; we need a partner who is willing to live and die together."
"I am willing!"
Before the words were even finished, Tanni nodded without hesitation.
Then he spoke very quickly, "Mr. Su Lun, my dream is to become a navigator, an adventurer! To venture into the great sea, to explore unknown waters, I am not afraid of any danger..."
As he spoke, he seemed to realize he was getting too excited and with less confidence, he added softly, "If possible, I... I... I want to be everyone's partner."
Su Lun listened, a faint smile on his lips, "Hmm."
He did not speak further, but Lolota, who was beside him, watched Tanni's cautious demeanor and slapped his shoulder carefreely, saying, "Hey, hey, hey, Mr. Navigator, you don't have to be so formal. Mr. Su Lun is actually very kind and easy to talk to. And look... we are none of those dirty pirate crews. Since we're partners now, no one on the ship will bully you."
She herself had come from a slave gladiatorial arena, and she understood all too well that kind of mentality, sensitive from being oppressed and alienated for long, fearing that one wrong move could strip away the tiny bit of "happiness" just acquired.
Listening to Lolota's words, as if someone had voiced his deepest desires, Tanni bit his lower lip and nodded seriously, "Hmm."
...
Finally, Tanni's intentions to be the chief navigator of the Dawn crew had been confirmed, resolving a important matter.
Fragments of wreckage floated on the sea surface, as the rescue operation continued in an orderly way.
At this point, Su Lun thought of something and asked, "Tanni, did your mother ever tell you who your father is?"
Upon the sudden mention of the father he had never met, Tanni's expression turned gloomy: "No..."
After thinking for a moment, he added, "Mother said my father was a very powerful big shot. I could only learn his name once I became strong enough. Otherwise, it would bring me trouble."
"..."
Su Lun, hearing this, was unsure whether to share his own guess with him.
After all, that 'Pirate King' Sam Bellamy really was one of the few people standing at the pinnacle of that era.
```
Being cautious about claiming someone as your father is probably for the best.
Otherwise, what if you guess wrong?
With a thought, Su Lun merely relayed the information he had discerned and said, "In the[Cursed Gold Coin]you hold, I can feel a mysterious power connected to your bloodline. It will protect you and keep misfortune at bay. Perhaps... it was left to you by your father."
Tanni's face flashed with a glimmer of hope upon hearing this.
However, he then thought of something else and took out his own gold coin and the other two given by Su Lun, saying, "My mother never told me where these gold coins came from. But when I was very little, she told me that only a person favored by destiny could possess these three cursed gold coins. She also said if someone else brings the other two coins to me, that person is to be trusted, and I could go on an adventure with them!"
Su Lun laughed at this, thinking to himself: Indeed, it takes great luck to obtain these two coins.
Just then, Tanni seemed to remember something; he rubbed the three coins in his palm and blew on them. Astonishingly, under the sunlight, the three coins suddenly sparkled with a dazzling golden glow.
Su Lun keenly caught this change, with a light sound of surprise.
All of a sudden, an even more magical scene unfolded.
Just like a rainbow appearing after a storm, an ethereal sea map materialized before their eyes.
The map displayed a vast expanse of blue ocean, dotted with tiny specks that were actually islands. It was as if they were looking down from a great height upon the sea, with the map detailing many islands with names, storm zones, dangerous waters, and areas where sea monsters lurked.
Bristone Trench, Otlantic Volcano, Senarius Chaos Winds, Burning Sea, Narachi Nightmare Phantoms...
One by one, landmark names appeared before them.
Many were infamous "death zones", untouched by man.
"This..."
Su Lun looked on, thunderstruck.
For now the names showing on his appraisal of the three cursed coins had changed; they had become the[Black Sam's World Sea Map]!
[Black Sam's World Sea Map]
Description: An ethereal map made of special memory material; drawn personally by the Pirate King Sam Bellamy, depicting the footprints of his lifetime of adventures at sea; a particularly unique alchemical item, capable of recording coordinates, terrain, climate, wind direction, currents...;
....
Su Lun, gazing at the transformed coins before him, realized what the Pirate King had left behind.
Such a magical alchemical sea map, it was undoubtedly a divine artifact for navigation!
It transformed the map from mere ink on paper to a panoramic view of the actual scenery... a sea area sandbox!
Clearly, Tanni had only tried it on a whim and had no idea the coins would exhibit such a wondrous phenomenon, stuttering, "This... I... I don't know why this is happening."
But as he beheld the stunningly accurate and realistic sea map, he could see the value of the alchemical item, exclaiming in amazement, "My goodness, it records so many places... many of which are uncharted territories never noted on any sea map!"
There is no treasure that could excite a navigator more than obtaining a map of unknown regions beyond their wildest knowledge.
```
The coordinates marked on the sea chart almost include the entire Emperor Luying Empire, the Mafa Empire, the Far North Ice Field, the four nations of the Northern Continent, the West Sea Islands, the Southern Sea... all the territories known to mankind.
"So this is what the world looks like..."
Su Lun's eyes were also filled with immense shock.
He still remembered the shock he felt the first time he saw a world map in his previous life.
Just like now, it was the first time he was seeing the "World Map" of this world.
He had thought that the four nations of the Northern Continent were huge, but on this sea chart, they were just specks of sesame seeds.
The Silent Forest located at the edge of the Far North Ice Field was just a thin line on the edge of the ice field...
Even the three large islands of the Emperor Luying Empire were only the size of fingernails.
There were too many place names marked on this sea chart, and even more regions Su Lun had never heard of.
What secrets did the Western Sea that ultimately sank Black Sam's ship hold?
What lies further to the west?
Does the ocean have an end?
Where does the endless mountain range to the east of the Mafa Empire lead to?
How vast is the Endless Ice Field in the Northern Sea?
Is this realm round, or does it extend infinitely?
...
A flurry of questions surfaced.
Su Lun didn't know how to describe the stir within him, his heart touched by the shock.
Upon seeing this sea chart, an uncontrollable thought emerged from the depths of his heart.
The world is so large, I want to see it all.
He had an urgent desire to set sail and explore, to uncover the secrets of those "fog-covered areas"… and then to mark them on this map.
It felt as if by doing so, he would truly leave his footprints in this world.
No matter the outcome of his life, it would prove that he had been here.
...
Tanni, the professional Navigator, obviously saw even more value in this map, and he was equally stunned.
Looking at Su Lun and Qianjiao, who were both casting glances his way, he explained, "I didn't know about the sea chart inside this Gold Coin before. Then... after I began to continuously hear the voices of sea beasts, I thought I could give it a try. And then, it just happened like this..."
"Hmm."
Su Lun had his suspicions.
Was this a secret that could only be unlocked after awakening a talent?
He felt that it was probably a threshold set by Black Sam for his son—if Tanni had not awakened the ability to "hear the voices of sea beasts," this sea chart would not have been revealed to him.
Now it seemed as if the Pirate King had left something for his child.
Some of Su Lun's concerns also dissipated a great deal.
Even though he knew previously that this was a sea chart left by the Pirate King Sam Bellamy, the level of danger was truly unknown.
After all, there are many malicious people in this world who create fake treasure maps pointing towards dangerous waters to lure adventurous and treasure-seeking navigators to their deaths.
But with Tanni around, those concerns could be put to rest.
Tanni then said, "This Gold Coin records a sea chart, and I already know where it points to. But it's a very dangerous area, to the west..."
Su Lun wasn't too surprised, and he nodded in agreement.
They, the Dawn Group, currently don't have the strength to explore that area.
...
Su Lun spent most of the day on the deck, and the crew had almost all surfaced, but they didn't find any more mechanical octopuses.
So he went to the cabin.
This battle had netted a large amount of war spoils which required his inventory.
In addition to over forty mechanical octopuses, there were also the Mafa Royal Guards they had killed when they intercepted the submarine earlier.
About twenty or thirty storage rings, and two damaged "Lieutenant Colonel level" Mecha suits.
Su Lun did an inventory check of those men's storage rings and found a large amount of ammunition, as well as replacement and supplementary equipment for the Mecha.
Mecha weren't just one thing; they could be outfitted to suit different combat scenarios,
Such as heavy firearms, missile launchers...
It must be said, those coming from the royal family are so rich they're dripping with wealth.
Although these storage rings didn't hold many miscellaneous items, the neat rows of spare military gear and ammunition dazzled Su Lun.
Just considering the few submariners they had killed, the value of their individual equipment was worth at least tens of millions, not to mention the priceless Mecha suits.
The equipment that those ten or twenty people carried could possibly rival plundering dozens of Pirate groups in terms of value.
The mechanical equipment of the Royal Guard Legion is the pinnacle product of Mafa's military achievements, hard to analyze—Su Lun knew the difficulty was immense.
He didn't bother to put in the effort.
Su Lun took out his experimental equipment and set up a temporary mechanical laboratory in the captain's room.
He intended to focus on researching the mechanical octopus, as this was the path to rapidly developing combat capabilities.
Once everything was in place, Su Lun sat at the workbench and carefully analyzed the blueprints he had drawn earlier.
He wanted to refine this batch of mechanical octopuses.
The design concept of the current mechanical octopus was actually quite perfect already. It had a super-strong metallic body with strong defense against both magic and physical attacks; it also had excitation alloys and special runes, making it less affected by spiritual power or other mysterious methods; motion control systems, kinetic systems... there was almost nothing to criticize.
This was definitely the result of many years of research and experimentation by a large team.
If it weren't for someone like Su Lun who could use spiritual threads for direct "physical control," under normal circumstances, a fourth or fifth-stage professional facing a single mechanical octopus would have to hack away for a long time. Either they had the strength to directly sever the metal tentacles like Thousand did, or a group of forty or fifty would be enough to give a sixth-stage professional pause.
Although Su Lun felt there probably wasn't anyone with physical "spiritual tentacles" like his, the extraordinary powers in this world were varied and strange.
Small workshops had their advantages, allowing for cutting-edge use of certain materials.
He planned to reinforce these mechanical octopuses in his area of expertise with rune enhancements and direct control using mysterious powers.
Once he had a clear plan, he became busy.
And so, Su Lun spent several days absorbed in the cabin.
...
One day, Su Lun was researching the mechanical octopus when he suddenly noticed the two decapitated mecha armors he had confiscated in the lab.
These were only "Lieutenant Colonel" level mecha armors, not very high-end.
And with only two, Su Lun hadn't originally planned to dismantle them first.
But then, an idea occurred to him—if there were mechanical octopuses underwater, what about on land?
Equipped with various gears, mecha armors were more than suitable.
Yet another thought crossed his mind—if he encountered them again, would he just have to slash them in two with the black scythe and hope for luck to pick up some scraps?
Without a complete mecha armor, even if he managed to repair one, there would be significant problems.
Su Lun's hands were still working with the mechanical octopus, but his thoughts became active.
The "Colonel Grade Slayer IX Mecha Armor" he had encountered before was killed directly by a special seal item like the "Bow of Time," which shot the controller inside the mecha.
He lacked such an item.
What he did have was a "Rune-Carved Human Skin Black Umbrella."
But this umbrella had strict usage conditions and was almost restricted to one-on-one encounters. Moreover, if he faced a high-grade armor, the opponent could still escape.
What if he ran into a group of mechanical warriors again? How would he deal with them?
Moreover, the people of the Mafa Empire had a habit of destroying their technology.
As Su Lun's thoughts branched out, he suddenly felt vexed.
Now he knew that it was highly probable there was a "secret mechanical research institute" near "Princess Frostmoon," and he had marked the location of one of the submarines.
But that presented a problem.
