If he met them again and managed to successfully ambush them, what if they triggered the self-destruct mechanism?
Su Lun was confident in picking off the enemy one by one, but he had no way to deal with self-destruction.
If he hustled and only managed to gather a pile of scrap metal afterward, that was certainly not what he wanted.
But neither he, Thousand, Dr. Banks, nor anyone from the Dawn Group had the means to kill someone through the mecha armor.
Show a hint of a domineering air, and the enemies would willingly bow down and submit?
Impossible...
"What method could there be to seize the submarine intact? Without a special curse item, it has to be a mysterious technique. Deploy a virus? Dr. Banks would have that capability, but how to deploy it inside is a big problem. Or maybe a mental sorcerer... I'm still far from that level," Su Lun pondered more, his frown deepening.
He went through all the possessions and abilities he had, even considering the people he knew.
There was no suitable method.
Even if Mr. Jing showed up, it seemed he couldn't resolve the issue.
Su Lun felt slightly frustrated.
It was like the gold mine was right in front of him, yet he lacked the tools to refine the ore. Could he only rely on luck to find nuggets?
"Eh...!"
Suddenly, something dawned on Su Lun, and his expression turned fierce.
If it was about mental control, Su Lun couldn't do it himself, but he knew someone far stronger than him.
"Pandora's seduction powers are extremely strong, isn't that the very pinnacle of spiritual control?"
It was then that Su Lun remembered the alchemy homunculus that had been locked away in the "Minor Void Realm" for a long time.

chapters.title: Chapter 362 - 361: Contract
chapters.content:
This was a draft to be reviewed later. Su Lun had never dared to release "Pandora" before, because he knew that doing so would definitely cause big trouble.
Although he still hadn't figured out exactly what the renamed "Princess of the Night" had been up to in Mountain Hermit, it was certain that the current "Moon Emperor" of Mountain Hermit, Takeda Nobuyasu, was her puppet. Moreover, she had special ways to communicate with the "Great God of Moon Reading."
This woman had countless secrets, the kind that you would know are bound to cause endless trouble, even if you thought with your toes.
If it hadn't been for his urgent effort to save people at the beginning, and if Su Lun were to consider it now, even with several more guts, he would not dare to provoke her.
However, also because of his decisiveness back then, he had now managed to bring her out, but was troubled about how to handle her.
In Pirate City Hastelin, there were many from Mountain Hermit, and previously Su Lun did not dare to release her. But now, in this deserted sea area, he felt that perhaps it was worth a try.
...
As Su Lun thought of this, he put down the mechanical octopus he had been tinkering with and stepped out of the captain's cabin.
On the deck, Qian Tiao and the crew were having a heated exchange.
They were wrestling, as was routine for Dawn Group.
Sailing days could be dull, and everyone found enjoyment in combat.
Among the trio of giant brothers, the constant wrestling champion faced his opponent "The Butcher" Banner, as if they were trying to distinguish a winner between mechanical and physical power.
The nearby crew cheered and shouted, creating a harmonious atmosphere.
In these past few days, Tanni and the former members of Squad 19 had fully integrated into the new "Dawn Group," enjoying themselves immensely.
Seeing Su Lun approach the deck, everyone greeted him, "Mr. Su Lun, you've come."
Even those who were unfamiliar with him from before had come to fully recognize this Mr. Su Lun during the battle a few days ago.
Whether it was his ability to control dozens of mechanical octopuses or conjure a large ship out of thin air, everyone was deeply impressed.
Though Qian Tiao was the captain of Dawn Group, no one felt excluded.
Because they all knew that Mr. Su Lun had a special relationship with their captain.
After all, both of them stayed in the captain's cabin at night.
Qian Tiao, seeing Su Lun emerge, joked, "Yo... you decided to come out and get some air?"
After responding to everyone and making some small talk, Su Lun finally got to the point, "I need your help with something."
"Oh?"
Qian Tiao was curious, not understanding the complexity of research, nor did she know what Su Lun might need her help with.
Su Lun did not explain further, "Come on, let's talk in the cabin."
He led Qian Tiao to the lab where Dr. Banks had been waiting for a while.
Seeing the elaborate setup of multiple alchemy arrays, Qian Tiao became even more puzzled, "What are you trying to do, setting up such an extravagant isolation formation?"
Su Lun said, "Haven't I told you before? I have also captured that 'Princess of the Night.'
Listening, an irksome glance flickered in Qian Tiao's eyes as she asked, "The 'First Beauty' of the world?"
Su Lun rolled his eyes, was that the point?
He continued, "This time, I plan to let her out. If I can control her, that would be best. If not, I'll need to talk with her. Of course, the worst-case scenario could lead to some undesirable incidents. So every three seconds, I'll pull a string. If I get controlled or any other abnormal situation occurs, please, Qian Tiao and Dr. Banks, handle it immediately..."
Su Lun knew that Pandora's mental enchantments wouldn't affect him, but since his own outbreak had been quite sudden last time, she had been caught off guard. Now that she had been confined for so long, releasing her inevitably might cause problems.
After all, she was a "Human-Shaped Sealed Artifact."
Dr. Banks, listening nearby, nodded, "Hmm."
Qian Tiao, having clashed with that synthetic human before, knew her prowess. Listening to Su Lun, she asked, "Are you confident?"
Su Lun replied indifferently, "It has to be handled eventually. If handled well, it could bring us much help later on."
Listening to Su Lun having considered everything thoroughly, both Qian Tiao and Dr. Banks did not say more.
After giving his instructions, Su Lun then entered a small room that had been arranged with various enchantments.
...
With Qian Tiao and Dr. Banks outside the room, Su Lun felt that if anything truly went wrong, it could still be managed in time.
Then he took a deep breath before starting to form the sorcerer's seals.
The Hexagram Alchemy Array beneath his feet brightened, and a vortex black hole slowly appeared in the palm of his hand.
Su Lun closed his eyes, relying on Soul Perception to pull out Pandora, who was wrapped in a cocoon in the "Minor Void Realm."
Fearing she might have hidden something special on her, Su Lun had already stripped her clean before capturing her.
To prevent her from struggling, he had performed many counter-joint movements. Now, suspended on the thread, she probably assumed a quite embarrassing posture.
Nevertheless, Su Lun did not open his eyes to look.
He pushed some thread forward, exposing Pandora's mouth.
It must have been the long confinement, but Pandora appeared very calm, so calm that, if not for her even breathing, one might think her a corpse hanging there.
For a long while, neither of them spoke.
Constantly monitoring his own panel, Su Lun saw no negative statuses and finally took the initiative to speak, "Do you not wish to talk?"
Hearing this, Pandora sneered coldly, "Hmph. What is there to talk about? You don't want to kill me, but you covet my powers. Isn't the only reason you're letting me out to enslave me and make me serve you? No matter what I say, would you actually let me go?"
Su Lun was not surprised by this reaction.
After all, she was a synthetically created being who had existed for a thousand years; her mental acuity was not lacking. Moreover, considering the schemes she concocted with Mountain Hermit to change dynasties, her cunning was far from ordinary.
He abandoned the idea of verbal persuasion.
Su Lun was merely testing the waters.
Calmly, he stated, "Oh. That's perfect then. I don't need to beat around the bush anymore."
With that, he pulled out various enslavement contract scrolls, interrogation potions, mental distortion spell scrolls, memory-altering hypnotic crystals from his storage ring...
He had been holding these items in Hastelin, and although he had been too scared to let her out, Su Lun had certainly come prepared.
He had scavenged various mind-enslaving cursed items, scrolls, and techniques from the black market, gathering dozens of assorted types—almost everything available had been procured.
Just like when he had subdued Sabina in Old Lington, contracts were very effective against enemy factions.
Since Pandora had called out his intentions, Su Lun felt no more guilt.
Against his enemies, he never hesitated.
Su Lun immediately took out an enslavement scroll and tore it open, a beam of light shooting onto Pandora's forehead.
This was a nefarious scroll from "Black Witchcraft," bought at a good price from the black market, usually used by traffickers to subdue people's wills. This was the highest grade available, costing nearly a million leise.
However, when the scroll's light fell on Pandora, there was absolutely no reaction.
Su Lun raised an eyebrow, unfazed, and picked up another object—a pink crystal skull.
This was a cursed item named "Ophelius's Crystal Skull," capable of altering a person's memories at a subconscious level.
Muttering the accompanying curse, the skull began to emit wisps of eerie pink light, resembling pale smoke...
But as soon as the pink light approached, it immediately dissipated, as if some mysterious force had thwarted the low-level spell.
"..."
Seeing this, Su Lun's eyebrows slowly furrowed, hinting at a puzzle forming yet guessing at something.
These attempts were not only tests of effectiveness but also to confirm some of his suspicions.
After several more failures, Su Lun continued patiently trying.
Following the eighth failure, he took out a scroll emitting sinister black smoke.
This was another "ancient artifact," a bargain picked up from the black market. A scroll used by a demon sorcerer of an ancient civilization to contract demons.
Su Lun took out the Black Scythe and gently waved it, unhesitatingly slicing across the exposed lips of Pandora, creating a cut.
Though the wound healed instantly, Su Lun had collected some of her blood and dripped it onto the scroll.
This time, however, the blood sizzled on the scroll like acid, erasing the entire black scroll in an instant.
Su Lun's pupils shrank sharply, finally confirming something, a realization dawned on him: so that's how it is...
But this act ultimately enraged Pandora. Although she was a synthetic being, no one had ever dared to cut her face. She scorned mercilessly, "Hmph! Stop wasting time on such foolish actions. If you knew what you were doing now, you'd find yourself ridiculous!"
Su Lun glanced at her, "You're finally willing to talk?"
"If I were you, I'd stop these foolish acts."
Pandora's tone was full of indifference, seemingly conveying a special confidence that she could not be enslaved by any means and would not die.
She was created to be the most perfect life form in the world. How could her proud self ever submit to a human?
Listening, Su Lun retorted, "Are you suggesting that even if you were killed, you wouldn't die?"
Pandora snorted coldly and did not respond.
But then, Su Lun added, "Or are you implying... that you are a deity?"
His tone was very calm yet conveyed a hint of mockery to Pandora.
Most importantly, he was right!
Upon hearing this, Pandora, though she said nothing, could not hide her shock.
Indeed, she would not die—she just couldn't bear to part with her perfect body.
Without beating around the bush, Su Lun spoke directly, "I've always been puzzled why you could summon the great deity 'Tsukiyomi.' After all, that's the personified avatar of the faith gathered by the people of Mountain Hermit. You, a synthetic alchemist creation, should not possibly have received a response from them. Now I generally have confirmed one thing... It wasn't Tsukiyomi who responded to you, but rather, you are 'Tsukiyomi' yourself, aren't you?!"
The previous scroll that burned away was an advanced level demon contract scroll already.
The material was made of demigod-level demon leather.
Theoretically, even eighth or ninth rank demons couldn't break such a high-level contract.
"It's not about whether the contract can succeed, at the very least it definitely wouldn't burn the entire scroll due to a backlash from the contract."
"Since it was burned, it means that the goal of his contract was higher than the upper limit of the scroll!"
"In this realm, that is nearly impossible."
"The only explanation would be those 'Outer Gods' or 'Pseudo-Gods' or something like that."
"Thinking back to the situation with Mountain Hermit, Su Lun's thoughts suddenly became clear."
He then said, "I'm very curious, how did you manage to have a god attach to your soul?"
....
Pandora had early on experienced the meticulousness of Su Lun's mind during the battle when she was captured.
Now, hearing her greatest mystery being broken down by someone else, she suddenly became very calm, all arrogance swept away; she remained silent without speaking.
Su Lun continued, "Although I don't know how you've done it, I think, I can guess what you really want to do."
"The more chips I hold in my hand, the more qualified I am to negotiate with this woman," he said. "My teacher and my master once had a project called 'Pandora,' an alchemist's artificial human project. Eventually, they wanted not only to create an artificial human but to create... a god! So, you used the stolen Power of Faith from Mountain Hermit and became a god through this method, right?"
Having finished, even Su Lun felt shocked.
To create a god?
My teachers were indeed incredibly powerful.
And, looking at it now, their plan had already succeeded halfway.
"Now the entire Mountain Hermit worships the 'Great God Tsukuyomi,' and perhaps in the future, this Pandora might indeed ascend from a 'Pseudo-God' to a 'True God.'
After all, as an alchemical artificial human, her life is extraordinarily long."
Hearing this, Pandora fell silent.
After pondering for quite a while, she suddenly asked, "Who is your teacher?"
Su Lun replied, "Miss Sereya."
Hearing that name, Pandora could no longer stay composed. "Heh, how is that possible?!"
That was the great person who created her, almost like a 'mother' to her. Even hearing that name stirred uncontrollable nostalgia within her.
Back then, her consciousness had just begun to sprout, pure like that of a baby. For an alchemical puppet to develop its own consciousness was incredibly difficult; it required endless nurturing and love. With emotions, a soul could be born.
Back then, the entire world was her voice, her shadow...
How nostalgic.
Su Lun caught the change in her tone, finally feeling like there might be a chance, "I don't know how to explain it to you, but it is a fact. I met Miss Sereya in the cursed space of the ruins in Dawn City, and I was fortunate to become her disciple."
He briefly explained what had happened, then added, "I think you can also see that I am a descendant of the 'Puppeteer' lineage."
Pandora naturally wouldn't believe such a thing just from a few words.
After all, that was a person from a thousand years ago.
But upon mentioning that name, her mindset gradually calmed down a lot, and she finally took the initiative to ask, "What are your terms?"
Su Lun said, "Obey me."
Upon hearing this, Pandora scoffed, not bothering to hide her disdain. "Impossible! Even if I abandon this body, you will not get your wish!"
Su Lun wasn't surprised, but he did catch a piece of information—she could abandon her body, but she didn't want to!
He then said, "Then let's change the terms. I can give you your freedom, but you'll need to help me with some things. In addition, you cannot do anything detrimental to me or to my friends."
He had just tried, and at the moment, he really had no way to deal with Pandora.
If he didn't kill her, it would certainly cause problems sooner or later.
After all, he now knew she had stolen the Power of Faith and become a 'Pseudo-God'!
And luckily, he had isolated her in the 'Little Void Realm'; otherwise, keeping her by his side would indeed cause major trouble.
Oh no!
If he let her out, she might have already made contact with the people in Mountain Hermit!
Su Lun suddenly thought of something, his tone urgent as he shouted, "You have one minute to consider. I need a definite answer!"
He even felt that Pandora's silence was just buying time.
If it dragged on, it could result in serious trouble!
Among smart people, once their intentions are seen through, there's no need for pretense.
Pandora listened, and understanding what Su Lun was thinking, her tone grew more confident; besides a cold laugh, she said nothing.
Seeing this, Su Lun said coldly, "Don't doubt my resolve. Even though you are my teacher's creation, I will not hesitate to kill you. My teacher would understand why I did this."
Although Pandora's alchemical body was a supreme treasure, Su Lun absolutely meant what he said!
He would not hesitate for a moment, even if it meant destroying a treasure under his control.
Pandora: "Are you threatening me?"
Su Lun: "You can think that."
Upon hearing this, Pandora no longer doubted his determination, but her tone became somewhat odd: "Are you truly a disciple of Seraya?"
Su Lun responded solemnly again: "Yes!"
Thinking of something, Pandora pondered for a moment.
Some people are too proud to lie.
She did not persist in her arrogance anymore and said, "You want to help the God Clan recover the divine rights of faith? Haha... I can tell you that it's impossible. Moreover, I can tell you responsibly that what you are doing won't change anything. Because 'Amaterasu' was defeated by me during the Black Sun Grand Festival. You guessed correctly, the divine faith of Amaterasu has been stripped by me, or rather, the entire faith of Mountain Hermit country has now been centered on me. Even if I allowed the God Clan to ascend, 'Amaterasu' would not descend again. Without a thousand years, do not even think about re-establishing the faith system of the Igahin Shrine. Moreover, doing so would cause the entire faith structure of Mountain Hermit to collapse..."
Her words were coherent and outlined the current religious predicament of Mountain Hermit.
Su Lun finally understood why Pandora had been so hostile and cautious.
To tamper with the divine rights of faith in Mountain Hermit was to shake her very foundation of godliness.
However, Su Lun originally had little regard for the faith in Mountain Hermit.
Although he very much wanted to help the Princess, the current circumstances, as Pandora described, were indeed factual.
Even if the God Clan rose to power again, it would not change anything.
This was a conclusion the Princess had already deduced herself.
Su Lun said, "Let's not discuss Mountain Hermit for now. My previous offer stands. What I need your help with is something else. I need you to intervene at critical moments and help me solve some problems."
Pandora: "That's all? Are you sure you won't bring it up again later?"
She was somewhat moved.
The condition was not too harsh.
Su Lun said, "We can sign a contract."
A contract of equality could easily be signed, provided that both parties were willing.
Upon hearing about the contract, Pandora agreed without hesitation: "Alright!"
Su Lun, hearing her readily agree, also breathed a sigh of relief.
The special measures he had prepared earlier would no longer be necessary, which saved him a lot of trouble.
He took out a top-level alchemy contract and wrote down a series of clauses. He had considered everything and written it in the terms, leaving no loophole for her to exploit.
After writing, Su Lun loosened a few threads, revealing Pandora's eyes.
He said, "There, you can look at the contract now. If there are no issues, we can proceed to sign."
After many days, Pandora finally saw light. She opened her eyes and saw the man before her with his eyes closed.
Thinking back on the humiliating days of her captivity, she couldn't help but sneer: "What, you dare to strip my clothes but don't have the courage to look at me directly?"
This tone naturally carried some resentment.
As a woman, an alchemist, and a deity, it was natural to harbor resentment being treated so shamefully.
Su Lun understood, of course, and said, "I meant no offense. If you feel so, after signing the contract, I can apologize for my actions."
Pandora, hearing this, swallowed her anger. After all, the situation had reached this point, and she was still bound, not allowing her much say.
Besides, since the beginning of their fight, this man had never opened his eyes.
Although it was this little fox's prudence, it wasn't too offensive.
Moreover, she was somewhat surprised that a man could resist looking at her body, known as 'The First Beauty'."
With a fleeting thought, Pandora glanced at the terms of the contract.
Indeed, it was very detailed.
So detailed that she could not find any opportunity to rebel.
However, she was filled with disdain.
A mortal and a deity signing a contract?
Tsk tsk... Don't you know that's utterly meaningless?
She simply stated, "Fine, just like that."
Su Lun simply handed her the pen, then released one of her arms from its bindings.
Pandora did not hesitate to sign her name and then dropped a drop of blood on the scroll.
Su Lun did not look, but through the threads, he precisely captured something — the name she signed was actually "Pandora P. Isaac"!
It was Isaac's surname?

chapters.title: Chapter 363 - 362: Void Ghost Hand
chapters.content:
Pandora signed her name and then turned and said, "Alright, I've signed the contract as well, can you let me go now?"
Su Lun listened but was not in a hurry.
He had already offended her and didn't mind tying her up a little longer.
He then picked up a pen and began to sign his own name.
However, he did not sign immediately.
Su Lun was very aware that a contract was reciprocal.
In the field of alchemy there is a basic concept, reciprocal energy that qualifies for stability.
This applies to contracts as well.
Even in equal contracts, the two parties are not far apart in strength, only then can there be equality.
If the strength differs too much, such contracts have no binding power.
Especially for those "pseudo-gods" who are inherently a level higher than humans in terms of life, if it's just a signature, that contract is nothing but waste paper.
But if he could think of using a contract to bind Pandora, where would he not consider this point?
Just then, Su Lun took out a beast skin scroll, mumbling words, and chanted, "In the name of the great God of Nature, the lord of the Wind and Rain Forest, the God of Poems and Freedom, I recite your sacred name, and request your witness to an equal contract..."
Since he himself didn't have that power, he might as well ask a real deity to be the notary.
The "God of Nature" at the law level is not something any ordinary deity can match.
With this witness, probably no one in this realm would dare defy the contract.
This was the divine scroll he had brought from the Dalu tribe, a farewell gift from Yuta, a cherishable item indeed.
Using it here, he could not consider it a loss.
After all, this Pandora was very special, not only a homunculus but also the "Moon Reader," with an immeasurable future.
At least in this realm, Su Lun did not want to become her enemy.
...
Pandora listened to the sacred names Su Lun recited and furrowed her brows instantly.
Being a cultivator of divine path herself, how could she not know that those sacred names actually pointed to the laws controlled by that deity? These consecutive titles made her frown even more.
"This guy isn't an alchemist; is he actually trying to invoke a response from a higher deity?"
Pandora was greatly puzzled.
This act was as incomprehensible as when Su Lun knew she was the "Moon Reader."'
Moreover, in this shattered realm, no deities existed.
The followers of deity were considered "The Forsaken," so this action made her somewhat puzzled.
However, the puzzlement only lasted a moment, then it turned into shock!
"He actually received a response from a real high deity?!"
When Pandora felt that indescribable will descend, her face drastically changed.
Although she herself was a "deity," she was merely flaunting her supremacy in this broken realm; in front of this true deity, she was nothing.
No one knew better than her how terrifying the "God of Nature" who had responded to Su Lun was!
Pandora immediately understood what Su Lun was up to; this sly guy, had actually summoned a real high deity as a witness?
Immediately, the slight hope she had vanished instantly, and she sighed slightly, conceding.
Fortunately, that indescribable will only lasted a moment before disappearing.
Both Su Lun and Pandora felt a great weight lifted from their shoulders.
After the descent of the divine will, the contract scroll also acquired a ring of bright, mysterious patterns.
It was a third-party witness's mark, left by a True God.
Su Lun saw the contract established and heaved a great sigh of relief.
Only then did he gather all the threads that had bound Pandora. He also took out the storage ring, clothes, everything that he had stripped from her before, and said, "These are your items. However, the 'Yata Mirror' has been given to someone else..."
When taking someone's belongings, it was naturally right to mention it.
"You gave it to that little princess of the Shinto family, didn't you?"
Pandora stepped onto the ground barefoot, no longer suspended; she felt incredibly relaxed.
She just stood there naked, moving her limbs. The threads left no marks on her body, that sculpted figure flawless from start to end, epitomizing 'perfection.'
If anyone else were here, seeing this stunningly beautiful body, they definitely would not be able to look away.
Unfortunately, the only spectator had his eyes closed.
Her tone was somewhat contemptuous, yet she did not pursue further, and said, "Forget it. That item is of no use to me now, given away is given away."
Now that she had taken the faith of the Mountain Hermit, becoming the "Great God Moon Reader," she was no longer constrained by a single divine artifact.
Rustling sounds of clothing came from beside his ear; Su Lun listened, she must have been getting dressed.
Between clever people, there's no need to beat around the bush, just say what you think directly.
He thought for a moment, then added, "As for that 'Death's Novel', if possible, I'd like to keep it in hand to use as material for job advancement in the future."
Although he still couldn't comprehend some of the information contained in the "novel", he felt it should be highly compatible. After all, his prosthetic gear had a "Little Void World"; what if it became a Great Void World, or even an entire plane in the future... wouldn't it be a complete world? The idea of "creating worlds" was all written in the novel, and there was much he could learn from it.
Hearing this, Pandora scoffed coldly, "Hah. You're really not shy."
But she seemed indifferent as well; after all, if that thing could be used once, it wouldn't count for much against high-tier professionals a second time.
Su Lun listened to her implicit consent and shamelessly thought: As a captive, it's only right to strip some spoils of war.
He then asked, "By the way, can you use this 'Death's Novel' to seal high-tier professions now?"
Pandora, hearing his increasingly outrageous words, replied discontentedly, "No! That ability can only be used within the Mountain Hermit Nation, in the places where faith is most concentrated. Here, the cost I would have to pay is huge."
At that point, before Su Lun could continue chatting, she directly added, "Give me a room, don't bother with me, I don't want to see anyone else. I agree to act once, but you better think it through before you call on me!"
"..."
Su Lun listened as she finished getting dressed and then he finally opened his eyes.
He caught sight of that exquisitely flawless, breathtaking face.
Heh, beautiful indeed, but that arrogant, haughty demeanor, just like a stubborn ancestor.
But after all, she is a "deity".
Su Lun was initially curious about how she became "Tsukiyomi", but seeing her attitude, it was good enough that they hadn't fallen out.
Perhaps... she would discuss it another day.
They might not be friends now, but they were no longer enemies either.
A cooperative relationship is also fine, no guilt in taking advantage thoroughly.
So thought Su Lun.
....
Su Lun left the "Sealing Chamber".
The two guards by the door saw him emerge and immediately looked as if they were facing a great enemy.
Sen's hand rested on the handle of his sword, while a dark aura rose from Dr. Banks.
"All's well now."
Su Lun shook his head and made a pre-arranged secret handshake.
Seeing this, Sen and Dr. Banks both let out a long breath, their expressions showing immense relief.
Both were very aware of Su Lun's character; any situation he handled with such caution inside had to be incredibly perilous.
Sen and Dr. Banks naturally sensed that there was an additional person inside. But due to the previous restrictions that completely blocked any energy fluctuations, they didn't know what had transpired.
Now that all was well, Sen finally spoke up, "So, you settled things with that woman?"
Su Lun heard his phrasing and felt something was amiss, so he honestly replied, "A contract has been signed; she won't be causing us any trouble."
Turning his head, he raised an eyebrow, "But she also doesn't want to deal with us."
"Hmph."
Sen gave a dismissive snort, indifferent.
She didn't even want to engage with that woman.
However, she was more curious about how Su Lun had managed it, considering that woman, being the "world's number one beauty," had been forcefully taken. And now she had willingly signed the contract?
She incredulously asked, "So, what did you do to that woman that made her not want to kill you? I thought there would be a fierce battle."
Su Lun furrowed his brows, recalling the events that had just transpired, which were too complex to cover in a few words, "Let's go to the deck and I'll explain slowly."
He had a feeling that Pandora was willing to sign the contract due to the situation, but perhaps, and more so, because of his master "Sereia."
Sen was greatly interested and, hooking her arm through Su Lun's, they headed to the deck. As Su Lun divulged that Pandora was "Tsukiyomi", her expression grew incredibly vivid...
...
An extra person was on the ship, unknown to everyone but Su Lun and a few others.
Pandora also never appeared before the people.
They trailed the submarine's markers, heading north.
The "Frost Moon Princess" Skadi, as Su Lun had guessed, really went to the waters near "Roman Nation."
Tanni's "cursed by the sea" reputation was well-earned; as they sailed north, they encountered storms and huge waves multiple times—events some sailors never experience in a lifetime, but they faced it repeatedly.
Fortunately, Tanni's keen sense of stormy weather always turned peril into safety.
Apart from some sea sickness among the crew and some damage to the ship, there were no severe impacts.
Moreover, after multiple storms, Tanni seemed to gain some insights into his unknown talent. He could sense storms earlier and handle them more calmly.
Even, Tanni felt, he might be able to actively manipulate storms to some extent.
If one could proactively control the storms, such ability would definitely defy the heavens. At sea, he alone would be worth countless fleets!
To hear the sounds of the sea beasts and to induce storms...
Su Lun still didn't know what his talent was called.
Since ancient times, humanity had many talents, the common ones recorded in the books, but there were also many rare awakening talents barely known, thus gradually fading from transmission.
Yet, often those very rare awakened talents carried some miraculously skilled abilities.
Su Lun felt that Tanni must be the son of Pirate King Sam, so perhaps he had also inherited some of his father's special abilities.
After all, to reach the top in this cruel supernatural world, one's talent must be exceptional.
....
With "Black Sam's World Navigation=Sea Map" and having Tanni, a top navigator aboard, Su Lun and his team were like having satellite positioning, clearly knowing their precise coordinates in the ocean. They didn't need to rely on just large directions and instinct as before.
During their journey, they continually perfected the map.
In the following days, Su Lun didn't leave his cabin again.
The job of modifying over forty mechanical octopuses was not small, and would likely take about half a month.
The crew of the Dawn group were still carefree, laughing all day long, engaged in various bizarre contests.
Now, there was also a major activity added, which was fishing out "big fellows" from the sea to improve their food.
Previously when they encountered fierce deep-sea monsters, they avoided them at all costs, because those big fellows could accidentally overturn and smash the ship.
But now with Tanni's perception, they could identify their position in advance.
Moreover, the most crucial factor was that Senjo was already a "Sword Saint." Rakshasa Woman was naturally born for combat, and no one on the ship could beat her; she was idle all day long. Apart from practicing her sword, she could only find adversaries in the sea.
Thus, hunting the giant beasts became the most exciting activity for the Dawn group.
The participation of the big fellows was also very high, after all, the supply of food carried by the ship was limited, and they couldn't possibly use all the space equipment to store food, nor could they store much. But the Giant Tribe's three brothers, the sumo wrestlers, ate a lot, and the limited amount always left them feeling hungry. Moreover, the higher the profession, the more calories food needed to provide, especially in battle, leading to a huge consumption of food.
Now without that concern, capturing a sea beast bigger than the ship meant everyone could eat until they burst.
Then, stuffed with food, they continued fighting and hunting sea beasts.
This vast sea provided countless delicious foods and treasures.
...
After sailing for several more days, they had already reached the vicinity of the "Roman Nation."
It was a theocratic nation known for producing "Heroes" and top "Gladiators."
That day, in the cabin,
Su Lun was tinkering with the mechanical octopuses.
After days of hard labor, he had essentially upgraded those dozens of mechanical octopuses to the "PLUS" version.
As for Pandora, Su Lun naturally took care of her daily.
After all, she would be a crucial determinant in how much they could harvest when they encountered a submarine again in the future.
Su Lun did not want some residual annoyance to affect his plans.
The more they talked, the better their relationship, not always cold anymore.
Although their topics mostly revolved around his teacher "Celia."
Everything was developing in a positive direction.
Just then, suddenly, a special communicator started making a "zzz" static noise.
"Huh...did it connect?"
Su Lun uttered in surprise, looking over.
This communicator was a military encrypted communicator from Lu Ying, previously left by the "Sacred Judgment Legion" commander "Ferocious Beast" Alek Barrett for convenient communication.
But this communicator had a limited connection range, and after leaving Pirate City for Mountain Hermit, there had been no contact.
After such a long time, Su Lun thought they had been annihilated.
After all, he hadn't heard that they had surrendered to King Oleg of the North Sea, so in this region of the North Sea, without supplies, they would hardly survive.
He even thought that those "Activated Silvers" had gone nowhere, but now they had managed to connect?
....
At the same time, hundreds of sea miles away.
Three pirate ships were chasing a modified Lu Ying sail military vessel.
The primary flags on those three pirate ships belonged to the North Sea Fleet, displaying the Wolf Fang Club insignia, but the squadron flag designs were not any known under Oleg's seventeen squadrons.
It was a flag featuring a skull and a starry background, resembling a pirate ship sailing through the void.
On the deck, a group of people huddled together, watching the clumsily fleeing ship ahead, faces sporting mocking, amused expressions.
Once chased around the world by the Lu Ying Navy, now it was their turn to have the prestigious "Sacred Judgment Legion" running all over the place.
The pirates chuckled and laughed, intermittently firing a few shots to create splashes on the sea surface.
This was Duo Luo Sai Er·Castillo, the deputy commander of the "Void Fleet," the newly formed eighteenth squadron of the North Sea Fleet, and a sixth-order professional known as the "Void Ghost Hand"!
Having chased for two days without success, the pirates were also losing their patience.
"Hey, boss, we've been chasing them for two days and nights," one of them said, "Why go to all this trouble? Barrett's only got one arm now, much weaker than before. If you were to make a move, wouldn't you capture him easily? After all, you have successfully fused with that extremely rare high-order dark gold artifact, the 'Void Ghost Hand.' No one below the seventh order can match you!"
"The commander trained by the RuYing royal family isn't so simple to deal with. I am confident that I could kill the Barrett, but you are underestimating him. Even with one arm gone, if he really fought desperately, he could take half our crew down with him. Do you believe that?"
"That strong?"
"What else? That guy is feigning weakness, actually waiting for us to charge in so that they can fight back desperately. Now, by dragging this out until their supplies are exhausted, slowly wearing them down, that's the best choice. Don't worry,"
"The boss is wise!"
"The boss is mighty!"
"Hahaha... The boss's strategies are unparalleled!"
"You guys shouldn't use the old way of thinking anymore. King Oleg now has his crown, we are no longer just pirates, but the royal special guard legion. Although RuYing has caused us a lot of trouble in the past, people with military talent are rare. His Majesty has said that if we want to move towards regularization, we start with reforming the fleet."
"But if we keep pursuing like this, could something go wrong?"
"What could go wrong? The targets that our North Sea Fleet wants, no one dares to protect them."
"Humph! Even if someone comes, they are just courting death. Our 'Void Fleet' has never shown itself before the public, and now that we have emerged, we must let the whole North Sea... no, the entire RuYing know our power!"
"..."
A group of pirates started to revel on the deck.
All of them had fused a few Void artifacts and space-related advanced materials, and with control over the void, their combat abilities were far beyond those of ordinary pirates.
...
On the dilapidated warship.
Barrett looked at the three pirate ships hanging not too far behind, his face looking grim.
"Commander, those pirates are not falling for it. They don't seem to intend to clash directly. It looks like they plan to wear us down alive," one spoke.
"We're running out of potions and fresh water. The wounds of the brothers who were injured earlier are worsening. If we don't find a way to resupply soon, we... we might be in trouble," another added.
"Commander, shall we charge at those dirty pirates?"
"..."
Hearing this, Barrett was silent, his fists clenched as if to squeeze water from them.
The "Sacred Judgment Legion" was indeed in a dire situation now.
Although they still had the strength to fight, without supplies, they would be worn down alive.
Should they submit to the pirates?
Though no longer royal knights, they would not betray their honor to survive.
The despicable pirates of the North Sea had always been enemies of RuYing, and now, with their own kingdom, they were even more so.
Thy had lost their honor and their status, but they still had their dignity.
Even though they weren't afraid of death as career soldiers, seeing his brothers, whom he personally led, dying from lack of medicine, Barrett felt bitterness in his heart.
Barrett was plunged into an unprecedented confusion.
Ever since the RuYing royal family declared the legion disbanded for "treason," he felt as if he and his brothers, who had once fought and died for the empire, were abandoned by the world.
They had no identity, nowhere to go, no one to take them in...
Aimlessly drifting on the sea.
They had heard that a group of members from the "Holy Legion" in the empire's capital had been secretly bought by slave traders and sent to Roma as gladiators.
They thought to rescue those brothers.
It was a ploy.
But knowing it was a ploy, they still had to come.
Now they were driven into a corner.
As Barrett's thoughts raced, he reminisced about his life.
He had fought for the empire, achieving famous victories, yet he never expected to end up in such a predicament.
Then suddenly, someone reported.
"Commander! Someone is contacting us through encrypted communication!"
"Who?"
"He said he's the person who traded 'Living Silver' with you last time!"
Upon hearing this, Barrett's expression and gaze sharpened slightly.
He thought of that young man named "Su Lun."

chapters.title: Chapter 364 - 363 I Alone Am The Legion
chapters.content:
"That young man is actually nearby?"
On the deck, Captain Barrett frowned tightly upon hearing the communication link.
In his heart, he also silently thought it was somewhat fortuitous, just didn't expect to encounter him at this time.
From the communicator, came a voice in conversation.
"Captain Barrett, are you in the nearby waters?"
"Yes."
"It's like this, didn't we have a deal last time? The 'Hand of Silver' you needed has been prepared, and I thought if it's convenient, we could meet and you could try it."
"..."
On the battered deck of the warship, about a hundred members of the "Sacred Judgment Legion" all stared at the communicator, a special gleam emerging in their eyes.
This was the only time they had been contacted by an outsider in such a long time.
Barrett listened to the words coming from the communicator, yet his eyes showed contemplation.
If it weren't for their current predicament, he really would want to meet.
The "New Dawn City" mentioned by the young man, he was also very interested in it.
These days drifting at sea, he truly had come to a realization. What royal knights, generational honors... they weren't that important anymore. Once how much he hoped for military achievements to be ennobled, now it seemed, even somewhat laughable.
On the other hand, the "Freedom City" which aimed for human civilization's advancement and for the study of alchemy, he had grown very interested. Though it was still just an "ideal state," if it really could be established, it seemed to be a good place to go.
Unfortunately, there was no chance now.
After not having spoken for a long time, Su Lun's inquiry came from the other end of the communicator.
"What's the matter, Captain Barrett, is there some inconvenience on your end?"
"..."
Hearing this, Barrett was just about to speak when his deputy suddenly interrupted, his face complex, saying, "Captain! We..."
He swallowed his words, but didn't speak them.
Barrett turned his head to look at other members again, all of whom were also looking at him synchronously. Seemingly twinkling in their eyes were stars, the despair at its extreme, the last flicker of hope.
Barrett shook his head, knowing well what his brothers were thinking.
This was their only hope.
If they could get supplies, perhaps they could hold on a bit longer.
"Su Lun my friend, could you help deploy some supplies in the nearby waters?"
"Supplies? Have you run into trouble?"
"Yes."
"How much trouble?"
"Quite troublesome."
"Is it pirates, or people from Ruying?"
"Pirates."
"Which group? Is it Oleg's people?"
"..."
From the other end of the communicator, came a series of inquiries.
The questions were very detailed, seemingly to confirm exactly who it was, before considering whether to provide supplies.
Barrett was just about to respond, when the deputy again interjected, "Captain! If we tell them our current real situation, they probably won't dare to come. After all, in the North Sea, no one dares to offend Oleg's fleet. Even if it's just deploying supplies, being known could cause trouble, nobody dares..."
He knew that his own Captain Barrett was absolutely honest and would not lie, but right now if they did not get supplies, they simply could not hold on.
Moreover, now they had enemies all over the world, really having no allies, and nothing much
Barrett looked at everyone, lightly shook his head, clearly indicating that their situation was not worth dragging others into.
The soldiers looked at him and said no more.
Barrett picked up the communicator and truthfully said, "We've been pursued by Oleg's 'Eighteenth Fleet' and are in a very dangerous situation. Su Lun my friend, if it's convenient, please deploy some potions and fresh water supplies in the sea. If it's not convenient... then we'll contact you later."
Upon hearing this, one could see the faces of all the soldiers of the "Sacred Judgment Legion" turn grim.
In their minds, since it was known it was the King of the North Sea's forces chasing them, naturally nobody would dare to come.
This lone hope for supplies was also slipping through their fingers.
As expected, after Barrett said that, the other end of the communicator fell silent for a while.
It seemed they were frightened, with no response coming through.
...
Barrett sighed lightly, feeling nothing particular about it.
Seeking benefits and avoiding harm, it's human nature.
Just as he was about to put down the communicator, suddenly, the other end spoke again, "Isn't Oleg supposed to have only seventeen fleets? What's this 'Eighteenth Fleet' about? Could it be... you've encountered the 'Void Fleet'?"
Barrett was startled hearing this, as the other party didn't mention anything about supplying, but instead inquired about these... irrelevant matters?
"You've heard of this fleet?"
"Yes. I've encountered a few before, and guessed a bit."
"Your information is surprisingly accurate."
"..."
Barrett's expression turned slightly odd, why did it seem that the other's tone, instead of being cautious of Oleg, contained a hint of anticipation?
Who exactly was this guy, knowing about the "Void Fleet"?
What did that expectant tone mean?
Could he have misheard?
Right at that moment, the communicator rang again, "That... what's the highest rank on their side? How many ships, how many people in total?"
Barrett's eye twitched sharply when he heard this.
He finally realized that he hadn't misheard, but rather, the person across from him was truly expecting something, "What do you mean?"
Barrett responded, but a highly unlikely yet seemingly factual thought had already emerged in his mind: Could this guy be planning to target that Void fleet?
Could it be that "Dawn City" has become so powerful that it can ignore the North Sea fleet?
However, he had guessed correctly.
At this moment, the voice came through the communicator again, "What I mean is, if they aren't above the seventh tier, I and my companions might be able to lend a small hand."
Hearing this, a dense anticipation shot through Barrett's eyes, his voice trembling slightly with excitement, "You... which power do you belong to?"
He had met Su Lun before and knew the young man to be meticulous and steady. Since he had spoken, he must be quite confident!
The response came through, "Didn't I tell you? New Dawn City. But we've just started organizing, calling it the 'Dawn Group.'"
Upon hearing this, not just Barrett, but all the soldiers aboard his ship showed expressions of shock.
Following the shock, they were overcome with the wild joy of having survived a close call.
After days of desperate escape, at last, they saw a glimmer of hope for survival!
...
On the other hand, aboard the Dawn.
Su Lun had gathered everyone on the deck.
The faces of the crew were filled with intense excitement and anticipation.
"Brothers, there's work to do this time! There are three ships on their side, a total of twelve hundred people. One sixth-tier professional, seven fifth-tier. It's time to see how many they can handle, and how many Barrett can hold off."
Su Lun explained the situation on the other side to everyone on the ship,
Although Barrett's "Sacred Judgment Corps" had been pursued for several days, they had figured out the strength of their pursuers, especially the abilities and tactics of those high-tier professionals, almost clearly.
With this detailed information, Su Lun benefited tremendously.
Now that he knew the overall combat power of his adversaries, naturally... he could take them on.
The King of the North Sea and his men were already enemies, the crew was thrilled at the prospect of beating them.
After assigning tasks, everyone began to organize their equipment and ammunition.
Su Lun also released the mechanical octopuses into the sea.
In the last two days, using components from the spoils of war, he had made two more, now totaling fifty mechanical octopuses.
These mechanical monsters would destroy the enemy ships at the first opportunity.
Tanni was also very excited, perched atop the mast holding the "Demon Blade Zongzheng," accumulating Sword Qi.
For her, the most anticipated thing was clashing with a master.
Su Lun climbed up to the mast, landing beside Tanni, and spoke in detail, "Sister Tanni, be careful when the time comes. The deputy commander of the eighteenth fleet, 'Demon Hand' Duo Luo Sai Er·Castillo, has fused with a high-tier dark gold Void-prosthesis, which can almost ignore elemental barriers and Protective True Qi of other professionals at the same tier, dealing actual damage to the body. He is a Fighter, but his weakness is that he can only fight in close combat. The troublesome part is his ability for Void Displacement..."
Even though he mentioned a sixth-tier, Tanni was not at all daunted. Her eyes brimmed with high fighting spirit, saying, "In that case, it indeed is a bit tricky. But my Sword Qi's long-range attack capability is not weak; even if I may not beat him, at least I should be able to hold him off."
Su Lun nodded, "Yes, that would be best. Once I have destroyed their ships, I'll come help you. I have a cursed item that can limit Spatial Displacement; we'll give that guy a severe blow at the crucial moment! As long as we kill that sixth-tier, the other problems won't be big. If they fall into the water, we'll fight together."
Tanni's face was full of eager fighting spirit, "Good!"
In the control room, Tanni was directing the sailors to maneuver the sails.
The sea breeze blew, the sails bulged, and the Dawn cut through the waves like an arrow released from its bow.
...
Meanwhile, on the "Sacred Judgment Corps" ship after the communication had been cut off.
Hearing that someone would come to support them, Barrett and his subordinates were also hopeful. They eagerly awaited on the deck, looking out over the endless sea.
The weather was very good today,
but they had not seen any ships for a long time.
After the excitement, they fell into contemplation.
"Captain, is that 'Su Lun' reliable? Dare they really come?"
"Yeah, this North Sea, no one dares to offend the North Sea fleet... and even if willing, they might not have the strength."
"Yes. Those pirates are very strong and have mastered Void abilities; ordinary fleets simply can't handle them. Unless a seventh-tier professional comes, we really can't resolve our predicament."
"..."
The team members discussed amidst themselves,
most fearful that after having hope, they might not see hope realized.
What if the hope turned out to be in vain?
Barrett remained silent, he alone knew that the young man named "Su Lun" would never act recklessly.
Just as everyone was peering expectantly, suddenly, the lookout atop the mast shouted.
"They're coming!"
"Captain, look quickly, there's the shadow of a sail at the five o'clock direction!"
"Really? Where?"
"My god, they've really come!"
"..."
The crew members were immensely excited, each grabbing telescopes to look in that direction.
They indeed saw the sails, then a warship appeared.
It was a three-masted sailing ship.
Everyone's eyes also showed wild joy. It seemed, they had indeed come!
But after waiting a moment more,
they could see clearly.
One ship?
"Only" one ship had come to support them?
"Only one ship?"
"This... Could there be a top-tier professional? It doesn't look like it."
"..."
The people on the ship gazed at the lone warship appearing on the screen, full of confusion.
They said they were wary of offending Oleg, but he really came.
They claimed to be sincerely coming to the rescue, but there was only one ship?
The enemy had three top-tier sailing warships, and if a sea battle truly ensued, they had not the slightest advantage.
Even Captain Barrett furrowed his brow as he watched.
Large-scale naval battles often hinge on the number of ships and cannons; if they were to clash directly, they had already fallen into a severe disadvantage before the fight could even begin.
At that moment, someone exclaimed.
"Captain, there are two people coming over the sea!"
"That spider rig is quite peculiar, actually allowing for rapid movement across the sea."
"Anyone daring enough to come over must be a high-level fighter. Sensor officer, what's the situation on your end?"
"Captain, it seems... their strongest is only level five, and the fluctuation from the other spider arm is only level four."
"..."
Hearing the report from the sensory professional, Captain Barrett and the crew were visibly astounded.
...
At the same time.
When Captain Barrett was able to spot Su Lun and his group, the scoundrels of the North Sea fleet noticed as well.
On the deck, the pirates looking at the three-masted sailboat showed no concern, just disdain and anger.
"Eh... Which group is this? Didn't they see our North Sea Fleet flag?"
"They aren't flying a flag, probably frightened of us recognizing them. Looks like it's support Barrett has found. Hmph, it doesn't matter who it is, the person the North Sea Fleet wants to intercept, even the Ruying Emperor cannot save!"
"Blind fools, no need for pleasantries, if they dare come close, sink them directly."
"Yes, Captain!"
The group of pirates didn't take the distant ship seriously at all.
Both in terms of cannons and ship strength, they were far behind!
...
Su Lun, moving swiftly across the sea with Qian Tiao, got close to the "Sacred Judgment Legion's" ship and, seeing the battered warship, they also immediately understood the predicament of Captain Barrett and his men.
The deck was crowded with people, each casting suspicious glances at the two people over the sea.
From a distance, the battle-scarred Barrett called out, "Su Lun, my young friend, long time no see."
His voice boomed like a bell, echoing across the entire sea.
Regardless of the outcome, since he dared come in person, Barrett owed him this favor.
Listening to the greeting, Su Lun responded with a smile, "Long time no see, Captain Barrett!"
But he could also see through Barrett's calm appearance to the fatigue he couldn't completely hide.
As the two approached, they stepped lightly over the water and boarded the ship.
Su Lun climbed onto the deck, and Barrett approached to greet him.
Even in such a dire situation, the legion commander, whose face was as chiseled as if by axe and knife, wore a broad, open-hearted smile, saying, "Young friend Su Lun's courage and wisdom impress me deeply! Your gesture is well noted by Barrett and all the soldiers of the 'Judgment Legion'!"
As he spoke, he immediately pulled out a storage ring, saying, "This is something from our last transaction. It would be even better, young friend Su Lun, if you brought some supplies."
"…"
Su Lun watched as Barrett handed the storage ring over directly, assuming it contained the "Living Silver" inside.
Barrett then pointed to the three pirate ships hanging not far away, saying, "The situation with these pirates I mentioned in the communicator previously is very tricky. They are targeting us specifically. We appreciate your gesture, Su Lun. Leave the supplies and then please make your departure quickly, to avoid any collateral damage."
Su Lun didn't dawdle, accepting the storage ring handed over.
Barrett's words were
this is his way of setting the threshold.
He probably thought that Su Lun came because he couldn't let go of these divine materials.
By giving him the items first, he acknowledged the "favour" of taking such a risk boarding the ship.
If they didn't have the power to assist, they could just as well leave then.
However, Su Lun showed no intention of leaving; instead, he said, "I have already prepared the 'Hand of Silver' I promised you before. But it looks like it's too late for transplantation now. Uh... what I mean is, Mr. Barrett, how much combat power do you have left?"
"Combat power?"
Barrett listened with an unchanged expression, but a hint of suspicion quickly flitted across his eyes. Why ask such a question at this crucial moment?
Nonetheless, he responded truthfully, "The loss of my arm has greatly affected my combat power; at most, I have only forty percent of my peak capabilities. However... if it comes to a desperate fight, I can still function like a common sixth-level professional."
Su Lun listened and nodded, "That's good then."
Asking about combat power naturally meant that there was a fight coming. Barrett vaguely guessed something but could hardly believe it, asking, "What do you mean?"
"Hmm…"
Pausing for a moment, Su Lun said emotionlessly, "I plan to annihilate that group of pirates behind us."
His words were soft, but clear enough for everyone on the ship to hear.
Upon hearing this, it was like a thunderclap on a clear day, setting off a storm in the hearts of the "Sacred Legion."
Annihilate?
This choice of words...
Could I have heard it wrong?
This brought deep suspicion in everyone's mind.
Captain Barrett glanced at the Dawn, being very cautious as he asked, "Did your Dawn team just bring top experts?"
Su Lun knew they had misunderstood and replied, "No, just us."
As he spoke, he introduced the person beside him, "This is the leader of our Dawn team, Ms. Ottilia Evelyn. My plan is for you and us to go first, hold off their high-end combat power. Then, we'll annihilate them all."
Barrett gave a knight's salute, "It's an honor to meet you, Miss Ottilia."
It had been a long time since anyone had called her by her real name, and it felt awkward, but she also said, "Captain Barrett, it's an honor to meet you as well."
Hearing that this "fifth order" swordsman was the leader, the nearby soldiers of the Sacred Judgment, though not showing any disrespect, couldn't help but feel stunned internally.
Is this it?
If the leader is only fifth order, the team members must be even lower.
And they have only one ship.
With neither numerical nor ship advantage, how could they fight against those pirates?
Barrett looked at Su Lun, feeling as if he had misunderstood something, then asked again, "You mean, just 'us' going to wipe out those pirates?"
"Yes."
Su Lun nodded his head, unsure how to explain further.
Both he and Ni Tanni's combat power were not something ordinary people could understand, but no matter what, outsiders surely wouldn't believe it.
Just as he was wondering how to start explaining, Ni Tanni suddenly rested her hand on the hilt of her sword.
In that instant, her aura burst forth. She hadn't moved, yet it felt as if she had stepped out of hell itself, a vast Sword Intent sweeping across the entire deck.
With that display of authority, the tremendous force of her presence caused everyone to step back in unison, their faces changing color instantly. They were all struck dumb, unable to speak as they stared at Ni Tanni in shock.
Those who had awakened to Sword Intent were renowned experts wherever they went.
But a fifth order professional managing to awaken to Sword Intent? Unheard of!
The soldiers began to wonder, who exactly was this hitherto unknown swordsman? What divine power did she possess?
Barrett, whose perception was deepest, looked at Ni Tanni with sheer disbelief and admiration, "Your excellency has come from afar as a Sword Saint; I have been disrespectful!"
With that, he saluted again.
A salute of respect for a formidable fighter.
The sharp Sword Qi that had flashed momentarily, even he felt a strong, fatal threat.
Swordsmen were reputed as one of the professions with the strongest killing intent.
And among them, a Sword Saint was extremely rare.
This one... was very strong!
Ni Tanni just nodded.
On the side, Su Lun said, "So, my plan is, Captain Barrett, the three of us will go first to restrain them. Once I destroy their ship, we'll go together. We need to resolve the battle as quickly as possible."
At that moment, Barrett finally believed that these two really came to rescue.
If there was a Sword Saint, indeed, they had the strength to fight.
However, were it to be a head-on clash, Barrett estimated, it might still end in a 20 to 80 situation?
Su Lun didn't explain further, because just then, he noticed that the three ships behind had already turned their cannons, seemingly ready to fire.
He looked at Barrett and said, "That's the plan. So, Mr. Barrett, are you willing to go first with us?"
Barrett hesitated only for a moment before saying boldly, "Alright!"
With that, his deputy and subordinates spoke up, "Captain!"
Just the three of them going, wasn't it a suicide mission?
And sending the leader... this tactic, didn't it seem like something an enemy spy would plan?
Barrett shook his head; he looked to Su Lun, his eyes full of resolve, "I trust in the strength of young Su Lun. Everyone, just follow his battle plan later and adapt to the situation!"
At this time, he had no other choice.
And indeed, his instincts also told him that the person before him was trustworthy.
Su Lun wasn't surprised to hear this.
From the previous incident in the Cursed Valley, when Barrett had defied the empress's orders to organize the intelligence people to break the seal, Su Lun knew this was a man he could work with.
Honest, brave, and trustworthy.
....
Su Lun didn't say much more.
He, Ni Tanni, and Barrett jumped onto an assault boat.
Under the anxious gazes of the Sacred Judgment team on board, they headed straight towards the three approaching pirate ships.
The wind today was not small, causing the assault boat to bob and weave significantly on the sea.
Su Lun watched the pirate ships in the distance, silent.
Ni Tanni's expression was also very calm.
Although Barrett appeared composed, the puzzlement in his heart grew stronger. Since boarding the ship, he had yet to understand where the confidence of these two people came from.
Finally, he couldn't hold back any longer and asked, "Young friend Su Lun...that is, although I'm not questioning your tactics. But are we directly charging over just like this?"
Su Lun explained briefly, "Yes. I need to get close to those three ships to employ my tactics. At that point, we will be focused with fire, and my safety will depend on you two. But as long as we restrain Demon Hand, Duo Luo Sai Er·Castillo, the rest should be manageable."
Upon hearing this, Barrett's eyelid twitched violently; so it wasn't that he had misunderstood, the plan was indeed just this straightforward and brutal.
He pondered momentarily, then said, "So all we need to do is hold off that Duo Luo Sai Er? But they have over a thousand men. And those with Void capabilities are very troublesome. My men and your Dawn team clashing head-on with them... might lead to severe losses..."
Su Lun interrupted and corrected, "Not us, but you and Ni Tanni sister to hold him off. The rest... you can leave to me."
Dawn Team + Sacred Judgment Team = two teams?
No,
It's three.
He, Su Lun, was an army by himself!

chapters.title: Chapter 365 - 364: Naval Battle
chapters.content:
Su Lun and his two companions rode the assault boat, cutting through the waves and heading straight towards their destination, while the people aboard those three pirate ships from the North Sea Fleet also took notice.
The pirates crowded the deck, ready for a good laugh.
"Yo... has Barrett finally decided not to be stubborn and is coming to surrender?"
"He only brought two people with him, probably here to negotiate."
"Something's wrong. Look at their warship, and that three-masted sailing ship at the nine o'clock direction that's not flying any flags. Why does it seem like they are approaching us?"
"If they dare enter firing range, sink them. Hmph, blind as a bat, they deserve death if they die. The high-caliber cannons supported by the Mafa Empire will come in handy..."
"Do you sense any other stealth units?"
"Boss, no. Our sensing feedback confirmed it too, aside from Barrett, the other swordsman is fifth order, and the guy steering at the back is just fourth order."
"..."
On the deck of the pirate ship.
The pirates, gathered in groups, stood there joking and laughing.
The sixth-order Vice Fleet Commander 'Demon Hand' Dorosel, along with several fifth-order squadron captains and fourth-order team leaders, watched the swiftly approaching assault boat with an air of ease, not regarding it as a serious threat.
No matter how one looked at it, the other party should be here to negotiate.
After all, with just three people, and without a seventh-order professional, any nefarious intentions would simply lead to a pointless death.
But as the assault boat drew closer, Dorosel started to feel an ominous premonition rising within him, for some reason.
Reaching the sixth order, his crisis detection ability was extraordinary.
He picked up the long telescope in his hands once more, squinting at that approaching assault boat, his gaze growing ever more solemn.
But he couldn't pinpoint the source of his unease.
...
Aboard the assault boat, even the battle-hardened Barrett's breathing grew slightly heavy.
The three pirate ships ahead exerted a deathly pressure on him, and the closer they got, the more the deck's dense hostility felt like a mountain pressing down, making his scalp tingle.
After so many years in the military, he had never attempted such a crazy "tactic."
The highest commander charging straight into the enemy's stronghold, with the legion behind?
But he didn't question any further.
When he agreed to this tactic, he had already put his life out of his mind.
Su Lun was also not careless, knowing full well that the North Sea Fleet was the pinnacle of pirate strength. There were many high-level fourth and fifth-order warriors on the three ships, and they were not to be underestimated with over a thousand enemies. The situation could change in an instant, and he was still analyzing every possibility based on the current circumstances.
Qian led the way without speaking, her hand resting on her sword sheath, continuously charging her Sword Qi.
At this point, Su Lun also noticed that those pirates seemed to be somewhat alert. He said, "Get a bit closer, within a hundred meters would be best."
Listening to this, Barrett frowned and responded, "Dorosel might not let us get that close. The guy is a sixth-order professional, after all. He must have sensed something."
"Then we'll raise a flag to negotiate."
Su Lun had a look of being prepared all along on his face.
As he spoke, he took out two small flags, signaling with them.
At sea, there was a universal flag signaling system for long-distance communication between ships.
Nearly every ship is fitted with a "Signal Officer."
Su Lun, having previously acquired this skill, wielded the small flags with extreme dexterity, signaling: We want to negotiate.
This move would also make the opposing pirates believe he was just a "minor character."
Su Lun never cared about being seen as an icon—minor character or big shot, it was all the same to him.
With a battle imminent, the more inconspicuous he was, the safer he would be.
Barrett watched his action, and the expression that flickered across his face was quickly concealed, thinking: He really did come prepared.
...
As expected.
Because of the negotiation flag signal that Su Lun sent, the cannons aimed at them did not open fire, and they smoothly closed in on the group of pirates.
The three pirate ships formed a '品' shape, surrounding the assault boat within.
The pirate underlings, not sensing the imminent danger, each gathered at the ship's railing to enjoy the spectacle.
'Demon Hand' Dorosel, though feeling uneasy, couldn't imagine by any stretch that these three before him stood any chance of success.
Where did this sense of crisis come from?
Out of caution, he didn't let Barrett board right away but instead spoke from a higher position, "Captain Barrett, what's this? You've seen the light and want to have a talk?"
"..."
Barrett looked at the pirates, each with a mocking expression, with utter disdain in his heart.
He would rather die than submit to these pirates.
However, Barrett also knew he needed to buy some time for Su Lun behind him.
So he didn't rush to express his stance.
At the stern of the boat, Su Lun appeared to be operating the engine, staying quiet as his "nobody." The invisible threads in his hands, however, had sunk into the sea below.
Dorosel was no fool; looking at Barrett's subtle facial expressions, his suspicion in his eyes deepened.
Seeing this, a squadron captain nearby immediately caught on. He threw a pair of shackles over and said, "Barrett, since you want to negotiate, put on these 'magic-restraining handcuffs' and come aboard to talk."
Barrett didn't even look at the handcuffs, his face flushed with the fury of feeling insulted and retorted, "This is how the North Sea Fleet treats its guests? Ha, I came here to negotiate, Barrett is not a prisoner of war!"
He was stalling for time, since a fight was inevitable anyway.
While saying this, he also didn't forget to mock, "Dorosel, such a big fleet commander you are, and that's all the courage you've got? Haha..."
With those words, the atmosphere instantly became awkward.
Dorosel, with furrowed brows on hearing this, wasn't upset because of the mockery but rather, the sense of unease within him grew stronger and stronger.
Yet he didn't know where this unease stemmed from.
A one-armed "Ferocious Beast" Barrett was not worth such treatment.
But after all, with three squadrons and over a thousand subordinates watching, Dorotheus could not possibly show weakness.
Everyone was talking about negotiations, after all, the mighty Northern Sea Fleet wouldn't possibly lack the courage to negotiate, right?
Just as he was about to call Barrett aboard...
Suddenly,
An unexpected situation arose!
These pirates were not all fools, there were various skilled individuals on the ship, and those with perceptive professions also keenly detected something was off in the sea.
At that moment, someone shouted loudly.
"Captain, something's not right! There's something in the sea!"
"It looks like a lot of big octopuses, and they're heading towards us!"
"Damn it, we've been tricked! Open fire, kill them!"
"..."
The pirates on the three pirate ships immediately reacted.
In this situation, it would indeed be foolish if they still didn't understand what was happening.
Upon hearing the news, "Demon Hand" Dorotheus's face turned pale, and seeing the group of transparent shadows rapidly approaching the ships through the sea, he finally understood the source of the unease in his heart!
Barrett was only pretending to negotiate, in reality, he was planning a battle to the death!
Yet even at this moment, he still couldn't understand, with over a thousand brothers, on what basis did the opposition dare to make a move?
...
The mechanical octopuses had a special light-absorbing coating on their surfaces, especially in the water, which made them look like transparent jelly, hard to detect with the naked eye.
Even if a "transparent octopus" were to be considered a new species, it wouldn't be surprising in the bountiful Endless Sea.
Even if someone did discover them, they would likely be mistaken for a new species and not immediately thought of as a means of attack.
But the cluster approaching the ships was too evident and was discovered.
Su Lun listened to the pirates discovering the mechanical octopuses approaching in the water, his gaze suddenly became sharp.
But he was not the least bit surprised.
Having dragged on for so long was already perfect.
Since they had been discovered, there was no need to hide any longer...
Su Lun's mouth curved into a sinister smile, his ten fingers clawed at the void, and he pulled out dozens of strands of thread. As soon as the kinetic system activated, the mechanical tentacles of the octopuses retracted and propelled forward, like pressurized springs being released, their speed increasing several-fold.
In the span of a few breaths, dozens of octopuses neared the bottoms of the three ships!
If any of the mechanical octopuses got a tentacle attached to the underside of a ship, the other tentacles could effortlessly wrap around it.
In just a moment, fifty mechanical octopuses had all climbed onto the three pirate ships, beginning their ship-sabotage operations.
"Boss, something doesn't seem right!"
"Damn it, those octopuses are made of steel, and our muskets can't affect them! Harpoons are useless too!"
"No good, those monsters are destroying our warships!"
"..."
The pirates quickly realized a terrifying fact.
They thought they were being attacked by sea monsters, only to find out they were "mechanical creatures" they had never heard of before.
This completely overturned their understanding.
Although they had been quick to notice and respond, mechanical octopuses, most of whose functions were designed for ship sabotage, were "ship-breaking tools." Once they were activated, there was simply no chance for human response.
Each ship had more than a dozen octopuses attached to it, and in an instant, the "crack" and "snap" of breaking wood was incessant.
The exaggerated twisting force of the mechanical tentacles and the ship-sabotaging equipment crushed the wrapped hulls into pieces in an instant.
Vast amounts of seawater poured into the cabins, and all three pirate ships began sinking rapidly almost simultaneously.
Even though a few fifth-order Pirate Squadron Captains reacted quickly and used Spatial Ability to sever some tentacles, they still couldn't prevent the three ships from breaking apart and sinking into the sea.
The pirates screamed and fell into the water, each one in a sorry state.
"How... how could this happen..."
"Demon Hand" Dorotheus's eyes were filled with disbelief.
He could never have imagined that just in one encounter, his three warships would be sunk right before his eyes!
At the same time, several dozen lifeboats were being lowered from that distant warship and the three-masted sailboat, and hundreds of people were rushing towards them.
"Damn it!"
The fleet commander's face darkened, and with a powerful stomp, he charged towards the assault boats, shouting: "Kill them first!"
Intuition told Dorotheus that he had to kill the three individuals in front of him first, otherwise big trouble would ensue.
Moreover, he just realized that the "Signal Officer" he initially thought was insignificant seemed to be the real ringleader controlling these mechanical octopuses!
...
The group of pirates was caught off guard and was utterly astonished.
Similarly, Barrett was just as deeply shocked by the scene before him as those pirates!
"Mechanical octopuses?!"
Though he had anticipated Su Lun would solve the problem with some surprising method, he had not expected it to be this kind of method.
But looking at the mechanical tentacles boiling on the sea surface, he still couldn't believe what he was seeing.
Having been a high-ranking officer in Ruying, he was naturally aware of some cutting-edge technology.
Looking at these mechanical octopuses, he immediately guessed something.
"So he has already mastered neural-mechanical technology..."
Barrett's heart was filled with deep amazement for a long time.
He actually did it... he sank three main battleships of the North Sea Fleet with just one encounter.
Moreover, what shocked him even more was yet to come!
...
"Demon Hand" Dorosel, after all a sixth-tier professional, charged towards the assault boat carrying Su Lun and two others as soon as he realized something was amiss.
Barrett had been keeping an eye on this guy. Seeing that disappearing figure, he suppressed his shock and urgently shouted in his heart, "He's coming!"
From the previous battle, he had already experienced this person's fearsomeness firsthand, with his Spatial Teleportation and "True Damage Demon Hand," undoubtedly a nightmare for any professional of the same class.
Not a hint of fear showed on Barrett's face; he resolved himself that, even at the cost of his life, he would not let this man harm Su Lun!
However, before he could even move, he suddenly felt a domineering and heaven-piercing Sword Intent rise beside him.
Suddenly, it was as if he heard the sharp clang of a sword being drawn from its sheath beside his ear.
In that moment, thunderclouds suddenly rolled in the sky, and the sky darkened instantly. All of a sudden, a purple-red lightning bolt flashed from the dark clouds, striking the sea with a "crack," casting a sinister red glow on the faces of hundreds of people.
"Thundering Hell!"
A thousand faces showed fierce battle intent, their robes fluttering loudly due to the overpowering aura.
The Sword Qi that had been accumulating for so long burst forth like a dam breaking at the moment the "Demon Blade Sect Master" was drawn from its sheath.
After she drew her sword, the six-armed Rakshasa shadow behind her instantly solidified.
Another look revealed three barrels of thunder drums, drawing countless lightning serpents from the sky, converging at the tip of the blade and sharply slashing down, "One Blade Style · Fleet Wind Battleship!"
A "whoosh" of sword Qi burst forth, tearing through the sky.
At such a close distance, Barrett felt the impact most deeply, instantly experiencing a hair-raising sense of impending death.
Even though the sword Qi wasn't directed at him, he felt as if countless sharp blades were grazing over his body, a sensation of steel scraping against bone.
"Is this her Sword Dao... such a tyrannical thunderous Sword Intent."
Barrett could no longer describe the shock in his heart.
The Sword Intent previously emitted on the ship was not even one-thousandth of what it was now!
He had never seen a fifth-tier Sword Saint with such a dominant and terrifying Sword Intent before.
Moreover, it wasn't just the exaggerated realm of her Sword Dao. Barrett looked at the second form of the Rakshasa Woman's shadow behind her; that was the rarest part.
"Second form, [Rakshasa Woman], a demonically talented nature..."
A myriad of thoughts flashed through Barrett's mind in an instant.
In his life, he had seen too many geniuses in Ruying; he himself had also grown up bearing the halo of a "prodigy." Yet, looking at the person before him, he felt like he was truly witnessing an "outstanding prodigy."
And that blade, filled with monstrous demonic energy... was clearly no ordinary item.
All of it...
Far exceeded Barrett's earlier expectations.
