The whole world had abandoned them once, now, the Dawn Squad gave them new hope.
...
Su Lun and his team wanted to catch up with the "White Eagle".
Earlier, they had received information that the ship carried a "national gift" from the King of the North Sea to the Mafa Empire.
Now knowing the "Devil's Island Treasure" incident was very likely a plot, that ship became even more special.
Dr. Banks pin-pointed the ship's position and found that instead of heading back to the Mafa Empire, it was also heading toward Devil's Island.
This was clearly unusual.
The Dawn Squad's three ships also swiftly pursued, hoping to intercept them before reaching Devil's Island.
On the three warships, everyone was making combat preparations: repairing the ships, maintaining the cannons, familiarizing with equipment, integrating new members...
Barrett, truly a highly experienced professional senior officer, had extensive experience in commanding large-scale wars and training troops. The staff on the three warships were rapidly reorganized under unified deployment , quickly finalizing secret signals, command authority, emergency plans, and reward and punishment systems…
Su Lun also felt it was very impressive; the inclusion of these professional military men like Barrett indeed completed one of Dawn Squad's weaknesses.
While they didn't necessarily adopt the whole set from the Luying Royal Knights, it still spared the Dawn Squad from the trial-and-error of future development.
But in large teams, scientific management can strengthen team cohesion, possessing a razor-sharp combat force!
The Dawn Squad, although a group that upheld freedom like pirates, would get bigger in the future, and these steps were necessary.
...
The three warships sliced through the waves at high speed.
"Mr. Hunk, do you need any help from me?"
"Oh, no, Miss Kama, handling the ropes and such heavy labor, leave it to us giants."
"Mr. Tamu, can I do something? I know how to..."
"No, Miss Kama. Scrubbing the deck is dirty work, let us rough men handle it."
"..."
It was Kama's first day on the ship.
She felt it wasn't very polite to just stay in her cabin on her first day.
On the deck, she also helped out everywhere, wanting to integrate and familiarize herself with the new team as quickly as possible.
After some interaction, she found that although everyone on the ship looked fierce, they were all easy to get along with.
Kama tried hard to participate in some of the ship's work, but it seemed that everyone else had their tasks, and there wasn't much she could help with.
But she had nearly gotten to know everyone: the domineering Sister Tamu, the mysterious Miss Pandora, the elusive Dr. Banks, the giant Hunk brothers, Captain Yuhaku, Captain Ran Saki...
After making a round of greetings, she found that everyone on the ship was very enthusiastic and kind to her, treating her tenderly like family.
Kama naturally knew this was because she was Su Lun's disciple.
Her teacher held a very special position within the Dawn Squad.
At that moment, she saw Lalota practicing swordsmanship at the bow of the ship.
Kama remembered, this was Sister Tamu's disciple.
Perhaps because they were of similar age, Kama felt she might be easier to get along with.
They were all orphans, but they had once been young nobles with many shared experiences.
After chatting for a bit, they quickly became familiar with each other.
Sitting on the edge of the ship, they swung their legs, their faces bright with the charming smiles characteristic of young girls.
As they chatted, the conversation turned to Su Lun.
Miss Kama felt that meeting Su Lun was the luckiest thing in her life.
But since last night, her shock had not stopped. She had also witnessed the fearsome strength of her teacher in the great battle today.
This was the Puppeteer she envisioned in her mind.
However, after boarding the ship, Su Lun was nowhere to be seen, which Miss Kama found a bit hard to adapt to.
She asked Lorota, "Miss Lorota, is the teacher always like this?"
Lorota smiled and said, "Yes. Mr. Su Lun works very hard. As long as he's on the ship, you can hardly see him. But if you go to the laboratory, you'll definitely find him."
As she spoke, she pouted and added, "Mr. Su Lun is one of those people who are already super talented and still work hard. I always get scolded by the teacher for being dumb and not working hard enough... "
Hearing this, Kama couldn't help but snicker, and suddenly, she asked another question, "Is the teacher and Sister Qian Tiao lovers?"
Lorota rolled her eyes and said, "Hmm... it's hard to say."
Kama was surprised, "Hard to say?"
Lorota didn't know how to explain and her face spread into a peculiar smile, "The relationship between the teacher and Mr. Su Lun is quite special; it can't be explained in a few words. Uh... you'll know eventually."
Kama: "Oh..."
At that moment, Tanni suddenly slid down from the ropes dangling from the mast at the watchtower, "Hey, Miss Kama, I'm Tanni, pleased to meet you!"
Kama was startled, "Ah... I'm Kama. The teacher mentioned you earlier; I remember your name."
Lorota, who was clearly familiar with him, rolled her eyes and jokingly said, "This is Mr. Navigator, the crybaby!"
Hearing this, a blush appeared on Tanni's face, "Lorota, can you not bring up the past..."
Lorota covered her mouth and giggled, "I won't stop."
Kama smiled and remained silent.
The three young people of similar ages mingled and laughed on the deck.
The crew members looked at them, their faces also breaking into kind smiles.
Their "Dawn" group would grow rapidly and shine brightly.
...
After the welcome party, Su Lun stayed in the captain's cabin, which had been transformed into a laboratory.
Previously, after ambushing the Seventh Team, he had stripped the soul of Vasili Tyermidó, the "Puppeteer with a Thousand Machines," and had acquired a vast amount of puppetry knowledge.
Although that guy was sinister and malicious, having harmed his own family master, it had to be said that his talent in puppetry was indeed not ordinary.
Otherwise, he wouldn't have secretly learned the secret techniques of the Boer family as a named disciple and developed many of his own remarkable puppetry skills, earning the title "Puppet Master."
Su Lun had to admit that reaping this wave of experience had saved him decades of grueling skill refinement.
It also compensated for his many shortcomings in puppet making, control, and techniques, even opening up some completely new ideas.
Although the Mechanism Puppeteer lineage also stems from the Puppeteer lineage, it surpasses in the precision and functionality of the puppets.
For example, the stripped technique "Mystery of a Thousand Hands" allowed one to control puppets to an extremely intricate and precise degree!
Su Lun directly stripped this skill, which had decades of proficiency, instantly elevating his puppet control to a whole new level.
Together with "Puppet Theater," these two secret techniques complemented each other, making the puppet army extremely formidable.
And it wasn't just these gains.
In Vasili's storage ring, Su Lun found a large number of inheritances from the "Mechanism Puppeteer" lineage, including works on mechanism studies, puppetry, secret techniques...
Besides the books, there were also some hereditary treasures from the Boer family and even two precious "Life Substitute Dolls."
Su Lun would need many years to assimilate those books himself.
But since Vasili had already intensely studied these books, the knowledge was rich in his memory, which also made it convenient for Su Lun. The "Reaper" talent directly stripped and assimilated that knowledge into his mind.
This also greatly advanced the progress of another important task.
That was to repair the "Mechanism Puppet Heart" and release his other disciple, Abec.
Originally, Su Lun had limited knowledge about mechanisms and was uncertain about repairing that top-level alchemic object.
Now, however, it seemed highly possible.
Su Lun had reaped too much; he needed ample time to digest, integrating the knowledge into his own "knowledge tree."
So, he stayed inside the cabin most of the time and did not go out.
...
The speed of the "Old Man's" ship was strangely fast, and it was only by using alchemic formations to sail at full speed that the Dawn group's three ships managed to close the distance to several dozen nautical miles.
But that was two days later.
While Su Lun was studying his puppets in the captain's room, suddenly an observer's warning came from the deck, "Everyone, be alert, there's a suspicious ship ahead!"
Immediately following this, the duty commander's voice came through the communicator, "All hands, prepare for battle!"
Su Lun glanced at the thick fog outside the window, then did not continue to stay in the cabin; he quickly went up to the deck.
At that moment, the deck was already crowded with people.
Su Lun walked to the bow and asked Qian Tiao, "What's the situation?"
Qi pointed ahead and said, "At eleven o'clock, there's a drifting ship. We've signaled them, but there's been no response. It seems... there are no living people on board."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's face also showed a hint of confusion as he pulled out a monocular and looked in that direction.
At this moment, a thick fog was drifting on the sea.
This was already a dangerous area.
His eyesight was better than others, so he could clearly see that the ship on the opposite side was drifting like a ghost.
On the ship's flag hung a "skull with three muskets", and Su Lun's mind instantly reflected the related information.
This seemed to be a large pirate group called the "Silver Spear Pirates," not weak in strength. The leader was a fifth-order professional, the "Sniper Shark Handler" Friedrich, with a bounty of one hundred and ten million and a crew of several hundred men.
Su Lun seemed to have discovered something, leaped onto the mast, and upon closer inspection, he immediately saw that there was no one on the ship's deck. However, on closer inspection, he could see bloodstains and bits of biological limbs on the side of the ship, along with traces that looked like a body being dragged.
But strangely, there were no signs of a fierce battle on the ship.
Su Lun's pupils slightly constricted as he immediately said, "Tanni, pay attention to the movements in the sea!"
"Yes, Mr. Su Lun!"
Tanni also dared not be careless, listening to the movements in the sea.
"Mr. Su Lun, what should we do now?"
"Let the 'Steamship' and 'Judgment Ship' stay in place, we'll go closer!"
"Okay!"
Since they had encountered it, it was clear that they couldn't avoid it now.
So, Su Lun and his crew cautiously moved closer.
With Tanni's abilities and the mechanical octopuses swimming rapidly under the ship, even if some sea monsters approached, they would be able to detect them immediately.
...
Su Lun and his crew approached the ship named "Musket."
After a ten-yard distance, the Assault Team jumped over first.
"Captain, no living people found! Nor any monsters..."
"There are no signs of fighting inside the ship cabin."
"..."
The Sensory professionals soon confirmed that there were no signs of life on the ship, just as they had seen, it was an empty ship.
Su Lun and Qi also jumped over.
They took another look on deck, then went into the ship cabin.
The cabin's supplies were still there, and there were no ammunition loaded in the cannons... all these signs showed no battle had taken place.
But the crew's sleeping quarters were a mess, with blankets thrown everywhere and scattered personal belongings. It looked like those sound asleep crew members had been dragged out of their beds without any resistance.
There was silence in the ship cabin, and the air was filled with a weird atmosphere.
Seeing this scene, everyone felt a chill running down their spine as if they were being targeted by some devil in the dark.
Just then, someone suddenly shouted from the bottom of the ship, "Boss, a body was found in the hold!"
Su Lun and Qi exchanged glances and immediately went downstairs.
The hold was a storage room, storing lots of tobacco, cured meat, and smoked fish, the air mixed with a strong, weird smell.
It was probably because of these strong smells that the monster overlooked this body.
Su Lun took a glance at the pirate "sleeping" among the cargo, clearly a sentinel.
The deceased was about twenty years old, dressed as a pirate, with no wounds on his body...
Su Lun looked and then pressed his hand on the corpse's abdomen, there were no apparent internal injuries either.
Being proficient in forensic autopsy himself, this bizarre death made him frown in confusion.
Seeing this, Qi placed one hand on his sword hilt and asked, "What do you think?"
Su Lun thought for a moment and said, "The deceased has no external injuries. He must have been killed by some sort of psychic attack, then the body was moved. Clearly, the perpetrator was not human but a monster. They were only interested in the body, not touching any money or materials. This is the 'Musket Pirates,' not weak in strength. To annihilate them silently, the monster involved must be very powerful."
Saying this, he added, "Tell everyone to be careful."
Qi nodded upon hearing this.
The few captains behind them passed down the orders.
At that moment, the sound of footsteps thudded on the ship deck, "I heard a body was found?"
Turning his head, it was indeed Dr. Banks who approached.
Su Lun said, "Doctor, your timing is perfect. Can you ascertain the specific cause of death for this person?"
Professional matters should be left to the professionals.
Dr. Banks nodded, saying little.
He walked straight to the body, observed for a bit, then placed his hand on it.
At that moment, everyone watched as his pitch-black arm seemed to melt, turning into streams of tar-like liquid that crawled into the corpse's nose and mouth.
Though Su Lun knew Dr. Banks's methods were a bit unusual, he still twitched at the sight.
However, the effect was extremely good. After sensing for a while, as if he had discovered something, Dr. Banks spoke, "The time of death was approximately ten hours ago, roughly last night. There are ruptures in the internal organs and blood vessels, especially the cranial tissues have suffered damage. This is the cause of death."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun, puzzled, said, "It wasn't a psychic attack that caused death?"
"No."
Dr. Banks said with definite certainty, "Some special frequencies of sound waves can cause this kind of widespread internal organ resonance damage."
Hearing this, Su Lun immediately realized something, "Are you saying the murderer is a 'Siren'?!"
This was a sea creature usually only mentioned in legends, very rarely seen by anyone.
Because those who saw it, all died.
Legend described it as a creature with a human face and a bird's body, possessing a heavenly voice, fond of eating humans, usually appearing at night.
The so-called "Song of the Siren" that people passed down was usually referring to this.
Humans would die to its beautiful song.
In fact, as magical as the legends were, essentially, the song was actually a kind of "Sub-Sonic Waves" that humans couldn't hear.
This type of subsonic wave had an extremely strong penetrating power; it could pass through the atmosphere, seawater, soil, and even obstacles.
Wooden ships, even steel ships, could not completely block the propagation of the sound waves. These waves did not easily decay and were not readily absorbed by water and air.
And some frequencies of subsonic waves, due to their similarity or even identical nature to the vibration frequencies of human organs, easily resonated with the human brain and organs causing mild symptoms such as fear and agitation to severe cases of ruptured blood vessels and immediate death.
Just like how this corpse died!
Most importantly... these subsonic waves, the ordinary human auditory system simply couldn't hear them!
Dr. Banks nodded, "Mmm."
Su Lun listened, his brows tightly furrowed, yet he breathed a sigh of relief in his heart.
At least knowing the cause of death made things much easier to handle.
Ordinary humans couldn't hear these subsonic waves, so they were silently killed.
However, some people who possessed awakened auditory talents could hear them.
Conveniently, there were people with the awakened talent of [D-032-Enhanced Hearing] on their ship.
And even if the awakened individuals were not fully capable of hearing some higher-grade sea creature songs, animals could!
Tanni could communicate with sea animals, and common creatures like whales and jellyfish could hear various subsonic waves!
Which means, that "Siren" posed no significant threat to the Dawn Group!
Since there was no threat, an idea popped into Su Lun's mind: Puppet materials!
The "Siren's" song was terrifying, but the creature's actual combat strength was very weak.
Yet, its vocal organs were extremely valuable,
Regardless of how skilled the Puppetry Technique was, artificially made items could never match the perfection of natural ones.
This [Siren's Larynx] was recorded in the Puppeteer's text as one of the ideal materials for creating the [Wailing Puppet]!
...
Dr. Banks had analyzed the cause of death of the corpse, which suddenly changed the incident from a horrifying event to a normal sea creature attack.
Everyone in the Dawn Group took a deep breath.
They all prepared for a sea creature attack.
The person with [Enhanced Hearing] was constantly on guard, and Tanni also focused intently on listening to the sounds in the sea.
To be cautious, all watch posts were doubled, one with ears sealed with red wax, the other standing guard normally.
This was the only method known in the legends to prevent the "Song of the Siren" from entering one's ears.
Su Lun returned to their own ship, his expression still contemplative.
Seeing his expression, Miss Kama asked, "What's wrong, is there still a problem?"
Su Lun pondered for a moment, then shared his thoughts, "We were pursuing 'Bald Eagle.' But in fact, this place is not the closest route to 'Devil's Island.' Why would the 'Silver Spear Pirate Group' be annihilated here?"
Miss Kama wasn't fond of cerebral guesswork, but upon hearing this, she sharply sensed something, "Are you suggesting that the 'Silver Spear Group' was also targeting 'Bald Eagle'?"
"Mmm. That's where the problem lies."
Su Lun nodded.
His information likely came from Van Gogh and was probably leaked by the Luying royal family or another major power.
Now, on 'Bald Eagle,' those who were well-informed knew about Oleg's return of treasures to the Mafa Empire.
There were definitely people targeting this batch of goods.
He expressed his concerns, "If we're right and the 'Silver Spear Group' really came for the Mafa goods, then why did they encounter death while 'Bald Eagle' continues to sail?"
Miss Kama continued the line of thought, "If it isn't a coincidence, then perhaps the people of Mafa have a method to avoid sea creatures or prevent them from attacking? Or even... are they connected to them?"
The people of the Mafa Empire were not fools.
They wouldn't have overlooked the potential leak of such information.
Moreover, their intelligence systems were by no means inferior to the Luying Empire, especially in the territory of the King of the North Sea.
Su Lun's gaze deepened, and he had roughly connected all the logic in his mind.
He murmured, "Thinking about it now, it's possible that those guys intentionally leaked the information, then used the sea creatures in this area to eliminate everyone in one fell swoop."
Miss Kama marvelled at the scheme, "What a cunning strategy."
At that moment, Su Lun added, "However, for us, it's not entirely bad news."
Miss Kama looked over, her expression curious, "Oh?"
Su Lun stared at the distant sea, his words laden with meaning: "After all, even for fishing, one must use real bait."
He paused, his pupils suddenly sharpening, "That 'Bald Eagle,' there must be a treasure aboard!"

chapters.title: Chapter 381 - 380: A Big Fish Called Princess
chapters.content:
The sea was shrouded in thick fog, rendering visibility very low, and the speed of the three Dawn Brigade ships slowed down.
Especially now that evening was approaching and the temperature was dropping, the fog became even denser. Visibility steadily dropped to just a few dozen meters, to the point where even the three ships could only see vague shadows of each other.
Under such visibility, ships normally wouldn't be able to navigate at all. Especially in unfamiliar waters, where hitting a reef or encountering other special circumstances would instantly result in the destruction of both ship and lives.
Fortunately, the Dawn Brigade had Tanni, a sailor who could "listen to the voices of sea beasts." The fish told him there were no reefs or shoals in these waters, which allowed them to proceed calmly into the depths of the mist.
The moonlight and starlight were obscured by the thick fog, and the sea surface was almost pitch black. It was only illuminated by the searchlights on the three warships, shining a light into this dark, vast sea.
Creatures of the sea that were attracted to light swam around the ships, glowing jellyfish, shimmering schools of silverfish...
On the ships, everyone was on high alert.
Su Lun and Qian Tiao stayed together.
Since he could read lips, he sealed his own ears with red wax.
Though he couldn't hear, it didn't interfere with communication.
That way, if one of them was affected, the other could still react.
As they waited for the sea monster to come, they chatted sporadically.
"This dense fog is probably also the work of the sea monsters. If we don't deal with them, our speed is nowhere near enough to catch up to the 'White Eagle.'
"Mm. The Siren sea monsters like to move around at night. If they've sensed us, there's an eighty percent chance they'll come hunting tonight."
"These female demons are afraid of light and have fragile bodies, ordinary alchemy bullets can cause fatal damage. But since they wiped out the 'Silver Lance Troop,' there must be 'Lord-level' creatures within their ranks. It shouldn't be too troublesome, though, Sister Qian Tiao, you should be able to kill one with a single strike. But if possible, don't aim for the neck to avoid damaging their vocal organs. Ideally, we should capture a few alive."
"Got it. Leave it to me."
"..."
"The Song of the Sirens" was infamous at sea, especially among fishermen, as it was hard to detect and almost certainly deadly.
But the mood within the Dawn Brigade wasn't too grim.
After all, since they knew what monsters they were facing, they had found targeted countermeasures, which greatly reduced the danger level.
As night fell, the sea breeze also turned a little chilly.
The moon would occasionally peek through the sky, with its light giving the fog a sinister white glow.
Apart from the sound of the waves, everything seemed peaceful.
At midnight, when everyone on the ship should have been sound asleep,
suddenly, Tanni's voice came through the communicator: "Captain, they're here! The jellyfish we passed earlier relayed some information; there's a distinct sound wave coming from the south, about five nautical miles away from us!"
Jellyfish are among the marine creatures most sensitive to subsonic waves.
The member of the crew with the "Enhanced Hearing" talent hadn't heard the subsonic waves yet, but the jellyfish had already sensed that the monsters had come out to feed.
Qian Tiao relayed this information to Su Lun and also sealed her own ears with red wax.
At the same time, everyone on the ship sprang into action, making the same ear-sealing movement.
Su Lun also took out his black umbrella, intently observing the sea around him.
But it seemed like nothing had happened, the calm around was eerily quiet.
However, gradually, even with his ears plugged, Su Lun started to feel a bit nauseous and sleepy.
He knew the sirens were drawing near.
Because they had arranged tactics in advance, at this moment nearly everyone on the three ships fell limp on the deck and in the cabins as if asleep, looking like a ship full of corpses.
Everyone held their breath and kept as still as possible to minimize signs of life.
Leaning against the ship's rail with his black umbrella in hand, Su Lun seemed just like them.
Though he could neither see nor hear, suddenly hundreds of spiritual fires appeared in his perception!
"They're really here!" he inwardly shouted.
While the dense fog hindered human vision, it also limited those Siren sea monsters. Unaware of anything amiss, they flew out of the fog without any guard up. The creatures, seemingly thinking they were about to feast, landed on the masts and rails of the three warships, their eyes glowing as they stared at the "corpses."
Su Lun was keenly aware of the location of each siren. Waiting until he could feel the faint vibrations of them landing on the ship,
he suddenly opened his eyes and fired the flare gun that had been prepared in his hand.
"Whoosh~~~~Bang!"
The flare exploded in the fog, emitting a brilliant light.
Even with their eyes closed, the piercing light like needle pricks roused everyone on the three warships!
Once people opened their eyes, they immediately saw the panicked faces of monsters.
It was said that the Sirens were beautiful in appearance.
But in reality... Beautiful my ass!
They had the bodies of birds and human faces, with mouths full of serrated teeth, hideous and fierce, and large, hook-like claws for feet!
The members of the Dawn Group were not the least bit courteous to these monsters that sought to make them into meals, as they promptly revealed their guns.
In an instant, gunfire crackled, and shots joined together in an uninterrupted barrage.
The night was thoroughly woken.
These one or two hundred Sirens hadn't even grasped what was happening when they were "bathed" by a rain of alchemy bullets.
Barrett had long arranged the detailed annihilation tactics, with the crew members banded in threes and fives, their tasks clear, firing at all the monsters on the deck with full coverage and no blind spots.
The trajectory of the bullets wove a net of fire in the darkness, leaving no chance for any Siren to escape.
Those Sirens that landed on the deck flapped their wings in panic, trying to fly away, but before they could lift off, they were shot dead and fell into pools of blood.
Even those elite monsters that tried to use the ship's hull for cover and fly low over the sea to re-enter the fog were taken care of by dedicated snipers...
As Su Lun predicted, among this group of Sirens there was a fifth-order "Lord" and several of silver and gold-tier monsters.
The bird bodies of those Sirens clearly couldn't take much; even as alchemy bullets caused feathers to fly in all directions, they still staggered in flight.
But the Dawn Group was not short of experts, where would they allow those monsters to come and go as they pleased?
After a volley of cannon fire, those professionals with the ability to leap into the air pulled out their weapons and furiously propelled themselves after them.
Su Lun, not one to hold back, twirled his black scythe and with a few swift strokes, several monsters fell into the sea in response.
Because they were prepared in advance, the fight was fierce but over within minutes.
After chasing them down, the other crew members began tidying up the battlefield.
Except for a few monsters with light injuries that were knocked unconscious for research samples, the rest were killed for their materials.
There wasn't much of value in these Siren monsters for anyone other than Puppeteers; the other professionals really couldn't make use of them.
Before long, they too returned, bringing back with them the Lord-level Siren monster.
Kama assisted Su Lun in removing the vocal organs from the corpses of the Sirens, while the other crew members began cleaning the bloodstains on the deck.
After this group of Sirens was killed, the fog on the sea visibly thinned to the naked eye.
And the night returned to tranquility.
The speed of the warship also picked up.
...
On the deck, some crew members stayed to deal with the battlefield, while others took turns resting.
Everyone settled into a normal sailing routine.
In the laboratory.
Su Lun was busy processing those fresh, living organs.
This "Siren's Throat" was an extremely precious material. He had previously inquired in various material markets, only hearing that some ancient specimens were occasionally found in the collections of nobles. They were simply not for sale outside, nor was anyone buying.
But handling such biological organs was not easy; it required sufficient experience.
At his side, Kama was also helping to process those bloody Siren organs.
She cleaned and sorted the material, then placed it into jars filled with green liquid.
While working, she asked questions about anything she didn't understand.
"Teacher, why don't we use 'Strong Silver Solution' to process the materials, but instead use 'Hippolytus Solution'?"
"Hmm... 'Strong Silver Solution' does indeed have excellent preservative effects. But what we are processing now are still active biological organs. To ensure that the organs maintain their original functionality and extend their usefulness, we must consider not just preservation but also maintaining vitality characteristics. That way the puppets created will last longer and be more effective."
"Oh. Teacher, how can this kind of biological material be used in puppets?"
"That would require inscribing special life runes on the puppets..."
"..."
Su Lun had the eight-armed arachnid spear and originally didn't need any assistants.
But now with two newly acquired disciples, he also devoted plenty of patience to teaching.
Karma also treasured this opportunity, working diligently, focusing intently, and striving hard, she showed all the qualities of an excellent Alchemist.
Given time, Su Lun also felt that she would surely become a formidable Puppeteer.
As for Yabec, trapped within the "Puppet Core," his talent was exceptionally outstanding.
The talent of the "B-060-Exquisite Heart" was inherently suited for Puppet Masters; before, it simply lacked guidance and systematic knowledge. Now, with a way to learn, he absorbed all the knowledge Su Lun taught like a sponge, often coming up with some incredibly imaginative and brilliant ideas.
Su Lun was more than happy to polish this uncut jade.
...
After passing through the waters haunted by Siren sea monsters, the speed of the Dawn group's ship increased significantly. By noon the next day, Dr. Banks had already confirmed that biological markers were in very close proximity.
The members of the Dawn group once again entered a state of battle readiness.
But what Su Lun and the others didn't know was that at some place at sea, a mysterious and ritualistic operation had already begun.
The sun was shining high in the sky, and several ships were anchored on the sea's surface. There, unmistakably, were the "White-headed Vulture" and several Pirate ships.
The people on the ships were completely unaware that they were being pursued.
On one of the ships, several cloaked individuals were muttering strange incantations over the sea. Their voices were deep and penetrating, cutting through the water and reaching the deepest ends of the abyss.
If an outsider were here, they would definitely see that beneath these cloaks were beautiful women with blond hair and blue eyes, each exuding a pure, holy aura.
These were the Priestesses of the Temple of Aghaparnon.
In their hands they held jars, one pouring a glowing Spiritual Body into the seawater, another a crimson liquid, yet another silver powder, and one pouring golden ears of wheat...
All were extremely precious top-tier materials, yet they poured them into the sea without regret.
The ritual was proceeding in an orderly fashion.
On another inconspicuous ship, a woman whose sensual figure could hardly be concealed by a large cloak, and who had a seductive appearance, was lazily watching everything before her.
This person was none other than Scatty Harris, the Thirteenth Princess of the Mafa Empire, known as the "Frost Moon Princess."
No one would have guessed that she had come here quietly without any royal mechanical guards.
At the moment, several individuals dressed as guards stood beside her.
As she watched, Princess Stika suddenly spoke up, "High Priestess Helvi had a prophecy, suggesting that this ritual might encounter some unexpected situations. She advised us to be cautious. Gentlemen, where do you think the problem might arise?"
Her demeanor was full of charm, but her eyes twinkled with intelligence.
She was not as others rumored, a Princess reliant solely on her beauty.
Her wisdom was matched by few.
Upon hearing this, one of the aides responded, "The covert forces sent by the Royal House of Ruying, Duke Raphael, and Duke Lance should all have perished in the jaws of the Siren sea monsters and the 'North Sea Leviathan' by now. The experts from Van Gogh are still tied up in the city. In the North Sea, there are no other forces left that can threaten us. Your subordinate feels that there will be no problems..."
Princess Stika seemed to also think this made sense, but the hint of doubt between her brows did not clear, "The prophetic abilities of the High Priests of the Temple of Aghaparnon have always been accurate through generations. We cannot afford to be careless."
The aide spoke again, "Your Highness, my intention is not to question your judgment. But the High Priestess has succumbed to the overwhelming power of Oleg; the Temple's authority is no longer what it once was. Moreover, you've seen for yourself that her faith is no longer pure. Intelligence indicates that she dotes on her son Onis Popov enormously. A prophet with personal desires will greatly diminish in ability..."
Listening to this, Princess Stika arched a beautiful eyebrow, saying nothing but obviously agreeing with her subordinate's words.
Yet thinking over it, her brow furrowed again, and she changed the subject, "What do you make of the turmoil that took place in the city-states of Moros? Who do you think stole the 'Golden God Spear' from the Temple of Aghaparnon?"
"This..."
At her words, several subordinates looked at one another, no one able to provide a clear reason.
Seeing the speechlessness of her followers, Princess Stika said, "Clearly, there is a 'mysterious force' we have not grasped moving about in Roman. My father once taught me, one must not take any enemy lightly."
"You speak very true, Your Highness."
With that, one subordinate lowered his head, and nobody else spoke.
But just then, an ill-timed voice rang out, "Your Royal Highness Princess need not worry about any threat."
It was a man with a scar on his face, his eyes as sharp as Hawkeye.
He spoke in a languid tone, "Having been hired by Mafa, I shall surely ensure the Princess's safety. In the North Sea, other than Oleg and the two deputy commanders of the North Sea Fleet making a personal appearance, no one else poses a threat to me."
Oleg and Mafa were now allies, and he was currently employed by this Frost Moon Princess.
That meant, in the vast expanse of the North Sea, there were no enemies.
Such bold and supremely confident words.
Yet upon hearing them, not a single person on the ship showed even the slightest hint of doubt on their face.
Because this man had a significant reputation.
He was Carlo Meldis, one of the "Top Ten Legendary Bounty Hunters," the "Pirate King"!
Hearing this person's stance, Princess Stika's tone of arrogance also receded quite a bit; it was respect for a powerful being, "This trip will of course require Mr. Meldis's careful attention."
Her slender white fingers tapped the ship's rail, producing a rhythmic knocking sound.
After some idle chat, Stika suddenly thought of something and turned to ask with a smile, "Last time, Mr. Meldis, I heard you ran into a bit of trouble in the Silent Forest. Who exactly is this 'Mr. Jing'?"
Her tone sounded teasing but did not evoke the slightest dislike.
Upon hearing this, the cloaked man's face flashed with embarrassment as if recalling some unpleasant memories.
But as a professional of his standing, he would not avoid the topic of defeat, only responding with a somber expression, "That woman... very strong! She is a high-ranking vampire, so she shouldn't be one of those sub-humans. I did some investigating later and it seems that no power is currently associated with her, as if she appeared out of nowhere."
Princess Stika said, "I have heard Oleg mention that the woman seems to come from Duke Raphael's mines. But at the time, she wasn't that strong. At least, nowhere near strong enough to harm Mr. Meldis. Later, there was news that she was closely related to 'Earl Blood' Antonio Harris... She might be an ancient vampire who had been dormant for a long time."
The cloaked man fell silent, then countered, "Does Your Highness suspect it's her?"
Princess Stika shook her head, saying, "No. Intelligence indicates that the major powers in Ruying are now paying attention to 'Mr. Jing', she couldn't possibly be in the North Sea right now. I was just asking casually."
The cloaked man said, "Once those temple priests make contact with the one in 'haixu' and offer up the sacrifice, Your Royal Highness Princess will get that thing, and then we can go directly to the Void Relics."
Princess Stika said, "That would be best."
But at this moment, quite abruptly, the lookout in the mast spotted something and shouted loudly.
"Attention all hands, three unidentified ships spotted at ten o'clock! They are not flying any flags, and it seems they are heading straight for us!"
"What?!"
Hearing this, not only Princess Stika and the cloaked man but everyone was taken aback.
This was not the route to Devil's Island; hence appearing here, they definitely were targeting them.
Someone actually followed them this far?
The sea monsters didn't kill them?
....
These three ships were naturally the three warships of the Dawn Group!
If Princess Stika's people spotted the ships of the Dawn Group, Su Lun and his companions naturally also noticed them.
"All hands, prepare for battle!"
"Cannons calibrated, ready to fire on command!"
"..."
Barrett gave the battle preparations order through the communicator.
There was no dithering, no need to confirm anything.
If "White Eagle" ships appeared here, they could fire without the risk of hitting the innocent.
In the sky, the death birds circled above, and Su Lun had long taken in every detail of those ships' movements.
Watching the acts of those cloaked priests on deck, Su Lun was even more certain that the conspiracy involved the Temple of Aghaparnon.
The behavior of those priests looked very sinister...
No matter who was on the other ships, it was better to strike first!
Moreover, the Dawn Group had a huge advantage, and that was the range of their cannons which far exceeded that of their opponents!
Those fellows, in order to conceal their identity, sailed on a few ordinary Pirate ships. Although he didn't know why they sailed so fast before, the onboard cannons were all pretty standard, just regular market goods.
But the cannons on the Dawn Group's three ships were confiscated Mafa military cannons, not something one could buy on the market!
The maximum range was several times that of the market's!
Meaning, they could hit the enemy while the enemy could not hit them.
So, the instant they reached firing range, Barrett promptly ordered, "Open fire!"
Nearly a hundred cannons fired simultaneously, creating an exaggerated commotion.
...
From afar, Princess Stika and her entourage on the "White Eagle" were dumbfounded.
As they watched the sky filled with incoming cannonballs, they were shocked, flabbergasted, and yet felt they could not die.
What enmity did they have to start with a barrage of cannons?
PS. If there are many typos, you can refresh the page. Due to recent changes in my sleep pattern, the chapters are posted first and corrected later. I apologize for the poor reading experience.

chapters.title: Chapter 382 - 381: The Giant Monster of the North Sea
chapters.content:
Naval battles are best fought with cannons.
Especially when there is a gap in the quality of equipment, the side with the advantage can crush the enemy from a distance with cannon fire, thus minimizing combat losses.
And as it happens, cannon operation is a compulsory subject for students of the "Royal War Academy."
The professional soldiers Barrett brought along with the Judgment Corps were all students of the Royal Academy, and nearly all of them were certified "senior gunners" or "expert gunners."
As a result, when the three warships of the Dawn Corps launched a volley of a hundred cannons, the cannonballs seemed guided by precision, covering the enemy vessels including the "Old Albatross" a few miles away with minimal deviation.
With such firepower, it wouldn't take many rounds to sink the enemy.
Even without using any spells
Su Lun also guessed that there must be experts among the enemies, since they were escorting valuable treasures.
Therefore, cannons were also the most suitable means of probing.
Before the battle began, Su Lun considered all possibilities.
He was convinced that the enemy would most likely choose to flee since the pirate ships had been pursued for days and must have some special acceleration devices.
But he never expected that the second the cannons roared, an astonishing scene took place, stunning everyone in the Dawn Corps.
...
"Boom!"
"Boom!"
"Boom!"
"..."
The thunderous roar of cannon fire was deafening.
Su Lun stood on the deck, squinting as he watched one cannonball after another hurtling towards the enemy ships.
Some cannonballs fell into the sea, creating waves over a dozen meters high; some hit the pirate ships, blasting cracks in the sails, masts, and wooden hulls...
There were a total of five enemy ships huddled together, which would normally make the best targets.
However, it was at this moment that the people of the Dawn Corps realized there was something abnormal; the cannonballs hit three of the ships as expected, penetrating and exploding...
But when they struck the other two vessels, the cannonballs were stopped by an invisible barrier in mid-air, detonating in visible ripples of air pressure!
Seeing this, everyone in the Dawn Corps got a shock.
Barrett, as if recognizing something, immediately issued a warning, "Bad news, there's a seventh-tier professional on the enemy ships!"
Hearing this, Su Lun's face suddenly changed.
He had sensed something amiss when he observed the priests from the Temple of Aghaparnon.
He had assumed that the escort team would at most have sixth-tier professionals, but withstanding a barrage from a hundred cannons was definitely not something a sixth-tier professional could withstand!
Su Lun immediately realized there might be a highly sensitive big shot on the enemy ship!
A thought flashed through his mind, and he guessed something, "Could it be Princess Mafa from Mafa, or maybe some big shot from the temple?"
If it were the North Sea pirates, they would not hide such things.
People from the temple, on the other hand, might...
But now in the whole North Sea, those needing to hide their tracks and accompanied by top-notch experts, the most likely person was Princess Stika!
"Clever tactics... intentionally leaking the information of the 'Old Albatross' escort, making it seem like a diversion. In reality, the person was really mixed in with the escort fleet!"
Su Lun immediately understood something.
This move by Princess Stika was probably to avoid those from "God's Hands," like Van Gogh.
The assassins wanting her dead were all drawn by the royal guards of the Moros city-state, allowing her to slip away unnoticed.
But why appear here?
Su Lun, looking at the ongoing sacrificial ritual, guessed that the princess must have some motives for coming here.
He thought it was an ordinary interception, never expecting to catch such a "big fish."
However, what the actual situation was no longer mattered; he ordered directly, "Continue the bombardment! Everyone, prepare for battle!"
The situation now was, since they had encountered each other, neither the enemy nor they would show any mercy.
At Su Lun's command, the second round of ammunition was quickly loaded, and in a short time, flames burst from the cannon muzzles again.
"Boom!"
"Boom!"
"Boom!"
"..."
The sound of cannon fire continued incessantly.
Although Su Lun didn't watch to see what the "sacrifice" was for, since those people would rather endure the cannon fire than flee, it indicated the ritual was of utmost importance and couldn't be interrupted.
Whatever the enemy was attempting, the Dawn Corps had to disrupt it!
Even a seventh-tier professional couldn't withstand a salvo of cannon fire for long.
....
Naturally, the enemies wouldn't allow the Dawn Corps to continue the bombardment.
Just then, the crows in the sky started cawing loudly.
Su Lun sensed danger approaching; his gaze sharp as a hawk, he observed everything on the sea surface.
Almost at the same time, Tanni reported urgently through the communicator, "Captain, there's a huge sea monster attacking us from the water! It seems to be the legendary 'North Sea Leviathan - Kraken'!"
"A sea monster?"
Su Lun had naturally heard of the legend of the "North Sea Leviathan" that pervaded the North Sea.
There was said to be an enormous tentacled creature in the deep sea, with a body as large as an island, capable of easily dragging a large warship into the depths.
Su Lun's expression darkened as he shouted, "Leave the sea monster to me! Captain Barrett, Sister Chian, Dr. Banks, guard against the enemy's seventh-tier headshot."
Chian and the others responded in unison, "Understood!"
Saying this, Su Lun leaped up to the ship's rail, looking out to sea.
His eyes could vaguely see a massive dark shadow swiftly swimming towards their battleship, and the waves on the sea surface began to churn.
Time was of the essence, and Su Lun clasped his hands in the sorcerer's seals, uttering a crisp command, "Armament Release!"
Behind him, the eight-armed spider spear unfurled, and with another shift of sorcerer's seals, dozens of glass jars appeared out of thin air.
Once the glass jars were opened, dozens of mechanical octopuses clattered into the water.
In this battle, Su Lun couldn't afford to be careless. He hadn't expected to employ so many mechanical octopuses, but now he had to deploy them all into the sea.
The tentacles of the mechanical octopuses extended ten to twenty meters, but they paled in comparison to the colossal shadow under the sea.
Fortunately, there were enough of them. Fifty mechanical octopuses hit the water and immediately became entangled with it.
It was then that Su Lun could clearly see the true form of the sea monster as it drew close to the surface.
It was indeed a super-sized octopus.
[North Sea Behemoth - Kraken]
Details: A sixth-rank dominating deep-sea behemoth; bloodline of ancient myth, a titanic titan sea beast; length of one hundred eighty meters, weighing over three hundred seventy tons; it possesses powerful tentacles and suction cups, controls the power of the water element, capable of long-range jets; its mucus has strong corrosive properties; its skin is flexible and has a power weakening layer, allowing it to easily deflect conventional physical attacks;
Reading the information, Su Lun's gaze slightly narrowed.
He had long wanted to find the giant octopus passed down through generations among the Roman fishermen, but he didn't expect to encounter it here.
But it also relieved him.
This huge sea behemoth was almost invincible in the sea, and just this one creature could easily sink the three warships of the Dawn Group.
With its massive body, even the Black Scythe would struggle to make a cut.
If it weren't for the mechanical octopus army, the Dawn Group would have really suffered a huge loss.
...
Before the "North Sea Behemoth" could approach the three warships at the surface, the mechanical octopus army swiftly swam towards it.
Even so, a thirty-meter-long tentacle covered with terrifying suction cups flailed out of the water. With a "slap," the resulting wave almost flipped a warship over.
Su Lun's gaze turned steely, and he hurriedly commanded the mechanical octopuses to swarm and kill.
All members of the same species, all adept at strangulating attacks, seven to eight mechanical octopuses latched onto a tentacle and quickly wrapped around it tightly.
To better control the mechanical octopus army, Su Lun had specifically studied the physiological structure of octopuses during these days, becoming extremely familiar with the way these creatures exerted force.
He wasn't aiming to kill it, but at least to trap it.
Even though the "North Sea Behemoth" had strongly corrosive mucus on its surface, the runes and coating layers that Su Lun had painted on the mechanical octopuses during this time now came in handy. For a short period, the enchanted coatings on the mechanical octopuses were not easily corroded.
And so, before the giant sea behemoth could emerge from the water, it was pressed down and struggled in the sea, unable to unleash its fury.
Beneath the sea, fierce battles raged on, and above, torrents surged.
The three warships of the Dawn Group swayed unstably amid the waves, but luckily, the deputy commanders inside the gun decks all had sufficient naval combat experience, and the cannons never ceased firing.
Although the hit rate was slightly off, a battery of a hundred or so cannons firing volleys would always strike plenty of targets.
The Magic Army's highly accurate artillery characteristics were also fully demonstrated in this battle.
At this distance, the enemy could not organize any effective counterattack.
After only a few rounds of cannon fire, five of the enemy's pirate ships, apart from the two shielded by barriers, the other three had their hulls shattered by the cannons, burning fiercely as they slowly sank.
The sea was littered with pirates falling overboard, their cries of anguish mingled with the waves, carrying across the source.
...
Not only were Su Lun and his group caught off guard by an unexpected encounter with a "big fish," but the crew of the "Frost Moon Princess" on the "White Beard" were even more bewildered.
Three ships suddenly appeared out of nowhere and started firing upon meeting, but now it seemed that even the "North Sea Behemoth" couldn't sink them?
The sounds of cannonballs cutting through the air were incessant, and the explosions were continuous. Princess Stika's face grew very grave as she saw this scene, "What is going on, why hasn't the 'Kraken' sunk their ships!"
She was well aware of that deep-sea monster, an almost invincible beast in the ocean, certainly not something a few wooden ships could withstand.
And now it was useless?
One of her subordinates hastily reported, "Your Highness, those people have some special means to control the sea monster. It looks like some mechanical octopuses."
"Duke Raphael's men?!"
Upon hearing this, Princess Stika's face grew even more somber.
Her first reaction was "assassin."
The enemy's preparations were well-informed and targeted, they must have solid intelligence.
Only then did Stika realize that the prophecy was referring to the present moment.
At this time, Carlo Meldis, known as the "Lord of Thieves," also wore a grim expression and spoke, "Your Highness, we have no advantage in an artillery exchange; this cannot continue. I will find a way to kill them. Otherwise, our situation will become very bad."
The energy barrier that blocked the cannonballs was his doing, and without him, the two ships would have been sunk already.
As soon as he spoke, a Priestess from the Temple of Aghaparnon turned pale with shock, disregarding decorum, she urgently interjected, "But the divine ritual is not yet complete, if the 'Sea King' becomes enraged, we... we will have wasted all our efforts! Moreover, interrupting the sea ritual midway could bring unpredictable... terrifying consequences!"
"Hmph!"
Hearing this, Meldis snorted coldly, "I am employed by the Magic Emperor, not your Roman. What do I care about your rituals?"
As he said this, the overbearing presence of a Seventh Order powerhouse made it difficult for others to breathe.
Hearing this, the Priestess turned anxious, but dared not speak further.
All she could do was turn to look at Princess Stika.
Unfortunately, Princess Stika's face was veiled in darkness, yet she did not speak.
Because she knew very well that even a Seventh Order professional could not withstand the bombardment of artillery fire for an extended period.
To protect the two ships, not to mention the rapid consumption of Spiritual Power, if a significant amount of power were spent on this matter, even her own situation would become very dangerous.
Although she was also aware of the dire consequences should the ritual be interrupted, once she ascertained that this was an "assassination" targeting her, the choice between life and protocol became immediately clear.
Thinking this, Stika said, "Mr. Meldis, be careful."
Meldis immediately understood, "Got it!"
This also implied another meaning: if things turned sour, prioritize saving me.
With that said, the "Top Ten Legendary Bounty Hunter" retracted his domain barrier, stepped down, and leaped onto the sea surface.
...
The experts of the Dawn Group were all on deck, constantly watching the enemy warships in the distance.
Just then, everyone saw the energy shield on those three ships suddenly disappear, and a figure leaped onto the sea surface, rushing toward them at high speed.
The lookout on the mast immediately shouted, "He's coming! Everyone be careful."
Su Lun issued the command, "Continue firing, sink those two ships!"
At the same time, Barret, along with Qiantiao and Dr. Banks, leaped into the sea and rushed towards the figure.
The professional draped in a black cloak was indistinct, but as they moved, a monstrous shadow with the heads of a ram, a snake, and a lion rose behind them.
"A Rank Two mythical beast talent [A-044-Chiramer]!"
Watching this anomaly, Su Lun immediately recognized the talent and even guessed the identity of the newcomer.
This talent was rare, a secondary awakening, and also level seven, there could only be one person.
It was one of the "Top Ten Legendary Bounty Hunters," the 'Thief Emperor' Carlo Meldis!
Su Lun felt a sense of foreboding and immediately warned everyone through the communicator, "Be careful, that's the 'Thief Emperor' Meldis!"
He truly hadn't expected that what seemed like a regular bout of piracy would encounter such a renowned top-tier powerhouse.
The strength of his Dawn Group was not weak, but they still lacked top-end combat power.
Although they were ready for battle, a head-on clash would certainly lead to heavy losses.
But the presence of this legendary bounty hunter confirmed to him that on the opposing ship was none other than the Frost Moon Princess of Mafa!
"No, they still don't know the true strength of our Dawn Group!"
Suddenly, a plan flashed through Su Lun's mind.
If it was truly so, perhaps they need not fight to the death...!
At that moment, Su Lun held a black sickle in his left hand and pulled out the [Bow of Time Curse from Chronos] in his right.
He was well aware that he had no place in a battle of this level, only these two sealed items could pose a threat to the enemy.
...
The battle was imminent.
The 'Thief Emperor' Meldis, seeing three people descend from the opposing ship, first sneered in disdain, "Without even forming a domain, they're not very strong..."
Lacking a domain also meant their power was at most sixth rank.
Such enemies, whether three or five, posed no threat.
But the next second, seeing the golden Rakshasa Woman appear behind Qiantiao, Meldis was stunned, blurting out as if seeing a ghost, "A Rank Three awakening [Rakshasa Woman]... How is this possible! There's actually someone in this world who has achieved a third awakening talent?"
Observing the thunderclouds of "Thundering Hell" gathering in the sky and the soaring Sword Qi, Meldis frowned.
How could he, a professional a full rank above, feel danger from a lower-ranked professional?
Meanwhile, his gaze turned to the figure that had transformed into a giant ape and he recognized, "The 'Ferocious Beast' Barrett?"
But he was also surprised, "Why is this guy here?"
This glance seemed to solve the mystery at once.
On the distant ship, Princess Stika also recognized Barrett and immediately realized that these people were the "mysterious force" that had caused a stir in Moros City-State that night.
Dr. Banks' methods were even more peculiar. As he leaped into the sea, the vast expanse of water turned pitch black, as if poisoned, and seabirds began to drop, insects dying in droves.
In just a moment, the group collided.
Even facing three opponents, Melidis still held the upper hand.
As soon as he activated his "void domain," be it Sword Qi, toxins, or physical hammering, the damage inflicted on him was very limited.
Compared to the three in front of him, he was more wary of the person on the distant ship who held a bow and sickle.
At this moment, Su Lun stood at the bow, having already drawn the "Bow of Time," his expression grave.
However, he did not aim at the 'Pirate King' Melidis, but instead pointed his bow at the cloaked figure surrounded by several people on the "Whitebeard."
He was well aware that Barrett and his two companions could hold out for a while, but they definitely had no chance of winning.
Dragging this out, the situation for their Dawn Group would only get worse.
The only advantage the Dawn Group had now was that the other party did not know their true situation.
"Continue the bombardment! Sink them as soon as possible!"
"Yes!"
Another piece of good news was that the members of the Dawn Group were very effective; the cannons on the three warships didn't stop, directly hitting the enemy's last two warships as well.
...
Su Lun did not hesitate and, after drawing his bow, immediately let an arrow fly.
"Arrow of Time" could ignore most defenses and hit the human body.
One of the guards stood in front of Princess Stika and was instantly drained of life by the light arrow, turning into a mummified corpse.
Seeing the corpse beside her, Stika turned pale with fright; she recognized the infamous sealed weapon longbow from the Lu Ying Military Intelligence Department — the "Chronos' Bow of Time Curse."
What was even more terrifying was that as soon as the first arrow had arrived, the second was already on its way!
A sealed weapon on its own wouldn't normally have caused Stika such alarm.
But seeing another one of her subordinates die, the unknown in her heart turned into fear in an instant, "How is it possible, how did that guy not suffer from the curse backlash?!"
And from afar, she could see that the man on the opposite deck had already emotionlessly drawn the longbow, ready to fire the third arrow.
....
Su Lun's mastery of "Master-level Archery" was no joke, and even Princess Stika's guards, despite desperately trying to dodge, could not avoid it.
In order to avoid the eyes of Lu Ying spies, she couldn't bring the Magic Empire's experts with her.
To have hired one of the "Top Ten Hunters" was already not easy, and those few fourth-tier guards were now utterly unable to provide her with any sense of security.
A sealed weapon without any curse backlash was just that unreasonable.
It could make even the top professionals
Su Lun was pained in his heart for using the "Sand of Time," but he didn't hesitate to release two arrows in succession. This decisive momentum scared the people of Magic Empire and also made 'Pirate King' Melidis wary of acting rashly.
The legendary bounty hunter knew all too well that if he continued to tangle with Barrett and the others, the Princess Stika he was protecting would meet her end right there and then.
This guy was also incredibly tough; even as Barrett's trio forcefully tried to keep him from approaching the ship, he repelled the three of them with a single blow, then the sorcerer's seals concentrated, and suddenly the Octagram Array lit up beneath his feet: "Fire Mystery - Holy Light Sword!"
Suddenly, he condensed a long sword emitting scorching white light in his hand, pointing it towards Su Lun.
As the Light Sword aimed at him, Su Lun instantly felt chills down his spine.
The murderous intent of a seventh-tier professional was palpable, even across several miles of sea.
At the same time, he also understood that this guy was likely accepting a hire from Mafa mainly because he was after the space relics.
[A-044-Chiramer] Possesses an extraordinarily high affinity for the laws of fire, space, and darkness.
That guy probably needed space materials too.
...
Against a seventh-tier spell, Su Lun would almost certainly have died if he took it head-on.
But his expression showed no sign of retreat, resembling very much the "death warriors" of the Luying Intelligence Agency. His longbow fully drawn, he fired another arrow.
The light arrow once again took the life of a guard beside Princess Stika.
And at the same time, that seventh-tier fiery spell formed by the laws materialized before Su Lun, leaving no room for avoidance.
Just then, a towering alchemical golem teleported in front of him. The Light Sword pierced the golem's abdomen, revealing a silvery metallic luster. The higher law was scorching the "wound," not healing quickly.
A gargoyle of this level was far from enough to stop a seventh-tier professional, but it ultimately blocked this lethal attack.
Su Lun's face was without a ripple as he drew his longbow for the fourth time and fired another arrow.
This time, another guard by Stika's side was killed.
Beside her, there were only two "shield bearers" left.
Almost at the exact moment when Su Lun shot the arrow, another seventh-tier spell "Shadow Magic Arrow" came hurtling toward him.
With the gargoyle not fully restored, its stability would be greatly decreased.
This time, it might not be able to hold back the attack.
But at this critical moment, a lovely figure quickly blocked in front of Su Lun, punching the shadow arrow away.
Su Lun looked relieved, "Phew... So she finally made a move."
Turning his head, the person who had acted was none other than the masked Pandora.
Her alchemic body was invulnerable to all sorts of laws at a certain level, and a seventh-tier professional could not injure her. At least, a ranged spell like that was still far from enough.
....
Seeing yet another mysterious and powerful figure with strange methods appear,
Princess Mafa finally showed a change in color.
How could she not see that this was clearly an attempt to "assassinate" her?
A few people were holding off Melidis, and the master archer with the "Bow of Time Curse" started killing people.
Now that someone capable of taking a seventh-tier spell head-on appeared, Princess Stika felt her life was hanging by a thread.
At the same time, Su Lun's fifth arrow was drawn, once again aiming at her.
Scared out of her wits and unable to care about anything else, she quickly used her communicator, "Mr. Melidis, stop bothering with those assassins and take me away! The ritual has gone wrong, the 'Marine Ruin' could appear at any moment!"
Fussing with a bunch of assassins wasn't worth it.
Even if she could kill them all, it wasn't worth risking her extremely valuable life.
In the distance, Melidis frowned upon receiving the order.
He suspected that the mysterious woman who could withstand his attack wasn't very strong and that she only had a peculiar body.
Perhaps... another test would reveal the truth.
But the reality was that the situation no longer allowed him to delay. If he wasn't certain he could kill the archer quickly, Princess Stika was in danger. Moreover, the "Marine Ruin" could not be underestimated.
Melidis' eyes flashed with hesitation but he also immediately left the battlefield and ran towards a few sunken ships.
Then, to the shock of the Dawn Group, he took Princess Stika with him, tore a special scroll, and after a few flickers, their figures disappeared from the surface of the sea.
Seeing this, Su Lun seemed unsurprised, exhaling a long breath, "Finally, they're gone."
If they really wanted to win, the Dawn Group should have focused all their strength on surrounding and killing that 'thief emperor' Melidis.
But the chances of a devastating loss were high.
But Su Lun didn't want to see that happen.
That's why he had been so resolute about killing Princess Stika, betting on this outcome.
The princess valued her life even more.
She would surely retreat first.
...
Pandora was willing to help, and Su Lun actually had a good chance of killing the princess.
But he didn't do it.
And he couldn't kill her.
Because Su Lun knew very well, they couldn't deal with 'thief emperor' Melidis for now.
Even if they could, the Dawn Group would suffer heavy losses.
On the other hand, keeping the princess alive would keep that guy wary.
Just like now.
An intense battle ended abruptly, and the members of the Dawn Group seemed not to understand what had happened.
Watching the enemy truly vanish above the sea, Chiramer came over, puzzled, "Why did that guy run away?"
With a sigh, Su Lun replied, "Princess Stika probably thought we came to 'assassinate' her. Unsure if we had any further tricks up our sleeves, she didn't dare to gamble with her life, so she ran away."
Speaking of which, his expression was complex.
He really hadn't expected so many coincidences, encountering a mysterious Princess Mafa and a legendary hunter.
Seems like luck wasn't on his side...
But, what's done is done, nothing much to say now.
Su Lun looked at the seabed, the mechanical octopus was still entangled with the North Sea monster.
He said, "Dr. Banks, help me anesthetize that big guy under the water. Everyone else, go clean up the battlefield over there."
Dr. Banks replied, "Got it!"
The other members of the Dawn Group also began to clear the battlefield.
The people were gone, but the precious sacrifices and the treasures on the "Old Man Whiskers" hadn't escaped.

chapters.title: Chapter 383 - 382: Sea Ruins
chapters.content:
The legend of the "North Sea Leviathan" has been circulating in the waters of northern Ruying for at least a thousand years.
It might not be this one we're dealing with right now, or perhaps it's a species of these Titan octopuses.
But Su Lun had to admit that these giants truly sat at the top of the food chain in the sea.
Fifty mechanical octopuses were enough to destroy a fleet of dozens of warships, yet in struggling with this creature, they gained no advantage, and several were consecutively scrapped. If the battle continued to the end, the entire mechanical octopus legion might be wiped out.
Fortunately, the "Pirate King" Melidis had taken off with Princess Stika, freeing up Su Lun's hands.
Together with Dr. Banks, they deployed poison and soul attacks among various methods. After a good half day's torment, they trapped the big fellow and used the winches on three warships to lift it, expending a great deal of energy before finally stuffing it into the "Little Void Realm."
Su Lun had always wanted to capture a massive octopus to create super-sized mechanical octopuses, but those available on the market fell far short of his needs.
This North Sea Leviathan was just like finding a pillow when sleepy.
It was of Titan bloodline and a dominator-class creature, with size, vitality, and growth potential far exceeding expectations.
It was simply the most ideal material.
And Su Lun just so happened to possess the ability to capture such gigantic sea monsters.
Dr. Banks also had a keen interest in this ancient-bloodline creature, extracting copious amounts of blue blood and body tissue samples for research.
He said that there might be a chance in the future to extract the "Titan genes" from the blood to create a [Ancestral Potion] that could possibly cultivate this type of "Titan octopus" artificially.
Not to say it would be as strong as this one, but at least much larger than ordinary octopuses.
Once it could be artificially bred, it would be a different ball game.
Su Lun felt optimistic about the future.
If they really had three or five lucky mechanical octopuses, not to mention sailing warships, even the steel mega ships of Mafa would stand a fighting chance.
However, with a single small octopus already costing over 100 million liso, the remodeling cost for one of this size... was probably astronomical.
For the time being, Su Lun hadn't thought that far ahead, taking things one step at a time.
Regardless, it was still a huge gain.
Of course, the price paid was not small either.
The arrows fired just now to drive away Princess Frost Moon consumed about one-tenth of the [Sand of Time], whose value was immeasurable.
Luckily, apart from the "North Sea Leviathan," there were other gains.
....
While Su Lun and some of the Dawn group were catching the octopus, others on the two ships went to salvage the previously sunk "Old Man Wan" and several pirate vessels' spoils.
Since they were covered by cannon fire, all five ships were beaten to a pulp. The sea was strewn with fragments of wood, treasure chests, barrels...
Of course, there were also some survivors.
As Su Lun's group completed capturing the "North Sea Leviathan," the salvage work on the other side continued.
Treasures were continuously fished out and brought back to the warships, piling up on the deck into mountains.
"Hahaha... This time's spoils of war can't be said to be a loss for our rounds of cannon fire!"
"Yeah. So many treasures I've never even seen before. These high-quality [Seven-Color Gemstones] are said to be offerings for the Temple of Aghaparnon in Roman, tsk tsk... What an eye-opener."
"Mr. Su Lun, come and see, isn't this the [Void God Hand of Chronos] you mentioned? Wow, there are also several spatial treasures..."
"..."
Su Lun watched as one treasure after another was fished out, joy appearing on his face.
The legendary-quality [Void God Hand of Chronos] was indeed on board the ship as expected, conveniently placed in a chest floating on the sea and among the first batch to be retrieved.
Upon appraisal, it turned out to be an alchemical prosthesis with a very high compatibility with Qiantiao, which, once fused, would grant the exaggerated ability of "Physical and Magical Penetration." This would be a qualitative enhancement in combat power for a light swordsman and would significantly increase slashing damage against heavy armored professions in the future.
The quality of the prosthesis was beyond doubt, but it provoked the concern that its strong curse properties might cause deformities upon fusion with Qiantiao.
Having fished out this treasure, Su Lun breathed a sigh of relief.
The initial purpose of their pursuit of the "Old Man Wan" was for this very item.
However, as the pile of treasures on the deck grew more extravagant, Su Lun's gaze slowly turned grave.
[Hero's Spirit], [Muse Goddess's Flowing Sand Crystal], [Frey's Golden Wheat Sheaf]...
These were all treasures of the same rank as the [Golden Fleece] they had captured before, and nearly each one could be linked to ancient myths.
Obviously, these were offerings the folks at the Temple of Aghaparnon had made to the sea.
But now they had been intercepted and salvaged by them.
Su Lun's brows were tightly knit.
Through the offerings, it was confirmed that the scale of this ritual was terrifyingly high.
What did it feel like...
It was as if you intended to rob a small noble under the guise of a Robin Hood, but ended up unsuspectingly robbing the disguised emperor out on a private excursion.
The abundance of treasure, on the contrary, made people feel uneasy.
This only intensified Su Lun's suspicion that there was a serious problem with the ritual.
Just then, Lolota, Kama, and Tanni came back in high spirits, piloting the assault boat. From afar, they waived their hands, shouting, "Mr. Su Lun, we caught a live one you wanted!"
The three of them brought the person aboard the ship, a priestess soaked to the bone, wearing a magic-binding bracelet. With blond hair, blue eyes, and a high nose bridge -- a classic Roman beauty.
Lolota excitedly recounted the process of capturing the prisoner of war, "She was hiding in the deep sea, sinking for some reason. If it weren't for Tanni, we wouldn't have found her..."
Tanni also wore a proud and coy expression, like a child waiting to be praised.
Su Lun listened and complimented the trio, "Hmm, not bad, you did well."
Probably realizing that Su Lun was the spokesperson for the Dawn group, the priestess looked up and glared at him venomously, saying, "You outsiders have desecrated the Sea God and angered the Sea King. You will be punished. You are enemies of Roman!"
Su Lun's brow furrowed upon hearing this. He didn't take the threat as just empty words.
Previously in the city, he was assassinated by the Golden God Spear, then there was the "Devil's Island Treasure", and now the ritual... The Temple of Aghaparnon played a key role behind the scenes in every event.
He hadn't intended to kill the captive, but the way she looked, he thought he could extract the information he wanted to know from her.
Without any hesitation, Su Lun raised his hand and flicked his fingers, and instantly a line of blood appeared on the beautiful priestess's neck.
Life quickly drained from her face, and her head thudded onto the deck, blood gushed like a fountain.
Blood sprayed onto Lolota and the others' faces, each one slightly puzzled in their eyes, not yet realizing why Su Lun suddenly took action to kill.
Su Lun didn't explain; behind him, the shadow of death emerged and directly devoured the "grey mist" on the corpse.
'You have stripped the soul of "Orlun"'
'You have learned some historical secrets about the Temple of Aghaparnon'
'You have obtained information: "Six months ago, the High Priest prophesied 'an outsider Puppet Master will bring disaster to the Roman nation'..."'
'You have learned: "A live Sea Sacrifice will bring good fortune to the Roman nation, receiving the Sea God's protection; no one will come out alive, they will remain forever in the ruins of the sea. This time, by attracting these outsider adventurers in search of treasure, Lord Sea King will surely be pleased with so many fresh souls, which will exchange for Roman's decades of peaceful maritime era..."'
'You have acquired: "The Golden God Spear can only be used by Onis Popov, a handsome and charming man, a born hero. Oh, he has intimate relations with the other priests in the temple, including me..."'
'You have obtained information: "Princess Stika heard that there was a piece of Urobolos shard on Devil's Island, so she wanted to use a sacrifice to exchange that treasure with Sea King Drake..."'
'...'
Through keyword searches, Su Lun abruptly resolved all the doubts in his heart.
The information was massive!
After digesting it, he found it quite a headache.
Turns out, the one who had shot at him using the Golden God Spear back in the city was Oleg's second son, Onis Popov.
Matching the rumors that circulated outside, this guy was a child born from Oleg and the High Priestess Helvi of the Temple of Aghaparnon.
Of course, any gossip about "the two of them tossing around in the temple for seven days and nights" became irrelevant.
What Su Lun cared more about was the reason the guy shot him, and it really was because of some inexplicable "prophecy."
Wasn't the cause and effect reversed here?
If you hadn't poked me with the spear, I would've been too lazy to deal with you...
A feud was definitely established.
But Su Lun felt that the priestess probably didn't know the whole truth either.
The prophecy was spoken by the "High Priestess" and only she knew exactly what it entailed.
Even the "Four Color Elemental Heart" of the Puppetry Technique was supposedly intentionally disseminated because of that prophecy, to attract the prophesied Puppet Master to Devil's Island.
And of course, spreading the news of the "Devil's Island Treasure" was also the temple's trickery from behind the scenes.
They wanted to lure outsiders to complete the "Sea Sacrifice" once every few decades.
In exchange for the lives of more than a hundred thousand people, Roman would enjoy decades of peace and prosperity.
In Roman, there has always been a tradition of sacrificing prisoners of war since ancient times; in the eyes of the faithful, offering one's life to the gods is not only not frightening, but also a glorious deed.
Perhaps those folks didn't think that "sacrificing hundreds of thousands of people" was particularly vile.
But hearing all this, Su Lun immediately lost any good feelings towards this so-called "Land of the War God", "Land of Heroes".
Indeed, the ancient alchemists were right to expel these believers of gods.
Some zealots, to humanity, are simply a cancer.
As for the consequences of interrupting the ritual, the priestess didn't know, except that it would lead to "terrible consequences," and everyone in this sea area would die in the "sea ruins," becoming sacrifices.
It included herself.
From the moment they left, these priestesses never intended to return alive.
...
Having extracted those pieces of information, Su Lun digested them quickly, and then barked into the communicator, "Everyone, back to the ship immediately!"
He immediately realized that there was no time to salvage the spoils of war, and they must leave the area at once.
The people at sea were surprised to hear Su Lun's order, and although it was a pity to watch those treasures sink into the sea, everyone began to rush back to the ship on the assault boats.
Qian Tiao listened to Su Lun's serious tone and came back from the sea's surface, asking, "What happened?"
Su Lun's brows were tightly furrowed as he replied, "There might be a major change in this sea area."
Coincidentally, just as he finished speaking, the world suddenly changed color.
The sky was filled with rolling thunder, fierce winds suddenly howled above the sea, and the waves became more and more exaggerated.
In a very short time, the dark clouds in the sky seemed to form a super huge skull shape, with its hollow eyes staring at the three warships of the Dawn Group, as if a deity was observing the mortal world, sending chills down everyone's spine.
Su Lun's eyes narrowed slightly.
He stared at that skull, and the identification display showed "Sea King Drake's Death Projection"; he murmured, "Sea King?"
Tanni also heard something and exclaimed, "Mr. Su Lun, the fish are panicking, it seems like something bad is going to happen!"
The crew reacted instantly, climbing aboard quickly.
"Forget about those spoils of war, get on the ship!"
"If we can't take the assault boats, leave them, grab the ropes!"
"Hurry, pull up the brothers who fell into the water..."
"..."
Luckily, Su Lun had warned the crew in the sea ahead of time, so after some effort, all the crew members got on board without any danger.
By this time, the sky was clouded over and the sea was pitch black. The waves were dozens of meters high, and the three warships seemed as insignificant as leaves, swaying violently.
Buckets of rain poured onto the deck, splashing loudly...
The previously calm seas had suddenly become terrifying.
No one had ever seen waves so exaggerated; in the face of nature's power, human strength seemed so insignificant. Waves of this magnitude could easily sink the Dawn Group's three galleons into the sea in an instant.
In the torrential rain, Tanni, the First Navigator, was desperately commanding.
"Second ship, a forty-five-degree angle, activate the alchemy sails, full speed up the wave!"
