"Third ship, secure your inner sails, hard to port, keep up!"
"First ship, remove the cannon's locking chains, let them move with the hull to stabilize it with inertia! Quick, or you'll be flipped by the waves!"
"..."
This kind of storm was not something ordinary navigators could handle; a slight mistake, and everyone would be buried at sea.
At this moment, only Tanni's voice could be heard on the communications channel; everyone was following his command.
Even Su Lun did not interject.
Having previously witnessed Tanni's exceptional ship-handling skills in a severe storm, the Dawn Group had absolute trust in him.
So even if the orders sounded like a "march to death," everyone complied fully, busying themselves at their posts.
The newly joined Arbitration Group members were professional soldiers. They had the resolve to absolutely obey military orders, even if they were not familiar with Tanni, the "First Navigator," they did not question him.
If it was a motley crew of ordinary pirates, they would have been wiped out by the first wave.
The three warships sailed through the giant whirlpools several sea miles in diameter, with waves dozens of meters high, like bizarre cliff-like sea gorges... They seemed to be about to be completely overturned by the waves several times, but they miraculously made it out each time.
Wave after wave...
The peril was extreme.
Su Lun, Qian Tiao, Barrett... everyone on the ship looked pale.
Even Pandora, who never liked to join in the excitement, appeared on the deck and looked up at the skull in the sky.
Su Lun was also clear that this was the so-called "punishment from the Sea King."
But in the eyes of an alchemist, the essence of all phenomena is actually the conversion of energy.
These waves were not naturally formed; if the "Sea King" who stirred up such a commotion used a significant amount of energy, it probably wouldn't last long if it couldn't sink the three ships of the Dawn Group.
As Su Lun predicted, after half an hour, the terrifying storm suddenly subsided.
But the dark clouds in the sky did not disperse, and between the sea and the sky was only a faint bluish light.
To Su Lun, it felt a bit like the sky in the "Netherworld," full of gloom.
...
After the storm subsided, aside from some damage to the ships and some supplies lost at sea, fortunately, there were no casualties.
The crew began to busy themselves again.
"Engineers, check the ship for damage and make repairs!"
"Everyone check your equipment; don't let your guard down. Sensing team, take note of the situation in the sea."
"It's getting foggy, turn on the fog lights."
"..."
Thanks to the emergency plan, everyone carried out their duties in an orderly fashion, busily at work.
Meanwhile, on deck.
Su Lun, Qian Jiao, Dr. Banks, and Barrett met up, their expressions solemn as they held a brief meeting.
Su Lun shared the intelligence he had gathered with everyone.
The peril did not seem to startle them much, for it was all part of a maritime adventure.
However, when they heard about the Temple of Aghaparnon's true intention to sacrifice hundreds of thousands of adventurers to the sea, everyone's faces turned grim.
Qian Jiao, "So, from the very beginning, the treasure of Devil's Island was a conspiracy?"
"Yes."
As Su Lun spoke, he pointed at the gloomy sky and said, "The current situation is that Devil's Island is actually a 'Sea Ruin'. The recent waves have brought us to this area. And unfortunately, we are now trapped here..."
The All-knowing Eye had already identified that, soon after the ghostly face appeared in the sky, this space became a 'Sea Ruin'.
'Sea Ruin' is a term from legend, described by minstrels as "the sea's land of the dead," "the place where the Sea God is buried."
It sounds quite romantic.
But in reality, it's a dangerous place.
All who die at sea are said to go to the 'Sea Ruin,' where there are pathways connected to the Netherworld and secrets unknown to man.
It's somewhat like a massive cursed space, but not quite.
The Dawn group is now trapped here.
Even Su Lun suspected that from the very beginning, the High Priest of the temple probably had this in mind.
By this means, to kill that person prophesied.
Once you enter this maritime region, there's no going back.
Su Lun then said, "There's also that mysterious 'Sea King'. I'm not sure what kind of being he is. He could be some false god, or maybe some sea monster but... he must be powerful. The recent storm was likely his handiwork. Of course, the most crucial problem is, we are trapped now and need to find a way out."
With those words, everyone on deck fell silent.
No one had ever been to the Sea Ruin before, so naturally, they had no idea how to leave.
At that moment, Qian Jiao, looking to lighten the heavy mood, spoke up, "Regardless of whether that 'Sea King' is a monster or whatever, if it comes after us, we'll just have to kill it."
She had once witnessed real deities at the Dawn Relic and had slain false gods in the Netherworld.
Therefore, she had no fears in her eyes, nothing that could daunt her.
Hearing this, Barrett analyzed, "Indeed, if it comes, we fight. Our strength in the Dawn group is not weak at the moment. It's not very likely that we'll encounter an unbeatable foe. Furthermore, false gods need faith to sustain them. If that 'Sea King' is a false god, then he might not be too strong. Otherwise, he would have taken action during the storm."
Those who have faced life-and-death situations appeared very calm in the face of adversity.
After a pause, he said, "Our biggest issue now should be figuring out how to leave."
Su Lun nodded; he thought the same.
But after inquiring over the communicator, no one knew.
That's when Qian Jiao suddenly suggested, "How about asking Philo? She might know something."
She was still accustomed to referring to Mr. Jing by this pseudonym.
Upon hearing this, Su Lun exclaimed, "Right!"
His senior sister had seen much of the world, and besides, she had a father who had seen even more.
Caught up in thinking of solving the problem on his own, his thoughts had inadvertently become limited.
With that, he directly called Mr. Jing's communicator.
Barrett twitched the corner of his eye, knowing who Su Lun was trying to contact.
Now that he had formally joined the Dawn group, he had come to know the true identity of the Dawn's leader.
There had been countless speculations about the mysterious "Mr. Jing's" identity, yet he could have never imagined that person was actually the daughter of Sir Isaac, the "Alchemical Demigod" from a thousand years ago!
Soon, the communicator connected.
And sure enough, Mr. Jing knew!
"You're trapped in a 'Sea Ruin'? That could be a bit troublesome. My father once visited a 'Sea Ruin' in the Southern Seas. He shared some of his experiences with me. To escape, first you need to find the 'River of the Underworld'. Only by going upstream against its flow can you return. Be cautious, though; the Sea Ruin is full of dead spirits... "
As Su Lun and the others listened, their expressions immediately turned lively.
The term 'dead end' has to be qualified.
To ordinary people, the Sea Ruin is an inescapable doom, but for someone as powerful as Sir Isaac, it might just be a sightseeing spot with a touch of danger, right?
PS. If there are errors, just refresh the page.

chapters.title: Chapter 384 - 383 Eternal Night Emperor's Decree
chapters.content:
Mr. Jing's words directly broke the deadlock that Dawn Group faced.
The legendary Sea Ruins, which were said to have no way out, actually had a method of escape.
Watching Su Lun finish communicating, everyone on the deck exchanged glances, and the serious atmosphere suddenly eased.
Qian had always worn an indifferent expression, but now he was even more relaxed, laughing and saying, "I knew it, Philo should know."
Dr. Banks didn't speak, but the venomous look on his face suddenly didn't seem so fierce.
Relief filled Barrett's eyes as well.
Indeed, the "Isaac" surname seemed to be favored by fate.
To rebuild Dawn with a figure from legend was indeed a great honor.
High atop the mast, the half-grown youngsters Lolo, Kama, and Tanni, who had been eavesdropping just now, also bared their neat white teeth in a smile.
Su Lun let out a long breath.
There was a method now, but he also said, "Now we need to go to the due west of the Sea Ruins to find the 'River of the Underworld' before we can possibly get out. There are many dangers, so everyone be careful."
Everyone nodded in agreement.
The magnetic field in the Sea Ruins was problematic, rendering the compass completely useless.
But the group had the "World Sea Map of Pirate King Black Sam," an alchemical item that would never allow sailors to lose their way.
And they had Tanni, an excellent navigator,
They were fully equipped to sail under adverse conditions.
...
And so, the three warships of the Dawn Group sailed calmly across the sea's surface.
The overall hue of the space in the Sea Ruins was dark aqua, like the world before dawn breaks.
The fog over the sea's surface wasn't very thick, and the water was very clear. But what was strange was that the sea water here seemed bottomless, the depths an endless blue-black. If you looked closely, your gaze would be sucked in, causing a dizzying sensation as if falling from the clouds.
Moreover, there were no marine creatures in the sea, making it eerily lifeless.
Even Tanni couldn't hear any sounds.
Unlike the previous storms and waves, there was no wind at all now, and the sea was as calm as a dead pond. The three ships were only able to move slowly forward by using the alchemical arrays on the sails.
The crew members were all on high alert.
Su Lun stayed on deck for a while, then he suddenly thought of something and went below deck.
Next to the captain's room, there was a small compartment, Pandora's private room, which no one could enter on normal days.
Knock, knock, knock!
Standing at the door, Su Lun knocked and asked, "Miss Pandora, may I come in?"
At that moment, a response came from inside, "Come in."
Su Lun's lips curled slightly, although the tone was cold, he still entered.
Upon entering the room, he was greeted by an intoxicating scent.
Pandora's body, when first created, was endowed with the most enchanting natural fragrance in the world.
That scent reaching his nose also brought Su Lun a sort of delightful pleasure.
Then looking up, that stunning visage appeared before his eyes. Thanks to the contract they had signed, he dared to look directly at her.
Hmm... indeed, her beauty was impeccable from any angle.
Pandora sat cross-legged on the bed, casting a sideways glance at Su Lun and asked, "What is it?"
Those clear blue eyes seemed to hide the world's most enticing depths. Even with a cold demeanor, that glance shimmered like the stars on a summer night.
Su Lun thought to himself, what a pair of soul-stirring eyes.
He said directly, "I want to thank Miss Pandora for your assistance in the previous battle."
He hadn't forgotten that during the naval battle, had she not blocked the attack by 'Pirate Emperor' Melidis, not to mention being killed, Su Lun himself was very likely to have received serious injuries.
Pandora listened without any change in expression, "It was only the contract."
Su Lun shrugged noncommittally and did not dwell on the topic further.
Instead, he took out the spoils of war he had salvaged from the sea earlier.
While treasures like "Heroic Spirits," "Muse Goddess's Quicksand Crystals," and "God Frey's Golden Wheat Ears" were precious, Su Lun had no immediate use for them.
However, upon re-assessing them, he found labels on these materials indicating "can carry faith."
Su Lun knew these items must be very important to Pandora.
But he also knew clearly that even though she needed them, she would definitely not ask a second time.
It was a matter of etiquette.
Su Lun thought this was also part of her deeply ingrained 'tsundere' attitude,
As well as the pride she should possess as a deity.
Su Lun said directly, "These things don't have much use in my hands for now, and it seems Miss Pandora needs them more. I've brought them to you. As part of the spoils of war, Miss Pandora is also entitled to a share."
He spoke politely, arranging the step-down all too well, just waiting for the response.
He wasn't doing this to curry favor.
Offering these items served two purposes: one, to thank her for her assistance in the battle, and importantly, they might need her help soon.
Su Lun suspected that whatever 'Sea King' resided in these Sea Ruins was a false god.
Facing an enemy that was not within the normal human category, whose methods and abilities were unknown, it would be best to consult this likewise divine lady.
Upon hearing his words, Pandora, well aware of how receiving gifts could create obligations, did not refuse, simply saying, "I understand."
Su Lun set down the Storage Ring and smiled faintly.
Having accepted the item, regardless of whether it was a trade, there was now an exchange of good will.
No need for excessive talk between the astute, Pandora clearly understood his additional purpose.
Su Lun was about to make some small talk when she went straight to the point, "The existence that controlled the storm earlier is a very special undead creature, I felt fluctuations of faith. If possible, I would still like to ask for your help."
"Oh?"
Su Lun wore a look of quiet expectancy.
As expected, that "Sea King" turned out to be a false god-like being.
Pandora's gaze narrowed slightly, and after a moment of contemplation, she said, "I want to take His faith."
The word "take" was very spiritual, Su Lun listened and his eyes flashed with brilliance before disappearing; he immediately agreed, "Okay!"
They planned to leave the Sea Ruins, and that "Sea King" was definitely an enemy.
Since Pandora had spoken, she obviously had some kind of method.
Dealing with the biggest threat in Su Lun's mind couldn't be better.
He then asked, "What do you need us to do to cooperate with you?"
Pandora looked at him, seemingly revealing a secret of her own, "You should have guessed that I have the ability to take the Power of Faith. When the time comes..."
Su Lun could guess some of it even without her saying.
Previously in the Mountain Hermit country, Pandora became "Moon Reading Great God," obviously using some special method.
Possibly, this was an "out-of-the-box setting" given to the alchemically created being by his teacher Cereia at the time of her creation.
Although Su Lun met Pandora in a rather unpleasant way, they had gradually forged a beneficial relationship and had developed a tacit understanding.
Su Lun also felt that since Pandora confirmed he was Cereia's disciple, that hostility seemed to have never been felt again.
....
While they were speaking, suddenly someone on the deck shouted loudly, "Everyone, watch out, there are strange shadows in the water!"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun glanced at Pandora and said, "I'll go out first!"
With that, he teleported and appeared on the deck.
At that moment, everyone was watching the water with their full attention, on alert.
Su Lun held a black umbrella and had already sensed clusters of cold Spiritual Bodies appearing in the water.
"Eh, aren't those the Priestesses from the Temple of Aghaparnon? What are they doing in the sea?"
"Not to mention, their figures really are impressive."
"Are these alive or dead? How can they swim in the sea?"
"Be careful, I feel something wicked about these things. They seem to be the 'Drowned Corpses' from the legends."
"..."
By the time Su Lun arrived, the crew was already pointing at something beneath the sea surface.
He too approached the ship's rail and took a careful look, to find that the water was filled with lifelike female corpses!
Blonde and blue-eyed with charming features, their semi-transparent dresses in the water made their proud breasts fully visible, and their elegant figures were crystal clear. They floated in the sea like sleeping beauties, eyes closed...
The number was increasing, and they moved through the water like fish, wandering underneath the three warships.
Su Lun's left eye flickered and he identified them.
[Drowned Corpses]
Details: Undead creatures, sacrificial offerings to the "Sea King" Francis Drake by the Temple of Aghaparnon; in other words, they are the Sea King's wives; skilled in spiritual power attacks, do not look directly into their eyes;
Having seen the identified information, Su Lun's heart tightened, and he immediately shouted through the communicator, "Be careful, don't look into the eyes of those corpses."
But it was a moment too late, the female corpses in the water suddenly opened their eyes, and those blue pupils emitted a faint glow.
Professionals of tier three and above were only slightly dazed by the sudden shout, woke up, and quickly came to their senses.
But those crew members with weak spiritual power on the battleships were like soulless shells, reaching out to grab the female corpses from the sea.
The moment they reached out, they leaned forward and involuntarily fell down.
Fortunately, Su Lun was quick to react, pulling seven or eight people who were just about to fall overboard back onto the ship with his threads, but still dozens of people fell from the other two ships.
"Plop," "plop," "plop"...
The sound of falling into the water was incessant.
"Quick, get the people up!"
"Spellcasters cast mental dispersion!"
"Medic team, inject the dazed brothers with Wakefulness Potion!"
"Open fire, kill those..."
"..."
Thousand and Barrett, the higher-tier professionals, also sprang into action, diving into the water and unleashing their powers on the group of corpses.
Su Lun deployed several mechanical octopuses, and their efficiency in slaughter was extremely high, instantly turning the water red with dark blood, with numerous severed limbs and body parts floating upwards.
Just at that moment, the lookout from the mast suddenly issued a warning, "Commander! At six o'clock there are numerous unidentified ships approaching! Not... also at nine o'clock, and three o'clock... we're surrounded!"
With these words, the tension in the atmosphere spiked instantly.
Su Lun looked up and indeed saw countless warships emerging from all directions within the mist.
Upon closer inspection, these warships looked very old and came in various styles, both new and old, the majority of which didn't match the shipbuilding style of this era. But what these ships had in common was that they were riddled with holes, their sails in tatters, and covered with a large amount of coral and other marine growth, as if they were sunken ships recently raised from the sea floor. It was a mystery how they were sailing at all...
Soon, ships broke through the mist and entered the sight of the Dawn Group. Only then could everyone see clearly that there were around a few thousand Ghost Ships, crammed with all sorts of decaying undead monsters aboard, holding their rotten weapons and staring over with their ghastly faces...
[Undead Ship Captain Drake (Gold Tier)], [Undead First Mate Anita (Iron Tier)], [Undead Sailors], [Undead Vultures]...
Because it was a monster, Su Lun identified it immediately.
Ordinary monsters, from black iron, silver, gold, even to lord-level monsters, were all present.
The numbers were so great that they were uncountable.
Barrett, as the group battle commander, also reacted immediately. He quickly assessed the situation and issued combat instructions, "Arrange the fleet in a 'line' formation, full speed ahead. Prepare the first round of cannons!"
"The first ship is loaded!"
"The second ship is loaded!"
"The third..."
In less than half a minute, all three ships' gun decks had reported back that they were ready to fire.
"Fire!"
At the command, almost two hundred cannons on both sides of the three ships simultaneously spewed flames.
There was no need to aim; the undead warships were everywhere.
"Boom," "Boom," "Boom"...
The cannonballs hit the undead warships' hulls, immediately bursting them into countless splinters.
But, to everyone's surprise, the targeted ships that should have sunk were defying the laws of physics and continued to sail.
"Ghost ships?"
Su Lun's gaze sharpened as he realized that these ships themselves were a kind of monster infused with the aura of the undead!
Unless completely shattered, even if riddled with a thousand holes, these ships would not take in water and sink.
This also meant that despite the fierce firepower from the Dawn Group's three warships, it did not stop the undead ships from the surrounding waves that were closing in on them.
Seeing that it wouldn't be long before they would be submerged in the tide made up of the undead warships.
Barrett was on the leading ship, Tanni was on the rear ship, and Su Lun was on the middle ship.
He unleashed the Octopus Spear, and the cross on his head nearly covered all three ships.
By his side, Kama's face was deathly pale as she prepared for what was to come.
Surrounded by ten mechanical puppets, her heavy breathing betrayed how nervous she was confronting such a situation.
A thousand people versus hundreds of thousands, even millions of undead monsters; this was a scene not everyone had the courage to face.
Especially a young girl.
Su Lun glanced at his disciple and patted her shoulder, offering a slight smile, "Relax a little. The right amount of tension can bring out the best in our bodies, but too much negative emotion can cloud your judgment in battle."
"Teacher..."
Kama trembled slightly as she turned her head to look.
She then realized that no matter what the situation, her teacher always remained incredibly composed.
Seeing the smile on her teacher's face, she suddenly felt courage in her heart and nodded seriously, "Yes."
...
"The rear ship, lay mines on the sea surface, incendiary shells..."
"Keep firing! Full speed ahead! All but the gunners, get on deck, prepare for boarding combat!"
"..."
On the ship, the members of the Dawn Group, weapons in hand, watched nervously as countless ghost ships drew closer.
Five hundred meters, three hundred meters, one hundred meters... Closer and closer.
Those who could shoot began sniping at a distance with their firearms.
For a time, the sound of gunfire and cannons blazed incessantly.
The Dawn Group was armed with Mafa standard equipment, some of the best firearms on the market, and there were even several temporary heavy machine gun positions added on deck.
"Tatatata..."
With covering fire, tons of shell casings poured onto the deck.
But then, everyone noticed a major problem: the monsters that seemed to be badly damaged could still stand!
"Damn it, these undead creatures can't be killed!"
"Truly bizarre. These monsters are blown in half, and they can still thrash around while lying down."
"Be careful, these are the legendary undead. Use Holy Light spells, Holy Light bullets!"
"..."
Nearly no one had ever seen undead creatures before.
The members of the Dawn Group looked at these unkillable monsters and felt equally troubled.
While Holy Light spells and Holy Light bullets were indeed effective, they were in limited supply, with too low an efficiency in killing monsters.
If this continued, they would eventually be worn down here.
Anxiety spread quickly.
Su Lun had been observing everything, already understanding the monsters' characteristics.
Sensing the crew's panic, he suddenly shouted, "Let the monsters board the ship later, just focus on fighting, I have a way to deal with them completely!"
At these words, as if injected with a shot of adrenaline, everyone's spirits were instantly lifted!
All members of the Dawn Group knew that "Mr. Su Lun" was someone who could always create miracles.
"Fight!"
"Fight!"
"Battle!"
The fighting spirit of the crowd flared up in an instant.
...
These undead creatures were indeed special; in this peculiar "Shipwreck Space," they were truly "dead" yet able to resurrect endlessly.
Su Lun had encountered such situations a few times before.
Because he had encountered them, he also had the confidence to face them.
A moment ago, he had also discovered that these undead monsters could indeed revive, but after being hit, their souls went from a stable state to a free-floating one.
Although they would recover after a short period, in Su Lun's eyes, that free-floating process turned into groups of harvestable "gray mist."
.....
A short while later, the Dawn Group's battleships charged like daggers into the pile of undead monsters' ghost ships.
The mechanical octopi cleared the path of undead ships with their cannons, ensuring that the three battleships were not completely trapped. But as the distance closed, countless undead monsters with rotting flesh leaped onto the ship, engaging in close combat with the Dawn Group's warriors.
Su Lun controlled hundreds of runic puppets, joining the fray.
With every sweep of the black scythe, one fell; with each punch from the gargoyle, another; the puppet legion was also slaughtering in swathes.
Clouds of gray mist rose.
Su Lun swiftly moved across the three ships, harvesting the mists.
'You harvested the soul fragments of a "Dead Sailor," spiritual power +0.7'
'You harvested the soul fragments of an "Elite Dead Sailor," spiritual power +1.1'
'You harvested the soul fragments of a "Silver First Mate of the Undead," spiritual power +3.2; you have obtained intelligence: "Lord Sea King orders, kill these humans"'
'...'
The souls of these undead monsters were very simple, almost entirely acting on instinct.
Those gray mists could only shed a bit of spiritual power and didn't hold much useful information.
As Su Lun harvested along the way, those monsters that leaped onto the deck died and could not revive.
Soon the deck was piled high with mountains of undead monsters' bodies.
But those undead creatures, oblivious to pain, still kept coming relentlessly...
The terror of the undead monsters lies in their trait of "immortality."
Now that they could be killed, their combat power was about the same as a skeleton's, not a significant threat.
Even if there was one "Gold Monster" among a thousand, it was only at the standard of a third-tier professional.
The Dawn Group's warriors were formidable, especially Qian Tiao and Barrett. One's sword qi soared hundreds of meters; the other's punches blasted half a ship with each strike, slaughtering large numbers without reasoning.
All kinds of heavy bombs were fired into the monster pile as if they cost nothing, and alchemy technology also gave these legendary creatures a clout on the head...
....
Normally, if the Dawn Group continued to confront the endless tide of monsters head-on, they'd probably be worn down to death before they even found the "Stygian River."
But Su Lun wasn't worried because that "Sea King" certainly wouldn't stand by and watch his subordinates continue to be slaughtered.
Especially since Su Lun's mechanical octopi specifically targeted his "beloved consorts" for killing.
In total, at least dozens had been killed.
Just a few sacrifices at the Temple of Aghaparnon would equal to several hundred years of accumulation.
Sure enough, as the battle raged, a warning from Pandora came by Su Lun's ear, "That guy is coming!"
It was then that Su Lun looked up and saw, amidst the distant mist, a colossal sailing ship slowly approaching!
Atop the mast of the ship hung a tattered flag, but it was still possible to make out the image of a skeleton set against a black sun.
"A Sea Emperor-class battleship!"
"Could it be... that's the 'Eternal Night Emperor' of the Pirate Emperor Francis Drake!"
"My goodness, that legendary great pirate from over two hundred years ago? I grew up on that legend."
"Is this guy the 'Sea King' from the Shipwreck?"
"..."
Seeing the over three-hundred-meter-long ship with three levels of cannon decks, everyone from the Dawn Group revealed faces of shock.
The Dawn Group's three battleships, with the best one barely qualifying as a "second-rate ship of the line."
With a single layer of cannon chambers and twenty regular-caliber cannons on one side.
The largest sailing ship currently available on the market is the "Sea King-class" battleship.
The "Princess Stika" that Su Lun had seen before was only over a hundred meters in total length, and when compared to the imposing black-sailed ship before him, the difference was simply immense.
It wasn't that larger ships couldn't be built; it was a matter of material limitations, and this was nearly the limit for sailing wooden ships.
And legend has it that there is an even higher class of ship that reigns over the sea—the "Sea Emperor-class" battleship!
Thirty years ago, Pirate King Black Sam's flagship was a "Sea Emperor-class" battleship. But after they went silent at sea, there has not been any other sail-powered wooden ship since that could be called a "Sea Emperor-class."
Moreover, upon closer inspection, Su Lun realized that this battleship was actually a legendary alchemical construct!
[Eternal Night Emperor]
Quality: Legendary
Description: A battleship made from the trunk of a "Gold Oak Tree Cursed by a Demon God," crafted by master shipbuilder Moises based on the dwarven race's "Stygian River Ship" blueprints; it has extraordinary natural corrosion resistance, unmatched toughness; the ship has wandered the Shipwreck for hundreds of years, shrouded in a rich undead miasma, and it has developed a powerful ghostly presence, making this warship sentient; it can self-repair; it can carry people to the Underworld; this is a super warship that can only be steered by a maritime overlord;
And on the deck of that ship stood a man nearly three meters tall, one of whose legs was a wooden peg.
The name displayed by the assessment was: [Sea King·Drake]

chapters.title: Chapter 385 - 384: Bait
chapters.content:
"Pirate Emperor" Francis Drake was a legendary pirate entered into the history books; over two hundred years ago, this man was active on the battlefields of the Luying Empire and Mafa.
Because his strength was so overpowering, he even obtained a "privateering license" from the Luying royal family for a while, becoming a semi-official pirate, plundering a vast amount of treasure along the coast of the Mafa Empire.
This man was excessively brutal, engaging in burning, killing, and looting without restraint, and constantly switching sides between the two great empires to reap huge profits.
Later, he suddenly disappeared.
It was said that he had been killed by the Luying navy. Others claimed he had stolen some sort of precious treasure of Mafa and was chased by a ninth-tier powerful being into a corner, dying at sea.
Staring at the undead monster leader before him, Su Lun identified it by this name, alongside the ship named "Eternal Night Emperor," a Sea Emperor-class battleship—it was undoubtedly that legendary figure.
Unexpectedly, he had died here in the Sea Ruins.
As a monster, Su Lun immediately identified this guy's attributes.
[Sea King·Drake]
Explanation: A mutant monster infected with the energy of the undead, a lord-tier zombie species, possessing a primary pseudo-divine power, adept at controlling high-tier water elemental forces and the force of death laws, extremely dangerous; in his lifetime, he lost a leg, which made him not adept at teleportation; in the sea, he could appear anywhere, but on land, his strength was only one-tenth; he possessed some divine powers beyond common knowledge;
The advantages and disadvantages were clear at a glance.
Looking at this, Su Lun immediately had a strategy in his mind.
...
"Eternal Night Emperor" was completely black, with black sails, a black hull, and surrounded by billowing black smoke. It was bigger than three Dawn ships combined. As it sailed in the sea, it was like an elephant charging towards three hyenas. Its sheer presence was enough to make one's scalp tingle.
"Cannons, aim!"
"Fire!"
"..."
At first encounter, the two sides immediately began a cannon battle.
Somehow, the cannons and gunpowder from two hundred years ago had not been damaged by moisture, but the hundreds of cannon mouths truly spewed out flames.
"Eternal Night" had more cannons in its three-tier gun tower than the three combined ships of the Dawn group. When it fired, it was like setting off fireworks, the sounds were deafening, and the burning of the black gunpowder produced a large amount of white smoke, the loudness frightfully exaggerated.
But after all, the cannons loaded on that sea ship were antiques from two hundred years ago, and the undead gunners seemed to have only the instinct to fire them from life; they could not calculate the distances in a cannon battle.
The range and accuracy were far inferior to the Dawn group.
In the end, after an exchange of cannon fires, the Dawn group's cannonballs hit the hull of the "Eternal Night," while the opponent's cannonballs mostly fell into the sea.
However, hitting them made little difference from missing them.
Su Lun watched as the cannonballs bombarded the opposing ship's hull, visibly creating ripples.
But other than the parts of the hull that were already damaged, none of the cannonballs broke through the wooden planks of the ship.
Su Lun, seeing this, was not surprised at all but a gleam flashed in his eyes.
Every adventurer who roamed the seas needed a ship, and no one would refuse the allure of a "Sea Emperor-class" battleship.
"What a fine ship!"
It was the first time Su Lun felt such a strong attraction to a ship.
At this moment, he was already thinking about how to turn this ship into the main battleship of the Dawn group.
But there was a premise he couldn't circumvent: defeating the Sea King.
The cannon battle was futile. It was nearly impossible for the three battleships of the Dawn group to sink the opponent by cannon fire.
And it would be pointless.
If it weren't for Pandora's warning, Su Lun would probably have opted for a "beheading" strategy now.
Only by killing this [Sea King·Drake] would they have a chance to break their predicament, and these undead creatures would stop coming incessantly.
But now, he chose not to do so but instead commanded through the communicator, "Activate the alchemy windsail; do not engage in battle! Head twenty nautical miles southwest. There's an island there; we'll land!"
That was because Su Lun had learned a little-known secret from Pandora. That is, a pseudo-god is a collective of faith, and they do not truly die when their bodies are killed.
It's necessary to destroy the "divinity" that holds the faith to thoroughly annihilate a pseudo-god.
This was also why Pandora was not afraid of Su Lun killing her alchemic body before. After the divinity of faith is condensed, that is the "pseudo-god's" true vulnerability.
Su Lun did not know where this "Sea King's" divinity was, but he could make an educated guess.
Previously, those from the Temple of Aghaparnon had circulated a treasure map to attract adventurers in search of treasure.
In order to make it as authentic as possible, the treasure map marked many "Treasure Islands" in this sea area.
Now knowing this was the Sea Ruin and there was a "Sea King," it usually meant that the place richest in treasures would be the great BOSS's lair.
Which is to say, that "Devil's Island" on the treasure map was most likely the residence of the "Sea King" Drake's divine power.
Moreover, in the sea, Su Lun didn't feel his Dawn Group had the capability to kill this guy.
The gap between warships was too large, and the enemy possessed control over the ocean.
On land, however, it only had one-tenth of its combat power.
In any case, landing on the island first was the most logical tactic.
"Yes!"
At that order, the three ships began to break through.
....
The fierce battle continued, and various undead monsters kept crazily jumping onto the three warships of the Dawn Group.
However, since Su Lun could harvest souls, he completely deprived these monsters of their ability to resurrect.
With the undead monster legions unable to resurrect, their threat was reduced by ninety percent.
After all, normal humans converted into undead would have significantly reduced strength; a Tier-7 professional managing to retain Tier-5 combat prowess was considered good.
Though the number of these undead creatures was horrifying, the vast majority were just skeletons, not even counting as Tier-1.
The Dawn Group's three teams already had a tacit agreement to live and die together, and their concerted efforts made the battle fierce yet not devastating.
"Clatter," "Clatter," "Clatter"...
The sound of skeletons being shattered was everywhere.
Qian Tao and Barrett moved around, slashing higher-tiered monsters.
The trio of giant warriors swung their Wolf Fang Clubs and giant shields, reaping a swath through the undead...
The sumo wrestler's palm strikes, exploding with force like cannon fire, reduced everything to bone dust with every hit...
The mechanical team, equipped with heavy mechanical limbs, rampaged through the crowd of monsters...
The Adjudication team formed battle formations, relentlessly pushing forward like an iron barrel...
Even Kama gradually adapted to the rhythm of the fight and performed exceptionally well.
With skillful puppetry technique and the rune-based strange puppets Su Lun gave her, she fought as ten, piling corpses high around her.
While fighting, the three warships used up their stored energy crystals to drive the alchemical sails, pushing their speed to the limit.
Because they decided decisively, they pierced through the encircling ring of undead monsters before it fully closed, like a dagger stabbing through rotten wood, and burst out in an instant.
....
"There are monsters in the water!"
"Those are 'Rotting Whales,' be careful not to let those creatures flip the ship!"
"Another group of 'Ironheaded Sharks' is here, damn, they've smashed a big hole in the bottom of Ship No. 3."
"Abandon ship, stack explosives, prepare to blow up Ship No. 3!"
"..."
Not long after the Dawn Group's three ships broke out, the calm sea surface suddenly stirred into large waves, and many large undead sea monsters emerged from the seabed.
Even with the Mechanical Octopus Legion engaging in separate killings, one ship was still damaged.
Worse yet, that sea emperor level "Eternal Night Emperor" ship had caught up with them.
The undead creatures that had climbed onto the ships were completely eradicated, and the Dawn Group's members crowded onto two ships, watching as the "Eternal Night" rode waves dozens of meters high, chasing after them.
"How can their huge ship be faster than us when we used the alchemical sails!"
"Sea Emperor level warships inherently possess some special wind propulsion systems; they have large displacement but are not unwieldy, always touted as 'the fastest warships on the sea.' Plus, that peg-legged guy holds a high-level cursed trident, controlling the local waves, which is very disadvantageous for us!"
"Damn it. If this continues, we'll be caught up soon."
"..."
Seeing this, Su Lun decisively ordered, "Abandon all cannons and warehouse materials, clear out the ship's storage!"
"Yes!"
Upon hearing that, although everyone felt the loss, they did not hesitate and quickly started moving.
Within the storage cabin, heavy cannons were pushed into the sea alongside boxes of cannonballs, barrels of rum, and bundles of other supplies.
Su Lun's "Little Void World" contained enough food to last them a long while, even if the ship ran out of other supplies.
But it was a real pity to lose those cannons.
Not only were they valuable, but they were also irreplaceable military supplies.
However, naval combat had become pointless now. Without increasing their speed, they would not have escaped.
In an instant, various supplies floated all over the sea surface, and the speed of the ship increased dramatically, several times faster than before.
Even so, the "Eternal Night Emperor" was closing in rapidly. Members of the Dawn Group could even see high-level undead creatures on decks watching them with their terrifying, empty eye sockets.
Small islands had begun to sporadically appear around them, but those islands, visible end-to-end, offered no place to hide.
If they didn't find a solution, they would never be able to reach and land on "Devil's Island."
At that moment, Su Lun stood on the deck, looking solemnly at the relentless undead legion pursuing them.
By his side, core officers such as Qian Tiao, Dr. Banks, and Barrett looked serious as well.
Su Lun's brain was like a high-speed computer calculating all possible outcomes.
A moment later, he came up with the most reasonable plan and immediately said, "Continuing this way definitely won't work. I think we should split into two groups—one to lure the enemy and the other to circumnavigate to Devil's Island. Those undead do not yet know our purpose. Only if we can create an opportunity for Miss Pandora can we possibly survive."
Upon hearing this, everyone nodded their heads.
This was the best, and the only feasible, plan.
Their opponent could catch up to them only with the "Eternal Night," so splitting Dawn Group into two would help divide the target.
One ship would act as the "bait," while the other might have a chance to reach Devil's Island.
At that time, Barrett said without hesitation, "I think this plan will work! I have the highest rank in the group; I'll take some brothers and stay to hold them off, Su Lun you go first."
Qian Tiao, not wanting to be outdone, added, "I'll stay. My 'Thunderous Hell' is more effective against undead creatures."
However, Su Lun shook his head and interrupted, "We need to have someone who can absolutely draw their attention. I'm the only one who can do that. Plus, I can handle the ship alone and have teleportation abilities. It's most suitable for me to stay."
His meaning was clear—he was prepared to stay behind alone to lure the enemy.
Upon hearing this, a look of concern appeared on Qian Tiao's face, "But..."
Su Lun did not let them speak further, shaking his head, "There's no time to hesitate. It's decided then."
After a pause, he continued, "Prepare the smoke bombs and sensory disruptors. Then everyone else should head to the other ship."
Barrett and the others, not insisting further, nodded gravely, "Alright!"
Qian Tiao looked at Su Lun and said, "Take care!"
Su Lun smiled faintly, "Hmm."
Through the communicator, Barrett gave the order, "Everyone, prepare to execute Emergency Plan T11!"
The next instant, two warships suddenly moved side by side, numerous smoke bombs launched, instantly creating a massive smoke cover on the sea surface.
Dozens of beams of Holy Light spell shot up into the sky, bursting out dazzling white light in the air.
Those undead creatures were startled and drew back. But as the light dissipated, they saw the two warships heading in different directions.
...
Su Lun was on Ship Two, surrounded by hundreds of sailors.
But in fact, he was the only living person on the entire ship.
The rest were "living dead"; there were more in the cabin, almost all he had left.
Undead creatures are highly sensitive to the life force of humans, and it was difficult to confuse them using just puppets.
Meanwhile on the other warship, all members of the Dawn Group were gathered there, hiding in the cabin and trying their best to conceal any signs of life.
Su Lun was on deck, busily controlling the "living dead sailors" as usual.
Now, his puppetry skills were profoundly proficient, and without looking closely, no anomalies could be detected. Moreover, most of those undead creatures lacked eyes, making them naturally hard to detect.
As soon as the two ships split, both accelerated to maximum speed.
Su Lun's ship lagged slightly behind, and without hesitation, he took out the black sickle and swung it towards the one-legged "Sea King" on the distant "Eternal Night."
He hadn't expected the swing to harm the tyrant-level monster but thought of it as "drawing aggro."
Due to the distance, when the spatial crack hit the "Sea King's" neck, it was less than a foot long.
Still, it was a "spatial crack"—enough to decapitate a normal creature!
But the "Sea King" didn't even flinch, and the cut was like slicing through a person made of water. His neck, adorned with fish scale tattoos, split open to reveal a jelly-like black water, which healed in an instant.
He cocked his head and twisted to look at Su Lun on the deck, as if staring at an ant.
Then, he raised his trident and casually pointed forward, condensing countless black drops of water out of thin air, suspended motionlessly.
Su Lun closed his right eye and stared at the creature with his left.
He identified it quickly—it was also a "banned item" level weapon.
[Aegir's Trident of the Sea God]
Quality: Legendary
Description: Owning it, you would feel as if commanding the entire sea;
Curse Trait: Possessing this item significantly increases affinity with water elements; using this item can control the sea currents within a certain range, with the scope and power dependent on the infused spiritual power; if not wielding high-level water element laws power, use will lead to the curse of the sea, suffering and dying of thirst;
Detailed Explanation: Aegir, the most ancient of the giant deities, holding the original power of sea laws; ancient alchemists crafted this Sea God's scepter to control the power of the ocean;
"As long as the plan succeeds, the Eternal Night, the trident... all these things will be spoils of war!"
Su Lun muttered to himself.
The next moment, those droplets shot through the air like bullets, "whoosh," "whoosh," "whoosh."
Su Lun identified the droplets—the display read [Death Arrow Rain]; he immediately judged he could handle it and hurriedly propped open the rune-laden black umbrella, with a barrier of death laws cascading around him.
Crackle and pop, the next moment, the sound resembled rain hitting banana leaves.
The raindrops struck the black umbrella but were completely blocked.
"It really did block it!"
Su Lun's eyes narrowed.
Apparently, the nearly seventh-tier spell power of [Death Arrow Rain]was something he could not withstand head-on, but incredibly, he could.
It was like using fire to burn another flame, hugely diminishing the effect.
Su Lun was sure he could maintain the aggro because he too understood the "laws of death," and not insignificantly so.
He originated from the same source as these necrotic creatures.
The "Sea King" sensed it and would definitely not let him go.
Sure enough, right after blocking that attack, the "Eternal Night Emperor" shifted its course and began chasing after Su Lun's ship.
"It worked!"
Su Lun felt a surge of joy and then steered the warship on a looping course.
A distant sister ship carrying others also seized the moment to head in another direction, frantically sailing towards Devil's Island.
...
Su Lun drove the warship, fleeing all the way. Although the monsters were getting closer and the warship was riddled with holes, he wasn't panicked.
He was just bait, while another ship of the Dawn Group was the main force.
That [Sea King · Drake] probably maintained divine arrogance, thinking if Su Lun didn't provoke it, it wouldn't bother to strike personally, or perhaps it felt all humans in these sea ruins must die, and toying with them was better—thus sending a bunch of lackeys and undead sea monsters to attack.
After a while, they didn't catch up.
Su Lun, alone on a ship, weaving through thousands of ships and tens of thousands of undead monsters, ran wildly.
Having approached the waters near "Devil's Island," islands became more frequent. Crows flew in the sky, and utilizing his knowledge of the terrain, Su Lun predicted dimensions in advance, constantly weaving through the islands like a snake.
Finally, the warship was completely wrecked.
But after all, with only one living person on board, Su Lun didn't feel much burden. He unhesitatingly abandoned the ship full of undead and switched to a speedboat, continuing his wild rampage. His spatial displacement ability had improved significantly, making him very capable of self-preservation. The escape was thrilling, yet not so easy to be caught.
Meanwhile, Su Lun contacted others and learned that the Dawn Group's main force had successfully landed on "Devil's Island."
The plan to lure the enemy was successful!

chapters.title: Chapter 386 - 385: First Contact
chapters.content:
Just when the Dawn Era group fell into the sea ruins, numerous treasure hunting teams had already followed the treasure map to this area.
Perhaps because the fish had not yet been netted, these treasure hunters smoothly made their way into the sea ruins, joyfully excavating treasures on various islands.
While Su Lun was being pursued, in the forests south of Devil's Island.
A group of adventurers discovered an ancient shipwreck in the forest and were enthusiastically digging it out.
The forest had a rainforest climate, humid and sweltering, but that did not dampen the enthusiasm of the treasure hunters.
With every shovel into the soil, they found numerous Ancient Coins. Occasionally, various precious gold and silver vessels, ceramics, and gemstones were unearthed.
It was evident that this was a treasure ship from hundreds of years ago, laden with riches.
Having found such abundant treasure shortly after landing on the island, the crew was very excited.
"Hahaha... Captain, we've struck it rich this time. There really are treasures everywhere on Devil's Island! Just finding this shipwreck has nearly filled our hold. It's hard to imagine how much more treasure remains undiscovered in the depths of the island..."
"Exactly. Lucky we have a Captain with such reliable information, and who got hold of first-hand sea charts. When we return to Lindun, we're definitely going to shock those guild guys! Hahaha..."
"Our 'Black Panther Group' is really going to prosper this time. Oh, when I get back I must tell my son the stories of our treasure hunting, he will be so proud to have an adventurer for a father."
"But it's strange how suddenly the weather changed in this sea area, we can't even see the sun... and where did this dense aura of the undead come from?"
"Weren't there rumors that the nearby sea areas of Devil's Island were very dangerous? We did encounter a few undead creatures, but haven't seen any dangerous sea monsters."
"Who knows, maybe we're just lucky? As you know, luck is always an indispensable part of a treasure hunter's life."
"..."
The full name of this treasure hunting team was the "Twenty-Seventh Treasure Hunting Team of Prince Carnap, the Black Panther Group."
Indeed, this was a treasure hunting team sponsored by Prince Carnap of the Luying Empire, an official treasure hunting team and a well-known, established group within the "Luying Adventurers' Guild."
The leader was a burly middle-aged man with a rosacea nose, none other than the Captain of the "Black Panther Team," Red Nose Adolf Myles.
Listening to his team's lively conversations and observing the deathly still forest, he had a bad feeling and cautioned in a standard Lindun accent, "Hey, everyone be careful. 'Beibei' is very restless; it seems a great danger is lurking on this island."
"Beibei" was a sleek black panther with a glossy coat. It was a purebred from the rare mountain species of North Luying, known as the "Lan Youtong Spirit Panther." This magical beast was naturally a medium for spirits and had sharp senses towards danger, making it the best companion for Beast Tamers and many diviners.
Myles said this as he stroked his closest companion.
"Got it, boss!"
"Oh, we need to hurry a bit; more treasure hunters are coming up behind us. We need to find the 'Heart of the Four Elements,' commissioned by Lord Antonio of the guild, before they do..."
"Hey, we must be the first ones to reach Devil's Island. If that item is here, no one is going to find it before us."
"..."
The crew members dug and talked at the same time.
But just then, suddenly, a sense-oriented professional spoke, "Something has triggered the warning device I set up to the west, seems like a human!"
Captain Myles's face changed dramatically, "Someone's come? How many people?"
The man furrowed his brow and added, "Looks like... just one."
"One?"
Myles looked puzzled.
How could there be a lone wanderer on Devil's Island?
A grave expression crossed his face as he said, "Let's go and check it out."
...
At this very moment, on the western beach of Devil's Island.
"Crack~"
A crisp bone-cracking sound.
Su Lun released the head he had crushed, then gasped heavily and pulled the bone spear that the creature had thrust into him out of his body.
With this pull, a jet of blood sprayed from the wound.
He grew pale and took out a Potion to pour over the wound on his shoulder, which emitted white smoke with a sizzling sound, slowly alleviating the burning sensation caused by the undead corruption.
Su Lun had just killed this undead creature and finally breathed a sigh of relief.
The undead creature, identified as "Pirate Captain Parker (Gold)," was very strong. It was likely a seventh-tier pirate in life and was fifth-tier in death.
The fact that its bone spear could penetrate his Rune Vajra Body indicated its potency.
And such a fifth-tier gold undead, there were many more among those tens of thousands of undead creatures earlier.
"Trouble is no small matter..."
Su Lun looked at the dense jungle ahead, his eyes filled with solemnity.
Devil's Island was a vast island, so large that even with the shared vision of black crows, he couldn't see the end.
Finding the Sea God's divine grace was not easy.
He originally planned to keep the "Sea King Drake" and those undead creatures going around at sea for as long as possible.
After all, the longer he held them off, the higher the likelihood of success for Qiantiao and the others.
But unexpectedly, not long after Qiantiao and the others landed on Devil's Island, the "Sea King Drake" detected something. The horde of undead creatures then abruptly switched from their previous cat-and-mouse attitude to attacking him furiously.
Fortunately, the big BOSS was probably drawn away by Qiān Tiáo, so he didn't personally pursue Su Lun. Su Lun had strong life-saving tactics, and only after exhausting all his methods had he barely managed to escape to Devil's Island.
However, killing hundreds of monsters that pursued him also depleted most of his dark spiritual power, which left him somewhat exhausted.
But now was clearly not the time to rest; he had to meet up with the main force.
Cold flames emerged from Su Lun's hands as he burned the blood and bone spears on the ground together, not intending to leave any traces behind.
Just as he was about to catch his breath and leave, he sensed a group of people approaching.
In the blink of an eye, a sleek black panther and several wind wolves emerged from the dense forest, baring their teeth from a distance.
"Beast Tamer?"
Observing these magical beasts, Su Lun raised his eyebrows, naturally sensing humans in the jungle.
Having seen numerous undead creatures, suddenly spotting some creatures of the living world improved his mood. He did not attack, but merely cast a brief glance at the magical beasts.
Yet, with just that look, the creatures took a collective half-step back, their threatening expressions much subdued, betraying a hint of fear.
It wasn't even two seconds later that more than twenty people sprung forth from the dense forest.
They brandished their weapons, displaying both puzzled and shocked expressions.
The leader, a big-bearded man with a reddened nose, stared at Su Lun standing alone and asked incredulously, "Sir, are you an adventurer?"
"Hmm."
Su Lun sized up these people, guessing some information about them; they didn't have the signature smoke-stained black teeth of pirates but looked like well-off adventurers, probably people from Emperor Luying's domain.
That big-bearded man cautiously asked, "Which group are you with? Why are you alone here?"
Su Lun knew the other party was probing his background, but he wasn't interested in conversing further with these people.
He looked at the team and noticed three people with the brand of the "Sun Slave Trading Company" on their necks, identifying them as slaves.
Moreover, coincidently, the rolled-up sleeves of these three revealed delicately tattooed anchor symbols on their arms.
Very familiar with the mark, which was the favorite insignia of Captain Barrett's group, Su Lun directly asked the three, "Are you three from the 'Sacred Judgment?"'
Even with weapons drawn towards him, he harbored no hostility towards these people, precisely because of these three.
Hearing this, the big-bearded man's expression swiftly changed from caution to wariness, "What do you mean by that?"
He didn't know how Su Lun had figured it out, but the "Judgment Group" was now wanted by the royal family of Emperor Luying, and sheltering them was a serious crime. He had risked a lot by buying a few acquaintances from a slave trader due to his past connections with the judgment group, and now, being discovered made him wary.
Seeing that the three didn't appear coerced, Su Lun also guessed some of their circumstances. After a moment of thought, he straightforwardly said, "I mean no harm. Captain Barrett is my friend. And… he's also on the island right now."
Hearing this, the three men from the Sacred Group visibly showed expressions of anticipation and excitement, wanting to ask more.
But due to caution, they neither admitted anything nor dared to speak.
Su Lun observed their defensive postures and attitudes, all indicating they didn't want him intruding into the forest behind them. He guessed they probably discovered some treasure and were excavating it. Otherwise, treasure hunters wouldn't bother intercepting anyone.
But it was impossible to explain it quickly, and Su Lun didn't want to linger there any longer. He kindly warned, "The treasure hunt on Devil's Island has been a conspiracy from the start. The high priest from the Temple of Aghaparnon has lured adventurers here to sacrifice them alive. This place is a 'Sea Ruin.'"
"Forget it, you're on your own now. Staying here will only harm you. Head west, there you'll find the River of the Underworld. If you can successfully navigate up its current, that's your only chance of leaving alive."
Having said that, he didn't look back and turned toward another direction, walking deeper into the forest.
[Sea King]Not dead, no one could leave the Sea Ruin alive.
Even his group from Dawn Era might not make it out alive, reminding them was already a sign of good faith.
...
Watching the stranger walk away, the group from Black Fang were dumbfounded.
At that moment, someone still hadn't grasped the severity of the situation, asking, "Captain, are we just letting that guy go? What if he's a spy sent by some pirate group..."
"Red Nose" Myles shook his head, his expression complex, "Didn't you notice how that man, faced with so many of us, remained completely composed from start to finish?"
As he spoke, he glanced at the black panther beside him and added, "Moreover, 'Beibei' sensed that that person is extremely dangerous!"
The words "extremely dangerous" were heavily emphasized,
Hearing this, everyone's faces changed simultaneously, the memory of the young man's composed attitude spontaneously recurring in their minds.
This realization came a bit too late.
Moreover, the stranger obviously had no interest in any treasure.
Rather, his words were deeply terrifying when pondered.
Another person asked, "Captain, how credible do you think his words were? Is this place really a 'Sea Ruin'?"
Myles grimaced, "Even if they can't be entirely trusted, we might still be in big trouble."
The few words spoken earlier were laden with significant information.
As adventurers who had drifted at sea, who hadn't heard of the "Sea Ruin"?
The Temple of Aghaparnon was using the treasure hunt to sacrifice them alive?
Although it seemed unbelievable, it… didn't appear to have a motive for deception.
The more they thought about it, the colder the members of the Black Fang felt.
Just then, they looked toward the misty horizon at sea and slowly saw some strange shadows emerge.
"Captain, look, what is that!"
This warning caught everyone's attention.
In the midst of intense focus, a shadow emerged from the thick fog, revealing itself to be a decrepit old ship with thousands of failures.
And on the ship, there were countless undead creatures packed densely together.
Seeing this scene, everyone from the Black Panther Group, having never seen such an extravagant display, was terrified to the point of turning pale.
Myles was beside himself with fear and shouted, "Damn it, retreat to the jungle and prepare for battle!"
It turned out that Devil's Island was not without danger; the dangers had just not yet found them.
Now, they had!
At the same time, nearly all the adventure groups that entered the ruins at sea encountered attacks from undead creatures.
...
Devil's Island was said to be an island, but its area was vast; Su Lun estimated that it was at least several dozen kilometers in diameter.
There indeed were many treasures on the island; Su Lun traveled through the forest, repeatedly seeing gold and silver utensils in the mud. Digging deeper, there were sure to be treasures.
All these were the accumulated "offerings" over countless years, including some valuable steles and artifacts from lost civilizations.
But Su Lun was not in the mood to dig for treasures because at that time, the main force led by Myles had already started fighting the undead creatures.
With the enhancement of an eight-armed spider spear, he moved swiftly through the jungle, and soon, he could hear the sounds of fierce combat.
"Boom" "Boom" "Boom"...
The sounds of gunfire became clearer and clearer.
However, Su Lun did not join the battle right away; he first released the Raven of Death to overlook the entire battlefield from the sky.
From this view, the creatures in the jungle surged toward one direction like a tide.
The members of Dawn Group were completely surrounded by a sea of undead creatures, a situation worse than any naval battle; no matter which direction they broke through, endless creatures awaited them.
Fortunately, this was on land, where the undead creatures, being "the dead from the sea," had significantly reduced strength.
The Dawn Group members also found a terrain advantageous for trench warfare, and with powerful modern firearms and sufficient ammunition, they were not wiped out.
Of course, Su Lun could not stand idly by; he wielded his black scythe, followed by gargoyles, chopping and teleporting his way through.
....
"Mr. Su Lun is back!"
"Wow! It's so great that Mr. Su Lun is back..."
"..."
As soon as Su Lun rushed into the encampment, members of the Dawn Group burst into cheers.
Earlier, he had alone held off the creatures in the sea, providing the Dawn Group members with a chance to escape. Now, seeing him return safely, everyone naturally cheered and celebrated.
The battle appeared fierce, but the casualties among the Dawn Group members were not substantial.
Under the command of Captain Barrett, a professional military, the camp fought scientifically and efficiently. With three shifts alternating at the frontline managing the monsters, there was time to rest and efficiently kill monsters, and the wounded also received effective treatment.
Because the undead creatures did not revive, Su Lun initially wanted to cut off that "gray mist" when he entered, but Myles stopped him.
Now entering, he also understood why.
Previously, because no one harvested the souls, it was difficult for the Dawn Group members to kill the undead creatures, but through continued battle, they discovered a trick.
That is, in situations where the enemy numbers hugely outnumbered theirs, there were benefits to not killing them outright.
The number of creatures was vast, but the actual number that could participate in the attack were only those few circles at the core of the encirclement (very few airborne units).
Once the creatures' bodies were battered, their combat effectiveness sharply dropped, but they still occupied the front "output position".
And most of the creatures were not very intelligent; they had only a few simple instincts: to encircle and kill.
Barrett discovered this point and decisively changed the tactics.
The members of the Dawn Group now aimed not to annihilate the creatures but to batter the low-tier creatures and then pile them up outside.
This way, the creatures behind could not surge in, and the actual number of creatures they had to deal with was only a fraction of a percent, or one thousandth.
Of course, if they did not resolve the issue, the number of creatures would continue to increase, and they would eventually be exhausted.
...
Perhaps because they were being blocked, the high-tier creatures also were no longer in a hurry to come and die.
After all, the strength of the Dawn Group was not weak.
Whenever a few high-tier creatures came in, they were immediately taken down by concentrated artillery fire or beheaded by Myles and Barrett.
After killing a few more, it became a lot calmer.
Myles even had time to come over and rest.
Seeing the blood on Su Lun, she asked, "Are you hurt?"
Su Lun shook his head: "A minor issue."
Now that they were trapped, the urgent matter at hand was to figure out how to resolve the predicament.
Su Lun was puzzled and asked, "Sister Myles, what did you trigger earlier?"
Qian Tiao said, "After we landed on the island, we searched the forest for the Sea King's 'Divinity.' Then, Miss Pandora discovered an ancient stele, which seemed to document some ancient secrets. But before the 'archaeologists' in our team could decipher it, it attracted a monster."
Hearing this, Su Lun realized why the Sea King had abruptly turned around—it was because of this.
As he spoke, Qian Tiao took out the previously taken rubbings of the stele.
When Su Lun saw those twisted ancient characters, he immediately recognized them and said, "These are 'Seram characters,' a script from a bygone civilization before the Dawn Era, at least a hundred thousand years old."
Upon hearing this, the few archaeologists and Scholars who were proficient in ancient scripts were overjoyed: "Mr. Su Lun recognizes it? Oh, that is wonderful."
Everyone knew that touching the stele had attracted the monster; it must be something crucial.
The inscription had already been partly deciphered by the experts in the team, and Su Lun also understood some of it.
He didn't need to decipher everything completely. After scanning it, he pretty much understood the meaning of the inscriptions, and with shock in his eyes, he said, "This sea ruin might indeed be the burial site of an ancient Sea God named 'Himinlewa'! This Devil's Island should contain the Sea God's altar, or perhaps a grave. The inscription records the deity slaying a nine-headed sea monster and repelling invaders from the River of the Underworld..."
Listening to him, everyone appeared thoughtful.
The inscription was full of mythological stories, which didn't seem to offer any useful clues.
Qian Tiao, however, bypassed the thoughtful process and directly asked, "Su Lun, what did you figure out?"
"Hmm. Knowing this is the deity's purpose, many things can be inferred."
Su Lun nodded and picked up the currency to draw a map.
While he had been fleeing earlier, he hadn't been idle, and through the vision of the telltale bird, he had memorized the layout of some of the islands near Devil's Island.
Others didn't know what he was doing, but they all watched intently.
Su Lun's highly developed cerebral area allowed him instantly to match the map on the paper to some patterns he had seen before, and suddenly, inspiration burst forth.
He continued with his pen, linking those islands together.
Although it was only part of it, Tanni who was watching suddenly exclaimed, "Mr. Su Lun, could this be the 'Sea God Constellation' sky map?"
An excellent navigator is deeply familiar with the stars, which serve as guiding lights for ships at night.
Su Lun nodded. He had not noticed it before, but after reading the inscription, insight struck him.
Then he said, "Sister Qian Tiao, where did you encounter that stele before?"
"Here."
Qian Tiao pointed out the location.
Su Lun marked it with his pen then used that point as a starting place, drawing several mystical geometric figures, and when combined with the "Sea God Constellation," everything seemed clear.
"Religions must have followers, but the 'Pirate Emperor,' Francis Drake, was just a great pirate; he didn't have a foundation of beliefs. Hence, such belief could only come through special means... If it indeed is a god's tomb, it all makes sense."
This was some divine knowledge that Pandora had told him before. Connecting all the clues together, he immediately figured out the situation.
He pointed out a few spots and said, "The locations where his divinity might be. These three points are the most likely."
Once the pattern was drawn, they no longer had to search blindly on such a large Devil's Island—the three points were highly likely.
Watching quietly under her cloak, Pandora didn't speak, but a flicker of something different passed through her eyes as she watched Su Lun adeptly analyze the situation.
With this sudden turn of events, Qian Tiao again said, "The current situation is that we've been discovered. A large-scale breakout is impossible. Moreover, it would alert the Sea King to personally come and surround us..."
At that moment, Captain Barrett also approached and interjected, "We can hold out for a long time, Su Lun. You could take Miss Pandora and a few elite members to sneak in. The smaller target, the less noticeable."
"Hmm."
Su Lun nodded, which was also his plan.
They needed to switch roles now, with Captain Barrett and others acting as the decoy.
The situation allowed no room for hesitation. He also said, "My 'Mummy Wraps of the Ossian Iceman' can avoid detection from those monsters. Just Miss Pandora and I should go. Fewer people, easier to maneuver. Later, you can be at this position... If anything happens, you can also support each other."
Direct confrontation with the Sea King was risky.
If they were discovered, sheer numbers wouldn't help much.
The duo of Su Lun and Pandora, capable of both fighting and fleeing, was the optimal choice.
This plan almost considered everything, and people like Qian Tiao and Barrett didn't say much, just "Good! Be careful."
"Hmm."
Su Lun said this and glanced at Pandora beside him.
Pandora nodded slightly without speaking, implicitly agreeing.
...
Qian Tiao and the others reengaged in the battlefield.
No one noticed that Su Lun and Pandora stayed in the marching tent.
Alone now, Su Lun looked at Pandora and said, "Forgive me."
Pandora nodded, "Hmm."
Su Lun, without any hesitation, stood behind her and formed a very close posture with her.
This was the first time the two of them had physical contact. Pandora's body was truly unique, incredibly soft and supple, irresistibly so. The contact of large areas of skin and her perfectly sculpted body were keenly felt.
Any stray thoughts vanished almost immediately as Su Lun used the 'Mummy Wraps of the Ossian Iceman' to wrap them together, completely vanishing into thin air.

chapters.title: Chapter 387 - 386: Sea God's Treasury
chapters.content:
Sounds of battle could be heard everywhere on Devil's Island, not just from Dawn Group, but many other adventure groups were also exchanging fire with the undead monsters.
That Sea King Drake had not appeared; he must have returned to his lair to guard his divine nature.
According to Pandora, the ancient Sea God Hininlewa buried here was a high-ranking deity, likely having not just one but possibly a "prophecy" divine nature. The Sea King, having absorbed some of his Faith, also obtained some prophetic abilities. However, since he didn't come directly to them, it was likely a half-baked prophetic ability.
But now that Su Lun and his group were going to trouble him, the more purposeful they were, the more likely they were to be foreseen.
So they had to be extremely cautious.
Before long, in the dense jungles of Devil's Island, a black crow hovered high in the sky.
On the ground, Su Lun unfolded his eight-limbed spider spear and sprinted through the jungle, holding a black umbrella in his left hand and cradling the eyes-closed, spell-preparing Pandora in his right arm.
Before making a move, Pandora would keep her aura as contained as possible. Otherwise, just like she had sensed the Sea King's Power of Faith earlier, the enemy could easily deduce that she was also a "divinity," and they might send a large number of high-level monsters to intercept them.
The resentful spirits of the black umbrella masked their auras, and with the black crow, their journey was smooth.
Su Lun's goal was clear.
He had used the stele to speculate on three possible locations of the altar (graveyard). When he reached the second location, he confirmed that they had found the place.
From a distance, they kept discovering steles inscribed with Celeram characters, as well as some giant columns and sculptures half-buried in the jungle. A long time ago, there might have been some very impressive ground structures here.
By identifying those inscriptions, Su Lun also confirmed that this was a "tomb burying a deity."
...
The climate on Devil's Island was that of a rainforest, with extremely tall trees and a constant drizzle in the air.
Two figures carefully made their way through the dense jungle, drawing closer to the divine tomb.
But the battle occurred very suddenly.
Without any warning, Pandora suddenly opened her eyes.
Her eyes, resembling red moons, flashed a blade-like coldness as she shouted sharply, "They're here!"
As she spoke, she suddenly withdrew forcefully, leaving "Su Lun" alone where he stood.
Almost simultaneously, a trident fell from the sky, striking "Su Lun" with lightning speed.
The full-power sneak attack that Sea King Drake had prepared for a long time was unavoidable. "Su Lun" was pierced through the chest by the trident. Not even a drop of blood could flow out before it was sucked dry by the trident, leaving him a lifeless corpse.
Meanwhile, it was as if a chant from the underworld could be heard by the ear, an arcane and majestic incantation was already formed, "Divine Art: Sea Burial Barrier!"
In an instant, a blue barrier lit up, enclosing the space for a kilometer around, like covering it with a giant "glass fishbowl."
Looking again, the magic power gathered torrential seas that poured in.
In the blink of an eye, the seawater submerged both Pandora and the vast forest, resembling a world within a tank.
Pandora was not to be outdone; her body suddenly burst forth with an indescribable aura, and behind her, the legendary form of the Divine Way's deity emerged.
She plunged into the seawater, releasing the long-prepared spell with her hands clasped, "Divine Way: Domain of Moon Reading!"
Looking again, that red, divine-energy like mesh twisted the light and quickly condensed behind her into a crimson moon. The bizarre red moonlight bathed everything around in a blood-like hue, even staining the seawater. Even more bizarrely, the eyes of all beings within the barrier showed a dazed expression, clearly falling into an "illusion."
Pandora's spells changed again, her blood-colored eyes sparkling, "Divine Art: World of Pain."
With this spell, the surrounding red seawater turned into clouds of fire at dusk, taking on various bizarre monster forms—ghost warriors, Great Tengu, Tall Woman, Slit-Mouthed Woman, pale-lady ghosts, lantern ghosts... clearly the hundred ghosts of Mountain Hermit.
Seeing this scene, Sea King Drake immediately realized his opponent was also a "deity" like him. Holding his trident, his body tattooed with pale blue glimmering fish scales, he instantly pushed back the bloody world.
Inside the barrier, the seawater was half green and half red, resisting each other.
The collision between divine arts exaggerated the commotion to the extreme.
...
While Pandora and Sea King Drake were engaged in fierce battle amid the towering waves, an invisible object was carried by the wave toward the depths of the divine tomb.
Naturally, this was Su Lun wrapped in "Oz's Mummy Wrappings."
The one killed by the trident just now was only a substitute zombie.
In fact, earlier in the jungle, when Su Lun recognized the raindrops were attached with spiritual power, he knew their whereabouts were already exposed to the Sea King's perception.
Even from the very beginning, he had guessed that the Sea King might foresee something about "two enemies."
Merely hiding might not be enough to deceive.
To be on the safe side, Su Lun had made some preparations.
Being "killed" by one "Su Lun" allowed him to better conceal himself and be safer.
Just like right now.
Under normal circumstances, even with a shroud covering him, Su Lun would most likely be discovered.
But with Pandora's deliberate overlay of ostentatious Divine Power, all of the Sea King's attention was drawn, allowing him to hide.
"Fights between gods" of this magnitude, battles that don't end day or night, are hard to decide.
This isn't Pandora's advantage ground, although her Alchemic body ensures that she won't lose for a while.
But winning was almost impossible.
Actually, from the beginning, the key to winning the battle wasn't on Pandora but on Su Lun.
Pandora seemed to be fighting, but her real purpose was actually to get Su Lun into the core area of the cemetery.
Under her seemingly casual push, Su Lun gradually moved away from the core of the battlefield and drifted toward the location of the divine tomb.
...
This was a real "fight between gods"; Su Lun held his breath and concentrated, afraid to be affected in the slightest.
It was also his first time witnessing a battle at this level.
He didn't quite understand it, but he could see that the spells they were using seemed to bypass some of the laws of heaven and earth, something beyond the scope of alchemy...
Luckily, Pandora was powerful enough, and Su Lun faced no mishaps.
The surroundings had already turned into a vast ocean, but this was not a big problem for an alchemist.
The "Underwater Breathing Potion" is a high-level alchemical product, and Su Lun happened to be prepared.
This potion doesn't let one breathe underwater like a fish but uses special ingredients to supplement the necessary oxygen for respiration, allowing for an "internal circulation" of breathing.
Like seaweed, Su Lun drifted along.
Then, he finally saw the true face of the "divine tomb".
It was a crystal palace of extreme beauty!
The entrance was in a forest, inside a pit. It was supposed to be submerged in seawater, and the water here was incredibly clear, emitting a pale blue sheen.
Before this, Su Lun thought he had seen a lot of the world.
But now, looking at the luxurious crystal palace before him, he wanted to say: No, I am just a country bumpkin!
Poverty limits one's imagination.
Su Lun found it hard to describe the shock he felt inside upon seeing this crystal palace.
This was beyond what mere mortals could even imagine.
Random crystal stone columns in the palace were a hundred meters tall and thick enough for several people to embrace.
The quality of these, if identified, would be [Flawless White Crystal]. In the alchemy market, a palm-sized piece of this purity of crystal is worth thousands of Lisos.
And these were just the most common "stone materials" used in the palace; inside, there were also very scarce pure color [Blue Crystal], [Purple Crystal], [Red Crystal] used in alchemy...
"Wow, are all the gods this rich?"
Su Lun's eyes sparkled.
