The materials in the laboratory were also collected along the way.
Despite being an ancient laboratory from many millennia ago, its equipment was not inferior to the modern, such as the basic culture dishes and isolation glass, which were better than any glass available outside.
Dr. Banks walked along, marveling the whole way. He even collected some usable materials and instruments, planning to take them back for his own laboratory.
As they walked, they came across a sealed metal door.
This was the bottommost "Zone T11" of Lab Zero according to the intel.
A region once used for experiments involving highly dangerous projects.
Su Lun looked at the door, exchanged glances with Qian Tiao and several others, and reminded, "Everyone, be careful, I'm going to open the door."
"Alright!"
Everyone nodded, visibly on full alert.
Su Lun took out the brass spring, activated the door's authorization device, and with a "click," the long-sealed door slowly opened.
Just at the moment the crack appeared, Su Lun immediately sensed the fluctuation of spiritual bodies, quickly teleported to dodge, and shouted, "Careful!"
No sooner had his words fallen than two shadows burst out from the gap in the door.
Because the Dawn group had prepared in advance, the moment Su Lun sensed the monster, he used the "Chronos Spatial Gloves" to grab one of them. Qian immediately took the opportunity to strike, cleaving the monster into two halves with a single slash.
The other monster was a little more troublesome. It used Void Displacement to evade a round of firepower and ran rampant in the laboratory. After injuring two members of the Dawn group, Barrett found an opportunity to punch it into the wall, killing it instantly.
These were two fifth-order Golden Oddities, resembling humanoid lizards, with ghostly Void Displacement abilities and claws and fangs that could easily pierce through steel plates.
Given the previously unstable spatial conditions, these two creatures were enough to wipe out a whole army of Mafa's mechanical warriors.
It was also lucky that the main force of the Dawn group was able to exert their full strength, otherwise, it wouldn't have been easy to say.
Ignoring the corpses of the two monsters, Su Lun fixed his gaze on the open door, but his eyes narrowed slightly. Because in his senses, there was another soul fluctuation inside. It seemed like a monster, but it did not move.
He issued a warning, "Everyone, be careful, there's something else inside."
At this time, someone threw a piece of cold light source crystal stone into the room, and a black crow fluttered its wings and flew inside.
With the help of vision sharing, Su Lun finally saw the location of the soul body he sensed: two glass cultivation vessels. Complicated tubing connected to the equipment, and in the pale green liquid floated two pieces of biological tissue. Upon closer inspection, one jar contained a piece of "black flesh"; the other actually contained a large human "brain".
And the spiritual body fluctuation, was it actually coming from that "brain"?
Seeing no other danger and leaving some people outside, Su Lun and a few others cautiously entered.
The All-Seeing Eye identified the contents of the cultivation vessels right away.
The piece of flesh was called "Void Mother's Brain Tissue", a material taken from a divine-level creature, which was the prototype of the earlier dimension-reducing monster.
And the other brain was identified as "Herbert Hillbilly's Brain", still alive.
....
Seeing these two items, Su Lun immediately understood what this was all about.
The black piece of flesh was naturally the original material that Herbert had used to refine his gene potion.
And the brain… it was the "master will" of this space.
Normally, when that "Bi-directional Beast" was banished, the incident should have ended.
But by coming here, Su Lun and his companions were actually seeing the "obsession" that formed this cursed space.
Su Lun could actually understand this feeling very well.
He had always suppressed other emotions in his heart, imprisoning those beast-like evil thoughts deep within.
However, Herbert's situation was the opposite.
His human rationality was suppressed by the monster's intellect, not disappeared, but "imprisoned" deep within the heart.
It was like the "T11 Zone" door, located in the deepest part of Laboratory Zero, locking up that brain.
The monster was him, but he wasn't just a monster. This was actually two independent, contradictory, and entangled "conscious bodies".
Now that the monster was banished by the old dean, Herbert's own human will could resurface.
This was also the final step in breaking the curse of this space.
Su Lun also breathed a sigh of relief; this was probably not dangerous anymore.
Dr. Banks, upon seeing the brain in that cultivation vessel, immediately acted as if he had discovered something, exclaiming, "He's talking to me!"
The others listened, curious, A conversation?
Although Su Lun knew that the brain was alive, he still found it somewhat incredible.
Dr. Banks nodded, saying, "Yes. Mr. Herbert said, he left his research achievements here, wishing for future alchemists to take less detours and go further on this path…"
Hearing this, everyone's eyes revealed contemplation.
Dr. Banks walked over and placed his hand on the cultivation chamber storing the brain, showing a complex expression.
In some ways, Dr. Banks could also be considered a "mutant monster", but unlike others, his rationality was still intact.
He could more deeply understand the genius alchemist of the Dawn Era, two biologists separated by time and space sharing thoughts, seemingly finding some resonance.
The room was silent for a long time, as everyone silently watched.
Only the restless crow flew onto the cultivation vessel containing the "black piece of flesh", pecking at the outer cover with its beak, creating a "clang", "clang", "clang" sound. After a few knocks, it also didn't forget to turn its head and use its pitch-black eyes to look towards its master.
Su Lun, noticing this, slightly raised the corner of his eye. How could he not know what it intended?
The silly bird was hungry and wanted to eat the flesh.
Su Lun internally commented, "You really know how to pick."
This crow was picky; ordinary pieces of meat were not even considered, as it usually fed on the energy of the undead.
This seemed to be the first time that it had shown such a strong desire for food.
But the material in this glass jar was of divine level, not something to be fed carelessly.
Su Lun initially did not intend to bother with it, but the silly bird kept pecking more vigorously, the "clang", "clang", "clang" noise echoing clearly in the quiet laboratory.
Hearing this noise, Qian and Barrett also looked at Su Lun with puzzled eyes.
Su Lun spread his hands openly and said, "The bird's just being greedy."
The others chuckled knowingly.
As Su Lun often kept this bird by his side to comprehend the spell of death, the Dawn group members were familiar with it and often played with it, which brought a lot of joy to everyone. Most importantly, during many past adventures, the herald of death had helped them avoid numerous life-threatening dangers. Although it couldn't speak, it was undeniably an important member of the Dawn group.
Su Lun certainly wouldn't treat it poorly.
But... that "Void Mother's Brain Tissue" was a critical material for Void Potions.
Just then, Dr. Banks spoke up, "It's okay. Producing gene potions no longer requires such high-level materials."
Su Lun listened, slightly surprised, "Doctor, have you finished talking with that person?"
"Yes. Spiritual communication is much more efficient than verbal."
Dr. Banks nodded, seemingly having gained a lot, his eyes sparkling with insight.
After pondering for a moment, he added, "Mr. Herbert and I have many overlapping areas in our research, and the comments he left have inspired me greatly."
Su Lun asked directly, "What about the research report you wanted?"
Dr. Banks looked complex and spoke with a grateful tone, "Mr. Herbert left it completely."
Hearing this, everyone's expectant faces showed a relieved expression.
This was what they had been hoping for; having it in their hands now made the trip worthwhile.
Just then, Su Lun suddenly felt a spatial fluctuation in the room. Looking again, near the glass container, there was a separate storage space opening.
"Mr. Herbert's storage space?"
Su Lun felt an inexplicable anticipation.
What kind of treasures might the storage space of a Great Alchemist contain?
He looked inside, and the first things he saw were various archives piled up like mountains.
But what caught his eye the most was that special colorful crystal... the size of a room!
[Fragmented Dimensional Crystal Source]
Explanation: A special crystal left behind after the collapse of dimensions, a spatial treasure containing the rudimentary principles of space; it can be used for dimensional expansion, various spatial techniques;
The description identified by this item is scarce.
But Su Lun was not puzzled; instead, he felt even more anticipated.
Being identified by the All-Seeing Eye as a "treasure" definitely meant it was no ordinary item!
Just like the [Sands of Time] he had obtained before, it wasn't that these materials were useless, but rather, because they were too high-end, Su Lun was not yet qualified to use them in his current range of applications!
He was incredibly shocked inside, "This size... it's exaggerated."
Before, he had bought various spatial attribute crystal cores on the market. However, due to their rarity, not only were they hard to come by, but even a piece the size of a fingernail was worth starting at a million Riso. How much would a piece as large as a house be worth?
And the energy it contained was also immensely different.
This enormous crystal in front of him was constantly radiating spatial energy like the sun, and from a distance of more than ten meters, Su Lun could clearly feel the terrifying spatial energy contained within it.
If a small piece of this was chipped off and used to perform spatial spells, it would completely eliminate the process of gathering elements. Wouldn't spells below the sixth order be instantaneous?
Su Lun immediately thought of some practical uses for the crystal, and his thoughts kept expanding.
...
The "primary will" had opened the storage space, clearly intending to give the items to Su Lun and the others.
The members of the Dawn Group did not hesitate, efficiently moving research materials and cursed materials out of there.
Dr. Banks looked at the stacks of materials, his face lit up like he had found a treasure, his body trembling slightly with excitement.
Su Lun also placed that colorful crystal into the mini-void realm.
While everyone was busy, the crow perched on the glass container called out "caw caw" again.
Su Lun glanced at it and casually said, "I'll get something for you to eat later."
Even though it was divine-grade material, he wasn't stingy about feeding it to the crow, but not while he was busy. After all, handling divine-grade materials was very troublesome; their curse-like characteristics were like nuclear radiation, which could contaminate the environment if handled carelessly.
Unexpectedly, it was because of Su Lun's permission that the crow excitedly cawed once more: The crow master is starting!
Su Lun understood its intention, sighed helplessly, and humorously remarked, "As you wish, Crow Master."
He was also curious: without his help, how would this silly bird manage to eat the meat inside the container?
The crow circled the container anxiously a few times, but because it couldn't eat the meat that was right before its eyes, it distressingly cawed again.
Su Lun looked sympathetically and just about wanted to help it when, perhaps due to the meat's enticing divine-quality, the crow slammed its head into the glass container.
Since the bird couldn't kill itself by doing so, Su Lun didn't stop it.
He was about to enjoy the spectacle when an astonishing scene unfolded before his eyes.
The crow flapped its wings to fly, and just as it seemed its head would hit the glass container, spatial fluctuations suddenly appeared on its feathers.
"Teleportation?"
Su Lun's jaw dropped, the spatial fluctuation was eerily familiar to him.
Wasn't this his "Teleportation" spell?
When did this silly bird learn this spell?
Looking again, the crow had dived into the culture fluid.
"..."
Su Lun hadn't forgotten, this bird was a young divine crow from the underworld, supposedly feeding on divine decayed flesh which allowed it to grow and learn death-related powers.
Clearly, this crow had learned "Teleportation" from him.
Su Lun watched, unable to hold back laughter. The bird hadn't shown this ability when saving its life, but had awakened it just to eat?
Then, an incredible scene played out once more.
He watched as the crow, which had wings just over a foot wide, opened its mouth and swallowed a lump of meat nearly one cubic meter in size!
Yes, just one bite!
This is another kind of spatial devouring ability...
Su Lun felt that this guy seemed to have evolved all his abilities into eating.
However, he also felt it was good, at least he was growing.
Then, the foolish creature got too full.
It barely exhausted the last bit of its energy to fly out of the jar, which saved it from drowning.
Unable to fly anymore, it lay next to the empty jar with a distended belly, looking extremely comical.
The walnut-sized head and the body a hundred times larger were disproportioned, making it look utterly ridiculous.
But the foolish bird was completely unaware, still wearing a satisfied, smug expression.
"..."
Su Lun once again fell speechless.
He did feel sorry for the materials, but since they were provisions, they were meant to be consumed sooner or later.
But these were divine-grade materials, cursed with strong properties that could easily kill a high-order magical beast. It ate such a large amount all at once, wouldn't there be a problem?
Obviously, there was a problem.
The damned bird's body began to emit strong spatial fluctuations, and its expression gradually became as tormented as constipation.
But it wasn't as though it was contaminated,
rather, it seemed like... it had indigestion?
The black crow didn't show any bad emotions, it looked as if it were constipated, struggling to defecate.
Su Lun didn't bother with it, as it wasn't going to die anyway.
....
While everyone was tallying their spoils, Qiān suddenly found a beautiful box among the materials, and upon opening it, it was actually three potions.
She called over Su Lun and Dr. Banks, "Su Lun, Dr. Banks, come see what potion this is?"
Su Lun walked over to take a look, and softly exclaimed, "It's actually the finished 'Void Gene Potion'."
'Void Gene Potion Raw Liquid'
Detailed description: A genetic potion made from the spinal fluid of divine-grade void mother insects; integration requires a body tolerance rating of S, spiritual power of S+, and a bloodline inferior to that of the void lineage humans. After injection, there is a high probability of severe mutation; 95% probability of success after injection by the host, 3% probability of mutation, 2% chance of unpredictable mutations; after potion integration, evolves into void bloodline, greatly enhancing spatial affinity;
These three potions were the first batch of genetic potion raw liquids originally researched by Mr. Herbert.
However, Su Lun was surprised that a gene potion that could cause top-tier professionals to mutate, had a 95% success rate for his own integration.
Dr. Banks, who was also examining one, seemed to have recognized it and said, "This is the 'Void Gene Raw Liquid' injected by Mr. Herbert. The energy contained in this potion is very rough, and normal humans almost certainly mutate upon integration, even those of the seventh or eighth rank."
Hearing this, Qiān asked, "Then isn't it useless?"
Dr. Banks replied, "Yes, it's currently unusable. But Mr. Herbert has already researched a solution to the mutation problem, which involves castrating and differentiating the void properties, and then injecting the potion in stages. This is another kind of gentler, safer method of using the potion. I already have an idea, just give me some time, and I can figure it out. And these few... require very special conditions to use."
Saying this, he suddenly turned to Su Lun and asked, "I think, Su Lun, you should try it."
Su Lun noncommittally shrugged his shoulders, curiously asking, "Doctor, how come you're so sure I can?"
"Because the 'X Serum' was developed under my leadership."
Dr. Banks smiled, "To suppress mutations at the genetic level, one must be biologically superior to the potion. And coincidentally, the 'Fallen Angel' gene sequence is far superior to that of these void creatures. Since you successfully integrated the 'X Potion,' this potion isn't too dangerous for you."
"Oh."
Su Lun, having some knowledge of biotechnology, understood about seventy to eighty percent of it.
But Qiān and Barrett and the others were completely lost,
Seeing everyone's confused expressions, Dr. Banks gave another easy-to-understand example: "Well... it's kind of like grafting a pear branch onto a strong apple tree."
With this explanation, even though Qiān and the others didn't understand the genetic technology, they grasped the general principle and showed expressions of sudden realization.
Su Lun, however, completely understood.
The Fallen Angel was very high on the biological scale, inherently of the True God bloodline.
That void mother worm, probably evolved from a tiny insect all the way to a divine-grade creature, was fundamentally still an insect.
Between them, there was absolute suppression at the genetic level.
Su Lun also hadn't expected that a past opportunity would also grant him
a 95% chance, more than enough to attempt it. Even if he mutated, there was an expert on biological mutation right here.
Su Lun had just obtained the 'Voidwalker's Portal' and was about to remark on the insufficient affinity for the void, wasn't this just perfect?
Indeed, to find the corresponding materials, coming to the specific place was the most direct way.
This journey into the void secret realm was immensely fruitful!
Speaking on this topic, Dr. Banks spoke with a solemn tone, "In fact, the 'Bloodline Potion' has always been one of the most important paths studied by ancient alchemists to strengthen themselves. It's just that so much heritage has been lost in the modern era, many things have to be researched from scratch. With these research data and materials, our Dawn Group can at least save a hundred years of detours in this field..."
With these words, whether it was Su Lun or the other members of the Dawn Group, all showed pleased expressions on their faces.
They all knew the significance of the 'Genetic Potion.'
It held great importance not just for their Dawn Group, but for the entire alchemical civilization!

chapters.title: Chapter 406 - 405: Advance to Level 5
chapters.content:
The members of the Dawn Group cleared out all the valuable items from Laboratory Zero.
Dr. Banks was eager to return to the minor void realm.
He wanted to research the newly acquired experimental data, hoping to quickly develop the "Void Gene Potion" that would then be tailored for each member of the Dawn Group according to their ranks, allowing everyone to integrate void armors and advanced materials.
The effects of this potion were incredibly exaggerated, as it directly altered a person's genetic sequence and permanently increased their affinity for the void.
In layman's terms, it meant making the impossible possible by force.
This potion allowed professionals to integrate higher-tier void materials beyond their own tolerance.
For instance, Qian Tiao, who originally at rank five could only barely integrate the dark-gold quality "Void Ghost Hand," but with the potion amplifying her void affinity, she could integrate legendary-quality materials. This boost to her combat power was tantamount to an increase by a good half a rank. Additionally, after her void affinity increased, she could more easily comprehend and master various spatial law sword techniques in her Sword Dao.
Su Lun had three vials of the "Void Gene Potion essence" as finished products, which he planned to integrate right there in the cursed space.
This also added an extra layer of security.
Originally, his plan was to follow those from the North Sea Fleet into the exploration, quietly secure some benefits, and then sneak back out with the crowd, likely going unnoticed.
But he hadn't expected that Princess Stika would also send a squadron of mechanical warriors.
And now, they were all annihilated.
This situation was different from the original plan.
To be precise, aside from some war slaves still alive in Su Lun's minor void realm, almost all the adventurers this time had perished.
So, the number of those who could survive and get out were few.
The moment he appeared, he would definitely become a prime target for attention.
With hundreds of thousands of pirates outside, Su Lun, now only at rank four, had no expectations of causing trouble in the North Sea Fleet's void stronghold.
Even if he could release the members of Dawn, battling in the secret realm would surely end in mutual destruction.
Thus, Su Lun planned to digest the potion, calculating enough time for him to integrate the "Voidwalker's Portal."
By then, moving directly to rank five, his chances of survival would skyrocket by dozens of times.
...
Dr. Banks still needed many materials to create the potions, so Su Lun released all combat personnel of the Dawn Group.
Since the ultimate boss of the cursed space was defeated, and the planar gateway was completely closed, there was no more danger in this cursed space.
Qian Tiao and Barrett led the Dawn Group members, forming several tactical squads to go to the experimental area inside the planar gateway and scrape up materials. With their investigator status, the NPCs wouldn't interfere. After all, with the void invasion now truly happening, searching for materials was more justified than ever.
The academy zone outside had fattened an entire North Sea void fleet, what more in a "T-level area" previously from the planar gateway?
This place held too many treasures and secrets to unearth.
Everyone was very enthusiastic.
Su Lun stayed behind in Laboratory Zero.
It was safe enough here, and no one would disturb him.
The crow had eaten itself into a stupor, unable to fly and sprawled out in the corner with its belly swollen.
Su Lun paid no mind to the foolish bird, took a moment to regulate his breathing, and then took out a potion, administering a sharp shock to his own arm.
The blue potion slowly entered his muscles, quickly bringing a chilling sensation into his bloodstream. He soon felt a dreamy scent drilling into his body's organs and bones, the effect overwhelming his brain, making him hallucinate that he had turned into a plump insect.
Su Lun knew this was the residual substance from the Matriarch Worm in the potion, signaling the onset of mutation.
Normally, if a professional remained immersed in such altered hallucinations without emerging, his body would mutate.
However, Su Lun had a Fallen Angel gene modification inside him, which caused the insect-like hallucination to vanish as quickly as it had appeared.
As the potency of the medicine gradually fused into his bloodstream, a new sequence was added to his genetic chain on a microscopic level.
As time passed, the chilly sensation became clearer and clearer, and Su Lun felt as if he were merging with the void itself.
Having previously merged with void materials at the second tier, he was quite familiar with this feeling. This indicated an enhancement of his void affinity.
.....
Time passed quietly.
In that moment, Su Lun abruptly opened his eyes, and it seemed as if the entire dazzling starry sky was hidden within his pupils.
"It worked!"
A slight joy rose in Su Lun's heart.
It was also within expectations.
With a 95% probability, and a stable mindset, failure was nearly impossible.
He checked his pocket watch, almost eight hours had passed since he injected the potion.
Su Lun then checked his data panel, the first wave of the drug's potency surged his void affinity from a value of 124 to 765, far surpassing his affinity for any other element.
Moreover, this "Void Gene Potion Essence" would continue to increase his void affinity over the coming months, potentially raising it well above a value of 1000.
"Truly potent... there's probably no other potion in this era with such an effect. The Dawn Era truly was the pinnacle of alchemy!"
Su Lun inwardly exclaimed.
He had previously studied affinity values in detail and estimated that pure elemental talents like "A-001-Pyromancer" had an innate fire affinity around 1500. He now nearly crafted himself half a spatial element talent.
This was the formidable aspect of alchemy, able to compensate for human weaknesses with external objects.
Those ancient alchemists had also relied on these miraculous secret techniques to create a gloriously brilliant civilization.
However, Su Lun also distinctly felt that after injecting this potion, his body had reached its limit, seemingly unable to endure any more foreign gene amplifications.
This completely matched with one of Dr. Banks' theories under research. He had once said that the essence of human mutation was the fragile body's inability to withstand foreign genes. But the stronger the body, the more it could endure.
A thought immediately crossed Su Lun's mind: "After the body becomes stronger, perhaps it can merge with other gene potions? No wonder Mr. Jing always says that in the domain of top-tier professionals, the physical body is essential..."
He didn't dwell on it much longer and once again took out the "Voidwalker's Portal" to appraise it.
This time, because both his void endurance and affinity had significantly increased, the displayed fusion success rate had now become 83%.
Su Lun laughed and continued to assimilate the energy, which should increase his affinity significantly, making the possibility of advancing to the fifth tier even higher.
He once again immersed himself in meditation.
He had originally estimated it would take several hours, but unexpectedly, just after he closed his eyes, Su Lun suddenly felt a familiar spatial fluctuation.
He was now very sensitive to spatial energy and could clearly discern that strange feeling, as if space itself was collapsing.
"Spatial Dimension Reduction?"
Su Lun instantly recognized the ability and abruptly opened his eyes.
He thought it was the "Bisect Worm" monster that hadn't been completely killed, but upon closer inspection, the source of the spatial collapse was actually the bird that predicts death.
"What's wrong with you?"
Su Lun looked at the bird in front of him, his eyes trembling.
Its belly had indeed shrunk quite a bit, but the previously glossy feathers had now turned into flat black lines.
It looked as if... drawn with an ink brush.
Very strange!
Having seen the Bisect Worm undergo dimension reduction before, Su Lun knew exactly what was happening.
Had the foolish bird been gluttonous and mutated?
Hearing its master's question, the bird turned its dim little eyes toward him and cawed, "Gaga" saying: uncomfortable.
Su Lun twitched his eyelids, "Did you mutate?"
But no sooner had he asked the question than the crow's little eyes shifted, revealing a look that seemed to mock its silly master, and lazily cawed: How could the great lord crow mutate?
Su Lun then confirmed it.
The foolish bird hadn't mutated but had indeed become cunning.
Previously, it couldn't show such cheeky emotional fluctuations in its eyes.
Perhaps this sly creature was getting back at him for always calling it a 'foolish bird', and now it was even mocking its master?
Su Lun didn't mind at all.
Even if it had mutated, this silly bird wouldn't die, and that didn't need anyone's worry.
Su Lun looked at its wings, which were becoming two-dimensional, and realized this was a manifestation of the bird's ability.
The innate ability of the bird that predicts death is to grow by consuming decay, acquiring some of the deceased's abilities.
Moreover, legend has it that it's a spectral bird wandering in the god's graveyard.
The flesh it ate was the flesh of gods.
Eating the flesh of a near-god-tier Matriarch Worm wouldn't cause it to mutate.
The crow seemed not to have any intention of mutating; it was purely overeating. Su Lun affirmed this and left it alone, instead looking forward to whether the bird could master that dimension-reducing ability.
If it could, that would truly be formidable.
Soon, the potion was almost fully assimilated, and Su Lun took out the rune stone door, beginning his attempt to advance to the fifth tier.
....
One day later.
The Dawn Group members all returned to Laboratory Zero together.
Seeing the uncontrollable excitement on everyone's faces, Su Lun knew they must have gained a great deal this time.
"Hahaha... Teacher, you have no idea, we've gathered so many treasures. My God, this has been the most unforgettable exploration experience of my life!"
"Yes, yes! Mr. Su Lun, look, I found a gold-grade Void material! Wow, once Dr. Banks researches the potion, I can directly merge it. Oh, I'll be invincible among my equals as soon as I can merge with a gold material!"
"Pfft—Tanni, you can't even beat me, and you talk about invincibility at your tier, aren't you embarrassed?"
"Lolota, I can't beat you now, but I definitely will later!"
"..."
The group of youngsters crowded around Su Lun as soon as they entered, chattering excitedly about their adventure experiences.
Void materials are the premium choice for any practitioner. Now, every member of the Dawn Group either had one or several, and combined with the "Genetic Potion", merging would definitely crush their peers. Indeed, this was an exciting matter.
At least, Su Lun had been just as thrilled when he had advanced to the second tier and acquired the "Magician's Top Hat".
Su Lun: "Alright, everyone go to the 'Little Void Realm' for now."
This was their seventieth hour in this cursed space, and they would soon prepare to leave.
The will of the space hadn't dissipated yet, but once they stepped out, the cursed space would collapse immediately.
The anomaly outside would be massive, and the Northern Sea Fleet would surely surround it with heavy troops.
Having more people would actually be disadvantageous for their retreat.
The crowd: "Yes."
Suren performed a Suren Sorcerer's Seal, and a doorway allowing passage in and out of the space appeared with a clap, and the Dawn Group members entered one after another.
Qian Tiao, seeing him instantly cast what was originally a difficult technique, felt quite surprised and teased, "Yo, you can cast this technique instantly now?"
In the underworld, she had watched Su Lun comprehend this "Void Whale Swallow" ability. Prior to yesterday, forming this technique required squeezing a series of seals for a long time, so its instantaneity naturally surprised people.
Su Lun smiled, "Yeah, I barely reached the fifth tier. My state isn't very stable yet."
After merging with the "Voidwalker's Portal", he would need another month or two to assimilate the materials for professional advancement, but it was barely enough for emergencies now.
Qian Tiao thought of something and asked, "Did you use that cursed 'stone door' from before?"
Su Lun nodded: "Hmm."
Hearing this, Qian Tiao gave Su Lun a thorough once-over: "Wow, your recent advancement seems to have awakened a very formidable ability, huh?"
Because they were very familiar with each other, she clearly sensed a magnificent change in Su Lun, giving him an ephemeral and elusive aura.
Su Lun noncommittally shrugged his shoulders, "I grasped the 'Voidwalker's' unique teleportation ability."
Qiān Tiáo cast a curious glance, "Oh?"
Su Lun didn't hide anything; he thought for a moment, took out an engraved dagger, and then, in front of Qiān Tiáo, he threw the dagger.
While Qiān Tiáo was still puzzled about what he was doing, her expression suddenly hardened.
Because at that moment, she watched as Su Lun, who was right in front of her, suddenly disappeared, and a figure appeared next to the dagger flying out several meters away.
It was not "Teleportation," nor were there any sorcerer's seals for spatial displacement. She even hadn't perceived any spatial fluctuations.
Qiān Tiáo understood some principles of this technique and exclaimed in surprise, "You used spatial runes for marking, and then performed fixed-point teleportation?"
Su Lun smiled and said, "Yes."
Qiān Tiáo suddenly thought of a shocking possibility and exclaimed again, "Does that mean you can mark anywhere and then teleport to that point?"
A glint crossed Su Lun's eyes as he nodded, "Theoretically, yes. As long as the energy is sufficient, I can mark any distance for teleportation. Even in the future, if I become strong enough, I could perform spatial displacements between planes."
Qiān Tiáo pondered for a moment before remarking, "This ability is really heaven-defying!"
As she spoke, she looked at Su Lun with a teasing gleam in her eye, "It really suits you, kid. Whether you can beat others or not, with this ability, even professionals a rank or two higher than you wouldn't be able to kill you..."
"Indeed."
Su Lun grinned broadly.
This was the powerful capability of the material used for advancing the "Voidwalker's Portal."
After advancement, it would exponentially increase Su Lun's ability to survive by dozens of times.
Moreover, it had a very convenient feature, which was fixed-coordinate teleportation.
For example, if Su Lun established a fixed spatial coordinate in the Emerald Holy Land of the Dalu tribe, he could teleport there anytime to see Yuta; or if he set a spatial coordinate in the Mountain Hermit's Edo, whenever he thought of it, he could go and chat with the Princess...
However, this scenario was just hypothetical, as ultra-long-distance teleportation also consumed a terrifying amount of energy.
With his current strength, Su Lun couldn't manage it. He could use the "shattered dimensional crystal nucleus" he had previously obtained, but using such a precious material just for traveling would be purely wasteful.
...
All of them entered the small void realm, and after chatting for a few moments, Qiān Tiáo also prepared to go inside.
Su Lun didn't plan to wait for seventy-two hours exactly to go out; leaving one or two hours early would catch that group of pirates by surprise.
Just then, he formed a Necromancer's Mark and summoned a black crow.
However, the instant the black bird appeared, Qiān Tiáo's expression sharply tensed, and an instinctual sense of crisis made her rest her hand on her sword hilt.
Because she saw a very strange bird—it appeared as if cut out from a sketch, a completely two-dimensional creature!
She naturally thought of the dimensional-reducing monster Su Lun had mentioned right away.
Su Lun looked at her cautious demeanor and smiled. Before he could explain, the black bird parroted in a flattering voice, "Qiān Tiáo sister, one of us! Qiān Tiáo sister, one of us!"
Qiān Tiáo raised an eyebrow at this, "This bird of yours?"
Su Lun facepalmed, "This is that silly bird. It's learned the 'dimensional reduction' ability. Oh... and it's learned to talk as well."
He had found out just a few hours ago.
After digesting that piece of meat, the bird seemed to have grown overnight; not only could it talk like a parrot, but its intelligence had also increased significantly.
Most importantly, it had now become a "Two-Dimensional Raven," possessing the ability to reduce dimensions.
Clearly understanding this, the black raven immediately cheekily corrected Su Lun's words, "It's Raven Lord! It's Raven Lord!"
Qiān Tiáo: "..."
Su Lun: "..."
Qiān Tiáo, astonished, asked the black raven in a peculiar tone, "Raven Lord, you can talk now?"
The black raven flapped its wings excitedly, responding, "Caw caw caw~"
It could talk, but not fully.
Seeing Qiān Tiáo's intrigued expression, Su Lun warned, "Don't touch it. It's not proficient with that 'dimensional reduction' ability yet, be careful not to get dimensionally reduced."
"Hahaha..."
Qiān Tiáo's laughter grew even more radiant.
Becoming well-acquainted with the bird through Su Lun, she knew it used to be really silly.
Now that it could talk and even act cheekily, it seemed like there was suddenly much more fun to be had.
As there was still a chance to tease it later, Qiān Tiáo didn't linger further on this subject, and waved at the black raven, "Raven Lord, see you in a bit~"
The black raven flapped its wings happily, "Caw caw~"
Watching Qiān Tiáo enter the small void realm, Su Lun also closed the black hole in his hand.
He glanced at the black raven and said, "Silly bird, let's go."
Watching Su Lun walking towards the door, the black raven followed, flapping its wings and continued to mutter, "It's Raven Lord! Raven Lord!"
Su Lun: "Got it, Raven Lord!"
....
With the brass clockwork sphere in his hand, Su Lun controlled all the restrictions of the academy; he didn't need to use the old methods to exit but could leave anytime he wished.
He passed through the library to the outside of the academy, then took out the brass sphere.
A flash of restriction light, and the scene of the "Tokster Alchemy Academy" began to gradually dissipate.
This was a sign of the curse space collapsing.
This commotion lasted for nearly half a minute. Watching the environment change around him, Su Lun reappeared within the ruins of the academy, already back in the real world.
It was still near that spatial fissure.
However, unlike when he had entered, the pupil-like twisted space in the sky had disappeared.
"Eh... look what's going on there. Isn't the cursed space still supposed to open in more than an hour?"
"The twisted space has collapsed, the cursed space has been breached! God, quickly inform the boss and Her Royal Highness Princess!"
"Major General Jina really broke through this T-level cursed space! Oh, this is unbelievable; who knows how many treasures will appear this time!"
"Haha, there definitely won't be just a few. Such a large-scale cursed space must contain top-tier treasures and at least yield many 'sealed items' quality treasures."
"Tsk tsk... I wonder how many of those who went in will survive."
"Eh... Doesn't look like many did? Only twelve... Wait, didn't Major General Tanni survive, only a few slaves came out alive?!"
"Something went wrong! Everyone, be alert!"
"..."
The pirates were no fools; the collapse of the cursed space definitely meant someone had broken it.
Moreover, as the main force, Major General Tanni and her group did not survive, only a few slaves did, which was quite thought-provoking.
Those who came out alive, must be within these slaves who broke the cursed space.
...
Su Lun hadn't fully grasped the surroundings when the raucous noise of the group of pirates reached his ears, it seemed like many pirates were heading their way.
In his soul perception, there were a dozen or more people who had been teleported out with him.
Clearly, those lucky ones must have avoided entering the spatial channel and stayed hidden for three days before being transported out together.
The moment the group was teleported out, numerous murderous intents locked onto them.
At the same time, the pirates yelled in terror.
"Watch out for the rocket launcher!"
"Get out of the way!"
"Damn it! Those two are infiltrated spies!"
"..."
Su Lun's attire, identical to that of the slaves, did not attract attention.
But not far from him, two zombies had launched a barrage from rocket launchers slung over their shoulders. The rockets, emitting long flames, exploded towards the crowd; the mechanical skeletons had six launchers in total, firing twelve projectiles at once. Five rockets blasted amidst the crowd, two hit buildings, and five shot towards the distant sky, leaving a long white trail of smoke, vanishing in the blink of an eye.
The two zombies had but a moment to trigger the launcher before several controlling spells immediately descended, subduing "both" on the spot.
Not far away, Princess Stika and the fleet commander of the Void Fleet, Samikina, had just hurried over amid a crowd.
They had rushed over intermixed with ecstasy and anticipation after hearing that someone had broken the cursed space, but did not expect to witness this chaotic scene of flying rockets.
And it was during the distraction caused by the rockets that the two zombies were controlled in that instant.
In the crowd, Su Lun crushed a small piece of spatial crystal in his hand and formed a sorcerer's seal with his fingers, "Teleport!"
Fleet Commander Samikina sharply sensed the spatial fluctuation and instantly spotted Su Lun's unusual action in the crowd, shouting, "Careful, that man is trying to escape!"
As he spoke, he had already teleported into the midst of a group of slaves, reaching his hand out to stop Su Lun engaging the spell!
Unfortunately, it was too late!
The [Planar Crystal Source] skipped all elemental condensation processes, allowing Su Lun to nearly instantaneously release the spell.
"Such a quick response, as expected of a seventh-tier professional..."
Smirking coldly, he watched the large hand almost within reach; a moment slower, and the [Spatial Confinement] spell would have detained him.
Samikina sensed something, his face suddenly changing. He turned to the southwest and roared, "Quick, chase after them!"
....
The scenery flashed around him, and Su Lun found himself in the sky.
Next to him, a rocket was flying, and upon close inspection, the rocket was engraved with spatial runes.
Su Lun's lips curved slightly, thinking, "Tsk tsk... done."
This was exactly as he had anticipated.
His "teleporting rocket", catching the group of pirates off guard.
Probably no one expected him to have such a capability.
In just that instant, the rocket had already flown past much of the decrepit academy. Even a seventh-tier professional could no longer pursue him.
To be on the safe side, Su Lun took out the rocket launcher again and fired two more rockets in different directions. After the rockets flew for a while, he teleported away again.
Although this way of retreating consumed a bit of regular spatial crystal, it was virtually without any risk.
Once he reached the sea area, the large numbers of pirates became irrelevant.
They couldn't find him before, and now they had even less chance.
....
Meanwhile, in the ruins of the academy.
Princess Stika had been watching Fleet Commander Samikina and a group of pirates chasing out of the city for quite some time, still seemingly clueless about what had happened.
The cursed space had been broken...
Someone had escaped right before her...
And that person took the treasures!
After a moment of stupor, her charming face was left with nothing but the cold frost of rage.
She had never imagined that someone would dare to escape right under her nose.
"Damn it! At any cost, I must find those guys!"
"Notify Oleg, block the North Sea!"
"Tell those at the temple, no matter what it costs, I want to know where those people are!"

chapters.title: Chapter 407 - 406: The Duel That Came Knocking
chapters.content:
Su Lun sprinted madly, and after several instances of directed displacement, the pursuers behind him were no longer visible.
After advancing to the fifth level, his physical attributes had increased significantly, as had his spatial abilities. Darting across the ocean surface with the eight-armed spider spear and continuously teleporting, his speed was so fast it was as if he were flying.
If Su Lun were to jest, there were many professionals stronger than himself, but now, there were not many who could outrun him.
Su Lun reached a deserted area of the sea and once again took out the brass wind-up sphere.
This was the key to controlling the entire secret realm. With it, he no longer had to wait for the once-in-a-while ocean currents and winds; he could leave at any time.
With a pinch of the sorcerer's seals in his hands, a black hole vortex that grew larger appeared before him, and the skull and black iron battering ram of a sea ship peeked out from the vortex, followed by the triangular foresails, mainmast, and the pitch-black hull.
Having successfully assimilated the "Voidwalker's Portal" and the "Void Gene Potion Concentrate," Su Lun's spatial abilities had leaped qualitatively, making it much smoother to summon and withdraw the colossal ship "Eternal Night Emperor" despite still needing the help of the Dawning team.
In a short time, the big ship "splash" hit the water, and cheers came from the crew of the Dawning team on deck.
Su Lun activated the sphere to unlock the permissions and restrictions, and suddenly, the starry galaxy above the sea reversed, a unique sea breeze blew the black sails taut, and the currents slowly sped up the ship.
"Wow~ we are setting sail!"
Everyone was happy, each leaning on the railings, watching the swiftly passing seascapes around them.
Soon, they would leave the Void Secret Realm, and the North Sea fleet pursuing them could not catch up anymore.
...
The speed of the Eternal Night was increasing.
On the deck, Su Lun took out the brass wind-up sphere. He looked at the tiny scale it bore, then gazed towards the distant direction of the academy, suddenly thinking of something.
The planar gateway in the academy ruins was still in place but sealed.
The void rifts he had observed were gaps that had naturally loosened in the seal, controllable by human effort.
Through these rifts, the North Sea fleet could still continuously capture some void creatures that strayed into the plane and could continue to cultivate a steady supply of professionals highly resistant to the void by utilizing the rich void energy leaking from the rifts.
Realizing this, Su Lun's brow lifted slightly in contemplation.
Then he gently turned the wind-up sphere, resetting the scale to zero.
"Click," "click," "click"...
The sphere produced a crisp and pleasant metallic sound.
It was as if an invisible restraint had been triggered, the air in the secret realm trembling along with it.
This small act caused the dozens of rifts over the academy ruins ten miles away to merge completely. The continuously leaking void energy also vanished without a trace.
The group of North Sea fleet pirates left behind stood agape.
From that moment on, no one could obtain new void materials from this secret realm. For the North Sea fleet, it was undoubtedly like killing a goose that laid golden eggs.
Since they were enemies, Su Lun had no qualms about completely closing the passage. There was an even more important reason: the current alchemy plane had no capability to defend against invasions from alien planes, and those rifts could also become breakthrough points for void creatures from other planes to discover the alchemical plane. Keeping them might invite disasters of alien invasion at any point.
Better to close it.
....
Half a month later, in the Darenmite Sea Area.
This was a deserted sea on the seafarers' map, located northwest of Romanus.
Today the weather was clear, the azure sky dotted with light clouds, and a cool sea breeze caused fish-scale-like ripples on the sea surface.
An intense sea battle was occurring over this uninhabited sea.
"Boom!"
"Boom!"
"Boom!"
"..."
The cannon fire was deafening, with a considerable amount of wooden debris floating on the sea surface.
One side consisted of five three-masted sailing ships, flying the Wolf Fang Club skull flag of the North Sea fleet.
The other side was a gigantic black-sailed warship.
The firepower of the black-sailed warship was extremely fierce. Once the two sides entered range, a volley of over five hundred cannons unleashed a deluge of cannonballs that rained down, covering a vast swath of the sea, something a normal warship couldn't withstand. Even the firepower of the five vessels couldn't suppress the single black-sailed ship, which had an unusually sturdy body, limited damage from standard cannonballs, even if hit.
After only a few rounds of cannon exchanges, three of the five three-masted pirate ships were sunk. The other two, seeing the situation grim, immediately attempted to escape. However, they hadn't gone far before terrifying mechanical octopus tentacles suddenly surged from the sea, smashing the fleeing ships into fragments.
The black-sailed warship chased after them, brutally pummeling the pirates who fell into the water.
On the deck, Barrett waved his signature silver arm commanding the fight.
"Brothers, get ready to salvage the spoils!"
"Hahaha... are these the three squadrons of the North Sea's Seventh Fleet? Tsk tsk, an elite group, and they've been routed just like that."
"I just saw they had a few large-caliber main cannons; ours are not bad either. Keep a close watch, don't miss any."
"Quickly, don't dawdle, reinforcements from the North Sea fleet are coming soon."
"..."
The members of the Dawning team were very excited and skillfully began the task of clearing the remaining pirates and salvaging the spoils.
This was already the fifth wave of pursuers they had thoroughly defeated recently.
Since they emerged from the Void Secret Realm, the North Sea fleet had mobilized nearly all available pirate squadrons, adventurers, and bounty hunters in the nearby seas of Romanus to form an interception cordon, aiming to intercept the Dawning team.
But now, how easy was it to intercept the Dawn Brigade?
Su Lun had mechanical octopuses and thousands of Barrett's exceptional combat powers; dealing with a couple of pirate squadrons was a breeze for them.
After several encounters, not only were those guys unable to stop them, but they also ended up providing the Dawn Brigade with massive supplies.
Initially, the Eternal Night didn't have any modern cannons at all, but now, the ship was equipped with standard Mafar military naval artillery, all thanks to those interceptors. With all the cannons in place, sea battles became much less challenging. After a volley of cannon fire, there was often no need even to board the enemy ship since the enemy would likely sink.
This is why the sea king-class warship held dominion over the seas!
Intercepting the current Dawn Brigade head-on would be almost impossible unless King Oleg and a few other powerful deputy fleet captains personally arrived.
However, the reality was that the number of top-level experts is limited. The North Sea was so vast that even if several mature routes were blocked, dozens of fleets wouldn't be able to stop everything.
Moreover, if the Dawn Brigade encountered a large force, could they not just run away if they weren't able to fight off the attack?
The speed of the "Eternal Night Dawn" was among the fastest in the fleet ships, and with Tanni's ability to control ocean currents and waves, they could easily break away from pursuit and interception.
Moreover, the Dawn Brigade had the most detailed sea charts of the North Sea, avoiding those complicated sea areas likely to be ambushed, making it nearly impossible to be blocked.
So far, their journey had been risky but safe.
The only trouble the Dawn Brigade now faced was being wanted by the North Sea fleet, which meant they couldn't dock anywhere.
But under the current circumstances, with the enemy providing supplies, not docking for a short time was not problematic.
...
Su Lun roamed the sea for a while, harvested a bunch of Soul Shards, and then returned to the Eternal Night.
He had just killed two Pirate Squadron Captains and also gathered the latest intelligence.
He shouted to Barrett, "Captain Barrett, that group of pirates' main fleet is now gathering to the southwest, and by the latest, they will complete the gathering by tomorrow noon. The third and seventh fleets are the main force, and they include a few pirates with bounties over a billion. They probably plan to use the war fog to move in during the night and encircle us. Oh and also, I heard that Princess Frostmoon has summoned some top experts to join the hunt, including the 'Pirate Emperor' Carlo Melidis from the top ten bounty hunters. We need to be extra careful these days."
It was because of such intelligence that they could always anticipate the enemy's movements.
Barrett responded loudly, "Okay."
Barrett and the other military professionals were responsible for combat matters, so Su Lun didn't need to worry.
Enjoying the rare sunshine, he wasn't in a hurry to return to his cabin and instead leapt onto the mast and started meditating.
It was only during this meditation that the fierce black flames surrounding him receded.
This was a sign that the dark spiritual power inside him was leaking out uncontrollably.
Su Lun wasn't wasting it intentionally; he couldn't control the tsunami-like surge of dark spiritual power within him.
In the past half month, he had almost assimilated the fifth-tier Void materials, and he had successfully merged with the epic alchemical gear, Isaac's Alchemical Heart—a true domain of a fifth-tier profession.
But because this piece of gear was of such a high grade, he couldn't completely control it immediately after the initial fusion.
This turned him into an energy radiator, leaking energy everywhere.
And after the fusion, Su Lun truly realized the tremendous enhancement this alchemical gear offered practitioners!
This Isaac's Alchemical Heart provided him with almost endless dark spiritual power; now he hardly needed to worry about spiritual power consumption and recovery when casting spells.
Whether it was Spatial Displacement, puppet manipulation, or various spells... every move was sufficiently amplified.
The Fallen Angel was a divine-being-level creature, and its heart resembled a nuclear power plant—small in size yet containing boundless energy.
Su Lun, being a fifth-tier professional, could not possibly deplete it, no matter how lavishly he used it.
Even if it was consumed too quickly, Sir Isaac had made it into alchemical gear, giving it high functionality in storage, conversion, and self-recovery abilities, all top-notch in the world.
This gear afforded Su Lun's combat abilities a qualitative leap.
Just like the battle he had just fought, which was really effortless.
If it were before, because of his limited dark spiritual power, Su Lun had to calculate carefully when using his puppets in battle; but now, he could waste as much as he wanted, and in fact, he had so much dark spiritual power that he had to be careful not to get distracted by controlling too many puppets at once. When he attacked, it was an immediate overwhelming number advantage with the puppet legion, making the enemy powerless to fight back.
This was a scenario he couldn't have imagined before.
Su Lun had just advanced to the fifth tier, and he couldn't even accurately assess his own combat strength now.
One-on-one, it might not demonstrate a significant advantage.
But with Isaac's Alchemical Heart, his puppet army tactic really came into form.
In a large-scale group battle, his strength would truly be terrifying.
One man, equivalent to an army of thousands!
Su Lun adjusted his internal breath, and the agitated dark spiritual power also calmed down.
At that moment, he took out Isaac's Alchemical Manuscript III and started reading it.
His teacher Seraya had once said, "Only by fully understanding the structure of everything can one truly comprehend the 'equivalent exchange,' the ultimate principle of alchemy." This manuscript meticulously recorded Sir Isaac's hard work.
Isaac's Alchemical Heart was a variant of the energy core, and seeing the detailed records and data parameters noted by the demigod before, Su Lun could now understand some of the principles behind the "Four-Color Elemental Heart."
The once incomprehensible notes now seemed fascinating to him.
Some things can only be understood when one's knowledge reaches that level.
...
Su Lun was engrossed in his reading.
But just then, the communicator buzzed.
He answered and said, "Sister, are you coming to Roman?"
Mr. Jing's calm response came from the communicator, "Yes. The situation on your side is complicated. I just received news that Mafa and the Temple of Aghaparnon have used mysterious means to prophesy some future events. The plan to rescue Kai is a trap. King Oleg will personally make a move to kill you. I have fully recovered my strength, so I'll come and meet up with you. We 'Dawn' should also show ourselves to the world now."
"..."
Su Lun's expression suddenly brightened as he listened.
The main reason the Dawn Group still lingered in the North Sea was that they were looking for an opportunity to rescue Kai.
And to carry out the rescue, they needed to find a way to get the slave collar from Princess Frost Moon of Mafa.
This opportunity was not easy to come by.
Su Lun had actually guessed the first part of Mr. Jing's statement.
The King of the North Sea and those guys should have already confirmed their relationship with Kai,
given the recognition of Rakshasa Woman's talent and his own peculiar puppet had once been exposed when they stormed the Black Tower, making it not difficult for others to guess that they were all in it together.
So there would inevitably be an ambush.
This was also something Su Lun found troubling.
Fortunately, the exposure of the information wasn't entirely bad news; at least it provided more security for Kai's life.
Su Lun felt that with enough patience, they could always wait for the right time to act.
Unexpectedly, Mr. Jing actually decided to come in person!
But after hearing the latter half of the bold statement, Su Lun immediately felt steadier.
He did not know how strong his older fellow apprentice was.
But at least, he was definitely no less formidable than King Oleg of the North Sea.
...
The Dawn Group encountered the North Sea Fleet's blockade in the Darenmite Sea Area and sank five pirate ships.
This news quickly spread throughout the entire North Sea Fleet, infuriating the pirates, who rapidly assembled all nearby ships and people, closing in on the area of the incident.
Meanwhile, a pirate ship flying the flag of the "Blue Knight Pirates" also received the news.
This pirate group was a somewhat famous old-brand in the North Sea, with its captain being the fifth-order professional Sword Exterminator, Jacob Ferdinand.
But in reality, nobody knew he was a sixth-order fighter.
Now, summoned by the King of the North Sea, they came to hunt down the Dawn Group.
On deck, Jacob, the billion-bounty great pirate, stood there respectfully instead of his usual arrogance, reporting to a burly man lounging on a deckchair in the sun.
"Duke, I just received intelligence that the seventh fleet's third, fourth, and fifth squadrons of the North Sea were wiped out. They are supposed to have headed west," he said.
"Well, how many squadrons have been wiped out now? Tsk tsk, it's getting busier," the man replied.
"It is said they managed to acquire an Emperor-class battleship, so they have a significant advantage in naval combat."
"Lucky? Haha..."
"Sir, do you really have to go there yourself? The situation in the North Sea is very complex right now, and if you are discovered here, it could bring unnecessary trouble. We could just wait until those North Sea Fleet guys capture the Dawn Group, then I can find a way to sneak them out," he added.
"Capture? As if it's that easy to catch them. You guys are too isolated with your information. Do you know why they are causing such a big ruckus this time? Hehe, because they went and destroyed the Void Sanctuary, which really made Oleg and Mafa furious!"
"What… how is that possible! The 'Dawn Group' is just a small team of a few hundred people; it's said they don't even have a seventh-order professional among them. How could they have the capability? Not to mention that the Void Sanctuary is top secret, unknown to outsiders. Moreover, as far as I know, Oleg still has hundreds of thousands of troops stationed in the Sanctuary; it's impossible to penetrate it without an army of a million. They…"
"Hehe, I also find it hard to believe. However, according to the reactions from all sides, it seems to be true," the man chuckled.
"..."
At this point, the man lying on the beach chair flipped the newspaper off his face and stood up, revealing a resolute visage.
His flashy, big floral shirt was unbuttoned, exposing a robust chest and thick brown chest hair, making him resemble a strong brown bear.
Upon closer inspection, there were hints of purple glints within his grizzled hair.
The man seemed completely unconcerned about any pursuit, grinning brazenly like a debauched old gentleman: "Besides… if she wasn't extraordinary, she wouldn't have caught that girl's eye. Now that the commotion has grown so big, I have to come and see for myself if I don't feel assured."
Hearing this, Jacob fell silent, sinking into deep thought.
Then, the robust man said, "Turn the course northward, there's no need to go west anymore."
Jacob looked perplexed, "Ah… this? But sir, there is intelligence that they have already gone west."
The man in the floral shirt looked towards the distant sea, shaking his head with a smile, "I bet those guys won't even see a ghost shadow if they go west. Do you believe that? It's a very clever naval tactical maneuver, probably directed by that young Barrett. Bold yet meticulous, decisive in action, thorough in planning… just like when I taught him back in the academy! Besides, up to now you haven't realized they are not actually fleeing, but constantly looking for opportunities to disperse and devour the pursuing troops, right..."
"..."
Upon hearing this, Jacob looked startled and grew respectful.
...
The Eternal Night Emperor sailed on the ocean surface, and half a day later, the lookout on the mast issued a warning, "Captain, a battleship has been spotted at nine o'clock! The flag is that of the 'Blue Knight Pirates'!"
Upon hearing this, everyone on deck got mobilized.
Encountering a pirate crew naturally meant facing enemies of the Dawn Group, and fighting was likely.
Barrett's voice immediately came through the communicator, "Everyone, prepare for battle!"
Su Lun was also meditating on the mast, and he too opened his eyes and looked over.
But to his surprise, there was only one ship?
It seemed like a mere coincidence they had run into an unlucky pirate crew.
Under normal circumstances, a fight would not have broken out since the opposing side wasn't blind; seeing the Emperor-class battleship of the Dawn Group, they definitely wouldn't have come seeking death.
It was highly likely they would either turn around to escape at the first sight of discovery or maintain a distance from afar.
However, contrary to expectations,
to everyone's surprise, the "Blue Knight Pirate Crew" didn't flee but made a very outrageous decision instead!
They activated their alchemical sails and sped straight toward us!
"Captain Barrett, they're still closing in at full speed,"
"Prepare the cannons, and sink them as soon as they come into range!"
"Yes, Sir!"
This action put everyone in the Dawn Crew on high alert.
This made Su Lun wonder, did the opposing ship have a top-tier professional on board that gave them such confidence?
He even released black crows into the sky to observe the surrounding sea area; with this visibility, it was not suitable for an ambush.
He was certain the enemy had only that one ship.
Strange occurrences always portend troubles.
Out of caution, Barrett immediately changed tactics.
"Change course, and shake them off!"
"Yes, Sir!"
"But... Mr. Su Lun, the other side is signaling us with flags to wait,"
"???"
The Dawn Crew found this flag signaling ridiculous.
If they were the enemy, why would we wait for anything!
The situation looked weird, and the Eternal Night didn't slow down one bit, instead preparing to activate the alchemical sails to speed away.
Unexpectedly, the observer's next words caught everyone off guard.
"The man on that ship is signaling with flags that their captain wants to challenge you to a one-on-one duel!"
"Challenge me?"
"Yes, Mr. Su Lun! The flag specifically named you!"
"..."
Su Lun was utterly baffled upon hearing this.
What does that mean?
A duel?
Before he could figure out what was happening, the opposing ship suddenly slowed down and launched a fast-moving object from its deck.
On closer inspection, it looked like a piece of broken mast shot over here, with a flamboyantly dressed man standing on it!
What was going on?
This fellow had broken his own ship's mast just to make such a flashy entrance?
Everyone in the Dawn Crew was thoroughly confused.
One thing was certain, this had to be a powerful individual.
Barrett thought the man looked somewhat familiar, and fell into deep thought.
Su Lun furrowed his brow, thought for a moment, and then decided, "I'll go have a look. You all keep sailing."
Qian tiao glanced at him and cautioned, "Be careful of treachery."
Su Lun nodded, "Hmm."
Without further discussion, he leaped down.
A sixth-tier professional was not to be feared. If not overpowerable, he could at least ensure his own safety.
Even if that flamboyantly dressed man was a seventh-tier professional, Su Lun thought it would be hard to detain him should he decide to leave.
If it were eighth-tier...
Whether he went or not, the Dawn Crew was bound to face a huge crisis.
Besides, among all known in the North Sea, only King Oleg was an eighth-tier, and this guy was clearly not him.
His instinct told Su Lun that the other party seemed to bear no ill will.
But why come looking for him?
At that moment, the crow overhead cawed, seemingly revealing the truth: "He wants to beat you up! He wants to beat you up!"
Su Lun twitched at the corner of his eye upon hearing this.
Although this foolish bird's tone was annoyingly gleeful, it had to be said, its words directly confirmed Su Lun's own judgment as correct.
The black crow had not sensed any mortal danger, which was virtually non-existent.
Yet, Su Lun racked his brains and couldn't recall ever meeting or offending such a person.
Why would he want to duel me?

chapters.title: Chapter 408 - 407: Duke Lance
chapters.content:
Su Lun used the Eight-Armed Spider Spear to swiftly travel across the sea surface for a while before stopping.
He then watched as the man in the floral shirt, who had been flying in on a broken mast, stomped his foot and also landed on the sea surface.
The two were tens of meters apart, and when he got a clear look, Su Lun confirmed once again that he had never seen this fellow before.
Assessing his attire, although dressed casually, the gaudy shirt's workmanship and materials were certainly not cheap and were definitely not what ordinary people could afford to wear. It looked a bit like the trend from Luying's imperial city. The white hair on his head suggested the man wasn't young, but the robust and sinewy muscles on his body also presented a strong visual contrast. Full of vigor, the man radiated excellent spirit and aura, domineering, dignified, with a sense of unrestrained nonchalance.
It wasn't just the appearance; a fierce and resolute look occasionally crossed the man's eyes, displaying a presence that was definitely not something an ordinary person could feign.
Gauging from his demeanor, was he a veteran of many battles?
In his Soul Perception, this guy... was very strong!
A hint of caution appeared in Su Lun's eyes, and he had some speculation about the newcomer's identity in his mind.
While he was sizing up the man in the floral shirt, the other party was appraising him as well.
However, this guy's gaze was far from friendly.
From head to toe, that look was as if he was viewing a thief who had stolen cabbages from his own garden.
This made Su Lun even more perplexed; how could this old man's demeanor exhibit such an exaggerated hint of petty jealousy?
But he hadn't started fighting upon meeting, which clearly indicated that he was here according to the rules of "dueling."
Feeling somewhat bewildered, Su Lun still asked a question, "Who might you be, sir?"
Upon saying this, he didn't expect the other party to forego any niceties and retorted instead, "Heh, the skin looks decent enough. But I wonder if it can take a beating."
Su Lun's eyes twitched slightly as he listened.
The intent of wanting to knuckle somebody is hard to hide.
Just as that foolish bird had prophesied, the man in the floral shirt was hell-bent on beating him up.
However, Su Lun felt even more baffled and asked cautiously again, "Sir, do we know each other?"
He wanted to make sure there's no misunderstanding about mistaken identity.
"Don't know you."
The floral-shirted man picked his nose, completely disregarding the meaning behind Su Lun's words, and directly said, "Kid, get ready to 'duel.' Don't worry, I won't kill you."
"..."
Su Lun had no idea where the inexplicable hostility came from, but he indeed did not sense any killing intent.
The custom of "dueling" had been prevalent in Luying for a long time, usually understood to mean that both parties shouldn't use external objects like equipment or cursed items.
They would simply compete with court swords, or rely on plain fists.
The fight would continue until one party conceded.
This kind of competition rarely resulted in death and could determine a clear winner, so it was a game favored by the nobility and gentlemen.
But normally, such duels took place between rivals in love.
Su Lun found it even more unreasonable.
But looking at the situation, the other party was not giving him any room to refuse.
The floral-shirted man, a proper gentleman, announced before initiating the duel, "Kid, I'm about to make a move!"
Not knowing how to respond, Su Lun's eyes twitched again, which could be taken as an acknowledgment.
But no sooner had the words fallen than suddenly a several meters high white wave exploded on the sea surface.
With a "snap" of Stepping on Air, the mast upon which the floral-shirted man had been standing was crushed to pieces by tremendous force, and the man himself had already charged over.
"Such incredible speed!"
Su Lun's expression tensed up upon seeing this.
The old man seemed erratic, yet his strength was truly formidable.
A distance of tens of meters was closed in a blink.
Even though the two had yet to make contact, Su Lun had already felt a mountainous pressure; the iron fist rushed forward, and an eerie force made his body involuntarily stiffen on the spot.
If it had been a regular Rank 5 professional, they probably would've taken a solid hit.
Unfortunately for the assailant, the moment Su Lun saw him move, he performed a "Teleportation," leaving only an afterimage in his place.
Of course, the punch fell through.
Yet before he could even take a breath of relief, he saw the man punch through the afterimage, causing an explosion like a cannonball hitting the water, creating a white splash.
The beast-like figure sharply turned on the sea surface, and before he knew it, the man was in his face again.
Su Lun recognized the maneuver of stopping abruptly mid-air and changing direction, and he exclaimed in his heart, "Extreme Air-Stepping Technique?"
He himself knew this technique, but compared to the man before him, he was far outclassed.
When the floral-shirted man executed it, it was almost indistinguishable from Teleportation, these consecutive two displacements left no chance for respite.
Su Lun Teleported again, evading the punch.
Another punch came, he evaded again...
And another, which he also dodged...
Su Lun's current ability of Void Displacement had improved significantly, and the casting gap of "Teleportation" was almost negligible. No matter how fast the opponent was, physical speed could hardly compete with Teleportation.
With this technique at his disposal, it was hard for him to be defeated.
This was the confidence that drove Su Lun to attend the meeting alone.
In just a breath or two, they had exchanged over a dozen rounds of blows.
The man in the floral shirt, frustrated by Su Lun's slippery tactics, suddenly stopped and shouted in a fit of rage, "Hey, kid! If this is a duel, then let's duel. If you keep pulling these stunts, don't blame me for using my rank to bully you!"
"..."
Su Lun listened, speechless.
By now he could clearly see the man's extraordinary close-combat abilities.
Me, a Puppeteer, engaging in close combat with a brute like you is one thing,
But you expect me not to use spatial skills and simply stand here to be hit?
"Hmph!"
The man in the floral shirt seemed to see through Su Lun's thoughts. He snorted coldly, and suddenly visible ripples converged on his body,
Like some strange energy field warping the air itself, those ripples quickly expanded over a large area, even causing the sea surface under his feet to form a crater over ten meters in diameter due to the pressure of his stance. The moment he released this move, a terrifying presence emanated from him.
In an instant, his aura shifted from that of a fierce brown bear to that of a dreadful ancient ferocious beast!
"A domain?"
Witnessing this scene, Su Lun's pupils shrank sharply, "A seventh-tier professional!"
Professionals of the sixth tier and above were too few, and the available samples too limited, making it difficult to judge their rank through the fluctuations of their souls.
He had suspected that the old man might be more than a sixth-tier. But without seeing him release his domain, Su Lun thought he might be just a sixth-tier.
Yet, the man was indeed a top-level professional!
Shit!
You're not fighting with honor!
You're not playing fair!
Su Lun complained inwardly. Upon seeing the domain deployed, he immediately knew he was outmatched.
He should have teleported away at a long distance immediately, but after a moment's thought, he felt that this fight had to be fought.
And without giving him a chance to think further, the man in the floral shirt suddenly charged at him.
This time, his speed was even faster – perhaps twice as fast as before.
His short-range Directed Displacement was even quicker than Su Lun's teleportation!
Before the man even arrived, the terrifying pressure swept over, the domineering presence of the domain and rank suppression emanating outward.
Su Lun felt his scalp tingle from the pressure. Before he could form the sorcerer's seals, his body was oppressed by the strange force field; it was as if a mountain of thousands of pounds was pressing on his chest, making even breathing stall, let alone raising his hand to pinch the sorcerer's seals.
A regular fifth-tier professional would likely have no chance to fight back under this domain.
But Su Lun was no ordinary fifth-tier, was he?
The moment he realized something was off, his eyes bloodshot and he murmured, "Flesh Alchemy·Five-Point Hormone Surge!"
A surge of hormones flooded into his muscles and organs, granting him immense strength in his limbs and enabling him to break free from the oppression.
As soon as he could raise his hands, Su Lun's fingers formed the sorcerer's seals, "Mystery: Rune Vajra!"
Then the flesh on his body shimmered with a layer of dark golden scale-like runes.
Having done all this, the punch was already bearing down on him.
Although he knew he was about to get hit, this time Su Lun refrained from teleporting to escape, choosing instead to take the punch head-on.
Because he had more or less guessed the identity of this person!
...
"Thump!"
The fist touched his cheek, causing the skin to ripple like the waves. Even though Su Lun tried to dodge by using his Stepping on Air, the punch landed solidly on his face.
Su Lun was sent flying backward instantly, smashing into the sea and causing a series of white waves before finally plummeting into the water.
Perhaps because Su Lun did not teleport away, the floral-shirted man, having landed a punch, suddenly felt much better.
The man did not pursue, retracted his domain, and seemed to prepare for a "fair duel."
He watched as Su Lun took his punch without showing any signs of trouble and recognized some tricks at play, licking his lips, "Yo~ this Flesh Alchemy Secret Technique is quite intriguing, and that 'Vajra' secret technique isn't bad either, plus the body refining methods from the lineage of rune sorcerers? Tsk tsk, you've got quite the repertoire for staying alive."
Twice Su Lun stepped on the water before finally stabilizing on the surface. He looked back at the man opposite with a complex gaze.
The old man in the floral shirt recognized his use of Stepping on Air and, as if discovering something amusing, squinted and mused, "The 'Extreme Air-Stepping Technique'? Tsk tsk, I was the one who refined that martial skill, which except for the War Academy's kids, no outsiders have learned. Your skills are mixed but it's a shame, the synergy between your martial skills and your physique is lacking."
"..."
Listening, Su Lun could not deny it in his heart.
The martial skills were all stripped from others, and while he had sufficient experience, they indeed did not integrate with his body as well as those he would've trained himself.
This disparity might not seem significant to the average observer, but to top-level professionals, it was a substantial difference.
The man in the floral shirt seemed determined to give Su Lun a beating without further talk and charged at him again.
Having guessed the man's identity, Su Lun stopped using teleportation and braced himself to meet the attack.
No matter the man's purpose in seeking him out, anything less than full commitment would be sure to result in a beating.
The two figures interwove in close combat, exchanging blows that were all about raw physical power.
This battle, the two fought fiercely.
Su Lun, a puppeteer, how could he possibly beat a professional with a power system that was already two major ranks higher?
He also got hit time and time again, fell into the water over and over, and the sea surface burst into waves of white foam.
He was in a sorry state.
...
Watching Su Lun being beaten up, the people of the Dawn Group on the deck of the Eternal Night were extremely nervous.
Lolota: "Why isn't Mr. Su Lun using teleportation anymore?"
Kama: "It seems like the other party is a seventh-ranker? I saw him use a domain just now."
Tanni: "Hmph, that old man is too despicable. A close-quarter combat professional actually dueling with a puppet master!"
Abel: "The teacher knew that close combat was not his strength, so why keep fighting..."
The group of youngsters was filled with righteous indignation, wishing they could help.
On the deck, Qiantiao and Barrett also watched with grave expressions.
Qiantiao's hand was always on her sword, ready to help at any moment.
But as she watched, she also became puzzled, "The kid can't beat him, he clearly has methods to hold his own, why does he keep getting hit? Is he really dueling?"
Barrett recognized the identity of the man in the floral shirt from his moves and suddenly his expression became strange as he said, "It seems like Su Lun has recognized the gentleman's identity, that's why he chose to fight head-on."
Qiantiao, hearing Barrett's strange tone, tilted her head and asked, "Do you know that person?"
Barrett let out a sigh, his voice complex, "Yes. That person... was my instructor at the Royal Academy."
As he spoke, he mumbled with a puzzled face, "But, why is he here? That shouldn't be. He has already inherited the Duke's title, why would he come to trouble Su Lun?"
Qiantiao also showed a puzzled look, "The Duke?"
Barrett nodded and said, "One of Luying's top nobility, 'Tulip Duke' Bartolo Lance. We probably don't need to worry. The instructor is a very upright person. But why is he here to trouble Su Lun?"
