Gradually, pirates truly became terrified of dying.
Su Lun's survival tactics had strengthened, and he could even take the initiative to attack.
He charged into the crowd, and the Reaper of Death madly absorbed all kinds of "gray mist" fragments from the bodies, greatly increasing his spiritual power and various unique skill knowledge.
The more he fought, the more ferocious he became.
With his own power, Su Lun had tens of thousands of pirates in the arena gasping for breath.
...
The city-state of Morolos had been completely ignited by this sudden battle.
Onlookers had long been stunned, and the battle reports had been transmitted out by various means of communication.
However, the number of people enjoying the show grew, but those truly participating in the battle became fewer.
If the North Sea Fleet had an absolute advantage to take down the Dawn Group, there might have been many forces wanting to please the North Sea King by adding a feather to their caps.
But the current situation was that not only did the Dawn Group have level-eight professionals, but the members were also ferocious, one more than the other.
It was akin to sending oneself to death.
No one was that foolish.
But the arena was already blood-drenched; aside from Oleg's die-hard loyalists and his direct subordinates, and those pirates who were pushed to a desperate end still charging, no other forces were helping.
Seeing the number of deaths increasing, even those within the North Sea Fleet began to harbor their own agendas.
After all, they were pirates chasing wealth; many didn't want to risk their lives.
The various military units received orders to assemble; originally, they were eager to reinforce the arena. However, upon hearing the intense battle reports midway, they instantly switched from speeding to reinforce to delaying by various excuses.
Deserters also increased.
At this moment, in the civilian district of the eastern city, a group of pirates were nestled in the complex buildings.
This was the Twelfth Regiment of the Third Fleet of the North Sea Fleet.
As the din of battle from the central square and the southern city arena grew more exaggerated, they were in no hurry to reinforce but instead hid in this building area.
"Boss, are we really not going? The fleet commander said, no matter where the battle breaks out in the city, we must arrive within twenty minutes to provide support. Otherwise... it's military punishment."
"Go now to die? Fight against the eighth-level professionals in the central plaza or go to the arena to die? Haven't you heard that the arena is already blood-saturated! Let me tell you, my cousin has just discretely sent warmings telling us by no means to go now; whoever goes will die... It's too damn terrifying. Our Fleet's second, eighth, ninth, and eleventh teams had already gone, and not a single one came out alive; several thousands have died there."
"Ah? Several thousands have died... My goodness, then never mind, I'm definitely not going."
"But, will we be punished for hiding here?"
"Hiding? Who the hell said we were hiding?! Haven't we been intercepted by the enemy and are pursuing them? Rest easy, our absence doesn't matter. Hurry up, set off a few bombs down a couple of streets to make some noise, then find a few scapegoats to set up the scene..."
"Yes, yes, Boss is wise!"
"..."
Finding an excuse might lead to punishment later, but at least they wouldn't die now; the pirates could still discern the risks.
This passive engagement was also enacted all over the city.
...
Su Lun and his group had only come to Morolos City-State to rescue Kai, not to fight to the death with the North Sea Fleet.
Almost nothing had deviated from the plan since the battle had started.
Such smooth progress, Mr. Jing's strength and Su Lun's thorough planning were part of it.
What was more important was that those from the North Sea Fleet were too arrogant.
They had greatly underestimated the "Dawn Group."
The distribution of their military forces, the number of high-level professionals, techniques, and secrets were almost completely known to outsiders.
They probably thought without sending hundreds of thousands of troops to launch a strong assault, no one could possibly rescue the prisoners.
That had led to the current situation.
Now, with corpses strewn all over the arena, those pirates had also become terrified of dying and did not foolishly charge in batches anymore. Instead, they amassed more and more troops outside the arena, seemingly planning when to make a total charge.
Of course, Su Lun wouldn't oblige their wishes.
Seeing the number of charging pirates decrease, he knew it was time to break out.
Having faced a few unexpected blows, the morale of those pirates had been utterly exhausted.
Su Lun wouldn't wait for them to regroup.
"Let's go!"
With a shout from Su Lun, Qiantiao, Barrett, and the others who were fiercely fighting immediately got the signal and thrust themselves forward.
Leading with the heavy mechanized puppet corps, they broke through with firepower coverage, all the people in the Dawn Group charging out towards one passage.
The pirates, already terrified by Su and his group, mostly did not try to block but avoid when they saw the group charging towards them.
Su Lun and his group smoothly charged out of the arena.
Behind them, a large group of relentless enemies followed, shouting and fighting.
Since there were no boats of the Dawn Group at the docks, the people of the North Sea Fleet couldn't discern their retreat route nor set up an interception.
They could only passively pursue.
After breaking out of the enclosing circle of the arena, the pressure suddenly became much less.
The low-level pirates couldn't keep up at all, and few were foolish enough to chase with real intent.
Su Lun and his group only had to deal with those sixth and seventh-level high professionals.
A group of people descended like tigers from the mountains, unstoppable.
Originally, if Roman's faith had not collapsed, Su Lun and his companions might still have faced endless Roman warriors coming to besiege them from the city-states of Moros.
But now, there were only North Sea Fleet personnel.
Moreover, since they had not managed to detain them in the arena before, starting their escape now made it even more impossible for those people to hold them back.
Su Lun looked up at the pale blue light shield covering the sky, from heading towards the docks for evacuation, he immediately headed to the eastern city.
As long as he could leave the range of the "Prism Barrier", he could immediately use long-range directed displacement to leave this place.
This way, the Dawn Brigade, followed by hundreds of thousands of people, moved vigorously from the southern city toward the eastern city...
...
The members of the Dawn Brigade evacuated from the arena, and the North Sea Fleet personnel also pursued them relentlessly.
As Princess of the Mafa royal household, "Frostmoon Princess" Scatty Harris, naturally could not afford to lose face by also giving chase.
But she also knew that she absolutely could not let the people of the Dawn Brigade escape.
She shouted fiercely, "Pursue! Damn it, they absolutely must not escape. All of you, go after them!"
"Yes, Your Royal Highness Princess!"
At her command, a host of guards also went, leaving only a few personal guards by Stika's side.
This pampered princess watched the departing crowd, her expression only showing frustrated anger at this moment.
But more than anger, despair and confusion were predominant in her heart.
Those guys had their "submarine research base", "neuromechanical technology", and many treasures from the Void Relics!
Especially the latter two, which were indispensable at any cost.
But now, she watched as treasures within easy reach slipped through her fingers.
Although still clinging to the last shred of hope, her reason was very clear, if even that kind of siege failed to hold them, how could they possibly catch up now?
The foundation of the alliance between their Mafa Empire and the North Sea Kingdom had almost completely collapsed.
Without those Void Relics, what right did these dirty pirates of the North Sea Fleet have to demand that she, a dignified imperial princess, come personally for a matrimonial alliance?
Originally thinking that coming to this remote backwater, with her skills and capabilities, and the support of the empire, it was not unlikely to build a powerful "North Sea Kingdom" that could directly threaten the rear of the Lurong, harvesting endless benefits, even creating a "Third Empire".
But now her dream hadn't even begun when the plan had been shattered.
"Damn it! Damn it! These useless pirates!"
Stika, remembering her all-in venture to the North Sea only to receive such an outcome, couldn't help but curse angrily.
The battle she had just watched, her own royal guards fought with all their might, almost decimated in the fight.
And those pirates?
Seeing heavy casualties, they actually crumbled!
Just losing ten or twenty thousand men, and they crumbled already?!
If it had been imperial soldiers, even under the same conditions, two hundred thousand troops would have been enough to completely annihilate these people!
Stika attributed everything to these ragtag pirates.
Her lovely face distorted with anger.
However, after anger, she became confused again.
Her gaze shifted distantly, her heart filled with all sorts of feelings.
"The prophecy," clearly, this was not the situation described...
That's right, the prophecy!
Suddenly, Stika thought of something, and snapped to alertness, "That bitch definitely hid some important information!"
She recalled why the Puppet Master had captured Onis Popov first?
Without a hostage exchange, there was no way the Dawn Brigade could have left so easily; they definitely would not have been so passive!
But throughout, the High Priest of the temple had never mentioned any prophecy related to Onis.
"Wrong! The contradiction isn't just because of that slave, Kai. When the Golden Spear from the temple was stolen, they already had a feud! The news of the [Four Elemental Hearts] from Devil's Island was clearly to entice the Puppet Master..."
In this moment, Stika understood something, her anger reaching its peak, "That bitch had foreseen a Puppet Master but never revealed even a bit to me!"
Remembering how the High Priest Helvi watched her own son being killed, Stika guessed that the person might have "foreseen" this scene much earlier!
Yet, for her own selfish interests, she hid it.
Doing all this, just to save her son!
Yet it caused the North Sea Fleet, and her Mafa, to suffer immeasurable losses.
"Damn those wretches! Damn those wretches..."
Stika's eyes trembled, her chest heaving violently with anger.
She wished she could immediately tear that despicable person to pieces.
But immediately afterwards, she seemed delirious, muttering to herself.
A Grand Priest Roman who had lost the support of faith was already valueless.
Now, even if she killed her, what would it change?
Stika still fell into mania, her pupils dilated, and her expression slightly dazed.
She was entirely unaware, the killing intent had already quietly descended.
One of her personal guards, as if noticing something, shouted angrily, "Your Highness, be careful!"
"Watch out, assassin!"
But it was already too late.
Stika looked over with vacant eyes when suddenly a parasitic tumor sprouted on her neck.
Then, this tumor visibly swelled at an alarming rate and in the blink of an eye, it transformed into a naked man.
"A person" had grown on Stika's shoulder!
He chuckled sinisterly, his throat emitting a chilling, demon-like laugh.
Because the parasitic tumor had drained most of the life energy from Stika, her originally plump body instantly withered.
The mechanical guards saw a "Parasitic Kind" growing from their princess and panicked momentarily.
The experienced captain of the guard swiftly sliced the man into two halves, blood splattered, and a Shikigami paper man fell to the ground.
Unfortunately, the strike that killed the "Parasitic Kind" had also landed on Princess Stika.
Even though the guards hastily employed various emergency measures, the sparkle in Princess Stika's eyes dimmed.
...
Meanwhile, atop a distant tower,
Yekaterina watched the Mafa princess laying in a pool of blood, her face devoid of any expression.
If she wanted to control the North Sea, she absolutely would not allow anyone from Mafa to interfere.
This Stika had to die.
Moreover, this battle had greatly weakened the North Sea fleet and the originally stable management would see major changes, allowing her to insert more of her own people.
The North Sea Kingdom was almost thoroughly under her control.
The timing had almost been off,
but now it was just right.
As Yekaterina pondered, she looked at the Dawn Group members who had already escaped far away, her eyes without a trace of fluctuation.
At that moment, a Shikigami paper man floated in from outside, landing inside the tower.
The paper man transformed into a bizarre man dressed in a black and white hunting outfit and wearing a tall hat.
If Su Lun were here, he would surely recognize this as an old acquaintance, the "Mountain Hermit" from Mountain Hermit Nation, Abe Yasukazu.
The Great Onmyoji respectfully clasped his hands and bowed, "Miss, the Shikigami Curse has been planted. She might live for another two days but her soul has been devoured by the 'Soul-Eating Ghost'; her death is certain."
Yekaterina blandly said, "Well done."
Upon hearing this, Abe Yasukazu did not dare overstep, "It is an honor to serve you, miss."
Yekaterina said no more and turned to walk down from the tower.
Suddenly, she thought of something and calmly added, "Oh, and next time, don't use such disgusting methods to kill someone in front of me."
"Yes."
Abe Yasukazu bowed his head and respectfully saw her off.
After a moment, once she had left, he tilted his head and muttered, "I actually think this 'Corpse Soul Parasitism' technique isn't bad. Thanks to the inspiration Su Lun gave me before."
He then glanced at the blood-rich atmosphere in the arena, "Tsk tsk, with so many bodies, I can thoroughly study my new technique..."
No sooner had he spoken than no one could be seen in the tower, just a Shikigami paper man fluttering down.
...
Su Lun didn't know why, but suddenly there were far fewer people chasing him.
Those mechanical warriors who had been chasing relentlessly, why had they suddenly turned back towards the arena?
Could it be that something had happened to Princess Stika?
Su Lun was unsure what had occurred.
However, this was good news for the Dawn Group, as their pressure was lessened.
From the very beginning, only those royal mechanical warriors fought so desperately, unyielding and fearless—they were the toughest of all.
It was even better now that they had stopped pursuing.
The plan had now moved into the retreat phase,
In the midst of battle,
Su Lun even took a moment to inquire with Mr. Jing.
The battle at the central square was also going very smoothly.
Though Mr. Jing was a newly advanced eighth rank, her foundation couldn't be compared to that of a Viking pirate.
A fierce battle ensued, and far from being at a disadvantage, she actually dominated her opponent, Oleg.
Having confirmed Mr. Jing's situation, Su Lun had no more concerns and led along with several others fiercely forward.
The [Prismatic Barrier] had left fragments of space everywhere throughout the city, impeding Su Lun's Spatial Displacement. But as long as no long-distance teleportation was attempted, it was almost always safe to dodge.
Su Lun and his group fiercely dashed out of the east town, and before long they had left the boundary of the barrier.
Although the heavily ranked six and seven pirates were still in hot pursuit, the Dawn Group was not unprepared.
Several ancient vampires, inheritors of a thousand-year-old legacy, surely had valuable items at hand.
They had prepared a sealed-level defensive artifact—[Vlad III's Coffin].
Once unveiled, it would deploy a half-minute invincible defense barrier.
This short duration of defense normally wouldn't mean much, but Su Lun methodically collected everyone into a small void realm, then calmly took the coffin, directly crushed the Spatial Crystal Core, and executed Directed Displacement.
In an instant, on the sunny ocean,
Eternal Night Emperor's deck

chapters.title: Chapter 416 - 415: I Want to Study the Alchemical Body
chapters.content:
Su Lun returned to the deck of the Eternal Night Emperor ship, and the Dawn Group members excitedly gathered around him.
The rescue mission to the Moros City-State required the Spiked Team to reduce the risk to a minimum, so those Dawn Group members who didn't participate felt quite regretful.
But they were able to catch glimpses of some of the battle scenes in the city through various high-powered telescopes.
Especially the White Day Falling Star, which was so exaggerated that it piqued everyone's curiosity.
Su Lun released the combatants from the small spatial realm.
Looking at the returning fighters, each with varying degrees of injuries, but all had returned, along with Mr. Kay.
This was surely a resounding victory for the rescue.
Any concerns in the hearts of the Dawn Group were swept away, and their faces were bursting with excitement.
"Mr. Kay has been rescued as well, wow~ the rescue plan was a success!"
"Teacher, teacher, please tell us what happened. I just saw a shooting star fall down... it was so exaggerated, can someone really summon a shooting star?"
"Haha, it must have been Mr. Su Lun who summoned it because he always brings miracles!"
"..."
Tanni, Lolo, and the other young teens babbled with questions.
The "Duke" Moore Wazhuaz and the other elder vampires, being of too high a status, naturally had no interest in boasting about their battle experiences with the younger generation.
Barrett also spoke very little, maintaining his composure as the commander in battle; the younger members were somewhat intimidated by him. And in the recent fight, as the vanguard tank who drew much aggro, he took the hardest hits from the enemy and was not lightly injured. Now, back on the ship, the Dawn Group's medics were treating his wounds.
The young teens could only gather around the more approachable Qiantiao, both concerned and curious, "Teacher, are you alright? Did you encounter any formidable enemies during the fight?"
Qiantiao, of course, was fine, with no serious injuries. She knocked on the heads of her disciples, seeing through their thoughts, "You guys want to ask about the meteor, right?"
As she spoke, she glanced meaningfully at Su Lun, "The meteor is naturally related to your Mr. Su Lun. In the fight just now, he was killing enemies left and right. If there were newspapers, you'd know how impressive he was tomorrow."
At this, the other participants also turned their gazes with slightly complex expressions.
Among those who participated in the rescue mission, only Su Lun was of the lowest rank. But everyone had to admit, his performance was indeed the most eye-catching.
No, it wouldn't be an exaggeration to say he turned the tide of the battle.
Hearing Qiantiao's words, Barrett, wrapping his bandages around his bare torso, also laughed and remarked, "Haha... Su Lun must have caused tens of thousands of casualties to the enemy, hah? Tsk tsk, I couldn't have done that even if I was exhausted. That puppet army, their combat power was really too strong."
"Indeed."
The "Duke" Wazhuaz also spoke up for a change, approval thick in his aged and hazy eyes.
He interjected, "The combat power of Su Lun is truly out of the ordinary. Looking back a few hundred years, puppeteers of this caliber were extremely rare. Without the puppet army, this battle would certainly not have gone so smoothly."
Tens of thousands of casualties?! My goodness.
What kind of exaggerated number was that!
The Dawn Group now only had a couple of thousand members.
So, did Su Lun single-handedly wipe out several dozens of pirate crews?
Hearing the words of the group leaders, the young teens' faces immediately lit up with an unrivaled exhilaration.
"Mr. Su Lun, was the meteor summoned by you?"
"You took down tens of thousands of enemies? Oh my god, teacher, you're too incredible!"
"..."
Hearing Lolo and the others' excited questions, Su Lun didn't know whether to laugh or cry.
Although the meteor wasn't summoned by him, it was indeed directly related to him.
But the reasons weren't easy to explain.
He couldn't exactly say that he had lived off a woman, and that a noble lady had given him a huge gift in return, could he?
As for the details of the battle, he truly didn't know where to begin.
Fortunately, before long, a familiar silhouette appeared on the distant sea surface through mirror-like light refraction, quickly leaping forward until she alighted on the deck.
Upon seeing her, who else could it be but Mr. Jing?
Fresh from a major battle, her aura was slightly disorganized, but she didn't appear to be injured.
The crowd exclaimed with joy, "The leader is back!"
Mr. Jing responded with a smile and a nod.
...
As a veteran member of the Dawn Group, Mr. Kay's successful rescue naturally called for a grand banquet to celebrate the victory.
As night fell, the night sky was dotted with stars.
The vast dining hall of the Eternal Night was illuminated by crystal chandeliers, casting a bright light over dozens of tables laden with an abundance of foods. Deep-sea behemoths hunted during the day had been turned into a variety of delicacies by the chefs, accompanied by mountains of fruit and hundreds of barrels of fine wine.
Everyone indulged in hearty eating and drinking amidst laughter and cheerful conversation, creating a very harmonious atmosphere.
As they listened to stories about Su Lun and others' bloody battles in the central arena, and how Mr. Jing and "Sea King" Olli had a fight that destroyed half a city...
The crowd became more and more excited.
A large team always becomes more cohesive through various battles, and their unity strengthens.
Mr. Jing was seated at the head of the table, with Su Lun by her side, and Pandora next to him.
This "ally," who rarely appeared in the group, had also played a key role in the rescue this time. It was only after Su Lun's cordial invitation that she agreed to come to the dinner, but she had been mostly silent throughout.
Next to Mr. Jing sat "Duke Blood" Moore Wazhuaz, an old vampire who was a living history. He shared with Su Lun and others the development of the Luying over the past few centuries, starting from Pona the Third to Bonaparte IX a few years ago. He even knew a great deal about secret stories and royal scandals unknown to others.
The crowd laughed heartily at times, and at other moments they were visibly excited.
Many emperors of Luying have come and gone, but Moore Wazhuaz remains the same.
Su Lun once again openly envied such counter-to-heaven longevity inherent to their bloodline; they truly have long lifespans.
However, the cultivation of the blood race is indeed much slower compared to humans, taking hundreds of years to advance to the seventh tier. Moreover, to live so long, not only does one's bloodline need to be of high quality, but the conditions for hibernation are also stringent.
There are gains as well as losses.
During the meal, the members of Dawn felt that their knowledge had greatly expanded.
In terms of being knowledgeable, there were hardly a few in Dawn who knew more than this old vampire.
Then there was dancing, drinking competitions, and all sorts of wild boasting and bantering.
As the conversation went on, Su Lun thought about some issues he faced in advancing to the sixth tier.
Suddenly, he turned to the old vampire and asked, "Mr. Wazhuaz, may I ask you a question?"
The old vampire duke, with a kindly smile on his face, replied, "There's no need for formalities, Su Lun. Just speak your mind."
Su Lun also smiled.
Because of his relationship with Mr. Jing, this vampire who had lived for eight hundred years was technically a generation younger than him.
But he couldn't take advantage of seniority; he held genuine respect in his heart for this powerful elder and asked politely, "That... I'm planning to enhance my physical strength as I advance to the sixth tier. So, I'm looking for professional materials that can amplify physical bodies, of as high a quality as possible. Preferably ones with unique effects that can provide a more lasting boost to physical strength. Do you have any suggestions?"
Su Lun roughly described his needs.
Ever since he had grasped the concept of domination, he was ready to step into the threshold of the sixth-tier professions, and it was time to start preparing for advancement.
But the higher the tier of professional material needed, the scarcer it becomes on the market, and the harder it is to find.
It was good to start preparing early.
Furthermore, most known high-tier materials were in the possession of a particular group of people.
That would be the nobles.
If one were to say where the most extraordinary items were located, it would undoubtedly be in the collections of the great noble families of Luying.
In a nobility-centric system, over ninety percent of society's wealth was concentrated in the upper class. The same was true for extraordinary items. Especially high-tier extraordinary items, 99% of which were in the hands of top-tier nobles. Those folks had collected countless treasures over the centuries, even those they couldn't use themselves, and they stored them in private treasuries unknown to the public.
Su Lun had asked Mr. Jing about this before, but since she had been in hibernation for a thousand years, she didn't understand the current situation.
Having Wazhuaz, a living history, by his side couldn't be better.
"Regarding advancement materials, you've indeed come to the right person. I do know quite a few..."
Upon hearing this, the old vampire smiled slightly.
After musing for a moment, he continued, "Our own castle's treasury does have plenty of cursed materials that enhance the flesh. For a tier six professional, the best quality we have is probably the Gold-grade 'Hannibal's Cannibal Cutlery.' But I think those materials might be a bit subpar for you; you need something better."
After the battle in the arena earlier that day, having seen Su Lun's exaggerated combat power, he knew that ordinary professional materials would never satisfy someone with such an exceptional foundation.
Su Lun said nothing, his face expressing attentive anticipation for more information.
Thinking of this, Wazhuaz shifted his thoughts to forbidden objects that ordinary people couldn't integrate.
His eyes shifted as he spoke directly: "I can think of several banned items that might suit you. The Luying royal treasury has a 'Tyrant's Secret Tome' artifact, which I saw at least three hundred years ago. It is well balanced for offense and defense and suitable for professionals related to fighters; the Wilson family has a 'Horror Angel Wax Figure,' which provides extremely high defense and flesh enhancement, and is also quite appropriate for dark spiritual power attributes; and then there is the 'Corpse of Corruption' held secretly by the military intelligence department... All of these are forbidden items that can enhance the professional's body. But since they're difficult to integrate, they should all still be there."
Su Lun's eyes lit up as he listened, indeed he had asked the right person.
These banned-level treasures, involving many secrets, wouldn't be known to just anyone.
But the old vampire listed them as if they were his personal treasures.
Wazhuaz listed seven or eight kinds in one breath, each seeming to have a certain degree of compatibility.
Su Lun thought it through and, considering his current ability and future professional planning, added another criterion: "Mr. Wazhuaz, among these cursed objects, which material has the greatest potential? I don't mind if the effects are weaker; preferably, it should be something that can continue to enhance physical strength in the long run."
Having gone through so many tough fights, Su Lun had increasingly understood that for a Puppeteer...
No matter how high the ceiling of a Puppeteer's combat power, the lower limit was definitely their physical strength.
Once a person dies, the most formidable puppet army becomes useless.
Moreover, his teacher, Sereia, had clearly stated that to reach the pinnacle of one's profession, one inevitably cannot avoid dealing with the physical body.
Therefore, choosing professional materials should not only consider the abilities gained at the time of fusion but also consider future potential.
It was like his "Void Whale's Spatial Stomach," an implant that started at a Grade B level among fourth stage materials, but had an SSS grade potential.
As long as it could advance, it would become stronger and stronger.
Previously, after Su Lun plundered in the spatial secret realm, his spatial ability surged dramatically.
Not only did the size of his small spatial realm expand by a multiple, but all sorts of spatial abilities associated with his implant also received a huge boost, and this increase showed no signs of reaching its limit in the future.
If given a choice, naturally, one would select the best from the suitable options!
Mr. Jing, standing by, let out a smile, seemingly in agreement that his choice was the right one.
"The one with the greatest potential?"
Moore Wazhuaz frowned in thought, then suddenly his expression brightened, "Now that you mention it, I also recall a very special cursed item."
Su Lun grew interested, "What is it?"
Moore Wazhuaz continued, "About two hundred years ago, an adventure group unearthed a cursed item called 'Lilia's Vampire Ring' in an ancient ruin in the South Sea. Because this treasure greatly matched the abilities of our bloodline, I had once sent people to inquire about its whereabouts. Unfortunately, it ended up in the hands of the Rodriguez family. After a few unsuccessful skirmishes, I eventually gave up."
After a pause, he added, "There was intelligence that the item could devour the spiritual blood of living beings to enhance the body, offering a permanent, continuous boost to professionals. Even for ordinary people, it could prolong life."
Su Lun listened to the description with interest, but also asked, "The Rodriguez family?"
Moore Wazhuaz nodded, "Yes. The strongest among the five Senior Councilors of the Luying Council, 'Kaka Rodriguez,' is from that family. That ring is surely in one of the 'Rodriguez's' hands. After all, those great nobles all desire to live longer and would never sell it."
"Oh..."
On hearing this, Su Lun showed a thoughtful expression.
The five Senior Councilors of the Luying nation are representatives of the most powerful and influential noble groups, with the background of Ekaterina's Lans family occupying one of those seats.
These noble families with hundreds of years of heritage have intricate and profound foundations, their power beyond imagination!
Despite Oleg's high profile claims of commanding hundreds of thousands of soldiers across the North Sea, he's just a pirate engaging in hit-and-run tactics. If he truly clashed with these top-tier nobles, even ten Kings of the North Sea might kneel in defeat.
Quite the dilemma...
Su Lun frowned slightly upon learning the whereabouts of "Lilia's Vampire Ring."
However, his mentality was rather positive.
Luying was the city of alchemy, where almost all top-tier treasures converged. There were many materials to choose from for advancement.
Now with a rough target in mind, whether it's suitable or not could only be determined after seeing the item.
He was due to attend Ekaterina's wedding in three months, which was a perfect opportunity to visit the city of Luying and decide then.
...
A dinner continued in a harmonious atmosphere until midnight, yet it still had not come to an end.
Mr. Jing preferred quiet, ate sparingyl, and retired early from the scene.
Though Mr. Jing wasn't particularly fussy, as a top-tier fighter, her departure strangely relaxed the atmosphere of the dinner. Her progeny felt less restrained, and the rough men aboard the ship were even more inclined to indulge in eating and drinking without regard for their image.
Su Lun usually secluded himself in his laboratory and had planned to use this opportunity to get more familiar with the crew.
But shortly after Mr. Jing left her seat, Pandora, who had been quiet all this time, suddenly spoke up, "If it's convenient, I have something to tell you."
Su Lun glanced at her, sensed the seriousness in her tone, and guessed what it was about. He nodded, "Sure, shall we take a walk on the deck?"
Pandora nodded, "Yes."
Su Lun excused himself to his comrades and left with Pandora towards the deck.
The moon was beautiful that night, its light cascading over the hull of the Eternal Night, giving it an ethereal beauty.
As Su Lun walked, he gently ran his hand along the ship's rail, gazing at the reflection of the moon on the sea.
Neither of them spoke as they walked.
Finally, at the stern of the ship, Pandora spoke calmly, "I am leaving."
Su Lun's expression shifted slightly upon hearing this, but he wasn't much surprised.
Everything written in the contract had been fulfilled; she was here to inform him, her ally, of her departure.
Although Pandora was not from the Dawn Group, she had indeed helped Su Lun a great deal during this period.
Whether it was capturing the submarine earlier or the rescue at the arena, this former enemy had done more than enough.
Su Lun looked at her and said, "You're leaving? I think everyone in the Dawn Group likes you. Plus, there are many cabins on the ship, and everyone would welcome you to stay. I also think we will have more opportunities to collaborate in the future."
He certainly did not want to miss such a formidable ally.
Besides, it would seem too impersonal if he didn't try to retain an ally who was leaving.
Pandora listened without showing any emotion but did not deny what he said.
After pondering for a moment, she merely said, "The Power of Faith has collapsed on Roman's side, but the faith system is still there; it's the best opportunity to seize the Power of Faith. For me, that's the very important opportunity I need."
Normally she wouldn't have explained so much, but Pandora chose to share this anyway.
"Oh?"
Su Lun listened to these words and finally understood why she wanted to leave before even finishing her meal. So that was it.
He understood in an instant.
Although it was a transaction, having fought side by side still established some rapport.
Of course, this rapport was very likely because of his teacher, Celia.
But these words also turned their awkward conversation into one that could continue.
Su Lun knew that Pandora must leave and didn't dwell on that topic. Instead, he said, "Miss Pandora, thank you for your help before. You've been a great help to me and the Dawn Brigade."
Pandora responded indifferently, "No need. It was just a condition of our cooperation."
Su Lun didn't correct her and continued, "Once things with Roman are settled, where do you plan to go? You've seen that everyone in the Dawn Brigade is very friendly, and it's a team without many constraints. What I mean is, if you're willing, you could come aboard and we could adventure together."
Pandora heard this clearly as a recruitment proposal and did not immediately reject it.
It seemed she pondered for a moment before saying, "When that time comes, I may return to the Mountain Hermit Kingdom. The divine system of cultivation is very special and requires a more stable source of faith."
"..."
Su Lun frowned; it was indeed a problem.
Magicians specializing in Alchemy clustered together, and everyone had the same path for improvement. Only she was a "divine being."
Su Lun couldn't think of a better argument to persuade her to stay, and suddenly the two of them fell into an awkward silence.
On the deck, the night breeze was gentle and carried a slight chill.
Pandora seemed to have no intention of staying any longer. She spoke again, "Is there anything else you need me to do? If not, I plan to leave now."
Su Lun felt it was a pity to hear this.
This farewell would last for a long time, possibly forever, and it was uncertain whether there would truly be another chance to meet.
Just as he was thinking of what to say as a farewell, a thought suddenly popped into his head.
He did indeed have something for which he needed Pandora's help.
But...it was a bit difficult to broach.
Yet he felt that if he didn't speak now, he would completely lose the opportunity.
For the first time, Su Lun found himself trapped in a conflicted and awkward demeanor.
Pandora, with her sharp perception, caught the change in Su Lun's expression and directly asked, "If you have something to say, just say it."
Su Lun looked at her, that calm expression, which seemed as if it wouldn't reject...right?
He gauged that at worst he would be met with a cold response, and after some thought, he still spoke up.
"That...Miss Pandora, I have an audacious request. I wonder if you could..."
Pandora gave him a curious look, and it seemed even she found it surprising to see the usually decisive Su Lun acting awkward. She followed up with a question, "What is it?"
Su Lun steeled himself and said, "I would like to research the body of alchemy."
"..."
Pandora's expression remained unchanged upon hearing this, but a fleeting, subtle change passed through her eyes.
....
Su Lun, watching her expressionless face, was prepared for rejection.
Although they were allies, such a request seemed excessive to anyone.
However, Su Lun swore that he was asking this question with the scientific rigor and sanctity of a Magician dedicated to Alchemy.
And indeed, Su Lun's "unreasonable request" was after much deliberation.
Ever since the last incident in the Sea Ruins where Pandora absorbed the Power of Faith from Sea King Drake, she seemed less and less human and more and more like an unreachable divine being. As the Mountain Hermit Kingdom's Moon Reading Goddess, the Power of Faith continued to gather upon her, and she would only grow stronger in the future.
Likewise, it would become increasingly difficult to communicate with her.
In these days, Su Lun had carefully observed that this fabricated body indeed held a fatal temptation for a Puppeteer.
She represented the ultimate skill of a Puppeteer and the peak understanding of Alchemy.
Without exaggeration, she was a treasure trove of alchemical knowledge.
Taking the chance to speak while they still could communicate, and while their relationship was still somewhat friendly, might just work out.
Otherwise, even if they could meet again in the future, the likelihood of her agreement would increasingly dwindle.
If he missed the opportunity to study the world's only fabricated person, Su Lun would undoubtedly regret it deeply.
As soon as he voiced his request, the atmosphere turned awkward.
Only the sound of the wind and the waves could be heard on the deck, and no one spoke for a long while.
Su Lun was already prepared for her to react coldly.
But unexpectedly, after some deliberation, Pandora asked, "Where do you want to conduct the research?"

chapters.title: Chapter 417 - 416 For Scientific Research
chapters.content:
"Where would you like to study?"
Upon hearing Pandora speak, Su Lun suddenly thought he had heard incorrectly.
It took a moment to react before he realized she had actually agreed?
Overjoyed, Su Lun suggested, "How about we go to my laboratory?"
Pandora raised an eyebrow and, without another word, made her way into the cabin, seeming to give her tacit consent.
Su Lun had a laboratory on the ship; she knew where it was.
Right next to her room.
...
Since Su Lun couldn't enter the minor void realm, he had a large fixed laboratory on the Eternal Night. When on board, he spent the majority of his time there.
Pandora, because she disliked interacting with anyone other than Su Lun, had her room next to the laboratory.
Now, to cooperate with Su Lun's research, the two of them went back to the cabin together.
As they entered the laboratory's entrance, the experimental area, mechanical workshop, and golem crafting room came into view.
The walls were densely packed with various tools, and on the left side of the room, more than a dozen large glass jars contained half-finished mechanical octopi, with living octopi writhing within the jars; in the center, mechanical armor had been disassembled into individual parts, and an array of guns, steam boilers, and the formidable steel monsters resembled an armory; on the right side of the room, various half-carved puppets were hung everywhere with transparent threads, resembling suspended corpses...
The air was thick with the smell of rust, the odor of culture fluid mixed with rotten eggs, and the mingling scent of wood shavings.
Although she lived next door, it was Pandora's first time entering Su Lun's laboratory.
She glanced around with a seemingly intrigued expression.
Having witnessed Su Lun's mechanical golem army's exaggerated combat power in a previous battle, a hint of unnoticeable intrigue flashed in her eyes upon seeing these half-finished creations.
After surveying the laboratory environment, Pandora didn't comment on its quality but simply turned to ask Su Lun, "How do you plan to study?"
Her tone was very calm, as if the subject of study wasn't her own body but something else.
"This..."
Su Lun originally wanted to suggest she lie on the dissection table, as it was the most convenient and looked the most professional.
But considering that it was usually used for studying corpses, magical beasts, and dissecting various odd and deformed creatures, it somehow felt impolite.
Being a laboratory, there weren't superfluous things like a bed.
Looking around, he could only point towards the couch, "Otherwise, if you don't mind, could you please lie on the sofa?"
Pandora glanced at it without a word, and her expression remained unchanged. She walked over to the sofa and asked, "Should I take off my clothes?"
"Hmm."
Su Lun replied, keeping his composure, then added, "If you don't mind. There are sterile surgical gowns over there."
Saying so, he also breathed a sigh of relief in his heart.
Since Pandora herself brought up the topic, the atmosphere wasn't so awkward.
No sooner had Su Lun finished speaking than he thought he should step out for a moment.
But unexpectedly, Pandora nonchalantly began to slip off the strap hanging over her delicate shoulder.
Today, she was dressed in a lightweight, gold thread-woven gown that revealed much of her back. As the dress was mostly made from the legendary material "Golden Fleece," it appeared sexily elegant yet with a hint of sacred grace.
Before Su Lun could look away, Pandora had already taken off both shoulder straps.
The entire floor-length gown couldn't stay put on her smooth skin, so it slid down to her waist. Due to her proud and perky hips, the garment hung there.
This type of backless gown naturally didn't include a bra, so as it slipped down, her upper body was completely exposed to the air.
From the side, her curves were prominent, proudly firm.
Even without any external support, they remained full and unyielding.
Although Pandora's back was turned to him as she undressed, Su Lun was still fully aware of her graceful curves.
Pandora seemed to notice his gaze but didn't stop.
Her delicate hand gently tugged the gown at the waist, and the garment smoothly fell to the ground.
Aside from the undeniably sexy lace panties, her lithe figure was now unobstructed.
Quite the enchanting scene.
Su Lun wasn't intentionally peeping; he simply hadn't expected Pandora to be so straightforward.
He averted his eyes and moved to the side of an experimental table to start preparing some research instruments that would be needed.
Listening to the rustling sound of clothing beside his ear, he knew Pandora was putting on the sterile suit.
After diligently preparing the necessary testing equipment, Su Lun turned back to see Pandora already lying there, dressed in a thin layer of a sterile gown.
He walked over, put on gloves, and with a focused and serious expression, politely said, "Miss Pandora, I am going to begin."
Pandora lay back with her eyes closed, responding with a calm "Mm."
...
Su Lun had always been curious about whether the body structure of an alchemical homunculus was completely the same as a human's and if those organs truly possessed the same functions as humans.
Now he finally had the opportunity to resolve his curiosity.
But even if she was willing to cooperate with the research, he could not possibly treat her like a lifeless body to be manipulated at will.
Su Lun behaved with enough politeness, asking before he began, "Miss Pandora, there might be some physical contact..."
Without waiting for him to finish, Pandora responded again with a "Mm."
With permission granted, Su Lun began his work.
"I might check the muscle texture of your buttocks and legs, which could be offensive..."
"Would you mind if I use some instruments to check your bioelectrical situation?"
"I might take some samples of your nails and hair..."
"..."
Because research often touched on private areas, Su Lun frequently asked for consent.
After several inquiries, Pandora seemed reluctant to expend more words and said something that granted wide latitude: "You don't need to keep asking me. Since I have agreed to cooperate with your research, I won't mind those details. Just do as you see fit."
Su Lun stopped being overly scrupulous and boldly began conducting various tests.
Organ and skeletal examinations, instrument testing, sample collection, energy monitoring, fluid collection, runic recording...
Each test was conducted in an orderly fashion.
Su Lun unfolded the Octospider Lance, examining and recording all data.
As he observed this homunculus, a work that could be considered a hall-of-fame piece of alchemy, the ultimate craftsmanship of a runic puppet, his amazement never ceased.
Piecing together the intricate techniques, Su Lun increasingly felt as though he stood before a towering "mountain of knowledge," more and more aware of his own insignificance and ignorance.
The technical aspects contained within this homunculus were for the most part completely beyond his current level of comprehension, unattainably out of reach.
He recognized a fair amount of the runes and materials, but once they were combined, they became unrecognizable.
This gave Su Lun a distinct feeling, leading him to believe that his current reserves of knowledge were only sufficient for him to develop a glider, while what lay before him was a highly sophisticated space shuttle.
This was not like the super mechanical warrior's bionic organs that Su Lun had seen with Number Nineteen; Pandora's organs, skeleton, and skin were almost indistinguishable from a human's.
Each organ was yet another piece that could be deemed perfect in alchemy.
There were pulse, heartbeat, fluid movement, hormone secretion...
Yet she also possessed the special characteristics of an alchemical homunculus, such as her extraordinary self-healing capability, and a body strength nearly immune to both physical and magical attacks.
A thousand years ago, Sir Isaac and Lady Isaac had used alchemical materials to create this almost perfect alchemical body.
Su Lun watched in awe.
This analytical research, rather than saying he'd learned something, he felt he was far from qualified.
It was more like opening a new path of thought, defining a direction, showing him the right path for future research.
Su Lun conducted various tests with single-minded focus, oblivious to the passing of time.
....
There was no extraneous noise in the laboratory, and on the wall hung a brass mechanical clock that ticked "click-clack, click-clack."
Unnoticed, the hour hand had moved from midnight to six in the morning.
Only when a pale blue dawn light shone into the lab from outside did Su Lun suddenly realize how much time had passed.
However, at this moment, nearly all the data that needed to be collected had been gathered, the samples would require a great deal of time to analyze and digest, so there was no need to rush.
"Whew..."
He exhaled a long breath, his thoughts slowing from their intense focus.
Putting aside his work, his demeanor seemed to shift from that of a cold machine back to human.
Only then did Su Lun's gaze fall upon Pandora on the sofa, and he involuntarily paused for a moment.
The "sterile gown" was really just a thin, blue, semi-transparent paper cloth.
And because of the thorough examination from top to bottom, the gown had become torn.
On the couch lay the bare figure of Pandora, practically unclothed.
Yet, her face showed no change in expression from start to finish, her breathing regular, her chest rising and falling softly, still portraying the appearance of being sound asleep.
Su Lun felt a strange attraction, his gaze unable to move away.
When Pandora was in Mountain Hermit, she had a nickname, the "White Jade Lioness Shining Night Princess."
Her skin was as white as a white jade lion, bewitchingly translucent and impactful under the light.
Su Lun couldn't help but reminisce about the touch, feeling like a plump koi, even through gloves there was an extreme delicacy to the sensation, as if it would slip away like silk if held in hand.
In myth, "Pandora" was created to beguile the gods, possessing an otherworldly beautiful visage and a flawless body.
The woman before him seemed as though she had stepped right out of those myths.
Su Lun's gaze lingered on her impeccable face for a moment before sliding down to rest on her slender neck and delicate clavicle, and then further down to the subtly rising curves, her bosom like sculpted snow peaks. Even while lying flat, their shape was full and round, exquisite to grasp. With each breath, they danced playfully, as if adding a mischievous charm.
Even with the closest scrutiny, there seemed to be no flaw to find.
The perfection was as though it could only be a gift from the creator.
She was a marvel that could fulfill any man's ultimate fantasy of beauty.
Utterly captivating, yet with an unassailable essence of sanctity.
Like a jade cup cradled in the palm, one handled her with such care for fear of causing any damage.
...
This was the first time Su Lun had observed Pandora's body so meticulously.
He felt fortunate to be able to detach his emotions, otherwise, any man witnessing such a blood-pumping scene would likely have lost control of his thoughts.
A shiver ran through him, and Su Lun quickly diverted his eyes.
After all, physical data was a matter of privacy, his own weakness, and without trust, he would never permit anyone to study it.
Su Lun felt that Pandora had already been very forthcoming with him, her ally.
To look any longer would be unbecoming.
He took a deep breath, gazing at the enticing body on the couch as if viewing it through a filter, and estimated in his mind, "Her charisma must be so high, it's probably over 15 points."
His own charisma of 12 points was already considered among the most handsome within humanity.
But even compared with Pandora, there was still a significant gap.
Charisma wasn't just about physical features, it also encompassed temperament and certain special abilities.
He guessed that after Pandora used her Bewitching Technique, the value might become frighteningly exaggerated, to the point where even he could be easily beguiled.
Uh... Bewitching Technique?
A spark flickered in Su Lun's mind.
But before he could reflect further, probably because he had been looking for too long, Pandora's closed eyelids suddenly fluttered.
Being no ordinary person, it was natural for her not to fall into a deep slumber.
She opened her eyes and calmly asked Su Lun, "Have you finished your research?"
While speaking, she glanced at her unabashedly exposed body and made no effort to cover it, boldly and openly.
"Yes."
Turning his gaze towards the ground, Su Lun performed a very gentlemanly apology, "Thank you, Miss Pandora. For any offense I may have caused, please allow me to express my sincere apologies."
Ever since their previous joint battles, he no longer saw Pandora as an enemy or simply an alchemical product.
Instead, he valued her as an ally, a friend with emotions and a soul.
To research her was a gesture of pure intent, aiming to delve into the heights of Alchemy.
And devoid of any complex motives.
Such research was also founded on significant respect.
What Su Lun didn't know was that this respect might have been Pandora's most crucial reason for agreeing to such an "impolite request."
"Oh."
With that, Pandora stood up from the couch.
At that moment, Su Lun's eyes caught sight of a pair of jade feet stepping on the floor, paused as if searching for something.
Su Lun, thinking of something, quickly took the neatly folded gown from the side and walked over to her.
This was the luxurious gold-threaded gown Pandora had removed earlier, which he had neatly arranged during his study.
He gentlemanly handed the dress over to her, intending to turn away.
But unexpectedly, Pandora spoke words that caught him off guard, "Having looked for so long, would you help me put it on?"
"???"
Su Lun suddenly felt as if he might have misheard.
Looking up, he saw her calm eyes that weren't as cold as he had imagined.
Although he knew the original Pandora was well aware and didn't seem to mind.
Voicing it out loud, however, was a different matter altogether.
The atmosphere suddenly became serious and a bit strange.
Although Su Lun felt that something was off, he had no reason to refuse. "Excuse me."
He straightened the dress but realized that he didn't know how to assist someone in putting on this type of dress that slips on.
Pandora, on the other hand, boldly walked over, stood naked in front of Su Lun.
She raised her hand to indicate that the dress should be lowered, then stepped into it with one foot before following with the other. When the dress was caught at her knees, she didn't pull it up herself, seemingly waiting for something.
The two were very close, even closer than they were during their previous research.
And they maintained this slightly ambiguous posture.
When Su Lun's fingers touched Pandora's thigh, an extremely smooth sensation was unmistakably felt.
He had touched her more during their research, so why did he feel a sudden rush of panic and restlessness now?
"Is she using Bewitching Technique?"
There was a slight twitch at the corner of Su Lun's eye as he came to a realization.
His body was agitated in a way that was completely beyond the control of reason.
Pandora looked up again, her lips curved up slightly, reminding him, "Although I don't mind you taking a few more glances… I would prefer you to pull up my dress first."
At that, Su Lun felt somewhat embarrassed. Since he was still holding the dress, he couldn't just maintain that position, so he started pulling it up.
The material of the dress was silky smooth and encountered almost no resistance gliding over her skin, but there was a moment's pause when it reached her hips, his fingers sinking into the soft flesh.
Pausing again, his touch lingered on the soft flesh by her ribs.
Pandora seemed unconcerned, boldly lifting her arms, then slipped the straps back onto her shoulders herself and flipped out her hair that had been trapped under the garment. She made no attempt to hide from Su Lun as she adjusted the majestic view, unconfined by a bra, and covered up the enchanting scenery.
Su Lun once again witnessed her stunning yet insouciant expression, seeming a bit puzzled.
Why had she suddenly changed, as if she became a different person?
Did Pandora not know?
Her gaze wasn't on Su Lun, yet she didn't avoid him either, casually stating, "My personality isn't as indifferent as you think."
"..."
Su Lun's expression turned awkward.
For the first time, he heard a tone from Pandora that wasn't indifferent, hostile, or angry.
It seemed naturally seductive, able to stir up one's most primal desires.
But what he didn't know was,
the "Pandora" of mythology existed to tempt the gods, embodying the world's most beautiful and seductive being.
And the Pandora before him was just the same.
Her seductiveness was a talent etched into her very bones.
It was just that at first, they had met as enemies, and in these past days, they had only interacted through cooperation.
Aside from cold stares, there didn't seem to be any other fitting expressions.
Now that they were somewhat acquainted and he found her quite agreeable,
she was, at least in her opinion, the most pleasant of all the people she had encountered.
Perhaps it was also because of Teacher Sereya's influence?
Pandora herself didn't know.
At any rate, she had a favorable impression of Su Lun.
That cautious respect had certainly earned points.
Now that it was time to leave, there was no need to keep a stern face.
Her lips finally curled into a charming smile as she said her goodbye, "You're quite a good person. Goodbye."
In that tone, where was there any hint of indifference?
It sounded more like a small act of playful revenge.
And when he looked again, she was gone.
Su Lun gazed at the spot where Pandora had vanished from the laboratory and after standing bewildered for a couple of seconds, he shook his head with a wry smile.
A good guy card?
Had he been teased?
Pandora's aloof persona had crumbled, huh!
But, that was quite all right.
Su Lun thought that once his alchemy level improved, if he had the chance to explore the alchemy body again, she probably wouldn't refuse.

chapters.content:
Just when the members of the Dawn Group were holding a grand banquet aboard the Eternal Night Emperor to celebrate the success of the rescue plan, intelligence about the battle in the city-states of Moros had spread to the world like it had grown wings.
Those professional intelligence merchants always had various ways to deliver the news in the shortest amount of time. Before dawn had even broken, the major newspaper groups in Old Lington had already started overtime work to rush out a special issue about the explosive news.
In the early morning, while the massive city was still asleep, early-rising newspaper boys were riding their bicycles through streets and alleys, stuffing this special issue into thousands of households' mailboxes.
Royalty, parliament members, Alchemy Guilds, Wild Hunt Guilds, Professional Leagues, Mercenary Guilds... members of all the major forces had gotten hold of that newspaper special issue, knowing about that distant battle thousands of miles away.
A new organization called "Dawn" had launched a surprise attack on the main base of the North Sea Fleet, causing tens of thousands of pirate casualties and then fully retreated unscathed.
The process of the battle was simply mind-boggling.
But it was indeed a fact.
Meteor falling, destroyed the Temple of Aghaparnon.
Then, an earth-shattering battle followed closely.
All sorts of bizarre events happened frequently.
Even though the names of the Dawn Group members, like Su Lun, were not known to outsiders, their nicknames had been spread first.
One who boldly and directly fought against the seasoned eighth-tier "King of the North Sea," Oleg, and even overwhelmingly prevailed, was "Mr. Jing."
Another, "Silver-Armed Beast," once the commander of the royal knight corps "Sacred Judgment Legion" Barrett, a new seventh-tier, with unmatched combat power through his Phantasmal Armor Layering technique.
A suspected triple-talent female Sword Saint, "Rakshasa Sword Saint," whose sword slashes through the Mafa Royal Mechanical Corps as easily as cutting vegetables, a single sword strike splitting sixteen armors.
And then there was a "Death God Puppeteer."
This person occupied a significant portion of the newspaper, even overshadowing the two eighth-tier main characters of the battle. The war reporters used a documentary style to depict that horrifyingly bloody battle in the central arena of the Moros city-states.
The headline read: 1V200,000!
One person controlling an advancing puppet army, like a flesh-grinding mill, slaughtered tens of thousands of pirates.
There was even a blurry black-and-white photo taken from a distance.
In the arena, the sky was dotted with a gigantic cross, and that cloaked figure was pulling countless threads, like directing a terrifying puppet show. In the photo, piles of bones stacked up like mountains, limbs and arms flying chaotically. Even through the newspaper, one could vividly feel the despair akin to walking into a slaughterhouse.
Puppet Masters were a very niche existence among professionals, not particularly outstanding in the realm of top-tier professionals.
For the first time in a century, people realized that Puppet Masters could actually possess such an outrageous combat effectiveness. Was the offensive capability of one individual really equivalent to several armies?
To ordinary people, pirates were synonymous with evil robbers, and the news of someone slaughtering massively in a pirate stronghold was incredibly uplifting.
Even Emperor Luying was deeply excited yet incredulous when he saw the contents of the newspaper.
To fight against two hundred thousand?
Although he knew the headline was surely exaggerated, wasn't this every Puppet Master's dream?
A puppet army passing through, slaughtering all four directions, making even ghosts and gods move aside in fear!
At this moment, the front page of the newspaper was the highlight moment for the profession of Puppet Masters!
It was foreseeable that after the news fermented, in many years to come, the Puppet Master profession would welcome a new spring.
As soon as the newspaper was published, a hush of Puppeteer trend quietly rose among the apprentices at various academies and in alchemical workshops.
In the newspaper, Su Lun had achieved what most seventh-tier professionals could not achieve, but in reality, it wasn't that he had the combat power of a top-tier professional.
It was just that those information traders overlooked the fact that Su Lun was able to freely control the Puppet Theater and kill enemies because Barrett and others restrained the top-tier professionals of the North Sea Fleet, resulting in such astonishing battle results.
Because it was difficult to determine life and death among top-tier professionals at the moment, a prolonged battle didn't result in casualties among the pirates with bounties over a billion. The spectacle was there, but it lacked the "newsworthiness" that attracts attention.
The newspaper skimmed over it as well.
Only against a dark background, can stars truly dazzle.
For this reason, the "star" Su Lun, making tens of thousands of pirates casualties, became even more sensational.
Pirates below the sixth-tier were slaughtered, their blood flowing like rivers, and more than ten most-wanted criminals with bounties over a billion died at his hands.
He single-handedly cleared a significant portion of the Bounty Hunters Guild's list all at once.
This battle introduced "Dawn" as a formidable force into people's view.
The well-informed major powers also got detailed news immediately.
When they saw several old bloodlines from Synodia Province who hadn't appeared in centuries participating in the battle, and knew Mr. Jing was a high-tier bloodline, everyone roughly guessed that this mysteriously emerged eighth-tier powerhouse was likely a Great Shot from a millennium ago.
Being able to face the North Sea Fleet head-on, this was certainly a new force not to be underestimated. Moreover, now it seemed that this "Dawn Organization" was an enemy of both the Mafa Empire and Luying Empire royal families, as well as the North Sea Fleet and Duke Rafael. For other powers, whether it was alignment, incorporation, or covert cooperation, this was the best entity to work with.
And seizing the moment they had just appeared was the best opportunity.
Once the news broke out, the sharp-minded top bosses also started thinking.
The information traders in the black market also got busy, searching everywhere for clues to confirm what "Dawn" really was and how they could establish contact.
While the news was still fermenting on the newspaper, Mr. Hei in a library in Lingdun City, had already gotten today's newspaper.
Although he already knew about that rescue mission, having read every word in the newspaper carefully, the old man's face broke out in a gratified smile, "Reading the report really gets one's blood boiling..."
Thinking, he wrote something on a parchment.
Not long after, rumors started circulating in the black market, roughly saying: "Dawn is a free and neutral organization, existing to research and promote the expansion of Alchemy civilization."
...
Pandora did leave, utterly unaffected by the water.
But in the laboratory of the Eternal Night, Su Lun looked at his still restless body reaction and couldn't help but smile bitterly, "Her Bewitching Technique is really powerful."
When Pandora left, she had played a trick on him, likely as a quirky revenge for the time she was considered an enemy by Su Lun and was stripped and hung roughly for several days.
Although the Bewitching Technique did no harm to Su Lun's body, the "aftereffects" seemed quite significant.
He had just tried meditating a moment ago but still couldn't calm the restlessness in his body.
This was the first time Su Lun had experienced his bodily desires not being controlled by his reason, his mouth dry and his tongue parched, a thin layer of sweat lightly coating his body.
Thinking about it, it also wasn't all bad.
At least this time, the one who used this trick was an acquaintance, not an enemy.
With the experience under his belt, he'd be better prepared next time.
After all, all spells have a time limit, and Su Lun figured that the aftereffects would subside soon, so he didn't think much of it and began to organize the instruments and data notes in the laboratory.
While tidying up, he found a sexy pair of panties in the corner.
It then dawned on Su Lun that Pandora had likely left wearing only her skirt?
Yes!
She was indeed commando underneath.
Seeing the panties, an image of a body as sculpted as a jade lion instinctively surfaced in Su Lun's mind, thoroughly convinced.
After all, he had worn that skirt himself.
But the moment this thought flickered through his mind, like the strong aftereffects of alcohol, the delicate touch brought a very real sense of pleasure lingering in his body, with his lower abdomen heating up instantly.
"Hmm..."
It was then that Su Lun noticed the abnormality.
He let out a long breath of turbid air, his gaze turning quite odd as he thought to himself, "Just a slight thought can arouse desire; is this Bewitching Technique some divine secret technique?"
He looked down at his own body and shook his head with a wry smile.
This technique was unlike any Bewitching Technique he knew of; there was something beyond his comprehension.
Glancing at the thin lace, Su Lun simply dismissed the thought.
He didn't pay much attention to his body's reaction, thinking perhaps... it would dissipate after a while?
Then he resumed organizing the laboratory.
Until... two hours later.
...
After cleaning up the lab, the data recorded in those notebooks were complex and profound, and the samples analyzed in the instruments would also take a lot of time to study. There was no rush to digest them just yet.
Having finished organizing, he looked at his body again and furrowed his brow slightly.
Only then did he realize, Pandora's prank was no simple matter.
Despite focusing his mind on work, his body showed no signs of calming down.
Soul and body, each going their own way.
His mind pondered on science, but his body was being brutally honest.
Always wearing out like this wasn't helping, Su Lun glanced at the wall clock; it was almost eight o'clock, so he thought about heading back to the captain's quarters for a cold shower.
On the ship, he rarely used his Soul Perception ability, considering the privacy of his companions.
Upon reaching the captain's quarters, he knocked on the door, but unsurprisingly, no one responded inside.
Having advanced to Sword Saint, Sen ends up diligently practicing swordsmanship on the deck early each morning around six, come rain or shine.
Mr. Jing didn't seem to be either.
So Su Lun just opened the door and went inside.
Entering the room, he took off his clothes and headed directly for the rudimentary shower behind a curtain, showering in cold water for a while.
The water gushing down refreshed him considerably.
But looking again at his restless body, Su Lun finally felt somewhat defeated and muttered, "This is really bizarre."
He knew cold water was useless, but continuing to shower was somewhat comforting.
Probably because he had showered for too long, at that moment, the door "cracked" open from outside.
Sen, done with her sword practice, sauntered in.
Seeing the clothes hanging on the coat rack and the sound of running water in the bathroom, she knew Su Lun had arrived.
She glanced at a bare-butted Su Lun behind the shower curtain and teasingly remarked, "Yo... coming back to shower this early, does this mean last night with Miss Pandora was pleasant?"
Accustomed to this kind of exchange, Su Lun didn't argue and casually responded, "Yeah."
"Tsk tsk... you really do have good luck with women,"
Sen's tone brimming with jest, she was used to it too and said, "Hurry up, I need to shower."
With that, sounds of undressing filled the room.
This was a normal scene between the two, Sen never avoided Su Lun and casually stripped off her training clothes, then untied her chest wrap, and took off her shorts, bare as born.
While undressing, she didn't hear the water off and urged, "Hey hey hey, are you done yet? I need to shower."
Impatiently, she added, "Forget it, you're taking too long. Help me put some hot water in the tub, I want to soak."
Her tone suggested she was planning to join him in the shower.
"..."
Su Lun stayed silent.
It wasn't that he didn't want to step out now, but, his body seemed really reluctant to obey that kind of command.
Especially with the sound of undressing, the aftereffects of the Bewitching Technique reflexively flared up again.
Ultimately caring for his dignity, Su Lun still faced the wall in contemplation.
Sen walked over, naked, and having realized the tap was running cold water, questioned curiously, "It's not even hot today, why are you showering in cold water?"
As she spoke, she stood beside Su Lun and twisted the hot water knob to adjust the temperature, intending to rinse off.
Feeling that Su Lun was acting strange today, a glance from the corner of her eye revealed the abnormality.
However, with her personality, seeing that ferocious state didn't shock her; instead, she laughed and teased, "Yo, does this mean you didn't have a pleasant time with that Miss Pandora?"
"..."
Su Lun rolled his eyes, ignoring her teasing remark.
Qian was even more excited, glancing from the corner of her eye, she couldn't help but tease, "Hahaha, you look like this? Isn't that ugly?"
Her words weren't awkward in the slightest.
The two had always been open and honest with each other, and they had shared a bed countless times, although Qian really had no interest in matters between men and women.
Since their experience in the Mountain Hermit, Su Lun's salacious hands had become more frequent, but Qian always found it boring, and occasionally she would smack his hand away if he tried to sneak a touch.
This way of getting along made both of them somewhat uncomfortable.
Su Lun wasn't the kind to be ruled by carnal desires, too much clinginess simply wasn't suitable.
Over these days, they had gradually returned to their past state where they were utterly unconstrained with each other.
Qian felt this type of relationship was the most comfortable.
So now she wouldn't avoid Su Lun anymore, whether changing clothes or bathing, she'd think, "If you want to look, then look."
Sometimes when sleeping in the same bed, she would lay spread-eagle, placing her limbs over him.
Even if Su Lun occasionally couldn't keep his hands to himself at night, as long as he didn't go too far, Qian would turn a blind eye.
...
Normally, Su Lun was perfectly rational.
But now, some of his bodily functions were beyond his control.
Qian stood naked next to him, squeezing past Su Lun to get under the shower head. Their skin touched, and Su Lun acutely felt the soft sensation from her arm, making his brows jump as if he were struggling to restrain himself.
The warm water showered down on Qian's body, opening all her pores pleasantly, eliciting a joyful murmur from her.
At that moment, as if sensing something, she turned her head to look at the slightly perturbed Su Lun, then let her gaze drift downward. She blinked, as if guessing something, and uncertainly said, "Are you under a Bewitching Technique?"
Su Lun shrugged his shoulders, not seeing any reason to deny it, and said with some reluctance, "Yeah."
Upon hearing this, a gleam of schadenfreude flashed in Qian's eyes, "Was that Miss Pandora's spell? Hey, what did you do to her?"
Just when she thought to tease him further, upon noticing Su Lun staring at her, she quickly switched to a more somber glance, almost as if warning him like guarding against a thief, "Hey, hey, hey, let me tell you, don't you think about it. I can't help you."
Su Lun rolled his eyes, said irritably, "I wasn't planning anything. I just wanted a cold shower, you came over on your own."
Qian's figure was also very seductive, especially standing bare next to him, any normal person would have thoughts.
Beauty lies not just in appearance or figure, but in a certain charm. In Su Lun's eyes, Qian had a unique allure that was second to none. However, he did not want their relationship to become weird. Rationality refused any overstep.
The two had a deep understanding of each other, and Qian instantly understood the contradiction in Su Lun's expression.
Her tone shifted from teasing to a touch of concern, asking, "Didn't you try using a potion?"
"It's not a negative toxin, what potion should I use? Besides, the technique is very tricky, I can't use any potions before figuring out its mechanism; it might suppress normal bodily functions later on."
Su Lun had thought about it, but such a strong Bewitching Technique might require a massive amount of suppressants to control his body's reactions.
And this was exactly the kind of treatment that was taboo in medical practices. Resolving symptoms with medication without understanding the underlying cause could bury the problem even deeper.
Besides, it was just a prank from Pandora without malice.
Su Lun felt it wasn't yet time to suppress it with medication.
Using medication recklessly could affect bodily functions which was unnecessary.
Qian tilted her head, pondering, "Then what do we do? Pandora has already left, the Princess is still in Mountain Hermit, your demon maid isn't here, and there's no one on the ship who can help you..."
After a pause, her expression turned serious, as if she had an idea, "Philo could possibly ask around for you. But I guess you wouldn't dare."
"..."
Su Lun was speechless.
This gambling-addicted lady really knew no restraint, even daring to catch Mr. Jing's attention.
As Qian glanced at Su Lun's fierce expression, she suggested, "Why don't you try traditional skills?"
Even now, she didn't deliberately cover her body, whether it was her impressively high chest or her toned, beautiful legs.
Not caring was one thing.
Looking at her expression now, it seemed she was hinting: if you want to look, just look, help yourself.
"..."
Su Lun felt that this gambling-addicted lady's suggestion was getting more outrageous.
If it were so simple to solve, he wouldn't still be troubled now.
Qian's suggestion not only didn't solve the problem but also caused Su Lun's gaze unconsciously to wander over her body. The influence of the Bewitching Technique was growing stronger.
Qian also felt uncomfortable being stared at, she pouted, "Forget it, you figure it out yourself."
With a bored expression, she couldn't think of any other solutions, "I'm going to take a bath."
The hot water was ready, and she climbed into the bathtub to soak.
...
In the simple bathroom, the two remained silent for a long time.
Su Lun thought about leaving after washing, but his body wouldn't let him leave.
Hearing no movement behind him for a long time, Qian looked back at a very strained Su Lun and said, "Why don't you join me? Perhaps relaxing might help?"
As Su Lun listened, his mind was still pondering the problem, but his feet stepped into the bathtub.
The splashing water overflowed from the large bathtub, spilling onto the floor.
His body soaked in the water, the buoyancy eased much of his strain.
He sat next to Qian, propping a towel behind his neck, and reclined against the edge of the bathtub.
They also occasionally soaked together like this, and although it was intimate, it never felt particularly special.
The steam boiler kept heating water, and gently flowing water sounds were "hurrying" by his ear.
No one disturbed them, the atmosphere was serene and peaceful, seemingly no different from any normal day.
Su Lun closed his eyes to rest, trying to focus his mind on the experiment.
Although there was a faint slippery touch beside him, he had no intention of taking advantage of it.
Hadn't they already understood each other's tacit agreement?
From the corner of her eye, she occasionally glanced at Su Lun's expression and then at the shadows in the water.
Finally, after about ten minutes of soaking, she tentatively said in an uncertain tone, "Should I... try to help you?"
Su Lun, still resting with his eyes closed, didn't think it was a good suggestion.
But whatever he thought of saying felt strangely awkward.
So he stayed silent.
She pursed her lips, looked at him, and then tentatively reached out her hand.
Her movements were exceedingly clumsy.
Su Lun found her gesture quite unexpected but also heartwarming.
This gambling-addicted lady was still quite nice to him.
At least for her personality, the gesture was quite a big effort.
She continued to try.
But her technique was indeed a bit off, making it comically awkward.
Finally, Su Lun couldn't help but say, "Hey, hey, hey… Sister Qiantiao, that's not how you hold a sword hilt. That's not right."
Qiantiao looked utterly confused and said, "Ah, then how should it be? I thought it was the same, the feel is also similar."
She felt it was too troublesome and muttered resignedly, "Forget it, I'll not help you. You figure it out yourself."
"…"
Su Lun felt that the phrase "figure it out yourself" had a mysterious power to it, almost like a sort of permission.
He placed his hand on Qiantiao's shoulder, just like they normally did.
But with a firm grip, he leaned even closer.
The touch of their large patches of skin was soft and the posture slightly suggestive.
Both were keenly aware of each other's heartbeat.
Qiantiao also realized something was off and slightly pouted, but after thinking about it, she let it be.
It was probably because of her tacit approval that Su Lun became more audacious.
His hands, unapologetically, wandered down, gently kneading.
Qiantiao lay there, resting with her eyes closed.
She neither minded nor reciprocated.
Because she really found such suggestive activities utterly unamusing.
But because it was Su Lun, she didn't hit him.
Sometimes she herself would lend a hand, closing her eyes, helping out a little.
Su Lun, on the other hand, thoroughly enjoyed himself.
His hands, without any hesitation, roamed everywhere, becoming more reckless.
