Su Lun had been wandering the banquet hall when he was unexpectedly stopped by this mysterious lady.
She was dressed in a black lace gown, her figure graceful and her demeanor not lacking in nobility; she appeared to be a well-nurtured noblewoman.
Of course, that would be if she weren't a professional.
The energetic fluctuations of a professional could be detected with certain special methods, such as the energy disruption devices used by the Mafa military, or by sensory professionals.
But the soul's fluctuations couldn't be hidden.
This busty and curvaceous mystery woman was at least a fourth-tier professional.
Furthermore, Su Lun had noticed that she had been observing them for quite some time now.
A high-level professional approaching him with such familiarity clearly wasn't because of his good looks; she must have an ulterior motive.
Su Lun even suspected that she was a member of the Giant's Covert Association, yet she showed no allergic reaction to the "perfume" he wore.
This left Su Lun puzzled about her intentions.
The two of them began to subtly probe each other in light conversation.
"Sir, are you an expert in ancient artifacts? Just now, I overheard you explaining the exhibits in great detail to your disciple. Sorry, I didn't mean to eavesdrop; I just happened to be nearby."
"I am no expert, I have a bit of research, that's all."
"How may I address you, sir?"
"You may call me Nicholas. And you, madam?"
"Mr. Nicholas, why do you assume I am a 'madam'?"
"Oh, sorry. It's just that, generally, a young lady wouldn't possess the charm and grace you exhibit..."
"You have such a way with words, sir."
"..."
Although Su Lun fancied himself a decent person, he wasn't about to be polite with a scheming woman who kept pressing up against him, maybe trying to gauge the strength of his muscles.
If you dare come close, I dare to touch.
Su Lun's hand gently rested on the woman's soft waist, then naturally explored further to her well-muscled buttocks.
The muscular suppleness was notable, indicating she was clearly a close-combat professional.
But strangely, the woman's body was frail, with an unnaturally soft touch to it.
Su Lun guessed that it might be some sort of innate gift.
One had to admit, the feel was quite nice.
There had always been talk that the sexual mores in the Emperor Luying's capital were very open, known as the city of romance. It probably referred to something like this. Gentlemen and ladies were happy to enjoy a pleasureful experience with someone of the opposite sex who caught their fancy, releasing passion without any psychological burden.
This woman displayed a forthright and hearty demeanor typical of the women from the capital.
...
It was while Su Lun was chatting with the woman that the charity auction dinner began.
The lights in the banquet hall dimmed, with several beams focusing on the stage.
After getting on stage, the auctioneer briefly introduced that all proceeds from this batch of auction items would be donated to a children's charity fund, and then the auction process began.
In the darkness, Su Lun continued to converse with the woman named Caroline.
"Sir, the scent of your cologne is quite distinctive~"
"Oh?"
"I happen to run a bit of a perfume business myself, but I've never smelled such a unique fragrance."
...
Su Lun knew this woman must have noticed something amiss.
He didn't plan to babble, the two of them were now clear on their understanding, "I think it would be best if you were more sincere, ma'am."
A hint of ambiguity with a trace of boldness appeared in Caroline's eyes as she almost clung to Su Lun's side and retorted, "And what, sir, do you think would constitute sincerity?"
The auction had started, and Su Lun had business to attend to. He had seen many beautiful women and did not wish to waste time on this one, "For instance, talk about your connection to the mysterious collector behind these auctioned items."
Upon hearing this, Caroline's brows lifted slightly, but she did not deny it, "How did you figure it out?"
Su Lun did not want to go into detail; he had guessed from certain details and took a shot in the dark, not expecting to be correct, "If you are willing to talk, we can continue this conversation. If not, then I apologize."
He was convinced the woman's approach was not only probing but also indicated she had a request to make.
Hearing this, Caroline gave Su Lun a thorough look.
After a moment's thought, she seemed to make a decision. With no further ado, she said directly, "The items come from my channel of resources. But now, I've discovered that this exhibition has surpassed my control. Some unscrupulous individuals have boarded the ship."
"Oh?"
Su Lun listened without any change in expression, maintaining a calm and attentive demeanor.
However, his mind was quite surprised. The person who arranged for these goods to be here was not from the Giant Conclave after all?
Caroline continued, "I must confess, I don't even know who owns these collectibles. They came through a mysterious channel. But I was the one who arranged for them to be on board. I'd noticed something fishy, so I came along in person."
Here, a serious look crossed her eyes. She added, "Coincidentally, just now, my subordinates found that the ship's long-range communication equipment malfunctioned. It wasn't a mechanical failure but deliberate sabotage. The external signals have been completely blocked."
...
Hearing this, Su Lun's gaze narrowed slightly, still without taking a stance.
He had known that there were members of the Giant Conclave on this ship, so the fact that someone was making a move did not surprise him.
He did not fully trust the woman's words either.
Seeing that Su Lun gave no response, Caroline's gaze narrowed slightly.
At least she felt that she hadn't misjudged the situation; the man before her was a strong professional. She said further, "The girl you sent earlier with a message probably knows the identity of that young master, and you wanted to warn him of something, right?"
This surprised Su Lun somewhat, as his covert observation had been detected. He inquired curiously, "How did you know she was sent to deliver a message?"
Caroline replied, "Because I am a woman too. That young girl had no interest in the young master named Alex. And I knew the inside story of the whole exhibition and the presence of the 'Hanged Man Card.' So it wasn't hard to deduce the content of the message. This is also the most important reason I came to you. Although I don't know which power you represent, you definitely aren't with that group of unscrupulous people."
...
Listening to her, Su Lun found this to be rather interesting.
He also confirmed that she was not the enemy.
At least not part of the Giant Conclave.
At the same time, he silently lamented how Lingdun City was truly full of hidden dragons and crouching tigers, wondering how every random woman he met could be so formidable.
But whether she had guessed correctly or not didn't really matter. In the face of absolute power, cunning and scheming played only a minor role.
At least for now, Su Lun had not encountered anyone aboard the ship who posed a threat to him.
...
The auction continued, with each item sold signifying a countdown to some sinister plot.
Caroline knew she could not afford to delay. She said directly, "What I mean is, with such a significant figure on board, if anything unexpected happens, coming from my lots, it would bring me into considerable trouble. And the manpower I have on the ship might not be enough to handle such an event. So, I was hoping you'd be willing to help, within your means, of course. Regardless, I will be very grateful when we reach Lingdun, where I still hold some influence."
Others might not take much note of her tone, but Su Lun, upon hearing this unmistakable underworld jargon, largely guessed her identity.
Su Lun glanced at her and asked indifferently, "Who might you be?"
Caroline did not continue to conceal her identity, extending a golden business card embossed with a black rose.
The card alone was quite valuable.
It bore the name 'Caroline Worster' and the name of a notorious gang from Lingdun.
Having seen that, Su Lun came to a fuller understanding.
Using another's hand for murder, killing three birds with one stone.
The gangs of Old Lington were a grotesque and unique product of their era, not something that ragtag groups could sustain. They all had backing from the most powerful and wealthy conglomerates.
The people of the Giant Conclave had used Caroline's channels to get a collection of antiques with the 'Hanged Man Card' onboard, drawing young Master Alex to come.
If a problem really did arise, an investigation would inevitably implicate Caroline and the forces behind her.
The Roberts family occupied one of the five seats of the Senior Councilor, wielding great power. A significant disturbance could even potentially lead to major changes in Emperor Luying's political landscape.
No wonder she was seeking emergency reinforcements. It seemed Caroline had realized the severity of the situation exceeded her expectations.
After all, outsiders could see that there must have been high-order professionals as bodyguards for that Alexei, as well as a sixth-order leading professor.
The enemies dared to make a move; they certainly possessed stronger combat power.
By then, Caroline's tone had become very serious, "I know your strength is extraordinary. Since those people dare to act, they must be powerful. If a fight breaks out, it could involve everyone on this ship. Helping me is also helping yourself. Of course, if the situation is truly beyond human control, you can decide whether to intervene."
...
The military intelligence, religious zealots, royal academy, and now, a mysterious woman related to a gang leader from the underworld.
This was already the fourth wave of influential forces.
Lingdun City truly lived up to its reputation as the imperial capital; even a random cruise ship was teeming with big fish.
Su Lun couldn't help but remark.
He didn't bother to wonder about the force behind this woman since it was likely she was holding back some information.
But it was of no consequence.
The enemy of an enemy could be considered half a friend.
He was definitely going to help.
If it was within his power.
However, Su Lun did not want to make any overtures towards a stranger he had only met for half an hour.
So he just listened without speaking.
Seeing the man before her not responding, Caroline's expression showed a trace of seriousness.
But at the same time, she found it somewhat unbelievable.
Even after hearing her out, this man's face did not show the slightest hint of panic; on the contrary, he was utterly composed?
This confidence was not ordinary.
Caroline, having established herself in the underground market of Lingdun, naturally had her ways of judging people.
She was already certain that the man before her was very powerful.
With no other choice, she took a deep breath and made a significant promise, "If you are willing to exert your full strength, and ensure that the young master doesn't die, I will meet any condition you propose afterward. Even if it's beyond my reach, the Big Shot behind me will surely be able to handle it."
Her words were heavy with significance and carried an unusual confidence.
The influence of Lingdun's underground market and the forces behind her could indeed save one a lot of trouble in Lingdun City.
Listening to her, Su Lun finally said, "Alright."
He hadn't wanted to make a statement, but her promises were too significant.
Upon hearing this response, Caroline's expression visibly relaxed as if she had finally gained some assurance.
Su Lun then asked, "Can you share any other intelligence you have? For instance, what do you think the origin of those with malicious intent might be?"
Caroline's expression became serious again, answering, "Most likely, they're the fanatical followers of some newly-emerging religion. I've been investigating this for a while..."
Her intelligence was almost the same as Su Lun's.
But some of it was more detailed, for example, the bishop in reality turned out to be a prominent lawyer.
After chatting for a while, Su Lun became curious as to how this woman had singled him out amid so many in the banquet hall and asked directly, "Why did you decide to come to me?"
Caroline smiled faintly, "Besides what was mentioned earlier, you have two very talented disciples. And also, because you are a very charming gentleman."
She said frankly, "I initially thought you were the Phantom Thief Kit, and I came to probe and seek cooperation. After all, that guy is not weak. But clearly, you are not him."
Su Lun understood upon hearing this that it seemed being too handsome was the reason, "How did you figure out I wasn't him?"
Caroline said, "Do you think that the suave gentleman like the Phantom Thief Kit could refuse me? Although you did make some moves, you are one of the few true gentlemen I've met."
Su Lun chuckled, "Heh..."
...
The auction continued, and the roomful of wealthy people energetically bid on antiques, completely unaware that a crisis was unfolding quietly.
Su Lun wasn't in a hurry and relayed the current situation to Kit before returning to his seat on the sofa.
At that moment, the Taro card was finally taken out of the safe.
It was one
With a flicker of light in his left eye, Su Lun immediately identified it.
[Mysterious Taro Card]
Description: One of the 'Twenty-Two Secret Vault Taro Cards' from the Dawn Era, the [Hanged Man Card]; this card still possesses strong mysterious properties and is suitable for various high-level divination rituals; possession of this card grants a certain immunity to divination rituals; the card contains some encrypted content; the card has some parasitic larvae sealed by mysterious means;
"Indeed a genuine article."
Su Lun, intrigued by the information identified, immediately took an interest.
However, the value of such a card is subjective.
For a Taro Magician, it indeed has a fatal attraction. Even after countless years, it still retains strong mysterious properties.
But what Su Lun was curious about was the encrypted information on the card.
After all, having passed through many hands over the years, the information might have been decrypted long ago, making the card likely worthless.
Or, the "hidden secret" was some kind of continuously accessible treasure trove of knowledge.
But as it was a genuine article, Su Lun was very interested.
As for the "parasites" identified, they were undoubtedly the method the followers intended to use to trap the young Alexei.
If there were no surprises, the card was bound to end up in the hands of the young master.
But there were bound to be surprises.
Because at that moment, Kit had also sent a message—he was about to make his move.

chapters.title: Chapter 423 - 422: Biohazard
chapters.content:
"Hey, I say, Kit, are you sure your plan won't blow our cover?"
"Don't worry about it, I've only had less than two hours of deep conversation with Ruth; she won't be suspicious. Next time, I need to be more careful, though. These intelligence guys are now using seduction to catch people—it's really despicable. Oh, my Ruth, to think that I was so in love with her..."
"..."
In the banquet hall restroom, Su Lun listened to the plan through the communicator, full of speechlessness.
That guy Kit was now squatting in the stall next door.
Somehow, he had just confirmed that the intelligence agent was the same "Ruth" from before.
Kit's plan was to have Su Lun impersonate one of his aliases, "Jack," while he himself would steal the Taro cards as "Phantom Thief Kit."
This way, the two identities could completely disassociate from each other.
The auction for that Taro card was about to start, and there was no time to dawdle, so Su Lun opened the restroom door.
As he stepped out, the original black tailcoat transformed as if by magic into a luxurious white suit. With a swipe over his skin, synthetic skin adhered to his face. The magic of costume change turned him into a completely different person in an instant.
Su Lun pulled out a cane from his sleeve and, donning a bowler hat, stepped out of the restroom.
He was indeed the dashing "Jack."
As soon as he came out, Su Lun felt a vague gaze fixed upon him.
The tailing technique was very sophisticated, clearly that of a professional agent.
...
The auction continued, and the price of the [Hanged Man Card] kept climbing.
This auction also attracted quite a few Taro enthusiasts.
However, it seemed that the young master Alex was determined to win it, as each bid was very decisive and confident.
Su Lun paid no attention to the auction and walked out toward the banquet outside.
He reached the deck.
It was completely dark by now, and the sea breeze was gentle and refreshing.
Just then, a beautiful woman with tea-colored wavy hair approached and greeted affectionately, "Jack~ why are you here all alone?"
Su Lun knew this woman had been watching him, ever since he had gone to the washroom.
Having previously harvested the skills of "acting" and "diction" and even without the use of the voice changer hidden in his bow tie, he could imitate up to ninety percent similarity.
He mimicked Kit's voice and cheesy tone, responding, "Ruth, I wanted to enjoy the sea breeze alone. The auction inside is just too noisy."
Although Kit had sworn that women wouldn't catch on, Su Lun still immersed himself as much as possible into the role.
Ruth walked over and gave an intimate cheek kiss as a greeting.
And meanwhile very quietly, she sniffed, trying to identify the scent of the cologne.
Su Lun was proficient in various "spy efficiency" techniques, and he keenly noticed some of her unusual actions.
He immediately knew that this woman might also be suspicious that he was a stand-in and was trying to figure him out.
Su Lun understood Kit's personality well; in this situation, the LSP (Licensed Sex Professional) would definitely get handsy. Keeping too much distance would certainly give away that something was off.
So in that instant, as Ruth came into his embrace, Su Lun's hand naturally wrapped around her slender waist, and then, as if by accident, he caressed her well-endowed posterior.
Ruth exclaimed coyly, "Oh, dear, this is the deck~"
Even though she protested verbally, her body didn't move away at all.
Su Lun felt these intelligence people were truly dedicated to their work.
But he could only play along with her act, engaging in a bit of flirtatious banter.
He thought that if it were actually Kit, with the atmosphere heating up like this, it was highly likely that it would end in a paid-for affair.
Fortunately, at that moment, there was movement inside the auction.
With a loud "boom," like the ignition of magnesium powder, a strong white light flashed through the venue.
Just then, someone shouted loudly, "Phantom Thief Kit has appeared!"
That shout shattered the tranquility of the night.
Su Lun felt the delicate body in his arms tremble fiercely.
Although Ruth tried her best to hide it, her sparkling eyes were filled with disbelief.
And through the secret communicator in her ear, she received a message from her teammate: "Captain, it's confirmed it's 'Phantom Thief Kit'. He has appeared in the venue and stolen the Taro card!"
Ruth's expression froze for an instant, and despite her professional poise, she couldn't help but seem a bit unnatural.
Acting as if he noticed nothing amiss, Su Lun's lips curled into a charming smile, inquiring, "Oh, what's the matter, dear Ruth, you look a bit pale?"
After a pause, as if reminding himself, he murmured, "Oh, did I just hear someone shout something? What's with the chaos at the auction?"
Ruth gently touched her forehead and said, "Darling, I'm feeling a little unwell."
With an expression of urgent concern, Su Lun asked, "Shall I escort you back to your room to rest?"
At that moment, Ruth's mind was in a whirl, and she felt dizzy, "Oh, no need, I just want to be alone for a while."
If "Phantom Thief Kit" had already appeared, what about the Jack in front of her?
They had painstakingly gathered so many clues, all pointing to this Jack, waiting to catch him in the act tonight, but now he wasn't the one?
Had she just been played for free?
Of course, given such a handsome guy, whether being played for free mattered wasn't really the point.
But still, would those above think their entire investigation team were fools?
And just then, the noise grew louder.
"Quick! Catch Kit!"
"Damn it, don't let him get away with that Taro card!"
"..."
Shortly after the commotion, a man wearing a Zorro mask broke through the glass of the banquet hall and flew out.
The figure did a graceful roll in the air, and "bang," a pair of angelic pure white wings unfolded behind him. Amid a hail of bullets, he glided towards the enchanting night sea.
Watching from the corner of his eye, Su Lun's eyebrow quirked slightly; the spectacle was indeed impressive!
No wonder he captured the hearts of young ladies and madams.
Ruth no longer had any interest in dalliances with "Jack" here; she had a Phantom Thief to catch.
He found an excuse and left.
...
Once Su Lun saw that no one was around, he took out a gold card. With a flick of his fingers, a "bang" released a wave of energy, and a guy in a white suit appeared out of thin air beside him.
The two identical "Jacks" looked at each other.
One was beaming with a brilliant smile, the other with a helpless one.
Su Lun reached out sharply, and with a magic trick, his attire instantly switched back to the black tailcoat from before, even tearing off the synthetic skin on his face.
Kit flaunted the Taro card in his hand and handed it over, "Oh, thanks, brother Su Lun, you've done me a big favor!"
As Su Lun reached out to take it, a black hole in his hand swiftly sucked the card into his own little void realm.
Now, even with tracking methods, it would be untraceable.
Kit's card short-distance teleportation was not a Spatial Technique, but rather a special "Necromancy"—his profession as a necromancer magician.
Although not as convenient as Spatial Techniques, it was quite suitable in certain special scenarios, like the "reverse necromancy" just now.
Without planning to stay any longer, Su Lun said to Kit, "Now that communication has been cut off and the Taro card stolen, the people from the Titan's Hidden Cult are likely to make their move. There might be some big upheaval on the ship, so be careful."
Kit smiled broadly, "Alright!"
Su Lun didn't say more, forming a hand seal with one hand, as the space around him flickered.
The next moment, he reappeared beside the store room of the banquet hall.
And at this very moment, the banquet hall had descended into chaos.
Armed personnel, whether from the cruise security or from military intelligence, were searching for someone everywhere.
"That guy is still on board! Search! Find any suspicious individuals!"
"We absolutely cannot let him take the Taro away!"
"..."
In this vast sea, although "Phantom Thief Kit" seemed to have flown away just now,
Everyone knew that he must still be hiding on the ship.
And since Su Lun had earlier disguised himself as "Jack," now that guy had his alibi too.
Plus, with the stolen goods on Su Lun himself, they were certain to be unfound.
This case was destined to remain unsolved.
Su Lun straightened his clothes and quietly walked out of the corner.
At this time, his two disciples were still sitting in the corner on the sofa.
Abel was still practicing with the mechanical cube, utterly indifferent to the noise.
Karma, on the other hand, watched with great interest as people scurried to capture someone.
Su Lun walked over and sat down too, watching along.
He wasn't so much interested in the commotion but wanted to see what the "Titan's Hidden Cult" members had planned to do.
Up to this point, those people had not shown what exactly they wanted to do.
But it was certain that with a crucial "prop" like the [Hanged Man card] being stolen, their plans had been disrupted.
Su Lun even took a special look around, and that sixth-order Professor Virginia had disappeared.
Where she had gone was anyone's guess.
However, he felt sure that as long as that young master Alexis was here, the followers of the outer gods would definitely come.
...
The auction could no longer proceed with this sudden incident.
And of course, it was impossible to capture Phantom Thief Kidd.
Because Su Lun was watching that guy in the banquet hall, flirting with some rich ladies.
Normally, everyone would stay a bit longer, wait until those people confirmed that the stolen goods could not be found, and then they would all head back to their rooms to sleep.
But just then, Karma suddenly furrowed his brow as if he sensed something and said, "Teacher, it seems like something bad has happened."
Hearing this, Su Lun turned his head to look.
He hadn't forgotten that this disciple's talent was [B-098-Sixth Sense], with a special ability to sense omens of good and bad.
Remembering this, Su Lun took out a black umbrella from his hand, extending his perception, and indeed found that something had changed in the cabins below.
Some souls that clearly belonged to humans suddenly became distorted.
Abel, seeing the gravity on Su Lun's face, also asked, "Teacher, is a battle coming?"
Su Lun nodded, "I'm afraid so."
The followers of the outer gods surely wouldn't hinge all their plans on a single Taro card. Now that the card was stolen, certain plans still had to go ahead.
And not far away, that gangster big shot Caroline, who had come to flirt earlier, seemed to have sensed something as well and was looking in their direction.
Just then, suddenly, screams erupted outside.
Then, a barrage of gunfire rattled off at once.
"It's bad! A bunch of deformed monsters have appeared in the hold, and they're biting anyone they see, now they're charging toward our upper decks!"
"Damn it, those who got bitten turned into monsters too, and there are more and more of them... Ah, help me!"
"Quick, block the passage! Monsters, lots of monsters are swarming up from the lower cabins!"
"Damn it, monsters are climbing up the outside of the ship!"
"..."
It only took less than a minute from the discovery of the monsters to the outbreak of intense gunfire.
The group of finely dressed nobles in the banquet hall hadn't understood what was happening when they saw the ship's security guards with guns firing wildly outside the ship.
At this moment, panic was the only thing on the faces of these nobles.
They didn't know what to do, each one like a frightened headless fly, unable to sit still or stand at ease.
The students from the royal academy, however, reacted rather well. After all, most of them were second-order professionals, and they regularly participated in extracurricular activities hunting deformed monsters and magical beasts.
Now, listening to the unidentified monster surge breaking out on the ship, they each pulled out various luxurious equipment, readying themselves for a big battle.
The young master Alexis, however, glanced over at Su Lun.
Because of the card Kama had previously handed over, Su Lun was also extra cautious.
He guessed that this monster tide might be targeting him.
The footsteps outside grew more hurried, the sounds of guns and screams drawing closer.
From the lower cabins all the way up, it seemed they were quickly approaching the level of the banquet hall.
Su Lun was carefully sensing the movements downstairs, pondering to himself, "Not moving too fast, can climb walls, people will be infected after being bitten... a kind of blood-transmitted zombie variant?"
So far, it seems there's no threat.
But he couldn't make a move right now.
It was already known that there was a bishop of the Giant Hidden Society on board, a Sixth Order professor, and more than thirty believers who hadn't shown up yet.
This monster tide was clearly just the beginning of the conspiracy.
And the ship's defensive force wasn't weak either, so there shouldn't be big problems in the short term.
Su Lun thought about it and didn't plan to just passively wait for the enemy to unfold their conspiracy; he had to actively gather some intelligence.
He said to the two disciples beside him, "Kama, Abek, the emerging monsters aren't very strong, you two stay here, I'll go down and take a look. Hmm... be careful, and act according to the situation."
Both of them nodded, "Okay, Teacher."
As Su Lun spoke, he found a corner out of the line of sight and teleported down.
...
Downstairs was the cabin area where Su Lun teleported to.
He knew that rooms V3011, A2066, and B1066 had special prohibitions, housing several waves of Outer God followers. He had previously refrained from entering the rooms for fear of startling the snake. Now that the event had erupted, it was a good time to check it out.
But not long after he arrived, as if they had sensed the breath of living people, several deformed monsters sprang out from around the corner of the corridor.
They looked somewhat like humans who had been skinned, their crimson muscle fibers writhing like living worms.
Su Lun assessed them at a glance; they seemed like ordinary people who had mutated into zombie variants, their strength not even reaching the first order.
No threat at all.
The only trouble was that the deforming factor was blood-transmitted, and one would be infected if bitten.
This was no different from his earlier prediction.
"Bang!"
"Bang!"
"Bang!"
Su Lun raised his hand and rapidly fired three shots, and the three deformed monsters fell to the ground in response.
Having easily dealt with the three monsters, he intended to proceed. However, to his surprise, the shattered "Spiritual Bodies" inside these three deformed monsters hadn't dissipated from his perception.
"Not dead?"
Su Lun noticed the anomaly and patiently stayed put to observe for a while longer.
Then, an eerie sight unfolded.
Under Su Lun's gaze, out from the hollow corpses of those three monsters slowly emerged worms as red as blood vessels. They stood up like blood-thirsty leeches, making one's scalp tingle.
"Are those the parasitic worms of that Outer God?"
Su Lun found them familiar because he had seen them twice before.
However, in the previous two instances, those worms died not long after their hosts did.
But now these worms were teeming with vitality, pouring out from the corpses' wounds in ever greater numbers.
"Evolved? Or has the strength of that Outer God been enhanced?"
Su Lun considered various possibilities.
Without intervening, he watched patiently from the side.
Then, right before his eyes, those three corpses, with the help of those red worms, started to stitch themselves together. They fused into one, flesh merging into a three-faced, six-armed deformed monster.
A face on the head, a face on the chest, a face on the abdomen...
The more one looked, the more disgusting it became.
Upon sensing again, the energy fluctuation of this deformed monster was significantly stronger than before when they were separate entities.
"Not only can't kill them, but also their corpses can merge, stacking their strength... now we have a big problem."
Su Lun, looking at the three-faced monster before him, finally understood the threat posed by those Outer God followers.
He had thought they were just low-level monsters that posed no threat.
But now, seeing them, he realized the problem was serious!
This three-faced monster posed no threat to Su Lun,
but what about a monster with three hundred faces?
Or three thousand faces?
Given the current situation, who knew how many passengers in the lower cabins had been contaminated.
The mere thought made it seem like it would turn into a living hell.
"Truly a cult! Not only are they targeting the young master Alexis, but they actually plan to sacrifice the whole ship?"
Su Lun, thinking of something, felt a surge of anger rising within him.
No wonder Mr. Jing always said that most Outer Gods are Evil Gods; they never considered humans, these "low-level creatures," to be life forms worthy of respect, at best they were just nourishment for faith.
Many ancient evil sacrificial activities involved living human sacrifices.
Su Lun watched the "Three-faced Monster" rise to its feet and cast his Flame Spell.
...
A few minutes later.
Su Lun, looking down at the deformed monster completely mashed into pulp at his feet, had a complex expression.
He switched on his communicator and spoke with seriousness, "Kama, Abek, be careful, if you can avoid killing those monsters, then don't kill them, or it will be troublesome..."
He had just tried various methods and found that these monsters, with red line parasites inside, simply couldn't be killed with physical damage from guns and swords; they'd instead merge into higher-level monsters after death.
Even magical damage was very limited.
Ultimately, to smash the creature to bits, Su Lun had to rely on "Haki," directly destroying its biological structure, which finally killed those worms completely.
But, not everyone can exude such an overbearing presence.
On a ship with five thousand people, Su Lun Jue figured that aside from himself and that sixth-level professor, it would be quite difficult to find a third person.
As soon as the situation erupted, it immediately reached an almost irreversible dire state.
These guys clearly had premeditated it!
Su Lun also suspected that followers of the Evil God probably had other plots in mind besides targeting that Young Master Alexis.
Seeing this, he didn't dare to delay any further and went straight to the rooms of those Outer God followers according to the plan.
....
Meanwhile, in the banquet hall on the top deck, chaos reigned supreme, resembling the terrifying scenes of a biohazard disaster.
The screams were as piercing as fingernails scraping a blackboard, even overshadowing the sound of gunfire, sending shivers down everyone's spine.
"Quick! Block all the stairway passages, we absolutely can't let the infected get up here!"
"Hurry, open the door, save us, the monsters are coming! Please..."
"We can't open the gate, they might already be infected!"
"Right, we must not open the door. It must be those dirty commoners who brought the mutants on board. Oh, damn it, I knew from the start that the cruise ship shouldn't have sold low-priced tickets!"
"..."
After sealing the passageways, the sounds of pleas, screams, and monsters feasting were incessant.
The terror weighed heavy on everyone's chest like a boulder, making it hard for anyone to breathe.
Nearly all who were qualified to attend the auction dinner were from the wealthy class staying in first-class cabins or above; nearly all of the cruise liner "Queen Rodrica's" security forces were concentrated here. The firepower was fierce, and although the monsters could climb the outer walls, they were being shot into the sea.
For the moment, it seemed they would not be able to climb up to this deck,
but for those in the lower deck economy cabins, there was no way out. The sounds of fighting indicated that some professionals mixed among the regular passengers were still desperately holding on.
They didn't know that the monsters they killed were quietly merging into even more terrifying beings like "Ten-Faced Monsters" and "Hundred-Faced Monsters" in the lower cabin areas.
While everyone in the banquet hall was fraught with tension, two people in a corner sat calmly on a sofa, quietly observing everything around them.
Kama had just received a communication from Su Lun and asked, "Abel, should we share the intelligence given by the teacher with them?"
Abel, still with an expressionless and indifferent face, said, "We can't tell them. There must still be followers of the Outer Gods among those people. If we speak up, we won't gain the trust of others, and it will put us in jeopardy."
He exuded the same absolute calm as Su Lun. After a pause, he added, "Besides, it's futile now. The focus of this incident is on the densely populated areas on the lower floors. If the teacher can't control it, everyone in this banquet hall is doomed."
Kama sighed upon hearing this, "Oh."
She knew the situation was just that.
But, if they didn't warn them, many innocent people would die.
Abel said nothing further, his gaze sweeping over the people in the banquet hall, and the Rubik's cube in his hand continued to twist and turn.
Just then, a woman in a black dress with a solemn expression approached quickly.
This was none other than Caroline Worster, the mob boss from Lington we'd seen before.
Seeing the two siblings sitting on the sofa but not spotting Su Lun, she spoke up, "Young man, where is your teacher?"
Abel glanced at her, seemingly uninterested in talking more, and simply replied calmly, "The teacher went downstairs."
"Oh."
Caroline also let out a slight sigh of relief.
The disciples were still here, so the person must not have left.
The situation had already spiraled beyond her control, and she knew from the get-go that she couldn't handle it.
She took a deep breath, praying in her heart, hoping that things wouldn't get any worse.
But, the followers of the Outer Gods hadn't made their move yet!
Caroline was already feeling suffocated by the immense pressure, her gaze fixed on the distant Young Master Alexis.
If this "Big Shot" really died, the consequences would be unthinkable.
However, quite unlike her anxiety, Abel and Kama remained seated calmly on the sofa.
As Caroline returned to her senses, she found their composure unbelievable.
Thinking about it, she asked, "Aren't you two nervous?"
At this, Abel countered with a question, "Why should we be nervous?"
Caroline was taken aback, thinking he was too young to understand the severity of the situation and added, "All these mutant monsters, maybe they will break through any minute now..."
Yet, as soon as she said this, Abel retorted, "If we 'get nervous,' will it stop the monsters from coming up?"
"..."
Hearing that and catching the look on the siblings' faces as if they were gazing at idiots, Caroline's eye twitched abruptly, and she turned her gaze to the siblings as if looking at monsters.
A second-level and a first-level... remaining calmer than her, a fourth-level?
Where did they get such confidence from?
But then, her gaze shifted to the mechanical puzzle cube in Abel's hand, which he hadn't stopped twisting even while speaking, as if she understood something.
This level of calm and composure almost made her see the shadow of that man from before.
Exactly the same!
Caroline thought Abel had a sharp tongue and despite his youthful face, he gave off the impression of being as unfazed as an old creature, with no secrets hidden under his bare skin.
She knew this kid was not easy to fool and turned to Kama, saying, "Oh, your teacher is the most gentlemanly man I've ever met. He must also be a powerful professional..."
She was trying to dig for more intelligence in case he was some top-tier professional so she could feel more confident.
But unexpectedly, Kama just gave her a look.
Then they locked eyes.
And there was no then.
Caroline: "..."
The atmosphere turned somewhat awkward for a moment.
The woman wanted to pry further, but just then, Abel noticed something, and his fingers playing with the cube abruptly stopped.
He suddenly said, "Sister, prepare for battle!"

chapters.title: Chapter 424 - 423: Siblings
chapters.content:
Albert put away the mechanical Rubik's cube and switched to a pair of black iron mechanical gloves.
Kama did the same.
However, hers were a pair of white ones, finely crafted and taking into account a young girl's aesthetic preferences.
These gloves had been made by Sulenty tailored to their habits for practicing control over thread and puppets as mechanical substitutes. They were more suitable for certain high-strength steel wires.
Caroline peered at the complex gears and mechanisms on their gloves, puzzled about what exactly their professions were.
They looked like close combat gauntlets, yet also something a mechanic might wear.
However, she was more surprised that this sharp-tongued brat had noticed the abnormality before she had?
Caroline's face had already taken on animalistic features like Catwoman. Sniffing, she could smell those monsters approaching.
As she was about to ask, Albert spoke first, "Ma'am, could you please inform those people that those mutated monsters are blood-borne zombies, and if bitten, one will be infected. It's best not to kill them, because conventional means can't kill them. Moreover, after a wound, they will fuse into even more formidable creatures. By then, the people here will face increasingly terrifying monsters..."
Caroline frowned at hearing this, "How do you know that?"
While twisting the spring on his mechanical glove, Albert calmly replied, "My teacher told me."
"..."
Caroline quickly understood what was going on.
Were these young ones putting her in the frontline?
She was well aware that as soon as she revealed this information, she would attract attention from those followers of the outer gods and might immediately be in mortal danger.
So you knew it was too dangerous to speak out, and you let me take the hit?
How could you be so scheming at such a young age?
Caroline's expression grew peculiar.
In any other situation, she would absolutely refuse.
But the current situation had spiraled out of control. If the monsters were as deathly converging as they said, failing to act could lead to an irredeemable situation.
With that thought, Caroline gritted her teeth and agreed, "Fine!"
...
Just as Albert and the others had detected something amiss, trouble inevitably occurred.
"Damn it! There's a monster!"
"Damn! Weren't all passages sealed off, how are there still monsters, check where the defense has failures!"
"Be careful, these mutated beasts might have been man-made!"
"..."
The banquet hall hadn't quieted down for long when several monsters fell from a dark spot on the ceiling, no one knew where they had crawled from.
Before Caroline could even open her mouth to warn, a barrage of gunshots rang out, and the monsters were shot into a sieve.
The corpses heavily fell to the ground, splattered like smashed watermelons, and blood covered the floor.
The shooters were students from the Royal Academy of Ruein, equipped with top-tier firearms and an abundance of alchemical bullets. Marksmanship was also a mandatory course, thus their aim was flawless.
A few shots later, these barely first-level zombie types were immediately shredded.
"Hahaha, these monsters are so weak, they pose no threat at all."
"Exactly, I see no need to block the passages anymore, just let the monsters in, we have enough ammunition to clear the whole ship."
"Tch, no need for alchemy, handguns do the job, all that fuss for nothing, made me worry for nothing. Those commoners really are weak..."
"..."
Having killed a few mutated beasts, these young students were full of confidence.
Initially, they had only heard noises, not expecting the monsters to be so frail.
Everyone breathed a huge sigh of relief.
Even a few bold students approached the corpses of the monsters, using their rods to examine what exactly the creatures were.
Seeing this, Caroline's face drastically changed, she yelled out at once, "Be careful, don't touch those monster corpses!"
Common mutated creatures indeed weren't formidable, but if they were mutated from professionals, they would be much more troublesome. She didn't want these students to get infected.
Her loud shout drew questioning glances from everyone.
Not delaying any further, Caroline hastily relayed the information Albert had previously spoken about, "Everyone, do not kill those monsters, they will merge and revive..."
After listening, everyone in the banquet hall was skeptical.
But soon, someone challenged, "Who are you? How do you know so well?"
Obviously, the outbreak of the mutated contamination on this "Rodrica Queen" cruise was peculiar, spreading rapidly in the lower decks, clearly manipulated by someone behind the scenes.
Suddenly, a person who understood the characteristics of the monsters so well inevitably aroused suspicion.
Moreover, when these monsters are so easy to kill, why instruct us not to kill them?
This motive couldn't help but raise doubts.
Caroline also knew she was suspected.
From the moment she spoke, she predicted this outcome.
Her gang lord identity worked well among the ordinary class, but in the eyes of these nobles, she was no different from a sewer cleaner, handling dirty, secretive matters. Speaking out, there was hardly any persuasiveness.
Initially intending to wait until the monsters merged to reveal the truth,
before that could happen,
just then,
someone suddenly shouted.
"Grab her, she knows too much, this mutation contamination definitely relates to her!"
With that, no chance for explanation was given, several figures swiftly charged at her.
Caroline knew these people were probably followers of the outer gods, and there might be others who misunderstood and wanted to help. But at this critical moment, she naturally couldn't afford to be captured and had to fight back.
With a pinch of her sorcerer's seals, her body's muscles bulged, completely entering a beast-like form, and her fingernails turned into sharp blades.
With a leap, her body was as flexible as if boneless, performing a complex backflip, dodging the cold shots fired at her.
At the same time, Caroline's subordinates also stepped forward to help, and the two groups instantly started fighting.
"Hmph! This woman definitely has something up her sleeve!"
"They have accomplices too!"
"Kill them, be careful they might sabotage us!"
"..."
Most people felt the battle had started bizarrely.
It was just a few monsters being killed, so why had internal strife broken out among them?
However, since both parties made sense just now, most people maintained a neutral stance and watched the fight.
...
Meanwhile, in a corner on a sofa, the Kama siblings were checking their gear.
Seeing the sudden fight, they were not surprised at all.
Kama muttered, "Albert, you were right. If we had spoken up just now, we probably would have been the ones attacked."
Albert's young face remained expressionless as he glanced at the beast-transformed Caroline and said, "So it's the 'C-011-Catwoman' talent. This aunt is really strong."
Kama shrugged noncommittally and then looked on, "Albert, should we help out?"
"Can't help."
Albert shook his head and added, "Don't worry, that aunt isn't so easy to kill. Besides, if she really wanted to save that Duke's son, she would have clashed with these people sooner or later. With the situation unclear, it's good for her to draw those people out."
Kama's eyes flickered with agreement and then said, "So what do we do now?"
Although Albert's expression did not change, his eyes were constantly observing the battlefield, and his mind swiftly deduced various scenarios.
After a moment, he said, "We just wait here. It's best to stay away from that Duke's son. Once the monsters rush in, he will definitely be the focus of their attention. Then, try to stay alive until the teacher settles the battle in the cargo hold."
Pausing, he added, "Of course, if the teacher can't handle it, then we'll have to prepare to run."
Kama pursed her lips, "..."
She felt that her brother was really becoming more and more like their teacher.
During battles, he was as calm as a machine.
It seemed like Kama had guessed his thoughts, and Albert continued, "Teacher said that in battle, we need to shed unnecessary emotions. Pity, mercy, reluctance, hesitation... all emotions that will put us in danger."
Kama rolled her eyes and retorted, "Albert, you're really becoming more like the teacher. The problem is you're not as handsome as him. Continuing like this, you might never have a girl like you."
"Girls?"
Listening to this, a look of maturity beyond his years flashed across Albert's face, a smirk of disdain on his lips, "That would only affect my speed in controlling puppets..."
However, what responded to him was a fierce knock on the head from Kama, his elder sister, accompanied by an angry roar, "How could you! Albert, you are meant to carry on the family name for our Boyer family!"
In an instant, Albert's aloof schoolboy demeanor collapsed as he pleaded, "Sis, don't hit my head~ It hurts!"
...
From the bodies on the ground, red parasites were emerging and starting to merge.
However, most people's attention was captured by the increasingly intense fight between the two groups in the banquet hall.
Just when someone noticed the change in the monster bodies,
suddenly,
a new crisis arose!
A large amount of stirring noise came from the storage room behind the banquet hall, as if something was swarming in.
Immediately, several extremely panicked security personnel ran out of the kitchen, "It's bad! Someone opened the vent of the prep room, and a lot of monsters have rushed in; we can't hold them off!"
Following their words, several swiftly moving aberrant monsters had burst out behind them.
No sooner had their words fallen than someone shouted, "Damn it, it must have been that woman's sabotage. We must kill her first!"
Another person bellowed, "Open fire, kill those monsters, don't let them in!"
Bang!
Bang!
Bang!
The sound of gunfire erupted instantly.
It proved that humans tend to exhibit conformist behavior in panic.
During this critical juncture, the disciples of the outer gods didn't give people a chance to think and judge, continuously leading everyone in the banquet hall to fight.
Seeing the tide-like monsters continuously pouring out of the kitchen, once someone fired the first shot, then everyone started shooting.
Crisp like rain, the gunfire was dense.
The air was filled with splattering blood plasma, and various bodily fluids floated in the air.
Seeing this scene, Albert quietly put on his gas mask and muttered softly, "I knew this would happen."
"Ah..."
Kama also sighed lightly and put on her gas mask.
After a round of gunfire, the entire kitchen had been shattered by alchemy bullets.
The cadets from the Royal Academy had studied emergency tactics; at this moment, they took out shields and a variety of firearms and set them up.
This round of firepower was mostly contributed by them.
Such focused firing, even high-ranked professionals could not withstand it, let alone a group of low-level monsters that were instantly extinguished.
After a moment, the gunfire ceased.
Looking around, the sight was gruesome.
The area around the kitchen was covered with crimson blood plasma and scattered limbs. Like meat mush in a grinder several meters thick, it was impossible to tell how many monster bodies were piled up there.
Seeing the monsters being repelled again, the cadets were somewhat excited, feeling a great sense of achievement.
"We drove the monsters away?"
"Hahaha... I told you so, that's all there is to these monsters. I don't think we should hide here any longer, let's go and clear out the monsters below."
"..."
But before they could celebrate further, someone noticed something odd.
"No, look! Something is wriggling in the bodies!"
"Damn it, these things won't really fuse together, will they?"
"..."
In an instant, they vaguely guessed that the woman just now hadn't been lying.
Unfortunately, it was too late.
...
Caroline was still tangled up with several people when suddenly, countless red thread-like parasites emerged from the bloody flesh on the ground.
The more flesh and blood from the corpses, the quicker the monsters fused together.
Then, the several hundred people in the banquet hall watched as one after another "multi-faced monster" revived and stood up again.
Everyone then realized that these monsters truly couldn't be killed.
"Physical attacks are useless! Quickly use the Fire System Spell and burn them all!"
Someone quickly realized something and executed the Fire System Technique.
But ordinary flames were utterly useless.
Then came freezing, lightning strikes... all sorts of methods were deployed.
All to minimal effect.
It was only then that people realized, what the woman said was right; if these bugs didn't die, the mutated monsters wouldn't die either.
"Don't shoot, these monsters become more dangerous the more you kill them!"
"If we don't kill them, what do we do, just watch them infect us?"
"Damn it, what should we do now! Someone save us..."
"Don't jump into the sea, there are monsters there too!"
"..."
When people realized the monsters couldn't be killed, despair spread instantly.
What's more terrifying, they destroyed several "multi-faced monsters," but the pools of their flesh instantly fused again into an even more terrifying "Hundred-Face Meat Mountain."
That monster was like a mountain of flesh, ten meters tall with human skin faces and eyes that looked like tumors, making everyone's scalp tingle.
Several hundred people in the banquet hall gradually became infected one after another; even those who jumped into the sea saw massive blood worms in the water, resembling gigantic sea anemones.
To jump from the ship meant death, and not jumping was waiting for death.
The attendees from the royal academy who previously thought they were well-armed and confident were now just frantically huddling together in terror. The meat mountain monster was slow, allowing them to hold it off for a while. But, as more and more people got infected around them, they realized that death had descended upon this cruise ship, and there was no escape.
At this moment, Alex remained relatively calmer than his fellow students.
He didn't reveal his guard but coldly observed everything around him. The situation was becoming increasingly complex, appearing to involve several factions, making it hard to identify who the real "mastermind" was.
Moreover, his guard also suggested his judgment: today, the situation was far more likely to end badly than well.
Alex, after all, was the heir to a top noble family, possessed a level of rationality and thoughtfulness beyond his age.
The Tarot cards in his hand continued to turn, his divination unceasing.
Suddenly, his gaze shifted to the other side of the banquet hall.
He hadn't forgotten someone had passed him a message earlier.
With that look, Alex's gaze instantly froze there.
...
The number of monsters in the banquet hall only kept increasing.
Albert and the Kama siblings couldn't stay out of it either.
They could only fight while dodging.
They clearly had a definite route for evading; wherever the royal academy students went, they went the opposite direction, staying as far away as possible.
The siblings' method of fighting was also completely different from others.
They didn't shoot or slash.
The mechanical gloves in their hands drew out slender rune steel wires, then they wrapped up all the mutated monsters that came their way and hung them in the air.
Since these were just lower-tier mutated monsters, they weren't much trouble, just numerous.
In no time, this corner of the banquet hall resembled a spider's lair, with twenty or thirty monsters hanging mid-air on wires. Although they struggled constantly, they were utterly unable to act viciously.
This truly set an example for everyone in the banquet hall.
So this was how to deal with the monsters?
Could it really be that simple?!
After all, the banquet hall was only so large; even if the two were low-key, the commotion there drew everyone's attention.
The students from the royal academy looked over one after another.
"Look over there! My God, those two actually got the monsters under control."
"Eh... isn't that the country girl who sent Alex a love letter? Apparently, she's incredibly capable."
"Yes, these solid fundamentals couldn't possibly be the product of those second-rate academies. No, not even our academy perhaps..."
"Eh... what professions are they, using threads as weapons?"
"..."
People then realized that those they thought were simple country folks were actually experts whom even these elite had to look up to.
Watching that method seemed simple, just using a few steel wires to tie the monsters up. But anyone knowledgeable immediately saw that the siblings' skill in controlling the threads was extremely proficient.
Such skilled maneuvers couldn't be achieved without ten or eight years of rigorous practice.
....
But regardless of the surprise, the monsters didn't give the people in the banquet hall any time to breathe.
Luckily, following the example set by the Kama siblings, the other students also came up with ideas on how to cope.
Even though they didn't know how to control threads, they thought of various Alchemy techniques: Vine Technique, Swamp Technique, Freezing Technique, Quicksand Technique...
The results were good.
But that didn't include the "Hundred-Face Meat Mountain."
If everyone had started out by controlling monsters this way instead of killing them, we would not have ended up being so passive.
Now, the "Hundred-Face Meat Mountain" has become unstoppable, and it's essentially unkillable at this point.
The attacks of lower-rank professionals are like mere scrapes; even the attacks from third or fourth-rank professionals can be healed in an instant.
Moreover, it keeps devouring other monsters and merging into an even larger mass of flesh.
Albert's performance was so "excellent" that it even caused the terrified noblemen and ladies in the banquet hall to run towards him and his sister for safety.
Seeking refuge is one thing, but they also noticed that there were the fewest monsters near Albert and his sister.
Some people vaguely realized that these monsters seemed to be specifically targeting those from the Royal Academy.
...
Albert frowned as he looked at the people suddenly rushing over for refuge and cautioned the Kama siblings, "Sister, be careful, there might be cultists of the Outer Gods among them."
Kama nodded and carefully scrutinized the group that had run over.
At that moment, one guy in the crowd, showing a blatant will to survive, swiftly darted out from among them and hid behind the siblings first.
Kama looked at the cowardly expression on Keith's face and muttered softly, "Senior, is this really a good look for you?"
She had always thought this senior was quite charming, but now this...
"You're still young and don't understand. This way those ladies won't bother me anymore."
Keith smiled and naturally slipped into a corner.
Kama: "..."
Albert: "..."
The siblings knew very well that although it seemed like Keith came to seek protection, in reality, this senior from the Dawn Group was protecting them.
The cultists of the Evil God would definitely eliminate anyone who tried to obstruct their plans.
Sure enough, one guy in the crowd suddenly raised a gun and pulled the trigger on the twenty-odd disfigured monsters that were bound by silk threads.
This guy's shooting was accurate; almost one bullet per creature, and he quickly destroyed all the monsters that Kama and her brother had barely managed to contain.
Blood splattered everywhere.
With that, everyone understood that the person who was shouting and encouraging the fight earlier was the "hidden mastermind."
Albert reacted extremely quickly. As the man started shooting, he yanked at the steel wire in his hand and instantly decapitated him.
Meanwhile, among the crowd, there were also cultists trying to assassinate the siblings, but before they could make their move, Keith, hidden in the shadows, flicked a card and silently pierced the man's heart.
As the suspended monsters were killed, blood parasites began to spread.
Kama and Albert's previous efforts were in vain.
The real tough battle had begun.
Both siblings simultaneously took out a sealing scroll and tore it apart.
Dozens of puppets formed a guard around them.
Before those "multi-faced monsters" could approach, the puppets formed a barrier of silk threads.
Their puppet controlling skills, having been perfected by Su Lun's teachings and their hard practice these days, now came into play.
Binding arms and legs separately, using various anti-joint control techniques, and manipulating the silk down to the fingers and toes... none of the approaching monsters got close before being suspended once again.
This scene left everyone in the banquet hall astonished.
No one had expected that the previously unremarkable siblings were actually two Puppet Masters.
And moreover, their move involved dozens of puppets, which was no small feat!
The students from the Royal Academy were gobsmacked.
Under the siblings' aura of genius, their pride and superiority as noble students completely vanished.
The chubby student who had previously mocked Albert felt a chill at his neck.
He now understood that the others were not just taunting back then, but genuinely disdaining a duel.
If it really came to a fight, his own head might have been cut off by the steel wire just like that gunman's was.
Caroline, who was still struggling in the fight, finally realized, thinking, "So they had this kind of strength, no wonder they were so composed."
Meanwhile, she looked forward to meeting "Mr. Nicholas" with a bit more anticipation.
If the disciples were this formidable, the teacher must be extraordinary as well.
...
Meanwhile, in the cruise ship's cargo area.
While the banquet hall was engaged in a fierce battle, Su Lun had already eliminated several rooms of Outer God cultists.
After reaping some fragmented souls, he discovered that the cultists' goal was not only to kill the young master Alex but indeed to secretly sacrifice almost five thousand people on the cruise ship.
It was all merely to restore strength to that Outer God.
Following the magical arrays set up by these people, Su Lun made his way to the cargo area below deck.
At this moment, thousands of passengers in the lower deck compartments were almost completely infected.
Only then did Su Lun realize that it was more than just an infection.
The passengers' souls and flesh were also converging together.
In the cargo area, a huge, horrifying space had formed. The ship's walls were covered with red worms like blood vessels, densely packed and enough to make one's scalp tingle.
These worms were transferring energy to the center of the cargo hold, which had turned into a blood pool.
A massive, blood-red Crystal Core was floating above the blood pool, emitting a sinister glow.
"Thousand-Men Blood Refining Crystal Core"
Details: "In the eyes of some evil deities, humans are just lower creatures that supplement nutrients for flesh; this is a crystal formed from an evil flesh-refining ritual, containing a large amount of vital blood and energy, capable of helping some flesh-related deities regain some strength."
Su Lun looked on, his gaze as sharp as a knife.
And opposite him stood a black-skinned woman who had hurriedly come to intercept him.
It was none other than the team leader professor from this Royal Academy, a sixth-rank professional, Virginia.
This woman was puzzled to see Su Lun suddenly appear here.
She couldn't understand how someone could have discovered the hidden blood-refining altar in such a short time.

chapters.title: Chapter 425 - 424: Killing, Harvesting
chapters.content:
"The Queen Rodrica" cruise ship had turned into a living hell in no time.
The fight in the banquet hall was intense, with multi-faced monsters pushing the people to their limits, and more and more were getting infected.
Suddenly, intense fighting erupted from below the deck.
"Thud!"
"Thud!"
"Thud!"
"..."
It was as if someone was firing cannons inside the hull; the exaggerated noise made the entire giant ship violently shake.
The lower-tier professionals who weren't very perceptive might not understand what was happening, but a fourth-tier professional like Caroline instantly realized something and was shocked, "A top-tier fighter is battling!"
She thought of "Mr. Nicholas," her eyes filled with disbelief.
Although she had guessed that he might be powerful, she hadn't expected the commotion to be so grand.
She also realized that what they had previously thought as a dangerous situation was merely a minor skirmish, the real fierce battle was still below in the cargo hold?
Caroline hadn't overlooked the possibility of other arrangements by the followers of the outer gods on the ship, but right now she had to protect that young master, Alexis.
Moreover, the cabins below were the most densely populated, with thousands packed together; it was unthinkable what monstrous horrors had manifested there.
If the "multi-faced monsters" above were nearly invincible, who would dare to go down?
At the same time, Caroline also sighed in relief.
She had been worried that he might deem the situation too hopeless and withdraw.
He had made a move, meaning he wasn't just watching from the sidelines.
Although she didn't know who Mr. Nicholas was facing, it was hard to imagine that without him holding back that powerful follower of the outer gods, this would probably be a completely disastrous outcome.
In her heart, Caroline prayed, "I hope he can win."
She glanced again at the siblings engaged in fierce battle, keeping an extra vigilant eye.
She now had to not only protect the young master Alexis, but also look after the two disciples of Mr. Nicholas.
Otherwise, if something unexpected happened, it would really be a disservice to that gentleman's efforts.
...
The noises of the battle from below the deck grew even more exaggerated, and now, even the lower-tier professionals could clearly feel it.
Alexis continuously flipped his tarot cards, but he could not divine any information about the battle.
But at this moment, he also realized something, "The one who's involved is at least a sixth-tier professional; it looks like Professor Virginia really is problematic. But who might the other party be?"
Under normal circumstances, with the situation being this dire, as the leading professor of the expedition, she should have shown up by now.
Being a sixth-tier professional herself, she should be able to handle this "multi-face monsters."
She even had the capability to turn the tides.
But she was nowhere to be seen.
Therefore, one of the parties in the cargo hold's fight must be her.
And by now, the conspiracy had become completely clear, someone had used the "Hanged Man" card to lure him onto the ship.
To dare to strike knowing the expedition leader is a sixth-tier, they must either have overwhelming power or... there's something wrong with this sixth-tier.
The tarot cards told Alexis the latter was more likely.
Meanwhile, the battle at the bottom of the ship shocked not only the passengers on the cruise ship but also the followers of the outer gods who plotted this scheme.
Normally, the Archbishop and Cardinal Vigilia would have joined forces and subdued Alexis and his shadow guard in a moment, settling the fight.
But now, someone had directly gone to the hidden altar in the storages, and the Cardinal was entangled with a mysterious strong fighter?
This was unexpected.
Moreover, orders had already come through the communicator, instructing them to resolve the matter quickly.
Just at that moment, the gentlemanly middle-aged man with glasses who was hidden in the crowd, suddenly acted up and charged at the group of royal academy students.
"Be careful!"
Caroline's face changed drastically.
Although she knew this senior lawyer from Zero Degrees Special Jenkins Law Firm was a follower of the outer gods, she hadn't thought he was a fifth-tier!
Watching him charge towards Alexis, Caroline could no longer care for anything else; her exceptional agility as Catwoman allowed her to instantly break free from her opponent and position herself in front of him.
Unfortunately, the middle-aged man with glasses merely scoffed, and his iron fist clad in a leather glove smashed into Caroline's waist. This rapid punch shattered the air, visibly condensing a spiral ripple on the fist and exploded. Luckily, Caroline's cat-transformed body was extremely supple. With a flying cross hold, she caught the man's arm, using the momentum of the punch to deflect and throw him away.
Alexis, who was not far away, glanced at Caroline, his gaze revealing a trace of an upper-tier's indifference.
But at this moment, he was also sure; this woman was trying to help him.
If he could survive, he would surely need to thank her afterward.
"Bang!"
In a clash, the bespectacled man was hurled backward, about to crash into the banquet hall's pillar when suddenly, he flipped mid-air and tread on the air.
With a "snap" sound, the wall exploded half a meter away with web-like cracks.
On a further look, the man charged again.
Caroline still didn't dodge or evade, relying on her superior hand-to-hand combat skills and agility to engage him for several moves.
Unfortunately, the suppression from the major rank made it completely impossible for her to defeat him.
Experts brought by the guild were also entangled by the followers of the outer gods and couldn't lend a hand, and the group of students from the academy seemed paralyzed by fear, not even daring to shoot.
Caroline's eyes were filled with seriousness, and she was very aware that she couldn't hold on much longer.
Indeed, it was just a minor mistake, and she was caught by the man with glasses, who hammered her brutally. "Bang" "Bang" "Bang" his fists smashed into her body, sending her flying backward like a punching bag, her crimson blood already soaking the lapel of her wet dress.
However, Caroline did not retreat an inch, dragging her heavily injured body to charge forward once again.
She thought, if she died here and someone could get the message out, it would at least reduce some trouble for her big boss behind the scenes.
The man with glasses showed no mercy, seizing Caroline again and clasping her neck with one hand as if it were an iron clamp, continuously exerting force. The intense squeezing of his fingers against her delicate skin made sounds akin to bones cracking.
Caroline's face turned purplish, veins bulging on her forehead, ready to be strangled to death on the spot.
Just then, no one heard Alexis murmuring to himself from afar, softly chanting, "Move!"
At that moment, the expression of the man with glasses suddenly changed.
Because in his shadow, there suddenly appeared an assassin holding a black dagger!
Before the man with glasses could react, the assassin stealthily slashed a terrifying, wide gash across his neck, causing blood to spray out like a fountain instantly.
Caroline felt the powerful hand on her neck lose its strength instantly, and the choking sensation finally disappeared.
She fell to the ground, breathing heavily, feeling immensely relieved and lucky that this young master had brought a Shadow Guard with him.
But before Caroline could relax, her perspective from the ground allowed her to see the "dead body's" wound rapidly sprouting some flesh-like blood tissues, which upon closer inspection, turned out to be red parasites.
"Be careful of him..."
Caroline wanted to warn, but before she could speak, she couldn't help but spit out another mouthful of blood.
The Shadow Guard was no ordinary either; he didn't fail to notice the anomaly.
At the moment the man with glasses had his throat slit, he also delivered an extra blow, digging out the man's entire heart with his dagger and cutting it into several pieces.
Unfortunately, it also didn't prevent this guy's resurrection.
The man with glasses, completely ignoring the bullets firing toward his body, slowly stood up, the blood-colored parasites quickly connecting the cuts on his neck: "Heh heh heh, death is only the beginning... You lower beings, how could you understand the 'master's' greatness."
At that moment, a sinister black-patterned cross appeared on his forehead, and the aura around his body suddenly turned chillingly sinister.
Caroline smelled the scent of a monster, her face drastically changing, finally catching her breath, she urgently cried out, "Be careful, he's transformed into a monster!"
If it were human, there might still be a chance to kill him, but if it transformed into a kind of monster that couldn't be killed, what were they to do!
Not dallying, the Shadow Guard raised his hand and delivered several swift slashes, deftly dismembering the man with glasses' limbs.
This dagger was clearly no ordinary weapon; it harbored a corrosive, deadly poison.
With each slash, the monster's wounds would rot significantly.
However, the speed of the rotting could ultimately not keep up with the monster's regenerative speed.
The more he cut, the stranger the body of the man with glasses revived by the parasites became, even merging with nearby multi-faced monsters, gradually losing any human form.
The number of red parasites bursting from the monster's body grew increasingly numerous, dense like seaweed, trapping the Shadow Guard within.
The Shadow Guard's dagger swung more laboriously, cutting ten strands only for a hundred more to sprout, never-ending...
Seeing his attacks were ineffective, he could only retreat, merging back into Alexis's shadow.
...
"Damn it! More and more monsters are coming out of the ventilation shaft!"
"Who will save us... Professor Virginia, where are you? Please come and save us!"
"..."
For the vast majority of noble descendants, studying alchemy was merely a hobby and a necessary part of their education.
They had never experienced a real life-or-death crisis.
The lower decks were being overrun by an increasing number of monsters, creating an unstoppable, unkillable tide that left everyone struggling for breath in utter despair.
Moreover, the students realized that the majority of the monsters were targeting them.
No, they were targeting Alex!
After fighting for so long, these young nobles of Luying knew something was amiss and instinctively distanced themselves from Alex.
Even those who were normally close associates made the choice for survival, with only a few staying by Alex's side to confront the monsters together.
Though Alex's forehead was already covered in sweat, his expression remained calm.
His Shadow Guard was currently using a cursed dagger, surrounded by a green ghostly fire, which was temporarily keeping him unharmed.
However, it was unlikely to hold for long.
The dagger exhibited ghostly fire abilities beyond its rank but also drained the life of the Shadow Guard.
Just as Alex had resolved to fight to the death, suddenly, he noticed a disturbance on the other side of the banquet hall.
...
From the beginning, by intentionally avoiding the young master Alex, the Ablok siblings faced relatively little pressure.
Moreover, with Phantom Thief Kit secretly protecting them, there was no real threat to their lives.
Hearing the intense noises coming from the cargo hold, Ablok suddenly said to Kama, "Sister, I'm going to use the 'Thousand-Mechanical Demon War' now."
Hearing him, Kama asked in confusion, "Are you going to help? Didn't you say you wouldn't help earlier?"
Ablok analyzed calmly, "I didn't help earlier because I was afraid of drawing attention. Now that everything that needed to be exposed has been, if we don't help and that guy gets killed, we'll be next. Moreover, if I'm not mistaken, these monsters acting so urgently probably means there's a situation in the cargo hold that's unfavorable for them. In other words, our teacher must be confident in defeating that sixth-rank enemy, otherwise the fight wouldn't be so fierce. If we just hold on for a little while, we should be able to see the victory. And since the monsters' attacks are merely physical, our Mechanical Demon War is specifically designed to counter that, so there isn't much danger."
As he spoke, he had already taken out several mechanical boxes and glanced at the young master Alex again, adding, "Since the teacher chose to cooperate with that woman, she certainly doesn't want this young master to die. That woman is seriously injured now, and the teacher can't spare any effort to help, so naturally, we can't just stand by and watch. While they still have some fighting capability left, concentrating our forces might help us hold out a bit longer."
The siblings knew that Su Lun had left them here instead of taking them into the mini void world specifically to give them a chance to train.
Of course, there was another force at play here, that was Phantom Thief Kit.
However, his methods were very unique, and using them would almost certainly reveal his identity as "Phantom Thief Kit." Naturally, they could not expose themselves unless absolutely necessary.
Having considered this, Kama also felt it made sense and responded, "Oh."
Then, she too took several mechanical boxes out of her Storage Ring.
This was their Boyle family's heirloom "Thousand-Mechanical Demon War," but the siblings were too low-rank to fully control it, so each sibling guarded a portion.
As soon as they took it out, the dense sounds of "click" "click" from interlocking gears erupted, and intricate mechanical compartments disassembled and covered their arms, then rune armor spread all over their bodies. Suddenly, long mechanical arms sprouted from their backs.
The moment these fantastical transformer-like enhancements were donned, their combat power surged immensely and could no longer be measured by ordinary ranks.
This is the advantage of a Puppet Master—if one possesses a sufficiently advanced puppet, their combat power can skyrocket immediately.
In an instant, dozens of extraordinary arms, like long spears, charged toward the many-faced monsters and that "Hundred-Faced Beast."
The mechanical arms of the [Thousand Arms War Demon], utilizing various gear winches, each matched the strength of three to four power-type professionals.
The siblings simultaneously controlled dozens of mechanical arms to break into the mass of monsters, coordinated a few arms, and managed to subdue several beasts. They did not kill them, for as soon as the mechanisms on the arms activated, various hinges and ropes shot out, restraining each monster tightly.
The mechanical arms were not at risk of being infected by the monsters, and soon more than ten arm tips transformed into sharp rune spears, piercing into the flesh-mountain-like "Hundred-Faced Beast."
The spears, engraved with fourth-tier [Breaking the Firmament Rune], could easily penetrate the elemental barriers of fourth-tier professionals. Against such clumsy monsters, almost every stab was accurate.
"Hiss," "hiss," "hiss"...
Blood plasma erupted, the monster was pierced with many bloody holes, and several mechanical arms even penetrated the thick body of the beast, firmly embedding into the floor.
It was somewhat like embedding steel bars into a pile of mushy mud, and although it didn't completely immobilize it, it prevented the mud from moving flexibly.
The Aberc siblings knew well that the monsters could not be killed.
They did not have any delusions about inflicting severe damage on the "Hundred-Faced Beast"; they simply used various steel ropes to securely trap it.
With this massive creature controlled, the pressure on the surviving people in the banquet hall was greatly reduced.
However, at the same time, those watching the siblings maneuvering dozens of mechanical arms were left speechless in amazement.
Are all Puppet Masters this outrageously strong?
...
In the lower cargo hold of the "Queen Rodrica" cruise ship, the battle was intense.
Just as Aberc had guessed, Su Lun tested and found that he indeed had a chance to kill this Professor Virginia.
"Tsk, tsk... Second form of [C-001-Magic-Banisher]. Lucky it's me dealing with you; otherwise, ordinary folks really couldn't handle it."
Su Lun looked at the panting dark-skinned woman in front of him and felt that this giant from the reclusive sect was really unlucky to have encountered him.
