He projected his Soul Perception outward, enveloping the first-floor dance floor, the second-floor private rooms...and everyone in the office area.
There were quite a few experts, two at the fourth rank, seven or eight at the third...they seemed to mostly be from the Vonn Brothers' association.
Naturally, Su Lun also noticed that he was being sized up, as unfamiliar faces were always noticeable.
At that moment, he deliberately took out a Crimson Potion and poured it into his own glass.
Sure enough, it wasn't long before a guy with a bright red comb-over came over, presumptuously saying, "Hey, boss, first time at Rolling Stone?"
As soon as he spoke, his mouth full of rotten teeth and the smell of decay, a clear sign of long-term use of hallucinogens, filled the air.
Su Lun glanced at the crow on the guy's shoulder and then at the inverted cross tattoo that was obviously new, and remarked lightly, "Nice pet. Death looks cool."
"Right? It's the latest fad in Lyndon with crow pets."
The guy with the comb-over was smug, pointing to the inverted cross on his forehead, "I think this tattoo is super cool!"
With that, he suppressed a sneeze.
Su Lun fanned himself slightly to dilute the odor around him and probed, "This tattoo, it's a symbol of some religion, right?"
The guy with the comb-over looked mysteriously and said, "Heard about the recent incident on the Queen Rodrica cruise ship, boss? It's the faith symbol of that cult."
He had immediately figured out that Su Lun was an old bird in the underworld and said directly, "Let me tell you, this is the trendiest tattoo on the streets. Amazing! The rich kids from the north city, they're the ones with the most..."
...
Su Lun just smiled and didn't say a word.
So it was a cult.
Indeed, the Outer God cult frightened decent folk, but to these already decayed guys, it was practically a messiah.
The more alternative and darker the stuff, the trendier it became.
Seeing that Su Lun wasn't talking and didn't want to be disturbed, the guy with the comb-over immediately stated his purpose, "Boss, need some Awakening Potion to spice things up?"
Su Lun replied indifferently, "I have some. And I can assure you, what you have can't compare to mine."
As he said this, he ostentatiously took out a Crimson Potion and waved it around.
The comb-over guy clearly recognized the potion and suddenly realized, "Oh, boss knows his stuff."
Su Lun looked unimpressed and said, "The stuff is good, but what a pity, that Bax guy's goods, they're diluted too much. The guy really lacks credibility."
Upon hearing a name from the gang circles, the comb-over guy lost all suspicion and defended, "This is top-notch stuff, production's very low. To be honest, if it weren't diluted, you might not even get your hands on it."
Su Lun's face showed disdain as he threw a stack of bills on the table, boasting, "Money is not an issue. Quality is what matters most."
The comb-over guy picked up on the hint and said, "Sorry, I don't have any on hand."
But worried about losing such a generous customer, he hesitated for an instant, then quickly said, "If you're not leaving just yet, there might be a shipment arriving tonight. I can keep some good stuff for you?"
"Oh?"
Su Lun mused to himself, was a shipment coming tonight?
He just had come to check out some leads, but it seemed he had stumbled directly onto one.
If there were goods coming, it meant someone would arrive?
He pulled out several bills as if to cover the expenses, impatiently saying, "Come find me when you get the goods."
The comb-over guy knew that look and glancing at Reina with a sly smile said, "All right. You have fun, boss, wait for my good news!"
...
Reina had been listening intently the whole time; only after the man left did she blink, a flash of reflection crossing her face.
But she didn't say much, just raised her glass.
Watching the man walk away, Su Lun quietly switched out his drink and clinked glasses for a cheers.
In the bar, there was no need to drink with delicacy; they drank in large gulps.
One after another, Reina, who had previously shown no change while drinking red wine, now had a tempting blush on her cheeks, seemingly slightly tipsy.
In the dance floor area, young men and women swayed their bodies unrestrainedly under the dim lights, exuding restlessness, passion, and sexy charm...
It was a rare visit, and she didn't know if she would come to such a place again. Reina pointed to the distant dance floor, hooked Su Lun's arm, and with an eager expression asked, "Mr. Su Lun, shall we go dance?"
She paused, then added weakly, "I haven't tried it before; I want to give it a go."

chapters.title: Chapter 429 - 428: Terrifying Wax Figure・Ghost Bride
chapters.content:
The music at midnight became even more passionate, thumping, thumping, thumping... It shook people as if their very souls were about to burst forth.
Su Lun looked at Lena, whose pretty face was brimming with excitement, and asked, "Do you want to go to the main dance floor?"
"Mhm."
Lena eagerly nodded and then, looking at Su Lun, counter-asked, "Can we?"
Having never been, she wanted to give it a try.
When someone is new and eager to play, that's probably the expression they have.
Seeing her look of anticipation, Su Lun smiled, stood up, and reached out his hand, "Let's go."
"Okay!"
Lena's face lit up with joy, super excited as she took his large hand.
Su Lun led the curiously baby-like girl out of their seats, and they made their way through the crowd, arriving at the center of the bar.
There was a dungeon-style stage here, where the famously rotten "Knight band" from Luying was performing live.
That dark and morbidly styled music was expressed through various instruments.
The clubbing scene in the alchemical world was wild, not just because of the cursed-like music but also because of the mental hypnosis. Su Lun noticed the tank-top wearing female DJ shouting into an alchemical microphone which was a cursed object. When activated, it would release a mild type of mental formula that caused excitement and agitation. However, the after-effects would leave people with continuous nervous weakness during the day.
But no one cared about that.
The bar-goers were all here to release the oppression in their hearts amidst the intensely frenetic music.
They were enjoying the moment.
Below the band's platform, there was a large dance floor, already teeming with people.
Groups of young men and women were indulging in frenzied revelry on the dance floor.
Linden was at the forefront of trends, the capital of fashion, and the young girls were not stingy in showcasing their beauty. They wore very sexy outfits, micro-skirts, low-cut tank tops, large expanses of skin exposed to the air... They swayed their graceful figures, utterly releasing their passion and charm.
And those young people with ear piercings and lip rings and a dark style were also swaying crazily with their eyes closed, immersed in their own marvelous and illusory world, hysterically.
Su Lun pulled Lena to the edge of the dance floor, and they looked at each other.
Lena had never tried it before and looked a bit timid.
But still unable to restrain the anticipation in her heart, she nodded.
With a slight smile, Su Lun led her onto the dance floor.
In an instant, Lena felt as if her entire sensory world began to shake.
The dance floor's flooring was made of flexible, bouncing wood. People swayed with the beat on it, like waves rising and falling on a board. If you didn't catch the rhythm of the rise and fall, it felt as though you were about to be flung into the air.
Initially stepping onto it, Lena was somewhat panicked, but Su Lun wrapped his arms around her, and they quickly adapted.
The DJ on stage was passionately hyping up the crowd, that mental contamination eroding everyone's nerves, leading them into excitement.
Experiencing it for the first time, Lena also began to excitedly raise her hands, shout, and sway after adapting to the rhythm.
Her happiness stemmed from not just the atmosphere but also the people around her, and that little bit of contentment in her heart.
Gradually, a trace of wildness appeared in her eyes.
The dance floor was crowded, with people rubbing shoulders with one another. Su Lun kept Lena in front of him, also noticing the happiness from the bottom of her heart reflected in her eyes, and he joined in the fun with her.
Under the dim lighting, the mood remained elevated.
The style of Rolling Stone Bar was dark dungeon.
As the dancing continued, the event organizers played a new trick.
The well-shaped female DJ was dancing hotly on stage when suddenly she ripped off the only vest she was wearing on her upper body, exposing large areas of skin to the air. The spotlight shone on her, causing a wave of jubilant cheers to erupt in the bar once again.
Witnessing such a bold and spicy dance, a trace of shyness flashed in Lena's eyes, but she also excitedly joined in with the noisy cheers.
Su Lun, on the other hand, was quite accustomed to it.
But what he didn't expect was the next thing the female DJ said, which caused him to look stunned.
"Next up, let's welcome our Puppet King—'Reaper'!"
At this call, the crowd below surged with excitement.
"Reaper!"
"Reaper!"
"Reaper!"
"..."
Hearing these shouts, and the titles Puppet King and Reaper, it was highly likely that no one else would bear that nickname.
Could it be that his arrival had been discovered?
Clearly, he was overthinking it.
At that moment, the music abruptly stopped, and the bar fell into sudden silence.
But at the same time, with a rustling noise, several human-shaped shadows plummeted from the sky.
The crowd shuddered with fright.
However, just as they were about to hit the ground, three meters below, the shadows were suddenly jerked to a halt.
The spotlight revealed that they were actually human-shaped puppets.
Connected by steel wires to the steel frame structure on the roof, they looked unsettling with strange postures. A flock of crows flew overhead with fitting cawing, and a cloaked figure wielding a huge scythe stylishly jumped onto the stage.
Then, a tide of cheers erupted from the crowd.
Looking at this spectacle, Su Lun couldn't help but twitch the corners of his eyes.
Crows, cloaks, black scythes, puppets... the props for this imitation show were all set.
Amidst the cheering, the person in the cloak suddenly started dancing awkwardly, and a group of puppets also began to dance with "clack clack" sounds.
Despite their clumsy puppeteering, the rigid dance moves of the puppets were oddly synchronized, creating a zombie dance-like eerie style.
Su Lun didn't quite know what to say.
But Lena, excited beside him, looked at Su Lun with eyes that seemed to speak, "Mr. Su Lun, come and see, they're imitating you too!"
She too excitedly cheered along with the others, without a trace of her previous ladylike demeanor.
Then, everyone in the dance floor began to awkwardly zombie-dance.
Boom, boom, boom...
The DJ picked up the beat, leading into a new wave of festivities.
The atmosphere grew increasingly fervent, the entire dance floor shaking intensely.
The dance floor was very crowded, and Su Lun, protecting Lena next to him, couldn't avoid body contact, but neither of them minded.
Song after song, and as they danced, suddenly the lights dimmed, and the rhythm of the music slowed down. Bathed in the dim red light, the atmosphere turned suggestive.
After an intense rhythm, there was a calmer dance tune.
Lena, not knowing what had happened, looked at the couples whispering sweet nothings beside her with curiosity. Following their example, she turned around and wrapped her arms around Su Lun's neck.
Su Lun smiled slightly and casually placed his hand along her waist, lightly holding her. Since he saw her as a friend, he did not overstep his bounds.
The two embraced and danced slowly to the tune.
Lena, as if drunk, almost completely collapsed against Su Lun, lost in thought.
As they danced, she suddenly took the initiative to move Su Lun's hand lower, then commanded in a firm tone, "You can put it here!"
Is that okay?
Su Lun was momentarily taken aback, realizing that his hand was caressing a soft sensation, their position suddenly becoming intimate.
Though separated by a skirt, the inherent soft and pliant feeling of Catwoman's body was undeniably real.
Feeling the warmth of the large hand that had climbed onto her protrusion, Lena glanced at him, then whispered against his neck, "I really don't mind~"
Her tender reproach dropped her ladylike restraint.
Su Lun also understood, his lips curving into a slight smile.
That moment, he came to the realization that the girl who once shared his hardships had grown up.
He knew that for this girl, pure as blank paper, to make such a gesture took quite a bit of courage.
So he did not withdraw his hand, but neither did he become more presumptuous.
But as they remained in that froze position for several moments, Su Lun clearly felt Lena's emotions gradually sinking, as if she was somewhat tentative.
She buried her head in Su Lun's neck, murmuring something in a plaintive whisper, "Really... I said... I wouldn't mind..."
With soft and gentle music, the dim dance floor, men and women indulged in the thrills of surging hormones.
A gentleman has to consider the scenario.
In some situations, a slight gesture of affection is a mark of respect.
Su Lun chuckled, understanding what was unsaid.
Do you like it?
Mhm.
After all, they were very close friends, weren't they?
Su Lun's hand flexed slightly, and he felt a firm softness in his grasp.
Such an intimate and presumptuous move, if not close enough, could invariably lead to a slap in the face.
But clearly, Lena in his arms didn't mind at all; instead, her mood suddenly became joyful.
She boldly took one of Su Lun's hands and placed it on her chest where her heartbeat was clearly felt.
The fine fabric lining was soft, and obviously without an undergarment, there was nearly no barrier to feeling the softness that begged to be kneaded, the details palpable.
Su Lun's night vision was superb, and she saw a face close by, radiating a brilliant smile.
Lena bared her white teeth in a grin, her eyes curving, a hint of playful charm glimmering within them as she suddenly became bold, "Ah~ Sabina sister was right..."
Su Lun felt a real touch on both hands and became curious, "What did she tell you?"
Lena's bright eyes shifted, glinting with mischief. She didn't directly answer but said meaningfully, "She said, Mr. Su Lun, you like the movement you're making right now."
As she spoke, her face revealed either a flush of shyness or the glow of tipsiness, a faint blush blossoming.
"???"
Su Lun listened with a mix of amusement and helplessness, his hands remaining in place.
Far from minding, Lena came even closer to facilitate his touch and continued, "Sabina sister also told me a lot about you, Mr. Su Lun. Mm... those things... I pretty much know them all."
Now Su Lun understood and complained, "She really has no filter. What has she been teaching you..."
Lena playfully stuck out her tongue, saying, "Sabina sister also said that Mr. Su Lun likes it when girls take the initiative. So I can't wait for you to make the move..."
Perhaps because certain barriers had been breached, her former subtlety was gone as she added, "It seems that's really the case, huh!"
Su Lun didn't bother explaining, simply finding the whole situation amusing and laughed lightly.
The dance floor was filled with an ambiguous atmosphere as bold young men and women danced closely in the dark.
Su Lun did not withdraw his hand, savoring the soft, graceful contours.
Still, the feel of it through the skirt was somewhat unsatisfactory.
Luckily, this punk Lolita dress was quite accommodating, with its light, soft hem being short in the front and long in the back. Lifting a corner, his hand could wander freely without anyone noticing a thing.
Once beneath the skirt, he encountered a sensation that was both silky and supple.
Black stockings, excellent!
Lena showed no inclination to dodge, her eyes slightly blurry, but after waiting for a while, she finally asked, "How does it feel?"
Su Lun answered truthfully, "It's terrific."
At his words, Lena seemed to finally relax completely, her smile blossoming on her cheeks like a radiant rose, "Ah... really? I was worried that you, Mr. Su Lun, only liked girls like sister Sabina... that type of..."
Su Lun simply smiled and shook his head.
Lena, sensing something, her cheeks warmed and she said obediently, "Ah... I was super happy just to see Mr. Su Lun today. Now I'm even happier~"
The darkness served as the perfect cover, concealing the flushed shyness.
...
After a lengthy slow dance, the music's tempo surged again, and a new performance began.
The impatient couples continued to retreat to the dark corners, the restrooms, the private rooms... to continue their intimacy.
Lena sneakily glanced at those people, her cheeks flushing as she latched onto Su Lun's arm, and the two returned to their seats.
With new glasses filled with liquor, they began to drink again.
The alcohol induced a slight buzz, and the mood was just right.
Su Lun found his time with Lena very enjoyable as well.
Suddenly, he perceived something, his eyebrows furrowing for a moment before he said to Lena, "Let's go check the back alley."
Lena obviously knew what he was talking about and nodded, "Okay."
Su Lun had sensed that Cock's Comb, the man who had been selling the potion, headed toward the back alley.
Not just him, several members of the Vaughan Brothers gang seemed to have received some order, all heading out through the back door.
Su Lun guessed that their shipment had probably arrived.
The two of them left their seats and headed to the security corridor near the restroom, without directly following the others. He noted that the gang members on lookout also paid attention to their departure.
Turning into an unoccupied corner, Su Lun took out a black umbrella, and his range of Soul Perception instantly expanded multiple times.
In his perception, the gang members were very cautious, frequently looking around to see if anyone was following them.
However, Su Lun's technique of Soul Perception would not be noticed by anyone.
He felt the direction of the gang members and, with Lena in his embrace, they chose a different path to follow.
The two avoided the crowded main streets, opting instead for the deserted back alleys.
Before long, they encountered a high wall they needed to climb over. Su Lun was about to jump over with Lena, but she laughed, refusing, and leapt up herself.
She landed lightly, making no sound at all.
Watching her, Su Lun remarked, "Hey... that's pretty impressive."
Lena happily responded, "Of course, I've grown stronger. I'm no longer that weak girl who always needs protecting."
Su Lun responded with a smile.
Soon, they arrived in front of a dilapidated warehouse.
A bunch of tattooed tough guys in black suits were at the entrance; Cock's Comb and his group had already gone inside.
There were clearly restrictions inside against probing, and even Rena's Catwoman talent could not pick up any sounds.
However, this couldn't stop Su Lun. His perception told him that there were more than twenty people inside, and the strongest among them was only a fourth-tier, likely the boss of the Vaughn Brothers gang, "Old Smoker" Fogleres.
It seemed like these guys were gathered here waiting for someone.
The two of them had the patience to lurk on the roof of the small building.
Rena occasionally stole glances at Su Lun, and the two would share a knowing smile.
The time spent lurking flew by quickly.
Half an hour later, a very distinctive soul appeared in his perception.
It was a person wearing a black trench coat that covered most of their face.
The several gang lackeys at the door obviously recognized him, not hindering him at all and letting the person walk in.
"Hehe, the goods have finally arrived. Hopefully, there's more this time."
"Tsk tsk... Even if it's just the same amount as last time, we'll make a fortune off this batch once it goes out."
"Don't you guys find the potion a bit weird? It's so cheap... I always feel like I hear strange whispers after using it."
"Bore, the hell's wrong with you, you high or something? Besides, who cares what it is, as long as we make money, right?"
"Tsk tsk, true that."
"..."
Overhearing the lackeys' exchange, Su Lun finally understood that the people delivering the goods had arrived.
But after a closer perception, he frowned, "Huh... that guy doesn't seem to be human?"
That soul fluctuation was very strange, making him feel it was somewhat like a vengeful spirit or some type of undead creature.
The two did not hurry to act rashly but continued to wait there.
About ten minutes later, the man in the trench coat walked out again.
Su Lun realized that this person might be extremely important.
He didn't bother with the gang members in the warehouse and signaled to Rena to keep an eye on the place while he followed in disguise.
A delivery person alone wasn't enough to prompt Su Lun to act; he wanted to follow and see if he could trace it to the source.
...
Lindon's night sky revealed no stars, only a depressing darkness.
Drizzle fell from the sky, and the continuous pitter-patter of raindrops was incessant beside his ears.
Su Lun followed very carefully, still using Soul Perception to gauge the direction and then tracking the other route.
In theory, such a method of tracking would be nearly flawless, and even high-tier professionals would struggle to detect it.
But as Su Lun walked down an alley and just stepped over a puddle of dirty water, he suddenly sensed something and whirled around!
His Soul Perception indicated that the person who was originally two hundred meters away had suddenly appeared right behind him!
There were no spatial fluctuations; the figure just appeared out of nowhere.
Su Lun retreated dozens of meters, looking somberly at the puddle where a humanoid shape slowly condensed on top of it. Water vapor around it rapidly coalesced, and in a blink, it turned into the man in the trench coat from earlier.
This person seemed surprised to have been followed, eyeing Su Lun with a click of the tongue, "Eh... you actually noticed. Tsk tsk, not a weak perception. I'm curious too, how did you manage to follow me?"
The voice was terrifying, but it seemed to be a woman's.
Realizing this ability, Su Lun understood something, thinking to himself, "Was it the rainwater that exposed me?"
However, he showed no signs of panic and tentatively said, "Your method is quite interesting. You can actually hide your elemental body in the water... could you be one of the four elemental talents, 'Raincaller'?"
At the same time, his left eye shimmered and rotated.
What was even more unbelievable was that the name identified by the All-knowing Eye was "Terrifying Wax Figure・Ghost Bride"!
Seeing this, Su Lun finally understood why he had previously felt like this person was not alive.
It turned out it really wasn't a person, but a wax figure?
He instantly thought of a description in a certain secret tome of a forbidden Puppetry Technique— "Spirit Medium Puppet."
This was not alchemy but black magic of those who worshipped certain undead external gods.
A god's disciple?
This was a puppet, which also meant there was a manipulator behind it.
Su Lun's face remained unchanged, as if he had noticed nothing.
But internally, he marveled, "Lindon truly is a place full of hidden dragons and crouching tigers!"
This "Wax Figure Puppet" not only had an abnormal soul but was also made to look exactly like a real person, complete with breath, flesh, intelligence, and most critically, it possessed the deceased's talents from before death?
Encountering such a fascinating opponent right away, Su Lun decided to thoroughly investigate this thing.

chapters.title: Chapter 430 - 429: Curator
chapters.content:
"Interesting puppetry technique..."
Although Su Lun had roughly guessed the origin of the puppet before him, he had not understood how it was being manipulated.
He felt no pull of strings, nor any fluctuation of energy, and thought that this "Terrifying Wax Figure" was probably a kind of black magic like Spirit Control.
"The spiritual intelligence doesn't seem too high; it must be direct soul control..."
Su Lun could sense the fluctuations of the soul. Typically, spectral guards like evil spirits had incomplete spiritual bodies and were not highly intelligent. It's probably like training a dog; long-term training of evil spirits could enable them to retain some of their abilities from when they were alive.
Before he could ponder further, the person in the trench coat not far away suddenly made a move.
Su Lun wasn't particularly alarmed; as long as it wasn't a Seventh Order professional, not many could pose a threat to him now.
With just a glance to the side, he saw the raindrops within tens of meters around his body suddenly freeze in mid-air. Each crystal-clear droplet trembled with high-frequency ripples on their surface, then morphed into the shape of willow leaf-shaped knife blades.
"Impressive control over water elements, and this technique is quite interesting as well..."
Su Lun narrowed his eyes slightly, silently remarking to himself.
"Swoosh!"
"Swoosh!"
"Swoosh!"
"..."
In the blink of an eye, those suspended raindrops shot towards Su Lun like bullets.
With full-coverage from every angle leaving no blind spots, it was impossible to dodge in the narrow alley, sounding like a fierce barrage of rain hitting banana leaves.
The raindrops tore through clothes, and some special drops even penetrated the protective elemental barrier, striking Su Lun directly.
Upon impact, the raindrops didn't completely disperse but swiped like knife blades across rock. Even if there wasn't much damage, the sharp sensation was distinctly felt.
This move, if confronted head-on by almost any professional below the Sixth Order, would result in severe injury if not death.
But Su Lun had the "Rune Golden Body" for protection, so it was akin to nothing more than scraping.
"What a sinister wax puppet!"
Su Lun stomped on the ground, charging through the sky full of arrows like a cannonball. He threw a punch and hit the man in the trench coat in the abdomen.
Yet, the punch that could shatter stones and split gold struck the target but felt like hitting a water bag. The force of the blow was dissipated by the layers of oscillating cushioning force, reducing its impact by ninety percent.
"Elemental Body!"
From this brief exchange, Su Lun had judged the opponent's combat strength to be about that of a Fifth Order professional. But, with the addition of the "A-004 Rain Prayer" type of affinity for the four basic elements, it was almost unbeatable among its peers.
At a nearly face-to-face distance, Su Lun also saw the face of the person in the trench coat.
It was a horrific face patched together with centipede-like stitches, jagged sharp teeth, and a neck skin that was a creepy dark cyan color. The face was covered with thick makeup foundation that couldn't hide the black blood vessels and livor mortis, adding an eerie touch instead. It also wore a white bridal headpiece on top of its head, with black lipstick and eyeshadow. Just as deduced, this was a "Ghost Bride."
And now, up close, Su Lun could see a thin layer of corpse wax on its body.
His punch had evidently caused no harm to the bride. He then made a move to leverage his body, swinging back a heavy kick that slammed into its head.
With that heavy leg, a "splash" sound was heard as the water balloon head burst open, spewing noxious black water everywhere.
The black water obviously had a strong corrosive toxicity, sizzling as it splashed on the ground and creating pockmarked holes after the smoke cleared.
However, even after its head was kicked to pieces, the "Ghost Bride's" presence did not wane. In an instant, it reformed a new head from the elements and fixed its empty gaze on Su Lun before it.
"Tsk, tsk... quite strong! I never thought a puppet could reach this level."
The more he tested, the more curious Su Lun became.
He was not only adept in puppetry techniques but also in animating corpses.
The abilities displayed by the "Ghost Bride" before him far exceeded those of the animated corpses, and were almost on par with a real person.
That tremendous affinity for elements certainly wasn't something simple Corpse Manipulation Techniques could achieve!
If he could capture it for research...
A thought suddenly crossed Su Lun's mind.
...
Clearly, capturing it alive was out of the question.
The "Ghost Bride's" intelligence clearly wasn't very high; it likely believed it could kill Su Lun. As soon as its head was reconstituted, it reached out with one hand, showing its long black fingernails.
```
In an instant, the spell was complete.
The water elements in the air formed a spherical water prison around Su Lun's body. No matter where he tried to escape, the water prison clung to him like a persistent ghost.
The water elements surrounding him became denser and denser, and Su Lun felt as if he had fallen into a pit of quickly drying glue, his movements becoming more and more difficult.
Not only did the spell restrict his movements, but it was also rapidly drawing water out of his body.
In a little while, he feared he would turn into a mummified corpse and die on the spot.
"Directional 'Water Element Stripping'? Quite a powerful comprehension of magic, at least the incomplete understanding of a sixth-rank law. It must be an ability that the corpse possessed in life. Which means, before death, this body was at least a sixth-rank professional, or even seventh-rank?"
Su Lun analyzed in his mind, finally feeling a tinge of the threat of death, "The soul fluctuation isn't very stable, so the resentful spirit inside it must not be original..."
He had to admit that this 'Ghost Bride' was truly strong. Its ability to turn into elemental form made it almost immune to any physical attacks, and its control over the basic elements was difficult to counter. The body's original elemental understanding had reached the sixth rank.
It could be said that any professional below the sixth rank stood no chance against it!
After a few exchanges, Su Lun had tested out some of the intelligence he wanted. Thinking that the puppeteer behind the scenes must have realized this too, he did not delay any longer and suddenly, his fist was wrapped in a layer of invisible energy.
He didn't even need to form the magician's seals for teleportation at this distance, and he teleported behind the 'Ghost Bride'. Without breaking a stride, he delivered a punch enveloped in domineering energy, blasting a hole in the chest of the monster.
"Boom!"
A punch pierced through!
For an elemental body, domineering energy was exceedingly effective.
Su Lun's punch didn't simply break the stable form of the water elements, but partially annihilated the elements at the microscopic level.
In recent days, he had mastered the use of domineering energy, and as he punched, Su Lun controlled the spiral of the energy to explode, blasting the upper half of the 'Ghost Bride's' body into fragments.
Under normal circumstances, this barrage would be enough to kill this wax puppet.
But before he could take a breath of relief, a bizarre scene unfolded before his eyes.
Though the target was critically hit and its presence dissipated for a moment, Su Lun didn't see the "gray mist" emerge.
"Not killed?"
He watched the black water scattered on the ground, puzzled.
Suddenly,
A few meters away at the sewer entrance, he sensed the familiar soul fluctuation again!
"Escaped?"
A twitch passed the corner of Su Lun's eye, not failing to understand what had happened.
The escape was decidedly swift; he wanted to pursue, but it was too late.
The 'Ghost Bride' had clearly realized that Su Lun had the ability to kill it. This time, without any hesitation, it reformed and chose to flee. Its ability to turn into elemental form disregarded terrain constraints. It dissolved into black water and flowed into the underground through the drainage pipes.
"Heh heh..."
Su Lun gave a self-deprecating laugh.
He had thought this was a sure victory, but unexpectedly, it had slipped away.
But more than that, he was perplexed.
"That shouldn't be right! How could it not have been killed?"
Su Lun contemplated, his punch with the domineering energy should not have allowed the 'Ghost Bride' to survive.
His mind raced, replaying what had just happened, he thought, "No, it didn't revive on its own! Was it some other mysterious force that reformed it just now?"
He quickly thought of some key points, his brain whirring into action.
Almost instantly, he remembered having seen such a situation before.
That time when he was exploring the Dawn Relic '1911 Hotel' cursed space, he encountered four unkillable oddities.
The evil black magic that had created the oddities was called 'Four Ghastly Spirits' Corruption Offering Formation,' which involved the collection of corpses with the characteristics of earth, wind, water, and fire. The final effect was an energy cycle that was self-sustaining and self-replenishing, achieving immortality.
If one corpse was killed, the others would revive it, creating an almost unsolvable closed loop.
No wonder it was used for delivery; such puppets are untouchable and undying, making them perfectly suited for the task.
"Could it be that the puppeteer behind the scenes has already gathered the four elemental wax figures?"
Su Lun frowned, feeling the level of difficulty had just escalated by several notches, "Undying and unkillable, these puppets are really formidable..."
Luckily, he only encountered one today. If there were four as he suspected, he would probably have to run.
```
But on the other hand, someone who can control such wax figures is definitely not a nobody in Lington.
Another practitioner related to the Puppetry Technique, the list of suspects narrows down even further.
...
Originally, the intention was to track down the source of the potion, but now that the delivery person has escaped, there's no point in Su Lun delaying any longer.
Plus, the person behind the scenes might send out a warning to the Vaughn Brothers Association since they discovered they were being tracked.
Goods of unknown origin, even the gangs wouldn't distribute them recklessly. At least Big Beard Fogleres, the chairman, must know some information about the supplier of this batch of goods.
Su Lun didn't want to let even the slightest clue slip away.
He sensed Rich Lady Lena's location, his hands swiftly gestured the sorcerer's seals, and after condensing the dark energy required for Directed Displacement, the space fluctuated for a moment.
When he looked again, he was already standing on top of that dilapidated building.
Rich Lady Lena was crawling on the rooftop with a sniper rifle, watching the warehouse through the scope. Suddenly, seeing Su Lun appear beside her, her crystal eyes shone, "Mr. Su Lun, you're back?"
As she spoke, she pointed to a few gang members near the warehouse door and quickly said, "Just now, they seemed to have received some message, and someone rushed in hurriedly."
Su Lun, hearing Rich Lady Lena's report, also guessed that his assassination had been exposed. He nodded decisively, "Be careful, I'm going in."
Then, thinking for a moment, he added, "If someone comes out, kill them. Try not to leave any survivors."
Rich Lady Lena nodded earnestly, "Mhm."
Su Lun didn't waste any more words and teleported again, appearing directly at the entrance of the warehouse.
Seeing an extra person suddenly appear caught the suited, tattooed musclemen by surprise, and before their expressions of astonishment could turn into vigilance, a bloody line formed on their necks.
A burst of blood sprayed out like a human fountain, and only then did the bloody, glistening silk threads reveal themselves.
Throughout the entire process, Su Lun didn't even give these men a direct glance and went straight into the warehouse.
The mastermind behind the scenes was likely already on the way here, and there was no time to slowly gather intel from these men. Killing them and stripping their Soul Shards was the most efficient way.
He teleported once more and appeared inside the warehouse.
The addition of one person in the warehouse caused the twenty or so fully armed brutes to turn their murderous gaze towards him, with dozens of gun barrels all pointing his way.
The leader, Big Beard, was holding a Magic-energy Firearm — it was 'Old Smoker' Fogleres.
Su Lun's eyes were cold and indifferent. Without further explanation, he pinched the sorcerer's seals, his eyes emitting a fierce light, "Hormonal Outburst・Quadruple Dissolution!"
With a flick of his fingers, gargoyles and several puppets appeared out of thin air in the warehouse.
Then, a fierce battle erupted.
Boom, boom, boom, boom...
The sound of gunfire in the enclosed warehouse was deafening like the rolling thunder.
Su Lun focused on giving 'Old Smoker' Fogleres a good beating.
After all, as a fourth-order professional, this guy took some effort to deal with.
Some of the underlings were trying to fight back, while others, seeing the enemy was too strong and sensing things were going south, tried to flee. But those attempting to escape barely reached the windows before sniper bullets precisely burst their heads open, splattering their brains like a busted watermelon.
The battle was fierce and ended very quickly.
Within two minutes, Su Lun had killed everyone in the warehouse.
After stripping Fogleres's soul, he indeed found information about the supplier.
Su Lun didn't delay, gathered the spoils of war, and walked straight out of the warehouse door.
Upon exiting, he saw Rich Lady Lena on the rooftop, sniping one target after another. Those gang members who heard the commotion and came to reinforce were pinned down before getting close to the corner.
Su Lun gestured a retreat signal to the silhouette on the rooftop, and Lena responded with a radiant smile.
She packed up her sniper rifle and, with cat-like agility, vanished silently into the alleyway.
Su Lun withdrew his gaze and casually threw an incendiary device behind him to destroy the corpses and erase the traces.
A loud boom erupted and the entire warehouse burst into flames.
The forensic doctors in this alchemical world were very skilled, able to make the dead "speak." They could deduce the killer's personality and methods from marks on the body, and some could even reconstruct a person's facial features. If one body doesn't yield enough, then many will, piecing together the evidence.
Su Lun had witnessed this before and didn't dare to be careless.
Now, with no survivors left in the warehouse, it was perfect.
He gestured with the sorcerer's seals and in a moment, he was standing beside Rich Lady Lena in an alley several hundred meters away.
The two changed back into their previous outfits and walked onto the street without attracting any attention.
...
Suddenly, sounds of combat burst from a warehouse, startling the entire block.
Without understanding what had happened, most probably thought it was a gang shootout. Members of various gangs appeared on the streets armed and looking ferocious, but they still didn't know who their enemy was.
Onlookers from the night market also flooded the streets upon hearing the news, swarming about like ants out of a nest, filling up the streets.
With his arm wrapped around the slender waist of Rich Lady Lena, Su Lun also blended into the crowd of gawkers without being noticed.
No one knew who fired the shot in the crowd, but suddenly the street erupted with "bang bang bang" as a shootout began.
Everyone scattered like birds and beasts, no longer daring to casually spectate the commotion. Within moments, the roar of motorcycles echoed from the alleys.
Su Lun and Rich Lady Lena retrieved their motorbike from the Rolling Stone Bar garage and joined the stream of vehicles leaving Fox Avenue.
Different from before, Rich Lady Lena held Su Lun close from the back seat, her pretty face sporting a joyous smile.
Amidst the rush of wind, just as they left the block, Su Lun suggested, "Want to grab some late-night food?"
After jumping around all night, Rich Lady Lena was also a bit hungry and happily responded, "Sure."
Normal restaurants would be closed at this hour. Rich Lady Lena's upscale restaurants could have specially opened for them, but Su Lun had no intention of troubling the chefs to work overtime in the middle of the night.
Before long, the steam motorbike stopped in Mann District.
This was a working-class district with a large number of manufacturing plants nearby. Workers would often come out looking for food at night. Over time, a lively night market had developed here.
Su Lun parked the bike at the head of the street and located a small stall called "Beef Mince Pies & Mashed Potatoes."
It was a shop he remembered having a good taste from the memories stripped from a gang member earlier.
As the workers hadn't yet rested, business was slow. The two found a table and sat down.
The food was delicious, reasonably priced, and the portions were quite generous.
Su Lun actually found it quite satisfactory, considering in his eyes, it was all just a matter of proteins and carbohydrates.
In the dark alley, rats squeaked as they foraged for food. Steam pipes with holes in the walls hissed white smoke into the air, and everyone passing by wore the simple attire of the lower-class...
The lady of affluent background, Rich Lady Lena, didn't mind the environment in the slightest. She could sit elegantly in high-class restaurants sipping wine, but she enjoyed the street food just as much.
While eating, they resumed their earlier conversation.
Su Lun had stripped the memories from that "Old Smoker" Fogleres and indeed learned about the supplier for this batch of goods.
The supplier was an underworld figure known as "The Curator."
This person had quite the reputation in Lindon's underworld and was said to be a Big Shot with real power in reality as well. Yet his real appearance remained a mystery, as no one had ever seen him. He was familiar with the Vaughn Brothers due to some illegal human trafficking dealings, and he often purchased black magic materials or ancient texts through the gangs.
Having previously fought with that "Terrifying Wax Figure・Ghost Bride," Su Lun was almost certain that it was this "Curator" who was behind the scenes supplying the goods.
However, Su Lun felt there was something even worse than that.
From the information he had stripped from the Vaughn Brothers' members, apart from learning that the person possibly supplying goods from behind the scenes might be "The Curator," he obtained a piece of information that seemed profoundly troubling.
That was the emergence of a disease in Lindon's lower class, known as "Red Death."
Plagues and diseases were nothing new to humanity. From the mythological era to the modern day, there have always been some incurable infections.
Like the bubonic plague, the Black Death, smallpox, and so on...
But this was different.
The reason Su Lun paid attention to it was because... the mode of transmission for this disease was also through body fluids.
This was strikingly similar to the incident on the "Queen Rodrica" cruise ship!
Moreover, what was peculiar was that this disease couldn't be cured by normal means, but could be suppressed, and even completely eradicated by using a Potion refined from Blood Crystals.
A conspiracy immediately surfaced in Su Lun's mind.
Even though it was known that the Potion was problematic, now a disease emerged that only the Potion could treat – it would be impossible to say there was no connection.
Su Lun initially thought that the Potion was spread just among drug addicts, and that would only affect a small area.
But if, as he suspected, the disease transmission was also related, then the problem was considerably more complicated.
Extremely complicated!
If the Potion tested free of any issues, then it might ultimately be used by the unsuspecting public to treat the disease.

chapters.title: Chapter 431 - 430: King of Lington's Underworld
chapters.content:
"So, Mr. Su Lun, you suspect that the followers of the outer gods are using the spread of the 'Red Death' as a means to achieve large-scale contamination?"
Hearing Su Lun's intelligence, Miss Lena's expression also turned very grave.
If that were truly the case, matters were indeed urgent.
Su Lun nodded, "Yes. The 'Red Death' has not yet spread widely, but there are already signs of it spreading in the lower echelons of society. If we do not find a way to stop it, the consequences could be unimaginable."
After a pause, he continued, "The trouble is that apart from knowing the nickname 'Curator' for the source of the potion, there is no other useful intelligence. The potion cannot be detected as problematic. This makes it hard to convince the public."
"..."
Listening, Miss Lena also furrowed her brows, deep in thought.
But she truly did not understand the underworld, and she had never even heard of this 'Curator'.
Thinking over it, she said, "How about we ask Sister Sabina? She has deep knowledge of Lingdun City's underworld; maybe she knows some information?"
Su Lun had naturally thought of this method too. The Dawn Organization during the camping had already established a mature intelligence system, certainly knowing more than he did himself.
But now it was already late at night. He had originally planned to disturb Mr. Hei tomorrow, but Miss Lena suddenly mentioned Sabina.
At that moment, Miss Lena took out a specially designed encrypted communicator and said, "This is the exclusive encrypted communicator between me and Sister Sabina; she can answer at any time. I'll try dialing…"
As she spoke, she had already dialed the communicator.
"What's up, what's up?"
"Mhm, mhm."
"..."
The two exchanged a few code words,
Su Lun found it quite interesting listening in.
True to their spy work, they thought of everything thoroughly.
It seemed they had confirmed that their counterpart was free to talk, and Miss Lena directly said, "Sister Sabina, Mr. Su Lun has a question for you."
Upon hearing this, the voice on the other side of the communicator immediately perked up with a soft and coquettish tone: "Oh~ my dear master, are you with Miss Lena? I hope I'm not disturbing you. Oh, I'm already on the train back, but it's a pity I can't arrive at Lingdun until tomorrow afternoon. My goodness, what a long night this is, I can't wait to see you, my dearest master..."
Su Lun listened with a helpless smile on his face.
The voice, seductive and tingling to the bone, seemed to bewitch even through the communicator.
It immediately reminded him of the seductive and multifaceted succubus.
Oh, Sabina's peach... how he missed it.
Truly as if by magic, that enchanting image emerged in his mind, and he couldn't get rid of it.
Since the communication was on speaker, Miss Lena had heard the entire conversation and let out a laugh, saying, "Sister Sabina usually acts like a cold queen to outsiders. With Mr. Su Lun, it's like she becomes a different person."
On the other side of the communicator, Sabina didn't shy away from the master-servant relationship at all, directly saying, "Oh, of course, Lena, you don't understand my feelings for the master."
Then with coyness, she added, "It's been so long since we met, master, have you missed your most tender and considerate maid?"
Hearing this, Miss Lena beside him covered her mouth and giggled incessantly.
Su Lun, hearing this, simply shook his head, uninvolved with the topic and said directly, "There's a very important matter that requires some information... that 'Curator', have you ever heard of him? Or is there any way to find people related to him?"
First the urgent matters, the rest… we'll discuss when we meet.
After all, it's not clear over the communicator.
Hearing Su Lun speak of serious matters, Sabina also put aside her frivolity and replied, "I've heard of him, he is a mysterious figure who seldom appears. There's not much information about him. Master, is this person important?"
Su Lun, "Yes, extremely important. I need to gather information on that fellow as soon as possible."
Sabina, "If that's the case... I actually have a channel that's about 80% likely to find information. It's that person known as the 'King of Lingdon's Underworld', 'Duke of Shadows'. He holds a full moon ball twice a month, and I just got a 'ticket'. Tomorrow night, when I meet up with you, master..."
Su Lun listened, somewhat surprised, and nodded, "Good!"
They didn't talk much longer and then hung up the communicator.
Only then did Miss Lena speak up, curious, "Mr. Su Lun, who is this 'Duke of Shadows'?"
Su Lun looked thoughtful and after a moment, said, "The king of Lingdun's underground mafia."
....
Even before coming to Lurin, Su Lun had heard of this 'Duke of Shadows'.
And those who could touch upon this name usually held no low status.
That "Duke of Shadows" was extremely mysterious, and he had been the real king of Lingdon's underworld for the past two or three decades.
Many people believe there are only two types of people in this world, those who follow the rules and those who don't.
But there is actually a third kind.
They are the ones who make the rules.
And this "Duke of Shadows" was the godfather who set the rules for Lingdon's underworld!
No, not just the underworld.
He even had an indescribable influence among the elite of Lurying.
Lingdon's underworld has a long history and is also a significant feature.
However, generally speaking, the underworld has too low a ceiling, so as they grow bigger, the ultimate path for these underworld bosses usually leads to going legitimate.
Otherwise, there is almost never a good end.
Going legitimate can consist of entering politics or engaging in business.
Consequently, two of the three big underworld gangs that once controlled Lingdon City, the "Hydra Society" and "Blackstone Gang," have almost gone legitimate.
Now they have become the "Hydra Commerce Group" and "Blackstone Security Consulting Company."
One monopolizes industries such as shipping, education, healthcare, energy, and most others in the black market;
While the other deals in private-military contractors, mercenary business, and arms smuggling.
They also have considerable influence in the parliament.
Caroline Worster, whom Su Lun had met earlier on the cruise, is an executive of the Hydra.
The two gangs have indeed gone legitimate, and many things on the street are inconvenient for them to handle directly, so the real low-end underworld does not trust them.
Thus, the only remaining gang, "The Red Oak Society," gradually took control of nearly the entire underworld of Lingdon.
The society's leader, "Duke of Shadows," then became the true king of Lingdon's underworld!
The nickname "Duke of Shadows" spread because people in the underworld thought he had rights nearly equivalent to a top nobleman, yet remained hidden in the shadows.
There were rumors in the underworld that he could accomplish anything.
If someone wanted to sleep with a certain royal princess, as long as the price was right, that princess would be lying in your bed, stripped and washed clean, by evening.
The power behind him could only be imagined.
But as time passed, after this overlord took control of Lingdon's underworld, he also retreated behind the scenes.
Although the "Red Oak" has never gone legitimate, their games have become more high-end.
Somehow, within the underground circles, this "Full Moon Gala" emerged.
It holds two events each month, at the beginning and in the middle, without a fixed location, and admission is by invitation only.
Though it's called a "gala," it's actually a top-level resource exchange platform.
Reportedly, the circle is no longer made up of common underworld thugs, but truly comprises nobility and big shots from high society.
The admission criteria for this gala are exceedingly high, and its confidentiality is extremely strong.
Only through the introduction of more than three veteran members can one join.
But correspondingly, at this venue, one can access the top resources of Lurying.
It is said that Lurying's hot celebrities at the gala can be freely picked by guests as female attendants; the male models from fashion shows are merely servers carrying trays.
Large-scale mineral transactions, large arms trades, black market assassination commissions, official appointments, conflict mediation, intelligence gathering...
Any need you can think of, you can fulfill at the gala.
No one dares to kill a person protected by that "Duke of Shadows," and nobody he wants dead can live.
Of course, these are mostly rumors.
Because none of the people whose memories Su Lun has harvested so far have been qualified to attend that gala.
At least the former boss of the Vaughn Brotherhood never qualified.
...
Su Lun did not expect Sabrina to have an invitation to that "Full Moon Gala."
If the gala really was as magical as rumored, perhaps it could indeed solve this problem.
Su Lun thought that he should share all the information he had obtained today with Mr. Hei. He let the early morning intelligence officers pass the message to "Duke Lance" and "Duke Roberts," two Senior Councilors, to give them a head start for precaution. Regardless of political stance, the "Giant Hermit Society's" foreign god was an enemy to all alchemists!
The late-night meal was almost finished, and several large plates on the table were empty.
Su Lun asked, "Are you full?"
"Mhm."
Miss Lena nodded obediently.
Su Lun called the owner over to pay the bill; the two of them had eaten quite a bit and only spent a little over two hundred Lisos.
He paid three hundred, the extra being the tip.
Then the two got up and walked towards the steam motorcycle parked by the roadside.
Miss Lena followed behind Su Lun, her demeanor slightly awkward, and asked, "Mr. Su Lun, have you booked a hotel for tonight?"
"Not yet."
Su Lun casually responded and took out the motorcycle keys, inserting them into the vehicle and started the steam engine.
Miss Lena's eyelashes fluttered slightly, her crystal eyes shimmering with hesitation.
Finally, she mustered her courage, her voice as delicate as a thread, "How about going to my apartment?"
The rumbling noise of the motorcycle seemed to drown out her voice, making it hard to discern those spring breeze-like gentle words.
The moment the words left her mouth, a thought surged in her heart, if he didn't hear, so be it.
Because of that phrase, she could no longer muster the courage to say it again.
Su Lun mounted the motorcycle, pausing for a moment as if deeply considering something. Turning back, he saw the girl with flushed cheeks, nodded, and smiled, "Sure. Get on!"
Miss Lena revealed her white teeth in a grin, climbed onto the back seat of the motorcycle, and smiled brightly, "Mhm!"
It turned out that bravery truly could receive a happy response.
...
The next morning.
Golden sunlight streamed through the gaps in the curtains into the room.
The fog of Lingdun mostly affected the poor in the southern city, who rarely saw the sun. However, the rich area in the north had special large air purifiers and fog dispersal devices, so the morning sun was still visible in the marketplace.
Rich Lady Lena's apartment in the rich northern area by the Lokwarren River was a high-end mansion that could enjoy the beautiful riverside scenery and the morning sunlight.
It was the start of another beautiful day.
At seven o'clock, even though he had gone to bed late the night before, Su Lun woke up driven by his biological clock.
Sunlight filtered through the thorn flower curtain gaps onto the wall, like uncollectable golden seeds, casting a spectacular pattern of light and shadow.
Unlike usual, there was someone extra by his side.
Su Lun looked at the delicate body he was holding in his arms and smiled slightly.
The pristine white sheets outlined stunning contours, and the intimate touch of shared body heat reminded Su Lun of the beautiful dream from the night before.
After tossing and turning for most of the night, the girl with black hair was probably tired and was sleeping soundly.
He stared at her for a couple of seconds, and, as if sensing his gaze, Miss Lena's long eyelashes fluttered, and she opened her eyes.
The night was the best shade to hide her allure, but now that it was light, the shy blush could no longer be concealed.
Seeing Su Lun looking at her, she too remembered the passion of the previous night, a shy joy flickered through her gleaming eyes for just a moment before disappearing.
She responded with a brimming smile, asking, "Mr. Su Lun, don't you want to sleep a bit more?"
Su Lun, holding the stunning body in his arms, replied, "No. I'm used to waking up early. Besides, I have to meet Mr. Hei in a while."
"Oh."
Miss Lena snuggled into his embrace,
quietly enjoying the rare moment alone together.
For a long time, neither spoke.
Su Lun's clothes were scattered around, some on the sofa, some on the coat rack, and some on the carpet."
After a while, likely knowing that Su Lun had things to attend to later, Miss Lena proactively got up and said, "I'll get your clothes for you."
With that, she lifted the silk duvet and stepped barefoot onto the carpet.
Miss Lena's innate grace made her walk soft as a feather, her steps resembling a fashion show, elegant and pleasing to the eye.
She walked over, bent down to pick up the clothes on the floor, her slender legs fully revealed.
Su Lun captured that stunning silhouette, his eyes gently rippling with a soft smile.
The feeling of being together was wonderful, like a spring breeze and first love, a subtle joy, a gentle desire.
Miss Lena naturally noticed that gaze, yet felt not the slightest discomfort, boldly displaying herself.
Because Mr. Su Lun had said he liked it very much.
Now and then, she glanced sideways, turning back a smile.
She didn't bring back the clothes Su Lun wore yesterday; instead, she picked up the dirty clothes and tossed them into the wicker storage basket.
Then she went to the wardrobe, rustling around for a moment before unexpectedly pulling out two sets of men's suits.
As she walked, she said, "Sabina said the apartment should have a few sets of suits that Mr. Su Lun can wear. Said that you would use them when you come…"
"Ha, ha..."
Su Lun heard this and couldn't help but laugh and cry at the same time.
Although it had been a long time since they'd seen each other, he knew that Sabina truly was the one who understood his temperament the best, having arranged everything perfectly.
Miss Lena showed off the two suits, clearly the workmanship of top-tier tailors, and asked, "Mr. Su Lun, which one do you like?"
One was black, and the other was also black.
The styles were slightly different, composed and understated, yet with a hint of luxury.
Miss Lena's aesthetic was naturally not lacking; Su Lun looked and was satisfied with both styles, saying, "Either is fine. Lena, choose whichever you think looks better."
Compared to the clothes, he found the person holding the clothes more beautiful.
"Oh."
Miss Lena knew she was not dressed and faced the man in front of her with composure.
As she faced that intense gaze, her face showed no embarrassment, instead boldly displaying, saying, "Then this set?"
Su Lun said, "Good."
Lena saw some changes, gently smiled.
Su Lun stood up, "I need to leave soon, or I will be late."
"Oh. Then let me help you get dressed."
Lena put down the outer coat and started bustling about like a caring little wife. She interrupted Su Lun's attempt to dress himself and seriously said, "No need. I'll help you."
Ru Ying's gentleman suits were quite complicated to wear, with several layers both inside and out.
This rich lady took the task very seriously, very meticulously dressing him.
Clearly unaccustomed to serving others, her movements were somewhat stiff. Bending over was quite inconvenient, so she simply knelt on the carpet.
Instantly, the atmosphere turned warmly intimate.
Su Lun, looking at the busy Lena in front of him, teased, "Did Sabina teach you this too?"
Everything was just right, capturing that teasing moment perfectly.
Lena had nothing to hide, she tilted her head to glance at him, her face brimming with a naturally gentle expression, "Yes, Sabina said you would definitely like it. But, this is also something I wanted to do for Mr. Su Lun myself."
While speaking, she smiled brightly, her charm evident.
Su Lun felt an inexplicable sense of thoughtfulness.
Being with Lena was truly delightful.
Even suddenly, there was such a moment, making one feel that such slow, beautiful times could stir the soul.
Once the clothes were on, Lena carefully adjusted the creases at the collar, showing a satisfied expression, "All done~"
She admired her handiwork, her eyes gleaming with pride as she complimented, "Mr. Su Lun really is the most handsome!"
Su Lun reached out to flick her forehead, his fingertips lightly touching, then stirring the loose strand of hair beside her ear, and he kissed this girl.
Another vibrant morning.
A beautiful day.
PS. Had to go out, got delayed, apologies for the fewer words.

chapters.title: Chapter 432 - 431: Seeing Sabina Again
chapters.content:
After enjoying a hearty breakfast at Rich Lady Lena's apartment, Su Lun stepped out, feeling refreshed.
He had arranged to meet Mr. Hei today.
Besides catching up, there was much he needed to ask in person.
Mr. Hei, employed as an inconspicuous librarian at the "Lingdun Royal Parliamentary Library," spent his days there immersed in books, organizing, and occasionally restoring ancient texts. Inconspicuous, yet this was the intelligence core of the Dawn Organization in Lingdun.
The library was located in the Franklin District—a zone without a clear divide between affluent and common classes—teeming with headquarters of various large and medium-sized enterprises, a hotspot for the work-lively elite populace.
Su Lun rode his steam motorcycle from the apartment across two city areas, taking half an hour to reach the library.
It was a very impressive set of buildings with a classical Gothic style, adorned with a beautiful golden bell tower and various other turrets. It was the most magnificent structure Su Lun had ever seen in Lingdun.
He parked his motorcycle near the library plaza, then walked over.
The weather was nice today, and the fountain plaza was bustling with many people feeding the plump pigeons with bread crumbs.
Where the wealthy gather, even the pets are fatter.
He contacted Mr. Hei, who was currently in Section A of the library, organizing ancient texts.
Su Lun checked the guide map and entered through the library's main entrance.
The library was open to everyone, but admission required proper attire.
In Lingdun, a decent ensemble including a top hat, leather boots, and a walking stick was valued at no less than ten thousand lire.
Most commoners could never afford such an expensive attire. Thus, although the library appeared open to all, it effectively barred the lower classes.
Allowing only a fraction of people access to knowledge was still a gesture of grace from the nobility to the commoners.
...
Su Lun stepped into the library as if entering a maze constructed of books.
This "Parliamentary Library" was known alongside the "Lingdun Royal Academy Library" as the largest libraries of their time.
Over two hundred million cataloged items were housed in the public areas of the library, with numerous societal donations still increasing that number annually.
The collection included books, manuscripts, newspapers, scrolls, stamps, artwork, and assorted curious cursed objects. The book area alone contained texts in over a thousand different languages, encompassing artifacts from numerous civilizations and ages.
All in all, it was enormous.
The library was brightly lit, a few people seated on mahogany chairs flipping through books.
As he walked by, Su Lun felt a tickle of desire, wishing he could have such a library within his own "little void realm" to carry with him.
The deeper he delved into alchemy, the more he revered the vastness of knowledge.
Soon, Su Lun reached a corner in Section A.
This was a book sorting area, free of outsiders, only admitting librarians.
He saw Mr. Hei meticulously organizing a large pile of ancient scrolls on the second floor as he arrived.
Su Lun called out, "Mr. Hei... long time no see."
Mr. Hei chuckled and responded, "I hardly deserve the 'Mr.' anymore. We mustn't mess up our seniority..."
He was a student of Mr. Jing, and Su Lun was Mr. Jing's junior disciple.
By seniority, Mr. Hei should actually call Su Lun "little uncle."
Su Lun would never presume so much respect, as this elderly gentleman had always been a revered sage, elder, and previously in Old Lington, he had solved many major problems for him.
Moreover, Mr. Hei was a true Scholar.
Despite Su Lun himself having amassed a variety of knowledge, it was mostly from pirates and warriors—how many books could they read? Excluding the repetitive, both the depth and quantity were far behind Mr. Hei.
With respect in his heart, upon seeing Mr. Hei, Su Lun still teased, "Should we each keep to our own? I'll still address you as 'Mr.', and you can call me 'little uncle'?"
Mr. Hei, far from offended, burst out laughing, "Hahaha..."
They both knew that the titles did not matter to them.
Mr. Hei gestured to a nearby chair, "Su Lun, just find a seat anywhere you like."
As they were no strangers, Su Lun didn't stand on ceremony; he pulled out a chair and sat beside Mr. Hei, immediately showing great interest in the collection of ancient scrolls on the table.
Mr. Hei noticed his interest and explained while pointing to the scrolls on the table, "Sorry, I wanted to meet elsewhere, but I'm just overwhelmed with work."
Su Lun wasn't bothered by this.
After a pause, Mr. Hei continued, "This is 'Cimbrian script,' recording a very rare interrupted civilization. An adventure team excavated it last month from a sunken ship in the South Sea, and it was just delivered to the library yesterday. This one box of scrolls, if searched for in all of Lingdun's libraries, likely wouldn't yield a second box..."
Those characters seemed almost magical, and sparkle danced in the Scholar's normally tranquil eyes as he spoke of them.
Su Lun had never even heard of this interrupted civilization, but looked on with interest as he queried, "It seems to record some kind of alchemy?"
Mr. Hei's scholarly expertise was immediately apparent, "Yes. Those texts preserved so well must inherently house valuable knowledge. Due to knowledge gaps, the translation isn't very precise, but it roughly records an ancient technique for refining seawater..."
"Oh."
Su Lun listened and learned.
He increasingly envied the "treasure magnet effect" of a capital like Lingdun.
Adventurers from Lingdun traveled worldwide seeking treasures, unearthing ancient relics. Yet ultimately, almost all valuable findings were transported to Lingdun.
Especially items like ancient relics.
Because only in a major city like Lingdun could people afford to buy these; only here was there a sufficiently knowledgeable expert team to translate them, uncovering their true value.
Simply observing these few scrolls in the library might represent a rarity completely unattainable in a commoner's lifetime.
And Lingdun is a vast empire.
Lingdun City had accumulated a thousand years of heritage, inconceivable to outsiders.
This heritage was also why it was called a "sacred land of alchemy."
Su Lun felt nothing but admiration, pure and unadulterated.
And when he compared himself to others, he felt increasingly like a nouveau riche.
He felt he needed much more knowledge to enrich himself.
In this library lay endless knowledge, as vast as the boundless cosmos.
Mr. Hei had chosen such an identity to conceal himself, out of both interest and career advancement.
Su Lun thought that, after seeing the world, retiring as a librarian would be a fine choice indeed.
...
Upon their reunion, Su Lun curiously sensed Mr. Hei's soul fluctuations, raised his eyebrows in astonishment, and directly asked, "Mr. Hei, just how powerful are you now? I feel like you've become incredibly formidable."
If it weren't extraordinary, he wouldn't have asked.
He knew Mr. Hei had also advanced to the fifth order, but he seemed as inscrutable as the ocean.
Even facing sixth or even seventh-order professionals he had met before, Su Lun had never felt this immeasurable depth.
Those eyes brimming with wisdom seemed as if they could see through everything.
Mr. Hei didn't respond directly but instead laughed, "Su Lun, my young friend, you're the formidable one. That battle in the City-States of Morlos, facing two hundred thousand enemies by yourself, no one else could achieve... Now you're considered the 'strongest professional' in the eyes of the younger generation of Lu Ying."
Listening to these words, Su Lun didn't know whether to laugh or cry, and said, "Mr. Hei, please don't flatter me too much. Don't you know the truth?"
Mr. Hei's eyes twinkled with mirth, not entirely joking, "I'm not making this up; it's written just like that in the newspapers. At the very least, even a seventh-order professional wouldn't be able to defeat so many enemies under those circumstances.
In the presence of a scholar, Su Lun didn't have the gall to boast, so he returned to the original topic and asked, "So, what is your power level now?"
Mr. Hei thought for a moment and said something ambiguous, "Knowledge makes me fearless."
"..."
Su Lun rolled his eyes, his expression almost speaking for itself: Speak plainly.
Seeing his mocking expression, Mr. Hei finally thought and replied solemnly, "Well... to be honest, I guess no one below the seventh order could defeat me."
Hearing this, Su Lun felt like he got the answer he wanted and said, "I think you are being modest."
Given this old man's modest character, to dare to say this meant it was probably an understatement.
Anyone else might take this to mean... undefeated below the seventh order!
Even though Su Lun felt he was very powerful, he never dared to claim to be invincible below the seventh order.
Like that time he encountered the puppeteer behind the "Ghost Bride," with those dark magic puppets, he wasn't sure he could defeat anyone, whether they were fifth or sixth order.
But Mr. Hei daring to say so must mean he had some assurance.
As strong as ever...
Su Lun silently admired.
Having been personally taken as a disciple by Mr. Jing, Mr. Hei's talent was unquestionably superior.
This old man had it all, only being a bit too low profile for his taste.
Though one of the most learned men of the era, he always behaved like a naive school-age child, always maintaining a modest and reserved stability.
After some small talk, Su Lun and Mr. Hei discussed serious matters.
The recent situation in Lu Ying, the current state of the Dawn Organization, and the reactions of the major forces...
Learning that Mr. Jing and others had gone to the province of Senodia, and that the organization was doing well there, Su Lun breathed a sigh of relief.
He also shared the clues he had discovered the day before with Mr. Hei.
At least to let the intelligence organization of Dawn prepare in advance.
Their conversation lasted from morning until afternoon.
If Su Lun didn't have other matters to attend to, he would have really considered staying in the library for a few days to seek guidance and learn.
As they parted, Su Lun gave Mr. Hei a "Void Tolerance Elixir" and a space material he had previously acquired that was highly compatible with the Scholar profession.
...
Not long after, Mr. Hei escorted Su Lun to the library entrance, "This professional material really suits me, Su Lun, you are thoughtful."
It wasn't just the material, but also the rare "Void Tolerance Elixir," that would greatly enhance his spatial affinity.
For a scholar like him, this enhancement in strength would be more terrifying than for most, that affinity would cause a qualitative change in his spatial techniques!
Su Lun didn't mind these features.
Not to mention the connection with Mr. Jing and their belonging to Dawn—Mr. Hei had also helped him a lot back in Old Lingdun.
Mr. Hei then said, "By the way, Su Lun, about that copy of 'Isaac's Alchemy Manuscript' you wanted—I've checked, and it's really in the Royal Academy Library. But it isn't easy to take out. It's a permanent collectible of the Royal Academy, and even members of the royal family have no rights to gift it to anyone. So... the only way to obtain it is through some extraordinary measures. However, the library has highly sophisticated security spells, and even now, I haven't figured out any way to circumvent these spells."
"Oh?"
Su Lun frowned upon hearing this.
He wanted not only the content within to craft "Isaac's Giant Strength" armament but also the manuscript itself.
It was left by Sir Isaac and besides the knowledge, was a formidable treasure in itself.
Su Lun felt it necessary to collect his sect's treasures, especially since his teacher Sereya mentioned that there was a great secret hidden in the manuscript.
However, it seemed not so easy to acquire.
Mr. Hei said, "I think you should take a look yourself when you have time; your 'All-knowing Eye' talent might see more."
Su Lun nodded, "Mm."
Visiting the Royal Academy of Lu Ying was also one of his plans for the upcoming days.
To inspect that manuscript, and also to visit his disciple Gek who loved researching bombs.
Mr. Hei added, "Also, you might consult Kit. He's an expert in breaking various spells and decoding locks, maybe he could help. Besides, he would probably be quite interested. After all, the treasures in the Royal Academy's Treasure Gallery are considered the 'ultimate challenge' for thief-type professionals. The last one to succeed was one of the top ten legendary hunters, 'Thief King' Carlo Meldis..."
Su Lun listened and smiled.
As they were parting, Mr. Hei added, "Danny has opened a potion shop at 171 Rodon Street in the Queen's District. When you go there, remember to tell him that I've already found the batch of ancient potion manuscripts he was looking for. He can come and pick them up anytime..."
Su Lun nodded, "Okay."
...
Before long, Su Lun rode his steam motorcycle to the Queen's District.
Rodon Street is the location of the headquarters of the "Lurion Pharmacists Guild," and it is the only place in the empire where one can certify as a senior pharmacist.
This district gathers pharmacists from all over the country, hence it also has Lurion's largest market for potion materials.
Potion studies is one of the most important fundamental disciplines within alchemy, which Su Lun himself mastered. Recently, his experimental research had been lacking some materials, and Dr. Banks had also issued a long list of items, so he decided to make the purchases himself.
After parking his motorcycle at the corner, Su Lun browsed the market with great interest.
Various shops with hanging signs offered a dazzling array of potion materials, and Su Lun casually visited a few.
One has to admit, this Rodon Street bulk distribution market truly deserves its status as Lurion's largest market for potion materials. One could find almost every potion material needed!
In the shops, there were also various finished potions for sale, from the lowest-grade healing medicines to life extension elixirs worth millions. Everything was available.
As long as you had the money, you could buy nearly any potion with the desired effects.
The pedestrians on the street were bustling, including pharmacists and professional merchants, with a large portion being adventurers coming to buy potions.
Being a main distribution center, the potions here were much cheaper than in other places.
However, after walking around, Su Lun only bought a few urgently needed materials before calling it quits.
It's not that he didn't want to buy more, but the materials were really too expensive!
Su Lun had been mixing in the northern sea pirate circles, accustomed to pirate black market's "bone-breaking prices."
Now at a regular market, he found the prices of those materials outrageously high.
In Pirate City Hastelin, what one could buy for a thousand lisos might cost ten thousand or even tens of thousands here.
The materials were on average four to five times more expensive, some even dozens of times more.
Su Lun gave up the idea of sweeping goods.
Though he was not short of money, there was no need to waste it like this.
These matters were better handled by Rich Lady Lena's trading company.
No middlemen, more suitable for bulk purchases.
Su Lun did not linger longer in the market. Watching the door numbers, he walked past the bustling Rodon Street. When he reached number 150, he was already in a very remote corner.
After circling for half a day and not finding his destination, he asked a local and then found number 171.
The shop was hidden in a dim alleyway.
It was somewhat like a village in the city; behind the glamorous commercial district of Rodon Street, there was a cluster of very old houses, where many laborers who moved goods for the medicine market lived.
Seeing the door number he had struggled to locate, Su Lun muttered, "No wonder Mr. Hei said it was hard to find..."
It was a very small shop, only sporting a small sign "Danny's Potion Shop."
Compared to the big shops on the main street, this was practically no different from a street stall.
However, the shop was closed.
Su Lun, who didn't want his visit to Lingdun City to be widely known, hadn't informed Danny of his arrival.
But he knew there were people inside the house, and not just a few.
With a pinch of a sorcerer's seal, a person cloaked in a cloak appeared.
Emerging from a mini spatial realm, Dr. Banks looked at the shop sign, his voice clearly agitated, "Is this Danny's shop?"
Su Lun nodded, "Hmm. They should be on the second floor. There are quite a few people there."
Just as the two were hesitating whether to knock, a young face with a peaked cap appeared on the second-floor roof.
The person cautiously asked, seeing the two obviously suspicious characters, "Who are you looking for?"
Su Lun looked up, and despite the hat obscuring the face, he recognized the person and called out, "Kai?"
He had felt there was a strong third-tier professional upstairs but hadn't expected it to be someone he knew.
It was none other than the former captain of the Old Lington Cross Society, Kai, who had a life-saving bond with Su Lun.
The peaked cap wearer was stunned for a moment when called by his name, "Su Lun?"
Once he saw Su Lun's face clearly, his expression turned incredulous, and excitedly exclaimed, "Oh my God, is that really you!"
Kai jumped down nimbly and gave Su Lun a warm hug.
Su Lun, looking at his old friend, was also very happy.
The alley was clearly not a place for idle chat. Kai suggested, "Let's go inside and talk!"
As he spoke, he knocked on the closed door of the potion shop and shouted, "Anisha, open the door quickly."
Listening to the footsteps of someone coming downstairs inside, the door soon opened.
It was a young nurse in isolation gear, a young girl with large eyes who sized up Su Lun and his companion, asking, "Mr. Kai, a new patient?"
Kai did not explain much, "No. An old friend of Danny and me."
"Oh."
The nurse named Anisha turned and went upstairs, "Then Mr. Kai, please entertain your guests, I need to go help Dr. Danny change a patient's dressing."
Kai, "Okay."
Su Lun looked at the few ready-made potions in the shop and casually asked, "Why is the shop not open?"
