Kai looked somewhat solemn and said, "These days, a strange disease has been rampaging through the city. There are too many patients, and if this continues, we won't be able to accommodate them all."
Before Su Lun could think further, they had already ascended to the second floor.
In a small room, more than ten sickbeds were separated by curtains, and a figure in a white coat was busily attending to them.
He seemed extremely focused, and didn't even realize two more people had entered the room, only saying, "Anisha, inject the patient in bed three with a dose of 'T3 antiviral'."
Kai had intended to call Danny to greet an old friend, but Dr. Banks stepped forward instead.
He barely glanced at his own son, instead focusing on the patients in bed three, and said, "The T3 level antiviral isn't enough to suppress the symptoms of the patients. You need at least a T5 level. Add five milliliters of 'mercury neutralizer' to neutralize the sepsis in the patient's organs."
Hearing this, Danny didn't turn around, and continued in conversation, "There's no T5 left. Let's use T3 for now. I'll figure out the potion later..."
Having said that, he then realized that someone had said something.
Turning around, he saw a stranger standing beside him.
Though he couldn't make out the face clearly, a familiar sense of closeness suddenly surged within him.
Danny wasn't sure who he had seen, but when he turned his face, he recognized Su Lun and exclaimed, "Su Lun?"
Su Lun nodded and smiled, "Long time no see, Danny."
Seeing an old friend, Danny could hardly conceal the astonishment in his eyes.
Since it was Su Lun...
Danny already knew his father was still alive; it was only because of those mutation suppressants sent from Pirate City that he had managed to survive.
So, this person was his father?
Dr. Banks also spoke, his tone complex, "Danny, are you doing alright?"
Hearing this, Danny's eyes brimmed with tears.
...
The father and son reunion was joyous beyond words.
Unfortunately, both had mutated, their appearances completely changed from before.
They couldn't briefly sum up each other's experiences with just a few words.
However, they had barely started reminiscing when the coughing of patients interrupted them.
Banks used some advanced potions he carried with him to temporarily suppress the patients' symptoms.
Su Lun watched the whole process, his gaze very solemn.
To him, the patients seemed to exhibit symptoms typical of the "Red Death".
This was confirmed by Danny as well.
"This is a new contagious disease, initially thought to be transmitted through rats. Infected individuals, particularly on their faces, develop red spots, often accompanied by dizziness, severe pain, and bleeding from the pores. I've tried many methods, but have yet to find a cure. Certain advanced potions can suppress some of the symptoms, allowing patients to temporarily survive, but unfortunately, ordinary people cannot afford the cost of these high-level injections."
He paused, then added, "Moreover, I've noticed that the well-informed speculative merchants have already started hoarding goods. Any potions or materials that can suppress this disease have skyrocketed several times in price, and they continue to soar... It's difficult to even purchase the materials to concoct potions."
Dr. Banks looked equally solemn as he said, "Judging by the symptoms, it should be the legendary 'Red Death'."
Danny, not knowing what was happening, asked puzzled, "Father, what is this disease?"
Dr. Banks and Su Lun exchanged a glance, sighed slightly, and said, "Let's go downstairs to talk about it."
The patient was stable for the moment, and Danny finally managed to step out of the sickroom.
They talked as soon as they reached downstairs.
Danny had disfigurements, and his facial features were frightening, which is why he didn't like making public appearances. However, since he had once been saved by the slum dwellers of Old Lington, that experience left him with a good will towards the lower classes. So after coming to Lington, he opened a small potion shop where he sold affordable potions on a daily basis to treat some of the local people.
Nurse Anisha was one of the previous patients. When Danny had cured her from a certain death, the girl stayed to work as a nurse in the shop.
Although old friends meeting might have had many things to discuss, their conversation revolved more around the "Red Death".
In the underbelly of Lington, this "Blood Terror" was silently spreading; the sinister conspiracy of that wicked Outer God was progressing.
Fortunately, Dr. Banks was an expert in this area. Having seen these cases, he also had some ideas about treatment strategies.
However, a large number of clinical trials were still needed for testing.
At this time, no one could be sure how long it would take.
This only made Su Lun more urgent to find out exactly who was spreading this disease and who was the supplier of the parasitic potion!
...
With professionals like Dr. Banks and Danny studying the Red Death, Su Lun didn't need to worry.
In the evening, he arrived at a café by the Lokwarren River called "The Enigmatic Bird".
He and Sabina had agreed to meet there at seven to go together to the "Full Moon Misunderstanding".
Su Lun ordered a coffee and sat in a corner seat by the window, a position that allowed him to observe most of the café.
The window gave a perfect view of the renowned Linden Iron Bridge.
This suspension bridge was a landmark of Lington, capable of automatically lifting its surface on both sides to allow ships to pass whenever a large vessel sounded its horn.
After sitting down, Su Lun took a few sips of coffee and checked his pocket watch; there were still fifteen minutes to the appointed time.
But just then, a woman whose face was largely covered by a scarf hurried into view. She scanned the people in the café and instantly spotted Su Lun in the corner.
With a light step, she walked over, all the while unwinding her scarf.
That shiny wave of red hair was the first thing to catch his eye, followed by that voluptuously charming smile—could it be anyone but Sabina?
Su Lun looked at this enchantress of a maid who he hadn't seen for a long while and raised an eyebrow in a smile.
Sabina didn't sit across from Su Lun. Instead, unashamedly, she sat right next to him.
Her sultry body pressing against him, the enchantress maid wrapped her arms around her master's neck, and with a coquettish glint in her eye, she pouted, "Sir, sorry to keep you waiting!"

chapters.title: Chapter 433 - 432: Business Comes First
chapters.content:
Su Lun looked at Sabina, who pouted and sat contently in his arms as if no one else was around, feeling quite helpless.
Although she was his contracted maid, except for being attentive in the beginning when they first met, she became increasingly "presumptuous" as they grew more familiar.
She truly understood the temperament of her master and always teased him just right.
And Su Lun didn't find anything wrong with it.
After all, his succubus maid was indeed a peerless beauty that was impossible to fault.
It's just... this coffee shop seems to be a public place!
While their spot was in a corner, the coffee house still had other people in it.
Sabina saw the way Su Lun glanced around and understood immediately. With a slight wave of her hand, a waiter promptly brought out a privacy screen to shield the corner. The screen was engraved with soundproofing charms, and in an instant, the corner was as if isolated into a small room.
She explained with a gleaming smile, "Master, I'm also one of the shareholders of this coffee shop, you know."
Su Lun wasn't surprised when he heard this.
As a professional intelligence agent, choosing this place to meet was surely primarily for security.
After speaking, Sabina hugged Su Lun's neck and nuzzled affectionately. Despite her mature and glamorous red-lipped look, she coquettishly put on the guise of a young girl, "Master, have you missed your most gentle and considerate maid~"
One should never doubt Sabina's taste in clothing; today, she wore a dark silver pencil skirt that perfectly accentuated her sexy and fiery figure.
The high-quality black stockings on her legs felt exquisite to the touch. These vintage garter belts with leather clasps were very popular among the ladies of high society in Lingdun. Along with her slightly plump figure, the mature allure was partially concealed yet partially revealed, tantalizingly so.
With a sidelong glance, she looked like a ripe peach, her juiciness seemingly about to spill out.
Since there was no one else around, she didn't care in the slightest if her sitting posture would cause any wardrobe malfunctions. Whether intentional or not, her pencil skirt rode up, perfectly exposing the lines of her buttocks, with the just-right glimpse of lace trim teasingly peeking out from the hem.
A bit more revealed would be too vulgar,
But a bit less would lack much allure.
She truly knew how to tease just enough.
The relationship between Su Lun and Sabina was anything but estranged. His fingertips grazed the fabric, shamelessly enjoying the delicate sensation, taking it as a response to her earlier question.
"I just knew Master had missed me," Sabina responded with heartfelt affection, her complexion flush and her face full of joy and a dreamy expression.
Having not seen each other for a while, she had so much to say, almost whispering into Su Lun's ear, "Oh, Master has become even more handsome~ When I read about the battle at Moross Federation in the newspaper, oh my, you have no idea how excited I was! I nearly wore out that paper, I guarantee I could recite every passage about you, Master..."
It seemed more like sweet nothings than catching up on old times.
Su Lun just felt his ear tickled by warm breaths.
But hearing those exaggerated descriptions in the newspapers, a wry smile yet again appeared on his lips.
For he had already heard it all in great detail from Lena's mouth before.
And he had heard quite a lot from Mr. Hei as well.
Knowing that there was serious business to attend to that night, Su Lun didn't dwell on the topic and directly asked, "Shall we get ready to go to the dance now?"
Upon hearing this, Sabina was not in the least bit hurried, "No rush. We still have an hour. This humble maid rushed over here just to see Master first."
Su Lun lifted his eyebrows as he listened, "Oh."
Sabina asked again, "Did Master bring me any gift~"
As she spoke, a sly glint passed through her coquettish beautiful eyes, and she said with a feigned sense of grievance, "Reina said she got hers. When I asked her just now, she even mentioned that Master left the apartment early this morning..."
Listening to this clearly suggestively teasing talk, Su Lun shook his head, not trying to hide anything. He took out an emerald gemstone ring that glittered brilliantly under the light.
It was also one selected from the spoils of war from the Sea Ruins, and it was very beautiful.
Su Lun had planned to give each person by his side a gift so that in the future he could find their locations anytime with directed displacement.
He said, "This is for you. It has space inscriptions on it, and if you wear it, I'll be able to sense where you are at any time."
"Oh, this is the most beautiful ring I've ever seen!"
Sabina gazed at the ring with genuine joy in her eyes.
Not to mention the emerald was a rare treasure in itself, but the meaning behind her master's gift made her extremely happy.
Su Lun wasn't intentionally going for something so grand, but after trying, he concluded that a gemstone of at least this size was necessary to engrave the complete spatial coordinates inscriptions.
Sabina certainly didn't mind.
Even if Su Lun had given her a rock, it would still be a priceless treasure in her eyes, and she would be very, very happy.
But at this moment, she didn't take the ring. Instead, she extended her fair and delicate hand with fingers spread and said in a soft, coquettish voice, "Sir, could you help me put it on?"
Su Lun looked at Sabina's expectant face and shook his head helplessly. Yet he didn't mind and slipped the ring onto the middle finger of her right hand, adding, "Alright, I've given the gift. Now let's discuss the important matters."
Some things weren't convenient to talk about over the communicator and naturally had to be said in person.
Su Lun knew very well that if he let her continue to fool around, they would certainly start playing with fire.
Once the ring was on, Sabina kept turning her hand over and over, her eyes filled with enchanting allure, growing more and more pleased with what she saw.
What made her happy was that she held a high place in her master's heart.
This was the happiness of feeling valued.
She didn't forget to discuss the important matters, saying, "My current identity is 'Countess Demacula,' a minor lord who lives as a widow in the White Stone Castle in the southern part of Anrogos County. Oh, my master, your identity is my personal physician. Obviously, our relationship is a very intimate one..."
"Oh."
Su Lun listened to the suggestive hint and smiled faintly.
Sabina continued to elaborate, "This identity needs attention to a few things..."
After her explanation, Su Lun also understood the entire process.
The tickets to the "Full Moon Ball" were difficult to obtain and required introductions from three veteran members.
This introduction system also eliminated almost all those with nefarious intentions, or those without family connections.
Usually, only the upper-class people from the Luying Empire with fixed property, traceable lineage for several generations, and a clear trail could join.
If a member got into any trouble, it would affect his introducers and their families as well.
This is why the Full Moon Ball has been running for so long without trouble and has grown even stronger.
Sabina, even with her great talent for intelligence, was on her own too weak to possibly get a ticket.
Fortunately, Mr. Jing's bloodline had been running an intelligence network for a few hundred years.
As soon as Sabina joined, she immediately had a plan.
The best identity was not a disguise, but a replacement.
The identity of "Countess Demacula" was a persona that Mr. Jing's bloodline had cultivated for many years, and now it had found its use.
It was solid and traceable.
Because of this identity, Sabina quickly integrated into Luying's high society and obtained a great deal of useful intelligence.
Su Lun was also very clear that Sabina was taking a great risk by taking him to the ball.
Should anything go wrong, she and the entire intelligence network behind her would suffer catastrophic repercussions.
Therefore, Su Lun also felt he should be more careful and cautious, trying not to give themselves away.
Oh, by the way, the intelligence organization to which Mr. Jing's bloodline and Sabina belonged was now using the name from the Old Lington era—Jing Organization.
...
Having nearly grasped all the necessary intelligence for the operation, Su Lun had no pressing matters to discuss.
He looked at Sabina and asked some idle questions, "Have you encountered any danger since you came to Lingdun? Or had some special experiences?"
"Yes."
Sabina thought for a moment and said calmly, "When I first arrived, my foundations were unstable, and I had several covert clashes with the people from Luying's military intelligence department. Those established intelligence organizations have a lot of resources and many experts; there were several times I almost got exposed..."
Su Lun's expression grew slightly stern as he listened.
Sabina always had an easy smile on her face, but the content of her words was anything but relaxed.
Intelligence work is always fraught with crisis—a single exposure could mean a life-threatening situation.
With a few understated sentences, Su Lun actually knew she had put in a lot of effort behind the scenes.
Sabina caught a glimpse of Su Lun's brief change in expression and knew that her master truly cared about her. Suddenly feeling that everything was worth it, she smiled and said, "But after Mr. Su Lun agreed, the leader took special care of me. Moreover, I found an alchemical outfit called 'Ancient Succubus Tail' in the castle of 'Blood Duke' Wazzhawaz. After merging with it, I even awakened my second-tier talent by luck. So, you don't have to worry too much, the chances of me getting exposed now are very, very low..."
Hearing her say this, Su Lun felt unexplainably relieved.
Out of curiosity, he asked, "What is the second-tier succubus ability?"
"It's..."
Sabina almost let it slip, then suddenly remembered something and with a sly sparkle in her eyes, she said, "I can't tell you for now. It's a surprise I've prepared for you, Master. I'll tell you after tonight's dance~"
"..."
Su Lun didn't think much of it after listening.
Looking at her demeanor, he could roughly guess that the second stage of succubus might have unlocked some very special abilities.
While talking, Sabina probably felt that sitting sideways on her master's lap was inconvenient, so she changed to a more intimate posture. Without a shred of shyness, she straddled and turned to face Su Lun squarely, kneeling on the couch.
At that moment, thinking of something, she complained, "I thought I had tried hard to become stronger. But compared to Master, I'm still too weak."
This posture was indeed much more convenient for Su Lun; his hands found a place to rest.
He sincerely complimented her, "You're already doing well."
"Not at all."
Sabina looked very serious and blinked, saying, "I need to become even stronger to keep up with Master's pace. So, Master also needs to whip me to work hard in cultivation~"
Su Lun smiled faintly and said nothing more.
He knew there was no need to worry about this issue; Sabina was very aware of her role.
In the future, he would grow stronger and stronger.
He would have no need for useless ornaments by his side.
Only strength would provide value to accompany him.
Moreover... there were shortcuts for a succubus to grow stronger.
Seeing Sabina's suggestive smile, how could Su Lun not understand?
Sabina had once said that succubus talents had a shortcut to improving strength: legend had it that ancient succubi were abyssal creatures by nature, usually choosing to serve powerful demon kings loyally for life, and they also had secret methods to enhance their prowess. The stronger the demon king, the stronger the servants would become as a benefit.
Her advancement to the third rank had once depended on Su Lun, her master.
Although Su Lun felt like he hadn't seen her in a long while and was quite interested in exchanging affections with his maid...
But... priorities first.
He couldn't help but say with a laugh and a cry, "Stop fooling around, there's serious business soon."
Sabina responded nonchalantly, "But... there's still an hour left."
Su Lun looked around the environment again and said, "This is a café."
Yet Sabina raised an eyebrow seductively, her eyes sultry as she teased, "Do you mind? Giggle..."
That chuckle, as though seeing through everything.
In the end, Su Lun could only helplessly shake his head and drop the subject.
...
Fifty minutes after the meeting.
Su Lun and Sabina appeared on the streets of Lingdun at night. They strolled along the walkway beside the Lokwarren River, admiring the riverside scenery as they walked.
The alluring night, the surging river flowing in the darkness, and occasionally a lighted boat passing over the water's surface.
The orange light from the gas lamps elongated their shadows, then shortened them, then elongated them again...
As night fell, many pedestrians also lingered by the lakeside, enjoying the cool breeze.
Both dressed in black coats, Su Lun and Sabina did not stand out among the crowd clad in dark attire.
The coat concealed Sabina's exquisite figure, hiding her myriad charms from the bystanders. She held Su Lun's arm affectionately, unable to resist teasing, "Sir, you've really become very powerful."
"Heh."
Hearing the double entendre, Su Lun's eyes narrowed, and he laughed without a word.
He had previously gone all out in several great battles in the Northern Sea, stripping away the law comprehension of several sixth-order professionals—Space Law, Strength Law, Water Elemental Law, and so on.
It could be said that his current level of law comprehension was no less than that of the vast majority of sixth-order professionals, and he had a variety of law comprehensions as well. He had almost everything one could need.
The secret cultivation method of a succubus like Sabina would also draw upon a portion of her master's insights and transform them into her own understanding. After this series of operations, it was probably like a hundred-year expert bestowing comprehension, which saved her a lot of detours.
But obviously, Sabina was referring to more than just that.
At this moment, her face still held a tempting flush of red as if intoxicated, and she said, "I had been stuck at the threshold of the fourth order for a long time. Now I suddenly feel like I understand the insights I was lacking, and I should be able to advance very soon. No, not just to the fourth order, fifth order, or even sixth order... I feel like I have touched upon some of them."
This was the demonic talent of a succubus; her own cultivation was not fast, but with a powerful Great Demon King as a master, she could immediately soar.
Besides, she had also been very diligent, and her foundation was solid.
Su Lun also said, "Having insights is good. If possible, try to comprehend your own 'dominance'. Now that you have awakened your two-stage talent, there is a high probability of advancing to the sixth order. Dominance will be an essential ability for you to become a top professional..."
He shared some of the professional advancement requirements Mr. Jing had once told him about.
He also shared some of his own experiences of comprehending dominance.
"Oh."
Sabina listened attentively.
After listening, she looked at Su Lun with spring in her eyes and added, "Master, you will be staying in Lingdun for the coming period, right? Then would it be fine for your servant to attend to your daily needs at your side? After all, my cultivation still depends on your guidance..."
Su Lun chuckled as he listened.
Sabina's charm technique was becoming more refined, a constant provocation that made one's heart race.
He did not linger on this topic but changed the subject, "I have prepared a Void Potion for you and a set of void-growing equipment suitable for you. After the fourth-order fusion, your teleportation ability will be significantly enhanced."
The talent of a succubus innately possessed some void abilities. After advancing with void materials this time, he didn't dare say how much her combat power would increase, but at least her survival ability would be very strong.
Hearing that there was a gift, Sabina clung to Su Lun's arm and cooed, "Thank you, Master~"
Su Lun found her intimate gesture a bit overwhelming and controlled his hormone secretion.
Reminding himself that important matters were at hand, he turned to her and said, "Are we just going to wait on the street like this?"
"Mhm."
Sabina nodded and said, "The request to attend the event has been sent. Someone will come to get us shortly."
"Oh."
Su Lun nodded, his mind also pondering the information about the Moon Dance soiree.
The two strolled by the riverside.
From the moment Sabina first saw Su Lun, the bright smile on her face had never faded.
She looked at Su Lun with a somewhat dazed look in her eyes, suddenly bringing up the topic again, "Sir, I told you the café was nice, didn't I?"
"?"
Su Lun was slightly startled, reflected for a moment, and then realized her question was clearly not about the taste of the café's coffee.
But something else.
He felt that he actually didn't have any particular fetishes.
But having just tried it out... it seemed... rather nice?
Having no issue admitting it, Su Lun raised an eyebrow and said, "Yeah. Pretty good."
Sabina, pleased with the response, glanced at the dark river path and said in a playful whisper, "Actually... this place is quite nice too."
With that, Su Lun couldn't help but sweep a glance over the area; the riverside had secluded thickets, just right for some very romantic activities under the dim moonlight.
Oh, my.
Was he actually seriously considering her suggestion, which seemed... a bit... absurd?
Su Lun suddenly felt that he might be led down a path of no return to "outdoor XX" by his succubus maid.
He cleared his throat and said firmly, "Important matters first!"
Sabina covered her mouth and giggled coyly, "Oh~"
Her eyes twinkled with a mischievous and alluring smile, "How about next time?"
It was a pity there wasn't enough time.
"..."
Su Lun intended to refuse uprightly.
But the words choked in his throat...
and then there was no more.
In certain respects, Sabina knew him better than he knew himself.
....
As night fell, the streets and alleys of Lingdun gradually fogged over.
While Su Lun and his companion walked by the riverside, right at the appointed time, the haze of the street mist revealed the glow of car lights.
A shiny black steam sedan pulled up to the curb.
Sabina, clinging to Su Lun's arm, said, "Sir, the car has arrived."
Su Lun nodded without any change of expression, scrutinizing the car.
As the car stopped, a driver in a black suit with white gloves stepped out and opened the door.
The two approached and got into the car.
There was no conversation between them throughout the entire process.
Once they were seated inside the carriage, Su Lun noticed that it was specially made, blocking almost all external senses. There was no sound and no reference points could be seen. The windows, cloaked in mist, were completely opaque, leaving no way to discern what lay outside. This meant that most professionals would be completely disoriented once they got inside the car.
Su Lun scanned the area with his All-knowing Eye but didn't notice anything unusual.
Although the sensory perception was limited, it had no effect on spatial perception.
Su Lun's comprehension of Space Law was already very high, which allowed him to clearly know they were heading south along the riverside street...
Oh, no.
They had now turned onto Baker Street.
Sabina, holding Su Lun's hand, explained, "The location of the ball changes each time. None of the guests know where it will be."
"Hmm."
Su Lun didn't say much in response.
If he were the organizer, such secrecy would indeed be necessary.
After all, the rulers of Old Lington would definitely not wish for such a powerful underground influence to exist.
The steam car drove very smoothly, as if it wasn't moving at all.
Su Lun himself was proficient in mechanical technology. He noticed that although the car appeared similar to an ordinary steam car, it actually contained many black technologies not available on the market.
To prevent the passengers from discerning their direction, first and foremost, the steering of the car must be extremely smooth.
At a minimum, the passengers inside the compartment should not feel any significant jolting.
This was nearly impossible for a regular steam car with ordinary rigid suspension given the less-than-perfect road conditions in Old Lington.
From this detail, Su Lun guessed that "Lord Ying," the alter ego, seemed to have mastered some secret military mechanical techniques, or perhaps some kind of ancient technology.
However, this did not prevent him from determining the route of the steam car.
The car drove around the city streets and alleys, through some special tunnels, and then directly out of the city.
...
It was over an hour before the car finally stopped.
"West outskirts of Lingdun City?"
Sensing his precise location, Su Lun murmured to himself.
At this moment, Su Lun and Sabina both put on masks provided by the organizers of the ball.
Listening to the "click" as the car door handle was opened from outside, a woman dressed in a sexy bunny girl outfit stood respectfully at the car door and said, "Welcome to the Full Moon Ball."
Su Lun glanced at the woman and suddenly felt she looked familiar.
She wasn't wearing a mask, had blond hair and blue eyes, an excellent figure, and a sexy beauty mark under one eye.
A moment later, Su Lun immediately recognized her as Susanna McPherson, the popular singer of Lingdun City, who fans affectionately called "Sweetie" – a pure and innocent singer.
He had seen her advertisements on billboards when he and Lena went to the Rolling Stone Bar, which is why he had some impression of her.
Could the rumors be true?
This billion-worth female superstar was high society in Emperor Luying too, yet she was only a greeter at this ball?
"Tsk tsk... the noble circle sure knows how to play."
Su Lun silently marveled and looked no further.
He was more interested in where he was.
Looking around, it seemed that the car had stopped in a sealed underground garage.
At that moment, the bunny girl gestured toward the nearby staircase and said most respectfully, "Distinguished guests, please follow me this way."
Sabina elegantly hooked her arm through Su Lun's, signaling to follow the woman.
The three of them ascended the staircase, and the decorations suddenly became much more luxurious.
Before them was a corridor carpeted with a high-end carpet that cost tens of thousands per square meter, glittering with gold and luxury materials.
Every few meters on the wall hung a painting that at a glance was obviously the work of a master; upon appraisal, they were all originals!
These were high-end artworks that would fetch millions of Riso each at the Lingdun Auction House. That is to say, the decorations in this corridor alone were worth hundreds of millions!
After a few steps, the bunny girl led Su Lun and his companion into a small, equally luxurious room along the corridor, saying, "Our distinguished guests, please wait here for a moment. The ball will begin in half an hour. If you have any needs or requests, please let me know. I am your assigned attendant for this evening."
Having led the two inside, she also stayed in the room, then gently closed the door.
Sabina had been here before. Seeing Su Lun looking at the female attendant again, she introduced, "If Mr. Nicolas is interested in her, you can have her serve you here. You can even try any of the attendants you see at the ball later. This is a privilege that the organizers provide to their members..."
This was said in front of the bunny girl who, upon hearing it, didn't show any change of expression, but instead, smiled professionally, "It would be my honor to serve you."
Su Lun wasn't surprised by this, but he wasn't interested either.
What he cared more about was how to obtain the information he wanted from this ball.
Otherwise, the next one would be half a month away.
With the outbreak of "Red Death" and that parasite potion, who knows what could happen if he waited half a month...
...
Su Lun and Sabina chatted idly, and before they knew it, half an hour had passed.
Although the room isolated their perception, their Soul Perception and Space Perception were not restricted in the slightest.
Su Lun was aware that during their waiting time, several more groups of guests had arrived in the neighboring rooms, one after another.
Each group was skillfully spaced to avoid any unwanted encounters, waiting in their respective rooms.
Just then, the room trembled slightly for a moment.
It was akin to an earthquake.
Sabina obviously didn't know what was happening, a hint of confusion flickering in her eyes.
But Su Lun had already guessed that it was the noise of the airship taking off.
Because they were on a gigantic floating airship!
"Tsk tsk, 'Lord Ying' really has an extravagant reach. Wealth, power, technology, connections... just who is this illustrious person?"
While Su Lun maintained an impassive face, his mind was bustling with thoughts.
He had been sensing the space around him the whole time. The scale of this airship exceeded any steam-powered floating airship he had ever seen.
Su Lun was certain that no civilian airship would be of such an exaggerated volume.
And the only piece of information that matched the description of such an airship was the legendary secret weapon of the Emperor Luying military—the Gusmao airship!
A "Sky Mechanical Castle" said to fly by magnetic force, lighter than air itself!

chapters.title: Chapter 434 - 433: Full Moon Ball
chapters.content:
Su Lun had heard of the "Gusmao Airship" before—this information had been gleaned from the memories of the Mafa Royal Mechanical Knight, who had once served Princess Stika in the North Sea.
The military of Mafa had some top-secret intelligence that the Luying military department was developing a super-strong aerial fortress, aiming to control the airspace to cope with future battlefields.
This was not the kind of ordinary airship that hangs a basket from a large balloon but a true steel beast, which could even be described as a steam-powered steel castle in the sky.
However, there had been no reports of it being used on the battlefield yet.
Even the intelligence department of Mafa had only heard rumors that the Luying military was secretly developing it, but no one had actually seen it.
Su Lun hadn't expected to actually see the real thing here.
Whatever means the "Shadow Duke" had used to obtain this airship, just this feat alone truly justified his title as the King of Lington's Underworld.
Seeing the military airship, Su Lun's thoughts began to race, "A gang leader surely couldn't achieve this step alone. Who exactly is the financial backer behind this 'Red Oak Society'?"
After all, the Luying Empire had a millennium of heritage, and there were plenty of hidden crocodiles lurking beneath the surface.
For example, the low-key Lans family, the ambitious Duke Raphael...
This made Su Lun feel even more that he needed to be cautious about the dance party this time.
....
Aside from the slight tremor earlier that felt like an earthquake, there had been no other abnormalities.
But in his spatial awareness, Su Lun knew that this massive object was slowly ascending.
He didn't show any signs of abnormality and continued chatting leisurely with Sabina.
Half an hour later, Su Lun sensed that they were now at least three thousand meters above the ground, and the airship was still ascending.
Suddenly, the sound of a mechanism opening came from behind one wall of the room they were in.
Su Lun and Sabina turned their heads to see that the previous decorative wall had folded up, revealing a large panel of tempered glass.
Looking at the floating clouds outside, a hint of surprise appeared in Sabina's crystal-clear eyes—apparently, she had not expected that they had already ascended to the skies. She glanced at Su Lun, a brief flicker of exoticism disappeared in an instant, and she smiled charmingly, "Sir, would you like to take in the view?"
"Sure."
Su Lun stood up, and Sabina naturally took his arm as they walked to the viewing window.
From there, the entire city of Lington lay beneath them.
The city streets at night were brilliantly lit, and they were already above the layer of dense fog, so everything could be seen clearly.
The perennial haze that enveloped Lington lent a mysterious veil to the staggered buildings.
The lights along the Lokwarren River were the brightest, with gas lamps along the riverwalk lighting up long rows of orange points, clearly dividing the city into distinct northern and southern halves.
The fog was thickest in the south of the city, where factory chimneys ceaselessly spewed white smoke. Although the lighting in the noble district of the north was not as dense, it was very bright.
The entire city resembled a giant beast lying dormant on the ground, with the buildings like its spikes.
At that moment, a bright moon hung in the sky, its pale moonlight casting over the haze-veiled land, adding a layer of mystique to the world in sight.
It was Su Lun's first time overlooking Lington, this super-sized city.
He squinted at the brilliant lights below, feeling strangely relieved, and exclaimed, "Being up high really does offer a different view."
While enjoying the scenery, his gaze also passed through the viewing glass, sizing up this aerial fortress.
The hull was made of huge rivets joined together into a steel shell; from the side, many propellers of various sizes and purposes could be seen. From this angle, parts of the power equipment could be seen, with steam pipes puffing out white smoke. There were no obvious gas bags, and the shape was very peculiar, resembling a plump giant whale.
A thick steampunk vibe.
Su Lun looked closely, roughly understanding the structure of the "Gusmao Airship," but he couldn't figure out how such a heavy steel castle could fly, as the key to the energy system was hidden inside the airship.
He thought to himself, "Could it be ancient goblin technology?"
Without a doubt, if it was a mechanical product beyond the current level of technology, it was most likely archaeologically derived from ancient black technology.
Even though Su Lun couldn't understand it, it didn't stop him from having heard of the once glorious goblin civilization that had legends of "Cities in the Sky."
Given the Luying Empire's adventurers had been treasure hunting and pioneering for so many years, it wasn't hard to understand that the royal family had some black technology in their hands.
...
Su Lun and Sabina were admiring the aerial view from the edge of the bed when suddenly, there was a "click" sound of gears meshing in the room again.
A folding staircase slowly descended from the ceiling.
Sabina, holding Su Lun's arm, said, "Sir, it's time for the dance."
Su Lun nodded, and the two of them walked up the staircase.
The interior space of the mechanical airship was quite large; they didn't encounter any other attendees in the hallway.
Soon, after the rabbit-woman pushed open a door, the view abruptly opened up.
It was a luxurious banquet hall with dim lighting.
By the time Su Lun and his companion arrived, there were already dozens of masked people there, both men and women, dressed lavishly—judging just by the jewelry they wore, one could tell these individuals were extraordinary.
The air was filled with a faint scent of incense, refreshing to Su Lun as he sniffed.
Focusing on the incense burner in the corner, he identified it as "Could it be Maiden's Legend?"—a strangely named potion.
Although the name was odd, Su Lun had long heard of its renown!
Because the potion had miraculous effects such as beautifying and prolonging life, it was a legendary alchemical formula.
It was said that people whose life was nearing its end could breathe it and instantly live another half a year, and regular use could prolong life by many years!
The main ingredient of the potion was a fossil found only in the permafrost layers of the Far North Ice Field, incredibly rare. It was said to be a special potion concocted by the Pharmacist's Guild for the Luying royal family, with absolutely no availability otherwise on the market.
"What a treasure..."
Seeing this, Su Lun suddenly felt a bit like a country bumpkin.
He had made a fortune in the sea ruins before, and though he had money, his demeanor hadn't caught up yet.
At this ball, there were many things he hadn't seen before if not identified by the All-knowing Eye.
What Su Lun couldn't understand was, how could such exquisite items be offered for free?
He looked again at the buffet laden with drinks and food, all rare delicacies and aged wines that were not just for satisfying hunger or taste, they were also for various buffs. Certainly, they weren't just ordinary food.
Seeing this, Su Lun realized that the things provided for guests by the organizers of the ball were items that couldn't be bought with money, or were extremely hard to obtain.
One after another, some of the guests emerged from hidden corners. It was easy to tell; attendees all wore special masks to cover their faces, while those young men and women without masks were the designated waitstaff.
High-society socialites, royal ballet dancers, big-time singers...
Among those bunny girls, Su Lun recognized several familiar faces.
These seductively dressed beauties, unattainable in the eyes of ordinary people, were just part of the atmosphere at the ball for the real big shots.
Sabina, who was beside Su Lun, noticed him looking around and said affectionately, "If sir is interested, you can give it a try~"
Su Lun chuckled. He wasn't ogling the beauties, but rather wanted to see clearly who was attending the ball to deduce more information they possessed.
He discreetly observed everything around, but unfortunately, the masks provided by the organizers had enchantments that interfered with perception, making it impossible to see faces.
Su Lun could only remember their soul fluctuations, thinking that he might recognize them if he encountered them later.
....
The Full Moon Ball was by invitation only, rarely adding new members, so most of the attendees were returning veterans.
The desires at high-society balls were hidden, but at the "Full Moon Ball," an underground event, desires were released.
Those wearing masks were not surprised by anything, each engaged in their own activities in the corners of the banquet hall. Big shots could flirt with bunny girls, and the noble ladies could seek delight with male models, creating a vibrant and lively scene everywhere.
After all, it was nominally a ball, and as the mellow music started, people embraced each other and danced. Su Lun and Sabina also embraced in a slow dance.
Sabina, noticing Su Lun's apparent puzzlement at the unabashed reveling of chubby aristocrats, whispered in his ear, "Actually, many people here don't mind revealing their identities. Because everything about the ball is strictly confidential, even privately discussing it is forbidden. Otherwise, they would be hunted down by Lord Shadow Duke. His intelligence network is very sophisticated, covering both the underworld and the legitimate, even surpassing the Emperor Luying's intelligence agency. No one who has leaked information about the ball has survived. Moreover, joining the ball also acts as a status symbol for high society, and for many, revealing their identities can elevate their status in real societal interactions..."
Su Lun had begun to understand.
Actually, the high society was rife with scandals, which were an open secret. Now, under the rule of "no leakage," people naturally had no reservations.
The ball was membership-based, and many attendees knew each other or were connected in some way.
This was a kind of special alliance.
Only when everyone had dirt on each other could such an alliance be more stable.
One could imagine that the "Shadow Duke," the organizer, must possess a substantial amount of compromising information about the high society.
....
It didn't take long before a mysterious figure draped in a black robe and wearing a golden face mask entered the banquet hall.
Su Lun noticed this person immediately, feeling those unique soul fluctuations, and murmured to himself, "Very strong."
This was the mysterious "Duke of Shadows."
It's difficult for top-level professionals to discern the ranks from soul fluctuations, but to Su Lun, it felt at least seventh rank, and even somewhat resembled Mr. Jing's ethereal fluctuations.
"However, his soul fluctuations... is his lifespan nearing its end?"
Despite the impressive aura, Su Lun sensed some information that others could not perceive.
Similar to the time he met Grandmother Katusha on the boat to Mountain Hermit Nation, the soul fire of the man in the golden mask seemed like a flickering candle in the wind.
Which meant, this man was nearing the end of his life, about to die.
Su Lun then realized, the arrangement of the "Legend of Youth" potion at the venue was meant for his own use.
Considering that this man had been the king of Lington's underworld over twenty years ago, his old age made sense.
Everyone halted and bowed ceremoniously.
The man in the golden mask gestured for them to rise, and said, "We are all old friends here, no need for such formality. Before the masquerade officially begins, our 'Lady Marquess Agnes' has a dance performance for everyone. I believe you all would rather see the beautiful lady dance than listen to an old man like me ramble on..."
As he spoke, a spotlight fell on a lady in a black evening gown in the hall. Although her face was masked and her features indistinct, her attire alone spoke of high nobility.
All eyes turned to her.
This noblewoman, without further ado, removed her mask and revealed a reluctantly amused smile, "Oh dear, dancing at my age can be quite embarrassing."
She was a charming, mature beauty; though she mocked her own age, her skin was as tender as a young woman's, and her voluptuous figure carried a distinctive mature charm.
She promptly slipped off her black evening gown and then continued, "A bet is a bet. Since the last ball made a request and a gentleman has fulfilled that request, and he wished to see me dance in front of everyone, I can only oblige and hope not to disappoint..."
None of the attendees showed any surprise, instead, they clapped in perfect harmony with the mood.
In truth, whether before or after crossing over, when it came to the GHS, the onlookers all displayed uniform gentlemanliness: may the good people live in peace.
Su Lun watched in astonishment as a lady marquess, truly a big shot of high society, boldly took the stage under the spotlight and began a provocative dance before everyone present.
Noble ladies were masters in various dances, and Lady Marquess Agnes was no exception, dancing confidently, her movements both sexy and pleasing to the eye.
Indeed, this opening dance was undeniably impressive.
Su Lun, accustomed to seeing all manners of lady performances in the night scene, found that watching flamboyant dances did not faze him ordinarily.
But watching the dance of this aristocratic Lady Marquess, brimming with grace, somehow intrigued him.
He also marveled at the strict rules of this ball.
"Truth or dare," saying dare, even the Lady Marquess herself had to perform personally?
Sabina, beside him, also watched with great interest, her voice sultry as she whispered in Su Lun's ear, "So this is what you like?"
Su Lun didn't deny that he found it quite interesting, "Not bad at all."
Sabina listened and chuckled lightly without speaking.
Su Lun thought about it and could understand.
The private lives of Luying's nobility were inherently chaotic. For ladies and madams who grew up in noble families, there often weren't any strong convictions about chastity. They clearly understood that their greatest value lay in marriage alliances. Beauty was merely a tool, available for a price if the offer was enough, not about liking or not.
That the Lady Marquess was dancing here meant that the benefits she received in exchange were certainly more than what she was currently giving.
And correspondingly, the "Duke of Shadow" held even more leverage over her.
These leverages were genuinely scarce resources.
After the integration of resources, some incredible uses would emerge.
This was the most important reason why the influence of this ball was growing.
Su Lun thought of this and felt as if he had glimpsed the tip of an iceberg, finding the "Full Moon Ball" increasingly ingenious.
As long as they weren't enemies, it was definitely a great asset.
....
An erotic opening dance unveiled the curtain of the ball.
After all, these people weren't here to enjoy, but to exchange resources and information.
After the man with the golden mask made his appearance, he did not speak again, but sat in a corner where the light just managed to highlight his silhouette.
A butler-like person presided over the ball next.
The interaction segment then began.
The masked individuals began speaking, each stating their needs.
"The reporter from 'Lingdun Entertainment News' has some scandalous information, which is detrimental to me, and happens to belong to Senator Physis, who is my political enemy. Someone is blackmailing me with this. I need someone to handle it. The reward is one Charon silver coin..."
"I can take care of that. I can assure you that it won't appear in the newspapers."
"..."
"The council will have a proposal on ore trade reform the day after tomorrow, I need some accurate internal information. The reward is two silver coins."
"I know. But I need three silver coins."
"Agreed!"
"..."
"I need information about the assassin involved in the assassination of Count Malory."
"I have a batch of sensitive heavy weapons that need to be shipped out, and I need a pass."
"There's a war going on in the Mastan Principality, I need a mediator. The reward is one gold coin."
"..."
One after another, issues were raised and then taken up by someone.
Everyone was evidently very familiar with this process.
If no one could take care of them, the issues would end up with the "Duke of Shadow."
Though immediate answers weren't given, everyone knew that as long as it wasn't outright refused, it could be resolved.
Aside from those who spoke out, some members unwilling to reveal their identity projected their requests on the public screen via a special projector.
Normally such a resource exchange could be achieved at an ordinary social gathering, but the members preferred to trade here.
Elsewhere, even with people known in real life, there was still the fear that the trade partners might have ulterior motives.
But here, the trade was absolutely safe.
Because all trades were guaranteed by the "Duke of Shadow."
If someone took on the request, they had to perform it according to the contract.
These were the rules of the ball.
Just like the erotic dance performed by that Lady Marquess at the beginning.
...
True to being a high-end exchange meeting, all the discussions were about real big business.
Su Lun listened to others, carefully observing everything without rushing to speak up.
From the issues raised, he could generally guess the identities and factions of those people, and there were some whose identities remained sheltered.
He also noticed that the attendees of the ball came from diverse backgrounds, including big shots from all sectors.
The issues special enough to be resolved at this ball were all very challenging.
Listening to them, Su Lun deeply realized that Luying's capital, Lingdun, concealed too many big players. Those issues that sounded unsolvable were often resolved in a mere sentence by these individuals.
Merely participating in this buzzing event allowed him to gather much top-secret information and infer many changes in Luying's upper echelons.
But Su Lun knew it was impossible to freeload information for a long time.
The members were active because there was an unwritten rule at the ball: frequent attendance without displaying "value" could lead to expulsion from the membership.
Su Lun understood another implication of this unwritten rule: those who didn't give the "Duke of Shadow" something to leverage might be doubted.
Because participating in the exchange allowed the organizers to confirm who you are, what you need, your purpose, motivation, and stance...
From the information Sabina held, this "Duke of Shadow" always represented absolute neutrality, taking no sides.
It was almost certain that he did not stand with the royalists, nor was he a force supported by any of the councilors from the six major nations...
But he wielded significant power within both the royal family and the parliament.
Members with conflicts could seek his mediation, but he favored no one.
This was also the most important reason why Su Lun had decided to come here in search of clues.
If "neutrality" was just a facade, this ball, having existed for over twenty years and survived numerous political shifts, would have collapsed long ago.
Yet, the descendants of Mr. Jing, those intelligence agents who had been embedded in Lingdun for centuries, had never heard of him.
On the contrary, the "Duke of Shadows" had become more mysterious over the years.
The only certainty was that he was extremely powerful.
There had long been rumors from both the criminal underworld and law enforcement that people wanted him dead, yet here he was, still very much alive.
Those who had wanted to kill him had all disappeared.
...
The atmosphere during the exchange session was very subtle.
There were quite a few people hiding their intentions, and after observing for a while, Su Lun entered his own request into the sensor, projecting it on the screen, "A special formula of hallucinogenic potion has recently surfaced in the gang circles of South City. I would like to know the source of the potion and some detailed intelligence; acquiring the formula would be even better. The reward is one Charon silver coin."
The "Charon silver coin" is the circulating currency at the ball, a token issued by the "Duke of Shadows".
The nature of exchanges at this ball is barter, but sometimes when the trading parties do not have equivalent exchange tokens, these silver coins come into play.
Naturally, Su Lun could not directly ask for the identity of the "Curator". Having just made contact, it would be too risky if the other party were also at the ball.
Moreover, the potion's appearance in South City was no longer a secret; many well-informed forces had received the news and were also inquiring.
However, finding the "Curator" was not the ultimate goal.
Su Lun's goal was to find out who crafted that batch of potions and how the Red Death had originated.
No sooner had the question been posed than a row of anonymous text appeared on the sensor, which looked like a notebook: "This batch of goods was secretly developed by the 'Buckidge Biopharmaceuticals'. The lab is at their headquarters, inaccessible to outsiders. Fortunately, I know they have a new drug release conference coming up, and they will be launching this potion. Forget about the formula; it is tied to major interests as a special remedy for a disease and will definitely not be sold externally. That's all the information I have. As for the reward, it's up to you. Oh, and one more thing—there are quite a few people interested in this potion, looking to invest, so you better act fast."
"..."
Upon reading this, Su Lun knew he had come to the right place!
This inquiry had lead directly to the source of the potion.
"Buckidge Biopharmaceuticals" is one of the huge pharmaceutical giants in Luying, and also a Rodriguez family business!
The Senior Councilor of the Rodriguez family is also the staunchest supporter of the "Faith Freedom Act."
Now knowing who the opponent was, the next steps were clear.
Su Lun hadn't expected to obtain such crucial intelligence so easily.
Having achieved his primary purpose for coming to the ball, he breathed a sigh of relief.
He could now quietly observe from the sidelines.
There was not only demand here at the ball, but also surplus resources.
Soon, however, Su Lun saw another piece of intelligence that greatly interested him.
Someone had posted a message: "I still have a batch of specialized equipment left over from when those guys from the new faction imported from Mafa during the Fog Moon coup, intended for replicating mechanical armor. It's 90% new, currently stored in the royal shipyard warehouse. Duke Rafael is operating in the shadows trying to buy it; if not sooner, the royal shipyard is likely to sell it to him in a fortnight. I don't want this equipment to end up in his hands. Interested parties can bid. Transaction includes two silver coins; the price of the machinery will be discussed separately. I will find a way to get it out, and ensure a safe transaction channel."
"Replicated mechanical armor import equipment?"
The news had Su Lun's attention immediately.
While Mafa banned the export of mechanical armor, it did not prohibit the export of various mechanical equipment.
Although Rich Lady Lena's trade guild had also helped gather a batch of second-hand mechanical equipment, Su Lun had seen those lists, and most of it was outdated production equipment from Luying.
Although it was barely usable, it could not meet the production needs of the mini void world's war workshop.
But this batch imported from Mafa was different!
During the Fog Moon coup, when the new faction seized power, they planned to reform Luying, including numerous initiatives to learn from Mafa's advanced systems.
Among these was the "mechanical armor factory" plan.
This imported equipment was obtained at a high cost and through special channels from Mafa. The Prime Minister at the time wanted to start with replication, gradually exploring and enabling Luying to pursue the path of a mechanical powerhouse.
However, the Empress swiftly regained control and power, and the old faction brutally terminated the new government that had been in office for a few months. All proposals related to the new policies were fiercely suppressed. As a result, those expensive imported machines hadn't even been put into production before they were stored away.
Without policy support, these specialized devices were useless in others' hands.
Because mechanical armor required high-level mechanics, blueprints, and a systematic training system for mechanical talent...
Nothing less would suffice.
Even Luying's major munitions merchants couldn't utilize these instruments effectively; the equipment was too specialized for the production of high-precision parts for mechanical armor. Thus, even in their possession, they couldn't produce even modestly decent mechanical armors.
Using these machines to manufacture Luying's decades-old mechanical weaponry would be even less efficient than using outdated equipment.
But it was different for Su Lun!
Whether it was mechanical armor designs, mechanical talents, or even precision core instruments (like those on the submarine), he had them all!
Seeing this information, Su Lun immediately became interested.
Indeed, high-end resources were in the hands of a select few.
This ball was incredibly worthwhile!
PS: I haven't deleted the comments from the past few days because of policy reasons that render them invisible. It should resolve in a few days.

chapters.title: Chapter 435 - 434: The scenery is nice in the alley
chapters.content:
"Good stuff..."
Su Lun looked at the projected sale information for that batch of mechanical equipment on the public screen, and it was impossible not to be envious.
This imported equipment from Mafa was top-notch. If it really fell into his hands, he wouldn't even need to make many modifications. Matched with the high-precision devices on the previous submarine, he could immediately assemble a mature industrial assembly line in the mechanical warfare factory in the minor void world.
This would save several years compared to the plan to modify an old equipment assembly line.
It was just in time, as the batch of materials from the Lei Cat Trading Company had also arrived, and there was no shortage of materials. Now with this batch of instruments, the mechanical puppet legion could form a collective combat force in a short time!
Moreover, more importantly, Su Lun didn't think he would have another channel to get such good equipment in a short time if he missed this opportunity.
The people from the new policy back then managed to get this batch of fine imported goods through means at the imperial level. Ordinary people, no matter how rich, wouldn't have such access.
Even if there were some smuggled goods on the black market, the quantity would definitely not be large, nor would the functionality be so complete!
For Su Lun, this was definitely a "great opportunity" that came along while he was figuratively sleeping on a pillow.
He had to obtain it at all costs!
....
However, after the surprise, Su Lun didn't let the sudden windfall cloud his judgment.
Instead, he sensed a whiff of conspiracy and began to think more calmly.
Nowadays, the entire mechanical industry of the Luying Empire was very backward; this equipment, which was decades ahead of the current era, was of little use to others. It was almost only useful to forces interested in researching mechanical warriors.
So, correspondingly, this special supply-and-demand relationship also filtered out potential buyers.
There were many wealthy people in the Luying Empire, but not many willing to be generous fools.
Thus, the news felt like a targeted bait.
Luring certain specific groups of people.
Once someone showed interest in them, it could be confirmed that they had a use for these instruments and were almost certainly aiming to use them to manufacture mechanical warriors.
Apart from Duke Raphael, whose technological level was unknown, and Su Lun, who had the capability to create mechanical warriors on his own, it was unlikely that anyone else would be interested in buying a bunch of "useless instruments" that cost several times more than ordinary equipment.
Before making a risky decision, Su Lun typically considered the worst possible outcome.
With that in mind, he pondered, "Suppose this batch of goods is bait for fishing; then, two major forces are under significant suspicion: one is Rafael's people, and the other is Mafa's people."
Su Lun had his hands on neural-mechanical technology and had intercepted the "secret submarine mechanical research institute" intended as a dowry from the Mafa Empire to King Oleg of the North Sea.
Both forces were the aggrieved parties.
But he didn't rule out the possibility that other forces, such as the Military Intelligence Department of Luying, or others might also know about this information.
After all, the news about the mechanical puppet legion's slaughter during the great war in Moros City-State had appeared in the newspapers. Those in the know could speculate, and they might guess that he had the ability to manufacture mechanical warriors.
Yet Su Lun thought that if this truly were a fishing conspiracy, it would certainly have enemies, regardless of who they were.
But he must be prepared for the worst.
...
Various possibilities flashed through Su Lun's mind in an instant.
After considering for a while, the biggest uncertainty was not someone else, but the organizer of this ball!
The 'Shadow Duke' with the Golden Mask had spoken only once since the beginning and had then fallen silent, sitting quietly in the shadowy part of the lights.
He was like a director of a stage play, silently watching everything happening on stage.
He organized the Round Moon Ball,
And he knew everything.
Su Lun, knowing that this was an old man at the end of his life, also understood his indifferent, detached attitude.
But this made people somewhat puzzled.
A Great Alchemist would not be unaware of his own physical condition. Death was approaching, and all the power and wealth would pass like fleeting clouds. So what was the purpose of him still being active at the ball?
Who did he represent, or... did he represent only himself?
The 'Shadow Duke' seemed more and more mysterious to Su Lun.
These doubts were something he didn't have time to explore for the time being.
Because the seller had already made it clear that if no one bought it, the batch of sealed equipment would end up in the hands of Duke Raphael, and it would be impossible to buy it back.
There was simply no room for hesitation.
The ball continued, and the pleasant classical dance music drifted through the banquet hall.
Su Lun thought for a moment, then asked the Sabrina he was embracing and dancing with, "Is there a way to confirm who sent that message?"
Sabrina was very smart. She naturally knew what her master was referring to and gently replied, "Not now. But it can be checked, though the risk is not small."
Su Lun's eyes flickered with contemplation at her words, but he didn't pursue the matter further.
Sabrina's response did not make him feel uncomfortable, as it was just an offhand question.
Because he was very clear, this method wouldn't work.
Even if he privately contacted the owner of the goods, if this were a conspiracy, the associated risks would still have to be faced.
Perhaps even more dangerous.
On the contrary, if he contacted them through the platform of the ball, intermediaries might provide a safety net.
He also wanted to determine just how truly neutral the 'Shadow Duke' was and how much power he really had.
After pondering for a moment, Su Lun said, "I'm planning to take on this batch of goods. Just in case, once we disembark the airship, be ready to instruct your people to go into hiding."
If there were issues with the organizers, Sabrina's cover identity would be exposed, and most of the painstakingly established intelligence network might have to be sacrificed.
Sabrina listened without the slightest surprise and promptly complied, "Mm."
She had this realization from the very beginning.
After all, everything she had belonged to her master.
...
Compared to what was gained, the risk was entirely worth taking a gamble on.
Su Lun had already thought of a countermeasure. Without hesitation, he directly messaged the person who provided the tip and then handed over two silver coins to finalize the deal.
The ball was taking place on an airship, thousands of meters in the sky.
For others, it probably meant there was nowhere to escape.
But for him, survival was not a big issue.
Moreover, he felt that even if the organizers were conspiring to set a trap, it was highly unlikely they would act on the airship.
Otherwise, the "Full Moon Ball's" many years of a neutral image would instantly collapse. Losing such an important resource platform, even if they obtained the technology, the cost would not be light.Besides, Sabina's identity was fake to begin with; no one could be certain they were the real targets.
If there was to be a move made, it would be after the airship had landed!
....
Just as Su Lun had predicted, after he and the buyer completed their transaction, no accidents occurred.
The Full Moon Ball lasted for over two hours.
Then they each returned to their rooms, the airship landed somewhere unknown, and a private car took them back to Lingdun City.
Before long, Su Lun and Sabina were sitting in the same special carriage they had arrived in.
In the sealed carriage, Su Lun took out a black umbrella and expanded his perceptual range.
Everything was normal.
Besides the driver, no one else followed them.
From the time they got on the carriage before the ball, to on the airship, and now, the whole process was jammed of any communication signals.
Now that they had come down, Su Lun used a Spatial Technique to open a channel for Sabina, allowing her to send a covert command to her line's person in the Mirror Organization at the first opportunity.
Thinking it over for safety's sake, Su Lun clenched his sorcerer's seals with both hands and uttered lightly, "Necromancy!"
A black pentagram formation lit up, and the void of a different plane connected; the carriage was suddenly assaulted with a strong whiff of necromantic energy.
On a closer look, a glossy-feathered crow had been summoned through necromancy.
As a professional intelligence agent, Sabina naturally had a strong psychological quality, and although she anticipated the possibility of danger, she remained very calm. Her eyes brightened as she saw the added presence of the black crow in the carriage, as if she found it amusing, "Wow~ Master, is this that legendary Dire Crow of yours?"
The ability of the Dire Crow to downgrade dimensions had shocked the entire world during the battle at the Moros City-State. This harbinger of death was now as famous as Su Lun, a true "celebrity."
Also because of it, the price of crow pets in Lingdun had exploded more than tenfold.
Su Lun nodded, "Yes."
"Wow..."
Sabina had read the detailed introduction in the newspapers, and she hadn't expected the legendary, extremely dangerous bird of death to look quite cute before its transformation, appearing dazed and foolish.
She then asked, "What's its name?"
Before Su Lun could respond, the black crow on his shoulder cried out, "Lord Crow, Lord Crow!"
"Eh...?"
Sabina found it miraculous and exclaimed in surprise, "It can talk?"
Speaking was secondary, the key was that it understood human speech!
"Yes."
Su Lun couldn't help but smile bitterly and added, "Its name is 'Lord Crow'."
Upon hearing this, Sabina's interest was piqued. Although the name sounded a bit undignified, it seemed fun!
Her eyes sparkling with curiosity, she eagerly asked, "Lord Crow, your feathers are so pretty, may I touch you?"
The black crow tilted its head, looking at her with a haughty expression.
Su Lun explained with a hint of resignation, "This silly bird doesn't care for people unless there's food."
"Is that so..."
Thinking it over, Sabina took out a piece of jerky to try her luck, but the crow didn't even give her a glance.
Su Lun handed her a piece of rotting flesh, saying, "It's very fussy. Try feeding this."
"Ah?"
Sabina's elegant brow rose, finding the situation increasingly amusing.
She took the rotting flesh from Su Lun and offered it to the crow.
And sure enough, when given what it liked, the black crow happily gulped it down and didn't forget to flatter in exchange for the treat, "Beautiful lady! Beautiful lady!"
Su Lun winced, giving the bird a glance.
"Thank you~"
Sabina chuckled joyfully, playing along and responding earnestly. She then carefully reached out to pet the black crow, treating it with the same courtesy one would show a person, "Wow, Lord Crow, you're quite the handsome bird."
Lord Crow apparently understood the compliment and, fluttering its little legs, hopped onto Sabina's hand.
Its proud demeanor seemed to say: Lord Crow allows you to pet me some more.
Sabina couldn't help but laugh at the crow's perfectly mimicked anthropomorphic mannerisms.
Su Lun was somewhat surprised, jesting, "You're the first person this silly bird has ever approached on its own."
Sabina blinked, clearly delighted, "Really?"
The master's pet, of course, must have a very good relationship.
...
The steam car carried Su Lun and his companion for about half an hour, moving from the suburbs to the urban area.
The first part of the journey was without issue, but it was at this moment that Su Lun suddenly sensed something, his expression changing ever so slightly.
Sabina was still teasing the black crow and, sensing the change in Su Lun's demeanor, asked, "What's wrong?"
Su Lun said gravely, "We've deviated from our route. We just turned onto 'Hotten Street.' This isn't the way to the Queen's District; it's the way to Franklin District."
Instantly understanding the implication, Sabina's expression also grew serious.
Logically, the car was supposed to take them to a designated location.
But now they had strayed.
This was a serious problem.
She glanced at the earnest-faced Su Lun and remained silent, evidently her master had anticipated this.
The worst possibility had indeed occurred.
Su Lun's brow furrowed tightly, recalling the web-like city routes of Lingdun City, clearly aware of their current location.
The inexplicable detour could have been understood as a temporary lane change due to some road condition, but several subsequent, unhesitant wrong turns convinced him that there was definitely something wrong with the driver!
"Is there really a problem with the organizers?"
Su Lun looked very serious, almost foreseeing the worst-case scenario.
Or could it be... that someone infiltrated the Full Moon Misunderstanding and bribed this driver?
But it was no longer important.
What was certain now was that a fight was imminent!
The carriage had barriers to prevent perception, so it was highly likely that the driver was still unaware that Su Lun had detected the problem. The car sped on.
But now that he was sure that there was a problem with the route, Su Lun naturally wouldn't just watch this driver take them into an ambush. The black crow hadn't given any warning yet, meaning that there was no fatal danger nearby. It was still timely to take action.
With that thought, Su Lun waved his hand, and suddenly a black scythe appeared in his grasp.
He had no intention of communicating with the driver and, without hesitation, swung his scythe, severing the upper part of the carriage and, together with it, the head of the driver in the cockpit.
The cold night wind whooshed in, and the enclosed carriage abruptly became a "convertible."
In front of the car seat, a headless corpse gushed blood in spurts.
Su Lun devoured the "grey mist" from the driver's body in one gulp, then quickly leapt from the car with Sabina in his arms.
Without control, the steam car crashed headlong into a red-brick residence ahead.
With a "bang," the front of the car collapsed a wall and charged straight in.
Su Lun barely glanced back as he pulled Sabina into a small alley and bolted, "Let's go!"
...
The time was now past midnight.
Aside from a few Drunkards who were unaware of their surroundings, the streets were nearly void of people.
After the temperature dropped, this time became the foggiest in Lingdun City, with visibility reduced to a mere twenty or thirty meters. In streets not main arteries of the city, gas street lamps were few and far between. The dim light from the other side of the street provided no feeling of safety. Pedestrians walking along these streets felt as if on the verge of an abyss.
However, this hardly affected Su Lun at all.
Even with low visibility, his spatial perception allowed him to clearly discern his surroundings.
He jumped aloft with Sabina in his arms, landing atop a nearby tower that was a perfect vantage point to observe the car crash site from a distance.
Su Lun watched for any movement on the streets, while digesting the memories he had just stripped away, and thought with some surprise, "So it wasn't the organizers after all?"
At the same time, he breathed a sigh of relief.
After stripping the memories from the driver, Su Lun realized the man was a long-term sleeper agent planted by other espionage forces at the Full Moon Ball.
As to who exactly was behind this lackey, he had no idea.
All he did was follow orders, directing him to drive to Franklin District's fresh fish market.
Now that it was clear this was not the doing of the mysterious 'Shadow Duke,' the pressure suddenly lessened by half.
There was no urgency for Su Lun to flee anymore.
He wanted to see if he could find more clues, uncover who was baiting the trap.
The car accident caused quite an uproar, gradually waking nearby residents and lighting up some lamps.
Seeing Sabina beside him with a tense expression, Su Lun gestured for her to relax, saying, "It wasn't the organizers who acted. Tell your people to stand down for now. We'll see how things go before deciding the next step."
He knew Sabina was waiting for his judgment to issue a second command.
"Okay!"
Upon hearing this, Sabina visibly relaxed.
Then she quickly sent a coded message through the communicator: Stand by.
There wasn't a small number of people on her intelligence team's chain of command, and to avoid leaving traces for investigation, some key "hardware" needed erasure.
Previously uncertain of the enemy's identity, Sabina had issued a command for all her agents to prepare for submergence.
If the second message she sent was "Execute," or if there was no command received after a certain amount of time, all intelligence personnel would immediately enter an emergency state of submersion, severing ties and "disappearing."
In the short term, even Sabina would struggle to reestablish contact with them, with some potentially lost forever.
The cost was akin to sacrificing a limb to save one's life, and the loss would certainly not be small.
Now that the loss could be avoided, it was indeed a relief.
Furthermore, if the enemy were the ball's organizers, that would be the true disaster.
The threat level had dropped significantly now that confirmation had been made that it wasn't them.
The worried frown on Sabina's forehead finally relaxed a bit. After pondering for a moment, a smile gradually appeared on her face, and she added, "If it's not the organizer's fault, Master, you might actually benefit from this misfortune."
Su Lun glanced at her, "Oh?"
Sabina explained, "We encountered trouble on the carriage from the ball, which obviously indicates an internal problem with them. Under such circumstances, the 'Shadow Duke' will definitely compensate us. There was a similar accident before, where someone disrupted the transaction rules of the ball, causing a huge loss to a member. But within two days, the 'Shadow Duke' had everything perfectly handled, made up for the loss of that member, and even offered a sincere compensation..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's respect for the organizers of the Lunar Ball increased a notch.
It took some audacity to handle things so well.
Thinking about the grandeur of the earlier ball, Su Lun guessed that the compensation must indeed be sincere.
But he thought that the matter of compensation could be discussed later.
What Su Lun was more concerned about was the cargo.
It would be a pity if they took such a big risk and didn't get the goods.
No matter how good the compensation, he felt that it could not compare to the value that the batch of imported machinery currently brought to him.
Sabina, obviously well acquainted with her master's thoughts, smiled with a tilt of her eyebrows and said reassuringly, "Master, rest assured, if that cargo truly exists, it will be delivered in accordance with the agreement made at the ball. The 'Shadow Duke's' influence in Lingdun is extremely terrifying."
Listening, Su Lun nodded, "I hope so."
Although it seemed like everything had turned out well so far, the goods were something he had gambled his life on.
If he had not detected the problem in advance, by now he might have already fallen into the enemy's ambush.
If the other party dared to bait them, then naturally they had the confidence to kill.
Lingdun City was a place where tigers and dragons lay hidden, and Su Lun did not delude himself into thinking he could definitely survive if caught in someone's trap.
...
The two hunkered down in the tower to observe for a while.
The car accident drew some onlookers, ordinary people and professionals alike.
Su Lun watched in secret, but the fishers he was expecting did not show.
Those guys probably knew that they had only one chance for an ambush, and once it was blown, they had to quickly clean up.
After all, the 'King of Lingdun's Underworld' was not to be trifled with. Daring to make a move on his territory meant being prepared for a mad retaliation.
Judging from the "cases" Sabina mentioned that had happened before, all those involved in the ambush would be dragged out.
The consequences would be something that not an average person could withstand.
Su Lun was somewhat looking forward to that.
Because he guessed that the Empire of Mafa or Duke Raphael could be behind this.
He also wanted to see how the 'Shadow Duke' would deal with these people.
Before the constables arrived, a group of mysterious men in trench coats got there first. They quickly cleaned up the scene, taking away the bodies and the vehicles.
The car accident ended right there and then.
Seeing the professionalism of the cleanup, Su Lun guessed that these men in trenches coats were certainly those sent by the 'King of Lingdun's Underworld' to clean up the aftermath.
This kind of matter could not possibly be escalated to the officials.
With the crisis resolved, Sabina was no longer tense, but to be safe, she did not contact anyone.
The two jumped down from the tower and began to wander aimlessly on the foggy Lingdun streets in the dead of night.
...
