This ghostly young lady's crystalline eyes sparkled playfully as she looked at the body and said, "Mr. Su Lun, could you make her into a doll for me? One that can sing. Her singing is so beautiful..."
When the two first met at the Storm Manor, Su Lun knew that Pestoya liked to collect various horror dolls.
Hearing her request, he was not surprised at all, and smiled slightly, "Sure."
And the art of horror wax figures could preserve many of the body's abilities from when it was alive. The legendary Hunter's body was a second solution, [C-025-Singer], and the wax figure produced wouldn't be bad at singing, at least combat-wise.
After Su Lun cleaned up the body, he sat cross-legged on the spot and meditated.
The battle had seriously injured him, and now that the overall situation was settled, he finally had time to heal.
His attention was also constantly on the distant valley where Pierre and the outer god were making their last stand.
It wasn't just him; almost everyone was watching.
At that moment, the valley's destructive energy was so dreadful that it felt like a radiation source, making one's heart tremble from several kilometers away.
Soon, when the glow of dawn rose, Mr. Jing's voice suddenly came through the communicator, "It's done."
Su Lun's eyes snapped open, and he listened joyfully: Senior sister understands me!
Without asking another question, he clenched the sorcerer's seal and teleported there decisively.
At that moment, the valley was a rotten black, with various chaotic law fluctuations and spatial rifts scattered everywhere.
The violent law of calamity eradicated all life in the valley, turning it into an intensely cursed land of calamity. It was likely that nothing would grow here for the next hundred years.
There were also flames of law left by Master Pierre, making the entire valley seem like a volcano's mouth; entering it would stir up internal fire, making one feel as though their body was being burned.
Very cautiously avoiding the spatial rifts, Su Lun, with his substantial understanding of calamity and fire laws and protected by his domain field, could carefully approach.
As he infused dark spiritual power into the black umbrella, he quickly sensed some soul fluctuations.
Su Lun teleported there and quickly collected several fragmented soul shards into the black umbrella.
Unfortunately, at the last moment of his life, Master Pierre had burned his soul power to trap that outer god. Later, when the energy had calmed down a bit, and after quite a bit of time had passed, the soul had not completely dissipated, all thanks to the master's far superior soul strength compared to ordinary professionals.
However, even as fragments, he did not dare to absorb them recklessly.
These shards contained both Master Pierre's and the outer god's soul, and directly absorbing their superior rank awareness could likely cause him to collapse on the spot.
Fortunately, the black umbrella could preserve the spiritual body, and Su Lun planned to find a safe environment to slowly absorb them.
He searched the rotten black valley again, but found no remnants of anything.
The place was like a nuclear explosion site, with no solid objects left behind.
...
Su Lun returned to the outside of the Alchemy Hall.
By now, there weren't many people left.
After the visiting nobility from the Lingdun Legion confirmed that the outer god was dead, they left the area.
The death of the outer god was just the beginning for the opposing nobles; what awaited them was a feast of rights as they prepared to divide the carcass of the decaying lion that was Ruying.
When Su Lun returned, Mr. Jing was still sitting cross-legged on a rock in the farm.
The previous battle had clearly taken a toll on her as well.
Around the farm were seven or eight people in gold-patterned cloaks, including Mr. Hei and Qiantiao, who had rushed over.
The core members of the Dawn were almost all here, each bearing some injuries.
The light of dawn scattered the darkness, and there was a trace of fatigue on everyone's faces.
But there was a sense of relief in everyone's expression.
Qiantiao, seeing Su Lun return, greeted him, "Su Lun boy, are you alright?"
The battle here had been the most dangerous, and from the beginning to tracking an individual all by himself for so long, the peril was naturally unspeakable.
Su Lun smiled and replied, "I'm fine."
As he spoke, he walked over to Qiantiao and the others.
Mr. Jing also spoke, asking, "How is it?"
Su Lun felt slightly regretful as he replied, "I found some Soul Shards."
Mr. Jing seemed unconcerned as usual, nodding his head.
The conspiracy of the outer gods was now thoroughly concluded, and although the dawn breeze was tinged with a hint of the scent of blood, it felt free and comfortable nonetheless.
This place was the northern suburbs of Lingdun City, where sounds of fierce gunfire still erupted from the city.
But the men of Dawn had no intention of joining in.
They had assembled in Lingdun precisely to deal with the outer gods.
As for the situation in Lingdun, what the outcome for the Bonaparte royal family would be, and who would eventually take power... these matters were of little significance to the people of Dawn.
As long as the followers of the divine were not in power, they were indifferent.
Some followers of the outer gods might have escaped, but if they were to rise again, it would not be for countless years. Continue reading at My Virtual Library Empire
As long as faith remained, the gods would not die.
Su Lun reflected on the events of the night and only afterward realized that so much had occurred.
From the scheming against the demon monk, the battle had been constant.
Large-scale wars truly were meat grinders; in this war, not to mention Master Pierre, Su Lun knew of three eighth-tier professionals who had perished. There were even more among the seventh-tier, including two of the "Top Ten Legendary Hunters" whom Su Lun had personally killed. Below them were truly just cannon fodder...
Having seen too much death, Su Lun felt deeply moved, and he increasingly felt his own strength was insufficient.
Witnessing such a large-scale war for the first time, he profoundly understood how weak an individual's power really was.
He also became more determined that his strategy of using an army of puppets must quickly increase in strength.
In the midst of continuous fierce battles, he also gained a lot, most notably realizing his own "Domain of Death."
Seventh-tier professionals represented a significant threshold, and now it seemed he was also approaching that threshold, and Su Lun's plans for his future path became clearer.
In his storage space, there was still a "Hundred Thousand Blood-Refined Crystal," and after digesting it, it should be enough to integrate the "Isaac's Giant Strength."
Then there was the matter of Master Pierre and the soul shard of that outer god; it was still uncertain what he would gain after digesting those...
But after digesting the gains from this battle, Su Lun felt his combat power had greatly leveled up.
Mr. Jing was hopeful about advancing to the ninth tier, and Dawn was also gradually growing stronger; everything seemed to be gradually improving.
By his side, Qian Tiao looked at Su Lun, who was lost in thought, and asked, "Su Lun, now that things here are concluded, where do you plan to go next?"
Su Lun thought for a moment, then seriously replied, "I might first visit the Mafa Empire. My mechanical puppets are still lacking in high-end technology, and I want to see for myself what's claimed to be the Mechanical Holy Land, the City of Freedom, Capitol Kapitron. Moreover, I also want to bring out the 'Sky Fortress'; the ancient Gusmao airship technology in Luying has too many flaws, and I need to find some talented mechanical engineers and large factories to see if I can reproduce the equipment from the schematics... and much more. In any case, I must make a trip there."
He didn't finish speaking, for previously, due to Yekaterina taking control of Luying's military intelligence service, he had learned many top-secret pieces of information.
The archives of the intelligence department contained a century-old sealed file, stating that Isaac's Alchemy Manuscript had once appeared in Mafa and that there were suspicions that Mafa's mechanical revolution was directly related to that notebook; there was also the "Urobolos Fragment," of which he already possessed three-quarters and was only missing a small piece—perhaps he could find a clue in Mafa.
Moreover, treasures like those of the Pirate King Black Sam, the "Upside-Down Man Tarot Card," Dragon Island... there were many interesting things he could plan.
Hearing this, Qian Tiao raised an eyebrow and said, "Oh. What about your new wife then? And what about being the prince of Reiya Kingdom, aren't you interested in that anymore?"
Su Lun knew she was joking, but he explained, "The deal has already ended, and the identity of Fick has nothing to do with me anymore. As for being a prince, I'm even less interested."
At this point, he paused and looked at Chien-tiao, saying, "Compared to that, I prefer going on adventures with Sister Chien-tiao."
Chien-tiao listened and teased with a smile, "Yo~"
Su Lun said no more.
Although his time as a pirate on the sea was short, he found it the most enjoyable period.
This trip to Lingdun City made Su Lun experience nobility, politics, and power.
Compared to that, he truly felt that chasing after power was really boring.
Even studying alchemy was far more interesting.
And the more he understood this world, the more Su Lun realized how vast it really was.
Not to mention the two great empires, there were also the endless wild seas to the far west, and the Monster Mountains in the east of Mafa filled with ancient civilization relics...
And then there were other dimensions such as the Void and the Abyss!
Not to see them would make him feel like a frog trapped in a well, never jumping out to see the wider world outside.
In such a fascinating world, being fixated on human squabbles over power seemed really uninteresting.
The matters in Lingdun City were resolved just right, and it seemed he could go traveling again.
Now his strength was not weak, wherever he went on an adventure, he had a certain ability to protect himself.
Su Lun and Chien-tiao talked about it, both harboring thoughts of venturing out to sea.
But just as they were discussing, suddenly, Mr. Jing, who had been silently listening with an occasional slight smile, suddenly opened his eyes wide, his gaze sharp, unable to hide his shock, "Not good! Something's happened!"
This was the first time Su Lun saw his senior sister looking so distressed, and he also frowned.
But his thoughts flickered and he was quite puzzled. Now that the outer gods were all killed, what could possibly go wrong?
Chien-tiao's expression became stern, and she directly asked, "What happened?"
Mr. Jing didn't rush to answer, seeming to use some secret technique to calculate something. After a long moment of contemplation, he finally said with a grim expression, "Someone has tampered with fate, altering the trajectory of fortune in the alchemy dimension!"
At dawn, everyone listened and for a long while didn't understand exactly what he meant, but they all felt a sense of impending crisis looming, and all their expressions grew solemn.
...
Meanwhile, in a church in Lingdun City.
This was a little-known small sect called "Eye of Heaven.".
Previously, in order to disguise the existence of the Giant Hermit Society, the Bonaparte royal family had issued the "Faith Freedom Act." However, the alchemy dimension had a very special historical past, and this act brought infinite hidden dangers. Various external god sects from Lingdun had legal identities to operate. Some mysterious sects that had been hidden for countless years now had the opportunity to recruit followers openly, and their advertisements could be seen everywhere in the newspapers, gathering believers in Lingdun.
The fierce battle outside had lasted all night, but the dozens of people in the church were unscathed.
Not a single person was mutated, nor were they affected by the Red Moon.
Because they had a stronger belief in their gods, the belief in the sea giants couldn't shake their faith at all.
The followers of this Heaven God sect were sitting around in the church, each standing on one side, beneath their feet was a massive nine-pointed star magic circle.
Right when the first light of dawn shone into the top of the church through the glass, someone walked in from the outside and reported, "Saint Heir, the mutated types outside are all dead. It looks like that sea giant must have been killed."
Upon hearing this, a young man in the center of the magic circle opened his eyes and sneered, "Hmph, just a pseudo-god who couldn't even condense a divine essence. But his death is just as well. It also created an opportunity for us..."
There wasn't a hint of respect for the divine in his tone, only disdain.
Upon closer inspection, the young man bore a strange visage; although his features were no different from a normal human's, there was a fine slit at his brow, like a tightly closed vertical pupil.
Upon hearing these words, a roomful of devotees knelt devoutly on the ground.
An elderly man asked, "Saint Heir, should we take action now? It has been confirmed that the key to the divine plane gateway is in the Bonar Royal Treasury. Queen Charlotte has been driven into a corner and is likely to make a final stand..."
Something occurred to the young man, and he said dismissively, "The Queen? Ha, just a short-sighted old hag. That old hag actually tried to contract with a pseudo-god who couldn't even condense divinity to maintain her power, laughable... She was given a chance to show loyalty to our divine clan, and she didn't treasure it. Now that she has no way out, she realizes it's too late."
At this point, a smile appeared on his lips, "Of course, that old hag's wrong decisions have also doomed Rulyn's fortunes, giving our divine clan an opportunity. If it weren't for her act, I wouldn't have had the chance to connect with you all. There's no better opportunity than the present, let's help her out. The bloodline of our divine clan has been trapped in this shattered plane for countless years, and finally, there is a chance to connect to the main plane..."
As soon as these words were spoken, all the devotees in the church started chanting magic spells, and the nine-pointed star magic circle gradually lit up.
The slit in the young man's brow slowly opened, and a light that seemed to pierce through the sanctity of the world shone forth as he uttered softly, "Universal Truths Decoded. Open!"
A vertical pupil on the forehead is a very rare bloodline talent.
If Mr. Jing were here, he would probably recognize this as [S-009-Universal Truths Decoded].
The young man unlocked the second-tier ability of his eyes, as if glimpsing an endlessly vast plane, he murmured to himself, "Divine Arts. Fate's Rebuttal!"
As the spell succeeded, an invisible force quietly spread out from the nine-pointed star magic circle.
...
At Andrew's farm, Mr. Jing had just expressed some ominous premonitions of his own.
At first, she also thought it was that the exterior god hadn't completely died, still searching for reasons in this vicinity.
Just then, Su Lun's communicator rang.
On the other end, Yekaterina urgently inquired, "Su Lun, what's happening there? I just divined a little, and the stars have shifted; a major event is going to happen!"
Upon hearing her tone, Su Lun had a faint guess that it might be related to Mr. Jing's prophecy.
Yekaterina initiated communication, probably thinking it was some issue with an exterior god.
But in fact, no situations had been discovered.
He responded, "There's nothing at the moment. What's up?"
Prophecy is usually a vague direction, and Yekaterina seemed unable to clarify from her end.
Pondering for a moment, as if she had received some new information, she suddenly communicated again, "Not good, there's trouble at the royal end!"
"The royal family?"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun distinctly felt something was off.
At this stage, what other trouble could the Bonar royal family stir up?
Mr. Jing was by his side; hearing this, a flash of intensity sparked in her eyes, clearly conceiving some thought, she said, "The problem might just be with the Bonar royal family!"
No sooner had she spoken than a flash of light occurred, and she disappeared from where she stood.
Su Lun looked at the targets of the people at Dawn and said, "Shall we check it out too?"
The people nodded in agreement.
As Su Lun made the Suren Sorcerer's Seal gesture, the small void opened, and everyone filed in.
He also performed Spatial Displacement, teleporting great distances, and soon arrived near the Frederic Royal Palace at the end of Holy Light Avenue!
At that moment, the area outside the royal palace was densely packed with various nobles' private soldiers.
With the death of the Evil God and the dispersal of the Red Moon, the fighting in the city had also subsided, leaving those followers who had not died either escaped or nearly so.
Even the mechanical warriors from the Mafa Empire who had come as reinforcements had broken through to the docks and escaped by submarine out to sea.
Those still in the palace were the loyal ministers of the Bonar royal family and the royal guards.
Duke Rafael, Duke Lance, Duke Roberts... The three opposing dukes had once again gathered their forces and blocked the palace gates.
Of the six Senior Councilors, only these three remained; their political rivals had almost all been eliminated in this great catastrophe.
Almost exactly as planned, all power in Luying was now concentrated in their hands.
This was a brilliant victory!
They had won this political high-stakes gamble!
Now, it was time to negotiate with the Bonar royal family.
The established nobility had previously found the existence of the royal family somewhat embarrassing, as the Bonar dynasty had ruled Luying for a thousand years, and the people were accustomed to and recognized only the Bonar clan as royalty.
To overturn them would be a great betrayal, but not to do so would leave endless troubles.
But just before the great battle, Queen Charlotte had admitted before everyone that it was she who had made a pact with that foreign god.
The casualties in Lingdun City numbered in the millions, and someone needed to bear the blame.
If the foreign god had been victorious, that would be another matter, as no one would dare to voice opposition.
But now that the opposition had won and the foreign god was dead,
even the royal family could not bear such a charge.
The abdication of Queen Charlotte was already a foregone conclusion!
About thirty reporters with cameras clicked away, documenting everything happening in front of the palace; they were about to witness the history of Luying.
The palace's defensive barrier was still unbroken, but there was no longer any attack going on.
As nobles themselves and bound by their lord-vassal relationship, they wanted to afford the Bonar royal family one last dignity.
As Su Lun teleported over, he watched Duke Rafael standing in front of the palace gate, representing the opposition as he called inside to the empress, "Your Majesty, tonight's catastrophe has cost Lingdun City millions of lives, all due to the descent of that Evil God..."
...
Su Lun watched this scene, feeling nothing was amiss.
After a coup, it was normal for the victors to perform a bloody purge of the defeated; there was nothing wrong with this process.
Furthermore, the actions of Queen Charlotte this time were utterly detestable, making exile or execution a justifiable outcome.
Mr. Jing also slightly frowned, clearly also puzzled.
He hadn't planned to interfere in Luying's internal politics, but he was wondering who else might be stirring fate and to what end.
However, it wasn't long before the palace doors opened, and Queen Charlotte, dressed neatly, arrived at the entrance.
She was dressed in the dark red gem-emblazoned emperor's garb she wore at her coronation, her head adorned with the Bonar royal heirloom, the "Balati Crown," her left hand holding the "Green Glow Rod of Kingship," and her right grasping the "Cross Rod of Sovereignty."
She appeared as regal as the day she ascended the throne, her gaze sternly sweeping over everyone. However, her eyes had long lost their composure, filled only with a soul-lost bewilderment.
Duke Raphael, seeing the true master appear, continued, "Your Majesty..."
He just wanted to say something when he was abruptly interrupted by Queen Charlotte, who countered, "Are you really forcing me..."
Raphael's gaze swept over sharply. At this point, there was no turning back. "Your Majesty, I and a few colleagues have eliminated that foreign god and its followers. This disaster has caused a million casualties in Lurying, and my heart is heavy with sorrow..."
Queen Charlotte seemed to not listen at all, her face twisted into a hysterical frenzy as she countered, "Are you really forcing me!"
Raphael frowned upon hearing this. No matter how he looked at it, she was a mad old woman.
He said lightly, "Your Majesty, no one is forcing you. I just want to say, this time you really made a mistake..."
Queen Charlotte scoffed, sweeping her gaze over everyone, still appearing as if she were the paramount existence. She looked at the three dukes and suddenly asked, "Are you still loyal to the royal family?"
The three Dukes Raphael responded, "Naturally. We are the Empire's servants, eternally loyal to the royal family."
In front of so many reporters, the royal family's face still had to be maintained.
Normally, now that the situation was settled and face had been given, the Empress should have invited them in for negotiations, aiming for an outcome of exile to a remote location.
Otherwise, tearing apart faces, even the last vestige of the royal family's dignity might not be preserved.
Unexpectedly, Queen Charlotte did not follow the script; she activated the Rod of Kingship in her hand and pulled out an ancient parchment from within the hollow staff, "This is the Loyalty Pact signed by thirty-six founding ministers at the inception of the empire, pledging their descendants' eternal loyalty to the empire, to the royal family!"
She exclaimed, "If you are still loyal to the Royal Family, then please inscribe your names and those of your families here!"
At those words, the vast square fell silent, the atmosphere instantly turning awkward.
The three Dukes Raphael exchanged glances, each seeing the coldness in the others' eyes.
...
From a distance, Su Lun, witnessing this, was also deeply puzzled.
"Loyalty pact" was no different from a slavery contract, once signed, they had to continue their loyalty.
But why would the three Dukes Raphael agree?
Their ancestors were not among the founding ministers, so this pact had no effect on them. They didn't sign when the royal family had control, and now they bring it out?
Had this old woman truly gone mad?
Could she not see her own situation clearly?
Not just Su Lun, everyone thought Queen Charlotte had gone mad.
Falling from a height of power, she wanted to use this last means to cling to the power she valued more than life itself.
But what right did she have!
The three Dukes Raphael remained silent, looking on coldly.
"Hahahaha..."
Queen Charlotte tilted her head and watched for a while, her expression already becoming manically peculiar. She glanced at everyone without saying a word, growling to herself: "I knew it! I knew you pack of jackals wanted to usurp my Bonar Royal Family's throne! Now, I give you one last chance, sign the pact, otherwise..."
Saying so, she opened her right hand, holding the "Cross Rod of Sovereignty," inside which a eyeball-shaped item startlingly appeared.
She clutched the eyeball and shouted, "Otherwise, I will open the key to the planar channel and have you traitorous scoundrels buried alongside the empire!"
Hearing this, everyone was greatly alarmed.
All eyes turned toward the eyeball.
Others might not have known the origin of the eyeball, but Su Lun's face changed drastically, "Has this old woman truly gone mad?!"
The name identified by the All-knowing Eye was "The Key to the Celestial Planar Channel"!
It was one thing for the extreme believers of Lingdun to worship the Evil God, but now to threaten these people with the planar channel to capture the completely elusive underworld?
Mad!
She must be mad!
No one in their right mind would do such a thing.
Su Lun then realized, this Empress Charlotte must have lost her mind!
Mr. Jing standing beside her finally understood what her prophecy was pointing towards, and looking at the key, her face turned ashen!
...
The royal family, in order to secure their rule, must have some contingencies.
But clearly, nobody expected the Bonaparte royal family to possess such a thing!
For most people, a planar channel is an unattainable topic.
Only a very few at the apex of this world's pyramid know what the planar key does!
It's like Pandora's box in myths, once opened, it signifies destruction.
Duke Rafael was among those who knew the dangers of this thing!
Yet, once the planar channel is opened, not to mention the empire, the entire civilization would be wiped out in an instant.
How could Empress Charlotte dare to do this?
Would she, alone for the sake of power, drag the entire alchemy civilization to its grave?
The expressions of several dukes changed drastically, knowing there was no negotiating with a mad old woman now.
At that moment, a prince by Empress Charlotte's side, also pale with fright, hurriedly persuaded, "Your Majesty, this must not be done. Opening the planar channel will destroy the entire civilization in an instant! You cannot do this!"
Empress Charlotte was already beyond hearing any words, and seeing that the dukes had not yet taken a stand, her face twisted into a mad sneer as she almost snarled, "Hahaha, why should I care about the floods after I die!"
The dukes were truly frightened by this scorched earth strategy, and they even began to consider whether to agree to her demands, just to postpone the old woman's suicidal intentions.
But just then, something unexpected happened.
Suddenly, as if struck by some mysterious force, Empress Charlotte's face contorted with hysterical madness, muttering incessantly, "It's your doing, it's your doing..."
As she spoke, she gave no chance to stop her, and pressed down on the mechanism of the eyeball.
In an instant, a beam of light shot up into the sky.
PS. I need monthly tickets, the start of the month is very important, thank you everyone! The new volume of the Dragon Island Adventure and the subsequent wars of the planes are about to begin, I think it's a very interesting volume, the main character will also become very strong, and the scenes of a one-man army will really slaughter on all fronts... I hope everyone will like it.

chapters.title: Chapter 490 - 489: Planar Invasion
chapters.content:
"What happened to the negotiation?"
Everyone was caught off-guard by Queen Charlotte's act of mutual destruction.
It was as if time had stopped, everyone's faces froze in place, expressionless.
Just seconds before, when they saw her take out the loyalty contract and the dimensional gate key, they really thought she was using these as leverage to gain some bargaining chips.
But who would have thought that this old woman would actually activate the switch in such a crazed manner!
When that beam of white light was fired towards the sky, everyone watched.
Those who knew what it meant looked ashen.
Those who didn't understand were completely at a loss.
The defensive barrier of the Frederic Royal Palace had not yet been broken; even if someone wanted to stop her, it was futile.
She looked up at the sky, her expression suddenly returning to its usual indifference, only a deeply complex sigh escaping her.
Su Lun, too, furrowed his brow tightly, the current situation truly rendering him somewhat helpless.
He had thought that they had thwarted the plots of the Outer Gods and the situation was greatly favorable.
He hadn't expected such a turn of events.
But it was too late.
Looking at that beam of white light, Su Lun also quickly pondered a few questions in his mind.
"What is this 'Divine Dimension'?
What beings exist there?
What impact will opening the dimensional gate have?"
Before he could think further, Mr. Jing's tone had returned to calm, and he spoke indifferently, "Let's go."
Su Lun, with an unusual expression, suggested, "Elder sister, shouldn't we… do something?"
He didn't know what he could do.
But he felt, perhaps they should do something.
To see if they could remedy the grave mistake made by that old woman.
Mr. Jing shook his head, his crystal-clear eyes slightly unfocused, and said, "The guy who was meddling with fate earlier had contacted a divine entity from a different dimension. Just now, in that instant, the alchemy dimension's spatial coordinates have already been captured by the gods of the other dimension. Now that both dimensions are connected, destroying the key is meaningless."
She gazed towards the sky, as if perceiving some changes, and murmured to herself, "That is a very high-level dimension..."
Su Lun asked, "Do you know who did this, elder sister?"
"I don't know. But it's not hard to guess."
Mr. Jing shook her head, continuing to walk as she spoke, "Our dimension has left behind many descendents of different dimensional beings. Even if civilizations have faced breaks, their bloodlines could be awakened by certain higher gods' calling. This is why many cults of Outer Gods have persisted for countless years and have never been discontinued. But the alchemy dimension was fragmented, and the followers of Outer Gods lacked the ability to establish spatial coordinates, so all was peaceful. I never thought the Bonaparte royal family had a 'Dimensional Key,'" she continued.
Having reached this point, she stopped, as though continuing to talk about the issues with the Bonaparte royal family was pointless.
She continued, "My father once said, once the spatial coordinates are exposed, the beginning of a civilizational war is inevitable. There will be no room for luck. Let's go, we also need to prepare."
"..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun also fell into thought.
He said no more, silently following Mr. Jing along the streets.
At that moment, noises erupted from the palace square behind them.
Queen Charlotte's insane act had completely cost her everyone's loyalty.
Someone had disabled the palace's defenses, and a crowd surged forward.
Major disasters, coups, compared to an invasion from another dimension, seemed just like trivial melodramas.
Su Lun and his companion seemingly ignored the noise behind them, and in a flicker of spatial fluctuation, they had vanished from the street.
...
Read new chapters at My Virtual Library Empire
A short while later, at an apartment by the Lokwarren River.
Mr. Jing, Su Lun, Qian Tiao, Pandora, Mr. Hei, Wazwas, Barrett... nearly all the key figures of Dawn were gathered together.
Everyone was aware of the significant incident of Queen Charlotte opening the gateway to another dimension.
While filled with righteous indignation, a strong sense of looming crisis weighed heavily on everyone's mind.
The atmosphere of the meeting was extremely solemn, as if even breathing had become stagnant.
Although the people of Dawn were not unfamiliar with other dimensions, except for Mr. Jing, no one had truly experienced the cruelty of a dimensional invasion.
Moreover, the information they knew was very limited, and everyone remained silent.
Most of the time, only Mr. Jing was speaking.
"The situation is as such now. That is definitely a dimension with real divine beings..."
After explaining some knowledge about other dimensions, Mr. Jing then continued, "Since it has come to this, the focus of Dawn's future development needs to shift... Now, we need to guard against the invasion of beings from other dimensional realms."
As she spoke, the room fell into silence.
Everyone was grappling with this overwhelmingly heavy topic.
This evening's great disaster had indeed exposed everyone to the force of deities.
But even a demigod who had not yet solidified his divinity had caused such terrifying losses. It required the concurrent sacrifice of the ninth-tier Master Pierre to eliminate him.
So how terrifying must a true deity be?
If there really were gods in the "Godly Plane", who could withstand them?
Barrett, with his military perspective, saw something else and asked, "Leader, we know very little about the 'Godly Plane'. Even if we are to prepare, what should we do? And just how strong are the creatures from other planes? Will it be a civilization-level invasion, or a small-scale infiltration like the previous Void Plane?"
This was a question on everyone's mind.
Hearing this question, Su Lun also looked toward Mr. Jing beside him.
Basing on his understanding of his senior sister and guessing the various arrangements made by Sir Isaac, he felt there might still be room for maneuver.
If it were an invasion by gods descending directly, there wouldn't be any need to consider defense. Once the top-tier fighters were decapitated, the remaining lower-tier professionals could hardly organize any resistance.
It would be better to wait in despair for destruction.
As expected.
Mr. Jing's tone suddenly became less serious as he replied, "Actually, everyone needn't worry too much, because we still have some time to prepare."
Still have time?
As soon as these words came out, everyone looked over expectantly, waiting for him to continue.
Mr. Jing continued, "The alchemical ancestors who initially designed these plane channels during the Dawn Era had considered the possibility of reverse invasions. Thus, the plane channels have some special protective settings, making the entrance here easy to open, but the exit on the other side difficult to open inversely. And the plane key is more like spatial coordinates; building a plane channel also requires vast energy and specific methods. Our Alchemy Plane currently lacks the conditions to fully open the plane channel, and the two great empires would absolutely not allow anyone to do that. Earlier's incident, at most, sent coordinates to the Godly Plane. For them to build a stable reverse plane channel, it will take a long time..."
She explained some technical issues and then said, "I'm not sure how long this time will be. But after reviewing the calculation formulas left by my father, I deduced that the possibility of a large-scale plane invasion is not substantial for at least the next few years."
This topic was highly specialized.
So specialized that ordinary people would never have heard of it.
Only a demigod like Sir Isaac would have the qualifications and ability to study plane channels.
But upon hearing these words, everyone finally breathed a sigh of relief.
There was still time for everyone to catch their breath, and the oppressive atmosphere seemed to ease a bit.
Then, Mr. Jing announced another piece of good news, "Moreover, there is a silver lining amidst the misfortune. Our Alchemy Plane's laws are shattered; in the next hundred years, it can at most bear the arrival of a lesser god, similar to the level of a Fallen Angel. Thus, as long as we are strong enough, there is a chance to prevent the powerful beings from other planes from enslaving and destroying our alchemical civilization, just like my predecessors."
That's right!
Hearing this, everyone's spirits inexplicably lifted.
Su Lun finally understood why it was considered a "stroke of good fortune"!
Because the old members of the Jing organization knew, Sir Isaac had personally captured a god-tier Fallen Angel a thousand years ago.
Since there was a precedent, it meant that mortals could defeat True Gods!
Although currently no one possessed the "demigod" strength that Isaac had back then, there was at least a glimmer of hope.
This instilled confidence immediately!
At that moment, someone asked, "Leader, what is a lesser god?"
Mr. Jing replied, "I'm not too clear on the specifics. But my father mentioned that deities also have rankings. A lesser god could roughly be understood as above the ninth rank, a 'tenth rank'. However, due to the consolidation of divine fire and divinity, their combat strength is vastly different from that of professionals."
She thought for a moment, then added, "In any case, it has been proven that such beings are not entirely unbeatable."
With these words, everyone's morale inexplicably surged again.
...
Most fears stem from the unknown.
Now, with an accurate concept of the enemy's strength, their fear immediately dissipated by a large margin.
Alchemists are a group of people in pursuit of truth.
Who among those advancing to the realm of high-order professionals hasn't endured hardships and death's threat?
With the discussion reaching this point, the furrowed brows on the faces of the Dawn Group members present simultaneously relaxed.
It was fortunate that the leader of the Dawn was Mr. Jing; otherwise, outsiders would never know such high-level information.
Nor would they have a fairly accurate understanding of the gods' strengths.
And Su Lun appeared much more relaxed.
He felt his mental realm was far inferior to his senior sister's; he carried no burden of civilization's heritage, nor did he care about the decline of a plane.
For him, a plane invasion was merely a high-fatality large-scale war.
In fact, hearing Mr. Jing's words, he felt an inexplicable hint of excitement? A kind of tenacity etched deep in his bones made him fearless.
Since he couldn't change the reality of the plane invasion, he might as well actively face it.
The worst outcome would just be death, right?
Death, in his current understanding, really didn't hold too much intimidation.
...
Two consecutive pieces of good news greatly relaxed the previously tense atmosphere of the meeting.
Then, Mr. Jing suddenly switched gears again, raising an issue that came as a surprise to everyone.
Her tone, serious yet imbued with a hopeful lightness, said, "Moreover, from a certain perspective, linking with other world planes might not entirely be a bad thing."
Hearing this, everyone showed puzzled expressions.
A plane invasion, something good?
Mr. Jing, facing the puzzled looks of the crowd, explained, "The powerful Great Alchemists from the Dawn Era who established numerous plane channels did not do so merely for the convenience of travel. There was also a very important reason... that is to perfect the plane laws, bringing Alchemy closer to the 'truth'."
Speaking, she glanced at the crowd again and continued, "My father once studied the function of the dimensional portal. He discovered that the laws of each dimension are not entirely the same, nor are they balanced. Just like the 'Void Dimension', the space laws there are much higher than our Alchemy Dimension, and divine creatures of the Void can even be born there. There are also some special fire element dimensions, water element dimensions, darkness element dimensions... and so on. The larger the dimension, the more perfect the cosmic laws. Accordingly, the upper limit for the growth of living beings is higher..."
So that was it!
Upon hearing this, everyone instantly understood.
The reason that the highest tier in the Alchemy Dimension was only ninth was primarily because the dimension had collapsed, shattering the laws.
Furthermore, upon hearing this explanation, Su Lun also vaguely guessed what the benefit his senior sister mentioned could be.
Mr. Jing immediately followed up, "Although I also don't know exactly what the situation is with the 'Divine Race Dimension', I clearly sensed that the integrity of the laws of that dimension is very high. Once the dimensional portal is connected, the high-level laws of that dimension will flow into the Alchemy Dimension, gradually perfecting its laws. Once a stable connection is established, it may even complement each other to become completely the same. That means... our magicians in the Alchemy Dimension, at some future moment, might also have the potential to peek into the secrets of godliness!"
The statement was delivered in a calm tone, but everyone in the room felt as if something had profoundly struck their souls, and their faces simultaneously showed exhilarated expressions.
All being alchemists, they naturally understood this reasoning right away.
It's like the phenomenon of heat conduction, where heat moves from the hotter part of an object to a cooler part, eventually balancing out.
This, indeed, was good news.
Godhood?
A topic that once seemed far beyond reach, the ceiling that frustrated numerous great alchemists of the ninth tier without finding a way out, now seemed within reach?
Not to say that it could be achieved, but at least there was hope!
Before, the Alchemy Dimension was like a well with a lid placed over it.
No matter how the frog jumped, it couldn't leap out of the lid.
Now, someone had drilled a hole in the lid, at least allowing some of the top individuals to see the outside world.
And there was a possibility of getting out!
...
Barrett had maintained that nonchalant demeanor throughout the meeting.
This gambling housewife's mind obviously didn't ponder things that were too complex, most likely thinking only of fight and kill.
Enemies come, just kill.
But now, hearing Mr. Jing say this, a spark suddenly appeared in her eyes, and she suddenly interjected, "So in this way, this is indeed an opportunity for our Alchemy Dimension!"
To glimpse a higher peak of cultivation—this was an even more exhilarating expectation than any dimensional invasion for her, a professional swordsman always pursuing the pinnacle.
As a military person, Barrett visibly anticipated, saying, "Indeed. If we seize this opportunity, just like the leader said, it might indeed be a chance for our Alchemy Dimension!"
Mr. Hei thought for a moment, then said very rationally, "Although it will take several years to establish the dimensional portal, I am fearful that the enemy's invasion might proceed faster than our development. When the divine beings execute their descent to fight, and we still don't have the strength to respond, that would be a major problem..."
Huaz Wuaz: "Indeed..."
Everyone: "..."
Everyone began to discuss openly.
Indeed, this dimensional opening concealed opportunities, but as things currently stood, the overall strength of the Alchemy Civilization was too weak, and the risks outstripped the opportunities.
Mr. Jing's statement was clearly to boost morale.
"So, as I just mentioned, we still have some time to prepare..."
She continued, "My father's notes contain detailed records of his research on dimensional portals. It is almost certain that once the dimensional portal is fully opened, and high-level laws start to overflow, our cultivation progress will become much easier than before. Therefore, during this time, everyone should strive hard to advance their strengths so that when the future crisis arrives, we might very well have the strength to fight."
Mr. Jing did not say that her father had also speculated this. That is opening the dimensional portal to give alchemists the chance to become gods. There was even a complete response plan.
But this plan was too crazy, and just a bit of carelessness could lead to the collapse of civilization.
Therefore, this plan remained only in the notes.
However, now that the dimensional portal had been opened by someone, some of the plans noted there could also be gradually tested.
...
Would opening the dimensional portal make professional advancement easier?
Su Lun suddenly brightened up.
Godhood and such was still too far off for him.
But if advancement became easier, that was a super big advantage.
He was currently stuck at the seventh-tier threshold, and if, as Mr. Jing said, advancement became easier, wouldn't he be guaranteed to advance into the realm of top-tier professionals?
This was quite sensible upon brief consideration.
Just as places with rich spiritual energy made advancement easier, after the dimension's laws were perfected, comprehension would naturally become easier.
Thinking of this, Su Lun once again marveled at the brilliance of Sir Isaac.
That Alchemical Demigod, having reached the peak of cultivation in the dimension, embarked on all sorts of bizarre research projects. From the manuscripts he left behind, this true god indeed covered nearly every field, with countless alchemical inventions to his credit.
This truly was a blessing for future generations.
Without these researches, Su Lun and the others would likely be completely in the dark facing this dimensional invasion, knowing nothing and being passively beaten.
And Mr. Jing was also a qualified leader.
Even with a crisis approaching, she analyzed and planned carefully, strategizing for the major upheaval that was coming.
...
The atmosphere of the meeting had shifted from a deadly quiet despair at the start to a dawn of hope now visible in everyone's eyes.
At this moment, Mr. Jing added, "During this time while the dimensional portal is being established, it is inevitable that strong beings from other dimensions will come one after another to plunder resources. Even if they are not divine beings, they are definitely not to be underestimated. What we need to do now is to address this crisis. We mustn't let them accelerate the construction of the dimensional portal, nor let them run rampant..."
The crowd listened solemnly, unanimously responding, "Yes, leader!"
Everyone was resolute, though not prepared for battle.
But when thinking about fighting with powerful beings from another dimension, everyone felt unsure.
Mr. Jing clearly noticed something and added, "Moreover, you all shouldn't assume that creatures from other dimensions are definitely strong. My father has captured many abyssal creatures for detailed study and has found that we Alchemists actually have certain advantages over beings from different planes. Theoretically, due to the lack of plane laws, advancing in rank requires a deeper understanding of the world. Compared to them, we Alchemists have a deeper comprehension of the world's laws..."
That was yet another uplifting advantage, mysteriously restoring confidence among the group.
Su Lun listened thoughtfully.
It was like the more barren and harsh the desert, the more tenaciously wildflowers could survive.
Conversely, flowers in a greenhouse, though delicately beautiful, might not have any advantage in the same environment.
At last, Mr. Jing looked at the group and said, "So, everyone, strive to become stronger! I hope by the time the enemy arrives, we have the power to fight. For the glory of alchemy, for eternal truth, for ourselves!"
With those words, everyone in the room stood up, their expressions solemn as they pressed their hands to their chests and said, "Yes, leader!"
...
The meeting was over.
Mr. Hei and the others left the apartment.
All other members of the Dawn organization had their duties; now, with crisis looming, everyone became busy.
It was as if someone had suddenly set up a time hourglass; they had to grow in strength with every second they could muster.
Only Su Lun, Qian Tiao, and Mr. Jing remained in the room.
After the meeting, the atmosphere in the apartment noticeably relaxed.
The three were accustomed to each other's company, as close as family.
But Mr. Jing's expression remained serious.
Su Lun looked over and asked, "Sister, do we need to leave Lingdun now?"
Mr. Jing thought for a moment and replied, "Let's wait a day. There might still be some changes. I also want to verify a few things."
Su Lun acknowledged with an 'Oh'.
Then, Mr. Jing suddenly turned her gaze to the two on the sofa and said: "Su Lun, Odilia, I've estimated that even if I advance to rank nine, it would be very hard to reach the strength level of my father. So, I will need a few peers to assist me to have a sure chance of stopping a 'Lesser God' so that we truly have the qualifications to resist..."
After a pause, she added earnestly, "I need your help."
Qian Tiao raised an eyebrow upon hearing this, returning the look as usual without saying much.
Su Lun felt the sense of crisis instantly upon hearing these words.
He had thought that once his sister advanced to rank nine, their status would be truly secured. At least the two great empires would no longer dare to target him with ill intentions.
He did not expect that just as this goal was about to be achieved, a greater crisis had descended.
An invasion from another plane was a crisis not even a rank nine professional could escape from safely.
To battle against gods?
But he was only at rank six now...
Thinking it over, he felt it was quite a challenge.
Now that the plane passage was established, advancing had become easier; reaching rank seven was already half accomplished. Given his conditions, rank eight might not be out of reach...
As for what follows, he would take things one step at a time.
The alchemical civilization was a treasure-laden plane, buried with many treasures left by ancient brilliant civilizations. Opportunities were plentiful; all one had to do was search, and perhaps fortune would fall into their lap.
Walking along this path, Su Lun had a deep realization; his dual S-rank talent would also grow stronger in battle.
Although he always had an ideal to lay back and be a salted fish, comparatively, he wanted to see what higher realms looked like.
He needed to hurry now more than ever to the Mafa Empire; mechanical puppets were a research direction with unlimited potential...
And then there was Western Sea Dragon Island—perhaps it really was time to consider it. He held notes in his hand with the methods to create the "Aisak Dragon-Patterned Golden Body," such a formidable prosthesis couldn't just be abandoned without trying. There were also treasures related to the origin secrets of the All-knowing Eye indicated by the "Upside-down Man Card."
These were the most direct paths he could see to becoming stronger.
Previously, because of the high probability of death in the Western Sea, he hesitated and hardly dared to go.
Now, however...
With enemies pointing guns at them, if they weren't strong enough, they would surely die.
With this comparison,
the situation suddenly became crystal clear.
Only by becoming stronger could he survive the tidal waves of a plane invasion without being shattered to pieces.
With this conclusion, the three in the room glanced at each other, and, understanding each other's thoughts, the corners of their mouths curled slightly upwards.
Having trustworthy companions to walk alongside made the obstacles in life seem not so daunting.
Just then, sunlight from outside entered the room, bathing it in a golden glow.
The bloodshed of the previous night had cleared the haze over Lingdun, and today, the sun shone brightly.
The ancient empire welcomed a new day.
It was also a new day for the entire alchemical plane.

chapters.title: Chapter 491 - 490: True Solution of Everything
chapters.content:
Su Lun and the other two stayed in the apartment without going out, waiting to see how the situation in Old Lington would change today.
Last night's battle had been so intense in the northern affluent district that mansions and luxurious estates were largely destroyed, leaving a scene of devastation. On the other hand, although many people died in the southern commoners' area, the damage to the city itself wasn't as severe.
With the dawn, light dispersed the darkness and fear.
People who had been frightened all night gradually took to the streets to start cleaning up the rubble and the bodies of the undead zombies.
Steam-powered vehicles hauled away the rocks, and jets of water washed away the crimson, and even the small vendors who sold fruits and vegetables were still opening their doors for business…
As long as people were alive, life must go on.
Although last night's catastrophe had almost caused the collapse of all public departments in Ling Dun, the response from the provisional congress was fast and extremely efficient. Before long, mounted police had already appeared on the streets, maintaining post-disaster law and order and the confidence of the citizens.
...
After battling all night, Su Lun felt his stomach was empty.
There was no hope of heading to a restaurant just yet, but luckily, the war workshop in the small void realm had chefs and ample food supplies.
Su Lun casually set a sumptuous breakfast on the dining table in the apartment.
The three of them sat down at the table, even the ghostly lady occupied a seat, even though she didn't need to eat.
Just about to have their meal, at that moment, Mr. Jing seemed to think of something and glanced at Su Lun.
Immediately getting the hint, Su Lun smiled and said, "I'll be right back."
Downstairs was a guest who wasn't exactly a guest.
He had actually sensed her earlier; after the meeting dispersed, Pandora had walked out, taken a round, and then lingered downstairs. It seemed she was hesitant, not knowing where to go or perhaps reconsidering, as if she had something to come back to say.
She hadn't made up her mind, and Su Lun didn't want to disturb her.
Since it was breakfast time, he thought to invite her up.
Su Lun opened the door and walked out, going downstairs, where he spotted Pandora standing at the balcony on the second floor, catching the breeze.
Although cloaked, he could still make out half of her strikingly beautiful face.
Compared to the last time he saw her, Su Lun distinctly felt that the fluctuations in her soul were much stronger, and the divine and transcendent aura around her was growing more ethereal.
She leaned against the white stone railing, blending into the city's backdrop as if she were a beautiful figure in an oil painting, to be admired from a distance but never touched, exuding aloofness and mystery.
But Su Lun also knew that Miss Pandora wasn't as indifferent as she seemed.
In fact, she was quite easy to get along with.
He walked over and greeted her with a smile, "Miss Pandora, if you haven't had breakfast, may I invite you to join us for a meal?"
The tone wasn't unfamiliar, more like hailing a friend.
After all, having studied her body, it was impossible to be strangers, even after a long absence.
Pandora took off her cloak, the wind ruffling her hair, and a flawless face lit up with a soft smile, "No, thank you. I came back just to tell you something."
Waiting for me?
Su Lun was slightly surprised.
But even that shallow smile, brimming with charm, made him instinctively twitch at the corner of his eye.
Su Lun remembered falling for it the last time they parted on the ship.
Pandora saw his fleeting unnatural expression and responded with a meaningful smile.
However, this time she wasn't up to any bewitching technique pranks, instead, she pointed at the briefcase beside her and said, "This is for you. Please keep it safe for me."
Su Lun looked at her with a hint of surprise in his question: "Oh?"
He hadn't opened it, but he guessed that it was probably the Faith Stele inside. Such divine artifacts containing high-level laws couldn't be stored in a storage space, and had to be carried personally.
Last night, the elimination of the "Sea Giant Clarence" was made much easier thanks to Pandora's appearance. Since the stele was of no use to anyone else, it naturally ended up in her hands. There was still the residual Power of Faith from the Outer God on it, which was highly beneficial to her.
That's why Su Lun was puzzled—why would she entrust him with its safekeeping?
To his great surprise, Pandora revealed another startling request.
She said, "This stele is a divine talisman of an Ancient God, far superior to the previous one that carried faith for me. It holds greater potential for the future. I have entrusted my very own divine soul to this stele. Now, I am also a God of Disaster, and those former followers of the Outer God have become my followers too, and they won't cause any more trouble..."
Su Lun listened with a slightly changed expression.
Although he had known about her ability for a while, hearing that she had become a God of Disaster still stirred some emotions within him.
He always thought that the "Faith Stealing" ability that his teacher couple had given to Miss Pandora was a super BUG.
The phony gods struggle for eons, recruiting followers painstakingly to accumulate faith, and she simply steals it away.
Having a better divine talisman to choose, it was normal for her to switch...
But in an instant, a flash of insight crossed his mind.
Su Lun's expression immediately froze.
Eh... something's not right!
If she considered this stele as her divine talisman, why would she entrust me with its safekeeping?
A divine talisman is like the "life gate" of a deity following the divine path—before they congeal their divine nature, this is their most critical vulnerability.
Just like before, that Outer God clearly had the power to fight, even possessing an immortal body. But it was only after its divine talisman was found that the tables were swiftly turned.
Giving it to someone else—isn't that like handing over one's life?
Now, Pandora was also a member of the Dawn group, an alchemical construct made by his own teacher, and had a good relationship with Mr. Jing...
Still, even with all that considered, Su Lun felt it shouldn't be the case.
And why me, of all people?
Even if she truly had to entrust someone with it, Mr. Jing would seem a more appropriate choice by any account.
Pandora obviously guessed Su Lun's thoughts and explained, "I've been thinking it over carefully, and now that the plane invasion is a certainty, the future looks very grim. But as long as this stele exists, I won't die. However, higher deities have the ability to investigate the source of faith. If a True God descends, my situation will become very dangerous..."
With this explanation, Su Lun instantly understood.
The discovery of the previous Outer God stele was detected by Pestoya's Soul Perception.
Therefore, no matter where it was hidden, being discovered would be fatal.
Pandora continued, "I don't feel safe leaving the stele anywhere else, but your little void realm can prevent faith investigation. Hence, I'm entrusting it to you."
"..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun realized that this was the reason.
No wonder she made such a decision.
Although he said that, Su Lun still felt that something was off.
It was indeed safe, but wasn't Pandora effectively handing over the keys to her life gate prematurely?
Didn't that mean...
That she could be threatened with it, compelled to do anything, and she wouldn't be able to refuse?
Even though Su Lun didn't harbor any strange ideas.
But as the plot had progressed this far, he couldn't help but draw such a conclusion in his mind.
Pandora, noticing his momentary distraction, with her beautiful eyes sparkling, held a barely perceptible smile at the corner of her lips.
That smile, as if she had seen through someone's runaway thoughts, yet appeared completely unconcerned.
She then asked, "Can you do me this favor?"
Trust can sometimes be just a thought.
She was, after all, an alchemical being, existing in solitude.
For a long thousand years, it seemed only now that she felt some ties to this world.
Since Pandora trusted her so much, coupled with various entanglements, Su Lun naturally couldn't refuse, and replied, "Of course."
As he spoke, he took the box related to Pandora's life and stored it inside the little void world.
Although it was a entrusted task, Su Lun still asked, "Would you like to have breakfast together?"
Pandora shook her head, pulling her cloak back up, "No need. I must return to the four nations of the Northern Continent, where the foundation of faith is not yet solid. If you need to contact me, just let me know with the communicator, and my spiritual will can always descend upon the stele."
"Oh."
Su Lun, listening, still politely waved goodbye and courteously said, "Then take care, Miss Pandora."
Pandora smiled faintly, turned to leave, but suddenly seemed to remember something, and added, "Once I've assimilated the power of faith I've obtained, my true form will probably be able to descend onto the stele as well. If necessary, you can also summon me with necromancy."
"Hmm..."
Su Lun listened and nodded.
But upon reflection, something seemed amiss.
There was nothing wrong with her words, but paired with the subtle smile she gave as she looked back, it suddenly felt like there was some other implication.
What could her true form do upon descending?
Could it... study the alchemical body?
Another look, and the person had already vanished from sight.
But thinking of research, Su Lun was indeed very interested in Pandora's alchemical body.
The more he understood about alchemy, the more he felt that Pandora's body itself was a great treasure.
Just then, a ghostly figure floated out beside Su Lun.
He had noticed that this spectral miss had been curiously peeking all along.
Pestoya, resting her chin in her hand, looked toward the corner where Pandora had disappeared and said, "I quite like that Miss Pandora."
Curious, Su Lun asked, "Why is that?"
Pestoya replied, "No particular reason. I just feel she's very approachable."
Su Lun listened and smiled.
...
Meanwhile, the opposition led by Duke Raphael successfully took over all of Luying's political power. The royal Ponar family had completely lost its supreme royal authority.
The three of the previously six senior councilors had been almost completely exterminated, and without political rivals, administrative efficiency increased a great deal.
Although Ling Dun had experienced an unprecedented disaster, the reconstruction work continued in an orderly fashion.
Although there was a slight mishap when Queen Charlotte opened a space-time portal,
it seemed to have no effect for the moment.
After all, the space-time portal was too remote for everyone. Not everyone knew what it meant and the serious consequences it would bring, like Mr. Jing did.
Even if a minority guessed that it spelled catastrophic disaster for the plane, they would not speak up about it.
The topic of plane invasion, a cause of despair, could not be reversed by human efforts.
Life must go on, and spreading panic serves no purpose.
The priority was to determine some future power divisions in Luying.
Frederic Royal Palace had already been overtaken by the opposition.
At this moment, within a sealed room, Queen Charlotte sat on a chair in a daze.
All her jewelry had been taken away, and every facility in the room had been meticulously inspected.
It was like a cage.
But after all, she was royalty, and no one dared to subject her to private punishment.
Even though her crimes were sufficient to send her to the gallows a hundred times over, it would only be after a trial.
When she came to her senses, Queen Charlotte realized she had become a prisoner. Thinking about what she had just done, she seemed to regret it somewhat.
I just intended to threaten those people, why did I act so impulsively...
She knew it was all too late.
She once held supreme authority and now had lost it completely; the bitterness was overwhelming.
Queen Charlotte stared at the ceiling in a daze.
Unexpectedly, at that moment, a hole appeared in the ceiling, and a young man bathed in Holy Light descended like a god incarnate, gradually landing on the cashmere carpet in the room.
The guards outside the door were completely unaware of the intruder in the room.
Queen Charlotte's expression was one of shock; before she could comprehend who this person was, she noticed the vertical pupil opening on the intruder's forehead.
That eye seemed to possess a bewitching power, making one lose consciousness immediately.
After a while, the triclops retracted his hand from Queen Charlotte's head, as if he had obtained the information he wanted.
However, his brows furrowed, and he muttered to himself, "The God-Blocking Coffin that seals the Ancient God indeed ended up in possession of the Bonaparte royal family, but it has been lost for several hundred years? Suspected to have vanished along with the Mirror Image Library? 'Phantom Thief' Kit...isn't that a member of the Dawn organization?"
After collecting the soul, the triclops was initially pleased, thinking he had completed the task effortlessly.
He did confirm the information, but the object had disappeared.
The only valuable intelligence was that the disappearance of the Mirror Image Library hundreds of years ago had been first discovered by the previously famous 'Phantom Thief' Curtis M. Kit in Ling Dun.
As something dawned on him, his eyes shifted and he murmured, "Seems like that 'Hanged Man Tarot card' is also in that Kit's hands... tsk, tsk, saves me the trouble of looking for someone."
Saying this, there was no longer a figure in the room.
Queen Charlotte still sat on the chair in a stupor, her eyes now devoid of any spirit.
...
Su Lun and his companions stayed at the apartment, and by noon, the Ling Dun City News had been printed.
The contents of the newspaper focused on last night's catastrophe.
Using the tone of the victors, it described a series of consequences caused by the support of the Faith Freedom Act, along with Red Plague, Crimson Potion, and so on... all depicted as conspiracies of the royal family and several Senior Councilors.
Reading this paper gave the impression that the old woman of the Bonaparte dynasty was the incarnation of a demon.
This newspaper was not only for residents of Ling Dun but also aimed to neutralize the influence of those political adversaries across Emperor Luying's territories.
Naturally, it omitted the political maneuvering behind this great disaster.
But that wasn't important anymore.
After all, it was the truth, and it had already passed.
Another piece of major news was that Duke Raphael had been elected Congress Speaker and concurrently appointed Interim Sovereign of the Empire of Luying.
Then this Sovereign ordered the immediate repeal of all faith-related acts, and at once began a citywide hunt to execute followers of foreign deities' cults, destroy their religious structures, and eradicate the breeding ground for these cults.
All in all, it was pretty much as expected.
On the sofa, Su Lun and his two companions were reading the newspaper.
Qian Tiao, seeing Raphael become the Interim Sovereign, couldn't help but speak out sarcastically, "Duke Raphael hid his capabilities deeply indeed. Even in the fierce battle last night, he only brought out a hundred thousand mechanical warriors. But after his victory, several hundred thousand-strong mechanical legions suddenly emerged in the city... Heh!"
"Indeed."
Su Lun echoed the sentiment, "Rich and powerful... The manufacturing cost of mechanical warriors on this scale is simply astronomical. I have no idea just how wealthy Rafael must be."
He too saw the sinister strategy behind it, concealing military strength clearly meant even allies were not fully trusted.
However, one had to admit that Rafael indeed had the power to overwhelm his peers in military strength.
A few years ago, PX911 was still a laboratory-level mechanical warrior, but now it had been mass-produced in astonishing quantities.
Although the power of a single super mechanical warrior was only at the third or fourth tier, what did hundreds of thousands signify?
This was almost enough to sweep across any lordship in Emperor Luying's dominion.
Mass-produced mechanical warriors have far greater advantages than traditional knights who take one or two decades to cultivate.
As for battle losses, as long as the materials still exist, they can be recycled.
The other notables dared not confront Rafael directly.
Upon hearing this, Qiantiao suddenly perked up, turning to Su Lun with a gleam in her eyes, "Didn't you say before that Rafael has a secret base on Prospector Sea Island? How about we go raid it?"
Stirred by the pirate blood in his veins, Su Lun also responded, "We can try."
The group had emerged from the slave mines of Old Lington, and they harbored no goodwill towards Duke Rafael.
Moreover, after the several assassination attempts by young master William, with Duke Rafael having a hand in them, a deadly feud had been cemented. If they were to raid, Su Lun would carry no psychological burden whatsoever.
Mr. Jing, who had been listening to the two conspiring, only smiled without saying a word.
He scrutinized the content of the newspaper carefully, seemingly pondering over what else to write.
...
He had read the newspaper and almost all the news he had been waiting for had arrived.
They weren't interested in the chaos of Ling Dun, and they planned to leave today for certain.
But Mr. Jing wasn't in a hurry to leave, as if he was still waiting for some news that his perception told him was on its way.
Su Lun and Qiantiao were not in a rush either, already plotting on the sofa.
However, just at that moment, Mr. Jing abruptly stopped flipping through the newspaper, her gaze intensifying, "They're here!"
Su Lun didn't know to whom she referred but sensed something too.
Through his Soul Perception, a very distinct soul fluctuation appeared at the bottom of the apartment building.
The crow on his shoulder cawed loudly, indicating that the visitor did not come with good intentions.
Qiantiao's hand also rested on the hilt of her sword.
No knocking was heard despite the familiarity.
A hole suddenly appeared in the wall of the room, and the uninvited guest entered with an air of arrogance.
He seemed to know that Mr. Jing was an eighth-tier professional, yet there wasn't the slightest hint of fear on his face, only a condescending scrutiny.
"Hey, hey, hey, you're quite rude. Ever heard of knocking before entering..."
Qiantiao was not one to indulge such impoliteness.
Her sword heart was clear, able to distinguish good from evil just by sensing the aura.
"Clang," the sword was drawn from its scabbard.
She performed a lightning-fast Iai Slash, sending a blade of Sword Qi slicing through the air.
Yet, a bizarre scene unfolded before them.
As the Sword Qi cut through the air with a "whoosh," the newcomer's vertical pupil in his brow tightened, and the Sword Qi disappeared completely!
It wasn't blocked, nor dodged, it just completely disappeared without a trace!
"How is this possible?"
Su Lun's gaze slightly narrowed, and he felt greatly surprised in his heart.
The scene before him exceeded his knowledge of conventional magic.
How did this person do it?
Even if that was just a casual slash from Qian Tian, it shouldn't have been blocked like that.
It's as if... the Sword Qi was disintegrated?
Arrogant as it may sound, this fellow really had the capital to be arrogant.
Before he could wonder any longer, Mr. Jing seemed to have seen something and revealed the mystery, "[S-009-All Things True Solution]. Your talent is quite impressive."
Upon hearing this, the pale young man with vertical pupils revealed a smug smile and proudly said, "The Dawn Leader truly has extraordinary insight. However, I must correct you, I have not only awakened the [All Things True Solution] divine talent, but I have also awakened my ancestral bloodline."
While speaking, he looked Su Lun and the others up and down with his eyes from his forehead, speaking from a position of superiority, "Let me introduce myself. I am from the all-knowing and omnipotent 'Divine Race.' You guys are not weak, and you're qualified to know my name. Remember it well, my name is Frank McAdam, the only Saint Heir of the Divine Race in this plane."
Listening to this sky-high self-introduction, Su Lun and the group started to find the situation somewhat amusing.
So it was you who tampered with fate, leading to that old lady activating the plane's key?
After this person revealed his identity, the atmosphere instantly became subtle.
Despite his arrogance, the three of them were patient enough to continue watching his show.
Su Lun, without changing his expression, used the All-knowing Eye to observe that the layer of Holy Light on Frank indeed seemed to be a symbol of divine protection.
That means, this guy could summon the will of a deity.
If it was a True God, he really did have the basis for such arrogance.
For a moment, the room fell into an awkward silence.
Frank thought they were unaware of the significance of the Divine Race and explained further, "Oh, you might not know what the great 'Divine Race' means. But you must have heard about what happened at the royal palace last night, right? The planar passageway opened by Queen Charlotte leads to my Divine Race's plane. Soon, my kin will arrive in this plane. Then, you will witness what true deities are!"
"..."
Su Lun seemed to understand.
This supposed Saint Heir was not any great noble, lacking his own network of information.
His source of news might also be incorrect and mixed reports from information merchants.
He obviously didn't know Mr. Jing's daughter, Isaac, nor how the Dawn used certain methods to kill that outer god.
He probably regarded the Dawn organization as just an ordinary civilian alchemical organization and considered Mr. Jing as some unsophisticated eighth-rank professional akin to King Oleg of the North Sea.
The three remained silent, quietly watching, also curious to know what this "Divine Race" was all about.
At this time, Mr. Jing asked in a tone devoid of any emotional fluctuations, "Then... what brings you here, sir?"
Frank seemed to feel that there was no need for roundabout ways and directly said, "You are quite strong. I am in need of a few subordinates right now."
Frank wasn't foolish. Although he had contacted his kin from the main plane, he knew full well that everything relied on strength and resources.
Now, through the will of a deity from his ancestors, he had learned about the specialty of the Alchemy plane.
Since he was in this "treasure house," he intended to gather as many resources and treasures as possible before his kin arrived.
This way, he would have more say in the future.
Of course, this was under the condition that he accomplished the investigation of a few treasures that his clan tasked him with.
Su Lun and the group fell silent upon hearing this.
So that was his game plan.
Seeing Su Lun and the others still not expressing any stance, Frank felt something seemed off but continued, "If you stay loyal to me, I can provide you with ample resources for advancement."
"""
As he spoke, he looked at Mr. Jing and said indifferently, "You must be lacking the cosmic essence required for advancing to the ninth tier by now, right? Stick with me, and I can provide you with all the resources needed for the advancement to the ninth tier. I can even have my ancestor give you some pointers."
He glanced at Su Lun and Qian Tiao, thinking about the intelligence he had garnered from the information dealer, and added, "As for you two, your talents aren't bad either. I guarantee that you can advance to the eighth tier."
...
The terms offered were indeed tempting.
Whether the cosmic essence could still be found in this plane was uncertain; this treasure that had stumped countless eighth-tier professionals was being offered so freely.
This promise was not to be taken lightly.
But after hearing this, Su Lun wasn't convinced that the guy was just talking big.
Having seen a True God, they knew what Frank was offering wouldn't be difficult for a civilization with a divine tier.
If it were someone else, they might have actually agreed.
But them? How could they possibly agree!
Frank had yet to realize that these three people before him would become deadly adversaries of their divine plane in the future.
Mr. Jing seemed to guess something and continued to probe, "Then, what would we need to do if we agree?"
Frank, thinking he had moved the other party with his recruitment terms, responded, "The 'Phantom Thief' Kit is a member of your organization, right? I want to know where he is now."
Mr. Jing, unflustered, asked in return, "What business do you have with him, sir?"
Hearing this disrespectful tone of questioning, Frank's face darkened immediately, and he said coldly, "That's not for you to ask. Just tell me where he is!"
Mr. Jing uttered an "oh" and suddenly formed sorcerer's seals with his hands.
Frank saw this and was not surprised. There was only a cold sneer on his face as he thought, "Hmph! Foolish!"
He felt it was a good opportunity to show these people a thing or two, lest they not understand whom they were up against.
However, the next second, before the scorn in his heart could fade, his expression dramatically changed!
Mr. Jing's magician seals solidified in an instant, and with a single hand, he struck the ground: "Mirror Image·God-Blocking Barrier!"
In an instant, the large room transformed into a house of mirrors, cutting off all external contact.
This caused Frank to instantly lose his connection with the deities!
...
They finally made their move!
Su Lun felt a surge of excitement in his heart.
Questioning this thing slowly was less efficient than killing and harvesting memories directly.
The domain of death emerged around him, and the black scythe and dagger appeared simultaneously in his hands.
Qian Tiao, on the other hand, reacted faster, drawing his sword and slashing in an Iai Slash move.
The three of them coordinated their moves with great tacit understanding!
This time it was the real deal.
A flash of lightning-fast sword Qi sliced at the man's waist.
The terrifying power of Qian Tiao's slash could even cleave through the seventh tier!
If it hit, a bisected fate would most likely await.
Surprisingly though, Frank's forehead pupil suddenly contracted, issuing a flash of white light, dissolving the sword Qi into nothing.
"As expected! The 'All-solving True Revelation' can deconstruct matter back to a primordial state..."
A chill went through Su Lun's heart; he now understood why the sword Qi had dissipated.
Nevertheless, his own dagger and scythe, which carried the domain of death, also lashed out.
Since it was a sneak attack, Frank couldn't dodge in time. He used his perpendicular pupil to break down the sword Qi, then turned to attempt to break down Su Lun's killing move.
But the always reliable 'All-solving True Revelation' failed for the first time in the face of the scythe and dagger enshrouded in black light!
Normally, anything hit by that beam of light would at least fall apart and the curses decay, or the domain and various spells would be broken.
But at this moment, when the white light shone on the black domain, it merely dimmed slightly without being stopped at all.
Seeing this, Su Lun didn't know why his attack went unabated, and with that, he landed a slash.
Frank could only resist desperately.
But, perhaps too reliant on his divine eye, his physical skills were not up to par.
A "swish" of a slash came down, blood sprayed several meters, and a severed arm also fell to the ground.
Seeing Qian Tiao slashing again, a strong sense of impending death left Frank pale and terrified.
This guy had no intention of staying any longer. His upright pupil focused, staring at an exit in the barrier.
Suddenly, a special divine power rose from him.
Everyone watched as the barrier was pierced by a breach and the man disappeared without a trace.
...
"He escaped?"
Qian Tiao's sword cut through air, frowning at the escaping individual.
Mr. Jing, however, seemed to have discerned something, and said, "That guy is protected by a deity. The barrier can't stop a True God. We only had one chance for a surprise attack. It's normal that we couldn't kill him."
Listening, Su Lun expressed his surprise, "Protected by a True God?"
