Although those two materials were precious, they indeed were miraculous lifesavers for him at the moment.
But to an alchemist, the most crucial principle was "equivalent exchange."
If repairing this fragment required such fine materials, then surely, if successful, the outcome would be exceptional!
Moreover, the main body of these fragments was the "Urobolos Space-Time Ring," an artifact whose level was unknown but surely more powerful than any known 'lesser god'!"
Even a speck of dust shaken from the clothes of the gods was a monumental mountain in the eyes of ordinary people.
But if really repaired successfully, restoring even a trace of its effect would be an immense upgrade for anyone below the god-tier!
Taking this risk was undoubtedly worth it.
Moreover, this Dwarf King's resentment was of a "divine craftsman" standard, perhaps the only existence in the alchemical realm capable of repairing this fragment.
This opportunity was not to be missed!
Hearing Su Lun's decision, Iron Helm Orr responded indifferently, "Oh, alright. Since you've decided so, I'll give it a try."
Speaking, he picked up the hammer again, placing the three fragments and materials into the burning forge. The Sand of Time and the Spatial Crystal Core also slowly melted into law-fluid in the divine fire.
Seeing this, Su Lun's heart surged with an unprecedented level of anticipation as he quietly watched.

chapters.title: Chapter 515 - 514 [Urobolos Space-Time Ring]
chapters.content:
[Urobolos Space-Time Ring]was a Divine King Artifact beyond Su Lun's understanding, where even what seemed like simple repairs were a time-consuming and energy-draining process.
After Dwarf King Tie Kui Ao lifted his rune-imbued hammer, he paid no further attention to Su Lun.
His mind was undistracted, focused only on the furnace and forging.
The space echoed with crisp and rhythmic clinking sounds.
"Clang," "Clang," "Clang"...
Su Lun watched intently from the side.
It must be said, watching a divine craftsman at work was anything but boring.
Especially for someone like Su Lun, who knew quite a bit about forging techniques, it was a magical experience from which one could greatly benefit.
Watching strokes that seemed like those of an ordinary blacksmith, Su Lun understood that this Dwarf King's hammering was not merely on a physical level. Underneath that heavy hammer, even the laws themselves were forged and transformed, molding into the required shape and fusing onto the ring.
The rhythm of the hammering was clearly a matter of sophisticated forging skills.
Su Lun silently watched, his own forging skills greatly improving in the process.
However, he also noticed a problem.
It was that the Dwarf King's resentment seemed to fade during the forging process, his rationality gradually dissipating as his actions seemed to rely completely on instinctive mechanical movements.
Su Lun realized this was a sign of the disappearance of obsession and the disintegration of the residual soul.
Frightened, he quickly covered the Dwarf King's residual soul with a rune-imbued black umbrella, using the umbrella's effect to nourish the undead and mend the wisp of residual soul.
Otherwise, if things were not repaired and top-tier materials were used up, that would indeed be a huge loss.
...
Su Lun always stayed by the forge.
At the exit of the curse space, to be cautious, Su Lun had enlisted Mr. Hei's help. With him and No. 19 guarding, the remaining divine plane mages could not stir up any trouble, and after two attempted attacks were driven back, they quieted down.
This repair process lasted nearly half a month.
Every day of repairs was nerve-wracking for Su Lun, always fearful that the Dwarf King's resentment might suddenly stop working one day.
Luckily, the rune-imbued black umbrella was powerful enough to continuously nourish, stabilizing the fluctuations of the residual soul even more than before.
As days passed, watching the cracks on the shard being glued together with the adhesive made from the Sand of Time and dimensional shards, Su Lun's feelings of anticipation and anxiety intensely conflicdted.
Finally, on the sixteenth day,
Su Lun heard the noise of forging cease and upon looking, the Dwarf King's resentment had taken the ring, glowing red-hot from the divine fire, out of the Eternal Forge, which brought him sudden joy.
"Repair succeeded!"
His left eye shimmering brilliantly, he identified the ring's attributes at first glance.
[Urobolos Space-Time Ring (Damaged)]
Quality: Divine King Artifact
Description: Time is a ring with past, present, and future; after ritual refinement, gain spatial casting affinity +999, temporal affinity +999, immune to influences of space-time laws not higher than the artifact's own laws; can integrate with spatial equipment, absorb curse spaces, space-time rifts to condense under one's control of space-time powers;
Detail: You see the origins of the curse space on the ring, the artifact broken, the laws of the universe overflowing and scattered across the fractured planes creating numerous cursed spaces. The artifact is now damaged, and apart from some space-time properties inherent in the materials, you cannot use any of its powers; this item contains vast amounts of information beyond comprehension;
"Such strong attributes!"
Seeing this, Su Lun's expression suddenly cleared as if the clouds had parted to reveal the sky.
He could tell at a glance that the repair of the ring wasn't very good, like gluing a shattered jade bracelet together with inferior glue, and the crude marks were very apparent.
But even the slight effectiveness of this repair made him extremely delighted!
Although it lacked direct combat functionality like the black scythe that could slash and kill, the ring still irresistibly drew Su Lun's gaze!
That casting affinity "+999" was strikingly conspicuous.
This wasn't a defined value, but rather because it exceeded the upper limits of comprehension.
Su Lun knew then that the Sand of Time and dimensional crystals he previously used had not been wasted, but had indeed earned him a huge gain!
When he had used these two types of law materials to release alchemy previously, he had utilized their temporary boost in casting affinity to enhance the power of the seals.
Now this ring could do the same.
What did that mean?
Previously, using these materials for casting was a one-time consumable affair, each use depleting a bit of the materials.
But now with the ring, it was reusable equipment.
It was many times stronger than casting spells using materials before!
That meant he could now use long-distance Spatial Displacement without any hesitation.
And he could use it infinitely!
Just by holding it in his hand, Su Lun could distinctly feel the exaggerated spell affinity enhancement.
With a rough estimate in his mind, he had already glimpsed the terrifying enhancement.
Previously, the limit for "Teleportation" was a few dozen meters; now with the ring in his possession, he estimated that the distance could reach a thousand meters; theoretically, it could explode to several thousand meters after a complete refinement!
This distance would continue to strengthen as his comprehension of the laws improved.
The distance of this instant-cast spell, "Teleportation," was comparable to long-distance Spatial Displacement that originally required seals and law condensation.
If he really refined this ring, Su Lun figured that theoretically, barring any other unforeseen factors, he could even Teleport directly back to Luying from the MaFa Space!
Could you imagine this survival capability?
In the future, even if he encountered formidable enemies, if he could not defeat them, nobody could hold him back!
Just this alone made Su Lun feel it was worth it.
Extremely worth it!
Furthermore, Su Lun saw the description of the ring and finally solved an ultimate mystery in the field of Alchemy: "So the curse space in the Alchemy plane formed because of the law overflow from this Divine Artifact's fracture!"
The energy spillover from one Divine Artifact affected an entire plane; can you imagine its high tier?
From the memories of the mages in those divine planes he had previously stripped away, he knew that there was no curse space in the divine planes.
There was something similar called "Space-Time Rifts," but they were extremely rare.
In contrast, the number in the Alchemy plane was almost as numerous as the stars in the sky, which was simply unbelievable.
Now that he understood it was due to this Divine Artifact.
No wonder this "Urobolos Space-Time Ring" was coveted by the divine beings of the divine planes!
...
"This really is like trading a bird gun for a cannon..."
Su Lun had never felt so good before.
In the past, he was always terrified in this survival-of-the-fittest world, always afraid of encountering top-level powerhouses who could annihilate him on the spot.
Now with this ring, he was confident about making his way in the Alchemy plane!
Even if he faced a ninth-tier head-on, he could still retreat with ease.
With the ring's terrifying affinity enhancement, if the enemy wanted to limit his Teleportation on the plane of Space Law, even a ninth-tier would find it difficult to restrain him.
With enhanced survival capabilities, his thoughts immediately became more active.
It seemed he could start planning for Dragon Island as well...
Su Lun's mind instantly conjured up countless scenes.
Previously, he felt that with his current level at the seventh tier, his survival chances in that dangerous sea area, which could annihilate even the Pirate King's fleet, were not high.
But now...
Even if he didn't find the treasure, it would be very hard to die.
Moreover, having battled the Black Dragon, he had a rough understanding of the legendary combat power of the dragon race.
As long as he didn't encounter a ninth-tier dragon, comparable to a divine being in strength, as Mr. Jing said, he thought the problem wasn't big.
With his mind racing, Su Lun had even thought through a whole series of adventure plans.
But now wasn't the time to dwell on those adventures, as he glanced at the scene before him where the spirit of the Dwarf King, Iron Helm Oll, was still woodenly standing.
Su Lun asked a question and received not a single response.
Thinking it over, he decided to collect this lingering spirit with his rune-marked black umbrella.
....
After doing all this, Su Lun then turned his thoughts back to this space.
This "Dwarf King's Grudge" curse space was very peculiar, not dissipating even now. Fundamentally, it formed a stable space reliant on the overflowed space-time power of the ring.
Upon seeing this, Su Lun recalled another piece of information identified from the ring: "This ring can absorb curse spaces?"
Some other ideas popped into his head.
Could he use the ring to expand the Minor Void Realm a bit?
It was like the time before, when he fused with the fragmented space of the mirror-like library.
The moment the thought struck him, he immediately set to work.
Having set up the highest level of ritual formation he knew, using various flawless crystals, alchemical arrays, and his own blood, Su Lun began to consecrate the "Urobolos Space-Time Ring."
Before long, the alchemical array glowed, and a dense force of Space-Time Law permeated the formation.
A day later, the consecration was complete.
Su Lun slowly opened his eyes from meditation.
He looked at the Ouroboros ring in his hand, his eyes gleaming with a sharp light.
Although he had previously identified the ring's effects, he couldn't help but remark, "The amplification of a Divine Artifact is indeed exaggerated."
After the consecration, wearing the ring, the affinity with space was indescribably enhanced.
Previously, her understanding of "Space-Time Law" was like viewing scenery from a mountain peak—a perspective already rare among her peers; but now, after the fusion, it was like viewing from an airship, with the land entirely in her sight.
The Divine Artifact had raised her affinity significantly.
And this increase was beyond what normal cultivation could reach.
The ring clearly had more uses to be uncovered, and Su Lun planned to research them slowly in the future.
The identified information was that the ring could integrate into spatial equipment.
His implant, "Endless Stomach of the Sky Whale," was a mini realm and theoretically, it was also possible.
After performing the consecration, Su Lun felt even more certain that his previous idea was sound.
With a pinch of the sorcerer's seals, he attempted to integrate the ring into his implant.
To his surprise, this attempt went very smoothly!
The ring, containing the supreme Space-Time Law, had a very high compatibility with the minor void realm and easily merged into the space.
Su Lun didn't dare to try absorbing the space in the cursed realm; he put away the "Eternal Furnace," along with treasures like hammers and Contract Scrolls.
Then, with a teleportation, he appeared at the exit of the cursed space.
...
Seeing Su Lun, whom they hadn't seen in over ten days, number nineteen and Mr. Hei standing at the exit were a bit surprised.
Number nineteen asked, "Did you manage it?"
"Yes,"
Su Lun nodded, smiling as he continued, "Let's go, we're leaving. I plan to try and absorb this cursed space."
Even Mr. Hei, experienced and knowledgeable, was incredulous at these words, "Absorb the cursed space?"
The three of them left one after another.
The surroundings changed instantly, and they were now in a dark mine tunnel.
Su Lun sensed for a moment; their current location was roughly beneath Giant God Mountain. This area was previously completely covered by dark energy and spatial fissures.
Right in front of them was an entrance to one of the fractures of the cursed space.
Su Lun didn't delay, pinching the sorcerer's seals; a seven-pointed star alchemy formation lit up beneath his feet.
He condensed a spatial vortex in his hand and reached out towards the spatial fracture. In an instant, the vortex seemed to have a strange suction force, pulling the fracture into it.
By his side, number nineteen and Mr. Hei watched in amazement.
Su Lun felt even more excited: "It really works!"
It was like connecting a draining machine to a pool, whooshing water from elsewhere.
He was well aware that his minor void realm was being filled with massive amounts of spatial energy, continually expanding.
That drain lasted a whole day.
...
When they emerged, it was around early morning; looking at his pocket watch, it was now midnight.
The spatial fissures that were previously visible everywhere in the mine had now completely disappeared.
The vast cursed space had been wholly devoured by Su Lun.
"Dwarf King's Resentment" was a space where reality and illusion overlapped and twisted.
Some things in the cursed space really existed in reality.
For example, the treasures in the underground city.
Most of the mountain dwarves had escaped through the secret passages before.
As for the few adventurers and some mountain dwarves still remaining in the space, they were expelled by Su Lun before they realized what had happened. Those remaining mages, he naturally finished off on the spot.
The cursed space had completely turned into nutrients, nourishing the Lesser Void Realm.
At this moment, the area of the Lesser Void Realm had expanded by several tens of square kilometers.
The previously cramped war workshop instantly became a corner of the space, surrounded by large swaths of vacant land.
The people in the Lesser Void Realm were happily arranging the various equipment that previously had no place to be set up.
With such a vast territory now available, they could even create a forest, a large lake, and a bustling town.
Su Lun and the Dawn Brigade could completely tailor this space to their liking.
And in the future, he could completely extract other cursed spaces to further expand the Lesser Void Realm.
In time, this space would slowly become an ideal little world.
...
Mr. Hei had returned to reside in the Lesser Void Realm. He was the librarian of Dawn, and now that the space was large enough, he also had to go back and plan the layout of the library.
Su Lun looked at Number Nineteen beside him and called out, "Come, let's go talk to the mountain dwarves."
"Alright."
Number Nineteen nodded, a flicker of different colors flashing in her eyes.
The formidable enemy had been killed, the cursed space completely broken, and it seemed this adventure was also nearing its end.
She was also glad she had come along this time, for she had gained such a great opportunity.
She was gradually getting used to being Su Lun's "lucky amulet".
Thinking of something, she smiled faintly.
Without much ado, Su Lun, wrapping his arm around her mechanical waist, disappeared from the spot.
Before, teleporting someone required seals to be formed and a moment of concentration, but now it took nearly one step to travel a thousand meters.
After several teleports, Su Lun had already sensed dense soul fluctuations.
Right in the dwarves' underground city, in a great hall stacked with treasures.
The Black Dragon had flown away, but it couldn't take the treasures stored here with it.
The [Dwarf King's Resentment] was a space where illusion and reality alternated, and the treasures seen before were still here.
Only the dwarf king's statue had been removed and melted down by Su Lun, so now there was no statue here.
At this moment, a golden-haired, crowned big-bearded dwarf was also leading a group of his people, sorting through something in the pile of treasures.
Previously this great hall had been covered by the cursed space, likely sensing the disappearance of the cursed space, they had felt their way here.
Seeing two people suddenly appear in the great hall, the dwarves were also immediately on alert.
Having mostly slipped away through the secret passage during the great battle, they were unclear about what had happened afterward.
But seeing Su Lun, the dwarf king recognized him instantly and also vaguely guessed something.
Su Lun knew what they were looking for.
Without waiting to be asked, he took out the hammer, rune codex, and other items, and bluntly said, "In the cursed space, I encountered the lingering spirit of your noble ancestor 'Iron Helmet Othar'. He entrusted me to bring these ancestral treasures out to the mountain dwarves..."
What!
Iron Helmet Othar?
Hearing this legendary name, the group of mountain dwarves looked at each other in disbelief.
As they saw the ancestral treasures that had been passed down from elder to elder truly appear before their eyes, their expressions became extremely complex, a mix of shock, sentiment, excitement, and exhilaration.
One by one, they looked at the treasures and then turned their gaze to the person who had brought them out.
This person could lift the [Dwarf King's Divine Forge], meaning, he was indeed recognized by the heroic spirits.
In an instant, the skepticism in the dwarves' eyes dissipated, replaced by gratitude and friendliness.
Su Lun had brought out these items not only to fulfill his promise but also to recruit these skilled mountain dwarves as blacksmiths.
Pointing to the pile, he didn't hide his intentions as he directly said, "Iron Helmet Othar asked me to pass on his words: if humans are willing to follow the terms of the alliance again one day, the mountain dwarves will still honor their promise to become steadfast allies like the steel of alchemy."
Pausing, Su Lun looked at the big-bearded dwarf king, who was deep in thought upon hearing these words, and said directly, "Now that the invasion of the planes has become a reality and the alchemy plane is in imminent danger, if Your Excellency the Dwarf King believes I am trustworthy, I would like, on behalf of the alchemists, to restart this alliance."
At this suggestion, the dwarf king's compact face showed an extremely solemn expression.

chapters.title: Chapter 516 - 515: Did Yekaterina Become an Empress?
chapters.content:
Su Lun wanted to recruit this group of mountain dwarfs.
The demands for craftsmanship in high-level puppets had been increasing, and although the war workshop could satisfy mass production requirements, it was not high-end enough.
Moreover, it wasn't just for his own needs that he required these craftsmen, who were all "advanced forging masters," but because the dawn also needed them.
By now, the invasion of the plane had become a certainty, and the Alchemy plane was at its most critical moment.
It was necessary to accumulate strength to meet the increasingly intense war.
Su Lun had stripped a lot of intelligence from the memories of those from the Celestial plane, and he was now certain that there was almost only one outcome for the plane invasion, which was to be enslaved by foreign divine beings.
All natives became followers of the gods of the Celestial plane, as that was the only way to survive.
Those who couldn't convert to believers only had one path: death.
If it had been another plane, it might have just meant toppling the old statues of the gods and replacing them with new ones.
But for the Alchemy plane, it was almost catastrophic.
Because alchemists didn't possess any belief in gods.
Their power came entirely from themselves and their alchemical knowledge.
Whether it was the advancement system or the bodily integration system, both relied on their own understanding of the universal laws and exploration of knowledge to obtain extraordinary powers.
In belief-centric planes, however, the concept promoted by the gods to their followers was that the only source of extraordinary power was the gods themselves.
If one wanted to gain extraordinary power, one had to devote belief to a specific deity.
This was also why magic flourished in the Celestial plane, yet the most basic machines were absent.
Believers were deeply convinced that everything, even seasons, harvests, wars, healing, and partners, was a gift from the gods.
The foreign gods did not tolerate the existence of "alchemy."
Because it could undermine their supreme authority.
When humans could change their lives relying on alchemy, their need for gods would diminish, and their faith would gradually weaken.
Thus, in nearly any belief-centric plane, any method of gaining power that bypassed gods was viewed as "taboo."
Similarly, once alchemists started believing in any god, the entire alchemical system would collapse.
All alchemical knowledge, bodily integrations, advancements, bloodline potions... would be abolished.
Su Lun himself did not want to become a servant or a nourishment of faith for any gods.
And he had never thought of giving up the alchemy system, which held infinite potential.
Therefore, a fight to the death was inevitable.
From this viewpoint, he increasingly understood the feelings of Sir Isaac when he wrote the famous phrase in his notes: "Gods, to some extent, are nothing more than higher-grade alchemical materials."
...
"So, that's the situation right now. As you can see, the Celestial plane has already invaded on a large scale. Deep beneath Celestial Mountain, there's a great secret hidden, and surely, there will be more invaders coming in the future..."
Su Lun held nothing back and shared all the information he knew.
All the dwarfs listened with a grave expression.
Although the mountain dwarf tribe was isolated and cut off from the world, they could distinguish the good from the bad in human nature.
Through this situation, they all understood that what Su Lun was saying was the truth.
Despite their immense strength, mountain dwarfs were not skilled in combat.
They were simply the best mining masters and forging craftsmen.
Just like how a group of ten thousand mages could have easily annihilated this group in the past.
Now, even the curse space was lost, stripping them of their last means of mutual destruction.
After speaking, the hall was quiet for a long time.
The current Dwarf King, Beer Barrel Beo, pondered for a moment before speaking, "Thank you for returning the heirloom of my mountain dwarf tribe to our ancestors. However, I'm sorry, what you said involves major issues, and I need to discuss it with the elders in the tribe before I can decide."
Listening, Su Lun was not surprised and replied, "Of course. I will wait here for a day, and if your tribe decides and is willing to restart the alliance, then we will be allies who advance and retreat together in the future."
Having seen the previous Dwarf King's exquisite forging skills, he was not willing to give up this rare recruitment opportunity easily.
Hand forging might seem inefficient, but the quality was very good. Moreover, hand forging was irreplaceable in some aspects, such as advanced enchantments, coating, and inscriptions, areas where modern mechanical technology still fell far short.
This was exactly what was needed to supplement the needs for high-level puppets and the Dawn squad's magic armor.
Seeing that the dwarfs needed to have a discussion, Su Lun did not intend to stay.
Dwarf King Beer Barrel Beo nodded and responded, "Regardless, one day later, we will give you a result of our discussion."
Su Lun said no more, turned around, and left the hall with No. 19, heading to the depths of the mine.
...
Now, with the curse space that covered the underground city gone, there was no danger anywhere.
Su Lun and No. 19 headed downward.
This was the path they had encountered when they met the malevolent spirit of the Dwarf King in the cursed space before.
Su Lun was still very curious about what secrets were hidden under the ground.
Soon, they saw the endlessly dark spiral staircase again.
"It really exists?"
Su Lun was also curious, as such a magical "endless staircase" truly existed in the physical space.
He had now cultivated the "Urobolos Space-Time Ring," and his spatial perception was extremely strong. Even so, he perceived this staircase as being infinite.
The area clearly operated under higher levels of Space Law.
After observing for a moment without seeing any dangers, Su Lun cautiously proceeded downward holding No. 19, his lucky charm.
They continued for almost half an hour without seeing an end in sight.
The staircase seemed to lead to the very depths of the earth.
Spatial perception had become chaotic, Su Lun even felt as if they were no longer in the alchemical plane.
But there was no danger, so he just kept walking downward.
As they walked, Number Nineteen suddenly discovered something on a stretch of staircase and whispered, "Su Lun, take a look."
When Su Lun looked over, one sentence was inscribed on the stone step: "You need to recite a spell to glimpse the truth."
"A spell?"
Su Lun had a flash of insight and immediately thought of something.
Magicians didn't have many flashy spells, the only one they knew was universal.
Thinking of this, he recited, "Follow the law of equivalent exchange, praise the glory of the original creator, witness the miracle of creation through alchemy."
Then, just as these words fell, suddenly, in his spatial perception, the endless staircase seemed to have an end.
"Huh..."
Su Lun immediately noticed something unusual, thought for a moment, and understood.
This was definitely not a simple sound-controlled restriction.
Spells were imbued with a direction of belief; without sincerity, there would be no response.
This spell was directed towards "The original creator" worshipped by alchemists.
Meaning if one wasn't an alchemist, even if they recited it, they couldn't trigger the restriction.
Having realized this, Su Lun knew that the secret beneath was left by some Great Alchemist for future generations.
At his side, Number Nineteen saw Su Lun hesitate for a moment and asked, "What's wrong?"
"Nothing."
Su Lun explained his guess, slightly smiling, "It seems the predecessor who created this space left something. This restriction isn't friendly to devout followers..."
"Oh."
Number Nineteen always felt that being with Su Lun made her realize her own mind wasn't as sharp.
As a warrior born for battle, she figured it was better to leave the thinking to her partner.
She shrugged her shoulders and righteously embraced her role as a lucky charm.
After the spell was recited, the two continued downward and quickly reached the bottom.
Before them stood a hundred-meter-high black iron gate.
The gate was engraved with some very special symbols.
Number Nineteen had already closed her eyes, and Su Lun only kept his left eye open.
He had seen a similar giant gate before in the Ruins of the Sea, an underwater tomb where a Sea God was buried, also with such a huge golden gate.
Su Lun had not understood it before, but after acquiring the knowledge of the Grave Digger, he knew it was a top-tier specification for a god's burial ground.
The gate represented the divine ranking and also sealed the chaotic Power of Laws radiating from it.
The huge black iron columns around it bore patterns distinctly characteristic of the dwarf race, likely built by the ancestors of the mountain dwarves.
Looking at this black iron gate, Su Lun speculated, "Could it really be the burial site of a deity? Perhaps the Time Traveler, Andreas Libavius?"
Who it was didn't matter.
What mattered was, the tomb's specifications were extremely high.
However, just as he was focusing on observing that black iron gate, suddenly, the view in front of him seemed to warp, forming the silhouette of a figure.
Because he understood the Time Law, he could see it.
"Time has warped?"
Su Lun had now grasped certain principles of the Time Law, and he immediately knew what he was seeing.
There was no soul fluctuation, and it was not a creature in the normal sense of understanding.
It was like a blur of light, but even though it was not clear, he could see it was an old man in a white robe.
The old man was beside the black iron gate, his finger sketching out a line of text: "The pattern of the ouroboros points to the ultimate secret of alchemy, through the path of time, one can glimpse the true appearance of truth."
When Su Lun saw this line of text, his eyebrows immediately furrowed tightly.
It seemed as though he understood something, yet as if he understood nothing at all.
It was after this line of text that he sketched out the pattern of an ouroboros.
As soon as Su Lun saw it, he recognized it as the pattern on the Urobolos Space-Time Ring he held in his hand.
He immediately guessed the identity of the figure of light.
As the distorted old man continued sketching, he muttered something to himself.
"When I was young, I mastered the mysteries of the power of space and time. Back then, I had thought how interesting it would be to inscribe an epitaph on my own tombstone."
"Every creature is a prisoner of time. Life is like the timeline divided into small squares, square by square. Because life is limited, no one can see the full extent of time. That's the mystery of time."
"Because of time, to some extent, everything gains meaning."
"..."
Su Lun was greatly shocked as he listened.
A few simple sentences felt like an enlightenment, as if revealing the true essence of time.
He had thought this figure was some sort of afterimage.
However, more amazingly, after the old man's mumbling, he actually turned back to look at him and spoke, "Hello there, 'favored by time' from the future timeline."
Silence clearly wasn't the right response, so Su Lun directly asked, "Predecessor, can you see me?"
The old man smiled, "Hadn't you considered that it is because you are bound to ask this question that I can see you? I'm merely responding to someone who will appear on this timeline, someone who can see me."
"..."
Su Lun listened thoughtfully.
He then asked, "Senior, are you Master Andreas?"
The figure laughed slightly, seemingly acknowledging by default, then counter-questioned without answering, "Are you wondering if I am not dead?"
Su Lun became even more puzzled.
This wasn't a cursed space, devoid of any regrets. In what form did "He" truly exist?
The old man clarified, "My story line had ended long before yours began... but did I truly die? It's like when you open a novel and a character dies within his story line, then when you reopen the book, that character is still alive. He is doomed to die, but in his timeline, he remains alive, never having changed. Doesn't that seem, to you, much like the life of a human being? From the moment of birth, death is destined."
"The mystery of time lies in whether you're someone capable of reopening the novel and reading it from the beginning. If not, you're merely one of the myriad beings within the book."
"If you can see the shadows of time I left behind, congratulations... you are now qualified to glimpse the true nature of reality."
"I wander through time, appearing in this timeline, merely out of a fleeting whim."
"..."
In the instant he heard these words, Su Lun stood rooted to the spot as if struck by lightning.
Only someone who truly understands the Time Law could fully comprehend the essence hinted by these words!
Like a guiding light, showing the way out of perpetual darkness.
After these words, the elder's light and shadow suddenly disappeared.
What remained was just the immense iron gate in front of him and the sentence inscribed upon it.
"Time is an ouroboros... The Time Traveler can wander through the long river of time..."
Su Lun muttered to himself, seemingly enlightened by something.
Then, the question arose.
The person he had just seen, was he dead or not?
With time as a factor, he suddenly felt that death could not be so simply defined.
...
Probably because Su Lun was muttering to himself incoherently, Number 19, standing next to him, asked alertly, "Su Lun, are you alright?"
Su Lun, puzzled, asked back, "Didn't you hear someone talking just now?"
Number 19 looked even more alert and replied, "No. You were the only one who spoke just now, saying 'Senior, can you see me?' and also 'Senior, are you Master Andreas?'"
Hearing this, Su Lun chuckled and suddenly realized, "Let's go back, I'll explain it to you slowly."
Number 19 frowned deeply and continued, "Are you really alright?"
Su Lun, knowing full well that only he had seen and heard that temporal illusion, said, "I'm really fine."
With that, he wrapped his arms around Number 19's mechanical waist and teleported, appearing on the surface.
The bizarre, indescribable surroundings had disappeared, and it was only then that Number 19 dared to open her eyes. Surveying the forest around her, she finally realized they had truly made it out.
The two strolled through the jungle, with Su Lun smiling as he explained what had just happened.
Only then did Number 19 understand what had occurred, and she couldn't help but feel amazed from time to time.
However, she didn't grasp the profound mysteries of time and didn't know what Su Lun had realized.
After thinking for a moment, she asked, "So... is there really a celestial tomb underground? You came out without looking around more?"
"Yes,"
Su Lun smiled and added, "I've already obtained what I should have, so naturally there's no need to stay any longer. As for the other treasures, I can't take them with me righ now."
Number 19 listened and raised her eyebrows but said nothing further.
The weather was beautiful today, strands of sunlight filtering into the forest like golden ribbons.
Su Lun had to wait for the results of the Dwarf tribe's discussions, so there was still a day to go.
Suddenly without any urgency, the pair walked somewhat listlessly.
As they walked, Su Lun suddenly thought of something and said, "Right, let's test my new ability!"
Number 19 looked at him with an inquiring gaze, "?"
"I'm planning to go find Sister Qiantiao and test out the new formation."
Su Lun smirked slightly, picked up the communication ring, and directly asked, "Sister Qiantiao, where are you now?"
The next second, the communicator buzzed back, "Yo, are you done with your tasks? I'm in the Zambula Ironfalls Province in the southern part of Mafa. Remember that interdimensional passage you mentioned before? The Mafa military has found the exact coordinates. It's quite lively here these days."
Su Lun heard this and sensed some major event, "Oh, are you busy right now? I'll come to you."
As he said this, Sister Qiantiao responded lazily, "What's the hassle? Come over if you want."
"Good."
Listening to this, Su Lun confirmed Sister Qiantiao's spatial coordinates and his hands swiftly formed the sorcerer's seals.
In an instant, a huge Seven-Pointed Star Formation illuminated beneath his feet.
Adequate rank wasn't enough, only power could make up for it.
In addition to the ring's great affinity for space, the "Heart of Giant Isaac" was also necessary for supplying the massive energy needed for long-distance teleportation.
...
Meanwhile, deep in the mountains of the southern Zambula Ironfalls Province.
In a remote and picturesque forest, clear springs flowed.
The misty waters of the springs hinted at a quality hot spring.
Within the spring, two graceful figures soaked.
"What's up?"
"Su Lun said he was going to come over."
"Oh? Wasn't he at the Dwarf tribe deep in the Monster Mountains, has he come to the south now?"
"Who knows."
"..."
After several days of fierce fighting, they had finally found a natural hot spring and were soaking in it.
Their clothes hung from a branch nearby, and a sword lay by the edge of the spring.
She was naked, comfortably soaking in the water.
The pool wasn't large, but it also contained the graceful figure of another person.
It was just after their conversation when suddenly both of their eyes snapped open, gazing at a spatial distortion forming a few meters away.
But recognizing who the newcomer was, the wariness in their eyes instantly evaporated, replaced by a relaxed expression.
She glanced over and then continued to lie back with her eyes closed, enjoying the nourishment of the hot spring.
Hearing the sound of footsteps, she murmured slightly surprised, "Yo... How did you get here so quickly, kiddo?"
The newcomer wasn't just anyone; it was Su Lun, who had teleported there.
From the Monster Beast Forest to here was over two thousand kilometers.
He hadn't expected to teleport so smoothly.
"Ah... didn't I tell you earlier, I got a spatial treasure and then tried a long-distance spatial displacement, and I didn't expect to arrive just like that," he said.
Su Lun replied, his tone laced with subtle excitement.
Using such long-range spatial displacement for the first time felt great.
Though it drained a terrifying amount of dark spiritual power, with the heart of alchemy, recovery was extremely fast.
This ability would make traveling anywhere in the future convenient.
As Su Lun spoke, he also took a moment to survey the surrounding environment.
The area was surrounded by dense pine woods covered with a layer of white snow.
In the woods, there was a steaming clear spring.
Seeing her by the water's edge did not surprise Su Lun, as he had come directly to the coordinates located on the pendant around her neck.
But seeing the other person in the water, he exclaimed in surprise, "Senior Sister?"
Mr. Jing responded with a slight smile, "Yes."
Out of curiosity, Su Lun asked, "Senior Sister, what are you doing here? Weren't you in the Senodia province before?"
Mr. Jing responded lightly, "The planar portal was discovered. The Mafa military has already fought many fierce battles with those plane mages. The situation here is not optimistic, so I came to check it out."
"Oh?"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun frowned.
No wonder he smelled a trace of bloodiness, emanating from the clothes and sword hanging nearby.
With a glance, he realized she had recently killed quite a few people.
However, the clothes were all hung on a branch...
Looking into the spring again, it was indeed as expected; the gambling-addicted lady was stark naked.
Beneath the shimmering light, her graceful contours were fully revealed.
She seemed utterly unconcerned, serenely at ease.
Su Lun's gaze then fell on Mr. Jing beside him, and he exclaimed, "Wow, Senior Sister, you have a great figure."/p>
Mr. Jing always carried an air of classical elegance. Even dressed in a thin, gossamer garment, her well-defined figure was showcased, but it was seductive without being vulgar, offering a sense of a lotus flower detached from its murky origins.
Listening to Su Lun's compliments, she simply smiled.
Meanwhile, she looked rather annoyed and said, "Su Lun, have you not bathed in a long time? You smell sour."
Then, without any hesitation, she invited him, "Come on in and soak together."
"Sure."
Thinking about it, Su Lun realized that it had been over a month since he had bathed, starting from when he had set off on his adventure to the Monster Mountains.
He didn't hesitate, he undressed and prepared to enter the water, casually asking, "Sister Qian Tao, has anything significant happened in the two great empires recently?"
Knowing he was advancing, no one had disturbed him.
He had been out of touch for a long time and wanted to catch up on the news, never expecting to become the subject of the gossip.
Qian Tao replied lazily, "The hottest news is about the war here in Mafa. There's not much to say, just various brutal sieges. The divine plane's magic corps is very strong..."
Su Lun listened, unsurprised by the content.
Finding a planar portal inevitably meant fighting.
However, Qian Tao suddenly changed the subject, her tone tinged with teasing, "Also... three days ago, your wife, Yekaterina Lants, proclaimed herself emperor in Lyung."
"???"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's action of undressing stiffened.
It took a moment for him to process what he had just heard.
Still, his face was filled with utter disbelief.
Yekaterina becoming an emperor?
How did she do it?
It had only been a few months; what had he missed?
No matter how he thought about it, it didn't seem right!

chapters.title: Chapter 517 - 517: 516
chapters.content:
Although Su Lun knew that Yekaterina was highly ambitious and unparalleled in her strategies,
it seemed that the various arrangements of the Lans family over the past few hundred years were also part of grand schemes.
In Luying, a first-class duke was already a top-ranking noble, next only to princes and the royal family.
Su Lun felt that they might have aspirations for the throne.
But the current situation was that they simply didn't possess the qualifications to claim the throne.
Or was it Yekaterina?
What on earth had happened?
"What about Duke Raphael, the 'Acting Head of State'?"
What about the other nobles of Luying?
No matter what, it was impossible for a young daughter of the Lans family to become the emperor, right?
If it were a few years later, Su Lun might still think it possible.
But it had been just a few months since he last saw her!
...
For a moment, Su Lun was shocked, then curiously asked, "What exactly happened? Isn't Luying still in the midst of a civil war? How could Yekaterina have become the emperor?"
While speaking, he had already taken off his clothes and, wearing only his boxer shorts, stepped into the water.
Back in Old Lington, the three of them had bathed like this before, and now it was no different.
The only difference was that the former gambling addict, who used to dress modestly, now appeared completely unashamed in her nakedness.
The hot spring wasn't large, with Qiantiao and Mr. Jing each standing at one side, and Su Lun lying down in the space they had made for him in the middle.
Upon hearing this query, Qiantiao replied, "After the divine battle outside of Lington, the Bonaparte royals completely exited the stage. Then Duke Raphael became the Acting Head of State... This duke also displayed the makings of a hero, almost sweeping through everything with his super mechanical warriors and mechanical monster legion. He, along with various allies, suppressed the old-fashioned nobles with extremely iron-fisted and ruthless methods. In just one or two months, the power of all the great lords was revoked and centralized in the hands of the temporary council, completely resolving the issue that the Bonaparte had with the royal authority not extending beyond Lington. After that... well, it's a very cliché plot, Duke Raphael declared himself emperor in Lington."
"Oh."
Su Lun listened, not too surprised.
Although he had little interest in politics, from every angle, Duke Raphael certainly possessed the strength to support his ambition.
If he wanted to be a stable emperor, he surely wouldn't leave behind the kind of mess where lords were everywhere like before.
He then asked, "Wasn't it Duke Raphael who became the emperor? How come it's Yekaterina?"
Qiantiao seemed to find the situation quite theatrical as well, a smile playing on his lips as he said, "Because it was just ten days ago. That is, on the eighth day after Raphael's ascension, this new emperor suddenly died violently in the palace."
At this, Su Lun felt a strong sense of conspiracy overwhelm him, and he said in astonishment, "Died violently?"
Qiantiao's tone also became somewhat somber, "Yes. After the forensic doctor's examination, they found no issues. It was just normal death from overwork, sudden and without any warning. If we're talking mystically, his fate just wasn't suited for being the emperor."
"..."
The more Su Lun heard of these dramatic changes, the more it sounded like a plot from some absurd script.
It was more likely a murder rather than a sudden death.
But the actual truth hardly mattered now.
The important thing was, with Duke Raphael dead, how did Yekaterina become the emperor?
He directly inquired, "Even if Raphael died, why would it be Yekaterina who became the emperor again? What exactly happened in Luying?"
"Indeed. No one expected your fiancée to ascend to the position," Qiantiao said, his eyes narrowing slightly as he added with a hint of admiration, "You'll understand just how astute your wife is once you hear the rest."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun rolled his eyes slightly but perked up his ears to continue listening.
...
Qiantiao continued, "After the disaster in Lington, everyone's attention was on Duke Raphael. No one cared that the Lans family's youngest daughter had gone to the Regadi kingdom in the south. Because... Regadi's first heir, 'William Regadi,' was killed by you, and then it was announced that 'Feck' would become the next heir. But you didn't show up, so as the primary queen, Yekaterina temporarily took over most of the rights of your position as the crown prince..."
Right!
The Regadi family!
As Su Lun heard this, he suddenly realized something.
It was as if he had found a crucial clue that made everything that didn't make sense suddenly seem logical.
Still, it didn't quite feel right.
Merely being married into it wasn't enough.
Qiantiao kept on speaking, "Whatever Miss Yekaterina did in the south these past few months is unknown to the outside world. But one thing that is known is that a month ago, the Regadi family publicly announced that they fully support any decisions she makes. In other words... she now speaks for the Regadi family. Once this news broke, all the major powers in Luying were shocked. After all, prior to this, your wife was only known for her beauty, without showing any political talent."
Su Lun's expression turned slightly odd as he listened.
Having spent some time with Yekaterina, he knew she certainly had the ability.
Yet for her to have taken control of the Regadi family so quickly was still hard to believe.
There was definitely something hidden beneath the surface.
As Qiantiao spoke, something seemed to occur to him, and he paused before adding, "Oh, and another thing... Just over a month after she went to the south, Kelson, the Family Head of the Regadi family, died suddenly. Murder was determined to be the cause. His wife, Lady Portia, colluded with Duke Raphael to use a kind of soul poison, aiming to have William ascend to the throne sooner... The specifics have been disclosed in the newspapers, basically, all that messy private life of nobility and their conspiracies to seize power, quite a dramatic thriller. Lady Portia was also discovered to be a believer in foreign gods and was promptly sent to the gallows."
"Kelson also died violently?"
Upon hearing this, a flicker of confusion crossed Su Lun's eyes.
He had seen this cheap father of the original owner once before in Old Lington, and he indeed knew that the man's days were numbered.
At the time, Su Lun didn't think much of it.
Only now, seeing the outcome, had he marveled at the numerous "coincidences."
People definitely didn't kill Yekaterina.
Previously, Su Lun knew that Duke Raphael had won over young William and his mother. The death of Kelson had to be their doing. After all, the Regadi still had capable people, and the King's death would definitely be thoroughly investigated. Most of what was disclosed in the newspapers should be true.
But now, coincidentally, William was dead, Lady Portia was dead, Kelson was dead, Duke Raphael was also dead...
It was just that coincidental.
The "melon" painstakingly planted by their schemes was not picked by anyone, and had fallen into the hands of Yekaterina, who had just become the queen.
Coincidence?
Clearly, it was not.
Although the House of Lance did not directly participate in these events, they must have played an ignominious role behind the scenes.
Since Su Lun had speculated this before, it was not too surprising.
And now, there was an even greater benefit.
Duke Raphael had made all the preparations to become Emperor.
He waged wars everywhere, eliminated political enemies, and reclaimed the rights of various lords within the Empire.
The troublesome problems were all solved by Raphael, who carried the burden of ill repute, only to suddenly die violently and have the fruits of his labor snatched away.
Others simply assumed that the House of Lance had picked up a huge bargain by chance.
But only those like Su Lun who knew the inside story realized the brilliance of the House of Lance's scheme.
It was simply mind-boggling.
...
Listening to all these "coincidences," Su Lun also understood why Yekaterina could become Emperor in just a few short months.
This was the planning of the House of Lance over several hundred years.
It was also the planning of the House of Raphael over several hundred years.
And the House of Regadi...
It was as if all the good fortune had converged upon one person.
It was not surprising that things went so smoothly.
At this moment, Qian Tiao also gave a summary of the events: "With the full support of the House of Regadi and the consent of the remaining two powerful councilor families, the Houses of Lance and Robci, naturally, there were no voices of opposition. Moreover, coincidentally, those stubborn old nobles who would have opposed them were all cleaned up by Duke Raphael. The remnants of the old-fashioned nobles were even more hopeful for a new emperor rather than the brutal Raphael family, so they naturally supported her. Hence, with support from all sides, three days ago, Yekaterina logically became the Emperor..."
"..."
The logic was sound, but as Su Lun listened, he also spotted something amiss.
Even if the family head Kelson had died violently, and "Fick" was not around, those uncles of his would still have come forward to vie for power.
How did it come to a queen?
Although he vaguely guessed that Yekaterina might have used some means and had plans in place, something crucial still seemed to be missing...
Before Su Lun could think further, Qian Tiao suddenly leaned closer, resting a hand on his shoulder without avoiding the intimacy of their bare skin touching, and teased, "Aren't you curious about how your wife managed to take control of the Regadi family so quickly?"
"Oh?"
Listening to this reference, Su Lun always felt something strange; everyone at dawn knew that the union between "Fick" and Yekaterina was a transaction.
This had nothing to do with him, Su Lun.
But today, Qian Tiao's references to "your wife" didn't seem to be merely teasing.
Indeed, Qian Tiao, with a mischievous look, suddenly dropped a bombshell: "There is reliable news that Yekaterina is pregnant."
What!
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's mind reeled.
Although he had previously guessed this possibility remotely... it shouldn't be! The Regadi were a bunch of decrepit antiques; they were bent on restoring their nation.
So pushing Yekaterina, the queen, to be Emperor did indeed have a certain rationale, but it wasn't enough.
If she was pregnant with the offspring of Regadi, then everything made perfect sense.
The continuation of the Regadi bloodline as rulers was what those old fossils dreamed of.
Given that Yekaterina's claim to the throne had become a fact, then working backward, the news of the pregnancy had to be accurate!
Because the news was accurate,
Therefore,
Su Lun was so astonished!
In this fantastic alchemical world, although there was no such thing as paternity testing, there were a multitude of secret bloodline techniques.
One thing was certain: if Yekaterina was indeed pregnant, then the child must carry the bloodline of Regadi.
Otherwise, those old folks from the Regadi family would definitely not support her.
This made Su Lun very puzzled. Previously in the newlywed residence Rose Manor, he and Yekaterina had indeed gotten along quite happily, even sharing a bed.
But nothing happened.
Could it be...?
No, that can't be right; with her proud nature, even if she did it, she would never dare not to admit it.
For a moment, various thoughts flashed through his mind.
Su Lun suddenly remembered what Yekaterina had said during the marriage parade on the carriage: "I will only get married once in my life, and there will be only one man. So if you hear any news later, don't be too surprised."
"So... was she referring to this news when she said that?"
Su Lun suddenly felt that it was very likely she was referring to this very news.
Well, the news of becoming a father is not surprising?
For the first time, Su Lun felt that his brain wasn't quite up to the task.
If she said that phrase...
So, is it really my doing?
But when did I do it?!
...
Watching Su Lun's expressions change was extremely amusing.
Even Mr. Jing, who was always indifferent, cast a curious glance at him.
Qian Tiao was also very curious, uttering a light "Huh".
Despite the "irrefutable evidence", looking at his expression, it doesn't seem like he did it, yet it somehow seems like he did.
Knowing Su Lun well, Qian Tiao didn't hold back and asked directly: "So... did you actually do it or not?"
Faced with this straightforward question, Su Lun responded with a roll of his eyes.
The key issue is that the gambling-addicted woman had pressed her body against his, her arm sinking into a towering expanse, and the atmosphere between the three of them was bound to be strange.
But since none of them were strangers here, he thought there was nothing to hide and said directly, "I don't know."
Qian Tiao said in surprise, "You don't know?"
Her brow furrowed, initially expecting to hear some juicy gossip, but she didn't expect this kind of response.
Su Lun spread his hands.
Qian Tiao, the spectator craving for gossip, didn't hear what she expected and looked visibly deflated, casually adding, "Could it be somewhere else that you've forgotten about?"
"How could that be possible..."
Su Lun was speechless at this suggestion.
With his enhanced brain development, his memory was not bad; he couldn't forget such an important matter.
He was just about to say it was impossible to forget, but as he began speaking, suddenly—
In his mind, as if a light had flickered, some fragmented images passed by.
Somewhere else?
Right!
Besides a few days at the Rose Manor after the wedding, there was one other intimate encounter between them.
It was at the Emerald Holy Land of the Daru tribe.
That time, he had also drunk the Poet's Honey Wine and got drunk.
Then, when he woke up, Yekaterina, who was "Katyusha" at that time, had already left.
As this thought surfaced, his brain seemed stimulated.
The fragmented memories flooded into his mind like a slide show, albeit not very clear, but they were all amorous scenes.
In an instant, Su Lun's eyes shone with a strange emotion.
From his memories, in the drunken bliss at the treehouse, apart from Yuta, there was another person!
Su Lun finally remembered why he had been bitten. (Chapter 260)
Because... he really did sleep with her!
Remembering this fragment of memory, Su Lun then recalled what happened at the Rose Manor after the wedding; no wonder Yekaterina said those words.
"Tonight is our wedding night; do you want to exercise your rights as a husband?"
"No, I am me, Fick is Fick."
"My proposal just now was only meant to make you feel less shortchanged when you hear certain news in the future."
So that's what she meant?
Su Lun finally understood.
Yekaterina had informed him early on.
It was just that he didn't recall it at the time, which is why he was so bewildered now.
Despite the discrepancy in timing, for alchemists, this was not an issue at all.
...
Seeing Su Lun's expression turn very odd, both Qian Tiao and Mr. Jing cast curious glances his way.
Qian Tiao's eyes suddenly rekindled with the fire of gossip and said, "Did you remember something?"
Su Lun revealed a wry smile, not sure how to respond outright, "I'll ask her when I see her in the future."
Hearing this tacit admission, Qian Tiao clicked her tongue, "That lady's scheme is genuinely intricate."
Su Lun listened and noncommittally raised his brow.
If it were Yekaterina, he could see the elements of a political transaction.
But with Katya, it felt more like he had taken advantage of the girl.
Compared to politics, Qian Tiao obviously cared more about gossip.
Upon hearing Su Lun indirectly confirm an intimate relationship with the new Empress, she pursued eagerly, "Hey, hey, hey, come on, tell us... what's really going on?"
"..."
Su Lun's forehead creased with exasperation, how could he possibly go into details over such a matter?
Though he didn't mind telling Qian Tiao, there was also his senior sister to consider.
Mr. Jing also recognized Su Lun's predicament and interjected surprisingly, "When I was talking to Master Pierre earlier, that young lady from the Luns family was in presence. Your fiancée is indeed a gifted strategist. Now, it's not just the Regadi family from the south, but even the small border kingdoms from the northern continent have declared joining the Luying Empire. She's truly achieved the unification of north and south, something even the Bona Royal Family never dreamed of. With direct control of the 'Intelligence Department,' her grip on Luying's political power is perhaps the strongest in centuries."
Su Lun nodded in acknowledgment, grateful his senior sister had helped change the subject, "Mm."
This was also Yekaterina's brilliance.
A series of "coincidences," and everything seemed to fall into place.
She had amassed a considerable concentration of power.
Mr. Jing couldn't hide his admiration in his tone, continuing, "What's more remarkable is this. She has gathered all this power, yet doesn't aspire to restore the old age's dictatorship like Duke Raphael does. As soon as she became the Empress, she introduced a series of new laws, following new political methods. She opened the Alchemy Academy, financially supporting the establishment of new basic academies everywhere, giving everyone the chance to study alchemy; she also introduced Mafa's labor machinery technology, liberating the workforce. With such measures, a great development era for alchemy civilization is inevitable..."
Understanding these initiatives, Su Lun realized why his senior sister praised Yekaterina so highly.
Because promoting the development of alchemy civilization was precisely what Dawn was doing.
Mr. Jing added, "Furthermore, following her ascension, Yekaterina proactively signed a permanent armistice alliance with the Mafa military, to jointly resist planar invasions. She's opened all military fortresses previously established due to war between the two empires, exposing Luying's heartland to Mafa, binding their fates together. Such courage is rare among emperors."
Upon hearing this, Qian Tiao seemed pensive.
Su Lun listened along.
Finally, Mr. Jing mentioned another piece of news: "Oh, and one more thing. Yekaterina, through Sabina, has sent word that the ancient Gusmao flying ship you were promised is ready and can be delivered at any time."
"Mm."
Su Lun nodded again.
Now that he had the flying ship, he needed to find a group of mechanics for modification.
He thought of Colonel Dora.
...
"The planar gate was discovered too late. A rough estimate suggests that several hundred thousand mages from different planes have infiltrated the alchemy plane. Moreover, several Rank 9 magic towers have already been constructed near the planar gate, making it difficult to breach. The Mafa military is also struggling in their assault..."
"Intelligence indicates that pirates under the 'King of the Western Sea' and the 'King of the South Sea' have been recruited or coerced by some mysterious people to venture to the Far Western Seas in search of treasure. The number of mages accompanying the ships is unknown..."
"..."
The three of them continued to soak in the hot spring pool.
After discussing current affairs, Su Lun also recounted his experiences from the past few days, including everything about the God's Tomb, the Ten Thousand Mage Group information, the Holy Church's army, leaving no detail unspoken.
Qian Tiao listened with boredom, while Mr. Jing was meticulous.
Su Lun had no immediate plans for the planar gate area; without needing to think about it, he knew it would be extremely bloody.
His current strength was not suitable for joining such a large-scale battle.
Conversely, disrupting the deities of the divine realm in their treasure-hunting plans was more appropriate.
And it would be an opportunity to enhance his own strength.
Su Lun said, "The deities of the divine realm are searching for the 'Mimir's Spring,' and I suspect it's connected to their 'Omniscient Revelation' talent, so we absolutely can't let them find it. So, once I've recruited some mechanics in Mafa's imperial capital Cabitron, I'll head over to Dragon Country to check things out."
Mr. Jing, hearing his plan, agreed, "Mm. It's good for you to investigate. Now with your exceptional spatial ability, the risks will be greatly reduced. I've also gathered some intelligence. It is rumored that Pirate King Black Sam ventured to that region with another goal of finding cosmic essence to advance to Rank 9. That area is rarely traveled, so there might truly be 'cosmic essence'. Both you and Odilia have the excellent talent to reach the threshold of Rank 9. If you can find cosmic essence, it's good to prepare in advance. Oh, one more thing, I've taken a thorough look at the alchemy manuscript my father left, and 'Isaac's Dragon-marked Golden Body,' if infused, will help you greatly endure the backlash from heavenly tribulations after advancing to Rank 8..."
"..."
Su Lun nodded.
This was also part of his plan.
Dawn's current combat configuration was already strong, sufficient to handle most crises. Additionally, there were mechanical warriors like Number 19 who could withstand dragons, dragon-slaying daggers, dragon-slaying armor, and dragon-slaying potions. Dragon Island was certainly within reach.
There was no need to aim too high; dealing with Rank 7 dragons shouldn't be too difficult.
If he could hunt down a few, creating a 'prosthetic' like 'Isaac's Dragon-marked Golden Body' would significantly enhance combat capabilities.
He then asked, "What about you, Senior Sister?"
Mr. Jing responded, "The Mage Corps' assault is fierce; I'll be near the planar gate, aiming to eliminate high-level individuals from different planes. Moreover, the laws of the area are the most refined, which is hugely beneficial for my advancement to Rank 9. If you encounter any dangers, you can inform me..."
Soaking in the pool, snowflakes began to drift down from the sky.
The three of them lazily lay in the hot spring.
With a cool breeze and warm waters, it was a rare moment of tranquility.

chapters.title: Chapter 518 - 517: Library Ghost
chapters.content:
After soaking in the hot springs and washing away the dust, Su Lun and Mr. Jing returned to the Monster Beast Forest.
Negotiations were ultimately better handled by his senior sister, especially since she was the Dawn Leader.
She met with the Dwarf King, Beo, discussed some pros and cons and the future of civilization, and without much hesitation, the Mountain Dwarves agreed to renew the alliance.
However, the dwarves agreed to ally with the Dawn Alliance only and did not trust other humans.
Luckily, Su Lun's small void realm was recently vast enough to temporarily accommodate them.
Apart from lacking mines to dig, everything else was quite satisfactory.
The peace-loving dwarves hammered and forged in the small void realm, continuing their secluded way of life from before.
Of course, they also helped Su Lun forge some gargoyles.
As for the countless treasures accumulated by the dwarves over the years, they were also temporarily stored in Su Lun's small void realm.
Various ores, treasures, forging tools, magical equipment, even a forge as big as a mountain was moved in.
It wasn't all Su Lun's now, but he could borrow them if he really needed to.
He also felt quite pleased, as the void realm became lively.
...
The dwarves had too much stuff to move, taking two full days to pack up.
Qian went to the seaside, gathering the Dawn group to prepare ample supplies for an adventure on Dragon Island; Mr. Jing returned to the planar passage near Zambra Ironfall Province.
On the third day, Su Lun instantly teleported back to Kabitrond, the capital of Mafa.
Initially, Su Lun planned to ask Miss Dora about the alchemy manuscript and intended to buy some large machinery workshops and recruit some mechanics.
But upon inquiry, he learned that Miss Dora was also on the front lines and wouldn't be back for another two days.
Without other acquaintances in Mafa, buying large equipment and recruiting mechanics would be much more straightforward with a familiar introduction, sparing much trouble.
Moreover, it wasn't just about lacking acquaintances; both identities as "Reaper" and "Feck" were major wanted criminals of the Mafa royal family.
Being too conspicuous was generally not good.
He mingled in various material markets with Number Nineteen, purchasing some scarce materials.
Kabitrond was the city of mechanics, with an immense array of materials. Almost every district had a large machinery market, the scale of which was hundreds to thousands of times larger than Ruying. As long as one could afford it, almost all materials could be purchased.
After a few days, Miss Dora finally sent a message that she would soon return to the capital.
...
That day, Su Lun and Number Nineteen were strolling around the Mafa Royal Mechanical Academy.
They had arranged to meet with Miss Dora there.
The two walked around the campus, which was also bustling.
Because of the planar war, the students were all spirited and enthusiastic. Previously, some peace-loving mechanics from Mafa were unwilling to fight with Ruying, but with the planar invasion, almost everyone was mobilized. Recruitment slogans and parades urging alumni to join the front lines were visible everywhere.
Unlike the students of the Ruying Royal Academy, who were either wealthy or noble, the mechanics here showed no signs of wealth or poverty, but their eyes all held a gleam of interest in mechanical alchemy.
The campus had a long, shaded boulevard lined with giant steel sculptures.
The statues in Ruying invariably honored some "great" noble lord.
In the Mafa campus, however, the statues were all of top-tier mechanics.
Underneath the statues were engravings of those mechanics' lifetimes and significant patent inventions.
Walking down this path, Su Lun felt quite moved.
No wonder Mafa had become so powerful in just over a hundred years since focusing on mechanics. In contrast, Ruying really was thoroughly decadent. Who knows how it would fare under Yekaterina's radical reforms...
As they walked, Number Nineteen introduced various aspects of the Mechanical Academy.
She had been staying here for years.
Suddenly thinking of something, she casually asked, "Su Lun, do you have a disciple at the Royal Mechanical Academy?"
Su Lun nodded, "Yes. Jike is a genius demolitions expert. Since he couldn't learn and grow in Ruying, I sent him to Mafa."
He hadn't planned to disturb his disciple's studies or let anyone know that Jike was his disciple.
However, upon hearing this, Number Nineteen's expression changed slightly, "Jike James? The genius freshman from the ammunition department?"
Surprised, Su Lun responded, "You've heard of him?"
"Of course," Number Nineteen recalled, her expression somewhat wistful. "Whenever a genius mechanic appears in the academy, they are treated like a star. When I was studying ammunition, I heard about a very talented new student who, within just a few months, had made quite a few astonishing explosives. Of course, his most famous incident was when he invented a special explosive that blew up the academy's bomb-proof laboratory... and then the whole school knew about this newcomer."
Listining, Su Lun chuckled.
Back in Ruying, Jike had blown up a few laboratories and was considered an oddity.
In Mafa, however, he had become a star student.
As the two talked and walked, they soon arrived at the Mafa Library.
This was a massive building; its ground part was made entirely of steel frames and glass, shining brilliantly under the sun and looking very beautiful.
The library had an excellent academic atmosphere, with many students borrowing books.
Almost every corner of the bookshelves was packed with people.
Su Lun and his companion walked in and sat in an inconspicuous spot, casually chatting while waiting for Dora.
Number 19 continued, "The academy library was established by Lucien Pepys Grandmaster. After he founded the 'Mechanic Alchemy Guild', he devoted the remainder of his life to establishing the Royal Academy. The library was his life's work. Thus, for a century, there has been a legend that studying in the library might occasionally bring one face to face with Lucien's spiritual blessing, enlightening them..."
Su Lun: "Spiritual blessing?"
Number 19 explained, "Yes. It's said that more than one person has experienced it. Many now-successful mechanics from Mafa Country, who studied at the academy in their youth, have had such experiences. The students all say it's a library blessed by the predecessors of mechanics, and only the top genius students will receive the 'Library Ghost's Blessing'... Of course, because of this legend, many attention-seekers claim to have been blessed."
"Oh?"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun took it seriously.
For magicians, there is always a reason behind everything that appears.
This seemingly inexplicable "Spiritual Blessing," if real, must have a cause.
Moreover, by chance, he himself was an expert in the spiritual realm.
He held a black umbrella in his hand and slightly sensed his surroundings, but he didn't detect any spiritual fluctuations.
However, the structure of the library was indeed quite complex.
Apart from the vast surface building, there were spaces hundreds of meters underground where some of the academy's laboratories were located.
...
The two did not wait long when a casually dressed young woman appeared at the library's entrance.
Although her appearance had changed, Su Lun recognized her at first glance as the hostage lady.
Miss Dora also saw Su Lun and walked straight toward him.
Su Lun did not pretend not to recognize her and greeted her, "Colonel Dora, long time no see."
Miss Dora, however, seemed to carry a hint of anger, all business, "Thank you for the information you provided. On behalf of the Mafa military, I extend the highest respect to you."
Su Lun, slightly startled, thought their acquaintance wasn't that distant, "Please, have a seat."
After inviting her to sit, he sensed something and directly inquired, "Colonel Dora, I hope I haven't caused you any trouble, have I?"
Dora didn't want to say it, but seeing this irritating guy pretending to be innocent, she couldn't help but coldly say, "Your tactics are quite cunning. Now that your wife has become the Ruying Emperor, voices immediately emerged within Mafa Country calling for us to set aside our hatred and unite against the external foe, with some even suggesting welcoming the Lei family back to the country... I think, although it's correct to employ such political tactics, with the dimensional invasion as our current priority, can we lessen these political maneuvers and unite?"
"???"
Su Lun, only upon hearing this, understood why the hostage lady was so angry.
It turned out she was blaming him for Catharina's ascension to the throne.
Previously, Su Lun had realized Catharina's choice of the Lei family as a stepping stone was not just about internal influences in Ruying.
The Lei family was quite special, being Mafa's old imperial family.
The two great empires of Mafa and Ruying had been at war for hundreds of years, with reconciliation between the authorities on both sides absolutely impossible. Even if the authorities wished it, the families of fallen soldiers would definitely not.
Having such an ancient imperial family mediate was very tricky indeed.
With a member of an old Mafa imperial family becoming the Ruying Emperor, the people of Mafa Country could emotionally accept their own emperor.
From this, it appeared Catharina's plan from the outset was to unify the two great empires.
However... the current situation with the dimensional invasion was peculiar.
Her plans were made before the invasion, which doesn't imply it was her idea.
It might also be the old folks of the Lei family who were anxious to reclaim their country.
After all, they haven't been idle for the past one or two hundred years and still had many "remnants of the old era" in Mafa Country.
Now that there was hope, they naturally wanted to make big moves.
But all of these were just speculations.
What the facts were had nothing to do with him.
Su Lun chuckled and defended himself, "Believe it or not, this has nothing to do with me. I have no interest in politics. Besides, I am Dawn Su Lun, Lei's 'Feck' will never appear again."
"..."
Miss Dora frowned as she listened.
Hearing this, she scrutinized Su Lun carefully with an evaluative look as if confirming he wasn't lying; the anger in her brows slightly faded.
But she still complained, "Running into you never brings anything good..."
Su Lun didn't mind, as the aftereffects of the kidnapping hadn't completely faded yet.
He directly changed the subject, asking, "How is the frontline?"
Miss Dora's expression had returned to normal, responding, "The battle is very fierce. But for now, it's under control. However, it's impossible to fully resolve the issue. We haven't yet found a way to break through the defense barriers set by the ninth-level magic towers. Moreover, as time passes, the dimensional portals become more stable, and the enemy's top mages will also arrive..."
As she spoke, the look of worry did not leave her face.
Su Lun was aware of this situation, and indeed, it was not optimistic.
After all, the divine dimensional planes were incomparably higher in terms of combat capabilities than the broken alchemical dimension, even possessing overwhelming power.
At present, there seemed to be no solution to stop it.
Even Mr. Jing, after calculating, found that only when the people of the alchemical dimension were qualified to leave the dimension, could there be hope of finding a solution.
"But thank you also to your organization for the military support provided. Especially Mr. Jing, the military department is also hoping to cooperate with your Dawn..."
Speaking of the war, fatigue showed on Miss Dora's face again.
She did not dwell further on this gloomy topic, but instead said, "Just forget about that manuscript of Isaac for now. After your wife became the emperor... Recently, all sorts of remnants from the old era have surfaced, and His Majesty the Emperor now doubts your motives. Even if I'm willing to believe you, it's not possible to obtain it anytime soon."
"Mm."
Su Lun heard these words, but his expression didn't change.
At the moment, he intended to take a trip to Dragon Island, and getting the notebook from the hands of the Mafa royal wasn't too urgent.
He thought for a moment and then said, "Another thing is, I need some mechanics to help me make some parts for the Mechanical Castle."
Miss Dora remembered that the two of them had discussed this matter verbally before, so she directly asked, "Where are the blueprints?"
Su Lun took out part of the blueprint of "Sky Combat Castle."
Miss Dora's attention was instantly captivated by the exquisite design on the blueprints, having the eye of a mechanic Grandmaster, she recognized them after a moment and exclaimed, "The ancient Gusmao airship blueprints of Ruying? You actually have these things?!"
Speaking, she suddenly seemed to recall something, and pursed her lips to correct herself, "Oh, I almost forgot. The Empress of Ruying is your wife."
Su Lun also felt somewhat helpless listening to this; the airship was indeed given by Yekaterina, but these blueprints were his own.
He didn't explain much, only asking, "Can these parts for the Mechanical Castle be manufactured by Mafa at the moment?"
Although he had the "Goblin Sky Combat Castle's Energy Core" in his hand, Ruying's mechanical technology could not possibly reproduce the high-pressure steam boilers described in the blueprints for sky castles.
Miss Dora didn't rush to answer; she carefully looked at several blueprints before saying, "The vast majority would be no problem."
After she finished viewing the blueprints, her eyes shifted slightly, as if she thought of something else, and she looked back at Su Lun, "These blueprints should be of an ancient goblin mechanical castle... I'm not wrong, Ruying's Gusmao airships were based on these blueprints. But to drive such a large mechanical castle in the sky, it requires tremendous power which current technology simply cannot support... that's why Ruying only managed to produce some crude airships."
Speaking, she looked at Su Lun, seemingly guessing that he had the crucial energy core in his possession.
But she deliberately didn't mention it.
How clever!
Su Lun also discerned her ideas from her expression.
Mr. Hei had previously asserted that this Miss Dora was extremely intelligent, and aside from her relatively young age and inexperience, she would certainly be able to stand at the apex of the world in the future.
After pondering for a moment, Miss Dora then said, "Could you sell these blueprints to me? Any terms can be negotiated."
As she said this, she realized her words might seem too abrupt, and quickly explained, "What I mean is, even if we can't build a Sky Combat Castle, we can still convert the blueprints for land use, or even for sea mechanical castles! This would be a great weapon against those invaders from other planes."
Su Lun wasn't too surprised to hear this and responded, "That's possible! But I have only one condition, these blueprints must not be used in the wars between Mafa and Ruying Empires. If you can make that decision, I can trade the blueprints with you."
"..."
Hearing this, Miss Dora instantly fell silent.
She couldn't guarantee that.
Even the military couldn't guarantee that.
The situation in a large empire is very complex; even the Great Marshal of the Moise family couldn't decide that.
Even though Mafa has no traditional nobility, its internal situation is not much better than Ruying's.
