Looking again, Su Lun and Number Nineteen had a calm demeanor.
Kit's expression was slightly odd.
However, just when everyone thought "King of the Western Sea" Morlock would attack first, an eerie scene unfolded before their eyes suddenly.
In their field of vision, a figure moved as if teleporting through the void, leaving a streak of afterimages.
On closer look, it was a blonde mage with an indifferent expression, holding a magic wand.
The others might have sensed the newcomer's strength, but the seventh-tier professionals aboard the Eternal Night sensed that deadly threat!
Barrett's brows furrowed slightly as he let out a soft "Eh?": "Spatial Displacement? No, that's not right, there is no spatial fluctuation..."
The members of the dawn group, somewhat knowledgeable in Spatial Techniques, all changed colors as they watched.
Number Nineteen said indifferently, "It's 'Time Powers.' That person is from the Saint Church Army."
Only she and Su Lun had seen this technique, so they recognized it at a glance.
Moreover, members of the Saint Church Army were easily recognizable by their black and white clergy-like robes.
Hearing Number Nineteen's words, everyone on alert together.
If it was someone Su Lun had warned to be careful of, they were definitely not simple.
And just this "Time Displacement" alone was already an incomprehensible technique.
This was perhaps even more of a concern than the eighth-tier Morlock.
But no one noticed that Su Lun's expression when he again looked at that person had a slight oddness to it.
...
A few nautical miles passed in the blink of an eye.
The blonde mage in the black and white nun's attire appeared directly on the deck of the Eternal Night.
She looked at everyone with indifference and arrogance, as if these people were utterly beneath her notice.
Indeed, with the ability of "time reversal," no one here could kill her.
However, just as this woman hadn't yet had the chance to show off,
Su Lun suddenly teleported in front of her, piercing through the magic shield formed by the power of time and grabbed her throat.
The woman reacted extremely quickly, her magic wand shimmering as if she had cast some spell.
Qiantiao and the others felt a moment of disorientation, although they didn't understand what had happened, but they realized the magic was definitely far from simple!
Everyone's expressions changed dramatically!
Yet, a bizarre scene ensued.
Everyone thought that with Su Lun's move, there should have been an intense battle.
However, a crisp "crack" sound of breaking bone echoed across the deck.
In the completely baffled eyes of all present, Su Lun easily broke the neck of that member of the Saint Church Army... just like that?
On a closer look, the expression of disbelief on the blonde woman's face had frozen, her head slumped and she was clearly lifeless.
Dead?
Really dead?
Everyone, just about to take action, froze in place, disbelief filling their gaze.
In an instant, the atmosphere turned eerily silent.
"Caw..."
"Caw..."
Crows cawed from the mast, finally dragging everyone's thoughts back to reality.
Su Lun was holding the woman's corpse in his hand, swaying in the breeze.
Seeing it once before was astonishing.
Now seeing it... it seemed, ordinary perhaps?
The "Urobolos Space-Time Ring" immunizes against time-space techniques not higher than the artifact itself, a natural counter to the one before him.
Therefore, the "time reversal" just now had no effect whatsoever.
And after immunizing against the power of time, this blonde woman's physical strength was far too weak for Su Lun.
Naturally, he strangled her to death with ease.
No one spoke, all was quiet.
Finally, the tense Lelota loosened the grip on the knife handle that was nearly imprinted and weakly said, "Teacher, didn't Mr. Su Lun say that the 'Saint Church Army' is supposed to be powerful... How... How come they don't seem very powerful?"
Not just her, almost all professionals below seventh-tier couldn't comprehend what had just transpired.
An individual clearly from the Saint Church Army crossed the void in a flashy manner.
Then... just delivered a free kill?
That's not right—they shouldn't be this weak, right?
Something didn't sit right with everyone.
Qiantiao's eyes flashed with a sharp light and profoundly said, "It's not that person's weakness, but rather that Su Lun is stronger than her and just happened to have a counter. If it wasn't for Su Lun restraining that person's time domain, you would all be dead."
Upon hearing this, everyone was shocked: "Ah?"
They hadn't realized that beneath that theatrical scene, a deadly crisis had been lurking.
As the dawn crew heard this explanation, they all blurted out in unison, "Holy shit."
...
Not just the crew at dawn, but the pirates watching from afar were also baffled.
The "King of the Western Sea" Morlock, still charging through the sea, stared at the corpse in Su Lun's hand, utterly dumbstruck: The great personage of the Saint Church Army, dead?

chapters.title: Chapter 525 - 525: 524 Annihilate Pursuers
chapters.content:
The golden-haired nun's corpse was clamped in Su Lun's hand, suspended in midair and swaying slightly.
From the moment this fellow arrogantly appeared on the deck to becoming a corpse, it seemed to have happened in the blink of an eye.
The members of the Dawn Group went from gaping in shock to being utterly astonished.
Although they didn't understand, they had now realized that it definitely wasn't because the enemy was weak.
It was because Su Lun was too strong!
Barrett, Wuzz Huzzo, and the other seventh-tier members came to their senses and belatedly realized the grievous danger hidden in that dramatic scene, as cold sweat faintly seeped from their foreheads.
This was the first time they had witnessed the legendary "power of time" and had barely skirted the edge of death.
This special high-level rule was almost entirely free from any form of restraint, and even they didn't understand it, let alone have any chance of defeating it.
Such an enigmatic enemy, coupled with Morlock, the "King of the Western Sea," would have indeed posed a threat of annihilation to the Dawn Group.
Alas, they had Su Lun on board.
As soon as they were about to face off, the person was killed, and the crisis hadn't even erupted before it had been averted.
Not far away, Morlock on the sea surface was momentarily stunned, but he roared as he continued the charge.
Su Lun harvested the soul of the corpse, didn't elaborate much, and only said indifferently, "Prepare for battle."
The members of the Dawn Group all had solemn expressions and instantly went into combat mode.
The sound of a "clang" from a drawn sword rang beside their ears, and upon looking again, Qiantiao's fighting spirit had already reached its peak, unsheathing his sword and vanishing on the deck.
Morlock had the nickname of "Eighth-Tier Gatekeeper" in the Bounty Hunters' Guild, and Qiantiao naturally wanted to test his might.
There were already few enemies within the same tier that could pressure her, and this eighth-tier was just right!
Alone, her chances of winning weren't great, so Barrett also let out a light shout and leapt off without any hesitation.
Behind Wuzz Huzzo, his bat wings vibrated, leaving behind an afterimage on the spot.
The three top combatants of the Dawn Group rushed towards Morlock, who was bearing down on them from the sea, and in the blink of an eye, they were locked in battle.
Huge waves erupted instantly on the sea surface, with shockwaves rolling higher and higher.
...
Top professionals in combat were not something ordinary people could meddle in, but there were still more than twenty pirate ships eyeing them covetously.
The members of the Dawn Group sharpened their knives eagerly as the ship, Eternal Night, shifted its sails. Tanni, the helmsman, maneuvered the vast ship to glide out a perfect arc over the several dozen meters high waves, immediately changing course like surfing, and charged towards those more than twenty pirate ships.
Even when the ships were still a great distance apart, the cannons had already spit out tongues of flame.
For a moment, the cannons roared.
The Dawn Group, outnumbered one to twenty, showed no signs of weakness, darting into the midst of wolves like a fierce tiger.
The opposing sides collided head-on, initiating a heated sea battle.
But the gap in cannon technology was too great, and the pirate ships were completely suppressed by the Dawn Group.
The battle started, and they were immediately at a disadvantage.
After two rounds of cannon fire, five or six pirate ships were severely damaged.
But the enemy's confidence was clearly not in their cannons. The moment the bombardment began, magical shields lit up on four or five of those pirate ships.
Su Lun was quite familiar with this setup. It was a five-hundred-person Mage group.
Rough estimates suggested there might be two to three thousand Mages in all.
As soon as the battle began, these Mages also started chanting legion magic, "Great Tsunami Art," "Great Gale Force Spell," "Great Thundering Spell"...
The sea surface was instantaneously filled with lightning and thunder, with the surging magic elements exaggerated like they were about to boil over.
The combat power of legion Mages was not to be underestimated, a five-hundred-person Mage group could cast legion magic capable of threatening the lives of eighth-tier professionals.
Windstorms, in conjunction with tsunamis, caused even ships of the Eternal Night's tonnage to sway as if they were mere paper, seemingly about to be overturned and sunk at any moment. The sky was flickering with thunderclouds, and the thunder magic was fully charged, promising to cause widespread casualties once it struck down.
Su Lun wasn't about to watch these fellows deliver a heavy blow to the Dawn Group.
Dispersing them was the best choice!
In that instant, he teleported over, appearing directly on a pirate ship.
The group of Mages wasn't completely unprepared.
When a stranger appeared on the ship, the air among the crowd suddenly became sticky. This was a compound control type magic, "Anti-Magic Air Swamp."
The air turned glue-like, firmly sticking Su Lun to the deck. The surrounding elements were isolated, restricting spellcasting. The space was compressed, making teleportation away a hundred times more difficult than coming.
This double-control magic combining physical and magical aspects could instantly kill most seventh-tier professionals.
But today's Su Lun was well-versed in dealing with Mage legions, and how could he not have anticipated such a scenario?
A glint flashed in his eyes, and as soon as he touched the ground, the spell was complete. He uttered a single command, "Domain: Living Forbidden Zone!"
In an instant, an air of terror swept over the entire ship.
Su Lun himself made no movements, but the layer of pitch-black luster on the surface of his body spread out rapidly.
The warship wasn't large, and in a blink of an eye, it was completely engulfed.
In a split second, everyone on the pirate ship felt a strange force draining their lives away. Their breaths surged uncontrollably, and the magic they were gathering in their hands was interrupted.
"Not good!"
The crowd was shocked and their complexions turned pale, but it was already too late for any sort of reaction.
The lower the mage's rank, the more they felt as if their bodies were like punctured balloons, with their vigor and life rapidly escaping.
In just a moment, those mages who had originally planned to subdue Su Lun and strike him down helplessly watched as liver spots appeared on their skin. Those spots rapidly grew larger, then merged together. Eventually, all their skin quickly darkened and decayed, emitting a stench of putrefaction.
The low-ranking mages were utterly powerless to stop this life-draining effect, their eyes filled only with shock and desperation, and they lost their lives in the blink of an eye.
A few sixth-tier mages and those two seventh-tier squad leaders, with three to four tenths of their life force drained, still had the strength to fight back. They cast their fire rings in reverse and rapidly retreated, jumping out of the eerie domain's range.
[Living Forbidden Zone] is a domain of death condensed from various laws. Without the capacity to resist its negative aura, the enemy doesn't even qualify to confront him.
This is why being ranked seventh-tier is the watershed that identifies top-tier professionals!
It was just three breaths' time since Su Lun teleported over, and on the vast pirate ship, only he stood alone.
The sea wind howled, and the giant waves never ceased.
With corpses strewn about his feet in disarray, Su Lun stood there expressionlessly, immovable as a mountain.
Behind him, the deathly shadow loomed with black vapors billowing as if it indeed had come from hell to harvest lives. In his indifferent demeanor, there was a complete dispassion towards his enemies.
This scene was witnessed by everyone on the battlefield.
When the magic shield of the pirate ship suddenly vanished, the people on the other nearby pirate ships also looked over, just in time to witness this scene, and were stunned with horror.
Killed six to seven hundred people without a sound?
Even the battle where a thousand seventh-tier mages ganged up to fight the 'King of the Western Sea,' Morlock Poppen, wasn't as chilling to the core.
Fear comes from the unknown.
At this moment, Su Lun, shrouded by the black domain, seemed to everyone not so much a human, but an indescribable "Great Terror."
This eerie spectacle didn't just terrify the pirate side; even the people on the Eternal Night gazing from afar were dumbstruck!
If the other members of the Dawn group had hardly understood how Su Lun had killed that sacred army nun earlier,
now, they understood.
One person... killed everyone on a ship in an instant?
Such a terrifying domain!
Such formidable combat strength!
On the deck of the Eternal Night, Lolo Ta, Tanni, Dora... everyone was absolutely astounded.
Mr. Su Lun is actually this strong?!
Kit let out an astonished cry, "Damn, what kind of domain is this? Why is it so bizarre?!"
He'd been rescued by Su Lun and had seen some of his methods, thinking he himself had already greatly overestimated Su Lun. He had assumed that Su Lun's strength might be on par with the "Top Ten Legendary Hunters."
But now with this move, he realized that Su Lun's prowess was beyond his wildest imagination.
That was a magical team of five hundred people... just killed like that?
Is this really only seventh-tier power?
While shocked, Kit was also filled with excitement.
Everyone from the Dawn group was also excitedly howling, their spirits high!
...
With an indifferent expression, Su Lun entered battle mode, his mind solely focused on how to end the fight quickly.
After he had killed the people on that one ship, the mages on the other ships simultaneously launched their instant-cast spells at him.
With a "crack," a lightning bolt as thick as a water barrel came crashing down, reducing both man and ship to dust in the attack.
A hundred meters away, the figure of Su Lun appeared once more.
Once again, numerous bolts of lightning struck forth, and he dodged again.
His now[Teleport]had virtually no casting delay, as fluid as breathing. While lightning spells were fast, as long as he was cautious, they were unlikely to trouble him.
However, Su Lun didn't attempt to teleport to the other remaining magical team's ships.
The Legion Mages were already on guard, going there again had a certain risk.
Su Lun didn't give those guys any chance.
With a single tug of his hand, shadows that moved extremely quickly passed beneath the water.
"There's something in the water!"
The pirates on those ships also noticed something, but it was too late.
Suddenly, a harsh "crack" "crack" of splintering wood could be heard by their ears.
Like a fountain erupting, tentacles of mechanical octopi instantly burst through the decks of several pirate ships.
The Legion's magical shields weren't meant to encompass entire ships, only the parts above water, to ward off cannon attacks.
And mechanical octopi were the best at breaching ships, a type of mechanical beasts those Mages had never seen.
Their powerful suckers could firmly attach to the hull, and with various ship-breaking tools on their mechanical arms, even armored ships could be easily breached. Let alone wooden warships?
Even elite warships with enchanted plating couldn't last long, they were quickly torn into pieces.
And these weren't the usual octopi with just a few meters-long tentacles, but gigantic octopi where each tentacle was dozens of meters long!
Ever since capturing that "Northern Sea Leviathan: Kraken" last time, Dr. Banks had cultivated a large batch of enlarged octopi. After the battle in the mines of Gold Digger Island, Su Lun had emptied the secret mechabeast research base of Duke Rafael. He had enough materials, equipment, and technicians to make plenty of large mechanical octopi.
Naval battle?
With these large mechanical octopi, even without the Eternal Night, those enemies didn't qualify for a naval battle in Su Lun's eyes.
Now, he had practically filled all the gaps in the Legion's combat capabilities.
Just while turning around, Su Lun's mechanical octopus legion, with hundreds of octopi, had already clung to those dozen-plus pirate ships. The sound of wood splintering was incessant, countless mechanical tentacles sprouted from the pirate ships.
The Magical Squad was not weak; they bombarded with all sorts of magic, killing some of the mechanical octopi.
But Su Lun had a large number of replacements at his disposal, able to sustain such combat losses.
With the Eternal Night providing accurate distant cannon fire, it didn't take many rounds before the ships that had escaped far away were also all sunk.
Once the ships were destroyed, the formations of the several five-hundred-member Mage groups were scattered, and the water surface for miles around was covered with floating Mages and pirates who had fallen overboard.
What followed was close combat.
In the sky, a giant cross appeared, with countless transparent threads dangling down.
Su Lun didn't unleash the full force of his puppet legion to kill the enemy, as these shipless foes no longer posed much of a threat. After dispersing several magical formations, he left the rest to the members of the Dawn Squad.
He had more important things to do.
Su Lun turned his attention to Qian Tiao and the others who were fighting fiercely.
He didn't want to miss the opportunity to fight against eighth-tier professionals directly.
King of the Western Sea Morlock, although called an Eighth-Tier Gatekeeper, was truly of the eighth order.
An eighth-tier Alchemist reaches the "Overlord Body Realm," which is a super-strong state of overpowering and dominating with an invincible physique, where normal attacks come with critical hits!
Moreover, Morlock himself was a "B-026 Stone Giant" with second phase innate talent; his attacks weren't strong among the eighth-order, but he was very hard to kill.
This realm's comprehension of elemental law brought a pressure as sharp as a knife, another level entirely.
Su Lun and Qian Tiao were both exceptional seventh-tier individuals, with such an opponent hard to come by.
There was also "Duke of Blood" Huazhuasi, the centuries-old vampire, who required the enlightenment of advancing to eighth-tier.
And so, several seventh-tier members of the Dawn Squad surrounded Morlock and gave him a beating.
Although they encountered many dangerous situations, once they held on, death was the only outcome left for Morlock.
...
Throughout the battle, Number 19 did not show herself or join in.
Su Lun didn't feel there was a need for her to join the fight.
It's best to keep one's trump card hidden.
Finally, after the Dawn Squad had almost wiped out everyone on the sea surface, Su Lun's battle also neared its end.
With the ships destroyed and multiple instances of teleportation making escape impossible, Morlock, outnumbered, was slain on the spot.
The Pirate King who once dominated the Western Sea ultimately died in this unknown part of the Far West Sea.
"You have stripped the soul of 'Morlock Poppen' "
"You have obtained a vast amount of 'Eighth Order Earth Elemental Law Fragments,' 'Eighth Order Strength Law Fragments'"
"You have gained some insight into the 'Overlord Body Realm'"
"You have learned some secrets about the West Sea Fleet..."
"Spiritual power+..."
Su Lun harvested the soul of this eighth-tier professional, reaping a bountiful harvest.
The members of the Dawn Patrol busied themselves salvaging the spoils of war from the sea.
The outcome of war was such that as long as you won, you were bound to make a huge profit.
This wave alone had swallowed up more than twenty ships and several thousand mages, marking another great harvest.
As the battle area had been selected deliberately, the water wasn't too deep. The mechanical octopuses that were killed were recollected and sent back to the War Workshop to be reforged.
The Dawn Patrol could almost say, with minimal battle damage, they had gained immense profit.
On the other hand, before the battle, the Dawn Patrol had used a signal jammer to block communication signals across a large swath of the nearby sea.
It was highly likely that the situation here hadn't reached the encampment island of the thousand-mage phalanx.
Even if it had been transmitted, since the previous artillery fire had destroyed most of the ships, those guys would have to think twice about sending reinforcements.
The current power of the Dawn Patrol was no weaker than any pirate fleet in the alchemy plane. Without a few eighth-tiers, anyone who came would be delivering themselves.
Besides, if they really couldn't beat the opposition, Su Lun could completely escape by teleporting.
There was almost no threat.
However, more coincidentally, while the battle on their side was still not over, Su Lun noticed that violent combat had broken out in the vicinity of the "Rainbow Well" island in the far distance.
When he teleported over to take a look, the mages from the celestial plane and a deep-sea monster were engaged in a fierce battle.
This maritime zone was not the domain of humans.
Dragons, Gorgons, deep-sea monsters... These natives were not rare.
The previous artillery commotion had attracted monsters from within a hundred miles, and that area was likely to be lively for a while.
But, the combat power of the thousand-mage phalanx was tremendous, and they had a steady stream of personnel teleporting in; they were not worried about trench warfare.
Su Lun didn't watch for long before that troublemaking sea monster was slain by the mage phalanx.
If he wanted to divert disaster elsewhere, he'd need to come up with a good long-term plan.
...
Before long, the Eternal Night continued to sail on the sea surface.
Su Lun also teleported back.
On the deck, people were counting the loot from this battle, with piles of magic wands, robes, crystal balls, and magic tomes stacked like mountains.
The members of the Dawn Patrol were witnessing the wealth of inter-planar mages for the first time, each one bubbling with excitement.
"Oh, these mages are really rich, much more so than those pirates. My God, every storage ring is filled with piles of magic gemstones..."
"Hahaha... High-ranking mages need a lot of magical tools for practice, being wealthy is normal. We've struck it rich this time."
"Oh, thanks to Mr. Su Lun! If it weren't for him sinking those guys' pirate ships, we couldn't possibly have stopped them all with just our cannons."
"Exactly, exactly! Mr. Su Lun is mighty!"
"..."
As soon as this was exclaimed, everyone on the large ship burst into cheers.
Su Lun, hearing the exaggerated praises of everyone, also responded with a smile.
Then he gathered with Qiantiao, Barrett, and a few other high-ranking fighters to hold a brief meeting on the deck.
Given the current situation, venturing blindly into the waters of Dragon Country was not a wise choice.
And unless the problem of the teleportation array was resolved, those guys from the celestial plane would be a huge hidden danger.
After some discussion, they couldn't come up with any good solutions.
The mages had established defensive positions on the island's mountain, even ninth-tiers would have problems charging in. It'd be even less likely for the Dawn Patrol to have any chance of success.
Just when everyone felt they had not come up with any good plans, Su Lun thought of the Naga tribe sacred item "Rainbow Conch" he had found when he saved Kite.
He looked up at Tanni, who was eavesdropping among the group of youths on the mast, and asked, "Tanni, do you think you can use this conch?"
Tanni leapt down, "Eh... this conch feels so familiar."
Su Lun explained, "This is a sacred item of the Naga tribe."
Tanni said, "No wonder, I feel like I've seen it when I was little."
He took the rainbow conch, and feeling an inexplicable familiarity, he put it to his mouth and blew into it, puffing his cheeks.
As he blew, a melodious and pleasing sound of the conch spread out.
PS: Hit a writer's block, hence there's less update.

chapters.title: Chapter 526 - 543: Lei Dian Blue Dragon
chapters.content:
Su Lun had previously obtained the "Colorful Conch Shell" and researched it a bit. He tried infusing a thread of wind, but heard no sound.
Unexpectedly, when Tanni put it to his mouth, it instantly produced a sound.
And it was so beautiful.
The sound of the conch shell was very special; despite not being loud, it seemed as if it could reach far, far away.
"Woooo..."
Though it was just a simple long tone, it somehow made one hear a delightful melody. The surrounding wind and water elements seemed to be drawn by a mysterious force, pulsating with the soundwaves.
Everyone on the deck and in the cabin, upon hearing this sound, showed a trace of a dazed expression in their eyes.
Looking up, a dazzling rainbow hundreds of meters long had appeared above the Eternal Night.
Su Lun also looked in amazement because he distinctly felt a high-level principle fluctuation from the melody, akin to touching an unreachable sandstorm.
He even thought that perhaps a conch girl would emerge.
However, after blowing once, Tanni's face displayed a near breathless expression as he took the conch out of his mouth while muttering, "Ah... that was tough."
As soon as the conch's sound stopped, the rainbow gradually faded and the surrounding joyous waves also calmed down.
Only the distant sound continued to spread towards the far off.
Su Lun had previously identified the conch's effect, it could control "wind" and "sea."
Currently, Tanni's strength was not strong, and it didn't seem very useful.
Su Lun let Tanni put away the conch shell.
The Eternal Night aimlessly drifted on the sea.
...
Su Lun did not plan to rush into the deeper parts of the sea for an adventure.
Previously, because two large pirate crews cleared the way for them and suffered 70% losses, their Dawn crew managed to reach here relatively safely.
Now, if they themselves mined for dangers in the sea, the risk would be enormous.
The Eternal Night Sea was like a moat, blocking outsiders from coming over and also keeping the dangers of the Dragon Country Waters enclosed.
Mere notations on the "Map of Dragon Country Waters" marked places full of dangers everywhere.
Moreover, this sea map was drawn many years ago, perhaps there had been some big changes.
It was a territory where even the Pirate King Black Sam's crew faced complete destruction, an area absolutely not to be underestimated.
Before figuring out a good plan, Su Lun was not in a hurry.
After continuous battles for several days, the crew members were all tired; it was a good time to rest.
The Eternal Night just drifted unhurriedly on the sea surface.
At night, the sky was dotted with stars.
The ship was quiet, the members of the Dawn crew, tired from consecutive fierce battles, were mostly deep in sleep.
The moon was dim tonight, and the sea was pitch black, even with light shining down, it was endlessly dark.
Su Lun meditated in the captain's quarters, keeping his perception constantly extended outward.
In these dangerous waters, he dared not be careless at all.
Suddenly, his eyes snapped open.
On the side, Qian Tiao, who had just been soundly asleep, also instantly sensed this chill and alertly rolled up. She did not perceive anything, and looking at Su Lun, she asked, "What happened?"
Su Lun frowned and said, "Just now, some people swam over and reached near our boat."
There were no other people in this sea area; his first thought was that the divine realm mages had sneaked over under the cover of night to probe their situation.
No sooner had the words left his mouth than he and Qian Tiao teleported onto the deck.
The patrolling crew members were still moving back and forth on the deck, obviously unaware of the anomaly.
Seeing Su Lun and Qian Tiao appear, the patrol team leader spoke, "Mr. Su Lun, Captain Qian Tiao, why have you come?"
Su Lun gestured for everyone to be quiet.
All crew members instantly became alert, sensing something was wrong.
It was dead quiet around, even with Su Lun's night vision he didn't spot anything unusual, but Soul Perception clearly detected more than ten people hidden in the water near their ship.
"Hmm, strange."
Su Lun did not rush to act, but he felt somewhat puzzled.
This method did not seem like that of mages, nor did it appear to involve pirates with underwater breathing apparatus.
He intended to observe a bit longer what those guys were up to, but those hiding under the water seemed to be very alert, as if they had sensed something. Only the slight "whoosh" of water could be heard, and then they darted away like dartfish.
"So fast!"
Su Lun was slightly amazed.
Qian Tiao evidently noticed this noise too, and was interestedly about to draw her sword.
But Su Lun was quicker; he had come to the deck prepared and with a single hand, his fingers acting as if to grasp at the void, one by one, strands of thread coalesced into a tangible form. Just as those figures in the water turned to flee, six or seven of them crashed into an invisible net.
Using the crane at the ship's side, Su Lun "whooshed" and pulled those figures out of the water, suspending them in mid-air.
In an instant, everyone on the deck knew they had caught spies, and the searchlight was immediately directed toward them.
It illuminated a swath of pale skin and shining scales.
Seeing this, Su Lun said in surprise, "Not human?"
Nagas?
Mermaids?
He did not know how to describe the humanoid creatures he was seeing; they had human bodies and fish tails, resembling nagas. But even when exposed to the air, the seven's fish tails gradually morphed into human forms, turning into six slick-skinned humans, two men and five women. Even so, they retained some marine characteristics, like their ears and some of their scales.
The sudden situation had attracted everyone on the deck, and they all gathered by the ship's rail to watch the spectacle.
But Su Lun suddenly thought of something and said to himself, "The Naga tribe?"
These seven individuals, for now let's just call them people, were captured in a net. They looked at the group of humans on the ship in panic and furiously struggled to escape from the net. But the silk threads used by Su Lun were not something that a few individuals, likely only having third or fourth level combat abilities, could break.
From the communicator, Tanni who hadn't slept for several days and nights called out, and moments later, a figure jumped down from the cockpit, "Mr. Su Lun, did you call me?"
Tanni steadied himself on his feet and before he had even finished speaking, he saw the seven people hanging in the net. He seemed to recognize something and immediately frowned.
Su Lun said, "Take a look, aren't these your tribespeople?"
Tanni was a half-blood of human and Naga origin, having left this maritime area when he was very young, and his memories of his homeland were vague.
But his mother was a pure-blooded Naga!
Tanni immediately confirmed, "Yes, these are people of the Naga tribe!"
The seven Naga were still struggling under the bright lights.
Su Lun felt they were probably scared, and he called out to the people around him watching the excitement, "Alright, disperse everyone."
Although curious, the crowd each returned to their posts.
If they were Tanni's tribespeople, they naturally weren't enemies. Su Lun placed them on deck but slightly restrained them, preventing them from jumping ship and escaping.
When the floodlights were turned off, the Naga were not as panicked anymore. They turned their gazes to the few humans in front of them.
Communication was troublesome.
Su Lun thought for a moment and said directly, "Don't panic, we won't harm you. This is Tanni, he is a Naga. His mother is Frida, and his father is a human, probably named Sam Bellamy..."
When he had previously detached from the divine plane of existence, he had learned a small spell "Language Proficiency."
It involved attaching spiritual power to the language to bypass the language barrier, allowing both sides of the conversation to somewhat understand the dialogue.
As Su Lun spoke, he released a wave of spiritual power, roughly expressing his lack of malice.
The names and such were transliterations, which sounded quite similar upon listening.
Sure enough, this straightforward speech immediately quieted the Naga in front of him. Hints of doubt appeared in their eyes, obviously having heard of a few names.
The seven appeared to be quite young, among them a slightly older blonde girl who seemed like the leader. Su Lun remembered that when he had captured them, she was clearly able to escape, but she came back to save others.
She looked Tanni up and down, hesitated for a moment, but still asked, "You know Frida**?"
Su Lun didn't quite understand that specific honorific, but he knew it was a kind of title for "leader," "chief," or "priest."
He directly placed Tanni's completely petrified mother from his little void world on the deck and said, "Tanni's mother was petrified by a Gorgon. We came here this time to look for a way to solve the petrification."
These past days, Dr. Banks had constantly been studying methods to deal with petrification, but progress was not very promising. The rules of petrification spells were too high-level, and current biological means could not solve the problem.
Seeing the petrified tribeswoman, the blonde girl's expression changed instantly.
She was young during the disaster thirty years ago, but had also experienced it. (Setting: Naga have a lifespan of about two hundred years, and thirty years is their youthful period.)
Seeing this, Su Lun lifted the spatial restrictions.
The Naga looked around as if they wanted to flee, but seeing the lead girl didn't move, they too stayed.
At that moment, Su Lun added, "We're not enemies. If possible, I'd like to meet with the elders of your Naga tribe."
There were too many unknowns in this maritime area, and he indeed needed some intelligence from the Naga to make headway.
Hearing this, the girl said, "I can't decide, but I can go inform the elders. If you don't trust me, you can let my companions go back, and I'll stay here."
Su Lun readily agreed to let them all leave.
But as they were about to leave, he glanced at their naked bodies and asked, "Do you need some clothes?"
The Naga girl said, "No, no need. We Naga are natural sprites, our bodies are naturally part of nature. Only you humans feel it's shameful and cover it up."
Saying this, they jumped off the deck.
Su Lun was also surprised to hear this.
This concept was somewhat similar to that of the Dalu Tribe.
Just like fish in the sea and deer in the forest, it would be stranger if they wore clothes.
Watching the Naga leave, a thousand gazes fell on the little splashes on the sea surface, Su Lun chuckled, "Ah, quite pretty indeed."
Su Lun laughed, "Indeed, quite beautiful."
The Naga are descendants of dark elves, known for their good looks.
And with more females than males, now it was evident.
...
Su Lun hadn't asked before, but he guessed it was probably the sound of "Rainbow Conch" Tanni blew during the day that attracted the Naga.
But the arrival of the Naga now was indeed a big benefit for the Dawn Group.
Releasing all seven Naga, he didn't feel they wouldn't return.
Su Lun and Chi Qian sat on the mast, letting the wind blow as they meditated.
Tanni also occasionally leaned over the railing, peering at something now and then.
Not long after, two hours later, a few Naga swam back, still led by the blonde Naga girl.
They didn't board the ship but called out from the water, "That human..."
Su Lun smiled slightly, "My name is Su Lun."
The blonde girl corrected herself, "Well... Su Lun, the human, the elder says you should come to Golden Brown Island for a meeting. But they don't want to see too many people."
Su Lun smiled, "Great. Where is that island? If possible, I'll go with you right now."
The blonde girl cautiously asked, "How many of you are going?"
Su Lun responded, "Just Tanni and myself."
The people of the Dawn Group on the ship listened and laughed silently.
No one thought Su Lun going alone would pose any danger.
If a change occurred, he alone had more capability to protect himself than the entire Dawn Group combined.
Hearing this, the blonde girl relaxed and then asked, "Are you going to row over there?"
Tanni, excited by the prospect of going, interjected, "I can swim."
Su Lun smiled and said, "I can go by myself."
As he spoke, he leapt down, and his octopus spear stood steady on the surface of the sea.
The young Naga girl watched the spear behind Su Lun and murmured to herself, "Is this human alchemy..."
Tanni also jumped into the water, revealing some of the Naga's aquatic traits.
Seeing him, the caution in the eyes of several Naga people lessened considerably.
They turned and swam speedily towards the northwest.
Su Lun and Tanni closely followed.
The Naga tribe excels in controlling water, moving extremely fast inside it.
They intentionally slowed down their speed to allow Su Lun and his companion to keep up.
After swimming for half an hour, the group reached a deserted island.
"Golden Brown Island" was clearly a hastily chosen deserted island, with many coconut trees on the beach.
When Su Lun arrived, he sensed about a dozen soul vibrations on the island; some were hidden, others waited on the beach.
The strongest among them didn't feel threatening at all, probably a sixth-level professional in terms of power.
Su Lun didn't mind and directly went onto the island.
What he saw was a lot of sleek handsome men and beautiful women.
There were noticeably more women than men.
Their appearances were handsome, and their figures elegantly curved.
Even the one called "Elder Sera" looked just like a woman of charm among humans of her age, hardly old at all.
The blonde girl first came ashore and introduced everyone for a few moments.
However, surprisingly, when Elder Sera saw Tanni, she exclaimed, "Little Tanni?"
Her tone was clearly filled with surprise.
Tanni was not so clear about who this female clan member was in front of him, but seemed to remember something. He forgot the language and did not know how to respond.
He turned his head and looked at Su Lun.
Su Lun asked, "Elder, do you know Tanni?"
"Of course. I even held him when he was very small."
Elder Sera looked at Tanni with a fondness typical of an elder, speaking in the common language of Emperor Luying 's empire, then muttered to herself, "I wondered who could blow the Holy Artifact [Rainbow Conch]; it turns out to be little Tanni."
Her expression sank into a moment of contemplation, then she asked, "May I see Frida?"
Su Lun laid Tanni's petrified mother back on the beach.
To his surprise, upon seeing the statue, several members of the Naga bowed solemnly on the ground, as if conducting a grand welcoming ceremony.
Su Lun discreetly stepped aside.
He also understood that Tanni's mother held a very special status within the Naga tribe.
After the crowd of Naga stood up, Elder Sera invited Su Lun, saying, "This human sir, please sit here. Sorry, our Naga tribe is in a bit of a delicate situation, so we've been somewhat cautious."
"Of course. Elder Sera, you can call me Su Lun."
Su Lun didn't mind at all, and sat down next to a rustic stone table that had fruits on it.
The blonde girl before brought over teacups, pouring tea.
Su Lun noticed that the porcelain clearly came from the Emperor Luying's empire.
Elder Sera asked, "Are you from the distant Emperor Luying's empire, the same country as Mr. Sam once mentioned?"
Su Lun took a sip of tea, smiling and nodding, then curiously said, "Elder, have you heard of Emperor Luying's empire?"
Elder Sera replied, "Of course. Mr. Sam brought us many stories from distant lands."
As she spoke, she beckoned Tanni to sit beside her, "Little Tanni, you can sit by my side."
Catching this, Su Lun asked, "Is Tanni's father really Mr. Sam Bellamy? I had guessed before, but wasn't sure."
"Of course."
Elder Sera's eyes showed a hint of reminiscence, and she said, "Over twenty years ago, that powerful human adventurer and his companions came to these waters. Mr. Sam and a priestess of our Naga tribe had a beautiful encounter, and then they fell in love and Tanni was born."
"I see."
Su Lun listened and smiled slightly, recalling seeing Tanni with the third [Black Sam Cursed Gold Coin] in Pirate City; he had suspected as much.
Now that he had confirmation, it wasn't too surprising.
Tanni, on the other hand, widened his eyes, learning for the first time that his father was none other than the famous "Pirate King Black Sam" of the pirate realm!
Following that, Su Lun inquired further, "What exactly happened back then? Why was Tanni's mother turned to stone? And what about Mr. Sam and his pirate crew?"
This was one of the several questions Su Lun wanted to understand from the Naga.
There were many purposes for his trip to the Dragon Country Waters, including helping to reverse Tanni's mother's petrification, finding Black Sam's ship's [Holy Grail of Fael], and the dragons, [Mimir's Well]...
Mentioning the past, Elder Sera's mature and charming face couldn't hide a sigh of sadness as she responded, "Mr. Sam and his companions went to explore the 'Old Dragon Kingdom Ruins' in the far west, a very dangerous sea area with powerful dragons and giants, and even ancient deities' battlegrounds... and then..."
She didn't finish; what came next was naturally unknown.
Su Lun, listening to the description, also roughly knew which direction the Pirate King's crew had gone.
It wasn't right to inquire deeply now, so he said no more.
Elder Sera sighed lightly, hardly concealing her regret, and added, "Originally, the Gorgon was nearby the ancient battlefield in the west; no one knows why it suddenly invaded our Naga territory. The High Priest, who is Tanni's grandmother, and the elders died in the battle with the Gorgon, trying to cover for the young ones to escape... and our ships were scattered by storms at sea..."
The situation was much as he had speculated.
Such a heavy topic did not lend itself to further inquiry, and Su Lun listened quietly.
Elder Sera spoke as if she didn't want to mention the disaster that had nearly exterminated the Naga tribe. She then changed the subject, asking, "By the way, Mr. Su Lun, may I boldly ask what brings you to the waters of Dragon Country this time? Are you here for an adventure as well?"
The atmosphere seemed harmonious, but she still held some reservations about the Dawn Group's intentions.
Su Lun was very clear, and truthfully said, "Adventure is indeed one of our objectives. But there are some more important matters too."
He then explained the matter of the planar invasion to Elder Sera.
Elder Sera initially wanted to ask about the huge booming noise near Rainbow Island during the day, but she didn't expect to hear news of a "planar invasion."
She asked in surprise, "Are you saying that some enemies not from this plane have arrived on Rainbow Island?"
Su Lun replied, "Yes. They are using the 'Rainbow Well' to establish a long-distance teleportation array, continuously transporting mages here. The situation will only get worse."
After pausing, he continued, "So I also want to ask if Elder Sera knows any way to stop their teleportation."
Elder Sera furrowed her brow and thought deeply for a while, her mind overwhelmed with shocking news. Finally, she said, "The High Priest can seal off the magical energy leakage from the 'Rainbow Well'."
Su Lun asked, "High Priest?"
Elder Sera replied, "Yes. Our Naga tribe's High Priest can use the power of the Holy Artifact 'Seven-colored Conch' to seal the Rainbow Well."
As she spoke, she looked regretful and said, "Unfortunately, the High Priest died in the battle over twenty years ago. Even if we recover the Holy Artifact, no one in our tribe is capable of casting such a powerful seal."
"..."
Su Lun's brow also furrowed.
The inability to shut down the teleportation array was a big problem.
Just when he thought the matter had hit a dead end, Elder Sera's gaze wandered thoughtfully toward a distant statue.
Su Lun, keenly catching her gaze, directly said, "Lady Frida, Tanni's mother, still shows signs of life. We are here to find a way to reverse petrification. Elder, do you know of any way to do that?"
The Naga tribe didn't have as many human intrigues. Elder Sera didn't hide her desire to save her tribespeople and responded, "Tanni's mother Frida is the daughter of the High Priest and was a priestess of our tribe. If she can be restored, perhaps she might seal the 'Rainbow Well'. The invasion started with the queen of the Gorgon tribe who unleashed the petrification curse, and we've tried many methods to reverse it, to no avail."
Hearing this, Tanni's small face was filled with tension and unease, as it involved her mother's life or death.
Su Lun, however, remained calm because he trusted that there would be a solution since it was brought up.
As expected, Elder Sera said, "However, it is said that human wizards in Dragon Country possess a secret potion that can undo petrification. There was once a human king who went to the territory of the Medusa and was petrified, but he was restored after using some miraculous potion."
Surprised, Su Lun asked, "A human realm? Are there humans in these waters?"
The map did have markings, but now
Elder Sera confirmed, "Yes. To the north, there is a human kingdom. They live alongside dragons and are known as 'Dragon Country.'"
After a pause, she looked at Su Lun earnestly and said, "Our Naga tribe isn't friendly with humans. If possible, I would like to entrust Mr. Su Lun and your associates to help find that potion and save our tribe."
Without hesitation, Su Lun replied, "Of course. That's what we intended to do anyway."
Even if it had nothing to do with the Naga, he had already planned to make the journey, as he had previously promised Tanni.
Moreover, with the existence of human kingdoms, their plan to come to the Dragon Country Waters this time would be much easier.
Dealing with humans was much easier than dealing with sea monsters and giant dragons.
Upon hearing this, Elder Sera suddenly stood up, and she, along with the dozens of Naga people, simultaneously bowed to Su Lun, expressing their most sincere gratitude.
Su Lun repeatedly returned the gesture.
...
The atmosphere of the conversation had become very harmonious from that moment on.
Su Lun could clearly feel that the last bit of wariness in the eyes of the Naga people had also disappeared.
The blonde girl previously called 'Tatu' also had a friendly smile on her face, and was extremely polite as she poured tea.
The atmosphere of the conversation grew increasingly congenial.
Su Lun had also learned a lot of urgently needed information from Elder Sera and had a more accurate assessment of the area.
The mood was pleasant, and light laughter could occasionally be heard.
The only thing that made Su Lun feel slightly uneasy was that his eyes had nowhere restful to focus.
No matter where he looked, there was an expanse of gleaming skin. Moreover, the natural charm of their elven bloodline made them seem like exquisite works of art.
Elder Sera was like this, Tatu was like this, and every Naga person was the same.
With pure intentions, it didn't feel too awkward, but he still felt it was somewhat impolite to stare.
As they chatted, Elder Sera also expressed more concern for the Dawn Group, "The 'Eternal Night Sea' is very dangerous. You must have suffered a lot coming here... This area hides many deadly dangers, and you'd better not go to sea recently. The noise from bombarding Rainbow Island yesterday was too loud, which is very dangerous. It must have already alarmed the nearby area... It might even awaken the evil dragon on Thunder Sea Island seven hundred nautical miles to the northwest."
"..."
Su Lun smiled and remained silent.
He had not failed to consider the consequences of the bombardment.
But with Spatial Teleportation and the Small Void Realm, even if this area were in uproar, it wouldn't be a big problem.
Worst case, he could just stuff everything into the Eternal Night and then escape.
The troublesome ones would only be the people from the divine realms on Rainbow Island.
But he had no intention of explaining.
However, when Su Lun heard the last sentence, he interjected with surprise, "Elder Sera, there's a giant dragon nearby?"
Elder Sera nodded, her expression grave as if describing a terrifying creature, "Yes. It is a pure-blood blue dragon, controlling the power of thunder and lightning, extremely dangerous!"
The Naga people, listening to the description of a top-tier creature in the food chain, also looked very solemn.
But they didn't notice that upon hearing this, an unusual gleam shone in the depths of Su Lun's eyes.
Just having arrived in the Dragon Country Waters, he had heard about a... solitary giant dragon?
Was his luck really that good?

chapters.title: Chapter 527 - 544 Medusa
chapters.content:
The Naga race possesses certain ancient memories that are transmitted through their bloodline, much more complete than those of humans.
Through conversations with Elder Sera, Su Lun came to understand many pieces of intelligence.
The current Dragon Country is not the Ancient Dragon Country outlined on maps. It had evolved into its current state following a certain ancient war of the gods.
It is said that thousands of years ago, the Ancient Dragon Country was an immensely large continent that nearly sunk entirely into the ocean due to a war that even the gods fell in. After countless years, the present day archipelago dotted with islands slowly emerged.
Their current location is merely a remote area of the Dragon Country Waters.
Further west lies the remnants of the Ancient Dragon Country, and according to legend, it was a place where deities once battled. The further one went in that direction, the more powerful the creatures became.
Su Lun speculated that the "Divine Fall War" Elder Sera mentioned was likely the great war that led to the fragmentation of the Dawn Era plane.
After hearing those mythical stories, he also surmised that it might also be a sea area where gods were buried.
Otherwise, there wouldn't be so many terrifying creatures present.
...
The conversation atmosphere grew increasingly harmonious. With Tanni and his mother involved, these Naga saw Su Lun, the human, with no further guards up.
Upon hearing that Su Lun wished to find the location of Black Sam's sunken ship, Elder Sera subtly cautioned, "Mr. Sam and his companions were very strong and excellent adventurers, even capable of hunting dragons. Yet they never returned from that sea area... When Mr. Sam and his partners set out on their adventure, they likely encountered the 'Hell Volcano' eruption season. Our Naga race has a legend that a volcano in the ancient battlefield connects to the underworld plane. Once it erupts, the 'Undead Catastrophe' it unleashes will drag all living creatures into hell, and countless terrifying hellish beasts will swarm in. It's an indescribably horrific scene..."
She didn't wish to see Su Lun and his companions fall into a crisis but was unable to dissuade others from going, just like the Black Sam Pirate crew before them.
Adventuring seems to be an activity humans are passionate about, which is somewhat incomprehensible to the Naga.
Su Lun, listening intently, nodded earnestly, "Hmm, thank you for the warning, Elder."
He had no intention of acting rashly.
With all the intelligence he acquired, his reverence for this sea area deepened.
This sea did not only bury the team of the Pirate King; it also became the grave of countless mighty beings.
Their Dawn team had nothing special about them.
But this sea area was as dangerous for them as it was for those from the Celestial plane.
The treasure wasn't about to flee. They could search for it slowly, there was no rush.
Only by reversing the petrification curse inflicted on Tanni's mother and sealing the Rainbow Well could they fully restrict the root problem of transport from the Celestial plane.
Moreover, now that Su Lun heard about the existence of human kingdoms in the "Dragon Country Waters," he felt the situation suddenly opened up.
If humans could survive in this sea area, perhaps they knew some other useful information.
Elder Sera mentioned that the human kingdoms had secret remedies to resolve petrification, and he planned to search for them first.
Besides, hunting dragons was also something to consider.
...
However, at the time Su Lun met with the Naga.
On Rainbow Island.
The Mages from the Celestial plane were building a Mage Tower overnight. Their magic camp was becoming more and more fortified.
Outside the island, ever since the daytime bombardment, a steady flow of monsters had attacked.
But they were all slain under the mass assault of the tens of thousands-strong Mage group.
Although there were some losses, it wasn't too bad.
They were an elite Mage group from the Celestial plane with abundant combat experience. Even in this perilous sea area, they still possessed absolute strength.
However, survival was never the issue.
They were here, guided by divinity, to find the "Fountain of Mimir."
In a Mage Tower, a Mage clad in a black and white priestly robe chanted a deep and arcane magic spell.
In front of him lay an ancient parchment scroll.
Drawn on the scroll was a woman's head full of serpentine hair, terrifying and ferocious; next to the scroll lay a golden scepter with a snake's head, symbolizing sacred authority.
As the magic incantations were chanted, the nine-pointed star formation on the scroll gradually lit up. The serpent-headed golden scepter seemed to come alive, coiling its body and flicking its scarlet tongue.
It was like an illusion, yet also as if the scepter was indeed transformed from a Poison Snake.
If Su Lun were here, he would have recognized that this Mage was none other than Zura Augustus, the leader of the Celestial plane delegation and an eighth-order Holy Army Mage.
This aged Mage had divine power emanating from him, and after chanting the spell on the parchment scroll, he released the summoning incantation in a deep voice, "Descendant of Golgotha's blood, heed my call and come forth in accordance with the pact!"
In an instant, the Mage Tower acted like a signal amplifier, spreading that arcane incantation.
Several hours later, the edge of the sky had begun to brighten with the first light of dawn.
```
But the sea surface remained pitch black.
The mages had also noticed the agitated sea monsters near Rainbow Island had unknowingly quieted down. It was as if some great terror was slowly drawing near.
All around on the sea surface floated fragments of warships, and in the gloom, a shadow not overly tall traced an S-shaped path across the water and slid past.
It seemed the mages had anticipated something's arrival, leaving a passage open outside their camp.
The figure left the water, donned a black cloak, and walked straight towards the tallest Mage Tower.
The camp was full of magic tents, and patrolling mages had received orders; everyone disregarded the mysterious newcomer, avoiding their gaze.
She thus strode across the entire camp.
But some young mages couldn't resist their curiosity and sneaked a peek.
In that instant, an expression of awe appeared on the young mage's face.
But a bizarre scene ensued.
His pupils instantly lost their luster, turning dull and white, as if petrified into stone.
Then the petrification curse spread rapidly; within two breaths, his body, along with his robe and magic wand, turned completely to stone.
Unsteady, the stone sculpture clattered to the ground and shattered into a pile of rubble.
The other mages swallowed nervously at this eerie sight.
But no one dared say anything, let alone spy on the mysterious visitor.
The cloaked person made their way to the Mage Tower.
She lifted her cloak, revealing the arrogance characteristic of divine blood.
Reflected by the campfires, a shadow appeared on the Mage Tower.
It was the silhouette of a woman with a graceful figure.
But atop her head writhed a mass of hideous serpentine hair that made one's scalp tingle.
This was a high-ranking Gorgon!
She looked at the Mage Tower's door and said coldly, "Humans, state your purpose."
At that moment, Augustus came out holding the Golden Snake Scepter in his hand.
He kept his eyes firmly shut, with only an illusory vertical pupil appearing on his forehead, staring at the gorgon, "I wish to make a trade with the Gorgon tribe using the scepter. I give you the scepter, you guide us to 'Mimir's Spring'."
The Gorgon with serpentine hair eyed the golden scepter in his hand, seemingly in great desire, as her hair of snakes boiled in excitement, each opening its vicious, crimson mouth to reveal fierce poison fangs.
She responded, "That's Cyclops territory. For the sake of the scepter, I can guide you there. But don't expect our Gorgon tribe to fight for you."
Augustus spoke in an even tone, raising the scepter in his hand, decisively, "No, I need more help! If we can't make a deal, I will immediately destroy this 'Serpentine Staff of Medusa'!"
The Gorgon's voice suddenly became shrill, roaring, "Human, you are provoking me. You will plunge yourself and all here into hell!"
With that, her head of serpentine hair roared along, each snake coiling and struggling to strike but being pulled back in restraint. Were they not attached to her head, they would likely have already lunged to bite the enemy before them.
Facing such a terrifying scene, Augustus remained unperturbed and said, "I am guided by the great deities. You should know I fear not death!"
Deities?
The Gorgon with serpentine hair looked at the holy light emanating from him and the vertical pupil on his forehead, her complexion growing suddenly grim.
But after a moment of contemplation, she relented, "I will do my utmost to help you approach the island."
Augustus said coldly, "The contract is established!"
The Gorgon with serpentine hair fell silent, evidently consenting to the deal.
The air was filled with magical fluctuations, carrying an indescribable will.
Upon another glance, the new runes had already fully illuminated on the parchment scroll inside the Mage Tower.
The Gorgon with serpentine hair snorted, took the golden scepter, and turned to leave.
...
The following morning.
Su Lun returned to the Eternal Night.
The negotiations with the Naga race last night had been very pleasant.
Su Lun had obtained the various intelligence he desperately needed.
But now the Naga race no longer had many of their kind and could not lend support to the Dawn group in terms of strength.
Only the golden-haired girl named Tatu from last night had come back with them, acting as a "guide."
The Naga race had no custom of wearing clothes, but it was overall inappropriate to remain uncovered on a human ship, so Tatu had put on the clothes given to her by Su Lun.
```
When the group of three returned to the deck, the crew was just having breakfast.
Su Lun greeted everyone on deck and headed to the dining area.
Seeing Su Lun approach, the members of the Dawn Group greeted him one after another.
However, everyone's gaze was curiously fixed on the blonde girl accompanying Su Lun.
Everybody had heard about last night's events, and they were all very interested in the legendary "mermaid."
Qian Tiao even joked, "Yo, Su Lun, you're back? And you've brought a young girl with you?"
Su Lun introduced her, "This is Tatu, a Naga warrior. She will be our guide in the Dawn Group for the days to come."
Tatu, knowing she was being introduced, replied in slightly accented Rulian Common Tongue, "Hello everyone, my name is Tatu."
But feeling embarrassed under the gaze of thousands of eyes, she felt a bit awkward.
The Naga tribe possesses a very strong language learning ability. Last night, by listening to the conversation between Su Lun and the elder, Tatu had already learned a lot of Rulian Common Tongue. She was here as a guide because she also spoke the Dragon Country's human common language.
The group was warm and cheerful, showing kind smiles and voicing their welcomes.
Tatu, feeling pleasantly surprised, appeared slightly restrained.
Qian Tiao invited her warmly, "Tatu, come sit over here."
Hearing this, Tatu glanced at Su Lun beside her, a trace of trepidation in her eyes.
Su Lun knew right away she was intimidated by the murderous aura emanating from Qian Tiao and introduced her, "That's Sister Qian Tiao, our leader in the Dawn Group. You'll get to know her, she's very approachable."
Tatu's expression changed subtly upon hearing this, but she also knew that accepting an invitation was a sign of friendship in human etiquette.
Su Lun led Tatu to sit at the dining table.
This Naga girl was seeing such a lavish breakfast for the first time; the array of exquisite dishes dazzled her. In addition to seafood, there was fragrant roast bread, cheese, fine wine, and some fruits she had never seen before. Compared to their diet of only fish, this was truly bountiful.
Luo Luo Ta, having slept heavily last night and missed the scene of the Naga people being captured, now blinked and examined Tatu closely, exclaiming in awe, "Wow... Tatu, you're really beautiful."
Tatu somewhat understood and responded, "Thank you."
But she felt she was just average for a Naga, not particularly good-looking.
Luo Luo Ta was enthusiastic and filled Tatu's plate with various delicacies.
The Dawn Group was very warm and friendly towards the beautiful Naga girl. No one treated her as an outsider, and they quickly became familiar with one another.
Su Lun also rarely had breakfast with his companions.
He shared most of the intelligence gathered the previous night with everyone.
Qian Tiao, Number Nineteen, Barrett, Wazhwaz, Kite, Dora... several high-ranking members of the Dawn Group also spoke up to discuss things.
They also agreed with Su Lun's plan.
This sea area was too dangerous; it was best to check out the human kingdoms first.
...
After breakfast, Luo Luo Ta and Tanni took Tatu for a tour around the ship.
Meanwhile, Su Lun and the others continued to discuss the details of the "Dragon Hunting Plan."
"I've asked around, except for the shallow seabed nearby, the western and northern areas are deep-sea zones. There are many deep-sea giants there, and flying sub-dragons that attack any royal vessel... Yesterday's cannon fire has ignited this sea area, so for now, we can't set sail either..."
"To the north, there's a human city that's perfect for us to learn about the strength of that blue dragon."
"..."
The presence of marine creatures is proportional to the depth of the sea; the deeper the sea, the more formidable the sea monsters become.
The sea monsters in this area were more numerous, stronger, and more terrifying than those in the Eternal Night Sea they had encountered previously.
The Naga were well-acquainted with this sea area and confirmed that some deep-sea giants in the deep-sea zones were as powerful as dragons.
Yesterday, in order to destroy the enemy's ships, the Dawn Group had chosen to conduct a cannonade.
As a result, the commotion stirred some deep-sea creatures.
Sailing rashly, the Dawn Group risked total destruction.
But this was all part of the plan.
Su Lun wanted to use those sea monsters to cause trouble for people from the divine realm, maybe even trap those fellows on Rainbow Island.
The pirates had limited numbers of ships, and with the watchful monsters around, even the mages who managed to secure a foothold on Rainbow Island wouldn't dare to set sail recklessly.
However, relatively speaking, while the cannonade plan restricted the navigation of the divines, it wouldn't restrict the Dawn Group.
For an ordinary pirate group, indeed, moving forward would be incredibly difficult.
But Su Lun could directly stow Eternal Night into a small void realm and teleport away from this region before releasing it.
Everyone also felt that Su Lun's plan had no issues whatsoever.
However, while they were discussing,
Su Lun seemed to have discovered something, suddenly letting out a soft exclamation, "Eh...?"
Qian Tiao asked, "What's wrong?"
Su Lun furrowed his brows, puzzled, "My warning system shows that those guys from the godly plane seem to have set sail."
Upon hearing this, Barrett by the side muttered in confusion, "How could that be?"
Knowing there was a lethal danger, yet they dared to set sail?
This was completely different from the scenario they had discussed before.
Su Lun immediately teleported over to confirm the situation.
Indeed, those mages had already boarded the ship and were preparing to voyage far.
Upon returning, Su Lun relayed the situation and thought for a moment before saying, "It looks like the people from the godly plane are not completely ignorant about these waters, and they even possess some means that we are unaware of."
This was an unusual situation, if the other party wasn't courting death, they likely had confidence in their actions.
Huazi Huasi also agreed, "Since the people from the godly plane knew about 'Mimir's Spring' in these waters, it makes sense that they have some other methods."
However, this unexpected maneuver by the enemy had put Dawn Group in a difficult position.
Dora analyzed, "The Thousand Mage Formation may be strong, but it's not enough to roam freely in these waters. If those guys dared to sail, they must be somewhat confident. I think maybe they have a way to avoid or reduce sea monster attacks..."
Number Nineteen also said, "Yesterday's artillery assault has put them on guard. Perhaps... they sailed out just to lure us into a trap. I think we must be cautious."
"Hmm."
With these words, everyone else found the argument sound and fell into deep thought.
Chasing after them was definitely not a good choice.
Su Lun's ability to preserve his own life was strong, but he was not so arrogant as to knowingly pursue into a set trap.
After some thought, Su Lun's expression suddenly relaxed, and he said, "Let's stick with the original plan, no need to bother with them."
Hearing this, everyone looked over.
Su Lun explained, "Maybe it's not a trap, but those guys must have received instructions from the divine ranks of the godly plane to find 'Mimir's Spring' as soon as possible. In the eyes of the gods, the lives of such inferior creatures like humans are not so important. After all, there is a continuous supply..."
After a pause, he continued, "Moreover, those guys currently only have enough intact ships for one Thousand Mage Formation to set sail. Even if everything goes smoothly from here to that horseshoe island, it would take at least half a month. Besides, it's extremely dangerous there, and the Thousand Mage Formation may not even make it alive. There's no need for us to follow them."
Dora, as the technical support of Dawn Group, immediately thought of something and said, "Su Lun, are you thinking of giving them a few 'elemental marker shells'?"
Su Lun smiled meaningfully and said, "Yes!"
Due to Dora's involvement, Dawn Group now had some black technology from the Mafa laboratories, such as the radiating elemental marker bombs.
Paired with some special instruments, they could monitor enemy ship targets from an extreme distance, leaving a trace all along the way. This was neither magic nor alchemy and could almost deceive any known counter-surveillance method.
They didn't need to follow the enemy to know their whereabouts.
If the enemy group was annihilated, they would also know the location of the sunken ships.
If the enemy really managed to approach the area, Su Lun could still teleport there.
It wouldn't be a blind map, jumping into some dangerous place with a teleport.
Everyone found this plan feasible when they heard it.
Before long, a barrage of shells was once again fired towards Rainbow Island.
The artillery was strong, but it no longer injured those ships that were tightly protected by the mages.
But what those people didn't know was that some special elements mixed into the shells had already marked the ships.
This black technology, unknown even to the military of Luying, was certainly unknown to the pirates and the people from the godly plane.
...
Following the original plan, Su Lun stowed Eternal Night into the small void realm.
Then, choosing the safe route pointed out by Tatu, he teleported hundreds of nautical miles, arriving at the southernmost city of the human kingdoms—Atalan City.
Legend had it that there were once nine great human kingdoms in Dragon Country, but over the years, only three remained: Pania, Akatiser, and Silver Dragon Kingdom.
Atalan City was also the southernmost city of the Silver Dragon Kingdom, a small city of just over a hundred thousand people.
But in the words of the Naga race, this human city was the hunting ground of that lightning blue dragon.
Su Lun and the others planned to visit here first to assess the strength of that blue dragon.

chapters.title: Chapter 528 - 527 Atalan City
chapters.content:
"Mr. Su Lun, my teacher said that you once battled a dragon. So, how can one defeat a giant dragon?"
"First, you must withstand the dragon's breath and the immense force of its claws; second, you must be able to break through the defense of its scales. Both requirements are quite difficult. Sir Isaac's notes mention that dragon scales have almost perfect defense runes, and dragon language magic is nearly as powerful as Divine Arts, with might that even far surpasses the spells of a higher rank. So typically, a seventh-order giant dragon is very difficult to defeat, even for someone of the eighth order profession."
"Oh."
"Moreover, the dragon I encountered was only a resentful giant dragon, which is still very different from a true giant dragon. According to the Naga tribe's intelligence, the bloodline purity of that lightning blue dragon is extremely high. It's not a good idea to act rashly without an accurate reference for its combat power."
"..."
Su Lun and Qian Chou were leisurely walking on a forest path, with the chatty little squire Lolo Tarta speaking incessantly by their side.
Being a dragon-slaying hero is a common aspiration among adventurers in various myths and legends.
Dragons represent the most powerful beings in the world, and only the mightiest warriors could defeat them.
Lolo Tarta, this little swordsman, also had a dream of hunting dragons.
Just a moment ago, they had teleported into this forest.
The other members of the Dawn Group stayed on the Eternal Night ship, familiarizing themselves with the nearby seas, preparing for the potential dragon-hunting battle that may occur.
Su Lun and Qian Chou landed and took Tatu, their guide, with them to gather information.
Unable to stay idle, Lolo Tarta followed along.
The four of them hadn't walked long before they saw a city built against a mountain.
The architectural style was unique, with tall, white walls surrounding the entire city. Its buildings were dense but not tall, each with a red lacquer roof resembling clusters of mushroom houses.
At the mountain's peak stood a castle with a sapphire blue spire.
Unlike the steam chimneys seen in the Lu Ying and Ma Fa empires, no such things could be observed in this city.
The sky was a clear blue, dotted with fluffy clouds.
In the city, only howling kitchen smoke and the smoky atmosphere of what seemed like blacksmith shops filled the air.
Tatu pointed to the city and introduced it, "This is Atalan City. The city is full of dragon riders, and they're not very friendly to our Naga tribe."
While saying this, her gaze shifted to Su Lun, seemingly to remind him of something: Bringing her into the city might cause trouble.
Since meeting him the previous night, Tatu had now realized that she still didn't know the extent of Su Lun's combat abilities. She was aware that anyone who could cross the Eternal Night Sea must be formidable. But in the eyes of the Naga, the dragon riders of Atalan City were also considered very powerful.
Without waiting for Su Lun to speak, Lolo Tarta pulled on Tatu's arm and laughed, "Don't worry, Mr. Su Lun and my teacher are both super powerful."
Tatu didn't respond, as she didn't quite grasp the concept of "super powerful."
Su Lun just smiled without much additional explanation.
Although he had no intention of underestimating the natives of Dragon Country, his current strength indeed made it difficult to find an opponent.
What intrigued him more was a term he had just heard, "Dragon riders?"
Tatu replied, "Yes. They are a kind of lesser dragon magical beast with thin dragon bloodlines, common in this sea area. Dragon Country has a tradition of taming dragons, and it is a glory for the knights to subdue powerful lesser dragons. One of the three great kingdoms we are in now, 'The Silver Dragon Kingdom,' is protected by a very powerful sacred silver dragon from the royal family."
The more Su Lun heard, the more curious he became. "So, are the relations between humans and dragons good here?"
"Not at all. On the contrary, the relationship is very hostile."
Tatu shook her head and explained, "That silver dragon stayed in the capital because of an outstanding dragon rider in the royal family of the Silver Dragon Kingdom a thousand years ago. After the dragon rider's death, the sacred silver dragon continued to protect the kingdom for a thousand years. Without it, this human kingdom might have perished long ago."
Dragons have long lifespans, living thousands or even tens of thousands of years is quite normal.
Su Lun listened thoughtfully.
Qian Chou also waited with interest for more information.
Tatu continued, "There are legends from the ancient Dragon Country era when dragons and humans got along very well. At that time, there were many powerful dragon riders and many legends about dragons and humans that were passed down. But from some point, humans became not so strong, and the situation changed. It might be, as you said, Mr. Su Lun, after the plane fracture and the weakening of the laws, that top-tier human powerhouses became rarer, and the knights who could tame dragons decreased in number. Dragons are an arrogant species and no longer wanted to be mounts for inferior creatures. They even felt that no creature could surpass the great dragon race... this led to the rise of evil dragon factions."
Su Lun asked, "Evil factions?"
Tatu elucidated further, "Yes, that's what the human kingdoms call them. Dragons like red, blue, green, black, and white almost all are hostile towards humans; they feed on humans and enslave them. But dragons like silver, gold, and gemstone dragons remain neutral. They are rarely seen in the open sea, typically dwelling in the dangerous depths of the western seas. Only a very few, like the guardian silver dragon, have a destiny with humans and will be close to them."
"I see."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun and his companions had an epiphany.
Tatu added, "So, that lightning blue dragon 'Kazzak' is also seen as an evil dragon in the eyes of humans. But since blue dragons are very fast flyers named for their lightning-like speed and no one can dodge their lightning dragon breath, the human kingdom cannot do anything, so they let it exist."
With this new information, Su Lun had a deeper understanding of the dragon race.
He thought of the "Dragon Knight Dragon Taming Secrets" in his possession, and a translated line from it resonated as quite true: "If you want to become a Dragon Knight, you must possess strength comparable to a giant dragon."
...
The four of them kept walking and soon arrived at the foot of the city.
Outside the city was a drawbridge, the only path leading into the city, where dozens of guards in silver armor were checking each person entering the city.
At the city gate, Su Lun also saw two dragons lying down and sleeping.
It was similar in shape to a dragon but much smaller, and its scales were less pronounced.
Any magical beast with even a hint of dragon bloodline is a powerhouse among its peers. Normally, these winged lizards are tier three black iron, but with a touch of Dragon Blood, they might be silver or gold level magical beasts.
This could be seen from the beasts that passed by.
Su Lun noticed that anyone entering the city dressed in adventurer leather armor almost always rode their own magical beasts, "Dragon Scale Warhorses," "Titan Gorillas," "Dragon Horn Rhinos"... These magical beasts would almost always steer clear of the two flying dragons.
The indigenous people of Dragon Country not only tamed dragons but also various other magical beasts.
To Su Lun and the other two outsiders, this was quite novel.
Tatu frowned at the city gate guards and said, "Huh, that's strange, there usually isn't a check."
Su Lun looked over and noticed a notice posted at the city gate, saying, "It seems like they are searching for someone."
Nobody paid it any mind.
After all, this kind of situation is common everywhere.
Su Lun didn't plan on stirring up trouble by crossing the drawbridge, so with a pinch of his sorcerer's seals, a spatial portal appeared before him, and he teleported into the city with Qian Tiao and three others.
The residents of the city dressed in very primitive, simple clothing, all made of coarse linen and leather armor.
The best-dressed were the flying dragon knights, but even their attire was rudimentary.
In comparison, the outfits of Su Lun and the other outsiders were far too refined.
As Su Lun had no such coarse clothing in stock, the group could only walk through the city wrapped in linen cloaks.
Perhaps because the city was close to a dangerous area, there were quite a few adventurers in the city.
The city's buildings were packed closely together, except for the main thoroughfare leading to the castle, which could accommodate carriages; the rest of the streets were very narrow.
City walls, houses, streets... All were made from stacked stones.
Due to the lack of a properly planned urban sewer system, the residential areas were always plagued with a foul stench.
Having thought that Ruying's rural territory was backward enough, they found this place to be practically in a primitive state.
There was no industry whatsoever.
There were also a few street vendors, selling very basic goods like grain, fruit, and some magical beast meat...
Su Lun and his party walked along, looking around.
Lolota whispered in awe looking at the passersby, "These people are all so strong!"
They had initially thought that only the city gate soldiers and adventurers looked sturdy.
But upon entering the city, they discovered that the ordinary residents were also very strong.
