Dr. Banks had already dissected the dragon's nervous and joint systems. That last strike, he directly stabbed into the dragon's wing nerve.
Otherwise, even with the mechanical octopus, it would have been impossible to gain an advantage in strength.
Now fully locked, it also meant they could start the true dragon-slaying phase!
The dragon's speed slowed, a thousand swordsman also drew swords and charged forward, and Hua​z​hua​s also turned into a demon state and flew over with wings flapping.
Barrett, too, had donned a set of full-body heavy armor, which was notably the Greystone Dragon Rider Heavy Armor (Legendary) that Su Lun had acquired from the royal treasury of Greystone previously.
Although his movements were still somewhat clumsy, the armor gave him absolute protection.
Surrounding and killing an eighth-tier giant dragon was a privilege reserved for top-tier professionals, and they all started the "blood wearing" process.
This was a familiar phase, and everyone cooperated tacitly.
Only far away, the Dragon Hunter Barrett wore a look of astonishment.
Seeing the mechanical octopus, he was also significantly shocked.
When he left Lu​ying, the Ma​fa mechanical armor had already become prevalent, but when had he ever seen such mechanical life forms?
Watching the Silver Dragon roar furiously to no avail, Barrett finally realized he had underestimated the situation.
After all, it was a dragon with combat power comparable to level nine!
Such a feat was beyond even an old eighth-tier like him to hunt.
He had initially thought these young people just wanted to try.
Young folks, having such courage and determination is precious.
He didn't mind risking his old bones to shield them from storm and stress.
If it doesn't work out, they could still retreat.
But unexpectedly, it wasn't just about courage; from the beginning, the Dawn Group actually had the capability to hunt a giant dragon!
A feat that three ten-thousand-person magic groups couldn't accomplish, this small Dawn Group had managed?
Watching this, Barrett's eyes shone with lingering glimmer through his dim pupils.
While incredulous, he looked at Su Lun and others with eyes full of relief.
The era of the old-age adventurers had passed, and a new era had arrived.
The light of hope at dawn was shining brightly on them.
They would write their own legendary stories.

chapters.title: Chapter 550 - 549: Bountiful Harvest
chapters.content:
The combat capabilities of an eighth-tier pure-blooded giant dragon were truly fierce. Even though the Dawn Squad had an extensive dragon-hunting plan beforehand, the actual confrontation was still perilous.
The silver dragon's hide was thick and its flesh tough. Originally, when it was in the King's City Aike-Lansa, a group of ten thousand mages hammered at it for a long time without managing to kill it, and now facing it as the Dawn Squad was no less challenging.
No one could kill it in a short amount of time, not even Bartholomew, who bore the title "Dragon Hunter."
Fortunately, though Su Lun and his team were few in number, they had Dragon Slaying Potions which could break through dragon scales and cause real damage.
That, too, met the basic conditions for "blood grinding."
The mechanical octopus had locked onto the back of the silver dragon, where Su Lun and the "Blood Duke" Vasquez performed various acrobatic vampire-suction on the dragon's back. The pure-blooded giant dragon's blood contained extremely rich energy and essence of life, the more they absorbed, the better they felt.
However, the process was extremely dangerous.
Although the dragon's back was a blind spot for claws and biting, the dragon breath from the silver dragon could still scorch them.
Any contact with it, if not fatal, would lead to severe injury.
Fortunately, the dragon breath had intervals and pre-release signs like swelling of the throat, which, if watched carefully, gave them just a moment to escape.
The two sucked blood while observing, and whenever the silver dragon showed signs of spewing its dragon breath, they quickly slipped off its back and fled far away. Then, after the dragon breath was expelled, they found an opportunity to continue sucking blood.
This cycle repeated itself.
The blood grinding process was akin to dancing on the blade of a knife, where half a point of error was not permitted; any slight misstep could lead to catastrophic consequences.
The battle continued in this fashion.
...
Unknowingly, the sky had completely darkened, the night fell, and the stars dotted the sky.
Angry dragon roars echoed through the heavens, occasionally a burst of Holy Light dragon breath lit up the sky, revealing several figures of people and the fuming silver dragon on a few mountains.
The process of "blood grinding" was a battle of attrition for both sides, which was a prolonged affair.
Fortunately, the members of the Dawn Squad cooperated tacitly, and the whole process was conducted without mistakes.
With Nineteen and Bartholomew holding the front, with Su Lun and Vasquez at the back.
Chian and Barrett found opportunities on the side to restrain the dragon.
The battle from the start was intensely fierce.
For the members of the Dawn Squad, this was not just a fierce battle but also a rare opportunity.
Actual combat was always the best shortcut to improving one's strength.
Although the silver dragon had the strength of a ninth-tier, it was still not a true ninth-tier.
And dragons, being the most perfect high-order creatures in low-tier planes, had an exceptional life-level oppressive force known as Dragon's Majesty, which they had found during their previous hunt of the Thunder Dragon, incredibly effective for the growth of their Dominance Aura.
Battling with a giant dragon, the insight gained from the fight was incomparable to fighting with fellow humans of the same tier.
And for Dawn Squad members like Su Lun and Chian, ordinary enemies could no longer pose a real mortal threat to them. Such enemies were hard to come by.
Just as it was now.
Dominance Aura is the air of tyranny that grows stronger in the presence of stronger foes.
Under the heavy pressure of Dragon's Majesty, the Dominance Aura of people participating in the dragon hunt continuously refined, visibly becoming more substantial.
The eighth-tier silver dragon presented a life-or-death pressure comparable to that of a whetstone for sharpening blades. The process of sharpening was agonizing, but once endured, the blade would become sharper and sharper.
There were three seventh-tier individuals present—Su Lun, Chian, and Barrett.
The disparity of their higher tiers also subjected these three to more terrific pressure.
Su Lun was better off; he had powerful Spatial Displacement abilities and Dragon Slayer armor, and he was not directly engaged in combat, so the danger wasn't too great.
Barrett, wearing the "Gracie's Heavy Dragon Rider Armor," though a bit cumbersome, fortunately had amazing defensive power and was not seriously injured despite being hit multiple times.
But Chian, who fought at the front, was in a bad situation.
She wore a bright red armor, which was the "Iron Red Scaled Armor" obtained from the Mountain Hermit Nation. Although of outstanding quality, it was still a light armor designed for agility favored by Guarding Swordsmen and wasn't sufficient against the defenses posed by the eighth-tier pure-blooded giant dragon. It had been heavily damaged after numerous severe blows.
At that moment, Chian's forehead was bloodied, and her body bore marks from being scorched by dragon breath.
Despite being seriously injured, at this moment, everyone, including Su Lun, was planning to urge her to withdraw.
Because at this moment, everyone was stunned by the extraordinary phenomenon that appeared on her!
Behind Chian, the three-headed Rakshasa Woman deity was glowing brilliantly, like flames flowing several meters around. The binding rope of her hair had burst, and her blue hair, with no wind stirring, rose up like flames, just like the Rakshasa phantom behind her.
What was even more mysterious, the Dominance Aura seeping from her body merged with the divine presence of the phantom, subtly contending with the Dragon's Majesty on equal footing.
She was fearlessly confronting the Silver Dragon, relying on the Rakshasa Woman in her third release form.
This state had appeared once before in the "Netherworld," and Su Lun had noticed that she seemed to have fallen into that profound state of insight again.
The stronger the enemy she faced, the stronger the Rakshasa Woman became, growing rapidly in battle.
The closer to death she was in battle, the clearer that sense of growth and enlightenment became.
This was the passive potential inherent in the "A-022-Rakshasa Woman" talent itself.
The talent of the third release was shrouded in mystery, considered "taboo" even by those on Su Lun's harvesting planes of the gods.
This was not a realm accessible to mortals but to deities.
In the perfected planes of the gods, it was said that one in a billion with excellent talent could release their talent thrice, in mortal form. Yet, those individuals invariably became top-tier powerhouses with a divine stature.
Su Lun did not understand what the third release of talent meant, but there was a saying in the planes of the gods that it was regarded as the reincarnation of a deity.
At this moment, Qian Jiao had the semblance of a hellish Rakshasa.
So, even though Qian Jiao was severely injured, nobody suggested she retreat, knowing well it was futile.
This state of self-forgetfulness was a grand opportunity that came from flirting with the line between life and death.
And at that moment, Qian Jiao's momentum had reached its peak after being blasted away once again.
She injected herself with a strong healing potion and charged again.
As she swung her blade, everyone seemed to hear a celestial chant echoing beside their ears: "I see the evil ghosts of all beings in hell, all forms are my forms... With my sword drawn, I can slay the gods and demons of heaven, and even the celestial dragons!"
It was at the exact moment this echoing voice rang out that a mixed aura of good and evil began winding through the air.
On one side was the merciful golden light, on the other, the infernal blood light.
In an instant, remarkable phenomena suddenly arose between heaven and earth.
The thunderclouds in the sky suddenly converged, thousands of lightning serpents gathered above the Demon Blade, making the blade's edge seem to unveil an endlessly terrifying scene of hell.
With one strike, the tyrannical Sword Qi cut across hundreds of meters, clanging against the silver dragon's neck scales, and with a "sizzle," it carved a bloody mark.
Su Lun and others watched, dumbfounded.
They never expected Qian Jiao to have drawn blood on the dragon's neck scales, the toughest part of a dragon's body, with only Sword Qi?
Though the wound was not large, to have struck the body of a dragon, comparable to a ninth-tier, with a seventh-tier sword, Qian Jiao was the only one seen to have achieved such a feat.
Barrett's murky eyes flashed fiercely, his heart trembling uncontrollably: "Truly a supreme talent..."
Only the Old Sword God understood the changes in Qian Jiao's Sword Intent at that moment better than anyone else. This was precisely the "Rule-Cutting Realm" he had taught before, which meant that this sword had already broken through the Saint Realm, touching the threshold of what was called the Sword God Realm.
Not only had she grasped the essence of the Godly Path of No Thought style, but she also had her unique Sword Dao.
This sword had made people witness the hellish scene in her eyes.
Barrett watched and once again exclaimed, "Such a profound understanding of the sword heart!"
...
In the battle, Qian Jiao seemed to have suddenly understood a new realm of Sword Dao, her momentum still rising.
The more she fought, the braver she became, and she was even able to directly confront the giant dragon alongside Barrett and Number Nineteen.
Correspondingly, her injuries also increased.
Luckily, Barrett and the others coordinated tacitly, fighting the dragon while also distracting and covering for Qian Jiao, allowing her to continue gaining insights in this state without falling into a fatal situation.
The sky was a flurry of action, and on the sea, the Eternal Night was also battling fiercely with a host of sea beasts, with cannons thundering through the pitch-black night.
The silver dragon had paid the price for its arrogance again. It knew it was facing the same near-death situation as before when it was besieged in the city of Aikelunsa.
It just had not expected that just a few humans could corner it into dire straits.
And due to the presence of the Dragon Slaying Potion, which prevented the dragon's super-strong self-healing talent, the physical condition of the silver dragon was deteriorating.
At this moment, the silver dragon no longer had the contempt it had before, its angry roars trying to summon nearby sea creatures for help. Unfortunately, during the previous siege of a thousand mages, most of the magical sea monsters in this area had been decimated. Now, a dragon struggling for survival was much less menacing, and the more intelligent sea creatures knew to keep their distance.
Even as some monsters still pursued, those aboard the Eternal Night, relying on the robust ship and powerful cannons, immediately kept the monsters from advancing on the sea surface, preventing them from disturbing the battle in the skies.
...
Only through first-hand combat did they realize how tenacious the life of an eighth-tier giant dragon was.
The Dawn Circle had been bleeding the dragon for one or two hours, and only then did the dragon's flailing wings begin to weaken.
Except for Su Lun, who still had the robust combat capabilities from "Isaac's Alchemy Heart," almost everyone was drained and exhausted.
Such a high-intensity battle was simply beyond the endurance of ordinary people.
Fortunately, the scales of victory still tipped toward the Dawn group, as the Dragon Slayer Potion prevented the Silver Dragon's wounds from healing, allowing the "Blood Grinding Tactic" to ultimately succeed.
At last, a mournful dragon's cry echoed through the sky, and the Silver Dragon, having lost too much blood, fell from the sky.
Su Lun, quick-eyed and deft-handed, firmly bound the Silver Dragon with mechanical ropes and stuffed it into the mini void realm in one go.
The night sky returned to silence, and this battle finally came to a close.
Above the sea, with the Silver Dragon's defeat, the monsters also receded like the tide and disappeared in the blink of an eye.
Cheers erupted from everyone on the Eternal Night.
Su Lun turned his head to see that everyone who had participated in the battle had more or less sustained injuries.
Number 19's mechanical body was damaged in several parts, but after replacement, there was a new Number 19; Bartolo's left ulna was broken by the Silver Dragon and he probably needed a few days of recovery; Wazwas had several exaggerated blood holes torn through his abdomen, but fortunately, as a vampire, he could recover by feeding on blood, a bit of vital energy was lost, but it was not serious; Barrett was wearing armor and seemed to have no major external injuries, but had multiple internal damages, also quite seriously injured; even the mechanical octopus was severely damaged and probably needed a major factory overhaul...
But the one most severely injured was Chien Tiao.
Her whole body was covered in wounds.
Only when the battle ended did she relax her tense nerves, her Rakshasa phantom dissipating as she returned from that frenzied state to normal.
Having fought a burst of sustained aerial combat, she was utterly exhausted, and the moment she sighed in relief, she drunkenly fell from the sky.
Number 19, quick and responsive, flapped its wings and instantly flew a hundred meters to catch Chien Tiao, who was falling.
A few of them landed on the sea surface, panting heavily, and exchanged smiles with each other.
Although exhaustion was evident on everyone's faces, the gains from this battle were immense. Hunting this eighth-tier giant dragon was a tremendous opportunity for the team, and for everyone involved, it was a battle experience worth remembering for a lifetime.
During the fight, they were only amazed at Chien Tiao's breakthrough in realm. Now that everyone had come back to their senses, they realized they all had significant insights from this battle.
Having climbed the peak, that mountain no longer required looking up to.
It was not just advances in realm understanding; this eighth-tier Silver Dragon brought many substantial benefits to everyone.
This was another top-tier material for fabricating breed suits.
And as Dr. Banks put it, the higher the dragon's tier, the more refined its dragon blood genes, and the higher its research value.
With this Silver Dragon, the "Dragon Blood Gene Potion" would likely become a reality in the not-so-distant future, providing another qualitative leap for everyone in the Dawn group.
After catching their breaths, expressions of victorious joy gradually surfaced on their faces.
There were no casualties, which was the greatest fortune.
Until the battle ended, Bartolo was still in disbelief; had they really hunted an eighth-tier pure-blooded giant dragon?
This must have been the most powerful dragon hunted by mankind in a thousand years.
The Dawn group had created another miracle.
Su Lun's thread was the best surgical method, and as soon as he landed, he began treating Chien Tiao's horrific wounds, where white bones were clearly visible.
As the thread stitched the wounds, the blood instantly stopped flowing and also prevented the wounds from worsening.
Chien Tiao winced slightly in pain and, seeing that she appeared more ragged than anyone else, muttered, "Ah, my body is still too weak."
At her words, everyone couldn't help but twitch the corners of their eyes, only the onlookers knew how fierce she had been just now.
Barrett couldn't help but laugh and cry, self-deprecatingly saying, "If Miss Chien Tiao's body is weak, then all my muscle is just gained for nothing."
As he spoke, he couldn't help but cough up a mouthful of blood, but the smile on his lips remained.
Both seventh-tier, facing the same opponent, he truly envied her. Chien Tiao's strength was not as frail as her self-mockery suggested. The terror of her sword, only those who experienced it firsthand could understand.
Number 19 also exclaimed, "Indeed. Sister Chien Tiao is very powerful."
Bartolo finally had a chance to speak, laughing, "Your talents truly amaze this old man. Not only did you touch the threshold above the Saint Realm, but you also touched the eighth-tier 'Dominant Body.' These wounds are not bad things. Once you completely grasp the insights from the previous battle, and advance your realm one major step..."
Su Lun was used to it by now; where was he not familiar with this gambling woman's nature? Mr. Jing had said before that Chien Tiao's sword heart was clear, her Rakshasa Woman talent seemed more like an instinct than a conscious layer, fighting and breaking through.
He was certain that this gambling woman had no awareness of what she had just done.
"Huh?"
Chien Tiao, hearing everyone speaking this way, showed a confused expression.
She recalled with rolling eyes and seemed to have no awareness of what she had just experienced.
Seeing her expression, everyone laughed lightly.
But this was not the place to talk; after simply stitching up the fatal wounds, Su Lun signaled everyone, "Let's go, we'll talk back on the ship."
...
Su Lun and his team returned to the Eternal Night, where the group members also cheered and rejoiced, celebrating another grand victory created by the Dawn group.
However, the celebration would have to wait, as they had something even more important to do right now.
That was to collect the spoils of war.
Far away on the icy expanse lay the corpses of three ten-thousand-man Mages teams, alongside countless magical beast materials—a fortune worth a fortune indeed.
The previous battlefield where they fought the Silver Dragon spanned dozens of kilometers, strewn with the corpses of magical beasts, and the people of Dawn Team excitedly recovered everything along the way.
Soon, the ship returned to the frozen sea shore, and over ten thousand members disembarked to loot the bodies.
The cold night wind could not dampen their enthusiasm as they searched the bloody battlefield for various corpses.
The Mages from the Divine Realm were wealthy, and it was the first time Dawn Team had harvested spoils from three full ten-thousand-man teams.
Before long, the deck of the Evernight was piled high with various treasures.
Magic Wand, magic robes, Magic Books, Crystal Ball, Magic Scrolls, gemstones of various colors, materials...
There were several extremely powerful legion magical devices, like the "Banished Sky Realm" that had confined Su Lun previously, the "Stalker's Cloak of Night" that the legions used to hide their traces, and the powerful "Energy Gathering Thunder Tower"...
These legion magical devices were mostly infused with Divine Power, making them ineffective for Alchemists. However, Mountain Dwarves from the Minor Void Realm were adept at forging and could repurpose some of them. Even if they could not be used, the top-grade materials harvested from dismantling these devices were still top-tier.
Then there were the countless monster corpses. These bodies were not just materials but also provided enough genetic samples for Dr. Banks' biological laboratory.
Indeed, as long as they won, it was always a huge profit.
Not only did they recover the money spent on ammunition, but they also earned hundreds, thousands of times more!
The material storage in the Minor Void Realm was now mountain-high, and Dawn Team members hardly lacked high-level materials anymore, whether for advancing or creating clones.
It wouldn't be an exaggeration to say they became overnight millionaires.
The Dawn Team fell into the joy of a bountiful harvest.
...
The task of organizing and counting the spoils was left to the crew, as Su Lun and the other high-ranking fighters had endured a fierce Dragon Slaying battle and were in dire need of rest and recuperation. They each retired to their own rooms to recover and meditate as soon as they boarded the ship.
Su Lun and Thousand Pieces returned to the Captain's quarters, treated their injuries, and immediately began meditating.
Thousand Piece had to grasp the rare combat insights, and Su Lun also reaped huge gains.
It wasn't just those fleeting combat insights, the Soul Shards of those thirty thousand Mages and countless monsters were tangible gains.
It was his first time absorbing so many high-quality souls; he needed a lot of time to assimilate them.
Once assimilated, there would certainly be a significant improvement.
The members of Dawn Team quickly reviewed the battlefield and did not dare to linger.
They were well aware that after annihilating three ten-thousand-man teams, those guys on the Divine Realm would surely not let things go, and waiting for reinforcements might lead to complications.
Evernight then changed its course and quietly disappeared into the night.
...
Shortly after Dawn Team's departure, a Mage clad in a black robe appeared on the icy expanse where the battle had taken place.
Though he had rushed here responding to the distress call, he was still too late.
Looking at the traces of the battle on the ice, where not even a single body was left behind, he softly clicked his tongue, "These natives are truly cautious, to even have disposed of the bodies."
The Cloaked Mage walked across the ice, growing more solemn with each step, seemingly searching for some clues.
However, after a long walk, he found no clues but, surprisingly, muttered to himself, "Not even a Soul Shard left behind. It seems it really is that legendary talent."
Seeing no point in continuing his search, the Mage raised his pitch-black Magic Wand and began chanting a magic spell: "Great God of Necromancy above, I reverently pronounce Your name, please grant Your emissary the power to summon the dead..."
As the spell was chanted, soon with "crack" and "crack" noises, several ice-enshrouded Mage corpses struggled and crawled out from beneath the ice.
The corpses' eye sockets burned with a strange green fire, and they shakily approached the robed figure.
The robed figure actually asked the corpses, "Tell me, what happened."
But what was even more bizarre came next.
At that moment, the green fire swirling in the eyes of the corpses seemed to narrate something.
The robed figure listened to the corpse murmurs, seemingly understanding them, and incredulously muttered to himself, "A Silver Dragon came?"
In that instant, he realized what had happened.
He could never have imagined that the seemingly foolproof ambush plan had failed in such a bizarre way.

chapters.title: Chapter 551 - 550 Golden Sea
chapters.content:
Ten days later.
On the boundless sea, a giant ship with black sails was sailing.
In the captain's cabin, Su Lun was meditating when suddenly a flash of golden light from outside the window dazzled him into opening his eyes.
Looking at the brilliant sunlight outside the window, he felt compelled to walk over and looked through the glass to see a sea of dazzling golden waves.
"So we've already reached the Golden Sea..."
Seeing the enchanting golden ocean outside the window, Su Lun mentally calculated the journey and guessed their current position in the Dawn Group.
This area was marked as the "Golden Sea" on the map of Dragon Country Waters. Because the sea contained a type of golden seaweed, the sunlight reflecting off the water made it gleam like a sea of liquid gold.
This was a spectacular sight not seen elsewhere.
The golden light filled the cabin, making every piece of furniture look as if it had been coated in a layer of gold paint.
Just then, a lazy voice rang out in the room, "Eh, where have we arrived now?"
"The Golden Sea."
Su Lun replied, and then added, "In about two or three more days, we will reach the Old Dragon Kingdom Ruins, which is a truly dangerous sea area."
In the past days, he and Mr. Hei in the little void realm had thoroughly studied all the documents and records they had robbed from the Silver Dragon Royalty, and almost confirmed many details about dangerous sea areas according to what Bartolo had said. Along the way, they had frequently encountered danger.
Indeed, they were about to reach the "Old Dragon Kingdom Ruins."
After hunting the desk Silver Dragon, Su Lun and his team did not continue to track the magical flying castle.
Because there wasn't much significance in following it.
Having wiped out three ten-thousand-member groups before, they reckoned the next encounter would be prepared and risky.
Without the external force of a Silver Dragon, the current Dawn Group didn't possess the strength to face tens of thousands in a magic battalion.
Following them further wouldn't have been advantageous.
Thus, changing the course and avoiding them was the best choice.
Moreover, those beings from the Angel realms came to the Dragon Country Waters to search for the "Mimir's Spring."
Su Lun knew where the spring was located. With the map of Dragon Country, Bartolo as a guide who had visited the ruins, and Tanni along with his mother Frida, two members with absolute navigational help, the chances of finding the spring were very high.
If they could successfully intercept it, it would not only foil the plans of those from the Angel realm but be even more effective than wiping them out.
So these days, the Dawn had been sailing along the route once taken by the Black Sam pirate crew, traveling all the way here.
Upon hearing this, Tanni showed no change in expression.
She lazily stretched herself, her chest unrestrained also shivered, and she invited Su Lun, "Shall we go up on deck for some fresh air?"
Su Lun, slightly surprised, a glint of anticipation flashed in his eyes, asked, "Sister Tanni, have you broken through?"
Since their last hunt for the Silver Dragon, Tanni had been in seclusion.
For someone as restless as her to stay indoors, it was unexpected for her to want to go out today.
It must have been a breakthrough.
Listening, her eyebrows slightly raised. She knew he was asking about her Sword Saint realm, but that description wasn't quite right. She found it too troublesome to explain and simply responded, "Not yet. Just a bit of insight."
"Oh."
Su Lun shrugged, figuring it wasn't easy to make a breakthrough after all.
Thinking he hadn't been on deck for several days either, he said, "Let's go, take a look."
Tanni also stood up, took off her swordsman's robe, walked to the mirror, and started wrapping her chest with bandages, her mouth pursed as if she felt it was troublesome to bind her chest whenever going out.
She wrapped the bandages while glancing in the mirror at Su Lun, who showed keen interest but didn't mind his gaze, and asked, "By the way, has Dr. Banks succeeded in developing the 'Thunder Dragon Bloodline Potion'?"
"Not yet."
Su Lun shook his head and added, "But it should be soon. The lab said they are already performing sample experiments."
He knew Tanni asked about the genetic potion because she naturally wanted to integrate it into her armor.
The seventh-rank lightning blue dragon they hunted before in the Dawn Group had already been made into an armor called "Isaac's Dragon-patterned Golden Body - Thunder Dragon."
However, because the main material is pure-blood blue dragon, the produced implant ranks very high. Even though Qiantiao inherently possesses a substantial affinity for lightning, there's still a high possibility of mutation during fusion.
Under normal circumstances, she might only have a chance of successful integration when she reaches the eighth order.
Fortunately, within the Dawn Group, there is a top-tier biological magician today in the plane of alchemy, providing a shortcut for this fusion.
Just waiting for the genetic potion to be successfully developed, she could, just like her fifth order integration with "Void Hand," upgrade this legendary implant.
This method of high-grade implanting would give an alchemist incomparable advantages in combat power compared to their peers.
Upon hearing this, Qiantiao's reflection in the mirror looked slightly regretful as she grumbled, "Oh, that's a pity. I was thinking about integrating a seventh order implant to see what an eighth order Dominator's Bodyguard is really like. After the battle with that silver dragon last time, I vaguely touched upon some deep insights into Dominator's Bodyguard. These past few days, I've had some ideas during meditation, but I'm not sure if they're correct, as my body's strength isn't sufficient to support my thoughts..."
"..."
Su Lun couldn't help but twitch the corner of her eye.
She had already grasped the insights of the eighth order Dominator's Bodyguard?
Just like when she previously thought that understanding realms had no threshold, these words always gave off an invisible air of show-off.
However, Su Lun was also filled with pride and anticipation.
Qiantiao's strength wasn't solely based on her talent; it was also the result of her relentless effort step by step.
But Qiantiao herself seemed to have no strong feelings about her own exaggerated progress, her expression still calm. She had already wrapped her chest bandage and hung her sword at her waist.
The two of them then walked out.
...
At this moment, the deck of the Eternal Night was bustling.
"Wow... I've got three more golden shells! Haha, I'm the group's 'Number One Lucky Star'!"
"You're not really, Miss Number Nineteen is our ship's 'First Lucky Angel'!"
"Oh, of course, how could I compare myself with Captain Number Nineteen."
"..."
This Golden Sea not only has golden seaweed but many shellfish that feed on the seaweed, giving them beautifully golden shells.
Though not high in gold content, those golden shells and conches are natural works of art. If really brought back to Luying Mafa for auction, they might fetch a price not any cheaper than real gold.
The crew was also enthusiastically salvaging in the sea, which counted as a little fun during the voyage.
Su Lun and Qiantiao had just come out when they heard First Navigator Tanni's voice through the ship's loudspeaker, "Everyone be careful, we've just passed Giant Elephant Island, and the territory of the Titan Sea Monsters is ahead, there could be many large deep-sea monsters..."
Everyone turned their heads to see Tanni in the helm.
However, his warning did not make the atmosphere aboard heavy, instead, the crew members laughed and teased him.
"Hahaha, are we going to improve the meal tonight? Captain Tanni, it's up to you to spot those sea monsters. Leave the rest to us 'Whaling Team'!"
"Oh, our 'Artillery Team' just got new equipment online, we need a big monster to test the firepower. If any monster that doesn't see the light attacks the ship, let us take care of it..."
"We can't let you Artillery guys take action! Last time, the prey shot by the cannon tasted like gunpowder, such a waste..."
"Don't just think about eating, guys. Our colleagues in the lab said they need samples, better to catch a few alive!"
"..."
Everyone chatted and laughed, the ship filled with cheerful voices.
The battles over the years had strengthened the cohesion of the Dawn Group, and the members coordinated more and more tacitly. For them, who had already hunted two pure-blood giant dragons, it seemed nothing was too difficult anymore.
So much so that even facing powerful sea monsters, they only thought about the addition of rare ingredients to their dinner, not the risks.
Everyone had an inexplicable confidence that, facing difficulties, they as the Dawn Group united, would definitely overcome them.
....
The fresh sea breeze was refreshing on their faces.
Su Lun and Qiantiao reached the deck, just in time to hear their companions discussing what to hunt for dinner.
At that moment, Lolo Tata, practicing slicing the wind on the mast, sharply noticed the two emerging, and her expression instantly brightened; she leaped down to the deck.
She seemed to want to startle Su Lun and Qiantiao, but both were unexpressive.
Lolo Tata's momentarily boring expression due to not scaring anyone suddenly turned expectant again, her pure eyes flitting with mischief as she indirectly probed, "Teacher, you've been secluded for so long, everyone says you're about to break through from Sword Saint to Sword God..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun irritably knocked her forehead with the scabbard, "It's too early! You, girl, don't understand your own Sword Intent and just blindly cause a ruckus every day..."
"Ouch, teacher, why are you hitting my head again?"
Lolota touched her forehead, pouting and complaining in a mournful tone, "Mr. Hei said that being hit on the head all the time can make a person stupid."
As she spoke, she cast a furtive glance at Su Lun beside her and revealed a mischievously sneaky smile.
Su Lun couldn't help but smirk.
At that moment in their conversation, as they walked onto the deck, the crew members greeted them enthusiastically, "Mr. Su Lun, Sister Qian Tiao!"
The crowd gathered around, chattering away, and of course, the most frequent question was whether Qian Tiao had ascended to become a Sword Saint.
Qian Tiao explained somewhat helplessly; the realm above Saint Realm was difficult to describe, and the so-called Sword Saint realm was too vague. She indeed touched a little threshold of the slashing rules, but that slight understanding couldn't be articulated in words.
And coincidentally, probably because the noise was too loud, it disturbed the sea monster underwater.
Just then, with a splashing sound, a tentacle suddenly emerged from the distant sea surface.
Someone excitedly shouted, "Wow, just talking about a sea demon, and a sea demon shows up!"
The crew, who initially thought it was a giant eel and were already deciding whether to grill or slice it for sushi, took another look.
But upon closer inspection, countless tentacles emerged from the sea.
It turned out not to be an eel but an ugly, tumorous tentacle monster. It had the characteristic multi-jawed mouths of hellish creatures and massive compound eyes that gave anyone the chills.
In comparison to its bloated tumorous body, the tentacles were very slender, like red threads.
No matter how you looked at it, this was not a normal creature but a mutated irregular monster.
Su Lun frowned as he identified it as a "Mutated Hell Titan Ghost Snake (Sixth Order Silver)."
The crew members, who had earlier been keen on hunting sea creatures for food, now looked quite uneasy.
"Ah... this sea demon is really ugly. Can we even eat this thing?"
"Is there some kind of mutation source nearby? Otherwise, why would there be mutated creatures? It looks like a legendary creature from hell..."
"Yes. If such a huge monster is mutated, the source of the pollution must be complex. We need to be careful."
"...."
Many of the people in the Dawn Group were from Old Lington, and they were all too familiar with mutations.
Seeing the grotesquely shaped monster in front of them, they immediately thought of the source of the mutation.
Su Lun frowned too, his mind also leaping to this concern.
It did not surprise him that there were mutated hell creatures in the sea.
Bartolomeo had mentioned that deep within the Old Dragon Kingdom Ruins, there were numerous hell creatures and mutated beings.
However, that creature should be hundreds of miles to the far west, so why had it appeared near the Golden Sea?
Before he could think further, the tentacle monster moved its tentacles as if they were seaweed, clearly looking to trouble the Dawn Group.
Due to its Titan lineage, the creature was huge with many tentacles underwater.
The sea surface churned with waves, clearly from the moving tentacles.
The Dawn Group, previously eager to hunt sea monsters for their flesh, looked disgusted and no one was keen on diving into the sea anymore. However, the Artilleryman had prepared, ready to fire at the ugly creature.
But just then, Qian Tiao blurted out, "So ugly!"
The moment her words fell, a domineering Sword Qi surged skyward on the deck.
Hearing the sharp clank of a sword being drawn, it seemed as if a flash of cold light had dashed past before their eyes.
But on closer inspection, all that could be seen was her slowing motion of sheathing the sword.
At that moment, a wave of air only then belatedly swept across, rustling the robes of everyone on deck.
Su Lun, with his keen sight, caught her action and muttered to himself, "As expected, she has grown stronger again."
Looking again, it was like a sliver of space had been torn apart by the rushing Sword Qi across the deck, heading straight for the monster.
If one looked from the side, they would see that it was a crescent Sword Qi. The Sword Qi grew larger and larger after leaving the blade, eventually stretching dozens of meters long.
A few hundred meters away, the sea monster that hadn't yet started its rampage bore a line of blood across one of its compound eyes. Then, with a "swoosh," blood splattered everywhere as half of its head slid off, revealing a clean, smooth cut.
One strike, and it burst open in scarlet!
Seeing this, everyone on deck was stunned for a moment before bursting into intense cheers.
"Wow, Sister Qiantiao is so amazing!"
"That sword was too terrifying—she killed such a powerful creature without even charging up!"
"My goodness, Sister Qiantiao—Is this the realm beyond that of a Sword Saint?"
"..."
Everyone discussed excitedly.
Even Su Lun thought it was very impressive.
A casual strike, and a sixth-tier silver-level monster was slain. It really was astonishing.
At least the previous Qiantiao would never have managed it so effortlessly.
Moreover, Su Lun noticed something else: that strike of Sword Qi wasn't merely a physical slash. It seemed to be some higher form of destruction.
Otherwise, the energy fluctuations he observed wouldn't have been enough to cut such a colossal creature in two.
After not drawing her sword for so many days, Qiantiao, with her temperament, must have felt very pent up. She had casually swung her sword just now. But looking at the result, she slightly furrowed her brows, seemingly not quite satisfied—as if something was lacking.
....
The monster was slain before it could even begin its attack, leaving the crew of the Dawn Circle with no spectacle to enjoy.
Some of them took small boats out to the sea to fish up some pieces of the corpse.
It wasn't edible, but they could disassemble it for cursed materials and keep some samples for the biological lab.
Su Lun and Qiantiao stood at the ship's railing, watching everyone busy themselves. At that moment, they heard soft footsteps.
Su Lun turned around, smiled, and called out, "Senior Bartolo, you've arrived."
Bartolo smiled and nodded, then turned to look at Qiantiao, whom he hadn't seen in ten days, and once again expressed his admiration, "That strike just now was truly impressive. Using intent to break through the laws suits your Sword Dao very well."
Qiantiao listened with a face full of respect, "Thank you also for your guidance before, senior."
Towards this senior who had directed her Sword Dao multiple times, she honestly expressed her doubts and asked for advice, "Senior, when I made that cut, it felt as if something was resisting me, preventing me from cutting downward. Otherwise, the power of that strike should have been even greater."
Bartolo responded with a complex smile, "That was the backlash of the laws of nature. Once your power reaches a certain limit, you'll find that the laws start to repel you because you are gradually beginning to comprehend 'their' essence. Normally, someone of your rank wouldn't understand or come into contact with this, so your confusion is understandable. Once you advance to the eighth rank, you will understand."
Qiantiao didn't know if she fully understood, her face thoughtful.
Su Lun certainly didn't understand.
But he did understand that Qiantiao's strike held a power that exceeded the limit of her current rank.
However, after the two discussed Sword Dao, Su Lun pointed at a distant piece of the distorted monster's corpse and asked, "Senior, I remember you saying hellspawn creatures were supposed to be further west. Is it normal for them to appear here?"
The Dragon Country Waters were a highly dangerous area, and Su Lun didn't dare to be careless.
It was better to understand any abnormalities.
"That's what I found strange too,"
Bartolo responded with a puzzled expression, pondering for a moment before replying, "More than twenty years ago when we first came here, we had to travel a few hundred nautical miles further west before encountering hellspawn aberrations. Plus, that boundary is very clear because hellspawn aberrations only live where the hellish aura is thick, increasingly so the higher their rank. That boundary forms a large circle, which doesn't even reach as far as this part of the Golden Sea."
Su Lun immediately understood, and asked in return, "So you mean the hellish aura has spread over here?"
Bartolo nodded, "That's the only possibility. Probably there was another eruption at the Hell Volcano deep within the ruins, causing the hellish aura to spread and the monsters' territory to expand outward."
Pondering for a moment, his gaze grew solemn as he added, "Which means...we're actually entering the most dangerous area starting now."
"Yes."
Su Lun listened, his eyes also becoming a bit more serious.
Though they were following the route used by Black Sam's team nearly thirty years ago, many maritime environments had changed since then, such as this aberration appearing in the periphery.
Which meant that even if they went the same way in, they would encounter many unpredictable dangers.
From now on, the real test had begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 552 - 551: The Red Robed Archmage
chapters.content:
Several days later.
The sky was drizzling.
Marked on the map of the Dragon Country Waters as "Troll Sea," which had a danger level of three skulls.
Thirty years ago, when the Black Sam Pirates had passed through these waters, they encountered some Titan-blooded trolls of enormous size. These monsters were terrifyingly strong and could easily lift a three-masted ship with their bare hands.
They were still around.
However, they had mutated into even more terrifying distortion zombies, and there were quite a few of them.
The Dawn Squad sailed into these waters as if entering the den of some monster.
Without warning, the monsters threw rocks from an island, drawing in numerous other creatures from the surroundings for combat.
Cannon fire resounded over the sea, echoing dozens of miles away.
"Fire support! Fire two volleys!"
"Quick, there are monsters approaching from the sea, deploy the whaling team to take them out before they damage the ship!"
"Service squad, pay attention to divert the newly attracted monsters on the periphery, focus our fire first and take down that ugly big fellow!"
"..."
Aboard the Eternal Night, the crew was engaged in a fierce battle.
Suddenly, the lookout on the crow's nest issued a frantic warning, "Careful, incoming rocks!"
No sooner had those words fallen than dozens of rocks, each several meters in diameter, shot over from a nearby island like torrential rain.
The whistling sound of the rocks cutting through the air was like meteors, terrifying in their force.
Just as the rain of stones was about to strike the Eternal Night, Lo-Lot and a group of swordsmen leaped up from the deck. Together, they drew their swords and swiftly formed a net of Sword Qi in the sky.
In an instant, the incoming boulders were sliced into countless smaller pieces.
Although most of the stone chunks fell into the sea, some the size of watermelons still densely pelted the hull, banging on it like cannonballs.
This kind of firepower, launching dozens of ten-ton stone balls like cannonballs, was utterly impossible for humans.
But for the 300-meter-tall, eighth-order lord, the Titan Zombie, it was just a handful of "small stones."
Indeed, it was 300 meters tall.
The creature was even more massive than the hull of the Eternal Night!
On a distant island, Su Lun, Qian Tiao, Barrett, and No. 19 among other elite fighters were surrounding and attacking this lord-level distortion zombie.
It was an enlarged troll with a humanoid torso but its head had mutated into a mass of tentacles and pus-filled fox face. Its belly, which yawned open, was filled with densely packed sharp teeth. Besides being able to spit acid that easily melted steel, this belly also acted like a bottomless pit, emitting countless crimson tentacles to devour everything around it. It could even consume cannonballs, Sword Qi, and various types of alchemy.
The battle was intensely fought.
For most monsters, their size was directly proportional to their combat strength.
Their massive bodies granted them monstrous strength and armor-like flesh.
And this Titan Zombie was no different; its 300-meter-tall body possessed strength and an almost unsolvable defense that humans couldn't match.
Because of its massive body, even Su Lun's black scythe and Qian Tiao's Sword Qi slashes on its rotting flesh were barely noticeable.
In terms of "HP," it was not much inferior to an eighth-order silver dragon the Dawn Squad had previously hunted.
However, thankfully, although the monster was high-ranking, it was clumsy and moved on two legs. Compared to the previously encountered dragons that could fly, it was much easier to deal with.
As long as they carefully avoided its attacks, the problem wasn't too big.
After a fierce battle lasting over half an hour, Su Lun and the others finally slew the beast.
With the lord monster dead, the nearby undead creatures quickly dispersed.
...
Cleaning up the battlefield was handled by a specialized disposal squad, and after the big fight, Su Lun and the others returned to the ship.
On the deck, Bartholo looked at the corpse in the distance, his brows still tightly furrowed.
It was not only the melancholy of revisiting an old place but also a hint of solemnity.
Su Lun approached and asked, "Senior, have you noticed anything?"
Barrett had not engaged in the battle earlier, primarily because it was unnecessary, and secondly, because he had a bad feeling about the "Angel of Justice" talent of subject nineteen. All along, he felt as if something was coveting them.
Out of caution, he did not let Barrett, a top-tier combatant, intervene. If something indeed went wrong, they would have a fallback.
Barrett, deep in thought, replied, "Undead creatures usually lack high intelligence. The accumulation of so many monsters nearby attacking us seems unusual."
"Hmm."
Su Lun had also noticed this point.
The density of regional creatures has an upper limit, and they wouldn't gather together without a special reason.
He asked, "Senior, do you think someone has done this intentionally?"
Barrett said, "It might not necessarily be humans. It could also be some special entities. The Old Dragon Kingdom Ruins are said to be the battleground of ancient gods, and too many ancient secrets are buried here. Besides, the eruption of Hell Volcano brings many undead creatures from different dimensions. It's only too normal to encounter things beyond human comprehension."
"..."
Su Lun frowned slightly and said no more.
Since they had killed the deformed monster in the Golden Sea a few days ago, they hadn't had a moment of peace, and the monsters were becoming more numerous.
But if it were just monsters, it would be manageable—they could fight or flee.
What they feared was encountering some "supernatural" entity beyond their understanding.
Just like the swarm of creatures they encountered today, something felt off.
Su Lun glanced again at Mr. Crow on his shoulder, who had not made a sound, indicating that the situation was not yet fatal.
They had come prepared to take risks, so there was nothing to shy away from.
Soon, the crew dealt with the corpses of the monsters, and the Eternal Night continued its voyage.
As a precaution, double watch was set on deck, and some sophisticated energy fluctuation detectors were installed, such as "Sub-Sonic Wave Detectors," "Psychic Sensitivity Instruments," and "Thermal Energy Fluctuation Detectors"... Mafa's research in this area over the years had been extraordinary, and the equipment was now capable of replacing most sensory methods.
Of course, there were also Tanni and his mother Frida.
Multiple safeguards nearly eliminated all possibilities of unwittingly falling into danger.
The workmen also smeared dragon dung on the hull, which deterred some lower-ranking monsters from disturbing them often.
And so they sailed into the night.
.....
After entering the Ancient Dragon Kingdom Ruins, in order to avoid attracting monsters with light, the Eternal Night had not been illuminated at night.
The darkness of the night was not too bright; the black-sailed ship moved across the pitch-black sea, blending into the night like a ghost.
The air had already begun to fill with a faint gray mist, the essence of hell.
It was similar to the dark spiritual power of Old Lington, a type of death-oriented aura. Prolonged inhalation could risk mutations.
However, for Su Lun, this type of aura not only had no adverse effects, but he also found breathing it quite pleasant. The deathly impurities within the aura, he could now easily digest, which was beneficial.
Therefore, he hadn't been cooped up in his cabin practicing but had been wandering on deck at night.
Those on watch, wearing gas masks, greeted him as they saw him.
"Mr. Su Lun!"
"Hmm."
Because of the battle during the day, Su Lun felt something was odd, so after walking around, he didn't return to his cabin but jumped up to the mainmast instead.
On the robust mast, Tanni was meditating.
She had realized the "Thunders of Hell" Sword Intent, inspired by the Netherworld. Now facing real hell aura, she felt an indescribable enlightenment. Moreover, the closer they got to the heart of the Old Dragon Kingdom Ruins, the more refined the natural laws of the world seemed. For the two of them, who could assimilate the hell aura, it was a rare cultivation opportunity.
The two didn't speak but meditated in silence as usual, sitting not far from each other.
Time swiftly passed, and before they knew, it was midnight.
The moon in the sky had already been completely obscured by the dark clouds, and the Evernight, devoid of light, seemed submerged in a pitch-blackness so dense one could hardly discern where the water ended and the night began.
With Tanni as a top-level navigator, there were no worries about hitting a reef, and the Evernight continued to glide smoothly towards its predetermined direction.
Su Lun placed the rune-laden black umbrella on her thigh, her senses extending over the entire ship.
All she could hear was the rushing sound of water.
Suddenly, she opened her eyes wide!
"Has someone come?"
Su Lun was also surprised.
Just now, a strange pulse of a soul had appeared on deck.
Even without using her eyes, Su Lun could now familiarly distinguish the soul of every one of the tens of thousands of members in the group.
That's why she noticed this uninvited guest instantly.
Noticing something amiss, Su Lun opened her eyes to look around.
With just a warning glance, Tanni immediately became alert and opened her eyes.
The two exchanged looks, and she immediately understood, her hand already stealthily resting on the hilt of her sword.
This reaction was because Su Lun had sensed that the newcomer's soul pulse was extremely strong!
It was so strong that she thought it might be some kind of "soul monster" rather than a human.
Even when she had encountered Master Pierre, a ninth-tier mage in Old Lington, his soul had not vibrated with such intensity.
The sudden appearance of someone in these lifeless waters sent a chill up her spine, no matter the circumstances.
"Where did 'he' come from?"
"What does 'he' want to do?"
This guy is clearly so strong, yet he sneaked aboard the ship, which was very odd.
"Eh... he's actually coming straight here?"
However, it didn't take long before Su Lun was even more astonished to find that the guy was heading straight for the mainmast.
She instantly realized that this person seemed to be coming for her?
Being able to pinpoint her location so accurately in the dark, Su Lun thought of a possibility—that the other party could also discern soul strength!
And in the entire Dawn group, her soul was the strongest.
Bartholomew had joked before, saying her soul was as strong as a monster's, indeed.
Thinking of this, Su Lun suddenly had a flash of insight: "Could it be a fellow practitioner who cultivates the soul?"
Sure enough, a few moments later, that soul pulse moved noiselessly to the base of the mainmast, and then "floated" up!
Yes, floated!
Without alarming any sentinels, he had floated up.
Although Su Lun couldn't see the floating figure with her own eyes, Old Crow on top of the mast saw everything clearly.
Old Crow was a raven of death and could see any form of spiritual body.
Su Lun watched with a furrowed brow but decided to strike first.
As the intruder vaulted up, she abruptly drew the rune-laden black umbrella and swung it fiercely behind her.
Simultaneously, there was the metallic clink of a sharp blade being drawn from its scabbard, and Tanni's eyes snapped open as she slashed her sword down.
The rune-laden black umbrella had a special effect—it could strike the soul!
And Tanni's slash could inflict lethal physical damage!
Now the combat prowess of both was considered top-notch among alchemical professionals, and with their well-established coordination, it made evasion impossible for the intruder.
Sure enough, the surprise attack was highly effective!
The sneaky guy initially intended to approach, but did not expect to be greeted by a blade and a club as soon as he arrived.
Su Lun had no idea how his opponent maintained this traceless "invisible" state, undetectable even by spatial perception.
Since his approach did not trigger any response, it meant that "he" was not a physical entity.
It was probably some special kind of magic device.
But at such close distance, Su Lun had confirmed that this was definitely a living person!
An enemy with malicious intent!
As long as it's a person, it can be killed.
At the moment of the outbreak, Qian Tiao's blade moved faster than Su Lun's.
The man probably felt that his abilities could ignore the slashes, so even though he was ambushed, he wasn't much panicked.
Qian Tiao's blade sliced through the void, as if cutting through air, not hitting anything at all.
However, the purpose of this blade was not to harm the enemy, but to keep the enemy in this ghost-like state!
Right after the Sword Qi swept past, Su Lun's rune-imbued black umbrella followed closely.
Then, the miraculous scene unfolded; on the seemingly empty mast, as if something was hit by the rune-imbued black umbrella, a semi-transparent figure immediately appeared.
Su Lun looked on and sneered coldly in his heart.
Just like the first time he encountered the "Curator" and was stunned by his club, the person before him apparently did not expect a weapon that could directly strike at the soul.
As soon as the semi-transparent figure appeared, one could visibly see his expression stiffen in "shock."
Seizing the opportunity, Qian Tiao's freshly slashed sword returned with "swoosh swoosh" over a dozen strokes, cutting the man into more than a dozen pieces with a flurry of domineering sword blossoms.
"Killed?"
Su Lun's hand was still waving in mid-air, but his eyes narrowed slightly.
Because he could distinctly feel the collapse of the opponent's soul, a clear sign of death.
But it shouldn't have been this easy...
Su Lun thought to himself, just planning to reap the enemy's soul to secure the victory when a bizarre scene unfolded before his eyes.
He watched as the soul that had just shattered was suddenly gathered together by an unfathomable force and then appeared hundreds of meters above the sea surface.
Seeing this, Su Lun's pupils suddenly contracted, "Resurrected..."
He wasn't surprised that such a strong enemy couldn't be killed on the first attempt, managing to ambush him was already good enough.
But what was unexpected was that this guy had mastered such a divine technique.
Su Lun himself had been resurrected before, how could he not know that this guy had actually died and then been resurrected?
But looking at the other's attire, he immediately wasn't surprised anymore, muttering to himself, "Archbishop in red from the Angelic Plane Holy Army, an eighth-tier Archmage, no wonder he could borrow divine power..."
And in the Angelic Plane, the ranks of the mages are strict; rank is status, and their robes have distinct markings.
Not every eighth-tier Archmage wears this kind of red robe, but those who wear it are definitely Archmages.
Moreover, those with such gold-threaded red robes have high positions in the Church.
At least, this guy was the highest-ranking individual from the Angelic Plane that Su Lun had encountered!
But what Su Lun couldn't figure out was, why would this guy appear in the Dragon Country Waters?
Moreover, did he come alone, or were there others?
Su Lun squinted into the depths of the night.
No matter what, being sought out like this, tonight seemed a bit out of the ordinary...
The folks from the Angelic Plane had been severely injured so many times, they must have quite the assurance this time for making a move.
Last time three ten-thousand-men groups were eliminated, had they come with ten or eight this time?
However, what Su Lun hadn't expected was, after watching for a long time, it seemed that only this one guy had come?

chapters.title: Chapter 553 - 552: Arcane Necromantic Disaster
chapters.content:
"Enemy attack!"
Although the commotion on the mainmast was subtle, the patrolling soldiers on deck still noticed it.
In that instant, various alarm devices triggered simultaneously, strong lights turned on, shining on the sea surrounding the Eternal Night, and everyone on the ship sprang into action.
Su Lun watched the figure in the red robe from afar, his gaze slightly grave.
No trace of any accomplices was seen around, which was puzzling.
Even for an eighth-tier Grand Magician, where did this guy get the confidence to provoke the Dawn Group alone?
Although Su Lun did not understand it, he did not underestimate the enemy in the slightest.
To join the Holy Army and be a high-ranking member, one must certainly possess some special abilities.
Like the Resurrection Technique just now.
However, at that moment, with the sound of a "snap" breaking the silence, Qian Tiao had already dashed forward aggressively. Her fighting instincts were incredibly sharp, not giving the enemy any time to breathe.
Thoughts only flashed through Su Lun's mind in an instant, and his movements were not slow at all; he formed the sorcerer's seals in his hands and vanished from his spot in an instant.
It was incomprehensible, but only by probing could he know what abilities the opponent possessed!
One stormed forward through the air, the other used Void Displacement, coordinating perfectly.
Just like just now, one in the front and one in the back, they surged forward hundreds of meters in an instant, blocking the Grand Magician's path with a blade and an umbrella.
Typically, a seventh-tier alchemist has much higher combat prowess than a believer of the same tier, as an alchemist's power stems from their own understanding, and the foundation is very solid.
And Su Lun and his companion were not just ordinary seventh-tiers; within their tier, they were nearly unbeatable.
They feared a legion of ten thousand mages, not a single eighth-tier mage!
Both had confidence in harming the enemy and protecting themselves!
Qian Tiao's sword was incredibly fast, arriving in a blink, which was simply beyond what the frail-bodied mage could react to.
Su Lun also used "Spatial Confinement" then; if the opponent's understanding of space was not higher than his, it was impossible for them to escape using any spatial spells. Even if the person was an eighth-tier or even borrowed the power of a deity, he did not believe they could escape the spatial constraints enhanced by the "Urobolos Space-Time Ring."
This method of confinement was generally unbreakable.
...
The red-robed Grand Magician, seeing the pincer attack coming, frowned deeply, internally cursing.
He had just been killed in a combined attack and was well aware of the lethal intent hidden within their teamwork.
Although taken by surprise earlier, even with prior knowledge, there was no solution.
He thought of using spatial spells to escape, but feeling the confinement around him as thick as steel, he instantly dismissed the thought.
Seeing the rune-engraved black umbrella in Su Lun's hand, the Archmage's eyelid twitched slightly as he murmured to himself, "The natives of the Alchemy Plane really do each possess precious treasures. An item that can inflict real damage on the soul is extremely scarce, even within the church. And to think this guy can wield such a high-tier soul artifact, tsk... very special indeed."
Then, without any countermeasure, he was split into two by the Sword Qi.
He didn't even manage to activate his magic shield.
The Archmage's thought process was clear. If he wasn't cut by the blade, he would be like before, hammered in the soul by the black umbrella.
Although not enough to kill him, that moment of shock was truly dangerous.
If he were restrained, there might be more sinister techniques to follow. It was better to resurrect again.
So this time, when Qian Tiao's sword cut through, the red-robed Grand Magician died very cleanly.
...
Su Lun had just teleported over when Qian Tiao's blade had already struck down, making his strike with the black umbrella miss.
Staring at the enemy re-forming in the distance, Su Lun's eyes shimmered slightly, "Revived again? It turns out to be a servant of god..."
He immediately realized what was amiss, suspecting that ordinary measures might hardly kill this opponent.
Seeing how nonchalantly the enemy was killed, it must be someone like the 'Spiritual Detective' Jerome that Old Lington encountered. A deity bore most of the cost of resurrection.
But Su Lun himself had been resurrected once; he knew well there must be a price to the resurrection itself.
When he was resurrected using a cursed item, he suffered from psychological distortions due to whispers he heard, an issue that had not been completely resolved to this day.
By thinking that if the enemy died enough times, a flaw must reveal itself!
And in that instant, as the enemy died the second time, Su Lun sharply detected that the opponent's soul fluctuation was not as solid as before.
Su Lun guessed that this Resurrection Technique had a cooldown time!
Both sides clashed in rapid succession within moments, and by then, the few people on deck witnessed this eerie scene. Hiding among the crowd, Rebato stared at the process of the enemy's resurrection, his wise yet murky eyes skimming a hint of realization, as if he sensed something.
But he didn't rush to make a move, instead quietly hiding among the crowd.
Qian Tiao reacted very quickly, and the moment she killed that red-robed Archmage for the second time, there was another explosive sound beneath her feet as she stepped on air.
With a "snap".
She had already dashed towards the location where the enemy resurrected.
Even faster than Su Lun's teleportation.
But after dying twice, the red-robed mage finally had time to cast a spell, the magic book in his hand flashed with light.
Qian Tiao had arrived.
This time, he wasn't killed again.
A slash fell, and the figure of the red-robed person dispersed.
Qian Tiao reacted extremely fast; after one slash, another followed, chopping towards the direction she sensed the qi from.
"Cackle cackle cackle..."
The red-robed mage was struck repeatedly, and a creepy laughter transmitted from the void.
Everyone sharpened their gaze, and at that moment, dozens of red-robed mages appeared in the sky, with all their qi exactly the same, making it impossible to distinguish the real from the fake.
With a flicker of light in his left eye, Su Lun recognized this as the seventh-level Necromantic Art "Dark Shadows," a life-saving technique similar to the substitution technique.
Only then did he realize something, thinking, "A necromancer?"
Qian Tiao couldn't tell which one was the real body at the moment, but slashing wildly in ignorance, she managed to cut down several red-robed mages.
However, with Soul Perception, Su Lun could clearly distinguish which one was the original.
"Ten o'clock direction!"
He mentally transmitted the position to Qian Tiao, and the two of them encircled again.
For the third time, that mage was killed.
In just a matter of moments, this eighth-level Grand Magician was killed three times.
He also felt somewhat dispirited from being killed repeatedly, after all, the umbrella truly thwarted his abilities.
Clearly, this guy also knew that he would gain no advantage alone, and just as he died for the third time, a composed and creepy laugh echoed from the void, "Ah yo... it has really been a long time since I encountered such a tough opponent."
...
However, just as these words were spoken, a sudden change escalated!
Su Lun's gaze dramatically sharpened upon hearing it, because in his perception, the soul fluctuation of that red-robed mage suddenly increased a hundredfold!
"How is this possible?"
He incredulously watched the individual who was now engulfed in green flames, thinking, "Divine fire? No... it's soul fire! What secret technique is this, and why is it so strong?"
It was hard to imagine that a person's soul could be so powerful that it overflowed like flames.
This was an unheard-of occurrence for Su Lun.
"Be careful!"
Just as the anomaly occurred, Su Lun instantly teleported next to Qian Tiao, blocking the sword she was about to slash down with his scythe, and instead struck with his own black umbrella.
Qian Tiao also sensed something off and instantly held back.
As Su Lun struck down with his staff, hitting the body engulfed in flames, the facial expression of that guy changed dramatically.
Indeed, something was amiss!
The red-robed mage was hit, sparks flying everywhere, scattering around, and some clinging to the protective aura on Su Lun's body, causing a bone-eroding burning sensation to instantly wrap around his heart.
Su Lun looked at the green flames, which resembled phosphorus flames, and cried out in his mind, "This green fire can scorch the soul!"
It didn't burn the body, but directly scorched the soul, and even the protective aura couldn't block it.
Luckily for Su Lun, his soul was strong enough. Otherwise, if an ordinary person were to be scorched even once, the consequences of a damaged soul were unimaginable.
Moreover, what was more eerie was that the scattered flames stuck to his body showed no sign of extinguishing, as if they intended to burn the soul completely.
"Such a diabolical tactic!"
This was Su Lun's first encounter with such, he took no chances and immediately activated his full domain, with a phantom of the Grim Reaper also rising behind him.
Indeed, the combat power of a divine being of a higher sacred echelon was not so simple. As thoughts flew through his mind, he quickly pondered the weaknesses of these green flames.
Only when the realm of Death was fully opened, did the flames extinguish.
The opposing red-robed Grand Magister, seeing his soul fire extinguished, narrowed his eyes slightly.
...
The soul-fires splashing from close combat would scorch the soul, meaning one couldn't get close to this fellow to fight. Otherwise, once scorched, the consequences were unimaginable.
Su Lun and Qian Jiao both retreated explosively at the same time.
From a distance, the spatial cracks of the Reaper's scythe and the slashes of Sword Qi passed through.
However, such long-range methods obviously posed no threat, the Red Robe Grand Magister didn't even spare an extra glance, standing there as his body suddenly turned ethereal, completely immune to the attacks.
This guy, seeing the Death's phantom behind Su Lun, had a cold glint in his eyes, which made him feel threatened. He muttered, "The 'Reaper's' second awakening talent... You Alchemy natives really make one envious."
Su Lun narrowed his eyes, ignoring the provocation and considering how to deal with him.
After the engagement, they realized why the enemy dared to come alone: he had special abilities.
This guy's combat power was among the pinnacle of eighth-tier Grand Magisters in the Divine Plane.
Meanwhile, Qian Jiao, seeing that her Sword Qi had not harmed the man, displayed the third awakening of the Rakshasa Golden Body behind her, already starting to accumulate Sword Qi.
The few strikes just now were hurried normal attacks, but now, knowing that the opponent was immune to physical attacks, she was getting serious.
As strong as Rakshasa Woman goes, the opponent's strange techniques provoked Qian Jiao into high spirits, her aura already faintly breaking beyond the Sword Saint.
In the distance, the Red Robe Grand Magister's pupils sharply constricted, somewhat puzzled but more shocked, "Is this... third awakening talent?"
This level of talent, hailed as a reincarnation of a deity, even he had only heard of, never expecting to see it with his own eyes in a fractured plane.
In an instant, his eyes were filled with murderous intent, "A second awakening 'Reaper' is surprising enough, I didn't expect another with third awakening talent, only a step from Sword Deity. No wonder my sect has been frustrated. How many good opportunities did those from the Alchemy Plane leave behind... tsk tsk, I really can't let you natives live."
Pausing briefly, this guy, his face set on moving the whole world against them, added, "It happens that I found a good material in an underwater relic, might as well try my hand..."
It was before his words fell completely that Su Lun was contemplating how to handle the opponent in front of him. Suddenly, a tyrannical Sword Qi surged to the sky!
In the perception, an unexpected soul fluctuation appeared.
Though not very strong, it was at the moment this soul fluctuation appeared, a tide of Sword Qi both deadly and divine surged to the heavens.
Su Lun and Qian Jiao's expressions changed simultaneously, "Sword Deity realm?!"
Because they had just recently seen this high-ceiling sword intent, on Rebato.
So they immediately recognized it.
Upon closer inspection, a figure in tattered monk robes, clearly a skeletal swordsman, appeared abruptly beside the Red Robe Grand Magister.
This figure seemed to have been dug up from a grave, a skeleton glowing green in the night. Within those hollow eye sockets flickered two orbs of phosphorescence—it was this green ghostly fire that made it feel almost alive, as if making eye contact!
Su Lun frowned slightly at this sight.
It was said that only those above the eighth-tier Overwhelming realm, once dead, would their bones show such a jade-bone color.
Certainly, this skeleton had to be a top-tier powerhouse in life.
But aside from the Sword Intent and skeleton, what caught the eye more was the sword in the skeleton's hand, intertwining gold and black light.
This sword bore ancient Sanskrit-like golden runes, emanating a divine aura like that of Buddha, yet its blade was pitch black as ink, with an eerie black mist swirling around, making one's spine chill. Inside, it seemed as if endless evil spirits were struggling, seeking to escape but sealed within the sword by the golden seals.
On seeing this, Qian Jiao almost blurted out, "The peerless Famed Sword 'Fó Tú'?"
Su Lun also identified it, indeed it was that legendary sword.
Ranked even higher than the third-ranked Demon Blade 'Guy Maru Hyakume Zakura' in Qian Jiao's hand, and the second-ranked 'Armor Cutter Frost Flower Whisper' in Rebato's grip—the peerless sword that straddles good and evil, ranked first among the twelve masterworks of Mountain Hermit—'Fó Tú'!
This sword was an ancient artifact forged by a relic blacksmith, having been lost for hundreds of years.
Su Lun and Qian Jiao, on their last visit to Mountain Hermit, had only heard of the legend of this sword, never expecting to encounter it here.
Legend had it that it was the partnered sword of 'Yào Shì', the Sword Deity from Mountain Hermit in the Warring States Period.
He was a grandmaster of the ancient Sword Dao, who attained enlightenment through slaughter.
Reportedly, he could both save lives with his unmatched medical skills and, with a single 'Fó Tú', decimate gods and demons!
The sword in hand, sealed with countless tormented souls it had claimed.
Many legends about that Sword Deity are still circulated in Mountain Hermit today, true and false indistinguishable.
But given that this skeleton was at least a tier-eight professional in life, Su Lun thought, it might truly be him.
...
Seeing this, Su Lun finally confirmed that the Red Robe Grand Magister was a Necromancer.
Although the skeleton might be the legendary Sword Deity, having long been dead, how much physical strength it retained was still uncertain.
However, the realm was genuinely solid.
Quite often, the realm of Sword Dao could even unleash more powerful fighting capabilities than the physical body.
This is indeed a rare opponent.
A famed sword and a suitable opponent are both opportunities that a top-level swordsman could only hope to encounter.
As Qian Tiao looked at the Skeleton Sword Deity, a thunderous Sword Intent burst forth just as fiercely, clashing head-on.
Encountering such a swordsman as an enemy, she could no longer restrain her fighting spirit and charged forward, "Leave this guy to me!"
Su Lun watched without speaking.
He kept his gaze fixed on the Red Robe Archmage, showing more interest in something else as he muttered to himself, "This Necromantic Arts are interesting..."
The ability to bring the skeleton back to life and retain its former comprehension is indeed a top-tier secret technique.
Su Lun's own undead lacked intelligence, which felt quite inferior.
Seeing this, he thought of something, if he could kill this guy... he would know what's going on.
.....
As the enemies approached, the alchemy arrays on the Eternal Night suddenly lit up.
Being able to survive the encirclement of Su Lun and Qian Tiao, everyone realized that the attacker must be a formidable foe. Cannons and firearms were obviously useless. For dealing with such especially tricky high-level enemies, the Dawn Group also had a specific contingency plan.
This time, the rarely seen Mr. Hei made his move!
At that moment, after preparing for a while, his eyes full of a chilling indifference to the world, he formed a sorcerer's seal with his hands and pointed forward, "Sealing Skill· Four Elements Magic Suppression Heaven Seal!"
If he couldn't be killed, then sealing him would suffice.
This was the only vulnerability he had spotted.
Looking again, the four elements of earth, wind, water, and fire quickly converged, turning into countless chains of law that locked towards the man.
This wasn't a seventh-tier spell, but an eighth-tier one!
Because he was well-prepared, and his timing was exquisitely clever, the Red-robed Mage had no time to dodge and was immediately tightly entangled.
Even though he was restrained, the Red-robed Mage was not alarmed but instead let out a light "hmm": "Rule stealing? You actually managed to cleverly cast a high-tier spell... haha, such a solid understanding of the laws, it's quite interesting."
Only from a high enough stand could one realize how special this seal was. It not only precisely targeted his vulnerability but also specifically used this all-isolating Four Elements Magic Suppression Seal.
Another very special alchemist.
At this moment, the Red Robed Mage finally understood why the Mage Group often faced setbacks.
On this ship... are all monsters!
Therefore, it's even more essential to eliminate them once and for all.
As he spoke, a cold gleam flashed in the eyes of the Red Robed Mage, and he glanced at the members of the Dawn Group, who were preparing to act on the deck, scoffing, "But do you think, me coming here alone, that it's just me alone?"
Before the sealing technique could fully bind him, suddenly a bony claw emerged from the dark light around his body.
The claw, like that of an eagle, tore apart several chains of laws in one swipe.
On closer inspection, a deathly creature with the head, claws, and wings of an eagle, but the body of a lion appeared.
"Necromantic Griffin?"
Su Lun looked at the form of this creature with a somewhat stern expression.
This was a legendary creature known to contend with dragons.
And it wasn't just one!
In that instant, dozens of griffins tore the sealing chains from all around the Red Robed Mage's body and surged out.
Su Lun looked at the number of these monsters, his eyes narrowing slightly.
Yet it was not over!
The Red Robed Mage raised his magic staff, chanting a very long magic spell for the first time, "O great god of the undead above, I respectfully invoke your name, please bestow the power of the undead to your messenger, summon the secret arts of the undead... Arcane Necromantic Disaster!"
As these words fell, he pointed his magic staff towards the sky, which suddenly became covered with an aura of death.
In an instant, as if doomsday had arrived, countless undead creatures surged out like a tidal wave from the clouds of death, overwhelming the sky.
