Upon hearing this, a gleam immediately sparked in Qian Tiao's eyes.
Su Lun nodded.
Just as they were discussing this, Dr. Banks came over, clearly exhilarated, holding several test tube samples and laughed, "Hahaha... Su Lun, we have made a big discovery this time."
He was already deformed, and his face, which resembled that of an insect, looked particularly strange.
Su Lun, who had never seen the composed Dr. Banks so excited, asked, "Doctor, was the discovery that significant?"
"More than significant?"
Excitement was barely contained in Banks' voice as he explained, "I just did a preliminary examination of several high-level undead samples' genes, and I found their gene sequences to be terrifyingly intact! This means that many of these undead are indeed legitimate mythological species..."
"???"
Upon hearing this, both Bartolo and Qian Tiao were clearly baffled.
One had never been exposed to genetic biology, while the other knew of it but didn't understand it at all.
Yet Su Lun did understand.
He also vaguely realized that the discovery might be even greater than he had anticipated.
Qian Tiao, who always asked when she didn't understand, pointed to the skeletons on the ice and directly asked, "Doctor, are these skeletons of any great use?"
"Yes!"
Dr. Banks elucidated, "It turns out that a significant reason why those mythological civilizations' gods were powerful is based on the genetic chains. The more powerful the individual, the more intact their gene link, like the dragon race, which has twelve more gene links than ordinary humans! And the gene links of every era's creatures become somewhat incomplete due to environmental reasons. Compared with beings from mythological civilizations, we modern ordinary humans are missing many 'powerful genes.' In the field of Alchemy, there is an ultimate topic where Alchemists believe that the truth lies at the very beginning with the creator, the origin of everything. Genes are like a tree that branches and spreads; the genes of ancient beings are the trunk, and we are already the fine leaves at the very end. If the gene links are sufficiently intact, we too could have the power of ancient humans. I even think that becoming a deity is a process of genetic reversion to a certain extent. Now that we have this batch of precious samples, it can provide enough material support for my research topics..."
As he excitedly rattled off a series of professional terms, Qian Tiao and Bartolo not only failed to understand but looked even more confused.
Dr. Banks immediately realized that what he had said seemed a bit too abstract for the layman, so he directly addressed the practical application of biotechnology, saying, "Simply put, given these gene sequence samples, our lab might experience a major breakthrough in genetic potions without any surprises!"
At this revelation, Qiān Tiáo suddenly came to an enlightened understanding, showing a look of anticipation, "Doctor, are you saying that the 'Dragon Potion' might see a breakthrough?"
"Not only that."
Dr. Banks smiled and shook his head, his voice filled with hope as well.
He said, "These undead creatures possess complete genes from the Mythological Era. Our lab now has the mature technology to extract and create genetic potions. In the near future, we will have not only 'Dragon Bloodline Potions' and 'Titan Bloodline Potions', but also 'Behemoth Potions', 'Griffon Potions', 'Dark Elf Potions'... and so on! By then, we will be able to mass-produce various bloodline genetic potions suitable for the group members! And, these bone gene sequences are very complete, so the potion effects will be excellent, even allowing us to revert to the Mythological Era's demigod bloodline level."
"Demigod bloodlines?!"
Su Lun felt an immense excitement upon hearing this.
A demigod bloodline... that's the equivalent of having an extra A or B-grade talent!
Previously, there was a significant issue with genetic potions, that being individual tolerance varied so much that many people didn't see great effects.
Like when Su Lun initially fused with the "X Potion", not only was it risky, but the effects weren't as good as those of Number Nineteen.
But now, Dr. Banks's new discovery had thoroughly resolved this problem.
The fundamental reason for the fusion's poor effects was the lack of choice.
As long as there are enough types of potions to choose from, there will always be one that suits oneself!
And among those undead, there were many mythological species samples.
With this, in the future, perhaps every member of the Dawn group might have various demigod bloodlines, which would lead to an extremely exaggerated enhancement in combat power.
Just the thought of it was incredibly exciting.
Qiān Tiáo, who had been listening on the side, finally understood and was instantly energized.
Even the usually composed Old Sword God Bartolo's eyes were filled with anticipation.
Potionology was an important branch of Alchemy, but the bloodline potions of the past relied on ancient formulations to improve bloodlines, and whether one could integrate them was up to chance. And now, we can systematically research and mass-produce bloodline potions targetedly?
He felt a profound sense of awe, Alchemy had evolved to such an extent in today's world.
...
Several days later.
On the endless expanse of the sea, a giant black sail ship was sailing at a steady pace.
Although this was a route once traversed by the Black Sam Pirate Crew nearly thirty years ago, the current situation had greatly diverged from the information Bartolo had.
After entering the range of the Old Dragon Kingdom Ruins, the air became increasingly suffused with the miasma of Hell, and encounters with monsters became more frequent and formidable.
The battles had also been quite frequent these past few days.
But thankfully, the combat prowess of the Dawn group was not weak, and with Tanni and his mother's perceptive abilities, they had managed to avoid extremely dangerous areas and sailed through without any accidents.
During the rare moments of calm, Su Lun stayed in the captain's cabin, focused on studying the secret technique known as "Death God's Fire."
At that moment, he was holding a newly acquired golden scroll, while comparing it against the several dozen volumes of cultivation insights from that Red-robed Mage's storage ring, completely engrossed in his research.
It was as if he were enchanted, reading while muttering to himself, pondering something.
Indeed!
Just the cultivation insights alone amounted to dozens of volumes!
This Soul Secret Technique had been passed down for over a thousand years in the Divine Plane, and every generation of Mages that had obtained this technique before the Red-robed Mage had their own understanding. They recorded their lifetime insights into texts for future generations.
This is what inheritance means.
With these cultivation insights, those who came after would have a much easier time.
The high-ranking Magicians in the Divine Plane all belonged to ancient and powerful inheritance systems, which was why they had such a prosperous magic civilization.
Finally, after a long time, Su Lun emerged from his focus with a slight sigh, "It's really hard to get started with..."
After all, it was Divine Arts, and the threshold for entry was extremely high.
If it weren't for his own comprehension of Death laws having already reached a very high level, someone else, even with those insights for guidance, most likely couldn't understand what the secret technique recorded on this golden page was.
Su Lun remembered Mr. Jing once saying that high-level languages like Divine Tongue and Dragon Tongue contained high-level laws, meaning they are not just literal.
The secret technique recorded on this golden scroll was interpreted by some deity from their original "Words of the Exalted" golden page, then rewritten in a simpler expression to pass on to their mortal followers.
But because the technique directly connects to the divine level, it remains very profound.
For those who haven't reached that realm, the only way to understand it is to complicate it until it becomes something they can grasp at their own level.
A thousand people might derive a thousand different interpretations.
This was the origin of those dozens of volumes of cultivation insights.
Su Lun didn't dwell on it any further.
Cultivating this soul Divine Art was not an overnight endeavor.
He closed the tome and tried to condense the secret technique. His soul converged, and a wisp of pale green flame emerged.
Looking at the small flame, he murmured with a hint of anticipation, "The 'Soul Fire' indeed can be controlled with the secret technique of 'Flame Control' from [Invisible Servitude]..."
The flame was weak, vastly different from the surge of flame from that red-robed mage.
But differently, Su Lun could control this flame.
Having carefully read the [Death God's Fire] secret technique, he discovered that there were similarities with [Invisible Servitude].
Back then, when he stripped a portion of the ninth-tier master Pierre's Soul Shard, he now had a profound understanding of this secret technique.
So this attempt came naturally to him.
It also meant that when he mastered [Death God's Fire] in the future, his combat capability would be even more terrifying than that red-robed mage.
It wouldn't just be passive splash damage from being hit; he could actively attack using the secret technique of [Invisible Servitude], undoubtedly another powerful move.
But that day was still far off, so Su Lun just looked forward to it.
As he was trying, intending to delve further into the details, he suddenly sensed something and looked up toward the cultivation room next to the captain's cabin, murmuring inquisitively, "Did it work?"
Three days ago, after Dr. Banks received those undead genetic samples, he quickly achieved results. Although the mass production of the dragon bloodline potion had not been fully solved, he managed to create a potion enhancing affinity toward the dragon bloodline specifically for Tanni!
That way, Tanni would be able to merge with the [Isaac's Dragon Pattern Golden Body - Thunder Dragon] prosthesis.
Tanni had been in seclusion for these three days, fusing with the prosthesis.
Sensing the subtle movements in the room next door, Su Lun guessed what was happening.
Just then, with a "click," the door opened and Tanni walked out.
When Su Lun saw the anomalies on her, his gaze narrowed slightly.
At that moment, Tanni was enveloped in a layer of purple light, with tiny lightning serpents flickering and darting about.
Upon closer inspection, the exposed skin looked as if it were covered in a dense layer of runic armor. Those purple runes connected into large swathes, forming a visible thick layer of defense akin to dragon scales.
Su Lun asked, "Sister Tanni, did you successfully merge?"
Tanni slightly raised her eyebrows and nodded, saying, "Hmm. Quite smoothly."
Su Lun inquired further, "How do you feel about the prosthesis?"
Tanni squinted, glancing at the dragon scale runes on her arm, and replied, "Very strong!"
After contemplating for a moment, she added, "I feel that with this prosthesis, even without breaking through to Sword Saint Realm, I might be able to fight at the eighth tier."
Hearing this, Su Lun's eyes brightened as well.
Fusing with each tier of prosthesis signified a significant enhancement for an alchemist.
According to Old Sword God Bartolo's trial experience, this prosthesis could multiply one's physical strength several times over!
Moreover, when he first merged, there were no Bloodline Potions, so he chose to forge a prosthesis from a very faint-blooded wyvern, with a grade around Gold.
But what Tanni merged with was the legendary prosthesis of a pure-blooded giant dragon!
However, the greater surprise came afterward when Tanni, having just spoken, paused and added, "Also... after merging with the prosthesis, I think I've glimpsed the mysteries of 'Supreme Body' at the eighth tier."
"..."
Listening, a twitch appeared at the corner of Su Lun's eye, but soon his heart leapt with joy.
He had heard from Tanni before that she had some insights, but he didn't expect her to have signs of breakthrough right after merging with the prosthesis.
This was indeed good news.
If Tanni could smoothly advance to the eighth tier, Dawn Group's top-tier combat strength would surge significantly.
Besides, she was now half a step into the Sword Saint Realm. Once she firmly established herself, her sword skills would become all the more terrifying.
Even Old Sword God Bartolo had personally stated that once she advanced, she would undoubtedly stand at the pinnacle of the Sword Dao of her era, likely finding few rivals within the eighth tier.
All of a sudden, Tanni grew significantly stronger, though she appeared very calm.
After talking to Su Lun for a bit, she walked back into the room and directly took off the Sword Dao robe she hadn't changed for three days, heading to the bathroom while casually saying, "I'm going to take a bath."
"Mhm."
Su Lun watched her graceful figure, smiling faintly.
At this moment, over the Rakshasa tattoo on her back, a layer of lightning runes emitted a barely visible light, exuding a fierce aura!
She was like the Rakshasa Woman, coming from hell.

chapters.title: Chapter 558 - 557: The Funeral
chapters.content:
Previously, Dr. Banks had left biomarkers on those warships left behind by the mages of the Divine Plane, so the Dawn Group has always had a rough understanding of the fleet's coordinates.
Now, sailing to the periphery of the Old Dragon Kingdom Ruins, they have discovered that those ships are within a few days' journey nearby.
Although it is unclear how those individuals managed to reach such remote waters, the markers have not moved for a long time. It's likely they encountered some special circumstances, or perhaps the enemy realized something and intentionally stopped to use as bait...
Regardless, Su Lun felt that he needed to confirm the situation first.
It wouldn't be long until he was nearby anyway; his initial plan was to get closer before going over to gather some intelligence.
Unexpectedly, at this time, Pandora, who had been stealing the Power of Faith in the Silver Dragon Kingdom, sent a message, saying that she had found a very important clue.
...
One day, on an unnamed deserted island not marked on any nautical chart.
The Eternal Night continued sailing the seas, while Su Lun alone, following the spatial coordinates left by Pandora, teleported to the island.
The island bore plenty of traces of human activity.
According to Pandora, the night before, a fleet of over one hundred thousand had moored here to rest for the night.
It was a funeral fleet from the Silver Dragon Kingdom.
Su Lun also found it incredible.
Because this deserted island was already near the Old Dragon Kingdom Ruins, according to the nautical chart, it was even closer to the core of the ruins than the Dawn Group.
But how was that possible?
On their journey here, Su Lun knew all too well the numerous dangerous creatures the Dawn Group had encountered to reach this place.
An ordinary fleet would simply not have the capacity to withstand such risks.
Yet, mysteriously, not only did the funeral fleet arrive here.
They also sailed smoothly all the way, encountering no mishaps whatsoever to reach these depths?
Su Lun naturally didn't believe it.
But Pandora was now on that fleet, having witnessed the entire voyage herself.
From her observations, various indications suggested that there seemed to be a secretive force protecting these people, and it was highly likely connected to the individuals from the Divine Plane.
That's why Su Lun came personally.
To avoid being detected, Su Lun didn't teleport directly onto the ship.
After carefully examining the traces on the deserted island, he teleported again, heading towards the next set of spatial coordinates left by Pandora.
After a few teleports, he already saw the fleet of over a hundred ships on the sea's surface.
Su Lun looked at those single-masted sailboats known as "Great Oar Warships" in the Dragon Country Waters and frowned.
These boats had a shallow draft, primarily powered by sails and rowing, utterly unsuitable for long voyages. A little bit of strong wind and waves could flip them over.
Yet, it was this kind of ship that had sailed deep into the Dragon Country Ruins without sinking, which was nothing short of miraculous.
Su Lun, fearing the presence of perception masters on the ship, dared not get too close to spy and asked Pandora about the situation on the ship. She said that she could teleport, and so he directly teleported over.
The scenery around him changed instantly, from the sea surface to a cramped and dim cabin.
Su Lun knew the space on the ship was limited, but it was only the moment before his teleportation that he realized just how small it was.
He had teleported here using the spatial coordinates on Pandora's necklace, and upon arrival, the two of them were squeezed tightly together.
This corner that seemed like a storeroom was surrounded by cargo.
The space, originally barely large enough for one-and-a-half individuals, now left them no choice but to press close together.
Warm and full arms, a touch smooth and fine.
Then, he saw a figure wearing a cloak just one foot away.
Su Lun looked up to see the stunning face of Pandora.
She raised an eyebrow and explained, "Don't look at me like that. It's not bad that there's such an independent space on this ship."
Listening to her words, Su Lun extended his senses and found it to be true.
This single-masted sailboat, originally designed for three to five hundred people, was now crammed with over a thousand.
Like those slave ships that Ruying used to run, the cabins were jam-packed with people like cargo.
As Pandora said, having such a place to stand and a small window for ventilation was already the best "single room" on the ship.
Not just this one, but all the ships within his sensing range were the same.
However, more puzzling to Su Lun than the crowding was why there were so many people?
Moreover, many of the souls felt through his perception on the ship were not powerful, likely ordinary people. It seemed odd anywhere you looked that the royal family of the Silver Dragon Kingdom would bring so many commoners for a funeral.
Seeing his thoughts, Pandora spoke, "These people only know that they have come to conduct a funeral service for the king. But I think it's not that simple..."
Su Lun listened thoughtfully.
The one being memorialized was, of course, Gracie the Eighth, the former king of the Silver Dragon.
Initially, during the battle between the two gorgons outside the outskirts of the royal capital Aike, the members of the royal family who managed to escape were turned to stone.
Later, a prince ascended the throne as the new king without considering lifting the curse on the former king; they directly arranged for people to conduct a funeral, stating that a sea burial in the Old Dragon Kingdom was the greatest respect for the old king.
But, does conducting a funeral require a hundred thousand people?
To travel deep into such dangerous waters at that?
Also, what was the mysterious force that ensured their safe arrival?
Doubts surfaced one after another, and Su Lun felt it all felt too familiar a set-up.
At that moment, Pandora roughly explained the situation and gave her conclusion, "I suspect these people have been brought here to be 'sacrificed'."
```
"Sacrifice?"
Su Lun listened and fell into deep thought.
He had also considered this point, which is why it seemed so familiar.
Once, during Dawn Group's adventures in the four nations of the Northern Continent, they had encountered the same pattern.
Back in the Roman Nation, at the Temple of Aghaparnon, the priests had used a treasure as bait to attract hundreds of thousands of adventurers to set out on a sea journey, only to discover in the end that it was a sacrifice to the fake Sea King god of the sea ruins, in exchange for favorable weather and good harvests.
And looking at this funeral procession, it seemed to be cut from the same cloth.
Some evil fake gods needed sacrifices to gain power, while humans could reach some sort of agreement with these evil gods through sacrifice.
With that in mind, the conspiracy behind the funeral became gradually clearer.
...
Su Lun was lost in thought.
Neither of them spoke.
Tucked in a cramped corner, they could even hear each other's breath clearly.
They maintained this position for a while, and Pandora seemed to feel a bit uncomfortable, so she shifted her body slightly.
With this movement, they ended up even closer to each other, and even through a layer of thin clothing, the graceful figure was distinctly felt.
Su Lun was distinctly aware of a large soft warmth pressing against him, which brought him back to his senses and he looked over at her.
But there was not a trace of discomfort on Pandora's face.
Her beautiful eyes shone brilliantly as she continued, "When I was collecting faith before, I discovered that the current King of the Silver Dragon Country is closely related to the white-robed wizard Garcia you mentioned and is likely a follower of one of the deities of the Divine Plane. This funeral sacrifice is probably orchestrated by those mages from the Divine Plane..."
At this point, she paused for a moment and added, "These days I have also found that the faith in the Silver Dragon Country is very complex, with many fake gods emerging. Among those that have gained a foothold is a faction called 'the Sect of the Grey Mist.' They worship a fake god called 'Lord of the Grey Mist,' who can bless the fishermen's harvests and safety at sea. And I found followers of the Grey Mist Sect on the ship, whose prayers, during their worship, directed a current of the Power of Faith toward the deep sea in the direction we are heading..."
"I see..."
Having heard this, Su Lun had almost completely understood the whole story of the matter.
Now that the long-distance teleportation formation on Rainbow Island was gone, those folks from the Divine Plane were left without reinforcements. Even if they have several Mage legions numbering in the tens of thousands, the likelihood of them finding the "Mimir's Spring" deep in the Dragon Country Waters alive was incredibly slim.
Therefore, they inevitably needed some external force.
Just like how they previously cooperated with the Gorgon chieftain, it was probably the external help they leveraged.
But since "Medusa" Helen killed that Gorgon, they now had to find another ally.
A fake god who could control the ocean couldn't be more suitable.
It just so happened that the current royal family of the Silver Dragon Country were followers of the Divine Plane, which made it easy to mobilize the public for sacrifices.
Thus, in the name of the funeral of the previous King, they had these over a hundred thousand people come for sacrifice.
And then they reached an agreement with the fake god in exchange for a smooth arrival at the deep sea?
After pondering, Su Lun drew the above conclusion.
Although all this was just Pandora's speculation, when combined with the current situation, it was practically factual.
Seeing that he had also figured it out, Pandora then said, "There are also a group of mysterious people on the main ship, which I suspect to be the wizards from the Divine Plane. Not to startle them prematurely, I didn't attempt any probing."
Her reason for joining was naturally her interest in the "Lord of the Grey Mist's" Divine Power of Faith.
She didn't shy away from her motives and said directly, "Thus, I plan to act during the sacrifice, stealing the fake god's faith. But after coming here, I realized that these waters connect to the hellish plane and the ancient Divine Power is dense here, which is extremely beneficial for me. It's beneficial for other entities as well. That fake god has formed a false godhood here, which might possess some special abilities. So, I might need your help."
"Sure."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun nodded without hesitation.
Pandora was now a core force of Dawn Group, and when she asked for help, naturally, he would not refuse.
Moreover, Pandora was currently very strong; if she could become even stronger, Dawn Group would gain more confidence in the upcoming full-scale war.
...
Su Lun mentally connected all the dots and felt Pandora's plan was a good one.
If they could eliminate that fake god, they would also directly disrupt the treasure hunt planned by those from the Divine Plane.
Considering this, he asked, "When do you think the sacrifice will take place?"
Pandora responded, "It should be soon. I can sense that the Divine Power of the fake god in the nearby waters is getting stronger with each passing day. In three more days at most, we should reach the target waters."
Su Lun nodded at her words, "Sure."
Waiting for two or three days was manageable. By not revealing themselves now, they could catch the fake god by surprise when the time came.
The two discussed some more details and roughly settled on a plan.
However, looking at their cramped surroundings, Su Lun wondered how they could possibly stay like this for two days?
Their corner was actually one of the better spots. In the outside cabin, with a ceiling height of over two meters, there were three tiers, and everyone was curled up on the floor, packed together tightly like sardines in a barrel, unable even to stand upright.
Pandora noticed his slightly odd expression, and without the slightest care, her exquisite face revealed a mischievous smile as she teased, "Oh, you seem a bit uncomfortable?"
"..."
Su Lun rolled his eyes at her words.
He knew Pandora's remark was not any flirtation of a romantic nature, but purely looking for some amusement.
Probably because she was used to being the lofty Moon Reading God in front of others, having someone to talk to normally meant she didn't need to maintain the dignity of a deity.
It occurred to Su Lun that she had only Mr. Jing and himself as people she could communicate with normally.
Being a deity seemed rather dull, he thought.
Perhaps there was also a bit of vengefulness from when Pandora was initially captured by Su Lun?
Regardless, Su Lun was not going to take it seriously.
```
But under the current circumstances, with two people squeezed into this narrow space, there's inevitably a great deal of bodily contact.
Yet oddly enough, Pandora needs to stay here to sense the situation with the Evil God, and Su Lun can't just take her into the little void world.
And he himself must remain on the ship, ready to respond to any emergency that might arise.
It seems the two can only maintain this arrangement.
Pandora probably feels that after two academic studies of alchemically created bodies, there's hardly any privacy left regarding her body where Su Lun is concerned, so she's always been very generous with her attitude, which was essentially: look if you want to look, touch if you please.
Even occasionally, she would amuse herself by flirting deliberately, passing the time during this dull voyage.
Su Lun originally didn't mind, but he couldn't resist the teasing and the Bewitching Technique. (Since the deity of the moon also governs sexual desires, this is also one of her secret techniques of divine practice.)
In the end, he was overwhelmed and defeated.
So Su Lun had to cut open some of the cargo with silken thread, just enough to expand the space for the two to sit and stand.
And so time passed, and it was two days later.
...
Su Lun was used to the Eternal Night, a super large-scale sailing warship, so suddenly being on this single-mast small boat, he felt somewhat unaccustomed.
On the Eternal Night, even if there were waves, the cabin was relatively stable. But on a small boat, even a slight wave felt like a world turned upside down.
However, paradoxically, it was this shallow-drafting boat—that looked like it should have sunk a hundred times over in these waters—that had managed to travel all the way without incident.
No severe storms were encountered, and even the larger sea creatures could be avoided.
Su Lun was gradually realizing that Pandora was right: the "Lord of the Grey Mist" indeed had some tricks up his sleeve. At the very least, to keep those high-level sea beasts and mutant creatures away, there must be a corresponding formidable ability.
It was going to be very tricky.
On the evening of the third day, the sunlight outside the window dimmed.
Su Lun and Pandora were hiding in a corner of the cabin in meditation.
Outside the window, the fog had grown dense, and the fleet had come to a halt.
Su Lun opened his eyes and glanced at the black mist outside the window.
This was already the edge of the central zone of the Old Dragon Kingdom Ruins. He calculated the distance, the volcanic connection to the hell plane in the legend was just a little over half a month's sail to the east.
The air was thick with hellish energies, and the people on the ship were showing signs of slight mutation. Wait a few more days, and most of them would likely turn into monsters.
Su Lun frowned slightly, as if he had thought of something.
The closer he got to this area, the more he felt something was off.
But he couldn't pinpoint the source of this unease.
Looking at Mr. Crow, who was dozing off on his shoulder. Since receiving that fragment of the undead plane a few days ago, Mr. Crow had been eating well every day, his feathers becoming especially lustrous and vibrant, suggesting that it was about to advance.
It was very quiet, giving Su Lun some confidence.
At that moment, outside, there suddenly came the sound of water rushing, as if someone had dumped a large amount of something into the sea.
Furthermore, the fleet was not resting as usual like the past two days but gradually gathering together.
Su Lun thought to himself, "Is the sacrifice about to begin?"
Pandora also opened her eyes next to him, sensing something, she said, "The Power of Faith outside is converging; that creature should be appearing soon..."
As she spoke, her face was very serious, appearing as if she was gradually entering the state of moon reading.
Listening to her, Su Lun's expression also became stern, anticipating a fierce battle soon.
He notified the Eternal Night of the potential need for support, ready to head there at any moment to call for reinforcements.
And he had a feeling that this sacrifice somehow had a connection with the Dawn Brigade.
...
At this time, calls were heard from the deck.
"Get some people to move the burial goods onto the deck!"
"Hurry up! Everyone get moving!"
"..."
At that shout, the people on the boat where Su Lun and Pandora were hiding were busy moving the cargo up before dumping it into the sea.
Many still thought these were burial goods for the royal family, not realizing they were sacrificial offerings.
As the boxes of goods were carried away, these people seemed completely oblivious to the presence of Su Lun and Pandora in the corner, each busy with their tasks.
Su Lun and Pandora were both waiting for the right moment.
However, as they waited, Su Lun let out a soft exclamation, "Huh... are those siblings on the boat too?"
With the hundred-odd ships in the fleet now gathered together, in his perception, he had detected two familiar soul fluctuations on another ship.
It was none other than Bennett and his sister Isabel from the Miraculous Legion.
Su Lun had a good impression of these two siblings, and to some extent, he felt a certain bond with them.
Not just him, but also the people of the Miraculous Legion were almost all in the fleet.
"They were also made into a sacrifice?"
Su Lun pondered for a moment and then understood.
The Miraculous Legion was loyal to the former King and firmly against the faith of the heavenly planes.
With the new King ascended, it was only natural for them to be sent here for burial as sacrificial offerings.
Because he had some affection for them, Su Lun decided to notify them.
Moreover, the people from the Miraculous Legion were strong fighters; the few hundred of them together could be a significant force.
With that thought in mind, he turned to Pandora beside him and said, "I'll be back in a moment."
Pandora nodded, not uttering another word.
At this moment, her presence was ethereal and elusive, divine power subtly overflowing from her, and her eyes shone like two crimson moons, looking incredibly eerie.
She had already transformed into the "Great Deity of Moon Reading."
...
Su Lun sensed a direction and, with a teleport, he appeared in the cabin of another ship.
This was the flagship, much larger than the one he had previously been on, with many private cabins supplied for the higher-ranking Knights.
When Su Lun teleported in, Bennett was on deck, gesturing for people to dump the burial goods into the sea.
Only his sister, Isabel, was in the cabin, her face clouded with worry, as if pondering something.
It wasn't until the room suddenly had an extra person that she abruptly turned around, drawing the dagger at her waist, and her figure disappeared on the spot.
Su Lun felt the blade against his neck and easily blocked it with two fingers, meanwhile saying, "It's me. Su Lun."
Knowing Isabel was a skilled assassin, he had not planned to cause any commotion, and so he directly restrained her completely.
Upon hearing his voice and taking another look, Isabel exclaimed in astonishment, "Mr. Su Lun?"
She had never expected to encounter that formidable overseas expert whom she had met once before.
Seeing her tense muscles relax, Su Lun let her go.
Isabel asked again, "Sir, how come you are here?"
Su Lun glanced at her and countered, "What are you all doing here?"
Upon hearing this, a trace of sorrow flitted across Isabel's brows, and she honestly replied, "We are here for His Majesty the King's sea burial."
Su Lun's acute awareness caught the change in her expression; clearly, she too realized that matters were not so simple, and he inquired further, "Do you know who's on the other main ship of this fleet?"
Isabel didn't know why he was asking but answered truthfully anyway, "I don't know. They say it's the Mage for the burial."
From her reply, Su Lun confirmed that Bennett and the others were completely unaware as well.
Time was of the essence, and he bluntly stated, "You and the others on the ship might have been made sacrifices for a sea ritual. The person on the other main ship might not be a Mage but someone from the divine plane."
At these words, Isabel's face drastically changed. Her eyes shifted in shock, murmuring to herself, "That explains why the royal household would send so many people..."
Su Lun had no intention of elaborating and directly said, "Call your brother here, I have something to tell him. Be careful not to let anyone notice."
"Yes!"
After pondering seriously for a moment upon hearing these words, Isabel nodded.
Although she did not feel well-acquainted with the man before her, her brother had always said that he was trustworthy.
For such a significant matter, she didn't hesitate and ran up to the deck.
Soon after, Bennett walked into the cabin with a puzzled look on his face.
Seeing that it was Su Lun, he was equally taken aback.
But when Su Lun explained the ins and outs of the situation, Bennett too was massively shocked.
He had already speculated many suspicious points about this burial journey, and now with Su Lun's explanation, how could he not understand?
Indeed, he was loyal to the Gracie royal family, but not to the current King!
Now that he, his family, and the brothers of the Miracle Legion were being used as sacrifices, how could he remain silent?
But at that moment, the sacrifices had already been cast into the sea.
Suddenly, the ship began to shake violently.
Outside the window, the mist had turned as black as ink, and an indescribable evil will had quietly arrived.
Watching unflinchingly, Su Lun whispered, "The Evil God has come!"
The Bennett siblings' expressions changed at the same time, and they tightened their grip on their weapons.
...
It was during this descent of the false deity amidst the fog that Pandora's voice came through the communicator: "We can act now!"
Hearing this, Su Lun's sorcerer's seals instantly flickered, and he disappeared from the cabin.
He didn't go directly to trouble the outer god but instead teleported onto another main ship.
He had already pinpointed the location of those Mages, and upon teleporting into the cabin, he saw two seventh-tier Mages leading a small magic squad, chanting incantations in front of a massive magical Formation.
As soon as Su Lun expanded his domain, he unceremoniously struck, decapitating the group before they could even react.
With his current strength, killing a small squad of Mages was as easy as flipping his hand!
However, his goal was not these few Mages; disrupting the ritual was just the beginning.
Their plan was for Su Lun to act first, and then when the pseudo deity exposed its methods, Pandora would launch a sneak attack to steal the divine power of faith!
As expected, the moment Su Lun disrupted the ritual Formation, the will within the black fog suddenly displayed rage and aggression, charging towards the ship where Su Lun was.
At the same time, a distant and terrifying voice echoed: "Foolish humans, you dare to desecrate the greatness of a deity!"
This voice resonated in the mind, accompanied by an almost worshipful faith-based pressure.
"Hmph!"
Su Lun snorted coldly, his expression stern.
Behind him, the shadow of the Reaper rose, instantly dispelling the daunting negative state.
A mere false god, and it truly thought it was a deity?
With Su Lun's current strength, he certainly didn't fear any false gods!

chapters.title: Chapter 559 - 559: 558
chapters.content:
The will of the Lord of the Grey Mist descended upon the ship, instantly causing Bennett and his sister to turn pale under the divine suppression.
Su Lun, with a commanding aura, dispersed the peculiar spiritual power inside the cabin, and only then did the siblings come to their senses.
With a grave expression, he said, "I'm going out now. You'd better gather your people together to stand a chance against the will of the Evil God."
"Hmm."
Bennett immediately understood and nodded in agreement.
As the commander of the royal legion, he knew a bit about dealing with false gods. His own strength wasn't enough to confront the will of the Evil God, but the legion could.
Su Lun didn't stay in the cabin any longer and used Spatial Teleportation to appear on the deck of another ship.
He had destroyed the main formation of the ritual, but there were still some followers of the "Grey Mist Sect" hiding within the fleet, which was also a significant threat.
This ship was previously confirmed by Pandora to be mostly harboring followers of the Evil God.
These fellows, seeing Su Lun approach, even tried to incite the knights and civilians on board to fight desperately, shouting, "Quick, grab that guy, he wants to disrupt His Majesty the King's funeral!"
Su Lun was not one to show mercy; with a swing of his black scythe, dozens of heads flew into the air, and blood sprayed all over the ship.
He paid no heed to the funeral attendees who were completely oblivious to the situation and continued teleporting to the next ship, creating another bloodbath.
The sudden change dumbfounded the funeral attendees on the ship; they originally thought the man with the black scythe was an enemy and just wanted to act. But at that moment, Bennett also burst onto the deck, roaring, "Miracle Troop, assemble!"
Upon seeing this, hundreds of people immediately obeyed, gathering on several ships near the flagship.
Although they didn't bring their dragon mounts on this sea voyage, the assembly of a few hundred people, with their fighting spirit merged together, was also incredibly formidable. At least with the legion's technique launched, they wouldn't be easily intimidated by the Evil God.
And in those few moments, Su Lun had almost wiped out all the mages and divine followers hidden in the fleet.
The "Lord of the Grey Mist" roared in anger beside his ear: "Stupid humans!"
Spreading faith in the Dragon Country Waters had never been easy. It took centuries to cultivate such a group of loyal followers. He thought this occasion would be a major feast, yet before the sacrifice could be enjoyed, the followers were all slain.
As these roars resounded, suddenly, the sea turned tumultuous as if signaling the apocalypse.
The black mist in the air also condensed into a human figure hundreds of meters tall.
Su Lun looked unfazed and continued to ignore the Evil God.
This guy was troublesome, but it was not easy to inflict a fatal wound on him.
Su Lun wasn't planning to collide head-on but to force the real body of this guy to appear, allowing Pandora a chance to sneak in an attack.
At this moment, the waves on the sea grew fiercer, and the single-masted sailboats in the funeral procession swayed in the storm, looking as if they might capsize at any moment. Those uninformed people didn't even know what was happening, with only terror on their faces.
After Bennett had assembled hundreds from the Miracle Troop, he roared, "That Evil God wants to use us as sacrifices. Brothers, slay the Evil God!"
The words of the royal legion commander evidently carried more conviction.
With that said, the fighting spirit of hundreds converged together, and the legion's technique charged towards the giant formed of black mist on the sea.
The fighting spirit transformed into a spear that instantly punched a hole several meters in diameter through the giant's chest.
But soon enough, the black mist reconverged, sealing the hole completely.
This way of attacking was neither painful nor itchy.
Meanwhile, that high and mighty Evil God began another round of faith brainwashing: "Ignorant and weak humans... you dare offend a great deity, beg for the forgiveness of the God of the Grey Mist, in exchange for protection and peace..."
No sooner had he spoken these mentally contaminating words than the over a hundred red boats, originally intended as sacrifices, showed fascinated expressions. Even some people's eyes gradually filled with reverence as they knelt before the giant of grey mist.
Ordinary people simply could not resist this kind of faith contamination.
Su Lun looked on, his eyebrows slightly furrowed.
An idea flashed through his mind, and in a teleport, he appeared on a ship, pinching a sorcerer's seal, and a spatial black hole appeared.
All the people he passed were sucked into the miniature void realm.
So far, Su Lun could not figure out the root of this Grey Mist Evil God and could only stop what He was trying to do.
He wanted to convert these people into followers, so Su Lun cut the ground from under His feet, taking the people away.
Since the people on the ship were very densely packed, Su Lun's collection was not slow. In just a few moments, he had taken most of the people on the ship into the miniature void realm.
Then, with another teleport, he appeared on another ship and again rushed into the most crowded cabin, chaotically taking more people.
The Grey Mist Evil God, seeing his prospective followers vanish into thin air, flew into a rage.
```
The ritual had been disrupted repeatedly, and its anger could no longer be contained. Clumps of grey mist surged towards the ship where Su Lun was.
Immediately, a sizzling corrosion sound filled the air.
Su Lun glanced at the corroded hull, a slight curve formed at the corner of his mouth. This level of corrosion might harm an average seventh-tier professional, but it couldn't breach his domain, so the impact was minimal.
He also realized that the deadly aspect of the grey mist's corrosion was its ability to cause "sustained damage."
The black fog engulfed the entire sea, affecting anyone within it. For most people, this constant damage would require the consumption of spiritual power, but for Su Lun, who possessed the "Isaac Alchemical Heart," it was not an issue. The energy consumed was far less than what was replenished.
What interested him more was how to completely solve the problem.
No news came from Pandora, so Su Lun continued his disruptions.
He teleported from one ship to another, watching as the grey mist almost whisked away nearly ten thousand people.
The "Lord of the Grey Mist" clearly realized that the mist alone could not resolve the problem. If it continued this way, not only would It fail to convert followers, but It would also run out of offerings.
Just then, suddenly, waves surged on the distant sea.
In Su Lun's perception, a massive amount of soul fluctuations surged towards him from the sea.
"A monster tide, eh..."
Su Lun was not surprised. He had guessed that this Evil God could control sea beasts since this funeral convoy had smoothly made it to the deep sea before.
Tens of thousands of monsters surged forward, their numbers seeming extremely frightening.
However, after perceiving them, it seemed there was nothing particularly troublesome. It was just their number, and to Su Lun, that was hardly a threat.
He continued rescuing the people from the ships and, at the same time, a massive cross appeared in the sky as he coalesced his spells.
Soon, fierce sea monsters began to emerge.
Su Lun did not stay on the ship but stood on the sea surface with his eight-armed spider spear. Not wanting to involve the innocent people, he moved the battlefield to the more open sea.
With a splash, a shark, several meters long, burst from the sea. It opened its massive maw, attempting to swallow Su Lun in one gulp.
But the next moment, a silent spatial rift swept across, and the large shark was cut into two sections and fell into the sea.
With that, it was as if the sea had boiled over after a drop of cold water had been added, instantly bubbling up.
Su Lun stood on the sea surface, his left hand wielding a black scythe and right holding a rune-inscribed black umbrella, wildly slashing around. Within moments, the sea was dyed red.
As numerous chunks of corpses sank into the water, it only fueled the ferocity of the sea beasts more.
Many of these creatures, driven purely by instinct, nibbled on their companions' corpses while launching attacks on Su Lun.
All kinds of sea monsters rolled in the water, akin to fresh meat thrown into a boiling, blood-red pot, churning flesh and blood.
Su Lun's eight-armed spider spear barely touched the water's surface, always landing on the rolling bodies of the monsters.
Moreover, these sea beasts were not only huge but also bizarrely deformed, like a shark with three heads, a lantern fish with hundreds of human arms, a sea eel with fleshy wings, a giant salamander covered in flesh tumors, and a tyrant sea crocodile whose mouth could open like petals into seven or eight lobes...
In short, none of them were normal.
"All mutated monsters of hellish breed... just what is this Lord of the Grey Mist?"
Su Lun looked on, not too pleased visually, but the chain scythe in his hand swung more and more deftly.
The death zone had unfolded, resulting in piles and piles of corpses. For slightly troublesome ones, the black scythe could take them away.
Soon, the sea surface was piled high with corpses.
Before long, seventh and eighth-tier distorted sea beasts also appeared, spewing fire, shooting water, dropping hail, releasing poison... all sorts of bizarre methods were employed.
But although these monsters' attacks were fierce, Su Lun was only one person. With spatial teleportation, he was almost impossible to trap.
As the number of monsters increased, they even began to injure each other, gradually turning into a massive melee.
Even if high-level monsters focused on Su Lun, if he couldn't beat them, he could still escape.
As long as no ninth-tier monsters appeared, no matter how many came, they were almost no threat to Su Lun.
Meanwhile, on the other side, the situation was not so good for the miracle legion led by Bennett.
Even though Su Lun had pulled the battlefield far away, they still faced a massive attack from the monsters.
Su Lun could hardly bear to see this group of brave knights annihilated and even asked during the fight if he should rescue them with everyone else.
But Bennett refused.
```
He said that a knight's mission was to die in battle for the country and honor, and their pride as knights made them absolutely refuse to escape before those civilians on the ship perished.
Su Lun did not say much and continued to fight.
He could only try his best to widen the battlefield, attracting the attention of the "Lord of the Grey Mist" solely towards him.
...
Thus, Su Lun drew countless deformed sea monsters around on the sea surface, causing chaos and slaughter everywhere.
Although there were some super large monsters that Su Lun could not kill, he also managed to avoid falling into peril himself.
Su Lun also realized that the "Lord of the Grey Mist" could move about through the hellish energy in the air.
But He was also completely unable to do anything against Su Lun.
This made Su Lun puzzled.
He and Pandora had previously calculated that this false god should be very strong.
But as of now, aside from using faith contamination, grey mist corrosion, manipulating storms, and controlling monsters, he did not have any other tactics.
This one seemed to be just an ordinary sea false god.
But it was because of its ordinariness that it felt abnormal.
The worse the environment, the stronger the false god that would be born, at least it should have some special abilities.
Su Lun knew that he probably hadn't really hurt him, that guy had not used his real skills yet.
So, while fighting, he also teleported to continue rescuing the civilians on those ships.
The Lord of the Grey Mist had come to feast on the sacrifices, and if Su Lun sucked all these people away, it would be strange if He did not rage.
Sure enough, just as Su Lun performed this maneuver, after he had taken away twenty to thirty thousand people, the fog on the sea surface suddenly became fierce.
"Damn humans, you have angered a great deity..."
The voice enveloped in divine wrath came through his ears again, but Su Lun did not pay any attention to it, and even internally criticized these false gods for not having the strength of a true god, yet they had thoroughly mastered this sense of superiority.
After expressing His anger through a storm, Su Lun saw a grey mist giant suddenly appearing in the distance, glowing with golden light, and knew that guy was about to reveal his true form.
As the golden light on the grey mist giant's body became denser, an indescribable oppressive force, like mountains, weighed down the sea surface.
The facial features of the grey mist giant became instantly clear, exuding majesty, as if a deity was looking down upon the mortal world.
It was this change that immediately suppressed the momentum of the Miracle Legion who was fighting Him, and they were about to be defeated.
Su Lun felt that overwhelming pressure, which was completely different from before, and thought, "Eh... it's actually divine pressure. Pandora guessed it right, this evil god might be an awareness formed from the fragmented divine force of some fallen deity from an ancient battlefield..."
This method was already at a rule level, which, under normal circumstances, even a tier-eight professional would not be able to contend with.
However, that was no longer his concern.
The best way to deal with a divine entity was to use Pandora, who belonged to the same divine system!
Almost the moment that terrifying divine power appeared, the sky suddenly turned a blood-red.
Another look revealed a crimson blood moon suspended in the sky.
The moonlight, like blood threads, easily penetrated the grey mist.
Wherever the moonlight shone, a bizarre and evil divine force, starkly different from the Lord of the Grey Mist, descended.
Just as the red and black divine forces intertwined for a moment, the red moonlight, like red silk threads piercing through black cotton, locked the black mist in place on the spot, completely unable to escape.
Simultaneously, a furious voice echoed from the void: "Damn outsider, my divine power is leaking, what exactly did you do!"
Suddenly, a fierce wind attacked the sea surface, and the golden radiant grey mist giant seemed to want to disperse his divine body to reclaim the rapidly leaking divine power.
However, strands of red moonlight confined him in place, and the grey mist giant could not free himself at all.
Su Lun saw this and his eyes slightly narrowed: "The theft was successful..."
Since Pandora made a move, the odds must not be small.
Su Lun had seen her use faith stealing several times before, skilled and seemingly without any problems.
...
And this scene left everyone on the sea surface dumbfounded.
For the vast majority of ordinary people, a false god is still a god.
They had just watched the terrifying will of the Grey Mist Evil God descend, thinking they were undoubtedly doomed.
Little did they expect the situation to turn around suddenly, and another deity appeared.
Everyone looked up to see a breathtaking figure within the red moon, dressed in a divine robe fluttering in the air, her eyebrows and eyes exuding an indescribable divine authority. She didn't make people feel fear or dominance; instead, she seemed approachable and kind, invoking a heartfelt reverence and adoration.
It was clear to everyone that the deity in the red moon was there to save them, and many clasped their hands in prayer.
After all, she had saved their lives, and no matter where this deity was from, She deserved their respect and gratitude.
As they prayed, strands of red moonlight began to intertwine, and faith was established.
Shimmering light flowed from Su Lun's left eye, witnessing this marvel.
He knew Pandora was using means to gather faith, but he didn't mind. These people, believing in the Great God under the red moon, could at least ensure
Moreover, Su Lun gradually felt a strange sensation in his heart.
It seemed... once strength reached a certain level, it naturally compelled one to protect the weaker beings, and then... faith became a sort of inevitable rule.
Now, Pandora's power ranked among the top in their realm, and her unique ability to steal faith gave her a significant advantage over ordinary false gods.
The giant from the Grey Mist, constrained by Pandora, struggled in vain.
The two sides exchanged blows with various divine techniques on the sea surface, each wave of the collision higher than the last.
Clearly, the Grey Mist giant was at a disadvantage, hanging like a giant suspended by ropes in mid-air, strong but unable to exert much force.
The Evil God tried to control sea beasts to attack Pandora, but Su Lun was not idle either. With a pinch of his sorcerer's seals, countless mechanical octopuses plunged into the water while his black scythe slashed wildly. With every stroke, a gale of bloodshed erupted.
With Pandora restraining the Evil God, Su Lun could finally unleash his full strength to kill.
Spatial ripples flashed frequently, and his figure appeared like a phantom at various points on the battleground, nearly every sweep of his scythe taking the life of a large monster; the threads were like fishing nets, ensnaring bunches of lower-tier monster carcasses...
On the other side, the Miracle Legion led by Bennett saw the dire situation turn hopeful and were overjoyed.
But they did not choose to flee, instead, they decided to join in killing those monsters.
Though they were unsure of the deity's origins in the red moon, they recognized her as an ally.
Bennett and Isabel, the siblings, even guessed that this helper was brought by "Mr. Su Lun."
...
The battle continued, and although the Miracle Legion suffered some casualties, they did not retreat.
They were truly people with the spirit of knights, and Su Lun had a favorable impression of them.
Both Su Lun and Pandora were well-prepared, so there were no unexpected occurrences.
This "Lord of the Grey Mist" was far weaker than the Evil God who had caused chaos in Lindon before, and the ambush went without any surprises.
And after a fierce battle, Su Lun realized that Pandora's power was stronger and kept growing stronger than he had initially anticipated.
She used the blood-red moonlight to imprison the Lord of the Grey Mist on the battlefield, then continuously stole Divine Power. With this give and take, the gap between them grew increasingly wider.
Thus, after fighting for an hour or two, the tumult on the sea gradually subsided.
Su Lun stood on the sea surface, littered with limbs and corpses, frowning at the weakening Evil God.
For some reason, the closer they came to the end of the battle, the more he felt something was amiss.
This "Lord of the Grey Mist" would indeed be strong in another place.
But this is the Old Dragon Kingdom Ruins.
Moreover, how could this creature control the forces of hell?
Not taking any chances, Su Lun extended his senses.
However, suddenly he saw something, his pupils narrowing sharply, "Oh, this creature's true form... is actually a mobile cursed space?"
At the horizon of Su Lun's vision, a tsunami-like black mist swept towards them.
Not from one side, but engulfing from all directions.
Identified as a cursed space, it was named the "Hell Dragon Country".
At that moment of seeing this mobile cursed space, Su Lun finally understood how the Black Sam pirate crew had been annihilated.

chapters.title: Chapter 560 - 559: Pureblood Dragons Everywhere
chapters.content:
"Su Lun, it's not good! There's a massive amount of black fog appearing above the sea. Senior Bartol said it's from the Hell Volcano eruption, and it looks like we can't avoid it..."
"Yes, I know. That's the cursed space, unavoidable. Everyone be careful not to trigger anything after entering the space. I'm dealing with a situation here and will be right over."
"...."
Just as the black fog tide appeared on the sea surface, Su Lun's communicator also received the situation from the Eternal Night.
The same black fog was about to engulf the Eternal Night as well.
Now, Su Lun had a clear understanding of the entire conspiracy of those in the Divine Plane.
It seemed that the strongest ability of the "Lord of the Grey Mist" was this. Its true form is the cursed space of the Hell Ancient Dragon Kingdom, and it can move.
The people of the Divine Plane had made a pact with this pseudo-god, offering Him a hundred thousand sacrifices in exchange for a safe passage to the deep parts of the ruins.
At the same time, there was probably also a condition to have Him eliminate Dawn Group, the team that had been a constant nuisance to them.
The "Lord of the Grey Mist" himself is not one of the strongest in combat among the pseudo-gods, but His true form is very troublesome.
For this is a "T-class" space.
Hell Dragon Country
Explanation: A T-class, super-sized cursed space where reality and illusion overlap; at the end of the Dawn Era, the Dragon God fought against the Titans' deities here, leading to a fracture in the realm, after which the energy of hell formed this cursed space; the space is filled with chaos, death, despair, plague, and disaster, as well as a large number of super-order hell creatures and vengeful spirits; unless guided by the Lord of the Grey Mist, don't expect to escape the space without Divine rank strength; the hellish energy in the space can contaminate the body and soul, eventually turning them into the dead of hell, and absorption of Spiritual Power, food, and water will all accelerate the contamination process; the black fog is like a mouth opened by the hell plane, swallowing all living beings it passes.
The grey fog stretched for dozens of miles without an end in sight, and it was unknown how large the covered area was.
Normally, even a ninth-order Space Wizard wouldn't be able to escape this range.
And this cursed space is also one of the most intractable sources of danger in this sea area.
It was the true culprit behind the annihilation of Pirate King Black Sam's pirate crew.
Having heard Old Sword God Bartolo speak in detail about the situation back then, Su Lun immediately confirmed that the grey fog was the hell energy they encountered.
T-class space, inescapable without Divine rank strength.
For anyone from the Alchemy Plane, it was almost a certain death situation.
However, Su Lun didn't look too panicked as he looked at the fog because, with the Divine King's Divine Artifact, the "Urobolos Space-Time Ring," he could almost ignore any spatial restrictions.
Including this T-class space.
Instead, he thought of something else.
The higher the level of the cursed space, the more certain it is to contain treasures.
This was a cursed space left over from the most prosperous period of alchemy civilization in the Dawn Era, and it's still T-class today, which means no living person has ever been able to bring the treasure out of the space, so naturally, the treasures go without saying.
Moreover, the "Chalice of Far" he needed was on Black Sam's St. Mary.
He had previously thought it unfindable, but wasn't it right in front of him now?
If a cursed space wasn't a dead end, then within the danger, opportunities were also hidden.
...
Watching the black fog approach, Su Lun didn't dare delay and hurried to save as many people from the sea as possible.
Save as many as could be saved.
On the other hand, the struggling grey fog giant finally dispersed.
Pandora descended from the sky and landed beside Su Lun.
At this moment, Divine Power surged all over her, and the dazzling red glow was like the light of a knife, almost too intimidating to look at directly; she appeared to have "feasted" abundantly.
Su Lun asked, "Did you kill it?"
"No."
Pandora landed next to him and then retracted her presence, shaking her head.
She continued, "But I've stolen most of His faith power, and now even forming a divine body is difficult for Him. At least for a hundred years, He won't have any strong autonomous consciousness."
The "Lord of the Grey Mist" itself was an entity formed by a trace of Divine Power within the cursed space, and with the Divine Power stolen, the consciousness would naturally slowly return to its primitive state, meaning it posed little threat.
At least, He wouldn't actively attack them anymore in the near future.
While saying this, Pandora looked at the tide-like black fog approaching and frowned, "What's with this fog tide? I have a bad feeling about it, there's a very chaotic mix of laws and Divine Power inside..."
Su Lun casually responded, "That's a cursed space."
As he spoke, he briefly explained.
Pandora listened with a slight surprise on her face, "A T-class space?"
This was not good news.
She had thought it was some kind of divine secret technique, but it turned out to be a moving cursed space.
But the next moment, she glanced at Su Lun again, her beautiful eyes gleamed, and the seriousness in her expression instantly disappeared. Instead, she asked teasingly, "Then why aren't you running?"
Based on her understanding of Su Lun's character, he was not the kind of person who would take action without certainty.
Su Lun didn't respond to the teasing tone and replied, "There's no time to escape. Besides, there's no need to run."
He had already estimated the time; the teleportation magic required time, but the dark tide would have engulfed them even sooner.
Su Lun added, "You go to the minor void realm first. I'll figure out a way to deal with this here."
Pandora shrugged and didn't ask why, lazily saying, "Okay. I do need some time to assimilate the divine power I just acquired."
"Mm."
Without further ado, Su Lun concentrated the black hole in his palm and took her into the minor void realm.
Then, glancing at the surrounded troops of the miracle legion on the sea, he teleported over and collected them as well.
Before long, the sky was filled with black mist, and the already hazy night seemed to be shrouded in another layer of netherworldly filter.
Su Lun was swept into the cursed space.
...
The light suddenly dimmed, but it was still the sea surface where they had been, with plenty of ships around.
This was a cursed space where reality and illusion overlapped.
The only difference from before was that the air was now saturated with the breath of hell.
If the concentration of the breath of hell was only 1% before, now it was 99%.
Moreover, each breath of this dense breath of hell felt like inhaling a mouthful of icy sludge, leaving both the body and soul with a chilling sensation, along with a dizzying feeling as if the soul was about to leave the body.
"So it is as I thought..."
Su Lun perceived for a moment, confirming some of the information he had previously deduced.
Hell is not a place for creatures; everything here leads to death.
However, for him, the problem was not too serious.
He didn't delay, sensed the position of the Dawn Troop, pinched the sorcerer's seals, and in the blink of an eye appeared on the deck of the Eternal Night.
As soon as he landed, countless vigilant gazes turned toward him.
Seeing that it was Su Lun, everyone breathed a sigh of relief.
Old Sword God Bartolo had previously detailed the dangers encountered before, so the Dawn Troop had also made preparations. Now the Eternal Night had erected a seal to isolate the breath, to prevent it from leaking out; everyone had put on special gas masks, for the short term.
Lolota called out, "Mr. Su Lun is back!"
Su Lun nodded, and with a grave expression, asked everyone, "How's the situation?"
Tanni replied, "The sea is full of undead monsters, with no normal creatures at all. I tried to communicate with some sea creatures before, but instead of getting any useful information, I was attacked. Fortunately, the ones attracted were low-level monsters, which we've already killed."
Upon saying this, her mother Frida also commented, "There is another worse situation, that no matter how sophisticated the seal is, it's impossible to completely isolate our breath. After all, the laws we use to draw the seals are from the living creature's plane, incompatible with the death-filled rules of hell. Our living breaths are like bright lights in hell, drifting farther and farther away... Low-level monsters are one thing, but I fear attracting those beyond our tier. I've already sensed through the wind that there are many powerful presences in this space..."
The mother and daughter were the most perceptive members of the Dawn Troop; in the cursed space, their perceptions were greatly restricted.
They couldn't actively perceive, only passively obtain some information, or else it would attract monsters.
It was like going into battle blindfolded, which is not a good start.
At that moment, Old Sword God Bartolo also confirmed, "Miss Fridel is correct. These were the conditions when our Black Sam Troop entered here before. Back then, we had a top-level cursed item that could isolate breath, thinking it could deceive these hellish monsters. But in reality, it only worked on low-tier monsters. Any trace of breath, and those beyond our tier could smell us from afar. Once found, we would certainly face monsters of the eighth tier or higher. Moreover, the water, food, lighting, and breathing here... all lead to mutations. Even with gas masks, the breath of hell will seep through our pores, leading to mutations. Back when we first came here, people got contaminated and mutated on the first day, and the number increased later on..."
Having entered this cursed space more than twenty years ago, he had the most authority to speak about it.
The members of the Dawn Troop on the deck listened intently with grave expressions.
The more they listened, the heavier the atmosphere became.
The air seemed to solidify, with not a single noisy sound, only the rigid narration of Balot.
After recounting the experience of the Black Sam Troop, he added, "The information I've gathered over the years indicates that the grey mist moves, and we can leave once the mist clears. But usually, this grey mist might last for years, or even decades. But under these conditions, the Black Sam Troop lasted less than a month, and even without encountering monsters or mutating, the repulsion of the hell plane's laws would cause our souls to leave our bodies and completely turn into undead monsters..."
Upon hearing this, everyone's complexion turned pale.
Because at this moment, they had all begun to feel their souls attempting to leave their bodies.
Although this was a cursed space, it was actually a reflection of the hell plane, and no living person had been to hell before – this fear was innate.
It was not that Old Sword God Bartolo was being alarmist, but this place had once doomed the Black Sam Troop; he spoke of the worst scenarios to prepare everyone.
Even though he was no longer at the peak of the seventh tier and had entered the so-called "Sword Saint Realm," he still had no assurance of making it out alive on his own.
After Old Sword God Bartolo finished speaking, the deck fell into dead silence.
All that could be heard was the heavy breathing of the people through their gas masks, "huff," "huff," "huff..."
However, while everyone in the Dawn Troop was immersed in grim contemplation, Su Lun and Qian Tiao exchanged glances.
Far from feeling any surprise, they shared a strange smile.
While for others it might have been their first time in such a predicament, for these two, it certainly wasn't.
Originally, inside the Mountain Yin Netherworld, besides the monsters not being of such high level, the other circumstances were almost exactly the same.
Su Lun had even confirmed by now that the Netherworld of Mountain Yin was indeed a plane within "Hell"!
And since he had previously been corrupted and mutated by the aura of the Netherworld, he felt no discomfort at all from the pollution of this hellish energy.
Instead, due to the direct connection to Hell's complete Space Law, where the ceiling was higher, he sensed his own realm showing faint signs of breaking through certain shackles.
And so did Qian Tiao beside him.
Her Sword Dao was innately pursuing the way of Hell, and the third stage of "Rakshasa Woman" had also been comprehended within the Netherworld; its insight was rooted in the plane of dead matter, the opposite of living beings.
Previously, she had said that the alchemical plane made her feel like something was missing in her cultivation. Now, back in this familiar hellish environment, she felt extremely good.
Even those who knew nothing of Sword Dao could sense that the Sword Intent radiating from her seemed to subtly resonate with the surrounding atmosphere.
Neither of them even wore gas masks, their expressions as usual.
At this moment, noticing the heavy atmosphere, Su Lun chuckled and said, "Actually, the situation isn't that bad. This cursed space, I can get out of..."
The Space-Time Ring of Urobolos was his biggest trump card to date, and even within the Dawn Era, few knew about it.
Although he didn't elaborate, with those words, the oppressive atmosphere on the deck visibly dissipated.
To escape from the cursed space?
While it sounded somewhat incredible, no one doubted it.
Everyone from the Dawn held an almost blind trust in Su Lun.
Upon hearing his words, sparks of hope lit up in their eyes.
"Really?"
"If Mr. Su Lun says so, it definitely can be done!"
"Yes!"
"Oh, I was just thinking that going to Hell is no big deal, but the greatest regret of my life is still being a virgin; dying like this would really be a pity."
"..."
In an instant, nearly everyone became excited.
Even Old Sword God Bartolo showed a fleeting unusual color in his dull eyes.
He knew very well that the law of this cursed space was frighteningly high-leveled. The Black Sam group had tried before, and it was nearly impossible to escape by any means.
Hearing Su Lun's words, he also vaguely guessed something but chose not to reveal it, merely reminiscing, "Seems like the old man was worrying too much..."
Then a faint smile surfaced on his aged face.
Su Lun didn't further explain and simply said, "This space overlaps with the outside, which means, if we continue to sail westward, we are also heading towards the target waters. There are no problems on that route."
Pausing, he continued in a relaxed tone, laughing, "If we look at it from an optimistic angle, even if we were sailing outside, the danger would still be increasing. In this cursed space, there are countless ancient treasures waiting for us to discover. If we encounter monsters that we cannot resist, we will implement Plan B. But everyone shouldn't be too careless, just like the senior Bartolo said, the dangers here will be greater than anything we've encountered before..."
But with that, the crowd got excited again.
"Hahaha... So, are we here for an adventure in Hell this time?"
"Oh, this cursed space has probably been around for hundreds of thousands of years; who knows how many treasures are here!"
"Hehe, I think this will be the most unforgettable adventure of my life..."
"Guys, we're here to adventure in Hell! It's a magical experience that no one else will ever have, only us from the Dawn Era!"
"We're off!"
"..."
Immediately, the previously tense atmosphere turned into one of anticipation for the adventure.
As long as it was not a situation certain to result in death, all members had been prepared for great risks.
It was after Su Lun's reassuring words that Dr. Banks also brought some good news.
He had been analyzing the composition of the air this whole time, and having now reached a conclusion, he interjected, "Additionally, the matter of mutation due to the hellish energy isn't too serious. Su Lun has previously experienced a similar mutation, so I've developed a specific anti-mutation Potion... in the short term, no one needs to worry too much about mutations."
Everyone, "Wow! Dr. Banks, mighty!"
With the threat of mutation gone, and it not being a death sentence, the situation completely turned around.
...
Not long after the captains' brief meeting on deck ended, the good news spread throughout the Eternal Night.
With morale boosted, it seemed like all difficulties were easily surmountable.
The members of the Dawn Era hurried about their posts, preparing for the tough battles ahead.
Because their perception was limited, the Eternal Night did not dare to sail at full speed. Everyone also tried their best to conceal their presence to avoid detection by higher-level monsters.
The only one unaffected was Grandpa Crow.
The death herald was a creature from hell, and this environment was its home turf.
It soared joyously through the sky, providing one of the few guarantees of visibility.
On the deck, Su Lun, Qiantiao, Barrett, and other high-level fighters from the Dawn Era group were also on full alert.
Bartolo was reminding everyone of some precautions: "If we encounter monsters, we must kill them quickly; if not, more and more will be drawn in over time. These hellish creatures lack intelligence, but their combat prowess was strong in life. And corrupted by the hellish qi, some are even more ferocious than before... Our Black Sam group didn't know this when we first came in and were entangled by an eighth-tier sea monster. We managed to kill it, but the fight attracted too many monsters. We fled, and the aura we left behind attracted even more monsters, resulting in the loss of over a third of our comrades..."
The others nodded frequently as they listened.
The Black Sam Pirates had fought desperately here for half a month years ago, eventually meeting their demise in this place.
But Bartolo had brought out the precious experience they had paid for with their lives.
It was also thanks to this experience that the Dawn Era group had prepared so many things in advance. Otherwise, they might have faced great trouble as soon as they entered the cursed space.
"Ah..."
As Bartolo spoke, sighs often escaped his lips.
He hadn't expected to come here again in his lifetime, nor did he imagine that his old bones could still offer some help to the younger generation.
Thinking back to the despair of those days, and now looking at the thriving Dawn Era group in front of him, it was clear that each generation was indeed stronger than the last.
Having shared much of his experience, there seemed little left to say; there were only two survival rules upon arriving here: first, either carefully avoid the monsters, or second, just keep killing.
At that moment, Bartolo turned to Qiantiao, his eyes narrowing slightly as if he noticed something, and asked, "Are you about to make a breakthrough?"
Qiantiao nodded calmly: "Yes. The rules of heaven and earth here are much more complete than outside. I feel... the opportunity to breakthrough to the eighth-tier body tyrant is coming."
Upon hearing this, the faces of the high-level fighters from the Dawn Era group changed in unison, expressing surprise.
If memory served, wasn't it just a few days ago that Qiantiao fused with a seventh-tier exoskeleton, and now she's already touching the threshold of eighth-tier?
Su Lun, however, was not surprised.
He had also noticed that since coming to this cursed space, Qiantiao seemed to be in her element as the rules from the hell plane seeping into the alchemical plane provided her with many visible benefits.
It was like when they were in the Netherworld, Su Lun discovered that her Sword Dao made astonishing progress in the hell environment, and it was then that she comprehended the Sword Saint Realm and her triple-solution talent.
Considering that the "Rakshasa Woman" mythological talent was believed to be that of a legendary Hell God General, and after her triple-solution, she had unlocked certain special hidden talents.
Su Lun felt that if they could safely get through this adventure in the Dragon Country, Qiantiao might become very strong.
However, while everyone was discussing and chatting on the deck, suddenly, a black crow in the sky let out a "caw caw."
Su Lun's pupils constricted, immediately warning, "A very powerful monster is coming at us!"
In an instant, everyone was on high alert.
The sky was shrouded in a grey haze, with low visibility, but in a flash, the Old Sword God Bartolo drew his sword without any hesitation and slashed out a Sword Qi.
By the time Su Lun and the others came to their senses and watched the Sword Qi enter the cloud cover, they saw two massive creatures falling from the sky.
On closer inspection, it turned out to be a giant dragon enveloped in dark qi?
Indeed, the reputation of the "Dragon Hunter" was well-deserved!
Moreover, this dragon looked very high-quality, with its dragon scales shiny and bright, obviously not a mixed-blood dragon.
To Su Lun's astonishment upon closer examination, it was... a pure-blooded sixth-tier necrotic dragon?
A casual slash, and a pure-blooded dragon was felled?
The people on the deck acted quickly as well, launching several steel cable nets that caught both parts of the dragon carcass and brought them back.
On realizing the truth, Su Lun understood instantly.
This was the cursed space left over from the Ancient Dragon Country era... the era when dragonkind thrived and pure-blooded giants roamed everywhere!
Most creatures in this cursed space were those that had died trapped within over countless years.
This was not some skeletal undead but a complete necrotic dragon.
"A necrotic pure-blooded dragon... isn't it perfect for my exoskeleton?"
Su Lun had wanted to find a death or darkness series dragon to forge an exoskeleton, but after inquiring in the Silver Dragon Country, found no clues.
He didn't expect to come across one so soon after arriving here, the first monster he encountered?
Although its tier was a bit low...
