But with death series creatures all over this space, why worry about not encountering higher-tier ones?
If this journey goes smoothly, not only him, but all the high-tier exoskeleton needs of other members of the Dawn Era group could be fully satisfied.
At that time, Bartolo warned again, "Be careful, there are a few more behind us!"
The members of the Dawn Era group became serious, no one expecting that their first encounter in this cursed space would be so grand!

chapters.title: Chapter 561 - 560: Terrifying Monster
chapters.content:
"Be careful, at least seven flying monsters are heading our way!"
"Close-range defense system activated, prepare to cover with fire control network!"
"..."
It was after Old Sword God Bartolo issued a warning that the ship's detection instruments also sounded an alarm, confirming the number of incoming monsters.
The appetizer was a sixth-order pureblood necrotic dragon, no one dared to take it lightly.
Everyone stared at the sky, simultaneously gulped down their taxes.
This cursed space was already dimly lit, and with thick gray fog overhead, no one had yet seen the monsters, but a terrifying draconic presence had already swept over them.
"It's a high-order dragon! Those below Rank 5, quickly head to the lower deck!"
Since the Dawn Brigade had previously hunted several dragons, they confirmed the enemy attack, and everything was tense but orderly.
However, the high-rank fighters on the deck showed their imposing presence all around them.
They had felt the oppressive power of an eighth-order pureblood dragon, but the terrifying draconic presence sweeping through the sky now was several times stronger than the previous eighth-order silver dragon!
Old Sword God Bartolo's expression became stern, he clearly realized something and urgently said, "Be careful, we may have attracted a flock of dragons!"
As soon as he finished speaking, he leaped from the deck into the sky.
The Black Sam Brigade had once encountered such an attack; he knew all too well that they absolutely couldn't let this group of necrotic dragons get close to the ship.
At the same time, the high-rank fighters of the Dawn Brigade exchanged glances and also entered combat mode.
Bartolo had previously advised that they must kill monsters quickly, otherwise the noise of the battle would attract even farther and stronger monsters.
No one dared to be careless.
As soon as his words fell, those massive shadows in the fog were already diving rapidly. Before their bodies arrived, a wave of poison gas swept over them, dizzying even through their gas masks.
Dr. Banks's body was the best toxin sensor; he noticed the problem and immediately warned, "Be careful, that's Green Dragon's Breath! It's a potent mixed toxin, extremely lethal; the gas masks can't fully isolate it. Immediately use 'Hairei Triple Luck Anti-Poison Potion,' and if poisoned, use 'Antidote Potion No. 7' for emergency treatment!"
Over the communicator, an adviser immediately relayed the instructions into everyone's ears on the ship.
The Dawn Brigade had their own biological potion factory with an abundant supply of various potions.
As a result, the toxin that could wipe out most adventure brigades posed no threat to the members of the Dawn Brigade.
When that yellow-green dragon breath was exhaled, there was immediately a sizzling corrosion sound in the air.
Just as the dragon breath was about to hit the Eternal Night, No. 19 Golden Wings spread out, already rushing to the forefront. Only her metallic body could perfectly block the exhaled dragon breath.
And Captain Barrett followed closely; clad in Dragon Knight heavy armor, he also acted as a tank attracting fire.
Following them, the 'Blood Duke' Wazwas led a group of high-ranking vampires into the highly corrosive poison fog.
No one held back, unleashing various killing moves.
Simultaneously, the ship's close-range guns automatically aimed at the sky, "rattling" like a torrential downpour of ammunition, creating sparks as they struck those dark shadows in the sky.
The battle had reached its most intense moment from the start.
Everyone on the deck sprang into action, but only Qianniao still hadn't moved.
It wasn't that she didn't plan to fight, but rather she was building up her Sword Qi.
At this moment, behind her, the six-armed Rakshasa Golden Body's phantom shone brightly, her body's Thunder Hell Sword Intent growing denser and denser.
Su Lun with his sorcerer's seals in hand, continued to reinforce the spatial restrictions on the Eternal Night, not allowing the dragon riders to approach.
But at this moment, he felt a familiar Sword Intent and glanced sideways.
All members of the Dawn Brigade in this cursed space felt suppressed by this hellish aura to varying degrees, including Su Lun himself. Only Qianniao not only felt no suppression at this moment as she entered combat mode, but more and more of that hellish aura gathered towards her.
Su Lun watched, whispering to himself, "Is she going to use that move..."
The Rakshasa Woman possessed a secret technique that could rob all beings of their vital essence.
She had used it once when she was in the Netherworld.
That time, she forcibly devoured a finger of a Fallen Angel, in exchange gaining a terrifying combat strength far exceeding her level.
After that, she never used it again.
The outside world didn't provide the conditions to use that move, nor was there a situation so desperate that survival demanded it.
But now, in this cursed space nearly identical to real hell, Qiantiao seemed to have regained that feeling.
At this moment, the Rakshasa phantom behind her once again condensed into a gilded physical form, radiating golden light that extended several meters. The Rakshasa form bore two faces, one with furrowed brows and angry eyes, the other sanctimoniously serene, with golden light spreading like burning golden flames, looking like a true deity, haughty, scornful, and domineering!
"She's really starting to look like a deity..."
Su Lun muttered to himself, never having seen her Rakshasa Golden Body shine so brilliantly, like a forbidden tale from the divine realms, where her triple transformation was said to be a deity reincarnate.
Once the Rakshasa apparition appeared behind Qiantiao, the sky suddenly darkened with dense clouds, and in an instant, a myriad of lightning converged upon her.
Bathed in endless purple-black lightning, Qiantiao "stepped on air," shooting into the sky like a bolt of lightning.
Watching Qiantiao fluidly teleport through the air, Su Lun was surprised and thought, "Hmm... has she mastered 'Imperial Air Walk'?"
This wasn't "Stepping on Air," but rather "Imperial Air Walk," a legendary-level movement technique.
This was a technique extremely difficult to master, and even martial arts grandmasters were not known to use it fluently.
Su Lun had so far only seen it demonstrated by Bartolo, and he was surprised that Qiantiao had mastered it?
This technique, unlike Stepping on Air which required continuous bursts to remain airborne, was about mastering the essence of Qi to float at will.
For any close-combat professional, this technique was nearly divine.
However, this movement was secondary, as what happened next was even more astonishing!
Qiantiao ascended into the air, her hand on the hilt of her sword, sword intent accumulating to its peak.
Everyone seemed to hear a whisper in their ears: "When I draw my sword, it is hell itself."
Watching her leap into the sky, her Demon Blade left its scabbard in a flash, releasing a sword Qi tens of meters long.
Sword Qi as fast as lightning, reaching its target in the blink of an eye.
This single strike seemed as if it could split the hellish space itself, its might absolutely terrifying.
"Whoosh," a shadow in the mist, leaping up, was instantly split in two and fell from the sky.
Su Lun's eyes flickered at this sight.
He was about to lend a hand but quickly dismissed the idea, thinking to himself, "She's really standing firm now..."
Dragons were not easy to kill, even if Su Lun could now kill an average tier-seven professional easily, killing a pure-blooded tier-six dragon alone was not an easy feat.
Even now, Duke Bloodsworn Wazhuas, who was at the eighth tier, also had to use some tricks.
To manage such a clean and quick dragon-slaying with one strike definitely involved the elusive realm of "cutting through rules" that Bartolo had spoken of.
Su Lun could tell that although Qiantiao's strike was still somewhat less compared to one of Bartolo's previous strikes, and the gathering of qi also took some time, it already far surpassed that of the previous Sword Saint.
This represented a true qualitative change in the realm for any swordsman.
...
The sudden eruption of Qiantiao left the whole Dawn Group stunned.
With her and Bartolo providing superior output, the seven dragons in the sky hadn't even had a chance to wreak havoc before four tier-six undead flying dragons were slain.
The crew on the deck quickly captured and collected the bodies.
Su Lun had identified that these seven undead dragons were green dragons in life, skilled in poison and natural dragon language magic, their combat abilities also somewhat lower among dragons of the same tier.
The only real trouble now was their number.
Seven pure-blooded giant dragons took off together... Such a scene could not be seen anywhere else outside.
There were also three seventh-tier dragons in the sky.
Though it was only one tier higher, their combat power was completely different from that of the sixth tier.
The high-level fighters of the Dawn group didn't dare delay, they employed every tactic they had. For even as they fought, the sea had already drawn various kinds of monsters, and more disturbances arose in the distance...
Fighting in this cursed space felt like lighting a bonfire in the Monster Beast Forest, suddenly illuminating countless green eyes from the depths of the jungle.
Three seventh-tier giant dragons were not a small trouble, if this were to be the imperial waters of the Luying Empire where pirate groups like the "King of the Western Sea" and "King of the South Sea" roamed, three dragons would be enough to annihilate any of their fleets.
Fortunately, the Dawn group already had ample experience in dragon hunting. Bartolo held off one, number nineteen held another, while Su Lun chose a dragon marked with spatial coordinates, and teleported onto its back in an instant.
The undead dragons in this cursed space retained most of their strength from when they were alive, but what they distinctly lacked was intelligence; their fighting was nearly all instinctive.
Compared to a cunning living giant dragon, an undead dragon was much easier to deal with.
When Su Lun teleported over, the undead dragon didn't even sense any danger and continued to attack the Huazhuas Nasir people, who were serving as bait. A mechanical octopus was summoned and effortlessly locked down its wings, followed by concentrated fire.
Before long, Su Lun had slashed off the enormous head of the dragon with his dragon-slaying dagger.
This was much easier than the time they had hunted the seventh-tier thunder lightning dragon.
However, just as they had killed one dragon, a demonic wind suddenly rose from the sea, and a hundred-meter-high wave surged from afar.
As the crows in the sky cawed loudly, Su Lun's gaze swiftly turned in that direction.
The All-knowing Eye allowed him to have the sharpest vision in the group, and he saw a "light ball" hidden within the waves, tens of meters in diameter.
At first, he was stunned and didn't realize what it was, but when he identified it as an eyeball, his expression drastically changed.
An eyeball tens of meters in size?
How big must the monster hidden in the sea be?
Yet, that was just the beginning.
The moment he focused his gaze, hundreds of similarly large "light balls" lit up in that patch of the sea; they belonged to a white-eyed monster.
Suddenly, Su Lun's hair stood on end, feeling even more dangerous than encountering an eighth-tier giant dragon.
He quickly said into the communicator, "Tanni, start the boat and leave fast! Full speed south!"
"Alright!"
Tanni responded, then immediately in the communicator, "Activate the alchemy sails!"
Though the others didn't understand what was happening, they executed the order immediately.
The alchemical runes on the sails of the Eternal Night lit up, furiously propelling the sails, and the several hundred meters long battleship instantly moved.
It was then that the people on the ship gradually realized that the ship had started to tilt, and a wall of tsunami hundreds of meters high appeared in front of them, like a giant hand trying to roll the ship to the north.
If this tsunami were to hit, even a ship the size of the Eternal Night might capsize on the spot.
Luckily, there was a top-tier navigator on board.
Tanni shouted, "Everyone, be careful, we're going to ride this wave!"
The ship was equipped with an automatic sail control device, which allowed precise control of the many sails on the Eternal Night at the right moment.
Not just the alchemy sails, Tanni's mother Frida transformed into the Goddess Naga, her mouth blowing into the "Rainbow Conch," and as the beautiful melody emanated, everyone felt an inexplicable exhilaration; the waves and wind also cheered up with the tune, and the speed of the Eternal Night shot up sharply, racing up the waves like an arrow loosed from a bowstring.
Under Tanni's exquisite navigation, the Eternal Night surfed the giant wave like a flexible surfboard. It didn't travel in the direction of the wave but raced up the wave crest, and with a lift of the alchemy sails, the whole battleship leaped clear of the wave's grasp.
Su Lun let out a huge sigh of relief at this sight.
At least they wouldn't need to use Spatial Ability to escape right away.
However, just as the Eternal Night escaped the wave, the terrifying sea beast seemed enraged, and a tentacle several meters in diameter whipped out from the sea.
"Captain Barrett, watch out!"
Because Su Lun sensed something abnormal in the sea ahead of time, his eyes and hands were quick, and he teleported next to Barrett, who was wearing heavy armor and moving slowly. In an instant, both disappeared.
Almost at the same moment, a tentacle in the sea whipped the space where Barrett had just stood like a whip.
It was not physically fast, but it was strangely "inevitable" on a rule level!
Although Su Lun and he narrowly avoided it, there was still a seventh-tier undead giant dragon there.
The dragon hadn't reacted yet when the fleshy tentacle suddenly wrapped around it and dragged it into the sea, creating a splash of white waves.
Seeing this, even the presence of Old Sword God Bartolo couldn't help but make his pupils shrink.
A single tentacle took down a seventh-tier dragon in seconds?
That whip seemed to strike at the heart of everyone present, sending a chill down everyone's back, marking the first time they witnessed the terror of this cursed space.
The creature from the depths wasn't just beyond its tier; at least it had the strength of the ninth tier unquestionably!
Fortunately, its enormous size meant it likely moved slowly, possibly even being rooted to the sea bed, unable to move at all.
This also meant the monster's hunting range with its tentacles was limited.
But the Eternal Night hadn't completely escaped the danger zone and still needed people to hold it off.
At that moment, Su Lun shouted, "You all go first, I'll stay behind to draw the monster's fire."
The members of Dawn Group didn't tangle further with the remaining seventh-tier undead dragon and decisively left the battlefield.
They were well aware that when it came to survival abilities, no one was stronger than Su Lun.
Once he saw everyone leave, Su Lun raised his hand to form sorcerer's seals, and suddenly, dozens of living corpses appeared around him.
Threads pulling, the living corpses flew all over the sky.
The living corpses retained all the signs of life, and their appearance immediately attracted the attention of the sea monster.
Just as everyone had just left, dozens of tentacles burst forth from the sea, and those living corpses, with virtually no room to evade, were wrapped up, their bodies burst open, and dragged into the water.
Even Su Lun's "substitute puppet" was pulled into the sea.
Fortunately, his small void realm contained a warehouse of living corpses, amply stocked.
As one batch was destroyed by the monster, Su Lun immediately fetched another batch.
These living corpses, without any attempt to mask their presence, emitted a strong "living breath," permeating the entire sea and drifting towards the distance...
Su Lun concentrated intently on the turbulent waters, using evasive movements to barely make out the monster's complete form. It resembled a sea anemone, its body alone spanning seventeen to eighteen kilometers in diameter, with numerous fleshy tentacles of varying lengths and a densely packed, writhing, toothy maw at its center.
The identified name was called "Hell Anemone (Overlord)."
It was also fortunate that the Eternal Night had fled quickly; the wave just now was caused by the monster contracting its body like a Venus flytrap, swallowing the sea and everything within a dozen kilometers.
Taking Su Lun along with it.
Fortunately, he teleported out safely.
At this point, Su Lun gave up all thoughts of trying to sneak advantages.
A monster of this scale was nearly invincible, so much so that even if Old Sword God Bartolo were to strike a hundred blows, it might only scratch it.
Having seen this monster, Su Lun finally got a glimpse of the tip of the iceberg of the dangers within this cursed space.
It's no wonder that Black Sam and his group of legendary adventurers had assembled and still fell here in the past.
Just the monster alone was an unsolvable knot.
The monster swallowed nearly every other creature nearby in the sea and then quieted down.
However, Su Lun didn't let it rest, deploying a few living corpse baits, alleviating some of Dawn Group's navigation pressure.
Seeing the Eternal Night was far enough away, he then teleported to catch up.

chapters.title: Chapter 562 - 561 Lost City
chapters.content:
```
PS. Slightly watered down.
The Alchemy Wind Sail and Steam Boiler-powered Eternal Night surged across the ocean like a swift shark.
From a far distance, everyone witnessed that terrifying creature's feast, each of them feeling a chill down their spine.
If they had been just a step slower and had gotten swallowed by that creature, the consequences would have been unimaginable.
However, when Su Lun teleported onto the deck, the heavy stone in the hearts of the Dawn group finally fell, and they all breathed a sigh of relief.
After all, they had escaped without harm.
Everyone exchanged glances, the smiles on their faces reflecting the joy of a narrow escape from death.
To adventurers, difficulties could be a rare experience, especially one as thrilling and hellish as this that probably nobody else could attempt.
With no casualties, everyone from the Dawn was in a good mood.
Seeing Su Lun return safely, the Sword Intent that had been gathered around Qian Tiao dissipated. She then lazily murmured, "Ah, what a pity. I was just getting into a combat state."
Hearing this, Lolo Tata, full of starry eyes, said, "Teacher, you just slashed a sixth-order undead dragon with one strike, super awesome!"
Qian Tiao looked at her disciple with a hint of irritation.
Su Lun also felt it was a pity, as her condition a moment ago was truly a rare opportunity.
Fortunately, in this environment rich with the energies of hell, Qian Tiao's condition seemed to be excellent all the time. That previous strike had almost solidified her new realm, and it might provide a new opportunity for consolidation.
Because they had already anticipated the dangers of the Dragon Country Waters, even after a battle that nearly wiped out their group, everyone's morale was still high.
The exploration of the unknown and adventure were, after all, also the greatest pleasures of sailing.
"Oh, I have never seen such a large creature in my life. Speaking of which, the beings from hell sure are strange."
"But, we got quite a harvest this time, four sixth-order pureblood undead dragons and one of the seventh order... You can't find such good materials easily outside."
"Hahaha, yes, I heard from Old Sword God Bartolo that there are many ancient relics in this space too."
"Tsk, tsk, a cursed space that no one has ever left alive, who knows how many treasures are hidden."
"..."
The atmosphere among the people chatting on the deck was relaxed. With the crisis behind them, they now had more anticipation for the route ahead.
The lights were out again on the ship, and the surroundings fell back into that dim, hellish gloom.
While chatting idly, the members of the Dawn also busily went about their duties, cleaning up the blood on the deck, collecting the tons of casings from the close defense cannons, restocking the ammunition... and so on.
After the battle ended, everyone knew that more fighting was bound to happen soon.
...
Su Lun walked onto the deck, and a few management and staff members of the Dawn group gathered around.
Barrett, having removed his heavy armor helmet, revealed his head and looked at the still tumultuous sea, laughing, "Hey, I've never seen such a big monster in my life. Tsk, tsk, what a marvelous adventure this has been."
Number Nineteen: "Yeah, where do the living get to come to hell. I also just found out hell is like this..."
'Duke of Blood' Wazhuaz chuckled, "Not just you, I've lived for nearly eight hundred years, and I've never seen anything like it either."
Dora: "But the harvest is truly bountiful. We've just arrived and already bagged five pureblood giant dragons. These materials are rare treasures indeed."
Old Sword God Bartolo also marveled, "Yes. In the outside world, you'd probably not encounter one in several years."
In his twenty years of dragon hunting, he had only encountered three pureblood giant dragons. Now, they had hunted five in one go—it was indeed a significant haul.
But what he marveled at even more was the vitality of the Dawn group.
Compared to the Black Sam group that had gradually despaired in this space, such peril became merely an exciting adventure for this young team.
There was some casual conversation among the group.
At this time, Su Lun took out a sea chart, getting down to the main topic, "You all saw the situation just now. I think we need to replan our sailing route..."
```
Upon hearing this, everyone's gaze converged on the sea map.
The map on the paper meticulously marked various islands in the Dragon Country Waters, wind directions, ocean currents, and the scale was also extremely precise.
Such an excellent sea map naturally came from the hands of the professional chart maker Tanni.
Su Lun had had a "Map of the Dragon Country Waters" before, but the ancient cartography skills were far from as accurate as modern ones, so he had Tanni redraw a new one.
Moreover, this new sea map not only included all the annotations of the previous map but also the route of Black Sam's crew, as told by Bartolo, and various other documents found in the treasury of the Silver Dragon Country. It already contained all the information known by the Dawn crew.
Compared to when Black Sam's crew set out with just a fragment of a treasure map, this map was already improved a countless number of times.
Su Lun pointed and said, "Our current situation has changed from our original plan, so I wanted to discuss with everyone about which course to take next..."
The location they entered the cursed space was more than ten days' sailing less than where Black Sam's crew had, which brought a lot more variables into the future.
The others understood Su Lun's point and began to discuss openly.
"Since this cursed space's navigation is pretty much the same as the outside world, I think we should continue sailing according to the original planned route. After all, every part of this unfamiliar sea carries risks..."
"Agreed."
"..."
The efficiency of the discussion was high, and they directly came up with a plan for the subsequent voyage.
Su Lun had already considered everything thoroughly, so the purpose of the discussion was mainly to inform everyone.
At this time, Su Lun added, "There's another issue... We have to deal with more than just the monsters in this cursed space. I believe those gods from the divine plane will probably be looking for us too."
Upon hearing this, everyone's expression became gravely serious.
In comparison to monsters, the threat of the mages from the divine plane was equally significant.
Especially in such an environment, if a significant battle broke out, it was hard to say who would have the upper hand.
However, Qiantiao seemed not only unbothered by this news but actually full of anticipation, and asked, "Su Lun, are you saying that the Red-robed Mage will actively seek us out?"
"Uh-huh. It's very likely he will come."
Su Lun nodded, then continued, "That guy is a Necromancer by nature, which makes this environment his home turf for battle. Most importantly, all the legacies of his and his necromancer line are with me. I think he would risk his life, if necessary, to try to take it back. And..."
"This is his only chance. Outside, he couldn't do anything to us even in his prime, and now that he's reduced to just a soul fire, it's even less likely."
After Su Lun had taken stock of the Red-robed Mage's spoils, he discovered the haul was even greater than it had seemed.
From those magic notes, Su Lun learned that the Red-robed Mage was named Yale Robbins, a member of the 'Holy Soul Fire' necromancy faction, and also a high-ranking cleric of the Holy Army.
The books and such were the secret techniques passed down through the "Robbins lineage" for a thousand years.
In essence, those items represented the legacy of a divine-grade magic system.
This kind of complete legacy was a priceless treasure even in the divine plane.
And the undead space and the countless monsters inside it were also the accumulations of a millennium of necromancer inheritance from that 'Holy Soul Fire' line.
Having lost such important things, that guy surely had no face to return to the divine plane.
That's why Su Lun was sure he would take the initiative to come after them.
And indeed, only in this cursed space did he stand a slight chance in a fight.
With this analysis, the members of the Dawn crew nodded in agreement.
Barrett said, "We definitely need to be wary of that guy causing trouble, yeah. Though a mage just with his soul might not be much of a threat, if he attracts monsters to besiege us, that could be bad."
Officer Nineteen said, "Necromancers specialize in controlling all sorts of undead creatures, and this cursed space is, sadly, full of such creatures, so we have to be especially careful..."
Dora commented, "That guy was able to find us last time, he'll surely be able to this time too. Maybe he's already laying in ambush somewhere."
Mr. Hei speculated, "He probably used divination spells to pinpoint our location. After all, that guy is a servant of the gods, capable of exempting himself from death's consequences, naturally he could also avoid some of the costs of divination. But we have no way to determine his coordinates, which puts us at a disadvantage."
Huazuwas said, "..."
"..."
The topic shifted, and everyone analyzed all sorts of possibilities from a tactical and strategic perspective.
Having used the tactic of luring the disaster east many times, Su Lun and the others were especially cautious.
But it was precisely the uncertainty of the enemy's location that made them feel passive.
The only one enthusiastic was Thousand Eyes with his bright and eager eyes, who muttered expectantly, "Ah...my 'Slaughter Buddha' is coming..."
Listening to him, Su Lun didn't know whether to laugh or cry, but then shared his own idea, saying, "What I mean is, since we can't pin down that guy's position, we can deduce where he's likely to set up an ambush, and then turn the tables."
"Oh?"
Everyone turned to look at him upon hearing this.
They knew all too well that Su Lun never disappointed, and whenever he spoke up, he certainly had a method in mind.
Su Lun went into detail, "I've studied all of the undead secret techniques of that guy's lineage in depth. Their lineage has weak physical combat power but specializes in soul secret techniques. Now that he only has his soul fire left, his ability to control ghost monsters is very limited. I estimate that he could at most command monsters around the eighth tier. Therefore, to pose a threat to our Dawn Group, he's unlikely to confront us head-on; he's more likely to choose a place dense with ghost-type monsters... And also, this place will be somewhere our route must pass through."
With that said, everyone remembered the scene of that guy's soul fleeing.
After a moment of thought, they immediately understood, and their expressions collectively brightened.
Yes, indeed...
From knowing the enemy's capabilities, they could deduce his intentions, and then easily infer the decisions the enemy would make, right?
As long as they could figure out what the enemy planned to do, wasn't that the same as indirectly determining the enemy's location?
Upon hearing this, Old Sword God Bartolo also looked at him with an approving gaze, saying, "Young Su Lun has a really good approach. There are indeed many ghost-type monsters in this cursed space, even more dangerous than ordinary monsters... Thinking about it this way, that guy has no other choice."
Everyone agreed with the plan after listening.
Su Lun shrugged as everyone agreed with his idea, then threw a damper on the enthusiasm, "However, there's one problem with this plan: there are many ghost-type monsters in the cursed space, and I'm not sure which place that guy will choose."
Hearing this, everyone felt it was indeed a problem.
The cursed space was never short of monsters.
Who could guarantee which monsters the enemy would command to attack them?
"This may not be a big issue."
But upon hearing this, Bartolo chuckled and shook his head.
Having been here before, he had a plan in mind, saying, "Although we can't be sure of where the enemy will ambush us, we can decide our own sailing direction! No matter by what means the enemy knows our whereabouts, they can only determine where we will go, not lead us there. The initiative is in our hands. We can simply find a place with many ghosts, making the enemy definitely choose to make a move there... and then get rid of that guy first."
Only by dealing with the enemy first could they sail with peace of mind.
Otherwise, endless dangers awaited.
Upon hearing this, Su Lun immediately knew that the Old Sword God must have an idea and asked, "Do you know of such a place, senior?"
"Hmm."
Bartolo thought and said, "When my Black Sam Group entered this space, we encountered a human kingdom's ruins where there were numerous ghost monsters. At that time, we had to flee to survive and didn't dare to look closely at the ruins. That place is very suitable for a necromancer's ambush."
He then pointed out the coordinates on the sea chart.
Seeing it, Su Lun immediately felt the plan was perfect!
Bartolo continued, "However, the only trouble is that ghost-type monsters have resistance to physical and magic attacks, which makes it tricky for those who have not mastered 'Haki'. Moreover, there might be many high-tier monsters in that ruin, and without a way to cope, that too would be a big problem."
Hearing this, Dora, the group's chief mechanic, butted in, "That's not too big of a problem. The Mafa military had previously developed special 'Purple Light Bullets' and 'Mithril Bullets' which are very effective against dark and ghost-type monsters. Although the ammunition reserves in our warehouse are not very plentiful, the war workshop could work overtime these next few days to produce some. As long as we have enough ammo, it should be enough to handle most situations."
At that, 'Blood Duke' Wazhawas twitched at the corner of his eye.
To his clan, that ammunition was all too familiar.
'Mithril Bullets' were anti-evil ammunition, which not only had killing power against ghost monsters but also inflicted massive damage on his blood clan.
Those Demon Hunters from the Bounty Guild had often used this type of ammunition to kill his blood kin.
But no one had heard of "Purple Light Bullets".
Dora explained that they were a type of ammunition that extracted divine elements from sunlight, and they were a product of secret research in magic.
Previously, these special types of ammunition hadn't been used much on the battlefields against the two great empires, so they were relatively unknown.
Su Lun, however, was aware of them, which is why he came up with this plan.
Moreover, he had powerful means of dealing with ghosts himself and said, "If we're talking about soul monsters, I can restrain them too. Plus, I've just repaired a soul curse item I obtained earlier, which can even handle high-tier spectral creatures."
With that said, no one had any more concerns.
The Dawn Team now consisted of some of the most elite experts from nearly every field in the alchemy plane: mechanics, biotechnology, traditional alchemy, legion command, sailing... So whenever a problem arose, they could almost immediately come up with a good solution.
Gathering around the map, everyone continued to discuss and finalize the details as they awaited the enemy's approach.
...
Half a month passed in the blink of an eye.
The "Eternal Night" continued its voyage on the Hellish Sea.
Their route remained the same as Black Sam's team's old route. Though equally fraught with danger and the unknown, at least that route avoided some particularly deep areas, where the monsters tended to be less powerful.
Nevertheless, in these past days, they had encountered many battles.
Fortunately, the Dawn Team was now much stronger than Black Sam's group had been and was well-prepared, so they managed to get through without any mishaps.
Though they encountered some hellish creatures of enormous size, thankfully, they did not come across anything insurmountable like the previous "Hellish Sea Anemones".
As for the mutative factors in this cursed space of Hell Dragon Country, which had brought despair to Black Sam's team regarding breathing, drinking water, food, and such, they posed only a limited threat to the Dawn Team. They had prepared ample supplies and could sustain themselves for quite some time without relying on external resources. Moreover, within Su Lun's pocket void, they already had their own farm and water recycling system. Even if they depleted their food reserves, they would be self-sufficient for countless years.
One day, the "Eternal Night" continued sailing forth.
On the deck, Su Lun and Tanni were meditating at the top of the mast.
Since entering this cursed space more than ten days ago, the danger alarms had almost never ceased.
Being on constant alert for battle all day was a torment for everyone's psyche. Normal people would break down in just a few days and be more prone to mutations.
Therefore, the senior warriors of the team took over most of the normal members' duties and assumed surveillance responsibilities, allowing others to rest in rotation.
Since the environment affected Su Lun and Tanni the least, both of them had been acting as lookouts atop the mast almost all the time.
Neither spoke, silently meditating.
Expanding their awareness, they watched over everything surrounding them.
Su Lun did not open his eyes, but that did not mean he was unaware of the changes happening to Tanni next to him.
Each breath sounded like thunder from within his chest.
On this voyage toward the heart of the ruins, he could clearly feel the laws of the world becoming more complete, given that this cursed space was connected to the actual hellish dimension.
In such an environment, Tanni blossomed, growing stronger and stronger.
She grew so strong that it seemed as if she and this hellish realm had become one.
Su Lun was pleased to see it.
However, during a moment of thoughts drifting by, suddenly!
Su Lun abruptly opened his eyes while meditating.
Mr. Crow at the top of the mast shared his vision, and he faintly saw traces of buildings in the extreme distance.
"Are we there?"
Seeing the majestic city with massive white columns, Su Lun immediately realized that it might be the ancient ruins mentioned by the Old Sword God Bartolo.
This could be a city from the Dawn Era, marked on the incomplete treasure map obtained by Black Sam's team as the Lost City—Atlantis.

chapters.title: Chapter 563 - 562: 【Descartes' Crystal Skull】
chapters.content:
Su Lun saw the city half submerged in seawater at the edge of his vision and issued a warning.
Before long, almost everyone on the ship had begun to move.
"Wow... to think there's such a magnificent city! It's almost on the same scale as Ruins City..."
"My God, all the buildings in the city are made of stone! What methods did the artisans of ancient times use to construct such tall houses from stone alone?"
"Hehe, this City of Atlantis is a relic from the Dawn Era, who knows what treasures are hidden inside..."
"..."
By the ship's rail and on the mast, members of the Dawn Group were peering through telescopes at the distant city.
The time and space within the cursed space are different from the outside world, thus preserving the ancient city that should have been lost in the river of time long ago.
The crew now appeared as though they were gradually turning a page already read in historical texts, crossing time to witness the remnants of that once-glorious civilization.
The crew also noticed a strange phenomenon; the surrounding seas were dim, but the seawater near the city exhibited a faint glowing blue.
As the ship drew nearer, the lookout immediately issued a warning, "There's something in the water! It looks like glowing jellyfish... Eh... no! They're ghosts!"
With that, everyone alert.
The sound of guns being cocked erupted in rapid succession.
Su Lun had actually noticed this much earlier; he was holding a rune umbrella, and many soul fluctuations had already appeared within his sensory range.
It's just that many ordinary people couldn't see them.
Old Sword God Bartolo had mentioned before that this ruins city was teeming with ghostly creatures, and they had planned to head in this direction.
Only the high-level warriors knew about the plan to ambush the celestial plane's necromancer which is why the crew were so astonished.
The Perpetual Night was slowly heading towards the Lost City, and more ghosts appeared near the ship, with some faint blue spiritual bodies visible to the naked eye.
Gradually, everyone realized that these ghosts weren't aggressive, and no one acted out.
At this moment, they finally understood that the faint glowing blue they had seen earlier was the light emitted by these ghosts.
These spiritual bodies were of a low rank, their features vague and expressionless, with no inclination to attack.
They were just drifting aimlessly on the surface and within the water.
Seeing the confusion of the crew, Mr. Hei explained, "According to texts from certain sects, after people die, their souls either go to heaven or to hell. Souls that linger on earth become ghosts, gradually forgetting everything about their lives, unable to find their way back or forward, forever lost in the mortal realm."
Listening to this, everyone nodded in understanding.
Su Lun was aware of this belief too.
But he saw something else.
His studies on souls were now profound, and he could clearly feel the condition of the soul bodies. He knew well that these were just ordinary remnants without any malevolent spirits, incapable of becoming malevolent ghosts.
However, the gathering of so many spiritual bodies in this City of Atlantis was quite unusual.
Su Lun narrowed his eyes at the distant city, and a guess emerged in his mind, "There's treasure..."
Souls also dissipate; the fact that so many spiritual bodies were gathered here without dissipating meant that something within the city was beneficial to soul bodies.
Nevertheless, it was normal for ancient ruins to contain treasures.
Su Lun's thoughts shifted again, wondering where exactly that necromancer would emerge from.
...
The journey was farther than it appeared.
After sailing for about half an hour, the Perpetual Night finally reached the outskirts of the city.
It was a huge city, half-drowned in seawater, with no visible end. But the buildings within looked like uneven rocks, and a large ship like the Perpetual Night couldn't enter.
Su Lun then called for everyone to prepare to disembark.
On hearing they were going to search for treasure in the ruins, the Dawn Group immediately became excited.
But as it was a dangerous place, they couldn't take too many people.
And with some going, some had to stay to watch the ship, and everyone hurried to volunteer.
Lolita, clutching at a thousand arms, didn't let go, clamoring, "Wow... Teacher, Teacher! I want to go!"
Tanni also looked at Su Lun excitedly, saying, "Mr. Su Lun, I want to go too, take me with you..."
The Naga Tatu also didn't want to fall behind, "This place is all seawater, our Naga race is more suited for finding treasures..."
Others: "Me too, me, me..."
Su Lun was well aware that he was the target of the enemy, and naturally, he had to go.
Qian Tiao was still keen on that Skeleton Sword Deity and the Famous Sword Fo Tu, so he also decided to go.
In the end, the two least affected by their surroundings, along with Mr. Hei, the scholar, led a group of excited Dawn Era youths in a small boat towards the ruins.
The Old Sword God Bartolo stayed on the ship, firstly to guard the vessel, and secondly to provide an opportunity for the Necromancer to make a move.
Otherwise, with such a presence capable of slaying his indestructible body, the Necromancer might not dare to show himself.
...
Su Lun and his group then rowed a small boat into the city.
Tens of meters high, most of the city walls were submerged in water, with only one or two meters exposed above the surface. There were signs of collapse everywhere, as if a tremendous force had pushed outwards from within.
The small boat navigated through a breach in the city walls.
Once inside, they found themselves in a residential area completely submerged under seawater.
The water was very clear, and under the blue light, the sharp angles of the buildings were distinctly visible; seaweed floated gently.
If it weren't for the many ugly, deformed marine creatures swimming around, this underwater ruins scene would definitely be considered stunningly beautiful.
Su Lun was now proficient in the architectural styles of various eras; the layout of the buildings in the City of Atlantis reminded him of the temple style in the northern four countries of Roman.
From the rooftops of the buildings in the city, he could roughly guess their functions.
Temples, concert halls, theaters, arenas, public baths... etc.
The city was too large, possibly accommodating tens of millions of residents; it was impossible for them to search every nook and cranny.
So Su Lun directly targeted the temple at the highest point of the city.
Typically, such places were where the most important treasures were stored.
He also noticed that the closer they got to the center of the ruins, the stronger the spirits became.
Su Lun felt that if he were the Necromancer, the best choice would be to ambush them after they delved deeper into the ruins.
He stood at the bow of the boat, silently holding an umbrella.
[Goddess Hel's Rune Soul Umbrella]had an effect of stunning and soothing spiritual entities.
With this black umbrella's protection, the spirits around them seemed not to have noticed their presence and floated by.
Su Lun also planned to avoid combat as much as possible.
The small boat thus moved steadily on the water, neither hurried nor slow, and they dared not move too fast.
Suddenly, Tanni saw something and pointed into the water, saying, "Look quickly, there are statues in that square!"
Lolota also spotted something, "Eh, those statues' weapons still emit a metallic sheen?"
Su Lun looked intently as well.
A hundred meters away on the seabed was a fountain square, surrounded by a group of seven to eight-meter-tall stone sculptures, clad in armor, wearing helmets, majestic and robust.
Most of the sculptures were shattered, with only two or three intact.
It was not unusual for such a large city to have statues, but what intrigued Su Lun was that those sculptures really had magical inscribed combat weapons.
Tanni called out, and a few of them had already picked up those weapons.
[Giant Spear (Silver)], [Giant Shield (Silver)], [Giant Two-Handed Sword (Gold)]...
The quality was still quite good!
Su Lun was also quite surprised.
But they were just too big.
A single weapon was three to five meters long, easily weighing hundreds of kilograms. They were clearly not equipment that could be used by humans, but rather weaponry for a race of giants.
"Wow... there are so many treasures just in this square, aren't there even more in the ruins?"
"There must be lots of treasures! Hahaha, Dawn Crew is probably going to strike it rich this time!"
"..."
Tanni and the others immediately became excited.
Su Lun, seeing this, also felt that there might be significant gains to be found in the ruins.
After all, even if these weapons were not usable, their value was considerable. Since they had not been taken by anyone else in such an obvious place, it meant that no living person had been to this city since its destruction. Thus, the city itself was probably unlooted.
With their excitement for treasure hunting, the small boat continued towards the deeper parts of the ruins.
Tanni, with his half Naga bloodline, had a strong ability to survive underwater, and Lolota and the others had also taken underwater breathing potions, swimming agilely like fish in search of treasure.
However, what was surprising was that they kept finding treasures along the way!
Although the ruins looked ancient and most things had decayed, most metal objects were still intact.
Along the way, Lolo and the others occasionally found various valuable items.
Even in the small houses that seemed to be civilian dwellings, they could find some scattered gold and silver coins and ancient pottery.
Su Lun did not stop their enthusiastic treasure-hunting activity; he even felt that making some noise was quite good.
As they delved deeper, he became more and more certain that the Red Robe Archmage was laying an ambush here.
Because their journey had been too smooth.
If it had been another ruin, smooth progress could still be explained.
But this place was a T-level cursed space!
The absence of danger was the greatest anomaly.
It seemed like some hidden force was holding the monsters back, deliberately allowing them to approach the depths of the ruins smoothly.
And since the ruin was full of ghost-type monsters, the one with the ability to manipulate could only be the Necromancer, Yale Robbins.
Upon thinking of this, Su Lun glanced at Qian Tiao beside him.
This gambling-addicted woman already had a gleefully expectant look on her face.
It actually wasn't that the enemy was foolish, revealing such an obvious flaw to be discerned.
Su Lun could figure it out, simply by using the difference in information between them.
The enemy did not know that Black Sam's pirate crew had been to these ruins before and thought the Dawn group knew nothing.
Although there were many ghosts in the ruins now, it still fell a bit short of the dense population of high-level ghost monsters described by Old Sword God Bartolo.
If Su Lun didn't know, he might not have thought much of it and would have assumed the ruins were just like this.
But since he knew, he naturally sensed something was wrong right away.
...
The boat headed towards the temple, the tallest structure in the city, where the main sanctuary was above the water.
From a distance, one could see a dazzling golden light; the entire temple was constructed from gold, silver, ivory, and beautifully carved stone columns.
The boat docked next to the stone steps leading to the temple.
Su Lun stepped down onto the stone steps.
Having not stepped on solid ground for a long time, he found the sensation quite peculiar.
As soon as they disembarked, Lolo, with his sharp eyes, pointed and said, "Look, there's a shield on the platform!"
Just a few dozen steps away on the platform, a shield bearing the pattern of the War God was emitting a dark golden glow.
Su Lun's left eye shimmered, and he immediately identified it.
[War God Atenia's Golden Shield (Dark Gold)]
Description: Even as a Divine Artifact, this is an absolutely solid shield; weight 1221 kilograms, durability +999, comes with perfect blocking, absolute magic rebound, vital strike effects; a shield with a certain sentience, only usable by a hero with dominant aura;
"This..."
Su Lun uttered in surprise.
A dark gold heavy shield, which could be considered a top-tier equipment even in the two great empires of Luying and Ma.
Su Lun felt he had seen quite a few good shields before, but this one definitely ranked in the top three.
But such a tranquil shield, just casually placed on the steps?
Su Lun and the others walked over.
Lolo tried to lift it but struggled immensely just to raise a corner.
Tanni also gave it a try, with the same result.
The two of them then looked despondently over and said, "Teacher, Mr. Su Lun, we can't lift it..."
Qian Tiao also walked over curiously and tried it; she easily picked it up with one arm.
However, as a swordsman, it was awkward for her to use, so she merely said, "This shield is imbued with the aura of a heroic spirit. Without mastering an overwhelming aura, it cannot be controlled."
Upon hearing this, Lolo immediately lost heart and stuck out his tongue, "Oh. No wonder."
Qian Tiao glanced at her disciple and seized the opportunity to teach a lesson, "See the problem now? If you don't cultivate well, you won't be able to use good equipment. And you're always clamoring for a famous sword, with your skills?"
Lolota pouted, a look of grievance on her face after being scolded, "Teacher, I've been working really hard, okay? Plus, I feel I'm just a tiny bit away from mastering dominance..."
"Working hard?"
Qiantiao looked disdainful at that statement and said irritably, "Do you practice as much as Su Lun does? And you call that working hard?"
Lolota initially wanted to defend herself, but upon hearing the latter half of the sentence, she immediately wilted and muttered dejectedly, "Of course, I can't compare to Mr. Su Lun..."
Su Lun just smiled, already used to being considered the "training unit of measurement" by various teachers in the group.
If they didn't train as long as he did, they weren't considered hardworking.
This notion didn't cause the young folks on the ship to complain endlessly.
After all, Su Lun was recognized as a training fanatic, capable of staying in his cabin for ten days to half a month without stepping out, which wasn't something everyone could achieve.
However, being scolded didn't affect Lolota and the others' enthusiasm for treasure hunting.
They sprinted up the steps when suddenly Tanni discovered something and exclaimed, "Look at the temple, so many skeletons! So many weapons!"
Su Lun also walked up.
In fact, Mr. Crow, who had flown there earlier, had seen it already.
The temple's design was open on all sides, so one could see through it at a glance.
At that moment, there were several skeletons at the entrance of the temple, some with decayed weapons and others intact, with the gold shield that had earlier fallen on the steps being one of them.
And there were many more inside the temple.
All sorts of jade-colored and even gold skeletons lay scattered on the ground, seemingly having witnessed a great battle.
Knives, swords, spears, shields, axes, daggers, rings, wristlets...
Gold, dark gold, legendary, even epic-grade equipment were scattered all over the floor.
It was unclear what had happened here, but seeing such an array of high-tier treasures, Su Lun and his companions were utterly astonished.
It certainly was an era of dawn alchemy, that most splendid time; just these equipment pieces were proof of how fierce and high-standard that ancient battle had been!
This temple was like a giant treasure chest, revealing its cherished treasures to outsiders for the first time in countless years.
However, just as everyone was getting excited, Su Lun suddenly shouted, "Don't get close to the temple!"
His left eye gleamed brightly, picking up strong soul fluctuations within the temple.
Upon hearing this, the excitement on Lolota and others' faces immediately faded, and they became alert.
Qiantiao also squinted slightly, hand resting on the hilt of his sword at his waist.
Su Lun, however, had already anticipated that the Necromancer Yale Robbins would make his move here, so his expression remained unchanged.
As expected, at that moment, the Skeleton Sword Deity, whom they had seen before, stood up from a pile of bones inside the temple.
It seemed that originally, this creature had intended to hide in the pile of bones and launch a surprise attack, but it hadn't worked.
However, this didn't seem to affect his plan.
The Skeleton Sword Deity stood up, the phosphorescent light blazing in its eye sockets, and its bony face seemingly conveyed a "I've finally waited for you" expression.
At the same time, a fierce ghostly wind started all around the temple, and countless spirits surged out like a massive swarm!
Su Lun's pupils slightly contracted.
He was not the slightest bit surprised at being ambushed by this creature.
Because this was the battlefield they had chosen.
But upon seeing the crystal skull beside the Skeleton Sword Deity, Su Lun's pupils contracted slightly again.
[Descartes' Crystal Skull]
Description: I think, therefore I am
Cursed Traits: The holder exerts 'Domination', 'Soul Capture', 'Soul Siphon', 'True Illusion' effects on nearby spiritual bodies, gaining a wide range of soul control abilities; immune to all soul attacks, stuns, hypnotics, curses, soul siphons, whisperings... and other negative effects not exceeding the spirit rating of this item itself; souls weaker than this item, when used, will suffer backlash, becoming a Soul Slave;
Explanation: An epic cursed item created by a Great Alchemist of the Dawn Era, copying a Divine Artifact. It is the skeleton of a soul after death, a treasure nurturing souls; can be used as a material for career advancement, requires dominating aura to merge, with a soul strength rating of S+ and a spiritual power rating of SS, mutation probability not exceeding 7%; after merging, acquires abilities 'Cognitive Presence', 'Capacity of Mind', 'Undying Soul Fire' (the soul remains intact even if a fatal attack is received, retention dependent on soul strength).
...
Seeing the information identified, Su Lun was both startled and delighted, his thoughts whirling, "An epic cursed item?! So that's why all the spirits in this relic are gathered around this treasure..."
This cursed item was truly a treasure for those specialized in soul-related careers!
Seeing this, Su Lun immediately determined what his material for eighth-tier career advancement would be.
This cursed item, he concluded, was the final piece in his ideal plan for advancing the Puppeteer career!

chapters.title: Chapter 564 - 563 Divine Curse Technique
chapters.content:
"Soul immortality means I can be like that guy, where even if my body dies, my soul won't dissipate? And brain domain expansion implies I can integrate a higher quality 'Isaac Blasphemer'..."
Looking at the "Descartes' Crystal Skull," Su Lun's mind raced with countless thoughts.
He had earlier planned for himself an advancement path as a Reaper Puppeteer, and the only piece of equipment missing was the 'Isaac Blasphemer' he intended to integrate at the eighth rank.
However, judging by the feedback from Dora and her teacher, Lucien Pepys Grandmaster, after their integration, this piece of equipment had very high requirements for brain domain development and cognitive abilities.
Under normal circumstances, Su Lun estimated that he would only be able to fuse with one silver-quality 'Blasphemer' piece of equipment of the same rank upon reaching the eighth rank.
He had been thinking about seeking professional advancement materials that could improve the conditions for equipment fusion.
But the materials available in his small void storage had never met expectations, so he had been without a clue.
Little did he expect that, by a fortunate coincidence, he would come across it in this cursed space.
Moreover, the effects of the skull far exceeded his expectations!
...
The Skeleton Sword Deity was the undead mage Yale Robbins, and there was extra hostility when enemies met.
The hollow eye sockets burning with soul fire stared at Su Lun, as if there were genuinely eyes gazing over, locking on to him directly.
One was lying in ambush, the other was waiting to be ambushed; both were well prepared.
The moment their gazes met, both men almost simultaneously made their moves.
With a flip of his hand, Su Lun summoned a bronze ancient lamp tethered with an iron chain.
Once Spiritual Power was infused, the ancient lamp immediately ignited, casting out a green beam of light.
In the temple, the skeleton somehow produced an iron hook that also seemed to be made of bronze, emitting a slightly paler green beam of light.
Both men took out their treasures at the same time and made their moves at the same time; neither could avoid it and were struck by the beams they each released.
"Eh... This iron hook is actually part of the soul lamp!"
However, just then, Su Lun's heart fluttered with surprise, as he had identified what the skeleton was holding—an iron hook called "Tartalus' Forbidden Soul Hook."
And coincidentally, the bronze lamp he held in his hand was the "Tartalus' Forbidden Soul Lamp," which he had obtained after blowing up a divine being in the capital of the silver dragon kingdom, Aikrensa.
It had been damaged in the explosion and discarded in his small void realm; he had combined it with the original iron chain component and had it repaired by the mountain dwarf clan.
Just a few days ago, it had been fully restored, regaining the majority of the cursed object's effects.
This thing had one main use: to lock a target's soul within a certain range.
Undead Great Magus Yale Robbins had escaped once before, and Su Lun did not want him to escape again, so the plan before coming here was precisely this—to confine the opponent's soul within a range upon first encounter.
The effect was as ideal as he hoped, locking the target immediately upon contact.
What Su Lun did not expect was that this guy would use exactly the same method!
Even the means employed were identical.
The iron hook was a piece of the soul lamp, not only capable of locking a soul but also possessing a special "soul-hooking" effect.
When Su Lun was hit by that beam of light, his status panel showed a soul-locking state, and in that moment, he felt as if his soul was being pulled out of his body by a force.
Only when his aura enveloped his entire body did this sensation instantly vanish.
....
"Heh, this is quite the coincidence."
Su Lun knitted his brows and murmured to himself.
Now, neither of them could run away.
They must kill each other to have a chance to leave.
However, since Dawn Group had set the trap with the resolve to deal with this guy, Su Lun didn't mind being locked down.
Yet, when the Skeleton Sword Deity realized his soul was locked down, his heart was significantly alarmed.
At this point, both sides knew the fight was to the death.
However, at that moment, one moved faster.
She had been waiting for this guy for a long time!
Just as Su Lun and the skeleton each made their move, the air suddenly erupted with the sounds of rapid footfall.
"Pop," "Pop," "Pop"...
Multiple figures surged forward, charging toward the temple.
The Skeleton Sword Deity had not even had time to lower the bronze iron hook before a Thunderous Sword Qi appeared less than a meter from his face.
"Clang!"
A sharp metallic sound rang out.
The famed sword "Buddha Slayer" had already been unsheathed, brandished in front to block the incoming Sword Qi.
Although it was blocked, the soul flame in the eye sockets of the Skeleton Sword Deity also trembled, clearly caught by surprise.
He didn't seem to understand why this woman had grown so much stronger after only half a month?
Before he could ponder any further, Qian Tiao had already rushed forward into the temple. The shadow of the Rakshasa Golden Body formed solidly behind her, dispelling the dense undead curses around, and she struck down with another slash of Thunderous Sword Qi.
"Clang~"
A sharp clash of metal resounded as the domineering "Onimaru Hyakume Zokusei" collided with the soul flame of "Buddha Slayer," sending sparks flying.
The skeleton figure was forced to retreat dozens of meters.
Qian Tiao, already aware of the potency of the soul flame from their last encounter, immediately withdrew upon contact, deftly avoiding the splattering soul flame. She extended the distance between them and then slashed again with Thunderous Sword Qi.
She made three consecutive slashes, smoothly executed in one breath.
At the same time, the skeleton, knowing it was at a disadvantage, immediately had the soul flame in its eye sockets become numb, devoid of any emotional fluctuation.
Outside the temple, Su Lun's pupils contracted slightly upon seeing this.
Others might not notice, but Su Lun clearly perceived that the guy's soul had transferred away from the Skeleton Sword Deity.
His gaze instantly shifted to the crystal skull on the ground, thinking to himself, "Being able to switch soul containers at any moment, this guy's 'Death God's Fire' secret technique must have been perfected to the point of mastery. He fears he's already obtained the power to advance to the ninth order..."
But this was just perfect.
After the harvest, it would all be his!
Su Lun wasn't idle either. He raised his hand and summoned Tanni and the others, drawing them all into a miniature void realm.
This battlefield was no place for those who hadn't comprehended the concept of domination.
Almost instantly, countless bizarre ghostly creatures emerged from all around the temple: ghostly tentacle monsters, ghostly whales, ghostly dragons, ghostly giants...
However, these ghost creatures were not in their normal form; instead, they were grotesquely deformed.
There were tens of thousands of them.
Driven by some force, these ghostly creatures surged towards Su Lun with ferocious intensity.
As soon as they appeared, a faint blue silver light immediately illuminated the entire city.
Gathering like a torrent, a mighty soul shockwave surged forth like a dam bursting.
However, Su Lun's expression didn't show the slightest bit of panic. In his hand, the Rune Umbrella opened with a "swoosh," and he chanted softly, "Nightfall Domain – Open!"
In an instant, night fell, and a bizarre pitch-black domain rapidly expanded several hundred meters around Su Lun.
An astonishing scene unfolded as the onrushing ghostly creatures, which could easily crush the soul of a top professional, became trapped in the dark domain and vanished without a trace.
"Goddess Hel's Rune Soul Umbrella" was designed specifically to counteract souls, possessing a powerful ability to capture and imprison them. The more souls it contained, the stronger its effect became.
After all, ghostly beings were very rare in the world, and Su Lun had a hard time encountering even a few ghost creatures outside, but in this cursed space, there were as many ghosts as there were other creature types, infinite and unending!
Originally, there were already more than a hundred thousand ghosts in the Rune Umbrella, and now, with these additional ghosts, the number instantly broke through two hundred thousand!
And as the holder of the umbrella, Su Lun was not only unaffected by the tide of ghosts, but his Soul Power also grew stronger.
At the same time, he didn't try to avoid the monster tide. Instead, he poured all his Spiritual Power into the "Bronze Lamp of Tartarus."
In the blink of an eye, the ancient lamp's green light flourished, illuminating several kilometers around the temple.
The ghost species illuminated by the ancient lamp's soul light were no longer able to escape the area.
The Bronze Lamp limited their escape, and the black umbrella captured souls – this was the foundation of Su Lun's plan!
With two curse artifacts specializing in souls in hand, even myriads of ghost creatures were powerless against him.
Su Lun had been worried about the presence of ultra-high-level soul creatures here, but seeing the undead Mage Yale Robbins choose to ambush here, that final fatal risk vanished.
This guy was left with only his soul, daring to come here meant that most likely, there were no creatures here higher than him.
...
Qian Tiao had already pushed the Skeleton Sword Deity out of the temple; the fight was extremely intense.
Last time they fought, Qian Tiao was slightly at a disadvantage. But now, after a half month of incredible progress and firmly standing at a half step into the Sword Deity realm, her momentum was in no way inferior.
The clash of sword and saber resounded through the void, emitting a shrill and sharp sound.
Su Lun glanced over and noticed that Qian Tiao was using the Skeleton Sword Deity as a whetstone. Her Thunderous Sword Intent was gradually transforming during the battle and was now able to clash directly with the Skeleton Sword Deity's Demonic Buddha Sword Intent without yielding.
Su Lun took a look and didn't bother to watch further.
Holding the black umbrella, he stood outside the temple, continuously devouring the attacking creatures.
This was also to help Qiantiao attract the attention of these evil spirit monsters, creating a better environment for her to gain insights.
It was the moment Qiantiao rushed in that Su Lun sensed the presence of a ghost with a strong soul force fluctuation lying in ambush inside the temple.
Now that both parties had been locked onto by souls, there was no point in considering escape; they could only fight to the death.
So, he was in no hurry, simply waiting for the enemy to take the initiative to attack.
If the enemy didn't come out, it would be even better. Once the Rune Umbrella had absorbed all the lower-tier ghosts in the area and the soul power had reached its peak, Su Lun's umbrella could likely kill a seventh-tier ghost with a single tap imbued with soul force.
Clearly, the necromancer Yale Robbins was not foolish either.
Being one who had mastered secret soul techniques, he definitely sensed that the Rune Umbrella in Su Lun's hand was growing stronger.
After seeing that the numerical advantage of ghosts was of no use, the guy started to panic.
The crystal skull he was inhabiting suddenly cracked and began to move, chanting a magic incantation as green phosphorescent light flared up significantly: "Forbidden Technique - Heroic Spirits' Transit!"
Once more, it seemed as though a massive gate to hell had opened in the temple hall.
The incantation was still echoing in the air when suddenly the "clang clank" sound of a marching army rang out in unison.
Su Lun looked over and saw an army of ghosts, armed with spears and clad in armor and helms, marching out of the magic gate opened by the spell, in neat formation.
If the previously scattered ghosts were like loose sand, then this was a regular army before his eyes.
Numbering in the tens of thousands, they coalesced into a terrifying oppressive force of soul power.
Among this ghost army, there were also a dozen soul beasts with soul force fluctuations comparable to eighth-tier professionals.
Hellhounds with three heads, war behemoths, nightmares, hydra, hell wolves...
These ghostly creatures appeared to be the top aberrant monsters that had died in this cursed space over countless years, their souls attracted by that crystal skull, preserved to this day.
Robbins had somehow mastered that crystal skull, thus also controlling the spectral monsters enslaved by the skull.
Tens of thousands of ghost soldiers and a dozen seventh- and eighth-tier spectral creatures would be an almost certain death trap for anyone else.
One hundred percent immune to physical and magical damage, and capable of psychic attacks, this was nearly unsolvable.
Even professionals who comprehended the concept of dominance would inflict limited damage.
But to Su Lun, it seemed routine, and in his mind, he even quipped, "Heh, they really do deliver themselves..."
Now he was sure that the guy knew of the talent "S-004-Reaper," but it was clear he didn't know about all the capabilities of the talent when it unfolded its second layer, otherwise he wouldn't have used this move.
After the second unfold of the S-class talent Reaper, it would be a super powerful ability that could deal real damage to Spiritual Bodies!
To Su Lun, the released souls were the best tonic.
As the dozen or so ghostly creatures charged at him, the shadow of the Reaper suddenly loomed large behind Su Lun. His gaze sharpened, and the shadow behind him also burst with dark brilliance.
By the time those beasts charged at him, Su Lun had already teleported amidst the ghost army.
With the Reaper's shadow flourishing behind him, as soon as he touched the ground, the nearby ghost army was instantly cleared out by a significant margin. To Su Lun, these ghosts were like biting into a cloud, easily done without the slightest crunch.
Although the undead army had military skills, Su Lun didn't give them a chance to use their tactics, ramming and disrupting the battle formation amidst the ghosts.
Wherever he passed, it was like tearing through withered vines; the ghosts were either devoured or absorbed by the Rune Umbrella.
"You have stripped 'Ghost Soldier' of its soul, spiritual power +14."
"You have stripped 'Ghost Legion Commander' of its soul, spiritual power +254."
"You have stripped 'Ghost General' of its soul, spiritual power +1136."
"..."
The ghost army was actually not weak; even eighth-tier professionals would typically avoid it.
Now, being harvested like wheat, it was only because Su Lun was too special.
His soul was now as strong as any ghost here, thus those psychic influences, illusions, whispers, and such had almost no effect on him.
Those seventh and eighth-tier ghost bosses did pose a certain threat to Su Lun, but he didn't confront them head-on.
Su Lun was merely preying on various lesser ghosts, which also made his Umbrella increasingly saturated, reducing the threat more and more.
He went on a rampage near the temple like this.
It wasn't that he was too strong, overpowering his enemies.
It was really because prepared combat made his response much easier.
Over these days, Su Lun along with Mr. Hei had almost gone through all the records of spoils of war they had on hand, and they had a very thorough understanding of the "Divine Soul Fire" lineage of undead magic.
It could be said that they had an absolutely clear grasp of any spell that Yale Robbins knew.
Su Lun and Mr. Hei had even deduced various battle situations based on this, what secret techniques that guy would use under what circumstances, what desperate moves he would use when cornered... They had anticipated nearly everything.
Looking at it now, from the start of the battle to the present, there had been nothing outside their expectations.
Necromancers only have a few tricks up their sleeve, controlling the dead and souls.
This guy's body had been killed, stripping him of the ability to cast other magics.
The remaining methods he could deploy were predictable.
He couldn't do anything to Su Lun even in his prime, and now it was even less likely.
However, that guy's innate Death God's Fire was quite troublesome.
Su Lun was in no hurry to clash head-on.
He planned to slowly harvest souls to strengthen himself since the enemy was the one in a rush.
...
Indeed.
Su Lun was slaughtering left and right among the ghost legions, and Robbins, hidden inside the crystal skull, was getting more anxious.
When he realized all his methods couldn't kill his opponent, the situation immediately became a dead end for him.
Robbins, watching the figure still wildly reaping ghosts, fumed in his heart, "The Reaper's talent actually suppresses high-order Spiritual Bodies, and that black umbrella is a high-tier treasure that restrains ghosts; this native's fortune really makes one jealous! Eh, this is bad now..."
He didn't understand why the situation had deteriorated so badly.
It was as if all his techniques were being countered.
But... it shouldn't be like this!
Previously, he had used divination to predict that the native fleet would pass through this route.
And this ruin was filled with countless ghosts, his home ground.
Robbins had also guessed that with so many ghosts in the ruins, there must be a soul treasure.
He also joyfully found this "Descartes' Crystal Skull" and gained the ability to control all the spirits in the ruins.
All this was initially hugely in his favor.
But why was he being forced back step by step?
But now, as the souls of both parties had locked on to each other, the result could only be a fight to the death.
The ghost legion not only failed to deal with the enemy but was being devoured in greater numbers, which only made the enemy stronger.
Once the ghost legion was cleared out, there would truly be no chance of turning things around.
Seeing this, Robbins's eyes flashed with determination.
Then, he began chanting an incredibly arcane spell, "Great Death God above, please grant strength to your most loyal servant..."
As a lengthy spell finished, Robbins softly chanted in his heart, "God Incantation Technique - Death's Gaze!"
...
The moment the spell began, Su Lun sensed a divine will descending into the temple.
But without guessing what spell the chant was meant for, he had already figured it out, "So this guy is finally resorting to using the power of the gods to cast Curse Magic, huh..."
Su Lun was thoroughly familiar with the spells Robbins knew.
Now that various methods had been ineffective against him, ultimately, this guy wouldn't be able to harm him either.
Therefore, at the beginning, Su Lun and Mr. Hei had deduced that the only option this guy would have when cornered was to borrow the power of the gods.
And Su Lun also knew now that the techniques wielded by a divine will were limited by the capabilities of the host itself.
A Spiritual Body could only erupt with a few types of methods – soul attacks, Illusion Techniques, and the like...
And to kill with a single strike, Su Lun and Mr. Hei had always believed that the guy would use "Curse Magic".
After all, this secret technique was one of the specialties of the lineage of the 'Holy Soul Fire' necromancer.
Another point was that Curse Magic required a targeted mark.
The enemy's planning had actually been quite thorough, as Su Lun had just decimated so many ghosts, he didn't notice an extra "Soul Mark" status on his attribute panel.
This was the enemy's trap set in advance.
Now, it really had come!
Seeing this, Su Lun also felt it was time to decide the outcome.
The Divine Arts level of Curse Magic didn't play by the rules, once marked it was unavoidable.
But fortunately, there had been prior experience.
And at this moment, Su Lun's aura began to grow more yin and feminine, "Pestoya, I'm counting on you once again."

chapters.title: Chapter 565 - 564 Secret Room
chapters.content:
Out of nowhere, a describable will descended upon the temple of Atlantis, and Su Lun immediately took off.
In the blink of an eye, he had teleported and hidden himself inside an inconspicuous house within the Ruins City.
It seemed as if he was panicking to avoid that magic.
This action was observed by Yale Robbins, who inhabited the crystal skull, his soul fire flickered with full of mockery and disdain.
The guy didn't pursue.
After all, no matter how much Su Lun ran, he couldn't possibly escape the range of the soul lock. Moreover, the Soul Cursing Technique was a secret technique that could be released regardless of spatial constraints.
In his view, everything was futile.
But in fact, Su Lun fled only to prevent the enemy from noticing Pestoia's possession, just to prevent the descending mysterious will from becoming wary.
Not only was there a fierce battle at the temple, but the Evernight, anchored outside the Ruins City, also signaled an attack at the same time.
Countless ghostly monsters launched a ferocious attack on the ship, including several very troublesome undead creatures.
This had all been planned by Robbins in advance, to prevent the Old Sword God Bartolo from coming to the aid.
Once he came to assist here, the ship would inevitably suffer devastating blows.
In the waters of the Ancient Dragon Country, without the ship, such a large team could almost be pronounced dead.
Overall, Robbins had calculated almost everything within his ability.
However, what he did not know was that in this shattered Alchemy Plane, there existed a Pestoia who had consolidated Divine Fire.
...
"Su Lun" took refuge in a house, suddenly revealing a playful and cute expression that seemed somewhat odd.
He seemed to have taken an interest in his body, touching here, pinching there, and his eyes were filled with a whimsical smile.
"Wow, Mr. Su Lun, you have become stronger recently~"
"Hey hey hey, don't mess with my body, okay?"
"Aiyaya~ Is that the tone of asking for a favor? You have a chance to rephrase that, call me junior sister~"
"..."
"Did you check the 'Death God's Fire' and the secret technique 'Wu Shi'? If you can learn it, you'll have a way to attack in the future."
Inside Su Lun, two souls were communicating.
Naturally, the one controlling the body now was Pestoia.
She had been staying in Su Lun's black umbrella all this time, in a semi-dormant state.
It's a rare opportunity for her to come out, and naturally, everything piqued her curiosity.
It wasn't that she didn't want to come out before, but this fragmented Alchemy Plane felt to her like a giant visiting a dwarf's house, which gave her a strong sense of oppression.
She had helped Su Lun once in Spiritualton and then went into dormancy for a long time.
It's only recently, since the plane's channel was opened, that she felt much better.
The curse space they were now in was even formed by the leakage of energy from a rift in the hell plane. The closer to the core, the higher the limit of the laws, and the less oppressive the feeling was. She had long wanted to come out.
Upon being questioned, "Su Lun" produced a green ghostly fire between his fingers and asked, "This? It wasn't very difficult, a bit of time spent studying it and I got it."
No sooner had the words left his mouth than the little flame cheerfully danced and turned into a fire crow, circling around.
Seeing that skillful fire control, Su Lun was also slightly surprised.
Pestoia had already condensed Divine Fire, so this secret technique was naturally not difficult for her.
Now that she has this secret technique, she finally could be more than just a ghostly young lady's pendant and actually possess strong combat abilities.
At least in this plane, her burning soul fire was something no one would dare to touch.
Seeing this, Su Lun's surprise turned into relief.
The excellent genes of the Aisak family meant she was naturally good at learning; the ghostly young lady might seem flighty, but in private she was diligent.
