Otherwise, in such a short time, she could not have mastered two secret techniques so proficiently.
The two hadn't spoken much when suddenly, a sensation like being stalked by a poison snake instantly surged into Su Lun's heart.
Even without controlling his body, he felt his soul targeted by a high-level curse powerful enough to obliterate it instantly.
Curse Magic inherently comes with "Magic Locking," and aside from brute resistance and protection from certain external objects, there really is no other way to deal with it.
It was precisely to guard against and be warned of Curse Magic that Su Lun always carried various curse defense artifacts collected from different places.
However, in an instant, "crack," "crack," a series of shattering sounds rang out as the various defensive objects he wore shattered almost simultaneously.
An absolutely overwhelming mysterious force destroyed these defenses.
It was like an arrow piercing through a paper mache armor, the attacker and defender were not on the same level of existence at all.
Su Lun also felt his heart trembling nonstop.
Divine-level Curse Magic is just so unreasonable.
When a lower plane being is targeted, it is almost certainly doomed to die.
After all, it is like a diminishment of dimensions when a will of a deity comes down personally, it is completely overpowering.
It's as if not even a human's little finger is something an ant can withstand.
The high-level curse hit "Su Lun" directly and fiercely on both soul and body.
Ordinarily, it was a curse that could kill a ninth level being instantly, but, against all odds, there was an accident.
The curse slammed into Su Lun as though it had hit an impenetrable armor.
After all, the undead grand magus Robins had only summoned a wisp of a deity's will, not a true divine descent.
Whereas, Pestoya was an authentic specialty being that had coalesced divine fire!
The moment it made contact, that curse power instantly dissipated.
When Curse Magic fails to kill, the caster must necessarily suffer from spell backlash.
As the curse power scattered in an instant, Su Lun thought he could hear a scream coming from the source of the spell: "Aah...!!!!"
At the same time, inside that temple not far away, the eerie green soul flame within the crystal skeleton instantly dissipated.
At almost the same time, clarity returned to Su Lun's eyes, he sensed something and felt overjoyed, "Got him!"
That soul flame of Robins had dissipated!
Without any hesitation, Su Lun's figure dispersed on the spot.
....
The scenery changed all around, and Su Lun stepped out from a spatial rift in the temple's grand hall.
Looking at the shattered soul fire on the crystal skeleton in front of him, a shadow of Death itself unfurled behind him, and he chose to harvest without hesitation.
Perhaps that fellow's soul hadn't completely died yet, but to Su Lun at that moment, in its free state, it was utterly defenseless.
He didn't give his enemy a chance to recover, with a gesture of his hand, he devoured those scattered soul flames in large chunks.
Once these soul flames were devoured, they could no longer be revived!
Su Lun also found it quite theatrical.
After all that fighting, victory was decided in an instant.
It could be said that if this guy hadn't actively courted death with Curse Magic, Su Lun really wouldn't have thought of a good way to handle this Death God's Fire.
"You have stripped away the soul of 'Yale Robbins'"
"You have obtained a large number of 'Eighth-level Death Law Shards'"
"You have comprehended the skill [Divine Technique: Death God Fire], gaining +15599 insight points..."
"You have mastered a great deal of holy soul fire lineage undead mage related abilities, magic spells, rituals, production of Magic Scrolls, Forbidden Techniques..."
"You have mastered a vast amount of soul secret techniques, Necromancy Control, crafting methods..."
"You have stripped away the forbidden words: Is the essence of death the cessation of matter, or the crumbling of the soul? By understanding this, you gained insight related to 'Forbidden Technique: Death Immunity'..."
"You have gained intelligence on the holy military order, and learned of the belief system of the celestial Death God, Karas..."
"Spiritual power +2231..."
"..."
In an instant, a torrent of Soul Shards flooded his mind, and the brilliance in Su Lun's eyes was hard to hide.
I'm rich!
A windfall in my profession!
I've had my eye on this guy's secret techniques for a while, and now I've reaped them all at once.
Complete understanding of "Death God's Fire" and the entire eighth order of Death Laws.
Even though part of a mage's comprehension comes from the divine, this guy was, after all, a genuine eighth-order grand mage!
Even if only fifty to sixty percent was his own insights, Su Lun's harvest was enormous.
This could save him decades of hard cultivation!
Death Laws encompass everything, and Su Lun's understanding was like just one star in the night sky. And now, he had devoured the light of another star!
Alchemists and mages belong to two different systems, and even the directions of their research into the same laws are completely different. And the "Holy Soul Fire" lineage of necromancers has accumulated over a thousand years, with an absolutely profound foundation in the realm of souls.
This was a domain that Su Lun lacked before.
Now that he has harvested this guy's soul, he instantly feels as though his eyes have been opened to a whole new world, as if his knowledge and understanding have surged forward!
And this is only just the beginning of the harvest.
He's certain that once he has fully digested these memories, they will greatly benefit his own professional advancement in the future.
...
With Yale Robbins's death, the "Descartes' Crystal Skull" on the ground immediately lost its control.
The ghostly creatures inside and outside of the temple, now lacking command, plunged into chaos.
Su Lun distinctly felt that the moment he approached the skull, a strange force sucked away some of his soul's power.
He knew this was the soul-draining characteristic innate to the skull, but it was of no concern, thanks to the protection of Pestoya's soul.
Su Lun picked up the skull and then took out a rune-encrypted casket to store this cursed object away.
The moment the casket closed, it was as if the connection with the temple's ghostly creatures was severed, and all the spectral beings in the ruins became disorderly. Although they continued to attack Su Lun, the living being, most of them drifted around aimlessly like headless flies.
Su Lun didn't bother with the ghosts any longer and, after storing the crystal skull, surveyed the temple's interior.
He hadn't forgotten that the temple was filled with various treasures left from the ancient past.
With the divine will of the temple's deity erased and the crisis averted, a female ghost drifted out from Su Lun's black umbrella.
Su Lun looked at her and asked, "Pestoya, are you alright?"
"Of course I'm fine. That was just a wisp of divine will, after all. Besides, that guy's divine fire is no match for mine."
Pestoya responded.
Seemingly feeling that she hadn't been out for a long time, she floated around in front of Su Lun as she spoke.
Su Lun, feeling dizzy from her movements, joked with a laugh, "Flying so high, you're going to expose yourself!"
From his angle, he could see right up her skirt.
Hearing this, Pestoya was utterly unconcerned, "Heh, no one can see anyway."
Su Lun twitched the corner of his eye. Am I not a person?
Pestoya, noticing the odd look in Su Lun's eyes, shifted her watery eyes and pretended to be resentful, "Mr. Su Lun, were you peeking at me just now?"
Su Lun had no interest in peeping.
Seeing the cunning in her eyes, he guessed she was probably up to some mischief again.
He ignored her and didn't engage with the banter.
Seeing that he didn't respond, Pestoya became even more interested. Suddenly, she put on a mischievous smile, lifted her skirt, stuck out her tongue, and teased, "Nyeh nyeh nyeh... you can't see, you can't see~"
Su Lun glanced at her and rolled his eyes, unamused.
Pestoya's clothing was an illusion, but as she was from a millennium ago, her style of dress was of that era.
Her classical gothic court dress was short, and even if she lifted her skirt, there were fluffy shorts underneath, naturally revealing nothing.
It seemed that teasing Su Lun brought the girl joy—laughter like tinkling bells filled the temple.
Pestoya was tirelessly floating about, while a smile remained on Su Lun's face.
At that moment, a skeleton, with its limbs twisting at the joints, came in and casually asked, "What's so funny?"
Pestoya revealed herself and immediately greeted politely, "Sister Qian Tiao."
Qian Tiao nodded with a smile and said, "Oh, it's Pestoya."
Pestoya nodded.
Qian Tiao smiled, placed the skeleton on the ground, then turned and asked, "Su Lun, do you think this skeleton frame is still of any use?"
Su Lun looked at the skeleton, which had been chopped in half, and recognized that it was indeed the previous Skeleton Sword Deity.
"Of course."
He replied and then asked, "How is it on your end?"
Qian Tiao seemed not entirely satisfied as she shrugged her shoulders, "Sigh, I actually wanted to fight a bit more with this Sword Dao predecessor. I didn't expect the skeleton to suddenly fall apart..."
However, as she spoke, she raised her hand to show the Famed Sword "Buddha Slayer," whose scabbard was already decaying, and her face could not hide her delight, "But I managed to get my hands on this famed sword as I wished."
Su Lun looked at the famed sword, which seemed even more sinister than the Demon Blade "Ghost Maru Hyakume Sojyou," and his expression showed a slight change.
From such a close distance, he clearly felt that strange and eerie fluctuation of the laws that were both Buddha-like and demonic.
Even with Qian Tiao holding it in her hand, her grip seemed to be constantly encompassed with a dominating aura, as if she were forcibly suppressing that power.
Seeing the look that Su Lun gave her, she flashed a sharp light in her eyes and explained, "The Buddha patterns on the blade seal a very powerful high-level Power of Laws. Tsk, it's still not settling down even in my hands..."
Hearing this, Su Lun wasn't surprised anymore.
Famed swords choose their masters. Qian Tiao had experienced such a situation before when she tamed "Ghost Maru Hyakume Sojyou."
...
With the crisis fully resolved, Su Lun released Tanni and the others from the small void realm, as well as Mr. Hei, the Scholar.
In the grand hall of the temple, the group continued the treasure hunting from before.
"Wow... so many treasures!"
"My God, look everyone, this 'Gauntlet' seems to be another piece of gold equipment!"
"Oh, what a pity, this magic wand must have been a legendary item, but the long years have caused its magic power to dissipate completely..."
"..."
Everyone sifted through the items one by one, collecting what was still intact.
But material things decay, and after the passage of countless years, the majority of the items in this temple had rotted and been damaged.
Even those skeletons and equipment that appeared intact crumbled into dust upon touch.
The remaining equipment had also seen their extraordinary powers nearly completely dissipated. The piece of dark gold shield they found on the steps earlier was considered exceptionally well-preserved.
Su Lun was in a good state of mind.
He thought that even if the equipment was decayed, the forging materials and basic runes were of excellent quality. Reinforcing them in a forge would not result in poor quality.
Moreover, having already obtained the "Descartes' Crystal Skull," Su Lun felt quite content.
With that, the ambush plan this time could be considered perfect.
However, it was at this moment that Mr. Hei's shout suddenly came from inside the temple: "Su Lun, come over here and take a look. I think I've found something."
Hearing this, Su Lun walked over.
Compared to the treasures, Mr. Hei was clearly more interested in the murals and reliefs on the walls.
He had been observing these reliefs and murals all this time.
As a Scholar, Mr. Hei was proficient in codes, mechanisms, architecture, ancient scripts, relic archaeology, and artifact appraisal, among other skills.
It was his careful observation that identified some clues on the mural.
He said in a slightly complex tone, "From the clues on the murals and the structure of this temple, there may be a secret chamber beneath this floor. And from the deciphered text I've read, it seems there is a huge secret tightly related to alchemy sealed beneath..."
"A secret chamber?"
Upon hearing Mr. Hei's words, Su Lun seemed to instantly grasp the key point.
In this grand hall, all these skeletons must have been top-tier powerhouses in life. So the question was, what made them fight to the death here?
It was obvious that this temple must be hiding something.

chapters.title: Chapter 566 - 547: The Alchemical Holy Object [The Philosopher's Stone]
chapters.content:
"If it weren't for the age, and the dissipating enchantment that once covered these murals, I would never have discovered such a cunning hidden prohibition..."
Mr. Hei pointed at the faded lines of the murals and then to the protruding ancient inscriptions at the corner of the wall, sharing his discovery.
Su Lun looked over, and saw the following text: "bὺςδὲπατὴρΤιτῆναςἐπίκλησινκαλέεσκε..."
Upon searching his mind, he realized he had seen it before, appearing to be a kind of disused ancient script. However, without systematic study, he stammered and couldn't translate it.
Mr. Hei, on the other hand, directly said, "This is an ancient Robe scripture, there was a discovery in southern Luying of some unique literary works; a few were excavated from a site, conveniently held in the Royal Library of Luying. The text roughly says, 'Titans represent giants of sin, and can only be sealed in the eternal darkness of Erebus'..."
He translated the text that seemed to be part of a mythological tale and then added, "Of course, this part is not very important. What's crucial comes later. It says that there is a secret chamber beneath this temple, sealed with alchemical treasures and some very dangerous things."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's mind immediately became active.
Curious, Qiantiao asked, "Alchemical treasures... what are those? And what's been sealed?"
It was obvious to them that this temple was of high importance. Correspondingly, whatever was sealed, as well as the seal itself and the items sealed, were definitely treasures.
Moreover, what was most important was that many of the treasures in the outer hall had decayed with time, but those sealed within were likely to be well-preserved.
When it came to treasure hunting, this secret chamber was undoubtedly the perfect place.
Hearing Qiantiao's inquiry, Mr. Hei shook his head and responded, "I don't know. Currently, we have only deciphered these clues from the texts and murals within this temple. I think we should completely break this hidden prohibition first before seeing what happens."
"Good!"
Both Su Lun and Qiantiao showed faces brimming with excitement.
The three of them consulted and immediately began decrypting the prohibition.
Su Lun and Mr. Hei were both proficient in various runes and prohibitions, and with the assistance of the All-knowing Eye, they were practically the strongest decryption combination in this plane.
They soon found the correct method.
After a while of research and tinkering, Mr. Hei touched several characters carved in the relief, and the temple's final hidden mechanism was triggered.
Almost simultaneously, Su Lun exclaimed in surprise, "Eh... there really is a hidden space."
Because in his perception, a considerable space had suddenly appeared beneath the floor that was previously solid.
This was what surprised him.
Before, this space was like a grain of normal sand, too small for anyone to notice any abnormality.
Now that it was broken open and exposed,
it meant that this was an extremely clever spatial prohibition, so advanced that even Su Lun's current understanding of the Space Law found it unbelievable.
...
Su Lun and the others gazed at the suddenly raised dragon-carved stone on the ground and lapsed into a brief silence.
The prohibition was broken; this was the last barrier to their treasure hunt.
All three looked at the seal, pondering over something.
At that moment, Mr. Hei said, "The extraordinary power of the seal has nearly dissipated, and it shouldn't be difficult to open. However... accordingly, it might trigger something unexpected."
This, of course, was meant as an inquiry.
After all, something that required such a magnificent temple to seal it must have been extremely dangerous. Nobody could guarantee there wouldn't be problems after opening it.
Without knowing what was inside, Su Lun was also hesitant to make a decision.
However, just when he felt troubled, the ghostly miss floating in the sky suddenly spoke up, "Shall I go down and check first?"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun immediately thought it was feasible!
He dared not go down in the flesh to investigate, but Pestoya could.
She was a Spiritual Body and had concentrated the divine fire; almost nothing in this plane could harm her.
Even if there were any calamities in the chamber below, she was the most suitable candidate for reconnaissance.
Although this was the case, Su Lun still felt slightly embarrassed to send a young girl into such an environment, asking in return, "Ah... can you do that?"
Pestoya, hearing this, gave him a 'I see right through you' look and wearily said, "Ah... Mr. Su Lun, don't pretend. You're clearly thinking: Go now, quickly!"
Su Lun laughed heartily.
"Hmph."
Pestoya snorted haughtily and flew towards the dragon-carved stone, then as a Spiritual Body, merged into it.
Su Lun and the others waited above with a mix of anticipation and anxiety.
The space below wasn't large; they should have received some feedback quickly in theory.
But after waiting for a couple of seconds with no sign of activity, their expressions instinctively grew tense, fearing some accident had occurred.
Because there was a soul connection established, Su Lun could feel that Pestoya's soul was stable, but he still directly asked, "Pestoya, how are things?"
Soon, a reply came from Pestoya: "Hmm... there doesn't seem to be any danger in this chamber. There's an altar with a golden spear, a red gem that glows, and a piece of black amber-like substance..."
As she spoke, her voice suddenly became excited, and she added, "How come I feel like that red gemstone is the Philosopher's Stone recorded in the scriptures?"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's pupils dilated sharply.
His mind went blank for a moment before he realized what he had heard.
The legendary Philosopher's Stone?
Damn, could it really exist?
...
Mr. Hei and Qiantiao, sensing the emotion in Su Lun's reaction, immediately grew alert and cast inquiring looks at him.
Su Lun took a deep breath before he managed to contain the shock in his eyes.
With a solemn voice, he said to Mr. Hei and the bewildered others, "Pestoya mentioned that there might be a gemstone resembling the 'Philosopher's Stone' below."
Even Mr. Hei, who was usually as unfazed as an ancient well, couldn't help but reveal the same look of shock and eager anticipation that Su Lun had just shown.
The normally unflappable Mr. Hei was a second late before blurting out, "The legendary Philosopher's Stone?"
It was no wonder that the three of them looked so astonished; the discovery was too shocking!
If Pestoya was not mistaken, and there indeed was an alchemical treasure—a Philosopher's Stone—in this secret chamber, then it might be the only one discovered in nearly ten thousand years in the alchemy plane!
Mr. Hei's eyes flickered with a shrewd light, clearly as unsettled on the inside as he said, "If... if that's really it, then no matter what, we have to try and break the seal."
The Philosopher's Stone is said to be an essential item made of cosmic essence needed by alchemy practitioners to advance to the ninth tier, encapsulating the ultimate secret of equivalent exchange.
Yes, a legend!
That's because in the recorded history of ten thousand years, no one on the alchemy plane had ever seen a real Philosopher's Stone.
Even the Alchemical Demigod, Sir Isaac, had only read about it in the books.
How could such a discovery not excite the heart?
....
While the three were lost in their thoughts, the ghostly miss had already floated up to them.
Su Lun quickly asked, "Pestoya, did you really see the Philosopher's Stone?"
"I don't know, it looked like it," she expressed with a somewhat unsure look.
After responding, she made a gesture with her hand, and a huge ruby took shape in the air, adding, "Anyway, it looked like this."
Upon seeing it, the eyes of Su Lun and the others were immediately fixed and could not look away.
No matter how one looked at it, it was exactly the same as the Philosopher's Stone recorded in the ancient books!
Seeing this, all three grew visibly excited.
While showing it, Pestoya also described what she saw in the secret chamber moments ago.
Mr. Hei's eyes darted around as he pondered for a while before making a judgment, "It seems to be the legendary Philosopher's Stone indeed. Such a high-grade altar requires energy circulation to maintain a long-term seal, and the Philosopher's Stone's ability for equivalent exchange is the perfect energy hub for all kinds of ultra-level seals. However...
He paused.
It wasn't just the Philosopher's Stone now; there was also that golden spear and the black amber, both of which were definitely treasures!
But the problem arose again, the higher the grade of the treasure, the greater the corresponding risk.
This made them hesitate.
Su Lun too understood the issue at stake and, after inquiring about some more details from Pestoya, he finally made a decision, "Then... shall we try to break the prohibition first?"
Mr. Hei nodded in agreement, "Hmm. Since we're pretty sure it's the Philosopher's Stone, the risk is worth taking. Plus, this is a cursed space, so even if something monstrous is released, the impact on the alchemy plane would be very limited."
As alchemists, they wouldn't give up the slightest chance to obtain the legendary Philosopher's Stone.
Su Lun shared the same thought.
After all, the cursed space was filled with all sorts of super-class monsters. Even releasing an extremely dangerous existence wouldn't be too much trouble.
...
Having made up their minds, Su Lun did not hesitate.
He first gathered his crew, who were still treasure hunting aside, and then notified the crew on the Eternal Night to prepare the activation of the ship's alchemical formation.
Originally, Su Lun wanted to take Mr. Hei and Mr. Qian with him and attempt to open the door alone.
But both of them refused.
They said it was to support each other and share the risk.
Moreover, if disaster struck so quickly that even Mr. Hei and Mr. Qian didn't have time to dodge, Su Lun's teleportation might not necessarily be able to avoid danger.
Su Lun did not insist.
There was no need for too many words between comrades who had faced adversity together.
The three of them and the ghost stared at the dragon relief on the ground, carefully studying it, afraid of getting a single detail wrong.
Finally, after feeling as though they had taken all details into account, they opened the prohibition.
However, their worries proved unnecessary.
The door-opening process went very smoothly.
Lord Raven perched on Su Lun's shoulder was quiet throughout the whole process, issuing no warnings.
"Click..."
"Click..."
The sound of the stone door grinding echoed through the temple, and the dragon-engraved ground slowly opened to reveal a staircase leading down to a dark secret chamber below.
Su Lun sent Lord Raven down first to scout around, and after detecting no problems, they then proceeded downwards.
The staircase descended dozens of meters before coming to an end.
The secret chamber was not large, only about two hundred square meters or so.
Su Lun, walking at the front, took in the whole room at a glance.
His left eye's pupil focused all around, reinforcing everything he saw.
Because Pestoya had previously described the layout of the secret chamber, Su Lun was quick to spot the key elements.
In the center of this secret chamber was an altar inscribed with densely packed high-level rune seals.
However, the attention of the three individuals was immediately drawn to the red gemstone at the center of the altar.
Su Lun's heart leaped with joy, "It really is the stuff of legends!"
While Pesto was uncertain, Su Lun recognized it at a glance.
[Philosopher's Stone]
Detailed explanation: An item originating from the ancient goblin civilization's alchemy, adhering to the principle of equivalent exchange; it contains the ultimate secrets of alchemy, granting the holder the ability to elevate all alchemy skills to 100% absolute equivalent exchange of any element; the item can gather cosmic power and manifest the essence of the universe, with the speed of condensation influenced by the environment and materials; it also contains too much information that surpasses common understanding.
Finally seeing the physical item, Mr. Hei and Qian Tiao were both filled with excitement and threw querying glances: Is it?
Su Lun nodded with certainty.
In an instant, the two felt an indescribable surge of exhilaration.
This is, after all, the "divine artifact" of alchemists in legends...
It represents the ultimate alchemical product of absolute equivalent exchange!
The Philosopher's Stone before them might be the most significant discovery in the history of alchemical adventures in recent millennia!
"So the records in the ancient texts are true..."
Seeing some of the limited information become clear, Su Lun could hardly contain his excitement.
Normally, the principle of "equivalent exchange" used by alchemists in their craft actually entails significant loss.
For example, exchanging 100 units of wind element for fire element would never yield 100 units in return and would be severely deficient, generally below 50 units.
The lower the rank of the practitioner, the lower the exchange rate.
Even now, at the seventh rank, Su Lun's equivalent exchange rate was only 50-60%.
Just as there is no such thing as an absolutely pure material in the world, this loss is normal.
But some ancient texts introduced that the Philosopher's Stone, a divine alchemical artifact, could make this conversion rate reach 100%.
Su Lun had originally thought it to be a rumor, but now he saw it was true.
Leaving aside other functions, with the Philosopher's Stone in hand, alchemy's power would increase exponentially under absolute equivalent exchange.
Su Lun felt that if it were him, his alchemy power could skyrocket by at least three times from nothing!
This is the most direct boost to combat power!
...
As alchemists, seeing this divine alchemical artifact, it was hard for Su Lun and the others to hide their excitement.
However, they did not rashly touch anything.
Su Lun then shifted his gaze to the "black amber" previously mentioned by Pesto.
Now he also had a deeper understanding of the world and knew that what meets the eye is not necessarily the essence of a thing.
It is just a representation limited by one's own understanding.
Just like the Naga's [Rainbow Well], though it looks like well water, it is actually a high-level manifestation of the Power of Laws in the form of rainbow-colored spring water.
The same is true for this amber.
Its essence is a manifestation of the universe's rules.
And indeed, it was.
[Universe Essence No. 31: Netherworld]
Detailed explanation: A crystallization of hell *** rules, one of the ultimate products of the principle of equivalent exchange in alchemy; can be used as a fusion material to allow the body to be recognized by the world's source quality and peek into the secrets of the universe's rules;
In fact, when Pesto described it previously, Su Lun had already guessed that it was an essence.
Because earlier, in the Royal Mirror Library of Luying, he had found one [Universe Essence No. 11: Myriad Forms].
This item is indispensable for alchemists to advance to the ninth rank.
Rare to come by.
But before this, even Mr. Jing only knew that the Philosopher's Stone was needed to refine the universe essence, unaware of the specifics of its formation.
Su Lun felt quite lucky as he looked at it.
This Universe Essence was like a "bonus" from the Philosopher's Stone.
The cursed space right now is connected to a hell rift, hence the thick hellish aura. And the Philosopher's Stone has the ability to collect the Power of Laws of the universe. It acts like a "purification refinery," manifesting the universe's rules scattered in the void into a physical state. Accumulated over countless years, this resulted in the [Netherworld].
Indispensable to the ninth rank, this too is an alchemical treasure.
Mr. Hei, who was beside, apparently also noticed the nature of the amber and asked Su Lun, "That amber seems to be a universe essence?"
Su Lun, too, smiled excitedly, "Yes."
After pausing for a moment, he glanced at Qian Tiao and said, "This is [Universe Essence No. 31: Netherworld], very suitable for Sister Qian Tiao."
Qian Tiao blinked, seemingly still not understanding what it was, and instinctively replied, "Suitable for me?"
Her naturally thick-skinned nature kept her from thinking too deeply.
Su Lun nodded affirmatively, "Mhm."
Identifying the essence as related to the laws of hell, although it had some compatibility with Su Lun himself, it wasn't very high.
It was more suitable for Qian Tiao, who followed the hell sword path.
Moreover, given her current pace of advancement, reaching the eighth rank was hopeful, and the ninth rank wasn't impossible either.
As for Su Lun himself, he was in no hurry.
Not to mention he hadn't even glimpsed the eighth rank, the ninth was still far off.
Besides, with the Philosopher's Stone in hand, he now had the possibility to refine essence on his own in the future.
With this alchemical relic, he could fully start to refine cosmic essence highly attuned to his own profession.
Even the whole Dawn Group, all the Magicians on the alchemical plane, wouldn't have to worry about a lack of ninth-rank essence blocking their path to advancement anymore!
This discovery was of crucial significance for the future of alchemical civilization.
Seeing this, Su Lun couldn't help but feel moved.
Before setting off, the Dawn Group had heard that Tanni's father, Sam Bellamy, leading the Black Sam pirate crew to the Dragon Country Waters, was also in search of cosmic essence and the opportunity to advance to the ninth rank.
But not only did they not find anything, they didn't even discover the east, instead they ended up buried in these seas.
Unexpectedly, the Dawn Group got lucky this time and actually found one.
They even found the legendary "Philosopher's Stone"!
...
After the two alchemical treasures had caught the trio's attention, they saw the last item in this secret chamber.
It was a golden spear.
The spear's tip had a single-edged blade, and the handle in the middle was inlaid with shining diamonds.
This was an incredibly luxurious spear.
Extravagant enough to seem like a ceremonial weapon used by royalty in a court.
However, upon closer inspection, Su Lun identified that it was a weapon made for actual combat.
"The Archangel's Golden Holy Spear"
Explanation: An alchemical replica of the eternal divine weapon "Spear of the Supreme," inscribed with the name of the Great Alchemist 'Alferic'; This is a sacred spear that brings fatal harm to demons, made from sun god metal that restrains the powers of darkness; it inherently bears the eternal holy attribute, inflicting real damage like burning, sanctifying, and soul searing on all dark and death-related creatures; it represents justice and light, and only those with a just heart can wield it;
This spear was also one of the core elements of the sealed prohibition.
In itself, it was a very powerful weapon.
But the conditions for its use were quite strict.
Seeing its attributes, Su Lun immediately thought of Number Nineteen.
Her talents should be well-suited to the usage conditions. And her mechanical armor was certainly lacking in means of inflicting damage on dark and death-related creatures, so this spear could not be more perfect.
Now, however, a problem arose.
All these things were treasures, but how were they to be taken away?
After scanning the other areas of the chamber once more and finding nothing else of value, the three members of the Su Lun party fell back into contemplation.
They certainly had to take the items, but the risk was also very great.
That these treasures were used for a seal made them even more wary of the potential dangers.
After thinking through several plans, it was still most appropriate for Su Lun to stay behind alone to take the treasure.
He said, "Sister Qiantiao, Mr. Hei, you two go back to the ship first. Once you are a good distance from this ruin, I'll make my move."
"Okay."
Qiantiao and the others nodded in agreement.
The plan was to "grab and run," as there were no better options at the moment.
Without further discussion, the two led Tanni and the others out of the temple.
As for Su Lun, he remained alone, beginning to set up a long-distance spatial alchemical formation.
This formation utilized a large number of energy barytes, saving him the energy-consuming process of forming the glyphs and achieving an almost instantaneous effect.
...
Half a day later, the Night Eternal was far enough away from the Atlantis Ruins.
At that moment, as Su Lun in the temple's secret chamber received the message that everything was going smoothly on their side, he began to take action.
He first activated the alchemical formation that had been prepared under his feet.
The moment the formation's light lit up, Su Lun raised his hand towards the three items on the altar, a myriad of threads wrapped around the three treasures in an instant, and he pulled them into the small void realm in the blink of an eye.
He had rehearsed this process countless times in his mind; there was no hesitation whatsoever.
However, at the very moment when the sealed treasures were extracted, Mr. Hei on his shoulder cawed sharply, signaling a deadly danger!
The sealing runes on the ground shattered into dust, and a terrifying oppressive force burst forth from the earth, sweeping through the entire chamber.
Just as Su Lun was engulfed, the spatial formation activated, and his body disappeared in the same instant the seal broke.
Meanwhile, on the deck of the Night Eternal several dozen miles away, all the members of the Dawn Group watched the alchemical formation light up, each of them on edge.
After a flash of intense light, the void passage opened.
Soon after, a figure "thumped" heavily onto the deck.
Su Lun spat out a mouthful of old blood, but seeing the worried faces around him, he bared his bloodstained teeth into a radiant grin.
He had narrowly escaped from the brink of danger.

chapters.title: Chapter 567 - 566: The Phantom Black Sam Group
chapters.content:
"Su Lun, are you okay?"
"Not too bad...cough cough..."
On deck, the members of the Dawn group looked at Su Lun, whose body was drenched in blood, with sincere concern on their faces.
Although Su Lun was smiling, his smile was accompanied by another mouthful of blood.
Everyone had never seen Su Lun so severely injured.
At the moment, Su Lun's right arm and half of his body were a blur of flesh and blood, as if pulverized by some tremendous force, making his bones and flesh nearly indistinguishable and creating a terrifying sight.
The medical team also gathered around immediately, bringing out various potions and healing devices, and the green light of emergency alchemy glowed right away.
Su Lun himself also felt it was a close call. After all, since he obtained the "Urobolos Space-Time Ring," no one had been able to inflict such severe injuries on him.
Moreover, his physical strength was top-notch even among the seventh rank, and it was not possible that mere abrasions from law domain fields of the ninth rank could injure him this badly.
Nonetheless, the mere leaking power domain field of that being sealed beneath the temple had shattered half of his body.
Luckily, he had managed to escape quickly, otherwise even an eighth-rank professional could have been reduced to dust on the spot.
"A Titan offspring... what a powerful force field."
Su Lun lamented in his heart, getting a sense of what battling against a transcendent being might be like.
It was the suffocating feeling of being crushed by just a finger.
It was certain that the sealed monster was a Titan offspring, but it did not quite reach the divine level.
After all, this was a cursed space in the alchemy plane.
Su Lun was not too surprised about the Titan race being sealed inside the temple. Previous intelligence indicated that there had once been a great war between the Titan race and the dragon race in the waters of the Dragon Country, which had resulted in this cursed space.
It was just that the timeline seemed a bit confused, and he did not know whether the sealing happened before or after the war.
But it seemed not to matter.
With that space existing, there was absolutely no chance for any sneaky shortcuts.
While his thoughts were drifting for that brief moment, the Healing Alchemy Formation and the potent healing potions continued to mend Su Lun's body.
He even began to feel some slight sensation returning to his crushed right arm, and the flesh of the wound solidified and took shape, looking less horrifying.
However, high-level law forces still rampaged within the wound, permeating the flesh and bones like a toxin.
This was not a surgical level injury, nor was it one easily resolved by medical treatments.
If it weren't for Su Lun's fusion with the "X Potion" and the vampiric healing from the Blood Devour ability, even the strongest potion couldn't compensate for the catastrophic loss of life essence leaking out.
Under normal circumstances, Su Lun's injuries would have required him to stay immobile for at least ten days to half a month to fully recover on board.
However, it was at this moment that he suddenly thought of something and turned out a gemstone the size of an ostrich egg from his left hand.
...
Seeing that Su Lun was not in life-threatening danger, the furrowed brows of the Dawn members unknotted in unison, and the tense atmosphere on deck instantly eased.
But no one spoke, thinking to let Su Lun rest quietly in the healing environment, and even the sounds of breathing on deck were deliberately softened.
Yet suddenly, they saw Su Lun take out the gemstone.
In an instant, the dazzling and strange radiance of the gemstone captivated everyone's gaze on deck.
Realizing something, the expressions on everyone's faces became inexplicably elated.
Bartolo, Number Nineteen, Dora, and other high-ranking members of the Dawn group could barely contain their excitement, and even Old Sword God Bartolo and the eight-hundred-year-old "Blood Duke," Wazwas, could not hide their anticipation.
Mr. Hei and the others had already mentioned on their return that they had discovered the legendary alchemic artifact, the [Philosopher's Stone], in the ruins.
After all, it was a treasure from the legends that everyone had only read about in ancient texts and had never actually seen.
Now, looking at this red gemstone, it was as if the air itself had solidified.
Someone cautiously asked, "Mr. Su Lun, is this the [Philosopher's Stone]?"
Su Lun replied with a light laugh and a nod, "Yes."
At those words, the deck erupted into a collective sharp intake of breath.
And at that moment, the glow of alchemy shone from Su Lun's hand.
Taking out the Philosopher's Stone was not just to show it off; Su Lun also wanted to test the legendary alchemic artifact's miraculous uses.
He was concentrating on a seventh-tier self-healing formula, [Singing Hymn of Praise], capable of clearing foreign transcendent power erosion from the body.
As the green light from the Seven-Pointed Star Formation ignited around his body, suddenly, the light intensified dramatically, and the Holy Light that signified life recovery and purification swirled on Su Lun's surface.
However, to everyone's astonishment, the brightening light was so intense that it felt akin to staring directly at the sun!
Seeing this, the members of the Dawn were all taken aback.
"What... what spell is Mr. Su Lun using?"
"It looks like [Hymn of Praise]..."
"Impossible, I remember that a seventh-tier [Hymn of Praise] couldn't possibly have such a strong dispelling effect. Could this be an eighth-tier secret technique?"
"..."
Confronted with this anomaly, everyone started discussing animatedly.
Looking at the glowing alchemy formation, it certainly belonged to a seventh-order spell; but considering its effects, it surpassed anything that a seventh-order spell could achieve.
This made it quite mysterious.
Even Su Lun, the caster, was dazzled by the healing technique he had unleashed.
It was during the aggregation of the spell that he distinctly felt that one hundred percent energy conversion brought on by an equitable exchange.
This one hundred percent equitable exchange didn't simply lift Su Lun's capability from the original 60% to 100%.
It was an increase by several folds!
Ordinarily, he needed skill to minimize energy loss during the conversion process, but with the Sage's Stone, he only had to focus on gathering the energy.
The Sage's Stone would transform all gathered energy into the wood and light elemental energies needed for alchemy, with the entire process free of any obstruction or consumption, a perfect equivalence.
The smoothness of the process was almost unbelievable to Su Lun.
And coincidentally, he also possessed the "Isaac Alchemy Heart," which allowed him to gather far more energy in a short time than mages of the same tier.
That's why the present effect was blinding with Holy Light.
It was as if... the light from the spell which should have been as gentle as moonlight ended up as glaring as the sun.
Mr. Hei, who was standing by, saw this and, clearly knowing something, murmured in astonishment, "Legend says the Sage's Stone has the power of absolute equitable exchange and the ability to enhance alchemy… Indeed it does..."
Having seen this effect, the last trace of doubt in his heart finally dissolved.
It matched exactly what was recorded in the books!
...
With this enhanced "Singing Hymn of Praise" deployed, the invasive force within Su Lun's body was rapidly eradicated.
At this moment, he took out the dragon blood, which he had prepared earlier, and devoured it.
Under the empowerment of the Sage's Stone, the efficiency of "Blood Devour" also skyrocketed, and its absorption and self-healing effects were visibly formidable.
Seeing this scene, Qian Tiao couldn't resist asking curiously, "Su Lun, how do you feel?"
"Very strong..."
Su Lun responded, paused for a moment, and then corrected himself, "No! Extremely strong!"
Only after personally utilizing it could he distinctly feel how exaggerated the effects of the legendary alchemy artifact indeed were.
Just a moment ago, Su Lun had not only experienced the "absolute equitable exchange" of the Sage's Stone but also its "sublimation"!
It was transforming ordinary alchemy into the power of arcane-level spells.
And arcane-level spells themselves would become stronger, potentially exhibiting effects beyond their tier.
That's why Su Lun's seventh-order "Singing Hymn of Praise" felt like an eighth-order spell just now.
This effect could be exploited with any alchemy technique.
That is to say, this Sage's Stone would multiply Su Lun's combat power by many times!
And he was certain that he was only using the most basic functions of the Sage's Stone. In the future, as his understanding of alchemy improved, he would truly grasp the mysteries of this alchemic relic, such as how it achieved absolute equitable exchange.
Hearing Su Lun's evaluation, everyone from the Dawn Group felt an inexplicable anticipation.
However, the good times did not last long.
While Su Lun was still healing his injuries, suddenly, the lookout on the watchtower spotted something and bellowed, "A tsunami is coming! An enormous tsunami!"
Hearing this, everyone jumped onto the masts to observe the situation.
Even Su Lun, through the shared vision of Black Crows, saw the hundred-meter-high waves on the distant sea.
Looking at the direction from which the waves were coming, he immediately deduced that the source of the energy burst was the Atlantis Ruins from earlier.
But with the Emperor Eternal Night warship already a hundred nautical miles away, what kind of terrifying energy burst could propel the waves so far and with such height?
Su Lun looked on with a slight frown, aware that the source of the energy must be the freed Titan offspring.
In no time, the hundred-meter-high wave arrived, and the Emperor Eternal Night, riding atop the wave, began to pitch violently.
The water gushed onto the deck, and everyone was focused, watching their surroundings intently.
Su Lun was ready at all times—if the Titan offspring chased after them, he would immediately escape the cursed space with the Dawn Group.
After all, they had already reaped enough benefits from this trip.
They could always try again another time.
But to his surprise, after the first wave, there were continuous torrents.
Seeing the rampaging waves, Su Lun felt increasingly puzzled, "Could it be a fight has broken out?"
The continuous disturbance of such magnitude was anything but normal.
Moreover, as time went on, the waves grew even more chaotic, as if countless different shockwaves were being mixed together—a scenario only possible in a brawl among transcendent beings.
But the good news was, the freed Titan offspring did not chase after them.
So Su Lun was not in a hurry to leave the cursed space.
Instead, he was pondering, what kind of being could be battling the Titan?
As time passed, not only did the waves show no sign of subsiding, they became even more fierce.
The tumbling waves made even the colossal Emperor Eternal Night warship resemble a leaf boat, tossed around by the waves, seemingly on the verge of capsizing at any moment.
However, the violent waves seemed to awaken the entire cursed space, and all sorts of monsters emerged from the sea and sky...
Once again, an alarm sounded through the Dawn Group's communicator, "Monsters are attacking! The creatures in the sea have been disturbed."
At that, everyone became tense.
In the previous half month, they had encountered countless battles and witnessed the ferocity of these hellish creatures.
Watching the monsters approach, the Dawn Group prepared themselves for a fierce battle.
However, to everyone's surprise, the monsters weren't charging at them?
Most of the monsters completely ignored the presence of these living people, as if summoned by some mysterious force, swarming towards the direction of Atlantis in groups.
Only a few monsters that happened to be very close to the Dawn Group resulted in conflict.
But such conflicts didn't lead to any chain reaction, once killed that was the end of it.
This was completely different from the situation before when attacking one was like stirring up a hornet's nest.
Seeing this, most of the Dawn Group members were somewhat confused.
Only Su Lun saw something, and a gleam suddenly lit up in his eyes.
He had previously identified some information about this cursed space, and seeing the abnormal collective actions of the monsters before him, he immediately concluded, "It's the will of the cursed space that is influencing the behavior of the monsters!"
This is a cursed space, after all!
Everything within the space operates according to the primary will.
That will is calling all the nearby monsters to converge towards the center of the battlefield.
This space was left behind after a battle between the Titan Tribe and the Dragon Tribe, so clearly, the current situation might have triggered a battlefield scene from the past.
This also explains why there were so many bodies in that temple.
Perhaps, the City of Atlantis was an ancient battlefield... Even if not the main battlefield, it was certainly an important local battlefield.
Thinking of this, Su Lun's thoughts quickly became fluid.
If the monsters weren't troubling them, then wasn't the greatest danger of this cursed space gone?
Perhaps, there might be opportunities to be found?
....
Indeed, Su Lun's inference was correct!
The onslaught of monsters had no intention of troubling the Dawn Group, heading straight for the battlefield.
The noise and expanse of the battle near Atlantis grew larger and larger...
Eventually, to avoid conflict with the monsters as much as possible, they chose a deserted island and hid the Nevernight on a harbor behind the isle.
This hiding lasted for several days.
The battle near Atlantis showed no sign of stopping, and the monsters from all directions seemed to be increasing even more.
Su Lun and the others had no intention of getting involved in the central battlefield, where an overlord-class monster was fighting, and anyone who went there would perish.
Moreover, with the monster tide continuously gathering, and their inability to continue on their way, they decided to stay on this Nameless Deserted Island.
They hunted monsters that accidentally encountered them while making repairs.
In the afternoon, another battle ended, and the fishing squad pulled up a hundred-meter-long rotting two-headed shark from the sea.
The sailors began cheerfully disassembling the materials.
"Hahaha... we've hunted another eighth-tier hell shark, and we're going to dismantle a pile of high-grade materials. Captain Bess needs a 'Water Lung' implant for her advancement, and this monster is just perfect."
"Oh, I'm starting to like this place more and more. Yesterday, we even came across an ancient pirate ship, filled with treasure."
"Haha, yesterday Mr. Su Lun even let us try the Philosopher's Stone, my goodness, that really is"
"..."
Since all the monsters are now being summoned by the will of the cursed space, even battles do not cause too much disturbance.
This environment had become the best opportunity to hunt hellish creatures.
Here, unlike outside where seventh-tier monsters are local lords, high-tier monsters are everywhere.
Although the Dawn Group currently isn't short of money, these quality materials are indeed beneficial to have in abundance.
Moreover, despite the dangers within this cursed space, the laws are complete, making it an excellent cultivation environment!
With the combined alchemy resources of the Mafa and Ruying empires focused in this small void realm, team members lacked for nothing in terms of cultivation books, implants, or professional materials.
The overall combat strength of the team members visibly grew day by day.
On the deck, Su Lun was still wrapped in bandages.
After a few days of recovery, his injuries had finally completely healed.
At that moment, a Golden Angel descended from the sky onto the deck, and Su Lun, seeing this, smiled and said, "Is the spear to your liking?"
Number Nineteen replied with a smile, "It's fantastic! I was in need of a weapon just like this."
While speaking, she casually swung the diamond gold spear in her hand, drawing a crescent arc of light through the air, and added, "This spear comes with true divine damage, which is extremely effective against dark creatures and Spiritual Body monsters. I just tried it and it has suppressive damage even on eighth-tier monsters..."
Listnening, Su Lun smiled, "That's good."
The weapon in Number Nineteen's hand was naturally the [Archangel's Golden War Spear] found in the temple.
This spear was something that Su Lun himself couldn't use, but in the hands of Number Nineteen, its power was extraordinary, boosting her capabilities as a super mechanical warrior in the higher-ranking domains where her offensive methods were lacking.
No wonder she had been in such a good mood these past few days.
After a brief chat, Number Nineteen went back to dealing with the monster they had just hunted.
Su Lun watched her leave and glanced at Qiantiao, who was meditating cross-legged on the mast.
This gamble-happy lady had been sitting on the mast for several days and nights without moving.
Su Lun knew she was taming the number one amongst the Twelve Fine Swords, "Fotu".
Getting recognition from a spirited famed sword was a lengthy process.
Su Lun withdrew his gaze, looking over the busy deck. Everything seemed to be developing in a good direction.
Just as he was lost in thought, a cheerful call suddenly rang out beside his ear, "Mr. Su Lun! Mr. Su Lun!"
Turning his head, he saw Tanni, Lolo, and a few other fellows approaching.
Lolo ran over, without the slightest inhibition, shook his arm, and blinked, asking, "Mr. Su Lun, are your injuries healed?"
Seeing her expression, Su Lun knew exactly what the girl was looking forward to.
He chuckled and pulled out several puppets shrouded in black qi.
Lolo joyously took them, "Thank you, Mr. Su Lun!"
Tanni and Tatu also chimed in, "I want one too! I want one too!"
Like the big sister, Lolo distributed a doll to each, and they treasured them in their hands as prized possessions.
Su Lun warned, "These dolls have a very strong curse characteristic, you must be very careful with them. Don't feel like you have a way out just because you have these dolls. Sometimes, death can be more of a release than such a resurrection..."
Lolo laughed playfully, "Got it, Mr. Su Lun."
Tanni said sincerely, "Thank you for the gift, Mr. Su Lun!"
Tatu chuckled, "Haha... Thank you, Mr. Su Lun."
Dora said, "Thank you..."
The group took the gifts without any pretense, happily accepting them.
What Su Lun gave them were [Life-forfeit Dolls] that he had made himself.
These things had an effect similar to the [Thanatos's Life-forfeit Puppet] he had obtained before. They could steal the power of deities and transfer death onto the doll.
The price, however, wasn't small; the curse backlash one might endure could be more terrifying than death itself.
The Life-forfeit Doll had once saved Su Lun, and he thought to create a few for Lolo and the others for protection as well.
It just so happened that he had harvested the memory of the undead mage Yale Robbins, which completed the most crucial part he was missing in making the dolls, namely the theft of the deity's name, direction, and offering.
That's right!
The deity targeted by the deathly price of these dolls made by Su Lun was the same one worshipped by Robbins, and he found all the offerings among the spoils of war.
If Tanni and the others were to have an accident and use the Life-forfeit Dolls, it would be that deity bearing the price.
While there were some unpredictable risks involved, ultimately, it meant an extra life, and the hoped-for outcome was a positive one.
...
After giving a small gift, Tanni and the others clustered around him, chattering and asking after his well-being.
He could hardly help but laugh and cry at the same time.
Time seemed good, not at all like a journey that was supposed to be extremely dangerous.
However, the calm didn't last long.
Suddenly, the lookout atop the mast spotted something and shouted, "All hands, pay attention, unidentified ships spotted at seven o'clock!"
There was fog on the sea, and the visibility wasn't very far.
Su Lun looked in that direction, seeing shadows of several ships vaguely through the fog.
This was otherwise quite ordinary.
This cursed space had swallowed up too many pirates and adventurers before; they had encountered several of them previously.
But this time was different.
The number of ships emerging from the fog kept increasing, becoming gradually clearer.
To their astonishment, among these ghost ships was a gigantic vessel roughly the same displacement as their Eternal Night!
"Be careful, everyone, it looks like a ghost fleet, with numerous ships... However, they are not heading in our direction," they announced.
"Look over there! That appears to be a Ghost Emperor-class ship!"
"Huh, that black beard and skull flag... looks somewhat familiar. Check it out, could it be the legendary 'Black Sam Pirate Crew'?"
"My God, it really is! That Ghost Emperor-class battleship is the 'Santa Maria'!"
"..."
With those words, the Dawn Brigade immediately buzzed with excitement.
They could never have imagined they would encounter the Pirate King crew that met their end in these waters more than twenty years ago—the Black Sam Crew!

chapters.title: Chapter 568 - 567: The Ferocious Death God's Fire
chapters.content:
The sudden appearance of a ghost fleet amidst the sea fog had everyone in the Dawn Group on high alert, but when they saw the pirate flag bearing a skull with a "graffiti-style smiley beard," everyone was stunned.
Because at the Bounty Hunters Guild camp, this flag still hangs as the symbol for the pirate group topping the bounty list.
It was also the armada of the Pirate King, revered as the pinnacle and faith by countless adventurers and navigators—the Black Sam Pirate Crew!
Apart from the flag, a second glance at that warship with its special ivory ramming prow affirmed it as the "Santa Maria," the legendary ship spoken of in hushed tones among the pirate circles.
Su Lun, too, found the sight extremely astonishing.
Seeing this legendary pirate crew in person, a profound respect for the adventurer predecessors suddenly welled up in his heart.
The Black Sam Crew were pioneers, legends of an era, the peak that innumerable adventurers aspired to climb.
And their meaning was particularly special for the Dawn Group.
Both Tanni and that "Black Sam's World Sea Map" had brought immense help to the Dawn Group.
But with his reverence, Su Lun also felt a twinge of melancholy, seeing the fall of this once legendary crew, a somber light inexplicably appeared in his eyes.
At this moment, the Pirate King's crew that once dominated the seas of the Luyingmafa Empires and remained untouchable by official navies, had now turned into a lifeless fleet of ghosts. The ivory behemoth was tattered, with its hull bearing the marks of battle everywhere, the sails riddled with holes, and even the pirate flag had become fade and lackluster... With no one to maintain it, the hull was overgrown with various shellfish and marine parasites, looking like a sunken ship dredged from the sea, ancient and decayed like a corpse crawled out of a grave.
There were many more ships amidst the foggy shadows, and the Santa Maria sailed on like this.
All members of the Dawn Group watched with a solemn respect, their gazes slightly complex.
Just then, a figure suddenly appeared on the deck with a Flash.
Bartolo, who rushed over upon hearing the news, looked at the all-too-familiar warship with moist eyes, murmuring to himself, "Old Pal... I've finally seen you again."
The Old Sword God, who wouldn't even tremble when drawing his blade before an eighth tier dragon, now trembled all over, raising his hand in the air to wave but lowered it again. It seemed he originally wanted to greet the distant ship, but realizing that the familiar companions were no longer there, he despondently lowered his hand.
Of all the companions who had shared life and death together, only he had survived alone, living in a daze for more than twenty years.
The Sword Demon, Saito Misaburo, the great grandmaster of the Swordsmanship of the Artless Path, had died here, leaving only the foreign soul, the "Dragon Hunter" Bartolo Figaro.
He had thought multiple times about leaving with his companions, but remembering that the captain and the others had given him the only chance to survive, he felt he should cherish his life more.
As long as he was still alive, there was still someone from the once Pirate King, Black Sam's crew.
But now, seeing his old companions, Bartolo couldn't help but let the tears flow.
The desolation in the expression of the Old Sword God was noticed by everyone in the Dawn Group.
Not just Bartolo, two others on the ship also had complicated expressions.
Tanni and his mother, Lady Frida, looked at the distant ghost ship.
Lady Frida, tears glistening on her stunningly beautiful face, whispered, "We meet again, Mr. Sam."
Seeing the colossal ship, she couldn't help but recall the first time she encountered it.
Back then, she was shocked at the sight of the huge vessel as well.
But on the ship was a man who always wore a radiant smile and seemed kind-hearted, someone who did not carry the usual malice toward Naga like other humans did.
He said his name was Sam Bellamy, a sea adventurer, and he and his companions came from the human empires east of the Eternal Night Sea.
From that moment, Frida felt the man's goodwill was like the warmth of the sun, always bringing comfort.
On reflection, the parting seemed as if it had been just yesterday.
She hadn't expected their next meeting to be here.
Tanni, too, stared blankly ahead.
He had never seen his father, Sam Bellamy, but his mother had recounted countless times, and he had heard legendary tales from his companions.
Always hoping to meet him, now looking at the warship, he felt a sting in his nose.
He who was once cursed as "Unlucky Tanni" suddenly felt as if all the injustice he had suffered faded away upon seeing the ship.
...
However, it was while everyone was observing the ghost pirate ships in the distant mist, the lookout on the watchtower issued another warning.
"Not right! It's not just one fleet, but many! The instruments detect at least over a thousand moving ships on the sea."
"Look there, not just the Santa Maria, a Sea Emperor level warship, there's another one at five o'clock direction!"
"And over there, nine o'clock direction too!"
"Ten o'clock direction... My God, that ship is several times the size of the Sea Emperor class warships, how can there be such a huge ship in the world?"
"Oh, I see it too. Are my eyes deceiving me? I see a large group of Undead Drakes flying above it, the ship must be enormous..."
"I thought it was a moving mountain..."
"That could be the legendary 'Sea God-class battleship.' No way, that shipbuilding technology has been lost for at least ten thousand years, what's the origin of this battleship?"
"..."
As the ghost fleet drew closer, the members of the Dawn group were astonished to find that it was not just one Sea Emperor battleship—there were many more in the mist.
Three ships, five, seven... the more they looked, the more they saw.
Even several ghost battleships that were the size of islands were visible.
Even Su Lun was shocked.
The shipbuilding skills of today, the displacement of a Sea Emperor class battleship was already the limit, because today's materials and structures simply can't withstand larger volumes.
Steel battleships could be built bigger, like the Sky Battleship being built in the small void realm, which is the size of a small town, but what was in front of them were all sail wooden ships!
Only in some ancient civilizations in legends, there were even larger ships.
They thought it was just a legend, but now, seeing the actual things, everyone was immensely shocked.
The Santa Maria of Black Sam's group was considered "medium-sized" amidst this huge ghost fleet.
And it wasn't just that the ships were big; the aura seeping from those monsters on board was terrifying.
Seventh order, eighth order, ninth order...
Several of them made Su Lun feel a vague palpitation in his heart, definitely beyond the ordinary realm!
It was a good thing that these monsters were called by the will of the cursed space to go to Atlantis; otherwise, if they had come for the Dawn group, Su Lun would have fled at the first opportunity.
When they had seen a few ghost ships earlier, everyone was thinking about boarding the ships to search for treasures like before, but now seeing this endless, dense ghost fleet, everyone fell silent.
The countless ships in the mist headed in the same direction, the oppressive feeling was overwhelming, and everyone on the Eternal Night kept their breaths low, not even daring to breathe heavily.
Even Su Lun frowned deeply.
It was one thing to respect the Black Sam group, but what he cared about more was the [Faar's Holy Grail] on board.
This was the most important item to completely solve his spiritual mutation, and it was also essential for his spiritual power to reach a new level.
Without that holy grail, his future plan for a puppet troops strategy would lose at least half of its combat effectiveness.
On the deck, the high-level fighters of the Dawn group converged together.
Barrett muttered a few words, "Strange, where did these ships come from? How did they all come together?"
The countless ghost ships in front of them were from numerous civilizations, spanning at least tens of thousands of years. Normally, encountering a couple of ghost fleets was quite normal, but oddly enough, they gathered together. It was as if they set off from someplace at the same time.
This was something no one could figure out.
Seeing this, Su Lun thought about it and then said, "I might still need to make a trip."
Before, he thought that if he couldn't find it this time, he'd have more chances to come back later and search more thoroughly.
But now, it seemed that if he didn't act this time, this might be the first and only time he encountered it.
The timeline in this cursed space might be chaotic, but it didn't seem to be the kind that would reset indefinitely; instead, it moved at a normal flow.
Now, all these ghost battleships were summoned by the will of the space to head towards the battleground at Atlantis.
But the center of the battlefield is currently like a nuclear explosion site, where anyone who goes will be turned to ash and scattered.
That means, if the ghostly Black Sam's group was wiped out in the battlefield, they would most likely cease to exist altogether.
It would then be even more impossible for Su Lun to find [Faar's Holy Grail].
And now was the best opportunity.
The monsters, summoned by the will of the cursed space to go to the battlefield, wouldn't trigger any chain reactions as long as they weren't deliberately provoked.
So, even though the ghost fleet on the sea surface was countless, being careful, the risk might not necessarily be greater than in other situations.
Hearing this, although the high-level fighters of the Dawn group were serious in their expression, they also knew this was crucial for Su Lun.
Qian asked, "Do you want me to accompany you?"
Su Lun shook his head, where would he not know that she was asking about his injury again, "I'm just going on board to look for something, and I'll leave immediately after I find it. Moreover, if I go up alone, I'm less likely to attract those undead."
Upon hearing this, no one said anything more. Indeed, there was no better choice than for Su Lun to go alone.
There was no excess noise on the ship, and it was so quiet that you could hear a pin drop.
However, at that moment, a faint voice rang out, "Mr. Su Lun, may I... come with you? I mean, if it doesn't interfere with your plan..."
Everyone looked closely and saw it was Tanni speaking, her face full of anticipation and nervousness.
Su Lun thought for a moment and smiled, "Of course."
He was well aware that Tanni was hoping to meet the father she had never seen before, even though he had become an undead.
Su Lun paused for a moment, then turned to look at Frida standing next to Tanni and said, "Lady Frida can come along if she wishes. But for the time being, you can only stay in the Minor Void. Only after ensuring that there is no danger will I let you out."
Tanni's expression brightened immediately upon receiving Su Lun's permission, and she nodded earnestly, "Mm!"
Hearing this, Frida's eyes were filled with gratitude. She didn't say much, just quietly said, "Thank you."
...
Su Lun marked a passing ghost ship with spatial coordinates but wasn't in a hurry, planning to wait until the ghost fleet had moved farther away from Eternal Night before he made his move.
The ghost fleet stretched out quite a distance on the sea surface, spanning dozens of miles.
However, after the larger ships at the front had passed, the ones following became progressively smaller.
Fortunately, these ships were all swift, and after waiting over an hour, the sea appeared empty of any such vessels.
Su Lun announced, "Alright, I'm ready to go."
"Mm."
The members of the Dawn group nodded in unison, watching him wrap himself in a funeral shroud, his body gradually turning transparent and his presence vanishing without a trace.
Suddenly, a spatial rift gleamed in the void and, within the distorted space, they saw a transparent figure step through.
The scene around him shifted, and Su Lun appeared aboard a small ghost ship.
There were around a dozen wobbly humanoid monsters on the deck. This was a pirate ship, and the monsters were pirates in life.
After assessing the monsters, information flashed before him: [Elite Ghost Pirate (Fourth-Order Bronze)] [Ghost First Mate (Fifth-Order Silver)] [Captain Morgan of the Crab Pirate Crew (Sixth-Order Gold)]...
In the outside world, these would be considered rare and bizarre monsters, but in this cursed space, even the minor monsters on a small ship were of this caliber.
Su Lun had no intention of disturbing these monsters. He remained undetected thanks to the shroud which kept his aura contained, but he still physically existed.
As he landed on the deck, some monsters seemed to detect something and turned their heads.
However, once Su Lun settled down and remained still, the sensation of being watched disappeared.
He breathed a sigh of relief.
With a flicker of spatial disturbance, a black crow flapped its wings and flew out.
Being a pure creature from hell, Raven's presence didn't attract any attention from the other monsters; it flew directly through the mist and towards the sea.
Sharing its vision, Su Lun quickly located the "Saint Maria" belonging to Black Sam's group amidst the fleet.
The crow slipped into a hole in the ship's hull and found a room devoid of undead.
Su Lun confirmed the coordinates and once again used Flash, appearing out of thin air in the ship's cabin.
No sooner had he arrived than his soul perception detected a dense cluster of soul fires.
The Saint Maria had a much higher concentration of undead than the small pirate ship he'd just been on.
And they were stronger!
Just as Su Lun landed, a foul stench and a strong gust of wind assailed him from above.
Knowing his appearance had alerted a monster, he swiftly leaped a few meters away to avoid it.
At the same moment, a thick, red-black octopus tentacle thrust through the wooden planks of the wall and slapped precisely where Su Lun had just stood.
Slimy, yellow-green mucus splattered on the flooring, hissing as it corroded the surface.
Su Lun's eye twitched slightly as he identified the creature: [Chef Chief of Black Sam's Group·Undead Solomon's Attack (Seventh-Order Dark Gold)].
A named monster was always the trickiest adversary within its tier.
Crucially, Su Lun had previously conversed with Old Sword God Bartolo and learned that Black Sam's group's chef chief was known as 'Wine Barrel' Solomon, a notorious pirate who had once had a bounty of over a billion, only to now be transformed into an octopus tentacle monster.
After a short wait, the tentacle retracted back into the dark crevice in the wall.
Once aboard the ship, Su Lun could distinctly sense every soul vibration.
So even though the tentacle was concealed behind the wall, he was acutely aware that the monster was cunningly lurking, not having been fooled into a rash move.
This wasn't intelligence in the monster, but the battle instinct from its previous life.
"There sure are a lot of high-level undead on this ship..." muttered Su Lun.
According to Old Sword God Bartolo, the Black Sam group originally had only two Eighth-Order professionals, the leader Sam Bellamy and the executive 'Bloody Witch Doctor' Elsa Lee.
Yet as it stands, even after becoming Black Sam's crew had become stronger.
And not just by a little bit, it felt like they had strengthened by an entire major rank at least.
Estimating, Su Lun feared that becoming the undead Sam Bellamy was a solid ninth rank or above in combat power.
Thinking so, he dared not act rashly.
Using spatial perception to distinguish the ship's structure, Su Lun already had a planned route in his mind and pondered, "Old Pal Bartolo said the treasure chamber should be on the third deck. There's a restricted room... If that's the case, it's a bit troublesome."
He also felt fortunate to have met the Old Sword God Bartolo, so he wouldn't have to search the treasure chamber room by room on his own.
Otherwise, he feared that all the creatures on the ship would be alerted.
However, the bad news was that, although he'd found the room where the treasure chamber was located, there was a very strong soul fluctuation nearby.
Luckily, the strongest soul fluctuation was on the deck, which must be Pirate King Sam Bellamy.
After all, since he had come all this way, he was definitely going to the treasure chamber first.
With the entire ship's structure and the distribution of creatures clear in his mind, Su Lun's brain had already formed a three-dimensional navigational map.
Without much hesitation, he flashed and appeared in a sparsely-monstered room dozens of meters below.
After a few flashes, he was already not far from the treasure chamber on the third deck.
However, just as he landed, a ghost creature immediately floated in front of him, with the name displayed as: [Undead Anchor Man Jack（Eighth Rank Silver）]
"A fight is still inevitable, huh..."
Seeing the attributes of the monster he had identified, Su Lun knew it was tricky.
Almost simultaneously, a wide-range Illusion Technique, "Agonizing Wail," was released.
Such an area attack was impossible to avoid, and given the creature's high rank, even the rune umbrella would take some time to deal with it.
Just a second before he felt dizzy, a pale green flame suddenly surged on Su Lun's body.
The moment the eighth-rank ghost species creature came into contact, it ignited like cotton meeting flame, and its entire Spiritual Body was set ablaze.
In an instant, the drifting ghost's face showed extreme pain, and its wails and screams broke more wildly into Su Lun's sea of consciousness.
Su Lun's consciousness went hazy in an instant.
But a moment later, that feeling of vertigo receded like the tide.
Su Lun focused his gaze to see that the once-fierce [Undead Jack] had its Spiritual Body burnt away by a large portion, its soul fluctuation weakening by ninety percent in an instant.
He felt secretly relieved at the sight, thankful that he had mastered this secret technique, or he might have been directly controlled by "dizziness" to death as soon as he came in.
The oppressive presence and psychic wails of an eighth-rank ghost species creature would greatly affect even ordinary ninth-rank individuals.
Moreover, it wasn't just one such creature here but many!
If he were controlled, he wouldn't even have a chance to flash away, and it would be a fight to the death.
The green flame burning on Su Lun's body was naturally the [Death God's Fire], a major weapon against souls.
His soul strength was not much less than that of the previous undead archmage. Having extracted that fellow's cultivation insights, he had instantly reached the level capable of severely damaging eighth-rank Spiritual Bodies.
And [Mushi] was also an excellent secret technique for controlling fire.
During the days he was recuperating, Su Lun had practiced the Death God's Fire to the point of proficiency.
This was the biggest confidence that Su Lun had to venture here!
The [Death God's Fire] secret technique gave him a fatal means against beings above the seventh rank.
...
Su Lun reacted extremely quickly, and in the moment he was attacked upon landing, he severely wounded the eighth-rank ghost species in front of him.
Once again retracting the black umbrella, he completely captured the weakened creature.
However, because using the [Death God's Fire] required unwrapping the anti-corpse cloth, it was during this moment that his aura had leaked, attracting the attention of the creatures all over the ship.
"Looks like a fight's inevitable!"
Su Lun inwardly let out a sharp shout.
If he couldn't enter unnoticed, then he'd have to finish the fight quickly!
Now that he'd been exposed, he didn't hesitate at all and teleported directly to the location of the treasure room.
It was at that moment that several terrifying soul fluctuations on the ship rushed over swiftly!

chapters.title: Chapter 569 - 569: 568
chapters.content:
Su Lun revealed his tracks and immediately pulled several living zombies out of the void realm, leaving them in place.
With a flash of spatial ripples, he appeared in another room on the lower deck.
Then he dropped another living zombie.
After teleporting several times like this, the enormous Saint Maria now had the "presence" of living beings everywhere, thoroughly stirring the undead on the ship. The previously silent cabins suddenly filled with various rustling sounds of monsters on the move.
Having had experience with using living zombies to lure enemies before, Su Lun, to ensure that the zombies lasted a bit longer, had specially dressed them in heavy armor.
This kind of heavy armor focused on defense without considering mobility, essentially turning them into thick iron boxes.
The cost of making them was not too high, but once put on a living zombie, even a Level 7 creature would risk breaking its teeth trying to bite through.
Just two or three breaths after Su Lun dropped the zombies, he immediately heard the grating sound of metal being chewed.
With these zombies drawing the attention of the monsters, he would be safer.
It was at this moment, when Su Lun sensed the powerful soul fluctuation near the treasure room moving away, that he immediately cast the teleportation magic, accurately appearing at the location of the treasure room on the third deck.
The hull of the Sea Emperor-class warship was sturdy to begin with, and this was also the core cabin of the Saint Maria, so the damage wasn't severe.
The good news was that the treasure room was still there.
The bad news was, when Su Lun arrived, he saw a room scattered with gold and silver items everywhere.
His brows immediately furrowed, "This... how do I search?"
According to what Old Sword God Bartolo had said, the Black Sam group also possessed a very small piece of space fragment. They used it to make the group's treasure room.
However, now the space fragment was shattered into pieces.
Gold and silver treasures were scattered all over the floor, with the thickest pile measuring a full meter or two.
It wasn't just gold and silver treasures, there were also many rare and unique curiosities.
The Black Sam group had robbed the rich to aid the poor in the past, raiding many great nobles, as well as looting many Duke and Marquis treasure vaults. The variety of high-grade cursed items, weapons, and materials here was no less than the wealth of a small kingdom.
A glance over the room yielded no sight of the [Chalice of Phar].
Perhaps it was buried in the gold coin piles, or maybe still inside the space fragment.
But not finding it immediately was a big problem!
...
Normally, dealing with these space fragments wouldn't be too troublesome for Su Lun; he could just absorb them into the void realm.
But this process would take quite a bit of time.
And the undead wouldn't give him that opportunity.
