Facing everyone's concerned looks, Su Lun responded as if it were all routine, "I just had a fight with that Heavenly God's Son. I may have gotten injured, but I've also dealt him a serious blow. It's not a bad trade."
His tone was so calm it was as if losing a leg involved no pain at all, rather indicating it was a great gain.
Upon hearing these words, everybody's expression was one of astonishment, seemingly hearing an unexpected response: not that he had fled after taking a beating, but... he had seriously injured the enemy?
In the next moment, even Old Sword God Bartolo cast him an incredulous look.
They had all witnessed firsthand how strong Saint Frank McAdam was. Against such an enemy, it would be quite an accomplishment just to escape alive with serious injuries, not to mention win.
Even Bartolo himself wasn't confident.
But now, Su Lun claimed to have caused the enemy serious harm?
Lolota's eyes instantly shimmered with excited stars as she asked eagerly, "Mr. Su Lun, you mean... you seriously injured that Heavenly God's Son?"
A faint smile appeared on Su Lun's face as he replied, "Yes. I scorched his soul with the Death God's Fire, and it'll be quite difficult for him to recover anytime soon."
He spoke lightly, but the peril of the previous battle was known only to him.
It wouldn't be an exaggeration to say it was a gamble with his life.
The last move that decided the battle—if he hadn't dodged that disintegrating light beam, more than just a leg would have been dissolved.
When everybody heard this, joy spread across their faces.
If Su Lun said he inflicted serious damage, then it was certain he had!
Yet they still found it hard to believe. A magical immunity of 100%, with all attacks dissolving upon him, and a Saint Heir of the divine race... such a flawless enemy was defeated?
An enemy one could defeat was no longer at all frightening. It was as if the oppressive, cloud-covered sky had been pierced by sunlight, clearing the gloom from everyone's hearts and sparking excitement, with all clamoring to know more.
"Ah... Mr. Su Lun, could you tell us exactly what happened?"
"Yes, that guy with three eyes can disassemble anything, how did you deal with him?"
"..."
Su Lun listened to everyone's discussion, smiled, and shook his head, as a few words couldn't clearly explain the battle they had just fought.
Besides, now was not the time to discuss it.
Qian Tiao looked at the crowd and said irritably, "Alright, alright! Haven't you seen that his leg is still broken?"
While a missing limb was a severe injury, it wasn't much of a concern within the Dawn Group nowadays. Whether it was Dr. Banks' limb regeneration technology, limb transplantation, or Mafa's mechanical prosthetics, all were quite advanced. As a magician specializing in Alchemy, getting a new arm or attaching a prosthetic leg was nothing unacceptable.
But as the big sister of the group, when Qian Tiao spoke, everyone quieted down without complaint: "Oh."
Su Lun also said with a smile, "Everyone should prepare as well. We may soon face a fierce battle."
The plan was initially just to see how things went and to help Queen Medusa within their capabilities.
They had thought to run if they couldn't win.
But now that they had heavily injured Saint Frank, they might have to face a tough fight.
An enemy that could be defeated certainly warranted a battle.
Moreover, since they almost killed the saint heir, those from the Heavenly God's plane would definitely regroup and attempt to annihilate them again.
Unless they planned to give up on targeting "Mimir's Well," there was no escaping it.
If they were to come again, it would probably be a fight to the death.
Once Su Lun mentioned this, the Dawn Group realized the gravity of the situation and immediately went to their respective positions to prepare for battle.
...
As the crowd dispersed, only the medical team and a few top fighters, including Qian Tiao, remained around Su Lun.
While treating his injuries, they discussed the upcoming battle plans.
At that moment, Su Lun received a mental message in his head, from Queen Medusa who was staying in the cabin.
Her tone was full of disbelief, "You actually inflicted heavy soul damage on that saint heir? How did you manage that?"
In her view, a human mage like Saint Frank was nearly unbeatable in this plane.
The reason she had signed a cooperation treaty with these humans wasn't that she had much faith in the strength of this human adventuring group.
It was simply because this human had once helped her successfully survive a tribulation.
Even then, she recognized him as a human with a legendary fate.
Originally, she just wanted to test whether the ancient prophecies of her Gorgon clan were true, that a hero with a legendary fate wouldn't die easily.
Queen Medusa didn't harbor much hope and considered it a trial.
She had noticed these humans were always ready to retreat.
This was part of the content of their equal treaty and there was nothing to complain about.
But unexpectedly, things turned out differently.
Upon encountering them, this human had actually defeated that mage?
It seemed like the tide had suddenly turned in their favor.
If these humans could indeed restrain that mage, she suddenly saw a glimmer of success.
...
The Dawn Group members knew about the peculiar secret technique "Death God's Fire," but she did not. Su Lun had no intention of revealing his trump cards everywhere; he simply replied, "I used a secret technique to heavily damage that saint heir's soul. But I wasn't able to kill him. And even so, that 'Immaculate Shield' can still be used by other believers, just with slightly less effect. The threat remains substantial."
After this response, there was a moment of silence from Medusa's side, as if she was pondering something.
After a while, she finally said, "Since you could heavily damage that saint heir, others who get their hands on it will also need to be wary of you."
"..."
Su Lun listened without responding.
Indeed, both his talent "Omnipotent Solution" and Artifact Projection required Divine Power to function.
If someone else used them, the threat would be considerably reduced.
However, as a result, Su Lun's secrets were also becoming scarcer.
This time, he had used "Philosopher's Stone" and "Death God's Fire," capitalizing on intelligence gaps to strike a heavy blow to Frank.
The next time we encounter them, the enemy will surely be on guard, and achieving a surprise effect won't be easy anymore.
At that time, Queen Medusa relayed a mental message, "This return to the ancestral land may be my only chance, and I won't hold back anymore... If possible, I hope you and your team can do everything in your power to help me complete the final inheritance. This process may take quite some time..."
Su Lun understood the meaning of these words.
Previously, the terms of the alliance were to assist each other within the limits of one's abilities, and if the enemy proved too strong, they would part ways.
But now, even though these words fell short of a life-and-death pact, the risks had clearly skyrocketed.
He was weighing the pros and cons when Queen Medusa spoke again, "Accordingly, if I can complete the inheritance this time, I will certainly do everything in my power to help you in the future."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun thought briefly before agreeing, "Good!"
His sight extended beyond the present to the future.
The planar war had just begun, and as the supreme masters from the Heavenly God's plane descended, the situation would only get tougher.
With just the current power of Dawn Brigade and the twin empires of Marfaruling, it was going to be very difficult...
As Mr. Jing had said, they needed allies to fight together, especially top-tier combatants.
If Queen Medusa could succeed in her inheritance this time, she might become a true "Demigod", and her combat power would certainly be astonishing.
In other parts of the Alchemy plane, even if there were other demigod-level intelligent beings, they might not entertain alliance requests from weaker parties, let alone choose to oppose the powerful higher planes, a choice fraught with immense risk.
This was a decision gambled on fate.
Su Lun decided to take on the risks of the present in order to reduce some of the pressure from the future all-out war.
Besides, if they did not help, the situation for Dawn Brigade would not improve. Facing those from the Heavenly God's plane alone, their chances of victory would be even smaller.
He briefed Queen Medusa on the situation, and she decisively agreed.
...
Su Lun shared the situation with Dawn Brigade's senior fighters, and everyone unanimously agreed with his decision.
In the current state of the Alchemy plane, no one could remain uninvolved; if they couldn't handle even these invading vanguards, the situation would worsen when faced with a full invasion.
The covenant was successfully signed.
The Evernight continued its rapid voyage across the sea.
Since they had taken a shortcut to avoid the Sea of Snakes ambush and Su Lun had seriously injured the pursuing Saint Frank, it seemed like the threat had disappeared.
However, Su Lun did not plan to sail slowly, as without the restraint of the "Mirror of Innocence", Queen Medusa had no rivals in this sea area.
Su Lun then led some of Dawn Brigade's senior fighters, along with Queen Medusa, and teleported directly to Cococolosi Island.
The Evernight, on the other hand, laid mines along the way and chose a different direction, heading towards another desolate island a few dozen nautical miles away from Cococolosi Island.
When the great battle unfolded, Cococolosi Island would inevitably become the central battlefield, which would certainly turn into a hellish scene.
If the entire Dawn Brigade were to stay there, they would instead be placing themselves in danger.
The Evernight's advantage lay in long-range artillery support, and splitting the battlefield was actually better.
This way, if the enemy focused on attacking Cococolosi Island, then Dawn Brigade could maximize their advantage in firepower support; if the enemy's main force attacked the Evernight, with the Old Sword God Bartolo and others on board, they would not be easily defeated in a short time, and it would also be easier to retreat.
Moreover, Su Lun could support them at any time.
With just a few ten-thousand-man battalions from the Heavenly God's plane in this sea area, and with Saint Frank severely injured, Su Lun did not believe the enemy's full-scale charge stood much chance.
As long as he could obtain the "Shield of Innocence", he would go where it led.
Not to say that victory was certain, but once Queen Medusa completed her inheritance, the overall situation would be settled.
Thus, Su Lun arrived at Cococolosi Island, the ancestral home of the Gorgon tribe, without much trouble.
"Cococolosi," when translated from the ancient language of Dragon Country, means: Island of Endless Poison Snakes.
It was a lush and vast island.
As soon as he teleported near the island, Su Lun sensed dense soul fluctuations within the primeval forest.
He was far from careless; although he was strong now, his odds against a high-ranking gorgon were even.
Both parties had the strength to annihilate each other instantaneously.
Su Lun raised his hand, summoning a spatial vortex in front of him.
The cloaked Queen Medusa and several senior Dawn Brigade fighters stepped out from the small void realm.
The Poison Snakes instantaneously sniffed out the presence of humans approaching, simultaneously rearing their necks as if dense clusters of duck necks sprouted throughout the jungle.
Looking closely, the underbrush, cracks in the rocks, treetops... everywhere were adorned with colorful Poison Snakes.
These Poison Snakes vary in size, some as thin as fingers, others a hundred meters in length.
Upon seeing the humans who had intruded into the forest, the Poison Snakes all split open their scarlet mouths, revealing their sharp Poison Fangs and surged forward en masse.
"Ssssss..." echoes resounded throughout the forest, sending chilling friction noises that made one's spine tingle.
Su Lun had long been aware of them and appeared unfazed as he watched.
The few companions beside him each showed slight unease, obviously discomforted by the intense phobia-inducing Snake Island.
However, before the Poison Snakes could unleash their ferocity, Queen Medusa suddenly lifted the cloak from her head.
In the blink of an eye, her head of snake hair was revealed, as she menacingly hissed silently towards the mass of snakes.
It was as if a queen was asserting her sovereignty to her subjects, exuding a domineering aura.
Su Lun and the others couldn't help but avert their eyes.
As soon as that head of snake hair appeared, the fierce demeanor of the myriad of Poison Snakes in the primal forest wilted away.
Just like the Sea of Snakes that had once driven back the "Eternal Night," the snakes seemed to be repelled by an invisible force, immediately clearing a path before everyone.
Upon seeing this, Queen Medusa narrowed her eyes and let out a cold sneer, "Hmph! Those treacherous sisters of mine, without outsiders to back them, don't even have the courage to stay on the island and meet me face to face..."
Hearing this, Su Lun's expression relaxed, finding it to be a good thing.
Just a moment ago, he too sensed several powerful souls flee at the moment Queen Medusa revealed her presence.
The island's high-ranking Gorgon sorceresses chose to flee, which meant fewer troubles for now at least.
The group did not linger in place, but followed Queen Medusa, rushing towards the center of the island.
While hurrying along, Su Lun also left Spatial Coordinates throughout the forest.
On the way, he discovered ancient architectural traces in various parts of the forest.
Those covered in green moss were not irregularities but rather the remains of intricately carved ancient buildings.
Su Lun and Mr. Hei exchanged looks; it was clear that the entire island was likely an ancient city ruin.
By its scale, it was even comparable to Atlantis, which they had previously encountered in the cursed space.
Moreover, it wasn't only the buildings; there were also stone sculptures of humans, magical beasts, and various other creatures—evidently the petrified remains of outsiders who had entered Kelosy Island over the years.
However, now was not the time for archeology or treasure hunting. The group continued without respite. Since there was no further hindrance, they quickly reached deeper into the island.
Upon arrival, Su Lun was immediately shocked.
He had never imagined that the ancestral land of the Gorgon race would be a magnificent palace!
Hundreds of meters high stone columns supported an ancient palace, where the ravages of time had collapsed much of its structure, with green moss creeping over it, and the reliefs that seemed to narrate mythological tales eroded...
But despite its antiquity, rather than a feeling of decay, it emitted an overwhelming sense of history.
This did not seem like the primitive dwellings of the Gorgon tribe but rather a grand palace left behind by a once-glorious human civilization, hidden away on this unassuming island.
Su Lun distinctly sensed that there were large spaces both inside and beneath the palace.
The palace itself clearly concealed countless secrets.
Before the palace was a pond of black water that could be identified as highly venomous, and the group stopped upon reaching it.
Queen Medusa said, "You are the first humans in countless years to witness the 'Temple of Gorgon.' However, you can't enter the temple, for it will bring you misfortune."
Su Lun nodded his head, showing his understanding.
The Gorgons are a lineage of demigods; it is normal for them to have their own secrets, and just because you are allies, doesn't mean you get to know everything.
Besides, the palace didn't seem like a good place; it was best avoided if possible.
Queen Medusa didn't explain further.
But, having signed the second alliance, her tone had become much friendlier, and she added another sentence, "After I go in, I'll leave the rest to you."
Su Lun nodded, "Alright."
....
Just as Su Lun and his party had reached Kelosy Island, the Dawn Brigade's outposts scattered across the sea also sent messages: "Mr. Su Lun, fleets of Mages from the Heavenly God's plane are heading your way!"

chapters.title: Chapter 578 - 577: The Mastery of All Weapons
chapters.content:
In front of the God Temple of Gorr, Su Lun and his companions were not surprised to hear the news of the enemy attack.
After all, it was certain that the enemy would come.
Moreover, after Saint Frank had come alone and was badly injured before, it was highly unlikely that anyone would come by themselves to seek death again.
If the enemy really wanted to send a large force, it would still take a long time.
They had enough time to slowly make preparations.
Queen Medusa had gone into the temple to accept her inheritance, and there was a specialized engineering team setting up defenses, which left the three main combatants, Su Lun, Qiantiao, and Mr. Hei, feeling somewhat idle.
Even with the great battle impending, Mr. Hei remained as calm as ever. He waited for a moment and then seemed to develop a keen interest in the history of the temple, examining the buildings all around.
They couldn't enter the temple, but looking around was no problem.
As Mr. Hei observed, he took out various professional measuring tools and began taking measurements all around the palace.
He quickly found something that interested him, muttering, "Huh... that's strange. Judging from the style of this architecture, it doesn't seem to be a product of the Dawn Era, it looks more like it belongs to an even older ancient goblin style. I've seen related archaeological records in the Ruyingt Library, only the goblins who were skilled in engineering would be so precise with architecture..."
As he spoke, he was aiming an observing glass at the buildings, as if he had discovered something else, he exclaimed, "Oh! Even after countless years, these main structures are still so precise, there's no doubt that this is an ancient goblin relic!"
Su Lun, listening, also looked over with interest.
Though he was not a professional archaeologist, he knew quite a lot about the subject.
Looking at the style of the architecture, he also felt Mr. Hei's observations were reasonable and continued the conversation, "Could it be that the Gorr clan enslaved goblins to build this temple? Or did they seize a goblin palace that already existed?"
Mr. Hei listened, gave a mysterious smile, and said, "I am more inclined to the latter."
He continued, "Look carefully, do the styles of the reliefs describing Gorr mythology differ slightly from the main architectural style? Although the craftsmen who carved these patterns have tried hard to imitate, no matter how they compensate, it's not easy to replicate goblin technology. The gap in skills has left this kind of discontinuity..."
Su Lun, upon further inspection, realized the truth, "It really is like that!"
Mr. Hei, clearly seeing more, added, "Moreover, I suspect that this temple, like the ancient Atlantis city we encountered in the Curse Space, has a dual purpose of possibly being a 'temple' or a 'mausoleum', designed in such a way that it can gather supernatural forces. That's why it became the ancestral land of the Gorr tribe."
Interested by the conversation, Su Lun chimed in, "Is that so..."
As the two were amiable in their discussion of archaeology, Qiantiao started to feel bored.
She clearly had little interest in matters that required thinking, complaining, "Ah... what's there to study about a bunch of old stones."
Instead, she seemed more intrigued by the black water pond and kicked a stone into it without much thought.
There wasn't even a "plop" as the stone fell into the water; just about ten centimeters above the surface, it was corroded by the pond's rising toxic gases into a hissing sound, instantly turning into a wisp of green smoke that disappeared.
Qiantiao raised an eyebrow and remarked, "That's a strong toxin."
Su Lun also glanced over and warned, "Sister Qiantiao, don't get too close. The vapors from this pond can paralyze the nerves, and breathing too much of it can induce powerful hallucinations."
Hearing this, Mr. Hei revealed his characteristic amiable smile and said to Qiantiao, "Archaeology is actually quite interesting. What seems like a pile of 'old stones' actually hides a lot of key information. Take this black water pond for example; it's built right on the central axis of the temple, which in ancient civilizations, especially those with divine beliefs, is a very special location. This shouldn't be just an ordinary pond but rather a special site with another purpose. I suspect there might be some kind of energy-gathering rune array underground, which is why the poisonous miasma from the forest has condensed into pond water over countless years. Perhaps there is some high-grade treasure below too..."
"Treasure?"
Qiantiao blinked her eyes, her face showing a confused yet impressed expression: How didn't I see that?
Hearing this, Su Lun too approached the pond to take a closer look.
In fact, he had felt there was something off about this black water pond before, but he couldn't pinpoint what it was.
Now, hearing Mr. Hei's words, he also believed it was very likely.
However, no matter what secrets lay beneath, they couldn't rashly explore without the owner's permission.
The group spent their time near the temple looking here and there, occasionally cleaning the moss-covered steles to read the fragmented texts left by ancient civilizations.
Su Lun and Mr. Hei deciphered more and more useful information.
So time passed in leisurely archaeological exploration.
Three to four hours later, the enemy's ships finally appeared on the horizon of Kekeluo Xi Island.
...
"Mr. Su Lun, Observation Post No. 7 has spotted the enemy approaching the island. They have about thirty ships coming from four directions to land…"
"There is also movement in the snake herds in the forest; it seems high-ranking gorgons have landed on the island. Be careful."
"The bombs in the target area have been installed and are ready to be detonated on command."
"The Eternal Night has taken position and is awaiting the fire command…"
"..."
A string of messages came through the communicator.
Su Lun looked at the two people beside him and said softly, "Prepare to fight."
Qiantiao was sleeping on a stone, but upon hearing the news, he jumped up, his face showing a hunger for battle, "Ah... finally, the battle begins."
Mr. Hei still had his unhurried demeanor. After hearing that the battle was about to start, he slowly put away his archaeological tools and remarked, "The enemy is slower than expected. It seems that they must have prepared something quite special."
Su Lun also smiled, "Exactly. Thirty ships are coming together, so it looks like it's a full mobilization. Next, we might be in for a fierce fight."
Qiantiao and Mr. Hei listened in silence.
They were already prepared.
The people from the Divine Realm were now aware of most of the Dawn Group's military capabilities; they knew about the presence of Old Sword God Bartolo on their ships and that Su Lun was capable of inflicting serious damage to Saint Frank. Thus, naturally, no one would come all alone to meet their death, not even an eighth-tier great Mage.
If it were a legion against a legion, the Dawn Group would have an even greater advantage.
After all, the range and precision of the cannons on those pirate ships were almost negligible; they couldn't even hit the Gorel Temple in the center of the Kokolos island.
There was only the Dawn Group hitting the enemy, not the enemy hitting them.
So, if the enemy wanted to surround and kill them, they had to land on the island.
Crows flew in the sky, and Su Lun shared their vision, but could only see a foggy expanse.
The people from the Divine Realm had used "War Fog" when they came over, blurring the actual position of their warships.
However, thanks to early detection devices and the perception abilities of Tanni and his mother, Dawn Group had already pinpointed almost all of the enemy pirate ships' locations.
Through the communicator, Tanni's report came again, "Mr. Su Lun, we have confirmed that two of the enemy's Sea King class warships landed near marker 46, and another near marker 77. A large number of people disembarked, and they have started to come ashore..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun looked at Qiantiao and the others, "Let's follow the original plan. I'll go take care of those pirate ships to prevent future troubles. The temple here, for the time being, will trouble you two."
Qiantiao and the others nodded.
While they were speaking, they could already hear the rustling sounds from the jungle. It was a sign that the Poison Snake horde was beginning to move again.
The Gorgon women who had landed on the island were probably initiating the Sea of Snakes disaster once more.
Ordinarily, this was an unsolvable disaster for humans. However, this time, they were not completely unprepared.
At that moment, the three of them each took out a small glass bottle.
The small glass bottle contained light golden blood, which was the "Blood of Redemption" of Queen Medusa, effective at immunizing against various curses not higher than the blood itself within a certain time limit.
It was particularly effective against the "Light of Petrification Curse."
This was the vital blood from Queen Medusa's right atrium, the best counter to the petrification curse by the Gorgon women.
Drawing blood was indeed harmful to her own body, and also restrained Medusa herself. If there hadn't been a deep collaborative covenant signed with sufficient trust, she would never offer this golden blood.
The three of them smeared the blood over their eyes and immediately felt a refreshing sensation.
Su Lun checked his attribute panel and saw a new temporary buff status added, "Immunity to Petrification Curse."
That is to say, even if they looked directly at a Gorgon, it wouldn't be a big problem.
Even with the curse light from a high-order Gorgon, they wouldn't be instantly turned into stone statues anymore.
With this, they dared to agree to land on the island, as it was their most important reliance.
After getting ready, Su Lun didn't delay any further and turned to the other two, "I'm off first."
With a flick of the sorcerer's seals, he vanished from the spot.
...
At the same time as those people from the Divine Realm began to land, the skies above Kokolos Island also suddenly erupted with the sound of heavy artillery fire.
The Eternal Night took advantage of the fire range from the ship's guns in the distance, and began to cover the confirmed enemy's landing positions with firepower.
It was not to kill enemies, but to first sink their ships.
A Mage legion needed to spread out according to certain angles when deploying a Super-Order Magic Circle, and multiple ten-thousand-person Mage teams couldn't possibly crowd together.
Moreover, according to current intelligence, the enemy had divided into at least eight landing points, apparently preparing for some kind of large-scale Legion Magic formation.
Su Lun, of course, wouldn't let them have their way.
The scenery shifted around him, and he found himself on the shore side, right where one Sea King class warship and three medium-sized pirate ships were anchored.
The Legion Magic Shield had already been deployed, with Mages on board defending against the shells from the sky.
Su Lun gripped the rune-etched black umbrella in his hand and immediately sensed tens of thousands of people packed upon the ship.
There was indeed an entire ten thousand-man Mage Formation here.
Even the moment Su Lun teleported over, the spatial fluctuations were clearly detected by the enemy's sensing Mages.
Three fire pythons surged over on the surface of the sea.
This was a seventh-order arcane spell, but Su Lun watched without any change in expression. He pinched a sorcerer's seal and whispered in his heart, "Secret Technique: Puppet Theater."
The sorcerer's seal was so well-practiced it instantly conjured a massive cross in the sky.
With the enhancement of the Philosopher's Stone, Su Lun's spellcasting speed was now several times faster than before!
During the actual casting process, he raised his hand, summoned a gargoyle to shield himself, and a black spatial vortex appeared, swallowing the three fire pythons into the void in the blink of an eye.
But in that brief delay, a barrage of dozens of spells was suddenly unleashed from the four warships in the distance. Lightning, fire snakes, hail, waves, wind blades... the thousand-man legion's magic coalesced and released over the entire sea surface in a sweeping assault.
In the past, Su Lun would have avoided a ten thousand-man Mage Formation at all costs.
Especially when aggregated into a combat Formation, they were both offensive and resistant, making even ninth-order professionals helpless against them for a while.
But now...
Su Lun just sneered.
You have a ten thousand-man unit; I have one too!
Su Lun teleported in mid-air, avoiding the first round of combined spellfire.
These spells exploded on the sea surface, creating white waves dozens of meters high—a terrifying force!
However, just as those pirates were about to use their second round of spells, he suddenly tore open dozens of spatial seal scrolls.
The scrolls "boom," "boom," "boom"... burst open.
Under the sunlight, the sky suddenly sparkled with silver light.
Upon closer inspection, the sky was now filled with fierce-looking metal gargoyles with muscular bodies and wings.
Not hundreds, not the one thousand from before... there were a full ten thousand of them!
These puppets spread out, covering the sky and blotting out the sun!
Su Lun summoned the gargoyle legion, narrowed his eyes slightly, and commanded in his heart, "Puppet Secret Technique: Army of Thousand Soldiers."
The threads in the sky instantly linked the puppets together, and the gargoyles seemed to come to life as their energy cores lit up.
With Su Lun at the center, ten thousand gargoyles raised their hands together, each creating twisted spatial vortexes that met the densely incoming spells head-on.
The legion's dozens of high-order spells that had previously churned the sea were now all silenced at once.
Most of the magic was devoured by the void, and even the few spells that penetrated the defense were ineffectual against the gargoyles' highly magic-resistant metal bodies.
If the Mages are a legion, the gargoyles are, likewise, a legion in battle formation!
From the sky above, the ten thousand gargoyles also happened to form a Nonagram Alchemy Formation.
When Su Lun designed the gargoyles, he had already considered their combination functions on a massive scale, such as how to defensively distribute damage and jointly unleash higher-order spells.
The "Army of Thousand Soldiers" now was not merely ten thousand gargoyles!
With Su Lun's current divine-level spiritual power, he was nearly able to precisely control each gargoyle.
Even after being hit by the second round of spells, the Void Runes on the gargoyles were all lit up at once.
It was when the ten thousand gargoyles activated the super-large legion Alchemy Formation that intense spatial fluctuations surged in the sky.
The vast spatial distortions were like a plane on the brink of collapse, a technique so fearsome that even top-ranked professionals would blanch.
Su Lun's expression turned stern, "Forbidden Curse: Layered Space Annihilation!"
Since the Dawn Era had sufficient Void materials, these gargoyles were imbued with Void Power above all else.
Currently, the average combat power of the gargoyles was roughly equivalent to fifth-order professionals; thus, the combined attack of ten thousand fifth-order professionals, akin to a divine legion from the celestial planes, could kill a ninth-order being!
And the drawback of the celestial plane legions was that they couldn't teleport at will. If their formations were broken, the consequences would be even worse.
But the gargoyles could stand and be bombarded with spells, something that flesh and blood could not withstand!
Even though the ten thousand-man Mage Formation had fully activated their magic shields, confronting such terrifying spatial fluctuations was definitely not a good strategy.
Just in that moment, the Nonagram rune array in the sky had already brightened to its limit.
Just as the spell was about to come crashing down in a blinding flash, suddenly, a mysterious figure in a cloak appeared on the deck of the Sea King's warship.
Even when a black cloak covered the entire body, how could Su Lun not recognize that this was a high-order Gorgon?
It was one from the Sea of Snakes calamity that had besieged the Dawn group before, whose soul fluctuations he had memorized and could never mistake.
From the very beginning, Su Lun had detected the presence of a high-order Gorgon hiding on the ship, and naturally, he was well prepared. Moreover, he had applied the "Blood of Queen Medusa's Redemption" and was utterly fearless.
These creatures naturally knew that to reverse the situation, they must deal with the puppeteer.
It was in that lightning-fast moment that the person on the deck suddenly unveiled their cloak.
The myriad snake hairs glared at Su Lun in the midst of the puppets, blanketing the sky in a grey light instantly.
Su Lun was probably the first in countless years to dare directly face the Light of Petrification Curse.
His left eye's luster shifted, and he seemed to understand something, murmuring to himself, "High-tier earth laws, so this is how it is..."
The All-knowing Eye identified some special law fluctuations, understanding part of the mechanism.
But before he had time to ponder, the overwhelming radiant light was already shining on his entire body.
Su Lun distinctly felt as if his gaze had stiffened, his entire body seemed paralyzed.
But this sensation only lasted for an instant before a more potent force within his body dispelled this paralysis.
In that split second, Su Lun experienced the Gorgons' legendary petrification curse and its instantaneous nullification, finding it quite marvelous.
As for the few stone gargoyles that were petrified, Su Lun didn't pay much attention.
He had tested before that the stone gargoyles had restorative properties; even if they were temporarily petrified, they would slowly recover.
There were ten thousand stone gargoyles here simply because he could only just about control that many, but that didn't mean he had only that many.
There were plenty more finished golems in the little void pocket.
In that same instant, not even the Gorgon's release of petrifying light could prevent Su Lun from casting his spells; the Nonagram Formation in the sky had already congealed into shape.
In front of the baffled and terrified gazes of the mages on the pirate ship, the forbidden curse-level Space Wizard unleashed his spell instantly.
A distorted black light, over a dozen meters long, rushed towards the legion's magic shield.
When the legion's magic clashed with the legion's alchemy, the spear met the shield, and they only withstood each other for an instant before a loud "boom" sounded like a burst balloon, creating a violent shockwave on the sea's surface.
Space Law nearly always restrains all common magic, and Su Lun had previously estimated the endurance limit of a ten-thousand-man magic troupe, so this strike was bound to succeed!
The "Layered Space Annihilation" exploded, instantly shattering the pirate ship; the mast was broken off, and the deck was cracked widely. The magic troupe on the ship had their formation blasted apart in an instant, sending limbs flying and filling the air with screams.
Countless space fractures appeared, and those fifth and sixth-tier mages were unable to regroup the formation in a short time.
The ten-thousand-man magic formation was broken!
To Su Lun, the magic troupe now presented a huge vulnerability!
Seeing this, he didn't delay a moment longer. The shadow of Death appeared behind him, a faint green soul fire surged over his body, and in the blink of an eye, he vanished.
At the same time, the swarm of stone gargoyles also charged towards the three warships!
Su Lun teleported and appeared beside the Gorgon, who was still puzzled, and then struck her with a palm.
Even if the petrification curse was useless, Gorgons possessed nearly an eighth-tier physique that normal attacks couldn't harm!
However, the "Death God's Fire" directly scorched the soul.
The Gorgon had not yet comprehended what happened when she suddenly felt her soul burning.
She tried to flee in terror, her snake hair whirling wildly in a panic, but how could Su Lun let her get away?
Su Lun completely ignored the petrification curse, grabbed her arm, and the Death God's Fire from his body poured fiercely into the monster's body.
The Gorgon felt the terror of imminent death. It wanted to struggle, and the snakes on its head wildly spewed grey beams in all directions.
But this final act of desperation didn't forestall its death. Instead, by indiscriminately unleashing petrifying beams, it turned the surrounding mages who tried to rescue it into exquisitely lifelike stone sculptures.
In an instant, Su Lun felt its soul dissipate; with a strike from the Rune-etched black umbrella in his right hand, he ejected the Gorgon's fragmented soul from its body.
With another sweep of the Death shadow, the Gorgon lost all signs of life.
The soul had vanished, but in its place lay a complete high-order Gorgon corpse!
This was top-tier material for crafting golems!
Delighted, Su Lun quickly collected the corpse.
Turning back, he saw the ten-thousand gargoyle army had stormed the breach caused by the troupe's defeat, tearing it even wider!

chapters.title: Chapter 579 - 578: Mr. Hei
chapters.content:
The mages on the Divine Plane were stunned by Su Lun's overwhelmingly swift combos.
They had never imagined that a fully assembled legion of ten thousand mages could be critically damaged by a mere handful of exchanges!
Before this, they couldn't have fathomed that the battle would start off on such a footing.
Normally, shouldn't it be their several ten-thousand mage legions overwhelming a small adventure group in a chaotic beatdown?
Why did it seem... as if they were the ones being besieged by a single person instead?
The one who defeated them was not some powerful enemy, but rather an army defined by its vast numbers.
But it was a puppet army!
Controlling ten thousand puppets at the same time?
If they hadn't seen it with their own eyes, no one would have believed it.
Because even in the Divine Plane, no Puppet Master had ever achieved such a feat.
And that puppet army's implementation of the Void Alchemy was clearly specifically designed to counter their magical military formations. Just from that alone, everyone knew the enemy knew the back of their hand when it came to their magic tower.
And how could that Alchemy's power be so exaggerated?
Why was the efficiency of the ritual so high?
And most puzzling of all, why was this guy not afraid of the Gorgon Queen's curse?
Before they could unravel these questions, Su Lun was already wreaking havoc inside the mage legion with his gargoyle legion.
...
Even Su Lun himself felt it was somewhat fortuitous.
Without the "Blood of Queen Medusa's Redemption," even with the puppet army, he never would have dared to confront the ten thousand mage legion head-on.
But as it happened, "Helen" was the first Gorgon Queen to successfully transcend tribulation in countless years. After her bloodline returned to its origin, she awakened some awareness and came to know the secrets of the curse only known to the demigod Goer.
In other words, Su Lun had mastered the only feasible strategy for a lower plane to tackle a high-order Gorgon.
This had taken the enemies on the Divine Plane completely by surprise.
Su Lun quickly put away the body of the Gorgon Queen, and without any delay, he directed the gargoyle legion to charge once again.
The mages had their formations scattered, regrouping into hundreds or thousands to stubbornly resist, bombarding Su Lun with various legion magic.
Unfortunately, in terms of numbers, combat strength, and other aspects, the gargoyle legion was not even slightly weaker than the ten thousand mage legion.
And since Su Lun knew everything about the ten thousand mage legion, the formation of the gargoyle legion was specifically designed to break through defensive barriers, like a sharp arrow, piercing everywhere.
Puppets, fearless of life and death, left devastation in their wake, facing bloodshed and carnage.
And Su Lun himself would seize the opportunity to teleport and decapitate higher-level mages.
Previously, his methods had not been sharp enough against high-level mages, but now, with the "Death God's Fire," almost no one dared to confront him directly.
Soul fire burned, ignoring all defenses, and those touched by it were either dead or severely mutilated.
With the Philosopher's Stone enhancing him, all his techniques were now enhanced versions of their former selves. Previously unbeatable within Level 7, he was even more so now.
Often, as the Field of Death unfolded, the mages it passed over died in droves.
For any troublesome beings, it was Death God's Fire to greet them.
This method of fighting was completely brutal and unreasonable; no one dared to confront it head-on.
So much so that even the great mage at the early stage of Level 8 in that ten thousand mage legion avoided Su Lun as much as possible.
Su Lun also had no intention of pursuing the few high-level mages with superior escape techniques who ran everywhere; he was like a lawnmower, mercilessly cutting down the lower-level mages.
Once the ten thousand mage legion lost its numerical advantage, it no longer held any fear.
After just a few rounds of assault, Su Lun's tactics of targeted decapitations plus the gargoyle legion's strategy had battered the ten thousand mage legion into shambles.
The gargoyles had no casualties, which spelled ultimate despair for the enemy.
The mages dwindled in number, while the puppet army's strength scarcely diminished at all.
As long as Su Lun lived, the puppet army's power would always be at its peak!
The more the battle dragged on, the smaller the enemy's chances of victory became.
...
While Su Lun was cutting down the unit of ten thousand mages, a report also came from Qian, indicating that enemy's top combat forces had gone straight to the Golgo Temple.
"Su Lun, a master has arrived at the temple! It looks like it's the celestial army leader Augustus you mentioned. He has the 'Shield of Purity'."
"Can you hold on?"
"So far, there are no problems. Mr. Hei has already entangled that guy, and they are in the chessboard space, the situation is unclear now. I'm dealing with the snake tide."
"Great! Hold on a bit longer, I'll come over once I finish here."
"..."
Su Lun listened to the transmission through the communicator, his eyes flashed with a fierce light.
It was reasonable that the enemy would send their top combat forces to raid the Golgo Temple.
After all, as far as it looked presently, the only one certain to pose a fatal threat to someone in possession of the Divine Artifact Projection 'Shield of Purity', was Su Lun himself.
And the only one qualified to kill Queen Medusa, was the bearer of the 'Shield of Purity'.
Now that Su Lun had exposed himself by attacking the pirate ship, the enemy naturally wanted to decapitate Queen Medusa, to eliminate this greatest hidden danger.
Normally, this would be the time for Su Lun to return and provide support.
After all, only his 'Death God's Fire' might pose a threat to the enemy.
But doing so would mean that the other landing units of ten thousand mages would not be dealt with in short order. Once they set up their formation, it would create an even worse situation.
However, if Su Lun did not return, no one could stop the army leader Augustus with the Divine Artifact Projection.
That man also possessed the talent "S-009-Essence of Infinite", although not as outwardly as the previous Saint Frank, he was equally strong. His postnatal development of talent was even not inferior to Frank.
That he would take up the shield was fully within Su Lun's expectation.
So, even Old Sword God Bartolo was not sure he could hold him back.
Not to mention the other members of the Dawn Group.
But Mr. Hei was an exception.
Despite being very low-profile within the Dawn Group and rarely showing any stunning performance in battle,
he lacked Lei's flashy Sword Intent and Su Lun's domineering puppet army...
But all the old members of the Dawn Group knew that Mr. Hei, always looking "utterly normal," had never lost a battle.
No matter how powerful the opponent was.
Only the high-ranking members knew how formidable this scholar was.
Lei, Barrett, Number Nineteen... During the Dawn Group's internal sparring, all were dominated by Mr. Hei's terrifying Mind Reading Technique.
Even now, Su Lun was very reluctant to face such an enemy.
Because fighting him was very uncomfortable.
An opponent who never exposes any flaws could make one feel restricted from start to finish, as if hitting cotton...
Mr. Hei had developed his Mind Reading Technique to an unfathomable extent, even more acute than Su Lun's All-knowing Eye in observing everything.
His fighting style was one word: "steady!"
Mr. Hei's attacks might not be sharp, but he excelled in control, strategizing, and various skillful Alchemy techniques, always achieving miraculous effects.
If any opponent showed even a slight flaw, it would be infinitely magnified into a fatal vulnerability.
Occasionally in jest, Su Lun would nickname Mr. Hei as "Fifty-Fifty,"
because whenever he fought, he would modestly say: "Before the outcome is decided, each has an equal chance of winning."
Even if the opponent seemed much stronger than him, he would say so.
This was also why when Su Lun landed on the island, he brought Mr. Hei along.
It wasn't just for archaeology.
Although Mr. Hei could not defeat the army leader Augustus, he was confident he could hold him off!
...
Su Lun, hearing the transmission from Qian, knew that the problem was temporary.
The mage group of tens of thousands before him had already been decimated, and Su Lun had no intention of wasting any more time on the soldiers who had fled into the forest.
"Dora, fire coverage at observation point 46!"
"Yes!"
Having issued the command via communicator, he quickly withdrew his puppet army and, with a pinch of the Suren Sorcerer's Seal, he had teleported away.
Just as Su Lun left, the next second, the sky was bombarded with alchemy cannonballs.
The pirate ships that hadn't been completely destroyed immediately got caught in a barrage of gunfire, and without the mages' defensive barrier, the ships were incredibly vulnerable. But in an instant, the Western Sea Fleet's Sea King class warship was completely destroyed, sinking into the sea along with those aboard who had prepared the formations.
Meanwhile, Su Lun had already appeared at another landing point.
This was another Sea King class warship controlled by the celestial mages, where another group of tens of thousands were setting up something.
When Su Lun arrived, the mages there had apparently just received the previous message.
Their faces showed disbelief, clearly shocked.
However, the next second, shock turned into horror.
Because everyone, looking into the sky, had abruptly seen an alchemy cross appear, followed by spatial fluctuations emerging, and dense silver puppets already blanketing the sky.
Su Lun repeated his tactic, starting off with the gargoyle army executing a combined attack forbidden curse, penetrating the mages' protective barrier, then quickly teleporting into the crowd, where the Death God's Fire and the Domain of Death swiftly tore open an entrance, followed by his puppet army storming in, executing various slaughters.
A series of ruthless combinations, was a tactic that Su Lun had simulated countless times before the battle, leaving no time for the enemy to react.
It didn't take long for the second group of tens of thousands to be utterly crushed.
Su Lun's speed in defeating a group of tens of thousands was incredibly fast.
So fast that the enemy didn't even have time to arrange countermeasures before he had already moved to the second location.
Normally, even discounting Gorgon Queens, a ninth-ranking professional would find a group of tens of thousands quite troublesome.
But Su Lun, the Puppeteer, was an exception.
He alone was an army.
A puppet army, whether in terms of number, quality, control, or tactic, was no less superior, how could it possibly lose to the enemy!
However, just as he crushed the second group of tens of thousands, on his way to the third landing point, a sudden change occurred.
The sunlight suddenly became blinding, and a golden light shone down from between the clouds, as if a mirage-like golden palace appeared out of nowhere in the sky.
Soon after, a distant and majestic voice echoed in his ears, "The Divine declares: 'Spatial transference is forbidden in this world.'
With these words, some sort of rule on the island of Cocoloxi seemed restrained by a mysterious force, and the space suddenly solidified.
Su Lun keenly sensed that divine power descending and noticed that the Space Law around him was "locked," making it extremely difficult to manipulate.
He murmured, "A wide-range space ban, it has finally come..."
Having just stripped many mages of their souls, he knew that the Divine Art Scroll had been activated.
This Divine Art level scroll was extremely expensive, even more so than training a group of tens of thousands.
Now, the enemy had no choice but to use it.
However, Su Lun's expression remained unchanged.
This Divine Art level space prohibition could restrict his spatial displacement, but it could not restrict the high-level Space Law of "Urobolos' Space-Time Ring" itself!
It was no longer the time to hide and protect; there were still four groups of tens of thousands left unhandled. Letting them set up magical formations to summon the will of a deity would mean having as many such Divine Arts as needed!
With a pinch of the Suren Sorcerer's Seal, slightly slower than before, his figure vanished from the spot.
When he reappeared, he was already at another landing point.
The fierce battle replayed.
...
Su Lun, in a devastation resembling pulling rotting roots, almost entirely bewildered the enemy.
At various times, he teleported to four different landing points, consecutively crushing four groups of tens of thousands into disarray.
The celestial mages who had survived, hearing information from their comrades, had long since become numb from shock.
Just like the Dawn Circle couldn't imagine any way to defeat Saint Frank before, the mages now couldn't think of any means to deal with Su Lun.
Ignoring spatial restrictions, ignoring petrification curses, possessing the combat power equivalent to tens of thousands in a mage group...
Such a tricky existence, who could solve it?
No one.
At least, no one below the ninth-order Sage of Law could kill him.
All the mages understood at this moment that these alchemical natives possessed divine-class treasures!
But it was all meaningless now.
The mages finally felt fear as they realized they had underestimated their opponent.
However, the battle was far from over.
Although Su Lun's puppet army had swept through several ten thousand mage groups with an unbeatable posture, the legion commander Augustus, who was entangled by Mr. Hei in the chessboard space, was also aware of the outside situation.
This guy was currently the strongest combat power in the divine plane, and as long as he wasn't dead, the problem still existed!
Just as Su Lun was preparing to deal with the last two ten thousand mage groups in one fell swoop, suddenly a thousand urgent messages came through the communicator: "Su Lun, Mr. Hei has been defeated!"
...
"Defeated?"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun, who was in the midst of battle, didn't hesitate at all, gathered up the puppet army and immediately executed a targeted teleportation.
That Mr. Hei had held on for so long was already a significant advantage.
With four of the six ten thousand mage groups now shattered, it was impossible to set up some super-large magical formations in the short term.
This reduced a major threat.
The surroundings changed in a blink, and Su Lun had already teleported back in front of the Golgond Temple.
No sooner had he landed than a strong, pungent smell of blood filled his nostrils.
Looking closely, the vicinity of the temple now resembled a hellish scene of a mountain of corpses and a sea of blood.
It was various poison snakes chopped into pieces, with bones piled up into a wall several meters high.
Meanwhile, the sky was thundering with lightning, and within the pile of snakes, various severed sections of snakes were still tumbling around; upon closer inspection, the six-armed fiend, externalized as a thousand arms, had already killed until blood flowed into rivers.
Unafraid of the petrification curse, she was now enveloped in a terrifying aura of killing intent, with her Sword Qi domineering and unmatched.
Yet, there were too many poison snakes, and at that moment, the thousand-armed monster was merely struggling to avoid defeat.
The situation on the other side was even worse.
Seeing the phantom of black and white spatial squares in the sky, Su Lun knew something was wrong inside.
It was the moment he teleported over, the person inside seemed to sense it and could no longer hold on, the chessboard instantly collapsed, and a figure flew backward, unable to restrain themselves and spewing a mouthful of blood in mid-air.
Looking closely, who could it be if not Mr. Hei?
But at that moment, his robes were tattered beyond recognition, his face pale as gold paper, and what was worse, both his arms were severed at the shoulders, and as he flew backward, fresh blood gushed wildly from the wounds.
Even his soul fluctuations were on the verge of dissipating into death.
Upon seeing this, Su Lun's eyes narrowed sharply, and with quick reflexes, he teleported over and caught the man, with a spatial phantom appearing in his palm, he immediately took the severely injured Mr. Hei into his pocket void.
At that time, the chessboard space completely collapsed, and an old mage with a white beard stood in void.
This guy was none other than the divine plane's magic legion commander, Augustus!
At that moment, the grand mage had a vertical pupil phantom on his forehead, a light shield in his left hand, and a magic wand in his right, carrying an air of authority without anger.
When Su Lun looked over, there were also two severed arms hanging from the guy's legs.
In that instant, those two severed arms suddenly lit up with a series of mysterious black runes, activating a deathly sealing forbidden curse, "Corpse Ling Curse."
Mr. Hei had calculated this guy with his last action!
Unfortunately, a beam of light from the vertical pupil on Augustus's forehead completely disintegrated the two rune-covered arms, causing no real damage.
But seeing this, Su Lun's pupils constricted slightly.
Mr. Hei had successfully left a spatial mark on this guy after all.

chapters.title: Chapter 580 - 579: 【The Horn of Doom of Galal】
chapters.content:
The seasoned Grand Magician Augustus of the Divine Plane watched as Su Lun teleported to him in an instant, a flash of cold light fleeting through his aged eyes.
Now that even a Divine Art banning flight couldn't restrict his teleportation, it must mean he possesses a divine-grade treasure.
What a fortuitous opportunity...
However, even though the man before him was an entire major rank lower, Augustus didn't dare to underestimate him in the slightest.
He used to think the natives of the Alchemy Plane weren't worth mentioning.
After all, with incomplete laws and a civilization with broken and missing eras, there was a limit to what its practictioners could achieve.
But over these past days, as the magic legion suffered repeated heavy losses, the contempt in his heart had dissipated, replaced by an unprecedented seriousness.
Just now, for instance, although the black-robed magician was only a seventh-rank, he somehow managed to entangle him for so long, even causing him a bit of trouble.
In the Divine Plane, it was absolutely impossible for such a person to exist!
Having encountered numerous strong foes throughout the majority of his life, Augustus had to admit that the black-robed magician he just faced was the strongest seventh-rank he had ever seen!
The secondary release of the "Mind Reading Technique," although not too exaggerated a talent, was especially effective when used by the black-robed magician. Those eyes of insight seemed to leave no secrets hidden, creating a sense of restraint and helplessness in battle.
This was his personal encounter; had it been any other eighth-rank Grand Magician from his group, it's not to say they could win, they might even have been defeated by this seventh-ranker!
But strangely, such an aberrantly powerful seventh-rank magician turned out to be an "invisible character" unmentioned in any intelligence report?
Another glance at the swordsman slaughtering his way through the mass of snakes in the distance... What was this situation?
A third-release Rakshasa Woman and a seventh-rank step-away Sword God, either trait would be considered top-tier talent.
Yet, both were seen in the same person?
This "Dawn" alchemy organization seemed more and more mystical.
Moreover, the current man had severely wounded that Puppet Master who had injured Saint Frank.
This guy, an even tougher nut to crack.
At this moment, Augustus no longer had the slightest hint of underestimation.
...
Su Lun had taken Mr. Hei into the Minor Void Realm and faced the legion commander Augustus, his expression just as tense.
Often, to judge if an enemy was strong, just sensing their aura was enough to tell.
This guy... was very powerful.
Su Lun even felt he was more difficult to deal with than that arrogant Saint Heir, Frank McAdam.
His gaze flickered towards the Golgion God Temple. Though he couldn't see clearly what was happening inside the dark palace, deep within the current uneasy atmosphere, the soul of Queen Medusa was in a very unstable state, as though undergoing some kind of transformation.
Unsure of how long the legacy of the Golgion clan would last, Su Lun knew he had to brace himself.
Before Su Lun had any chance to catch his breath, the opposite Augustus raised his staff, and instantly a bolt of lightning shot from his right-hand wand.
With a "crack," faster than thunder, the lightning bolt had already struck where Su Lun was standing.
The afterimage dissipated, and tens of meters away, Su Lun looked at the spot where he had just stood, still glowing with residual lightning, and murmured, "Instant-cast seventh-level arcane magic, so this is the strength of a seasoned Grand Magician..."
And at the same moment he attacked, the Gorgons in the forest also launched a full assault, a tidal wave of Poison Snakes crazily flooded into the temple, quickly burying the fighting Chians in a mass of serpents.
Several high-ranking Gorgons with human upper bodies and serpentine lower halves also appeared in view.
Su Lun dared not take any chances, clenching his sorcerer's seals, a giant crucifix swiftly appeared in the sky.
He swung his black scythe, and with a space-tearing slash, the surrounding Sea of Snakes was instantly cut into several bloody sections as if slicing through a cake.
However, in the next second, the severed tide of snakes was covered by even more Poison Snakes pouring in.
In that instant, though, Su Lun had already summoned hundreds of gargoyle guards to his side.
This three-hundred-strong gargoyle legion appeared and immediately blocked another sudden release of Mystic Arts magic.
Seeing this, Augustus's face darkened significantly, muttering to himself, "Puppets, huh..."
He had heard reports from the legion sub-commanders earlier, that a ten-thousand-strong puppet legion had crushed their ten-thousand-strong magic legion. He found it hard to believe, suspecting whether it was an advanced Illusion Technique or some other special methods that had confused everyone's senses.
However, looking at the puppet army that had suddenly blotted out the sky, Augustus's expression was also very solemn.
"Ten thousand puppets, how did this guy manage to control them so freely?"
...
Su Lun didn't give his enemies any time to be surprised; in the puppet theater, he was the master of everything!
The moment the gargoyle legion spread out, they had already formed into a battle formation.
When the gigantic Nonagram Alchemy Formation began to light up, the energy fluctuations grew more and more terrifying, "Mystic Arts: Subsonic Oscillation!"
Augustus, seeing the scale of the spell's deployment, comparable to that of a ten-thousand-person magician group casting a spell, dared not to be the slightest bit careless. With a gesture, he thickened the magic shield around his body by another layer. At the same time, he recited incantations, already conjuring countermagic.
In the next instant, the sky exploded with the activation of the Nonagram Alchemy Formation, a "boom" like the eruption of a volcano thundering through the heavens.
Augustus instantly understood something, his brows tightly furrowed, "A sonic spell?!"
But it was too late to stop it.
The moment after the explosion sounded, if one looked down from the sky, they would immediately see shockwaves rapidly spreading ripples over the forest around the center point of the Gole Work Temple on the island of Cocorosi.
The spell's might was not great; the shockwaves didn't even break the trees.
However, after the sound wave persisted for a few seconds, a bizarre scene unfolded.
The countless Poison Snakes from the "Sea of Snakes Calamity" were surging toward the temple, but as the wave of sound swept over the tide of snakes, the ones closest to the temple began to tremble strangely. Upon closer look, each snake was trembling so intensely that they appeared to have multiple shadows.
However, the phenomenon didn't last long, and suddenly there was a "crackling" sound, like firecrackers exploding; the trembling Poison Snakes burst into a cloud of blood mist in an instant.
This strange explosion continued to spread, swiftly clearing out a large number of Poison Snakes, staining the sky red with the resulting blood mist.
[Subsonic Oscillation]was aimed specifically at a massive number of lower-tier monsters!
Even if it didn't kill them, it would severely damage their internal organs.
Thousands of Sword Qi were sharp, but each strike could only kill a few hundred to a thousand Poison Snakes. However, the sonic spell released by the puppet army killed tens to hundreds of thousands of lower-tier Poison Snakes in one fell swoop!
In just this instant, the sky lit up once more as the gargoyle legion's second Nonagram Formation came into action.
The endless Sea of Snakes Calamity, though ferocious, might not be able to withstand such attrition.
...
Realizing this, Augustus could not help but feel surprised, "These puppets actually serve the purpose of magic towers!"
At this moment, he finally understood why a ten-thousand-strong puppet army could easily defeat a ten-thousand-person magician group.
These puppets seemed to be just that, puppets, but they were also like miniature magic towers.
Gathering magic power, solidifying spells, enhancing the might of spell techniques... These abilities that magic towers possessed were also present in the puppets.
Even though the puppets' functions were far from matching those of magic towers, they were smaller and more convenient.
The key was the number of ten thousand, capable of perfectly coordinating as a battle formation, which was simply impregnable!
"What exquisite puppet legions..."
Seeing this, Augustus couldn't help but marvel at the ingenious design of the puppet army before him.
But such a feat could not be replicated by just anyone else.
Not to mention that in the realm of the gods, no Puppet Master was known to control ten thousand puppets.
Even if there were, where would they find so many divine-grade materials that could bear such effects?
"It's actually Living Silver! Where did these aborigines find so much Living Silver?"
Augustus's complexion darkened at the sight.
Even in the realm of the gods, it was an extremely rare magical material.
In this moment, he was once again astonished by the "brazenness" of these alchemical aborigines.
Even a mighty eighth-tier Grand Arcanist accustomed to grand scenes felt like a country bumpkin from the backwoods.
Members of this "Dawn Organization" casually handled artifacts of divine-grade, divine materials, mythical talents... Damn it, they really boggle the mind!
...
The gargoyle legion released the first round of spells, and Augustus also reacted, the vertical pupil on his forehead suddenly blazing with light, and a beam shot towards them.
Su Lun was well-prepared and easily teleported to evade it.
The blue beam from the [All-Encompassing True Solution] then hit the bodies of several gargoyles beside him.
The spatial black holes of the gargoyles, which could absorb various kinds of spells, suddenly ceased to function under this beam.
Instead, the moment the light entered the black holes, everything around started to disintegrate.
Not only the spells, but also the gargoyles themselves, were broken down into granular form.
However, in the blink of an eye, the seven or eight gargoyles that were hit by the blue light were disassembled, dissolving into fine metallic particles.
Seeing that he didn't hit Su Lun, Augustus did not continue to release the beam.
However, activated silver itself has an extremely strong memory feature, and the disassembled pools of liquid metal quickly reverted to their original shape.
But the inscribed runes, energy cores, solidified spells, and the like had been irreversibly dismantled, leaving only the material itself.
Seeing this, Su Lun felt not a twinge of heartache, but actually rejoiced.
As long as the materials remained, the loss wasn't significant.
The [All-Encompassing True Solution] was said to be capable of dismantling all matter, but only if it was within the comprehension of the caster.
It seemed Augustus, this eighth-level Grand Magician, was unable to dismantle divine-grade materials like activated silver, only destroying the gargoyle's structure.
Even if he were able, the casting itself required a tremendous amount of magic power.
These ten thousand puppets...
If he were left to disassemble them, he wouldn't have the time to do so, nor would he dare!
After all, Su Lun certainly wouldn't just watch his enemy destroy his puppets!
It was in the very moment that the blue light flashed, with a swift teleport, he appeared right behind Augustus.
A rune umbrella wrapped in Death God's Fire struck lightning-fast at the opponent's magic shield.
With a 'bang,' the figure shattered, leaving behind only a tattered magic scroll.
Su Lun knew without looking that the true body had fled.
Having exposed the Death God's Fire when he gravely wounded Saint Frank previously, it was expected that the enemy would be on their guard.
And since Augustus was a seasoned eighth-level Grand Magician, Su Lun knew his odds of a successful sneak attack were slim to begin with, and even slimmer now.
But, at this critical juncture, the one in a hurry wasn't Su Lun.
It was the enemy.
Now that six ten-thousand-member spell formations had crushed four and the other two were under fierce attack by the Dawn Brigade, the situation was very favorable.
Su Lun just had to hold out until Queen Medusa successfully completed her inheritance, and the situation would immediately take a turn for the better.
If the enemy wanted to drag things out, he wouldn't chase after them.
He just needed to defend the temple.
The gargoyle legion, standing in the void, coalesced the second round of legion spells; another wave of sound exploded, and tens of thousands of Poison Snakes burst into blood mist.
As for those high-ranking Poison Snakes not affected by the sonic waves, crosses in the sky quietly descended with strands of transparent threads...
Physical control over nerves takes precedence over mental control, and now with Su Lun's greatly enhanced spiritual power, the number of Poison Snakes he could manipulate was terrifying.
In the Puppet Theater, the number of enemies wasn't necessarily advantageous.
After all, the temple could only be attacked within a certain range, and just as he had against the undead legion, once he gained control over some of the Poison Snakes, the tide of the snake onslaught temporarily abated.
Furthermore, Su Lun noticed that the low-ranking Poison Snakes seemed very wary of the temple and stopped at the edge of the black water pond.
Seeing this, he was even less worried.
...
The two sides were locked in fierce battle.
Su Lun marveled at how absurdly strong Augustus truly was.
With the "Shield of Innocence" in hand, other than Death God's Fire, Su Lun could hardly threaten this man with any of his means.
The more Su Lun fought, the more he wondered how Mr. Hei had managed to hold on for so long against this guy before.
S-009: Omniscient Solution was said to be all-knowing and almighty; a gifted one would naturally possess extensive knowledge. Augustus had almost mastered all magic under the ninth rank. Because of this, the man's combat style was dazzling to the point of confusion, casually brandishing Mystic Arts—even occasionally releasing forbidden-level spells...
Su Lun himself was several times pushed to the brink during the fight.
Fortunately, Su Lun's own means of survival were not weak, and with the cooperation of Qian, they could barely stall for time.
He also had an ace up his sleeve that he had not yet revealed, thinking about finding a good opportunity to completely eliminate the enemy.
Suddenly, he realized something was wrong: The enemy didn't seem as anxious as he had imagined?
"No! What else is he waiting for?!"
Su Lun's heart chilled, his mind rapidly processing the tens of thousands of pieces of information he had harvested but not yet digested.
His thoughts whirled at breakneck speed, and only after a while did he find a crucial clue among the jumbled information: "There is still a force of the Sacred Army's ascetics that weren't part of the landing troops!"
The magic legion also had a strict hierarchy of authority, and not everyone was privy to the full plan to surround and kill Queen Medusa. From the information Su Lun had previously acquired, almost everyone had subconsciously overlooked the existence of that group of five hundred Sacred Army ascetics.
But it was this oversight that was most crucial.
Given that the enemy knew Su Lun had the capability to severely damage Saint Frank, they would certainly be prepared for him to target the legion commander Augustus. Therefore, they must have a backup plan.
And the ascetics were among those closest to the divine, one of the groups of believers. The absence of those five hundred from the battlefield likely meant they were the backup plan.
Realizing this, Su Lun felt somewhat helpless.
After all, it was a battle for position, and even if he knew the enemy had schemes, he had to withstand it.
He could only inform the members of the Dawn group to be cautious.
...
Augustus, who was at a distance, watched as Su Lun's fighting style suddenly changed and sneered, "Hehe, have you just noticed? Too late."
Hadn't he seen Su Lun trying to stall for time?
And wasn't he also stalling?
Rather than risk a decisive outcome, it was better to wait for an absolutely sure method!
After all... the Titan gods who had fought in these seas were the supreme deities of their heavenly plane!
Just then, a long, drawn-out charge of a horn suddenly reverberated through the sky.
"Woo woo woo..."
This low and distant sound seemed to possess a magic power that made people's blood surge with excitement.
Su Lun furrowed his brows when he heard this sound.
He thought it was some sort of sonic attack, but upon careful discernment, he realized it was not.
"War horns? Charge?"
Su Lun was filled with confusion, not believing this to be a charge by the remaining two ten-thousand-strong magic formations.
As the sound of the horn became more and more distinct, a projection suddenly appeared in the sky.
Su Lun looked up, his eyelid twitching violently: "Another Artifact Projection?"
Galal's Horn of Doom (Artifact Projection)
Detailed explanation: A Divine Artifact made from a Titan god-demon's horn, capable of summoning the spirits of Titan warriors to charge; it has a bloodline suppression effect on creatures with Titan ancestry, and when Divine Power blows the horn, it compels all Titan descendants not exceeding demigods within range to join the battle of apocalypse;
Upon seeing the information from the identification, he instantly understood what the enemy was planning.
Almost at the same moment that the horn's phantom appeared, the seas near the island of Kokoros seemed to boil, the ground shook, and it appeared as if numerous enormous creatures were awakened from the depths.
What troubled Su Lun more was that the Hell Volcano in the distance erupted once again, and powerful auras surged forth!

chapters.title: Chapter 581 - 580: The Spoils of a Formidable Enemy
chapters.content:
Su Lun listened to the horn sound that seemed to pierce through a person's soul, his expression turning visibly grim as he murmured, "This is troublesome."
Having harvested too many fragments of mage memories, these characters from the Divine Plane now were essentially an "open book" for Su Lun, so he had speculated on his chances of victory before the battle.
He deduced that the enemy's final trump card was nothing more than summoning Divine Power.
He briefly assessed the situation, and concluded that the Dawn Group still had a fighting chance.
After all, it was the fragmented Alchemy Plane, and an eighth-tier great magic conductor could carry the divine will of a god, which probably wouldn't be extremely formidable. Winning might not be certain, but it seemed manageable to stall them.
However, the current situation with this "Galar's Horn of Apocalypse" was unexpected.
This Divine Artifact Projection was a "secret weapon," one unknown even to the division leaders of the mages.
Moreover, the complication was that it was a summoning-type Divine Artifact.
Out of the corner of his eye, Su Lun observed the surroundings, and his thoughts also touched on some other crucial information, "These guys can actually summon Titan spirits... It seems that the Titans from that battle years ago have a significant connection with the Divine Plane."
Being proficient in various Necromantic Spell Formulas himself, he knew that summoning the protection of departed spirits usually required not only related items but also sufficient devotion or perhaps some bloodline descendants. Otherwise, they couldn't possibly summon spirits or monsters of high orders.
But thinking about this now seemed somewhat pointless.
...
Right at the moment when the horn sounded, the surrounding sea began to tumult immediately.
Tanni had detected something unusual ahead of time; a warning came over the communicator, "Mr. Su Lun, there's trouble, the fish in the sea report that many terrifying deep-sea monsters have appeared. Be careful on your side; they seem to be heading towards Cocoa Lox Island!"
Levitating mid-air, Su Lun looked afar and saw the giant creatures emerging from the sea, his scalp numb.
Titan Nine-Headed Eels, Titan Armored King Crabs, Titan Man-Footed Snakes, Leviathan Sea Monsters...
Almost every creature with Titan's bloodline had been awakened by that horn. These sovereign behemoths, usually hidden in the deep sea, were now driven by a mysterious force, surging towards Cocoa Lox Island.
And it wasn't just these sea monsters; the distant Hell Volcano also roared and burst, spewing dense gases of hell.
The sound of the horn seemed to pierce through the planar rift, summoning all the necrotic spirits from below.
Dark clouds spread across the sky like the end of times, accompanied by thunder and lightning.
Looking further, one could see figures as tall as hundred meters, giant spectral monsters, emerging from the volcano.
"Titan spirits..."
Seeing this, Su Lun's eyes were filled with solemnity.
He decisively responded through the communicator, "Implement Plan C! Be extra careful, avoid the core battlefield, and try to constrain them with firepower from the periphery!"
"Yes!"
The reply came through the communicator.
There wasn't much to worry about with the Evernight ship.
The Titan monsters were summoned by the horn for battle, seemingly directed only towards Golar Temple. With Old Sword God Bartolo and the Dawn Group's high combatants, the effect of containment on the periphery would even be better.
But the situation on Su Lun's side looked very grim.
He glanced at the temple, which was still unresponsive, and muttered in his heart, "Your Highness, I can only try my best to buy you time..."
The moment he identified the properties of the Artifact Projection, he had already concluded that it was not a scenario where he could match strength.
Even though he had a profound alliance with Queen Medusa.
The current situation was simply not something a mere Dawn Group could withstand.
All Su Lun could do was to help her delay for a while.
...
Clearly, the enemy had perceived Su Lun's intention to retreat.
But since they had already played their trump card, they had no intention of letting Su Lun go.
In Augustus' eyes, this group called Dawn, was even a greater threat than Medusa!
It was just when Su Lun was communicating with the Evernight ship, suddenly a crow in the sky "cawed" loudly.
He instantly knew that a crisis was upon him.
On the battlefield, it was either kill or be killed; Su Lun was not surprised that his enemies had the intent to kill. His gaze fixed on a white-bearded grand magic conductor nearby, his heart hardened, "Since the problem cannot be solved, then let's resolve the person who caused the problem first!"
Currently, he simply couldn't stop those Titan creatures from attacking.
Thus, the only thing he could do, and possibly effective, was to kill this supreme commander!
In the face of lethal danger, Su Lun still resolutely chose to teleport towards Augustus.
This time, he had to gamble!
Only if the opponent truly harbored the intent to kill, would he have the chance to get close.
Sure enough, seeing Su Lun teleport again, a triumphant gleam flashed through Augustus' eyes from afar, deliberately exposing a flaw, just waiting for him to teleport in!
In that lightning-fast moment, Su Lun's figure dissipated on the spot.
With a flicker of spatial fluctuation, he had already appeared behind Augustus, his black umbrella aimed at his back, enveloped in phosphorescent flame.
However, at the very same instant, the grand magic conductor crushed a magic scroll hidden within his robe, and a burst of spatial fluctuation surged as well.
As Su Lun poised his umbrella, he saw a figure with beautiful features but horrific snake hair emerge from the spatial rift in front of him!
And in this snake-haired gorgon's head not only was the soul fluctuation extremely strong, but among her snake locks, there were also two golden ones.
Seeing this figure, Su Lun not only showed no surprise but his expression grew more stern: "Finally showing yourself!"
