Staking his fate on the challenge, Su Lun's expression was solemn, "Please enlighten me, senior."
The giant did not waste words; at this moment, he turned his body backward, his long, pole-like arm reaching out behind him to the bookshelf, flipping out a parchment bag and a stone tablet book.
He brought out the strap, placed it on the stand, then reached in and pulled out a dark fruit, asking, "The first question tests your erudition; do you know what this is?"
Su Lun looked at the item, maintaining his expression, but inside, he found it peculiar: wasn't this a giveaway question?
The identification displayed it was "a rotten Aphrodite's golden apple."
To the average person, this might only be something heard in fragments from books, and even if they saw the actual object, they might not recognize it.
But Su Lun had the All-knowing Eye, which made this no challenge at all.
The giant, hearing the correct answer, smiled and then procured a colorful stone.
Su Lun answered again, "This is a 'solar meteorite.'"
If it were merely identifying objects, he felt this test was being handed to him on a silver platter, given his talents.
However, after asking twice, the giant seemed to have realized something as well, laughing, "There were a few more questions. But since you have the 'Eye of Truth,' there's no need to continue asking."
"..."
Su Lun did not deny this.
He suspected that his "S-018 All-knowing Eye" was directly related to the mythological "Spring of Wisdom," and it was not surprising that the giant could see this.
The giant did not seem to think this broke the rules and still looked kindly as he flipped through the stone book, then said, "Now comes the true test of wisdom."
Su Lun looked on attentively.
The giant started, "It has three forms, gentle as caressing the skin, soft as embracing the sky, hard enough to split rocks. Please, what is it?"
As there was no time limit for answering, Su Lun took a good while to think, wracking his brain with all the knowledge he had. Then he cautiously answered, "Water."
He felt there was nothing wrong with his answer.
The giant did not clarify right or wrong and continued, "What can devour stones, level mountains, corrode metal, push apart clouds, and make the young grow old?"
After thinking it over, Su Lun answered again, "Time."
Thus, the two of them alternated between question and answer, continuing for several questions until the giant finally stopped and fell silent.
After no one spoke, Su Lun felt somewhat uneasy.
Had he answered the question correctly, or not?
Reflecting on his own answer, he felt that if not correct, it was at least not wrong.
Thinking it over, Su Lun decided to ask, "Senior, did I answer the question correctly just then?"
Unexpectedly, the old giant shook his head and said, "I do not know, because I am not an all-knowing deity, nor can I provide a precise answer. Your answer needs to be recognized by this 'Book of Trials.'
Su Lun listened, slightly surprised. Was there really no answer?
Seeing his puzzled expression, the old giant added, "The questions just now tested your understanding of the world, and were not meant to have a singular answer. If you look carefully, you will find there are definitely more than one thing in the world that fits the answer to the riddle. In fact, there are many... many..."
"..."
Su Lun felt puzzled; if there were no precise answers, how could one pass?
He vaguely felt that there was another layer of meaning to this test.
However, the next question proved difficult for him.
At this moment, the old giant spoke again, "This is the last question."
With that, he pointed to the oil lamp in front of him and asked, "What do you see?"
"..."
With furrowed brows, Su Lun saw "an ordinary whale oil lamp."
No matter how he looked at it, it was still an oil lamp.
Recalling what the old giant had said earlier, he immediately realized that this was not a question of perception, but one of philosophy.
He had already been given hints.
No, to be precise... those previous questions had subtly suggested directions for the answers.
The answer was not fixed; it depended on your understanding of the world.
What you see, what you understand, that is your answer.
No matter what the truth of the world is, the world in your eyes is what you believe to be real.
This was an open-ended question with no precise or singular answer!
The room was dim and unlit; only that one oil lamp illuminated the corner, helping him to see the items bathed in its light.
His eyes caught sight of stone scriptures, a table, people, shadows, wisps of blue smoke...
Seeing this, Su Lun fell into prolonged contemplation.
The old giant did not interrupt; he casually flipped through a stone book, seemingly in no rush to get an answer.
Su Lun understood the critical importance of the last question.
So, he too furrowed his brows in deep thought, numerous potential answers came to mind, but something seemed off about all of them.
This cautious approach, however, made his thoughts increasingly chaotic.
"No... the answer must be in what I've seen..."
Su Lun stripped away all emotion, his expression becoming cold and numb, as if the world he saw through his eyes also turned cold.
Seeing him like this, the old giant glanced sideways as if he had thought of something.
Suddenly, a flash of insight struck Su Lun.
Beyond the light, there is more darkness, and everything hidden in that darkness!
Because it hasn't been seen doesn't mean it doesn't exist.
It's just that one's own cognition hadn't perceived the presence of that darkness.
Finally, after a quarter of an hour of thinking, Su Lun spoke, "The truth lies behind the appearances."
The old giant looked over.
Su Lun continued, "We are originally living in darkness. In our quest for the truth, to see the world clearly, we lit candles, chasing after the light. But the more we fixate on light, the more we only see brightness, forgetting that we are still in darkness. As a result, we lose ourselves in the light…"
As he spoke, the old giant's expression gradually broke into a smile.
And miraculously, as if Su Lun's answer had been acknowledged by some mysterious cosmic force, the stone scripture suddenly burst into brilliant light.
Seeing this, the old giant smiled and said, "If you had not realized this point, even if the 'truth' were in front of you, you would not be able to see it."
After a pause, he solemnly added, "Congratulations, you have earned the qualification to glimpse the truth."
Listening to this, Su Lun was still emerging from his state of utmost calm contemplation, his expression neither happy nor sad.
But it seemed as though a thought in his heart had suddenly become clear.
This "Test of Wisdom" was a test, but also a guide.
A guide to help one glimpse the true nature of reality!

chapters.title: Chapter 589 - 588: Sacrificing the Right Eye for the Spring Water
chapters.content:
PS. Got held up with something, so this update's a bit brief, content as per the title.
"I passed?"
Su Lun snapped out of his emotionally detached, indifferent state and finally felt the joy of having passed the challenge.
The old giant Morey across from him smiled and said, "Yes, you now have the qualifications to glimpse the truth."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun thought back to the questions from the earlier test and realized that the Cyclops tribe, guarding the Spring of Wisdom, had set challenges not to obstruct people from obtaining the water, but rather to guide those who came to understand what "wisdom" truly is.
At that moment, old giant Morey spoke again, "For ordinary people, the Spring of Wisdom is but a slightly sweet and tasty spring water. Only in the mouth of a truly wise person does it taste of all the wisdom in the world."
"Hmm."
By now, Su Lun had come to understand the meaning behind these words.
Just like the Power of Laws is omnipresent, but if you are not aware of its existence, then in your world, it does not exist.
Old giant Morey smiled meaningfully once more and said, "Congratulations, you are the second adventurer to complete the challenges of courage and wisdom in ten thousand years. The spring water is atop the Spring of Wisdom Peak, at the center of Giant Island. You may take what you need now. Of course, if you bring some human wine, the elder guarding the spring might not be so troublesome..."
Su Lun nodded, respectfully saying, "Thank you for your guidance, senior."
...
Su Lun stepped out the door, his mind still pondering the questions from before.
Even though he had passed the test, those questions still seemed endlessly fascinating upon reflection.
The two challenges were a form of gain in themselves, as if his thinking had been enlightened, and a new world had suddenly opened up before him.
As Su Lun left the Clan Leader's house, the Cyclops in the village now looked at him with an even more solemn expression in their single, large eyes.
Only an outsider could see the milky white halo shining around Su Lun's body; it was the light of an uplifted soul. The definition of a higher being lay not only in bloodline inheritance but also in the cognitive realm of the soul.
Su Lun himself was completely unaware, his thoughts whirling.
He nodded to the group of giants who cast friendly looks at him and made his way along the path behind the village toward the peak in the center of the island.
He glanced back and saw Mr. Hei and the Cyclops' battle on the beach outside the village still locked in fierce combat, with no sign of either gaining the upper hand.
Su Lun didn't look any further and step by step walked into the forest.
For some reason, everything on Giant Island was very large.
Flowers several meters tall, trees a hundred meters tall, beetles as big as elephants...
Every living creature seemed remarkably large.
The sheep's path that was meant for giants became a wide thoroughfare where several carriages could travel side by side for Su Lun, a human.
He walked on, while crows shared his aerial view high in the sky.
After flying high enough, Su Lun suddenly let out a soft exclamation, "Eh... could this island be the skull of some ancient creature?"
Only then did he realize that Giant Island, which looked like a horseshoe on the sea chart, resembled an incredible giant skull even more.
The lower jaw of the skull lay beneath the surface of the sea, with only the upper eye sockets and the upper part of the cranium visible, looking like a horseshoe.
Su Lun found it somewhat unbelievable.
But in the waters of Dragon Country, it seemed like nothing was impossible.
His thoughts shifted, and he had already walked through the primeval forest. Giant Island was not without danger—this vast forest was home to some magical beasts that the Cyclops tribe would consider "snack food."
Apparently considering the flesh of this human not enough to even stick between their teeth, those massive creatures, although occasionally curious, did not come to prey on him.
Su Lun continued up the mountain road to the not-too-high main peak.
From a distance, he sensed two strong soul fluctuations.
"These two Cyclops guarding the spring are quite powerful..."
Su Lun discerned the soul fluctuations, and found that these two souls hidden in the mountains were even stronger than Clan Leader Morey whom he had previously encountered.
Fortunately, they were not enemies, so he walked straight over and said loudly, "Esteemed predecessors of the Giant tribe, my name is Su Lun, guided here by Clan Leader Morey to seek the Spring of Wisdom."
Upon hearing this, two heads suddenly popped out from the side of the mountain, cluttered with big yellow teeth as thick as ivory.
Seeing Su Lun, they immediately started to clamor.
"Oh, it's been many years since a human has been able to come here."
"Yes, Godo, a thousand years."
"Hey, human, have you brought any fine liquor? If not, we will not let you obtain the spring water."
"Right, we won't let you have it."
"..."
Su Lun listened, his expression slightly amused and strange.
Compared to other giants, these two didn't seem very bright.
Liquor was not usually something people carried with them to occupy storage space. Fortunately, Su Lun had a small void realm, not only stocked with ample fine liquors but even a brewery.
Su Lun hadn't forgotten the reminder from Clan Leader Morey earlier, and he took out dozens of wooden barrels and placed them on the ground, saying, "Of course."
The two Cyclops came over, picked up the hundred-pound barrels of rum, and gurgled them down their throats.
This was "Gold Rum," which in terms of taste and brewing technique, was already considered top-notch liquor on the market.
However, after drinking more than a dozen barrels in one gulp, the giants muttered unsatisfied, "Oh, human, this liquor of yours is too lousy. It even makes me think the fruit wine brewed by the monkeys in the forest tastes better."
The other one followed with the critique, "Yes, I remember the last human brought a very delicious drink. Oh, how I miss that flavor~"
Su Lun watched with a full face of speechless lines.
He watched helplessly as the two giants kept saying how terrible it was while gulping down dozens of barrels of Gold Rum.
Seeing the look they cast over, Su Lun brought out dozens of tons of various fine liquors from his small void realm.
Yet, as he brought them out, the two giants kept guzzling them down.
They kept complaining about the taste, saying this and that liquor was no good.
No matter how precious some liquors were, they weren't worth much, so Su Lun didn't feel too distressed.
But seeing that the giants hadn't mentioned letting him fetch the water, he started to ponder.
In a short span, these two had already drunk several thousand pounds of fine liquor, and judging from their manner, they would probably just keep on drinking no matter how much more was offered.
Moreover, the two giants had given a key hint: the drink brought by the last human.
"Could Sir Isaac have given them 'Poetic Honey Wine'?" Su Lun suddenly thought of something.
Sir Isaac was the one who had negotiated an alliance with the Dalu tribe, and he had been to the Emerald Holy Land, so having 'Poetic Honey Wine' was reasonable.
Su Lun did have some in his possession, but it was a rare spirit that could provide instant enlightenment.
Pouring it down like this truly pained his heart.
However, these two giants were such picky drinkers that no ordinary fine liquor would probably satisfy them now.
Considering the Spring of Wisdom, Su Lun still took out two large jars, each containing several hundred pounds of 'Poetic Honey Wine'.
Yet, as soon as he took out the jars, the two giants immediately smelled the aroma and their expressions brightened instantly.
Without any nitpicking or complaints, each giant grabbed a jar, guzzled down a big gulp, and then revealed a look of immense satisfaction.
"Yes, that's the flavor!"
"Oh my god, I never thought I'd get to taste this exquisite wine again!"
As Su Lun watched the several hundred jin of the precious Poet's Honey Wine pour down, he couldn't help but feel a twinge of pain, despite its inestimable value.
Fortunately, Yuta is now the Great Druid of the Dalu Tribe; getting a refill on my next visit shouldn't be a problem.
And just after those two gulps, a drunken blush appeared on the faces of the two giants who had just gulped down hundreds of tons of wine.
Burping drunkenly, their eyes gradually became hazy, and they mumbled, "Oh, the taste of this wine is so delightful... There are so many sheep floating in the sky... The Spring of Wisdom demands a sacrifice..."
Before they could finish their rambling, the two giants collapsed to the ground, snoring loudly.
Su Lun's eye twitched as he saw this: Asleep?
Ordinary people would get drunk off just a little Poet's Honey Wine, so it was only natural that each giant got drunk after downing several hundred jin.
But it seems we can pass now?
Still, Su Lun asked, "Excuse me, gentlemen giants, may I go fetch the spring water now?"
The two giants could no longer open their eyes, but one of them seemed to grunt an affirmative "Hmm."
Listening to this, Su Lun let out a sigh of relief.
Expending a bit of spare wine to avoid trouble at the last hurdle seemed worth it after all.
He stepped past the two giants and made his way toward the mountain peak.
...
Before long, he heard the sound of a gentle stream.
Walking over, Su Lun discovered a small pool with a diameter of only a few meters.
"Is this the 'Mimir's Spring'?"
If the information identified wasn't convincing, he would have found it hard to believe that such an unassuming little pool was the fabled Spring of Wisdom.
However, as Su Lun approached, he realized the extraordinary nature of this spring.
The seemingly small pool was endlessly clear and, to the naked eye, seemed bottomless.
The sight felt like staring into an infinite starry sky, inducing a dizzying sensation that threatened to draw one's gaze inward.
The bottom of the spring seemed to connect the entire world.
Su Lun did not hurry to fetch the water.
Because the spring water required a sacrifice.
The old Clan Leader Morey had hinted at this: To ordinary people, the Spring of Wisdom is nothing more than sweet and refreshing water. Only in the mouth of one who truly possesses wisdom does it taste of the world's collective knowledge.
Something occurred to Su Lun, and he pulled out a tarot card.
It was one of the twenty-two secret Taro cards he had obtained, the "Cyclops Hanged Man Card."
The hidden message on the card was a rite of sacrifice: 'I offered my own right eye and hung myself upside down from a leafless tree for nine whole days and nights. Pierced by a spear on one side, I was buffeted by cold and hot winds alike, swinging in the air without food or water. It was a sacrifice I made to myself. And then... the secrets of the whole world unfolded before me.'
Clearly, the Great Alchemist who had made this tarot card knew all the secrets of 'Mimir's Spring.'
It was a detailed sacrificial rite, one that the Cyclops themselves might not be fully aware of despite their alchemical system.
Su Lun had long since memorized the sacrificial process by heart.
But seeing the 'treasure' hidden on the tarot card for countless years now before him brought a different kind of feeling.
"It seems that even if this tarot card wasn't made by one of the five elders of the Dawn Twilight Cross Society, it was crafted by a high-ranking divine alchemist..."
Su Lun gave the card one last look, then began setting up a Nonagram Alchemy Formation at the edge of the spring.
With preparations in place, the formation was quickly completed.
He stood at the center of the Alchemy Formation, exhaling a breath of murky air before reaching towards his own eyes.
To others, the act of sacrificing an eye might have warranted some hesitation.
But to Su Lun, it was all too familiar.
In that instant, he felt as though he had returned to the first day he crossed into this world—when he had sacrificed his eye in the cellar of the Storm Manor to obtain the "S-018 All-knowing Eye."
How striking the resemblance.
Su Lun did not hesitate; his fingers formed sorcerer's seals, and his mouth recited that universal chant used by alchemists in critical moments, "In adherence to the principle of equivalent exchange, I praise the glory of the original creator, and witness the miracle of creation through Alchemy..."
No sooner had the words left his mouth than the Nonagram Alchemy Formation lit up with a dazzling light.
Su Lun applied a slight force with his fingers, and his right eye was detached.
The piercing pain of having lost the sense of touch did not affect his thoughts in the slightest.
Blood flowed down his cheek, yet he expressionlessly placed his eye in the Alchemy Formation.
In an instant, the sacrificed eye seemed to have formed a contract with the heavens and the earth.
Su Lun felt as though the colors he could see had suddenly become richer.
Now when he looked at that clear spring water, it seemed to contain all the splendid colors of the world.
It was as if the rainbow had transformed into a spring, vibrant with colors.
Moments later, a strand of colorful spring water drifted out of the pool, landing before him.
Su Lun opened his mouth and swallowed it in one gulp, feeling as though he had tasted every flavor in the world at that moment—sour, sweet, bitter, spicy, sorrow, joy, sentimentality, fear, anger...
It was as though he had experienced all the flavors of human life in an instant.
Suddenly, Su Lun felt his mind flooded with myriad things.
Some he understood and treasured as if gaining life experience,
while others were lofty like the flowing sands, slipping through his grasp when he tried to hold on.
The world before his eyes began to resemble an abstract painting, where flowers, grass, and trees were all distorted and gradually turned into twisted symbols in his vision.
"The physical manifestation of Laws! Is this... the fabled original runes of the Runes?"
Su Lun was startled, and as he looked more closely, he was shocked to find that he was seeing the cosmic fundamental runes manifested by the natural world!
Had he not seen those stone tablets at Clan Leader Morey's place, he wouldn't have had such an acute awareness at this moment.
He was well aware that he had entered a state of profound and mystical enlightenment.
Looking at the panel, his status now included a condition called "Great Enlightenment of Wisdom."
This was the temporary boon brought by drinking from the "Spring of Wisdom," a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity!
Su Lun knew he mustn't let this chance slip by. Without a second thought, he drank a big gulp of "Poet's Honey Wine," then hung himself upside down with a string from a bare tree next to the spring.
The moment he was inverted, the "Runes" in his eyes immediately became clear!
Su Lun fell into a state similar to drunkenness.
The Poet's Honey Wine enhanced his moment of enlightenment in understanding texts, while the "Imitated Original Runes" he had previously advanced to the fourth stage now allowed him to clearly comprehend those symbols.
One by one, the runes fell like leaves from the sky, and Su Lun's All-knowing Eye shone with an otherworldly light at this moment.
A spear pierced his body, blood flowed into the sacrificial formation, maintaining the ritual of sacrifice.
Suspended in mid-air, Su Lun looked on coldly at the entirety of time.
And so he hung, for nine days and nine nights.

chapters.title: Chapter 590 - 589: Second Explanation [All-knowing Eye]
chapters.content:
This day,
beside the Spring of Mimir, Su Lun was hanging upside down on a withered tree, swaying with the wind.
His body, pierced by spears, was riddled with holes, and the blood that flowed within the alchemy formation had congealed into black clots.
For nine days, not a drop of water nor any food had touched his lips, and he hung from the branches like a pale corpse.
Yet it was this very act of sacrificing himself that immersed Su Lun in an extraordinary state.
As if through the alchemic formation's sacrificial process, he briefly merged his consciousness with the entire world.
In those eyes that had not closed for nine days and nights, the secrets of the world manifested as falling runes,
Finally, the light from the sacrificial alchemical formation slowly faded, and the mystical state enhanced by the Spring of Wisdom gradually left his body.
Su Lun's consciousness slowly returned from that mysterious universe-traversing condition.
It was as if his soul had just returned to his body.
The confusion dispersed, his eyes clearing as if reflecting the spring beside him.
...
The thread loosened, and Su Lun slowly descended from the tree branch where he had been hanging upside down, the upside-down world before his eyes righting itself.
But it took him quite a while to recover from the dizziness caused by excessive blood loss.
Su Lun opened his eyes, focusing his gaze on an old man in a black robe who was meditating not far from him.
As he looked over, the old man also looked back with his wise, one-eyed gaze.
His thoughts froze for a moment before Su Lun remembered he knew this old man.
His expression, devoid of emotional fluctuation, almost reflexively asked, "Mr. Hei?"
Mr. Hei, as if understanding his state, a flicker of different light crossing his eyes, asked, "Su Lun, has your sacrificial ceremony concluded?"
"Sacrifice?"
Su Lun murmured to himself.
He glanced at his body and the nine-pointed star formation under his feet, and his brain finally realized what had happened.
So he had just completed a sacrifice?
Oh, to obtain wisdom from the Spring of Wisdom, I had sacrificed myself.
It seems like many days have passed.
After pondering for a moment, Su Lun finally recalled everything.
He had arrived at Giant Island, passed through the tests of courage and wisdom twice, and was given two barrels of ambrosial mead before he could retrieve the water.
Realizing this, Su Lun felt he should show a happy emotion. After all, he had attained the legendary Spring of Mimir.
But why were his emotions so calm?
Su Lun's thoughts uncontrollably explored this new depth.
At that moment, Mr. Hei certainly knew something and said to himself, "It seems you have gained a lot."
Su Lun looked over.
At that moment, Mr. Hei thought of something and reminded, "Su Lun, are your eyes all right?"
"Eyes?"
Su Lun then realized something, looking at his own hands, which seemed unchanged.
But across from him, Mr. Hei had covered one of his eyes with a black cloth.
Mr. Hei, also curious, asked, "Did you not sacrifice your own eyes?"
Su Lun recalled for a moment and said, "I sacrificed them."
He then realized where the problem lay.
Now, both of his eyes could still see, whereas Mr. Hei, who had undergone the same sacrificial ceremony, had lost one of his eyes.
Su Lun examined his own panel and finally discovered the issue.
The previously named "S-018-All-knowing Eye" was now labeled "S-018-Eye of Truth."
...
"Has my talent evolved?"
Su Lun suddenly understood.
Just as he had acquired this S-tier talent by sacrificing his left eye for the first time at the underground altar of the Storm Manor, now he had sacrificed his right eye and unlocked the second evolution of his talent.
But his eyes were still intact.
Su Lun felt he had grasped a new Pupil Skill ability.
Just then, a gigantic lizard crawled out from a rock in the distance, staring at the two of them.
Su Lun looked over, his eyes suddenly focusing sharply.
His gaze suddenly became devoid of any emotional fluctuation, as if a deity were watching the world with cold indifference.
In an instant, it was like opening a compressed file of vast information, as countless data burst into his field of view.
[Gigantic Poisonous Venom Lizard]
Grade: Fifth-order silver
Details: A terrestrial highly toxic lizard, 13.13 meters in length, weighing 566 kilograms, aged 16; bloodline composition, 94.3% armoured toxic lizard, 0.13% dragon, 0.07% titan, 4.7% hellish, 0.8% other; skilled in venomous bites, poison gas emission, biting and pouncing, maximum crawling speed 102/second, bite force of 7700 kilograms; possesses extremely strong olfactory nerves and thermosensitive vision, can detect the presence of living beings within a 9.5 km radius, excellent night vision; the venom can cause multiple fatal injuries including blood coagulation, muscle paralysis, and hypothermia; scale armor as strong as type VI metal; weaknesses include the anus, tongue, old injury on the hind legs, poor at turning; in heat, seeking a mate; toxin composition detailed below...Your brain couldn't bear any more information, you saw a blackout.
In an instant, Su Lun entered a mysterious state.
He felt as if the secrets of the world had opened up to him, and everything became incredibly clear.
He wanted to take this opportunity to clearly see the giant lizard, but just a second later, a flood of information surged into his mind.
It was information far beyond what his brain could handle, instantly overwhelming him and causing dizziness and blurred vision.
It was like when he was still at the second-order, and he forcibly absorbed a fifth-order memory fragment.
Su Lun staggered, slightly pained as he covered his eyes, nearly losing his balance.
At the same time, a sharp pain shot through his eyes, as if burnt by the sun from overuse.
The whole person was disoriented.
It felt as though a powerful spiritual spell had struck him, leaving him in a momentary trance.
Mr. Hei, not far away, witnessed this scene and swiftly cast a "Clarity Spell" by pinching a sorcerer's seal.
Su Lun instantly felt a cool sensation, which greatly alleviated the splitting headache.
...
"Huff...ah..."
"Huff...ah..."
Su Lun breathed heavily, his forehead now covered in cold sweat.
After a few moments, the double vision before his eyes slowly converged back together, his focus returning.
Yet, his vision was not clear but rather blurred, as if he had severe nearsightedness.
However, in this abnormal state, Su Lun was not alarmed but rather delighted.
He fully understood what had happened.
Previously, his All-knowing Eye could identify the details of things.
It was only seeing the "appearance" manifested by things out of time, but just now, he had seen the "truth" behind that appearance!
He had not only seen the detailed information about this giant lizard but had also perceived the object's past, present, and future.
The information he saw suddenly increased from 1% to 99%!
At that moment, in Su Lun's eyes, it seemed that there were no secrets left in this world.
These eyes made him feel as if he understood the entire world.
...
Mr. Hei, looking at Su Lun, faintly guessed something and asked, "Did you see information about high-order laws that you couldn't handle?"
Su Lun nodded, "Hmm."
The state of his mind, muddled like muddy water, even prevented him from explaining further.
In that instant, Su Lun felt as if he understood what the world looks like through the eyes of a deity.
Deities cannot look directly, cannot describe, cannot name, all because the amount of information is too vast, far exceeding the threshold that lower life forms can handle.
Just like what he had seen in that moment.
His eyes still ached faintly, but Su Lun was filled with anticipation.
With this ability, beneath the divine tier, there were no secrets left for him to uncover.
This meant... even advancing to the eighth or ninth order, the thresholds posed no secret for the "Eye of Truth."
With just one look, all mysteries were clearly laid out before his eyes.
The path of advancement was clear.
The "Spring of Wisdom" not only developed Su Lun's second interpretation of the All-knowing Eye but also bestowed upon him "wisdom." The runes offered during the ritual were like keys, unlocking the doors to treasure troves of knowledge.
Su Lun also knew why using the second interpretation of All-knowing Eye once was damaging; aside from the overwhelming amount of irrelevant information, essentially, his body couldn't handle it.
He muttered to himself, "The body is too weak. The brain can't handle such a vast amount of information, and the eyes can't yet bear peeking into the higher-level information of the world..."
This negative state would be much improved after he became proficient in the Pupil Skill.
As for those higher cognitive abilities, once he advanced to the eighth level and merged with the "Isaac Blasphemer," the problem would also be completely resolved.
Until that moment, Su Lun increasingly marveled at Sir Isaac's foresight.
Of the five alchemical manuscripts he had left behind, Su Lun now possessed four.
And the four types of enhancement recorded in the manuscripts were all aimed at secrets beyond the divine level.
"Isaac's Alchemical Heart," "Isaac's Giant Strength," "Isaac's Dragon Pattern Golden Body," "Isaac Blasphemer"...
The body bore beyond-tier laws, the brain bore high-tier cognition, and the Spiritual Power bore beyond-tier consumption.
Looking at it now, the design of these enhancements truly contained great wisdom.
Su Lun didn't think much.
Mr. Hei then said, "Do you know? Just now, you looked like a god who indifferently overlooks all lower beings."
Thinking over it, Su Lun asked, "I think my emotions are a bit off."
After drinking from the "Spring of Wisdom" and achieving an enhancement in wisdom, as well as unraveling the All-knowing Eye, this was originally a qualitative leap in strength, even comparable to advancing a great tier.
This should have been a joyous occasion.
Yet, there were no ripples in his heart.
Previously, he had to actively detach his emotions to enter such a state of absolute calm thinking.
Now it seemed he was always in this state.
As if nothing in the world could stir his emotions anymore.
Listening, Mr. Hei smiled and said, "That's a good thing."
Su Lun gave him a puzzled look, "???"
Mr. Hei explained, "Knowledge is heavy, and as you gradually understand this world, you will gradually lose emotional fluctuations and look at everything indifferently. This is why in many ancient texts, the great sages spoke of gods viewing all beings as ants. I didn't quite understand before, but now... I think I get some of it."
As he spoke, he looked at Su Lun again. "It seems you understand it more thoroughly than I do."
Su Lun instantly understood too.
It was like knowing the cause of everything and receiving a predictable result, as if it was no surprise at all.
Wisdom allowed him to consider everything rationally and calmly, so emotions seemed very superfluous.
This state...
Su Lun frowned slightly, feeling that a self without emotional fluctuations was not too good.
However, as if Mr. Hei had seen through his thoughts, he said, "This state is like enlightenment, very rare. It's brought by the 'Spring of Wisdom,' but it will gradually fade in the next few days. I was like this a few days ago too."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun pondered.
He looked at Mr. Hei, and nothing escaped his notice; this knowledgeable elder was much stronger than before. "Mr. Hei, your eyes?"
"Yes, I also passed the test. Of course, I must thank you for getting those two giant elders drunk."
Mr. Hei smiled, shrugged, and gestured to his eyes, explaining, "And as you can see, I sacrificed my eyes and drank the water. But I only hung on the tree for three days, while you were up for nine."
His tone carried barely concealed happiness, obviously having achieved what he expected.
Su Lun wasn't surprised that Mr. Hei had passed the Cyclops clan's test; instead, he felt relieved that his companion had gotten stronger.
This Spring of Wisdom was almost perfectly compatible with Mr. Hei's career path.
Su Lun was also looking forward to seeing how much stronger Mr. Hei would become after having gained "wisdom."
Only someone who had also drunk the water could understand that feeling. He asked, "Mr. Hei, did you also see the secrets of the world?"
Mr. Hei nodded with a smile, but then changed the subject, "No, what we saw might be different. The spring only let me see what I could understand."
After pausing for a while, he continued, "But that's enough. On the third day of my sacrifice, I saw the Rune scripts opening the gates to the world's secrets, and for my future career progression... it may now be possible for me to touch upon the mysteries beyond the ninth tier."
Since Mr. Hei knew Su Lun was in such a state of overlooking everything, there wasn't much to talk about. He then said, "Let's go back first. Qian Tiao mentioned that he needed to see you."
Su Lun heard this and simply nodded lightly.
....
Su Lun and Mr. Hei went to the Cyclops tribe's village, thanked the old Clan Leader Morey, and then left Giant Island.
Soon after, the two returned to the ship called Evernight.
Thanks to the success of their challenge, many members of the Dawn group had also gone to Giant Island to take the test in these days.
But without exception, all had failed.
Nearly everyone was defeated in the first challenge of "Courageous Challenge."
And like Qian Tiao, those who had the ability to pass the first challenge couldn't get past the second.
So out of tens of thousands in the Dawn group, only Su Lun and Mr. Hei had successfully obtained wisdom from the Spring of Wisdom.
So when the two reappeared on the deck, a tidal wave of cheers immediately erupted aboard the Eternal Night.
"Mr. Su Lun and Mr. Hei are back!"
"Hahaha, Mr. Su Lun, Mr. Hei, come on, tell everyone, what does the Spring of Wisdom taste like?"
"Exactly! I almost went ashore, but seeing the Cyclops tribe, I simply didn't have the courage to confront them directly. Oh, the mythical spring remains beyond my reach, such a pity..."
"..."
The crowd surrounded Su Lun and Mr. Hei, chattering and asking questions, even the captains were very curious.
But the insights from the Spring of Wisdom were such that they could only be understood, not easily explained.
Mr. Hei, who had once been the dean of Old Lyndon Academy, was obviously better suited for explaining and teaching. He stayed on the deck, recounting the magical experiences on Giant Island to satisfy everyone's curiosity.
While Su Lun exchanged greetings with everyone, he entered the cabin.
In those days, the Dawn Group hadn't rested, scavenging relics and treasures everywhere.
The Eternal Night was also filled with all sorts of treasures.
Su Lun took these tons of treasures into his small void realm and headed back to the captain's quarters.
As he opened the door and walked in, the room was filled with swirling smoke.
Chen Tiao was in the bathroom, taking a bath.
Hearing his footsteps, she called out, "You're back, huh?"
Su Lun nodded and walked over.
He noticed the blood-stained Sword Dao robe in the room and asked concernedly, "Sister Chen Tiao, are you injured?"
"Yes. It's not serious."
From the bathroom, Chen Tiao's response came.
Pausing momentarily, she added, "I went to Hell Volcano."
Su Lun frowned as he listened, "???"
He was now sure that Hell Volcano was the seal of a hellish dimensional rift, home to many superior beings. Even ninth level beings might not come back alive.
Chen Tiao had actually gone there personally?
"Wisdom" made Su Lun instantly realize that Chen Tiao was seeking the opportunity to enter the divine realm of swords; she truly wished to step into hell herself.
He wasn't sure what to say.
Their deep understanding meant Chen Tiao knew what he was thinking without him speaking, and she added, "It's not as bad as you think. When you were on Giant Island, I successfully understood 'Dominant Body'. It's indeed dangerous there, but I wasn't completely helpless."
Su Lun was still in that special state conferred by the spring water, his expression unchanged.
It was expected that Chen Tiao could comprehend the Dominant Body.
He walked over and saw Chen Tiao, nude, soaking in the bathtub.
However, on her smooth delicate left shoulder, there was clearly a wound oozing dark energy.
A glint flashed in Su Lun's eyes, and the wisp of smoke took on a solid form before him.
This was a strand of chaotic high-level hellish law preventing the wound from healing, extremely troublesome.
If one's understanding of this chaotic energy wasn't sufficient, it might leave a lifelong problem.
Without speaking, he approached, and with a sorcerer's instant concentration, he conjured a green orb of light in his palm, then gently touched it to the wound on Chen Tiao's shoulder.
Chen Tiao said nothing, comfortably lying there.
But as a cool sensation hit her shoulder, she opened her eyes in surprise and looked at Su Lun, "Eh...Dr. Banks said it would be difficult to deal with this negative energy erosion in a short time. How did you manage to do it?"
After speaking, as if she had just recalled something, she said, "Oh, I almost forgot, you gained the [Mimir's Spring]. Looks like you had quite the harvest."
"Yes."
Su Lun replied indifferently, "My [All-knowing Eye] talent advanced to the second level. To me, this plane holds no secrets."
There was nothing to hide from Chen Tiao.
At his words, the gambling-addicted swordswoman's commanding eyebrows twitched, her face full of relief.
A crystal tear sparkled in her eye, seemingly reflecting some complex inner emotional struggle, she simply uttered three words: "That's good."
Su Lun said nothing, quietly continuing to treat her wound.
The injury was more severe than it appeared, and Chen Tiao had been enduring the bone-deep pain all along.
The furrowed brows that had been tormented finally relaxed at that moment.
The two remained silent, enjoying a rare moment of peace together.
Suddenly, Chen Tiao thought of something and spoke again, "Oh, right. Weren't you still short of material for your implant? I discovered an eighth-level mutated Black Dragon at Hell Volcano."

chapters.title: Chapter 591 - 590 Dragon Language Magic
chapters.content:
"Hell Black Dragon?"
"Yes. A pure-blood Black Dragon mutated by the hellish energy. The wound on my leg was left during an entanglement with that foul dragon."
Upon hearing Chientiao's words, Su Lun's gaze shifted to the outside of her right leg, where he noticed a patch of dragon breath burns for the first time.
A flash of insight in his eyes, the absolutely calm train of thought allowed Su Lun to analyze the rough capabilities of the Black Dragon from the negative energy within the wound.
It was ultimately inconvenient in the bath, so he spoke indifferently, "Chientiao, stand up, and I'll help you deal with the wound on your leg."
"Oh."
Chientiao glanced at him, then stood up.
The sound of water splashing, her well-proportioned figure completely exposed to the air without any cover.
Without the warm water of the bath to obscure, every detail was revealed, a sight full of undulating splendor.
Su Lun glanced at her, then crouched down, his hands wreathed in a healing green light, and without any hesitation, he touched the wound.
The corrosive wound on her shoulder and the dragon breath burns on her thigh were two different types of injuries, requiring different treatments.
Su Lun understood the nature of the negative energy that prevented the wounds from healing, multi-tasking with ease as he treated them.
After several attempts, he could now roughly grasp the ability of the All-knowing Eye.
By only looking for the specific information he needed, the burden was much lighter.
Not like the first time he used it, rashly attempting to perceive all information from the surface to the world's source of the targeted object. That would be too much for his brain to handle, and unnecessary.
No one spoke in the bathhouse, the sound of flowing water from the boiler pipes clear to the ear.
Seeing Su Lun's crouching posture, Chientiao, apparently finding it quite inconvenient for him, suggested, "Should I go lie down on the couch? It seems you're not very comfortable."
"Good."
Su Lun responded calmly.
He didn't say much, just extended his hand to embrace Chientiao's waist, and with a flash of spatial fluctuation, they appeared next to the couch a dozen meters away.
Chientiao then lay down on the couch, lazily muttering, "Huh... this is much more comfortable."
Su Lun didn't speak, continuing to treat the wounds.
At this moment, Chientiao, looking at his eyes that were clear and focused like the starry sky, as if noticing something, asked, "Why do I feel like you're in a strange state right now?"
"Hmm. This is the state of 'wisdom' induced from drinking from the Spring of Mimir, which has plunged my thoughts into a state of absolute rationality. It will disappear in a few days..."
Su Lun replied, repeating what Mr. Hei had told him before.
"Oh. I see."
Chientiao listened, somewhat understanding, pursed her lips, and didn't ask further about the topic.
Su Lun was busy treating the wound while Chientiao, lying on her back, seemed a bit bored. She changed the subject, asking curiously, "By the way, what's the situation on Giant Island, what is the second trial like? And does the mythical Spring of Mimir hold any secrets…"
These were the most discussed topics among their team these days, and she was quite interested as well.
Listening to her questions, Su Lun recounted his previous experiences.
Chientiao listened, occasionally expressing amazement.
But upon hearing about the questions in the second trial, she felt lucky that she did not have to endure such an ordeal.
...
Wounds caused by high-level laws were troublesome to deal with, and even though Su Lun knew the method of treatment, he found it a bit strenuous with his current level.
About an hour later, the injuries on Chientiao finally were completely healed.
The previously corroded hole on her shoulder and the burnt scars on her thigh were both treated, leaving the regrown skin as smooth as that of a newborn baby.
Su Lun checked and found no issues, and he heaved a sigh of relief.
This wasn't the first time he was treating Chientiao's injuries. Having finished everything, his large hand confidently and lightly patted her buttocks, signaling, "It's done."
Because she was not wearing clothes, the slap was solid.
A ripple spread across her firm and round form, a crisp "snap" echoing clearly in the room.
Chientiao gave him a glare, but she was already accustomed to such intimacy.
She got up with a usual expression, took out a Sword Dao robe, and prepared to put it on, muttering, "Ah... finally, the injury has healed."
Listening to the relieved tone, it seemed that not going out for the last two days due to the injury meant she was gearing up for a major fight.
Su Lun, seeing Qian Tiao getting ready to wrap the chest band around herself, also stretched out his hand to help and took the band.
Qian Tiao raised her eyebrows and glanced at him but did not refuse.
As Su Lun took over the bandage, he had genuinely wanted to help, but then, as if he thought of something, his palm casually climbed up.
Such intimate gestures had become normal for the two of them.
Qian Tiao knocked away that increasingly improper hand and spat out, "Hey, hey, hey... no getting handsy. Hurry up, I need to go out and practice swordplay. After not moving for two days, I feel like I'm about to rust."
As she spoke, she glanced at the restless hand and complained grumpily, "Didn't you say you were in that 'Absolute Rationality' state, without any emotional fluctuations?"
Su Lun maintained his usual expression and replied, "Absolute rationality doesn't mean there are no emotional fluctuations. It just means I can control my emotions more actively."
"Huh...?"
Hearing that explanation, Qian Tiao obviously didn't believe a word of it.
While talking, Su Lun didn't stop; his fingers sank into a touch of soft warmth, and with his expression unchanged, he said, "Besides, I'm testing how much this state affects the body."
"..."
Qian Tiao rolled her eyes, seemingly out of arguments for this shameless yet seemingly reasonable explanation.
But she seemed to accept it by default, and didn't say anything to stop him.
Unable to put on her clothes, she took out a hair tie and started to tie up her blue hair on her own.
With a high ponytail, her demeanor instantly became spirited and valiant.
But this motion of her arms lifting and extending made things even more convenient for Su Lun behind her, his hands touching nothing but warm, jade-like softness.
In the captain's room, the scene was harmonious.
This kind of interlude had become part of their daily interactions.
Although Qian Tiao found it uninteresting, it did not prevent Su Lun from enjoying it a bit, and she was willing to tacitly allow it.
Time also seemed to pass gently.
The air was filled with a sense of small joy.
Before long, Su Lun finally finished wrapping the chest band for Qian Tiao, who picked up the sword from the rack and strapped it around her waist.
Su Lun seemed to think of something and said, "Qian Tiao, can I have a look at your 'Dominator's Body'?"
Upon hearing this, Qian Tiao turned her head to look at him and asked in return, "You mean... you've touched the threshold of 'Dominator's Body'?"
"No."
Su Lun shook his head and added, "I'm still far from comprehending it. But I can understand it."
"You understand it?"
Qian Tiao was stunned for a moment before she realized what she had heard, her expression slightly incredulous.
But then her eyes lit up with excitement as she remarked, "Ah... I used to think that your talent didn't quite seem like an S-class level. Now, it's so astounding that even I am amazed. You can understand 'Dominator's Body', does that mean you can advance to the eighth tier at any time?"
"Yes," Su Lun responded with a meaningful tone, "At least I feel that the threshold of the eighth tier doesn't hold any secrets for me anymore."
Before, he had always thought that the S-018 All-knowing Eye was merely a supportive ability.
Compared to other S-talents, this talent offered a very limited direct boost to combat, and it wasn't even on par with most A and B talents.
But it wasn't until he developed his second level of awakening that Su Lun realized his talent wasn't just worthy of being in the S-class; it was just as effective and significant as any other S-class talent he knew!
Knowledge empowers fearlessness.
When there are no more secrets in sight, an overwhelming sense of superiority naturally arises.
...
A few days later, in the captain's room.
Su Lun hadn't left his room for several days, continuously drawing on the remaining benefits of the Spring of Wisdom to digest the new abilities he had acquired on Giant Island.
The sea breeze blew gently through the window, and the people on deck were bustling with activity in the early morning light, still busily salvaging treasures from the sunken ship on the sea floor.
Suddenly, Su Lun, who was in meditation, opened his eyes.
His eyes sparkled with vitality, and he murmured to himself, "Now there are basically no cognitive barriers left."
With this thought, he picked up the rune black umbrella in his hand, reached out, and grabbed a dragon-shaped Spiritual Body.
This was the soul of an eighth-tier Silver Dragon that the Dawn group had once captured.
Previously, Su Lun had attempted to strip away the dragon soul, but because the souls of dragon-kind were very different from humans, especially at the cognitive level. Higher beings perceived the world in a way that was beyond human comprehension.
As a result, after stripping the soul, he had ended up with a lot of "gibberish," and the valuable dragon soul had gone largely to waste.
Therefore, after obtaining such a precious material as the soul of the eighth-tier Silver Dragon, he kept it and had been nurturing it within the Rune Umbrella ever since.
It wasn't until today that Su Lun felt confident enough to attempt the stripping again.
The wisdom gained from the Spring of Wisdom had lifted the "manhole cover" on the cognitive level, and attributes such as perception, intelligence, and brain development on his attribute panel had increased several times or even by tens of times.
A shadow of death appeared behind him, and the domineering aura of death immediately swallowed the dragon soul.
Just as a two-dimensional being cannot understand a three-dimensional existence, but once your cognition is high enough, the secrets of lower dimensions are completely revealed before your eyes.
"You have stripped the 'memory fragments' of 'Silver Dragon Angralas'."
"You have mastered one of the higher language systems, [Dragon Language]."
"You have gained a massive amount of insight into the elemental laws of water and a slight grasp of the power of ice rules; elemental experience +521412."
"You have mastered Dragon Magic: [Ice Dragon Breath], [Dragon Language: Absolute Zero], [Dragon Language: Extreme Cold Storm]..."
"You have attained a vast number of cold ice dragon clan rune languages."
"You've uncovered some of the dragon lineage's secret legacies."
"Spiritual power +91251."
"..."
This time, Su Lun finally managed to strip away clear and detailed information.
Just like stripping a human soul, he obtained everything he wanted.
After digesting those memories in his mind, Su Lun's expression became quite marvelous, and he joyfully thought, "I even stripped the Dragon Language and its magic...!"
The Dragon Language is one of the legendary high-order languages.
Mr. Jing had said that only ninth-tier professionals might be able to touch the threshold of this language.
But now, Su Lun had easily stripped it away and had completely mastered it.
Just like the difference between "runes" and ordinary text, "Dragon Language" is a language that inherently possesses extraordinary powers.
Su Lun had previously wondered why Dragon Magic was so strong. Even though it was released at the same energy level, Dragon Magic was much stronger than Alchemy of the same tier.
Now, he fully understood.
Magic chanted in higher language systems can summon and condense more elemental power and can directly manipulate the primal forces of the plane's laws. It is not like the arduous process humans need, which requires extremely high skills to refine.
It's as if one is drawing water from a reservoir and the other is trying to condense droplets from the air; they're not on the same path at all.
The efficiency is worlds apart.
That's why each Dragon Magic is equivalent to ordinary human magic of a whole tier higher.
This is one of the most important reasons for the strength of the dragon race.
Although Su Lun is not a Mage, many aspects of these law-level principles have much in common with Alchemy.
His current understanding of laws can easily be transformed into spells he can use.
However, the Dragon Language Magic mastered by dragons is mostly an innate talent associated with their bloodline, and Su Lun hadn't stripped anything like a systematic magic learning system from a divine plane like the mages do.
Thus the Dragon Language Magic that Su Lun had stripped away could only be used by himself.
To teach it to others, at least for now, was not feasible as others could not understand it.
"Maybe... Mr. Hei could understand?"
A thought flashed through Su Lun's mind; he could exchange some of this Dragon Language Magic with Mr. Hei in the future.
Others may not understand, but that Scholar who likewise possessed the "Wisdom" was very skilled at all kinds of spell-based Alchemy, and he was probably the one who could understand.
Su Lun was also looking forward to seeing how strong Mr. Hei would be, using Dragon Magic.
...
Once the dragon soul was stripped away, his vision vastly expanded.
Su Lun then brought out some of the high-ranking ghosts and monster souls he had previously collected to reap them altogether.
What used to be considered "blind box draws" for souls, at this moment, he could almost find everything he wanted.
Before long, after digesting those souls, Su Lun then took out a pitch-black book.
That was the very same [Fatal Novel·Netherworld] he had never been able to comprehend before.
The great adventurer and literary giant, Fujiwara Hayato, recorded his experiences in the Netherworld within its pages.
Su Lun opened the novel and began to read it carefully, page by page.
The content, once muddled to him, now unveiled all its secrets before his eyes.
As he read line after line, he finally understood the world of the dead depicted by the author.
Engrossed in the reading, he lost track of time.
Two days later.
Su Lun had reached the last page of the novel.
When he closed the book, he took a deep breath and said, "Fujiwara Hayato truly was an extraordinary literary giant..."
After finishing, he felt a deep respect within his heart. The strength of Fujiwara Hayato's writing was undoubtedly deserving of being called one of the greatest literary figures of the past millennium.
Through the expressive text and descriptions, Su Lun felt as if he had personally experienced each of those bizarre adventures.
There are too many indescribably powerful beings in the higher planes, but Fujiwara Hayato, with his pen, ingeniously recorded those "indescribable" entities in a way that mortals could comprehend.
That gave Su Lun a direct impression of the Netherworld.
But now that he understood, his brow furrowed with worry: "Even with this detailed travelogue, it's still extremely risky for Sister Qiantiao to go."
It must be said, Fujiwara Hayato was incredibly lucky; saying it was a close call between life and death would not be an exaggeration.
Considering the experiences in the novel that seemed beyond belief, Su Lun felt that even if he were to go himself, there was no guarantee he would make it back alive.
This was not simply a trip to a higher plane.
After all, the Netherworld does not welcome the living.
With this in mind, Su Lun's brow knitted slightly, thinking to himself, "Sister Qiantiao has made up her mind to go to the Netherworld."
Lately, Qiantiao had been frequenting Hell Volcano in search of an opportunity for a breakthrough, often returning with wounds all over her body.
Su Lun clearly saw her unwavering conviction to reach the ultimate realm in Sword Dao.
From the moment they had met, this was something she had never changed.
As her closest friend, how could Su Lun not understand this desire of hers?
The only thing he could do was to help her prepare for everything.
The adventure in the Dragon Country Waters was drawing to a close, the Dawn Group had thwarted the plans of the celestial planes, and had reaped many benefits.
Although Qiantiao had not said anything, Su Lun knew she wanted to pursue her own path to the ultimate Sword Dao.
His thoughts grew intricate in a flash. Without dwelling on it further, Su Lun had already deduced a detailed route in his mind.
Just as he was pondering, a sudden knocking sound "tap tap tap" came from the door.
Su Lun: "Come in."
The door opened, and a small head peeked in first; it was Lolo Ta.
Looking at Su Lun, she flashed a radiant smile, showing her white teeth, and asked, "Mr. Su Lun, we are now approaching the predetermined waters, and the scouting party has also spotted traces of the Hell Black Dragon. The teacher sent me to ask if we are going to execute the dragon hunting plan?"
Hearing this, Su Lun stood up and said, "Good!"
He needed a giant dragon as the main material for his level seven armor, and after the upgrade, the doors to the level eight Alchemy realm would also be open to him.

chapters.title: Chapter 592 - 591: Hell Black Dragon
chapters.content:
After returning from Giant Island that day, Su Lun hadn't left his cabin.
The members of Dawn Group had long since grown accustomed to this because everyone knew that "Mr. Su Lun" was either cultivating or on the path to cultivation.
Stepping out of the captain's quarters, Lolo looked at Su Lun playfully. Regardless of whether she understood or not, she lavished praise, "Wow... Mr. Su Lun seems to have gotten stronger again!"
Su Lun just smiled noncommittally and gave her a glance, then said, "Lolo, have you been practicing diligently lately? You've made great progress as well."
Now his eyes held no secrets, at a glance he could see that the girl's strength had rapidly improved recently.
Not to mention that deliberately leaked hint of dominance.
"Yes!"
Lolo seemed to have been waiting for the compliment and happily said, "The day before yesterday in the battle, I successfully grasped dominance. And I have also mastered the domain of wind, barely half a step away from comprehending my own domain."
Advancing to the sixth rank was already a sure thing for her, and once she comprehended a domain, she would be able to advance to the seventh rank, making her a truly top professional.
As she spoke, she excitedly shared her recent experiences, "Mr. Su Lun, you have no idea how hard I've been working these days. Also, Dr. Banks' Dragon Blood Gene Potion has given me a huge boost. I successfully merged a pure-blood Wind Dragon Potion, and now, among my peers in the group, I have no rivals~"
"Is that so."
Su Lun smiled and then said, "Congratulations. If you continue to train with your teacher, perhaps you'll become the youngest Sword Saint in the group."
Perceiving everything around him, he had noticed that not only Lolo, but the entire strength of Dawn Group had skyrocketed these days.
The presence of Hell Volcano meant that, in the Dragon Country Waters, the natural Power of Laws was more complete, making advancement easier.
Not to mention the major opportunity presented by gene potions, which could be considered a shortcut.
With a large number of gene samples, Dr. Banks had made significant breakthroughs with both the Giant Dragon Gene Potion and the Titan Gene Potion.
The genes of these higher beings, dragons and Titans, were quite special.
This caliber of gene potion visibly elevated the cultivation talents of humans, thus relatively lowering the threshold for professional advancement by a great margin.
Hearing Su Lun's acknowledgment, Lolo smiled happily but then, as if something occurred to her, added, "But..."
She hesitated for a moment and then said, "Mr. Su Lun, do you know, my teacher has been acting very strange lately. She's become stricter with me, and then she sometimes says things... as if she's planning to leave. I don't know what's gotten into her."
As Su Lun listened, his eyes gazed into the distance, and he said lightly, "Your teacher is going to pursue her Sword Dao."
"Ah?"
Lolo listened with a puzzled expression on her face.
Su Lun did not explain further.
He didn't want others to know about his trip to the Netherworld yet and didn't want to disrupt Qianbao's mood by speaking out.
...
The two walked unhurriedly and soon arrived on the deck.
"Mr. Su Lun is here!"
As the crew members saw them come out, someone shouted out, and they all warmly greeted him.
Su Lun smiled back responding to everyone busy preparing for dragon hunting.
When they first came to the Dragon Country Waters, hunting giant dragons was a major event that filled everyone with nervousness. After all, no one had seen the legendary dragons before, and nobody knew what might happen; it was all unknown.
Now they had successfully hunted many giant dragons and powerful monsters, so fear was no longer present.
Moreover, everyone's strength had increased significantly, so even the news of hunting an eighth-rank giant dragon did not bring tension aboard, only excitement.
This seemed to have become a routine daily activity for everyone.
When Su Lun arrived, Barrett was donning the heavy "Gracie's Dragon Knight Armor."
The once strenuous armor now seemed effortless on him.
Barrett, originally the captain of the Royal Knights, already had an excellent physical foundation. He was also one of the few in Dawn Group who had completed both Dragon Blood and Titan gene modifications.
Thanks to the supercharged body from both potions, he too was on the threshold of the eighth rank of physical dominance.
Seeing Su Lun arrive, Barrett looked him over and couldn't hide his amazement, laughing and remarked, "Su Lun, why do I feel that after a few days, you're giving off a vibe more and more like Mr. Hei?"
Despite both being seventh rank, Barrett felt like he was looking at an unfathomably deep ancient well when he saw Su Lun.
After a pause, he described his feeling, "It's that kind of... filled with wisdom vibe, making one feel like there's nowhere to attack, as if no matter where you hit, you couldn't land a blow."
Hearing this, Phantom Thief Kit joined in, "Yeah... how exactly do you train? Your strength has increased so dramatically it's a bit exaggerated. I thought I'd finally gained a little ground by grasping dominance and stepping half into the seventh rank, but now it seems the gap is only widening."
At this, the members of Dawn Group on the deck also chimed in.
"Yeah, Mr. Su Lun feels so strange now. If we really had to fight, I wouldn't even know where to attack; it's like no matter where you strike, it would miss."
"Mhm, I feel the same way."
"..."
Even Old Sword God Bartolo and "Blood Duke" Watzhaus, two bona fide eighth rankers, found Su Lun's current state unbelievable.
Only they knew how exaggerated Su Lun's state was now.
Even so, they felt the same way.
Despite their rank's overwhelming advantage, it seemed as if they were to strike, they would have nowhere to begin.
"Heh heh."
Su Lun listened with a smile but didn't know how to respond.
After drinking from the Spring of Wisdom and developing the second level of the All-knowing Eye, his perception of anything had become incredibly "clear."
When a person no longer holds any secrets in their eyes, they harbor no doubts, and naturally, they reveal no flaws.
Moreover, his own strength was extremely formidable, and unless he faced an overwhelmingly powerful opponent, opportunities would not bring him any pressure.
But such beings were now few and far between in the world of Alchemy.
A short distance away, Mr. Hei smiled slightly, only he, who had also partaken from the spring, could understand Su Lun's current state.
This was only the present, for the "wisdom" that came with it affected one's entire future.
...
After greeting the others, Su Lun and Mr. Hei walked at a leisurely pace on the deck, chatting as they went.
"Are you talking about Dragon Language Magic?"
"Yes."
"Say a few words, let's hear it."
"Jili gulu..."
"..."
It wasn't just about the pronunciation. As soon as Su Lun spoke, it was as if he summoned the power of the surrounding ice, and snowflakes began to drift down on the vast deck.
The members of the Dawn group sent puzzled yet astonished glances his way, for they faintly heard the sound of a dragon's chant.
Only a few realized that Su Lun was speaking in the Dragon's Tongue.
Mr. Hei's expression brightened as if he immediately understood something, whispering to himself, "So this is the mystery of a higher linguistic system..."
Once in Lington, when Su Lun found the Rodriguez family's secret box at the headquarters of the Royal Bank of Ruying, it was Mr. Hei who deciphered it for him.
But at that time, neither of them knew Dragon Language, and it was only after they sought Mr. Jing's help that they opened it and obtained the map of the Dragon Country Waters.
Though Mr. Hei didn't understand the Dragon language at the time, as a Scholar, he had continued his research.
After coming to the Dragon Country, he had come into contact with more of the Dragon civilization, and his research had gone deeper.
Now, having also drunk from the Spring of Wisdom, Mr. Hei, too, could understand those secrets of the Power of Laws that went beyond the cognition of lower life forms.
Su Lun spoke a few sentences in the Dragon language and then stopped, finding it somewhat strenuous with his human vocal cords, and then asked, "Mr. Hei, can you understand it?"
"Barely."
Mr. Hei nodded, then added, "However, mastering this superior language seems like it will take quite some time."
"That's good to hear."
Su Lun laughed as he listened. Being a Puppet Master, he himself didn't quite fit with Dragon Language Magic.
But it was different for Mr. Hei.
As a [Scholar], he was one of the most traditional sorcerers in the art of Alchemy. If he were to master the Dragon language, his combat capabilities would likely be formidable.
However, learning the Dragon language was not something that could be accomplished in a short time, so they switched to another topic.
It was then that Mr. Hei suddenly asked with profound significance, "Have you ever thought that there might be some unexpected events during the dragon hunt?"
Despite the question's lack of specificity, Su Lun seemed to grasp the implication immediately, "Of course."
He looked towards the distant Hell Volcano, his pupils narrowing, murmuring, "If that guy is still not dead, this might also be the last chance."
...
After a brief exchange, Su Lun saw Qian Tiao blowing in the wind atop the mast and hailed her before leaping up to join.
The weather was fine today, and even the black vapors from Hell Volcano couldn't block out the brilliant sunshine.
The two sat atop the mast, with the sea breeze on their faces and a few seagulls nearby grooming their white feathers.
Seeing Su Lun, who hadn't been out in days, Qian Tiao's mouth curved into a gratified smile.
As she had done countless times before, she casually draped an arm over Su Lun's shoulder, praising, "Yo, you've changed a lot in just a few days."
Su Lun chuckled in response, "I've nearly assimilated the benefits from the Spring of Wisdom. It's been somewhat fruitful."
He then asked, "How about you, Sister Qian Tiao?"
"Same old."
Qian Tiao shrugged her shoulders, retracted her gaze, and looked towards the distant Hell Volcano.
After pondering for a while, she added, "If I can't make this step, it might trouble me for the rest of my life."
"..."
Su Lun also fell silent without responding.
The realm of the Sword Saint wasn't easy to reach.
Otherwise, with so many masters of the Sword Dao in the world, there wouldn't only have been one Sword Saint like Bartolo.
Moreover, his entry into the Sword Saint realm had come after experiencing the great setback of the annihilation of Black Sam's pirate crew, forcing him into a moment of despair from which he emerged enlightened.
That process of experiencing despair is something one can't understand without going through it personally.
It was then that Su Lun took out a booklet and handed it over, saying, "This is for you."
"What is this?"
Sen casually asked as he took it and flipped it open, only to discover that it was filled with dense, handwritten text.
He had no particular interest in text, but a casual glance through a few pages revealed that it was a map with annotations and detailed explanations.
It was then that Sen realized what he was looking at, and he turned to Su Lun with excitement, "Is this a map of the Netherworld?"
"Yes."
Su Lun nodded.
In the past few days, he had carefully read the novel [Netherworld] and then deconstructed Fujiwara Hayato's travelogue into this map, decipherable to ordinary people.
He added, "Be careful. If you encounter dangers you can't solve, contact me using the communicator."
Sen immediately muttered in response, "Hey hey hey, you're underestimating me, kid."
Su Lun wore a serious smile on his face but said nothing more.
Actually going to the Netherworld was most certainly a perilous venture.
From the corner of his eye, Sen pursed his lips.
Their tacit understanding meant she knew exactly what he meant without saying it.
The two sat on the mast, continuing to enjoy the sea breeze.
Even without speaking, this rare moment of solitude felt very comfortable.
...
The Eternal Night continued sailing towards the Hell Volcano.
Because of the massive battle between the dragons and the Titans a few days before, the sea was filled with various chaotic remnants of war, like debris fields and spatial rifts.
"All hands, pay attention, the Black Dragon has been lured to observation point seven, 150 nautical miles from us."
"Prepare the Dragon Hunting Crossbow!"
"..."
Throughout the communicator, the staff continually reported the movement of the Hell Black Dragon.
An eighth-tier Black Dragon, though it had mutated into a dominant aberration, was not much of a problem for the Dawn Group now.
The greatest danger they had always faced was the other creatures inside the Hell Volcano, so the only option was to lure them out.
Before long, three dark spots appeared on the horizon.
"They're coming!"
Su Lun's pupils narrowed as he focused on the sight.
In his view, it was two wind dragons with two figures on them—the siblings Bennett and Isabel.
Over these past days, Miracle Legion and the members of the Dawn Group had gotten along very well.
Having been abandoned by the royal family of the Silver Dragon Kingdom, they naturally could no longer return.
Enticed by Su Lun's warm invitation, they had now become part of the Dawn Group.
Moreover, Su Lun possessed the Rodriguez family's complete dragon-taming Secret Technique, which was a royal secret of the once nine sovereign kingdoms.
This was far more comprehensive than the truncated Secret Technique inherited by Bennett's knightly family.
The group had no hierarchy, and all members of Miracle Legion learned the ancient dragon-taming Secret Technique that had been handed down.
In these days, the members of the Dawn Group had cleared several Asian Dragon's Lairs, allowing many of Miracle Legion's Dragon Knights to find new mounts.
And in the Dragon Country Waters, needless to say, there was an endless variety of dragonkin creatures with high bloodline purity.
Just like the two that Bennett and his sister Isabel were riding at the moment!
The two wind dragons were incredibly fast, and in the blink of an eye, they went from distant black dots a hundred miles away to large flying dragons visible to the naked eye.
And behind the two flying dragons, a massive Black Dragon followed closely.
This Black Dragon was covered in billowing black mist, and its flesh wings were riddled with rotten holes—it was a Hell breed Black Dragon.
"Release!"
Su Lun's eyes sharpened as he activated the second stage of the All-knowing Eye to look.
He saw that the black mist rising from the Black Dragon was not only filled with fluctuations of darkness-based Power of Laws but also all sorts of hellish Laws—death, contamination, curses, disaster, annihilation, plague, famine...
"Just as I thought."
Su Lun murmured to himself, not surprised at all; this was information he had already confirmed while treating Sen's wounds earlier.
One could say that this Hell Black Dragon was a walking, top-tier cursed object, deadly upon contact.
But to Su Lun, it was the ideal material for his armament.
....
"All hands, prepare for battle!"
A command came from the control room.
The flight speed of Black Dragons was not outstanding among dragon species, and after mutating into a hellish creature, it had lost its natural cunning and wariness.
As a result, it was readily lured over by the bait flying dragons ridden by the Bennett siblings.
However, the Dragon Hunting Crossbows on deck had been prepared for quite a while.
Waiting for the moment the three dragons swooped down from the sky, with a "whoosh," a spear was launched.
Tied to the back of the spear was a thin rope.
This was the "Cadmos's Dragon Hunting Spear" and "Grapnel of Glaupnir."
A spear capable of breaking dragon scales and the toughest rope in the world.
Once, with these two magical artifacts, the mages from the heavenly domain nearly killed an eighth-tier Silver Dragon—how much more for a sneak attack on an instinct-driven Hell Black Dragon?
The spear pierced the Black Dragon's wing, and the rope trailing it instantly solidified, trapping the Black Dragon at once.
But being of naturally enormous strength, the dragon, despite being bound by the rope, didn't slow down but instead dragged the massive Nevernight along the surface of the sea in a wild sprint.
Nevertheless, the Dawn Brigade was well-prepared—once the Alchemy sails were activated, they instantly sailed in the opposite direction.
Dragon and ship began a tug-of-war on the ocean's surface.
Seeing that it couldn't catch up to its "prey," the Hell Black Dragon turned in anger to charge at the Nevernight, spewing out a breath of black flame.
The Dawn's crew faced a formidable enemy, and a host of high-level fighters swiftly responded.
Today's Dawn Brigade's combined strength was incomparable to before; even facing the eighth-tier Black Dragon head-on wouldn't pose a significant problem.
But just then, Su Lun formed a sorcerer's seal, and in an instant, he disappeared from the mast.
After all, this was Hell Volcano; various infernal creatures still dwelled upon that massive mountain in the distance—and a drawn-out battle of attrition could attract even more monsters.
So, it was essential to make it a quick battle.
When his surroundings changed, Su Lun was seen to have teleported next to the spear that pierced through the Black Dragon's wing.
The eighth-tier Black Dragon also noticed the "insignificant insect" on its back, issuing a curse-like, deep dragon chant. An aura of dragon's might condemned others, and a visible layer of black mist rose up, the dragon scales glistening with a crystal-black sheen.
Previously, Su Lun had been greatly affected by the eighth-tier Giant Dragon's oppressive presence, and even his dominance might not have entirely withstood it.
But now, having mastered the Dragon Language... the threat was virtually reduced by more than half.
The rough meaning of that roar just now would be: "Wretched insect, be gone!"
Fearless with the All-knowing Eye, Su Lun was now not intimidated by any entity he could comprehend.
And as for the black mist and dragon breath from the dragon scales, how could he not have seen that the Black Dragon was condensing the Power of High Laws?
In the second stage of the All-knowing Eye, there were no secrets to the Black Dragon's every move.
A threat from an attack that can be understood is greatly reduced.
Moreover, Su Lun immediately spotted a "weakness."
He drew out his dragon-slaying dagger and stabbed it into the spot on the dragon's neck where the scales had once been replaced.
With a "rip," the dagger plunged smoothly in, and a stream of pus-like black blood gushed out, hissing as it corroded the air upon exposure.
At the same time, the Death God's Fire blazed up around Su Lun, beginning to scorch the mutated soul within the dragon.
...
The Dragon Hunting Dagger was laced with Dragon Slaying Potion, and with the soul also being scorched, a double fatal damage caused the Hell Black Dragon to reveal its ferocity.
It thrashed wildly in the air, desperate to shake off the human on its back.
Dragon Breath spewed, infernal energies corroded, all its tricks were exhausted.
Still, being an eighth-tier Giant Dragon, although Su Lun could understand its attacks, the difference in tiers meant he sometimes had to carefully dodge.
A dragon's life force was tenacious, and even the soul would take a long time to burn completely.
Su Lun dared not drag it out.
Being able to stand firmly on the dragon's back made his actions much easier,
He summoned a mechanical octopus to physically control the wicked dragon. With "Grapnel of Glaupnir" in place, the Black Dragon had been thoroughly trapped, with no chance to escape.
With assistance from Number 19, the Old Sword God Bartolo, and the other high-level fighters of the Dawn Brigade, the fight immediately got easier.
Because the Dawn Brigade had executed many dragon hunt plans, even an eighth-tier Hell Black Dragon couldn't last long.
However, amidst the battle, a sudden, unexpected change occurred!
Suddenly, without any warning, the crow on Su Lun's shoulder let out a piercing caw.
The Black Dragon was already being overwhelmed by the onslaught, yet the omen bird still issued a fatal warning.
Su Lun's pupils shrank slightly, and he muttered under his breath, "So you couldn't resist making a move..."
No other creatures were spotted within dozens of miles in his field of vision, and the only hidden threat had to be that one.
Su Lun had certainly not forgotten about Saint Frank.
Alive, he should be seen; dead, his body should be found—yet despite the Dawn Brigade's extensive search, he was nowhere to be found.
Thus, the only explanation was that the god who possessed Frank's body used some means undetectable to mortals to conceal him away.
If "Frank" intended to keep hiding, Su Lun would have been powerless anyway.
But now this guy, probably coveting the Dawn Brigade's spoils, was about to strike, suddenly revealing himself.
In the All-knowing Eye of Su Lun, he saw a ray of sunlight that was different from the rest, prompting him to realize, "So you were hiding in the sunlight."

chapters.title: Chapter 593 - 592: The Dawn Group's Ten Thousand Member Magic Formation
chapters.content:
