Old Sword God Bartolo, looking at the distant island, could not hide his emotion in his eyes and said, "When I passed through my own cataclysmic backlash, the power was barely one-tenth of this. One can imagine how strong Su Lun's body must be to have suffered such a strong backlash from the plane."
Next to him, 'Blood Duke' Wuzzhuas also responded, "Indeed. The higher the intensity of the cataclysmic backlash one can withstand, the greater the enhancement one will receive after successful advancement. What's terrifying is that Su Lun is also a Puppet Master. Now that he has comprehended the dominator body, I can hardly imagine who now could pose a lethal threat to him on this plane. With an indestructible body, his puppet army is indeed unstoppable..."
Number Nineteen said, "One person is an army, the lineage of Puppeteers truly is an exaggerated professional series..."
Barrett added, "I have a feeling that those fellows from the Divine Plane are going to have one more 'nightmare' to contend with in their ten-thousand-person magic formations."
The group agreed, "Yes, hahahaha..."
Su Lun's strength was something all members of the Dawn Group had witnessed.
The most terrifying thing was that he was not only immensely powerful in his own right but also a Puppet Master.
When he was at the seventh rank, he could single-handedly annihilate a ten-thousand-person magic formation. Now that he has advanced to the eighth rank and achieved the dominator body state, it would be very difficult to kill him.
This exaggerated level of combat power made it seem like there was no limit in sight.
At least, no one in the Dawn Group could think of anyone they knew who could defeat Su Lun.
...
On the other hand.
On the island, the sky was filled with thunderclouds, and the Nonagram Alchemy Formation in the center of the island had already lost its luster.
A few days ago, the island was lush and green, but now it was barren, with the beaches turned into a thick layer of hard crystal.
All over the island were elements of chaotic laws, the remnants of a cataclysmic backlash that could easily kill a high-ranking professional.
In the center of the alchemical formation, Su Lun sat bare-chested and motionless in meditation.
At this moment, his skin shimmered with the lustrous black and golden color of dragon scale runes, his muscles bulging and knotted, exuding a metallic quality.
The chaotic elements seemed to be repelled by an invisible force a few meters from his body, unable to disturb his meditation.
He was like a piece of iron forged a thousand times, purged of all impurities, having turned into steel.
Finally, as the cataclysmic backlash completely subsided, the dark clouds in the sky also quickly dissipated.
Sunlight broke through the clouds, shining on Su Lun.
He opened his eyes and muttered to himself, "So this is the dominator body."
Su Lun stood up and examined his body.
He could clearly feel that after integrating dominance and domain into his body, its resilience had surpassed physical limits and reached a height of law-level consistency.
For lower-ranked professionals, this state was akin to the dragon race's innate high resistance against both physical and magical attacks, almost akin to physical immunity and impervious to all magic.
Checking his body's data, he saw a significant increase after the advancement.
Today, he had stepped into the eighth rank and now stood at the pinnacle of the Alchemists' pyramid.
Standing at this height, he saw a different landscape.
Su Lun had many reflections.
But since everything was within expectations, his expression did not show joy or sorrow.
He glanced into the distance, his eyes briefly flashing with a strange light that seemed capable of capturing souls, and he felt even more reflective, "The soul is immortal now."
The material Su Lun used for his eighth-rank advancement was the [Crystal Skull of Descartes] he had found earlier in the Atlantis Ruins, which upon fusion, granted him the trait of undying soulfire.
This also meant that it was now nearly impossible for anyone to successfully target him with Curse Magic or any other mysterious techniques.
Even Divine Arts couldn't destroy Su Lun's soul no matter how gravely injured he became.
With an indestructible soul and his body's resistance to both physical and magical damage at the overlord level, Su Lun now truly had no weaknesses in defense.
If the Puppet Master himself could not be killed, estimating his combat power became extremely difficult.
Moreover, after advancing to the eighth rank, Su Lun's control over the number of puppets increased significantly.
Previously, he could control a little over ten thousand, but now, managing twenty thousand would not be a problem.
And this advancement material also greatly increased his brain's capacity to bear burdens; after fully digesting the benefits brought by the advancement, he could also consider the eighth-rank parasite equipment [Isaac Blasphemer].
Once that equipment was fused, it would be the ultimate goal he had set for himself as a Puppeteer, the "Infinite Manipulation".
Thinking this, Su Lun murmured, "I need to find some top-quality material for crafting the [Blasphemer]. I wonder if that void Matriarch Worm is still alive..."
He didn't linger on the deserted island; after all, advancing to the eighth rank didn't present him with any unexpected issues.
With arms outstretched, he performed a trick to change his attire and, in a single step, he was already standing on the deck of the Eternal Night outside the West Sea of Luying.
...
"Mr. Su Lun is back!"
The Dawn group excitedly gathered around upon seeing Su Lun return, congratulating him one after another.
Even Old Sword God Bartolo and "Duke of Blood" Watts, two eighth-rankers, couldn't help but be astonished at his strength.
Only those of the same rank could truly sense how powerful Su Lun had become.
After chatting for a while, everyone dispersed. The Dawn would have a grand banquet tonight to celebrate this special day.
But at this moment, the Dawn's management gathered together for the first time.
Because they had received intelligence from the side of Luying.
The strategist unfolded a sea chart and pointed at a strait, saying, "A few hours ago, we received intelligence from the Mirror Organization that a joint legion from the Luying and Mafa empires was preparing for a secret surprise attack on the Divine Plane near the Imperial Strait. But something seems to have gone wrong, and the entire fleet has lost contact. That fleet was led by the former Mafa Navy Grand Marshal 'Tiger of Lei' Meredith Ben Moses and General Rostov, and a significant portion of the elite forces from both empires was concentrated in it. If something has indeed gone wrong, it will negatively impact the war situation and morale. The empires are now searching everywhere for the whereabouts of the fleet, and the intelligence group has also asked if we can offer any help... Since Mr. Su Lun, you were in the midst of advancement, so..."
They were too far away to respond quickly, even with the intelligence they had received.
This was a decision that only Su Lun could make.
Hearing this, Su Lun frowned and asked, "What's the war situation like now?"
The strategist continued, "It's not optimistic. A month ago, the Mafa Empire's imperial capital, Kabibelron, was breached by the Divine Plane's Magic Corps, and now almost the entire territory is fallen. The only good news is not too many people have descended from the Divine Plane, and they have only occupied some cities. Also, since the Mafa higher-ups previously ordered all domestic shipyards to be destroyed, the invaders don't have access to large warships, and the natural defenses of the Imperial Strait have prevented further invasion. The remaining legions of Mafa are now conducting guerrilla warfare in the wilderness, and the current situation is somewhat at a stalemate..."
After hearing this and looking at the sea chart the strategists had brought out, Su Lun immediately decided, "Then let's first check out the area where the joint fleet went missing. Everyone, prepare for battle!"
Everyone: "Yes!"
Although their current location was tens of thousands of nautical miles away from the Imperial Strait, distance was never an issue for Su Lun.
...
On the other side.
Somewhere within the Imperial Strait, between the two great empires of Luying and Mafa, a huge fleet was assembling in a defensive formation, swiftly sailing across the sea.
Giant smokestacks billowed out black smoke, and countless rivets joined together to form warships as large as steel beasts.
These were some of the top steam warships of both empires, armed with the most sophisticated cannons and defense systems.
Looking at the flags, this was at least a combined legion made up of seven major fleets.
This was a super fleet capable of annihilating any city.
But at that very moment, a fierce debate was taking place in the conference room at the core of the fleet's flagship.
"Damn it, how could our movements have been discovered?"
"I'm afraid some of the 'surrender faction' have already made contact with the Divine Plane. And since this surprise attack plan was top secret, those with access to the intelligence must undoubtedly occupy high positions..."
"What a bunch of bastards, willing to betray their fellow countrymen, to sell out the entire Alchemy Plane, just to save their own skins!"
"There's no point in discussing this now. We'd better think about how to break through..."
"..."
The group of professionals in military uniforms were angrily and excitedly discussing the situation.
What was supposed to be a top-secret surprise attack had turned into an ambush; they knew there must be a mole who leaked their plans.
Sitting at the head of the conference table were two men, a Baldy and a man with a square face.
Neither spoke, their presence exuding a powerful aura without a trace of anger.
Yet as they listened to their staff members, their expressions turned grim.
If Su Lun were here, he would surely recognize Baldy to be Dora's grandfather, the Matriarch Navy Grand Marshal "Lei Tiger" Meredith Ben Moses.
The other man with the goatee and square face was none other than General Rostov, the former commander of the Luying Royal Fleet.
Now nearby, the topic of discussion among everyone was naturally how to break through the encirclement.
But no matter how they analyzed the situation, it was clearly a long-planned ambush by the enemy, leaving them no chance to break through.
"Currently, it appears that at least six Great Magic Legions from the Divine Realm are near us. Judging by the legion flags, they should be the elite legions that breached Cabitrón..."
"It will take at least half a month to arrive here from the closest imperial naval base, and we're afraid we won't last until reinforcements arrive. Besides, waiting for reinforcements may not necessarily be a good thing."
"Yes. The enemy is obviously employing a 'besiege to relieve' strategy... Those fellows intend to trap us while annihilating as many reinforcement fleets as possible. If the imperial main fleet is lured out of port to support us, we'll lose our defensive advantage. If those guys breach our lines, we're doomed."
"..."
All those present were battle-hardened professionals, and the situation was crystal clear to them.
The battle had not yet started, and it seemed as though they were already trapped in a hopeless situation.
After much discussion, they couldn't come to any conclusion.
At the main seats, "Lei Tiger" Meredith and General Rostov exchanged a look, understanding the resolve in each other's eyes.
Having risen from mere soldiers to the rank of marshal, they had been through countless fierce battles and were not ones to shrink back.
They were the decision-makers.
Moreover, the Combined Fleet was composed of elites; even in this dire situation, not a trace of fear could be seen on anyone's face.
In the war between realms where one could be faced with either death or survival, they were prepared to shed their last drop of blood for the cause of civilization.
It was at this moment that "Lei Tiger" Meredith made a decisive decision, his voice resounding clearly, "Continue signaling, notify the empire not to send reinforcements! Scout teams, search for an appropriate naval battle location, and prepare to engage the enemy. Even if we die in battle, we must at least take out a few of the enemy's ten-thousand-strong magic legions with us!"
Upon hearing these words, the staff members all stood up, paying a solemn military salute in unison, saying, "Yes!"
The order was relayed in an instant, and the personnel of the Combined Fleet were also making ready, the entire fleet suffused with a tragic atmosphere.
However, just as the fleet was preparing for a last stand, suddenly, a lookout relayed a most unexpected message, "Attention all, a ship is rapidly approaching us!"
Upon hearing this, everyone assumed it was an enemy attack, and the atmosphere immediately grew tense.
Even the two marshals went up on deck, fully armed, ready for battle.
But the distance was too great, and apart from the reconnaissance teams on the periphery, no one in the fleet could see which ship was approaching.
"Lei Tiger" Meredith, holding a communicator, asked, "How many ships?"
The communication officer replied, "One!"
Meredith was taken aback, "One? What is the situation?"
As if confirming something, the communication officer's voice shook with astonishment, "It's an Emperor-class battleship! It's an Emperor-class sailing battleship!"
Upon hearing this, the whole Combined Fleet was puzzled.
Because the construction craftsmanship of Emperor-class battleships had been lost to time, such dominant battleships from hundreds of years ago now numbered only one in the world.
And that was the one belonging to the Dawn Group!
Sure enough, a scout immediately reported, "Marshal, it has been confirmed as the Eternal Night Emperor! Based on the flag on its mast, it is Dawn Group!"
Upon hearing this, everyone in the Combined Fleet was thoroughly surprised.
They did not expect to encounter the Dawn Adventure Group before the imperial fleet's support arrived.
Could it be mere coincidence?
But this sea area was under military control, and no ships other than those carrying military orders were allowed to enter. Could the Dawn Group have come as reinforcements?
Everyone was now aware of the "Dawn Organization" and naturally knew they were friends, not foes.
But what significance could a single ship have?
The enemy had brought at least six ten-thousand-strong magic legions, and against the several dozen top-tier battleships and more than two hundred thousand troops of their Combined Fleet, they had been at a stalemate. The arrival of the Dawn Group could not change the outcome of the battle.
...
Upon hearing this news, "Lei Tiger" Meredith's expression turned slightly odd, "Dawn Group?"
He immediately thought of that fellow who had "kidnapped, seduced, and extorted" his granddaughter.
Only he knew that Dora was still with the Dawn Group, and their arrival now must surely be to provide support.
Meredith also acknowledged the strength of the Dawn Brigade, noting that Su Lun's methods were not bad either. However, in his recollection, the overall strength of the Dawn Brigade was on par with the adventure groups of the past like the "West Sea Fleet" and the "South Sea Fleet".
On the battlefield of a real large-scale legion, this wouldn't solve anything.
Fearing that the Dawn Brigade was unaware of the current situation and didn't want them to come and die in vain, he quickly gave the order, "Immediately inform them to leave this sea area, do not approach us!"
Communications Officer: "Yes!"
However, not long after this order was issued, the outer scouts relayed new information: "Marshal, we have conveyed your instructions to the Dawn Brigade, but they... they did not leave, instead, they are continuing to sail towards us."
"What?!"
Meredith's face darkened upon hearing this.
What reckless youths, the law brigades of the Divine Plane, each comparable to the power of a ninth-order...
He even thought it was his granddaughter Dora who insisted on coming to rescue her grandfather, and he felt that his granddaughter was too willful.
As their main target was them, and considering the tremendous speed advantage of the sail warships, it was possible they could escape without entering the enemy's encirclement.
Meredith did not want to add casualties to an already hopeless battle, and frowned tightly, "Can you contact them? Tell them not to intervene, this is a military order!"
The Communications Officer relayed this directive, but soon an even more absurd piece of news came: "They said... we are trapped by the enemy's legion magic, going in circles in place. East, South, West, Northeast... from several directions, plus eight brigades of ten thousand law enforcers are encircling us. They also told us to stop and lure the enemy out."
All who could hear this communication were the high-ranking officers of the joint fleet, and upon hearing these words, everyone exchanged puzzled glances.
These old generals, who would not frown in the face of death, now only had expressions of disbelief in their eyes.
The fleet is trapped?
Although they had also begun to vaguely sense it.
But whether true or false, let's not discuss it for now.
The meaning of the latter part of the sentence is, they want us to stop... and act as bait?
A small adventure group, asking them to use their professional fleet of over two hundred thousand as bait?
Absurd, preposterous, naive...
These were everyone's first impressions.
However, just when everyone found it unbelievable, General Rostov showed a thoughtful expression.
He pondered for a moment and then said, "There is a student of mine in the Dawn Brigade, Alek Barrett. He was once the brigade commander of the Sacred Judgment Legion, and he definitely would not make such a low-level mistake on the battlefield. Moreover, they knew that there were eight brigades of ten thousand law enforcers encircling us nearby, information that even goes beyond what we knew..."
The joint fleet had information on six brigades of ten thousand law enforcers, but the other side said it was eight?
If the other side wasn't guessing blindly, then it meant that the Dawn Brigade had better sensing capabilities to confirm this information.
But how could that be?
How could a small adventure group have sensing capabilities that could match theirs, armed with the top-tier warship equipment of the planes?
All these bizarre situations not only failed to reassure anyone, but an eerie feeling swept over everyone's hearts.
Sinister enough to send shivers down one's spine.
Could it be an enemy plot?
Or had they fallen into some sort of higher-order group Illusion Technique?
Upon hearing this, "Lei Tiger" Meredith also showed a contemplative expression, and directly said, "Connect me to their communication!"
"Yes!"
The next second, the communicator was connected.
A young yet stable voice entered his ears, "Marshal Meredith, this is Su Lun, I have met with you before..."
Hearing that voice, how could Meredith not recognize it as the very Su Lun who had extorted his beloved granddaughter?
However, voices can be faked, and no one would completely trust them.
Meredith just wanted to confirm some things.
But before he could speak, the person on the other end of the communicator seemed to realize this.
At that moment, the voice once again came through the communicator, "Forget it, I'll come in person."
Upon hearing this, the high-ranking officers on the deck were all taken aback.
But before they could fully express their surprise, at the same time as these words were spoken, a ripple in space flashed, and a figure had already appeared on the deck of the warship.
Everyone focused and saw that it was Su Lun with a crow on his shoulder, looking composed and young.

chapters.title: Chapter 598 - 597: He Descends Like a Deity
chapters.content:
On the main ship of the joint fleet, a group of soldiers looked at the figure that had appeared out of nowhere, their gazes becoming fixed in astonishment for a moment.
Most of the soldiers did not know the content of the communication between "Thunder Tiger" Meredith and Su Lun, but the sudden appearance at this critical moment clearly indicated a high probability of an enemy presence.
They also reacted instantaneously for combat, with various mechanical warriors' armor clattering and guns instantly aiming, while the floor beneath those in the Magician professions lit up with the glow of Alchemy arrays.
Everyone had a surge of anger, appearing directly on the deck of the legion's main ship, as if there were no one in their alchemical plane.
However, when they got a clear look at the newcomer, nearly everyone's serious expression turned to surprise.
Because they found the face very familiar.
There were many high-ranking officers on the main ship's deck, and many of them had attended the wedding of Fike and Yekaterina. Especially the younger officers, how could they not remember the guy who once made them so jealous that they gritted their teeth?
Even those who had not seen him in person had grown incredibly familiar with his face from the newspapers of the two great empires during the days of the wedding.
And that signature crow familiar.
Fike Regadi?
How could this guy appear here?
Although it was hard to believe, everyone stopped the actions they had been about to execute.
Having recognized the face, "Thunder Tiger" Meredith's eyes twitched inexplicably, also finding it somewhat inconceivable: it really was this kid.
But what shocked him even more was that Su Lun had Teleported here directly and accurately right after their call?
This mechanism was impressive.
It was known that military ships were equipped with various devices to interfere with Spatial Teleportation, and during the call, the Eternal Night was at least far away from the joint fleet. And he had Teleported here directly?
At least of all the Spatial professionals he had seen, none could do it so effortlessly.
Before he could think more, Su Lun smiled slightly, "Long time no see, Marshal Meredith sir."
Although many of these people had seen Su Lun, the only one Su Lun was close with was Old Marshal Baldy.
...
Just half an hour ago, Su Lun had traveled a great distance with the Eternal Night through multiple Teleportations.
After consuming a large amount of Energy Baryte during several Teleportations, they arrived at the Imperial Strait.
Originally, the Imperial Strait was vast, and finding a lost fleet was like searching for a needle in a haystack.
But with Tanni and his mother's sensory abilities, asking the fish in the sea, they easily confirmed an unusual area on the sea surface.
Then they followed it here.
Luckily, they ran into the joint fleet directly.
And they were not too late.
The fleet, although slightly damaged, still had its main forces intact.
"Thunder Tiger" Meredith looked at Su Lun, his expression slightly complex.
He was one of the few who knew that the Dawn Group was entrusted by Master Lucien to carry the seed of mechanical alchemy civilization.
Having not heard any news from the Dawn Group, he thought they had gone to the western barren sea to find a place to establish the "New Land" of alchemy civilization.
It turned out they had been near the Imperial Strait all along?
Seeing the Dawn Group coming to support them, he felt relieved.
But deep in his heart, he did not want to see them here.
Under the current circumstances, even several large imperial fleets might not be able to save them, let alone an adventure group.
Marshal Meredith frowned and asked, "How come you are here, young man?"
Su Lun did not elaborate on the process, but simply responded with a light laugh, "Earlier, we received a message from the Lu Ying side that an imperial fleet had lost contact nearby. We came over to check it out and unexpectedly ran into them."
Hearing this, Meredith's expression did not ease up as he inquired, "Was it Dora who insisted on coming?"
He still thought it was his granddaughter being willful, so his tone was not very pleasant.
Su Lun shook his head. "No. Dora is currently undergoing a full mechanical transformation, and it's not finished yet. You might have to wait a while before you can see her."
Old Marshal was Dora's biological grandfather, so using honorifics was not wrong.
On hearing this, Meredith's eyes visibly trembled, and he sighed softly, "That girl has finally taken that step, huh..."
As a grandfather, while he understood his granddaughter's grand ambitions, he still felt somewhat regretful in his heart.
But obviously, now was not the time for such discussions.
The enemy was on the enclosing path, and the situation could already be described as a matter of life and death.
But Su Lun was not at all anxious.
After all, Dawn Group had already reached the ambush position.
A few ten-thousand-person mage legions were no big threat; it's not like he hadn't killed any before.
But the soldiers on the joint fleet didn't know this and never relaxed their expressions in the face of a formidable enemy.
Su Lun could certainly feel that atmosphere of tragic determination within the fleet.
Meredith did not ask any more trivial questions, instead, he directly said, "Have you come to reinforce us?"
After a pause, he spoke straightforwardly with a grave expression, "The ones ambushing us are the Ten Thousand Mage Legions from the Divine Plane. You might not be quite aware of what a Ten Thousand Mage Legion entails, but it's a terrifying force Comparable in strength to ninth-tier professionals. Without a fleet multiple times larger than the enemy, there is simply no chance of victory... "
To avoid unnecessary panic, the United Empire's official channels had not revealed too much about the terror of a Ten Thousand Mage Legion.
Only those military professionals who had fought them head-on knew.
And only they knew just how desperate a fighting force the "Ten Thousand Mage Legion" could be.
Those mages from the Divine Plane using ten thousand men as a legion could unleash divine prohibitive curses capable of devastation, with no city able to withstand such firepower.
The fall of the entire Mafa region was due to a dozen Ten Thousand Mage Legions pushing forward.
Up until a month ago, they had already breached the imperial capital, Kabitrone.
The Alchemy Plane, lacking in high-end combat power, had few who could stand up to those seventh and eighth-tier mages stacked in the Ten Thousand Mage Legions.
Saying they were consistently pushed back would be an understatement.
This time, after receiving secret intelligence that the Ten Thousand Mage Legion was trying to covertly pass through the Imperial Strait, they had hoped to gather their legions and use the advantage of their ships to launch a surprise attack to bolster their morale. Unfortunately, the information leaked, and instead, they were ambushed.
Leading to their current dire predicament.
....
Old Marshal continued to share his concerns.
Su Lun was in no hurry; he just quietly listened.
Having clashed so many times already, how could he not know the formidable nature of the Ten Thousand Mage Legion?
Because the enemy's encirclement had not yet closed, acting now might scare some away. Therefore, he was not in a hurry and planned to wait until they were closer before capturing them all at once.
Meredith originally said these things intending to persuade the Dawn Organization to prioritize the overall situation and preserve the seed of alchemy civilization by leaving this area.
But as he spoke, he noticed Su Lun's face remained calm, and he began to wonder: How could this young man show no reaction at all?
He looked at Su Lun again, feeling that Su Lun was much stronger than during their last encounter, yet it seemed impossible that he showed no reaction to the mention of the "Legion of a Thousand Mages."
What was the source of this guy's inexplicable confidence?
Meredith thought of something, suddenly changing the topic, and asked, "Has Mr. Jing from your Dawn Organization arrived?"
As he spoke, he immediately added with doubt, "But... wasn't Mr. Jing injured before?"
Without a ninth rank, he could not think of any reason Su Lun would have such confidence.
Su Lun had been listening casually.
But upon hearing this, his expression subtly changed, and he immediately retorted, "Mr. Jing was injured?"
Mr. Jing advancing to the ninth rank did not surprise him, but he was surprised that his own sister had been injured.
Meredith strangely countered, "You didn't know? After Mr. Jing advanced to the ninth rank, he had been in the southern part of Mafa, Zambra Ironfall Province, thwarting the descent of celestial experts from the Divine Plane. But about half a month ago, it is said that a divine will from another world descended, and he was attacked by experts of the Divine Plane, suffering not light injuries. His injury led to the fall of the imperial capital, Kabitrone..."
"..."
Su Lun listened with a furrowed brow.
He truly did not know about this.
Based on the timing, it must have been when the Dawn Organization was still in the waters of Dragon Country.
Su Lun knew all too well his sister's aloof nature; if she could avoid bothering others, she certainly would.
She hadn't mentioned the injury, likely feeling that Su Lun and the others wouldn't be able to help anyway.
Realizing this, Su Lun directly asked through the communicator, "Sister, you were injured?"
On the other end of the communicator, Mr. Jing's calm response soon came, "Yes."
It seemed he had no intention of elaborating.
Su Lun, well aware of his sister's character, wouldn't dig deeper unless she volunteered the information, so he directly asked, "What exactly happened? Is it serious?"
Upon hearing this, Mr. Jing finally responded, "A ninth-rank Sage of Law descended from the Divine Plane, using high-level Holy Light divine power. The injuries are somewhat troublesome and will need some time to heal."
Although spoken lightly, Su Lun knew that if Mr. Jing mentioned needing time to heal, the injuries were indeed serious.
Upon hearing this, his face suddenly turned grim.
He sensed for a moment, and Mr. Jing's location was probably still in the southern part of Mafa.
Su Lun thought for a bit, then said, "Sister, I still have some matters to deal with here. I will come over later. Is it convenient for you there?"
On the other end of the communicator, Mr. Jing didn't refuse, only faintly responding with a "Yes."
...
The entire fleet watched as Su Lun stood there, seemingly "spacing out" for a moment.
Meredith did not understand what exactly was happening, nor did he intrude.
But seeing the suddenly sharp aura of Su Lun, his eyes slightly narrowed, vaguely sensing a strange feeling that even he found unsettling.
Before he could ponder further.
At that time, Su Lun had terminated the communication. Abandoning his previous composure, he spoke of serious matters, "Marshal, you are now trapped by the army's magic from the Divine Realm, under the 'Legion Curse: Mirror Sea'. No matter which direction you sail, you can't escape. In no time, a complete encirclement will be formed, and by then, eight legions of ten thousand mages each will converge to form the 'Octagram Siege Array'. By the time you retaliate, even if the steamships have an equipment advantage, it will still be very passive..."
He wasn't anxious before because he believed the enemy would definitely not give up such a huge opportunity and would eventually fall into the trap.
But now, he was eager to check on Mr. Jing's situation, so he didn't want to delay any further.
A swift battle would be best.
Hearing Su Lun say this, Meredith expressed his doubt, "Octagram Siege Array?"
Su Lun nodded and explained, "Yes. It's a massive battle array formed by eight legions of ten thousand mages each. It's usually used for demolishing fortresses, and its power is tremendous."
The ten thousand mage legions of the Divine Realm were not just independent units; multiple legions could also combine to form a gigantic magical array.
Once formed, the combined fleet's ships, no matter how sturdy, were sitting ducks.
Meredith knew quite a bit about the Divine Realm and had heard a little about this as well.
Realizing the severity of the situation upon hearing Su Lun's explanation, he frowned and asked, "What do you mean by that?"
Su Lun stated calmly, "I think we should stop the ships now and wait for them to come to us for a battle."
As soon as these words were spoken, it stirred up a tempest in everyone's hearts.
...
The conversation between the two did not avoid the senior officers on the deck.
Listening to Su Lun, some showed shock while others displayed skeptical expressions.
Rushing might still offer a chance for a breakout.
Stopping, wouldn't that be waiting for death?
Their understanding of Su Lun was still limited to him being Yekaterina's husband and the crown prince of the Regadi family.
Although he held a high station, the military usually disliked these high nobles who had never been on a battlefield, knew nothing, yet liked to offer impractical suggestions.
Meredith, aware of everyone's thoughts, asked directly, "But if we stop, do we have a chance of winning?"
Su Lun nodded and calmly said, "Yes."
Seeing the doubtful looks on everyone's faces, he added, "When those guys from the Divine Realm surround us, the fleet just needs to focus on defense and counterattack. The rest of the combat, the Dawn Group will handle."
He still said it very diplomatically.
Yet, with those words, the vast steamship fell eerily silent.
Everyone looked at him with expressions of strangeness and skepticism.
Meredith didn't think Su Lun was joking, but he also felt it was impossible.
Out of concern for his comrades' safety, he cautiously asked again, "Have... have other ninth-tier members from the Dawn Group come?"
Su Lun, hearing this, didn't know how to explain.
Under normal circumstances, it would indeed require the presence of a ninth-tier professional or an army of a million to change the course of battle.
But Su Lun couldn't just say that he alone could take on a ten thousand mage legion, could he?
Such a statement would be even less believable.
Strength, after all, is proven in battle, not just talked about.
Su Lun pondered for a moment and simply stated, "Although whichever choice we make, the result will be the same. But stopping now to gather in a defensive formation will reduce many losses for the fleet."
Indeed, that was the case. With the arrival of the Dawn Group, the enemy's fate was already sealed. The only uncertainty now was the casualty ratio between us and them.
But upon hearing this remark, which carried an air of arrogance beyond compare, the expressions on the faces of the soldiers on deck varied greatly.
There were doubts, some found it amusing, others were sarcastic, and some were angry...
But no one chose to believe it.
Because it was simply impossible!
Even Old Marshal Meredith, who could be said to have the broadest knowledge of alchemy, had a frozen expression.
To say he didn't trust Su Lun — his instincts told him Su Lun was not joking.
To say he trusted him — he couldn't gamble the lives of two hundred thousand warriors of the fleet.
The atmosphere of the conversation turned somewhat awkward from that moment.
Su Lun didn't know how to explain further.
But just then, another Marshal, General Rostov, broke the tension.
He pondered for a moment and said, "I think... our fleet can stop fighting too. After all, it can't get worse than it is now."
Sometimes, intuition plays a big part in decisions on the battlefield.
Meredith had the same idea, but since it was a joint fleet, he couldn't decide alone.
Hearing General Rostov speak, he nodded, "Well, if that's the case, let's stop the ships and face the combat."
Now the situation was basically clear. The enemy's aim was to annihilate them and then encircle and help each other.
Stopping to engage in battle would also end the fight sooner.
Perhaps it could even prevent needless sacrifices from reinforcements.
...
Although the crew members had doubts about the incredible reinforcement "Dawn Group," since the two great marshals had ordered, no one objected.
Seven large fleets of over a hundred steam iron vessels slowed down and then assembled into a defensive formation on the sea, waiting for the enemy's arrival.
The soldiers busied themselves at their respective posts.
At that moment, unable to contain his curiosity, Meredith, known as "Lei Tiger," asked, "Su Lun kid, now that the ships have stopped. Can you tell me, do you have any secret trump card? What exactly is your plan?"
He always felt that Su Lun was secretive but confident, surely hiding some powerful trump card.
Listening to the old man's inquiry, Su Lun explained further, "Ah... my plan is just to wait for those enemies from the divine plane to approach, and then take action."
Meredith was expecting to hear some explosive plan, but as he listened, the conversation just ended.
His old face twitched, "That's it?"
"Yes."
Su Lun nodded and then revealed his true thoughts, "That way, when they're all gathered together, it will be difficult for them to escape."
Upon hearing this, Meredith and General Rostov did not know how to describe their mixed feelings.
If someone else had said this, they would have thought the young man was insane.
They must be insane themselves.
To believe such an outrageous plan.
But after the initial shock, as the saying replayed in their minds...
Wait a minute!
Something seemed off.
This guy had stopped the ship, not to repel the enemies but to prevent them from easily escaping?
Was he planning to annihilate the enemy completely?
The two old marshals exchanged glances, feeling a chill in their hearts.
Meredith cast an inquiring gaze, "What do you think?"
General Rostov, understanding the gravity, offered a wry smile, "Honestly, with my knowledge of the world and decades of combat experience, I can't believe such a plan. But I trust her Majesty's judgment. The person she chooses must be extraordinary."
Meredith also reflected, "Yes, Empress Yekaterina is indeed a brilliant monarch with grand visions. The person she picks surely won't be lacking. Moreover, if it weren't for my granddaughter saying this kid was impressive, I wouldn't dare believe such a crazy plan."
The two imperial military leaders spoke softly and then sighed in unison.
They looked again at Su Lun, who maintained his calm and composed demeanor from beginning to end, feeling very complicated inside.
This was even more unbelievable than the dire situations they had faced before.
At this point, all they could do was wait for a miracle to happen.
...
And so, the joint fleet stopped on the sea surface, with vessels arranged into a defensive battle array.
At this time, the peripheral reconnaissance group had already spotted the enemy fleet approaching.
In the distance, Su Lun also saw those civilian sailing merchant ships, some pirate ships, and large fishing vessels.
All of Mafa's shipyards had been destroyed, and all military ships had been dispatched to Luying. Additionally, Mafa's maritime shipping was not very developed to begin with. Hence, those guys from the divine plane didn't find any large ships. They only gathered some small vessels.
But eight massive mage groups had assembled thousands of ships, big and small, from all directions, which looked quite impressive.
Knowing the huge disparity in naval artillery between the two fleets, those from the divine plane began their magic attacks before even entering firing range.
The ocean roared, fierce winds raged, and thunder and lightning filled the sky, creating an apocalyptic scene on the sea...
Several mage groups wielded the formidable power of the elements; Tsunami Technique, Hurricane Technique, Ten Thousand Thunder Strikes... one forbidden-level legion magic spell after another was cast from afar.
Truly, the joint fleet had an absolute advantage in battleship equipment, but compared to the mage groups in manipulating the forces of nature, the fleet's alchemists fell far short.
The naval battle commenced from a great distance.
The sound of cannon fire was incessant, and the forces of the elements grew more violent.
Through the communicator, reports from the forward scout legions came intermittently:
"Marshal, the enemy has stopped fifteen nautical miles from us!"
"Confirmed, there are eight mage legions!"
"Not good, their position... seems like they are preparing some legion magic!"
"..."
Messages kept coming from the periphery.
On the deck, Meredith and General Rostov held a monocular each, looking sternly at the ships at the edge of their vision.
It was indeed eight legions of ten thousand mages each!
They really were preparing a formation!
They only now realized that this completely matched what Su Lun had said before!
All eyes on the ship glanced at the man in black on the deck, a crow resting on his shoulder.
Although the two sides were still far apart, the battle was becoming increasingly fierce.
Yet Su Lun did not take action.
He simply watched quietly.
He was still waiting for the right moment.
He would wait until the enemy's "Octagram Siege Array" became irreversible, then he would move, and by then, the magical backlash would be enough to trouble those guys.
...
The joint fleet, after all, possessed over two hundred thousand elite troops, including the best warship equipment.
Even the gods from the divine plane would find it tough to swallow an easy bite and might break their teeth.
So, those people were not in a hurry, especially since some high-level magics required a long time to prepare.
Ironically, it was while Su Lun was observing the battle that the sky above them suddenly filled with dark clouds, flashing with terrifying red lightning.
And strangely enough, those red lightnings, under the guidance of some mysterious force, rapidly converged into a terrifying thunder dragon!
Su Lun looked up, dismissed it with a glance, and muttered to himself, "Legion Curse: Thunder Dragon... it seems the enemy legion has a very powerful eighth-tier lightning mage."
The response from the major warships was immediate.
"Everyone, be careful! The enemy has conjured a lightning curse!"
"Activate the ninth level defensive aura! Prepare the lightning rods!"
"Magic professionals, steal elements to reduce the enemy's magic power!"
"..."
The joint fleet consisted of elites; they had plenty of experience and didn't need Su Lun's involvement, as the strategists made the best responses.
However, they still found this ninth-tier curse-level legion magic quite challenging to handle.
The lightning in the sky grew more ferocious, striking the ocean and linking the sea to the sky with chains of scarlet veins, turning the world crimson.
The ships had activated their energy shields, and those lightnings hit without causing harm.
But the sea was now filled with masses of electrocuted dead fish.
By then, the thunder dragon in the sky had taken shape, hundreds of meters long, exuding a scalp-numbing draconic might!
Nobody on deck had ever seen a real dragon, nor knew what draconic might was, yet they felt their souls tremble mysteriously, as if the thunder dragon in the sky was pressing down on them, making it hard to breathe.
Even the eighth-tier professionals on the ship were all looking grave.
Only Su Lun remained unfazed, the corners of his mouth slightly lifted in disdain for the dragon's might.
Compared to the dragons he had encountered in the Dragon Country Waters, this level of draconic might was nothing.
Seeing this, his eyes sparkled with light. He glanced at the sky, deduced something, and suddenly felt a slight surprise, thinking to himself, "Hmm... there's actually a hidden epic magical artifact 'Fang of the Thunder Dragon' involved here, quite an interesting item."
Just as this thought surfaced,
suddenly, a loud "crack" resounded!
A thick red lightning bolt streaked through the sky, slashing down as if it would cleave open a rift in space.
This red lightning bolt was aimed directly at the main ship where Su Lun was, hitting with precision!
However, the joint fleet was backed by the royal navy, and the ship was equipped with various alchemical cursed items!
Even such formidable lightning was entirely blocked by the defense shield.
But before everyone could breathe a sigh of relief,
the thunder dragon in the sky flapped its wings, and charged directly towards the main ship.
The bright red glow illuminated the pale faces of everyone, under the terrifying draconic might, they all felt the despair of imminent destruction.
Only Su Lun stood tall and unmoved. Seeing this, he had already seen through the hidden murderous intent of this magic and sneered, "Tsk tsk, so that's your plan... but how could you possibly behead the commander right away!"
With a loud "bang", the Thunder Dragon crashed into the defense shield and exploded.
Even if it didn't penetrate the shield, the massive shockwave made many lower-tier professionals on the ship faint.
They blocked it!
Just as everyone was relieved that the energy shield had blocked this fatal blow,
However,
a sudden turn of events occurred!
What nobody had expected happened.
The exploding Thunder Dragon at the site released an inconspicuous red dragon tooth that, like lightning, pierced through the defense shield and charged directly at Marshals Meredith and General Rostov!
The gods of the divine plane had found some method to lock onto the marshals' positions, but the lightning came in an instant, leaving no room to avoid.
The dragon tooth itself had incredible physical and magical penetration; this epic ninth-tier "Fang of the Thunder Dragon" magical artifact could make the defense of all high-tier mechanical armors virtually useless.
Though this lightning might not kill the two marshals, a serious injury was inevitable.
Watching the red lightning dart toward the two marshals, everyone's eyes widened in shock, but even their personal guards couldn't prevent it in time.
Marshals Meredith and General Rostov looked stern, showing no fear and were already prepared for defense. However, they knew that if they were severely injured, the morale of the entire battle would collapse before it even began.
Just when everyone's hearts were filled with despair,
Suddenly, a miracle happened!
A figure teleported and appeared tens of meters in front of the two old marshals, precisely in the trajectory of that red lightning.
But what followed made everyone's jaws drop in astonishment.
That figure actually... caught the incoming red lightning with his hand.
Got it!
Barehanded!
Seeing this, everyone, including Marshals Meredith and General Rostov, was dumbfounded!
Upon closer inspection, the figure was covered in dragon scales, a terrifying aura more fearsome than the dragon's might instantly swept across the field.
The figure stood proudly, like a divine god descending upon them!

chapters.title: Chapter 599 - 598: One-Man Army
chapters.content:
Su Lun grasped the "Dragon's Tooth of Thunder" in one hand, as if capturing a scarlet thunder serpent.
When he took hold of it, the spiritually endowed thunder serpent struggled, trying to escape.
But Su Lun tensed his muscles and firmly clamped down on it. The thunder serpent couldn't break free, and the massive force of thunder it carried suddenly exploded. A muffled sound like a clap of thunder burst forth, emitting an energy wave as violent as a ninth-tier spell.
Su Lun was prepared, activating his impervious body, with dragon scale runes swirling around him. The exploding thunder serpent emitted countless scarlet thunder lights on the surface of his body, sending a paralyzing sensation throughout his body. He muttered to himself, "Such a powerful high-tier law of thunder..."
But he merely frowned slightly.
After enduring the release of magic power for a moment, the thunder serpent in his hand dissipated, reverting to a dragon tooth about a foot long.
This was indeed a fine epic-quality magic conductor.
After a glance, Su Lun casually stored it in his smaller void realm.
And with this magic conductor, crucial to the formation, taken away, the red thunder in the sky vanished instantly.
The thunderclouds quickly dispersed, as sunlight once again illuminated the sea and the stunned faces of the allied fleet members.
With this single move, Su Lun astounded everyone in the fleet.
This was a legion magic of power comparable to ninth-tier spells... and he just caught it with his bare hands?
It was said that some top eighth-tier alchemists could perhaps withstand such an attack, but catching it barehanded, regardless of whether the combat skills reached that level, how strong must one's body be to endure the eruption of ninth-tier magical power?
Moreover, observing his composed demeanor, it was clear he still had reserve strength.
In the fleet, if anyone witnessed this scene, the impact on their minds was indelible.
After the shock, they looked at Su Lun again, unable to harbor any doubts in their minds.
At this moment, they realized that the Dawn Squad was indeed here to reinforce them.
General Rostov, an old eighth-tier powerhouse, felt a tingling sensation along his scalp from the aura Su Lun had unleashed in that instant.
Ninth-tier?
Clearly not.
Observing the invisible energy layer swirling around Su Lun's body, they knew it was the eighth-tier impervious body.
Yet in the allied fleet, there were several eighth-tier professionals, none of whom felt even slightly confident about catching that earlier legion spell.
'Thunder Tiger' Meredith's eye twitched sharply, as if looking at a monster.
Regaining his senses, he murmured to himself, "So he has become this strong."
Not just strong, but exceedingly so.
This was beyond the level any eighth-tier professional he knew could reach.
They couldn't understand it.
Giant Dragon Gene Potion, Titan Gene Potion, and the knowledge of Alchemical Demigod Sir Isaac from five notebooks including "Dragon Rune Golden Body," "Heart of Alchemy," "Giant's Strength," and the alchemical relic "Philosopher's Stone"...
All of these, unheard of by average professionals except in legends.
Su Lun's combat power now vastly exceeded that of a typical eighth-tier professional.
...
Su Lun also noticed those astonished looks directed at him, but he didn't plan to explain much.
The battle had already begun, and there was no time for lengthy explanations.
Far off, the eight legion mages had taken their positions, forming a vast Octagram Array above the sea.
This was the legion magic "Siege Battle Array," which once completed, could summon a vast range of destructive beams. By then, even the well-armed allied fleet wouldn't stand a chance against such a bombardment.
Unfortunately for them, Su Lun was all too familiar with this legion technique and wouldn't give the enemy a chance.
His eyes detected the massive magic power gathering within the eight magic groups, immediately recognizing that the legion spell was at a critical juncture.
Now was the moment!
He took a step forward, entering a spatial rift, and disappeared from the deck completely.
The members of the allied fleet looked at each other, confusion flashing in their eyes.
What was this?
Their minds were still reeling from the shock of him catching the thunder with his bare hands, and now they saw Su Lun suddenly vanish.
Why would he leave at this critical moment?
Where else could he be if not on the ship, defending and counterattacking?
Could it be...
A possibility sprang up in everyone's mind—a thought they themselves could hardly believe.
They indeed acknowledged Su Lun's strength; his combat power just demonstrated might even match a ninth-tier professional.
But however strong, he was still just one person.
The enemy consisted of eight legion mages!
That type of legion formed into a battle array, solely existing for warfare, was the nightmare of any loner.
However, Su Lun's teleportation speed was faster than everyone's wild guesses.
Before the combined fleet could react and figure out what to do, an absurd scene played out before their eyes once again.
"Look there! At nine o'clock!"
"Oh, what is that?"
"It's puppets! My God, how come there are so many puppets!"
"..."
The very second after Su Lun disappeared, everyone saw a swarm of gargoyle puppets appear out of nowhere above a fleet of ten thousand mages.
The sight was dumbfounding.
In that instant, everyone understood what Su Lun had left the ship to do.
Meredith and General Rostov, the two old marshals, finally understood the true meaning of the plan Su Lun had mentioned earlier.
Although they did not know how he was controlling it, such a massive puppet army... This guy had intended from the start to annihilate the ten thousand mage formation!
Before, they thought his plan was mere fantasy.
Now, seeing this horde of gargoyle puppets that blotted out the sky, everyone felt a surge of hope so strong they could scarcely believe it themselves.
They had not yet recovered from the shock of witnessing Su Lun's combat strength and were once again stunned by the puppet army.
The number... it must be at least tens of thousands!
Those who had heard of Su Lun knew he was a formidable puppet master.
Back in Lyndon, Su Lun had even battled Aubrey Hernandez, the president of the Puppet Masters Guild, when one of his apprentices was kidnapped.
Even then, his puppetry technique had already reached a master level.
But in the eyes of top-notch powerhouses like Meredith and General Rostov, he was merely a young man with promising potential.
However, having not seen him for a year or two, they now saw a drastic transformation.
Not only had he entered the ranks of eighth-tier professionals, but he also possessed such an unimaginably massive puppet army.
...
"Am I seeing things? That... that person... he actually charged directly into the ten thousand mage formation?"
"That's too reckless! The ten thousand mage formation is both offensive and defensive. Even a ninth-tier professional would find it hard to escape unscathed, and he... "
"No, look! He... he broke through! The main ship of the ten thousand mage formation has been destroyed."
"My God, the puppets in the sky have formed into a battle array too! It's unbelievable, those puppets are also unleashing combined attacks!"
"Look, not just in the sky, but in the sea too! And... and mechanical octopuses! Those mechanical octopuses have destroyed the ships!"
"..."
In everyone's astonished gaze, one incredible scene after another unfolded.
They watched as that figure teleported directly into the enemy's headquarters, then rampaged through the equally dumbfounded mages like a destructive storm.
Behind him, the shadow of the grim reaper was almost tangible, his path marked by mages falling like harvested wheat.
At the same time, the puppet army in the sky formed a battle formation, the Nonagram Alchemy Formation lit up, and there erupted a terrifying spatial fluctuation that instantly shattered the fleet's defensive shields. As the shields broke, countless mechanical octopuses extended their tentacles and in moments nearly destroyed the wooden sailing ships.
A combination of moves swiftly breached the ten thousand mage formation's defenses.
Watching the scene unfold, the people of the combined fleet were rooted to the spot.
Was this the same ten thousand mage formation that had forced two great empires into retreat?
How come it seemed as fragile as an eggshell, breaking upon the slightest touch?
At that moment, time seemed to stop because their brains were too shocked to think on their own.
But it felt as though time was also flying because in a blink, the ten thousand mage formation's ships had mostly sunk, and the sea was ablaze.
From the moment that figure disappeared from the deck, it only took a few exchanges to determine the outcome of the battle—it seemed... the fight was already decided.
In the midst of her shock, Meredith couldn't help but murmur to herself, "A single person as a legion... The combat power of a puppeteer is simply too exaggerated."
Hearing her, General Rostov next to her responded, "The glow of dawn will eventually pierce through the darkness... A miracle has truly arrived."
Meredith: "Yes..."
The two old marshals, looking on, found themselves unexpectedly teary-eyed.
They had never feared death, so even in such a dire situation before, they thought only of fighting to the death.
But what they feared was, their defeat might forever extinguish hope for the Alchemical plane.
After the planar invasion, the Alchemical plane seemed to enter an eternal night, continuously losing battles. Seeing the deepening despair was only possible for these front-line career soldiers.
But at this moment, they felt as though they were witnessing the first light of dawn break.
The lone figure who had stormed into the enemy's headquarters had given the entire combined fleet a beam of uplifting light!
....
The people of the combined fleet watched nervously as Su Lun entered the enemy camp alone.
But actually, when he charged into the group of ten thousand mages, his emotions hardly fluctuated.
He had charged through many times before and was already familiar with the process.
Initially, when he was at the seventh rank, controlling a puppet army to kill the group of ten thousand mages carried some risks, and he had to avoid their combination attack technique.
Now, after reaching the eighth rank with a dominant body, he truly had no more concerns.
The group of ten thousand was originally well-balanced in attack and defense, and breaking through would also bring about emergency teams using magic to restrain and counterattack.
But once Su Lun activated his dominant body, he didn't even avoid instant-cast magic from an eighth-rank Grand Magician, instead charging straight through.
He possessed the Second Form of the All-knowing Eye, and almost as soon as an enemy's magic was still condensing, he already knew what the magic was and what level of magic power fluctuation it would be.
Even if there were any high-order magic conductors, at this moment they held no secrets in his eyes.
And the integration into the eighth rank "Descartes' Crystal Skull" made Su Lun's thinking so meticulous that he could almost precisely judge everything.
In battle, there were no mistakes, so it was the enemies who should be feeling despair.
Domain of Death, Soul Intimidation, left hand black scythe, right hand black umbrella...
After breaking into the group of ten thousand, those low-ranked mages within Su Lun's domain burst to death one after another.
Then there was the trump card "Death God's Fire," and even though there were seventh and eighth-rank mages who could withstand it, no one could block him.
Su Lun's eighth rank was different from the others.
Without the suppression of ranks, eighth-rank Grand Magicians had no arrogance left in front of him.
At least such was the case with the ones he encountered.
The only difference was how many moves they could withstand.
Meanwhile, on the other side, after the enemy's methods couldn't cope with Su Lun, it was time for the puppet army to wreak havoc.
As long as he, the controller, didn't die, the combat power of the puppet army was maximized.
He alone entered the enemy's ships, while the puppet army in the sky also simultaneously released their formation techniques. With the Second Form of the All-knowing Eye, he could easily see through the weak points of their battle formations, break their shields, and then start reaping like cutting wheat...
Army against the army, this tactic had already been used very adeptly.
There were also mechanical octopuses in the sea, perfect for breaking ships.
Su Lun knew clearly that army formations required necessary positions to assemble and stable environments for output, and with the ships destroyed, those mages also lost the convenience to continue assembling their formations.
Though not to the extent of drowning, they were one by one awkwardly flying in the sky, struggling on the planks.
Unable to assemble into formations, the gargoyles found it even more convenient to reap.
With Su Lun's intervention, it was almost a one-sided situation.
Aside from him being genuinely strong and capable of overpowering, the more important aspect was the vast gap in intelligence between both sides.
He knew nearly everything about the group of ten thousand, while the enemy knew almost nothing about him.
After a few exchanges, Su Lun had already slain that eighth-rank Grand Magician corps leader.
The remaining group of ten thousand still had many people, but he didn't waste much time on this already broken formation.
Their ships were destroyed, and they had no chance to escape; he would just slowly reap them later.
And in the distance, there were still seven other fully organized groups of ten thousand each!
From the beginning, Su Lun had already thought of such a plan.
After the decapitation, he withdrew the puppet army and teleported again, already appearing in another group of ten thousand.
Then he repeated the old tactic.
Moreover, because the eight groups of ten thousand had been gathering large-scale army magic during the previous surprise attack, Su Lun's interruption at a critical moment caused magic backlash that severely injured many.
So the journey of slaughter was exceptionally smooth.
...
The gods from the Divine Plane were in big trouble now.
Even though they witnessed the annihilation of a ten-thousand strong army, they were helpless.
The only noticeable weak point of a Puppet Master was the controller.
Now, Su Lun was simply not someone any from the Divine Plane could handle.
With him alive, even if the group of ten thousand could unleash various army forbidden curses, they wouldn't be effective at all.
No one expected that the roles of the hunter and the prey would switch so abruptly.
The balance of the war had initially tipped towards the Divine Plane's side, but the drop of a significant chip unexpectedly changed the dynamics of the battle instantly.
The folks from the Divine Plane never anticipated this turn of events.
Originally, even if the Empire of Luying sent reinforcements, it would take them ten to fifteen days to arrive. By then, they would have already engulfed this fleet, potentially dealing with some reinforcements as well.
But now, suddenly, this killer god appeared, and the leaders of several ten-thousand strong armies could do nothing but passively defend.
The progress of the battle was so smooth that even Su Lun himself found it somewhat surprising.
He had thought there would at least be some measures targeting his spatial displacement, or against his puppets.
After all, during the battle in the Dragon Country Waters, he and the Dawn Brigade had exposed almost all of their techniques.
If the enemy had known that information, they would not have been caught so completely unprepared.
But, there was nothing.
It was only after harvesting the souls of those mages that Su Lun realized that these people knew absolutely nothing about him or the Dawn Brigade.
With a bit of thought, he understood why.
The few tens of thousands in formations who had witnessed his techniques were all entirely annihilated, and the only one who survived was that strand of divine will.
Based on Su Lun's current understanding of gods, even if those higher beings were beaten, they wouldn't share their humiliating experiences with lower beings like humans.
To a god, losing a lowly believer is far less important than losing face.
This also made it easier for Su Lun.
He fought through enemy lines, and in the blink of an eye, he had already crushed several tens of thousands in formations.
...
This outlandish scene was witnessed by all on the combined fleet.
Everyone felt that they had never been as shocked in their entire life as they were on this day.
Previously, they had assembled in a defensive formation, ready to fight the enemy to the death.
But the situation had changed dramatically in the time it took to watch this spectacle.
The reinforcements, like a tiger diving into a flock of sheep, single-handedly tore open a gap in the enemy's defenses.
"Marshal, three tens of thousands in formations have been annihilated... At this rate, it won't be long before all eight tens of thousands in formations are destroyed," said one of his commanders.
"Su Lun wants to wipe them all out, first by crippling their ships, making it impossible for them to escape. It's truly unbelievable how one person can drive eighty thousand enemies into a corner, this Puppeteer is just too strong..."
"Yes, really too strong."
"..."
The previously somber atmosphere on the combined fleet vanished in an instant.
All that remained in everyone's hearts were feelings of exhilaration, exhilaration, exhilaration!
Seeing Su Lun hacking through the enemy formations easily, everyone's blood was pumping with excitement.
However, it was then that something unexpected occurred!
On the communication device, watchers suddenly noticed some black dots appearing in the sky, which upon closer inspection, turned out to be gigantic creatures with massive flesh wings.
"Look quick! What is that on the horizon...?" someone shouted.
"Dragonkind?"
"My god, those are real dragons! And the people on their backs, could they be the legendary Dragon Knights? What's happening?!"
"They're attacking the heavenly beings; those Dragon Knights are our reinforcements!"
"..."
Hundreds of dragons arrived simultaneously, with an imposing presence.
It was as though a legion of Dragon Knights from mythological tales had come to life, making everyone feel as if they were dreaming.
The appearance of a god-like Su Lun was shocking enough, and now actual Dragon Knights had arrived?
No one in the combined fleet had ever seen true dragons, and these high-purity sub-dragons closely resembled the dragons described in the books, so they mistook them for true dragons.
They didn't know, these were the flying dragon units from the Dawn Brigade!
Regardless, the arrival of hundreds of flying dragons, like a mythological descent, greatly shocked everyone.
In that moment, the Dawn Brigade, having waited on the outskirts, also made their move!
...
Seeing the Dragon Legion suddenly joining the battlefield, the two old marshals were also astonished.
Meredith murmured, recalling something: "Legend says there are dragons in the Far Western Seas; I never expected it to be true... There had been reports that some time ago the fleets from the West and South Seas were summoned by those from the heavenly realm to the Far Western Seas to seek treasures. Now it seems, the Dawn Brigade also disappeared during that time to go there."
"Yes, I never thought I would see legendary dragons in my lifetime," said General Rostov with a deep sigh, then added, "The Dawn Brigade even has a Dragon Knight corps to help, what great fortune..."
However, Meredith shook his head, "Didn't you notice? Su Lun's presence even overshadows that of the Dragon Knight corps?"
General Rostov: "Indeed. Youth to be feared...
Seeing this, any tension they had felt vanished from their hearts.
It seemed the situation was now secure.
They were not only saved but the enemy was about to be completely annihilated.
Pausing for a moment, General Rostov's eyes flashed fiercely, "Enough of this. Our two hundred thousand troops can't just stand by and watch the show."
Meredith nodded and gave the command, "All forces attack! Charge and annihilate the enemy!"
At the command, the eagerly waiting soldiers manned their ships and charged toward the scattered enemies across the sea surface.

chapters.title: Chapter 600 - 599 We Are the Dawn
chapters.content:
The might of the magicians from the Divine Plane lies in their magic formations; once these formations are broken, their combat power plummets dramatically.
Su Lun was like a sledgehammer, brutally smashing the solid turtle shells of the ten-thousand-man formations, and what remained was all too easy to handle.
When the joint fleet saw this opportunity, how could they not seize it?
Hundreds of steam-powered ironclad ships charged towards those scattered magical formations.
The time for counterattack had come!
The defensive formation of the ten-thousand-man formations was broken and their wooden ships were destroyed by mechanical octopuses, presenting the perfect opportunity for an assault.
The remaining magicians, severely hit, quickly regrouped into five-hundred-man and thousand-man teams to stubbornly hold their ground.
But to such small formations, the alchemical cannonballs were not impenetrable shells.
"Boom," "Boom," "Boom"...
The deafening sound of cannon fire erupted, as countless alchemical cannonballs fell, shattering the sea's magical shields into fragments.
"Hahaha, we've broken through! We've shattered those magicians' military formations!"
"To hell with them!"
"Lieutenant General Cook, have your Third Fleet encircle from the left flank; Suzanna Winning, lead the Seventh Fleet to penetrate the central line and divide the enemy; Major General Barbara, take the Sixth Fleet... All forces, attack—don't let those enemies escape!"
"Yes!"
"..."
An unprecedented enthusiasm erupted among the joint fleet, as all soldiers charged fearlessly towards the enemy.
After many harsh battles with the forces from the Divine Plane, only today's fight was truly satisfying.
All the frustrations and grudges of the past were finally being vented.
Normally, when facing a ten-thousand-man formation, the best tactic would be to first deplete the enemy's magical shields with cannonballs, and then attack when a breach appeared.
But this method of attack was inefficient, time-consuming, and costly.
Usually, during this process, the enemy's legion magic would have already been cast several times.
The longer the stalemate, the greater the power of the prepared legion magic, and some forbidden spells could deliver devastating blows upon release.
Therefore, in an exchange of firepower, it was the Empire's army that typically suffered losses.
To stand a chance of victory, generally one would need several times the number of men as the enemy, and the expenditure of a large number of high-tier alchemical rounds to have a possibility of annihilating a ten-thousand-man formation.
But now, things were different!
Because Su Lun had broken the ten-thousand-man formations' magical shields, the joint fleet easily infiltrated the enemy's ranks and began close combat.
When mages of equal rank faced the alchemical plane's professionals and mechanical warriors, there wasn't much advantage to speak of.
And so, fierce battle erupted on the open sea.
...
On the main ship of the joint fleet, Meredith and General Rostov watched the unfolding battle with rapt attention.
The two old marshals could hardly contain their excitement.
The outcome of the battle was already clear.
This was destined to be a resounding victory.
And this battle held extraordinary significance!
The Empire, having faced consecutive defeats, needed this victory badly.
A decisive victory at sea would undoubtedly boost the morale of the Empire's soldiers tremendously.
Moreover, these eight ten-thousand-man formations constituted the main active force of the Divine Plane near the Imperial Strait. Their annihilation would alleviate the defense pressure on the Imperial Strait for a significant period.
Furthermore, with their ships destroyed, it would be difficult for them to gather the large vessels needed to cross the strait anytime soon.
The pressure that had been suffocating the alchemical plane could finally ease.
But most importantly, the old marshals saw a deeper meaning in the Dawn Group before them.
This was not just an adventure group; it was the hope of alchemical civilization!
...
However, this hope was not solely Su Lun.
As they looked on, the expressions of the joint fleet's soldiers stiffened with shock.
Following Su Lun's godlike descent, the Dawn Group made their appearance.
The sea emperor-class sailing battleship moved with unparalleled speed in this era.
Everyone watched as the sailing warship, riding the giant waves, forcefully entered the battlefield.
The domineering manner of its entrance left everyone in awe.
But in a large-scale, legion-level battlefield, normally only a legion itself is qualified to stand firm. Everyone in the joint fleet thought that a single ship, an adventure group, would not impact the overall situation.
However, to their surprise, the moment the black sailed warship appeared, it charged straight towards a fully assembled ten-thousand-man formation.
"This is bad, they're going to collide with the enemy's legion magic!"
"Quick! Provide fire support for them!"
"..."
The joint fleet watched in great urgency.
Even with their force of over two hundred thousand, they had conservatively chosen to attack the ten-thousand-man formations that Su Lun had disrupted.
Yet the Dawn Group, which was not a professional fighting legion, foolishly charged at the enemy's well-organized formations?
And despite the obvious reconsolidating legion magic, they did not attempt to dodge?
The black sailed warship moved rapidly, and in an instant, the two forces were about to engage in close combat.
But the distance was too great, and aside from providing cannon fire support, the joint fleet could do little to help. Moreover, with both sides so close, the cannons risked inflicting friendly fire.
"That's the legion's forbidden spell, 'Sacred Judgment of the Grand Sun'!"
"No good, that legion magic is coated with alchemical film. If they take this hit, the Dawn Group's ship might be destroyed!"
"They are being too careless... Now that the enemy's legion magic has been successfully consolidated, their ship is too big to evade it..."
"..."
The combined fleet watched as a "mini sun" suddenly formed in the sky above the ten-thousand strong mage formation; they knew all too well what spell this was.
The legion magic "Great Sun Holy Light" could use light elements to converge into an extremely high temperature, shining upon the target and even easily melting steel warships into molten iron.
They had already suffered losses in previous battles, so each of them watched, with hearts full of concern for the Dawn group.
Just when they thought Su Lun would teleport over to create a breakthrough, another jaw-dropping scene unfolded.
Elsewhere on a distant battlefield, Su Lun was controlling his puppet legion to heavily damage another ten-thousand mage formation, showing no intention of going over to help.
This left everyone in the combined fleet puzzled.
Even the two old marshals were watching with tightly furrowed brows.
Although they had recognized Su Lun's overwhelming strength, it couldn't possibly be... Could an adventure group really withstand an attack comparable to a ninth-tier ten-thousand mage formation?
However, before they could ponder further, they saw the sky above the Eternal Night ship also light up with the glow of the Nonagram Alchemy Formation.
Was the Dawn group also condensing a legion formation?!
At this, everyone understood what was happening, but they couldn't quite believe it.
After all, in all these years on the alchemy plane, there had never been a true ten-thousand magician group.
But the reality was right before their eyes!
It was in that instant that the "mini sun" in the sky of the divine realm had already reached its peak brightness, suddenly emitting a light beam several tens of meters in diameter.
The scorching beam seared the sea surface, steaming it white. In the blink of an eye, it streaked across several nautical miles, creating a huge white column of light on the sea.
Such swift attack left no chance for evasion!
Yet, instead of watching a scene of the ship being destroyed and the crew perishing, they saw the light beam that should have pierced the ship's hull, unexpectedly being reflected back!
Aboard the Eternal Night, a black-robed old man wearing an eyepatch suddenly raised his hand, and the condensing Nonagram Formation abruptly turned into a massive ice crystal mirror.
It was this mirror that reflected the white light back.
"This is... mirror reflection!"
"This seems like a variant of the eighth-tier ice series secret technique "Absolute Mirror". My God, how did they do it?"
"This is very ingenious elemental reversal... That black-robed magician is quite powerful. This move, I can't think of any eighth-tier professionals I know could manage. Yet he seems to have not even reached the eighth tier, his strength is truly bewildering..."
"I recognize that black-robed magician. He was on the wanted notice issued by the Rafaels before, seems to be an important member of the Dawn group, named... Mr. Hei!"
"..."
Seeing this countermeasure, the crew of the combined fleet were overjoyed, and couldn't help but marvel at the ingenuity of the response.
However, they couldn't fathom how someone would dare to respond in such a way!
To reflect a legion technique with power comparable to the ninth-tier, it required not just equivalent strength but also the prediction of timing, data calculation, energy control, precise release... The factors involved were extremely complex.
Such a feat demanded a terrifying ability to calculate instantly.
Even the slightest error could lead to the destruction of the ship and the loss of life.
Therefore, even if someone could think of this method, they would definitely not dare to execute it.
But the black-robed magicians of the Dawn Brigade did just that!
And they blocked it perfectly!
Before everyone could marvel at this divine counter-spell, they saw the beam of white light instantly reflecting back.
This destructive beam had the power to devastate any warship, even more so those divine vessels from the heavens.
As soon as the beam struck, the legion's magical shield stiffened for a moment, then was immediately pierced through, creating a massive hole.
In the blink of an eye, several medium-sized ships, including the flagship, disappeared into ashes in the light beam.
Seeing the flames erupt in the distance on the sea surface, the hearts of the allied fleet's crew, which had been hanging by their throats, now fell back into place.
Following that, a wave of euphoria set in!
So we've broken through!
The Dawn Brigade, using the same legion spell, had broken through a group of ten thousand mages.
In the eyes of those high-ranking officers, this was not just a breakthrough but a giant leap for the alchemy realm.
Meredith's voice trembled slightly with excitement, "It's incredible, the Dawn Brigade actually has a fully functional group of ten thousand magicians. This... this really is a huge surprise for us. Hahaha... we alchemists can now have our own groups of ten thousand mages too!"
He laughed, tears streaming down his face.
With these words, General Rostov beside him became excited as well, saying, "Yes."
He knew too well the significance of this battle, murmuring, "Before, the Royal Academy was still studying those legion formations from the heavenly realm, wondering whether we could condense our own alchemist legion formations to resist foreign enemies. It was a pity that due to the lack of intelligence, everything was still in the early stages. Compared to the countless years of experience of magical groups from the heavenly realm, we were far too lacking... but now the Dawn Brigade has given us a huge surprise. This is the experience of a fully matured magical group. Once the Imperial Legion manages to master those battle formations, they'll be able to replicate groups of ten thousand mages. Although we can't create many groups, by gathering the strength of the entire Unified Empire, we could form a few dozen teams.
