By then, when we face groups of ten thousand mages in direct combat, we won't be at such a disadvantage..."
The senior officers were thrilled at this proclamation.
Only they knew how brutal and despairing the previous battles were.
Facing groups of ten thousand mages, they had to sacrifice many times, even tens of times, the number of lives to contend, not to mention the horrors of such scenes.
And now, the alchemy realm finally had the means to respond!
...
Seeing this, the people of the allied fleet finally understood where the Dawn Brigade's confidence came from when they faced the ten thousand mages head-on.
However, aside from their collective strength, the high warriors of the Dawn Brigade also opened the eyes of the others.
"Good heavens, that Sword Qi is terrifying, that swordsman actually severely injured a group of a thousand mages with a single strike!"
"A sword that breaks a thousand spells... Could he be a master of the legendary 'Sword God Realm'? Snowflakes fluttering in the sky... The sword in his hand, could it be the second-ranked among the Twelve Master Craftsmen Famed Swords, '[Jiachiqinghua Light Whisper]'? It can't be that swordsman from Black Sam's pirate crew, can it?"
"Look up there, there's a Golden Angel in the sky! Oh, she's actually withstanding the legion's magic and remains unharmed!"
"That Golden Angel is the 'Number Nineteen Lady' from the Dawn organization. Watch closely, this is the pinnacle of mechanical warriors' combat power. Our mechanical warriors are second to none!"
"Haven't you noticed, the waves are aiding the Dawn Brigade? They must have an extremely powerful sea sorcerer among them."
"That is an eighth-order vampire, oh, 'Blood Duke' Moore Wazhuaz has actually reached the eighth-tier."
"Those giants of over ten meters on their ship..."
"..."
One by one, the high warriors of the Dawn Brigade revealed themselves, launching into the enemy ranks.
After the adventure in the Dragon Country Waters, the high-ranking professionals of the Dawn Brigade had all strengthened by one or two entire ranks. And although their power was not as exaggerated as Su Lun's, gene potions and dragon armaments had given everyone the strength of the top of their respective ranks.
It could be said that any of the Dawn Brigade's seventh-rank combatants were not the least bit inferior to the once famous "Top Ten Legendary Bounty Hunters" of the Emperor Luying's empire.
With this appearance, the high-level combatants were in the limelight.
Not only did their legion crush the opponents, but their high-end combat power did, too.
The ten-thousand-member mage formation was continuously beaten back in the face of the Dawn Brigade.
Although the rest of Dawn and the Combined Fleet had heard of them through various channels, they were not familiar with them.
But there was one person that many recognized.
Just then, someone spotted a burly figure rampaging through the ten-thousand-member mage formation and exclaimed.
"Look, you guys, that... that seems to be Captain Barrett?"
Barrett was once the captain of the "Sacred Judgment Legion," affiliated with the Royal Knight Legion.
Moreover, he graduated from the Royal Military Academy, and many people in the Combined Fleet were his former classmates and comrades-in-arms.
"I heard that guy was promoted to the seventh rank before. But how has he become so strong now?"
"Yeah. Barrett's combat power is so exaggerated; this is still the seventh rank? Saying he's almost the eighth rank wouldn't be far off."
"Didn't you notice that Barrett's body has grown a lot bigger?"
"Back in the academy, that guy and I were about the same. What on earth has he been through these past few years to have gained two whole rank levels over me?"
"..."
Those who recognized Barrett looked at one another, their faces reflecting shock, confusion, and... envy.
The people of the Sacred Judgment Legion were indeed carefully selected knights, but even so, they hadn't seen each other in a year or two; the gap couldn't have grown that much, right?
This increase in strength truly left people feeling that they had no hope of catching up.
Even General Rostov, who was Barrett's former teacher, was pleased but also incredibly surprised: "How did that kid become so strong?!"
There were many seventh-rank professionals in the Combined Fleet, but as they looked around, they realized that they had no chance of winning against any of the seventh-rank members from the Dawn Brigade.
Not only Barrett, but a significant portion of the backbone of the Dawn Brigade were former Royal Knights of the Sacred Judgment Legion.
The more people began to scrutinize, the more familiar faces they recognized.
But it was precisely because they recognized them that they felt even more surprised.
How could the gap be so big between them and their former classmates, whom they were once comparable to?
Visibly, they were one or two whole rank levels behind, not to mention the difference in equipment and enhancements!
When they fought, the radiance of their treasures was blinding.
Gold quality, dark gold... even legendary!
All sorts of high-rank cursed items were used as if they were free of charge, one or even several per person, pummeling those mages without mercy.
"My god, their equipment is too good, isn't it? Did I see every one of those guys carrying a gold-quality cursed item?"
"Yeah. Their enhancement grades are terrifyingly high, too."
"And the mechanical warriors. Aren't those laboratory-level equipment from our Mafa? How come it's already equipped on their ships when the empire's most advanced warships don't have them yet?"
"..."
The Combined Fleet truly envied them.
But something felt off the more they thought about it.
They were supposed to be the empire's most elite fleet, so how could a civilian adventure group have better equipment than them?
If it was just one or two individuals, that would be one thing, but the average equipment of the entire "Dawn Brigade" was far better than theirs!
Meredith smiled with satisfaction upon seeing this, "It seems they've had great fortune in the Far Western Seas."
General Rostov also agreed, "Only by surviving that legendary, fatal Far Western Seas could their strength be explained."
The atmosphere of the battle had lost all tension.
All that was left was to reap the rewards.
...
This strange and unpredictable sea battle lost all suspense after the Dawn Brigade's strong intervention.
Su Lun had not taken action earlier on purpose; he was waiting for the eight ten-thousand-member mage formations to get close enough so they had no chance of escape.
And just as he had anticipated, Su Lun broke through five of the mage formations, leaving the rest to the Dawn Brigade and the Combined Fleet to handle.
After that was the complete encirclement and slaughter at sea.
Without their ships, the divine plane mages, except for a few who excelled at escape techniques, were essentially fighting a losing battle.
The only one whom Su Lun found slightly troublesome was the overall commander of the Holy Army.
That was the eighth-rank great mage who had almost beheaded the two marshals of the Combined Fleet with his lightning spells.
However, after some time, Su Lun successfully dispatched the man as well.
With the situation under control, all that remained was to mop up the remnants and clear the battlefield.
Su Lun did not plan to linger there any longer; he teleported to the main fleet, greeted the two old marshals, and then left.
He was going to Mr. Jing's place to check on his sister's injuries as well.
...
After Su Lun left, the battle continued for most of the day before ceasing almost entirely.
The Combined Fleet had over two hundred thousand people, so there was no need for the Dawn Brigade to be involved in clean-up.
Soon after, the ship Eternal Night headed for the Combined Fleet's flagship.
As his mentor was on board, Barrett naturally paid a visit.
Not only for the teaching grace he had received but when the Bonaparte royal family had colluded with the Evil God and he and the Sacred Judgment Legion were denationalized and wanted, it was General Rostov who had gone through various channels to save some of the family members of the Sacred Judgment Legion.
And now that Barrett was the vice-captain of the Dawn Brigade, he also represented the Dawn Brigade.
He and a few core members of the Dawn Brigade boarded the ship.
"Barrett, long time no see!"
"Tegus, it's been years. How did you become so strong?"
"Oh, I watched your battle just now; it was truly unbelievable."
"..."
Barrett and the core members of his group had many acquaintances in the combined fleet, and there was no awkwardness after boarding; everyone received a warm welcome.
It was not just the warmth of old friends meeting, but also gratitude.
Everyone knew that without the Dawn Group's reinforcements, their combined fleet of over two hundred thousand might have been doomed in these waters.
General Rostov said, "I really owe you one for before. Without the Dawn Group, our combined fleet would have probably taken a big tumble this time."
With those words, he suddenly stood up straight as an arrow and gave Barrett a very solemn military salute, saying, "On behalf of the empire, and these two hundred thousand soldiers, I extend the most genuine thanks to the Dawn."
At that military salute, including Old Marshal Meredith, all the soldiers on the main ship's deck saluted in unison.
The atmosphere suddenly turned solemn and fiery.
Seeing his own mentor and everyone's military salute, Barrett also responded with a solemn and respectful salute.
...
After the Dawn Group boarded the ship and observed closely, the people of the combined fleet realized just how extraordinarily strong these individuals were.
Having been oppressed by the might of dragons all this time, they all carried an aura of fearlessness.
Although not many boarded, the aura they unintentionally emitted was enough to make the eighth-rankers on the deck feel a chill down their spines.
And up close, that visual impact was even more direct.
They noticed that the members of the Dawn Group, led by Barrett, were uniformly over three meters tall and significantly more robust than the average magician.
As fellow alchemists, the combined fleet's personnel knew well that this must surely be the result of gene potion modifications.
And looking at this situation, it was definitely a high-quality gene potion that provided such enhancement.
There were also some with horns and scales, clearly signs of incomplete fusions from bloodline potions.
Then looking at the flying dragon troupe on the Evernight, they were most likely enhanced with the Dragon Blood Gene Potion.
It wasn't just one or two people, but everyone had undergone gene modification, which meant that the Dawn Group controlled the technology to mass-produce gene potions!
Although it was unbelievable, this was something not even the imperial military had mastered.
But there it was, right before their eyes.
After a brief exchange of pleasantries, General Rostov, with a flash of a strange expression, took the initiative to speak.
He knew that he was the most appropriate to make such a request, "I have an impolite request... I would like to ask whether it's possible for your group to conditionally transfer the Combination Attack Technique and gene potions? Of course, the empire is willing to pay a substantial price."
Whether it was the Combination Attack Technique of the ten thousand magicians or the gene potions, these were technologies that could be replicated!
If the Dawn Group was willing to transfer this knowledge, the military strength of the combined empire could leap to a higher level in an instant.
This would have far-reaching significance for the plane wars!
It could even change the course of the war to a certain extent, saving countless lives from death!
Alchemists have always believed in equivalent exchange, and the military wouldn't take advantage of an adventure group.
After all, they knew that the Dawn Group must have exchanged their lives for these opportunities.
So, paying a price for resources was a given.
Upon hearing this, everyone in the combined fleet turned their gaze to Barrett and his group.
The request was indeed quite impolite.
After all, they had just been saved by these people, and now they were asking for their secrets; it didn't seem very honorable.
But in the face of the greater good of civilization, General Rostov was ready to put his old face and any personal feelings on the line to make an attempt.
However, what no one expected was that Barrett seemed to have anticipated this request.
Upon hearing it, he laughed and said directly, "Teacher, I was actually just about to discuss this matter. Our Dawn Group indeed has the 'Giant Dragon Gene Potion', 'Titan Gene Potion', and others like the 'Behemoth', 'Elf', 'Griffon' amongst many mythical creature gene potions... as well as some ancient alchemy manuscripts and secret techniques. These were what we gained from our venture to the Far Western Seas..."
As he listed the Dawn Group's treasures like an inventory, the expressions of the combined fleet were extraordinarily animated.
Most of the people on the main ship were high-ranking officers who had seen the world.
But hearing the names of those mythical creature gene potions, their eyes widened in shock, barely concealing their anticipation.
My God, there were so many!
No wonder the entire Dawn Group was so strong!
Continuing, Barrett said, "Su Lun Jue, the leader of our group, had already instructed us that these technologies and knowledge will be provided to the imperial military and the Alchemy Guild without any charge. Now that the planar pathway is established and the planar law's upper limit keeps rising, this is also the best opportunity for advancement. With the aid of gene potions, we can quickly create a large number of mid-level combatants. And this is also the basis for the ten thousand magician army..."
This was something the Dawn Group had discussed early on.
The alchemical plane had reached a critical juncture, and it was not the time to remain complacent.
Moreover, they were never afraid of leaking things like gene potions.
Because the heavenly plane was a plane of divine belief where even if they got their hands on these technologies, they would consider them "heresy" and "sacrilege to the powers of the gods," and erase them instead of using them.
On the contrary, the more widely alchemy was spread, the further the seeds of civilization were sown.
Someday, some of these seeds would grow into towering trees.
Furthermore, they were only providing finished technological formulas, not the detailed research data, so there was no fear of sabotage by ill-intentioned individuals.
What?
Provided without charge?
Upon hearing this, the two old marshals and all the senior officers of the combined fleet straightened up, fully aware of the significance in those words.
General Rostov's expression became complicated for a moment.
At that moment, thousands of words of gratitude seemed so colorless.
He saluted again, his voice resonant, "Thank you, gentlemen, for your selfless contribution to civilization!"
The people behind him followed with a salute.
At that moment, the vast deck of the ship was so quiet you could hear a pin drop. The sudden good news energized everyone in the combined fleet, their eyes shimmering with endless anticipation for the future.

chapters.title: Chapter 601 - 600: Great Victory
chapters.content:
It was when the combined fleet of the Imperial Strait and the godly plane's Mage Council were locked in fierce battle that Lingdun City, now the capital of the United Empire, was bearing witness to these events.
At number 19 on Holy Radiance Avenue resided the mansion of Duke Reginard Roberts, known as "Duke of Misty Mountain."
Once, the Roberts family was one of the six Senior Councilors of the Luying Empire, and now, Archduke Roberts held the position of Minister of Military Affairs for the United Empire.
Half a month ago, the Empire's secret intelligence agency received confidential information: Mages from the godly plane were planning to secretly cross the sea. The Empire's command center immediately made a decision, dispatching the combined fleet led by Marshals Meredith Ben Moses, nicknamed "Thunder Tiger," and General Rostov to set sail in secret and launch a surprise attack on their port while the enemy's fleet was still convening.
Should the surprise attack prove successful, not only would it greatly delay the invasion of Luying by those from the godly plane, but it would also provide a substantial boost to the morale, which was otherwise flagging.
Although the risk was significant, it was a gamble that had to be taken.
However, they hadn't expected that, just last night, disastrous news arrived.
The combined fleet lost contact before they even reached the predetermined waters.
People speculated that perhaps they had encountered a storm, or perhaps a special magnetic field... and temporarily lost contact.
But Archduke Roberts, one of the decision-makers of the entire surprise attack operation, was plagued by an increasingly ominous premonition that the fleet might have been ambushed.
To cause a disappearance of a well-equipped fleet of more than two hundred thousand, one need not think hard to know that the only ones capable of such a deed were the foes from the godly plane.
Such a top-secret plan was not known by many within Luying, yet it still got exposed beforehand, which was quite mystifying.
And this situation also meant that a significant issue might have arisen among some high-ranking individuals within their own ranks.
It was noon, and the sun was shining brightly.
In the manor's garden, with his goatee, Archduke Roberts was sipping coffee, his gaze on the sea charts he had been studying all night, the furrows of worry between his brows never dissipating.
At that moment, a handsome young man in a crisp military uniform walked into the garden from afar and said with concern, "Father, you haven't rested all night. I think you should get some sleep rather than drink more coffee."
This was Alexis, the eldest son of the Roberts family.
Archduke Roberts, looking at his son, finally allowed a trace of a smile to appear on his face.
He didn't respond to the comment about the coffee; instead, he asked, "Alexis, when are you planning to hold your wedding with Kama?"
As if they had a silent agreement, Alexis didn't answer the question but instead started talking about another matter, "Father, I've come to bid you farewell. I've decided to join the reinforcement fleet heading to the Imperial Strait. We sail tonight."
Upon hearing this, Archduke Roberts was not particularly surprised.
He had watched his son grow up; how could he not know what he was thinking? He simply said, "Your mother's opinion is..."
Before he could finish, Alexis, thinking his father wanted to persuade him otherwise, interrupted, "No, Father, my mind is made up. I am an officer of the Empire, and our Roberts family is part of the Alchemy civilization. We, the former grand nobles, have the best resources and the best equipment. In such a civilization's disaster, no matter what, I shouldn't be shrinking back. I should be on the front lines of the battlefield now!"
His words were resolute and filled with conviction.
Hearing this, Archduke Roberts looked at his son with eyes full of pride, "You are truly worthy of being the eldest son of the Roberts family. But I wasn't trying to persuade you."
After pausing, he continued, "What I meant to say is, it would be best to hold the wedding before you go to the front lines. Such a fine lady, you can't let her down..."
Alexis, upon hearing his father's words, showed a hint of a reaction and replied, "I've asked Kama about it. She said that with the Empire in crisis, a modest ceremony will suffice. I've also told her about my decision to go to the front lines, and she supports it."
"Hmm," was all Archduke Roberts said, with no further commentary, "then take care."
If the mansion collapses, no one will remain unscathed.
Moreover, as the eldest son of the Minister of Military Affairs, he could not shrink back during such a sensitive time.
Alexis nodded, "I understand, Father."
...
The father and son were chatting in the garden when, all of a sudden, a figure flickered in the courtyard, adding a shadow from seemingly nowhere.
Being able to evade the manor's guards, this person was clearly a highly skilled assassin.
Archduke Roberts's gaze sharpened slightly, as if he was not surprised, and remained calm.
Alexis, however, frowned deeply, looking at this uninvited guest and asked coldly, "Who are you?!"
The newcomer did not lift the hood, exuding a cold and mysterious aura like a Poison Snake.
He addressed the father and son, his voice chilly, "Who I am is not important. What is important is that I can bring a piece of news that you, Archduke, might be very interested in."
Hearing this, Archduke Roberts's expression flickered briefly, as if he guessed the identity of the visitor, and replied indifferently, "Oh? Let's hear it."
The mysterious person seemed to smile upon seeing the interest of the Archduke and said, "I can responsibly inform you of an intelligence, that the combined fleet is destined not to return. I hear your son is heading to support the front lines... Consider this news a word of caution."
Upon hearing this, Archduke Roberts had yet to reply when Alexis's complexion changed drastically, and a surge of anger rose within him.
This man's words were certain... the fleet had been ambushed!
Indeed, there were traitors among them; someone had leaked the fleet's surprise attack plan to those from the godly plane.
And this person before him was one of those traitors!
Initially wanting to summon the manor's guards to capture and interrogate this intruder, a glance at his father made him suppress his fury and remain in place.
Archduke Roberts, listening, remained calm and composed. After pondering for a moment, he simply asked, "Are you a member of the 'Heaven's Eye Sect'?"
The mysterious person seemed to laugh, "Duke, who I am is not important. What matters is that I can offer you some advice."
Archduke Roberts glanced at him, "Oh?"
The mysterious person then spoke, "If the Duke is willing to cooperate, someone else will discuss the details with you later. Of course, you must have guessed that I am but a minor character, whereas behind me is a power nobody in this plane can resist. So I can assure you, once you agree to cooperate, you and your Roberts family will remain safe and sound."
Archduke Roberts, upon hearing this, laughed, "Tsk tsk... I am curious, traitor alchemists who surrendered and became slaves, do you people really not feel any shame at all?"
Hearing this, the mysterious person's tone became murderous, "Are you refusing?"
Archduke Roberts, not in the least bit intimidated, has already guessed the identity of his visitor and scoffed instead, "The once Legendary Bounty Hunter 'Thief Emperor' Carlo Meldis, has become a slave to the foreign gods' sect, how laughable."
Continuing, he said, "If I were you, I'd run fast. Maybe you could cling to life for a few more days. Tsk tsk, a seventh-tier assassin, do you really think you can go wherever you want in Lingdun?"
With these words spoken, the mysterious person also seemed to sense something, his expression under the hood changing drastically.
He didn't dare delay, his figure already fading into transparency.
However, before leaving, he did not forget to threaten, "Hmph, you don't know what's good for you! You and your family will regret your decision today!"
Archduke Roberts did not attempt to stop the other from fleeing, his expression still indifferent, but with a hint of contemplation in his eyes.
...
Luying and Mafaxi had now formed a united empire. After Empress Yekaterina's enthronement, she carried out a series of sweeping reforms.
One could say that the overall power of the United Empire now is much stronger than during the era of the Bonaparte royal family.
With the Imperial Strait as a natural moat, even the gods from the heavenly plane would find it impossible to dismantle the alchemy civilization in a short time.
Therefore, Archduke Roberts was not the least bit surprised to find himself approached by someone.
As the Minister of Military Intelligence, he controlled information and resources that could be equated to the lifeblood of nearly half the empire. The enemy would naturally not overlook such a loophole.
Watching the enemy flee, Alexis asked, "Father, aren't we going to chase him?"
Archduke Roberts shook his head as if everything was under control, "He won't escape. His Majesty the Emperor had already guessed that someone would come knocking at this critical moment, preparations were made in advance."
Alexis: "His Majesty the Emperor?"
"Yes, His Majesty has control over the largest intelligence organization, the Military Intelligence Division. He would certainly be aware of the situation in Lingdun."
Archduke Roberts, with a flash of something unusual in his eyes, spoke.
Although Empress Yekaterina once had to call him uncle, he had to admit she was a convincing sovereign.
He couldn't help but reflect, "Empress Yekaterina is the most talented monarch I have ever seen, a hundred times better than Queen Charlotte. If she remains in power, it won't be long before the alchemy civilization will enter an unprecedented golden age. It's a pity that the plane invasion came so suddenly, this situation is difficult to handle..."
Alexis also looked pensive for a moment.
After all, Yekaterina was still his junior from his first term. He never imagined she would become such a capable emperor.
However, the empress's resolve and boldness were widely recognized, and this was also why the empire could remain stable during these times of crisis.
Obviously, now was not the time to be contemplative. Alexis, after a moment of thought, asked again, "Father, are you saying that guy just now was from the 'Heaven's Eye Sect'?"
To the Roberts family, a bounty hunter, even one with the famed title of one of the "Top Ten Legendary," was no big deal.
By contrast, the power behind him was of crucial importance.
"Of course," said Archduke Roberts with a complex expression. "Queen Charlotte's Faith Freedom Act not only led to the invasion of the heavenly plane but also left behind some followers of the outer gods. We didn't completely eradicate them at the time, and now the consequences have surfaced. What's worse, if they could approach us, they would naturally approach others too. It seems like some of the empire's top-level officials have become the 'Surrender Faction,' swayed by the forces of the heavenly plane."
The topic made both father and son appear grave.
Alexis furrowed his brows, "Should we report this to Her Majesty the Queen? It seems that the joint fleet may have been betrayed by a mole, and the odds are grim. The enemy might even be attempting a 'divide and conquer' strategy, aiming to erode more of the empire's fleet."
"It's too late," said Archduke Roberts, shaking his head.
That was the reason he hadn't slept all night.
Because he had already anticipated this possibility. Now, he had only confirmed the worst-case scenario from the mouth of another.
He added, "If they dare to speak openly, it must be that they are confident the matter has been settled. In the face of absolute power, all schemes are but an illusion. The joint fleet, I'm afraid, is more likely doomed than not."
It was this very feeling, of being aware of an enemy's schemes but unable to counteract them effectively, that felt like a heavy stone pressing on one's chest.
Alexis, with a hint of urgency, asked, "But do we just do nothing? Should the fleet still attempt to provide reinforcement? If we don't go and if Marshals Meredith and Rostov need rescue, and we don't go..."
Upon hearing this, Archduke Roberts suddenly looked up at the sky, his gaze growing deep.
He too seemed full of doubts.
After a moment of deep thought, he said, "Last night I had sent a message to Her Majesty, and she responded with a phrase: 'Even in the darkest night, there will be stars all over the sky'."
Alexis listened, his face full of confusion.
Just then, the sound of combat erupted from the distant streets.
The battle was intense, and even within the manor, the vibrations could be felt.
Archduke Roberts knew that it was the assassin he had sent out earlier who had been cornered by the people from Imperial Intelligence.
From the start, the fate of this assassin had been sealed.
Remembering the communication from last night, Roberts felt a bit more at ease.
He glanced at his son again and said, "Alexis, do you know that even yesterday, His Majesty had already guessed that the 'Thief Emperor' Carlo Meldis would come knocking, and warned me to be extra careful."
Alexis was clearly quite shocked. No wonder his father wasn't the least bit flustered—it turned out he had been prepared: "Imperial Intelligence's information is that precise?"
Duke Roberts shook his head, "No, it's not just that. Few people know that His Majesty is an inscrutable 'Astrology Magician.' So it's likely he's aware of what's happening now and what's about to happen in the future. His Majesty's strategic foresight is something beyond our comprehension."
Alexis's gaze became complicated as he listened, then said, "But...we should still do something, right?"
Archduke Roberts, too, seemed at a loss and shook his head, "I don't know. His Majesty has made no statement, leaving it to the council to decide. I suspect that this time, he seems to want those rats hiding in the gutters of Lingdun to come out into the sunlight. As for the joint naval fleets, it feels like he has some other assurance, as if there's a turnaround in the situation."
Alexis said, "Ah... but how could there be a reversal without the empire's main fleet going to the rescue against such strong foes from the divine portal plane?"
Archduke Roberts was still puzzled and shook his head, "We'll just do what we need to do, and within our power, to remain blameless. Those fiends from the divine portal plane will definitely not preserve Alchemy civilization. Even if some choose to live as slaves, our Roberts family will absolutely not betray our family honor or abandon Alchemy! If the joint fleets really were ambushed, the nearest reinforcements won't arrive at the site of the incident until half a month later. So there's no need to rush these one or two days. But I feel that there might be some major changes happening with this situation."
Hearing this, Alexis donned a solemn expression and gave a military salute, saying, "Yes, Father!
At that moment, the sounds of battle just outside the street abruptly ceased.
It had started unexpectedly and ended just as quickly.
Yet as someone visited the Roberts family manor, there were also several mysterious visitors heading to the residences of other ministers.
Almost everyone in the higher echelons of Lingdun now knew about the likely annihilation of the joint fleets, leaving the capital covered in a pall of gloom.
For the followers of the "Eye of Heaven Sect," it was a pre-victory celebration.
With the joint fleet destroyed, the breakthrough of Luying's homeland was within reach.
In such times on the brink of collapse, there were those within the united empire who, like the Roberts family, firmly chose to live or die with Alchemy civilization, while others opted to join the "surrender faction," choosing to betray their civilization and their compatriots.
Suddenly, various forces of unrest reared their heads in Lingdun.
However, most of these scenes were under the surveillance of Imperial Intelligence.
Just as Archduke Roberts had surmised, the figure in the palace planned to take this opportunity to deal with those rats hiding in the gutters.
....
In the evening, at Frederic Royal Palace.
Inside the stately palace, what was supposed to be an urgent meeting turned into a fierce argument among the ministers.
The joint fleet's loss of contact was now almost certainly due to an attack.
The conservative and rescue-faction ministers were red in the face arguing over whether to mount a large-scale rescue.
"The enemy has cut off the signals, clearly employing a 'surround and support' tactic. We must not send more troops to their deaths! Now the best choice is to hold our positions. Without our ships, the enemy cannot mount a serious attack, and holding our ground is the best course of action."
"Even if the joint fleet has indeed suffered a misfortune, I believe that the experienced marshals Meredith and Rostov would never leave the enemy with a single good warship. We still have naval superiority. If we rashly strike and lose more fleets, we'll completely lose our advantage!"
"A defensive strategy is correct, but if we don't rescue, we'll lose the two marshals and more than two hundred thousand seasoned soldiers. This is a loss not just in terms of equipment and personnel but also in morale! If we don't rescue, how disheartened do you think the front-line soldiers will feel?"
"Exactly! General Tosf is right. Moreover, the enemy's arrangements on Mafaxi Coast are still rudimentary. Now is the best chance for a surprise attack. If we take no action till they establish a good defense line, we'll have no opportunity. I support continuing reinforcements and raids!"
"I agree!"
"..."
Everyone was aware that sending reinforcements carried a huge risk, but to not reinforce was also wrong.
It was a debate doomed to have no resolution.
And upon the throne, Empress Yekaterina, clad in an embroidered golden robe, silently watched. Her purple hair stood tall, her beauty masking an imperial majesty.
She remained silent, fiddling with two meteorites in her hands, silently observing everything before her.
The ministers were perplexed. Why was the usually decisive and swift Empress so quiet today, letting the ministers argue among themselves?
But, judging by the speed with which the chaos in Lingdun City was quelled before it could rise, Her Majesty the Empress clearly had an accurate judgment and control of the situation.
No one knew what Yekaterina was thinking.
Then, suddenly, an elderly voice broke the silence, "Your Majesty, in my opinion, there's no point in continuing this argument. What do you think?"
The speaker was Merlin Gregory, clad in a gray mage's robe.
He was the current Chief Court Mage and the only ninth-tier professional in Lingdun.
Merlin was once an eighth-tier magistrate for Prince Carnap of a certain Bonaparte royal family. With the opening of the portal and the raising of the limit on laws of nature, the threshold for advancement had been greatly reduced.
No one expected that the Prince would have a Cosmic Essence, which also allowed Merlin to advance smoothly to the ninth tier.
But this Merlin was also a typical representative of the "Old Faction."
This faction, composed mostly of old nobility, supported the traditional feudal rights of hereditary lands and opposed the new policies in secret.
Now that Yekaterina had ascended the throne, a series of new policies had abolished the royalty and the hereditary rights to fiefs of the nobility.
These "old factions" were now both a support and a great hindrance to the empire.
After all, he was a ninth-tier alchemist, and at this critical moment for foreign affairs, no one could do anything to him. This Merlin also had significant influence in the imperial court, even showing signs of wielding power over the authorities.
When Yekaterina heard the inquiry, she simply said, "Let the council decide by vote."
Master Merlin, however, seemed somewhat dissatisfied and said, "Your Majesty, I believe we should dispatch a large force to rescue them, that would be the best course of action."
Yekaterina listened, her expression unchanged, and responded indifferently, "Very well."
Upon hearing this, a faint triumphant smile that was hard to detect flashed across Master Merlin's eyes, "Good, since that is the case, I think we should immediately send a fleet to reinforce!"
The ministers present heard this and said no more.
Although Yekaterina had not been on the throne for long, everyone realized she was an emperor of great talent and grand strategies. In this situation, no one could have done better than her.
The ministers also thought she needed the support of the "old factions" and had made the necessary compromises.
Naturally, no one else had anything more to say.
However, just when everyone thought the meeting had concluded,
suddenly a messenger guard burst in, exclaiming excitedly, "Urgent report! Urgent report!"
Normally, no matter what the urgency of the report, it had to be relayed through a specialized intelligence department and even be kept confidential.
Not like this, storming into the palace.
But there was one exception.
That was a war victory report!
Looking at the intruding messenger guard, all the ministers felt a great sense of perplexity.
Since the start of the war with the invaders from the celestial planes, they had suffered defeat after defeat, and even the minor victories were Pyrrhic. Where could such a victory report come from?
Yet, unbeknownst to everyone, the Yekaterina seated on the throne muttered under her breath in the same voice she alone had just heard, "Has it finally arrived..."
The messenger guard's face was flush with excitement as he quickly reported, "Your Majesty, a great victory! A great victory! The coalition fleet has sent an urgent message, reporting that between three to five this afternoon, our fleet near the Larman Archipelago in the Imperial Strait annihilated eight celestial plane battalions, each ten thousand strong in magic units!"
His voice echoed like a mighty bell throughout the entire great hall of the palace.
But upon hearing this, the expressions of all the ministers in the palace stiffened synchronously, as if they couldn't believe their own ears.
The more senior ministers even rubbed their eyes and ears, thinking they were having hallucinations.
For a moment, the vast palace was silent, save for the increasingly heavy breathing.
Listening, Yekaterina's own clear purple pupils trembled slightly. Although she had divined some positive outcomes with astrology, she had not expected a victory so great.
She commanded authoritatively, "Report in detail."
The messenger guard opened the scroll in his hands and reported loudly once more, "Just received the report, the imperial coalition fleet was supported by the 'Dawn Group,' and together they wiped out eight celestial plane magic battalions, slaughtering over eighty thousand enemies, destroying more than five hundred enemy warships. Our fleet only lost one battleship, thirty-two killed in action, and seven hundred injured..."
Upon saying this, everyone in the palace heard him clearly.
And because they heard him clearly, it was even more unbelievable.
What!
To annihilate eight ten-thousand-strong magic battalions with such minimal casualties?
If they were told that the coalition fleet had paid a terrible price to repel the enemy, they would have already considered it a great victory.
After all, no one was more aware of the combat power of the celestial plane magic battalions than they were.
Yet, the fleet had managed to "wipe out" eighty thousand enemy combatants with an incredibly low number of casualties?
How could this be!
Could this be a false report?
But everyone also faintly hoped it was true.
Even if it was a dream, they did not want to wake up.
At that moment, Yekaterina on the throne, upon hearing "Dawn Group," suddenly understood and murmured to herself, "So that's how it is."
As more and more detailed war reports came in and the ministers rushed to peruse them one after another, they finally dared to believe it was true.
Suddenly, the palace was alive with emotion; old ministers wept openly, an outburst of jubilation filled the air!
...
Before long, news of the "Imperial Strait Great Victory" spread throughout Lingdun City via special newspaper extras, and then swiftly across the entire empire.
This great victory served as a shot in the arm for everyone on the alchemical plane, significantly boosting military morale.
At the same time, the "Dawn Group" forcefully entered everyone's field of vision.

chapters.title: Chapter 602 - 601 Pandora Says It's Possible
chapters.content:
The combined fleet in the vicinity of the Imperial Strait had annihilated eight ten-thousand-man Mage companies from the Celestial Realm, and word of the victory spread quickly throughout the Alchemy Realm like it had grown wings.
Not just Ruying, but also those teams fighting a guerrilla campaign within the Mafa region heard this news and were immensely exhilarated.
For the first time, such a magnificent victory gave everyone a glimpse of hope for a combat triumph.
And along with the victorious news, a piece of secret intelligence was also transmitted back.
Apart from Emperor Yekaterina, no one knew what was written in that confidential report.
But that very night, various pharmaceutical factories received instructions to prepare a large amount of specific materials and equipment.
Some military secret laboratories had already begun mass production tests of genetic potions.
The senior generals of the military and military supply departments also received secret orders to draft a special military merit exchange scheme, and some elite magic Magicians were dispatched to carry out a certain secret mission.
The higher-ups vaguely guessed that the royal family seemed to have a very special prize to bestow for military merits, which also seemed to concern the secret of winning the great victory.
This made everyone inexplicably anticipate it.
If a ten-thousand-man Mage company from the Celestial Realm was annihilated, this could be the crucial turning point in the inter-plane war!
...
However, while the nation celebrated, in a gloomy sewer of Lington City, several cloaked figures gathered together.
These were members of the "Heaven's Eye Sect."
Like sewer rats, they could only hide in the dark sewers.
"Is the news confirmed? At the Imperial Strait, the vanguard Mage company was really wiped out?"
"No news from Mafa yet, but... judging from all reactions, it seems to be true."
"Damn it, how could the combined fleet win?"
"It's said it was because of the support from that 'Dawn Group.'"
"I've heard of the Dawn Group too; it's just an adventure group, no stronger than some former Pirate King fleets. A small group like that, any ten-thousand-man Mage company could handle it, how could it possibly help the combined fleet annihilate the vanguard Mage company?"
"Don't know. But for now, Emperor Yekaterina's attitude also poses a big problem. It's clear she still has cards up her sleeve. Just like today's operation by our sect, it seems it had been under surveillance by military intelligence for a long time, leading to heavy losses. Even the legendary Hunter 'Thief King' Carlo Meldis we recruited with difficulty was executed in the street."
"..."
The cloaked figures felt a chill down their spines as they discussed this, as if every action they took was being watched.
At that moment, the leader spoke again.
"Can we get that secret battle report?"
"Not for the time being. Right now, only Emperor Yekaterina has seen that detailed battle report. Our people also don't dare to expose themselves too much."
"What about Merlin Gregory?"
"He hasn't given a clear response. However, when our people visited him, he didn't alert the guards and seemed not to refuse us."
"Hmpf! Greedy old fox, it seems the chips we offered were still not enough."
"..."
After discussing for a moment, the cloaked figures dispersed.
...
On the other hand.
15 Holy Light Boulevard, once the residence of a certain Duke.
Now it was the residence of Merlin Gregory.
As the top confidant of the United Empire, this ninth-order Master Merlin enjoyed a treatment on par with a prince.
Originally, after Yekaterina's accession and reform policies, the empire had abolished slavery and the hereditary rights of nobility, no longer ennobling anyone.
But this Master Merlin, relying on his ninth-order power and the support of the "Old Faction," those remnants of the old noble regime, still indulged in the decadent lifestyle of the old nobility.
In the midst of the plane war, nobody spoke openly, nor dared to.
After all, a ninth-order power held extraordinary significance.
Certainly, Master Merlin was also keenly aware of his own status. Utilizing his increasingly influential position, he gathered more power and had a line of direct followers in the court.
In the evening, after Master Merlin returned from the Frederick Palace,
inside the mansion, some old faction ministers had long been waiting.
These people convened to discuss today's sudden developments.
Unlike in Lingdun City, where the atmosphere was festive everywhere, Master Merlin and his group felt unease rather than joy about the great victory in the Imperial Strait.
The grand victory by the imperial legions posed some potential threat to him as a ninth-order.
In the secret meeting room, candlelight illuminated several gloomy, aged faces.
"Strange... the combined fleet's power, how could it possibly defeat eight ten-thousand-man Mage companies?"
"Indeed. Logically, even with the advantage of ships and numbers, the fleet could at most confront four or five ten-thousand-man Mage companies head-on. And the eight companies were forewarned; how could they have been defeated?"
"Hey, you mentioned the 'Dawn Group' in the report... could it be that Mr. Jing, the leader of Dawn Order, went there?"
"Impossible! The previous leader of Dawn Order, 'Mr. Jing,' was severely injured by a master from Celestial Realm. I got reliable information; it's impossible for him to recover in less than ten or eight years."
"Then it's strange, could it be that Her Imperial Majesty has other ninth-order trump cards up her sleeve?"
"Unlikely. If advancing to ninth-order was so easy, there wouldn't be so few in the Alchemy Realm. Not to mention whether there are any eighth-order-complete professionals, that 'Cosmic Essence' is also elusive. Moreover, even if there are ninth-order beings who can withstand a ten-thousand-man Mage company, that was a total of eight..."
"Could it be about the 'Dawn Group' mentioned in the report?"
"Absolutely impossible! How could a mere adventure group sway the battle on the frontal battlefield? This must be a maneuver by Her Majesty to consolidate power. The common folks naively believed it, but how could we possibly believe such a flawed report?"
"Indeed. It might have been a severe storm that scattered the Celestial Realm's Mage companies, then the combined fleet opportunistically claimed a large victory. After all, those from the Celestial Realm lack decent ships, so it's possible..."
"It's regrettable that we couldn't see the detailed battle report."
"..."
Several old nobles were discussing fervently.
Master Merlin's face was grim.
Whether there were other Tier 9s or something else, it wasn't good news for him.
It now seemed that the royal family indeed had a means to deal with a mage group of ten thousand.
This meant that the United Empire's reliance on him as a Tier 9 would be greatly reduced.
This was not good news.
At this moment, an old noble asked, "Master Merlin, about the Heavenly Eye Sect... what should we do?"
Master Merlin said, "Leave them be for now."
The old noble asked, "You mean, reject them?"
Master Merlin chuckled meaningfully, "No. How can we reject them? We can't possibly win this war. You do not understand the power beyond Tier 9, so you have no idea how the dimensional war will unfold. Right now, the tension is merely because the dimensional passage has just connected, and it still can't bring down beings beyond Tier 9."
Upon hearing this, everyone in the room displayed expressions of eager anticipation for what was to come.
Since they were destined to lose, the natural course was to preserve themselves as much as possible.
As for lofty ideals of civilization, in the eyes of these selfish old nobles, what could be more important than their lives and properties?
Master Merlin continued, "So we need to prepare for several eventualities. Even if the Alchemy civilization does collapse, we need to ensure that our surnames, flowing with our noble blood, will continue to exist."
At his words, everyone nodded in agreement, saying, "Master, what should we do?"
Master Merlin said, "Right now, the gods of the heavenly dimension lack top-tier warriors and warships. They cannot breach Lord Ruying's several coastal defense lines anytime soon. We need to hold as much power in the United Empire as possible. The more speaking rights we hold, the more bargaining chips we'll have when the time comes. So it doesn't matter whether this 'Battle of the Imperial Strait' is real or not, we can't win anyway. Instead, it's good to let those heavenly dimension folks face setbacks, as they will then recognize our value more. If they want to quickly break through our sea defense, they must rely on us!"
This group, which had intended to surrender from the start, started boasting and flattering as soon as they heard these words.
"Right! Master Merlin has the long view."
"Indeed so. If we agree to the people from the Heavenly Eye Sect now, they definitely wouldn't value us. But the more control we have later, the more they will take us seriously."
"..."
Listening to everyone's praise, a self-satisfied look appeared on Master Merlin's face.
From once being a prince's offering to now the empire's chief offering, power represented rights, and this surge in authority made him feel increasingly pleased.
He thought for a moment and then said, "Prepare a proposal for tomorrow to let the council agree that we control part of the sea defense rights."
At this, someone uncertainly said, "But… the Empress has already legislated that sea defense is in the hands of the military alone, strictly prohibiting any interference. Wouldn't our interference cause backlash from all parties?"
Master Merlin heard this, yet laughed unconcernedly, "Don't worry, the Empress dares not confront me openly."
With that, a sinister gleam flashed quickly in his eyes: "Only I can stop a mage group of ten thousand. Even if they are dissatisfied, they must agree. If they really want to oppose me, they shouldn't blame me for being ruthless. At that time, her position as empress might not be secure!"
Hearing this, rather than finding it treacherous, everyone in the room secretly felt some anticipation.
These remnants of the old era hadn't forgotten who had stripped them of their supreme noble rights.
...
Su Lun knew that after the battle at the Imperial Strait, it would inevitably have a massive influence on the situation of the dimensional war.
But, he left it unattended.
After dealing with those eight mage groups of ten thousand, he followed Mr. Jing's spatial coordinates by teleporting.
After several teleports, he arrived in Zambula Ironfalls Province in the southern part of Mafa.
"Eh..."
Upon closer inspection, Su Lun was surprised to find that Mr. Jing's coordinates were still in that same forest as before.
He teleported again, and in a changed scenery, he appeared in a pine forest.
Looking around, Mr. Jing was indeed there.
Perhaps because there was a natural hot spring?
Last time he came here, she and Qian Zhao were soaking in the hot springs.
This time, only Mr. Jing was here by herself.
Last time he came it was winter, snowflakes covered the sky, and the pine forest was a winter landscape clad in silver.
Now it was late autumn, with fallen leaves everywhere, the forest replete with ripe, heavy, orange hues.
When Su Lun sensed the coordinate location, he guessed that Mr. Jing was soaking in the hot springs.
He looked intently, and saw in the misty vapors of the hot spring pool, a stunning figure soaking in the water.
It was none other than his own senior sister.
She was wearing that kind of gauzy robe from the "Akun Family Bathhouse" back in Old Lington.
Su Lun himself felt that among the robes for soaking, this was the most comfortable.
But such gauzy robes became semi-translucent and clung tight to the body upon being soaked, revealing her graceful figure completely.
Yet Su Lun hadn't expected, upon teleporting here, to be instantly chilled to the bone.
The hot spring water hadn't frozen, but the chill was emanating from Mr. Jing's body.
As she had been forewarned, Mr. Jing wasn't surprised by someone's arrival; she opened her eyes and smiled faintly, "Su Lun, you have come."
Su Lun walked over and observing the chilly mist dissipating from her body, he asked, "Sister, your injury?"
Before Mr. Jing could speak, a ghostly figure drifted from a rune-sealed umbrella.
Pestoya looked at her elder sister wounded and expressed her concern, "Sister, your injuries seem very severe."
Mr. Jing smiled gently at Pestoya. She seemed unconcerned about her injuries, saying, "I might need a few months to recuperate, but it's nothing serious."
Hearing this, Su Lun furrowed his brow.
His eyes suddenly became emotionless, a flicker passing through, and the secrets of the whitish glow seeping from Mr. Jing's wounds were layer by layer peeled back and revealed.
Strangely, despite the wound being of holy damage, there was also an overwhelmingly domineering chill.
Mr. Jing, being of the vampire clan, suffered particularly deep wounds from this holy damage.
The injury was far more serious than she let on.
She was soaking in the hot springs here, largely to lessen the piercing chill deep in her bones.
Mr. Jing looked at him with a touch of surprise in his focused observation.
With his calm demeanor, she felt that Su Lun seemed to have pinpointed the root of her injury.
But, how could that be?
This was a high-level holy law injury, something she found very troublesome; how could Su Lun understand it?
Yet, Mr. Jing remained silent, watching the serious-faced Su Lun thoughtfully.
Pestoya beside him looked on nervously too, not daring to make a sound.
It was only after a long while that Su Lun finally emerged from that utterly rational state, blinked his eyes to ease the fatigue, and said, "Senior sister, your injury is quite dangerous. Even several years of recuperation won't heal it. If it isn't thoroughly dealt with, that high-level holy power will damage your essence for many years to come."
"Eh..."
Hearing this, Mr. Jing couldn't hide her astonishment, "You noticed?"
"Yes."
Su Lun nodded, thought for a moment, then added, "I think I can fix it, but it might take some time."
"You can fix it?"
Mr. Jing was genuinely surprised upon hearing this.
She knew all too well that her injury was so complex that even a ninth-level wouldn't find it easy to handle, let alone Su Lun... an eighth-level?
Mr. Jing smiled faintly, "So you've advanced."
"Yes."
Su Lun, having fully understood the bizarre injury, also sighed in relief.
Though tricky, it was fortunate that he could manage it.
Especially since among those Holy Light mages he had dealt with before, there were similar experiences.
But now he was only eighth-level, and handling such high-level laws required extra caution and considerable effort and time.
However, he had nothing to hold back for his own senior sister.
Su Lun continued, "Didn't I go to the Dragon Country Waters that time? It was the sea map you helped me translate... and later we encountered some things..."
The Dawn group had encountered too many things in the Dragon Country Waters, and previously, it was impossible to explain clearly over the communicator; now, while they were idle, it was a good topic to chat about.
He began to speak, then changed the subject, "Senior sister, I'm going to begin treating your injury now."
"Okay."
Mr. Jing's brow twitched slightly, she didn't refuse, but instead playfully suggested with a smirk, "If you're not afraid of the cold, why don't you come in too?"
Su Lun didn't mind, feeling already that crouching by the water's edge was inconvenient.
Changing outfits as if by magic, he donned an appropriate bathing garment and immersed himself in the water.
The spring water was warm, but oddly, it felt bone-chillingly cold near Mr. Jing.
Su Lun moved closer and sat next to Mr. Jing, from this angle, he could perfectly view her stunning figure.
The soaked sheer gown did little to obscure the view.
Mr. Jing's figure didn't tower like Sabina's and Qianyu's, but her proportions were always just right.
With the autumn breeze in their ears and the murmuring of the pool water, the scene was enchantingly beautiful.
Watching, Su Lun unabashedly complimented, "Wow... Senior sister, you have a great figure."
Mr. Jing gave him a look, her eyebrows slightly bent, with a hint of reproach, "Flatterer."
She didn't say much more, diverting her gaze and lying there with her eyes closed, contented.
Su Lun chuckled softly, a healing green light curling around his hands as he delved deeper, explaining, "We went to the Dragon Country, right? And then we found that Giant Island on the map, discovered the legendary 'Mimir's Spring'..."
While attempting to coax out the burning holy power within Mr. Jing's wound, he recounted their previous adventures.
Mr. Jing listened intently, interjecting occasionally with exclamations of amazement.
However, the injury was indeed a bit beyond what Su Lun could handle at his level; if he hadn't understood the secret of the laws within the wound, even a ninth-level would hardly be able to manage it.
Even though he was being extremely cautious, drawing out this holy power felt like tearing a piece of flesh from a person.
From Mr. Jing's occasional slight frown, it was apparent she was enduring quite some pain.
Su Lun could only handle the injury more delicately, bit by bit.
Fortunately, the adventure story in the Dragon Country was long, allowing for a slow narration and treatment.
"Ah... Senior sister, your wound extends to below your ribs, I need to open your clothing."
"Okay."
The thin layer of fabric easily unraveled, floating like cicada wings in the water, and in no time, her proud and snowy peaks were completely in view.
Mr. Jing's demeanor remained cool and composed, even in bare skin, she didn't show the slightest discomfort.
Su Lun, too, kept his gaze straightforward, meticulously tending to his senior sister's wound.
But, there was a third person present.
Now with Mr. Jing's upper body mostly exposed and clearly visible in the water, the somewhat bored specter lady imitated Su Lun's earlier remark with a playful laugh, "Wow... Sister, you really do have a great figure."
Su Lun had genuinely admired the beauty.
And clearly, Pestoya was just teasing.
With that remark, the atmosphere became slightly awkward.
Mr. Jing was both amused and exasperated.
Luckily, both of them ignored her, and the ghost lady also felt bored. However, she suddenly became intensely interested in soaking and drifted into the water, sitting next to Su Lun, "Wow... I always see you guys soaking in hot springs. Is it really that comfortable? I've never tried it either."
She hadn't tried it a thousand years ago, and she hadn't tried it now either.
As they were quite familiar with each other, Su Lun casually teased, "You're a ghost, what hot spring are you going to soak in?"
Pestoia said with a melancholic face, "What's wrong with a ghost? Can't ghosts soak in hot springs?"
Although she said that, she tilted her head and thought about it, and seemed to agree with the reasoning.
She gave it a try, but even though she could materialize a body, the pleasure of soaking was hardly felt.
It suddenly seemed very dull.
Just then, Pestoia's quirky eyes lit up, and she suddenly had an idea, urgently saying, "Su Lun, quickly open the little void. I want to go in."
"What?"
Listening, Su Lun, driven by curiosity, yet without much thought, raised his hand, and took the ghost lady into the little void realm.
He thought that without this chatty lady, the treatment would be much quieter.
But unexpectedly, not long after Pestoia went in, she suddenly said, "Su Lun, let me out quickly!"
Su Lun could control everything inside the little void realm, but he noticed nothing amiss.
Although he sensed something unusual, he still raised his hand and let her out.
At that moment, Pandora, dressed in a divine mage robe, walked out.
Not!
To be exact, it was Pestoia's spirit that had attached to Pandora's body.
Just like the previous two times when she had attached to Su Lun's body.
But differently, the spirit attached to this alchemical body seemed to be a perfect fit.
In Su Lun's perception, she was entirely like a living person, with no abnormalities.
...
Su Lun looked at Pestoia attached to Pandora's body, his expression also quite strange.
A little girl's spirit, yet possessing one of the most perfect and mature bodies under heaven, this contrast made it seem very... special.
Even Mr. Jing would look awestruck if he saw it.
Su Lun directly asked, "Pestoia, how did you attach to Miss Pandora's body?"
Though the face in front of him was alluring, she replied in a playful tone, "Sister Pandora said it was okay."
"..."
Su Lun stared with corner of his eyes full of dark lines.
Due to their previous battles together, he knew that in these days this ghost lady and Pandora had become very familiar.
From the tone of their conversation, their relationship seemed like that of real sisters, even to the extent of sharing bodies.
Pestoia seemed very pleased with Pandora's body, and with a "plop", she jumped into the water, excitedly exclaiming, "Wow... so this is what soaking feels like."
The warm spring water touched her skin, giving her a sensation of her pores relaxing all over her body.
This made the ghost lady feel very curious.
Su Lun was splashed in the face with water.
He glanced over at a vast expanse of magnificently curvy landscape, dizzyingly attractive.
"Pandora" was wearing a loose, inner-lining-free divine robe.
The moment she jumped into the water, the wet clothes revealed everything immediately.
There was no need to speak of Pandora's figure, flawlessly graceful and exuding a mature charm everywhere.
But after all, with a little girl's spirit, Su Lun felt something was off, and warned in a ghostly tone, "Pestoia, you are revealing too much."
Pestoia appeared startled, with a charming yet dumbfounded expression on her beautiful face.
It was her first time experiencing such a luscious body, and she was a bit perplexed.
But then, as if someone whispered something to her, she hesitated for a moment, then responded in a transmission-like manner, "Ah... Sister Pandora said it doesn't matter. Since you've seen it all, a little exposure doesn't matter."
"..."
Su Lun rolled his eyes upon hearing this.
This girl really dared to say anything.
Pandora's consciousness was also within the body, just not in charge.
Listening to their banter, Mr. Jing nearby couldn't help but laugh softly.
Su Lun always felt like some weird uncle in the mouth of this girl, and again said in a ghostly tone, "You don't quite suit this body."
Pestoia, like a duck out of water in the hot spring, splashed around and swam up to sit obediently next to Su Lun, asking, "Why?"
Su Lun glanced at the deep cleavage and the proud figure, then countered, "What do you think?"
At your young age, how could you shoulder such a weighty presence?
Pestoia seemed to realize something was off too, and muttered, "Ah… I also think, Sister Pandora's chest seems a bit too heavy."
While saying this, she poked it with her own finger, seeing a very bouncy feeling.
Su Lun watched, his eyelid twitching, utterly helpless.
Mr. Jing nearby chose to rest with closed eyes, smiling without a word.
Unexpectedly then, Pestoia added, "Su Lun, do you think the sister looks better this way too?"
Su Lun: "..."
Mr. Jing: "..."

chapters.title: Chapter 603 - 602: Su Lun's Thoughts on Alchemical Homunculi
chapters.content:
Seeing Pestoia attached to Pandora's body, Su Lun couldn't help but laugh and cry at the same time, while his second solution All-knowing Eye also discovered some deeper issues.
That was that the compatibility between Pestoia and Pandora's alchemical body was extremely high!
So high that it was theoretically impossible.
Su Lun had actually been pondering a question all along.
If his teacher and Sir Isaac had managed to preserve Pestoia's soul and condense divine fire, had they considered creating a body for her?
Clearly, they had.
After encountering Pandora, Su Lun actually had some guesses.
The research project of creating alchemical humans might have been a direction the couple tried in order to rebuild a body for Pestoia.
But this involved a very profound issue.
That was, the bodies and souls of humans and all creatures are a perfect match by nature. Transplanted bodies, no matter what, could never achieve this 100% compatibility.
Thus, the soul would not stay indefinitely in a body.
Just like some ancient evil magicians who took over other people's bodies, but had to change them frequently. The mutual rejection of soul and body was the most important reason.
This was not a conclusion Su Lun had come up with on his own.
It was found in the "Research Journal on Living Corpses" recorded by a mad researcher named Tillmido M. Chekhov, in the cursed space of "Havier's Mortuary of Grudges" at 88 Old Linden Ginkgo Street while he was still in Old Lington.
Su Lun had asked Mr. Jing and knew Chekhov's identity.
He was also a great alchemist from a thousand years ago, the chief biological expert of Old Lington at that time.
That was also the person initially in charge of researching the autopsy of the fallen angel captured by Sir Isaac.
But due to some experimental accidents caused by insufficient understanding of divine entities, the fallen angel's soul became entangled with Pestoia, leading to her being burned to death later and her resentment being preserved at Storm Manor.
Chekhov, harboring guilt, then began to tackle the three ultimate questions in the field of alchemy: resurrection of the dead, life transfer, and life creation.
Su Lun's secret technique of the living dead was a byproduct of Chekhov's research.
However, at least the portion of the "Research Journal on Living Corpses" that Su Lun obtained did not have the results for "resurrection of the dead."
Pestoia was not successfully revived, and until now, she remains a ghost.
Once, Su Lun thought Chekhov's experiment had failed.
After all, "resurrection of the dead" is a power only the gods possess.
Su Lun hadn't thought much about it before.
But seeing "Pandora," Su Lun knew there was another direction to this matter.
It wasn't just resurrection, but using the legendary technology of creating artificial humans.
And seeing the current 98% compatibility between Pestoia and Pandora's body, he knew, this might just be Sir Isaac's ultimate plan.
Using alchemy to create a miracle, crafting a perfectly compatible body for Pestoia!
And now that Su Lun had achieved his second solution with the All-knowing Eye, his understanding of the world became much clearer. Just from this one glance, he saw more about the fundamental meanings of "death" and "resurrection."
The technology of creating artificial humans also suddenly made sense.
...
However, clearly, Pandora was not the body Sir Isaac created for Pestoia.
First, the compatibility wasn't absolutely perfect;
Second, Pandora's "Faith Stealing" ability was very special, and this must have been intentional.
Pandora is Pandora.
She is an alchemical miracle created by Sir Isaac and Lady Isaac using alchemy.
Su Lun guessed that possibly during the catastrophic disaster that led to the destruction of Old Lington, Pestoia's body wasn't manufactured in time.
Or perhaps for some other reason.
Nevertheless, Sir Isaac, who had mastered the laws of fate, surely had some profound intentions.
For a moment, Su Lun's thoughts whirled and he considered too much.
He pondered for an instant and suddenly had an idea, thinking to himself, "It looks like I need to find time to return to Old Lington."
Although he understood the technical principles, there was still a long way to go before he could produce a finished product.
And he was still missing some experimental data.
Su Lun speculated that the information related to "alchemy-created humans" and "soul bonding" might be hidden in the cursed space of the mortuary on the minus third floor of 88 Old Linden Ginkgo Street—a floor he had never managed to reach.
Perhaps lost in thought, Su Lun did not immediately respond to the young lady ghost.
It was at this moment that reality snapped him back.
Seeing the direct stare Su Lun gave her body, Pestoya still felt somewhat uncomfortable.
Although it wasn't her own body, she covered her chest and murmured in exasperation, "Hey, Su Lun... Although Sister Pandora doesn't mind you looking, can you at least try to be discreet? That lecherous look makes it feel quite sleazy."
Since it was her soul that was attached, her body's reactions were being fed back to her soul senses. The looks coming her way felt like a feather trailing along her skin, itchy and also a bit warm.
Pestoya felt as if she was bare and being scrutinized, something about it made her feel oddly uneasy inside.
This was a strange sensation she hadn't experienced in over a thousand years.
Lecherous?
And how am I sleazy?
Listenting, Su Lun gave the young lady ghost a glance, realizing she was becoming more and more sharp-tongued.
He glanced sideways and teased, "What's wrong with looking? If it were you, there'd be nothing interesting to see anyways."
"Huh???"
At this, Pestoya reacted like a cat whose tail had been stepped on, immediately bristling.
Without caring if her robe was showing too much, she fiercely pounced and grabbed Su Lun's neck, shaking his head while continuing to rant discontentedly, "Ah... you nasty fellow, what do you mean by that! What is with that disdainful look? How am I indecent?!"
Not satisfied, she then climbed onto Su Lun's neck, unselfconsciously scratching, grabbing, and biting.
Su Lun felt neither pain nor discomfort.
Having often horsed around like this before, both were accustomed to interacting this way.
Fortunately, Su Lun's multitasking skills were top-notch, so being choked did not impede his healing abilities.
Mr. Jing watched the two of them create a commotion, yet he remained smiling and silent.
Despite her fierce demeanor, there was a strangely warm atmosphere.
It would be harmless for Pestoya's dark Lolita ghost form to be on his neck, but now that it was Pandora's body, it felt very strange.
Plus, Su Lun was well aware of the structure of the divine robe. Wet and close like this, it was completely unrestrained.
Their extensive skin contact allowed them both to feel each other's scorching body heat.
Pandora had an impeccable figure, and although Su Lun had studied it, he had never been this close before.
Especially in this mounted position - her thighs and buttocks were soft and smooth to the touch, offering an exquisite sensation. Even some details were distinctly felt.
Su Lun was aware of this, but it was not appropriate to speak up, so he let her fuss over him.
But since the bodily sensations were completely real, Pestoya, after causing a commotion for a while, seemed to realize something was off and gradually quieted down.
Being essentially a teenager in mindset, the instinctive blush that swept across her face was either from the temperature rise from the springs or a fleeting shyness.
Seeing her embarrassment, Mr. Jing timely spoke up, laughing, "Alright, Pestoya, come down now. You're hardly acting like a lady."
"Oh~"
Pestoya complied, sheepishly climbing down from Su Lun's shoulder.
Then she submerged herself thoroughly in the water, only her head halfway above it, blowing bubbles like a goldfish.
This was the first time Su Lun saw such a bashful side of Pestoya. He chuckled to himself, finding it quite amusing.
He did not continue to tease the girl, switching topics, he said, "Pestoya, remember I told you I would help make you a body? I now have an idea and should be confident in helping you craft an alchemical body."
Indeed, she did not continue with the earlier topic, and this ghostly young lady seemed to have immediately rejuvenated herself.
Emerging from the water, her eyes gleaming with anticipation, she exclaimed, "Ah? Really?"
"Yes."
Su Lun nodded and shared his earlier thoughts, "Technically, it's not a big issue. We just lack some precise data on soul fusion and a few key materials. I roughly know where to find some clues..."
He had studied Pandora's alchemical body many times and had already solved many of its technical difficulties.
Now that he had awakened the second level of All-knowing Eye, even those high-level designs that were previously indecipherable to him were now comprehensible.
However, understanding them and creating them were still quite different matters.
This would still need time to be attempted bit by bit.
Pestoya, having been a ghost for a thousand years, already had stars of hope in her eyes at the prospect of having a body again, dreaming aloud, "Ah... Su Lun, what kind of body are you going to make for me?"
She tilted her head, pondering, then looked down at her current form, concerned that Su Lun might not understand her meaning, she added, "Um... I mean... I mean... As good as sister Pandora's body is, it seems... it might not suit me."
Su Lun smiled and said, "Of course. I will create one according to your liking."
He had fully understood now; Pestoya's compatibility with Pandora's body was as high as 97%. The minor incompatibility was due to details of the physical form, such as a body image compatible with the soul, various capabilities, elemental affinities, and physiological state.
It was like... Pandora's voluptuous figure did not quite match this young girl's soul. If changed to a petite frame, it might increase the compatibility further.
"Su Lun, you are amazing!"
Overjoyed upon hearing this, Pestoya enthusiastically embraced Su Lun.
Su Lun, already used to her shifts in mood, felt the suffocating tenderness and reminded her with a smile, "Pestoya, you are exposing yourself again."
Unexpectedly, Pestoya didn't show any embarrassment this time and embraced him openly, "Ah... It's sister Pandora's body anyway. If you want to take advantage, go ahead."
Saying that, she revealed a mischievous smirk and asked teasingly, "Little junior brother, I am good to you, right?"
"..."
Su Lun was amused yet exasperated.
This cunning young girl, who had just a moment ago not even allowed a glance, now readily 'sold' Pandora.
Mr. Jing, too, smiled with amusement in her beautiful eyes.
Yet watching Su Lun, a fleeting moment of contemplation flashed in her eyes.
She had thought it over.
But creating alchemical humanoids involved several ultimate questions in the field of alchemy, presenting extremely high difficulty, unimaginable to ordinary people. Apart from her own half-demigod father, she hardly imagined anyone else capable of crafting a legendary alchemical humanoid.
Now, unexpectedly, Su Lun had managed it.
....
In a pine forest in a secluded mountain, the autumn wind was howling.
In the hot spring pool, three people were leisurely soaking.
Su Lun recounted his adventurous journey to the Dragon Country, Mr. Jing listening with amazement and occasionally interjecting.
"Oh, my father also went to Giant Island? No wonder some of the details you mentioned about the Dragon Country Waters seemed familiar like childhood stories..."
"The talent of 'All-knowing Eye' really relates to the Spring of Wisdom..."
"So Ottilia went to Netherworld, huh..."
"Emmerich successfully transplanted the Eye of the God and obtained some of the 'All-Phenomena Truth' talent? That's quite good. It aligns well with his Scholar career path, and his future prospects are high. At that time, our Dawn will also gain another top-tier combatant."
"It turns out everyone in the team has changed so much, huh..."
"..."
Su Lun pretty much finished recounting his adventures.
At that moment, he thought of something and asked about his senior sister's situation, "Senior sister, how's the battle situation on Mafa's side? Also, how were you injured?"
Thanks to Su Lun's healing, Mr. Jing noticeably felt the rampaging divine force within her easing a lot, and the pain also lessened much.
Upon hearing this question, she replied, "The dimensional passage can now withstand the arrival of a ninth-tier Sage of Law. But the cost of arrival is likely considerable, and as far as I know, only one Sage of Law has descended so far. Knowing this, I planned to see if I could take a shot at the enemy's top combatants, but then I ran into an ambush."
At this point, Mr. Jing paused.
After pondering for a moment, she continued, "Later, I carefully thought back on the details of the operation and realized the oversight might not have been on my part. I suspect the information might have been leaked."
"Information leakage?"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's eyebrows slightly furrowed.
When he previously heard at the joint fleet that Mr. Jing had been injured, he had already guessed this possibility.
No one knew the extent of his elder sister's abilities better than he did.
The Second Solution [S-011-Image Guardian], along with the various abilities replicated over a millennium, made Mr. Jing's combat power far beyond that of an ordinary ninth-tier.
There was also her ability to teleport using mirrors; anyone who wanted to seriously wound her on this plane had to be extremely cautious.
Not to mention a surprise attack.
How could she have been ambushed instead?
Su Lun immediately thought of the situation with the joint fleet. That fleet had also set out to raid the gods' plane harbor, but it ended up trapped at sea.
If it was not due to some special divination ability, it was clearly someone leaking intelligence.
Su Lun tended toward the latter option.
Because, on this plane, there absolutely did not exist a ninth-tier capable of predicting!
Mr. Jing obviously knew this as well and she continued, "During the previous operation, there was some exchange of intelligence with the officers of the Unified Empire. Naturally, their existing intelligence network within the Mapha Territory is somewhat more accurate. The intelligence on my operations must have leaked from this channel."
After hearing this, Su Lun took a moment to think and then asked, "Elder sister, are you saying someone at the high levels of the empire has defected?"
Mr. Jing said, "It's not necessarily true defection. Those who had access to that class of information are now certainly holding high ranks within the Unified Empire. True defection would bring much greater impacts than merely selling some intelligence. Moreover... your empress wife's skills are not so simple; if there were a high-level defection, the exposure would ensure that no matter who they were, their outcome would not be favorable."
As she spoke, she let out a slight sigh,"Probably, some of the high officials are just making sure they have a fallback plan. Thinking if the Alchemy plane really was defeated, they could still act as the 'Surrender Faction' and save their lives."
"..."
Su Lun fell into thought upon hearing this.
Although he felt somewhat strange about the term 'elder sister' used for his mentor, he couldn't deny that Yekaterina's meticulousness, adeptness, and subtlety in handling people were indeed unparalleled.
Speaking of being an emperor, Su Lun really thought she was quite suited to the role.
Even the former Mapha's Grand Naval Marshal 'Thunder Tiger' Meredith had nothing but high praises for her.
