After reviewing the content of the golden scroll, Su Lun's thoughts became clearer.
Thinking about it, he decided to put the idea that had been lingering in his mind these past few days into practice.
"Let's do it."
At that moment, Su Lun pulled out a lab rat from a biological experiment.
With a slight flick of his fingers, a transparent thread immediately decapitated the rat, splattering blood everywhere. Almost instantly, a thin wisp of "gray mist" emerged above the corpse.
However, Su Lun didn't let it die, and a sorcerer's seal formed in an instant: "Rewind!"
A miraculous scene immediately unfolded.
The rat's wound reversed as if time flowed backward, instantly healing completely, even the splattered blood was drawn back.
Su Lun once again concentrated on the secret technique, a layer of corpse wax then enveloped the rat's body. With a wave of his hand, before the soul could drift away, it was immediately sealed back into the rat's body.
A magical scene played out right before their eyes.
The rat was immediately hopping around lively, no different from before.
Seeing this, Su Lun's eyebrows slightly furrowed, seemingly still not quite satisfied, he muttered, "Is this the best I can do..."
Yet, this scene made Mr. Jing, who was not far away, freeze; she put down the ancient tome in her hands and curiously asked, "Su Lun, have you grasped the mystery of 'resurrection'?"
"Resurrection" is indeed one of the ultimate subjects in the field of alchemy.
She remembered her father once asserting that this was a power only deities could wield.
But now, Su Lun had resurrected a rat right before her eyes?
Although Mr. Jing also noticed some flaws in this small experiment, merely making a dead rat hop around held extraordinary significance.
"No. It's not truly the Resurrection Technique."
Su Lun shook his head, pondered for a moment, and then said, "Hmm... I think 'Corpse Soul Reincarnation Technique' is a more suitable name. The rat is actually already dead, I just used alchemy to keep it alive. To be precise, it's a special form of undead creature."
Mr. Jing pondered for a moment, faintly discerning some tricks, but was mostly puzzled.
She raised her eyebrows and said, "Oh?"
Having no reservations with his own senior sister, Su Lun explained: "Just now, to resurrect this rat, I used the laws of Time, Death, and Life—three high-level laws—along with the Living Corpse Secret Technique and Wax Figure Secret Technique. I reversed local time to restore the rat's cellular activity, then forcibly sealed the soul with the soul secret technique, and finally used the living corpse wax figurine technique to preserve its pre-death capabilities..."
As he spoke, he spread his hands and added, "Although the outcome is the same as 'resurrection,' the approach is completely different. Without the wax seal, the rat would instantly die from soul departure."
Mr. Jing clearly understood this explanation.
However, she didn't feel this technique was imperfect; instead, she smiled slightly, meaningfully saying, "To achieve this is already quite impressive."
As she spoke, she glanced at Su Lun and added, "I've never heard of anyone reaching this stage. Not even my parents."
Resurrection is a divine power, and Su Lun achieving this step meant he was now glimpsing some divine mysteries.
This was an excellent start.
Moreover, even if this "Corpse Soul Reincarnation" is an unfinished resurrection technique,
its significance for humanity is immense.
If one could truly preserve complete memories and abilities in life, death would seemingly become less frightening.
Moreover, he's only at the eighth tier.
Hearing his sister praise him, Su Lun noncommittally shrugged his shoulders.
Although he also knew his technique had great potential for the future, he felt there were many areas for improvement.
He then pointed at the "High Wisdom Scroll" and said, "The rules of death recorded on this golden scroll are too profound, many things beyond my current understanding. Probably after reaching the ninth tier, I could truly comprehend some of its mysteries."
Listening to him, Mr. Jing nodded encouragingly and said, "Hmm."
...
A day later, the train arrived at the station.
Finally, Su Lun and Mr. Jing reached Clementon in the Stormgar region.
This was a bustling south large city.

chapters.title: Chapter 616 - 615: Dawn VS Magic Group
chapters.content:
A few years ago, aside from the imperial capital Lington and a few other mega-cities, one could hardly see any industry in Lu Ying.
Like other traditional cities in Lu Ying, Clementon, despite being a major city in the south with a large population, had remained a primitive agricultural society for hundreds of years, with virtually no progress in civilization.
But after the establishment of the United Empire, things were completely different here.
At the steam train station of Clementon, Su Lun and Mr. Jing stepped off the train to a vibrant and bustling scene.
In the gigantic steel-framed station, workers with mechanical arms were busily constructing various infrastructure.
The sparsely populated southern regions of Lu Ying were a focal area for immigrants, and a large number of Mafa mechanics had poured in. The machinery had empowered labor with higher work efficiency, and the city construction changed with each passing day. A huge, new super-city had already been built, with tall buildings looming everywhere.
As soon as the two stepped out of the station, an elderly butler dressed in a black suit had been waiting for some time.
This was the butler from Sabina's estate and also a member of the Mirror Organization.
The old butler bowed respectfully, "Madam, sir, this way, please."
What slightly surprised Su Lun was that the vehicle the old butler had called for them was actually a classical carriage.
The carriage, pulled by four glossy black horses, bore golden paint patterns of eagles and lions on its hubs, the noble crest of the Rasel family.
Even though this transaction clearly seemed a trap, that old earl with the "Dark Holy Lamp" in hand had played his part well, sending a carriage to welcome the guests from the imperial city.
Getting on the carriage, an unexpected comfort.
Su Lun remembered that this was only the second time he had ridden in this antique mode of transport favored by the noble lords.
The last time was during his wedding with Yekaterina.
...
The carriage left the city and after a while, it was traveling upon a rugged wilderness trail.
The carriage's shock absorption was high-end, resulting in a smooth ride without any bumps.
Su Lun leaned against the edge of the carriage, casually observing the scenery outside the window.
Across from him, Mr. Jing, who could always read quietly no matter where she was, was flipping through an ancient book.
After about an hour's journey, they found themselves surrounded by a dense forest with a range of mountains stretching endlessly into the distance.
Before long, the view cleared, and a spectacular white stone castle appeared within sight.
This was a classic-style castle, built against a mountain, with a moat and drawbridge, and surrounded by a ring of piled stone walls, nearly devoid of any modern steam machinery.
Those old nobles just loved these ancient things to highlight their families' long history.
Su Lun looked through the carriage window at the castle and murmured, "What a beautiful castle..."
A flash of light passed through Mr. Jing's eyes, and she replied faintly, "Yes. It's a fine residence."
Unfortunately, it probably wouldn't exist after today.
The carriage crossed the drawbridge and stopped at the entrance of the castle.
The sale was arranged by Sabina, whose disguised identity was that of Countess Demacula. Her standing was comparable to that of Earl Rasel, owner of the castle; he, too, had spared no effort in demonstrating noble etiquette, arranging a group of people waiting at the entrance.
The leader was the butler of the Rasel family, a middle-aged man with goat-horn whiskers. He greeted Su Lun as they got off, "Sir, madam, please come inside. The lord has been awaiting your arrival for some time."
Su Lun exited the carriage unhurriedly and, like a gentleman, extended his hand to help Mr. Jing down.
The two followed the butler into the estate.
The estate was even more beautiful than it appeared from the outside, with gothic white towers, lovely cloisters, and vast beautiful roses and lavender permeating the air with a faint scent of flowers. The castle's setting harmoniously integrated with the mountains and forest; it was clearly designed by a master.
As they entered the estate, they saw a corpulent middle-aged man.
This fellow was Earl Rasel himself.
The portly earl greeted them with a stream of impeccable polite pleasantries before leading Su Lun and Mr. Jing around the estate to view the Rasel family's collection.
Su Lun was well aware that this fellow was simply biding time; after all, those mages needed quite a bit of time to set up the formations.
He pretended not to notice and leisurely toured the estate with Mr. Jing.
...
Meanwhile, as Su Lun and his company headed for the Stormgar region, in the study of Frederic Royal Palace in the imperial capital Lington, Yekaterina, crowned upon her head, was gazing into a crystal ball.
The scene within the crystal ball showed a forest; in the far, far distance, a white stone castle the size of a sesame seed could be seen.
She had been watching for a long time and no one knew what she was thinking. Her beautiful purple pupils were as deep as the starry sky.
There was no one else in the room.
But then, a strange voice spoke, "Your Majesty, aren't we going to send reinforcements? According to the intelligence we've gathered, the three ninth-order sages of the Divine Plane that have descended are all missing, presumably having smuggled themselves here. If we concentrate our top-tier powers, we might stand a chance, but if... if something happens to the Mirror Organization's Mr. Jing on this mission, our situation could worsen."
...
Yekaterina listened quietly, her gaze still fixed on the crystal ball without responding for a long while.
From the direction of the shadowy corner behind the curtains, the voice belonged to the head of the intelligence department, known as the "Black Clown," March Creton.
No one knew of this person's existence, nor had anyone ever seen him before.
But he was indeed a powerful professional, at the pinnacle of the eighth order.
This was one of the most important aides left to her by her former teacher, Master Pierre, when he handed over the intelligence department to her.
No one knew of these hidden forces within the intelligence department, which were sufficient to overthrow the Bonaparte royal family before.
Indeed, after the scandal of Marquis Heins defecting to the enemy broke out days ago, Yekaterina guessed everything.
The people Marquis Heins would rather commit suicide than betray are few within the empire.
But even though she'd guessed, the current situation didn't allow for reckless movements.
First, those fellows were meticulous in their actions, without solid evidence to point to, no one could touch them.
The second was the current state of the empire, which couldn't smash the original structure before other pillars of support were in place, or the consequences would be unpredictable.
It was only after Yekaterina learned of Mr. Jing's plans that she saw a major turning point.
As long as the Dawn Organization could win, her plans might also be carried out, and the last bit of hidden trouble inside the empire would be completely resolved.
But... as March Creton said, it was almost like betting the fate of the nation.
If Dawn were defeated, those top-tier mages of the enemy might even directly threaten Lington.
With a traitor working from the inside, those guys might even have plans to behead her, the emperor herself.
By then, the Alchemy Plane would not even have a last stand.
In the study, there had been no sound for a long time.
Yekaterina looked out the window, the rain in Lington always pattering.
After pondering for a moment, she spoke indifferently, "Get ready. Once the results from there come out, Lington will also undergo its last major purge."
With these words, the person lurking in the shadow of the curtains grew anxious, "Your Majesty, if you'll permit my bluntness, do you believe that Dawn is certain to win?"
Yekaterina thought that she should give everyone a bit of confidence, and spoke lightly, "Go prepare. Divination tells me that this battle will be most auspicious."
Hearing this, March Creton, "Black Clown," said no more.
Only he knew that the Empress before his eyes was unmatched in political strategy and her strength far exceeded everyone's expectations.
He responded, "Yes, Your Majesty."
Upon sensing the person departing, Yekaterina turned her gaze toward the Crystal Ball, slightly furrowing her brow, and her lips curled slightly.
There was still one thing she hadn't said, and that was, she knew Su Lun never engaged in matters without certainty.
...
In the forest manor of Earl Rasel.
In a classically decorated and luxurious salon, the chubby Earl Rasel was still stalling for time, "Two distinguished guests, since Countess Demacula sent the two of you here to discuss, clearly there's sincerity. It's not that I don't want to sell this 'Dark Holy Lamp'; it's just that it is a treasured heirloom of my family. Selling it is somewhat difficult for me. What I mean is... I can consider lending it to seal me if you require it..."
Opposite him, Su Lun and Mr. Jing were leisurely sipping tea, watching the man's desperate performance.
The man had already delayed them for half an hour, but the two were not in a hurry.
At that moment, the black raven on his shoulder suddenly cawed.
Su Lun then looked out the window, his eyes shimmering, as he saw the surge of magic power and put down his teacup.
Mr. Jing also appeared very calm, asking, "What do you see?"
At this question, Earl Rasel's face across from them became embarrassed.
He thought he hadn't been exposed and countered, "Are you asking me, my lady?"
However, Mr. Jing completely ignored the man's intent.
Su Lun didn't pay attention to him either.
Continuing their conversation, he responded, "The ninth-tier Forbidden Curse 'Holy Shackles' has already formed. It seems there are at least nine eighth-tier mages lying in ambush nearby."
Mr. Jing listened with an unchanged expression, taking another sip of his tea.
But this abrupt dialogue made Earl Rasel's face change dramatically, stammering, "This..."
Hearing words like "mages" and "ambush," he knew something had gone wrong.
He couldn't understand, there had been no abnormalities a second before, so why were they suddenly detected?
And if they were detected, why were these two so composed?
The man was about to argue when suddenly a line of blood appeared on his neck.
The seventh-tier captain of the guards by his side reacted slightly, but when he looked at Mr. Jing, his eyes were met with an endless mirage, and then his vitality strangely and rapidly dissipated.
Su Lun casually harvested both souls, and the ins and outs of this conspiracy immediately became clear.
It was just as they had suspected.
Su Lun murmured, "So it is indeed Master Merlin... heh, quite the technique, never intervening from start to finish, letting these old nobles be the go-between, playing both ends for the middle. Tsk, such a clever ploy."
As he spoke, he gripped the black umbrella in his hand. His Soul Perception had already sensed the strong soul fluctuations rapidly approaching from outside the manor.
Su Lun glanced at his senior sister and said, "Looks like there are three ninth-tier Law Sages. Quite tricky, senior sister."
Mr. Jing's expression finally showed a hint of unusual color, yet still devoid of any fear, "Mm, leave it to me."
Su Lun raised an eyebrow, "Alright, I'll go break the formation then."
"Mm."
Mr. Jing nodded.
It was in the moment she set down her teacup that she erupted with an incomparably terrifying aura, pinching the sorcerer's seals, "Domain: Mirror of All Aspects!"
How frightful is it when a Nine-Rank Professional fully unleashes their domain?
The furniture in the parlor couldn't withstand the pressure of that mysterious force and in an instant turned into dust.
For Su Lun, this was his first encounter with his sister's peak state after reaching the ninth rank. His pupils shrank slightly, and he exclaimed with a smile, "Sister, you're so strong."
Mr. Jing glanced at him, having already entered an absolutely indifferent mirrored state, and said in a deep voice, "I'll go and draw their attention first."
Before the words even faded, a flash of mirror light swept the room, and she had already vanished on the spot.
Upon seeing this, Su Lun sensed the enemy's location and with a flicker of spatial fluctuation, he too disappeared from the spot.
...
The mages of the divine plane had no idea what was happening in the estate, but sensing the sudden burst of powerful energy, they thought their target was about to flee, and they immediately took action.
Almost simultaneously, a nine-pointed star magic circle of holy light materialized in the sky.
One after another, chains of white light wove into a vast net in the sky, sealing off a radius of more than ten miles around the manor with stringent tightness.
The Nine-Rank Forbidden Curse "Holy Shackles" is a large-scale holy spell, inflicting massive damage bonuses to creatures of the darkness.
The moment Mr. Jing emerged, she collided with the dense web of magic like a spider's web; chains of holy light immediately ensnared her body.
Moreover, the magic circle in the sky not only restrained her but also acted like a focusing lens, concentrating sunlight, which was hugely damaging to the vampiric race, especially the ultraviolet rays, into the magic circle.
The sunlight scorched Mr. Jing's skin with a sizzling and distressing sound, and visibly charred marks appeared on her pale skin.
Even Mr. Jing frowned for a moment, but her wounds healed instantly.
In such a situation, even if she wanted to escape, it would be difficult.
And the deities from the divine plane did not just prepare a magic circle, but three Nine-Rank Sages of Law had personally arrived!
The very instant Mr. Jing appeared, three mages in magic cloaks charged at her from three different directions. Enveloped by powerful sanctified auras, they launched Ninth-Rank magic spells at the outset.
"O Supreme God of Light, here I beseech you for the power of light... Forbidden Curse: Holy Light Judgment!"
"I swim against the flow of time's long river, peering into the secrets of the ages, the great god bestows upon me to witness the mysteries of time magic... Chronal Forbidden Curse: Time Stop!"
"Awaken, O Great All-knowing Deity, buried deep within my blood is endless magic power... Earth's Mysteries: Hundred Thousand Gravities!"
Three arcane magic incantations were recited from their mouths, and suddenly, a tremendous magic power surged above the estate.
Sages of Law had already touched the pinnacle of human power, casting Ninth-Rank spells in an instant.
All were of the ninth rank, and the opponents gave no chance for response; three magic spells were hurled at Mr. Jing, ensnared by the magic formation.
During the previous ambush, it was because they underestimated Mr. Jing's mirror image replication ability that their efforts came to nothing.
However, post that engagement, they had come to know of Mr. Jing's special ability.
Mirror image replication had guaranteed her near-invulnerability against any opponent.
But this time, there were three of ninth rank.
Meaning, even if Mr. Jing could ward off one, the other two would be enough to doom her.
The plan was perfect.
It was enough to kill any Ninth-Rank Professional.
But that was the Jing of the past.
Not the Jing of now!
Mr. Jing, facing the three Ninth-Rank spells coming at her, remained expressionless. Her gaze suddenly intensified, "Mirror Kaleidoscope Gear!"
At that instant, a bizarre scene unfolded.
Suddenly, a flash of mirror light crossed her body.
Like creating afterimages, her body split into three, turning into three identical figures!
This was not a simple replication but three mirror duplicates that were indistinguishable even in aura.
As the three Mr. Jings appeared, they simultaneously pinched the sorcerer's seals, "Ultimate Mirror: Mirror Image Collapse."
Upon completion of the incantation, a transparent spell mirror materialized in front of each of them.
Almost at the same moment, the three spells struck the Mr. Jing in the sky, but the three mirrors replicated the time, earth, and holy light triad of Ninth-Rank spells on them, colliding and exploding in the sky.
This was not only a clash of magical incantations but also a collision between high-order laws. The shockwave wasn't just a wave on the energy level; it was as if the surrounding world turned into a canvas that someone had violently torn down.
Ripples from the clash of laws spread instantaneously, and the Earl Rasel's forest manor bore the brunt.
The sturdy walls crumbled like a sand castle under the horrific shockwave, instantly turning into dust, while the beautiful garden was reduced to ruins; behind the manor, the snow mountain's rocks and snow surged down like a burst dam; birds and beasts startled in the forest, but before they could flee far, they perished in droves...
Such is the fearsome power of combat between Ninth-Ranks!
The three Sages of Law on the other side turned pale, shocked that Mr. Jing remained unharmed.
Even more surprisingly, she had single-handedly withstood their combined finishing blow?
Mr. Jing, having withstood three Ninth-Rank spells, looked at her enemies and each of her mirror duplicates charged fiercely at a Sage of Law.
The battle instantly escalated to a heated pitch.
...
Meanwhile, Su Lun had already teleported to a forest several miles away.
Watching Mr. Jing face three opponents without falling behind in the slightest, he exclaimed in admiration, "Sister's ability is really strong."
The second solution [Mirror Guardian] was able to replicate anything.
It might not be able to replicate as quickly in a one-on-one situation, but now with the [Mirror Kaleidoscope Gear], it was an ideal combination.
Not to mention three, Su Lun believed that once his senior sister grew even stronger, she could replicate up to ten or eight of herself, wouldn't that mean there would be ten or eight ninth-rank Mages?
Nevertheless, Su Lun also noticed something.
Although Mr. Jing's ability was strong, replicating others' possessions was easy to stave off, but achieving victory was significantly harder.
In a one-versus-three scenario, she had to divide her strength in three, so at least in the short term, there was no possibility of determining a winner.
Su Lun narrowed his eyes slightly and did not dare to delay for even a moment.
He hadn't forgotten his mission.
There were at least nine eighth-rank great Mages nearby the manor, gathering a ninth-rank forbidden magic circle—[Holy Shackles].
Once that magic formation was dealt with, Mr. Jing's combat power would be fully unleashed.
It was then that Su Lun raised his hand and a flicker of spatial fluctuation occurred, and several people wearing gold-patterned cloaks appeared around him.
Number 19, the Old Sword God Bartolo, 'Blood Duke' Wazhwas, Mr. Hei...
If the enemy was bringing reinforcements, the Dawn was not short on them either.
The Dawn organization might not have many above the eighth rank, but each one was an elite, more than enough to deal with the current situation.
With a large-scale spatial transmission formation on the Eternal Night, for Su Lun, it was simply a matter of expending a bit more energy to make a trip, regardless of where the ship was located.
Usually, a magic formation formed by nine eighth-rank great Mages was impenetrable, and even Mr. Jing couldn't escape from it.
But within Su Lun's grasp was the [Urobolos Space-Time Ring], which meant he could walk sideways in the alchemy plane.
Since the enemy couldn't set up a magic formation beyond the plane's regulations, any spatial restrictions were meaningless to him.
When the members of the Dawn surfaced, they nodded at each other and vanished on the spot, each dashing towards a corner of the magic formation.
From the moment Su Lun felt the magic fluctuations, the formation held no secrets from him.
He had already distributed the battle plans, and as long as they could instantly break through three corners of the formation, it would immediately collapse.
Only then would the real battle commence.
...
Just how terrifying was the power in a ninth-rank battle?
It was at the same time as the battle erupted in Earl Rasel's forest manor that Clemington, dozens of kilometers away, was immediately aware of it.
The weather was clear that day, and even the most proficient professionals could clearly see the terrifying disturbance, akin to a volcanic eruption.
Mountain ranges collapsed, towering trees fell in large swaths, and everyone instantly realized that top experts were battling there.
On the other hand, this news also traveled through various channels back to the imperial capital, Lynden.
The high-ranking officials of the United Empire all received the message, each of them greatly surprised.
They were curious to know, who exactly was in the battle?
There were currently only two known ninth-rank professionals in the alchemy plane: one was the court's foremost Master Merlin, and the other was the Dawn's Mr. Jing.
Those well-informed big shots knew that Mr. Jing was injured and immediately connected the dots with the recent underground market reward, realizing that Mr. Jing might have fallen into a conspiracy ambush.
The big shots immediately realized that something terrible was afoot.
To be attacked within the heartland of Luying meant that the most important traitors within the Empire had made their move!
Everyone knew that if Mr. Jing were indeed to be killed in ambush, the traitors would certainly join forces with the enemies of the Divine plane, bringing irreversible calamitous consequences to the Empire. The alchemy plane might not recover from such a setback.
Almost immediately, countless military dignitaries rushed to the Royal Palace, hoping that the Emperor would send reinforcements.
But no one held out much hope, as the enemy had planned an ambush and had chosen the location far away from the capital, in the southern territory of Stormgarde.
If reinforcements were to be sent, it was feared everything would be too late.
However, before the wave of pessimism could spread, a series of battle reports fed back, dispersing the despair in the hearts of the Lynden officials a bit, and they began to feel an increasing sense of joy instead.
An ambush that should have ended quickly in a short time was stretching out, fought to a standstill?
The news shocked everyone.
Three ninth-rank Law Sages had come from the Divine plane, joined by over nine eighth-rank great Mages, a force capable of destroying any city other than Lynden.
Yet what shocked everyone even more was that the Dawn organization had managed to withstand these forces head-on with their own strength!
And it was not just a struggle to a draw; as one report after another of the ongoing battle conditions came back, everyone realized that the Dawn organization might even have a chance of winning.
Although they did not know why the Dawn would create such a miracle, the news spread, and for a time, the entire United Empire's military morale soared.
However, this turn of events threw those in the capital who had secretly defected to the enemy, the surrender faction, into complete panic.

chapters.title: Chapter 617 - 616: Siege on the Ninth Order
chapters.content:
Claymington, Earl Rasel's forest estate.
The ninth tier is where humans grasp the ultimate laws that can be understood, the pinnacle of combat power. Whether they are mages or alchemists, they possess extraordinary powers capable of destroying heaven and earth.
In a three-against-three encounter, they started with various forbidden spells, fighting so fiercely that the shockwaves quickly reduced the originally classical and beautiful estate to ruins, along with the nearby mountains and forests.
In the sky, Mr. Jing split into three and continued to fiercely battle with those three ninth-tier Sages of Law.
On the other hand, Su Lun and a group of high-end warriors from the Dawn Brigade had already ambushed their respective targets.
In the blink of an eye, fierce battles erupted throughout the mountain forest.
Sword Qi crisscrossed, various high-level spells emerged endlessly, and the noise of the battle surged wave after wave.
The celestial beings on the divine plane were completely baffled; before they began, they had not anticipated such fierce resistance.
They thought it was a foolproof beheading ambush, but just at the first encounter, they immediately felt something was terribly wrong.
This was not like an ambush; rather, it seemed like they had been ambushed!
That "Mr. Jing" was not only unharmed but had become much stronger than before. So much so that the three ninth-tier Sages of Law found him extremely troublesome.
Moreover, these were clearly beings from a dark abyss race, yet their resistance to the Holy Light was so high?
They had inflicted heavy damage last time; why was the same tactic so ineffective this time?
Moreover, other circumstances greatly differed from the information they had received from the deserters. They were supposed to eliminate targets at the eighth and ninth tiers, yet it turned out there were many powerhouses ambushed?
Where did so many experts from the Alchemy plane come from?
But even though they knew something was wrong, they had no choice but to fight; the magic formation was set, and they were bound to clash.
Especially under the current circumstances, the Dawn Brigade would not let them leave easily.
...
Su Lun also teleported and appeared in front of a cave.
This location was equipped with a simple magic tower; immense magic power surged, and an eighth-tier Red-robed Archmage was continuously gathering magic power into the formation at his feet.
Seeing Su Lun approaching, the Red-robed Mage did not panic at all and immediately started chanting a complex spell.
In an instant, the light from the nine-pointed star formation at his feet flared up, and a visibly thick golden defensive barrier was already fortified around him.
Su Lun recognized this as the ninth-tier arcanum-level legionary combined magic barrier "Ninefold Golden Light Spell."
This barrier could withstand almost any ninth-tier spell and was the most suitable for standing ground and dealing damage.
With this restraint, even if several eighth-tier fighters came, he could hold his ground without defeat for a short time.
The guy did not take Su Lun seriously but continued to maintain the magic formation beneath him as lines of Holy Light Chains kept flying towards Mr. Jing in the sky.
They knew very well that, cutting off this ninth-tier alchemical native could allow the three Sages of Law to free their hands, instantly stabilizing the situation.
Regrettably,
this Red-robed Archmage had yet to realize what kind of opponent he was facing.
Seeing someone approaching, the man casually tore a precious eighth-tier magic scroll from the sleeve of his robe and instantly cast a Lightning Technique, striking with a crack.
This experienced Grand Magician's reaction was beyond reproach. Lightning magic was known for its attack speed and potency, and since he was prepared, it was unavoidable; thus, even a fighter of the same tier would have been severely damaged.
However, it was this sure-hit strike that led to an unexpected scene unfolding before him.
When he saw the opponent's body covered in dragon scale glyphs withstand the blast of this lightning spell, the Red-robed Mage's expression changed dramatically.
He could not comprehend how someone could directly withstand a blow of eighth-tier lightning magic.
Was this another ninth-tier alchemical native?
Clearly not.
...
Su Lun, observing the countless tiny lightning serpents erupting across his body, revealed a stern look in his eyes.
The Dragon-poised Golden Body enhancement, even Mr. Jing had highly praised it, How could a mere eighth-tier lightning spell injure him?
Yet he did not underestimate his enemy.
After all, it was the same tier, and he had formed a special formation.
The "Forbidden Curse: Holy Shackles" maintained by these nine eighth-tier Grand Magicians formed a legion with the magic power of the formation connecting them.
Facing one was like facing nine; their offensive and defensive capabilities were not inferior to facing a true ninth-tier.
And Su Lun was aware that besides forcefully breaking it, there was no other way to combat this kind of magic battle array.
That also meant, breaking through the first defensive corner would be the hardest.
Su Lun knew that conventional methods would hardly break through in a short time; if he could not break through, neither could any of the other formation points.
Meanwhile, Mr. Jing, still restricted by the Holy Light Chains, was facing three enemies alone. Each second of delay was a minute of danger, and he had to break through the situation quickly.
Su Lun had been prepared.
He raised his hand and pulled out several space scrolls, shouting crisply, "Release!"
The scrolls burst open, and ten thousand alchemical stone ghosts appeared on the scene, darkening the sky.
At the same time, a giant cross appeared in the sky. Threads connected the puppets, and the ten thousand stone ghosts instantly formed a legion formation.
The stone ghost legion moved uniformly. As soon as they appeared, they lifted their arms towards the Red-robed Mage without hesitation, a powerful spatial fluctuation rapidly building up.
The power of Su Lun's puppet legion's Combination Attack Technique could easily break through the defenses of a ten thousand-mage group; how could this one Grand Magician withstand it?
The Red-robed Mage, viewing the overwhelming horde of ten thousand puppets, looked incredulous and pallid.
He, a leader of a ten thousand-mage group, did not fail to recognize that these puppets were arranged in some kind of combination attack formation.
However, to maintain the formation, he could not retreat.
In his moment of despair, after destroying over a hundred stone ghosts with a few spells, the Red-robed Mage faced the crushing blow.
A massive fist formed by the Space Law in the sky and with a boom, it struck like a falling meteor.
The golden magic shield lasted only a moment, shattering like a broken eggshell, and after fracturing, the situation became irreversible.
The mage tower at the formation point was forcibly breached, and the shockwave continued, creating a huge crater with a hundred-meter diameter on the ground before finally dissipating.
The Red-robed Mage was crushed into a pulp, his blood spattering through the air.
Su Lun casually harvested the soul, glanced at it, and muttered, "The puppet legion loves these stationary type of opponents."
...
With the first formation point broken, the complete battle formation of the nine Grand Magicians quickly collapsed.
In other areas, the high-ranking fighters of Dawn Group also quickly achieved their victories.
The elite fighters of the Dawn Group, two against one, now found it no problem to quickly eliminate an eighth-level Mage now that the formation had broken.
Su Lun was not idle either; he had already teleported to another formation point and repeated his tactic, using the puppet legion and the secret technique of "Death God's Fire," to quickly dispose of the second eighth-level Grand Magician.
He had previously killed eighth-level Grand Magicians in the Dragon Country Waters, but those fights were risky gambles, each encounter walking on thin ice. For a seventh-level, the domain of the eighth-level Grand Magician was a crushing threat at the level of the laws.
But now, having advanced to the eighth level, Su Lun's understanding of the laws was incomparable to before, and the dominance granted by his "Isaac Dragon Patterned Golden Body" allowed him to possess a virtually indestructible body against all eighth-level magic.
Su Lun could kill enemies, but it was hard for his opponents to harm him.
Thus, the threat from ordinary eighth-levels was very limited now.
In just a short time after the battle had begun, many formation points had already been broken.
With each broken formation point, the bonds of Holy Light Chains on Mr. Jing in the sky loosened, and her combat power grew fiercer.
In the blink of an eye, five formation points were successively broken, completely collapsing the Forbidden Curse: Holy Shackles.
This change shocked the three Sages of Law once again.
Seeing Mr. Jing's growing combat strength, they realized the magic formation had been compromised.
Even though it would take them considerable time to break the formation created by the nine eighth-level Grand Magicians, they could not fathom how the natives of the Alchemy Plane had managed it.
However surprising it was, the ability to advance to the ninth level was not just about talent; all three were combatants who had survived numerous deadly battles. They reacted immediately.
Almost at the moment Su Lun killed the second Grand Magician, Mr. Jing urgently cautioned through the communicator, "Everyone, be careful, a Sage of Law is heading your way!"
Mr. Jing's cloning ability could withstand three Sages of Law undefeated, which was no small feat. But if the enemy took other actions in the meantime, she couldn't completely stop them.
Especially one with the very unique ability of the Time Sage of Law!
Hearing the warning, Su Lun's expression hardened.
With a flash in the spatial fluctuation, he did not hesitate to confront the ninth-level Sage of Law head-on.
...
Even though Dawn Group had previously hunted down eighth-level dragons in the Dragon Country Waters, comparable to ninth-level professionals in strength, those were still eighth-level creatures.
At the level of the laws, a ninth-level Sage of Law holds the ultimate understanding of humanly accessible laws, touching the threshold of the rules themselves.
Beyond the seventh level, each level represents a massive threshold.
Without reaching that height, one cannot comprehend why the capabilities of the ninth level are so fearsomely powerful.
This overwhelming dominance at the level of laws poses a lethal threat to those below the ninth level.
Just like during the Spiritdon Catastrophe, Master Pierre, even severely injured, could easily eliminate an eighth-level expert who attempted to assault him.
Yet strangely, Su Lun could understand the gap between the laws.
He was currently the most physically resilient in the Dawn Group, and only he had some confidence in confronting the ninth level head-on.
Moreover, he found it hard to feel pressured by his peers now and wanted to test just how strong a ninth-level Sage of Law really was.
In that instant, Su Lun had already teleported several miles.
Upon his arrival, he saw an old mage with a white beard charging toward Old Sword God Bartolo and Number Nineteen, who were ganging up on a Grand Magician of the eighth level.
As soon as the ninth-level Sage of Law arrived, the terrifying pressure caused everyone's scalp to tingle.
However, a bizarre scene immediately unfolded.
The white-bearded Sage of Law did not use magic to fly; instead, his figure flickered and teleported forward.
As he closed in, he softly chanted, and his magic wand suddenly emitted a gentle white light, instantly unfurling a holy field.
This white light spread like ripples, seemingly invoking some high-level Power of Laws, instantly covering the entire area.
Although Old Sword God Bartolo and Number Nineteen were extremely strong among their peers, they were far from understanding the laws at the ninth level. They had no idea what had happened.
Moreover, it was the exceedingly rare Time Law.
To others, the old man simply teleported over, but to Su Lun, who was also proficient in Time Law, it appeared different.
He clearly saw local time being distorted, cycling at a speed nearly a hundred times that of the stopping forbidden.
And only the old man was unaffected.
That is to say, time in the senses of Old Sword God Bartolo and the others was nearly stopped, while the old man was completely unaffected.
Just this move alone was enough to trap them in a fatal situation!
This level of combat was often just so, in the blink of an eye, life and death could be decided.
Unfortunately, Su Lun made a decisive move.
From the first sight of the three Sages of Law, he had already roughly gauged their strength.
And after harvesting the memories of two Grand Magicians of the eighth level just now, his intelligence gathering was complete.
He knew very well that this man named "Sage of Time" Ralph Zimmerman was a Sage of Law who had mastered Time Law.
Light streamed brilliantly in Su Lun's eyes, and no matter how clever the enemy's methods, there were no secrets in his view.
Looking at the legendary wand in the old man's hand, he couldn't help but mutter, "The wand is actually inlaid with a 'Time Crystal Core'. Tsk tsk, what a treasure..."
In the past, he also had a bit of "Sand of Time" which was already a treasure of the planes. Now this fellow was luckier, having obtained a crystalized time gemstone as the energy core of the wand.
Even just the materials from dismantling this legendary quality wand were invaluable.
Indeed, great treasures were always amassed by the top powerhouses.
...
Using temporal methods to kill, even if Old Sword God Bartolo's swordsmanship was extremely sophisticated, he couldn't exert half of his power. Unwittingly, he would be killed.
This was the tricky aspect of Time Law.
If you can't understand the mysteries of time's flow, you can only drift along in the river of time.
Moreover, Ralph Zimmerman's understanding of Time Law was very profound, so profound that although Su Lun could understand it, he knew he was at least one or two major levels below in understanding.
Trapped in the Time Holy Domain, they could only be slaughtered at will.
Unfortunately for them, Su Lun possessed the "Urobolos Space-Time Ring," a supreme artifact of space-time.
If his cultivation was insufficient, artifacts would make up for it.
This ring allowed him to ignore almost all sub-divine levels of time law erosion.
When the Time Holy Domain was spread, Su Lun also acted as if he was caught, his body entering a state of relative stasis, just like Bartolo and the others.
However, the moment the old man with the wand drew near, he suddenly burst forth!
His body was wrapped in a layer of surging green flames as he slashed at the old man with his sword.
...
Ralph Zimmerman initially thought that this strike was sufficient to instantly kill these alchemy natives, yet he never expected that just as he was about to act, out of the corner of his eye, he spotted someone rushing toward him within his Holy Light Domain.
How did this guy manage it?
He couldn't understand how an alchemy native, much lower in rank than himself, could ignore the twists of time.
"He has a temporal artifact on him!"
Ralph Zimmerman immediately realized what was happening.
Upon seeing the glaring Death God's Fire, his brow furrowed tightly, sensing a fatal threat.
After all, being a Sage of Law, his reaction was extremely swift, and a magic power shield instantly formed around his body, this was clearly the ninth-level Arcane Art "Elemental Symphony".
It was when Su Lun attacked, engulfed in flames, that the shield suddenly burst open.
A muffled "bang" sounded, and a figure was instantly blasted hundreds of meters away.
But before he could catch his breath, the space next to him fluctuated, and the person holding the black scythe reappeared.
"Eh?"
Ralph Zimmerman, holding his magic wand, had just targeted Number Nineteen with his piercing light beam when he stopped, deeply puzzled in his heart.
Having taken on an "Elemental Symphony" head-on, even if he wasn't severely injured, there shouldn't be no sign of damage at all, and immediately being able to counterattack, right?
This was definitely not something an ordinary eighth-level Alchemist could achieve!
Seeing the dragon scale runes faintly visible on Su Lun, the old man immediately guessed something: "This guy's body is also strange!"
He knew that advancements in the alchemy system involved integrating some special cursed objects to enhance oneself, and if this person could withstand a ninth-level spell, it meant the quality of the object integrated during his advancement was very high.
Ralph thought of this, his eyes momentarily clouded then cleared.
But the black scythe was already slashing towards him, and he had no choice but to perform a magical teleportation to evade.
Upon looking again, he had reappeared hundreds of meters away.
...
It was this brief skirmish in which Su Lun repelled the ninth-level Sage of Law and let out a slight sigh, murmuring to himself, "How strong. So this is the ninth-level..."
Meanwhile, the three not far away felt as if there was a visual skip.
Suddenly, they saw the old man reappear hundreds of meters away, while Su Lun holding the black scythe had already appeared as if ready for a grand battle.
Number Nineteen looked at the burn mark on her chest, her gaze extremely solemn.
Her skin had been burned through, exposing the charred mechanical armor beneath, yet she hadn't even realized how these marks had appeared; it was as if they simply popped up in the blink of an eye.
The Old Sword God Bartolo frowned, immediately perceiving something.
The timing was off!
Before he could think further, Su Lun warned, "Be careful, this guy has mastery over Time Law."
Number Nineteen and Old Sword God Bartolo knew they had just walked along the line of death.
In that moment, mirror light flashed in the sky, and Mr. Jing's doppelganger also arrived.
As Ralph Zimmerman's aura had not yet stabilized from his previous retreat, he was struck by Mr. Jing, causing his body to briefly stiffen.
Seeing his chance, the Old Sword God Bartolo drew his sword swiftly, slashing a snowflake Sword Qi towards the sky.
This sword could cleave an eighth-level giant dragon, and could certainly chop down a Sage of Law!
Ralph Zimmerman's face slightly changed, unable to completely avoid the attack, and with a "sizzle", the Sword Qi tore through the magic shield, carving a wound on his body.
Seeing the blood from his wound, the Sage of Law realized that these people had the strength to kill him, and said with heavy seriousness, "To have reached the realm of laws... it turns out he is a Sword God..."
Before he could ponder further, in his field of view, Su Lun with the black scythe charged at him again.
Ralph frowned deeply; in his view, this man who ignored his time sanctuary was the biggest threat.
No!
All these people are strong.
He was also surprised, how could the alchemy plane produce so many eighth-level Magicians capable of withstanding ninth-level ones?
Su Lun and the others wouldn't give the enemy a chance, already collectively swarming to attack.
And Bartolo and his group knew their mission well; they did not pause, attacking again towards those eighth-level grand Magic Conductors still alive.
The communicator also continued to transmit good news, with only a few left of the nine formation corners.
Now that the formation was broken, the Dawn Group merely needed to defeat those eighth-level enemies, then they could focus their strength to gradually encircle and kill the three Sages of Law.
This was the heartland of Luying, where there was no ten-thousand-strong magic group for reinforcements.
The longer the delay, the more advantageous it was for the Dawn Group.
As for Su Lun, he teamed up with Mr. Jing's avatar to first engage Ralph Zimmerman.
Among the three Sages of Law, this time-weaving elder was the most troublesome.
As for the other Elemental Sage of Law and the Holy Light Sage of Law, their abilities, though deadly to the other Dawn Group members, were common elemental magic, posing far less threat than those mastering Time Law.
Such a high level of risk was inherent in this battle; from the start, the members of the Dawn Group were prepared for a fierce fight.

chapters.title: Chapter 618 - 617: Harvesting Ninth-Order Souls
chapters.content:
"Tsk tsk, so this is the ninth tier..."
Su Lun remembered this was the eighth time he had been blasted away by a magic missile.
The magic shockwave threw him hard to the ground, his bones and muscles aching as if a glass bottle had shattered; the violent Power of Laws felt like needles trying to pierce his domain, an indescribable pain.
But as soon as he landed, Su Lun immediately teleported away from the spot, dodging the subsequent deadly strikes.
Despite looking disheveled, he remained lively and vigorous.
For someone of the eighth tier to withstand so many attacks from a ninth tier Sage of Law and still not die was enough to make anyone proud.
It was proven that the Alchemical Growth Armor "Isaac Dragon Pattern Golden Body," known to be the strongest defensive gear in the alchemy plane, had no equal.
Dragons inherently possessed high immunity against physical and magical damage, and merging with this gear was equivalent to wearing a set of portable full-body armor. Moreover, the main material Su Lun used to craft this gear was from an eighth-tier Hell Dragon of the darkness type, which inherently could withstand the impact of ninth-tier spells.
The dragon race's physical talent compensated for the defensive gap at the level of Laws, resisting most of the energy impacts and law erosion from ninth-tier magic.
Furthermore, the "Isaac Alchemy Heart" provided nearly infinite dark spiritual power, allowing the Dragon Pattern Golden Body to maintain its strongest defense state almost continuously.
During the battle, Su Lun also roughly estimated that, with the armor and his overwhelming body, even facing ninth-tier spells, the damage reduction exceeded 95%.
The remaining damage was insignificant to Su Lun's already formidable physical body. He also had the "Blood Devour" ability to continuously heal his injuries.
As long as he avoided some fatal attacks, it was almost impossible for the ninth-tier Sage of Law to kill him in a short period of time.
The two sides continued their fierce battle in the mountains.
The tactics of the Dawn team were clear, all members first concentrated their power to kill those eighth-tier great magic conductors.
Under normal circumstances, an eighth-tier magic conductor from the Heavenly God's plane standing alone against an eighth-tier alchemist had hardly any chance of winning.
Moreover, the members of the Dawn team were all elites among their ranks, possessing the most top-tier abilities and equipment of the plane.
It didn't take long before nine eighth-tier great magic conductors were all slain.
Pestoya, Pandora, Number Nineteen, Old Sword God Bartolo, "Blood Duke" Wazhuvas, Mr. Hei, and other high fighters of Dawn, along with Mr. Jing and Su Lun, began to encircle and attack the three Sages of Law.
...
The three opposing Sages of Law grew increasingly frustrated as the battle progressed.
Originally, the most powerful among them was "Time Saint" Ralph Zimmerman. His time magic posed a great threat to anyone.
Even when he had previously encountered Mr. Jing, he had gained the upper hand.
The secrets of time were not simply a matter of copying spells.
It could be said without exaggeration that as long as he was present, any number of eighth-tier attackers would be meaningless.
Under the mystery of time, all beings are equal.
This was almost a counter to all laws, yet unaffected by any.
That's why they dared to lead a group deep into the heart of Luying.
Even when they realized they were ambushed at first, Ralph Zimmerman was confident enough that he could easily kill these alchemists of the alchemical plane alone. If not, he could easily escape.
However, he never expected someone like Su Lun, completely unaffected by his Time Holy Domain, to emerge.
Moreover, not only was he unaffected, but even after being hit directly by ninth-tier spells multiple times, this eighth-tier alchemist couldn't be killed?
More importantly, the "Death God's Fire," which directly burns the soul, posed a lethal threat even to ninth-tiers, and no Sage of Law dared to confront it directly.
Ability to resist, physical body comparable to ninth-tier, attacking methods comparable to ninth-tier...
This made Ralph Zimmerman feel increasingly limited, his usual prowess in time manipulation hardly displayed at all.
The situation grew increasingly dire.
There was also Mr. Jing, whose ability to copy was extremely troublesome.
With three avatars each possessing ninth-tier combat power, copying various spells to clash, this type of attack was not particularly tricky, but it was incredibly tenacious.
Even with all the diverse methods employed by the three Sages of Law, they couldn't do anything to her in a short time.
The longer the battle dragged on, the less favorable it became for the three Sages of Law from the Heavenly God's plane.
...
"O great earth elements roaming between heaven and earth, gods sleeping in the mountains, heed my command... Summon: Emperor Rock Demon!"
"Dark Rule: Light Banishing Technique!"
"Forbidden Curse: Sun God Bird!"
"Arcane: Blazing Angel!"
"..."
In the mountains outside Clementon, it was like a cauldron gathering magic, where various high-tier forbidden spells and arcanes were unleashed freely.
Gargantuan rock giants hundreds of meters tall, sun god birds made of sunlight, endless domains of darkness, close-combat mages transformed into blazing angels...
After being encircled by members of Dawn, the three Sages of Law unleashed all kinds of methods, resembling a grand magic exhibition, with dazzling magic light waves exploding in the sky.
With Mr. Jing's ability to copy, almost all forbidden curses were summoned in double.
The terrifying aftermath of the explosions surged wave after wave.
The two sides were evenly matched.
But in fact, right after the Dawn Brigade had killed those nine eighth-level grand Magic Conductors, the scale of victory had already quietly tilted towards the Dawn Brigade.
The one who mastered the Power of Laws of time, "Saint Time" Ralph Zimmerman, was the strongest in this surprise attack squad of the Heavenly Plane, originally the main force in the offense.
But for Su Lun, this guy was actually the easiest to deal with.
With him always watching this one, the other members of the Dawn Brigade concentrated their firepower to surround and kill the other two.
Unit 19's mechanical angelic body still performed outstandingly in the ninth-level battle, charging fearlessly at the forefront;
Old Sword God Bartolo's sword energy swept through hundreds of meters, wherever it passed, it severed mountains and split the earth;
Pestoya and Pandora, one with divine technique and the other with the Death God's Fire, posed a huge threat to the ninth level;
And there were Mr. Hei, Vazhuvas...
Then Mr. Jing's clones were also giving the three Sage of Laws of the Heavenly Plane quite a headache.
However, seeing no chance of victory, they wanted to retreat, but it was simply not possible.
Whether it was Su Lun's Spatial Teleportation or Mr. Jing's mirror Teleportation, both were top-notch means of movement in the realm. How could they give their enemies a chance to escape?
If the enemy fled, they would immediately stick to them.
The two sides continued this fierce battle, the fighting unabated and lasted for nearly half a day.
The shockwave of the battle wreaked havoc over an area of a hundred miles; even the city of Klemington was affected. The buildings in the city were massively destroyed by the shockwave, and the people panicked and fled out of the city for refuge.
The governor led by Stormga assembled an army of over one hundred thousand and arrived at Klemington promptly.
But no one dared to approach the center of that terrifying battlefield.
This level of battle left no room for practitioners below the eighth level; anyone who tried would die.
The motivation for the battle grew larger, and journalists and information traders became active; the situation in Klemington, along with various news channels, was factually relayed back to the capital, Lindon.
...
After all, being ninth-level Sages of Law, even though Su Lun and his team had thoroughly planned, this battle was very tough and fraught with danger.
Not until the evening, did a turning point arrive.
It happened during the fight when Mr. Hei suddenly found a breakthrough opportunity.
"Plan C!"
"Okay!"
The methods used by the high-level warriors of the Dawn Brigade posed a certain deadly threat to the ninth level.
But to say whose methods were the most covert and sharp, Mr. Hei was second to none!
This Scholar had now successfully transplanted the "Heavenly God's Eye" of Saint Frank, and because of this divine eye, he also possessed the ability "All-encompassing True Resolution," akin to a bug in power.
Combined with the understanding of the world gained after drinking from the Spring of Wisdom, Mr. Hei's lethality was far beyond what could be measured by a novice at the eighth level.
Clearly, the three Sages of Laws were still completely unaware.
Mr. Hei had been performing in a standard manner in the previous battles.
Not outstanding, neither appearing very weak.
Just like an ordinary eighth-level alchemist.
Mr. Hei's combat style had always been like tepid water, without sharp methods to defeat strong enemies, but capable of steady output that was hard to beat.
So even when clashing with ninth-level magic several times just now, he calmly used alchemy to resolve the crises.
His defense was more than adequate, but his offensive methods were not seen as a great threat to the ninth level.
And it was these moderate offensive methods that led the three enemy Sages of Laws to regard him as the least threatening among the Dawn Brigade, gradually coming to neglect him.
It was this impression that Mr. Hei had intentionally created for the enemy that brought a turning point in the battle.
...
This level of ninth-tier combat actually had a minimal effect when it came to strategies.
Practitioners become more alert to crises as they rise in level.
But this alertness tends to decrease the longer the battle drags on.
From the beginning, Su Lun had already considered this.
Seeing the enemy's strength, he had calculated and knew that even if the members of the Dawn Brigade used all their methods, the potential to quickly kill the three Sages of Laws was not great.
But revealing all their cards from the start would instead likely lead to some other variables.
After the battle started, Su Lun confirmed this idea even more.
The three Sages of Laws were very strong and highly alert, making a quick kill highly unlikely.
On the contrary, pushing the enemy into desperation might lead to casualties among the Dawn Brigade.
A quick kill wasn't feasible, but a prolonged battle was easy.
As long as they couldn't lose, the more desperate the enemy became as time dragged on.
They would always find an opportunity.
This was also part of the "Plan C" they had foreseen during the previous combat sand table simulation.
Sure enough, reality matched what was anticipated.
They could neither escape nor decide the outcome of the fight, and after battling fiercely for half a day, the three Mages from the Heavenly God's plane grew increasingly desperate to break the deadlock.
Their long engagement was actually a cautious tactic.
After fighting for so long, nearly all kinds of trump cards had been played, and the trio had also figured out the strategies of the Dawn party.
They themselves were ninth-tier Mages, not so easily killed.
Moreover, the defensive formation assembled by the three was almost flawless.
But the Alchemy natives before them were of mixed strength, so the trio thought of eliminating some of the other eighth-tiers first, then breaking through one by one.
But Mr. Jing, a ninth-tier, was temporarily impossible to kill, Su Lun and the others were also helpless against him, Mechanical Warrior No. 19 might not be killable, that Sword God had a strong body, the vampire was of an undead race and not easy to kill, and as for the spirit and the demi-god, they were even more impossible to kill...
Thus, the "weakest" Mr. Hei naturally became the first choice.
...
After the fierce battle had dragged on, both sides began to show signs of fatigue, and more vulnerabilities gradually emerged.
The "weakest" Mr. Hei naturally exposed a vulnerability during the combat.
Seizing the opportunity, Elemental Mage Grelec Laman suddenly appeared right in front of Mr. Hei.
The other two also burst forth suddenly, holding back the other members of the Dawn party to create an opportunity for attack.
Grelec Laman chanted a spell instantly, raised his magic wand, and cast a ninth-tier magic: "Earth Mystery: Hundred Thousand Gravity!"
He had already seen that Mr. Hei, being an Alchemy Mage, had a relatively frail body, which this could restrict with a ninth-tier earth curse.
Upon casting it, Mr. Hei was immediately restrained on the spot.
Not only was his body bound, but even the domineering aura and domain around him were instantly pulled away from his body by that strange gravitational field, completely exposing his vulnerabilities.
This was an overpowering of tiers, such a close-range attack left Mr. Hei no chance to move.
Right after the restraint, Grelec Laman's magic wand was already gathering a spell for another instant cast: "Arcane: Thunder Punisher's Spear!"
The series of killer moves flowed smoothly, not even giving Su Lun and the others a chance to reinforce.
However, Mr. Hei was indeed restrained, hanging by a thread of life and death.
But his expression showed no hint of panic.
Exposing such a huge vulnerability was just waiting for this moment!
The spell that had restrained his limbs meant he couldn't even form his sorcerer's seals, but just then, his left eye, concealed by an eyepatch, suddenly flashed with blue light, and in his heart he quietly commanded: "All Things True Solution!"
The beam instantly dissolved the eyepatch into particles, then shot towards the enemy in front of him.
The moment Grelec Laman saw Mr. Hei's expression, he sensed big trouble.
Because he noticed that the opponent was too calm, calm to the point of not even disturbing his breath as death approached.
He also anticipated that the opponent might have some life-saving measure.
However, he never expected it to be the "All Things True Solution," considered a holy art by the Heavenly God's plane!
How could this be?
Watching the bursting blue light from the eyes, Grelec Laman's eyes trembled uncontrollably, his face filled with disbelief.
He had never expected to see the bloodline symbol of the Heavenly God's tribe on an Alchemy native!
Yet, reality didn't give him time to be shocked, as the beam of All Things True Solution shot forth, leaving him no chance to dodge at such a close range.
"biu~"
Grelec Laman could only watch as the beam directly pierced through his Body-Protecting Sanctuary, then through his robe, and made a large hole in his body without any impediment.
He felt his life rapidly draining, still unable to comprehend: "How could this be..."
The All Things True Solution was indeed powerful, but it could only dissolve what it understood.
He could not fathom how an eighth-tier Alchemy Mage managed to dissolve his own ninth-tier sanctuary.
Mr. Hei's face remained cold.
He would not explain the secrets of the "Spring of Wisdom" to his enemy; having gained "wisdom," the realm of ninth-tier laws was no longer an absolute secret to him.
"Mind Reading Technique" had already penetrated the enemy's thoughts; even just predicting the enemy's intentions 0.1 seconds in advance was enough for him.
Moreover, after battling for so long, Su Lun had clearly communicated all the details of the three Mages via spiritual transmission.
Having prepared for so long, how could he possibly not kill him!
...
"Killed him!"
The Dawn party's members all showed joy on their faces.
Su Lun reacted extremely quickly, immediately teleporting over, harvesting the ash mist from the corpse, and then collecting the body as well.
'You have stripped the soul of 'Grelec Laman''
'You have gained a wealth of ninth-tier elemental law insights from earth, wind, water, fire, light, dark, thunder... Elemental experience +331412'
'You have mastered 'Elemental Forbidden Curse Secrets' and gained control of numerous high-tier elemental magics'
'You have learned some secrets of the saint-tier.'
"Spiritual Power +33211"
"..."
In an instant, a massive influx of knowledge surged into his mind from his soul.
This fellow was a Mage Sage of the elements, almost proficient in all conventional elemental magic, comprehending each set of elemental laws to at least the level of the eighth rank, and he had a complete understanding of the ninth rank!
This was crucial for understandings of laws important to all professionals!
This was also the first complete ninth rank soul that Su Lun had harvested.
In the past, when he harvested ninth rank souls, he couldn't fully assimilate the insights due to the difference in rank and his inadequate understanding of the world's laws.
It was like trying to digest a rock with the stomach meant for bread, ultimately only gaining a tenth or twentieth of the potential insight.
However, now that he had advanced to the eighth rank and with the support of the Spring of Wisdom, Su Lun could almost completely digest the ninth rank souls he harvested.
For the first time, he saw complete ninth rank laws.
It was like standing at the highest peak of a plane for the first time, overlooking the scenery below where all mountains seemed dwarfed.
His eyes sparkled with vitality as he murmured within, "This is the realm of a ninth rank Mage Sage..."
In an instant, the world in his eyes became much clearer.
The talent "Reaper of Death" now manifested its S-class ability incredibly.
Previously, Su Lun's All-knowing Eye could understand it, but now he possessed this understanding of the ninth-rank level laws.
Although the mage system's insights were mixed with a significant part of divine power which was not perfect for Alchemy, it was still a massive gain.
Enough for Su Lun's power to obviously climb a huge step!
His understanding of various elemental laws was like a skyward leap!
However, now was not the time to ponder over his gains; the excited expression in Su Lun's eyes flickered and disappeared.
...
In the sky, the remaining two Mage Sages stared in disbelief.
They could never have imagined that in just an instant, one of their companions would be killed.
They had just realized that this black-robed alchemist had always been hiding his true capability.
But what shocked them even more was something else.
Both looked toward Mr. Hei, whose left eye radiated blue light, obviously recognizing the "True Solution of All Things."
This... how is this possible!
Even now, they could not believe that someone among these alchemists had mastered the sacred art of their Heavenly God's plane.
In the Heavenly God's plane, this was an unparalleled existence.
Seeing that Mr. Hei did not have a third unusual eye, they guessed there was something off about him.
However, before they could recover from their shock, another beam of light shot towards them.
The two Mage Sages grimaced and dodged in time.
But after this, the people of Dawn regrouped once again.
With one less Mage Sage, the three's defensive formation was immediately compromised, significantly reducing the pressure on Su Lun's group!
Previously, with three Mage Sages versus the team of Dawn, the odds could be said to be fifty-fifty.
Now, there wasn't even a ten to ninety chance!
Having tasted the sweetness of harvesting a ninth rank soul, Su Lun immediately instructed Pestoya, "Pestoya, try not to kill them with 'Death God's Fire'!"
He needed the complete souls.
Pestoya promptly replied, "Okay!"
The battle continued.
And it was even more intense than before.
The enemies could not escape.
All they could do was fight to the death!
The members of the Dawn group did not underestimate their adversaries and continued to wear them down methodically.
But the situation was increasingly in their favor.
From the start, they had opted for Plan C, choosing a war of attrition, just for this moment.
The two mages had expended most of their magic power over half a day, the Mage Sages had played their last cards, and even if it came to a do-or-die attempt, the risk was almost predictable now!
...
The battle, previously in deadlock, suddenly intensified.
Hundreds of miles away in the city of Klaymington, everyone who witnessed this battle was shocked.
The team of Dawn had actually slain a ninth rank Mage Sage?
News and photos were immediately relayed to Lington, the capital; everyone who knew this news was immediately astir!

chapters.title: Chapter 619 - 618: Major Alchemical Discovery
chapters.content:
Three ninth-tier Sages of Law had been killed, and the remaining two already knew their destiny.
Their every move was now a fight for their lives.
This battle was even more fierce than when all three were still alive.
Unfortunately for them, Su Lun had every advantage of time, location, and support. How could he give his enemies a chance?
If the battlefield had been elsewhere, the two Sages might have been able to summon reinforcements.
But since this was the Lu Ying residence, it was destined that no magical corps from the celestial planes would come to their aid. Only more and more troops from the United Empire arrived.
Even though there were a few followers of the Heavenly Eye Sect hidden in the city of Craylimenton trying to create chaos to free the two Sages, the imperial military intelligence had long been prepared. Before those people could act, they were all captured.
The enemy was like a trapped beast; the people of Dawn were not fighting hard.
They would attack or retreat, appearing in no hurry and slowly exhausting the hunt.
When the enemy desperately unleashed powerful spells, they would temporarily avoid the brunt; once the enemy was weary, they would surround them again.
Despite the strength of the two Sages, they were utterly helpless against this tactic.
Unable to overpower nor escape, the trapped beast still fought.
Even using a Minor Divine Art-level Space-Time Scroll for survival was useless under Su Lun's Urobolos' Space-Time Ring constraints.
No magic scroll on the alchemy plane could have a rule level higher than the plane's limit.
As a result, even the "Minor Divine Art" was definitely restricted by the ring.
Another factor was the Tartalos's Forbidden Soul Lantern, a cursed item that locked souls. Previously, Su Lun and his team weren't sure they could eliminate all these people, so they hadn't used this sealing item. Now that the overall situation had been settled, he directly locked the enemies' souls within the range of the light. The enemies couldn't escape and were doomed to fight to the death.
...
One had to admit, the magic power of a ninth-tier Sage of Law was truly profound.
At the pinnacle of human strength, their source of magic was no longer merely drawing elemental forces from their surroundings but had already gained control over certain rules.
Once they spread their holy domain, it was like a whale devouring the surrounding elemental forces, endless and inexhaustible.
Mr. Hei and other eighth-tiers found themselves greatly suppressed in this situation, facing dangerous moments multiple times.
Fortunately, with Mr. Jing, a true ninth-tier in front of them, who could copy and steal elements with his mirror ability, they gradually drained the two Sages of their original magic power.
The battle continued for several more hours.
They fought from dawn till dusk.
The outskirts of Craylimenton looked like a nuclear explosion site, utterly ravaged.
Finally, as they wore them down, an opportunity arose once more.
Mr. Jing found a chance to trap the magic-exhausted Holy Light Sage. Mr. Hei then used the "All-encompassing True Solution" to find a breakthrough and struck a severe blow to the enemy. Immediately after, Old Sword God Bartolo seized the moment and beheaded the enemy with a slash of Sword Qi.
After one was killed, the last "Time Sage," Ralph Zimmerman, could no longer conjure any waves. After struggling for just a quarter of an hour, he too was slain.
From start to finish, his abilities with time had been countered by Su Lun, and even when he used the desperate Forbidden Art: Time Exhaustion to try to strip the lives of the Dawn members, he failed.
In the eyes of Su Lun's All-knowing Eye, these techniques had no secrets.
Moreover, after repeatedly harvesting the souls of two Sages, he almost completely grasped the old time man's methods.
Understanding their trump cards made even the most formidable enemies far less threatening.
...
The battle finally ended.
It was the joyously anticipated moment of reaping rewards.
"You have stripped the soul of 'Ralph Zimmerman.'"
"You have gained the ninth-tier 'Rule of Time,' increasing law comprehension by 112457."
"You stripped a thread of the divine-grade 'Rule of Time,' gaining some insights into the Divine Art: Time."
"You have comprehended the 'Mysteries of Time Magic,' increasing time magic experience by 55324."
"You have uncovered some secrets of the 'Holy Order of Time.'"
"Spiritual Power +40112"
"..."
"You have stripped the soul of 'Ault Baker.'"
"You have gained ninth-tier 'Holy Light Rule' insights, increasing light-series law comprehension by 154211."
"You have mastered the secrets of light-series magic, mastering [Forbidden Curse: Holy Judgement], [Forbidden Curse: Blazing Angel], [Arcane Magic: Light Banishment]..."
"You have uncovered some secrets of the 'Holy Order of Light.'"
"Spiritual Power +30112"
"..."
Soon, the worn-out members of Dawn were sitting on a small hillside, gasping for breath.
The surrounding vegetation was withered, a scene dead and gloomy, the result of Ralph Zimmerman's last desperate attack, a widespread Time Exhaustion Forbidden Technique that had drained the vitality of the plants.
Su Lun, Mr. Jing, Pestoia, Pandora, Number Nineteen, Old Sword God Bartolo, 'Duke of Blood' Wazhvuas, Mr. Hei… all the participating members of Dawn bore injuries.
But in this battle, which could be considered a peak confrontation of planes, no one dying was the best news of all.
Although everyone's faces were worn out, their eyes were filled with the joy of a great victory.
There was also a sense of relief in their smiles.
In the alchemical plane, there are currently only two ninth-tier Great Alchemists known.
Yet now, the Dawn Group had surrounded and killed three ninth-tier Sages of Law.
This accomplishment was heartening, no matter how one looked at it.
The people of Dawn also felt immensely proud.
"We did it... It's really incredible. We actually killed three ninth-tier Sages of Law, nine eighth-tier Great Mages."
"Yes, it wasn't easy."
"Hey, those ninth-tier Sages of Law were really tricky. The pressure at the level of the laws was outrageous, felt even tougher than the eighth-tier dragons we hunted in the Dragon Country Waters."
"Indeed. But this battle has been quite enlightening for me. The previously unattainable ninth-tier realm seems clearer to me now. Tsk, tsk, where else could we find such suitable opponents?"
"..."
Having fought from noon until now, not only had the Dawn group drained their enemies, but they themselves were also exhausted.
The tight strings loosened, and it felt as if they could hardly muster any strength in their bodies. Some lay down, others sat or meditated, still others leaned against rocks; in any case, none could stand.
Even Mr. Jing was sitting on a large rock, meditating to recover.
Earlier, she alone had dragged along three Sages of Law, depleting her greatly. Though vampires possess strong self-healing abilities and show no external wounds, her origin injury was not light.
Only Su Lun seemed the most relaxed.
After catching his breath for a bit, he quickly recovered.
The "Isaac's Heart of Alchemy" provided strong recovery, quickly replenishing his body's depleted spiritual power. After gulping down several big mouthfuls of dragon blood, his body's injuries also rapidly healed.
Everyone else was still recovering their energy, too drained to make any extra movements, only occasionally chatting.
But Su Lun began to get busy dealing with the corpses of the three Sages of Law.
The pyramid effect of the magical system was more pronounced than in the alchemical system; the more powerful the mage, the greater the resources at their disposal.
From the loot on these three Sages of Law alone, Su Lun estimated he could arm several dozen fully-manned fleets.
It wasn't just about the money
Those magical artifacts were priceless treasures.
The magical robes, wands, tomes, crystal balls on the bodies... were identified to be "dark gold," "legendary," and even one piece of "epic" equipment.
It solidified spells of the eighth and ninth tiers that could be cast instantly, without the need of chanting incantations, just needed energy to be activated.
Comparable to banned items.
In Su Lun's eyes, these were the finest equipment he had ever seen.
However, he was busy with the bodies for reasons beyond just gathering loot.
He had noticed something unusual when he had killed the three Sages of Law, thanks to his All-knowing Eye.
If his guess was correct, this could be a "great discovery" that might change the future landscape of the alchemical plane!
....
While the bodies were still warm, it was the perfect time to test his theory.
With a thought, a ring on Su Lun's hand glowed brightly with red light, revealing itself to be the "Philosopher's Stone."
Then, under the puzzled gazes of the others, he formed a sorcerer's seal, and suddenly a profoundly mysterious Nonagram Alchemy Formation lit up beneath his feet.
Aside from the perfect equilibrium of exchanges, the Philosopher's Stone had another very important function – that is, to gather "cosmic essence"!
A practitioner's advancement to the ninth tier involves the integration of "cosmic essence," a method of refining that had been lost in ancient alchemy.
When the Philosopher's Stone was discovered in the cursed space of the Hell Dragon Country, this alchemical creature had formed a "Cosmos Thirtieth Essence: Phantasm."
So the question arises, what exactly is cosmic essence?
Due to the collapse of civilizations in epochs, knowledge of alchemy beyond the divine realm had almost completely vanished for various special reasons, or hidden in places unreachable by humans.
Over countless years, the majority of people on the alchemical plane had limited understanding of cosmic essence to its function.
That is, it is an indispensable element for a practitioner's advancement to the ninth tier.
But in reality, because everyone uses ancient relics and the methods of refining have been lost, very few truly understand what cosmic essence is.
However, a thousand years ago, Sir Isaac systematically studied the essence of this matter.
In his fifth alchemical manuscript, he detailed his research.
First, Sir Isaac believed that the reason alchemists need cosmic essence is to use this external aid to touch upon the laws above, and thresholds of deeper cosmic rules.
Looking at the splendid alchemical civilization of ancient times, alchemists could ascend to the divine realm.
