But after some thought, he decided not to act hastily.
Firstly, those mage groups had built numerous magic towers within the cities, and a forceful charge would result in great losses.
The second concern was not to startle the enemy prematurely.
Once the enemy realized that the ten-thousand-person puppet groups could easily counter the ten-thousand-person mage groups, they would surely be on guard.
After one or two times, it would be difficult to achieve surprise effects.
If those guys were to hide or gather into super-large groups, Su Lun would not be able to do anything to them then.
To migrate people on a large scale, therefore,
So he thought of the current plan.
Wait for the enemy to leave the cities with the magic towers, and then kill them outside. Attract several ten-thousand-person mage groups at once, and once they are dealt with, there would be peace for a long time.
Now, it seemed that the situation was as expected.
The twelve ten-thousand-person mage groups had taken the bait.
Even in the divine realm, real-time communicators were rare. The previous annihilation of eight ten-thousand-member mage squads at the Imperial Strait was very thorough, and the intelligence clearly had not spread.
The enemy was unaware of the Dawn Squad's methods.
Mr. Jing nodded upon hearing this and said, "Prepare for battle. Don't let them get close to Hepitasong Port."
Su Lun also nodded, "Mhm."
There were many civilians here, and if a large-scale legion battle spread to this area, the casualties would certainly be severe.
However, just as the two had determined the enemy's location and were about to teleport over, something unexpected happened!
To the southeast, several tens of kilometers away, a mushroom cloud suddenly surged into the sky.
Su Lun and Mr. Jing had keen senses and looked over the moment the anomaly occurred.
"An explosion?"
Both of them frowned at once.
The mushroom cloud was clearly caused by an explosion.
But the flames from the explosion were very special, displaying a strange deep blue color.
After a few seconds, there was a "boom." Only then did the terrifying sound and shockwave reach Habitson City.
A glint flashed in Su Lun's eyes as he watched the blue mushroom cloud, his gaze also filled with confusion.
...
Clearly, someone had taken the initiative to strike.
Mr. Jing was just as perplexed, muttering to himself, "That direction holds a ten-thousand-member mage squad. It seems someone took the initiative to strike."
Su Lun let out a light exclamation, "Eh... could it be the joint fleet? No, that's not right. The power of the explosion is not something that shipborne artillery could produce."
Before the two could ponder over it any further, first-hand information had already come in through the communicator.
However, after listening, Su Lun's expression turned slightly strange, "The intelligence department says that someone just detonated a bomb, ambushing a ten-thousand-member mage squad. At present, that mage squad has suffered significant losses."
Mr. Jing was also visibly shocked upon hearing this and thought of something, then questioned with doubt, "Strange, does the rebellion have the power to contend with a ten-thousand-member mage squad?"
The reason she was surprised was that this was completely outside the plan.
This ambush was a top-secret plan discussed between Dawn and the United Empire, unknown to anyone else.
So even if there were to be action taken, she would certainly know about it.
Now, this explosion was so sudden that the military obviously did not initiate it.
In the communicator, intelligence personnel had already reported back, and Su Lun listened with a bizarre expression, "It's not a power. The intelligence department suspects the cause of this blast is... 'Explosives Genius' Jike James."
Mr. Jing, having never met Jike but having heard of such a disciple of Su Lun, looked at the still present blue mushroom cloud and smiled lightly, "Your disciple is quite impressive."
"I had no idea he could cause such a big commotion," Su Lun replied as he shrugged, not knowing what else to say.
Jike had been his disciple from a very early on, but essentially, he was left to his own devices.
Since the disciple's research was in the field of alchemy explosives, there wasn't much Su Lun could teach him.
He had sent him to study at the Mafa Royal Academy before, but not long after, the plane was invaded.
Contact was lost afterwards due to various circumstances.
Su Lun had thought something bad had happened to his disciple, but to hear news of him again in such an unexpected manner was a surprise.
...
This operation, to ensure the secrecy of the information, had not been communicated to the rebellion, so the overwhelming majority of people were also unaware of the early arrangements made by the imperial military.
At the very moment the explosion occurred, the rebel camp also quickly reacted.
"Everyone prepare for battle, those divines have come again!"
"Damn it! We absolutely can't let those guys get close to Hepitasong. Brothers of the Knight Alliance, come strike with me, snipe those divines!"
"Yes!"
"..."
The camp was a hubbub of noise as the rebels immediately sprang into action. Various firearms, ammunition, mechanical armor, and heavy-duty motorcycles roared to life.
Almost in the blink of an eye, various motorcycles and armored vehicles streamed out from the camp, toward the direction of the explosion's roar.
Barely glimpsing hope, everyone knew they couldn't let the enemy get close to the dock.
Even knowing the strength of the enemy, the rebels charged forward without hesitation.
Su Lun and Mr. Jing watched the rebels advance one after the other, their own expressions growing stern. Without exchanging many words, they raised their hands and donned their Gold-Patterned Cloaks.
With a flicker of spatial fluctuation, the two figures disappeared on the spot.
This battle was not about the rebels being the main force.
It was them, Dawn.
...
Just as Su Lun and the others vanished, sentries on the camp walls noticed these two odd individuals.
They were surprised that anyone would be foolish enough to stand on top of the walls.
However, before they could wonder further, they spotted the characteristic Gold-Patterned Cloaks.
The gold alchemy patterns on the cloak were dazzling in the sunlight.
The guards were stunned for a moment: How could someone just disappear like that?
However, in the next instant, as they matched the gold-patterned cloak to its owner, the guards were dumbfounded, pointing in the direction where Su Lun and company had disappeared, wanting to say something, but it seemed as if an invisible hand was choking them, preventing them from speaking.
Other sentinels looked on, thinking their comrade had a stroke, just about to step forward to help, when the shock on their faces suddenly turned into ecstasy and excitement of seeing an idol, their voices trembling, "That was... a master from Dawn!"
The entire camp was stunned by this declaration.
They never imagined that legendary figures they had heard so much about that their ears could develop calluses would actually be in the camp!
In an instant, the camp was boiling with excitement.
....
The explosion sounded, and the battle suddenly started.
The Mage Legion from the Godly plane intended to form battle arrays, which would inevitably slow down their marching speed.
The Alliance fleet also changed their plans and began long-range firepower suppression.
The aim was not to kill the enemy but to prevent the thousands-strong mage corps from rapidly approaching the dock.
In an instant, thousands of cannons from the fleet fired in unison, creating a terrifying and exaggerated commotion.
This massive firepower gave everyone a mysterious sense of confidence.
Normally, those waiting at the dock to board the ships would have taken up weapons again and returned to the city to snipe at the enemy, giving the opportunity to board first to the elderly, women, and children.
Because they knew the mages' strength, and they also knew that relying solely on the Alliance fleet, it would probably be difficult to stop too many enemies.
At this critical moment, everyone knew that only by working together could they overcome this challenge.
Yet the next moment, an even more heart-stirring scene occurred.
On the Alliance fleet's warships, tens of thousands of well-equipped professional soldiers disembarked, and the overwhelming presence of a regiment in battle array gave everyone a sense of security.
Not only that, but there was also Mr. Hei's Dawn brigade.
This time the main attackers were Su Lun and Mr. Jing, while they were responsible for the defense tasks at the dock and in Habitson City.
"Hahaha, Marshal Meredith's Alliance fleet has also come ashore! Charge, damn it!"
"That black-sailed ship is 'Dawn's' Eternal Night Emperor, they've come too! Look, that gold-patterned cloak... that's top fighting power!"
"Our top fighters have come too, hahaha... victory is ours!"
"Victory!"
"Victory!"
"..."
When they saw the appearance of that iconic gold-patterned cloak from Dawn, people on the docks instantly boiled with excitement, and a tidal wave of cheers broke out.
With top fighters, a large-scale legion, and warships, no words could provide more confidence than such support.
The situation at the docks became chaotic for a moment after the explosion but quickly stabilized.
...
Meanwhile, Su Lun and Mr. Jing had already teleported to the southeast where the mushroom cloud had appeared before.
Upon their arrival, they immediately saw a giant deep pit with a diameter of a kilometer at the blast site of the mushroom cloud.
And beside that deep pit, a magic circle consisting of thousands of mages stood as if facing a great enemy, forming a defensive formation.
These mages were covered in dirt, with injuries varying in severity. On closer inspection, there were even some severed limbs and broken arms near the deep pit.
With just a glance, Su Lun concluded that this well-organized mage legion of ten thousand now had only seven or eight thousand people left; the missing ones had clearly been killed in the explosion.
He murmured to himself lightly, "Eh... this explosive could break through the legion's magic shield?"
Normally, the impact of purely energetic explosives on top-tier magic domains would become increasingly minor.
Therefore, this had always been a shackling point for the mechanics and alchemy fields. Failing to break through it meant that mechanical warriors always fell short at the top levels of power.
Unexpectedly, this explosion had directly caused heavy damage to the ten-thousand-person mage legion?
Just as Su Lun and his companion were observing, the mages searching for the enemy seemed to have triggered another detonation device, and "bang," another explosion erupted.
Like the previous one, eerie dark blue flames shot up to the sky, forming a mushroom cloud.
The terrifying shockwave from the explosion swept out instantly, and the surviving mage legion bore the brunt of it.
Even as the magic formation of the legion negated the majority of the explosion's force, a portion of that strange blue flame still managed to break through the magic shield, sending the ten-thousand-person legion tumbling.
Merely by observing the blast wave, complex formulas began to emerge in Su Lun's mind.
The person who had placed the bombs was extremely meticulous, having seemingly anticipated the mage legion's every move, resulting in this second precise explosion.
Seeing this, Su Lun immediately remembered Jike from when they were in Blizzard City, who was still an alchemy apprentice and had nearly used the explosives to kill the second-order professional who had nearly killed his father.
A thought flashed through his mind.
Now was obviously not the time to dwell on it.
Because the blast wave was already upon them, even though he and Mr. Jing were several kilometers away, the magnitude of its power left them both slightly numb.
Mr. Jing raised his hand, extending it forward, and a reflective shield appeared in front of them.
Normally, it would be a piece of cake for a ninth-order professional to protect against any blast wave.
But in that instant, Mr. Jing sensed something and frowned, raising another hand, reinforcing the mirror-like shield before them.
By Su Lun's side, who could overlook such a detail, he was astonished, "This... this explosive actually involves rule-breaking power?"
Having witnessed the explosion firsthand, he had already used the All-knowing Eye to discern the essence of this explosive.
It was not only powerful, but the explosion also contained a rule-breaking force of destruction.
In an instant, he understood why the previous explosion managed to break through the magic shield of the ten-thousand-person mage legion—it was because of this!
The first shockwave passed, and Mr. Jing also cast a somewhat peculiar look: "This disciple of yours?"
Su Lun also found it somewhat amusing yet helpless.
He hadn't expected Jike to concoct such an exaggerated explosive.
However, it was clear that this kind of explosive alone was not enough to completely annihilate a legion of ten thousand mages.
Although the two explosions had killed nearly five thousand people, most of the dead were lower-level magicians of the fifth and sixth orders.
The remaining eight-order commander and the seven-order sub-commanders had hardly decreased in number, so the combat power of the ten thousand mage legion hadn't suffered too much.
Moreover, after the two explosions, the magical aura was exposed, and the magicians used their methods to track down the location of the person who had planted the bombs.
"The enemy is on the northwestern hillside!"
In an instant, the several thousand magicians charged toward the hillside to the northwest.
However, just as the mages from the divine plane had not long charged over, an explosion rang out again, triggered by some mechanism.
Clearly, Jike had even anticipated that the enemy would pursue them.
This time, however, the power of the explosion was much smaller, and it wasn't the previous peculiar green flame, lacking that rule-breaking effect.
Su Lun guessed that they must have run out of that special kind of explosive.
The explosion had slowed the assault of the ten thousand mage legion a bit, but this time it did not cause much damage. The eight-order commander, furious, led the legion forward, and then area-of-effect legion magic was released.
...
After the third explosion, hidden in a concealed defense bunker on the distant hillside, there lay a few mysterious rebels.
The youth with the mechanical arm observed the magic array in the sky and cursed silently, "Damn, they didn't die. That's large-area legion magic, quick, get to the tunnels!"
After this strange shout, the youths planned to crawl into the escape tunnel they had dug ahead of time.
They had escaped many times before with this method, and as long as the plan was meticulous enough, the remaining explosions would be sufficient to stop the enemy from catching up.
This time, however, they miscalculated.
Because amongst their enemies was a spatial mage.
Just as the first youth jumped into the escape tunnel, the space inside the bunker flashed, and a gloomy-faced white-bearded mage appeared out of thin air.
When the mage saw that he had nearly killed five thousand legionnaires and the culprits were just a few youngsters, the murderous intent billowed from him like a fierce wind, instantly stiffening the youths on the spot.
The youth with the mechanical arm turned pale in an instant, "No good, it's a seventh-order magic conductor!"
The youths despaired in an instant; with such a formidable enemy so close, they didn't even have the chance to detonate the explosives on them.
Are they going to die?
Even as he could feel the impending death, the youth with the mechanical arm showed no fear in his eyes, only unwillingness.
There was only one thought in his mind: What a pity, it would have been good if there were more dark matter explosives.
Thinking this, the youth with the mechanical arm looked toward the seventh-order mage opposite him and a cold smile suddenly appeared on his lips, thinking, "At such a close range, even a seventh-order will surely die... worth it!"
Just as the thought arose, the detonation device on his body suddenly activated.
This was a heart rate-triggered detonator set to go off at an extremely high heart rate.
For instance, at that moment, when he was locked on to by the killing intent of a top-ranking powerhouse!
Once the self-destruction was initiated, the blast would be enough to kill a seventh-order!
The mage opposite sensed the crisis and frowned deeply.
He sneered inwardly.
A top mage's sense of danger was not something these low-order magicians could grasp!
He did not doubt that these young people had the means to kill him, but they had to hit him first!
Feeling the danger, the old mage instantly used spatial displacement magic and prepared to leave the bunker.
However, the next second, the old mage's expression froze on the spot.
He looked around in horror to find that the space around him had been locked.
Could it be a high-level law restraint?
Impossible! If these youths possessed such power, how could they allow him to get close?
No, that's not right!
A top-ranking power must have arrived!
As the thought flickered through the old mage's mind, his shocked gaze fell upon two figures in gold-patterned cloaks appearing in the bunker.
He looked at the two figures and his eyes suddenly widened.
To be able to lock his teleportation and to appear silently... that meant these were indeed top-ranking powerhouses!
The youths across from him, however, were dumbstruck.
They thought that two more enemies had arrived and were ready to accept their death.
But to their ultimate surprise, as soon as the cloaked figures appeared, the overpowering killing intent that had suffocated them abruptly vanished.
Moreover, upon recognizing the familiar gold-patterned cloaks, the youth with the mechanical arm seemed to guess who had arrived, his heart bursting with joy.
He had a vague idea who it was!
The teacher!
Others only knew that the gold-patterned cloak was the symbol of the Dawn Organization; what they didn't know was that those gold motifs had subtle differences representing different members.
The one with the golden scythe pattern was his teacher!
Right there before his eyes!

chapters.title: Chapter 624 - 623: 2VS120000
chapters.content:
Suddenly, two individuals clad in gold-patterned cloaks appeared inside the bunker, startling Gik and his companions.
The topic most discussed recently in the rebellion camp was "Dawn", and the photograph of the gold-patterned cloak had been indelibly etched in their minds like a brand.
Although many people had begun donning various cloaks to imitate Dawn, the moment these two appeared, their first reaction was that they had encountered the real deal. That domineering aura, that oppressive feeling, were exactly like in the photograph!
In contrast, the despair in the eyes of the seventh-tier mage was all that remained.
As he was confined spatially, he discovered an eerie power eroding his whole body that he couldn't resist. His vitality rapidly fading, any resistance was futile, and he died instantly on the spot.
Su Lun did not harvest the mage's soul but instead took out a black umbrella and collected the intact soul and body. Seventh-tier magic was no longer much beneficial to him, and he planned to try his "Soul-Body Transference" secret technique.
After doing all this, he then turned his gaze towards the young man with the mechanical arm.
Seeing that excited and expectant gaze, it was clear that Gik recognized him.
Su Lun, removing his cloak and revealing his face, said, "Gik, long time no see."
In the bunker, there were other rebellion companions of Gik who, seeing the mysterious and powerful figure from Dawn instantly kill the despair-inducing seventh-tier mage, first felt joy.
However, now hearing him actually call out Gik's name, they were immediately too shocked to speak.
Such a powerful figure from Dawn knew Gik?
Yet what was to shock them even more was about to happen.
Hearing this, Gik finally dared to speak, excitedly shouting, "Teacher!"
He had been afraid of recognizing the wrong person before and hadn't dared to speak up until now.
"Hmm."
Su Lun listened and smiled slightly.
He also looked at the girl beside Gik, and smiling, said, "Phoebe, long time no see."
The girl was Gik's girlfriend, Phoebe Shelley, who once was the elegant young lady from a noble family and now dressed like an adventurer, beautiful yet full of courageous determination. Compared to when he had last seen them at the Royal Academy in Lerian, both had lost their youthful naivety and had a few more traces of decisiveness between their brows.
Phoebe, hearing the powerful, mysterious man call her name, was visibly startled for a moment before recognizing him, and joyfully exclaimed, "Mr. Su Lun?"
Su Lun smiled slightly, "Hmm."
But now was not the time for extensive conversation. He turned to Gik again and introduced the person beside him, "This here is your senior, Mr. Jing."
Mr. Jing, hearing this, also removed his cloak, revealing a stunningly beautiful face that instantly mesmerized everyone in the bunker.
Gik hastily bowed respectfully and called out, "Senior."
Mr. Jing nodded with a light smile.
Since it clearly wasn't time for a long chat, Su Lun continued, "We'll handle the matters outside. You and your companions be careful; I'll come find you later."
Gik, feeling an inexplicable pride, nodded seriously, "Hmm!"
With that, even before his voice had faded, the two gold-patterned cloak figures had vanished from the bunker.
...
Watching them leave, only then did the feeling of restraint from facing top-tier experts dissipate.
Gik's companions, recovering from their stupor of having narrowly escaped disaster, immediately became incredibly excited and began to ask questions all at once.
All these people had been classmates at the Mafa Royal Academy in Ammunition Studies, united by shared ideas and joined the rebellion alliances.
They thought they already knew each other quite well, but it turned out there was such a hidden powerhouse among them!
"Ah! Gik, your teacher is a top-tier combatant from Dawn?! Good heavens, you've never mentioned this before."
"My teacher... my teacher is very low-key, he doesn't really like others knowing his identity. So, I just never mentioned it."
"It's really unbelievable. I was just dreaming last night, wishing that I could be fortunate enough to encounter a high-ranking officer from Dawn one day, maybe even become their disciple... and yet here you are, Gik, already at the endpoint of my dream!"
"Oh, he looks just like he does in the pictures! Hahaha, this is definitely a story I can brag about for a lifetime."
...
Everyone continued to chat excitedly.
For all the rebellion forces, Dawn represented their faith, and seeing two top-tier figures materialize before their eyes inspired an indescribable excitement.
Even Gik and Phoebe were incredibly excited.
Just then, a young man looking out of the watchpoint shouted, "Look quickly! Those two great experts are heading towards the Thousand Mage Regiment!"
Everyone then snapped back to reality.
They realized that now was not the time for optimism, for outside was an invincible Thousand Mage Regiment.
Although the newspapers had informed them about the prowess of "Dawn",
there were only two of them, yet the enemy numbered in the thousands.
This left them somewhat apprehensive.
Someone asked, "Jick, your teacher can definitely defeat those enemies, right?"
"This..."
Jick, listening, also filled with uncertainty, did not speak.
Having personally clashed with the ten-thousand mage battalion, he knew the terror of such a magic army.
The battalion's magic was also the strongest attack method he had ever seen, and he felt that it was definitely not something any individual's power could stop.
Even the top mechanical armor of Mafa wouldn't suffice!
However, before his worries could show on his face, in their field of vision, they saw his own teacher and master uncle charging towards the ten-thousand mage battalion.
There were only two of them, yet they seemed to have the strength of thousands, matching the five to six thousand without any deficit in momentum.
This momentum was inexplicably uplifting.
They went head-on?
Jick looked at the sky where a gigantic battalion magic array was already forming, frowning.
However, in the next instant, a miraculous scene occurred.
Spatial fluctuations blinked rapidly, and in the blink of an eye, towering creatures appeared out of nowhere, covering the sky and sun, in numbers reaching tens of thousands.
Once the puppet battalion was deployed, they smashed into the ten-thousand mage battalion like a torrential steel stream.
The previously outnumbered two in Gold-Patterned Cloaks not only overpowered the mage battalion in momentum but also outnumbered their enemies!
Seeing this, someone immediately exclaimed, "What are those winged monsters? Are they puppets? Oh, are my eyes seeing double? How can there be so many puppets?"
Jick, feeling his blood boiling, excitedly said, "Ah... Actually, my teacher is a very formidable puppet master!"
Phoebe, standing beside him, was so shocked she couldn't speak a word.
Although she knew Jick had a very formidable teacher, having seen him once, she had never imagined him to be so strong.
And that master uncle, she actually single-handedly took on a battalion magic attack?
Amidst the crowd's stupefied expressions at the fortress, the puppet army instantly breached the ten-thousand mage battalion's magic shield. And the two in Gold-Patterned Cloaks rushed into the mage positions.
The ten-thousand mage battalion, once considered invincible across the major cities of Mafa, now resembled a cracked eggshell, breaking apart instantly once breached.
Wherever the two in Gold-Patterned Cloaks went, mages fell like cut wheat.
Whether it was Mr. Jing or Su Lun, both had the power to directly confront a ten-thousand mage battalion.
Magic could not harm them; what remained was just a harvest.
"Quick look! Jick, your teacher actually blocked an eighth-tier magic with his bare hands!"
"Your master uncle even completely reflected all the attack magic? My goodness, even battalion magic has no effect on her! Is this what top professionals are like?!"
"It's truly unbelievable. I've never left Mafa since I was born and thought our mechanical magicians were the strongest. But traditional alchemists are so powerful! Even stronger than what the newspapers describe!"
"..."
The youths in the fortress could no longer contain their excitement, their eyes shimmering with emotion.
In this moment, they witnessed a legend and bore witness to a legendary battle.
...
For Su Lun and Mr. Jing, an average ten-thousand mage battalion posed almost no threat.
Su Lun's control over the puppet battalion had become more refined, and breaking through the ten-thousand mage battalion's formations seemed effortless.
Having an advantage in rank and adopting a menacing and aggressive strategy, they left the enemy no time to react and instantly killed the eighth-tier battalion leader.
What followed was an exhaustive reaping.
The ten-thousand mage battalion had obviously never encountered such adversaries and were instantly overwhelmed.
The puppet battalion swiftly broke through the defenses, and both the battalion leader and various division leaders were swiftly executed. Even if the remaining thousands still had combat power, they could hardly organize any effective defense.
Against a puppet battalion that even the ten-thousand mage battalion's magic shield couldn't stop, they tried to hold out in formations of five hundred or a thousand.
But what awaited them was only an overwhelming destruction.
Su Lun, controlling the puppet battalion, formed battle formations and rampaged through the mage battalion, swiftly annihilating its main force.
The few hundred remaining mages, seeing the turn of events, scattered and fled. Su Lun and Mr. Jing had no intention of pursuing them.
The mage battalion was broken; they posed no threat to Hebitsong Dock any longer, leaving the rest to the rebel alliance.
Having broken through this route of the ten-thousand mage battalion without any delay, they teleported again, arriving at another battlefield less than ten kilometers away.
This mage battalion was under fierce bombardment by a united fleet, enduring the ten-thousand mage battalion as it advanced under the cover of their magic shield.
Once the two arrived, the bombardment immediately ceased.
Su Lun repeated the tactic, first having the puppet battalion instantly breach the defenses, then he and Mr. Jing charged in to decapitate the enemy's higher ranks.
The seventh and eighth-tier commanders were killed instantly, and the magic battle formation broke immediately.
The twelve magic guilds on the deific plane, though not united, actually employed very prudent tactical assaults.
Each guild was just a few kilometers away from the others.
For a guild, it didn't take much time to reinforce one another.
Under normal conditions, even a force of the ninth rank faced these ten-thousand-member guilds with enough confidence to withstand them head-on. Should any guild encounter enemies, within a short time they could at least receive reinforcements from several nearby guilds.
Even if the enemy was tough, once they were tied up, reinforcements continued to arrive endlessly.
This would eventually lead to a situation where twelve guilds surrounded one.
However, the current situation was something they had never anticipated.
Mr. Jing and Su Lun broke through the ten thousand-member guild far too swiftly!
So swiftly that before the other guilds could even mobilize, the team had already been wiped out.
This second guild was originally meant to provide reinforcements, but they had not expected that just as they faced the barrage and hadn't gone far, the enemy already charged at them.
Before the majority of the mages could react to what was happening, their formation had been broken.
Then it was a one-sided massacre.
The two could fight, withstand, and teleport... They were like a flexible dagger.
The mages of the deific plane nearly had no way to deal with such opponents.
No matter the type of magic, forbidden spells, powerful magic devices... Or even some malicious Curse Magic or soul attacks, nothing was effective.
Mr. Jing could use the Mirror Domain to reflect any magical attacks, while Su Lun was an almost invincible Puppet Master without any real weaknesses. Without actual ninth-rank Sages of Law, it was nearly impossible to contend against them.
...
In the face of the enemy, Mr. Jing and Su Lun showed no mercy.
They shattered the second ten-thousand-member guild and teleported immediately to the third.
With real-time intelligence support from the imperial military through their communicators, they also learned that among these twelve ten-thousand-member guilds, "suspected" to have ninth-rank Sages of Law within two of them.
The two deliberately avoided these two guilds first, choosing instead to attack the others that were easier to handle.
If they could first eliminate these other ten-thousand-member guilds, the subsequent major battle would be easier to fight.
While Mr. Jing and Su Lun were attacking the ten-thousand-member guilds, the joint imperial military also closely monitored the battle.
For this battle, too, the Empire held high hopes.
They aimed to rebuild the Alchemy plane, and restore everyone's confidence in warfare at the Mafa frontline.
The strength of the Dawn Organization was the Empire's top-secret, although everyone had seen from the newspapers that the Dawn members were strong. But how strong they were, and what skills they possessed, almost no one knew.
Right from the first moment the battle commenced, within the transferring fleet, secret experts from the imperial military stared nervously at their communicators, waiting for the battle report.
The enemy consisted of twelve ten-thousand-member guilds, including two which likely housed ninth-rank beings.
This military strength, in the minds of ordinary people, was even stronger than the previous siege at Ruelington Cleyton that involved three Sages of Law.
But only the combined fleet's commanders, 'Thunder Tiger' Meredith Ben Moses and General Rostov, were not overly anxious but instead held a vague confidence in their hearts.
Because only they had witnessed Su Lun's formidable capabilities firsthand.
Initially, it was just one person, with a group of puppets, who had broken through several ten-thousand-member guilds.
These twelve would likewise be no exception.
Sure enough, it wasn't long before the communicators buzzed with intelligence personnel excitedly reporting the situation: "The first target guild has been breached by Dawn! The rebel forces have already gone to intercept the fleeing mages, about seven to eight hundred enemies..."
As this news came, cheers erupted throughout the fleet.
The battle was going smoothly, relaxing everyone who had been on edge.
But just as the excitement remained, those unfamiliar with Dawn among the military personnel wondered: How could it be so fast?
Annihilating a ten-thousand-member guild was a major battle, and according to normal experience, army against army, combat took hours to even begin.
If it were a positional battle, fighting for three to five days was normal.
But how long had it been?
A few minutes?
The commander, thinking there was some mistake in the report, asked tensely, "What's going on, the battle ended so quickly?"
Through the communicator, an intelligence officer, now so excited his voice shook, stuttered in response, "The elites from Dawn are just too strong, they... the two of them directly breached through the ten-thousand-member guild... so many puppets, they instantly broke the guild's magical formation!"
What?
What puppets?
Two people?
Hearing this, military personnel on the ship were dumbfounded, their inquiries leading to more confusion.
He even started to doubt his own ears.
It had seemed outrageous before,
but now that they heard it, it seemed even more ludicrous.
Only two people had charged into a group of ten thousand mages?
Their main task this time was to cover the migration, then guard Hebitsong Dock, and finally serve as backup forces for emergencies.
However, the main assault force was Dawn.
Although they found this plan a bit odd, as professional soldiers, following the high command of the empire was the primary rule, and they didn't ask too many questions.
Nonetheless, they hadn't expected that Dawn's main assault would consist of just two people?
The ten-thousand magician group at the dock didn't go either?
However, before everyone could wonder too much, not long after the first combat report sounded, another piece of good news transmitted through the communicator channel.
"The 7th target group of mages has been breached!"
"The 9th target group of mages has been breached!"
"The 11th target has been breached, Dawn is moving to the 12th target..."
"..."
A series of combat reports came one after another, and only at this moment did the officers at the command post dare to believe that it seemed true.
But they could hardly believe it, fearing it was all a dream.
Even 'Lei Tiger' Meredith Ben Moses and General Rostov were left speechless by this series of rapid victories.
Although they knew Su Lun was very strong, and they had guessed that Dawn's leader, Mr. Jing, was extremely powerful, watching these continuous victories, they still thought... it was too inconceivable.
Could two people really be that powerful?
But after verification, this was the reality.
Su Lun and his companion swept through, successively breaching five groups of ten thousand mages.
The war correspondents also used the most concise language to report the battle situation back to Ru Ying, thousands of miles away.
But suddenly, the message came again: "Bad news, Dawn's top fighters have encountered two ninth-tire Sages of Law sniping at them, and both parties have already started a fierce battle!"
As soon as this news came back, everyone's hearts immediately rose to their throats.
Because even without seeing it, from the monstrous shockwaves of a ninth-tier professional's fight alone, they could already clearly feel it.
...
Contrary to the tense atmosphere at the headquarters, on another front, the parties involved in the battle, Su Lun and Mr. Jing, were not the least bit panicked.
Because it was all within their expectations, and as they charged along, there were no surprises.
Even when they encountered two proactive Sages of Law, they fought as they should, fully composed.
After all, before the battle, they had observed the interdimensional gateways and calculated that the most these enemies would send in these few weeks were two ninth-tiers.
Moreover, after attacking several mage groups, Su Lun was already very familiar with the capabilities of both Sages of Law.
One 'Arcane King' Kost Vaughn and 'Snakebelly Witch' Jacqueline Cooper, neither had any particularly tricky abilities—they were both typical elemental Sages of Law.
With a thorough understanding of the enemy's capabilities, the threat had already halved.
Having destroyed five ten-thousand mage groups, now that the ninth-tiers had arrived, it simply meant the major battle had come early.
Using the same tactics, Mr. Jing created two mirror duplicates, singlehandedly pinning down both Sages of Law.
Su Lun then went on to take down several other ten-thousand mage groups.
It can be said that from the beginning of the fight, the outcome was already determined.
The enemy couldn't possibly deal with both of them, and it was just a matter of time before they settled the victory.
Even though the remaining few magic towers of the enemy formed a supergroup in desperation, with a ninth-tire at its core,
for Su Lun and Mr. Jing, it didn't make much difference to the outcome.
Mr. Jing's confidence came from absolute power.
As time passed, his symbiosis with ancestral blood had become very perfect; compared to the battle in Lington half a month ago, his strength had increased significantly.
If before he couldn't be defeated by three Sages of Law, now facing two would naturally be a breeze.
And Su Lun himself had fought against ten-thousand mage groups many times before.
If he could slaughter at level seven, there was no reason level eight would pose much difficulty now.
This epic battle was being staged on the outskirts of Hebitsong City; the battle of ninth-tiers was earth-shattering.
Under the witness of tens of millions, Dawn displayed again the top-tier combat capabilities of the alchemy dimension and also showed the world that the enemies were not unbeatable!

chapters.title: Chapter 625 - 624: [The 25th Primordial Element of the Universe]
chapters.content:
Outside Hepitasong City, an intense battle raged in the sky.
Mr. Jing split into two, and two mirror images were each surrounded by a layer of the Mirror Light Domain. She fought invincibly against two ninth-tier Sages of Law.
Various high-level spells bombarded each other, exploding in the sky like fabulous fireworks of elemental shockwaves. The sound was deafening, and the entire sky seemed like a canvas painted in a myriad of colors.
Meanwhile, Su Lun controlled two ten-thousand-strong stone gargoyle legions, engaging in a corps battle on another battlefield with the divine magicians' ten-thousand-person formations.
The opposing corps clashed and interweaved, with army alchemy and magic colliding fiercely against each other.
Before, he and Mr. Jing had broken through five formations as if they were cutting through butter, leaving seven formations remaining. The beings from the divine realm were aware of their prowess and thought to counter with a super formation.
But Su Lun had a grasp of all the enemy's tactics. How could he give them a chance?
At the very moment the enemy was concentrating on their formation, he teleported and shattered three more.
The remaining four ten-thousand-person formations created a forty-thousand-person super formation, which continued to be whittled down to the present.
Now, whether it was the battle among the ninth-tier or the skirmishes between troops, everything was at a standstill.
It was impossible to determine a victor in the short term.
However, for Su Lun, a war of attrition was precisely the situation he enjoyed watching most.
With the "Heart of Aisak Alchemy" and the "Blood Devour" providing dual recovery of qi and blood, a war of attrition was perfect for him—the longer it lasted, the better.
Moreover, the puppet legion feared no losses. No matter when, they were utterly fearless in their charges and bombardments.
Whereas the magicians from the divine plane were still flesh and blood. With each bombardment, they would lose hundreds of troops. As the battle went on, the fewer they became, and the more their legion's combat power diminished.
As time passed, the enemy's chance of victory grew slimmer and slimmer.
The divine beings fought desperately and attempted to break the stalemate, but after employing various methods, they became increasingly despondent.
Because they were only facing two opponents.
However, from the start, when they couldn't deal with Su Lun and Mr. Jing, it was destined that they could only be defeated and not victorious.
...
Outside the city, the battle was fierce, and shockwaves surged like tidal waves, one after another.
Already a ruin, pieces of Hepitasong architecture collapsed under the impact from time to time. Occasionally, long-range spells like Earthquake Technique, Meteor Magic, and Storm Magic would fall within the city by mistake, toppling large swathes of buildings.
But even at such great risk, the public's enthusiasm to witness this epic battle was unstoppable.
Around Hepitasong City, atop various tall buildings, iron towers, and high bridges, the crowds were packed, each person holding telescopes and watching the battlefield.
"That's Mr. Jing from the Order of Dawn, truly powerful!"
"Hahaha, to suppress two ninth-tier Sages of Law without any chance to retaliate, our alchemy is indeed much stronger than magic!"
"Look at that Puppet Master, incredibly powerful as well! Just by himself, he's blocking four ten-thousand-person formations?! It's unbelievable; he alone is equal to an army of several hundreds of thousands."
"Yeah, it's so strong. Once thought to be invincible, the ten-thousand-person magician formations are now beaten to such a state by a Puppet Master. Oh, I even saw mechanical puppets within the puppet legion!"
"That's no ordinary Puppet Master! I've heard people say, that's a Puppeteer, a faction founded by Lady Sereya, the wife of Sir Isaac from a thousand years ago..."
"One person is an army, that's a Puppet Master... so cool! I've decided, I'm going to become a Puppet Master in the future!"
"The top military might of our alchemy plane is really too powerful!"
"Hahaha, yes, I thought it was incredible when I read it in the newspaper. Now that I've seen it with my own eyes, I know that the Order of Dawn is really too strong!"
"..."
Seeing the divine plane's magic troops being beaten so miserably for the first time, the spectating crowd was overwhelmingly excited.
They looked at the two figures in the gold-patterned cloaks on the battlefield and felt as if their hearts pulsed with surging passion, wishing they could also stand on the battlefield and slay the enemy personally.
The figures in their field of vision seemed magical, capturing the onlookers' attention. That domineering aura gave rise to a belief in everyone's hearts: We will surely win!
...
The outcome of a battle that had already been predetermined was finally decided after several hours of fighting.
Su Lun gradually wore down those ten-thousand-person formations with his puppet legion, and Mr. Jing kept up the pressure without showing any weakness. The divine beings grew more and more anxious. Seeing no hope of turning the tide, the two ninth-tier Sages of Law tried to attack the people at Hepitasong Port to look for a chance to escape.
However, Mr. Hei's ten-thousand-person magician corps had been waiting for a long time.
In a desperate struggle, the two ninth-tier Sages of Law did cause some casualties to their opponents, but in the end, one was trapped in a magician formation by Mr. Hei and was killed amidst the corps formations, and the other was slain on the spot by Mr. Jing.
Two ninth-tier Sages of Law and twelve ten-thousand-person formations suffered heavy losses this time.
Indeed, the magicians from the divine plane were not entirely underestimating their enemy.
But they had to fight.
After losing eight ten-thousand-person formations in the battle at the Imperial Strait, followed by the loss of three Sages of Law and nine eighth-tier grand magicians in the battle at Klayminton, the divine beings had already been on alert.
They also guessed that the Alchemy plane might possess top-tier powers beyond the intelligence they had.
But now, with thousands of ships arriving from the United Coalition Empire, this was the only opportunity since the invasion to seize a vast number of ships for an offensive.
How could they not seize such a golden opportunity?
Besides, even without considering the matter of the ships, they couldn't just watch as the inhabitants of the occupied zones, who could have been converted into believers, were all relocated away.
For this operation, they had marshaled almost every available force apart from those guarding near the planar passage—should they avoid battle now, they would have no chance later.
Without engaging in battle, their presence as the advance pioneer troops would have no purpose.
After all, their actions were not solely for themselves, but mainly to follow the divine will of the gods.
In the eyes of the gods, human lives were like weeds.
A few hundred thousand human believers dying was probably akin to the loss of a strand of hair.
...
This epic battle concluded with the enemy being completely annihilated, and a festive ocean emerged within Habitson City.
People warmly embraced each other, cheering, dancing, and celebrating this unprecedented grand victory.
After the celebration, the previously chaotic boarding lines at the docks orderly reformed, and no longer did people seem as desperate to board the ships as before.
Because everyone understood that, as promised by the military, the population relocation plan at the port would now continue for a long time.
With the limited number of beings descended from the Divine Plane, the annihilation of these twelve hundred-thousand-strong Mage Regiments meant that the magical forces of Northern Mafa were almost entirely wiped out, leaving them incapable of launching another attack on the port.
This battle was not just a remarkable military success, but more importantly, it served as a deterrence to the enemy.
Today, Su Lun and Mr. Jing together wiped out two ninth-tier Sage of Laws and twelve hundred-thousand-strong Mage Regiments, showcasing the fearsome combat strength of the top-tier powers of the Alchemy plane to everyone.
If the enemy still wanted to make a move, they would now have to weigh whether they were qualified enough.
Besides, dawn would not give the enemy that chance.
Now that Su Lun and Mr. Jing had already arrived, they would be staying in Mafa for a considerable duration in the future.
They intended to create more breathing space for the Alchemy plane.
In the major cities that fell in Mafa, only one or two hundred-thousand-strong Mage Regiments were usually stationed, which posed almost no threat to them.
The days ahead would still be filled with battles.
Only now, it was the enemies from the Divine Plane who would live in fear and trepidation.
...
The news of the great victory at Habitson quickly spread back to Luying via various channels, and soon, it spread throughout the entire Mafa.
Even the resistance armies still fighting persistently in the mountainous frontlines received this exhilarating information.
A scene of joyous celebration prevailed in the city.
Yet Su Lun and Mr. Jing, the ones who contributed the most to this victory, didn't join in the celebrations—they preferred quiet. After the great battle, they merely retreated to a nondescript little valley on the outskirts to recover in silence.
Mr. Jing sat cross-legged in meditation, recuperating from the physical exhaustion and battle insights of the previous fight.
Su Lun, on the other hand, recovered quickly.
He took out the Philosopher's Stone again and began refining the corpses of those two ninth-tier Sages of Law.
The nine-pointed star Formation glowed brightly as the two corpses gradually transformed into strands of law, which then fused together to become "Elemental Law Threads."
Both Sages were elemental Mages, and the laws they comprehended were of the same type.
Seeing that the two Sages had yielded a total of 72% law threads, Su Lun took out the previously stored 29% bundle.
Attempting to merge it with the Philosopher's Stone, it smoothly turned into a dazzling seven-colored gemstone.
"It really worked!"
Looking at the gemstone identified as [Universe Essence Twenty-Fifth, Elemental], Su Lun's face overflowed with joy.
Although he had known theoretically it was possible, this was his first time refining a complete Universe Essence.
It was also the first time in many millennia that someone from the Alchemy plane had refined a Universe Essence!
Seeing this, even Mr. Jing, who was beside him, opened his eyes, his bright eyes brimming with joy and he couldn't help but ask, "Did it succeed?"
Su Lun nodded, happily saying, "Yes! It's an Elemental Essence."
[Universe Essence Twenty-Fifth, Elemental] is considered a versatile essence that can be used by almost all elemental system professions for amalgamation and advancement.
Not only do many in the Magic system as elemental Mages benefit from it, but many Alchemists following the elemental path also benefit greatly.
For someone like Mr. Hei, a Scholar well-versed in various laws, this type of essence would be exceptionally suitable.
Hearing this, Mr. Jing's eyes flickered with excitement, barely concealing his delight.
This is of great significance to the alchemy civilization!
The newly refined cosmic essence has solved the biggest constraint that alchemy magicians used to face when advancing to the ninth rank. From now on, practitioners of the eighth rank in the alchemy plane can advance to the ninth rank by refining it themselves, rather than relying solely on luck to find cosmic essence in ancient ruins!
But clearly, problems remain.
After finishing his words, Su Lun, in his excitement, muttered, "It took three ninth-rank Sages of Law to refine a single cosmic essence—there's still a huge shortage. Not to mention that hunting ninth-rank mages will become even more difficult."
The enemy is not a fool, having been killed twice in a row, they will assuredly take precautions.
Not to say they will hide and not give Dawn the opportunity to hunt, but the next time we really encounter them, there might not be just two or three.
It will become increasingly difficult to find such opportunities to extract threads of law from their corpses.
"Mm."
Mr. Jing nodded, also realizing the problem.
Although ninth-rank practitioners are scarce in the alchemy plane, there are still quite a few at the eighth rank.
From what we can see now, at least ten to twenty cosmic essences are needed to fully meet the demand and to advance a batch of new ninth-rank practitioners.
Moreover, as the plane's upper limit increases in the future, more practitioners will advance to the eighth rank, and the gap will become even larger then.
From a longer-term perspective, she wanted the alchemy plane to still have access to cosmic essence hundreds of years from now.
Not that it would end with their generation's usage.
At this point, Su Lun looked at Mr. Jing and said, "Senior Sister, I have an idea..."
Before he could finish, Mr. Jing clearly understood and said, "Are you thinking of the 'God Burial Ground'?"
Su Lun nodded, "Mm!"
Whether it's hunting ninth-rank mages or some ninth-rank magical beasts, it's down to luck, and there is also the factor of chance.
This still leaves a big shortfall in terms of the current demand for cosmic essence.
Even Su Lun himself had no clue about the cosmic essences he needed.
Therefore, he had already considered whether there was another solution to the problem.
If cosmic essence can be refined from the corpses of ninth-rank beings, then what about the corpses of gods?
The alchemy plane is very special; it was once the battlefield of the gods' war. Even though the plane was shattered during the war, it was not entirely without benefits.
Countless treasures were left behind on this broken plane, as well as divine relics!
Because the law's upper limit is low in the alchemy plane, those divine relics remain untouched, buried in the dust of history for countless years.
Just within Su Lun's knowledge, there are several godly tombs, such as the Sea God tomb in the deep sea ruins, the divine tomb of Giant God Mountain in the mountain dwarf tribe, and the "God Burial Ground" in the Silent Forest!
Mr. Jing could guess what Su Lun was thinking; her expression serious, she said, "The God Burial Ground is very dangerous... Even my father was not sure if he could investigate it thoroughly."
"Mm."
Su Lun nodded as well.
He was of course aware of the dangers.
If there was enough time, Su Lun might have looked for other opportunities to produce the cosmic essence he needed.
But now, they didn't have much time left.
Once the plane's passageway is fully stabilized, a large number of ninth-ranks could descend en masse. At that point, the enemy might not give the alchemy plane any chance to resist, simply rolling over it with concentrated fire.
Relying solely on the two ninth-ranks currently in the alchemy plane is simply not enough to hold back.
Therefore, it is necessary to take risks to accelerate the process and quickly enhance the overall combat power of the alchemy plane.
Moreover, the God Burial Ground, for others, is a forbidden land that is completely untouchable, but for the Dalu people living in the Silent Forest in this era, they have much more information.
According to the intelligence Su Lun received from Yuta, the primary reason the Dalu ancestors sealed the God Burial Ground was for fear of the demonic kings with sentient minds, strange and terrifying beings born from the godly corpses.
Furthermore, the tomb itself gives off an emanation of "great panic."
Previously, Su Lun did not know what those things were that the Dalu tribe's legends called the "great terror," but from his understanding, he guessed that it's highly likely to be the chaotic force of law emanating from the decomposition of the gods' corpses.
This indeed poses a fatal threat to those below the level of gods.
But it is also the most important ingredient for refining cosmic essence.
The two did not discuss further; after exchanging a few key words, they understood what each other meant.
Mr. Jing fell into a long silence pondering.
She was well aware of the great risks of unlocking the God Burial Ground, but if they did not go, it was indeed impossible to resolve the pressing needs of the alchemy plane.
Thinking over, she did not rush to make a decision but looked back at Su Lun and asked, "Are you confident?"
"I don't know."
Su Lun shook his head, naturally uncertain, and said, "I plan to go take a look once the situation in Mafa stabilizes. If I have the chance, I still intend to give it a try."
Mr. Jing heard this and said seriously, "Good. I'll accompany you when the time comes."
Compared to the unknown disasters that releasing the seal could bring to the alchemy plane, the disasters caused by the invasion of the celestial plane were obviously more direct and more urgent.
Between two evils, she was more inclined toward the former.
Besides, their current strength also allowed them to make some attempts.
"Hmm."
Su Lun nodded, having his elder sister apprentice with him naturally increased the success rate.
The God Burial Ground was bound to have a multitude of death rule threads, which was the only way he could think of to obtain the essence of death.
Although that was a place Sir Isaac himself deemed very dangerous, Su Lun's situation was now quite different.
He now had the Philosopher's Stone in his hand.
As of now, this item being called an alchemical relic was not simply because it could perform absolute equivalent exchange.
The mere ability to handle the rule threads that even Mr. Jing couldn't cope with, already gave Su Lun an additional confidence.
As long as there weren't too many, there seemed to be some chance of success.
Moreover, there was the support of the Dalu tribe's Great Druid, Yuta.
The God Burial Ground was very much worth exploring.
...
Before long, Su Lun and Mr. Jing, having rested, quietly returned to the ruins of Hepitasong City.
Celebrations were still underway everywhere in the city ruins, and the people moving around the docks were orderly.
Su Lun sensed the coordinates and, in the blink of an eye, appeared inside a ruined building.
As soon as they arrived, they heard a group of people excitedly discussing something.
"Hey, Brulu, you're not fooling me, are you? Is Jick really the disciple of that Puppet Master of the dawn?"
"How could I fool you!"
"That was told to me by Garen himself! They were there for the explosion because the two lords wanted to save them and they survived. They even saw the lords' faces with their own eyes. Besides, he heard Jick calling the Puppet Master 'teacher'! Oh, and that lord knows Phoebe too. If you don't believe us, ask Polly and Owen, they were there at the time."
"Jick is so low-key, with such a powerful sect and we didn't know! If it were me, with such a powerful teacher and uncle, I would let the whole world know. Oh, if I could become Jick's junior brother..."
"Hahaha... Keep dreaming, those two grandmasters wouldn't take you in. Also, don't go bothering Jick while he's doing experiments, you know, his laboratory is very dangerous."
"..."
The ruined building was full of people; it seemed to be a resistance base.
Beyond the people, there was a hidden mechanical factory.
It housed numerous steam machines and lathes for processing weapons and equipment, and the air was thick with the scent of rust.
In the drafty ruin, groups of people, mostly discussing the epic battle that had just taken place, and also Jick's jaw-dropping "identity."
Those wearing uniforms from the Royal Mechanical Academy seemed to all know Jick, chatting excitedly.
Although the aftermath of the previous battle had collapsed part of the building, everyone was still happily clearing the rubble off the machines.
Su Lun and Mr. Jing walked over, and the others paid them no mind.
At their current level, it was all too easy for them not to be noticed.
Su Lun sensed that Jick was in the basement, but he hesitated to teleport right next to him, fearing it might trigger some unnecessary accidents.
Just like before in the bunker, hadn't he noticed Jick's precise heart rate detonator?
The two walked down, passing through specially reinforced staircases, and reached the underground.
Before seeing anyone, they heard the sound of a conversation.
"Ah... Phoebe, can you help me tidy up? The teacher might come looking for me later."
"Sure. But thinking back, we're really lucky this time, running into Mr. Su Lun, otherwise, we might have died."
"Yeah, I had to personally go to detonate the 'dark matter bomb,' I didn't expect there to be a space mage among the enemies. Luckily the teacher arrived..."
"..."
In the underground laboratory, Jick and Phoebe were tidying the messy lab, and as they talked and looked up, they saw Su Lun and Mr. Jing standing at the door.
Jick's face lit up with joy: "Teacher! Uncle!"

chapters.title: Chapter 626 - 625: Explaining the Principle of a Bomb
chapters.content:
Su Lun watched as Jike and Phoebe busied themselves organizing the laboratory, a slight smile on his face.
Glancing around, he remarked casually, "So this is your lab? Not bad at all."
The lab was filled with all sorts of alchemical equipment, with operating tables holding a multitude of flasks and test tubes filled with colorful liquids. In the reaction boilers, a green potion bubbled and boiled beneath the flames.
The air was thick with a rich mix of potion scents.
It resembled a pharmacist's lab.
But upon closer inspection, many of the containers held explosive potions that were highly reactive to touch.
Those who could understand these materials would think this place was more akin to an ammunition depot than a laboratory.
Beyond the hazardous substances, there were also precision instruments connected to energy devices hard at work in the lab.
The most striking piece was the "Higgs T3-type high-pressure test machine" with a diameter of more than ten meters.
Su Lun recognized the device as one from the military sector of Mafa, a top-tier machine in the field of plane mechanics, used for testing experiments under extremely high pressure and temperature.
He knew it because the mechanical factory in the minor void realm had two of these.
These were gifts from Lucien Pepys Grandmaster, one of the founders of the Mechanical Empire, when he joined the Dawn with Dora.
Su Lun was also surprised to find such top-tier equipment in Jike's lab.
"Hmm."
Jike, seeing his teacher's interest in the lab, began to explain enthusiastically, "Teacher, we evacuated all this equipment from the mechanical academy before Caperton fell. It just so happened that I needed it for my research on 'antimatter bombs,' so everyone let me move it into the lab."
Standing beside a top-level powerhouse like his teacher, Phoebe appeared somewhat reserved.
And given that Jike was his teacher and mentor, she too felt the nervousness of meeting an elder.
Upon Jike's cue, Phoebe came to her senses and brought over some stools from the lab, "Mr. Su Lun, Mentor, please take a seat."
Uncertain how to address Mr. Jing, she followed along and called him "Mentor" as well.
Mr. Jing smiled slightly hearing this.
Both men took their seats.
Though the setting was simple, the atmosphere was warm.
...
Su Lun had noticed the numerous scars on Jike's body back in the bunker and guessed that his disciple must have had a rough time these past years. After all, before today, Mafa was purely occupied territory, constantly beaten back by the beings of the Celestial Plane.
He asked, "After the planar invasion, have you been with the resistance all this time?"
"Yes, teacher,"
Jike nodded, then went on, "Originally, we, the students of the academy, were among the first who could evacuate. But I thought that my knowledge in ammunition could help the front lines, so I stayed. Phoebe decided to stay as well when she saw that I wasn't leaving."
He briefly recounted his experiences over the years following the occupation - a series of hide and seek guerrilla tactics, with several near-death moments.
Although the impact the resistance had on the enemies of the Celestial Plane was limited, it let the people in the occupied areas know that there were still those who steadfastly fought.
Listening to his words, both Su Lun and Mr. Jing could hear the hardships of these years between the lines.
Jike continued, "However, the damage the mechanical technology can inflict on the large mage units is still too limited, and the resistance is suffering heavy casualties, with cities continually falling... I have always wanted to create an explosive capable of inflicting damage on the mage units. After consulting ancient texts for inspiration and utilizing these experimental devices, I was able to create the 'dark matter bomb'..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun's expression subtly changed.
He had been surprised by the bomb that created a blue mushroom cloud and heavily damaged the large mage unit for it seemed to have an effect at the level of laws.
His visit to seek out Jike was also to inquire about the situation.
Now that the topic had come up, he asked directly, "Jike, what exactly is this 'dark matter bomb' you're talking about?"
When the conversation turned to his specialty, Jike became very talkative. Excitedly, he said, "Oh! Teacher, I actually have some related questions I was hoping to consult you on."
He paused, then added, "As my professional rank is too low and my understanding of the laws is weak, I have indeed created the 'dark matter bomb,' but due to my limited knowledge, I still don't understand many of its principles. However, I feel it could be perfected. That's why I wanted to consult with you..."
Without rush, Su Lun listened quietly.
....
"Since I wanted to create an explosive that could break through the domains of high-ranking professionals, even killing high-ranking mages within their sanctuaries, I realized that it wasn't enough to design the bomb solely on the basis of energy fluctuations. The new explosive had to have the characteristic to penetrate those high-order domains..."
"But this idea was difficult to implement, as the most powerful bomb in Mafa remained at the level of energy. So, I thought to look for clues in ancient texts. After all, the plane of alchemy was once magnificent, and perhaps a predecessor had researched it. Then I started to comb through various ancient texts. Oh, I must say, the academy's collection was a tremendous help..."
"..."
Jim began to speak at length.
Su Lun listened with great satisfaction.
He had already seen the shadow of a future Great Alchemist in this disciple of his.
It should be known that ancient texts are not so easy to browse through.
To comprehend the manuscripts left by Alchemists from various eras, one must be proficient in many areas, such as ancient texts, cryptography, mysticism, and even ethics, customs, geography, archaeology, and so on.
The Great Alchemists of ancient times took pride in encrypting their research findings. The more advanced the text, the more sophisticated the encryption.
To understand them, one needs extraordinary willpower and talent.
Jim then said, "Fortunately, I found a fragment of 'Dirac's Book of Dark Matter' among those ancient alchemical documents, and I finally made a discovery after decryption. In the field of alchemy, nearly everyone agrees that the universe began with the 'primordial creator.' And it is possible that all things in the universe evolved from the 'primordial matter explosion.' But then Master Dirac posed a question: What kind of explosion would that have been?"
"..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun fell into deep thought.
He was familiar with this viewpoint, and it was even mentioned in many alchemical texts.
For countless years, alchemists in pursuit of truth naturally considered the origin of the universe and how the world came into being.
"The Primordial Explosion" is one of the mainstream views.
But Jim's approach was clearly different.
His considerations were not as profound; he only cared about "the explosion."
He continued, "The problem lies with the 'explosion.' In 'Dirac's Book of Dark Matter,' the master wrote that the conversion of primordial matter into matter, this kind of explosion, must be different from explosions as we understand them; it cannot merely be a change of energy states. There must be something we are overlooking. For example, some special energies, patterns, laws, or something else. Like a catalyst, they completed this process, but due to certain constraints, we cannot observe them..."
When Su Lun heard the beginning of this explanation, he felt a strange familiarity.
Upon closer thought, wasn't this the same as Sir Isaac's conjecture theory about "dark rules" in his fifth alchemical manuscript?
Jim continued to speak, "The master wrote in the book that he thinks our usual understanding of equivalent exchange might be erroneous... The conclusion is correct, but the process was misunderstood. There must be a special kind of matter involved in this process, otherwise, the explosions we understand would not achieve the effects of the original explosion. This special matter is invisible to the naked eye, unobservable, not revealed in the outcome, like a 'ghost' lurking in the dark. They do not exist after the reaction, but that does not mean they were not involved. They are a real existence. And Master Dirac referred to this ghostly matter as—'Dark Matter.'"
"..."
Su Lun's eyes shifted slightly upon hearing this.
He probably understood the meaning of these words better than anyone else.
Mr. Jing, who was listening on the side, also showed a thoughtful expression. Although she had also read the fifth Isaac manuscript, she had not yet touched upon that field.
Now hearing a similar theory from another source, she naturally became very interested.
Seeing the serious expressions on their faces, Jim wondered if his own description was too crude and felt a bit perturbed.
After all, the theory did sound quite preposterous.
He paused for a moment, then said, "Teacher, Senior Master, I know this theory sounds absurd to you. I felt the same when I first encountered it. But please keep listening. Because, in later experiments, I confirmed that Master Dirac was right. Because my 'Dark Matter Bomb' came from this principle."
"Hmm."
Having witnessed it with their own eyes, Su Lun and Mr. Jing naturally did not doubt it.
They nodded without saying much and listened quietly for what was to come.
Jim went on to say, "The book 'Dirac's Book of Dark Matter' is incomplete, and I don't know how the original master discovered 'Dark Matter.' But it says in the book that it is an existence that cannot be observed on a human level. I have tried as well, but so far, no method can observe it. So, I cannot provide any evidence for this theory. Of course, that's not the point I want to make. Because everything about 'Dark Matter' is just too profound, even now, I don't understand it at all."
"What I want to talk about is the issue of Dark Matter explosions."
He paused before saying, "In the book, Master Dirac comes to a conclusion, which is that when that kind of Dark Matter comes into contact with the matter we normally observe, annihilation occurs. And this process of annihilation releases vast energy and disrupts certain high-level laws. This was the inspiration for my 'Dark Matter Bomb'..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun already understood most of it.
His disciple knew nothing about the level of rules but had used this annihilation property to create a bomb.
This was actually the ancient method of Alchemy.
Ancient Alchemy does not delve into the specific micro-level actions of the materials, focusing instead on the overall effects of the recipe.
To put it simply: it works, so there is no need to ponder why.
Pointing at the experimental apparatus, Jim said, "Dark Matter is very unstable; it annihilates upon contact with regular matter. So the production process is difficult, requiring extremely high temperatures and a perfect vacuum to occur. With these conditions, it is almost impossible under normal circumstances. However, I found an ancient recipe in the Dwarven metallurgical Potion formula that can create extremely high temperatures. By using these devices, I finally achieved the environmental conditions... and then, I successfully created 'Dark Matter'!"
Seeing his research results, Jim's face was filled with excitement, gesturing wildly as he spoke, "Teacher, do you know? The power of this annihilation is a million times stronger than ordinary explosives; only one gram is needed! Just one gram, to achieve the previous effect. But Dark Matter is very unstable and can only be controlled by me on-site. That's why you saw me in the bunker before, Teacher..."
Not only was Jim excited, but Su Lun was also very proud after listening.
"The dark matter bomb" could definitely be considered as a milestone discovery in the field of mechanical alchemy.
The explosion could destroy high-level Power of Laws—only then could mechanical alchemy be truly considered to have entered the realm of top-tier alchemy in the context of combat.
This discovery was enough to immortalize the name of Jike James in the annals of history.
However, the technology was clearly not yet mature.
....
"I have also asked some senior ammunition experts and mechanical grandmasters, but no one could give me an answer. So, I wanted to ask my teacher..."
Having said this, Jike's excitement cooled down.
This unsolvable issue was his greatest trouble.
It even kept him awake at night.
The problem really was beyond the scope of the curriculum.
Because it simply wasn't within the realm of human comprehension.
If Jike had asked anyone else, even a ninth-order practitioner might be totally confused after hearing it.
Maybe even less knowledgeable than Jike himself.
But his teacher happened to be Su Lun.
He might be the only one on this plane of existence who could explain the principles of this bomb to Jike.
After hearing about Jike's discovery of dark matter, Su Lun was also full of sentiments: Talent in certain fields really mattered.
Otherwise, when an apple fell to the ground, most people would just realize the apple was ripe; only a few would wonder why it fell to the ground instead of rising into the sky.
Although Su Lun had been silent just now, he had in fact fully understood the principles of this antimatter bomb.
He pondered for a moment before speaking solemnly, "Jike, your idea is correct, but perhaps you've misunderstood. This dark matter bomb doesn't just destroy the laws on a regulatory level, but a higher level of 'rules'."
Jike cast a puzzled look, "Rules?"
Clearly, this was not what he understood by 'rules'.
At the same time, he was filled with anticipation; his teacher really knew!
To him now, nothing was more exciting than solving the doubt in his heart.
Su Lun nodded and explained, "'Rules' are forces that can only be mastered above the rank of gods—they are secrets hidden deep within the universe. And the dark matter you speak of, is also an area of study for your mentor, Sir Isaac..."
This "dark matter" was actually a physical manifestation of some aspect of Sir Isaac's "dark rules," similar to how flame is a physical manifestation of the fire element.
His student clearly hadn't reached that level of understanding and was only using the part relevant for making the bomb.
But the topics of "rules" and "dark rules" were not something ordinary humans could comprehend.
Fortunately, after drinking from the "Spring of Mimir," Su Lun had gained enough wisdom to describe "rules" in a way mortals could understand.
Mr. Jing, himself a ninth-order practitioner, managed to understand a good portion of it.
While Jike and Phoebe listened very attentively and even took notes, the troubled expressions on their faces made it clear that they found it very challenging.
It took Su Lun the whole night to explain.
...
Before they knew it, morning had arrived.
In the laboratory, Su Lun was still continuing his explanation.
Jike and Phoebe, showing not the slightest hint of fatigue, listened intently.
They listened and recorded at the same time, their notebooks becoming thick with notes they were unaware that, in the many years to come, would become one of the holy texts of the alchemy plane.
Su Lun, having walked this path, understood clearly that certain realizations were beyond grasp if one's professional rank did not reach a certain height, no matter how well explained.
He did not expect that after talking all night, Jike would fully understand.
The content served more to "guide the way" than to be understood in and of itself.
It would let Jike know the direction his path was heading in the future.
As he spoke, Su Lun moved away from the arcane alchemy knowledge and concluded, "I can only explain so much about the rules. This knowledge is too profound for you at present. You will need to progress to a higher rank in the future to truly understand."
Although the lesson was structured from simple to complex, it may represent the sum of knowledge that an average alchemist would accumulate over hundreds of years, nearly encompassing the pinnacle of alchemy that humanity could currently master.
Even with Jike's astounding talent, he might spend many years immersed in this content.
It was only when Jike heard these words that he snapped back to reality from the immersed state of listening to the lecture.
He quickly stood up and bowed deeply, "Thank you, Teacher."
Phoebe, who was at his side, also dutifully bowed in respect.
Su Lun smiled and added, "Advanced alchemy knowledge cannot be obtained overnight. Study hard, and you will surely reap rewards in the future. The field of ammunition experts, in particular, holds much promise..."
After listening to top-tier alchemy knowledge all evening, Jike felt as if his mind was suffering from indigestion and responded blankly, "Yes, Teacher."
Su Lun, seeing his disciple's state, could tell that he was probably already eager to begin experimenting and continued, "However, you mentioned that you want to use 'dark matter explosives' in machinery to make it more stable. I do have something very special here that you could use as a reference."
As he spoke, he displayed the projection of an item that looked black and glossy, similar to obsidian.
The item was too unique, and he didn't dare to take it out from the small pocket dimension.
This was the energy stone from an ancient weapon, the "Twilight of the Gods," a demonic energy cannon, found in the secret chamber of the Goruan Tribe's temple in the Dragon Country Waters.
"Twilight of the Gods"
Detailed description: Also known as 'Zosimus Dark Matter,' a miraculous substance named after its discoverer; once, the mythological dwarven race discovered this magical ore in the endless void of the dark world, containing immense energy and high-order powers of laws beyond your comprehension; through research, the dwarves found it to possess special properties that could counter the divine power of faith, thus making this stone a taboo among the gods;
Upon seeing this item, Jike's gaze seemed to sharpen as he returned to his senses from his dazed state: "Teacher, this is...?"
"This is a special type of 'dark matter.'"
Su Lun previously couldn't understand this item.
Even after he understood it, he didn't know what it meant.
It was only after viewing Sir Isaac's fifth manuscript and now Jike's book "Dirac's Dark Matter" that he gained a firm understanding.
This was indeed a solidified piece of "dark matter."
Although he didn't know how this natural material came to be, and it seemed different from what Jike had made,
the essence was the same.
There were many aspects from which it could be learned.
Moreover, this piece was much larger compared to the one or two grams that Jike could temporarily produce, which were incomparable.
What was most crucial was that it was stable and had a mature method of use.
Upon hearing this, Jike's eyes widened in shock, "This... this..."
He seemed to see a treasure vault opening its doors to him, completely captivated.
There are those who specialize in specific trades, and in the small void world, no one understood this material. Su Lun felt there was no one better than Jike to study it and added, "There is a very complex alchemical matrix on this crystal core that confines and isolates the dark matter, which is why it hasn't been annihilated. You could study it. Perhaps it will stabilize the dark matter you make, reaching a state where it can be stored.
