"Indeed. Currently, it seems the enemy plans to cross the Imperial Strait using magical airships, and we still have sufficient time to prepare. In a direct confrontation, we have a decent chance of victory. The only concern is the enemy's top-tier combat strength..."
"Top-tier combat strength is indeed a problem. These two years, we've been searching hard for the 'Cosmic Essences,' but unfortunately, we've found just one. However, the army corps trained in tens of thousands of mage formations are already taking shape, and we have the mechanized airship corps. Against magic troops, we have fighting power."
"..."
The discussion was lively.
Since the battle at Klemington two years ago, the surrender faction within the empire was entirely purged, and imperial power became highly centralized.
The Empire was almost single-minded, concentrating resources in a single direction, allowing policies to be executed with utmost efficiency.
This was one of the key reasons for the explosive development of the United Empire over these last two years!
Although the situation was dire, since they were all proponents of going to war, there was no sign of fear on anyone's faces.
Everyone's thoughts were quite unanimous: the fight must happen, and they had already made ample preparations over these two years.
Without exaggeration, the United Empire's current military strength was several dozen times stronger than the two great empires of Rueing and Mafa combined, back in their time.
If given another decade, or even more time to continue this development, the Alchemy civilization was sure to shine with undeniable brilliance.
Unfortunately, the enemy would not give them further time.
Yekaijelina, listening to everyone's debates, maintained an expression calm as still water.
She was more aware than anyone else of the current state of the Empire and had even factored in the potential arrival of Demigods in her calculations.
Over the past two years, the Empire had made all the preparations it could.
The rest was left to fate.
Yekaijelina's purple pupils slightly scattered as she seemed to contemplate something; her hand subconsciously touched the sapphire pendant hanging on her chest. The pendant was engraved with extremely intricate spatial runes—a gift from the past.
However, just then, an unexpected change occurred very suddenly.
While listening to the communications, the ministers had thought that the battle at the Magic front had ended and were discussing the pre-war mobilization plan.
But unexpectedly, the communicator rang out again.
The cryptanalyst, not knowing what news they had heard, suddenly looked pale and reported to Yekaijelina above with an urgent voice, "Your Majesty, the latest news from the front! A great disturbance has emerged near the portal in Zambra Ironfall Province! It seems... it seems that someone has attacked the Mage camp. The battle is very intense!"
What?
Someone attacked the Mage camp?
On hearing this, everyone in the council hall stared in disbelief.
The situation near the portal was clear to everyone present. It was the origin of the war; the Empire had also tried many ways to destroy the portal over the years.
But all attempts had ended in failure.
That Mage camp had undefeatable defenses; anyone who went there did not return!
And now, someone had launched an attack on the camp?
Even Yekaijelina was surprised to hear this, her eyes flashed with a cold light as she asked, "What exactly is happening?"
After listening to another piece of encrypted intelligence, the cryptanalyst reported, "The details are still unclear. But from what the observer has seen, the Mage camp is in complete chaos. It appears that some terrifying creatures have emerged. The observer saw flashes of light and conjectures that it might be the act of someone from the Dawn..."
It could only be the Dawn.
Upon hearing this, everyone guessed as much.
But their expressions were still full of disbelief.
Hadn't they just fought the enemy to a standstill at Manushil Mine just a while ago? How in a blink of an eye had they gone to attack the Magic camp?
And how did they manage it?
Who would dare to forcefully breach that camp without dozens of ninth-level mages?
...
While the high echelons of the Unified Empire were in a state of shock, at the Magic frontline, near the portal on a hillside, Su Lun and Mr. Jing watching the battle were having a far more leisurely time.
The bidimensional worms had already been released; the rest was just watching the show and waiting for the outcome.
Through the telescope, the Mage camp was in utter disarray.
The camp had floors made of solidified ground that not even explosives could penetrate, but under the bidimensional worms' spatial dimension reduction ability, they turned into a mud pit in an instant.
The magic towers, like chocolate towers baked at high temperatures, melted away onto the ground in large swaths.
The bidimensional worms rampaged through the camp, feeding everywhere.
Wherever they passed, all matter was reduced dimensionally into food.
The mages of the seventh level or higher were still able to use their domains to sense spatial fluctuations and predict the movements of the bidimensional worms. The lower-level mages were not so lucky; they gathered in formations, only to be devoured by the "black lines" that emerged suddenly from the void.
In just a few minutes, over a hundred thousand mages had vanished within the camp, leaving no trace behind.
Even the demigod Mage was utterly powerless, with elemental magic blasting on the creature's body as if merely adding a dab of colorful dessert. Even the remaining precious time magic and slowing light beams were too rare to stop the creature's rampage.
The camp was in complete disarray.
The million-strong Mage army of the Divine Plane, capable of destructive power, could only watch helplessly as the bidimensional worms rampaged through the camp unopposed.
On the hillside, watching the rampaging creatures, Su Lun's eyes also sparkled as he murmured to himself, "Higher spatial laws, that might be a power even ordinary gods can't master..."
The spatial dimension reduction ability of the void bidimensional worm was the most magical and mysterious application of spatial abilities he had ever seen.
He had never understood how this ability could reduce a three-dimensional object to two dimensions, neither from a physical nor a law perspective.
Now, even with the wisdom from the waters of Mimir and the insight from the All-knowing Eye, he still didn't understand it.
It wasn't a matter of lack of insight but rather the cognitive level involved was too high above his current self, and his brain, unable to handle such high-order cognition, automatically blocked it.
Su Lun even speculated that this might be some kind of fundamental cosmic rule.
Not the superficial aspect of "rules" he currently understood.
However, the more prominently the bidimensional worms performed, the better it was for the Alchemical Plane.
In just a few moments, the worms had devoured hundreds of magic towers.
The previous invincible defenses, the dense accumulation of magic towers like walls, were now like chocolate sticks, devoured unselectively by the undiscriminating bidimensional worms.
Looking at the strengthening bidimensional worms, Su Lun couldn't help but exclaim, "The Divine Plane's forces have suffered heavy losses now. This wave alone means at least a year and a half's worth of supplies sent over are gone. To wage war again, they will have to start preparations anew..."
Mr. Jing, who was standing nearby, also showed a rare relaxed expression, "Yes."
However, not long after, a ten-story magic tower in the camp suddenly lit up with the fluctuations of spatial transportation, and a female mage wearing a golden mask hastily returned to the battlefield.
It was none other than Grand Princess Octavia J. Fielding, who had fought with them a thousand miles away at the great battle of Manushil.
Su Lun looked at the familiar face and raised an eyebrow, "Yo, she's finally made it back."
Without the ability for ultra-long-distance spatial teleportation, even receiving the message immediately, she was still late in returning by using the magic circle.
Already, the camp's core magic tower had been devoured in large chunks, with two of the ten-story towers that could empty an entire large kingdom being consumed by the biaxial worms.
Upon seeing this, a chill went through Octavia's eyes; that was the empire's wealth. She set aside her aloof demeanor as a holy tribal princess and took off her golden mask right away.
The vertical pupil on her forehead shone brightly with dissolving beams, firing straight at the biaxial worms.
It had to be said, the "All-knowing Eye" was truly powerful, even the biaxial worms retracted and flinched from the penetrating beams.
But that was all there was to it.
Such damage was akin to evaporating a bit of mud off a mud monster's body, and it could not kill the biaxial worms.
Seeing this, Su Lun's gaze also narrowed slightly.
So far, almost everything was within expectations.
Now, with two demigods present in the heavens' battlefield, it was the liveliest moment.
Mr. Jing muttered beside him, "Next, they should summon the will of the gods to descend…"
Smiling, Su Lun nodded, "Yes. Let's see just how strong she will be after the descent of the god."
....
Just as the two had predicted, it wasn't long before the two demigod mages of the heavens' plane recognized the fact that they couldn't kill the biaxial worms.
Moreover, with plenty of "food" in the camp, the monster had no intention of leaving.
Although the magic gods' methods couldn't kill it, their rule-based magic could still harm it, causing the biaxial worm to become increasingly enraged, slaughtering the mages even more ruthlessly.
Every moment the biaxial worm rampaged in the camp was a huge loss for the people of the heavens' plane.
This would have been the best opportunity for a surprise attack, but Su Lun and his companion made no move.
They had not failed to notice that, despite the chaos, several ten-story magic towers were always prepared, just waiting to deal a heavy blow to anyone attempting to profit from the disorder.
The previous mirror light projection had summoned the Void Gate and unleashed monsters, making it clear to the enemies that it was their backstage maneuver, naturally, they were on guard.
Those magic towers might not pose a problem for a special void creature like the biaxial worm, but that didn't mean they would be harmless to the two beings of flesh and blood.
Su Lun and his companion quietly watched the excitement, waiting for a better opportunity.
If this exhaustion continued, even if the million-strong magic army could deal with the biaxial worm, they would surely suffer heavy casualties.
By then, with the various magic formations of the camp shattered, Su Lun and his party might really have the chance to stir up trouble in the camp.
But the enemy, of course, would not give them that chance.
The Grand Princess Octavia was decisively quick to act—upon realizing she couldn't kill the beast, she immediately began chanting an arcane incantation.
The spell to summon the gods seemed magical; upon hearing it, the million people in the camp stopped in unison, their faces free of fear and panic, filled only with piety and fervor, as they awaited the arrival of their deity of faith.
Su Lun saw more than just that; every person was connected by strands that converged in the sky.
He had not understood what faith was before, but now, watching the scene of a million people in worship, he seemed to grasp something and muttered to himself, "This is the power of faith… Strange, it's not spiritual power, nor is it the soul, but rather consciousness coalescing into reality..."
The collective will of a million people was a terrifying force indeed.
Was this an important source of the gods' power?
Su Lun pondered.
This was the gateway between planes after all, and it was much easier for a god to descend here than elsewhere.
He had no time to ponder further when, in an instant with the chant, the sky began to surge as countless powers of faith gathered and formed a huge, vague human face in the blink of an eye.
In that instant, an indescribable will descended.
Su Lun, having witnessed the descent of gods numerous times, saw no mystery in what was deemed ineffable.
Looking at the fuzzy face in the sky, he recognized it and said to himself, "It's the same one from before…"
The divine will that descended was none other than the unfortunate deity who had coveted the "Mimir's Spring" in the waters of the Dragon Country and was ultimately defeated by the Cyclops Demigod Tribal Chief.
Mr. Jing, initially solemn at the arrival of the True God's will, looked over upon hearing Su Lun's words, "Seen it before?"
Su Lun nodded, "Mhm. It's the one I told you about before, in the waters of Dragon Country."
Mr. Jing responded, "Oh."
As the two were discussing, the gigantic face in the sky had already taken shape, and almost all the energy of the magic towers in the mage camp was mobilized.
The overwhelming magic power coalesced into two large hands, which then grabbed the bi-dimensional worm in the camp, tearing it off like a canvas.
What followed was a very strange scene, where the two hands kneaded the creature as if it were taffy, ripping it apart piece by piece.
With each tear, the breath of the bi-dimensional worm grew weaker and weaker.
When a True God took action, it was indeed extraordinary.
Mr. Jing, who stood by, watched with closely knit brows, as if calculating his chances of victory against that will.
Although Su Lun hadn't fully understood the methods of the deity, by observing the threads of rules, he vaguely guessed that it was an advanced application of the Space Law.
It was those large hands that employed a technique similar to "Spatial Isolation," grasping the entire space rather than the creature itself.
It was akin to using a piece of paper to wrap a sticky candy, thereby avoiding the bi-dimensional worm's bizarre ability to reduce anything it touched to a lower dimension.
Seeing this, Su Lun murmured, "It seems that 'Spatial Dimension Reduction' is a power even lower deities fear..."
As he had surmised, "reduction" could be a kind of advanced cosmic spatial law, one that lower gods could not master.
Otherwise, the deity before him wouldn't have been so hamstrung in dealing with the bi-dimensional worm.
And he wasn't too surprised that the will of the deity could severely wound the Matriarch Worm.
The terror of the Void Matriarch Worm lay in its intelligence and its ability to reproduce spawn, not in its combat strength.
They were inherently the weakest in their tier, and not fast at teleportation.
Even though they ranked as demigods, without their dimension-reducing talent, probably even an eighth-order could kill them.
However, the battle was still very intense.
The bi-dimensional worm, exiled for countless years, had a strong will to survive; it struggled, trying to kill and escape.
But those massive hands had no intention of letting it go.
The deity did not wish to release such a troublesome creature, lest it return to the camp and cause unpredictable losses in the future.
The hands continued to tear, and more and more pieces of the bi-dimensional worm's body fell into the camp; the fragments of various corpses still had the capacity to reduce dimensions, causing enormous losses to the people from the celestial domain.
But from the moment the bi-dimensional worm could not escape, its fate was sealed.
As time passed, Princess Oktaavia's face became increasingly pale. The burden was tremendous, as summoning the will of a deity to descend took its toll on her.
Especially since she had mobilized such a potent force.
But the outcome was still favorable for her.
Using the power of the deity, she finally pushed the bi-dimensional worm to the brink of death.
From a distance, Su Lun could also sense the soul vibrations of the bi-dimensional worm becoming fainter and fainter.
In the end, it could no longer maintain a bi-dimensional state.
Some fragments of magic towers and various corpse remnants yet to be digested fell into the camp like dumping garbage, scattering everywhere.
It was finally killed.
...
Although the creature hadn't managed to kill one of the two Magic Gods, it did kill quite a few seventh- and eighth-order Mages, as well as two or three tens of thousand-person magic squads, causing hundreds of thousands of casualties.
It also destroyed at least one-third of the various supplies, magic towers, and magical restrictions in the camp.
It could be said that it severely weakened them.
Su Lun and Mr. Jing were quite satisfied with the outcome.
After this event, they could at least delay the celestial domain's offensive for half a year.
Besides, with the celestial folks having dealt with the worm, Su Lun himself breathed a sigh of relief, spared from having to exile it personally.
It also reduced many risks.
Suddenly, Su Lun felt quite pleased, and the solemn expression of Mr. Jing beside him relaxed as well.
His eyes fell on the corpses of the creatures within the camp, feeling a bit envious, "Those materials are out of reach for now..."
But having now witnessed a magic camp protected by the will of a deity, he dismissed the last bit of wishful thinking in his heart.
It would be impossible to come out alive if they were to forcibly storm in.
Clearly, this matter required long-term planning.
Just then, Mr. Jing thought of something and said, "We need not worry about the situation here for several months. Let's go, we are heading to the 'God Burial Ground'."
Su Lun immediately understood and nodded, "Hmm."
In the current situation, they had to take risks.
They needed to explore the legendary site of a deity's fall within the Silent Forest; if they could really refine a large amount of "Cosmic Essence," the tide of battle might change significantly.

chapters.title: Chapter 631 - 630: The New Face of the Dawn Group
chapters.content:
Su Lun and Mr. Jing's surprise attack plan had achieved very ideal results.
By releasing the two-dimensional worms, they not only caused heavy casualties in the magic camp at the planar passageway but also, due to the loss of personnel and resources, left the enemy without the capability to wage a full-scale war for the short term.
Moreover, the enemy had to constantly guard against another potential raid by Su Lun and his accomplice.
After all, it had been proven that the camp's standard defenses had vulnerabilities.
And this vulnerability was not something that could be rectified.
The enemy had no idea where these two-dimensional worms came from, nor could they be sure whether Su Lun would repeat his trick and attack the camp with more bizarre items.
The two Magic Gods also dared not leave the camp now, having to guard it around the clock.
Furthermore, Princess Octavia J. Fielding had already tried and failed to kill the top-tier combatants of the Alchemical plane, which became their greatest concern.
Clearly, more Magic Gods would be needed to ensure absolute victory.
Whether it was resupplying resources or descending more masters, all these would take quite some time.
The magic camp once again returned to its state of shrinkage from two years ago, and any significant maneuvers would have to be postponed for at least a few months.
On the other hand, Su Lun and Mr. Jing did not linger in Mafa.
He first returned to Luying, then made a trip to pick up someone from the Eternal Night, and afterward, he and Mr. Jing went straight to the Silent Forest in the northern part of Luying.
They were well aware that the enemy would not take any significant action for a while, so there was no point in staying in Mafa.
Besides, with Empire intelligence personnel under strict surveillance, they could rush back in time if there was any movement.
....
Previously, Su Lun had left Yuta a necklace with a fixed teleportation coordinate, making transportation very convenient.
A few hours later, he arrived at the Dalu clan's Emerald Holy Land with Mr. Jing.
The Emerald Holy Land had changed dramatically, with the massive gray elm in the center now blotting out the sun. As soon as Su Lun and his companion arrived, the dense force of nature hit them in the face.
After the Empire banned the slave trade, there had been an explosive increase in the population of the Dalu clan, with the inhabitants of the Holy Land alone being ten times more than before.
Standing on the edge of a cliff, Mr. Jing, looking at the dense forest in front of him, murmured, "The Emerald Holy Land has changed so much..."
Her last visit was when the Dalu clan re-signed the alliance agreement, which, counting the time, was already several years ago.
Listening, Su Lun nodded and casually said, "Yes, it has changed a lot."
But just as he uttered these words, a ghost lady suddenly popped out of the runic umbrella, exposing his pretense.
"Su Lun, didn't you just come here last month? Do you really think it's changed that much?"
Pestoya teased him with a mischievous smile on her face, never tiring of calling out Su Lun's bluffs.
Su Lun rolled his eyes and reached out to pinch the girl's cheek.
He wasn't really surprised; after all, he would teleport here every few months to chat with Yuta, absorb some natural force, and exchange insights on their practice.
"Ah... you despicable Su Lun, pinching my face again!"
Although Pestoya was in her Spiritual Body state, Su Lun still managed to stretch her face out long.
She huffed and straddled Su Lun's neck, turning into a little devil with long horns on her head, and declared fiercely, "I'll strangle you!"
Mr. Jing, who was used to seeing the two bicker, simply smiled and said, "Alright, stop messing around, someone's coming."
While Pestoya was in the midst of sinking her neat white teeth into Su Lun's head, upon hearing this, she responded, "Sis, you don't know, Su Lun is a creep... I also know about that succubus maid of his who turned into..."
Before she could finish, Su Lun flicked his finger and tossed a piece of soul candy made from spiritual energy into her mouth.
"Smack... smack..."
Pestoya's words were cut short as the candy landed in her mouth; instinctively, she chewed a few times, seemingly forgetting what she was about to say, her eyes instantly sparkling with stars: "Wow... what flavor is this? It's so delicious~"
"Rainbow candy."
Su Lun had used this trick many times before, and it was very effective.
Souls can't taste flavors, and this ghost lady hadn't tasted food in over a thousand years, particularly since she had quite a sweet tooth.
Su Lun thought of a method.
The flavor of food is a signal transmitted to the brain through the taste nerves and, in theory, it can be simulated. He made candy using soul material and then added some psychic signals to simulate the taste, which allowed the girl to also enjoy the flavors.
These soul candies were also used to bribe the young lady.
After Su Lun had been complained to by the ghost girl for putting the rune-black umbrella into the little void realm at the apartment in Spirit Dun Lena, he had been carrying it with him ever since.
Firstly, it was to respect Pestoya's wishes; secondly, it was for his own protection.
So the quirky ghost girl almost knew everything about him.
Aside from some personal privacy, there was nothing shameful or secret to hide.
Su Lun let her be.
Of course, awkward situations would occasionally arise.
He would give the girl a piece of candy to eat, to keep her mouth shut.
Mr. Jing watched the two of them bickering in their daily life, his expression showing no sign of discomfort. After nearly two years of living together, they had become very familiar with each other, with no hint of unease.
It was during their conversation that the blue-tailed hawk soaring in the sky already informed those in the Sanctuary Forest that there were guests.
Several figures dashed out from the forest quickly.
The leader, a white-haired girl wearing an animal skin skirt and with a graceful figure, turned out to be Yuta.
Seeing Su Lun, a surprised expression immediately appeared on her face, and she greeted him from afar with enthusiasm, "Mr. Su Lun!"
Behind her were her brother Arcu and some of the Dalu tribespeople who all knew Su Lun; they were there to welcome him.
Before the words were finished, he was already enveloped in a tender touch, as Yuta gave Su Lun a warm embrace.
During the embrace, a ghost girl floated out from Su Lun's body, but Yuta was not at all surprised and instead greeted her familiarly, "Pestoya is here too."
"Mm. Hello, Sister Yuta~"
Pestoya floated in the air, smiling with curved eyebrows and still chewing on candy, calling out sweetly.
The girl might have a quirky temperament, but she naturally liked pure souls. Su Lun had visited the Emerald Holy Land a few times in the last two years, and she had become quite familiar with Yuta.
After greeting Su Lun with an embrace and not losing etiquette, Yuta turned to look at Mr. Jing beside her and bowed, "Mr. Jing, welcome to the Emerald Holy Land."
The friendly treaty between the Dalu tribe and humans was a bridge established by Isaac's family; hence, she had deep respect for Mr. Jing.
Mr. Jing smiled faintly, "Elder Yuta, you are the great Druid of the Dalu tribe; there's no need for such courtesy."
The presence of Su Lun made the atmosphere less formal.
Yuta also smiled upon hearing this.
Seeing that Mr. Jing had also come this time, she asked, "Mr. Su Lun, did you come this time to go to the Cursed Valley?"
Su Lun nodded seriously, "Yes."
He had discussed the plan with Yuta during his last visit and had detailed the potential ways to break the seal.
The "Tree Seal - God Burial" inside the Cursed Valley was a divine seal of the Dalu tribe. With the help of the Dalu tribe, the risk would be smaller.
Yuta, aware of the seriousness of the matter, asked, "Then, Mr. Su Lun, when do you plan to go? Do you want to rest in the village first? Everyone will be very happy to know that you and Mr. Jing have arrived."
Su Lun considered it and replied, "We might have to go directly to the seal."
Nowadays, with the interplane war changing daily, today a demigod had appeared, and perhaps a real god would descend tomorrow. Time was running short for them.
The matter of the God Burial Ground had to be sorted out as soon as possible.
Yuta understood and nodded her head, "Okay!"
She turned to her brother Arcu behind her and said, "Arcu, go inform the tribal elders in the village that we'll make a trip to the north."
Arcu, who had grown into a robust young White Wolf tribesman over two meters tall, responded, "Okay!"
With that, he turned and left, disappearing into the forest.
Before long, a group of people quickly arrived from the forest.
Wolf Granny Mara, Elder Pasu, Elder Tagu, Elder Koula... all were Dalu tribespeople whom Su Lun had known for a long time.
...
The venture to undo the seals of the God Burial Ground came with great risk, and Su Lun originally did not want the Dalu tribe to be involved.
But once Yuta knew he was going, she insisted on joining.
Now she was the Dalu tribe's Grand Druid, possessing two sacred artifacts: the "Chalice of Fal" and "Dagda's Magic Cauldron," along with the blessing of the Nature God, her strength was not to be underestimated.
With Yuta's help, the plan's chances of success were slightly increased.
And when the Dalu tribespeople learned that Su Lun needed their help, they too wanted to contribute.
They worshipped the gods of peace and nature and couldn't actively participate in war, but they could offer this help.
Su Lun couldn't refuse the enthusiasm of his tribespeople.
Before long, the assembly was completed, and everyone headed towards the northern Cursed Valley.
They needed to set up defensive measures in the forests along the way to prevent the emergence of dangerous entities once the seal was broken.
Most of the Dalu tribal elders were setting up defensive perimeters, while Su Lun, Mr. Jing, and Yuta were inside the Cursed Valley.
The valley was still shrouded in a thick mist of death.
Su Lun remembered the last time he had come here at tier three, when the negative spiritual power in the mist affected him, making him hear the whispers of the dead. Now at tier eight, he no longer felt any discomfort.
In a flash of spatial fluctuations, the three of them were already standing atop the hundred-meter high broken city wall.
This was the ruins of a giant race's city, and the entire relic rested atop a massive tree.
This tree was the result of the "Tree Seal - God Burial Ritual" once cast by the Dalu ancestors.
Sunlight filtered through the leaves, the cascade of white water from the tree canopy still abundant, and bizarre winged creatures could be seen flitting among the treetops...
Looking at the towering giant tree again, Su Lun felt a sense of nostalgia for the old haunt.
The three of them stood on the city wall, observing for a moment.
Then Yuta, with a hint of uncertainty, asked Su Lun, "Mr. Su Lun, shall we unseal it now?"
Although she had absolute trust in Su Lun, she was still somewhat worried about the place that had almost led to the Dalu tribe's annihilation.
While she was quite powerful now, she still lacked confidence.
Su Lun, seeing Yuta's concern, smiled lightly and said, "Mm. We'll get started once I summon our comrades from Dawn Group."
Even if the three of them were strong, they were not presumptuous enough to think they could open the burial ground of the deities by themselves.
Yuta was somewhat surprised upon hearing this, "Mr. Su Lun's comrades?"
"Mm."
Su Lun nodded and without further explanation, formed sorcerer's seals in an instant, creating an ever-growing black hole in his palm.
Just then, a stream of figures began to emerge.
Old Sword God Bartolo, Mr. Hei, Barrett, "Duke of Blood" Wazhuas, Kit, Number Nineteen, his disciple Abek, Lolota, Tanni... Almost all the combat members of the Dawn Group were there.
A total of tens of thousands!
Having been at the front lines with Mr. Jing for so long, Su Lun had not seen everyone for a while.
Previously, in a hurry, he had called them into the miniature void without the chance for interaction. Now that they had arrived, the place immediately grew lively.
"Hahahaha... Captain Barrett, did you advance to the eighth tier after a month of secluded cultivation?"
"Yes, I was lucky!"
"Kit, you're at tier seven now?"
"Ah... is it strange for me to be at tier seven when you're at tier eight already? It would be embarrassing to say that I, the 'Empire's Number One Phantom Thief,' was still at just tier six."
"Yo, Lolota has reached the realm of Sword Saint?"
"Of course. After Chian went to train in hell, Lolota has also been practicing very hard. She has now comfortably secured the position of 'Dawn's Third Swordsman'..."
"Wow, Miss Nineteen, your mechanical gear is updated again? Looks so cool."
"Yeah, the Imperial Royal Mechanical Factory produced a batch of super mechanical warriors and helped me customize some special components."
"..."
Over the past two years, there had been almost no battles on the frontlines, and Dawn Brigade hadn't gone on adventures; instead, they entered a state of rapid development.
With access to the best resources of the entire Alchemy plane, everyone in the brigade naturally progressed quickly, with most experiencing a sharp increase of one or two major ranks.
Even those who were previously in the lowly first or second ranks soared to become mid-level experts of the fourth or fifth ranks.
The elite forces of Dawn Brigade also made breakthroughs one after another.
There was a time when the upper limit of the fragmented Alchemy plane's laws restricted them to reaching only the sixth or seventh ranks, as their talents were one in ten thousand. Now, after the connection of the planar channels and the completion of the laws, they found it easier to break through than others.
In these two years, hundreds advanced to the sixth rank, and dozens reached the seventh rank.
Barrett successfully stepped into the eighth rank, and Old Sword God Bartolo touched the threshold of the ninth rank, and No. 19's mechanical body was fitted with secret black technology akin to "dark matter weapons"...
Young geniuses of Dawn Brigade like Tanni, Lorraine, and Yaberk also climbed to the sixth rank and touched upon the seventh.
Most astonishing were Mr. Hei's Dragon Tongue Magician Corps!
Alchemists are not like the devout followers of gods who reject all powers outside of their faith system; to alchemists, everything in the world is potential material for Alchemy as long as it can be utilized.
They had firsthand experience of the formidable power of the Divine plane's tens of thousands-strong Magic corps, which is why in these past two years Mr. Hei devoted himself to creating Dawn's own unique corps of sorcery.
Dawn Brigade's home base also had the foundation to become a top-tier fighting force.
Most of the members had undergone various degrees of dragon gene bloodline enhancements and even integrated some draconic breeding armor, which endowed them with certain innate dragon talents.
Not only did this give them strength far beyond that of their peers,
but since they were all Dragon Blood warriors, the compatibility of their powers was very high, making the battle arrays they formed even more potent.
Mr. Hei also personally designed an exclusive 'Dragon Tongue Legion Battle Array' tailored to Dawn Brigade's forces!
The draconic tongue is a high-level language system capable of mobilizing the laws of heaven and earth, a realm that only those above the ninth rank could delve into.
However, Mr. Hei, who attained wisdom from drinking from the [Mimir's Spring], not only mastered this superior language, but he also used his wisdom to create a tiered Dragon Tongue Magician system.
As a result, the people of Dawn Brigade could harness a portion of it as well.
This is the Dragon Tongue Battle Array!
When the language of dragons was fused into Alchemy, its might increased exponentially.
The tens of thousands-strong Magician corps of Dawn was now taking shape and was far stronger than any Magic corps of tens of thousands.
This Magician corps' combat power was even above that of the ninth rank!
...
Yuta observed the sudden appearance of Dawn Brigade's members, and it was clear to her that there were many formidable warriors among them.
Only now did she understand the confidence behind Su Lun's decision to open the seal.
The forebears of the Dalu clan had indeed paid with their lives to seal the God Burial Ground centuries ago—it was definitely one of the most dangerous places in the Alchemy plane.
But Dawn Brigade's current combat power was far stronger than the Dalu clan's had ever been.
Apart from Mr. Jing, a supreme powerhouse capable of matching a Magic God, there was Su Lun, everyone else, and Mr. Hei's tens of thousands-strong Magician corps...
It could be said that even if two or three Demigods appeared, they might not be able to do anything against them.
Clearly, now was not the time for idle chat. After a brief exchange of pleasantries, Su Lun said, "Gentlemen, prepare to take action."
"Yes!"
The crowd responded in unison.
Previously, in the lesser void world, Su Lun had thoroughly briefed the members of Dawn Brigade on the situation, and the strategists had also drawn up a detailed plan; there wasn't much else to say now.
No sooner had these words been spoken than over ten thousand people dispersed to begin setting up a huge Alchemy array around the massive tree.
Before the seal was undone, they needed to be fully prepared.
If something unexpected did happen, they would have to ensure that this dangerous place could be sealed once more.
PS. The writing is a bit choppy, and shorter than usual.

chapters.title: Chapter 632 - 631: The Monsters in the Cave are all Materials
chapters.content:
Dawn's people were busy setting up the super-large alchemy formation, and after about an hour, the sky had already darkened.
With Mr. Hei directing the layout, there was no need for others to worry.
Su Lun and Mr. Jing, having expended a great deal today, sat down cross-legged to meditate.
Unconsciously, night fell, and the sky above Silent Forest was a brilliant Milky Way, captivating with its profound depth.
It was then that Lulota suddenly leapt down from the treetop and reported, "Leader, Mr. Su Lun, the setup is complete!"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun and Mr. Jing opened their eyes from meditation, "Everybody prepare to take action."
Immediately, responses came through the communicators: "Yes!"
Soon after, Dawn's tens of thousands of people gathered on the clearing, and the green glow of the alchemy formations gradually lit up around them.
Looking down from the sky above, one could see a Nonagram Alchemy Formation with a diameter of several kilometers near the foot of the giant tree slowly lighting up.
This was the ancient seal "Light Realm Arrival," a divine arts-level large-scale sealing prohibition on par with the Dalu Clan's "Burial God Ritual."
...
With everything ready, Su Lun, looking at Yuta beside him, said in a heavy voice, "Open the seal."
Yuta, too, nodded solemnly, "Mhm."
As she spoke, she began chanting a spell: "Great nature god above, listen to your faithful's devout prayers..."
Ethereal prayers filled the air as two Dalu relics, the "Chalice of Far" and "Dagda's Magic Cauldron," floated beside Yuta, unleashing a majestic natural force.
This was a secret technique that only a Great Druid could perform, capable of protecting people from negative energy contamination. It was a very gentle energy that made one feel as though their soul had been cleansed.
Suddenly, a radiant divine light burst from Yuta. With her hands devoutly clasped together, the towering giant tree behind everyone seemed to have its vitality stripped away as its lush branches and leaves withered slowly.
As the giant tree withered, the natural force gradually dissipated. In its place, a heart-palpitating evil energy surged from the ground. That energy transformed into visible strands of black gas, steaming forth.
Everyone held their breath.
Because they knew they were about to witness a "secret" that surpassed their knowledge.
In Su Lun's eyes, reflected by Yuta's figure, the All-knowing Eye saw strands of Rule Threads, the power of the gods.
And those steaming strands of black gas were also threads of incomplete rules.
Seeing this, Su Lun's pupils shrank slightly as he muttered to himself, "Just as expected, the God Burial Ground has a large number of rule threads remaining."
Although the rule threads emanating from underground were still extremely sparse and heavily broken.
But this was just the beginning of the seal breaking, it wasn't hard to surmise that there must be more underground.
This was also their most important reason for coming here.
Only with enough Rule Threads could he refine the "Universe Essence"!
...
Yuta swiftly extracted the energy from the giant tree's seal using the two Dalu relics.
Before long, the seal barrier of the giant tree was finally breached.
Billowing black gas gushed from beneath the ground like black flames, engulfing the entire tree and setting it "ablaze."
At the same time, on the island-sized tree canopy, a horde of mutated monsters, startled, rushed out in swarms like locusts.
Had it not been seen with their own eyes, no one would have believed that so many monsters could live within a single tree.
However, the monsters didn't even have time to flee before the vast amounts of black gas erupting like from an underground volcano instantly enveloped the mutating creatures within.
Even if the monsters on the tree canopy weren't strong, most being only rank one, two, or three, with the strongest lord being only rank seven.
Yet, contained within that black gas were terrifying higher-order rules and dark energy. In just an instant, the monsters exploded from being unable to withstand the corrosion of the black gas, dying, or transforming into even more horrifying mutated monsters.
Seeing this sight, all of Dawn's people could not help but look on with gravity.
Even Mr. Jing furrowed his brow, his face solemn.
Nobody had ever seen what the land of a fallen deity looked like, but evidently, even she found the black gas before her somewhat incomprehensible.
However, this was just the beginning.
Although Dawn's people were mentally prepared for unsealing the seal, nobody expected that after being sealed for hundreds of years, the God Burial Ground would present them with such a grand welcome gift.
Su Lun sensed the powerful soul fluctuation and his expression shifted slightly, thinking to himself: A pseudo-god?!
He wasn't surprised that over the long years, some pseudo-gods would emerge in the God Burial Ground. But he didn't expect to encounter such a troublesome existence upon arrival.
Mr. Hei, too, sensed something a moment later and shouted, "Everyone, be ready!"
"Yes!"
The ten thousand mage squad by his side had long been prepared, reciting low dragon tongue chants in unison. In an instant, the super-large Nonagram Alchemy Formation blazed brightly.
Almost simultaneously, the ground cracked open, and rocks tumbled down with a "rattle." A hand over a hundred meters long burst through the ground. Like a resurrecting corpse trying to struggle out from the soil, it tore through the dried trunk and revealed half a shoulder.
This was a half-transparent, black jelly-like giant Spiritual Body.
Su Lun focused his gaze and identified the name as "False God·Titan Spirit Fallen into Wickedness (Grade Nine)".
This was a false god born from the dissipation of the Power of Faith in the corpses of deities.
The members of the Dawn Brigade were not unfamiliar with such an opponent, for they had clashed with them many times before.
"Attack!"
With Mr. Hei's command, the Ten Thousand Magician Brigade exerted their power simultaneously. Before the giant could even stand, the chains of laws within the Alchemy Formation had already bound it tightly.
Originally, a Ninth Grade False God was considered a top existence anywhere, but in the eyes of the present Dawn Brigade, it did not pose much of a threat.
The team members coordinated seamlessly, and while controlling the monster, nine Holy Light Divine Spears had already pierced through the body of the false god at various places—wrists, neck, chest... pinning it firmly to the ground. Even the lamenting howls that could bewilder one's mind were preemptively blocked by set restrictions, not causing the slightest effect on the Ten Thousand Magician Brigade.
With the Magicians in action, control of the situation was assured, so naturally, the high-ranked fighters didn't need to intervene. They watched from the side.
Mr. Jing said indifferently, "This pressure far exceeds that of an ordinary false god... It seems that the deity that fell here was quite significant."
Su Lun also observed something else and said, "The faith is very mixed too. More than one deity, perhaps even many, are buried here."
Old Sword God Bartolo said, "To be greeted with such a 'welcoming gift' upon arrival. It's dangerous underground..."
Barrett said, "Yes, it is."
Everyone expressed their opinions one after another, but there was no trace of fear on anyone's face, only the desire to explore the unknown and anticipation.
The Dawn Brigade had come this far, having ventured through many perilous lands. In everyone's heart, there was an inexplicable conviction that no matter the difficulty, the Dawn Brigade would surely be able to tackle it successfully!
Although the monster before them was formidable, since it did not pose a threat to the Dawn Brigade, it became material.
The one who liked false gods the most was still Pandora, for she could steal the Power of Faith.
Previously, she had descended in the Four Nations of North Continent and the waters of Dragon Country to absorb faith. Upon hearing Su Lun and their plans, her Divine Power also returned to her true form.
Upon seeing the giant, her eyes already turned a demonic blood red, "I'm going."
No sooner had she spoken than she transformed into streaks of red light. One glance at the moon in the sky, and it was already a crimson red.
Su Lun was not idle either. Watching Pandora leave, he also said, "The false god contains a rich essence of laws; I'll give it a try too."
Mr. Jing beside him nodded.
Yuta, not knowing how strong Su Lun had become, said, "Be careful."
Su Lun smiled faintly, "Mhm."
...
Under the control of Mr. Hei's Ten Thousand Magician Brigade, Pandora's power, transformed into strands of red light, ceaselessly extracted the Power of Faith from the giant. The monster, sealed for countless years, had no time to wreak havoc before it was drained, its nascent consciousness erased. Although its body was still struggling, it was already dead.
Su Lun also teleported next to the giant's corpse. His ring, inlaid with the Philosopher's Stone, shone brightly with a red light, and an Alchemy Formation instantly condensed beneath his feet.
Having refined it many times before, the process was exceedingly proficient for him, and in an instant, the refining glow enveloped the giant's body. The strands of laws, visible only to him, were refined out.
Looking at the threads extracted from the giant's corpse, Su Lun was also somewhat surprised, "There's so much?"
Despite the fragmented rules and the chaotic mix of colored threads, the sheer quantity was overwhelming.
In just a moment, Su Lun refined far more strands of laws than expected.
These threads formed clusters of amber-hued energy in the Alchemy Formation, scattered here and there, a dozen or so clusters.
Like 3% "Threads of Darkness Law," 5% "Threads of Death Law," 1.4% "Threads of Elemental Law," 2.6% "Threads of War Law,"...
Though they were not much, they were indeed rules strands that could not be found anywhere else!
Moreover, gathered together, they amounted to over 60%, far exceeding the yield from previously harvested Ninth Grade Sage of Law corpses.
Soon, Pandora finished extracting the Power of Faith, and Su Lun had cleanly extracted all the threads of law from the body.
The monster, which was a concentration of energy, immediately dissipated, revealing a large hole in the ground.
...
"Is it dead?"
"It seems so..."
"..."
The members of the Dawn Brigade looked at the suddenly collapsed monster and exchanged glances.
The process had gone so smoothly that it was almost unbelievable.
At least from the oppressive aura that the monster had given off when it first appeared, it should have been a powerful Ninth Grade creature, right?
But, was it really killed off just like that?
The majority could not understand Pandora's Faith Stealing method, nor did they grasp what Su Lun's extraction of the threads of law really entailed; they only saw that the monster ceased to exist moments after the two high-ranked fighters made their move.
Although the Dragon Language Magician Brigade had been practicing for two years, this was their first encounter with such a powerful enemy.
Because they had never faced an enemy that could push them to their limits, most of the members did not have an accurate concept of the team's combat power.
Now, seeing this Ninth Grade monster be killed in the blink of an eye, someone muttered, "That monster didn't seem to be particularly strong."
Someone uncertainly said, "Could it be... that we are just too powerful?"
After the giant monster died, it seemed to quiet down for a moment, and everyone immediately started discussing.
Yuta, who had never seen such a large group before, watched with great surprise and curiosity filling her sparkling eyes.
After all, she was the one who had broken the seal, and when she saw the terrifying monster that made her scalp tingle emerge, she was initially worried.
But seeing that the monster hadn't even crawled out of the ground before being annihilated like that, she was instantly—
Seeing Su Lun return, she excitedly said, "Mr. Su Lun, you've become so powerful."
There were only a few at the scene who understood what Su Lun had just done, and Yuta was one of them.
Listening, Su Lun gave a slight smile, well aware that she was referring to the ability to extract threads of law, and responded, "Not really powerful. I just made use of an alchemical treasure."
Yuta blinked and then smiled with her lips pursed, "Even without treasures, it's still very impressive."
"Hehe."
Su Lun's lips curved up slightly, and he didn't elaborate further.
Turning his head, he looked at Mr. Jing and showed the loot he had just acquired, saying, "Senior sister, as expected, the God Burial Ground has plenty of threads of law."
As he spoke, he opened his right hand, revealing the ten or so bundles of threads of law he had just collected, "If there are enough such monsters, then we can also have enough 'Cosmic Essence'."
Mr. Jing nodded lightly in response, "Mhm."
This was the outcome they had anticipated.
But the high-level fighters of the Dawn Group nearby didn't know this; hearing the news, the desire in their eyes grew intense, and their breaths became visibly heavier.
If there were enough 'Cosmic Essence,' the shackles on alchemists' advancement to the ninth rank would be completely broken.
For someone like the Old Sword God Bartolo at the peak of the eighth rank, a single Cosmic Essence would allow him to directly ascend a major rank, an absolute qualitative increase in combat power!
However, just as everyone hadn't had the chance to catch their breath, suddenly the observer shouted, "Careful, more monsters are coming out from that pit! A lot of them!"
All heads turned in unison to look, and there was a rush like a volcanic eruption spewing out a tide of monsters.
On a closer look, they were winged humanoid monsters.
Unlike the demon transformations of the blood clan, these monsters had no hair, a sickly pale complexion all over, and heads were eyeless lumps of flesh with a pair of grotesque fleshy wings on their backs, like human palms.
Su Lun identified them and saw they were listed as "Flesh Winged Aberrants (Golden Level Weirds)"
They were only of the fifth or sixth rank, but there were so many of them!
And each one was a boss of a weird level; upon their appearance, a terrifying chill immediately swept through.
That is to say, their combat strength would be several times that of other monsters of their rank.
This was the God Burial Ground, and Su Lun felt that he shouldn't be surprised to see any level of monsters. But after observing with the second solution of the All-knowing Eye, he was surprised to find threads of law even on these lower-level monsters.
Each one had about 0.001 or so, quite fragmented, but they were indeed present.
This was a situation that would be impossible to find on any other monsters outside.
"Low-level monsters also have threads of law?"
Su Lun was greatly surprised in his heart.
Clearly, these were monsters born from the corpse of a deity, not to be viewed by common standards.
But he immediately thought of something, and urgently said through the communicator, "Be careful, these monsters are special; only by burning them with fire system techniques can you kill them!"
Hearing Su Lun's intelligence, Mr. Hei also reacted promptly; the alchemy formation under the feet of the thousands of magicians suddenly burst into red light. With all magicians forming sorcerer's seals at once, thick fire elements converged within the formation.
The monsters could fly, and they were quite fast. They burst out of the underground hole, some scattering in all directions in the sky, while others charged towards the Dawn Group.
But before they could get close, Mr. Hei yelled sternly, "Dragon Breath!"
In an instant, the magicians formed their sorcerer's seals in unison, and within the formation, the thick fire elements coalesced into nine ferocious, hundred-meter-long fire dragons that rushed toward the horde in the sky.
The scorching white-hot flames surged towards the monsters.
The legion's technique utilized by the ten-thousand-person group had power comparable to a ninth rank, so even if these monsters were special, under the extreme heat and law of fire elements, they were instantly turned to ash.
But the sheer number of monsters was too great; even though the "Eight Divine Flames Dragon Breath" technique had killed two to three thousand of them, an unending stream still poured forth from that hole.
Like moths to a flame, they headed towards the Dawn Group, attracted to the strong scents of living humans.
Mr. Hei was not idle; he controlled the nine fire dragons to wreak havoc in the swarm, and the winged monsters fell like raindrops.
However, more of them flew haphazardly towards the sky, probably intending to break through to other places.
Unfortunately for them, because the Dawn Group had set up defensive barriers beforehand, as these monsters rose into the sky, a giant golden energy dome suddenly enveloped the entire towering tree space.
The defensive barrier also had high-level sensory confusion prohibitions, capable of disrupting spatial awareness near the target.
The monsters that rushed towards it immediately lost direction, darting around aimlessly.
While the barrier was effective, due to the overwhelming number of monsters, as they flew in all directions, some inevitably collided with the barrier's edge and began attacking.
Noticing this, Mr. Hei shouted sharply, "Hurry up and deal with the source; these monsters are attacking the prohibitions very fast!"
It was in that fleeting moment that hundreds of thousands of monsters had burst forth. The vast space within the barrier was swarmed with the figures of those white-skinned creatures.
Upon hearing this, the Dawn Brigade, save for the ten-thousand-strong Magician contingent, also joined the battlefield, along with the Old Sword God Bartolo and other elite warriors.
However, as peerless as their combat strength was, it seemed insufficient against the endless horde of monsters. In just a moment, the number of beasts seemed to multiply as they were slain.
Witnessing this, everyone gained a newfound respect for the formidable nature of the God Burial Ground.
This was just the beginning, yet they were already faced with a ninth-tier monster, followed by countless others.
Although their own safety was not immediately threatened, a slight worry began to take root in everyone's hearts.
If they couldn't deal with these cold-breath-spewing, flying abominations and more of such creatures emerged from the sealed caverns, the defensive enchantment might not be able to contain them entirely.
Once these monsters broke free, they would pose a catastrophic threat to the Dalu of the Silent Forest, perhaps even to the entire Alchemical Plane.
And yet, it was at this critical juncture.
Mr. Jing remained unfazed. She made no move to join the fray, simply standing there in silence.
For she alone knew the extent of Su Lun's capabilities.
Sure enough, it was then that Su Lun took action.
Where others saw only a dire threat in the unending horde of monsters, to him, they were highly sought-after materials.
A strand of rule at 0.001%, a thousand would make it 1%, ten thousand would equate to 10%...
In theory, slaughtering a hundred thousand would nearly yield one "Cosmic Essence".
Although difficult to kill, these creatures were much easier to defeat than a ninth-tier foe.
The key point was the seemingly infinite number of such creatures here!
Monsters would die, but the "strands of rules" wouldn't disappear immediately; as long as harvested promptly, they could be perfectly preserved.
Plus, when it came to numbers, Su Lun feared nothing.
With the situation pressing, he didn't delay even for a moment. Forming a sorcerer's seal, he uttered a command, "Arcanum: Grand Puppet Theater!"
With the Philosopher's Stone's aid, Su Lun almost instantly brought the Puppet Theater into existence.
In a flash, a massive scaffold appeared in the sky. It continued to expand, and in just a moment, it had already stretched beyond a kilometer.
But Su Lun was not idle; he pulled out five spatial scrolls, shouting, "Release!"
"Boom!"
"Boom!"
"Boom!"
"..."
The spatial scrolls exploded, and upon refocusing, an overwhelming force of over thirty thousand gargoyles materialized around Su Lun!
These gargoyles, their bodies faintly glowing with a cold light, exuded a daunting presence. As soon as they emerged, one felt as if they were witnessing a torrential flow of iron.
....
The instance the gargoyle army materialized, the peripheral vision of the Dawn Brigade caught the sight and they immediately erupted with excitement.
"Mr. Su Lun has made his move!"
"Hahaha, has the Puppet Brigade finally appeared?!"
"No matter how many times one sees it, one can't help but be astonished. Mr. Su Lun's one-man army is truly thrilling."
"Indeed."
"..."
Although the members of the Dawn Brigade had witnessed Su Lun's interventions many times, the appearance of the Puppet Brigade invigorated everyone.
Moreover, they noticed that two years ago, he seemed to be able to control only ten thousand puppets.
Now, there were actually thirty thousand?
Not just the quantity had increased exponentially, it seemed... those gargoyles were different too.
The lower rank members could not discern the changes in Su Lun, but the top warriors of the Dawn Brigade had noticed.
Fighting amid the monsters, Old Sword God Bartolo muttered with content, "Su Lun has grown stronger."
Barrett was shocked, "If I hadn't advanced to the eighth tier, I would've failed to grasp the prowess of this Puppet Brigade. It's absolutely exaggerated; even a ninth-tier might face a no-return scenario..."
Mr. Hei's wise eyes twinkled with insight, "Two years apart, and he has become so strong..."
Number Nineteen smiled slightly, "Such an exaggerated transformation..."
Keet cried out, "Ah... how on earth does Su Lun train? Every time I see him, his strength has surged by leaps and bounds. Oh, what a monster..."
Yuta, with a bright smile on his face, said, "As expected, very impressive."

chapters.title: Chapter 633 - 632: Ancient God
chapters.content:
Over the past two years, nearly everyone in the Dawn Brigade had experienced explosive increases in combat power, and Su Lun, who had been constantly fighting on the frontlines, certainly hadn't been treading water.
Not to mention a significant improvement in his own cultivation, the change in his gargoyle legion was also very dramatic.
From barely being able to control two ten-thousand-strong legions two years ago, he could now command over thirty thousand. But managing this number had almost reached the limit of his spiritual power and mental capacity. Without merging with the Isaac Blasphemer, the growth in the number of puppet troops he controlled would increasingly slow, and might even halt at this point.
However, over the past two years, the combat power of the more than thirty thousand gargoyles had already changed beyond recognition.
Puppets could continuously improve in quality through enhancements to runes and materials. And a god-tier main material like "Activated Silver" possessed almost limitless malleability. This was one of the most critical reasons why, a thousand years ago, Su Lun's teacher Sereya considered the gargoyles her "most perfect design."
In these two years, the puppet production line process in the war workshop had matured daily, with the entire dwarven clan helping to engrave high-level runes. Su Lun, for his part, was not short of various high-quality materials, including the perfect core material—Dragon Crystal—which gave him the conditions to mass-produce high-tier puppets.
Furthermore, two years were enough for Su Lun to personally engrave a batch of top-tier gargoyle runes.
...
The moment Su Lun engaged the puppet army, his expression suddenly tensed, and he whispered silently, "Puppet Mastery · Grand Theater's Curtain Call!"
The cross in the sky grew larger and larger, soon covering the entire restricted space.
A myriad of transparent strands fell from the cross, interweaving into a network of webs.
Embodying might and laws, "Wailing Witch's Hair" was already indestructible; the monsters charging towards it were like fish caught in a net, struggling and being sliced by steel-like strands into bloody wounds. The winged creatures still tried to struggle, but the more they did, the more strands bound them, wrapping tighter and tighter.
While the strings controlled a massive number of enemies, Su Lun pinched the Suren Sorcerer's Seal, and the more than thirty thousand gargoyles instantly sprang into action.
The significance of legion warfare lay in the ability to gather both number and members, complementing each other's strengths and weaknesses to achieve the most perfect fit, bringing the team's combat power to its peak.
Even the simplest well-coordinated tank, support, and damage-dealer five-person squad had at least three to five times the combat power of five individuals.
Each of Su Lun's more than thirty thousand gargoyles had their role in the battle formation. There were heavy-armored gargoyles acting as tanks in the front, supportive gargoyles focused on elemental convergence, main output spatial gargoyles, as well as sonic, crowd control, assassin-type gargoyles, and various other functional mechanized armors...
In the past, he reaped enough knowledge of legion battle formations, and over the past two years of continuous experimentation, he devised several sets that almost perfectly matched the puppet legion.
Today, his puppet legion could be said to be an invincible army without any flaws!
Su Lun's puppet army was entirely under his control. Though consisting of tens of thousands, commanding them was like using his own hands. Orders were instantaneously received—attack and defense were all in a single thought.
In the blink of an eye, three ten-thousand-strong mage legions charged fearlessly towards the densest part of the monster horde.
Although the monsters were still dozens or hundreds of times more numerous than the puppet army, they knew nothing of tactics or warfare, like a scattering of sand trying to hold back a steel torrent, scattering upon contact.
Gargoyles were puppets after all, completely fearless of negative energy corrosion, unafraid of life or death, charging forward, unstoppable.
...
The scene of the puppet army descending out of nowhere had already stunned the distant members of the Dawn Brigade.
Su Lun stood in the sky, his robe fluttering mightily in a surging aura. With a cold expression, he had already entered a state of absolute rationality, focusing on controlling the more than thirty thousand gargoyles as they indiscriminately slaughtered their way through.
With the addition of the puppet army to the battlefield, the earlier torrential surge of monsters was immediately curtailed.
Limbs and severed extremities rained down from the sky.
The commotion even overshadowed the Dragon Language Magicians, who had just shone brightly.
After all, they numbered ten thousand.
And Su Lun had always been just one man.
He single-handedly suppressed hundreds of thousands of high-ranking aberrant monsters, who were unable to rampage as they pleased.
How overwhelmingly dominant was that?
"My God, it's been two years since we saw Mr. Su Lun, and his puppet army has become this powerful? I fear that even if ten or eight rank nine came, they wouldn't be able to do anything, right?"
"Hahaha, the biggest weakness of a puppet army is the Puppet Master himself. But I feel that no one would be able to do anything to Mr. Su Lun."
"Yeah, truly an invincible army..."
"..."
The team members felt at a loss for words, unable to describe the shock in their hearts.
In their eyes, as strong as rank nine might be, where could one find such a sense of... blood-boiling excitement as with Su Lun, where a single person is an army?
Yes!
It was blood-boiling excitement!
That proud figure standing aloof in the sky, hovering in the void, provided everyone with a sense of security.
The members of the Dawn Brigade had seen such scenes several times before; in their memories, it seemed that every time they encountered danger, Su Lun would appear like a god descending from the heavens, reversing the situation.
Even the high-combat members of the Dawn Brigade were filled with shock and heartfelt relief.
However, now was clearly not the time for hesitation. Watching Su Lun enter the fray and suppress the explosive momentum of the monster tide, they too didn't idle, charging into the crowd of monsters and causing havoc.
Meanwhile, Su Lun watched the dense, rain-like cascade of monster corpses, and the sorcerer's seal in his hand changed: "Condense!"
As he controlled the stone gargoyle legion with his Puppet Theater, a Nonagram Alchemy Formation lit up underneath him.
These monsters all possessed a tiny bit of "Thread of Law" that would quickly dissipate after their death.
He couldn't wait until the battle was over to clean up the battlefield for extraction.
Su Lun had to act quickly, so he prepared to refine those corpses while still engaged in battle.
The sheer number of corpses, reaching tens of thousands, required an extremely large alchemy formation.
Luckily, with the blessing of the "Heart of Isaac's Alchemy" and the alchemical holy relic "Philosopher's Stone," all the spells Su Lun cast were "sublimated versions."
Not only was the cross above his head very large, but the scale of the Nine-Pointed Star Refinement Array beneath his feet grew increasingly exaggerated.
The monsters, lacking any real intelligence, saw Su Lun alone in the air and instinctively rushed to bite and swarm him.
Unfortunately for them, monsters of the fifth or sixth order no longer posed any threat to Su Lun.
Even though these monsters had a bit of Thread of Law and could trouble professionals of the same rank, Su Lun was no ordinary eighth-tier. Whether in terms of rank or understanding of the laws, he absolutely crushed these monsters.
Not to mention whether the monsters could break through the defense of the puppet legion, even if some slipped through, once the Death domain unfolded, any that entered its coverage would be instantly stripped of vitality, raining down and then refined into materials within the alchemy formation.
Even if some lord-level creatures among these monsters managed to enter his domain, with the protection of "Death God's Fire," he could quickly kill them.
Watching that "0.001%," "0.001%," "0.001%,"... Those thin threads being extracted one by one, the joy in Su Lun's eyes grew stronger.
He had the premonition that this loot would be extremely satisfying.
...
The moment Su Lun made his move, the tide of monsters was immediately suppressed.
What initially seemed an endless trouble became manageable in an instant.
Most of the monsters were distracted by the puppet legion and the draconic incantation military troop, and the defensive barriers set up on the giant tree no longer faced the threat of being shattered.
No matter how numerous, they probably couldn't exhaust Su Lun, the "perpetual motion machine."
Obviously, the monsters in the pit wouldn't truly be infinite.
After the explosive surge of monsters lasted for about half an hour, their density gradually began to decrease.
Finally, after an intense fight that lasted an hour, only a few stray flesh-winged creatures occasionally emerged from the pit, with no large groups flying out anymore.
The monsters trapped in the barrier, without support, were quickly eradicated.
There were probably still a few thousand monsters scattered around, but Su Lun no longer controlled the puppet legion to clean them up, leaving the task to the members of the Dawn Group.
He withdrew most of his puppets and landed on the ground.
The high-ranking fighters also gathered around.
They had just witnessed Su Lun's exaggeratedly overwhelming tactics and were greatly shocked.
Now that the battle was over, they excitedly crowded around, joking with each other.
"Hahaha, Su Lun, your puppet legion has really become ridiculously exaggerated now."
"Indeed. I thought I'd be unmatched as an advanced eighth-ranker, but looking at your puppet legion, I realize I don't stand a chance at all."
"Tsk tsk, truly exaggerated. Your thirty-thousand-strong puppet legion could hold off more than ten troops from a godly domain's ten-thousand-man magical unit by itself! And with your personal combat power, it's hard to imagine just how strong you've become."
"..."
In that recent bout, Su Lun merely showcased the strength of his puppet legion, but everyone knew his own combat power was also incredibly strong.
Capable in mass battles and one-on-one fights, such a Puppet Master was simply unbeatable.
However, this was good news for Dawn.
Everyone was happy for him.
After the laughter and chatting, the group turned to more serious matters.
Barrett asked eagerly, "Su Lun, how was the loot?"
With that, everyone's attention turned toward him.
Even Mr. Jing's gaze flashed with expectation.
The big risks they had taken to unseal this "God Burial Ground" wasn't for the sake of killing monsters but to find enough Source Essence.
Just now, they had all seen with their own eyes Su Lun refining hundreds of thousands of monsters.
Su Lun didn't let everyone down. He smiled, spread his hands to reveal dozens of bundles of Cosmic Essence of different colors, and said, "The harvest was quite bountiful."
What?
Quite bountiful!
Hearing this keyword, everyone's expressions visibly brightened, unable to hide their thick anticipation.
Su Lun didn't keep everyone in suspense and continued, "The monsters we just faced were mostly Ice rules. I managed to condense a bead of the nineteenth Cosmic Essence, 'Extreme Cold.' And the other incomplete strands of rules, when added together, are equivalent to about four beads of essence. With more fragments, we might be able to obtain even more complete Cosmic Essence..."
Upon hearing this, everyone from Dawn's breath became faintly heavier.
Cosmic Essence, for any Alchemist, was a treasure they could only dream of.
Especially for this group of top-tier professionals, it represented the key to breaking free of their chains and seeing a new world.
Looking at the crystal exuding intense coldness in Su Lun's hand, everyone was overjoyed.
Cosmic Essence...
This was a treasure that the United Empire had been searching for two years with all its might, yet hadn't found. But now, Dawn had managed to "easily" obtain one, plus fragments of another four.
Oh, it wasn't easy.
It's just that Dawn had made sufficient preparations and was strong enough.
If it were the Imperial Legion opening this seal, setting aside whether they could refine Cosmic Essence, just the two waves of monster attacks earlier would have caused at least hundreds of thousands of casualties.
Su Lun took out the Cosmic Essence and exchanged a glance with his senior sister standing nearby.
Even though they didn't speak, Mr. Jing immediately understood and nodded slightly.
Su Lun didn't say much, turned, and handed the Cosmic Essence to Old Sword God Bartolo, who was wiping his Famed Sword "Jia Qie Frost Flower Whisper," and said, "Elder Bartolo, this essence is most compatible with you, so I'll leave it in your care."
The Old Sword God looked surprised and hesitated, "But..."
He had intended to say that he was one of the later members to join Dawn, and by rights, he shouldn't be the first to receive such a treasure in terms of merits and rewards.
However, there was such a thing as compatibility with Cosmic Essence, and only those of the eighth tier could use it. Old Sword God Bartolo cultivated the Ice rules, and there was no one more suitable for this essence in the whole of Dawn.
Moreover, although Old Sword God hadn't been with Dawn for long, his contributions were far from small.
This was evident to everyone.
Despite the incalculable value of Cosmic Essence, he was absolutely deserving of it.
Before the Old Sword God could refuse, Su Lun sealed the essence in a rune box and gave it to him, "Elder Bartolo, the Alchemy plane now needs top experts, please do not hesitate to accept."
People around them wore smiles and said, "Indeed. Elder Bartolo advancing to the ninth tier holds significant meaning both for Dawn and for the Alchemy plane."
The current Dawn was united in purpose, dispensing with any insincere beating around the bush, offering only sincere blessings.
Besides, everyone knew this was just the beginning.
Based on the current situation, more essence could be refined later on with high probability.
Listening, a solemn glint appeared in Old Sword God's cloudy eyes, and he no longer objected, "Alright."
...
With most monsters within the barrier eliminated, the team members began to clean up the battlefield and, by the way, strengthen the barrier.
Su Lun and Mr. Jing, along with several high-level fighters, cautiously approached the pitch-black pit on the ground.
This pit was the sealing entrance to the God Burial Ground; many monsters had run out from it, so there must be a very large space inside.
But strangely, Su Lun sensed that there was no "space" inside that pit.
Instead of calling it a pit, it was more like a spot on the ground where black ooze absorbed light without reflecting any, a special area.
It was like... a two-dimensional plane.
Su Lun glanced at Lord Crow on his shoulder and pondered.
Mr. Jing apparently knew something, and looking at that dark hole, she pondered for a moment before saying, "Legend has it that some higher beings had realms within themselves. When they fell, their realms collapsed, but some broken spaces remained..."
Everyone frowned deeply upon hearing this.
The pit in front of them blocked nearly all perception; it was impossible to tell what was inside.
Even if a communicator was thrown in, it would lose signal instantly.
The fear was that this black hole led to some bizarre space beyond cognition, where entry might lead to an unknown destination. Considering the current situation, there was definitely no simple creature inside the pit.
Luckily, they had Lord Crow.
The undying raven was most suitable for exploring such dangerous places.
Su Lun looked at the black crow on his shoulder, took out a piece of rotten meat, and said, "Mr. Crow, please do me a favor."
After eating the meat, the black crow flapped its wings with a haughty air, seemingly enjoying the attention it was receiving from everyone.
Despite the constant banter between Su Lun and the seemingly foolish bird, their relationship had grown incredibly close over time.
Mr. Crow did not delay and plunged into the black hole.
....
The black crow entered the mysterious space.
Everyone completely lost their sense of it and turned to look at Su Lun.
Su Lun shared his vision with Mr. Crow, and the moment Mr. Crow entered the space, he saw a crimson expanse: "It seems... like it's another plane?"
He wasn't sure because the space Mr. Crow perceived was so vast that he couldn't see the boundaries.
After a pause, he cautiously added, "It seems to be a sea."
Everyone, finding this very curious, responded, "A sea?"
A sea emerging from the depths of the earth?
"Yes. The perception is interfered with; it might not be a sea, maybe something else."
Su Lun also wanted to investigate, but just then, his vision went dark. The black crow had been suddenly destroyed by an attack from some creature.
Without waiting two seconds, a wisp of death's breath rose from his shoulder, and Mr. Crow's body reformed once again.
Seeing this, everyone couldn't help but twitch at the corners of their eyes.
Frowning, Su Lun said, "Didn't see what kind of monster it was. But one thing is certain... it's very strong."
Hearing this, no one dared to take it lightly and continued to reinforce the restrictions around the black hole, fearing that something terrifying might suddenly burst out.
They were fortunate to have Mr. Crow.
Su Lun took out another piece of rotten meat and requested, "Mr. Crow, I need to ask you again."
The black crow didn't dawdle and, after eating the meat, flew headfirst back into the black hole.
After more than a dozen annihilations of Mr. Crow, Su Lun finally managed to glimpse the creature that was attacking him.
It seemed to be a segment of a fleshy tentacle.
Emerging from the "sea."
But since Mr. Crow was almost always destroyed as soon as it flew in, he never managed to get very far, so Su Lun wasn't sure what else might be inside.
However, their mission to open the sealed land was undertaken with great expectations, and what they had found so far was far from sufficient; clearly, they would not back down so easily.
Everyone knew that someone needed to go down and explore in person.
Su Lun didn't wait for others to speak up and said directly, "I'll go down and take a look."
Barrett and the others wanted to say something, but the words died on their lips.
Everyone knew the great risk of exploring this unknown space, but except for Su Lun, no one else could be sure of surviving.
Su Lun's Spatial Displacement ability was unmatched within the Dawn group, and with the "Urobolos Space-Time Ring," he was almost certain not to be trapped in any space.
Moreover, his own strength was formidable, he possessed the All-knowing Eye, and without a weak point, he was definitely the most suitable in the group.
Yuta appeared worried and proposed, "Should I accompany you?"
"I'm actually safer on my own. Don't worry, if I encounter something I can't handle, I'll come back immediately."
Su Lun shook his head, refusing Yuta's offer and discouraging any thoughts from other members of the Dawn group who wished to help.
He had his own confidence; today's Alchemical planes that could give him trouble were possible, but definitely not widespread.
Even though Yuta wanted to say more, he realized that whatever he could say seemed pale and powerless and simply said, "Be careful."
Su Lun nodded, "Yeah."
As he spoke, he didn't take any chances, wrapped himself in the long-unused "Oz's Mummy Wrappings," and instantly disappeared; he leaped down through the black hole.
Upon another glance, the surroundings changed, and his vision was filled with red.
It turned out that the "sea" Mr. Crow had seen before was actually a bloody sea with an intense odor of blood.
This was a world where the senses were distorted.
As soon as Su Lun entered, he immediately felt an indescribable presence hitting him, ancient and mysterious, with a sense of power beyond description.
Upon examining it with the second level of the All-knowing Eye, a vast amount of information beyond current knowledge filled his mind, and Su Lun exclaimed to himself, "This is... inside the body of an Ancient God?"

chapters.title: Chapter 634 - 633: Huge Harvest
chapters.content:
Su Lun didn't know how to describe the world before him, for he had clearly realized that his perception was distorted.
To the human eye, it seemed as if he was placed within an abstract painting, with the entire world appearing abstract, devoid of any reality.
Yet, under the scrutiny of his second-evolved All-knowing Eye, another true world unfolded before him, where he saw the flow of countless chaotic rules.
These rules were untamed and irregular, like all colors of paint swirled together, but not fully blended, becoming complex hues incomprehensible to the mind.
"Faith contamination?"
Su Lun's brows furrowed deeply, for this was more than just chaotic rules.
The moment he entered this space, he felt as if whispers were in his ears, incessant, instilling in him the urge to prostrate in pilgrimage toward some indescribable existence.
"How strong must that Ancient God have been to leave behind such a dense Power of Faith after so many years?" he pondered.
