If he could advance to the ninth rank, then Su Lun would truly be able to touch the pinnacle of power humans could grasp, such as the mysteries of "rules".
Although he had previously extracted some insights from two demigods, after all, the world perception of a mage was incomplete.
Besides, those were after all someone else's insights, and some sceneries could only be truly appreciated by reaching that height oneself.
Upon hearing this, Mr. Jing nodded and said, "Indeed, after the battle in the Imperial Strait, the divine realms won't be making any movements for a long while. Now is indeed the best opportunity for your advancement."
As he spoke, he paused for a moment before adding, "A few days ago, after the defeat of the magic legions, personnel from the Imperial Intelligence Department monitoring the realm portal in Zambra Ironfalls province confirmed that two new banners appeared in the magic encampment. One is a blood-colored griffin banner, the other a star-striped crown banner. They should be the armies of the 'Golden Griffin Empire' and 'Holy Crown Empire' you've mentioned, bordering the Ascieden Empire. If the enemy launches another attack, we may face not just one or two demigods and a million-strong legion, but at least several times that number of enemies..."
"Indeed."
Su Lun's gaze slightly sharpened as he listened, which was one of the reasons he wanted to advance to the ninth rank as quickly as possible.
Having stripped two magic gods of their memories, he was very clear on the divine realm's invasion plans.
In the battle of the Imperial Strait, a million magic legions were annihilated, and the enemy suffered a heavy loss; they definitely wouldn't act rashly.
This indeed gave the Alchemy dimension a long period of breathing time.
But now, with the Ascieden Empire's lackluster campaign, next would be the joint campaign of the three great empires against the Alchemy dimension.
Without solving the root problem of the realm portal, the war would never see its end; instead, the number of enemies would only increase.
Su Lun had also considered raiding the realm portal's magic encampment, but it would be meaningless.
Not to mention that the enemy was already on guard and that a surprise attack would be extremely risky; even if it were successful, the portal was already completely stable. The exit was controlled by the gods of the divine realms, and they were powerless to stop the mages from descending.
As Su Lun's mind automatically deduced various possibilities, a careless voice rang in the room, "Ah... If they come, then battle it is."
After saying this, she smacked her lips and added with enthusiasm, "Just right, my understanding of sword dao has deepened from these last two battles with demigods. Maybe by checking out that black stele you mentioned, I might have a chance to make further progress."
In her tone, there seemed to be an anticipation for battling strong adversaries.
"..."
Hearing this, both Su Lun and Mr. Jing had a strange look on their faces.
To the Rakshasa Woman, terms like demigod sparked no reverence in her voice; after all, apart from the two this time, she had already killed a demigod monster in the Netherworld.
It was as if seeing a few more the next time made no difference to her.
The reason Su Lun and Mr. Jing's expressions were odd was not only because of that but for another reason.
For others, the realms of profound understanding that were difficult to reach seemed to have no threshold for the Rakshasa Woman.
The Rakshasa Woman had a natural talent for warfare; as long as she didn't die, the more she battled, the stronger she got.
This time, severely wounded and on the brink of death, she had a new insight. And now, as a ninth rank sword deity, she had already touched the mysteries of the rules. Her next step was the realm of a demigod.
For most people, this was a realm heard of only in legends, but in her mouth, it seemed as simple as getting into a fight.
Su Lun had not failed to notice that after her trip to the Netherworld, the Rakshasa Woman's innate gift had been fully unleashed.
While the Rakshasa Woman herself couldn't clearly describe those changes, Su Lun had observed the Rakshasa Golden Body Law closely. It was an existence beyond the "rules". He even started to believe that the legend of "godly reincarnation" might really have some truth to it.
...
The Rakshasa Woman's casual words lightened up the conversation in the room.
Su Lun also chuckled lightly.
Indeed, if the enemy came, they would just fight.
Once he advanced to the ninth rank, the situation would improve a lot.
The Puppet Master's greatest weakness still lay within himself. The battle before had been fortunate with Mr. Jing, Qiantiao, Pandora, and Pestroya adopting a four-protect-one strategy, which gave him the space to fully concentrate on controlling his puppets' offensive. Otherwise, in front of a Demigod, he truly wasn't certain he could have preserved his own life.
But once he advanced to rank nine, everything would change.
By then, even against a Demigod, Su Lun was confident he would have the ability to protect himself.
Moreover, the War Workshop was now continuously producing high-quality gargoyles, and his puppet legion was destined to grow stronger.
If he were to encounter an equally large-scale magic army of a million again, it would pose much less of a threat to Su Lun.
By that time, if the enemies didn't send at least ten or eight Magic Gods, Su Lun would truly feel underestimated.
However, there was another reason he was considering advancing to rank nine.
Su Lun had never forgotten that he was bound by a demon contract.
Following the integration with the eighth-rank implant, he increasingly had a premonition that the time to honor the contract was approaching.
He himself was proficient in various prophecies and divinations; his intuition could not be misleading, and the fulfillment was bound to come.
This was also the most crucial reason Su Lun wished to advance to rank nine as quickly as possible.
A contract involving gods and demons could only be survived through sufficient strength.
...
Mr. Jing, at his side, seemed to perceive the unusual expression between his brows and asked, "What's wrong?"
Qiantiao often appeared somewhat dim-witted, but her instincts were frighteningly accurate.
It was this question that led her to immediately guess the issue, and frowning, she said, "That contract?"
"Mmmhmm."
Su Lun nodded.
His elder sister and Qiantiao were not outsiders, so he spoke openly, "I have a feeling... that the lord of the contract may want me to fulfill it."
Back then, in the country of Mountain Hermit, within the world of "Lyndon Daily News: Netherworld,"
Su Lun had resurrected Qiantiao and Shinfuku Mitsuko using the method left by the great author Fujiwara Hayato and had signed a pact with a demon in exchange.
At that time, he made no sacrifice to bring back the two lives of Qiantiao.
Fujiwara Hayato had stated that when the time was right, he would have to board the legendary "cursed ship" and travel to a mysterious place to fulfill that pact.
Years had passed, and the contract had remained silent.
But Su Lun had never forgotten it.
His current understanding of the world now stood at the pinnacle humanity could reach. With hindsight, the significance of the demon contract became ever clearer.
At the time, what he exchanged was his "fate."
This was absolutely unavoidable.
Upon hearing this, Qiantiao pursed her lips, and without hesitation said, "I'll accompany you."
Mr. Jing also cast a concerned look.
Su Lun shook his head, "It must be me alone."
He had never known when that "appropriate" time would come, but now, that vague feeling was close and likely after his advancement to rank nine.
It appeared that the lord of the contract required him to possess a certain fighting strength to be eligible.
However, Su Lun had never intended to evade the contract. Since he made the exchange, he would naturally honor it.
As he spoke, he noticed the seriousness on their faces and explained in a lighter tone, "Perhaps it's not as bad as imagined. All things adhere to equivalence. If that god or demon requires me to fulfill the contract and is waiting for me until I reach rank nine, it's highly likely they see value in my abilities. If they see value, then it implies there's an equitable matter at hand, and I won't be completely without opportunity. After advancing to rank nine, it will be difficult to feel fatally threatened by anything below a godly level..."
Su Lun's words were not solely to reassure them, but reflected his genuinely positive mindset.
At his current level, having weathered great storms and even died once, he could calmly accept anything.
In fact, he anticipated the mysterious contract.
To Su Lun, the fragmented alchemy plane held few true secrets. The "cursed ship" and the lord of the contract, on the other hand, intrigued him greatly.
According to the current situation, the legend of the cursed ship has been circulating for tens of thousands of years.
Yet no one has ever lifted its veil of mystery.
In his mind, Su Lun even pieced together various clues and legends to derive a scenario he found most plausible: a demon, for some special reasons unable to handle certain matters, required low-level humans to intervene and thus created the contract.
And the task at hand would certainly be within human capability. It was definitely not a stalemate.
...
After this explanation, the look of concern in Mr. Jing and Qiantiao's eyes discernibly dissipated.
Su Lun's analysis was indeed plausible.
No contract demon would be so idle as to make some trivial pact for amusement. If they needed someone to fulfill it, success was certainly possible.
Moreover, indeed very few things below a divine level could threaten Su Lun after his advancement to rank nine.
The Puppeteer's strongest state is in solo combat, where one can face a million-strong army.
Assistance from others would only be a hindrance.
Even Mr. Jing and Qiantiao, who were rank nine themselves, felt far inferior in this aspect.
But they also knew Su Lun had merely discussed the positive side.
On the other hand, fulfilling the contract would undoubtedly involve immense risk.
Otherwise, the contract demon wouldn't be still seeking someone to enter the pact after tens of thousands of years.
Qiantiao pursed her lips, feeling uneasy about being unable to help.
At that moment, something occurred to Su Lun, and he added calmly, "Moreover... if that lord of the contract truly wants me to fulfill it, perhaps it's the hope for solving the conundrum of the alchemy plane's invasion."
"Oh?"
Upon hearing this, Mr. Jing's eyelashes fluttered slightly, swiftly grasping the implications, and his gaze deepened.
Although it seemed like the alchemy plane was gaining the upper hand in the current plane war, the underlying problem was unresolved.
Unless the plane portal was closed, collapse was an almost inevitable outcome.
And within the alchemy plane itself, there was very little chance left to turn the tide.
The only option was to look outside.
Previously, there had been no leads, but now there was one.
Since avoiding the obligation of the contract was impossible, the mindset naturally gravitated toward optimism.
The lord of the contract Su Lun referred to, whether benevolent or malevolent, was undoubtedly a divine entity.
This just might be the hope to turn the tide!

chapters.title: Chapter 651 - 650: Enter Rank 9
chapters.content:
Months passed in a flash.
After the last battle at the Imperial Strait, the mages of the Heavenly Plane had completely quieted down.
In the southern part of Mapha, in the Zambra Ironfall Province, the magic camp at the planar gateway had gradually assembled a million-strong army, but no magic legion dared to leave the camp at will. They holed up near the entrance of the planar gateway, reinforcing and expanding their defenses in a strict and vigilant manner.
The reason was largely because Su Lun's incredible feat of controlling a puppet army to break through the million-strong magic legion was too astonishing, letting the mages know that the Alchemy Plane also had the capability to defeat over a million troops. Moreover, capable of both fighting and fleeing, they couldn't be restrained without Magic God-level power. Therefore, they no longer dared to send out forces of ten thousand or more, fearing ambushes.
Correspondingly, the allied empire was also incapable of attacking the magic camp at the planar gateway. The military could only increase the number of guerrilla members, setting traps around Mapha and ambushing small groups of exploratory magic mages, also preparing for future wars.
The two sides thus fell into a stalemate.
This period of time also provided the Alchemy Plane with a rare chance to catch its breath and develop.
With the planar gateway open and the upper limit of laws elevated, the adverse conditions of war also became a driving force for breakthroughs by professionals. Additionally, due to Su Lun and others previously providing a large batch of "Cosmic Essences" to the official authorities of the empire, inside the united empire, more than ten seasoned 8th-tier powerhouses had broken through to the 9th-tier. This had greatly inspired the Alchemy Plane.
The new policies of Empress Yekaterina had also brought sustained and visible effects to the alchemy civilization. Even in times of peril, the nation was strong and the people wealthy. The universal implementation of the alchemy academy had allowed numerous geniuses to emerge, as various 10,000-person magicians' groups gradually took shape and mechanical warfare equipment was mass-produced from factories...
Whether from the number of professionals, combat power, or the number of top-tier professionals, the united empire was unprecedentedly powerful, perhaps even the strongest era in the ten-thousand-year history of the Alchemy Plane.
The newspapers also dubbed this era as the "Golden Age" belonging to the alchemy civilization.
But the bad news was that Mapha's intelligence operatives had observed that not one but several Magic Gods had descended upon the three great magic empires of the Ascieden Empire, the Golden Gryphon Empire, and the Holy Crown Empire from the Heavenly Plane.
The fuse for an all-out war had already been quietly lit.
...
On another note.
During these months without war, the Dawn Group had entered a state of recuperation and growth.
They had collectively gone to the God Burial Ground.
This place of the fallen gods, despite its chaotic laws and some indescribable monsters, offered unmatched conditions for training. The twisted space had chaotic, yet extremely high, law limits and numerous "treasures" left behind by ancient gods. As long as one could withstand distortion and glean even a little insight, it was tremendously beneficial for any professional.
The Dawn Group had turned this place into their training ground.
Hunting those terrifying mutant monsters was part of their daily routine.
Armed with the best genetic potions and resources, many had made breakthroughs in these months, and their collective strength had soared greatly once again.
This day, near the second layer's seal where a black stele stood.
A large mechanized town capable of accommodating tens of thousands of people had been established here.
In the town, various steam boilers billowed white smoke, and mechanics operated mining carts to transport tons of ore from the Blood Sea into the smeltery.
On closer inspection, the entire town was actually one massive ore mining field.
This period had continually involved the mining of a precious divine metal ore known as "Activating Silver."
With a steady supply of materials, in Su Lun's small void realm, the War Workshop continued to produce high-quality alchemical golems and various latest-technology mechanical octopuses.
In the camp, the Eternal Night was docked in the port.
In the sky, a super-large Nonagram Alchemy Formation was continuously bright, with a red gemstone at the center of the formation, the alchemical holy relic "Philosopher's Stone."
With the Philosopher's Stone bolstering the Nonagram Alchemy Formation, it could continuously extract threads of chaotic laws from the space, refining "Cosmic Essence." It also filtered out hazardous elements from the twisted space, allowing the area near the Eternal Night to be habitable for long periods.
At this moment, in the captain's cabin.
Sabina, wearing only a thin silk nightgown, poked her head out from the washroom and playfully asked, "Master, with work reports completed, your servant must return to Lington... I mean, if you allow, may I stay a few more days?"
Upon the disheveled bed, Su Lun, having a rare night of rest, felt exhilarated.
He clearly understood the double entendre in his succubus maid's words and responded, "The training environment here is ten times better than outside. You can stay a few more days if you like. You've just advanced to the 8th-tier, and your rank isn't stable yet, so it's a good idea to consolidate it a bit."
Yesterday, Sabina had come all the way from Lington, claiming it was to report on work, but another reason was to seek acknowledgment from Su Lun, her master, for her advancement to the 8th tier.
In the entire alchemy plane, she was considered among the top combatants.
Su Lun had not expected Sabina to advance so quickly.
So quickly that it seemed incredible to anyone.
This absurd advancement rate was due primarily to her dual-succubus talent, but the most important reason was Su Lun.
Sabina had come this time not only to ease her master's worries but also to ask for some small rewards.
Having tasted the sweetness, she became even more greedy for that rapid advancement feeling.
Su Lun also felt it was good.
Sabina's capability in running an intelligence organization was evident to all, and although she appeared very meek in front of her master, her skills as the former intelligence leader of the Umbrella Organization were nothing ordinary. Being stronger was also of great benefit to him.
Hearing her master's permission, Sabina's seductive eyes shimmered, and she smiled brilliantly, "Thank you, master."
As soon as she finished speaking, her body dissolved into a pink mist, and in a blink, she had teleported several meters and was clinging to Su Lun, "Master, shall I help you get dressed?"
Although it was phrased as a question, she had already begun carefully arranging his clothes.
Su Lun did not mind it at all.
Sabina was very smart; like a qualified maid, she always thoughtfully considered everything, making her company extremely comfortable.
...
Before long, Su Lun left the room and walked onto the deck of the Eternal Night.
The atmosphere of cultivation on the ship was excellent; these days, everyone was either cultivating or intensely training.
The deck was filled with members sparring.
At dawn, the people greeted him as he stepped onto the deck, "Mr. Su Lun is here!"
The battle at the Imperial Strait had left an indelible impression on everyone, especially the new members, who regarded him almost like a god.
Abel, upon seeing his teacher approaching, stopped manipulating the Thousand Machineries and greeted him respectfully, "Teacher."
Su Lun nodded, "Hmm."
Just then, a figure dashed by, and Lulota jumped down from the mast, landing lightly on the deck. She blinked and asked, "Mr. Su Lun, did you rest well?"
Though not many knew that Sabina had come aboard, Lulota, who often visited the captain's chamber, was aware.
Su Lun could not help but notice the playfulness in the girl's tone.
He was used to it, though.
He flicked her forehead and asked, "Where's your teacher?"
That flick made Lulota feel a buzzing in her head, and she yelped, holding her forehead.
She puffed her cheeks and complained pitifully, "Ah... even though I've already mastered dominance, and bullets can't penetrate it. Why does it still hurt so much when Mr. Su Lun flicks me?"
Su Lun smiled, "You've only just started understanding dominance. Once you stabilize in the Sword Saint Realm, you'll know why."
It had been years since their first meeting in Blizzard City, where she was just a little girl holding a sword; now, she had grown up.
"Oh."
Lulota pouted, looking resigned.
Even though she was already very strong, in Mr. Su Lun's eyes, she was always just a beginner.
She replied, "Teacher has gone to the island."
"Hmm."
Su Lun smiled.
With another look, he had already vanished from the deck.
...
A nameless island, here lay a black stele left by Sir Isaac.
The stele held some ultimate secrets of alchemic origins from the "Emerald Record".
However, peering into this secret required a high threshold, usually at least a tier-nine profession level of cognition to be qualified to glimpse into its mysteries.
When Su Lun arrived, there were several people sitting in front of the stele, engaged in meditation.
Mr. Jing, Senjo, Pandora, Pestroya, along with Mr. Hei, who had recently advanced to the ninth tier, and Old Sword God Bartolo.
As they saw Su Lun approaching, they all opened their eyes from their focused state of meditation.
Senjo, as always unabashed, directly joked, "Yo~ Su Lun, how's that succubus maid of yours reporting her work?"
The monotony of day-to-day cultivation rarely brought any amusement, so everyone chuckled knowingly.
Being familiar with everyone present, Su Lun felt no embarrassment and simply raised his eyebrow, "Pretty well."
Mr. Hei, rarely speaking, also smiled and said, "Miss Sabina's advancement to the eighth tier so quickly is indeed astonishing to this old man as well."
Half teasing, half genuinely amazed.
Sabina's advancement rate, throughout the entire alchemy dimension apart from pioneers like Su Lun and Senjo, was indeed unique, a speed that even this old man envied.
"..."
Su Lun could only smile wryly, knowing that others might be unaware of the hidden talent abilities of a dual-succubus, but Mr. Hei, the scholar, certainly knew.
Mr. Jing's eyes also rippled gently with laughter but did not dwell further on the topic, changing the subject to ask, "Su Lun, when do you plan to advance to the ninth tier?"
"Quite soon," Su Lun replied, sitting cross-legged beside him on the spot, responding, "I have already felt the barriers of understanding, and without advancing to the ninth tier, many things cannot be truly mastered."
"Oh?"
Hearing this, a flash of sharp light appeared in their eyes, all eager to see just how powerful the ninth tier would make Su Lun.
After a brief chat, they all fell silent again, continuing to observe the stele and began their meditation, quickly immersing themselves in their cultivation.
Su Lun, too, took out his alchemy notes, focusing his gaze on the swirling vortex of knowledge in the stele.
Truly, at their level, there were few things in the world that could shake their spirits.
If there were others here, they would see a few people sitting beside the stele, appearing as though they were always meant to be there, seamlessly integrated with their surroundings.
...
Over these days, Su Lun had gradually grown accustomed to the exaggerated augmentation of abilities brought by the "God Profaner" parasite gear, and marveled more at the magic of the gear.
With the enhancement of the parasite gear, he now possessed a cognition far beyond the limits of humankind, nearing that of a deity.
This was akin to an elevation of life's tier.
Looking back at the original world, it seemed like gazing afar from a high summit, everything was different.
It was like an extremely complex top-tier magic cube in human thought, which now, in Su Lun's eyes, just a casual glance was enough to instantly know the solution.
Su Lun estimated that the enhancement in mental capacity was currently about... ten thousand times, perhaps.
Knowledge that would take ten thousand years to assimilate, he could see through in just one year.
Moreover, this parasite gear would continue to grow with cognition.
This was the most powerful.
The previously incomprehensible cosmic secrets on the stele gradually became clear to him.
Although he could still only understand the parts he was able to.
But even just that part made him feel he had glimpsed the extreme of power that humanity could touch.
It seemed that given enough time, he could uncover all the secrets of the universe and deduce a complete new cosmos.
This cognitive ability also had a high compatibility with the advancement material Su Lun planned to integrate as he advanced to the ninth rank.
Su Lun had always wanted to integrate the tome "Lethal Novel·Netherworld."
This was a supremely cursed item that still exceeded his current understanding.
Because the book contained a complete, unimaginably detailed Netherworld, with timelines, monsters, the deceased... everything.
Originally, Fujiwara Hayato, that great literary genius and adventurer, had compiled all the treasures he collected in his lifetime into this book, creating a Netherworld within the pages.
Among those treasures were the "Void Whale's Stomach" from Su Lun's miniature void realm and the Buddhist treasure "Bodhi Seed" that allowed the Senjo Rakshasa Woman to reach her third transformation.
That great literary genius must have had enormous fortune to enter the Netherworld and not die.
Heaven knows how many treasures he hid in the book.
Su Lun originally could have taken out the other treasures.
But he did not do so.
Instead, over the years, he continuously added more items to it.
Because he understood a part of it, the rules of the world within the book became more complete with the "feeding" of some law-bound treasures.
In recent years, Su Lun had cultivated it almost to the limit of its plane.
Currently, a very high level of world cognition is needed to integrate this novel as an advancement material.
After the integration of advancement materials, one can comprehend "World."
Previously, Su Lun did not understand what that was, but now he realized that Fujiwara Hayato had depicted some of the cosmic rules' fundamental mysteries with his writing.
This was something he confirmed after deciphering the "Emerald Record" using the stele.
Su Lun was also amazed that predecessors in the alchemical field indeed possessed extraordinary talents; those were realms only gods could touch, and it was unknown how that great literary genius came to understand them. Yet he did understand and even recorded them.
In some ways, the significance of this novel was even comparable to the alchemical manuscripts left by Sir Isaac.
...
Several days later, in the secret chamber of the Eternal Night.
In front of Su Lun was placed a dark amber crystal and a novel emitting black mists.
Advancing to the ninth rank required universal essence to help the practitioner gain a shortcut to touching the mysteries of the laws, and Su Lun had prepared this "Fourth Universal Essence·Death" well ahead.
Having prepared the materials, he began chanting the alchemical spell, "By the law of equivalent exchange of all things, praise be to the glory of the original creator, witness the miracle of creation through alchemy..."
Suddenly, the light in the Nonagram Alchemy Formation intensified.
The universal essence gradually melted within the alchemy formation, slowly merging into Su Lun's body.
On the other side, the "Netherworld" tome also began to turn its pages one by one, and Su Lun's eyes seemed to open a miraculous world within the book, instantly enveloped by the galaxy, endlessly deep in his view.
In a fleeting moment, he felt as if he were a god, having created a world and also controlling everything.
As he had hoped, the entire advancement process encountered almost no unexpected situations and was exceedingly smooth.
On this day, Su Lun successfully entered the ninth realm.

chapters.title: Chapter 652 - 561: God Slayer, Pact, Outrageous Proposal
chapters.content:
In the captain's secret chamber of the Eternal Night, Su Lun sat cross-legged in the Alchemy Formation and suddenly opened his eyes, muttering something to himself, "The evolution of the world..."
Two days ago, he had successfully integrated materials to advance to the ninth stage and obtained the power of the "World".
However, it was this newly acquired ability that seemed to open a new cognitive domain for him, plunging him into new doubts.
Originally, he chose to integrate this material to gain the cognitive ability to peek into the foundational rules of the world.
And indeed, he acquired this ability.
But after advancing, Su Lun's vision reached a previously unimaginable height, and he pondered deeper questions, such as: How is the world formed?
The great writer Fujiwara Hayato described a world within a book in his novel, which, when viewed from the perspective of our reality, should be a fictitious, low-dimensional world.
But Su Lun had been there before, and it was a real world.
At that time, Fujiwara Hayato's level should have been the eighth stage, yet the rules touched upon in the "Netherworld" novel, even a demigod might not have been capable of.
Therefore, there was a secret divine technique involved.
Originally, the "Netherworld" novel wasn't as powerful as when Su Lun obtained it, and that imaginative writer had grafted the novel onto the divine belief system of Mountain Hermit, then absorbed countless souls over several decades into the novel's world, to perfect that world within the book.
And then came later.
In his own words: "Actually, no matter how knowledgeable a person is, or how many laws they comprehend, they cannot construct a completely flawless world. Even the ancient deities that I know of can't do it. Therefore, I turned the novel I wrote into a cursed object, to collect some souls. Those souls will live, cultivate, and reproduce in the Netherworld... Their experiences all serve to perfect and infer the world within the book. And with the passage of time, it will become more and more perfected..."
Su Lun had once communicated with the remnant will that Fujiwara Hayato left in the book and received these words.
At that time, his realm was too low, and he completely failed to understand these concepts on this level.
Now that he had touched the human pinnacle, Su Lun suddenly became enlightened.
Even... Those words might directly point to the essence of "Faith".
Divinities need a divine kingdom to gather the power of faith, isn't this also using believers to perfect and complete their own divine world view?
However, the cognition involved was too complex, and even Su Lun with his current intellectual capacity couldn't clarify it in a short time.
For a moment, his thoughts drifted.
Yet another idea emerged in Su Lun's mind: "Could my little void realm also evolve into a complete world in the same way as the novel's world?"
After trying, he found that the answer was: possibly.
...
After Su Lun's advancement to the ninth stage, the little void realm also underwent noticeable changes.
The little void realm was originally "the Void Stomach of a Skyroaming Whale", a divine artifact of space that could grow into a complete plane as the host's understanding of Space Law increased and space gemstones were fused into it.
Originally, the little void realm was just a slightly larger space, which over the years had absorbed some cursed spaces and space fragments, and had become the size of a city.
But in reality, it was still just a space and not a complete plane.
Everything inside relied on external inputs, like the air and water circulation systems, which were also supported by various mechanical devices and Alchemy Formations.
However, after Su Lun advanced to the ninth level, he found that space could easily be altered according to his own thoughts.
Not only did the space expand several times over, but if he envisioned a mountain, the earthen elements within the space would converge and solidify into a mountain; if he wanted a river, the water elements would gather to form rivers...
Su Lun was dissatisfied with the excessive consumption of elements in the miniature void realm and their slow convergence. Then he took the fragment of the necromantic plane he had obtained from the Necromancer he killed in the Dragon Country Waters and linked it with a rules conflict, creating a light-darkness rules convection in the miniature void realm.
With this experiment, the miniature void realm miraculously formed an interdependent elemental cycle that didn't require any external intervention!
Although it couldn't achieve a 100% internal cycle, the consumption had been reduced by 99% compared to before.
Then Su Lun created the sun, the earth, forests...and even the four seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter.
Theoretically, the miniature void realm is a sealed space; the energy elements inside won't leak out—they only change form, rather than disappearing.
Therefore, even with complex energy conversions like the seasons, the consumption is not great. Instead, the fluctuation of energy makes the elements of the miniature void realm more active.
After this series of modifications, the tens of thousands of people in the war workshop and research facilities inside could continue to develop for hundreds of years without any external intervention.
Su Lun, like a creator, took great interest in continuing to modify the miniature void realm.
However, in terms of scale, what he has created is not a world, but at most resembled a sandbox game.
He knew his understanding still lacked some key aspects, but he was not in a hurry.
From what he could see, his approach was most likely correct.
The concept described in Fujiwara Hayato's "Netherworld" about using a vast amount of human thought to deduce the laws of the universe also seemed feasible!
And as the "miniature world" of the miniature void realm was perfected, Su Lun was also amazed to find that his own understanding of certain rules had gradually deepened.
Su Lun faintly felt that this sandbox game seemed to point towards some profound and mysterious rules in the universe.
...
So, several days flashed by.
Su Lun was constantly immersed in the sandbox game of the miniature world.
At this moment, the miniature void realm had undergone a drastic transformation, with mountain ranges and forests, lakes, sunlight, birdsong, and meadows of blooming flowers.
At the foot of the mountains, there was a beautiful Gothic spire castle, an industrialized city, and a huge library...
And tens of thousands of residents.
In just a few days, the miniature void realm had turned into a small kingdom.
The Dr. Banks and others in the miniature void realm also noticed this amazing change. Delighted by the transformation, they offered advice and suggestions to Su Lun on what kind of structures were still needed.
Just in terms of the environment, it was a utopia created entirely according to the ideal model, no longer the simplicity of the past, and utterly refreshing to the spirit.
Su Lun was also very satisfied.
"Myriad Hearts and Uses" also allowed him to multitask, handling many affairs: in the miniature void realm, he read thousands of books in the library while transforming the realm and simultaneously carved advanced puppets with a chisel...
His one day of work and study efficiency was probably equivalent to many years for an ordinary person.
Su Lun had never felt so well before.
Miraculous alchemy had endowed him with divine-like abilities.
...
The modifications within the minor void did not affect Su Lun's ability to do other things.
In the secret chamber, he took out five copies of Isaac's Alchemy Manuscript and neatly arranged them on the ground.
Sir Aikesa noted in his records that only a ninth-tier magician was qualified to open the last sealed device in the notes—Isaac's God Slayer.
He had wanted to open it before but couldn't.
This was because Sir Isaac had used an extremely complicated encryption method to seal away this device.
It would normally take hundreds of years to decrypt.
Now, Su Lun, having merged with the God Profaner, merely glanced over it a few times and had already understood the decryption method.
He uttered softly, "Unseal!"
The alchemy formation beneath his feet lit up, and the five manuscripts began to float.
Upon closer inspection, the flesh-like cover designs of the five manuscripts came together like a key to open a vault, and a small black hole appeared in the void.
Su Lun realized with a start, "No wonder such a complex method was used to seal it; the previously shattered alchemical plane couldn't bear the weight of this device at all..."
Because it was a sub- Divine Artifact.
Even with a layer of restrictive divine power separating it, one could still feel the pinprick-like curse characteristics.
Just as an ordinary storage ring couldn't hold sealed items, the previously shattered alchemical plane couldn't carry an artifact with complete laws either.
Had the artifact been taken out before the plane was invaded, it likely would have pierced through the plane and fallen into the chaos of spatial currents.
But now it was no problem at all.
Su Lun's own strength was more than enough to keep it under control.
Before him lay a very special device, a translucent garment inset with a glowing black gemstone.
The gemstone seemed to embrace all the colors of the world; despite being as black as ink, its splendor was captivating. A practitioner below the ninth tier might fall into this array of colors just by looking at it.
Gazing at the gemstone, a sparkle in his eyes, Su Lun felt a shock in his heart, "So this is a divine aura..."
A thousand years ago, Sir Isaac captured a lower-ranked Fallen Angel whose divine flame Pesutoya fused, and the divine aura was turned into this device.
Isaac's God Slayer
Quality: Sub-Divine Artifact
Details: This device contains a force which you temporarily cannot comprehend, recognized as "dark rule"; taking control of this energy allows ignoring any form of defense known in your current world and inflicting "annihilation" – a true damage on the target; you see a realm of the unknown; fusion requirements: physical evaluation SSS+, spiritual power evaluation SSS+, requires Divine Power ***; divines auras can be added to increase the quality of the device;
Evaluation: This device is very dangerous and unstable; fusing it will result in a 100% fatality rate due to body explosion; you need corresponding divine power to suppress the cursed characteristics of the device to balance the power of the dark rules.
...
The moment he saw the device, Su Lun couldn't help but smile bitterly, "No wonder Sir Isaac stated in the notes that this device is difficult to merge with..."
No!
It can't even be described as difficult.
This wasn't even created for the human body, was it?
Su Lun's own physical fitness might not be the strongest in the plane, but he had at least seen beings stronger than him.
However, the conditions of a physical evaluation SSS+ and spiritual power evaluation SSS+ are nearly impossible for others to achieve. But for him, with some effort, there might be some hope to reach them after stabilizing at the ninth tier in the future.
But that "Divine Power ***" requirement was completely beyond his comprehension.
The existence that he couldn't understand at present can only belong to the divine tier beyond his recognition.
This was a requirement for which he had absolutely no idea how to improve.
Looking at it, Su Lun also felt a sense of helplessness.
The device was indeed excellent, providing the ability to inflict true damage on everything post-fusion.
No wonder Sir Isaac claimed it could slay gods.
But if Su Lun couldn't understand it, then it was likely incomprehensible to anyone below the level of gods.
Without some significant opportunity, he felt that it would probably just gather dust in storage and end up as a family heirloom...
Having satisfied his curiosity, Su Lun took only a moment to put away the device.
Collecting his thoughts, he once again fell into a state of meditation.
Advancing to the ninth tier was different for Su Lun compared to others.
Other practitioners needed to rely on "Cosmic Origin Substance" to comprehend ninth-tier cosmic laws and secrets. That process was like blazing a trail; everything was unknown and a new experience. It was an incredibly lengthy process, possibly taking many years to stabilize at that level.
But Su Lun already had a distinct understanding of the ninth tier while at the eighth tier.
Now, advancing to the ninth tier was almost free of unfamiliarity for him.
The stabilization he needed was just to assimilate the ninth-tier insights he had previously separated, along with the insights from the two demigods, making them his own.
Consequently, the time he needed for this process was much shorter than others.
With the celestial beings of the Heavenly Plane remaining inactive, time seemed very peaceful, with no unforeseen incidents.
Before long, having secluded himself in the secret chamber for half a month, Su Lun had already stabilized his realm; he began to probe the path he ought to take.
However, on this day.
What was expected to come, still came.
...
Su Lun, engrossed in his meditation, suddenly felt a call arising from within, and he abruptly opened his eyes.
His eyes shone with a bright light, and suddenly a wisp of black air rose before him, then formed into a black contract.
He recognized it too; it was the document of the contract he had signed with the demon god when he resurrected Qian Tiao and the Princess.
He had always had a premonition, and now looking at this contract, Su Lun's expression held no surprise; he merely thought, "So it has come..."
This calmness came not only from his premonition but more importantly, from his strength.
Before advancing to the ninth rank, Su Lun could only estimate what situation he would be in afterwards.
At that time, he had felt that fulfilling the contract might encounter some unpredictable factors.
But now.
He felt that, below the rank of a god, he could clash with anyone.
Therefore, when the contract came, he did not feel even the slightest ripple of emotion.
"So it's time to go to the 'Cursed Ship'..."
Su Lun glanced at the content of the contract, which was a set of coordinates.
He did not dwell on it, instead, he stood up.
The scenery around him changed instantly, and he had already appeared on the Nameless Deserted Island.
Mr. Jing, Qian Tiao, Pandora, Pestoya, Mr. Hei, and the Old Sword God Bartolo were still on the island, comprehending the black stele.
Seeing Su Lun approach, everyone opened their eyes almost in unison, and anticipation was evident in them all.
Everyone knew that Su Lun had been in seclusion to advance to the ninth rank these past days, and seeing him emerge now, they were certain he had succeeded.
They had intended to congratulate him on his successful advancement, but upon seeing his serious expression, they immediately guessed something and fell silent.
Mr. Jing's eyebrows furrowed slightly as he asked, "Are you leaving?"
Su Lun nodded indifferently and confirmed, "Yes. The contract is calling me."
As these words were spoken, everyone fell into silence.
Qian Tiao glanced at him, wanting to say something, but then held back.
Mr. Hei and Bartolo's old faces were solemn.
Pestoya pouted, with a look of unhappiness on her face.
Su Lun was naturally here to say farewell. He looked at everyone's serious expressions, smiled, and spoke in a relaxed tone, "It's not that bad. I've already solidified my ninth rank, and now my self-preservation skills are not weak."
As he spoke, he raised his hand and pointed his fingertip, which began to wind around with threads of black light.
Ordinary people wouldn't understand what this was, but those present, being of the ninth rank like Mr. Jing, knew this was the "Threads of Law."
Being able to so easily condense the Threads of Law was something none of them could do.
This also meant that Su Lun's power was now tremendously formidable!
Seeing this, the previously worried expressions of everyone relaxed.
They suddenly felt much reassured.
With this strength, it was hard for them not to realize that there were very few, if any, enemies he couldn't handle below the rank of a god.
Qian Tiao, always direct, asked in astonishment, "Have you reached the 'Demigod Territory'?"
This situation was only ever seen before when battling with demigods from two angelic planes.
"No. This is considered..."
Su Lun paused, finding it difficult to explain.
His current situation was very special; he was different from other ninth rankers. He had harvested two demigods, so he possessed some abilities only demigods had.
Yet he had just advanced to the ninth rank and hadn't fully mastered many things.
In terms of realm, he was a beginner at the ninth rank.
But in terms of combat power, he was confident he was no less than the two demigods he encountered before.
Moreover, he was a Puppeteer.
Su Lun smiled and joked with a bit of a grin, "Anyway, I think I'm pretty strong now."
Hearing this, everyone's faces showed a hint of relief and a smile.
Indeed, very strong!
If he were an enemy, they could hardly imagine how he could be defeated.
But they also realized that Su Lun had come to say goodbye.
A contract bound with the Path Demon Lord was never simple.
The specter lady floating in the air was not pleased and muttered, "Su Lun, I want to go with you."
Although Pestoya often bickered and was somewhat willful with Su Lun on ordinary days, in her heart, Su Lun was her most important friend. She had always been like Su Lun's little shadow, inseparable from him, and she did not want to part with Su Lun.
As soon as she said this, Qian Tiao on the side also wanted to speak.
But Su Lun shook his head, cutting off what they were about to continue saying, "The Alchemy world needs you more right now. Besides, it's more convenient for me to come and go alone."
He knew if he were to bring anyone with him, even if it were to face death, Mr. Jing, Qian Tiao, and everyone else present, or the entire Dawn Group, would join him without hesitation.
But Su Lun did not have such intentions.
He could not be so selfish; he did not want to drag his best companions into danger with him.
Moreover, if his own strength was not enough to resolve the crises, bringing more people would likely lead to the same outcome.
Everyone understood this too; Su Lun alone was indeed the strongest.
Saying more would only seem pretentious.
The atmosphere was silent for a moment.
However, at this time, Pandora, who had been silent at one side, spoke up, "I'll accompany you. My abilities might be of use to you. I'll leave the divine artifact on the ship, so even if..."
She didn't finish her sentence, but the rest meant that even if something unexpected happened, her consciousness wouldn't completely vanish.
Su Lun looked at her flawless face, and smiled slightly.
Although the process of getting to know this moon reader wasn't particularly pleasant.
She truly valued loyalty.
She always charged ahead in fights, and whenever Su Lun had a request, she never refused.
Now, knowing full well the journey was likely a matter of life and death, she didn't hesitate.
Moreover, her ability of Faith Stealing was indeed very useful.
Their tacit understanding required no fuss, and Su Lun nodded, "Mhmm."
...
Originally, Su Lun wanted to leave the alchemical divine artifact, the Philosopher's Stone, behind in case something happened to him, to prevent the hard-won alchemical artifact from being lost again.
But Mr. Jing refused this suggestion, responding simply with, "You are more important than any divine artifact."
Those words said it all.
Su Lun did not insist any further.
To any magician, the Philosopher's Stone was indeed a treasure.
The artifact could enhance his strength by at least thirty percent.
Su Lun held a special place within the Dawn Brigade and was currently a top-tier fighter in the Alchemy realm. He didn't want his departure to be widely known, affecting morale.
So, he only said his goodbyes to Mr. Jing and a few others.
Before long, Su Lun returned to the captain's quarters to pack some things and leave others behind before setting off.
Senjo seemed a bit listless and followed him back.
Just like when she wanted to go to the Netherworld, she knew Su Lun surely understood her.
Now that Su Lun was leaving, Senjo understood as well.
"Hey, you be careful, all right?"
"Mhmm."
"If you can't win, find somewhere to hide and train. When I become a Demigod one day, I'll come to save you."
"Okay!"
"..."
Su Lun packed his things in the room while chatting idly with her.
They started with topics urging carefulness, but then Senjo suddenly asked a leisurely question, "Hey, Su Lun, since you are leaving, do you have any regrets?"
This straightforward, gambling-addicted housewife never beat around the bush, and Su Lun found it both amusing and baffling to hear her query as if he was to give his last words.
But on second thought, what was there to regret?
Even if fulfilling the contract led to an accident, arriving in this mysterious world of Alchemy had been so wonderful that he deemed his life fulfilled.
Su Lun didn't really think about it and joked offhandedly, "Would not having slept with you, Sister Senjo, be considered one?"
This would have been a normal tease between them on any other day.
Senjo's typical response would be to retort with a wisecrack or just roll her eyes at him.
But at this moment, she seemed to seriously contemplate the question for a moment before replying, "Do you really want to?"
"..."
Su Lun chuckled, obviously not taking it seriously.
Yet Senjo seemed to vividly imagine a few scenarios, pondering for a moment before smacking her lips and saying, "Ah... nevermind then. I still find it bizarre."
Seeing her expression, Su Lun couldn't help but laugh, thinking to himself: Did she really consider it?
At their level of existence, desires were completely controlled by rationality, with a greater focus on the state of mind.
He felt that their current way of interacting was just fine.
Su Lun was about to tease her further when, unexpectedly, Senjo came up with a shocking suggestion, "Or, if you really want to, go ask Philo? She definitely won't refuse."
"..."
Hearing this, Su Lun rolled his eyes.
The slightly sad atmosphere of farewell suddenly took a weird turn due to this preposterous suggestion.
How did this end up involving his senior sister?
"Heh..."
Senjo, seeing a hint of discomfort in Su Lun's expression, draped her arm companionably over his shoulder.
She seemed to think her suggestion was excellent and said excitedly, "You've changed your succubus maid so many times, and Philo never got angry. She surely won't mind such a small parting request."
"..."
Su Lun's eyelid twitched at that; she knew about this?
Senjo, oblivious to his thoughts, bluntly mentioned, "I heard it from Pestoia. She also said you guys have quite the assortment of moves, hahaha... Don't worry, Philo was there when she talked about it, and she didn't say anything, so she surely doesn't mind."
"..."
Hearing this, Su Lun felt an involuntary twitch at the corner of his eye.
He suddenly thought, better the world be destroyed, if only to preserve my innocence on this earth.

chapters.title: Chapter 653 - 652: Centaur, Berserker, Dou Saint, Dragon Maiden, and an Old Six
chapters.content:
Su Lun and Mr. Jing bid farewell to the others and left the Eternal Night quietly without disturbing the other members of the Dawn group.
He left the God Burial Ground and headed south towards the open sea.
By nightfall, he had already reached near the Cobros Strait, eight hundred miles south of Blizzard City.
The moon was faint tonight, and a thick fog enshrouded the sea surface.
Su Lun walked on the sea as if strolling in his own courtyard.
A legend known to nearly every sailor in the Alchemy plane persisted: on foggy nights, lucky individuals might encounter a ghost ship adrift on the sea. Aboard were treasures, fine wine, and beautiful women for the taking and revelry. However, one must disembark before midnight, or they would never leave again, becoming a phantom of the ship once it disappeared.
Su Lun had heard numerous variations of the "Cursed Ship" tale within the island communities, mostly related to beauty and fortune.
But regardless of the version, they were all shrouded in mystery.
Now at Su Lun's level, there were few events on the Alchemy plane that could truly be considered mysterious.
He was also curious about the true nature of this cursed ship, a legend that had persisted for at least tens of thousands of years.
Now knowing it was related to a contract with a demon, it certainly wasn't as simple as just a ghost ship.
Soon, darkness enveloped the area, and the night breeze chilled his neck slightly.
For Su Lun, however, the darkness made him feel more at ease.
His state of mind was as steady as his steps.
As he walked, suddenly, the crow perched on his shoulder cawed loudly.
Su Lun looked toward the southeast and mused, "Oh? Even you can't discern that entity, Mr. Crow?"
He stopped and waited quietly.
Small waves rippled underfoot, and the shadowy outline of a large ship started to emerge from the thick fog in the distance.
Su Lun's eyes flashed with wisdom as he activated the second level of the All-knowing Eye, carefully observing his surroundings.
It wasn't long before an opulently lit three-masted sailing ship came into view.
He saw no ghosts, nor did he sense any fluctuations of souls.
The reflection of the ship in Su Lun's eyes was accompanied by a slight curl of his lips, a realization dawning on him: Oh, this isn't even a ship at all.
He had seen through it, this so-called "Cursed Ship" appeared to be a ship to the naked eye, but in actuality, it was merely a mass of energy covered by a spiritual illusion technique.
It was recognized as a ship because it had assumed a form that humans on the Alchemy plane could comprehend.
As for the beauties and treasures, those too were mere illusions.
Those below the ninth tier likely couldn't see through the true nature of this ship.
Even if they did encounter it, they would surely regard it as a serendipitous ghost ship adventure.
The rumored fine wines, romantic encounters, and treasures... were all hallucinations created by those who boarded.
Having seen through its nature, Su Lun immediately felt it was uninteresting.
But his expression remained completely unchanged.
This kind of tedium was an inevitable part of glimpsing the truth.
Mr. Hei once told him that knowledge was heavy, and as you gradually understand the world, you will gradually lose your sense of fun and become indifferent to everything around you.
The feeling was real now that Su Lun had ascended to the ninth tier and touched the ceiling of the Alchemy plane.
That god or demon probably concocted this spectacle just to make the legend of the "Cursed Ship" widely known, luring more people to seek this legendary ghost ship.
As the ghost ship slowly sailed across the surface, Su Lun didn't hesitate and leaped aboard.
With his current spiritual power, unless he willed it, it was impossible for the illusion technique to confound him.
There was no one on the ship, just a piece of paper with a contract on it, so he sat down quietly and began to meditate cross-legged.
Now that the cursed paper ship held no more secrets, Su Lun was curious about where it would go.
...
After taking Su Lun aboard as its only passenger, the speed of the Cursed Ship suddenly increased.
The colors of the night streaked by faster and faster, but Su Lun's expression remained utterly unchanged.
However, suddenly, he felt the whole ship lurch downward, and then it plunged headfirst into the water.
The surge of divine power in that instant caused Su Lun to snap open his eyes, uttering a soft exclamation of surprise.
He glanced around, only to see the entire ship had sunk into the sea.
But strangely, the seawater didn't flood in; instead, it acted like a filter, suggesting that the ship was no longer in the same space.
"High-order Void Displacement?"
Thoughts stirred in Su Lun's mind. This was an advanced technique of Spatial Displacement he had yet to master.
While observing subtly, he casually threw out several Crystal Stones marked with Spatial Coordinates.
Before long, the cursed ship plunged into a rift in the earth's crust. Instantly, the view transformed into various twisted, abstract lines and fragments of space that resembled shards of broken glass.
These were "planar rifts," something Su Lun had witnessed once in the waters of Dragon Country.
The Alchemy plane was a fragmented plane with countless fissures resembling tree roots, leading to unknown destinations deep within.
It was a dangerous region that Su Lun did not dare to explore now.
One wrong step would suck him into the spatial maelstrom, almost certainly sealing his fate.
At this moment, the cursed ship was carrying him through these fissures, diving deeper and deeper.
Su Lun felt as if he had entered a kaleidoscope, his vision a complete chaos.
Being proficient in the laws of space himself, he knew well that a single fissure could span tens of thousands of miles.
In just this brief period, the cursed ship had transported him to an extremely distant place, so far that even the communicators of the Dawn organization couldn't detect his presence.
If it were a normal human being, they would have likely suffered "seasickness" by now, becoming dizzy and losing their sense of direction.
Luckily, having merged with the God Profaner, Su Lun's cognitive abilities had become incredibly strong. He recorded the route while leaving spatial markers at key points within the complex network of spatial rifts.
And so, Su Lun was carried by the ship, traveling through the rifts for three whole days.
Throughout this period, he felt himself leave the subterranean realm full of space fragments in the Alchemy plane, cross a river-like temporal flux, and then dart into another dense cluster of spatial rifts...
Su Lun knew he had definitely left the Alchemy plane.
He had even crossed many different planes.
He had never imagined that he would make an inter-planar journey in this manner.
Previously, Su Lun thought that traveling to other planes was only possible through planar portals. But now, passing through spatial rifts felt like "smuggling" himself.
He also guessed that the situation of that demon god was clearly not very good.
However, the situation changed on the fourth day.
Su Lun remained alert, recording the route.
He suddenly noticed that the space around him had become stable, indicating that the cursed ship must have arrived at a stable plane.
Su Lun became extremely cautious, with a Rune Umbrella in his left hand, a black scythe in his right, and Mr. Crow on his shoulder fully focused and on guard.
Soon, before seeing anyone, his sensory range suddenly detected four soul fluctuations that seemed human.
"Humans?"
Su Lun breathed a sigh of relief.
At least they were humans, and not some bizarre entities.
As the surroundings changed, Su Lun found himself in a confined small space akin to a cellar.
Upon his arrival, four pairs of eyes turned to him.
To be precise, they were not all human.
...
Four beings appeared before Su Lun's eyes.
A barbarian over three meters tall, a young man with a pale face and a long robe, a woman clad in beast skins with dragon scales, and the last one was the strangest—his upper body was human, but his lower half was that of a horse.
"Centaur?"
Su Lun did not fail to recognize this creature from the myths.
From the attire and aura of these four, he knew they were from different civilizations, different races, and different planes.
Perhaps, in their eyes, he himself, an alchemical magician, was just as strange?
Su Lun observed the four without betraying any emotion, while they too were examining him in the silence of the space.
It seemed they had arrived before him, the four pairs of eyes examining him, each in their own way. Su Lun felt very clearly that someone was probing with their aura, divining with secret techniques, and even using bloodline sensing...
The atmosphere was unfamiliar, and there was caution between them.
"What kind of odd bunch is this?"
Su Lun mumbled to himself.
The soul fluctuations of the few people in front of him were impossibly strong, each at least at the pinnacle of power equivalent to that of the Old Sword God Bartolo.
In other words, judging solely from their spiritual power, these fellows probably all possessed the combat strength of ninth-order pinnacles!
And that barbarian, he might even be a Demigod.
Looking at the situation, it seemed it was not just himself who had come for the meeting.
These individuals as well.
Just as Su Lun was observing them, a touch of puzzlement flitted across the eyes of the young man in white, and he silently thought, "Eh... Strange, he's clearly a novice at the ninth-order, yet he's the last to arrive? That's not right. According to the order of arrivals before, the higher the rank, the later the Curse Ship should bring... Does this fellow have something special about him?"
....
Su Lun, the newcomer, did not speak, which made the atmosphere inside the cellar somewhat tense.
Although he guessed that these individuals were not enemies, he maintained an instinctual guard.
This subtle vigilance, while not directed at anyone in particular, did not go unnoticed by the four top experts present.
The towering barbarian, standing over three meters tall and built like an iron tower, noticed something, and with a frown voiced in a deep tone, "Sir, you carry a heavy killing aura."
Killing aura? Strong?
For this murderer of many to say someone has a heavy killing aura, could that not indicate a heartless monster and a horrific killer?
With those words, the expressions of the other two became somewhat strange as they glanced at Su Lun.
Truly, at their level of existence, they knew all too well that the more inscrutable someone is... the stranger their origins!
They chattered away in what seemed to be the native tongue of a plane, but with Su Lun's "Language Proficiency", understanding was no obstacle.
He glanced at the barbarian, whose faint scent of blood seemed to be some sort of secret technique that could sense people's killing intent.
As soon as Su Lun had entered, the fellow had been probing.
Su Lun did not explain when the other mentioned his heavy killing aura. Indeed, he had killed not a few on his way here, not to mention the millions by his puppet army.
No wonder the few in front of him viewed him with a look reserved for monsters.
Su Lun had no intention of explaining to a few strangers.
However, the young man with the pale face smiled and struck up a conversation in a familiar manner, asking, "Are you also here to fulfill the divine demon covenant?"
The language he used was one that Su Lun had not heard before.
But this person clearly used a similar "Language Proficiency" secret technique.
Listening, Su Lun nodded his head and asked with a calm expression, "The same for you?"
The young man with the pale face chuckled and replied, "Yes, indeed. Then we might not be enemies after all. Sir, you need not be so on guard."
It seemed he had no desire to provoke a "suspected psychopathic killer."
He took the initiative and introduced himself, "My name is Jay, from the Dou Qi continent. A ninth-order Fighting Saint."
Then he pointed to the others, introducing, "This is Mr. Kamur Tu, a Demigod archer of the centaur race... This is Otter Ralph, a barbaric berserker from the Atira continent... and this is Miss Masia, a Dragonkin. We arrived a few days before you and have been here waiting to fulfill the divine demon covenant. We don't know if there will be others coming…"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun realized that they had indeed met each other before.
What Dou Qi continent, Atira continent, Dragonkin, centaur—some of these were civilizations he had heard of in mythological stories, while others were new to him.
Su Lun also felt that this world was truly vast.
And although their cultivation systems and ranks were different, the cultivation of all four individuals was indeed consistent with the concept of ninth-order Magicians, a ceiling of power inaccessible to lower-order beings.
Even from this simple introduction, Su Lun gleaned quite a bit of useful information.
Faced with their gazes, he also introduced himself indifferently, "Nicholas, a Death Magician, from a very small and remote plane."
It was better not to mention his real name.
Although he was now not very afraid of any Curse Magic, there was no guarantee that there would not be some method that used names in various strange ways.
In an unknown environment, safety comes first.
Besides, he did not mention that he was a Puppet Master or an Alchemist.
From his knowledge stripped from the memories of Mages from the divine plane, he had learned that Alchemists did not have a very good reputation across the planes.
Alchemists were called "God-Thieves" by many plane dwellers.
Because in the eyes of devout believers, transcendent abilities were gifts from the gods. Alchemists, however, used various Alchemy to steal the fundamental secrets of the universe, which was considered an act of blasphemy against the gods and theft of powers that only the gods should possess.
Another factor was that the ancestors during the Dawn Era were too powerful. They fought across countless planes and defeated too many civilizations, leaving behind these planar pathways as "evidence."
The ones in front of us could very well have been enemies, or even sworn adversaries, of the Alchemical plane at some point.
No!
I'm almost 99% certain they are foes!
Due to the peculiar nature of Alchemy, the alchemical civilization hardly has any real friendly planes. Any plane with a divine faith would not allow the spread of Alchemy; they are all in opposition.
The four of them appeared reserved upon hearing this, but showed no surprise.
After all, we're strangers to each other, and who doesn't have secrets?
At least, the information divulged just now was true.
A Death Magician?
Does that sound like some kind of undead Mage?
They glanced at the sickle wrapped in black cloth that Su Lun held; that weapon is a common symbol of the Grim Reaper across many civilizations.
No wonder...
That explains the exaggerated aura of slaughter.
At that moment, the beast-skin clad woman with patches of dragon scales, as if having realized something, asked, "Are you also of dragon heritage?"
"Hmm."
How could Su Lun not know that someone had just probed him with a bloodline secret technique? He replied ambiguously, "There is indeed a trace of dragon lineage in my blood."
He certainly wouldn't admit that it was due to an alchemist's gene Potion, and the prosthetic enhancement "Dragon Patterned Golden Body."
It's widely known that dragons are lustful beings; even in myths, many races carry a hint of dragon blood. It's not strange for humans to have Dragon Blood in them.
Upon hearing this, a dark glint flashed through Miss Masia's eyes, clearly disbelieving: "You're being too modest. I sense that your dragon lineage is very rich, no less pure than my own."
With that statement, the expressions of the other three turned slightly curious.
Aren't you a Death Magician? How did you become a highly pure-blooded dragonkin?
Normally, those with dragon heritage are incredibly strong physically and have no need for other professional systems.
Even though each of them had secrets, it was at that moment they uniformly realized that this "newcomer" was a bit too enigmatic.
...
The five people in the cellar merely exchanged some innocuous conversation.
But those capable of advancing to the ninth tier were no average individuals.
Their conversations were also probes of each other.
Su Lun was well aware that these fellows were sly.
That seemingly simple-minded, physically robust barbarian Ralph, who at first mention spoke of the "heavy murderous aura," was actually trying to divert the attention of the other three to the newcomer; and the Dragon Maiden Masia had the same aim—while she seemed to be inquiring, she was actually exposing Su Lun's dragon heritage to highlight his strength to the others.
This way, in the event of any unforeseen situation, the one who stands out would be the first target, the primary subject for special attention.
Ha!
They're all a bunch of sly old foxes.
Su Lun pretended not to notice, and spoke only of things that wouldn't reveal his identity.
While conversing, he was also observing; they seemed to be deep underground.
He was curious about what that godly being, who has deemed them—one of the top contenders from their respective planes—to be worthy Contractors, was in such a hurry to accomplish.
From the current situation, it appeared that the deity-like being had spent many tens of thousands of years summoning Contractors by various means.
Yet it's still ongoing to this day.
That means, whatever it is they are supposed to do, it hasn't been accomplished yet.
From this perspective... the contract matter seems complicated.
Su Lun was the last to arrive among the five.
He had thought there might be others yet to come, but it turned out he was the final one.
They did not have to wait long before the cellar suddenly turned chill.
An indescribable will descended.
All five tensed and turned their gaze toward the direction of the tunnel.
They recognized at first glance, this was the mysterious Contractor Master.

chapters.title: Chapter 654 - 654: 653
chapters.content:
In the cellar, Su Lun and four other powerhouses from different planes looked at the sudden descent of divine will, each wearing a solemn expression.
They had all once signed contracts with this demon god and traded destinies.
Facing the approach of their creditor, naturally, they all felt a bit uneasy.
But all five had touched the peak of human strength, and even before gods, they were not as lost as ordinary people.
Su Lun, an alchemist, believed only in truth and had no particular reverence. The others clung to their own divine faiths, holding only a reverence of power toward foreign gods.
In the presence of this unfathomable existence, they each used their own methods to probe.
The will had descended into the cellar, appearing like a mysterious figure cloaked in a mantle.
It wasn't the entity itself but a sliver of its will.
Others might not have noticed, but through Su Lun's All-knowing Eye, the ineffable will seemed to be attached to a rat.
His guess was indeed correct—the demon god was in dire straits, and the rat had come by burrowing in such a primitive manner.
However, it was just this one glance that caused Su Lun to immediately recoil his gaze, his hair standing on end.
Because in that instant,
he saw true "great terror,"
and his entire soul shuddered along with it!
Su Lun had witnessed the descent of divine will more than once and had even seen the actual divinity and divine fire of lesser gods. Although he knew the vast gulf between the ninth rank and the divine rank was indescribable, from a cosmic rule perspective, he was no stranger to the divine rank.
It was like a person at the foot of a mountain peering at a peak through the clouds—even shrouded in mist, one could still make out its form somewhat.
Yet, that look had revealed a completely incomprehensible "indescribable."
That glance was like beholding the vast ocean, while he was merely a speck of dust, an indescribable existence.
This was a height that one couldn't even see when looking up.
Even attached to a rat, it had the power to destroy worlds.
If it was beyond comprehension even with Su Lun's current understanding, then there was only one possibility: "A higher god!"
He was deeply terrified.
This was the most horrifying being he had encountered so far.
Su Lun immediately dismissed the naive thoughts he had before coming here.
He had thought that if it were a lesser god, he might entertain some other ideas. Now, those thoughts vanished in an instant.
...
The same held true for the other four in the cellar. After probing with their own means, each was likewise stunned on the spot.
Su Lun knew it was probably the intention of the demon god to intimidate them, but no matter how you looked at it, if this deity decided to kill everyone in the cellar, it would probably be done in the blink of an eye.
The tense atmosphere instead became utterly hollow, and they all found a kind of resignation to face death.
At that moment, the pale-faced youth bowed and said, "Great demon god, we have come as per the contract. May I ask what we need to do?"
He spoke quite straightforwardly.
After all, they were not the demon god's followers or servants; this was a trade.
The demon god glanced at them and didn't beat around the bush, saying directly, "I need you to do something for me."
The words carried an authority that seemed to strike right into one's soul, repeatedly compelling one to kneel and worship.
Upon hearing this, no one was surprised.
At their level, not even death could truly instill fear, and they all remained composed.
However, it was clear that everyone was curious about what task they were to undertake.
No one spoke, and an eerie silence fell upon the cellar.
Su Lun detached himself from any emotional fluctuations, listening quietly.
His face showed an expression that said, 'If you're not panicking, neither am I.'
He knew that someone else would be more anxious than him.
Because... for the others, it was a one-way ticket, and they couldn't return now.
But Su Lun had memorized the route to get here, and although spatial displacement across planes would most likely result in death for him, there was still a glimmer of hope.
The other four had no hope at all.
As expected, the silence didn't last long.
Finally, the centaur Makamul could no longer hold back and spoke, "Forgive my ignorance, but why do you, a mighty high god who could do anything with the flick of a finger, need to summon us, these insignificant lower beings?"
Perhaps the deities from the divine realm have grown accustomed to dealing with gods, so Makamul spoke with a very humble posture.
This kind of sincere awe could not be feigned.
However, Su Lun had no belief in gods, so his expression didn't show the slightest change.
Yet, to the others watching from the side, this scenario raised questions: Even when faced with such a terrifying entity, did this "newcomer" not display a trace of reverence on his face?
The demon god's tone revealed no fluctuation and he didn't intend to explain, stating directly, "Since you have all once used my power, it's good to complete the contract exchange. I will send you out in a moment. All you need to do is to never reveal my existence at any time, then kill Pharaoh Cleopatra, who guards the tomb, to obtain the 'Key to Immortality', and open the gates of the tomb..."
The tomb?
Upon these words, the gazes of the five people in the cellar were filled with different emotions.
Su Lun's mind also began to work at high speed.
This matter of the tomb and killing the Pharaoh, one would know just by listening that it was bound to be deadly; otherwise, it wouldn't have remained unaccomplished for tens of thousands of years.
The key point was, up to now, he had no external intelligence at all, he didn't even know where he was.
But clearly, that wasn't the most important thing.
The important thing was, if by some luck they do survive and complete the task, what then?
Upon this thought, silence fell over the cellar once again.
Su Lun could remain calm, but the other few were more eager to grasp at a sliver of survival.
Then, the barbarian Ralph mustered his courage and said in a deep voice, "May I ask the great demon god, once this is done, will our contract be over? Can we return to our original realm?"
They were here to fulfill a contract indeed, but they weren't to be enslaved to a heretical demon god for eternity.
Even if raising this question risked offending and enraging the god, it had to be asked clearly first.
Su Lun felt the same way.
Before doing anything, it was essential to eliminate potential problems.
All five originally thought something untoward might happen, yet to their surprise, the demon god agreed very decisively: "Yes."
Saying so, as if to alleviate their worries, a contract appeared in front of each of them, with an additional clause added: Upon completion of the task, the contract would be terminated.
Seeing this, the five of them simultaneously relaxed.
With no worries left behind, they could give their all to fulfilling the contract.
At that moment, the demon god reminded them, "After you go out, you will assume the identity of slaves building the tomb; no one can help you. Find a way to get close to the Sun Temple, then kill Pharaoh Cleopatra. From your perspective, the Pharaoh is a 'Demigod.' It won't be difficult for the five of you to kill her if you work together."
Listening to this plan,
They inexplicably breathed a sigh of relief.
Was it only to kill a Demigod?
Although they didn't understand why the demon god wouldn't take action himself, the five of them clearly had some confidence.
...
After the demon god gave a few more admonitions, the surroundings suddenly darkened into complete blackness.
Then, as if through Spatial Displacement, the gloomy cellar transformed into a wooden prison cell?
"An airship?"
Su Lun sensed the surrounding space and discovered that he had appeared in a room resembling a prison cell.
And the entire cell was actually within the cabin of a large ship?
Putting aside how this ship could fly in the sky, he was more astonished that the Spatial Coordinates he left in the cellar were now incredibly remote, estimating... tens of thousands of miles underground?
Before he could figure out what was going on, his attention was immediately drawn to a feeling of "weakness."
Looking down, he saw that his hands and neck were locked with chains that were like gold but not gold.
"A slave collar? Anti-Magic Runes?"
Su Lun understood at a glance what the runes on the collar were for, and his mind, blessed by the God Profaner, quickly started to work: "Ninth-tier light binding Anti-Magic Rune, solidifying the 'Solar Burst' spell, will explode immediately if forcefully opened... Three million six hundred thousand methods of breaking it, not too difficult."
This slave collar wasn't a complete magic seal, but rather a sort of limiter valve, preventing the slaves from unleashing too much power.
With this thing, Su Lun estimated that he could at most use one-tenth of his original combat strength.
It restricted combat strength, yet not the strength for labor.
The demon god had mentioned before that someone would deliver the key to them at the right time.
Telling them to wait for the opportunity.
But this level of rune encryption was hardly a challenge for Su Lun at this point.
For an alchemist, all systems of runes were essentially variations of cosmic rules and laws; as long as one could see through the patterns, a solution could be found.
Although this was definitely a divine plane, setting a mousetrap did not require a bear trap.
To an alchemist's eyes, the encryption of this slave collar was equivalent to a challenge for a ninth-rank alchemist.
For Su Lun, it was even easier.
The slave collar posed no threat, so he didn't give it much thought.
While decrypting and figuring out how to unlock it in his head, he also turned his gaze to the other prisoners in the jail.
The battlesaint Jay, the centaur Makamul, the barbarian Ralph, the Dragon Maiden Masia... the four he had met before were now also caged, wearing collars.
Su Lun also realized that this was a slave ship.
