And now, it seemed the demon god had made a meticulous plan for its escape. Over these tens of thousands of years, it had not only summoned some Contractors but had also nurtured a super massive rat army.
In the blink of an eye, rats were emerging from the cracks surrounding the tomb from all directions, the commotion growing louder. The sea of rats built up into a tower, continuously converging toward the bronze lamp.
The demon god wanted to break free!
After watching for a while, Su Lun felt a stinging pain in his eyes and quickly averted his gaze.
In that space, he had seen too much "forbidden" information, causing a great burden on his eyes and brain.
This was after all the ancestral tomb of the Taris pantheon, inevitably involving the secrets of high-ranking deities.
Otherwise, it would not be a mere Tomb Keeper; it would be a genuine mummified god.
Su Lun had no inclination to guess at the secrets within or care about how that demon god was to extricate itself from its predicament.
He himself was now in a deadlock.
Any movement would result in immediate death at the hands of the jackal-headed mummy.
And to continue in this standoff was equally a path to death.
If that demon god managed to escape, and the Tares clan came to open the tomb, his own death was inevitable.
Su Lun did not believe for a second that a high-ranking demon god had any interest in helping a trapped ant like himself.
His only option was to figure out a way to save himself.
The jackal-headed mummy might have been strong, but it was after all a dead thing, lacking its own consciousness.
Therefore, its targets for attack must have some triggering condition.
Just like these rats, which did not trigger it.
Speedily, Su Lun's mind raced through various possibilities, finally arriving at the most plausible explanation, "Could it be that these rats carry the murky aura of divine power from the tomb, which is why the jackal-headed mummy ignored them?"
In simpler terms, these were native-born rats, with the distinct scent of the local vermin.
Considering Su Lun was an outsider, he couldn't possibly acquire that "local scent" in a short amount of time.
Moreover, the white fog within the crypt was a terrifying curse energy, which to humans was almost certainly fatal on contact.
He couldn't understand why these rats were unaffected, but he figured it must be some bug-exploiting method prepared by the demon god over thousands of years, something he most likely couldn't replicate.
....
"This is quite the predicament..."
All thoughts in Su Lun's mind were flying, but his calculations only led to one outcome: a dead end.
Could he only hope against hope that the demon god would be so kind as to save him on a whim?
He didn't think waiting was a good choice.
And it was at that moment, the "white fog" around him also grew increasingly dense.
Just then, a miracle occurred very abruptly.
Su Lun, focusing intently on the fog, keenly observed something familiar, and a thought suddenly struck him, "Eh... The 'Isaac God Slayer' symbiotic armor integration, doesn't it require a massive amount of superior divine power to neutralize dark regulations?"
Although he couldn't completely understand what the fog was, he understood that the integration of the symbiotic armor required that superior divine power, which was a component of the fog!
With this realization, a wild plan popped into Su Lun's head: Could he use this divine power fog to integrate the symbiotic armor?
If the integration was successful, he would instantly acquire the "scent of a local," his strength would surge dramatically, and he might even stand a chance to confront the jackal-headed mummy!
Sir Isaac had designed this symbiotic armor specifically to confront divine beings.
Once this idea manifested, Su Lun's brain worked like a supercomputer running at high speed.
He quickly calculated all sorts of parameters and came to a conclusion: theoretically, it was absolutely feasible!
...
Having thought of this plan, Su Lun's thoughts became crystal clear.
The 'God Slayer' symbiotic armor, because it involved 'dark regulations,' an unobservable cosmic dark energy, was nearly impossible for the human body to integrate successfully.
Even Sir Isaac, the creator of the symbiotic armor, believed it to be so.
Su Lun had thoroughly studied the properties of the 'God Slayer' armor. The rigorous process of integration demanded more than just high physical qualifications in an individual; the bigger obstacle was that neither 'dark regulations' nor the superior divine power required for neutralization could be endured by humans.
Integrating this symbiotic armor was essentially like infusing two highly curse-attributed objects with opposing properties into a regular human body and letting their overflow of cursed properties neutralize each other. Only if the energies perfectly balanced could the integration succeed.
Even a slight excess would cause the integrator to explode and die.
The likelihood of a successful integration was almost zero.
But Su Lun's current conditions were not the same as they were a thousand years ago.
In his possession was a treasure, the 'Philosopher's Stone'!
The most important function of this alchemic holy object was absolute equivalent energy exchange.
Su Lun had already tested it, whether it be divine power or any other form of energy; every type of energy he'd encountered in the universe could be exchanged equivalently!
Previously, he had no way to find the necessary superior divine power to neutralize the dark regulations, but now, wasn't the crypt filled with the white fog everywhere?
The Tares divine family had created numerous 'divine slaves' to refine divine power to operate some unspeakable formation, leaving the crypt saturated with murky various divine energies.
You wouldn't find such an environment anywhere else.
Theoretically, if the Philosopher's Stone could precisely extract the necessary portion of energy and neutralize the dark divine power on the armor, the integration could be successful.
And the greatest risk that Su Lun calculated was that he had to personally grasp that balance point of energy.
With the 'God Profaner' enhancement, his mental capacity was, barring external interference, nearly impossible to fail.
...
"Take a gamble?"
Su Lun made a split-second decision in his heart.
On a normal day, he might have hesitated, given the immense risk of integration and the fact that the slightest mistake could result in a violent death.
But in this situation, with not much room for consideration, he decided to try immediately.
Because there was no other choice.
If nothing was done, the end would still be a dead end.
Moreover, if he could successfully fuse with the God Slayer artifact, everything in the future would be different.
This was a risk, but also a huge opportunity.
Let's do it!
Although Su Lun didn't know when the Taris divinities would enter, from the current pace, it would take those rats several more days to destroy that bronze lamp.
If that demigod dared to act, there was nothing he dared not to do.
This period of time was completely enough to fuse with the artifact.
However, before that, he still needed to test some necessary data.
Su Lun didn't delay. With a thought, the sky lit up with the Spirit Communion Array, and a black crow flew out from the array.
The previously killed Crow Lord was once again condensed and resurrected.
However, as soon as it came back to life, the dog-headed mummy in the distance immediately noticed it and darted over with a lightning-quick punch, exploding the Crow Lord into a cloud of death energy instantaneously.
But as long as the death energy was not exhausted, the telltale crow could resurrect infinitely.
If there was one thing this tomb did not lack, it was an incessant supply of various types of death energy.
No sooner had it been blown apart than the Crow Lord resurrected once again, and even took advantage of the moment to voraciously consume several mouthfuls of death energy from the tomb.
Then it was blown up again, consumed a few more mouthfuls of death energy, and resurrected again... repeating this cycle over and over.
After being killed over a hundred times, the Crow Lord's aura of being a 'native bird' grew increasingly intense.
Su Lun also noticed that the perception of the dog-headed being towards the black crow was becoming increasingly dull.
In the underground palace, the Crow Lord began to gleefully devour death energy to its heart's content, eventually completely ignored by the dog-headed mummy.
"It really works!"
Seeing this, Su Lun was delighted in his heart.
His conjecture was correct!
And those more than a hundred deaths of the Crow Lord earlier provided him with enough data through observation.
Seeing this, Su Lun hesitated no further.
The fog around was now quite thick, so he tried to infiltrate a bit of the Guo Wrapping Cloth of Oz Ice Man.
Before the white mist even touched his skin, Su Lun felt an indescribable chill sweep over his entire body as if his soul was shivering with it.
This force almost made him explode on the spot.
Fortunately, the Philosopher's Stone filtered out the unnecessary energy, allowing that super-order divine power to smoothly merge into the Isaac Blasphemer artifact, worn like a vest over his body.
Su Lun held his breath, pondering over all the data he had just calculated, guiding that divine power.
And then, a miraculous scene occurred.
The terrifying super-order divine power simply vanished into thin air!
"This... this is the power of the unspoken rules!"
Su Lun was unable to detect the presence of that dark energy, but through the vanishing imagery of divine power, he knew there must be some mysterious force that had neutralized these divine powers.
Having witnessed this miraculous scene, he could not contain his surging emotions.
It could be said that the "unspoken rules" were definitely one of the greatest discoveries of the alchemical civilization over the countless years.
Meanwhile, the All-knowing Eye identified that the success rate of fusing with the God Eater had gone from 0% to 0.001%.
Although it was only a slight change,
it was exactly what Su Lun wanted.
He had bet correctly!
It really worked!
He could hardly contain his joy, and continued with excitement and caution to try to bring in those divine powers little by little.
The Guo Wrapping Cloth of Oz Ice Man isolated energy leakage and created an internal space.
Su Lun had consumed a large amount of Dragon Blood, temporarily bringing his body to the threshold of fusion, and then he began to slowly fuse with the sub-divine artifact.
Two amazing forces were intermingling and vanishing within his body.
It was as chaotic as setting off a bomb inside his body, one after another, creating quite the spectacle.
It also came with immense risks.
Su Lun felt like his body was a balance scale, with the Philosopher's Stone in the middle, continuously adding weights to both sides, reaching a delicate equilibrium. Gradually, the weights on both sides had been added beyond the limit a human could bear and were still rising.
Any slight imbalance would lead to his body exploding instantaneously.
...
On the other hand, the dog-headed mummy, lacking intelligence, had not discovered Su Lun, who had not budged from the spot.
But while the corpse might not have noticed him, that demonic god knew very well.
The divine power in the underground palace had mysteriously diminished; there was clearly something absorbing it.
And the earlier appearance of the black crow had not escaped Its notice, either.
Su Lun had originally thought that the demonic god would not pay attention to his insignificant existence, yet during the fusion, a voice of surprise suddenly rang beside his ear, "Huh... you're still alive?"
This tone of surprise clearly showed that the demonic god also thought that after the altar was opened, there shouldn't be any survivors.
After all, this tomb was in essence, a dead end.
There were restrictions on the descent of divine beings, yet a divine corpse was guarding it.
Under normal circumstances, it was impossible for any living person to be there.
Even a demigod with their might would have to die.
But now, a survivor had appeared, and the demonic god seemed to have taken an interest.
"..."
Su Lun felt a sense of foreboding upon hearing this.
At this critical juncture, he didn't want to attract attention.
But it seemed as though the demonic god had already pierced through everything, as a distant and ethereal voice reached his ear again, "Human, rest assured. Although the contract has ended, my escape from confinement this time was also thanks to your fortune, and naturally, I won't make things difficult for you."
Listening to those words, Su Lun automatically translated them to mean: Insect, relax, you have too little flesh; I'm not interested in eating you.
It was as if a powerful entity, trapped for tens of thousands of years, was simply lonesome and wanted to exchange a few words.
However, this was good news.
A higher demonic god would not have interest in deceiving him, and with these words spoken, his life was likely spared.
Su Lun responded to this thought, feigning ignorance as he asked, "Are you the demonic god who guided our actions earlier?"
Although he did not have a divine faith, it was still best not to provoke trouble with such beings.
As expected, the demonic god seemed not to mind this attitude and said, "Human, you are worthy to know my venerated name. You may address me as 'The God of Darkness and Destruction, the Great Lord of Chaos, the Supreme Destruction Demon Pillar, Lord Apophis'."
"..."
Hearing this series of titles, Su Lun felt not annoyance in his heart but increased humility instead.
He now had some understanding of the gods and knew that the titles of deities were not given at random. Each title pointed to a cosmic rule.
This was faith.
In other words, this deity had merged at least the divine powers of [Darkness] and [Destruction].
This was no longer a matter where a lower deity with a single divine aspect could be compared.
He said in awe, "Great Lord Apophis."
In the presence of a god, it was best not to ask questions, but to wait for the deity to speak first.
Such conversations were not equal, and any accidental word might offend a deity and bring about a fatal disaster.
Then Lord Apophis spoke again, "Oh... So you are an Alchemist. That Formation of yours is quite interesting, actually capable of withstanding the erosion of these murky divine powers. A pity though, if you believed in darkness, you might have had the fortune of becoming my follower..."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun breathed another sigh of relief.
There was no hostility because he was an Alchemist, so his safety was quite secure.
And the arrogance of higher holy beings deemed it beneath them to pry into the secrets of a low-ranking human.
In the eyes of this deity, Su Lun guessed he was no different from the rodents.
But the treasures and secrets on him had been preserved.
He responded with more banal flattery, "Ah... Great Lord Apophis, you are powerful, wise, and sagacious, you see through everything in the world..."
Having harvested the memories of many divine followers, Su Lun knew how to deal with deities, and humility was key.
In front of a god, do not act like you understand everything.
It is best to be ignorant and foolish.
Deities like the sensation of being far superior to lower creatures, reigning supreme from above.
This deity before him certainly had that right.
The demonic god chose to speak, merely because after tens of thousands of years of confinement, there was hope for escape, and in good spirits, he chatted with an insect for a brief moment.
Su Lun did not fancy himself to be the lifesaver of a high-ranking demonic god.
If he entertained such a thought, he would have been courting death.
His response was properly respectful, not causing any trouble.
Indeed, it could lead to fatal implications.
After that, Lord Apophis did not speak again.
Su Lun also let out a sigh of relief and continued to absorb divine power, merging with the godly artifact.
...
In the underground palace, countless rodents continued their futile efforts, relentlessly gnawing at the bronze lamp.
Meanwhile, Su Lun was also hastening to merge with the god-tier artifact, and the percentage of fusion gradually increased.
1%...2%...6%…9%…13%…
He did not ask the demonic god any questions, nor did he contemplate probing the underground palace's secrets, focusing solely on absorbing Divine Power and merging with the god-tier artifact.
Finally, his concentration was rewarded.
After three days, Su Lun forcibly completed the fusion with the [God Slayer] artifact!

chapters.title: Chapter 662 - 661: Obtaining Another Treasure
chapters.content:
Before Su Lun came to fulfill the mythical pact, he had never thought that he would be able to fuse with the "Isaac God Slayer," this special artifact.
After all, he had already come into contact with various top-tier resources within the realm of Alchemy, but he didn't feel any hope of successful fusion.
Unexpectedly, by a stroke of fate, he found the opportunity for fusion in the ancestral realm of the Tares civilization.
Even now that the fusion had succeeded and he clearly felt the indescribable dark power the divine artifact bestowed, he still felt as if he were in a dream.
Had he really succeeded in the fusion?
Indeed!
Su Lun sensed the feeling brought by the fusion of the artifact, and his heart was shocked, "So this is the 'Power of Dark Rules'... Specifically countering divine power, Sir Isaac's talent is truly unparalleled!"
Different from being a bystander before, now that he had integrated the artifact into his body, he clearly perceived the existence of the "Dark Rules."
This was an unknown realm that no one had observed for countless years.
Su Lun could hardly describe his thoughts at the moment; this artifact had opened the door to a new world for him, suddenly enlightening his understanding.
It was as if he had always been in the light before, using his five senses to perceive a world.
And now, he had discovered the night.
I cannot see in the darkness, but the night is not devoid of things.
I have a new understanding, this is the "Dark World."
This is an unknown realm as vast and boundless as the bright universe I previously knew.
Su Lun realized that dark matter indeed existed in his world.
This was a mysterious realm that countless highly talented Great Alchemists had never touched for many years.
No!
Even some lower-tier gods could not touch this... the realm pointing to the secret of the cosmic origin!
At this moment, he felt like the first time he had fused job materials to become an extraordinary professional, when a new world's door had just opened, giving him a feeling that everything was brand new.
This was just the beginning; he still needed much time to digest and understand.
Su Lun was not in a hurry.
Understanding it now might not matter, the significance of the artifact was that it allowed him to wield the annihilating "Power of Dark Rules."
This artifact was called the "God Slayer" because it could kill gods!
This meant that the mummy with a dog's head inside the crypt might not be a certain death for Su Lun now.
...
Wrapped in his shroud, Su Lun completed the fusion with the artifact, and finally felt a bit of confidence that he could leave alive.
But he still did not act recklessly.
Now was not the time.
Over these few days, countless rats had swarmed into the tomb beneath the altar, gnawing at the bronze lamp.
Su Lun watched the increasingly faint runes on the lamp and knew that the demon god Apophis was about to escape.
Before the demon god Apophis could free himself, it was best for him to stay put and do nothing.
Don't be fooled, even though this demon god is trapped, with its ability to control endless swarms of rats to escape, it could easily kill a human.
And Su Lun did not want to reveal too much.
Higher-tier demon gods disdain to probe the secrets of lower-tier creatures, but that doesn't mean that if he exposed himself, the other party wouldn't be interested.
He had too many secrets on him.
Should the demon god realize that a human could master the "Power of Dark Rules", who knows what could happen.
Right now was a good time to adjust to the changes the fused artifact had brought to his body.
Previously Su Lun's physical condition was far from ready to fuse with the artifact; he had forcibly consumed a large amount of Dragon Blood making his attributes reach high values, only then succeeding in the fusion. Like the effect of a stimulant that couldn't last forever, his current state was very dangerous.
He needed time to recover.
However, after not absorbing the low-level divine power mist,
The demon god naturally discovered it immediately.
It seemed to regain interest, and Su Lun heard a whispering murmur beside his ear, "Tsk tsk, interesting... absorbing so much divine power, and a human did not burst apart? That's somewhat clever. You found the method to absorb divine power to avoid triggering the tomb's killing restrictions so quickly..."
Su Lun listened and once again adopted a humble tone, "Great Apophis, in your presence, this is nothing but a trifling art."
This humble approach had no issues, and the demon god Apophis seemed quite satisfied.
But it then said, "Human, you are already good enough. At least you are more special than other lower beings I have encountered over tens of thousands of years. Oh~ I almost forgot, there is a secret technique called 'equivalent exchange' among alchemists, indeed capable of eliminating foreign divine powers. Tsk tsk, back in the Dawn Era, when the Five Divine Kings of the Twilight Cross intimidated all realms, this technique was a taboo among the heavens..."
"..."
Hearing this, Su Lun couldn't help but be slightly shocked.
The Dawn Era indeed represented the peak moments of the Alchemy realm. But due to a discontinuity in civilizations, the timeline wasn't certain. Su Lun estimated that it was at least hundreds of thousands of years ago.
This demon god... could it have lived for hundreds of thousands of years?
How powerful must it be?
Fortunately, from the tone of the conversation, this demon god did not harbor hostility towards the Alchemy civilization.
Su Lun spoke again, "Great Apophis, in your presence, no secret in this world can escape your wise eyes."
Apophis seemed to be in a good mood, willing to talk more with a human, "In half a day, I will be able to free myself. Human, it is because of you that I was able to escape this prison that has trapped me for tens of thousands of years. As compensation, so the great Apophis allows you to ask one question."
Hearing this, Su Lun also became hopeful.
A powerful high-tier demon god, indeed, any question he had within his understanding could be answered by this being!
This compensation was not insignificant.
Su Lun pondered for a moment and thought of something, asking, "Um... Great Apophis, I have a question for you."
Apophis: "Oh?"
Su Lun asked, "Due to some reasons, my plane is being invaded by another dimensional plane. Do you have a method to close the dimensional gateway?"
Since the other party had summoned him, it was likely they knew about the existence of the alchemy plane. Hence, hiding it didn't make much sense.
Upon hearing this, Apophis showed a trace of surprise, "A dimensional gateway? Tsk tsk, such a gateway can only be constructed by a very advanced civilization. Oh~ I almost forgot, the alchemy plane was once a main god plane, but unfortunately, it was shattered later... You must be on one of its fragments, right?"
As if he had been confined for too long, his speech was somewhat rambling.
As he spoke, he had already understood everything and then said, "However... are you sure you want to ask me this question? You only have one chance. I think you could ask something more valuable. For example, how to condense a divine nature? After all, with your current realm, you should be puzzled about this. And stepping into the divine tier of the alchemy civilization is not that easy."
After thinking it over, Su Lun said, "Yes, Great God of Darkness and Destruction, I am sure I need the answer to this question."
Although the path to becoming a god was extremely tempting, he felt some beliefs were more important.
Upon hearing this, Apophis said, "Foolish and short-sighted human, you do not know what an excellent opportunity you just missed."
His tone seemed mocking, yet it didn't sound mocking.
Then, he directly answered, "Once a dimensional gateway is opened, it must be closed from both sides to be completely sealed. It seems like your plane is probably not capable of doing that. Typically, strong civilizations would not voluntarily close a dimensional gateway, and the weaker side lacks the power to close it. Hehe..."
His tone was filled with disdain from a superior being towards inferior creatures.
"..."
Hearing this, Su Lun's mood instantly became solemn.
If the problem of the dimensional gateway was not resolved, the alchemy plane would eventually be conquered.
But if even a high-level demon god couldn't do it, then it was genuinely impossible.
However, since he asked, the all-knowing and all-powerful god would naturally not say it was impossible.
Apophis clearly had a way as he spoke a meaningful proverb, "When I was very young, there was a saying in my family: if you discover a thief often crosses the river behind the garden to steal the roses, then scatter some broken glass in the river."
Upon hearing this, Su Lun suddenly had an epiphany, vaguely guessing something, "Are you saying...?"
Apophis directly said, "The most important thing about a dimensional gateway is its stability and safety. If you have the capability, collect some void fragments and throw them into the dimensional gateway. They will be a nightmare for travelers, very troublesome to clean, and the cost is immense. If there are enough fragments, even divine beings may risk falling, and then they will carefully consider whether to go through the dimensional gateway."
"!!!"
Upon hearing this, Su Lun immediately became excited.
This was indeed a method!
If the gateway could not be closed, then make it unsafe. This way, the number of individuals passing through would significantly decrease.
Especially for gods, most would not risk falling to invade another dimensional plane but would likely send their followers to die.
If they could indeed prevent the coming of divine beings from the godly planes, then there was still a fight to be had in the war of dimensional invasion!
Apophis said a few words, seemingly losing interest afterward, and finally said, "I will transmit to you a secret space technique, which will make the void fragments even more difficult to clear. Whether you can use it depends on you..."
"Thank you, Supreme Lord of the Destruction Demon Pillar!"
Su Lun promptly responded.
As soon as he spoke, he immediately sensed a thought in his mind transmitting a secret technique—[Divine Art: Star Shatter]!
Constructing a spatial gateway is very difficult, but causing a little destruction costs much less.
This secret technique was purely wicked.
To explode spatial fragments into tiny glass-like shards, scattering like stars across the dimensional gateway, would cost millions more to clean up.
Moreover, it was a very powerful attack divine art.
Ordinary beings below divinity couldn't use it, but Su Lun could.
He had the [Urobolos Space-Time Ring] and deploying this technique was no problem at all.
Indeed, high-tier planes were risky, but they also offered much more opportunity!
He had discussed the issue of the dimensional gateway countless times with Mr. Jing and others, already concluding that it was nearly a dead end.
But coming to the yellow sand plane, not only did he successfully merge with the [God Slayer], but also found a solution for the spatial gateway!
...
Apophis merely provided a few hints when interest struck him, and after speaking a few words, he was no longer interested in discussing further with this human.
In the empty underground palace, only the sound of countless rats scurrying across the floor and then being incinerated into ashes remained.
Su Lun didn't push further, quietly digesting his gains.
As the demon god had said, within half a day, countless rats had already nibbled away the runes on the copper lamp.
Suddenly, a "crack" sound, like that of metal breaking, echoed.
Su Lun sensed something and abruptly looked towards the sealed underground palace.
Previously, there were dozens of soul lamps emitting green light along the path of god, but now, the third copper lamp on the left side of the entrance had unexpectedly gone out?
Su Lun realized, that demon god was freed.
But in the very next moment, a terrifying will descended upon the entire underground palace.
Su Lun stared at the extinguished copper lamp area, where darkness twisted into a human figure.
"This isn't good!"
A sense of unprecedented horror arose inside him, and even wrapped up, he felt an indescribable terror.
Even stripped of fear emotions, there was a shiver from deep within his soul.
Even in the two 解 "All-knowing Eye," what he saw was only distorted darkness and threads of destruction rules. It seemed as if that presence was not just some entity but a part of the universe itself.
Su Lun had never seen such a terrifying being before and immediately closed his eyes.
Indescribable, unspeakable, and not to be looked upon directly...
This was a true high-tier demon god!
Then, a reckless laughter echoed, "Hahaha, I am finally free..."
Being trapped for tens of thousands of years, even a high-tier demon god could not hide his joy.
Su Lun was so shocked by the truly terrifying presence that he found himself speechless. He felt like a speck of dust; a mere sneeze from that being could obliterate him instantly.
And clearly, Apophis had not forgotten there was a human who helped him escape.
As a high-ranking demon god, He could see through the causes and effects of the universe's fate.
Even if it were just an insect, if it had favorable causality with His own fate, He should repay it.
Because it wasn't certain whether the fluttering of the insect's wings might cause a hurricane to strike Him.
He said, "Human, I know you have the ability to escape. There is a passage beneath the crevice in the southeast of the tomb, which was originally left as a secret escape route by the dwarven divine craftsmen who built this tomb. Only by taking that path can you avoid being stopped by the descendants of the Tariths. Once I leave, high-ranking gods will surely descend on this realm from the Tarith plane, arriving here within an hour at most. Take care of yourself."
Su Lun, fully aware that the demon god was guiding him, thanked Him promptly, "Thank you, God of Darkness and Destruction, the Great Lord of Chaos, the Supreme Destruction Demon Pillar, Lord Apophis, for your guidance!"
Although the "Urobolos Space-Time Ring" allowed him to teleport out of the tomb, he would inevitably encounter the encirclement and blockade of the Tarith clan once outside.
With this secret passage, there couldn't be a better option.
Moreover, he now knew he had about an hour of safety.
Apophis: "You are not bad. Divination tells me, a lower plane cannot confine you. I hope someday, I will have the chance to see you in the realm of gods. Let me give you another piece of advice, if there were only the sun without darkness, then light would no longer be the incarnation of justice, and the world would become a terrifying hell."
Su Lun had no time to ponder the profound meaning of these words and replied, "Thank you, my lord!"
However, before he could finish, that terrifying will had already dissipated.
Su Lun also knew that the demon god had left the underground palace.
Just as he breathed a sigh of relief, a reminder echoed beside his ear again: "By the way, don't touch those coffins. Otherwise, the old fellows of the Tarith clan would not hesitate to use their last breath to climb out and kill you."
On hearing this, Su Lun's eyelids twitched slightly.
Was the demon god not only powerful but also aware of his thoughts about looting along the secret passage?
But... climb out?
Were the beings inside those coffins still alive?
This statement thoroughly discouraged Su Lun from targeting those coffins.
After waiting for a moment, the underground palace became utterly silent, even the rats had disappeared without a trace.
This time, the demon god Apophis had truly left.
....
Su Lun recalled what an Old Cowboy once said in Lyndon: In some ways, making a deal with a demon is quite fair; at least when you give something, He will definitely compensate you equally.
Although coming here to fulfill the contract was perilously close to a matter of life and death, the demon god had indeed been quite generous.
Though His advice was casual, it was all crucial.
Su Lun collected his thoughts and looked around the spacious hall.
He was naturally planning to leave.
But before leaving, with a little time to spare, he could consider taking some local specialties from the Tarith clan.
A grain of rice dropped by a god might be food enough to stuff an ant.
What high-ranking demon gods disregarded, for him, a human, could be treasures.
But before that, there was a little trouble to deal with.
Su Lun's gaze landed on a mummy body that had gathered divinity in the distance.
At that moment, he slowly removed a bit of the burial shroud wrapped around his body, leaking a bit of scent.
"It really worked!"
Su Lun rejoiced in his heart.
Having absorbed a large amount of impure divine power from the underground palace over the past few days, his body had also been contaminated with the aura of those Tarith gods. As he'd hoped, it had not triggered the mummy's killing mechanism.
When he completely removed the burial shroud, the mummy seemed to sense something and moved slightly, but uncertain of what and did not take action.
Su Lun also thoroughly breathed a sigh of relief.
At this moment, the vast underground palace was filled with gray-white mist, permeated with the strange smell of the millions of rats that had previously been burned here.
Mr. Crow had already divided into hundreds, greedily consuming the dense aura of death here while also sharing the vision.
Su Lun carefully walked inside the underground palace.
Previously, he had almost emptied all the items on this floor, there was nothing good to see, his target was the mysterious space beneath that altar.
Although Apophis had cautioned him not to think about disrupting those divine-tier coffins, if Su Lun wasn't mistaken, there were many other things inside the tomb besides coffins.
As he walked past, he saw the "Key of Immortality" embedded in the floor.
"What a good thing..."
Su Lun felt he definitely had to take it with him when he left.
This key still held a lot of pure life energy, enough to resurrect someone.
As for the belief divine power needed to activate the talisman, Pandora had it!
Having this by his side was like suddenly having an extra life.
Probably after picking it up, the doors of the underground palace would close, so Su Lun was not in a hurry to act. He looked towards the inside of the underground palace.
On getting closer, that soul-chilling sensation became even clearer.
Green lights from spirit lamps illuminated colorful coffins; many other places were pitch black.
Su Lun did not step inside, just stood at the doorway.
A glance inside revealed not much was moving.
Though the All-knowing Eye held too many secrets, he also understood that the underground was a massive formation, with crystal obelisks linking the coffins and various divine-tier restraints.
All were divine-tier treasures of immeasurable value.
But none dared to be touched.
However, Su Lun's gaze fell on the ground.
As the spirit lamps burned, oil dripped into boxes forming pools of amber-like crystalline residues.
On inspection, they turned out to be what he recognized from harvesting a Pharaoh's memories.
"Flawless Divine Womb"
Detailed Explanation: A pristine embryo, formed from concentrated Divine Power, used by the Taris clan to carry soul entities; it possesses high malleability and can be nurtured into various biological forms;
....
"This 'Flawless Divine Embryo' was actually concocted from the lamps of gods' souls?"
Su Lun suddenly realized.
The Taris clan has always had the legend of the "Chosen of the Gods."
It is said that every few decades, a deity with top-tier talent, destined to become a demigod, would appear in the divine planes.
They gave guidance to believers and spread faith.
The strength of the Taris civilization was directly related to these Chosen!
Su Lun had originally thought that the devotees were just exceptionally talented people chosen by the deities, but seeing this Divine Embryo, he immediately realized that this could be the source of the 'Chosen of the Taris' and might also be closely linked to resurrection techniques!
However, he had no interest in caring about the Chosen; in the eyes of an alchemist, this was just a material!
"It's actually such a divine-grade material..."
Su Lun looked at it, eyes gleaming.
This "Divine Embryo" also has a special role in the field of Alchemy, that is, creating artificial humans!
Having read various notes beforehand, he discovered that Pandora's body was made from this material.
A thousand years ago, Sir Isaac and Lady Isaac somehow found such a Divine Embryo and then created Pandora.
Su Lun had completely mastered the technique of creating artificial humans, but he was still lacking the right main material.
Unexpectedly, he encountered it here.
"Ah... there we go, the material for that girl Pesutoya's body."
Su Lun's mind whirled, and he became lively immediately.
Since the "Divine Embryo" is the crystallization of Divine Power corpse oil, with no magical imprints or restrictions involved, taking it would not affect those beings inside the sarcophagus.
He thought that taking a little bit should not be a problem.
Su Lun observed again and indeed, there was nothing else worth taking.
He didn't dare to enter himself, so he signaled Mr. Crow to grasp the silk thread, tying it to the two Divine Embryos closest to the main gate.
He had planned to take a few more pieces together, but at that moment, a sudden change occurred.
A chilling aura of killing intent came crashing down from behind!
Since Su Lun chose tomb raiding, he naturally had his defenses prepared.
His gaze sharpened, and he threw a heavy counterpunch to block.
At the same time, he suddenly realized something, "Does merely intending to rob the tomb immediately trigger this dog-headed mummy's slaughter mechanism?"
It wasn't particularly surprising.
In just a flash, the dog-headed mummy appeared in front of him, with a punch enshrouded by a domain of rules aiming straight for his face, making Su Lun's scalp tingle.
It was this very punch that had blasted the barbarian Ralph, who had demigod combat power, to pieces three days earlier.
Any demigod taking this punch would likely die instantly!
However, Su Lun had already unleashed the "God Eater" exoskeleton, his punch also enveloped in a layer of invisible energy, launching out without any hesitation.
As the two punches collided, something miraculous happened.
The scene that should have been gory was nowhere to be seen!
As the mummy's fist unleashed a rule-breaking destructive force, it seemed as if it was neutralized and obliterated by some energy, disappearing without a trace.
Su Lun felt the mummy's fist, which was simply a bit stronger, lacking the rule-level destructive power.
"It really works!"
Although he was blown back, he was overjoyed in his heart.
Being able to withstand a strike from this divine-tier mummy meant it no longer posed a lethal threat to him!
It also meant he now had a real means to counter at a divine level.
....
Su Lun was blown backward, but he used this force to pull, and the threads tugged, causing two pieces of the 'Divine Embryo' to fly out from the crypt.
He flashed forward and instantly stored them in his spatial storage.
The treasure was now in hand!
However, at that moment, the mummy flashed forward again, launching another punch, and Su Lun was blown back once more.
Without the lethal threat, as long as he spent some time, Su Lun felt he might be able to defeat this divine-tier dog-headed mummy.
After all, the mummy possessed a Divine Emblem, a true treasure!
But having just integrated the exoskeleton, he was not perfectly in control of this completely unfamiliar "dark rule" power, and the risk of defeat was not small.
Moreover, since this was the Taris clan's tomb, it was not advisable to linger in battle.
He knew he couldn't take down the dog-headed mummy in a short time, and the risks of further tomb raiding would only increase.
There's a time to be greedy,
and a time when you must decisively retreat,
As Su Lun was blown away, he decisively tugged on the threads again.
"Click," the "Key of Eternity" embedded in the altar was also pulled out.
Just then, the entire crypt began to creak and groan, as if some restriction had been triggered.
Su Lun didn't plan to delay any longer. The moment he took the key, he turned his head and teleported towards the southeast tunnel to escape.
Although the mummy was fast, Su Lun was focused on escaping. In the crypt, built with indestructible 'Asgard Divine Stones', it wasn't easy to chase him.
"Thud" "Thud" "Thud" After breaking through several walls, Su Lun successfully shook off the mummy and plunged into a space crack.

chapters.title: Chapter 663 - 662: Return to the Alchemy Plane
chapters.content:
Su Lun had escaped the pursuit of the jackal-headed mummy and followed the direction indicated by the demigod Apophis to find a very hidden underground passage.
This passage, left by the divine craftsmen who originally built the pyramid for their own survival, would have remained undiscovered by Su Lun if the demigod had not pointed out its exact location, hidden within a spatial rift.
Su Lun dived in and slid down the sandy tunnel that was like a slide.
The skilled Dwarf Divine General had created a "wormhole" within the nearly airtight, beyond-advanced prohibition array of the pyramid, allowing one to escape without triggering those prohibitions.
It was only in his escape that Su Lun realized the pyramid was more than just the surface; there was a hugely vast and complex foundation underneath.
Now that he was fleeing, he made no apologies, stuffing every "Asgard gemstone" he encountered, which could be disassembled and carried away, into his small void world.
And because the passage was extremely covert, avoiding direct confrontation with the Taris divine tribe on the surface, he wasn't the least bit worried about being discovered.
So he continued downward, likely leaving the pyramid's foundation riddled with holes, until he saw an underground world that resembled a mass of roots.
It was then that Su Lun realized, could these root-bearing pyramids be alive? Seemed like they were absorbing energy from the entire sandy plane?
This was probably part of the Taris divine tribe's secret of resurrection. Although Su Lun had an interest in exploring, the grave warning from Mr. Crow on his shoulder meant he couldn't delay and immediately used spatial teleportation to enter the spatial rift deep underground.
With the "Urobolos Space-Time Ring" protecting his body, he wasn't afraid of being stirred into the turbulent flows of space by spatial winds.
Because he had left markers all along his way when he first arrived, Su Lun teleported towards them.
Coming here was smooth sailing under the demigod's divine power, but now alone on his return, he had to be cautious at every step.
Spatial winds posed a risk of falling even for divine beings, let alone for a ninth-rank like himself.
So Su Lun carefully navigated through the space rifts that resembled roots.
During his travel, he increasingly sensed that the world was like a tree, planted in the infinite soil of the universe.
Each plane was like a giant tree, forming an endless forest.
Without coordinates, one would surely get lost in this forest.
Thus, a journey that took three days on the way took a full four months to return.
Even with utmost caution, the omnipresent spatial winds nearly cost him his life in the void on several occasions.
Still, he returned safely to the Alchemy plane in the end, collecting some stray pieces of space and spatial gemstones along the way to expand his small void world.
...
On this day, atop the azure sea,
two people, a Dragon Maiden, and a centaur stood on the sea surface.
Su Lun let out a long breath, "Finally back."
Pandora, with her face hidden under the cloak, also revealed a warm smile, "Yes, indeed. While the journey outside brought great harvests, it feels better to be back."
However, standing atop the sea and sensing nature's spiritual energy, the other two wore slightly odd expressions.
The centaur Makamul frowned in confusion, "Is this the Alchemy plane? Why do the laws of nature seem a bit low here..."
As he spoke, he glanced at Su Lun. Assuming that such a formidable being had emerged from the Alchemy plane, Makamul had expected it to be a powerful plane.
But upon arrival, he found the ceiling of this plane's laws to be much lower, even less than that of the Centaur plane.
Seemingly... a shattered plane?
Though aware of the ancient legend that the Alchemy plane had been destroyed, it was unlikely for a ninth-rank to appear from a broken plane, let alone such an anomaly as Su Lun.
Masia, the Dragon Maiden beside him, harbored similar doubts.
Su Lun looked at the two of them and said calmly, "The laws of nature here have improved a lot from before."
Hearing this, Makamul and Masia both felt relieved, thinking in unison: Fortunately, there's only one oddity like him.
Without intending to explain further, Su Lun smiled, "Let's go. As we travel, I'll introduce you to our Alchemy plane."
Without saying much more, Makamul and the others nodded. After all, they had signed a war pact and were prepared for what lay ahead.
Plus, the prospect of seeing the legendary Alchemy civilization filled them with anticipation.
With that, a spatial fluctuation flashed, and the four of them vanished on the spot.
...
Including the time spent on the journey, nearly half a year had passed since Su Lun had left the Alchemy plane until his return.
Leading the three others via teleportation across the sea, upon returning, he immediately reached for his communicator, "Sister, I'm back."
After a moment's wait, a voice from the communicator replied, "Hmm."
His sister's tone was as indifferent as ever, but then she added, "Good to have you back."
Listening to her, the corners of Su Lun's mouth lifted slightly.
Teleporting from the North Sea, he noticed that the coastal defenses had become much denser than before, with patrol warships almost everywhere in key maritime areas.
Which meant that the condition of the inter-plane war might already be quite dire.
Hopefully, he had not returned too late.
Su Lun didn't dare delay and teleported swiftly.
Shortly, the four appeared over the Imperial Strait.
Before they could get close to Mr. Jing's position, Su Lun noticed the turbulent waves and chaotic storm cyclones howling across the sea. Clearly, these were not normal weather patterns, but the result of legion magics and battle.
There were also fragments of warships and flying ships floating on the surface.
As a centaur bound by a battle pact, Makamul was ready for war and immediately assumed his role.
The centaur race possessed a strong sense of perception. Sniffing the elemental air, he said, "Twenty nautical miles to the north and about seventy to the northwest, there are intense energy fluctuations in both directions."
"Hmm."
Su Lun nodded.
Although he knew behind him was Mr. Jing's location, he was unaware that the enemy from the divine plane had come so close on the other side.
It seemed both sides were in a standoff.
After a brief halt, they teleported again.
As the scenery around them changed, they had already arrived in the direction of the United Empire's fleet headquarters.
Both the centaur Makamul and the Dragon Maiden Masia came from a world completely devoid of technology, a realm of pure magic. They had originally thought that the war would be much like the conflicts in their world.
But as they teleported over and saw the sky full of mechanical airships and the sea teeming with massive cannon warships, they were awe-struck, their eyes wide with disbelief.
Makamul: "What... what kind of airships are these? Made of steel? And they can actually fly in the sky?"
Masia: "All these warships are made of steel? So heavy, and yet they float on water?"
Makamul: "And those long tubes, what are they? They feel a bit like the dwarf's cannons."
Masia: "Is this alchemy..."
The Divine Power realm had been an agrarian society for countless years; they had never seen such technology. Even as ninth-tier beings, they were like curious babies, seeing everything as brand new.
When the four appeared above the sea, the people in the imperial fleet naturally spotted them immediately.
Just as they were touching down, a part of the clouds in the sky suddenly dispersed, revealing numerous unevenly sized gun barrels aiming at them. That was when the four realized that the cloud concealed an incredibly large city of steel, its constructions and defensive towers densely packed and large rivets joining giant, thick armor plates.
It was simply too massive, resembling a huge whale while the floating steam airships nearby looked like little fish.
Upon close inspection, a faint layer of rune energy encircled the fortress.
"What's all this about!"
Makamul and Masia felt like they were facing a formidable enemy. Even though they didn't recognize the cannons, the black muzzles still conveyed a deadly threat.
Su Lun saw this and chuckled, raising his voice to shout at the war fortress, "Dora, stop messing around. We've got guests."
This was, of course, the "Sky Mechanical War Fortress" that had been secretly under construction for many years.
And at the control core of this mechanical war fortress was Dora, who had also integrated the mechanism of a "God Profaner" mechanical lifeform.
No sooner had he spoken than the sound of sirens rang out next to his ear, "Wow... Mr. Su Lun is back."
With that, the mechanical arms on the steel fortress waved in unison towards the four, as if excitedly welcoming them.
Su Lun looked on and smiled faintly, "Hmm."
Now, looking at the scale of the Sky War Fortress, it had reached the design envisioned at its conception; it was the ultimate mechanical creation, an absolute weapon of war.
But employing this Sky War Fortress also meant that the current interdimensional war was edging towards a grand decisive battle.
Yet to Makamul and Masia, outsiders, the scene was once again astonishing.
They hadn't yet figured out why the steel fortress could fly in the sky, and now they watched as the entire fortress's mechanical arms greeted them.
It was then that they realized... the fortress was alive?
Unable to contain his curiosity, Makamul inquired earnestly, "Mr. Su Lun, were you just... greeting this flying steel city?"
"Hmm. The fortress is a companion of mine."
Su Lun, not knowing quite where to start explaining, and realizing that mechanical life was difficult to explain to most alchemists, let alone divine followers, laughed and said, "Let's go aboard the ship and talk more."
With a flicker of spatial disturbance, the four vanished on the spot.
....
"Mr. Su Lun is back!"
"Hahaha, everyone come quick, Mr. Su Lun is back!"
"Oh, Mr. Su Lun has brought two very special guests!"
"..."
Su Lun and his companions landed on the deck, and as soon as someone shouted out, the entire fleet immediately erupted in excitement.
From inside the cabins and on the gun platforms, windows swung open, and faces full of anticipation turned towards the deck.
The moment they saw Su Lun, they cheered him on excitedly.
Su Lun scanned with his senses and noted that there were over 200,000 people within the entire Sky War Fortress.
Some belonged to the Dawn Group, and many were imperial soldiers; after all, such a colossal Sky Mechanical War Fortress required a substantial number of combat forces and mechanics to operate.
But everyone recognized Su Lun, the "Puppet Emperor" whose face had been printed countless times in the newspapers.
His solo feat of breaking through the million-strong legion of the Heavenly Divine realm was too shocking, and it remained the most legendary battle in the history of the alchemy realm to date.
As soon as the four stepped onto the ship, the crowd immediately swarmed them.
Makamul and Masia were astounded as their feet stepped onto the hard steel deck; the sky fortress felt no different from standing on solid ground.
Listening to the tide-like cheers, their awe was quite overwhelming.
But it was as expected, after all, such an outlandish powerhouse was naturally a leader.
The two glanced around and were immediately drawn to the highest structure in the steel city. In the sky, numerous thunderbolts poured down, landing on that tower which resembled a lightning rod.
What caught their attention was not the tower, but the half-revealed, flickering white lance of lightning within it.
Makamul's eyelids twitched at the sight: "A fragment of a Divine Artifact?"
Su Lun offered an explanation, "Hmm."
This lance was a treasure found during their very first hunt for a pure-blooded giant dragon in the waters of Dragon Country.
The lance had already shattered, its sole purpose being to attract lightning.
With current technology in the alchemy realm capable of harnessing lightning for power, it had become a continuous source of energy for the fortress.
The tower itself had been converted into a supercharged lightning magic cannon.
Before they could ask more questions,
a striking figure with golden wings swooped down from the sky. Her metal wings retracted as she landed before Su Lun, unable to hide her joy, "Su Lun, you're back!"
Of course, this was Number 19, the "Mechanical Angel."
At this moment, most of her body was in combat mode, without synthetic skin, giving her an extremely sharp, metallic presence.
Makamul didn't know how to describe his feelings at the moment: "A... metal person?"
Dragon Maiden Masia's expression was equally complex.
Their understanding just couldn't grasp the concept of a super mechanical warrior.
And turning around, it wasn't just this one—on the vast deck, there were also quite a few people with mechanical arms, mechanical legs, mechanical eyes, operating mechanical tools...
The sight left the two newcomers greatly shocked, to the point where even their world views began to crumble.
In the divine realm, power always came from the gods, and all unusual skills were considered heresy.
But in the alchemy realm, these things were everywhere.
Fortunately for them, these strange mechanical humans didn't seem to pose much of a threat to them, being ninth-tier power holders, based on their energy fluctuations.
Barrett and Masia both sighed with relief in their hearts: indeed, not all alchemists were freaks.
But just as they had relaxed a bit, something else shocking happened.
At this moment, the crowd had already gathered around.
"Mr. Su Lun!"
"..."
The people crowded around, excitedly asking all sorts of questions.
Having not seen Su Lun for nearly half a year, those with keen intuition had faintly guessed that something might have gone wrong. But now, seeing his return, everyone's anxiety was eased.
It was then that Barrett and Masia realized that those gathering around were all unusually tall, with a very obvious bloodline oppression that belonged to superior creatures.
A large group of people coming together made this feeling particularly evident.
This was... the might of a dragon!
Masia was a high-blooded dragonblood herself, and she felt a certain kinship with these warriors, noticing an echo in their bloodlines.
What shocked her was not the discovery of her kin; after all, "Mr. Su Lun" himself had a strong dragon lineage.
What shocked her was that among the tens of thousands of people who had gathered on the ship, almost every one of them was a dragonblood!
Even if they were not dragonbloods, there were some who possessed the aura of ancient mythological bloodlines.
This... what was going on?
In her realm, bloodline was a gift from heaven. Someone with as pure a dragonblood lineage as herself was one in a billion.
Yet here, she found that nearly every person had an exceptionally high dragon blood resonance.
She remembered the words Su Lun had said when she signed the contract, that he could evolve her bloodline... Now it seemed, he had spoken the truth.
Barrett and Masia exchanged glances, both seeing the shock in each other's eyes.
But they said nothing.
After all, they still needed to maintain the demeanor of ninth-tier masters.
"Mr. Su Lun!"
"Teacher!"
"..."
At this time, Lolo, Gik, Tanni, the disciple Aberk, Kama... and others who were very familiar with Su Lun all crowded around.
A robust voice also greeted, "Su Lun, you're back?"
Upon closer look, it was Barrett.
Seeing his robust life force, Barrett and Masia turned their eyes slightly, thinking: Only eighth-tier? How can he achieve this level, strange...
Immediately after, an old man with a sword at his waist also appeared on the tower above, smiling and calling out, "Young friend Su Lun, you've returned."
Just looking at this old man, Barrett and Masia felt a sense of gravity: so strong!
This old man posed a lethal threat to them.
Su Lun smiled, "Elder Bartolo, it's been a while~"
No sooner had he spoken, two other persons approached.
One was a middle-aged man in a black robe, with an eyepatch over one eye; the other was a middle-aged man with a pale face, wearing a black cape with a red lining, whose age was indiscernible.
Su Lun took the initiative to greet them: "Mr. Hei, Wazhwas, all's well I trust."
Both were ninth-tier members of the Dawn group, and they both knew where Su Lun had been during this time.
Seeing him return, both of them also felt relieved.
Mr. Hei said with a kindly smile, "It's good you're back."
Wazhwas also said, "Indeed..."
Before they could finish speaking, suddenly a small head popped out from below deck.
The little ghostly miss suddenly emerged from the lower deck, shooting up and clinging to Su Lun's neck like a koala, muttering, "Ah... Su Lun, why did you take so long to come back?"
As she spoke, Pestoia's eyes reddened, and then she opened her mouth and began to cry loudly.
She had the closest relationship with Su Lun, and without any news for half a year, she had feared the worst.
Now, seeing him return, little Pestoia was naturally the happiest.
Su Lun gently patted her head, soothing the crying ghostly miss: "Alright, I have brought you a gift."
On hearing this, Pestoia's expression instantly brightened up and she stopped crying, "Really?"
Su Lun couldn't help but smile wryly, "Yes. I'll give it to you in a bit."
Yet this scene had Barrett and Masia's eyes twitching.
Others couldn't see Pestoia, but they could see that indescribable twist of soul fire.
If they weren't mistaken, that was an entity... that had congealed god-fire!
What was this?
A god?
There was a godly presence aboard this ship?
However, before they could ponder any further, a flash of mirror light, and suddenly another person appeared on the deck.
As Mr. Jing arrived, everyone together responded, "Leader."
Su Lun looked on and smiled, "Senior sister."
Mr. Jing nodded slightly, a tender joy emerging in his eyes.
Kamul and Masia observed discreetly, several threats having already appeared that made them feel uneasy.
Being powerful was one thing, but this was a peculiar kind of powerful.
It gave off an inscrutable and mysterious vibe.
Having seen the endless tricks up Su Lun's sleeve before, the two felt no contempt for the alchemists before them.
However, upon the appearance of this leader, both immediately recognized a top-tier powerhouse.
Su Lun introduced them, "This is Mr. Kamul, a ninth-tier centaur master. And this is Miss Masia, a very formidable Dragonborn."
He had mentioned them briefly in the communicator before, and Mr. Jing, aware that the two were allies, also politely said, "Welcome, friends from another plane of existence."
Kamul and his companion did not dare to take their status for granted and hurriedly placed their hands over their chests in a gesture of courtesy.
Thanks to language proficiency, communication was not an issue.
....
After meeting Su Lun, everyone on the ship was curious about the two friends she had brought back.
After all, whether it was centaurs from mythological tales or Dragonborn, no one had seen such beings before, and they gazed upon them with fascination, as if they were a novel species.
But the tradition of the Dawn group was to be very hospitable; friends would invariably be welcomed and treated warmly.
Lolota said, "Wow... so are centaurs also those that can sprout wings and fly into the sky?"
Tanni replied, "You dummy, Lolota, that's not it, those are pegasus. Centaurs are powerful warriors... In the Mythological Era, they were considered among the higher races alongside dwarves, elves, and gnomes."
Lolota commented, "Oh, I see. That Dragon Maiden sister looks really powerful, like her dragon's might is no less than the ninth-tier dragon we encountered before."
Gic said, "I don't know. But friends brought back by Mr. Su Lun must be extremely capable."
"..."
There was much discussion among the crowd.
Kamul and Masia did not feel uncomfortable, as goodwill transcends species, and they could easily tell the humans were friendly toward them.
They were also slightly surprised.
After all, on their planes, tolerance amongst races wasn't so strong; encountering guests of different species usually triggered necessary caution.
But these humans... seemed special, the benevolence in their eyes made both guests comfortable.
However, it was at this moment that the alarming "woo woo woo" siren sounded on the Sky Mechanical War Fortress's deck.
Su Lun thought it was a hostile attack and glanced at her senior sister, "???"
Mr. Jing, accustomed to such occurrences, said, "Typical surveillance behavior of the Angelic plane. They probably detected something unusual on the deck and sent someone to check it out."
Mr. Hei's expression also showed a hint of helplessness as he said, "An Angelic plane's ninth-tier wind mage with a rather special magic apparatus, very fast and cautious. We've tried several times but failed to catch him."
Su Lun followed the direction and saw a bearded figure in the winds almost ten kilometers away.
A ninth-tier Sage of Law on a reconnaissance mission would naturally be hard to capture.
At that moment, Kamul seemed to understand something and proactively asked, "An enemy?"
Su Lun nodded, "Yes."
Kamul's eyes flashed with resolve, "Then may I try?"
Su Lun thought for a moment and then smiled, "Then I'll trouble Mr. Kamul."
Others might not know of Kamul's abilities, but he was very aware.
An archer to deal with a fleet-footed target couldn't be more fitting.
Su Lun also noted that Kamul was eager to showcase his strength. After all, whether it was a contract or something else, powerhouses have their own pride.
With that, Kamul's expression turned solemn, and a terrifying aura of destruction rose around him as he made a bow-pulling gesture.
To the astonishment of all watching, a space-twisting arrow formed on the bow made of the elements.
In the distance, the wind mage conducting reconnaissance seemed to sense the danger and instantly transformed into a gust of wind, disappearing from sight.
Su Lun watched with an intense gaze, thinking: It's too late!
He had witnessed the power of that arrow; it could slay a demigod, let alone someone of the ninth-tier.
By the time one saw it, the arrow would have already struck its target.
And sure enough, as Kamul's bowstring was released, a storm erupted in the distance, exploding into fragments.
Blood stained the sky, and the ninth-tier wind mage could no longer maintain his elemental form, plummeting from the sky.
Witnessing this scene, everyone on the deck, both the Dawn members and the imperial warriors, were stunned: An arrow had severely wounded a ninth-tier Sage of Law?
Even Mr. Jing and a few of the Dawn group's ninth-tier forces took a moment to look on seriously.
To achieve this was to say, did this Kamul possess the power to contend with a demigod?
That strong?
The Dragon Maiden Masia also didn't want to be outdone. Seeing the enemy struck by the arrow, she leaped from the deck, transforming into a grim fiery dragon midair.
"Aaang~"
The high-pitched dragon roar sent a shiver through everyone.
The members of the Dawn had seen real dragons before, and at this moment, they realized that Miss Masia was truly a humanoid dragon!
The fiery figure shot through the sky like lightning, seizing the falling Sage of Law mid-plummet.
The mage, who seemed to have been spared death by some secret artifact just moments ago, coughed up blood and turned deathly pale from the grip, completely losing consciousness.
A gust of wind swept across the deck, and in the next moment, the red dragon had already returned with the captive in tow.
This time, it was the turn of everyone on the deck to be dumbfounded.
Only then did everyone realize just how astoundingly strong Su Lun's two friends were!

chapters.title: Chapter 664 - 663: Daily Life on the Sky Fortress
chapters.content:
"Wow, Mr. Makamul is so amazing!"
"Miss Masia can actually transform into a giant dragon, that's so cool~"
"..."
As the two effortlessly inflicted heavy injuries and captured a ninth-tier Mage, cheers erupted throughout the sky fortress and the entire fleet of mechanical flying ships.
Everyone had just realized that the two friends Su Lun had brought back from who knows where possessed combat abilities far exceeding those of the ninth tier.
Powerful individuals are respected everywhere, and the atmosphere instantly became warm and friendly.
Having severely injured that Mage, Makamul and Masia also felt a mysterious sense of relief. The bizarre oppressive feeling they had been under the whole time in the yellow sand dimension, pressed down by a certain freak without daring to breathe, had finally dissipated.
Su Lun watched with a faint smile on his face.
He glanced around and, not seeing someone, asked, "Sister, where is Qian Tiao? How come I haven't seen her?"
Mr. Jing's elegant eyebrows raised slightly as he said, "She cannot sit still for a day. She has been causing trouble for the Celestial Empire fleet these days. I just told her you were back, so she should be returning soon."
Su Lun: "Oh."
Speaking of coincidences, it was shortly after these words were spoken that suddenly a lookout on the watchtower shouted, "Qian Tiao is back!"
Everyone looked over to see a figure in the distant sky, coming with the force of wind and thunder, moving extremely fast.
Even from a great distance, they could sense an uncontrollable aura of fierce energy emanating from that person.
Su Lun's expression immediately turned strange and he glanced at Mr. Jing, asking, "Sister, has Qian Tiao reached the Demigod realm?"
Compared to half a year ago, that oppressive feeling had intensified too much.
Moreover, that outward radiating fierce energy, in the eyes of the All-knowing Eye, had already become threads of rules.
This was the clearest sign of being a Demigod.
"Yes."
Mr. Jing nodded, his smile full of relief yet his tone somewhat melancholic, "The three realms of 'Rakshasa Woman' are quite special. After she went to the Yellow Springs Country, she seems to have realized something impressive. Later, observing the 'Green Jade' black stele, her enlightenment progressed unlike others. Two fronts before, during Dawn's encounter with the Celestial Empire's ambush, she suddenly came to master the power of rules."
Su Lun listened and came to understand, but at the same time, his expression grew slightly solemn: "Is the current battle situation not very good?"
Although his Sister's tone was laid-back, he too detected that the recent dimensional wars were definitely not looking good. The fact that the Celestial Empire's forces dared to ambush the Dawn meant there must have been overwhelming force present.
After pondering for a moment, Mr. Jing nodded seriously, "Yes. It's pretty bad. We'll discuss this in detail later."
Before they could discuss further, Qian Tiao had already arrived, stepping on the deck.
...
Qian Tiao landed on the deck of the fortress and strode directly towards Su Lun with a bright smile, saying, "Hey! Su Lun, you finally came back!"
She came over and gave Su Lun a firm hug.
Su Lun felt a surge of tenderness in his arms, "Yes, I'm back."
Qian Tiao hugged his arm and whispered in his ear, "It's good you're alive."
Su Lun smiled faintly.
Naturally forthright, Qian Tiao didn't say much in front of others. She turned her gaze to the two friends Su Lun had brought back, as if she had discovered some treasure, her eyes gleaming, "The two of you are very strong~"
Recognizing them as allies, she enthusiastically introduced herself, "It's a pleasure to meet you both. Since you are friends of Su Lun, you are friends of Dawn too. Got time for a spar?"
At her mention of "spar", both Makamul and Masia couldn't help but twitch, thinking, "So strong!"
No,
Not just strong
But terrifyingly strong!
Just now, having defeated a ninth-tier Mage, they had felt a surge of confidence as top-tier warriors, but their confidence was instantly dispersed by the swordsman before them.
This female swordsman seemed to have killed many recently; her Sword Dao robe was stained with dark red blood spots everywhere. The blood of high-class professionals doesn't fade easily and retains some very special energy fluctuations.
Both the centaur and the dragon maiden had very sharp senses, and they certainly knew this person must have killed a lot of top-class masters.
That gaze just now felt like a blade had passed over their bodies, giving them a feeling that any sign of hostility would lead to immediate beheading.
For beings of their realm, the existence below the divine tier should hardly ever give such a terrifying oppressive feeling.
Just who was this female swordsman?
Makamul and Masia glanced at Su Lun who stood beside her, both thinking the same thing.
Indeed, this freak from the Alchemy Plane was not an exception.
Damn, here's another one!
No, three!
And that leader with the mirror-light ability, utterly unfathomable.
Among thousands on the vast deck, no one knew how complicated the feelings of these two extraordinary realm forces were at this moment.
Su Lun, seeing Qian Tiao's genuinely enthusiastic expression, quickly intervened to ease the situation, with a laugh, "Qian Tiao, Mr. Makamul and Miss Masia are guests, let's talk about the sparring later."
Hearing this from someone else, it might sound somewhat like taking advantage of their long journey.
But in Qian Tiao's mouth, there was absolutely no hidden agenda.
She was purely eager for a chance to spar and to see the power of masters from other dimensions.
Sword heart transparent.
With these words, tens of thousands on the deck cheered in unison.
Today was a day worth celebrating, Su Lun's return, and bringing back two immensely strong friends, brought a glimmer of hope to an otherwise dismal war situation.
...
A grand banquet was held in the sky fortress to celebrate Su Lun's return and welcome the two friends from afar.
Before long, everyone was satisfied with food and drink.
The fortress had an enormous internal structure, designed to maximize defense, almost completely cutting off natural light.
In the slightly gloomy metallic corridor, alchemical lamps on the walls illuminated the riveted metal walls.
Su Lun, Qian Tiao, and Pandora walked unhurriedly, planning to head back to their cabins to rest.
At that moment, a translucent little head suddenly popped out from the wall. She blinked her eyes, full of anticipation, and asked, "Su Lun, where's the gift you said you'd bring me?"
Su Lun looked at the little ghost Miss and pretended not to know, "Ah... did I say I would bring you a gift?"
Seeing his demeanor, Pestoya suddenly jumped onto his neck, baring her tiny sharp teeth and angrily threatened, "You nasty fellow... hand over the gift now, or I'll bite you to death!"
Su Lun laughed heartily, "Hahaha, of course, I brought it. Do you like it?"
With that, he took out a well-behaved life-sized doll from his miniature void realm, and it floated in mid-air.
This was no ordinary puppet doll.
In the months since he returned from the Yellow Sand Realm, Su Lun had been busy, crafting a Flawless Spirit Embryo into this alchemic homunculus.
This was the body he had promised to the ghost Miss who was riding on his neck; he had always taken it to heart.
"This..."
Seeing it, Pestoya instantly covered her small mouth with both hands, her starry clear eyes immediately sparkled with brilliance.
Looking at the doll, it was like looking in a mirror, she saw an exact replica of herself.
Light brown wavy curls, delicate and well-behaved features, goth-style smokey makeup, she looked exactly like a little princess deep in sleep. Even with her eyes closed, that quirky spirit seemed as if it had come to life. The dress she wore was also Pestoya's favorite dark Lolita dress, with lots of pretty lace and adorable puffy skirts. Just one look at it sent a rush of pure maidenly essence.
Seeing the doll, Qiantiao also brightened up, admiringly said, "Yo~ it's just like Pestoya."
The materials were all top-notch, and the craftsmanship was meticulous to perfection, naturally flawless.
Pandora also pursed her lips and smiled, chiming in, "Su Lun put a lot of thought into this homunculus body."
Su Lun gazed at his work, clearly very satisfied, "Do you like it?"
Pestoya nodded earnestly, "Mm!"
Her playful big eyes surveyed "her" body up and down, her eyelashes fluttering lightly, her eyes filled with joy and fraught with eager anticipation.
"I'm glad you like it."
Su Lun's eyes softly rippled with laughter, then he suggested, "Why don't you try it?"
Pestoya couldn't wait and, with permission granted, she no longer restrained herself but drifted over and attached herself to the alchemic body.
It had been a thousand years.
She had been a ghost for a whole thousand years.
Although she had used Pandora's body before, it was ultimately not her own.
After possession, that feeling of sensing her own body's presence finally returned.
Not only was the Flawless Spirit Embryo a divine-tier material well-matched to the soul, but Su Lun's extensive top-tier understanding and thorough research on souls meant that after the soul possession, there would absolutely be no rejection.
It was just like her own body.
Therefore, it took only a very short time for Pestoya to completely adapt to her body.
She looked at her hands, no longer just a spiritual body, her face filled with delight. But, not knowing what crossed her mind, her eyes suddenly began glistening with shining ripples.
Su Lun chuckled and asked, "How does it feel? If there's anything you're too pleased with, tell me, and we can still make adjustments."
After all, this was made just based on his own intuition.
Pestoya heard this and looked up at Su Lun, then she jumped up like a kangaroo, hanging around his neck, giving him a passionate kiss, "mua~very satisfied!"
Feeling the moist touch on his cheek, Su Lun couldn't help but laugh and cry at the same time.
Since he was no longer a ghost, he was afraid that this girl might fall off him, so he reached out and held her in his arms.
Pestoya yelled with a smile, "Wow...I love it! Su Lun, you're amazing!"
Su Lun had long gotten used to this girl's capricious personality, but with this hug, his hand was also just under her poufy skirt, feeling very tangible.
He wasn't really thinking anything untoward and joked, "A lady should be careful with her image, you're exposing yourself."
Although this alchemical body was crafted by him down to the smallest detail, sculpted and shaped bit by bit, he was more than familiar with it.
But now that the alchemical being had a soul, she was truly a person with feelings.
Pestoya also felt the big hand supporting her butt and instinctively blushed a bit.
But her eyes twinkled mischievously, clinging on and not climbing down, "Hehehe...there's no one else here, just giving Su Lun a bargain~"
Su Lun rolled his eyes and released a devastating retort, "I'm not even interested in little girls. No chest, no butt."
Upon hearing this, Pestoya reacted like a cat stepped on its tail, her fangs bared instantaneously, "Ah... you dreadful fellow, despising me after taking advantage! I...I will bite you to death!"
Saying this, she unceremoniously mounted Su Lun's neck, baring her teeth and bit at him.
But since she was not in her spiritual body anymore and was wearing a dress, this whole action was ambiguous and intimate.
Qiǎntiáo and Pandora, watching them joke around, were already used to it and only smiled, saying nothing.
Su Lun also felt quite helpless, only able to carry this girl on his shoulders and continue walking towards the cabin.
...
The sky fortress could accommodate two hundred thousand people; naturally, the space was enormous.
Although the ordinary combat member cabins were somewhat cramped, the captain's quarters were quite spacious.
Mr. Jing always had a cool disposition, disliking bustling environments. He returned to his room to rest soon after the party began.
Qiǎntiáo directly pushed open the door, and several people walked in.
After entering, Su Lun discovered that the captain's quarters on the fortress, apart from being somewhat larger, were almost identical to those on the Eternal Night.
Except for the same furniture, that 4x4 meters huge bathtub was also in the same spot.
When the four of them entered, the curtains of the bath were drawn, and steam was wafting around, apparently, Mr. Jing was taking a bath.
"Ah...finally back again..."
As soon as Qiǎntiáo entered the room, she removed her sword and placed it on a nearby rack, then began to peel off her blood-stained Sword Dao robe, revealing a back full of fierce tattoos and a wrapped chest underneath.
With no strangers around, she unabashedly began unwinding her bandages, letting them fall to the floor while speaking, "Philo, make the water hotter, I want to soak too."
Someone responded from the other side, "Okay."
Fortunately, everyone in the room was used to it, and no one thought it strange.
Su Lun also felt that the familiar environment gave a very relaxing feeling. He walked to the sofa and dumped Pestoya, who was still huffing, on it.
The little girl still looked puffed up, like a groundhog puffing out its cheeks.
Su Lun reached out his finger and rubbed her chubby cheeks, magically producing a few candies.
He knew well that this greedy girl loved candies of various flavors.
Now that she had a body and could smell the candies, it was a whole different experience from the simulated candies before.
As expected, upon smelling the candies, Pestoaya's eyes lit up immediately. She snatched the candies and popped two into her mouth, chewing and exclaiming with delight, "Wow...so delicious~"
This girl, even though a bit peculiar in temperament, was easily satisfied.
That settled her.
Su Lun smiled and ruffled her hair.
Pestoaya seemed to recall something and ran towards the bathroom. "Sister, look, Su Lun helped me create a body too~"
